Unlike the 事務次官, the 政務官 is not a civil servant but a politician, often a younger lawmaker at the start of a government career. Typical: 〜大臣政務官に起用される/就任する.

examples[].german: The hippocampus plays an important role in memory formation and spatial recognition.
There is research showing that the hippocampus shrinks when strong stress continues.
It seems that while we sleep, the hippocampus organizes the day's memories.
en.notes: 海馬 is the "hippocampus" in anatomy, the brain region for memory formation; the name (literally "sea horse") comes from its shape. Typical: 海馬が萎縮する "the hippocampus shrinks" (e.g. in Alzheimer's), 海馬の働き. In addition, 海馬 can also mean "seahorse" or "walrus", but in everyday speech today people say タツノオトシゴ and セイウチ for these. Popular-science books about learning and memory use the word often.

examples[].german: The amygdala is involved in processing emotions such as fear and anxiety.
The moment you see a snake, the amygdala reacts before you can think.
People with anxiety disorders are thought to have an overactive amygdala.
en.notes: 扁桃体 is the "amygdala" in the brain, named after its almond shape (扁桃 "almond"). It processes mainly fear and emotional reactions: 扁桃体が反応する/過剰に働く. Do not confuse it with 扁桃 or 扁桃腺 "tonsils (in the throat)", as in 扁桃腺が腫れる "the tonsils are swollen". The word appears in psychology, neuroscience and popular books about stress.

examples[].german: A synapse is the junction for signal transmission between nerve cells.
When you practice the same thing many times, the synaptic connections become stronger.
In a baby's brain, many synapses are formed every second.
en.notes: シナプス is the "synapse", the junction between nerve cells (ニューロン). Typical: シナプスを形成する "to form synapses", シナプスの結合が強まる, シナプス伝達 "synaptic transmission". Popular texts about learning often say that repetition strengthens the シナプス. The word is neurological technical vocabulary, but familiar through nonfiction books and school biology.

examples[].german: The human brain contains about one hundred billion neurons.
Neurons transmit information using electrical signals.
The mechanism of AI was made by imitating the connections of neurons in the brain.
en.notes: ニューロン is the "neuron", the loanword for the nerve cell; the Japanese word for it is 神経細胞, which is equally common in textbooks. Typical: ニューロンが発火する "a neuron fires", ニューロン同士がつながる, ミラーニューロン "mirror neuron". In IT it also stands for the nodes of artificial neural networks (ニューラルネットワーク).

examples[].german: Thanks to the plasticity of the brain, functional recovery is possible even after damage.
Clay has high plasticity, so it can be freely reshaped.
Children's brains are rich in plasticity, so they pick up the sounds of foreign languages quickly.
en.notes: 可塑性 is "plasticity, formability": 可 "possible" + 塑 "to mold" + 性 "property". Originally a term from physics and materials science (粘土の可塑性 "formability of clay"), it is today very common as 脳の可塑性 "neural plasticity", the ability of the brain to reorganize itself. Figuratively, one also speaks of the 可塑性 of children or systems. Typical: 可塑性がある/高い. Written-language and technical.

examples[].german: Heart failure can cause edema in the lower limbs.
The doctor pressed the shin with a finger to check for the presence of edema.
With kidney disease, edema often appears on the face and eyelids.
en.notes: 浮腫 (ふしゅ) is the medical technical term for "edema, water retention". The same kanji are read むくみ in everyday speech (also written 浮腫み), and that is how patients talk: 足がむくむ "the legs are swollen". Technical use: 浮腫が生じる/出現する, 下肢浮腫, 肺水腫 as a special form in the lung. So the reading ふしゅ is doctors' and textbook language.

examples[].german: Febrile convulsions caused by high fever are common in children.
Maybe because I'm tired, my eyelid has been twitching a lot lately.
The man suddenly collapsed and had convulsions, and he was taken away by ambulance.
en.notes: 痙攣 is a "cramp, twitch" and is also used as an intransitive する-verb: 足が痙攣する. Typical: 痙攣を起こす "to have a cramp / convulsion", 熱性痙攣 "febrile convulsion", まぶたが痙攣する "the eyelid twitches". Because of the difficult kanji, it is very often written in kana as けいれん. For a calf cramp, people in everyday speech rather say 足がつる; 痙攣 is more general and also medical.

examples[].german: If circulatory disorders progress, there is a danger that the tissue falls into gangrene.
My diabetes worsened and the toes developed gangrene, so they had to be amputated.
If frostbite is left untreated, fingers can also become gangrenous.
en.notes: 壊疽 is "gangrene", the death of tissue due to lack of blood flow or infection (壊 "destroy" + 疽 "ulcer"). Typical: 壊疽を起こす, 壊疽になる, 壊疽に陥る, 糖尿病性壊疽 "diabetic gangrene". Related is 壊死 "necrosis", which generally denotes the death of tissue; 壊疽 is a special form of it, often with blackening. Purely medical; in an emergency an amputation (切断) may become necessary.

examples[].german: Perforation of the appendix can lead to concurrent peritonitis.
I put up with my appendicitis for too long and nearly got peritonitis.
Peritonitis is life-threatening, so surgery is needed immediately.
en.notes: 腹膜炎 is "peritonitis": 腹膜 "peritoneum" + 炎 "inflammation". It often arises as a complication, for example when an inflamed appendix (虫垂, colloquially 盲腸) bursts. Typical: 腹膜炎を起こす/併発する, 腹膜炎になる. The classic warning is that a neglected appendicitis (盲腸) can lead to 腹膜炎. A medical technical term, but generally known.

examples[].german: Acute pulmonary edema is a serious complication of heart failure.
If you climb a high mountain quickly, there is a risk of getting pulmonary edema.
I went to see a doctor complaining of difficulty breathing and was diagnosed with pulmonary edema.
en.notes: 肺水腫 is "pulmonary edema": 肺 "lung" + 水腫 "dropsy, edema". A typical cause is 心不全 "heart failure"; it is then called 心原性肺水腫. Further combinations: 肺水腫を起こす, 急性肺水腫. Also well known is 高地肺水腫 "high-altitude pulmonary edema" in mountaineering. Related is 浮腫 "edema" in general. Purely a technical term.

examples[].german: The council's members were selected from experts.
Discussions about the new system continue in the council.
The Legislative Council compiled an outline for the reform of the Civil Code.
en.notes: 審議会 is an advisory council of experts and representatives of social groups established at ministries or municipalities. It receives a 諮問 "request for advice" and responds with a 答申 "report". Many have fixed names, such as 中央教育審議会 (abbreviated 中教審) or 法制審議会. Typical: 審議会に諮る, 審議会で議論する, 審議会の委員. A word from administration and the news.

examples[].german: Spontaneous pneumothorax is relatively common in young men.
He was hospitalized for a week with a pneumothorax.
I suddenly got a pain in my chest and was diagnosed with a pneumothorax at the hospital.
en.notes: 気胸 is the medical technical term for a "pneumothorax": air enters the pleural space and the lung partially collapses. Typical are 気胸になる, 気胸を起こす and 気胸と診断される; the spontaneous form is called 自然気胸, the dangerous tension form 緊張性気胸. In everyday speech it is often paraphrased as 肺に穴が開く "there is a hole in the lung".

examples[].german: Preventing pressure sores is important for patients who are bedridden for a long time.
We change your position every two hours so that no pressure sores form.
A small pressure sore was found on my grandmother's heel.
en.notes: 褥瘡 is the medical and nursing technical term for "decubitus, pressure ulcer". In everyday speech people almost always say 床ずれ; 褥瘡 is heard mainly in hospitals, nursing care and technical texts (褥瘡ケア, 褥瘡予防). Typical combinations are 褥瘡ができる "a pressure sore forms" and 褥瘡を防ぐ. Because of the rare character 褥, government offices often write じょく瘡.

examples[].german: Aspiration pneumonia in the elderly ranks high among causes of death.
My father drinks thickened drinks so that he doesn't aspirate during meals.
When the ability to swallow weakens, a person can aspirate even saliva.
en.notes: 誤嚥 denotes "swallowing the wrong way" in the medical sense: food, liquid or saliva enters the windpipe instead of the esophagus. As a する-verb: 食べ物を誤嚥する; a feared consequence is 誤嚥性肺炎 "aspiration pneumonia". In everyday speech people say むせる or 気管に入る. Do not confuse it with 誤飲 "accidentally swallowing" an object into the stomach, for example when a child swallows a coin.

examples[].german: Long periods of immobility raise the risk of deep vein thromboembolism.
After a long flight, I developed a pulmonary embolism.
Atrial fibrillation is one of the main causes of cerebral embolism.
en.notes: 塞栓症 is an "embolism": a blood clot, fat or air (塞栓) is carried along in the blood and blocks a vessel. It mostly appears in compounds: 肺塞栓症 "pulmonary embolism", 脳塞栓症 "cerebral embolism", 血栓塞栓症 "thromboembolism". The pulmonary embolism after sitting for a long time on a plane is popularly known as エコノミークラス症候群. Purely technical; in everyday speech people rather say 血管が詰まる.

examples[].german: Intestinal obstruction is an acute disease accompanied by severe abdominal pain and vomiting.
My grandfather developed an intestinal obstruction caused by adhesions from a previous surgery.
With suspected intestinal obstruction, I was admitted to the hospital as an emergency right away.
en.notes: 腸閉塞 is an "intestinal obstruction": the intestinal contents can no longer be transported onward. In hospital routine you often hear the loanword イレウス, used largely with the same meaning. Typical are 腸閉塞になる and 腸閉塞を起こす; a frequent cause is adhesions (癒着) after abdominal surgery. Key symptoms are 腹痛, 嘔吐 and absent bowel movements.

examples[].german: Cystitis is a urinary tract infection commonly seen in women.
When urine accumulates in the bladder, you want to go to the toilet.
Please fill your bladder before the examination.
en.notes: 膀胱 is the "urinary bladder", an anatomical term that also comes up in everyday life when talking about complaints. Common compounds are 膀胱炎 "bladder infection", 膀胱がん "bladder cancer" and 過活動膀胱 "overactive bladder". Because of the rare characters, guides often write ぼうこう. For frequent urges to urinate, people in everyday speech simply say トイレが近い.

examples[].german: Prostate cancer is a malignant tumor common in elderly men.
My father has an enlarged prostate and gets up to go to the toilet many times in the night.
Once you pass fifty, you should have your prostate examined.
en.notes: 前立腺 is the "prostate", a gland below the bladder in men. Important compounds are 前立腺がん "prostate cancer" and 前立腺肥大(症) "benign prostatic enlargement"; the latter is the typical reason for nighttime urges to urinate in older men. At screening examinations you hear 前立腺の検査 or PSA検査. A technical term, but generally familiar in health topics.

examples[].german: Cervical cancer can be prevented by vaccination.
A baby grows in the womb for about forty weeks.
My older sister had surgery for uterine fibroids.
en.notes: 子宮 is the "uterus"; the word is both a technical term and a normal everyday word. Important compounds are 子宮頸がん "cervical cancer", 子宮体がん "endometrial cancer", 子宮筋腫 "fibroid", 子宮内膜症 "endometriosis" and 子宮外妊娠 "ectopic pregnancy". Attributively it takes の: 子宮の中の赤ちゃん.

examples[].german: Ovarian cancer is easily detected late because early symptoms are scarce.
A small swelling was found in the right ovary on the ultrasound.
The ovaries are also organs that secrete female hormones.
en.notes: 卵巣 is the "ovary". It is a paired organ, so people say 右の卵巣, 左の卵巣 or 両側の卵巣. Common compounds are 卵巣がん "ovarian cancer", 卵巣嚢腫 "ovarian cyst" and 卵巣機能 "ovarian function". The male counterpart is 精巣 "testis". A technical term, but generally understandable in health topics.

examples[].german: The placenta is the organ that supplies nutrients and oxygen from the mother to the fetus.
Some time after the baby was born, the placenta came out.
The test showed placenta previa, so I ended up having a cesarean section.
en.notes: 胎盤 is the "placenta, afterbirth". Typical combinations are 胎盤が出る (expulsion after birth), 前置胎盤 "placenta previa" and 胎盤早期剥離 "placental abruption". In cosmetics and advertising language, the loanword プラセンタ is usually used for placenta extracts. 胎盤 itself is a technical term of obstetrics.

examples[].german: The prime minister's advisory body compiled a report.
The council is an advisory body to the minister, and its reports are not legally binding.
The city set up a new advisory body made up of experts.
en.notes: 諮問機関 is a body that prepares opinions at the request (諮問) of an authority or official; the typical example is the 審議会. Its recommendations (答申, 提言) are not legally binding - unlike a 議決機関 "decision-making body". Common: 〜の諮問機関, 私的諮問機関 "informal advisory group" (e.g. of the prime minister). An administrative term.

examples[].german: Amniocentesis is a method of diagnosing chromosomal abnormalities in the fetus.
At the checkup I was told that the amount of amniotic fluid is a little low.
My water broke in the middle of the night, and the amniotic fluid flowed out.
en.notes: 羊水 is the "amniotic fluid" in which the fetus floats in the uterus. Important combinations are 羊水検査 "amniotic fluid test", 羊水が少ない / 多い and 羊水が流れ出る. The rupture of the membranes itself is called 破水 (破水する). A technical word of obstetrics, but generally known to pregnant women.

examples[].german: In the case of a breech baby, a cesarean section is often chosen.
My eldest daughter was born by cesarean section.
Because the baby's heartbeat dropped, an emergency cesarean section was performed.
en.notes: 帝王切開 is the "cesarean section"; 帝王 "emperor" + 切開 "incision" is a calque of the European term. Typical combinations are 帝王切開で産む / 生まれる, 帝王切開になる (when one becomes necessary), 緊急帝王切開 and 予定帝王切開. The opposite is 自然分娩 or 経腟分娩. Among hospital staff and mothers the short form 帝切 (ていせつ) is also widespread.

examples[].german: Once contractions become regular, the start of delivery is near.
When the interval between contractions becomes ten minutes, please call the hospital.
My wife endured contractions for twelve hours and gave birth to a healthy baby boy.
en.notes: 陣痛 are "labor pains, contractions". Typical combinations are 陣痛が始まる / 来る, 陣痛が強くなる, 陣痛の間隔 "contraction interval" and 陣痛促進剤 "labor-inducing drug". Irregular practice contractions are called 前駆陣痛. The word is in general use, not only in hospitals; for childbirth as a whole people say 出産 or お産.

examples[].german: Painless delivery is a childbirth method that uses epidural anesthesia.
My husband went into the delivery room and was present at the birth.
This hospital handles about a thousand deliveries a year.
en.notes: 分娩 is the medical term for "delivery, childbirth"; in everyday speech people rather say 出産 or お産. Typical are compounds such as 分娩室 "delivery room", 分娩台, 自然分娩 and 無痛分娩 "birth with epidural anesthesia". As a する-verb (分娩する) it sounds clinical; normal are 出産する or 産む.

examples[].german: Screening tests for newborns detect congenital diseases early.
Newborns spend most of the day sleeping.
Because it was a premature birth, my daughter spent some time in the neonatal intensive care unit.
en.notes: 新生児 is a "newborn", medically a child in the first 28 days of life. Compounds: 新生児室, 新生児集中治療室 (NICU), 新生児黄疸 "neonatal jaundice". In everyday speech people rather say 生まれたばかりの赤ちゃん. Distinguish 乳児 "infant" (up to about one year) and 幼児 "toddler".

examples[].german: Algae are attracting attention as a raw material for biofuel.
The pond water is green because algae are increasing.
Algae in the sea produce large amounts of oxygen through photosynthesis.
en.notes: 藻類 is the biological collective term for "algae", from microscopic green algae to large seaweeds. In everyday speech people say 藻 (も) for algae in a pond or aquarium and 海藻 for edible seaweed such as わかめ or 昆布. 藻類 sounds scientific and often appears in compounds such as 微細藻類 "microalgae" or in expressions like 藻類が増える / 繁殖する.

examples[].german: Fungi play an important role in ecosystems as decomposers.
Mushrooms and molds are both members of the fungi.
Yeast, which is used to make bread and beer, is also a kind of fungus.
en.notes: 菌類 is the biological umbrella term for "fungi" in the broad sense: yeasts, molds and mushrooms. In everyday speech people say キノコ for edible mushrooms and カビ for mold; 菌類 is the scientific word. Do not confuse it with 細菌 "bacteria"; the single character 菌 colloquially means "germs" in general.

examples[].german: Enzymes have the selectivity to act only on specific substrates.
An enzyme binds to its substrate and moves the reaction forward.
Cartilage cells are surrounded by a matrix they have made themselves.
en.notes: 基質 is above all a term of biochemistry: the substance on which an enzyme acts, i.e. the "substrate". Typical combinations are 基質特異性 "substrate specificity", 酵素と基質 and 基質と結合する. In histology 基質 also means "matrix, ground substance" (細胞外基質). Do not confuse it with the identically pronounced 気質 "temperament"; a substrate in electronics is called 基板.

examples[].german: Enzymes are proteins that promote chemical reactions in living organisms.
The enzyme contained in saliva breaks down starch.
This detergent contains enzymes that remove dirt.
en.notes: 酵素 is an "enzyme". Typical combinations are 酵素が働く, 酵素の働き, 消化酵素 "digestive enzyme" and 酵素反応. In everyday life the word also appears in advertising, for example for detergents (酵素入り洗剤) or drinks (酵素ドリンク). Do not confuse it with 酵母 "yeast", which is a living organism.

en.meaning: field office; local branch of a government agency
examples[].german: Applications are accepted at field offices in each region.
Hello Work is a field office of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare.
Some argue that the state's regional field offices should be abolished and their powers transferred to local governments.
en.notes: 出先機関 are regional branch offices of central government agencies, especially the ministries' offices in the regions (国の出先機関), e.g. employment offices or regional construction bureaus. 出先 alone means "the place one is currently visiting" or "branch office". In the debate on decentralization one often hears 出先機関の廃止/統合. An administrative word.

examples[].german: Ribosomes synthesize proteins based on the information of messenger RNA.
Some antibiotics interfere with the function of bacterial ribosomes.
Ribosomes are also attached to the surface of the endoplasmic reticulum.
en.notes: リボソーム is the "ribosome", the cell structure at which proteins are built. A purely biological technical term; the spelling リボゾーム also occurs. Typical combinations are リボソームで合成される and リボソームRNA. In everyday life the word appears almost only in connection with antibiotics that inhibit bacterial ribosomes.

examples[].german: Mitochondria are the cell organelles responsible for producing the cell's energy.
Mitochondria are often called the "power plants of the cell".
Mitochondrial DNA is inherited only from the mother.
en.notes: ミトコンドリア is the "mitochondrion"; Japanese does not mark number, so the word also stands for "mitochondria". In popular science it is often called 細胞の発電所 "power plant of the cell". Typical combinations are ミトコンドリアDNA and ミトコンドリアの機能. A technical term, but quite well known through health and fitness topics.

examples[].german: Eukaryotic cells have a distinct nucleus surrounded by a nuclear membrane.
The cells of animals and plants are all eukaryotic cells.
Exam questions often ask you to explain the difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
en.notes: 真核細胞 is the "eukaryotic cell": 真 "true" + 核 "nucleus" + 細胞 "cell", i.e. a cell with a true cell nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane. The opposite is 原核細胞; organisms made of such cells are called 真核生物. Purely technical, typical of biology class and textbooks.

examples[].german: Bacteria are organisms made up of prokaryotic cells that have no nuclear membrane.
Prokaryotic cells have no organelles such as mitochondria.
Prokaryotic cells are much smaller than eukaryotic cells.
en.notes: 原核細胞 is the "prokaryotic cell": 原 "original" + 核 "nucleus" + 細胞 "cell", i.e. a cell without a true, membrane-enclosed cell nucleus. This includes bacteria and archaea, together called 原核生物. The opposite is 真核細胞. A purely technical biology term.

examples[].german: The double helix structure of DNA was discovered by Watson and Crick.
The two strands of the double helix are connected by bonds between bases.
A large model shaped like the DNA double helix is displayed at the entrance of the science museum.
en.notes: 二重螺旋 is the "double helix", mostly as the 二重螺旋構造 of DNA. Because 螺 and 旋 are difficult characters, 二重らせん is very often written. 螺旋 alone means "spiral, helix", e.g. in 螺旋階段 "spiral staircase". Technical, but generally known through the history of the discovery of DNA.

examples[].german: Transcription is the process in which the information of DNA is copied into RNA.
I transfer the lines of the pattern onto the fabric before cutting.
The child is playing with a transfer sticker from a candy giveaway stuck on his arm.
en.notes: 転写 generally means "to transfer, to copy": text or an image is copied from a template onto something else. In biology it is the technical term for "transcription" (DNAからRNAへの転写); the next step, translation into protein, is called 翻訳. In everyday life it appears with decals (転写シール) or when transferring sewing patterns. As a transitive する-verb: 情報を転写する, passive 転写される.

examples[].german: The human genome consists of about three billion base pairs.
Adenine forms a base pair with thymine, and guanine with cytosine.
A difference of just a single base pair can cause disease.
en.notes: 塩基対 is a "base pair": two complementary bases of DNA (A-T, G-C) joined by hydrogen bonds. It also serves as a unit of measurement for the length of DNA, for example 約三十億塩基対. Composition: 塩基 "base" + 対 "pair", read つい here as in 一対. Purely technical.

examples[].german: Nanotechnology is a technology that manipulates matter at the atomic level.
This sunscreen uses an ingredient that applies nanotechnology.
I am thinking of majoring in nanotechnology at university.
en.notes: ナノテクノロジー is "nanotechnology", i.e. engineering in the range of billionths of a meter (ナノメートル). In headlines and conversation it is often abbreviated to ナノテク. Typical combinations are ナノテクノロジーを応用する, ナノテクノロジーの研究 and ナノテクノロジー分野. A loanword of technical and newspaper language.

examples[].german: 3D printing technology has greatly shortened the time needed to manufacture prototypes.
Prosthetic hands made by 3D printing are much cheaper than conventional ones.
At the factory, parts are made one by one using 3D printing.
en.notes: 三次元印刷 is a rare, formal expression for "3D printing". In normal usage people almost always say 3Dプリント or speak of the device as 3Dプリンター; in industry and standards the process is called 積層造形 "additive manufacturing". 三次元印刷 is found mainly in written, factual texts. Composition: 三次元 "three-dimensional" + 印刷 "printing".

examples[].german: Carbon fiber reinforced composite materials contribute to making aircraft lighter.
This tennis racket is made of a lightweight and strong composite material.
Reinforced concrete is also a kind of composite material in the broad sense.
en.notes: 複合材料 is a "composite material": a material made of two or more components that together have better properties than individually. The best-known example is 炭素繊維強化プラスチック, but in a broader sense reinforced concrete also belongs here. Typical are 複合材料を使う / 採用する and 複合材料製の…; 複合素材 is used similarly but is somewhat more general-language. Technical language of engineering and materials science.

examples[].german: The operating costs of the independent administrative agency were reviewed.
The Japan International Cooperation Agency is one of the independent administrative agencies.
After graduating from university, he got a job at a research institute run as an independent administrative agency.
en.notes: 独立行政法人 are institutions that were spun off from ministries in 2001 and are legally independent, carrying out public tasks with more autonomy, such as the development agency JICA, national museums or research institutes. Abbreviated, one says 独法. Typical: 独立行政法人化 "conversion into an independent agency", 〜は独立行政法人の一つだ. A term from administration and the business press.

examples[].german: Nickel-based superalloys are heat-resistant materials used for turbine blades.
The new superalloy retains its strength even at temperatures exceeding a thousand degrees.
When I was a child, my superalloy robot toy was my treasure.
en.notes: 超合金 is a "superalloy", mostly nickel- or cobalt-based, that stays strong even at very high temperatures; it is used in jet engines and gas turbines. Many Japanese people, however, first associate the word with toys: 超合金 is also the name of a well-known series of robot figures made of die-cast metal. Composition: 超 "super-" + 合金 "alloy". Reading note: in タービン翼 "turbine blade", 翼 is read よく in technical language.

examples[].german: Technology for producing hydrogen fuel by the electrolysis of water is being researched.
In a science experiment, when we electrolyzed water, hydrogen and oxygen were produced.
Aluminum is made by electrolyzing the raw material.
en.notes: 電気分解 is "electrolysis": a substance is broken down with electric current. As a transitive する-verb: 水を電気分解する "to electrolyze water", passive 電気分解される. In technical texts it is often shortened to 電解 (電解質 "electrolyte", 電解液). A classic topic in chemistry class and today frequent in reports about hydrogen production.

examples[].german: The heat exchanger is a device indispensable for energy saving in industrial processes.
If dust accumulates on the air conditioner's heat exchanger, its efficiency drops.
This ventilation system uses a heat exchanger so that the warmth of the room is not lost.
en.notes: 熱交換器 is a "heat exchanger", a device that transfers heat from one medium to another without the two mixing. It is found in air conditioners, boilers, car radiators and ventilation systems. Composition: 熱 "heat" + 交換 "exchange" + 器 "device". For home ventilation you often read 熱交換型換気 or simply 熱交換. Technical language of engineering.

examples[].german: The dielectric of a capacitor increases its ability to store charge.
A microwave oven heats a dielectric such as food by applying electromagnetic waves to it.
Glass and ceramics are typical dielectrics.
en.notes: 誘電体 is a "dielectric": an insulator that can be polarized in an electric field. It matters above all in capacitors (コンデンサ) and in high-frequency engineering. Related terms are 誘電率 "permittivity" and 絶縁体 "insulator", the more general term without emphasis on polarization. Purely technical.

examples[].german: A piezoelectric element converts mechanical deformation into an electrical signal.
A piezoelectric element is used to ignite gas stoves.
An experiment was carried out in which piezoelectric elements were laid on the floor to generate electricity from the vibrations of people walking.
en.notes: 圧電素子 is a "piezo element": a component that generates an electric voltage under pressure and, conversely, vibrates or deforms under voltage. Composition: 圧 "pressure" + 電 "electricity" + 素子 "component". ピエゾ素子 is synonymous; the phenomenon itself is called 圧電効果. Applications are lighters, gas stoves, ultrasonic sensors and small speakers. Technical language.

examples[].german: Einstein received the Nobel Prize for his theoretical explanation of the photoelectric effect.
In the photoelectric effect, it is the frequency, not the intensity, of the light that determines whether electrons are ejected.
Solar cells produce electricity using the photoelectric effect.
en.notes: 光電効果 is the "photoelectric effect": light releases electrons from a material. Composition: 光 "light" + 電 "electricity" + 効果 "effect". It is famous through Einstein's light quantum hypothesis (光量子仮説); as the internal photoelectric effect (内部光電効果) it is used in photocells and solar cells. A purely technical physics term.

examples[].german: Ultrasound diagnosis is a non-invasive and safe imaging examination method.
At prenatal checkups, the baby's growth is confirmed by ultrasound diagnosis.
Gallstones were found as a result of the ultrasound diagnosis.
en.notes: 超音波診断 is "ultrasound diagnostics". In everyday speech people mostly say エコー or エコー検査, and in hospitals also 超音波検査; 超音波診断 sounds more formal and appears in technical texts and device names (超音波診断装置). Typical areas of use are prenatal care, abdominal organs and the heart (心エコー). 超音波 alone is "ultrasound".

examples[].german: Magnetic resonance imaging is excellent at depicting soft tissue.
A small abnormality was found in my brain on the MRI.
The MRI exam makes loud noises, so I was handed earplugs.
en.notes: 磁気共鳴画像 is the image or procedure of "magnetic resonance imaging"; the procedure is precisely called 磁気共鳴画像法. In everyday speech practically everyone says MRI or MRI検査; the long Japanese form is read almost only in technical literature and official texts. Composition: 磁気 "magnetism" + 共鳴 "resonance" + 画像 "image". Unlike CT, the method works without X-rays.

examples[].german: Positron emission tomography detects the metabolic activity of cancer cells.
I had a PET scan at my comprehensive medical checkup.
In PET imaging, a drug similar to glucose is injected before the scan.
en.notes: 陽電子断層撮影 denotes "positron emission tomography"; the full technical name is 陽電子放射断層撮影. In everyday speech people almost always say PET検査 or PET-CT. Composition: 陽電子 "positron" + 断層撮影 "cross-sectional imaging, tomography". The method is used mainly to look for cancer, because tumor cells take up a lot of sugar.

examples[].german: Pharmacokinetics studies how a drug is absorbed, distributed, metabolized and excreted in the body.
In the elderly, pharmacokinetics easily changes because of declining kidney function.
In clinical trials of new drugs, pharmacokinetics is first examined in healthy people.
en.notes: 薬物動態 denotes "pharmacokinetics": how a drug is absorbed, distributed, metabolized and excreted in the body. The associated science is called 薬物動態学. Typical combinations are 薬物動態を調べる / 評価する. Distinguish it from 薬力学 "pharmacodynamics", i.e. what the drug does in the body. Purely technical.

examples[].german: The certification criteria for public-interest corporations were tightened.
This art museum is run by a public interest incorporated foundation.
Public-interest corporations enjoy tax preferences.
en.notes: 公益法人 are legal entities that serve the public good. Since the 2008 reform there are 公益社団法人 "public interest incorporated association" and 公益財団法人 "public interest incorporated foundation", which require a 公益認定 "public-interest certification" and are tax-privileged. To be distinguished are 一般社団法人, which lack this certification, and NPO法人. A term from law and administration.

examples[].german: Simulation software is indispensable for designing electronic circuits.
As a hobby, I built a simple electronic circuit and made a radio.
The electronic circuit shorted after getting wet, and my smartphone stopped working.
en.notes: 電子回路 is an "electronic circuit" with components such as transistors, resistors and capacitors. Typical combinations are 電子回路を設計する / 組む and 電子回路図 "circuit diagram". Distinguish 電気回路, the more general "electric circuit", and 基板, the circuit board on which the circuit sits. Technical language, but familiar among hobbyists and students.

examples[].german: Strengthening cybersecurity is an important issue for companies.
The government plans to increase the number of cybersecurity experts.
Cybersecurity training was held for employees.
en.notes: サイバーセキュリティ is "cybersecurity", the protection of computers, networks and data from attacks. The spelling with a long vowel, サイバーセキュリティー, is equally common. Typical combinations are サイバーセキュリティを強化する and サイバーセキュリティ対策. Related are サイバー攻撃 "cyberattack" and 情報セキュリティ "information security". Language of the media, government offices and companies.

examples[].german: Biodegradable plastics contribute to reducing environmental impact.
This straw is made of a biodegradable material.
Even if something is called biodegradable, some things are not readily broken down in the sea.
en.notes: 生分解性 is "biodegradability": the property of a substance to be broken down by microorganisms into water and carbon dioxide. It mostly stands attributively before a noun, directly or with の: 生分解性プラスチック, 生分解性の素材 "biodegradable material". Composition: 生 "biological" + 分解 "decomposition" + 性 "property, -ability". A technical word, but frequent in environmental reports.

examples[].german: Carbon fiber is a lightweight material with about ten times the strength of steel.
The frame of this road bike is made of carbon fiber.
Demand for carbon fiber is also growing in the fields of automobiles and wind power generation.
en.notes: 炭素繊維 is "carbon fiber", very light and at the same time extremely strong. In advertising and everyday speech people often say カーボン or カーボンファイバー (カーボン製の自転車). Typical are 炭素繊維強化プラスチック "carbon-fiber-reinforced plastic" and 炭素繊維製の…. Since Japanese manufacturers are world leaders, the word often appears in business news.

examples[].german: Plasma is the fourth state of matter after solid, liquid and gas.
Lightning and auroras are examples of plasma seen in nature.
In a fusion reactor, ultra-high-temperature plasma is confined with a magnetic field.
en.notes: プラズマ is "plasma" in the physical sense: an ionized gas, often called the fourth state of matter. Natural examples are lightning, auroras and the sun; technically one speaks of プラズマ切断 "plasma cutting" or 核融合プラズマ "fusion plasma". Note: blood plasma is normally called 血漿 in Japanese, not プラズマ.

examples[].german: Dark matter is thought to make up most of the mass of the universe.
The true nature of dark matter is still not known today.
At an experimental facility deep underground, researchers are trying to detect dark matter.
en.notes: 暗黒物質 is "dark matter": invisible matter that makes itself noticeable only through its gravity. In popular media people often say ダークマター; 暗黒物質 is the somewhat more formal, technical expression. The counterpart 暗黒エネルギー or ダークエネルギー is "dark energy". Typical expressions are 暗黒物質の正体 "what dark matter actually is" and 暗黒物質を検出する.

examples[].german: The direct detection of gravitational waves confirmed Einstein's prediction.
Gravitational waves from the merger of two black holes were observed.
The observation of gravitational waves has created a new way of looking at the universe.
en.notes: 重力波 are "gravitational waves": distortions of spacetime that propagate at the speed of light, for example when two black holes merge. Typical combinations are 重力波を観測する / 検出する and 重力波望遠鏡. For this purpose Japan operates the underground detector KAGRA in Gifu. In meteorology, 重力波 also denotes "gravity waves" in the atmosphere.

examples[].german: It is difficult to get a research position with only a bachelor's degree.
After earning a bachelor's degree in literature, she got a job at a publishing company.
The medical school has a system that allows working adults who hold a bachelor's degree to enroll.
en.notes: 学士 denotes the "bachelor's" degree or a person with a university degree. The degree itself is called 学士号, the course of study 学士課程; above it come 修士 "master's" and 博士 "doctorate". On a résumé one writes, for example, 学士(経済学). In everyday speech people usually say 大卒 or 大学卒業 instead of 学士; 学士 sounds official.

examples[].german: That theory was overturned by later research.
On this problem, scholars are divided in their theories.
He advanced a theory that was bold for its time.
en.notes: 学説 is an "academic theory, doctrine", as represented by a scholar or a school. Typical combinations are 学説を唱える "to advance a theory", 学説が分かれる "scholarly opinions are divided" and 新しい学説; the prevailing view is called 通説. Compared with 理論, 学説 emphasizes the position that is held; 仮説 is a still unproven "hypothesis". Written language.

examples[].german: The philosophy of the Kyoto School achieved its own development.
In economics there are many schools, starting with the Keynesian school.
He took a unique position, belonging to no school of thought.
en.notes: 学派 is a "school" in the sense of a scholarly or philosophical movement whose representatives share a common doctrine. It mostly stands after a place or person name: 京都学派, フランクフルト学派, ケインズ学派. Typical combinations are 学派に属する and 学派を形成する. Distinguish 流派, a school in art and martial arts (such as ikebana), and 派閥, a political "faction, clique".

en.meaning: parliamentary investigative power; right of investigation in government affairs
examples[].german: The Diet exercised its investigative power and demanded documents.
The opposition, citing the right of investigation, demanded that those involved be summoned as witnesses.
The right of investigation in government affairs is recognized in Article 62 of the Constitution.
en.notes: 国政調査権 is the right, anchored in Art. 62 of the Constitution, of both houses of parliament to investigate government affairs, summon witnesses (証人喚問) and demand documents. Typical: 国政調査権を行使する/発動する, 国政調査権に基づき. One hears the word above all in scandals, when the opposition demands clarification. Technical and formal.

examples[].german: It is important to acquire a broad general education.
She is cultured, and it is fun to talk with her.
In my first year, I mainly took liberal arts courses.
en.notes: 教養 is broad cultural and intellectual education that makes a person "cultivated" - not specialized knowledge and not the formal degree (that is 学歴). Typical are 教養がある／ない, 教養のある人 and 教養を身につける. At universities, 一般教養 or 教養科目 denotes the general-education basic courses of the first years. Compared with 知識 ("knowledge"), 教養 also emphasizes judgment, taste and manners.

examples[].german: People with a grounding in music also learn languages quickly.
My grandmother was a person with accomplishment in tea ceremony and calligraphy.
This job requires a grounding in statistics.
en.notes: 素養 is a foundation in a particular field acquired through practice or instruction, often since childhood: 音楽の素養, 漢文の素養, 数学の素養. Almost always in the frames 〜の素養がある／ない or 素養を身につける. Unlike 教養 ("broad general education"), 素養 refers to a concrete subject or art; unlike 素質 ("innate aptitude, talent"), it is learned. Rather elevated, written-leaning style.

examples[].german: I plan to take five subjects this semester.
The deadline for course registration is next Friday.
If you complete the teacher-training course, you can obtain a teaching license.
en.notes: 履修 is the technical term in schools and universities for enrolling in and completing courses: 科目を履修する (transitive, with を). Common compounds are 履修登録 ("course registration"), 履修科目 and 履修単位. In contrast to 受講 ("to attend a class"), 履修 means the official enrollment with credit for assessed work; 修了 is the completion of an entire program. In everyday speech people often just say 授業を取る.

examples[].german: Even working adults can attend university classes as auditors.
Anyone can attend this public lecture series free of charge.
I asked the professor and was allowed to sit in on a graduate-school lecture.
en.notes: 聴講 means to listen to a lecture or talk, especially without being formally enrolled: 講義を聴講する. Very common is 聴講生 ("auditor"); on posters you read 聴講無料 ("admission free") or 聴講料. A regular student who attends a course for credit would 受講する or 履修する; 聴講 emphasizes mere listening.

examples[].german: I was forced to drop out for financial reasons.
He was expelled for violating school rules.
He dropped out of university and started his own company.
en.notes: 退学 is the final departure from a school or university without a degree, whether voluntary or as a punishment: 大学を退学する (intransitive する-verb; を marks the place being left). The punishment is called 退学処分 ("expulsion from school"), passive 退学になる; the form is the 退学届. Colloquially people often say 中退 (from 中途退学). Distinguish it from 休学 ("leave of absence", you stay enrolled) and 卒業 ("graduation").

examples[].german: I took a year's leave of absence to recover from an illness.
I intend to take a year off from university to study abroad.
Students on a leave of absence can also use the library.
en.notes: 休学 is the official, time-limited interruption of school attendance or studies during which you remain enrolled: 大学を一年休学する. You submit a 休学届, are then 休学中 and later return with 復学. In contrast to 退学 ("final withdrawal"), 休学 is temporary; for being absent on individual days, one says 欠席 or 学校を休む instead.

examples[].german: I am still enrolled in graduate school now.
He was on the staff of this company for ten years.
About fifty players are on this club's roster.
en.notes: 在籍 means to be officially listed in a register, at a school but also at a company, team or club: 〜に在籍する (intransitive, with に). Common are 在籍者数, 在籍期間 and 在籍証明書. 在学 refers only to schools and universities, 所属 emphasizes belonging to a group; 在籍 highlights the formal status.

examples[].german: Please don't forget to enter your student ID number.
Your student status remains even during a leave of absence.
If you leave tuition unpaid for a long time, you may lose your student status.
en.notes: 学籍 is the official entry as a pupil or student in a school's register, that is, student status itself. It most often appears in 学籍番号 ("student ID number") and 学籍簿 ("student register"). One says 学籍を置く ("to be enrolled") and 学籍を失う; the process of being enrolled, on the other hand, is expressed with 在籍する. A purely administrative term.

examples[].german: He devoted his whole life to scholarship.
My older brother is the typical scholarly type and has no interest in career advancement at all.
Even after retirement, he continues his research as a man of learning.
en.notes: 学究 refers to a person who devotes himself entirely to study and research, and also to this devotion itself. Typical are 学究肌 ("scholarly temperament"), 学究の徒 ("disciple of learning") and 学究生活. Unlike 学者 ("scholar" as a profession), 学究 emphasizes unworldly devotion, sometimes with a slight undertone of being out of touch with real life. Elevated, literary style.

examples[].german: It was fortunate that I could study under a great scholar.
He is known as an eminent authority on Oriental history.
One of the foremost scholars of our time was invited to give the commemorative lecture.
en.notes: 碩学 is a very elevated, respectful word for a scholar of exceptional learning, roughly "an eminent authority". It appears mainly in obituaries, commemorative volumes and introductions: 当代きっての碩学, 〜の碩学として知られる, 碩学の士. 博学, by contrast, describes the quality ("well-read, learned"), and 学者 is the neutral term for the profession. Rare in everyday speech.

examples[].german: A no-confidence motion against the Cabinet was submitted to the Diet.
The no-confidence motion was rejected, with few in favor.
The city council passed a resolution of no confidence in the mayor.
en.notes: 不信任 means "no confidence, lack of trust" and is known above all from politics: 内閣不信任案 "no-confidence motion against the Cabinet", 不信任決議 "vote of no confidence", 不信任案を可決/否決する. If a no-confidence vote is passed in the lower house, the Cabinet must resign or dissolve the house. In the personal sphere, one rather says 不信感 "distrust" or 信用できない.

examples[].german: He is known as a person of wide learning and many talents.
My grandfather was very learned and could answer any question I asked.
Even the professors were amazed at his erudition.
en.notes: 博学 means "broadly learned, very well-read" and is used as a noun and as a な-adjective: 博学な人, 博学ぶり ("his erudition"). A set phrase is 博学多才 ("learned and versatilely gifted"). Almost synonymous is 博識, which emphasizes more the amount of knowledge; colloquially one says 物知り. 碩学, on the other hand, refers to the person himself and is even more elevated.

examples[].german: The era shifted from an age of ignorance to an age of enlightenment.
It is arrogant to dismiss the common people as ignorant and backward.
People at that time were unenlightened and believed that illnesses were caused by evil spirits.
en.notes: 蒙昧 means "ignorant, unenlightened" and is used mainly as a な-adjective; its counterpart is 啓蒙 ("enlightenment", literally "to open up the darkness"). Most common is the set phrase 無知蒙昧 ("utterly ignorant and unenlightened"). The word is literary and strongly pejorative; applied to specific people it sounds condescending. In everyday speech one rather says 無知.

examples[].german: Enlightenment thought had a great influence on modern Japan.
For many years she has been engaged in educational campaigns for environmental protection.
He wrote an easy-to-follow guidebook to educate the general reader.
en.notes: 啓蒙 is enlightenment in the sense of conveying knowledge to the uninformed; as a する-verb it is transitive: 市民を啓蒙する. Common are 啓蒙活動 ("educational campaign"), 啓蒙書 ("popular-science book") and, historically, 啓蒙思想 and 啓蒙主義 for the European Enlightenment. Because 啓蒙 can mean condescendingly "enlightening the ignorant", government agencies today often prefer 啓発 ("raising awareness"). The counterpart is 蒙昧.

examples[].german: The cultivation of character is the true purpose of education.
Through strict training he forged both body and mind.
This school places great emphasis on the cultivation of character through sports.
en.notes: 陶冶 literally comes from "pottery making and metal casting" and figuratively means the shaping of character and abilities. It is a strongly literary term from pedagogy and philosophy, used almost only in 人格の陶冶 or 人格を陶冶する (transitive). More everyday words are 人格形成 or 育成; 涵養 emphasizes rather the gradual growth of a quality.

examples[].german: We are expected to strive to cultivate a moral sense.
I want to cultivate a rich sensibility through reading.
Forests have the function of recharging water sources.
en.notes: 涵養 means to let a quality or ability grow slowly and naturally, like water seeping into the ground. Typical of curricula and official documents: 道徳心の涵養, 豊かな情操を涵養する (transitive). A second meaning is groundwater recharge: 水源涵養, 水源涵養林 ("water-source protection forest"). In contrast to 育成 or 養成 ("to train deliberately"), 涵養 emphasizes gradual growth.

examples[].german: Under the guidance of his revered teacher, he became an excellent scholar.
I owe who I am today to your guidance, professor.
Players shaped by the great coach are now active as coaches themselves in many places.
en.notes: 薫陶 is made up of "fumigating with fragrance" and "pottery making": a revered teacher shapes his students through his personality, as fragrance seeps into clothes. Almost always in the form 〜の薫陶を受ける, politely ご薫陶; the phrase 薫陶よろしきを得る praises a successful upbringing. The word stands for the influence of a respected person, not for mere teaching (指導), and is very elevated, for example in speeches and words of thanks.

examples[].german: He taught until his retirement.
She currently teaches Japanese literature at a university in America.
After graduating, he ended up teaching at a local high school.
en.notes: 教鞭 is literally the teacher's pointer or rod, but it is used practically only in the set phrase 教鞭を執る ("to teach, to work as a teacher"), usually with a place: 大学で教鞭を執る. It is elevated and suitable for résumés, introductions and obituaries; in everyday speech one says 教える or 教師をしている. 執る is often also written 取る.

en.meaning: teacher and pupil; master and disciple
examples[].german: The master-disciple relationship carries an important meaning in Japanese culture.
The two have been in a teacher-student relationship for thirty years.
The final turned into a clash between master and pupil.
en.notes: 師弟 combines "master/teacher and pupil" as a pair and emphasizes the personal bond, for example in art, martial arts or scholarship: 師弟関係, 師弟愛, 師弟の絆, 師弟の間柄. Careful, 子弟 ("sons, young people", e.g. 良家の子弟) is read the same way. For the relationship in school in general, one rather says 先生と生徒.

examples[].german: He became a pupil of a famous painter.
Akutagawa Ryunosuke was one of Natsume Soseki's pupils.
This dojo has over a hundred students.
en.notes: 門下 refers to the body of pupils of a master, literally "under the gate" of his house. Typical are 〜の門下に入る ("to become someone's pupil"), 〜門下の作家 and 門下生 ("pupil, disciple"), e.g. 漱石門下. Compared with 弟子, 門下 is more elevated and emphasizes belonging to a school or tradition, for example in art, literature, martial arts or scholarship.

en.meaning: to study under; to become a pupil of
examples[].german: From a young age he studied under a master craftsman and refined his skills.
In graduate school I studied linguistics under Professor Yamada.
She has been studying under a certain pianist since the age of five.
en.notes: 師事する means to go to someone as a teacher and study under him; the teacher takes に: 〜に師事する (intransitive). It is elevated and typical of the résumés of artists, musicians and scholars: 〜に師事し、〜を学ぶ. More colloquial is 〜に弟子入りする; 門下に入る is similar. Do not confuse it with 指示 ("instruction") or 支持 ("support"), which are read the same way.

examples[].german: A censure resolution against the minister was passed.
A censure resolution is not legally binding.
The person in charge who mishandled the response to the accident was held accountable within the company.
en.notes: 問責 means to hold someone responsible for a failure. In politics, a 問責決議 is a censure by the upper house against the prime minister or a minister; unlike a 不信任決議 in the lower house, it is not legally binding, but it puts those concerned under political pressure. As a verb, 〜を問責する (rather written); in normal usage one says 責任を問う.

examples[].german: Many talented people have left this school to make their way in the world.
Today I say goodbye to this school where I spent three years.
At the reunion I visited my beloved old school for the first time in a long while.
en.notes: 学舎 in the reading まなびや is a poetic, nostalgic word for the school as a place, especially one's own former school. It sounds like school songs, graduation speeches and anniversary publications: 懐かしい学舎, 学舎を巣立つ. In factual language, for example for buildings, 学舎 is also read がくしゃ, or one says 校舎; in everyday speech simply 学校.

examples[].german: I got the opportunity to study at the highest institution of learning.
The University of Tokyo is often called Japan's highest institution of learning.
Just because someone graduated from a top university doesn't mean they are good at their job.
en.notes: 学府 is an elevated word for a seat of learning and occurs almost only in the fixed combination 最高学府, which designates the "university" as the highest educational institution; sometimes it specifically means the University of Tokyo. In the sense of "bastion of scholarship" there is also 学問の府. In everyday speech one says 大学.

examples[].german: Twenty years have passed since I left school.
Once you leave school and go out into society, opportunities to learn tend to decrease.
I still keep in touch with friends from my student days.
en.notes: 学窓 is literally the "window of the school" and stands elegantly for school or university as a phase of life. It occurs almost only in fixed phrases: 学窓を巣立つ ("to graduate and go out into the world"), 学窓を離れる and 学窓時代 ("school or student days"). Typical of speeches, letters and reminiscences; in everyday speech one says 学生時代.

examples[].german: A modern school system was introduced in the Meiji period.
With the postwar educational reform, the 6-3-3-4 system began.
A change of the school system to a September start is being discussed.
en.notes: 学制 is the legally established school and education system of a country, such as the Japanese 六・三・三・四制. Common are 学制改革 ("reform of the education system") and, historically, 学制 as a proper name for the education ordinance of 1872 (明治五年), with which universal schooling began. Unlike 教育課程 ("curriculum"), 学制 concerns the structure: school levels, duration, start of the school year.

examples[].german: Reform of the curriculum is being discussed.
This school draws up its own curriculum.
English was officially added to the elementary school curriculum.
en.notes: 教育課程 is the official term for the curriculum of a school or school level; in Japan it is drawn up on the basis of the 学習指導要領 ("national curriculum guidelines"): 教育課程を編成する. In everyday and business language people mostly say カリキュラム. Do not confuse it with 教職課程, the teacher-training program at universities.

examples[].german: English is a required subject for all grades.
This class is compulsory, so if you fail it you can't graduate.
Programming education has been made compulsory in elementary schools.
en.notes: 必修 designates what must be taken as a requirement in a curriculum: 必修科目, 必修単位, 必修の授業; the counterpart is 選択 or 選択科目. 必修化 means "to make compulsory". Do not confuse it with 必須 ("indispensable"), which is used generally for the essential, e.g. 必須条件. 必修 is limited to school and training.

examples[].german: You must choose three from among the elective subjects.
I decided to take Chinese as an elective.
From third year on, the number of electives increases.
en.notes: 選択科目 is an elective that you freely choose from an offering; its counterpart is 必修科目 ("required subject"). One says 選択科目を取る or, more formally, 選択科目を履修する. At universities one often also distinguishes 選択必修科目 ("restricted elective"), where you must choose from a certain group.

examples[].german: I improved my classes by adopting new teaching methods.
At university I'm taking a class on methods of teaching Japanese.
The communicative approach is a teaching method that puts emphasis on conversation.
en.notes: In 教授法, 教授 does not mean "professor" but "teaching, instructing": it is the "teaching method" or instructional methodology of a subject. Particularly well known is 日本語教授法, the pedagogy of teaching Japanese as a foreign language. Related are 指導法 ("method of guidance") and 教育法 ("method of education"); colloquially one says 教え方. Typical: 教授法を学ぶ/取り入れる/工夫する.

examples[].german: The paper was published in a peer-reviewed academic journal.
The paper I submitted finally passed peer review.
She serves as a reviewer for an international academic conference.
en.notes: 査読 is the expert evaluation of a submitted scholarly article by fellow specialists: 論文を査読する (transitive). Common are 査読付き論文／査読付きの学術誌 ("peer-reviewed"), 査読者 ("reviewer") and 査読を通る ("to pass peer review"). General checking of texts, on the other hand, is called 校閲 ("copyediting") or simply チェック.

examples[].german: I published my research results in the university bulletin.
This paper appeared in the in-house journal and has not been peer-reviewed.
The institute's bulletin is published every March.
en.notes: 紀要 is the in-house series of a university, faculty or research institute in which mainly its own staff publish: 大学の紀要, 研究紀要, 紀要論文. In Japanese scholarship, contributions in a 紀要 are often considered less weighty than those in a peer-reviewed academic journal (学術誌), because they usually do not go through strict 査読. A purely academic technical term.

examples[].german: The international situation is changing rapidly.
I'll decide whether to postpone the trip while watching the situation in the Middle East.
Amid the harsh economic conditions, many companies reduced hiring.
en.notes: 情勢 is the overall situation as it develops from many factors, mostly in politics, economy or society: 国際情勢, 中東情勢, 経済情勢, 社会情勢, 選挙情勢. Typical: 情勢を見守る, 情勢が緊迫する, 情勢が悪化する. 状況 is more general and more concrete ("the situation here and now"), 事情 means "circumstances, background", 形勢 the balance of forces in a contest.

examples[].german: The spokesperson was removed because of a verbal gaffe.
The manager was dismissed due to poor results.
Following the scandal, the company president removed the executive in charge.
en.notes: 更迭 is the replacement of an official by another, usually initiated from above and often after a mistake or scandal - that is, a veiled dismissal. Typical: 〜を更迭する, 〜が更迭される, 事実上の更迭 "de facto removal". Neutral is 交代 "change", considerably harsher 解任 "dismissal"; for a voluntary resignation one says 辞任. Common in political and sports news.

examples[].german: The research was evaluated as having high academic value.
Academic papers must be written in a fixed format.
This archaeological site is extremely valuable academically.
en.notes: 学術 denotes science and research as an institutional field, mostly as the first element of compounds: 学術論文, 学術誌, 学術用語, 学術調査, 学術会議. With 的 it becomes 学術的 ("scholarly, academic"). 学問 rather means learning and the individual discipline, 科学 (natural) science; 学術 sounds official and abstract.

examples[].german: The theory was revised on the basis of the latest findings.
New findings were obtained from this survey.
Through working abroad, he broadened his business know-how.
en.notes: 知見 refers to insights gained through research, observation or experience, especially of a specialist kind. Typical phrases: 新たな知見を得る, 知見を広げる／深める, 最新の知見, 専門的な知見. In contrast to 知識 ("knowledge" in general), 知見 emphasizes insights from investigation and experience; 見解, on the other hand, is a "view, statement of opinion". Formal, typical of reports and scholarship.

examples[].german: She has deep knowledge of Japanese art.
The company president is also known for his deep knowledge of classical music.
I asked a specialist well versed in medieval history for his opinion.
en.notes: 造詣 is used almost exclusively in the set phrase 〜に造詣が深い ("to be very well versed in something"), attributively 〜に造詣の深い人. It means a deep understanding acquired over years, often in art, culture or a field of study. The phrase is appreciative and elevated; one does not use it about oneself. More neutral is 〜に詳しい.

examples[].german: He held forth with his knowledge about wine.
Every time he drinks, the department head starts expounding his knowledge.
I had to listen endlessly to ramen trivia and got fed up.
en.notes: 蘊蓄 is accumulated, deep knowledge; it is mostly written うんちく in kana. In elevated usage, 蘊蓄を傾ける means "to bring all one's knowledge to bear". Today うんちく is mainly colloquial and slightly mocking: うんちくを語る／垂れる ("to show off with detailed knowledge, to hold forth") about wine, ramen or cars, plus うんちく好き. Neutral would be 知識, appreciative 造詣.

examples[].german: Conversations with her, who is so widely learned, are always interesting.
He knows an astonishing amount about history.
Because of his enormous knowledge, he is called a "walking encyclopedia".
en.notes: 博識 means "very well-read, broadly informed" and is a noun and a な-adjective: 博識な人, 博識ぶり. It is almost synonymous with 博学; 博識 emphasizes more the amount of knowledge about many things, 博学 thorough scholarship. Colloquially one says 物知り. Praising, rather elevated style.

examples[].german: Ashamed of my lack of education, I started studying on my own.
My grandfather had no schooling, but he had more life wisdom than anyone.
This is a difficult topic for an uneducated person like me, but please allow me to ask one question.
en.notes: 無学 means not having received any (school) education; noun and な-adjective: 無学な人. Said about others it sounds pejorative, so today one hears it mainly modestly about oneself (無学な私には…) or in stories about earlier generations. 無知, by contrast, means ignorance in general or in a particular matter; colloquially one says 学がない.

examples[].german: He mastered three languages through self-study.
He passed the bar exam through self-study.
Feeling the limits of self-study, I started going to a piano school.
en.notes: 独学 is learning without a teacher or school, usually with で: 独学で学ぶ／身につける／合格する; as a する-verb it is transitive (英語を独学する), attributively 独学の画家. Antonyms are 師事する or 学校に通う. Similar is 自習, which however rather means independent practice within a course, e.g. 自習時間.

examples[].german: There is a system that supports students who work hard at their studies.
I decided to cut back on part-time work and concentrate on my studies.
A student's essential duty is study.
en.notes: 勉学 is an elevated word for serious learning and studying as a life task, above all of pupils and students. Typical are 勉学に励む ("to study diligently"), 勉学に専念する and 勉学の場. For concrete everyday studying (studying for a test tonight) one says 勉強; 勉学 sounds like speeches, scholarship conditions and school regulations.

examples[].german: On the school trip, we toured temples in Kyoto.
There is a program that supports the education of financially struggling students.
The standard period of study for this department is set at four years.
en.notes: 修学 means "to learn, to receive an education", but occurs almost only in compounds: 修学旅行 ("school trip", the multi-day school excursion in middle and high school), 修学年限 ("standard period of study") and 修学支援 ("educational support"). Careful: 就学 ("school entry, school attendance") is read the same way and concerns entry into compulsory schooling.

examples[].german: A rise in the school enrollment rate is an indicator of social development.
My daughter reaches school age next year.
Support money is paid to families with preschool-age children.
en.notes: 就学 is entering school or attending school within the framework of compulsory education, a term from administration and education policy: 就学年齢, 就学前の子ども ("preschool children"), 就学率, 就学援助 ("school assistance"), 就学通知. As a する-verb it is intransitive: 小学校に就学する. 修学 (learning, esp. 修学旅行) is read the same way; in everyday speech one says 入学 or 学校に上がる.

examples[].german: The impeachment trial of the judge was opened.
In Japan, members of the Diet act as judges and conduct impeachment trials.
In the United States, an impeachment trial of the president was held in the Senate.
en.notes: 弾劾裁判 is a procedure for removal from office. In Japan it is directed only against judges: an 弾劾裁判所 "impeachment court" made up of lawmakers from both houses decides on their 罷免 "removal". In reports about foreign countries, it means e.g. the impeachment proceedings against a president. 弾劾 alone means "impeachment, removal from office" or "harsh denunciation" (〜を弾劾する). Legal and formal.

en.meaning: commuting to school; way to school
examples[].german: A one-hour commute to school each way is physically demanding.
I go to school by bicycle every morning.
This road is a school route for elementary school children, so please slow down.
en.notes: 通学 is the regular trip to school or university, i.e. commuting: 電車で通学する (intransitive), 自転車通学. Common are 通学路 ("school route" as a road), 通学時間 and 通学定期 ("student commuter pass"). For working people one says 通勤; 登校, by contrast, means showing up at school on a particular day (登校日, 不登校).

examples[].german: After recovering, he returned to school and graduated without problems.
My study abroad is over, so I plan to return to my university next month.
After his suspension ended, he was finally able to return to school.
en.notes: 復学 is the return to school or university after an interruption, for example after 休学 ("leave of absence") or 停学 ("temporary suspension"): 復学する (intransitive), 大学に復学する. In administrative language there are 復学届 and 復学手続き. After a 退学, on the other hand, re-admission (再入学) is usually necessary.

examples[].german: He transferred to another school for family reasons.
To transfer to an American university, you need a transcript.
Students who wish to transfer, please consult the academic affairs office.
en.notes: 転学 is the change to another school, especially to another university, or to another faculty: 他大学に転学する (intransitive). It is a formal, administrative term; for changes between elementary, middle and high schools, people say 転校 in everyday speech. A change of faculty within the same university is more precisely called 転学部.

en.meaning: going on to higher education; advancing to the next school level
examples[].german: Regional disparities in the rate of advancement to higher education are seen as a problem.
After graduating from high school, I want to go on to a university in Tokyo.
I still can't decide between further study and a job.
en.notes: 進学 is the transition to the next higher level of education, especially from high school to university: 大学に進学する (intransitive, with に). Common are 進学率 ("advancement rate, university enrollment rate"), 進学校 ("high school with a high university-entry rate"), 進学塾 and 進学か就職か ("study or work"). 入学, by contrast, is the concrete entry into a particular school.

examples[].german: The child prodigy skipped grades and entered university.
Japanese schools have almost no system for skipping grades.
She skipped two grades and graduated from high school at fifteen.
en.notes: 飛び級 is skipping one or more grade levels because of exceptional performance: 飛び級する (intransitive), 飛び級で大学に入る, 二年飛び級する. In Japan this is hardly possible; only in exceptional cases is there 飛び入学 ("early admission to university"). The word therefore often comes up in connection with foreign school systems. The opposite is 留年 or 落第 ("to repeat a year").

examples[].german: I passed the exam with barely the minimum score.
For a newcomer's proposal, it's probably passable.
In ancient China, it was extremely difficult to pass the imperial examination.
en.notes: 及第 means to pass an exam or to meet the requirements for the next year; the opposite is 落第. As a verb (試験に及第する) it sounds old-fashioned today; normally one says 合格する. Mainly alive is 及第点 ("passing mark"), also figuratively: 及第点をつける／及第点だ ("quite decent, adequate"). Historically one speaks of 及第 in the Chinese civil service examination (科挙).

examples[].german: I studied desperately for fear of failing.
If things go on like this, you'll fail and have to repeat the year.
If you keep making customers wait, you fail as a service.
en.notes: 落第 means failing an exam or not being promoted and having to repeat the class: 落第する (intransitive). At universities, 留年 is mostly used today, and for exams 不合格 or 試験に落ちる. Figuratively, 落第 also means "to fall short of expectations": 落第点, 〜としては落第だ. The opposite is 及第.

en.meaning: top of the class; first place
examples[].german: She graduated from university at the top of her class.
He entered the school with the top score, but his grades didn't improve after that.
She was chosen as principal player of the orchestra.
en.notes: 首席 is the first person in a ranking. In education it appears mainly as 首席で卒業する／入学する ("to graduate as the top of the class, or to pass the entrance exam with the top score"). It also designates the highest position: 首席代表, 首席補佐官, and in an orchestra 首席奏者 ("principal player"). Do not confuse it with the identically read 主席, the title of a head of state or party (国家主席).

examples[].german: The degree was conferred with honors.
My older brother has always been a model student and was constantly praised by the teachers.
His answer is so much like a model student's that you can't see what he really thinks.
en.notes: 優等 means "outstanding, of the highest rank" and occurs mainly in compounds: 優等生 ("model student"), 優等賞, 優等の成績. 優等生 is also used figuratively and slightly ironically: 優等生的な答え ("a well-behaved, conformist answer"). The opposite is 劣等. A degree "with honors" is rarely described this way in Japan; more usual are 首席で卒業 or 成績優秀.

examples[].german: He overcame his inferiority complex and regained his self-confidence.
Because I was always compared with my gifted older brother, I felt inferior all the time.
He was a poor student as a child, but now he teaches at a university.
en.notes: 劣等 means "inferior, of low rank" and appears almost only in compounds: 劣等感 ("inferiority complex", 劣等感を抱く／持つ) and 劣等生 ("poor student"). The opposite is 優等 (優等生). Used alone, 劣等 is strongly pejorative and rare; 劣った or 劣る are more usual.

examples[].german: The Supreme Court ruled the law unconstitutional.
Some scholars argue that exercising the right of collective self-defense is unconstitutional.
The plaintiffs filed an unconstitutionality suit against the state.
en.notes: 違憲 is a noun ("unconstitutionality"), but is mostly used predicatively: 〜は違憲だ, 違憲と判断する, 違憲判決. Well known is 違憲状態 "unconstitutional state", for example with unequally weighted votes (一票の格差). The opposite is 合憲. Note: it is read the same as 意見 "opinion" - context decides.

examples[].german: A survey was conducted to explore the causes of the decline in academic ability.
By attending cram school, he greatly improved his academic ability in a year.
The results of the national academic achievement test were announced.
en.notes: 学力 is the level of attainment acquired at school, that is, knowledge and skills in school subjects - not the ability to learn. Typical: 学力が高い／低い, 学力をつける／伸ばす, 基礎学力, 学力低下 and 学力テスト (e.g. the nationwide 全国学力テスト). 能力 is more general, 実力 means the ability that one can actually produce, for example in an exam.

examples[].german: Improvement of after-school care for schoolchildren is being called for.
On the way to school, please give top priority to the safety of schoolchildren.
Since both of us work, our daughter goes to the after-school program.
en.notes: 学童 designates children of elementary-school age and is a rather official word that mainly appears in compounds: 学童保育 "after-school care", 学童期 "elementary-school age", 学童用 "for schoolchildren". In everyday speech one says 小学生 or simply 子ども. Colloquially 学童 is also the short form of 学童保育, that is, the "after-school program": 学童に行く, 学童に預ける. Do not confuse it with 児童 (official term for children; in school likewise elementary pupils) and 生徒 (middle and high school students).

examples[].german: The result of whether you passed or failed will be announced next week.
You will be notified personally by e-mail whether you passed.
Sometimes the impression made in the interview decides whether you are accepted.
en.notes: 合否 combines 合格 "passed" and 否 "not" and designates the result of an exam or selection as a decision of "pass or not". It is a formal word from announcements and official language: 合否を発表する, 合否を通知する, 合否判定, 合否に関わる. In conversation one rather asks 受かった？ or 結果はどうだった？. Similarly built are 成否 "success or failure" and 可否 "whether permissible or not".

examples[].german: You shouldn't choose a school based on the standard score alone.
In the summer mock exam, my deviation score went over 60.
This university has a high deviation score, so getting in is difficult.
en.notes: 偏差値 is a statistical standard score (mean 50, standard deviation 10) that is used in Japan above all for mock exams (模試) and for ranking schools and universities. Typical: 偏差値が高い / 低い, 偏差値が上がる, 偏差値60の大学. The word often stands for the whole performance-oriented selection system; 偏差値教育 and 偏差値偏重 are critical terms. The term "standard deviation" itself, on the other hand, is 標準偏差.

examples[].german: A teaching practicum is required to obtain a teaching license.
I have a teaching license, but I currently work as an office worker.
The requirement to renew teaching licenses was abolished in 2022.
en.notes: 教員免許 is the state teaching qualification; officially the document is called 教員免許状. One says 教員免許を取る / 取得する / 持っている; for this you need certain courses of study and a school practicum (教育実習). 教員 is the formal word for teaching staff, while in everyday speech one says 先生 or 教師. The type is named more precisely, for example 小学校の教員免許 or 英語の教員免許.

examples[].german: A list of recommended books was handed out as supplementary reading for the class.
We learned the history of our region from a supplementary booklet produced by the city.
In moral education class, we read a story from the supplementary reader and then discuss it.
en.notes: 副読本 is made up of 副 "secondary, supplementary" and 読本 "reader": a companion booklet or supplementary book that is used in class alongside the official textbook (教科書). Typical are booklets published by municipalities on local studies or books for moral education (道徳の副読本). Not to be confused with 参考書, which is a study aid that you buy yourself for exam preparation. Usage: 副読本として使う / 配る.

examples[].german: The development of digital teaching materials is progressing.
Ms. Tanaka always teaches with handmade materials.
This drama can also be used as material for learning Japanese.
en.notes: 教材 covers everything used for teaching or learning: textbooks, worksheets, videos, apps. 教科書, by contrast, is only the official school textbook; 教具 are physical aids such as blackboards or models. Common patterns: 〜を教材にする / 教材として使う, 手作りの教材, デジタル教材, 教材費 "cost of materials", 教材研究 "lesson preparation".

examples[].german: I chose a school known for its liberal atmosphere.
The school's tradition-minded spirit has been handed down to this day.
Before enrolling, I visited the school to see whether its atmosphere suited me.
en.notes: 校風 is the spirit or atmosphere of a school: its traditions, values and the way people treat each other. Typical: 自由な校風, 伝統を重んじる校風, 校風に合う / 合わない. Distinguish it from 校則 (concrete school rules), 校訓 (a formulated school motto) and the analogously formed 社風 "company culture". The word is neutral to slightly elevated.

examples[].german: Simplicity and fortitude are this school's motto.
The school motto hangs large on the wall of the gymnasium.
At the graduation ceremony, the principal explained the meaning of the school motto once again.
en.notes: 校訓 is the official guiding maxim of a school, often a four-character phrase such as 質実剛健 or 自主自律. It is 掲げる "displayed, held high", for example in the assembly hall or the classroom, and quoted at ceremonies. Distinguish: 校則 "school rules", 校風 "school atmosphere", 校歌 "school song"; analogously formed are 社訓 "company motto" and 家訓 "family motto".

examples[].german: A ruling came down that this law is constitutional.
The government explains that this measure is constitutional.
Courts review the constitutionality of laws.
en.notes: 合憲 means "constitutionality" and is mostly used predicatively: 〜は合憲だ, 合憲と判断する, 合憲判決. The derived 合憲性 "constitutionality" is examined or disputed (合憲性を審査する). The opposite is 違憲. A word of legal and political language that often appears in news about court rulings.

examples[].german: Violations of the school regulations are subject to disciplinary action.
The regulations set the maximum period of enrollment at eight years.
At this high school, part-time jobs require permission under the school regulations.
en.notes: 学則 is the official, written regulation of a school or university: admission, length of study, credits, degrees and disciplinary measures. Typical: 学則に定める, 学則で定められている, 学則に違反する. The everyday rules of conduct for pupils (hairstyle, uniform, ban on mobile phones), by contrast, are called 校則; at universities one speaks of 学則. The word is formal.

examples[].german: We cultivate social skills through extracurricular activities.
On an extracurricular outing, we visited a nearby factory.
Third-year students take extracurricular exam-prep courses after school.
en.notes: 課外 means "outside the regular curriculum" (課 "lesson, workload" + 外 "outside") and appears almost always in compounds or with の: 課外活動 "extracurricular activities, clubs", 課外授業 "extra class, field trip", 課外講座 "supplementary course". Do not confuse it with 放課後 "after class" (time) and 校外 "outside the school grounds" (place). For school clubs one usually says 部活 in everyday speech.

en.meaning: arts and sciences; learning and the arts
examples[].german: I did a practicum at a museum to obtain a curator's qualification.
At the elementary school's arts festival, I played the lead in a play.
A review of a newly published book appeared in the newspaper's culture section.
en.notes: 学芸 means "the sciences and the arts" and hardly occurs alone, but almost only in fixed compounds: 学芸員 "curator (museum)", 学芸会 "elementary-school event with plays and music", 学芸欄 / 学芸部 "culture section or arts desk of a newspaper". It also appears in names such as 東京学芸大学. For "art and science" in general, one rather says 学問と芸術 today.

examples[].german: After finishing the beginner course, you move on to the intermediate level.
At the driving school, you learn theory and practice following a fixed curriculum.
This course is designed so that you can learn step by step from the basics.
en.notes: 教程 is a formal word for a course of instruction built up in stages or the corresponding textbook series. You encounter it in driving schools (教習所の教程), in the training plans of the police or military, and in the titles of music and language textbooks (e.g. ピアノ教程). For the curriculum of a school, one rather says カリキュラム or 教育課程; 課程 alone designates a course of study (博士課程). Typical: 教程に沿って進める, 初級教程.

en.meaning: study room; reception room (shoin style); publisher (in names)
examples[].german: From the temple's shoin, we gazed at the beautiful garden.
The shoin-zukuri style became the prototype of the modern Japanese tatami room.
My grandfather would shut himself in his study and write Chinese poetry.
en.notes: 書院 was originally a study and writing room in temples and samurai residences, later a formal reception room. From it developed the architectural style 書院造 of the Muromachi period with 床の間 and 違い棚, the model of today's 和室. Today the word is encountered mainly in architecture and history and in publishers' names (〜書院). An ordinary study is called 書斎; in a Chinese context, 書院 also designates a Confucian academy.

examples[].german: Fukuzawa Yukichi opened a private school called Keio Gijuku.
Yoshida Shoin's Shokasonjuku is a famous private academy of the late Edo period.
A retired former teacher runs a small private school at home.
en.notes: 私塾 is a school run by a private individual. Historically it means the private academies of the Edo period in which a scholar gathered pupils around him, such as 松下村塾 or 適塾; they stood alongside 藩校 (domain schools) and 寺子屋 (elementary schools). Today it designates small-scale private teaching, for example in one's own home. A state-recognized private school, on the other hand, is a 私立学校, and a cram school is simply 塾 in everyday speech.

examples[].german: Terakoya functioned as educational institutions for the common people.
At terakoya, reading, writing and the abacus were taught.
A "modern terakoya", where local adults help children with their studies, is popular.
en.notes: 寺子屋 were the elementary schools for the common people in the Edo period, in which children (寺子) learned reading, writing and arithmetic with the abacus (読み書きそろばん). Despite the name, they by no means took place only in temples; teachers also included samurai, doctors or townspeople. They are regarded as the reason for the high literacy in premodern Japan. Today 寺子屋 is also used figuratively for free learning offerings in the neighborhood, often in quotation marks.

examples[].german: At domain schools, the sons of samurai studied Confucianism.
The Nisshinkan in Aizu is one of the representative domain schools.
There are still high schools in many places that carry on the tradition of a domain school.
en.notes: 藩校 (also 藩学) were the schools that the feudal lords (大名) of the individual domains (藩) established in the Edo period for the children of their retainers. Taught were mainly the Confucian classics, later also martial arts, medicine and Western sciences. Well-known examples are 日新館 in Aizu or 明倫館 in Hagi. Distinguish from 寺子屋 (for the common people) and 私塾 (private academies). A purely historical term.

examples[].german: Confucian teachings are deeply rooted in Japanese educational thought.
The Edo shogunate valued Confucianism, centered on Neo-Confucianism (Shushigaku).
She studies Chinese Confucian thought in graduate school.
en.notes: 儒学 is the teaching of Confucius (孔子) as scholarship and learning, that is, the study of the Confucian classics. 儒教, by contrast, means Confucianism as an ethical-religious system and social influence (儒教的な価値観). Related are 儒学者 "Confucian scholar" as well as the schools 朱子学 and 陽明学. Typical: 儒学を学ぶ / 重んじる, 儒学の教え.
