en.notes: 仮定形 is one of the six conjugation forms (活用形) of Japanese school grammar: 未然形, 連用形, 終止形, 連体形, 仮定形, 命令形. It is the form before ば: 行け（ば）, 高けれ（ば）, 静かなら（ば）. In the West the result is usually called the ば-form or conditional. In classical grammar this position is occupied by the 已然形, which has a different function.

examples[].german: The verb form listed in the dictionary is the terminal form.
「らしい」 and the hearsay 「そうだ」 attach to the terminal form of a verb.
In classical Japanese there are verbs such as 「あり」 whose terminal form differs from modern Japanese.
en.notes: 終止形 is one of the six conjugation forms (活用形) of Japanese school grammar: the form with which a sentence ends (書く。高い。). For modern verbs and adjectives it is identical to the 連体形 and the dictionary form; differences exist with だ (終止形 だ, 連体形 な) and in classical Japanese (あり／ある). It is followed by, among others, らしい, だろう and the hearsay そうだ. In Japanese-as-a-foreign-language teaching one mostly says 辞書形.

examples[].german: The attributive form is used when modifying a noun.
In modern Japanese, the terminal form and the attributive form of a verb have the same shape.
The attributive form of 「静かだ」 is 「静かな」, used as in 「静かな部屋」.
en.notes: 連体形 is the conjugation form that connects to a noun (体言) – literally "the form that links with a 体言". For modern verbs and い-adjectives it is the same as the 終止形; it becomes clear with な-adjectives and the copula: 静かだ→静かな部屋, 学生だ→学生なので. It also stands before ので and のに. In classical Japanese it often differs from the 終止形 and plays a role in 係り結び (after ぞ, なむ, や, か). Grammatical term.

examples[].german: The irrealis form combines with negative and passive affixes.
The 「書か」 in 「書かない」 is the irrealis form of 「書く」.
In classical Japanese, the irrealis form plus 「ば」 gives a hypothetical meaning.
en.notes: 未然形 literally means "not-yet-realized form". It is followed by ない (書かない), the passive れる／られる, the causative せる／させる and, in school grammar, also う／よう (書こう). In classical Japanese, 未然形＋ば expresses a hypothetical condition, whereas 已然形＋ば denotes a condition that has already occurred. In modern Japanese the 仮定形 has taken its place. Grammatical term of school and classical grammar; in foreign-language teaching one speaks rather of the ない-form.

examples[].german: The realis form is one of the conjugation forms in classical grammar.
When 「ば」 is attached to the realis form, it expresses something that has already happened as a condition.
When the emphasizing particle 「こそ」 is present, the sentence ends in the realis form.
en.notes: 已然形 literally means "already-so form" and is one of the six conjugation forms of classical grammar. 已然形＋ば denotes a condition that has already occurred ("since, when"), in contrast to 未然形＋ば "if"; in addition, a sentence ends in the 已然形 after こそ (係り結び). In modern Japanese the 仮定形 has taken its place (書けば = "if"). Beware of the kanji: 已 "already" is not 己 "oneself" or 巳 "snake". Technical term of classical-Japanese teaching.

examples[].german: Pragmatics studies the relationship between language use and context.
Pragmatics explains how 「ちょっと寒いね」 can function as a request to close the window.
The appropriate choice of honorific speech is an important research topic in pragmatics.
en.notes: 語用論 is pragmatics, the branch of linguistics that studies how meaning arises in concrete use and context – for example indirect requests, implicatures (含意), speech acts (発話行為) and politeness (ポライトネス). Distinctions: 意味論 studies literal, context-independent meaning, 統語論 sentence structure. For Japanese, with its many indirect ways of expressing things, 語用論 is especially central. Academic technical term.

en.meaning: false accusation; wrongful conviction; miscarriage of justice
examples[].german: The miscarriage of justice was revealed by DNA testing.
It took him twenty years to clear his name of the false charge.
On crowded trains, some people hold the strap with both hands, fearing a false groping accusation.
en.notes: 冤罪 is a false accusation or the conviction of an innocent person. Typical: 冤罪を晴らす ("to clear oneself of a false suspicion"), 冤罪事件, 冤罪を生む, 冤罪の被害者. It is also used outside the courtroom for false suspicions, such as 痴漢冤罪 (falsely accused of groping). Compared with 誤審 ("misjudgment" by a judge, also in sports), 冤罪 stresses the injustice done to the person affected.

examples[].german: Semantics systematically analyzes the meanings of words and sentences.
Whether 「独身」 and 「結婚していない」 mean the same thing is a question of semantics.
He is in the philosophy department and specializes in the semantics of language.
en.notes: 意味論 is semantics, the study of the meaning of words and sentences. It examines, for instance, meaning relations such as 類義語 and 対義語 or the truth conditions of sentences (形式意味論). Distinctions: 語用論 asks what a speaker means in a situation, 統語論 deals with sentence structure. Also used in philosophy and computer science (プログラム言語の意味論). Academic technical term.

examples[].german: Syntax is the field that studies sentence structure and rules.
From a syntactic point of view, this sentence can be interpreted in two ways.
Chomsky's generative grammar had a major influence on syntax research.
en.notes: 統語論 is syntax as an academic discipline, i.e. the study of sentence structure and the rules by which words are combined into sentences; 構文論 is equivalent. The adjective is 統語的 "syntactic". Distinctions: 構文 is a concrete sentence construction, 形態論 studies the structure of words, 意味論 meaning. Academic technical term.

examples[].german: Phonology analyzes systematic patterns of sound.
In my phonology class I learned that Japanese 「ん」 is pronounced as several different sounds.
Whereas phonetics deals with actual pronunciation, phonology deals with the sound system.
en.notes: 音韻論 is phonology, the study of the sound system of a language: which sounds distinguish meaning (音素), how syllables and morae (拍) are built, and what role アクセント plays. Distinction: 音声学 "phonetics" describes the actual pronunciation and acoustics of sounds. The base word 音韻 denotes the sound system itself. Academic technical term.

examples[].german: Morphology studies the internal structure of words.
In the morphology of Japanese, verb conjugation is a central topic.
The boundary between morphology and syntax is not always clear, depending on the language.
en.notes: 形態論 is morphology, the study of the internal structure of words: 形態素, word formation (語形成) and inflection (語形変化, 活用). In Japanese, verb conjugation and compounds such as 本棚 are typical topics. The base word 形態 generally means "form, shape"; in biology, morphology is called 形態学. Academic technical term.

examples[].german: Knowledge of phonetics is indispensable for foreign-language teaching.
I majored in phonetics at university and am researching the pronunciation of vowels.
In phonetics class I recorded my own voice and analyzed it.
en.notes: 音声学 is phonetics, the study of the production, transmission and perception of speech sounds. To be distinguished from it is 音韻論 "phonology", which examines which sounds distinguish meaning in a language. Typical are 音声学を専攻する, 音声学の授業 and the adjective 音声学的な／音声学的に "phonetic(ally)". Note: 音声 alone in everyday use mostly means just "sound, audio" (音声ガイド, 音声入力).

examples[].german: Linguistics is the discipline that studies human language scientifically.
Studying linguistics does not mean you will necessarily speak foreign languages well.
I went to hear a lecture by a famous linguist.
en.notes: 言語学 is linguistics as an academic subject; someone who practices it is a 言語学者. Not to be confused with 語学: that denotes the practical learning of foreign languages (語学が得意 "to be good at languages", 語学学校 "language school"). Typical combinations are 言語学を専攻する, 言語学的に分析する and subfields such as 社会言語学 or 応用言語学.

examples[].german: Applied linguistics provides the theoretical basis for language teaching.
To become a Japanese teacher, I am studying applied linguistics in a master's program.
From the perspective of applied linguistics, I analyzed the weaknesses of this textbook.
en.notes: 応用言語学 is applied linguistics: it uses linguistic findings for practical questions such as foreign-language teaching, 第二言語習得 "second-language acquisition", translation or language testing. The counterpart is 理論言語学 "theoretical linguistics". The word belongs in academic contexts, e.g. 応用言語学の修士課程 or 応用言語学の観点から.

examples[].german: Sociolinguistics studies the relationship between language and society.
The change in youth language is an interesting topic in sociolinguistics.
A sociolinguistic survey showed that the use of honorific speech differs by generation.
en.notes: 社会言語学 is sociolinguistics, which examines how language and society are connected: dialects, the use of 敬語 depending on social relationship, youth language (若者言葉), differences between men's and women's speech, or multilingualism. One says 社会言語学の研究, 社会言語学的な視点 or 社会言語学者. It is purely a technical term from scholarship and teaching.

examples[].german: A retrial was opened after the discovery of new evidence.
The defense team petitioned the court for a retrial.
As a result of the retrial, the former death-row inmate was acquitted.
en.notes: 再審 in criminal law is the reopening of a proceeding that has already been finally concluded, usually because of new evidence; typical: 再審を請求する, 再審開始の決定, 再審で無罪となる. Clearly distinct from this are 控訴 and 上告 (appeals against a judgment that is not yet final). The general meaning "renewed examination" (sense 2) is rarer and occurs mainly in official and examination contexts.

examples[].german: Linguistic typology classifies the world's languages by structural features.
From a typological point of view, Japanese and Korean share very similar features.
In the typology class we learned to classify languages by their word order.
en.notes: 言語類型論 is linguistic typology: it groups languages by the way they are built, regardless of whether they are related. Classic categories are word-order types such as SOV型 and SVO型 as well as 膠着語 "agglutinative language", 屈折語 "inflecting language" and 孤立語 "isolating language"; Japanese is thus regarded as an SOV language and a 膠着語. The counterpart is 比較言語学, which asks about common descent.

examples[].german: Dialectological surveys documented regional language differences.
Dialectologists record the speech of elderly people and document it.
In the dialectology class we put the different ways of saying 「ありがとう」 together on a map.
en.notes: 方言学 is dialectology, which studies the regional varieties of a language, such as differences in vocabulary, pronunciation and accent. Typical are 方言調査 "dialect survey" and 方言地図 "dialect map"; well known in Japan is the 方言周圏論 of 柳田国男, according to which old words have been preserved in concentric circles around the old center 京都. The base word 方言 "dialect" is an everyday word, whereas 方言学 is a technical term.

examples[].german: Slang should not be used in formal situations.
In this dictionary, slang words are marked with the symbol 「俗」.
「ヤバい」 was originally slang, but today it is used widely.
en.notes: 俗語 denotes casual, colloquial words and slang that do not belong to standard or written language. The word itself is matter-of-fact and descriptive and appears above all in dictionaries and discussions of language (俗語的な表現; related is 俗に言う "as one says colloquially"); in casual conversation one rather says スラング. To be distinguished are 口語 "spoken language" as the opposite of 文語 and 隠語 "secret language of a group".

examples[].german: Industry jargon is hard for outsiders to understand.
「ホシ」 is police slang and means the culprit.
The shop staff talked in code so that the customers would not understand.
en.notes: 隠語 is a secret or special language that a certain group uses so that outsiders do not understand – for example police, crooks, but also merchants or restaurant staff. Well-known examples are ホシ for the culprit or デカ for a detective. Less secretive is 業界用語 "industry jargon"; 専門用語 and 術語 are official technical terms, 俗語 general slang. Typical combinations: 隠語を使う, 〜の隠語で.

examples[].german: Many coined words were created in the Meiji period.
「哲学」 is a coined word created by Nishi Amane in the Meiji period.
This author is good at coining words, and many new words appear in his works.
en.notes: 造語 means both the forming of new words (造語する, 造語力 "word-formation ability") and the word created in this way. Many words that are everyday today, such as 哲学 "philosophy", arose in the Meiji period as 造語 for Western concepts; 和製英語 such as サラリーマン are also a kind of 造語. In contrast to 新語, 造語 emphasizes the deliberate creation; 新語 only says that a word is new.

examples[].german: Latin is regarded as a dead language, but it is still used in academic fields.
Nobody says 「ナウい」 anymore; it is completely obsolete now.
When I used the word with a young colleague, he laughed and said it was already an obsolete word.
en.notes: 死語 has two meanings: technically a "dead language" that nobody speaks as a native language anymore (ラテン語, サンスクリット語), and colloquially an "obsolete word" that has gone out of fashion. In everyday life one hears almost only the second: 「ナウい」はもう死語だ or 死語になる. For endangered languages one says 消滅危機言語, not 死語.

examples[].german: I read classical works by consulting a dictionary of classical Japanese.
「あはれ」 is an old word expressing deep, quiet emotion.
Some old words have meanings different from those in modern Japanese.
en.notes: 古語 are words and expressions of earlier stages of the language, above all of classical Japanese, that are no longer in use today or meant something different back then (e.g. をかし "charming"). A 古語辞典 is the dictionary for classical Japanese that students use in the subject 古典. The opposite term is 現代語 "modern language"; a word that has only recently gone out of fashion is, by contrast, colloquially called 死語.

examples[].german: Questioning about the bill took place in committee.
After the presentation, there will be a ten-minute question-and-answer session.
An opposition lawmaker questioned the prime minister sharply.
en.notes: 質疑 is the formal asking of questions about a bill, report or lecture in a session; in parliament, e.g. 代表質疑 or 質疑を行う. The word is most often met in 質疑応答 ("questions and answers") after presentations, lectures and press conferences. 質問 is the general word for "question"; 質疑 emphasizes the official setting and is hardly used for single everyday questions.

en.meaning: remand (to a lower court); sending back
examples[].german: The Supreme Court remanded the case to the High Court.
In the retrial after remand, a different verdict from the first instance was handed down.
The application form was incomplete and was sent back.
en.notes: 差し戻し is the noun for 差し戻す ("to send back, remand"). In law it means that a higher court overturns a judgment and sends the case back to the lower court for a new hearing: 高裁に差し戻す, 差し戻し審 ("hearing after remand"). In office life it is also said when an application or document is returned for revision (書類が差し戻される). In official texts the spelling 差戻し is also common.

examples[].german: Every year new words and buzzwords are added to the dictionary.
With the spread of the Internet, many new words have come into being.
In today's class, let's first check the meaning and reading of the new vocabulary.
en.notes: 新語 is a newly emerged word, i.e. a neologism, for example from technology or society (新語が生まれる, 新語を辞書に収録する). In class, 新語 also denotes the new vocabulary of a lesson. 造語, by contrast, emphasizes the process of forming words, and 流行語 a buzzword that may quickly disappear again; the annual prize 新語・流行語大賞 combines both.

examples[].german: The Buzzword Award chooses the word that symbolizes the year.
A line spoken by the main character of a drama became the buzzword of the year.
Buzzwords quickly become dated, so you should be careful how you use them.
en.notes: 流行語 is a buzzword or catchphrase that suddenly gets used everywhere at a certain time and often disappears just as quickly. Typical are 流行語になる and 〜年の流行語. Every year in December the 新語・流行語大賞 is awarded, colloquially shortened to 流行語大賞. A buzzword that nobody uses any more becomes, colloquially, a 死語.

examples[].german: Abbreviations are used frequently in everyday conversation.
「就活」 is an abbreviation of 「就職活動」.
The report contains so many abbreviations that it is hard for new employees to read.
en.notes: 略語 is an abbreviated word: in Japanese often formed by shortening and combining (スマホ from スマートフォン, 就活 from 就職活動) or as an initialism such as NHK. In conversation, abbreviations are usually explained with 〜の略だ "is short for ..."; the verb for it is 略す. Typical combinations: 略語を使う, 略語が多い.

examples[].german: 「出鱈目」 is an example of ateji.
「珈琲」 is an ateji for 「コーヒー」.
Recently, many parents use ateji for their children's names.
en.notes: 当て字 are kanji used only for their sound (or by free association) for a word, without fitting its actual meaning: 出鱈目, 珈琲 for コーヒー, 亜米利加 for America. In a broader sense the term also covers a spelling by meaning with no fitting reading. Today the word often comes up in connection with unusual given names: 名前に当て字を使う. Variant spellings are あて字 and 宛字.

examples[].german: Reading 「大人」 as 「おとな」 is a jukujikun.
「今日」 and 「明日」 are also examples of jukujikun.
Jukujikun cannot be divided into readings for individual characters, so you just have to memorize them.
en.notes: 熟字訓 is a reading that belongs only to the whole kanji compound and cannot be divided among the individual characters: 大人＝おとな, 今日＝きょう, 明日＝あした, 時雨＝しぐれ. The characters fit the meaning, not the sound – this is the difference from 当て字 in the narrower sense. One says 熟字訓で読む; lists of such readings are in the appendix of the 常用漢字表.

examples[].german: The on reading derives from Chinese pronunciation.
The on reading of 「山」 is 「サン」 and its kun reading is 「やま」.
Kanji within compounds are usually read with the on reading.
en.notes: 音読み is the Sino-Japanese reading of a kanji, going back to the Chinese pronunciation at the time of borrowing (depending on the period 呉音, 漢音 or 唐音). It appears above all in kanji compounds (山 as サン in 富士山), while 訓読み is the native reading; as a する-verb, 音読みする means "to read with the on reading". Not to be confused with 音読（おんどく）"reading aloud".

examples[].german: The kun reading is the way of reading in which a Japanese meaning is assigned to a kanji.
The kanji 「生」 has many kun readings, as in 「生きる」, 「生まれる」 and 「生える」.
With kanji in names, it is often hard to tell whether they are read with the on or kun reading.
en.notes: 訓読み is the native Japanese reading of a kanji: a Japanese word (和語) of the same meaning was assigned to the character, e.g. 山 → やま. It typically occurs with standalone kanji and with verbs and adjectives with okurigana (食べる, 高い), while compounds mostly have 音読み. Not to be confused with 訓読（くんどく）, the reading of Chinese texts (漢文) in Japanese word order.

examples[].german: Kanji are a representative example of ideograms.
Because kanji are ideograms, you can sometimes guess their meaning from their form.
Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs include both ideograms and phonograms.
en.notes: 表意文字 is a written character that represents a meaning rather than a sound, i.e. an "ideogram"; the opposite term is 表音文字 "phonogram". Kanji are traditionally called 表意文字, but in the specialist literature they are more precisely called 表語文字 "logograms", because each character represents a whole word or morpheme together with its pronunciation. Typical: 表意文字である, 表意文字の一種.

examples[].german: Hiragana and katakana are phonograms.
The alphabet is a phonetic script, but in English spelling and pronunciation often do not match.
Hangul is a phonetic script created in the 15th century.
en.notes: 表音文字 is a written character that represents a sound rather than a meaning; the opposite term is 表意文字. One distinguishes 音節文字 "syllabary" such as hiragana and katakana and 音素文字 "alphabet" such as the Latin alphabet. Not to be confused with 発音記号 "phonetic transcription" in the sense of pronunciation notation such as the IPA.

examples[].german: The Japanese writing system is said to be the most complex in the world.
The Korean writing system changed in the 20th century from kanji to being centered on hangul.
New writing systems are sometimes created for languages that have no script.
en.notes: 書記体系 is the technical term for the writing system of a language, i.e. the totality of the characters used and their rules; the Japanese 書記体系 combines kanji, hiragana, katakana and in part Latin letters. In everyday life one rather says 文字 or 表記 (日本語の表記); 書記体系 sounds scholarly. Not to be confused with 書記 alone, which means "clerk, secretary".

examples[].german: Considering that it was his first offense, the sentence was suspended.
He received a suspended sentence and was released that same day.
If you commit another crime during the suspension period, the suspension may be revoked.
en.notes: 執行猶予 is the suspension of the execution of a sentence on probation: the sentence is imposed but not carried out if the convicted person does not reoffend within the period. Typical phrases: 執行猶予が付く, 執行猶予付きの判決, in verdicts "〇年、執行猶予〇年". The counterpart is 実刑 ("a sentence without suspension that must be served"). Colloquially, it is also jokingly used for a grace period.

en.meaning: okurigana; kana ending after a kanji
examples[].german: There are rules for how to attach okurigana.
Some words, like 行う and 行なう, have two possible okurigana forms.
I wrote the okurigana wrong on a kanji test and lost points.
en.notes: 送り仮名 are the kana that follow a kanji and spell out the rest of the word, above all the inflectional ending: 書く, 新しい, 静かだ. The official rules are laid down in the guidelines 送り仮名の付け方; nevertheless there are permitted double forms such as 行う／行なう or 表す／表わす. One says 送り仮名を付ける, 送り仮名を間違える. Not to be confused with 振り仮名, the small reading aid above or beside a kanji.

en.meaning: furigana; kana reading aid above kanji
examples[].german: Furigana are provided for difficult kanji.
In children's books, every kanji has furigana.
Please also write your name in furigana in the name field of the application form.
en.notes: 振り仮名 (usually written in kana: ふりがな) is the small reading aid in kana above or beside a kanji. The typical verb is 振る or 付ける: ふりがなを振る, ふりがなが振ってある; in printing, ルビ is also used. On forms, フリガナ in katakana means you should enter the reading of your name in katakana. Not to be confused with 送り仮名, the kana endings after a kanji.

examples[].german: The jōyō kanji list contains 2,136 characters.
Newspapers often add furigana to kanji that are not jōyō kanji.
The kanji 「鬱」 was added to the jōyō kanji in 2010.
en.notes: 常用漢字 are the 2136 kanji of the official list 常用漢字表 (introduced in 1981, expanded in 2010), which serves as a guideline for government offices, newspapers and school textbooks. Kanji outside the list are called 表外漢字; for given names there are in addition the 人名用漢字, and the characters learned in elementary school are called 教育漢字. Newspapers often add ふりがな to non-常用漢字 or write the word in kana.

examples[].german: Variant characters used in personal names can cause confusion.
Some people write the 「高」 in their surname with the variant 「はしごだか」.
Some variant characters cannot be displayed on a computer.
en.notes: 異体字 are different written forms of one and the same character with the same meaning and reading, e.g. 髙 beside 高, or 齋 and 斎 in the name 斎藤. These also include the old full forms (旧字体) such as 國 for 国. In everyday life one meets them above all in family names, where they often cause problems at government offices or on computers; 字体, by contrast, denotes the shape of a character in general.

examples[].german: 「峠」 is one of the kokuji created in Japan.
Many kokuji such as 「畑」 and 「込」 have no on reading.
Among kanji with the fish radical there are many kokuji like 「鰯」.
en.notes: 国字 has several meanings ("national script", formerly also "kana"); in a learning context it almost always means kanji created in Japan itself (also 和製漢字), such as 峠, 畑, 込, 働 or many fish names like 鰯. Most 国字 have only a kun reading; some, like 働（ドウ）, have acquired an on reading. Typical: 〜は国字の一つだ.

examples[].german: It is important to write kanji in the correct stroke order.
「右」 and 「左」 look similar, but their stroke order is different.
You can check the stroke order of kanji you don't know in an app.
en.notes: 筆順 is the fixed order of strokes when writing a kanji or kana. In everyday life and at school one mostly says 書き順; 筆順 sounds somewhat more technical and appears e.g. in dictionaries and textbooks. Typical are 筆順を守る, 正しい筆順で書く and 筆順を間違える. Similar-looking characters can have different stroke orders, such as 右 and 左.

examples[].german: Sometimes you can infer the meaning of a kanji from its radical.
The radical of 海 and 池 is "sanzui", and it is related to water.
In a kanji dictionary, you can look up characters by their radical.
en.notes: 部首 is the radical by which kanji are classified in dictionaries, e.g. さんずい (氵) for water or にんべん (亻) for people. Many 部首 have their own names, which depend on their position: 〜へん on the left, 〜かんむり on top, 〜あし at the bottom. Typical are 部首で引く "to look up by radical" and 部首索引 "radical index". Note: a kanji has only one 部首, even if it consists of several components.

examples[].german: Kanji with many strokes are hard to write.
If you don't know the reading of a kanji, it's best to look it up by stroke count.
Many parents pay attention to stroke count when choosing their child's name.
en.notes: 画数 is the number of strokes of a kanji; the total number is more precisely called 総画数. Typical are 画数が多い／少ない and 画数で引く "to look up by stroke count" when you know neither the reading nor the radical. In Japan 画数 also plays a role in choosing names, because 姓名判断 "name divination" reads good or bad fortune from the stroke count. The counter for single strokes is 〜画 (十画の漢字).

examples[].german: There are various styles such as regular script and semi-cursive script.
For presentation slides, it is best to choose an easy-to-read typeface.
I changed the typeface to a bold gothic only for the title of the poster.
en.notes: 書体 has two meanings: in printing and on computers the typeface, such as 明朝体 or ゴシック体 (today often also フォント), and in calligraphy the script style such as 楷書, 行書, 草書, 隷書 and 篆書. Typical are 書体を選ぶ, 書体を変える. Not to be confused with 字体, which means the form of an individual character (新字体／旧字体).

examples[].german: The defendant was sentenced to three years' imprisonment without labor.
The driver who caused a death in a traffic accident was sentenced to two years' imprisonment without suspension.
The difference between imprisonment without labor and imprisonment with labor was whether prison work was required.
en.notes: 禁固 (officially written 禁錮) was a custodial sentence without an obligation to do prison labor, imposed mainly for negligent offenses such as fatal traffic accidents, e.g. 禁固2年. With 懲役, by contrast, one had to work in prison. Since June 2025, both types of punishment have been merged into the single 拘禁刑; 禁固 is therefore encountered today mainly in older verdicts, reports and texts about the former law.

examples[].german: It is desirable to write formal documents in regular script.
Please fill in the application form clearly in block script.
People who start calligraphy first practice regular script.
en.notes: 楷書 is the regular script in which every stroke is written clearly and separately; it corresponds to printed kanji and is learned first at school. On forms one often reads 楷書で記入してください "please fill in in clear block script". The more flowing counterparts are 行書 "semi-cursive" and 草書 "grass script"; together the three styles are called 楷行草.

examples[].german: Cursive script is characterized by a flowing brushwork.
Old letters written in cursive script can only be read by experts.
Hiragana arose from the cursive forms of man'yōgana.
en.notes: 草書 is the heavily abbreviated, flowing "grass script" in which strokes are run together; for the untrained it is hardly legible. Hiragana arose from 草書 forms of 万葉仮名. By comparison: 楷書 is the regular script and 行書 the semi-cursive in between; as a style name one also says 草書体.

examples[].german: Semi-cursive script is a style between regular script and cursive script.
My grandfather always writes the addresses on New Year's cards in semi-cursive script.
Semi-cursive can be written faster than regular script, so it is often used for everyday handwriting.
en.notes: 行書 is the semi-cursive: strokes are partly joined and simplified, but the characters remain easy to read. It lies between 楷書 and 草書 and is the typical style for quick but neat handwriting, e.g. in letters, addresses on New Year's cards or signatures. One says 行書で書く or 行書体.

examples[].german: Man'yōgana is a way of writing in which kanji are used for their sound alone.
The poems of the 『万葉集』 are mainly written in man'yōgana.
The 「あ」 arose from the man'yōgana 「安」 and the 「い」 from 「以」.
en.notes: 万葉仮名 are kanji that were used for their sound value alone and not for their meaning in order to write Japanese, e.g. 安 for あ or 以 for い. The name comes from the poetry collection 万葉集, in which this system is used extensively. Hiragana (from the cursive form) and katakana (from parts of the characters) later arose from simplified 万葉仮名. The word is a technical term of language and writing history.

examples[].german: Hentaigana can be seen on signs of soba restaurants and the like.
Letters from the Meiji period contain many hentaigana and are very hard to read.
In 1900 the kana forms were standardized into one each, and the other forms came to be called hentaigana.
en.notes: 変体仮名 are hiragana forms that derive from different source kanji than the present-day standard characters. Only in 1900 was a single form fixed for each syllable by a school ordinance; all the others have been considered 変体仮名 since. Today they are seen mainly on traditional shop signs (e.g. at soba restaurants), in old documents and in calligraphy.

examples[].german: It is important to take care to use polite phrasing.
She has a distinctive way of putting things, so it is fun to listen to her.
This phrasing is a little unnatural as Japanese.
en.notes: 言い回し is the way one formulates something, i.e. a particular turn of phrase or manner of expression. Typical are 独特な言い回し, 回りくどい言い回し "roundabout phrasing", 言い回しを工夫する and 言い回しが上手. 表現 is more general "expression", 言葉遣い concerns rather word choice and politeness, and 言い方 is the everyday equivalent of 言い回し.

en.meaning: tone of speech; manner of speaking
examples[].german: If you speak in a softened tone, the other person calms down too.
He suddenly raised his tone and argued back.
To make the tone of the text uniform, I unified everything into 「です・ます」.
en.notes: 語調 is the tone in which something is said or written: the strength, sharpness or softness of the manner of expression. Typical are 語調を強める, 語調を和らげる, 語調が荒い and 激しい語調で. 口調 is almost synonymous and more common in everyday use; 語気 emphasizes the vehemence more (語気を荒らげる). 語調 can also refer to the style of a text.

examples[].german: Early detection and treatment of speech disorders is important.
A mild speech disorder remained as an after-effect of the accident.
Speech-language therapists are in charge of rehabilitation for people with speech disorders.
en.notes: 言語障害 is the umbrella term for disorders of speech or language, such as 構音障害 "articulation disorder", 吃音 "stuttering" or 失語症 "aphasia". It is a medical, matter-of-fact term; such disorders are treated by 言語聴覚士 "speech-language therapists". Typical are 言語障害がある, 言語障害が残る. In official texts 障害 is sometimes also written 障がい.

examples[].german: Aphasia can occur as an after-effect of a stroke.
My father developed aphasia from a cerebral infarction, and words no longer come out properly.
When talking with a person with aphasia, it is good to speak slowly in short sentences.
en.notes: 失語症 is aphasia: a disorder acquired through brain damage, mostly after a stroke, in which speaking, understanding, reading or writing are impaired. Typical are 失語症になる, 失語症の患者. To be distinguished is 構音障害, in which only pronunciation is disturbed while language ability itself is preserved; 失語症 is part of the umbrella term 言語障害.

examples[].german: Stuttering can often be improved with appropriate training.
He has suffered from stuttering since childhood.
When a person who stutters is speaking, it is important to wait and listen until the end.
en.notes: 吃音 is the matter-of-fact, medical term for stuttering; the diagnosis is also called 吃音症. The everyday verb どもる is now regarded as pejorative and is avoided in respectful speech. Typical are 吃音がある, 吃音に悩む and 吃音のある人.

examples[].german: A sentence of five years' imprisonment with labor, without suspension, was handed down.
The prosecution demanded ten years' imprisonment for the defendant.
After serving his sentence and being released, he started working at a bakery.
en.notes: 懲役 was the most common custodial sentence in Japanese criminal law and involved the obligation of prison labor (刑務作業); typical: 懲役5年, 懲役刑, 懲役〇年を求刑する (the prosecution's sentencing request). With 実刑 the sentence is actually served, with 執行猶予 it is suspended on probation. Since June 2025, 懲役 and 禁固 have been merged into the new 拘禁刑, but the word remains widespread in reports on older cases and in general usage.

examples[].german: In multi-ethnic countries, language policy becomes an important issue.
Through the Meiji government's language policy, the standard language was spread throughout the country.
Singapore pursues a language policy that makes English the common language.
en.notes: 言語政策 is the language policy of a state or organization: determining official languages (公用語), language teaching, and the promotion or suppression of minority languages. Typical are 言語政策をとる "to pursue a language policy" and 〜の言語政策. For Japan's policy regarding its own language (kanji lists, writing rules), one traditionally says 国語政策.

examples[].german: Guaranteeing the language rights of ethnic minorities is called for.
Receiving education in one's mother tongue is considered one of the basic language rights.
The revival of the Ainu language is also drawing attention from the standpoint of language rights.
en.notes: 言語権 are the linguistic rights of a person or a group, such as the right to speak one's own language, to be taught in it, or to use it in court and before authorities. The term appears above all in discussions about minorities and indigenous languages; typical are 言語権を保障する "to guarantee language rights" and 言語権の侵害. It is a technical term from law and language policy.

examples[].german: Acquisition of the mother tongue progresses rapidly during the first few years of life.
I am researching second language acquisition in graduate school.
Conversation with the adults around them is indispensable for children's language acquisition.
en.notes: 言語習得 is the technical term for "language acquisition", especially in linguistics, psychology and pedagogy. One distinguishes 母語の言語習得 (first-language acquisition) and 第二言語習得 (second-language acquisition, often as a research field). 習得 emphasizes making something one's own until one has mastered it; in everyday life one rather says 言葉を覚える or 語学を勉強する. As a verb: 言語を習得する.

examples[].german: Extensive reading is effective for increasing vocabulary.
People who read a lot of books really do have a large vocabulary.
The live show was so amazing that I lost all my words.
en.notes: 語彙力 is the extent and command of one's own vocabulary, i.e. how many words one knows and can use aptly. Typical are 語彙力がある／ない, 語彙力を高める／鍛える and 語彙力が豊富. Colloquially and jokingly, one says 語彙力がなくなる when one is lost for words out of enthusiasm. 語彙 alone is the vocabulary itself, 語彙力 the ability.

examples[].german: Improving reading comprehension forms the foundation of all learning.
An international survey made the decline in Japanese students' reading comprehension a topic of discussion.
The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test tests both reading and listening comprehension.
en.notes: 読解力 is the ability to read texts and understand them correctly, i.e. reading comprehension or reading literacy. Typical are 読解力がある, 読解力を身につける／伸ばす and 読解力の低下, for instance in discussions about PISA results. Together with 聴解力 "listening comprehension" and 作文力 "writing ability" it forms a series of competence terms; 読解 alone is reading and understanding, or the reading task in an exam.

examples[].german: I listen to podcasts to train my listening comprehension.
My listening comprehension was lacking, so my exam score did not go up.
Listening to even a little Japanese every day is the shortcut to improving listening comprehension.
en.notes: 聴解力 is listening comprehension, especially in foreign-language learning and exams; the exam section is called 聴解 in the JLPT. Typical are 聴解力を鍛える／伸ばす and 聴解力が足りない. In everyday life one often says the more casual リスニング力 or 聞き取る力. The counterpart for reading is 読解力.

examples[].german: Writing ability improves with continuous practice.
Since I started writing a diary every day, my writing has gradually improved.
This cram school offers classes that develop elementary school students' writing skills.
en.notes: 作文力 is the ability to write compositions or texts; the term comes from school and language teaching, where 作文 is the "composition". For adults and in working life one rather speaks of 文章力 "writing skill, style" (文章力がある). Typical are 作文力をつける, 作文力を伸ばす; together with 読解力 and 聴解力 it denotes the basic skills in language teaching.

examples[].german: Interacting with native speakers is indispensable for improving conversational ability.
After a year studying abroad, my speaking ability improved considerably.
In this company's interviews, English speaking ability is also evaluated.
en.notes: 会話力 is the ability to converse orally in a language, formed with the suffix 〜力 "ability" like 読解力 "reading comprehension" or 聴解力 "listening comprehension". Typical combinations are 会話力を伸ばす/高める/つける and 会話力が上がる; for foreign languages one often says 英会話力. The more general 語学力 means foreign-language proficiency as a whole, including reading and writing. Neutral, common in education, job applications and language-school advertising.

examples[].german: Japanese has a variety of honorific titles such as 「さん」 and 「様」.
You must not attach an honorific such as 「さん」 to your own name.
I wrote 「敬称略」 at the end of the attendee list.
en.notes: 敬称 are honorific forms of address attached to names or designations: さん, 様, 殿, 先生, and 御中 for companies. One says 敬称を付ける; one never adds a 敬称 to one's own name. In lists of participants one often finds 敬称略 "honorifics omitted". Not to be confused with 尊敬語, the respectful verb forms of 敬語.

examples[].german: A minor fine was imposed for a petty offense.
He was charged with insult and sentenced to a minor fine of 9,000 yen.
A minor fine is a lighter punishment than a regular fine.
en.notes: 科料 is the lightest monetary penalty in criminal law (1,000 up to under 10,000 yen), for example for insult (侮辱罪) or minor offenses; from 10,000 yen up, one speaks of 罰金. Read the same but different is 過料, an administrative fine without criminal character, e.g. for late notifications. To tell them apart in conversation, 科料 is often read とがりょう and 過料 あやまちりょう. Typical: 科料に処する, 科料を科す.

examples[].german: Using vulgar language is said to show a lack of education.
Vulgar words cannot be used on television broadcasts.
The boundary between vulgar words and slang is surprisingly vague.
en.notes: 卑語 is a linguistic or written-language term for vulgar, coarse or obscene words. It stands beside 俗語 "slang, casual colloquial language" and 隠語 "secret language, jargon"; 卑語 emphasizes the low and offensive. In everyday life one rather says 汚い言葉 or 下品な言葉. Typical are 卑語を使う and 卑語を避ける.

examples[].german: 「瑞穂の国」 is a poetic name for Japan.
「花の都」 is known as a poetic name for Paris.
In old waka poems, poetic names for places and mountains often appear.
en.notes: 美称 is an embellishing, praising or poetic name for something, such as 瑞穂の国 for Japan or 花の都 for Paris. It mostly appears in the pattern AはBの美称だ. For euphemistic paraphrases of unpleasant things (亡くなる instead of 死ぬ), by contrast, one rather says 婉曲表現; for the polite お in お茶 there is the term 美化語. The word is literary.

examples[].german: Euphemistic expressions are used often in Japanese.
「考えておきます」 is often used as a euphemism when declining.
「亡くなる」 is a euphemism for 「死ぬ」.
en.notes: 婉曲表現 is an expression that says something unpleasant or delicate indirectly and in a softened way, e.g. 亡くなる instead of 死ぬ or 考えておきます as a polite refusal. The element 婉曲 is also used alone as a な-adjective: 婉曲な言い方, 婉曲に断る. Colloquially, 遠回しな言い方 "beating around the bush" corresponds to it. Typical: 婉曲表現を使う/用いる; a slightly elevated term, often used in linguistics.

examples[].german: Japanese is a language extremely rich in onomatopoeia.
「ガチャン」 and 「ドンドン」 are examples of onomatopoeia.
In manga, sound-effect words are drawn large in katakana.
en.notes: 擬音語 are sound-imitating words for actual noises such as ドンドン "boom-boom" or ガチャン "clang"; animal calls and human voices are more precisely called 擬声語. To be distinguished from them are 擬態語, which depict states or movements without sound (きらきら, じろじろ). As an umbrella term for all of them, オノマトペ is common today. 擬音語 are mostly written in katakana, especially in manga.

examples[].german: 「きらきら」 and 「ふわふわ」 are examples of mimetic words.
「にこにこ」 in 「にこにこ笑う」 is a mimetic word and does not represent an actual sound.
Japanese is rich in mimetic words, which is quite difficult for foreigners.
en.notes: 擬態語 are sound-symbolic words for states, movements or impressions that make no noise at all: きらきら, ふわふわ, じろじろ, にこにこ. The counterpart is 擬音語 or 擬声語 for real sounds (ワンワン, ドンドン); both together are called オノマトペ. Feeling words such as いらいら are sometimes set apart as 擬情語. In a sentence, 擬態語 mostly stand adverbially, often with と or as a 〜する verb.

examples[].german: In translating poetry, a free translation is often necessary.
This proverb doesn't come across when translated literally, so I translated it freely.
Movie subtitles have a limit on the number of characters, so they are often freely translated.
en.notes: 意訳 is the free translation that renders the content rather than the word order; as a transitive する-verb: 文を意訳する. The opposite terms are 直訳 "literal translation" and the even stricter 逐語訳 "word-for-word translation". Typical in discussions about literature, subtitles and song lyrics; translating too freely is criticized with 意訳しすぎ.

examples[].german: A literal translation can result in unnatural sentences.
Even if you translate 「猫の手も借りたい」 literally into English, the meaning doesn't come across.
「いただきます」 is a word that is difficult to translate literally.
en.notes: 直訳 is the literal translation that sticks closely to the words and sentence structure of the original; as a transitive する-verb: 英文を直訳する. Very common is 直訳すると "translated literally, this means ...". The opposite is 意訳 "free translation"; 逐語訳 is even stricter, word for word. Clumsy translationese is called 直訳調.

examples[].german: There are cases where a mistranslation developed into a diplomatic problem.
A mistranslation was found in the translated book, and the publisher corrected it.
I was embarrassed when a reader pointed out a mistranslation.
en.notes: 誤訳 is a wrong translation or translation error; as a transitive する-verb it means "to translate wrongly": 一文を誤訳する. Typical combinations are 誤訳がある/見つかる, 誤訳を指摘する and 誤訳を訂正する. Colloquially one also says 翻訳ミス. Not to be confused with 誤字 "typo, wrong character".

examples[].german: Nuances of the original tend to be lost in a word-for-word translation.
In classical-literature class, you first translate word for word and then think about the meaning as a whole.
To avoid misunderstandings, the contract was translated in a form close to word for word.
en.notes: 逐語訳 is the word-for-word translation in which each word is rendered in sequence (逐 "in sequence", 語 "word"). It is narrower and more technical than 直訳, which generally means "literal translation"; the opposite term is 意訳 "free translation". As an adverb: 逐語的に訳す. Typical in foreign-language and classical-literature teaching as well as with legal texts.

examples[].german: Linguistic ability is greatly influenced by environment and education.
Children's language ability develops rapidly around the age of three.
After the stroke, my grandfather's language ability declined temporarily.
en.notes: 言語能力 denotes a person's linguistic ability in general, for instance in psychology, pedagogy and medicine: 言語能力が高い/低い, 言語能力が発達する/低下する. In linguistics it is also the technical term for Chomsky's "linguistic competence". For foreign-language skills one rather says 語学力 in everyday life, and 会話力 for speaking.

examples[].german: The tools used in the crime were confiscated.
When I was playing games during class, the teacher confiscated my device.
The match was ruled a forfeit and awarded to the opposing team.
en.notes: 没収 is the seizure or taking away of items by an authority; as a する-verb it is transitive, often passive: 財産を没収される. In criminal law it is an additional penalty (forfeiture of instruments or proceeds of a crime); in everyday life it is very common when teachers take something away: 授業中にスマホを没収された. 没収試合 is, in sports, a game that is declared lost because of a rule violation. Close in meaning are 押収 ("seizure" as evidence during an investigation) and 差し押さえ ("attachment, garnishment").

examples[].german: Loanwords arise through language contact.
As a result of language contact, pidgins and creoles can arise.
The dialect of this region changed greatly through language contact with the speech of immigrants.
en.notes: 言語接触 is a technical term of linguistics for contact between languages or their speakers, which can lead to borrowings (借用語), mixed languages such as ピジン and クレオール, or to language shift. Typical frames are 〜との言語接触 and 言語接触によって/の結果. Hardly used in everyday life; there one rather speaks of 外国語の影響.

examples[].german: 「パン」 is a loanword from Portuguese.
Japanese kango too are originally loanwords from Chinese.
English has loanwords from Japanese, such as 「tsunami」 and 「sushi」.
en.notes: 借用語 is the linguistic umbrella term for "loanword": any word taken over from another language, including the 漢語 from Chinese. 外来語, by contrast, in ordinary usage means above all newer words from Western languages, mostly written in katakana. Typical: 〜語からの借用語. In everyday life one hears almost only 外来語; 借用語 sounds technical.

examples[].german: Romanization of Japanese is a form of transliteration.
I transliterate the cursive kuzushiji of old documents into modern characters.
If you transliterate Russian personal names into the Latin alphabet, there are several possible spellings.
en.notes: 翻字 is transliteration, i.e. the character-faithful transfer of a text from one script to another; as a transitive する-verb: ラテン文字に翻字する. To be distinguished from it are 翻訳 "translation" (content into another language) and 音訳 "transcription by sound". In Japanese philology, 翻字 also denotes the transfer of cursive script (くずし字) of old manuscripts into present-day characters. Technical.

examples[].german: Garbled text occurred because of a difference in character encoding.
When I opened the attachment, the text was garbled and I couldn't read it.
After I changed the browser settings, the garbled text was fixed.
en.notes: 文字化け denotes unreadable character salad caused by a wrong character encoding; the word has even been borrowed into English. As an intransitive する-verb: メールが文字化けする, 文字化けしている. Typical are 文字化けが起きる and 文字化けを直す. Neutral and everyday in an IT context; almost always written with kanji and け in hiragana.

examples[].german: Facts are required to be described objectively.
The author narrates his own war experiences in a matter-of-fact way.
This adjective can only be used predicatively.
en.notes: 叙述する means to present and narrate facts or events in order in language; transitive with を: 事実を叙述する. It is literary and sounds more matter-of-fact than 描写 "vivid depiction, portrayal"; 記述 emphasizes more the setting down in writing. In grammar, 叙述 means "predication", e.g. 叙述用法 "predicative use".

examples[].german: He is known as a writer skilled at psychological portrayal.
This movie has a lot of depictions of violence and is not suitable for children.
The author describes the town on a rainy night in detail.
en.notes: 描写 is the vivid depiction of scenes, people or feelings in literature, film or art; as a transitive する-verb: 町の様子を描写する. Common compounds are 心理描写, 情景描写, 人物描写 and 暴力描写. In contrast to the matter-of-fact 叙述, 描写 emphasizes the pictorial; 描写が細かい/リアルだ praises the level of detail. Neutral, very common in reviews and teaching.

examples[].german: Skillfully laid foreshadowing is paid off at the end of the story.
In the final episode, all the foreshadowing was neatly paid off.
He said "I might be busy next week," laying the groundwork for turning down the drinking party.
en.notes: 伏線 is a hint hidden early in a story that later turns out to be significant. The fixed combinations are 伏線を張る "to lay foreshadowing" and 伏線を回収する "to pay it off". In a figurative sense it also means a precautionary preparation in everyday life, e.g. in order to have an excuse later. Similar is 布石, but it rather denotes a strategic setting of the course.

examples[].german: The unexpected ending surprised the readers.
The long-running negotiations came to an unexpected conclusion.
Don't tell me the ending! I'm still in the middle of reading it.
en.notes: 結末 is the ending or outcome of a story, but also of a real event such as a case or dispute. Typical are 結末を迎える "to come to an end", 意外な結末 and 悲しい結末. In contrast to 結論 "conclusion of an argument" and 結果 "result", 結末 emphasizes the outcome of a sequence of events. Neutral; also when spoiling: 結末を言わないで.

examples[].german: I structure the text with the ki-shō-ten-ketsu structure in mind.
Four-panel manga are often made in the ki-shō-ten-ketsu form.
His stories have no ki-shō-ten-ketsu structure, so I can't tell what he wants to say.
en.notes: 起承転結 denotes the four-part structure of introduction (起), development (承), twist (転) and conclusion (結). It originally comes from Chinese four-line poetry; today it serves as a model for essays, stories and yonkoma manga. Typical: 起承転結を意識する, 起承転結がはっきりしている. Colloquially, 起承転結がない criticizes an aimless, unstructured narrative.

examples[].german: This scene is groundwork for later developments.
As groundwork for expanding overseas, they opened an office locally.
In go, the opening moves in the early game greatly affect victory or defeat.
en.notes: 布石 comes from the game of go, where it denotes the strategic placement of stones in the opening. In a figurative sense it is a preparatory step with which one sets the course for the future: 〜への布石, 布石を打つ. Unlike 伏線, a hidden hint in a narrative, 布石 emphasizes planned, strategic action. Frequent in business and political reports.

en.meaning: additional levy; collection of back payment
examples[].german: An additional tax was levied on the amount of tax evaded.
Unreported income was discovered, and about one million yen was collected in back payment.
The court ordered the defendant to pay an amount equal to the bribe he had received.
en.notes: 追徴 means to demand a missing amount afterward. Most common in 追徴課税 ("additional tax assessment") and 追徴金: in criminal law, this is the sum of money levied when confiscation (没収) is no longer possible, for example because bribe money has already been spent. Typical: 〇円を追徴する, 追徴される. The word belongs to the technical language of tax authorities and courts.

examples[].german: The theme of this novel is human loneliness.
The theme song of this anime was a huge hit.
Discuss the theme the author wanted to convey in this work.
en.notes: 主題 is the central theme or motif of a work, such as a novel, film or piece of music. In everyday life one often says テーマ; 主題 sounds more analytical and is typical in literature classes and criticism. Well-known compound: 主題歌 "theme song". Not to be confused with 題名 "title" or 話題 "topic of conversation"; in grammar, 主題 is the topic of a sentence (with は).

examples[].german: I summarized the synopsis of the story concisely.
A summary of about two thousand characters must be attached to the graduation thesis.
At the start of the book review, the synopsis of the work is introduced first.
en.notes: 梗概 is a brief summary of the content, for example of a novel, play or academic paper. It is literary and formal; in everyday life one says あらすじ, and for essays and reports also 要約 or 概要. Typical are 梗概をまとめる, 論文の梗概 and 梗概を提出する. The word is used almost only in writing.

examples[].german: Owing to space limitations, the details are omitted.
The incident was splashed across the next morning's newspaper pages.
The newspapers devoted a lot of space to special coverage of the election.
en.notes: 紙面 denotes the surface of a printed page, above all the available space in a newspaper. Common are 紙面の都合で/紙面の制約上 "due to space limitations", 紙面を割く "to devote space" and 紙面を飾る "to make headlines". For magazines one writes 誌面, for screens 画面. Rather literary and typical of the press and publishing.

en.meaning: unification of spoken and written language (genbun itchi)
examples[].german: The genbun itchi movement began in the Meiji period.
Futabatei Shimei's 『浮雲』 is known as an early novel written in the genbun itchi style.
Thanks to the progress of genbun itchi, we can write the way we speak.
en.notes: 言文一致 denotes the approximation of written language to spoken language, especially the reform movement (言文一致運動) of the Meiji period that replaced the classical 文語体 with the modern 口語体. Literary pioneers were 二葉亭四迷 with 浮雲 and 山田美妙. The style is called 言文一致体. A technical term from the history of language and literature.

examples[].german: Texts written in the classical literary style give an impression of dignity.
The Meiji Constitution is written in the classical literary style, so it is hard for people today to read.
The classical 「なり」 corresponds to the modern 「である」.
en.notes: 文語体 is the writing style that follows the classical written language (文語) with its own grammar, recognizable by forms such as 〜なり, 〜けり or 〜べし. The opposite term is 口語体, which is based on modern spoken language. Until the 20th century, laws and official texts were written in 文語体; today it is encountered in classics, poems and set formulas. Technical term, neutral.

en.meaning: modern written style (based on spoken language)
examples[].german: Modern novels are almost all written in the colloquial style.
The Penal Code was rewritten from the classical to the colloquial style in 1995.
Even in the colloquial style, you don't simply write down speech as it is.
en.notes: 口語体 is the writing style based on modern spoken language, i.e. today's normal written Japanese with です/ます or だ/である. The opposite term is the classical 文語体; 口語体 therefore does not mean "casual" or "slang". For truly colloquial speech one says 話し言葉 or くだけた言い方. Technical term from grammar and the history of language.

examples[].german: Official documents before the Meiji period were written in sōrō-bun.
Until before the war, not a few people wrote their letters in sōrō-bun.
「御座候」 is an expression that often appears in sōrō-bun.
en.notes: 候文 is the historical formal style of letters and documents in which the auxiliary verb 候 (そうろう) takes the role of ある or ます, as in 〜に候 or 御座候. It shaped letters and official documents from the Kamakura period to the early Shōwa period. Today it is encountered only in historical sources that are deciphered in class or in research. Historical technical term.

examples[].german: Kundoku reading of kanbun is a reading method unique to Japan.
In high-school Japanese class, you also study classical Japanese and kanbun.
The samurai of old could read and write kanbun as part of their education.
en.notes: 漢文 denotes classical Chinese texts, as they have been read, and also composed, in Japan for centuries. At school, 漢文 is, alongside 古文 "classical Japanese", part of the subject 国語. It is usually read by 訓読, i.e. with reading marks in Japanese word order; the result is called 書き下し文. Not to be confused with 中国語, modern Chinese.

en.meaning: kundoku; Japanese reading of Chinese texts; kun reading (of a kanji)
examples[].german: Kanbun is read through kundoku in Japanese word order.
A kundoku-read text written out mixed with kana is called kakikudashi-bun.
Chinese people don't read kanbun by kundoku but directly with Chinese pronunciation.
en.notes: 訓読 is the reading of a classical Chinese text (漢文) in Japanese: with the help of 返り点 and 送り仮名, the Chinese word order is rearranged into Japanese; as a transitive する-verb: 漢文を訓読する. The result is called 書き下し文. In addition, 訓読 means the kun reading of a kanji, in everyday life usually called 訓読み. Technical term from school and philology.

examples[].german: Relying on the kaeriten, I read the kanbun out in Japanese.
The re mark is a kaeriten that indicates that you read the lower character first and then go back up one character.
Add kaeriten and okurigana to the following unpunctuated text.
en.notes: 返り点 are small marks at the lower left of the characters of a 漢文 text that show in which order one has to jump back when reading it in Japanese (訓読). The most important are レ点, 一二点 and 上下点. Typical: 返り点を付ける, 返り点に従って読む. Together with 送り仮名 and punctuation they belong to the 訓点; a text without them is called 白文.

examples[].german: Minor cases are handled in summary trials.
She took one look at the house and decided to buy it on the spot.
The company president approved the new plan on the spot.
en.notes: 即決 means "to decide immediately"; as a する-verb it is transitive: 購入を即決する. It is very common in everyday life: その場で即決する, 即決で決まる, 即断即決 ("quick and decisive"); in online auctions, 即決価格 is the buy-it-now price. In law, 即決裁判 refers to an expedited procedure for simple, admitted cases. The opposite would be e.g. 保留する ("to put on hold") or 検討する ("to think it over").

examples[].german: Reading kanbun as hakubun requires a high level of kanbun skill.
The kanbun in textbooks has reading marks attached, but the originals are hakubun.
The exam included a question asking you to add kaeriten to a hakubun.
en.notes: 白文 is a classical Chinese text without Japanese reading aids (訓点), i.e. without 返り点, 送り仮名 and usually without punctuation. The counterpart is a text provided with 訓点 or the rewritten 書き下し文. 白文で読む is regarded as a sign of high kanbun proficiency. Technical term from school teaching and philology; not to be confused with 白紙 "blank sheet".

examples[].german: It was deeply moving to visit my nostalgic old school.
The principal addressed the graduates, saying 「この学び舎を巣立つ皆さんへ」.
The hundred-year-old wooden schoolhouse will be torn down this year.
en.notes: 学び舎 is a poetic, emotional word for the school or school building, literally "house of learning". It appears in school songs, graduation speeches, anniversary publications and the memories of former pupils, often with 懐かしい, 母校 or 巣立つ. In ordinary conversation one says 学校 or 校舎; the Sino-Japanese reading 学舎（がくしゃ） is also elevated.

examples[].german: The vice principal stood in for the principal.
I was summoned by the vice principal for being late too often.
Complaints from parents are handled first by the vice principal.
en.notes: 教頭 is the vice principal at elementary, middle and high schools; he or she supports the 校長 and represents him or her in his or her absence. Pupils and parents address the person as 教頭先生. Some schools have a 副校長 instead or in addition. Universities have no 教頭; the offices there are called 学長 and 副学長.

examples[].german: The entrance ceremony began with the dean's address.
She will serve as dean of the Faculty of Letters from next academic year.
You need the dean's permission to extend the submission deadline.
en.notes: 学部長 is the dean of a faculty (学部) at a university, e.g. 文学部長 or 法学部長. Above this position is the 学長 "university president"; the head of a graduate school (研究科) is called 研究科長. Typical: 学部長を務める, 学部長に選ばれる, 学部長の許可. Neutral, usual in the university context.

examples[].german: The president gave words of encouragement to the graduates.
The new president took office and declared university reform.
Three professors ran in the presidential election.
en.notes: 学長 is the president of a university, i.e. the supreme head of the institution. Some old universities, such as the University of Tokyo, use the title 総長 instead. At schools the head is called 校長, at faculties 学部長. Typical: 学長に就任する, 学長選挙, 学長の式辞.

examples[].german: I am engaged in research and teaching at a university as an assistant professor.
She was hired as an assistant professor at her alma mater right after earning her doctorate.
It took five years to be promoted from assistant professor to associate professor.
en.notes: 助教 has been, since 2007, the lowest rank of the Japanese academic career: 教授 "professor", 准教授 "associate professor", 講師 "lecturer", then 助教. The post partly replaced the former 助手 "assistant" and is often fixed-term, with teaching and one's own research. Not to be confused with 助教授, the old title for today's 准教授.

examples[].german: After retirement, he was awarded the title of professor emeritus.
A professor emeritus of Kyoto University appeared on the news program as a commentator.
Even now that he is a professor emeritus, my grandfather continues his research in the library every day.
en.notes: 名誉教授 is an honorary title that a university confers on professors of merit after retirement; it corresponds to "professor emeritus". Typical: 名誉教授の称号を授与される, 名誉教授になる. In the media, experts are often introduced as 〜大学名誉教授. The title carries no teaching obligation.

examples[].german: I belong to the Graduate School of Humanities.
After graduating, I intend to go on to the Graduate School of Economics.
The deadline for submitting the master's thesis differs depending on the graduate school.
en.notes: 研究科 is the subject department of a graduate school (大学院), such as 法学研究科 or 人文科学研究科; for master's and doctoral study it corresponds to what 学部 is for undergraduate study. Typical: 〜研究科に所属する/進学する, 研究科長 "head of the graduate school". Neutral, usual in university administration and in résumés.

en.meaning: line of argument; main point of an argument
examples[].german: You should clarify the line of argument and structure the paper around it.
Choose the option that best captures the main argument of this text.
Partway through, his remarks strayed from the main argument.
en.notes: 論旨 is the core and train of thought of an argument in a text or lecture. Typical are 論旨が明快だ/一貫している, 論旨がずれる and 論旨をつかむ; the set phrase 論旨明快 praises a clear argument. 要旨 is the brief summary of the content, 論点 the point at issue. Literary, frequent in exams and scholarship.

examples[].german: Clearly stating the sources of one's claims is fundamental to academic papers.
The source of this proverb lies in a Chinese classic.
You must not write unsourced rumors as if they were facts.
en.notes: 典拠 is the reliable source or authority on which a statement, quotation or phrase rests. Typical: 典拠を示す/明示する, 典拠がある/ない, 〜の典拠は…にある. The more common 出典 specifically denotes the place where a quotation is found; 根拠 is generally "reason, basis". Literary, in scholarly and editorial work.

examples[].german: When citing, the source must be clearly stated.
This sentence is quoted from a novel by Natsume Soseki.
The company president often quotes the words of great figures in his speeches.
en.notes: 引用 is quoting or a quotation; as a transitive する-verb: 〜から…を引用する. Typical are 引用文, 引用元 "quoted source" and 出典を明記する "to state the source". In contrast to 転載 "reprint, taking over in full", with 引用 only a part is taken over and marked as someone else's. Neutral, in everyday life as well as in scholarship.

examples[].german: Plagiarism is the most serious misconduct in academia.
It turned out that part of the graduation thesis was plagiarized from an online article.
The writer was heavily criticized for plagiarizing other people's ideas.
en.notes: 剽窃 is plagiarism, i.e. taking over other people's texts or ideas as one's own; as a transitive する-verb: 論文を剽窃する. It is literary and legal-academic; for artworks and music one often says 盗作, colloquially パクリ or パクる. Typical: 剽窃が発覚する/判明する, 剽窃を疑われる.

examples[].german: In Western poetry, end rhyme is an important element.
In rap lyrics, rhyming at the end of lines is basic.
These two lines rhyme with 「ハート」 and 「スタート」.
en.notes: 脚韻 is end rhyme, i.e. the matching sound at the end of verses or lines; the verb for it is 踏む: 脚韻を踏む. The opposite term is 頭韻 "alliteration"; in general one says 韻を踏む "to rhyme". Classical Japanese poetry has hardly any rhyme; today 脚韻 is encountered mainly in rap, pop and translations of Western poetry.

examples[].german: Alliterative phrases are easy to remember.
"Coca-Cola" is an example of an alliterative product name.
In old Germanic poetry, alliteration was valued more than end rhyme.
en.notes: 頭韻 is the matching sound at the beginning of words, i.e. alliteration; as with end rhyme one says 頭韻を踏む. The opposite term is 脚韻 "end rhyme". Typical fields of application are advertising slogans, brand names and old Germanic poetry. Technical term from literary studies and rhetoric.

examples[].german: Engo is a technique of scattering related words through a waka poem.
Engo is often used in combination with kakekotoba.
In this poem, 「着る」 and 「張る」 are worked in as engo of 「衣」.
en.notes: 縁語 is a stylistic device of classical Japanese poetry, above all in 和歌: around a key word, words related in meaning are scattered that form an image field, e.g. for 衣 "garment" the words 着る, 張る and 褄. It is often combined with 掛詞 "pun with double meaning". Typical: 〜の縁語. Technical term from literature teaching.

en.meaning: honkadori; allusion to an older poem
examples[].german: Honkadori is a creative technique that builds on an earlier waka.
Honkadori was practiced vigorously in the age of the Shinkokinshū.
These lyrics are a honkadori of a famous waka.
en.notes: 本歌取り is a technique of waka poetry in which words or phrases of a famous older poem (本歌) are deliberately taken over to carry its mood into a new poem. Its heyday was the period of the 新古今和歌集, for instance with 藤原定家. Today the term is also used figuratively for a homage in song lyrics or films.

en.meaning: utamakura; poetic place name; literary topos
examples[].german: I set out on a trip to visit scenic spots known as utamakura.
On his journey for 『おくのほそ道』, Bashō visited many utamakura.
The Tatsuta River is famous as an utamakura for autumn leaves.
en.notes: 歌枕 is a place that is sung about again and again in waka poetry and carries fixed associations, such as 竜田川 with autumn leaves or 吉野 with cherry blossoms. Originally the word also denoted collections of such poetic terms. 芭蕉 deliberately visited many 歌枕 on his journey of the 奥の細道. Technical term from literature and cultural history.

examples[].german: 「や」, 「かな」 and 「けり」 are typical kireji.
The 「や」 in 「古池や」 is a kireji, creating a pause and lingering resonance in the verse.
It is better to avoid using two kireji in one verse.
en.notes: 切れ字 are "cutting words" in haiku and renga that set a caesura and create lingering resonance (余韻), above all や, かな and けり, as in Bashō's 古池や. Traditionally one speaks of eighteen 切れ字. A basic rule is not to use two 切れ字 in one verse. The word belongs to the technical language of poetry and literature teaching.

examples[].german: Renga is a poetic form in which several poets compose verses in turn.
In the Muromachi period, renga was enormously popular among samurai and monks.
Haiku arose when the opening verse of renga, the hokku, became independent.
en.notes: 連歌 is a form of linked poetry in which several poets string together verses in turn in the patterns 5-7-5 and 7-7. It flourished in the Middle Ages, especially in the Muromachi period with masters such as 宗祇. From the more humorous 俳諧連歌 the 俳句 later developed, whose origin is the opening verse 発句. Typical: 連歌を詠む, 連歌会, 連歌師.

examples[].german: Kyōka is a comic poem that borrows the form of waka.
In the middle of the Edo period, kyōka became hugely popular among townspeople.
Kyōka laughs at the world in waka form, senryū in haiku form.
en.notes: 狂歌 is a comic or satirical poem in the waka form 5-7-5-7-7 that mocks society and politics with wordplay and parody. Its heyday was the middle Edo period, with figures such as 大田南畝. The counterpart in the haiku form 5-7-5 is called 川柳. Typical: 狂歌を詠む; technical term from literary history.

examples[].german: Extenuating circumstances were recognized and the sentence was reduced.
The prosecution argued that the crime was so brutal that there was no room for leniency.
If the train stopped and you didn't just oversleep, then there's room for leniency.
en.notes: 情状酌量 means that the court takes the special circumstances of a case (motive, remorse, living situation) into account and mitigates the sentence; literally 情状 "circumstances, state of affairs" + 酌量 "to weigh, take into consideration". Typical: 情状酌量が認められる, 情状酌量の余地がある/ない ("extenuating circumstances can / cannot be considered"), 情状酌量を求める. In everyday life, too, one says half jokingly 情状酌量の余地はある when someone deserves leniency.

examples[].german: The Tale of the Heike is a representative war tale.
The 『太平記』 is a war tale depicting the turmoil of the Northern and Southern Courts period.
Many war tales were handed down orally by biwa hōshi.
en.notes: 軍記物語 is a genre of the Japanese Middle Ages that tells of the wars and battles of the samurai, often with the Buddhist idea of impermanence. Well-known works are 平家物語, 保元物語 and 太平記. More briefly one also says 軍記物 or 軍記. The 平家物語 was recited by blind lute players (琵琶法師). Technical term from literary history.

examples[].german: The Konjaku Monogatari-shū is a masterpiece of setsuwa literature.
Akutagawa Ryūnosuke's 『羅生門』 was written based on an old setsuwa.
Many setsuwa were created to convey Buddhist teachings in an easy-to-understand way.
en.notes: 説話 denotes handed-down narratives such as Buddhist teaching tales, legends and popular anecdotes, especially the genre 説話文学 with collections such as 今昔物語集 or 宇治拾遺物語. In everyday life, for folktales one rather says 昔話, for stories of gods 神話, and for place-bound legends 伝説. Technical term, above all in the history of literature and religion.

examples[].german: Using elegant words gives the writing dignity.
「いにしえ」 is the elegant word for 「昔」.
This author is known for a style that skillfully mixes elegant words and colloquial words.
en.notes: 雅語 are elevated, poetic words, especially the classical vocabulary of the Heian period that was used in 和歌, such as いにしえ instead of 昔 or 月影 instead of 月の光. The opposite term is 俗語 "colloquial language, slang". Almost synonymous is 雅言, which rather means the refined language as a whole. Technical term from linguistics and literature.

examples[].german: Waka poems in elegant language are full of grace.
The kokugaku scholars of the Edo period valued the language of the Heian period as gagen.
Explain the difference between gagen and zokugo, giving examples.
en.notes: 雅言 is the elegant, refined language, especially the classical court language of the Heian period, which scholars of the Edo period (国学) regarded as an ideal. The opposite terms are 俗語 or 俗言 "vernacular" and 俚言 "dialect word". In content almost the same as 雅語, which refers more to individual words. A rarer, scholarly technical term.

en.meaning: Japanese linguistics; study of the Japanese language
examples[].german: Kokugogaku studies the historical changes of the Japanese language.
At university I major in kokugogaku and research dialects.
Recently, more and more universities use the name Nihongogaku rather than kokugogaku.
en.notes: 国語学 is the traditional name for the scholarly study of the Japanese language – phonology, grammar, vocabulary, writing and above all their historical development. 国語 here means "the national language", i.e. Japanese from a Japanese insider's point of view. Today many universities and academic societies call the field, more neutrally, 日本語学. Not to be confused with 国文学, the study of Japanese literature; typical are 国語学を専攻する and 国語学者.

examples[].german: Research on Old Japanese is indispensable for deciphering the Man'yōshū.
There is a theory that Old Japanese had eight vowels.
The songs in the Kojiki are valuable materials for learning about Old Japanese.
en.notes: 上代語 is a technical term of language history for the Japanese of the earliest written period, roughly up to the end of the Nara period (the early 8th century and before). The main sources are the 古事記, 日本書紀 and 万葉集, which are written with Chinese characters as phonetic signs (万葉仮名). In the usual division, 中古語 (Heian), 中世語 and 近世語 (Edo) follow. In a more general sense 上代語 can also simply mean "old word, old language".

examples[].german: The Tale of Genji is a work written in Early Middle Japanese.
To read The Pillow Book, you need to know the grammar of Early Middle Japanese.
The Early Middle Japanese 「いと」 corresponds to today's 「とても」.
en.notes: 中古語 denotes in Japanese language history the Japanese of the Heian period (approx. 9th-12th century), the language of 源氏物語 and 枕草子; in Western terminology "Early Middle Japanese". Classical school grammar (古典文法) is largely based on this stage of the language. The order of the period terms is 上代語 → 中古語 → 中世語 → 近世語. Note: 中古 alone means "used, second-hand" in everyday life (中古車), but with 語 it is always the period term.

examples[].german: Research on Early Modern Japanese helps in understanding Edo literature.
Many expressions of Early Modern Japanese still remain in rakugo today.
Early Modern Japanese is often discussed divided into Kamigata and Edo speech.
en.notes: 近世語 is the Japanese of the early modern period, i.e. the Edo period (1603-1868). It is often divided into 上方語 (Kyōto/Ōsaka, mainly the early Edo period) and 江戸語 (the language of Edo, which later dominates). Sources are e.g. 浮世草子, 歌舞伎 and 落語. Compared with 中古語, 近世語 is already quite close to present-day Japanese, but contains many words and expressions that are obsolete today.

en.meaning: kakari-musubi (classical grammar: emphasis particle requiring a special sentence ending)
examples[].german: Kakari-musubi is a sentence structure peculiar to classical grammar.
In kakari-musubi with 「こそ」, the sentence ends in the realis form.
In high-school classical Japanese class, I learned the rules of kakari-musubi.
en.notes: 係り結び is a rule of classical Japanese: if the sentence contains an emphasizing particle (係助詞) such as ぞ, なむ, や or か, the sentence does not end in the terminal form (終止形) but in the attributive form (連体形); after こそ the realis form (已然形) is used. 係り is the triggering particle, 結び the required ending form. One speaks of the 係り結びの法則; it is standard material in the high-school subject 古文 and is no longer alive in modern Japanese.

examples[].german: If you get the particles wrong, the meaning becomes unintelligible.
I had my teacher correct the particles in my composition.
His speech has mismatched particles, so I can't tell what he wants to say.
en.notes: テニヲハ (usually written てにをは) stands for the Japanese particles and function words as a whole; the name comes from the reading marks of the old kanbun reading, whose corner points stood for て, に, を and は. In everyday life it is almost always about correct usage: テニヲハがおかしい "the particles are off", テニヲハを直す "to correct particle mistakes". Figuratively, テニヲハが合わない means that a speech is not coherent in itself.

en.meaning: member of the House of Representatives; diet member
examples[].german: He has served as a Diet member for three consecutive terms.
My grandfather was a Diet member elected from the local district.
For ten years after graduating from university, I worked as a Diet member's secretary.
en.notes: 代議士 denotes a member of parliament, in current usage usually a member of the lower house (衆議院議員). The word sounds somewhat old-fashioned or journalistic; neutrally one says 国会議員 or 議員. Typical: 代議士を務める, 地元の代議士, 代議士の秘書. Literally it is "someone who deliberates on behalf of others", i.e. a representative of the people.

examples[].german: Evidence was submitted that influences the judge's formation of conviction.
If you keep being late, you'll end up leaving a bad impression on your boss.
He seems to have made a bad impression on the interviewer because of his poor attitude in the interview.
en.notes: 心証 has two uses: in general, the impression someone makes on others through their behavior, especially in 心証を害する ("to leave a bad impression, to put someone off") and 心証が良い/悪い; in law, the conviction that the judge forms from the evidence (心証形成, 自由心証主義 "principle of free evaluation of evidence"). Compared with 印象 ("impression" in the most general sense), 心証 refers to a judgment about a person's credibility or character and sounds more formal.

examples[].german: The 「び」 in 「花火」 is an example of rendaku.
In 「本棚」, 「たな」 undergoes rendaku and becomes 「だな」.
When rendaku occurs is a difficult question for foreigners.
en.notes: 連濁 denotes the voicing of the initial of the second member of a compound: 花＋火 → はなび, 本＋棚 → ほんだな, 人＋人 → ひとびと. It can also stand as an intransitive する-verb: 「たな」が連濁して「だな」になる. 連濁 is not predictable, but there are tendencies, e.g. it mostly fails to occur when the second member already contains a voiced consonant (Lyman's law). Technical word of phonetics and grammar.

examples[].german: The sokuon is written with a small 「っ」.
「きて」 and 「きって」 differ in meaning depending on whether there is a sokuon or not.
The sokuon also counts as one mora, so 「きって」 has three morae.
en.notes: 促音 is the "stopped" sound written with a small っ／ッ and pronounced as a doubling of the following consonant: きって, ベッド. It counts as a mora (拍) of its own. Whether a 促音 is present distinguishes words (きて "come" / きって "stamp"). Related terms are 撥音 (ん), 長音 and 拗音; the sound change in 待って or 買って is called 促音便.

examples[].german: The pronunciation of the moraic nasal 「ん」 changes depending on the following sound.
The moraic nasal in 「さんぽ」 becomes a sound close to "m" under the influence of the following 「ぽ」.
Japanese words basically never begin with the moraic nasal.
en.notes: 撥音 is the syllabic nasal ん／ン. It counts as a mora of its own and is pronounced, depending on the following sound, as [m], [n], [ŋ] or a nasalized vowel (さんぽ, あんない, りんご). Caution: 撥音 sounds exactly like 発音 "pronunciation", hence sentences like 撥音の発音. The sound change in 読んで or 死んで is called 撥音便. Related terms: 促音, 長音, 拗音.

examples[].german: There are words whose meaning changes depending on whether there is a long vowel.
Long vowels in loanwords are written with 「ー」.
A long vowel in Japanese is counted as one mora.
en.notes: 長音 is the long vowel or vowel lengthening, e.g. in おばあさん or こうこう. In Japanese the lengthened part counts as a mora (拍) of its own, as do 促音 (the small っ) and 撥音 (ん). In katakana the 長音 is written with the dash "ー" (長音符), in hiragana with a vowel letter such as う or い. Because 長音 distinguishes meaning, it is a typical source of errors for learners.

examples[].german: Yōon are sounds such as 「きゃ」, 「しゅ」 and 「ちょ」.
Yōon are written using the small 「ゃ」, 「ゅ」 and 「ょ」.
「びょういん」 and 「びよういん」 are different words depending on whether there is a yōon.
en.notes: 拗音 are the palatalized syllables written with an i-kana plus a small ゃ・ゅ・ょ: きゃ, しゅ, ちょ, りょ. Although they consist of two characters, they count as one mora.
