To be distinguished from it is 太陽熱, which uses the sun's heat, for example for hot water. It is used equally in the news and in everyday life.

examples[].german: Offshore wind power is attracting attention as a new energy source.
Because the wind is strong all year round on this coast, it is well suited to wind power generation.
Residents complained that the noise from the wind power turbines was loud.
en.notes: 風力発電 refers to "power generation from wind power", not the individual installation. A single wind turbine is called 風車 or 風力発電機, and a wind farm 風力発電所 or ウィンドファーム. Offshore wind power is 洋上風力発電 or 海上風力発電, and on land one speaks of 陸上風力発電. Typical expressions: 風力発電を導入する, 風力発電に適した地域.

examples[].german: Hydroelectric power has been used in Japan since long ago.
This country meets almost all of its electricity needs with hydroelectric power.
In years with little rain, the output of hydroelectric power falls.
en.notes: 水力発電 is "power generation from water power", usually with dams; the power plant is called 水力発電所. It forms a series with 火力発電 "thermal power", 原子力発電 "nuclear power", 太陽光発電 and 風力発電. Small installations on streams or canals are called 小水力発電. Typical expressions: ダムを使った水力発電, 水力発電に頼る.

examples[].german: Moving away from fossil fuels has become an international challenge.
Japan relies on imported fossil fuels for much of its energy.
Burning fossil fuels produces carbon dioxide.
en.notes: 化石燃料 is the general term for "fossil fuels" such as 石油, 石炭 and 天然ガス. Typical are 化石燃料に頼る/依存する "to be dependent on fossil fuels", 化石燃料を燃やす and 化石燃料からの脱却 "moving away from fossil fuels". Its counterpart in debates is 再生可能エネルギー "renewable energy". Register: news, politics, textbooks.

examples[].german: The development of energy-saving technology is being pushed forward.
After I replaced my old air conditioner with an energy-saving model, my electricity bill went down.
This building does not meet the energy conservation standards.
en.notes: 省エネルギー means "saving energy"; in everyday speech the short form 省エネ is almost always used, while the long form sounds official or technical. 省エネ often stands before nouns (省エネ家電 "energy-saving appliances", 省エネ性能) or as an adjective with 型: 省エネ型の冷蔵庫. As a verb one says 省エネする or, descriptively, エネルギーを節約する; 節電 refers more narrowly to electricity.

examples[].german: Recycling is being promoted to realize a sound material-cycle society.
Aiming for a sound material-cycle society, the city has started composting kitchen waste.
In class, I researched the sound material-cycle society and gave a presentation.
en.notes: 循環型社会 is a guiding concept of policy: a "recycling-oriented society" that avoids, reuses and recycles waste. It appears almost always in fixed expressions such as 循環型社会の実現, 循環型社会を目指す or 循環型社会を築く. The principles behind it are the 3 Rs: リデュース, リユース, リサイクル. Today one also hears サーキュラーエコノミー "circular economy" alongside it. Typical of government agencies, news and textbooks.

examples[].german: An international treaty for ecosystem conservation was concluded.
A local NPO is working on the conservation of the tidal flat ecosystem.
The dam construction was reviewed from the standpoint of ecosystem conservation.
en.notes: 生態系保全 is composed of 生態系 "ecosystem" and 保全 "preservation, protection" and means the protection of ecosystems as a whole. 保全 emphasizes maintaining a condition; 保護 sounds more like protecting individual animals or areas (動物保護, 自然保護). Typical expressions are 生態系保全のための, 生態系保全に取り組む and 生態系保全活動. Used almost exclusively in technical, official and news language.

examples[].german: The Labor Relations Commission mediated in the labor dispute.
The university career center finds jobs for graduates.
Through an acquaintance's arrangement, I was able to rent an apartment cheaply.
en.notes: 斡旋 means to mediate between two sides or to procure something for someone: 仕事を斡旋する "to arrange a job", 労使紛争の斡旋 "mediation in a labor dispute". As a する-verb it is transitive (〜を斡旋する); the person arranging it takes の: 知人の斡旋で. Because of the difficult kanji, authorities and media often write あっせん. Unlike the neutral 仲介 (e.g. in real estate) or the mere 紹介 "introducing", 斡旋 stresses the active effort of the go-between.

examples[].german: The crested ibis is a representative endangered species of Japan.
The Japanese eel was designated an endangered species a few years ago.
Public phones are an endangered species by now, aren't they.
en.notes: 絶滅危惧種 is the technical term for an "endangered species", officially listed in the Red List (レッドリスト). Typical are 絶滅危惧種に指定される "to be designated as endangered" and 絶滅危惧種を守る. Already extinct is 絶滅した, "extinct in the wild" is 野生絶滅. Colloquially, the word is also used jokingly for dying-out things, such as 絶滅危惧種のガラケー.

examples[].german: Development activities in nature reserves are strictly restricted.
This wetland was designated a nature reserve for migratory birds.
Plants must not be picked inside the nature reserve.
en.notes: 自然保護区 is a "nature reserve" in which interventions are restricted by law. Typical expressions: 自然保護区に指定する, 自然保護区内では…が禁止されている. In Japan, many areas carry more specific names such as 自然環境保全地域 or 鳥獣保護区 "bird and wildlife sanctuary"; 国立公園, by contrast, is a "national park" that is used for tourism. Register: official and news language, travel guides.

examples[].german: Air pollution is a cause of respiratory diseases.
The air pollution was so bad that the town looked hazy all day.
They are trying to prevent air pollution by reducing the number of cars.
en.notes: 大気汚染 is "air pollution" caused by exhaust gases, industry or fine particulate matter. Typical are 大気汚染が深刻だ, 大気汚染が進む and 大気汚染を防ぐ. It belongs to the series of environmental problems 水質汚濁, 土壌汚染 and 騒音. In everyday speech one often simply says 空気が汚い; 大気汚染 is the objective term from the news and reports.

examples[].german: Effluent standards are set by the Water Pollution Control Act.
Domestic wastewater from households is also a major cause of water pollution.
Pollution of the lake advanced, and large numbers of fish died.
en.notes: 水質汚濁 is the official term for "water pollution"; 汚濁 literally means "contamination and turbidity". It appears mainly in laws and reports, e.g. in the 水質汚濁防止法 "Water Pollution Control Act". In general usage, 水質汚染 is more common and has the same meaning. Typical expressions: 水質汚濁が進む, 水質汚濁の原因.

examples[].german: Soil contamination at former factory sites is regarded as a problem.
Soil contamination was found at the planned construction site, and the work was postponed.
Before buying the land, I commissioned a soil contamination survey.
en.notes: 土壌汚染 is "soil pollution" or "soil contamination" by chemicals, heavy metals or oil. Typical expressions are 土壌汚染が見つかる/判明する, 土壌汚染を調査する and 土壌汚染対策. The word became known in Japan through, among other things, land issues when building markets and housing complexes on former industrial sites. 土壌 is the technical word for "soil"; in everyday speech one says 土.

examples[].german: Measures against noise pollution around the airport were strengthened.
Residents along the expressway have suffered from noise pollution for many years.
The residents sued the factory on the grounds of noise pollution.
en.notes: 騒音公害 refers to noise as an "environmental burden" affecting many people, for example from airports, expressways or factories; 公害 is the general term for such public environmental damage. For everyday noise, such as from a neighbor, one simply says 騒音 or 近所の騒音. Typical expressions: 騒音公害に悩まされる, 騒音公害対策, 騒音公害で訴える. Register: news, official language.

examples[].german: Because of light pollution in urban areas, stars have become hard to see.
For astronomical observation, a mountaintop with little light pollution is best.
As a measure against light pollution, the town replaced its street lamps with downward-facing ones.
en.notes: 光害 is "light pollution" caused by excessive artificial light, which, for example, hides the starry sky or disturbs animals. It is read こうがい and is thus homophonous with 公害 "environmental pollution"; to avoid confusion, people often say ひかりがい in speech. Typical expressions: 光害が少ない場所, 光害対策. A still fairly new technical term from astronomy and environmental protection.

examples[].german: Acid rain is causing serious damage to forests and lakes.
Acid rain has eroded the surface of the old stone statue.
In science class, we learned how acid rain forms.
en.notes: 酸性雨 is "acid rain", which is caused by sulfur and nitrogen oxides from exhaust gases. Typical expressions are 酸性雨が降る, 酸性雨の被害 and 酸性雨で森が枯れる. The topic was very prominent in the 1980s and today appears mainly in textbooks and environmental reports. 酸性 means "acidic" in the chemical sense; for taste one says 酸っぱい.

examples[].german: The destruction of the ozone layer by chlorofluorocarbons became a problem.
The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays from the sun.
Thanks to international regulations, the ozone layer is gradually recovering.
en.notes: オゾン層 is the "ozone layer" in the stratosphere, which protects against UV radiation. Typical expressions are オゾン層の破壊 "depletion of the ozone layer", オゾン層を守る and オゾンホール "ozone hole". The main culprit, CFCs, is called フロン or フロンガス in Japanese. 層 means "layer" and also appears in 地層 or 富裕層.

examples[].german: Due to the destruction of the ozone layer, the amount of ultraviolet radiation is increasing.
UV rays are strong in summer, so let's wear a hat when we go out.
This window glass blocks ninety percent of UV rays.
en.notes: 紫外線 is "UV radiation", literally "rays beyond violet"; its counterpart is 赤外線 "infrared". It is very common in everyday life, above all in connection with skin protection: 紫外線が強い, 紫外線を浴びる, 紫外線対策, 紫外線カット. UV or UVカット are used with the same meaning. Sunburn itself is called 日焼け.

examples[].german: A new development plan surfaced for the land in dispute.
The company declined to comment because it is in a legal dispute with a former employee.
The two countries continue to negotiate over the disputed border area.
en.notes: 係争 refers to a dispute between parties, usually fought out in court. Most common is 係争中 "in dispute, sub judice": 係争中の土地, 〜と係争中である. Other combinations are 係争地 "disputed territory" (also between states) and 係争事件. Formal language of lawyers and media; in everyday life one says 争い, 裁判中 or もめている. As a する-verb it hardly occurs.

examples[].german: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Cow burps contain large amounts of methane.
Methane from the landfill is collected and used to generate electricity.
en.notes: メタン is the gas "methane" and is always written in katakana; one often also hears メタンガス. In an environmental context it appears mainly as a 温室効果ガス; sources include 牛のげっぷ "cow burps", 水田 "paddy fields" and landfills. Typical expressions: メタンを排出する, メタンが発生する. The fuel ice on the seabed is called メタンハイドレート.

examples[].german: Exhaust gas regulations for motor vehicles are being tightened.
Walking along the main street, the smell of exhaust fumes is terrible.
Electric vehicles do not emit exhaust gas while driving.
en.notes: 排気ガス is "exhaust gas", especially from cars, motorcycles and machines; 排気 means "exhaust, venting". Typical are 排気ガスを出す, 排気ガス規制 and 排気ガスを吸い込む. In everyday speech the short form 排ガス is often used, especially in the news (排ガス規制). For smoke from factory chimneys one tends to say 排煙.

examples[].german: Dust from the construction site is threatening the health of nearby residents.
Please wear a mask while working so that you do not inhale dust.
If flour dust catches fire, an explosion can occur.
en.notes: 粉塵 refers to fine dust that gets into the air during construction work, in mining or in factories. Because 塵 is not one of the standard kanji, 粉じん is often written in official documents and on signs. Typical expressions: 粉塵が舞う, 粉塵を吸い込む, 粉塵対策 and 粉塵爆発 "dust explosion". For household dust one says ほこり; fine particulate matter in the sense of PM2.5 is 微小粒子状物質.

examples[].german: There are areas where the development of sewage treatment facilities is lagging behind.
The factory had been discharging its wastewater untreated into the river.
Heavy rain made the sewers overflow, and sewage flowed out onto the road.
en.notes: 汚水 is "dirty water" or "sewage", especially from households, toilets and factories. 下水 refers to the wastewater and sewer system (下水道), and 排水 to drained water in general, without emphasis on pollution. Typical expressions: 汚水を処理する, 汚水を垂れ流す "to discharge untreated", 汚水処理場. Register: rather written and technical.

examples[].german: Policies aimed at realizing a decarbonized society are being promoted.
Many companies are switching to renewable energy in order to decarbonize.
In the trend toward decarbonization, coal-fired power plants are being closed one after another.
en.notes: 脱炭素 means "decarbonization", that is, giving up CO₂ emissions; 脱 means "away from, exit from" as in 脱原発. It mostly stands before nouns: 脱炭素社会, 脱炭素化, 脱炭素経営. Closely related is カーボンニュートラル "carbon neutrality", the goal of balancing emissions and absorption. A very current buzzword in politics and business.

examples[].german: Many countries have set carbon neutrality as a goal.
The government declared that it will achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.
The company claims to have achieved carbon neutrality through tree planting.
en.notes: 炭素中立 is the literal translation of "carbon neutrality": emissions and absorption of CO₂ balance each other out. In Japanese practice, however, the loanword カーボンニュートラル is far more common; 炭素中立 is read more in technical texts or translations. Typical expressions: 炭素中立を目指す, 炭素中立を達成する, 炭素中立を目標に掲げる. Related is 脱炭素 "decarbonization", the path toward it.

examples[].german: Emissions trading is an economic method of reducing greenhouse gases.
The EU introduced an emissions trading system early on.
Companies that fail to meet their targets have to buy allowances on the emissions trading market.
en.notes: 排出権取引 is "emissions trading": companies or states buy and sell rights to emit a certain amount of CO₂. 排出権 is the "emission right", 取引 the "trading". In official Japanese texts the system is nowadays usually called 排出量取引 (制度); 排出権取引, however, remains common in the media. Typical expressions: 排出権取引制度, 排出権取引市場, 排出権を購入する.

examples[].german: Pollutants exceeding the environmental standards were detected.
The rivers in this region have finally come to meet the environmental standards for water quality.
The state decided to review the environmental standards for noise.
en.notes: 環境基準 are the legally set "environmental standards" or "environmental quality standards" for air, water, soil and noise. Typical expressions are 環境基準を超える "to exceed the limits", 環境基準を満たす/達成する "to meet" and 環境基準値. To be distinguished from it is 排出基準, which sets how much a single facility may emit. Register: official and news language.

examples[].german: The remaining capacity of landfills is running short.
Kansai International Airport stands on reclaimed land built by filling in the sea.
Reclaimed land is prone to liquefaction during earthquakes.
en.notes: 埋立地 (also 埋め立て地) is land created by filling in, especially in the sea or in bays: parts of Tokyo Bay, お台場 and Kansai International Airport are on 埋立地. In an environmental context it also refers to a landfill where waste is buried (ごみの埋立地, technically 最終処分場). The related verb is 埋め立てる. In earthquakes, 埋立地 is considered prone to soil liquefaction (液状化).

examples[].german: Waste incineration can be a source of dioxins.
Please incinerate all documents containing personal information.
The heat produced at the city's incineration plant is used for a heated swimming pool.
en.notes: 焼却 means "incineration, destruction by fire", especially of garbage and documents; as a transitive する-verb: ごみを焼却する. Typical expressions are 焼却処分 "disposal by incineration", 焼却炉 "incinerator" and ごみ焼却場. 燃やす is the everyday word, while 焼却 sounds official and technical. For cremation, on the other hand, one says 火葬.

en.meaning: conforming to; compliance (with a standard); based on
examples[].german: A law conforming to international standards was enacted.
This cable conforms to the USB standard.
I bought a workbook that is aligned with the textbook.
en.notes: 準拠 means to follow a norm, rule or template, or to be based on it. It almost always appears as 〜に準拠する or attributively 〜に準拠した + noun: 国際規格に準拠した製品, 教科書準拠の問題集 "workbook aligned with the textbook". Intransitive する-verb. Unlike 遵守 "to observe (laws)", 準拠 means "to conform to a norm, to model oneself on"; compared with the general 基づく, it is more technical. Common in technology, law and education.

examples[].german: Separate waste collection is thoroughly implemented in Japan.
From next month, plastic will be collected separately.
The rules for separate waste collection differ by municipality, so check after you move.
en.notes: 分別収集 is "separate waste collection": the municipality collects waste sorted by type, e.g. 燃えるごみ, 燃えないごみ, 資源ごみ. 分別 is read ぶんべつ here; ふんべつ, on the other hand, means "good sense, discretion". Citizens themselves 分別する or ごみを分別して出す "sort their waste"; 分別収集 emphasizes the municipal collection system. Typical of municipal notices and the news.

examples[].german: There is a demand to raise the recycling rate of used products.
Gold and copper are being recovered from collected old smartphones.
Much of the concrete from construction sites is recycled into resources.
en.notes: 再資源化 literally means "making into resources again" and refers to the material recycling of waste and old equipment. As a transitive する-verb: 廃家電を再資源化する. Typical expressions: 再資源化率 "recycling rate", 再資源化を進める. Compared with the everyday リサイクル, 再資源化 sounds official and technical; it often appears in laws and company reports.

examples[].german: Products with a low environmental impact are favored by consumers.
By switching freight to rail, we reduced the environmental impact.
Large quantities of disposable containers put a heavy burden on the environment.
en.notes: 環境負荷 is the "environmental burden" or "environmental impact" caused by a product, an activity or a company. Typical expressions are 環境負荷が低い/小さい, 環境負荷を減らす/低減する and 環境に負荷をかける. 負荷 actually means "load, burden" as in engineering. The word is typical of company reports, advertising and technical texts; in everyday speech one tends to say 環境に悪い／優しい.

examples[].german: Deforestation in tropical regions has become a serious environmental problem.
Satellite images are used to crack down on illegal logging.
Because of deforestation, landslides now occur every time there is heavy rain.
en.notes: 森林伐採 refers to the "clearing of forests", often as a large-scale environmental problem ("deforestation"). 伐採 is the felling of trees; as a verb one says 木を伐採する or 森林を伐採する. Typical expressions: 違法な森林伐採, 森林伐採が進む. The opposite is 植林 "afforestation". Register: news, textbooks, technical texts.

examples[].german: Overgrazing is accelerating desertification.
Rainfall decreased, and what was once farmland has turned into desert.
Drought-resistant trees are being planted to prevent desertification.
en.notes: 砂漠化 is "desertification", that is, the emergence of desert-like landscapes through climate or overuse. As an intransitive する-verb: 土地が砂漠化する; also common are 砂漠化が進む "desertification advances" and 砂漠化を防ぐ. The suffix 化 "-ization, becoming" is also known from 温暖化 or 都市化. In a figurative sense it is sometimes used loosely, e.g. 頭皮の砂漠化 for a dry scalp.

examples[].german: Eutrophication of lakes is causing mass outbreaks of algae.
Fertilizer from the fields flowed into the river, and the eutrophication of the bay progressed.
The pond became eutrophic because of phosphorus contained in detergents.
en.notes: 富栄養化 is "eutrophication": bodies of water become over-enriched with nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus from wastewater and fertilizer. As an intransitive する-verb: 湖が富栄養化する; 富栄養化が進む is also common. Consequences are algal blooms, アオコ in fresh water and 赤潮 in the sea. A technical word from biology and environmental reports.

examples[].german: The outbreak of a red tide killed large numbers of farmed fish.
This summer the water was warm, and a red tide occurred in the bay.
Because of the red tide, shipments of shellfish were stopped for a while.
en.notes: 赤潮 is the "red tide": a mass proliferation of plankton in the sea that colors the water reddish and kills fish. Typical expressions are 赤潮が発生する, 赤潮の被害 and 赤潮で魚が死ぬ. A related phenomenon is 青潮, oxygen-poor water that appears bluish-white; in fresh water one speaks of アオコ. Frequent in news from fishing and coastal regions.

en.meaning: ground subsidence; erosion of one's base
examples[].german: Excessive pumping of groundwater is causing land subsidence.
Even the once-industrial city is now suffering an economic decline.
The crushing election defeat made clear the erosion of the party's base.
en.notes: 地盤沈下 is the sinking of the ground, for example through excessive groundwater extraction; as an intransitive する-verb: 地盤が沈下する or 地盤沈下する. Very common is the figurative use for the gradual loss of importance or power of a party, industry or region: 地方経済の地盤沈下. The word is formal and typical of news and economic reports.

examples[].german: Reconciling environmental conservation with economic development is required.
Our company is actively working on environmental conservation around our factories.
Students took part in an environmental conservation activity on the riverbank.
en.notes: 環境保全 means "environmental protection" in the sense of "preserving the environment" in good condition. 環境保護 is largely synonymous, but emphasizes protecting from damage; 保全 sounds somewhat more official and is popular in laws and corporate mission statements. Typical expressions: 環境保全に取り組む, 環境保全活動, 環境保全と経済の両立. Register: formal, government agencies and companies.

examples[].german: The main source of greenhouse gases is the burning of fossil fuels.
This company publishes its greenhouse gas emissions every year.
Let's use the train instead of flying and cut greenhouse gases.
en.notes: 温室効果ガス are "greenhouse gases" such as 二酸化炭素, メタン or 一酸化二窒素. Typical expressions are 温室効果ガスを排出する, 温室効果ガスの排出量 and 温室効果ガスを削減する. In the news it is often shortened to "CO₂", although that actually means only a single gas. ガス is always written in katakana.

examples[].german: All employees are required to comply with laws and regulations.
Please observe the terms of the contract.
In the factory, strict observance of safety standards is enforced.
en.notes: 遵守 is the formal observing of laws, rules, contracts or deadlines: 法律を遵守する, 法令遵守 (corresponds to コンプライアンス). Transitive する-verb with を. In everyday life one simply says 守る; 遵守 sounds official and written. Newspapers often write 順守, with the same reading. Not to be confused with 準拠 "to conform to a norm, to be based on something".

examples[].german: Japan, a volcanic country, has high potential for geothermal power generation.
The owners of hot springs oppose the development of geothermal power generation.
The strength of geothermal power is that it is not affected by the weather.
en.notes: 地熱発電 is "power generation from geothermal heat"; 地熱 (ちねつ, less often じねつ) is the heat of the Earth. As a volcanic country, Japan has large reserves, but development often stalls because many sources lie within national parks or because operators of thermal baths (温泉) fear for their water. Typical expressions: 地熱発電所, 地熱発電の潜在力, 地熱発電を開発する.

examples[].german: Biomass power generation is one form of renewable energy.
In this town, thinned timber is used as biomass fuel.
Biomass material is mixed into the plastic bags at convenience stores.
en.notes: バイオマス refers to "biomass", that is, organic material such as wood residue, straw, manure or food waste that is used as an energy source or raw material. It mostly stands before other nouns: バイオマス発電 "biomass power plant/power", バイオマス燃料, バイオマスプラスチック. Biofuels are called バイオ燃料. Register: technical and news language.

examples[].german: Resource-saving manufacturing processes are in demand.
Simplifying the packaging contributes to resource conservation.
This company has set resource conservation and energy conservation as its management goals.
en.notes: 省資源 means "resource saving, resource conservation" and is the counterpart of 省エネ for raw materials and materials. It almost always stands before nouns or with 型/化: 省資源型の製品, 省資源化を進める, 省資源・省エネルギー. In everyday speech one would rather say 資源を節約する or 無駄を減らす; 省資源 belongs in company, official and technical texts.

examples[].german: Improvements in wastewater treatment technology are contributing to better water environments.
This factory's wastewater treatment equipment was old, and it had not been meeting the standards.
Sludge produced in the wastewater treatment process is also used as fertilizer.
en.notes: 廃水処理 is "wastewater treatment", especially of industrial and factory wastewater. 廃水 is "used, unusable water"; the homophone 排水 means more generally "drainage, discharge", and 排水処理 is often used with the same meaning. Household wastewater usually falls under 下水処理. Typical expressions: 廃水処理施設, 廃水処理技術, 廃水を処理する.

examples[].german: Converting sludge into fertilizer is being researched as an effective use of it.
Efforts have begun to turn the sludge from sewage treatment plants into fuel.
Heavy metals were detected in the factory's sludge.
en.notes: 汚泥 is "sludge", especially the "sewage sludge" (下水汚泥) or industrial sludge produced during wastewater treatment. Typical expressions: 汚泥を処理する, 汚泥処理, 汚泥を肥料にする. For the stinking mud at the bottom of rivers and harbors, one colloquially says ヘドロ, and for ordinary mud 泥. In elevated language, 汚泥 rarely also stands figuratively for a "hopeless situation".

examples[].german: There is a risk that leachate from landfills will contaminate groundwater.
At the disposal site, the leachate is treated before being released into the river.
The quality of the leachate is tested every month.
en.notes: 浸出水 is a technical term of waste management: the leachate that runs through a landfill, picks up pollutants and emerges at the bottom. Typical are 浸出水処理（施設） and 浸出水が漏れる. It belongs to 浸出（しんしゅつ）"leaching, seeping out". The word hardly occurs in everyday life, but does in environmental reports and news about landfills.

examples[].german: Decontamination work after the nuclear plant accident has continued over a long period.
For the sake of the children, the school playground was decontaminated first.
A storage site for the soil removed during decontamination has not been decided.
en.notes: 除染 means "decontamination", the removal of radioactive or chemical contamination from soil, buildings or people. As a transitive する-verb: 校庭を除染する. Since the Fukushima nuclear accident in 2011, the word has been generally known; typical expressions are 除染作業, 除染土 "contaminated soil from decontamination" and 除染が進む. Register: news, government agencies.

examples[].german: The radiation doses of workers must be strictly controlled.
The radiation exposure from an X-ray examination is extremely small.
In the accident, several workers were exposed to radiation.
en.notes: 被曝 means "radiation exposure", that is, being exposed to radioactive radiation; as an intransitive する-verb: 作業員が被曝した. Typical are 被曝線量 "radiation dose", 内部被曝 and 外部被曝. Not to be confused with the identically read 被爆 "to be hit by an (atomic) bomb", as in 被爆者 "atomic bomb victim". Since 曝 is not a standard kanji, government agencies often write 被ばく.

examples[].german: The half-life of plutonium-239 is about 24,000 years.
Cesium-137 has a long half-life of about 30 years.
This medicine has a short half-life, so it has to be taken three times a day.
en.notes: 半減期 is the "half-life", the time in which the amount of a radioactive substance (or active ingredient) is halved. Typical patterns: Xの半減期は…年だ, 半減期が長い/短い. The word is also used in pharmacology for medicines (薬の半減期) and occasionally figuratively, e.g. for quickly fading interest. Register: scientific, but familiar from the news.

examples[].german: Research evaluating the economic value of ecosystem services is advancing.
Pollination by bees is also one important ecosystem service.
When forests are lost, the ecosystem service of cleaning water is lost as well.
en.notes: 生態系サービス is the technical term for "ecosystem services": the benefits people derive from nature, such as food, clean water, pollination or recreation. Typical expressions are 生態系サービスを評価する, 生態系サービスの価値 and 生態系サービスを受ける. サービス here does not mean a service in the economic sense, but a "provision" of nature. Used almost only in science and environmental policy.

examples[].german: This act may violate the Antimonopoly Act.
Using other people's photos without permission may infringe copyright.
We checked whether the new rule conflicts with existing provisions.
en.notes: 抵触 means to violate a law, rule or provision, or to come into conflict with it; intransitive with に: 法律に抵触する, 著作権に抵触する. Often worded cautiously: 抵触する恐れがある, 抵触しかねない. It sounds more indirect than 違反する "to violate". It also denotes contradictions between rules or statements: 規定と抵触する. Formal, legal language.

examples[].german: Harmful substances become biologically concentrated through the food chain.
Minamata disease is a pollution disease caused by the bioconcentration of mercury.
Large fish such as tuna are more susceptible to the effects of bioconcentration.
en.notes: 生物濃縮 is "bioaccumulation" or "biomagnification": pollutants such as mercury or PCBs accumulate in organisms through the food chain. It mostly appears in the passive or as a subject: 生物濃縮される, 生物濃縮が起こる; typical is 食物連鎖を通じて "through the food chain". In Japan the concept is closely tied to Minamata disease (水俣病). A technical word from biology and environmental science.

examples[].german: Environmental hormones are affecting the reproductive function of wild animals.
Some people worry that environmental hormones leach out when plastic containers are heated in a microwave.
The term "environmental hormones" became a big topic in the 1990s.
en.notes: 環境ホルモン is the popular term coined in Japan for "endocrine disruptors", that is, chemicals that act like hormones and disturb the hormone system. The technical term is 内分泌かく乱物質. The word was a major media topic in the late 1990s (e.g. bisphenol A in plastic tableware). Typical expressions: 環境ホルモンの影響, 環境ホルモンが溶け出す.

examples[].german: The urban heat island phenomenon is leading to an increase in heatstroke.
As a measure against the heat island effect, greenery is being added to building rooftops.
Because of the heat island effect, the temperature in Tokyo does not drop even at night.
en.notes: ヒートアイランド refers to the "urban heat island": cities are noticeably warmer than their surroundings because of asphalt, concrete and waste heat. It mostly appears in the combination ヒートアイランド現象 "heat island effect" or ヒートアイランド対策. Countermeasures include 屋上緑化 "rooftop greening" and 打ち水 "sprinkling water". Frequent in weather reports and urban planning.

examples[].german: Rooftop greening is attracting attention as a measure against the heat island effect.
The city is promoting greening in front of the station.
I took part as a volunteer in a project to green the desert.
en.notes: 緑化 means greening areas with plants and trees, as a transitive する-verb: 町を緑化する. Common compounds are 屋上緑化 "rooftop greening", 壁面緑化 "wall greening", 緑化運動 and 砂漠の緑化. Besides りょくか, the reading りょっか is also in use. The word belongs to urban planning and environmental policy.

examples[].german: Tree planting activities are being carried out on devastated mountain land.
After the war, my grandfather planted cedars on this mountain.
As part of the company's social contribution, employees took part in a tree-planting volunteer event.
en.notes: 植林 means deliberately planting trees on bare or logged-over land so that forest (re)grows. As a する-verb: 山に杉を植林する; also 植林地 "afforested land" and 植林活動. To be distinguished from 植樹 "planting individual trees" (often ceremonial, 植樹祭); the opposite is 伐採 "logging". Neutral, common in environmental and forestry contexts.

examples[].german: Proper thinning promotes the healthy growth of the forest.
Plantation forests that are not thinned in time become neglected because sunlight does not reach the ground.
These disposable chopsticks are made from thinned timber.
en.notes: 間伐 is the planned removal of individual trees from a stand that is too dense, so that the remaining ones receive light and grow strongly. As a する-verb: 森を間伐する; the wood produced in the process is called 間伐材 (e.g. for chopsticks). To be distinguished from 伐採 "felling trees" in general and 皆伐 "clear-cutting". Note: the identically pronounced 干ばつ/旱魃 means "drought". Technical, from forestry.

examples[].german: Making use of idle farmland is the key to regional revival.
Since my grandparents died, the field at my parents' home has become idle farmland.
The town leases idle farmland to young new entrants to farming.
en.notes: 遊休農地 is farmland that could be used for agriculture but is currently not being cultivated. 遊休 means "unused, lying idle" (cf. 遊休地, 遊休資産). Typical: 遊休農地を活用する/解消する/貸し出す. Closely related is 耕作放棄地 "abandoned farmland", which emphasizes permanent abandonment. Language of government agencies and newspapers; in everyday speech one tends to say 使っていない畑.

examples[].german: Companies are required to design products with environmental considerations in mind.
For this product, the packaging was changed to paper from the standpoint of environmental consideration.
The new city hall was praised for its environmental considerations, such as solar power generation.
en.notes: 環境配慮 is a compound of 環境 "environment" and 配慮 "consideration" and refers to taking environmental concerns into account in products, buildings or corporate decisions. Typical are 環境配慮型 "eco-friendly" (環境配慮型製品) and 環境配慮の観点から. In running text, the verbal form 環境に配慮した〜 is even more common. Business and administrative language.

examples[].german: Wetland restoration projects are being carried out in various places.
An attempt at nature restoration has begun to return a concrete-lined river to its original form.
Nature restoration takes decades, so the cooperation of local residents is indispensable.
en.notes: 自然再生 refers to the restoration of damaged ecosystems such as wetlands, tidal flats or straightened rivers, that is, "renaturation". Typical: 自然再生事業, 自然再生に取り組む; the legal basis is the 自然再生推進法. In contrast to 自然保護 (protecting existing nature), this is about bringing back lost nature. 再生 alone is also known as "playback" for videos. Technical and administrative language.

examples[].german: Volunteers are taking part in conservation activities for sea turtles.
Local high school students continue conservation activities for wild birds on the tidal flats.
Conservation activities require funds, so we are appealing for donations.
en.notes: 保護活動 are organized efforts to protect animals, nature or cultural properties: ウミガメの保護活動, 文化財の保護活動. Common verbs are 保護活動に参加する/取り組む and 保護活動を行う/続ける. 保護 emphasizes protecting something endangered; for the lasting preservation of whole ecosystems one tends to say 保全 (環境保全). Neutral, frequent in the news and among associations.

examples[].german: There is a dispute among scholars over the interpretation of the constitution.
Is it right to interpret his silence as agreement?
This poem allows for many interpretations.
en.notes: 解釈 is the interpretation or construal of texts, laws, statements or behavior: 法律の解釈, 解釈の違い, 〜を〜と解釈する "to take something as ...". A transitive する-verb. Unlike 説明 "explanation for others", 解釈 is one's own reading; translating and interpreting are called 翻訳 and 通訳. It is general-purpose, not only legal: 好意的に解釈する "to interpret charitably", 拡大解釈 "overly broad interpretation".

en.meaning: population count; number of individuals living in an area
examples[].german: Thanks to conservation activities, the crested ibis population has recovered.
The research team surveys the number of swans at the lake every year.
The deer population has grown too large, and damage to crops is spreading.
en.notes: 生息数 is the population count of a wild animal species in an area; 生息 means "to live, inhabit (as an animal)". Typical: 生息数が増える/減る/回復する, 生息数を調査する. For humans one says 人口, and in biology also 個体数 "number of individuals". Objective, in reports and news about nature conservation and wildlife damage.

examples[].german: Overfishing of tuna has become an international problem.
Whales were once overhunted around the world, and their numbers plummeted.
To prevent overfishing of eels, the catch of glass eels was restricted.
en.notes: 乱獲 is the indiscriminate, excessive catching or hunting of fish and wild animals, so that the stock is endangered; 乱 "disorderly", 獲 "to capture". As a する-verb, mostly in the passive: クジラが乱獲される. Unlike 密猟, 乱獲 need not be illegal, only excessive. For forests, the counterpart is 乱伐. Occasionally written 濫獲; objective, in environmental reports.

examples[].german: Poaching for ivory is driving African elephants to the brink of extinction.
In the national park, rangers patrol even at night to prevent poaching.
The men who poached rhinoceroses were arrested.
en.notes: 密猟 is the prohibited, secret hunting of wild animals: 密 "secret", 猟 "hunting". As a する-verb: サイを密猟する; the offender is called 密猟者. Not to be confused with the identically pronounced 密漁 "illegal fishing" (character 漁 with the water radical). In contrast to 乱獲, 密猟 emphasizes illegality. Objective, in the news.

examples[].german: Illegal logging is accelerating the decline of tropical rainforests.
Dealers are required to confirm that they are not importing illegally logged timber.
A site of illegal logging was found on satellite images.
en.notes: 違法伐採 is the felling of trees without a permit or in violation of forestry laws, especially in tropical forests. Typical: 違法伐採された木材 "illegally logged timber", 違法伐採対策, 違法伐採を取り締まる. 伐採 is the neutral term for logging; 乱伐 means excessive, but not necessarily illegal, felling. News and government language.

examples[].german: Microplastics in the oceans are having a serious impact on ecosystems.
Microplastics contained in facial cleansers have come to be regulated.
A survey found microplastics in the stomachs of fish.
en.notes: マイクロプラスチック are plastic particles smaller than about 5 mm, which come, for example, from disintegrating plastic waste or from cosmetics. Typical: マイクロプラスチックが海に流れ出る, 魚の体内から検出される, マイクロプラスチック汚染. A katakana loanword, treated as a mass noun (no counter needed). Neutral, very common in the news and in science.

examples[].german: Marine pollution from oil spill accidents is becoming more serious.
Marine pollution from plastic waste is closely tied to our daily lives.
In class, I researched marine pollution and gave a presentation.
en.notes: 海洋汚染 is the pollution of the seas by oil, plastic waste, chemicals or wastewater. 海洋 is the formal word for "ocean, sea"; in conversation one tends to say 海の汚れ or 海が汚れる. Typical: 海洋汚染が深刻化する, 海洋汚染を防ぐ, 〜による海洋汚染. It joins the series 大気汚染, 水質汚染, 土壌汚染. Objective, in the news and at school.

examples[].german: Heated effluent from the power plant is affecting the ecosystem of the surrounding waters.
Nuclear power plants discharge large amounts of heated cooling water into the sea.
Because of the thermal discharge, fish from southern seas can now be seen in this bay.
en.notes: 温排水 is the heated cooling water that thermal and nuclear power plants or factories return to the sea or rivers; it is usually several degrees warmer than the surrounding water. Typical: 温排水を放出する/海に流す, 温排水の影響. It is thus about the water itself, not household wastewater (生活排水). Technical language from energy and environmental engineering.

examples[].german: Forests have the function of recharging water sources.
For the sake of water source conservation, logging is restricted in the upstream forests.
The city provides subsidies for the upkeep of watershed protection forests.
en.notes: 水源涵養 refers to the ability of forests and soils to store rain, even out the runoff into rivers and purify water; 涵養 means "to nourish gradually, to build up". It occurs almost only in fixed expressions: 水源涵養機能, 水源涵養林. Since 涵 is not a jōyō kanji, government agencies often write 水源かん養. Very formal, forestry and administrative language.

examples[].german: The disaster-prevention forest along the coast reduced tsunami damage.
After the earthquake, citizens planted pine seedlings to create a new disaster-prevention forest on the coast.
The disaster-prevention forest on the mountain slope plays a role in preventing landslides during heavy rain.
en.notes: 防災林 is a forest that is deliberately created or maintained to protect land, roads or settlements from natural disasters. Depending on the hazard there are special terms: 防風林 "windbreak forest", 防潮林 or 海岸防災林 against storm surges and tsunamis, 防砂林 against drifting sand. Typical: 防災林を整備する/植える. Objective, in administration and the news, especially since 2011.

examples[].german: The introduction of an environmental tax is expected to curb carbon dioxide emissions.
If an environmental tax is introduced, gasoline might get more expensive.
Revenue from the environmental tax is used to promote the spread of renewable energy.
en.notes: 環境税 is a tax that makes environmentally harmful behavior (above all CO2 emissions) more expensive or finances environmental protection. In Japan, concrete examples are the 地球温暖化対策税 and the 森林環境税; closely related is 炭素税 "carbon tax". Typical: 環境税を導入する/課す, 環境税の税収. Objective, language of politics and business.

examples[].german: A law that no longer suited the times was abolished.
Because of low ridership, this bus route will be discontinued next year.
Quite a few countries have abolished the death penalty.
en.notes: 廃止 means to officially and permanently abolish or discontinue an institution, rule or service: 制度を廃止する, 路線の廃止, 死刑廃止. Transitive する-verb; in the news mostly passive: 〜が廃止される. Unlike 中止 "cancellation or halting of a plan or event", 廃止 is final; 撤廃 stresses the removal of barriers (関税の撤廃).

examples[].german: Through environmental audits, companies' environmental management systems are evaluated.
Next month, we are scheduled to undergo an environmental audit by outside experts.
The environmental audit pointed out that the waste records were insufficient.
en.notes: 環境監査 is the systematic examination of whether a company complies with environmental regulations and its own environmental management (e.g. ISO 14001). Typical: 環境監査を受ける/実施する, 内部環境監査. 監査 means an examination of processes and documents (like 会計監査); 検査 is more a technical inspection, and 審査 an assessment, for example for certification. Business and technical language.

examples[].german: Penalties are imposed on factories that exceed the effluent standards.
This factory's wastewater fully meets the national effluent standards.
The prefecture set its own standards that are stricter than the national effluent standards.
en.notes: 排水基準 are the legally set maximum values for pollutants in the wastewater of factories and businesses (in Japan under the 水質汚濁防止法). Typical: 排水基準を守る/満たす/超える, 排水基準に違反する. Not to be confused with 環境基準, which describes quality targets for rivers or air and does not apply directly to individual businesses. Language of government agencies and technical texts.

examples[].german: In mountainous regions, temperatures are low and the climate is harsh.
At university I joined the mountaineering club and climbed mountains every weekend.
The mountain rescue team rescued the climbers who got into trouble in the winter mountains.
en.notes: 山岳 is the literary word for "mountains, mountain range" and rarely stands alone, mostly appearing as a modifier: 山岳地帯 "mountainous region", 山岳部 "mountaineering club", 山岳救助隊 "mountain rescue team", 山岳信仰 "mountain worship". In everyday speech one simply says 山. 山脈, by contrast, refers to a specific, named mountain chain (アルプス山脈).

examples[].german: The top of the plateau is well drained and suitable for farming.
In the old days, people built villages on top of plateaus to avoid floods.
From the station you have to climb a steep slope to the residential area on top of the plateau.
en.notes: 台地 refers to a raised piece of land, largely flat on top, with steep edges, such as the 武蔵野台地 near Tokyo; many fields and suburbs lie on such terraces. Unlike 高原 "highland", which lies considerably higher and is often a holiday region, a 台地 only needs to lie a few dozen meters above the plain; the counterpart is 低地 "lowland". Not to be confused with the identically read 大地 "earth, ground". A neutral term from geography and local history, mostly in 台地の上.

examples[].german: Vineyards spread across the gently rolling hill country.
Large residential areas were developed in the Tama Hills.
Hiking courses through the hill country are popular even with beginners.
en.notes: 丘陵 is extensive, gently undulating hill country, lower than real mountains. Typical: 丘陵地, 丘陵地帯 and in proper names such as 多摩丘陵. The everyday 丘 refers to a single hill (丘の上の家), whereas 丘陵 refers more to the landform; it is literary and geographical. Often with なだらかな "gentle".

examples[].german: A large industrial zone stretches along the coast of Tokyo Bay.
The waves inside the bay are calm, so it is well suited to oyster farming.
From the hotel facing the bay, you can see a beautiful sunset.
en.notes: 湾 means "bay, gulf" and mostly appears as a suffix after names: 東京湾, 大阪湾, ペルシャ湾 "Persian Gulf", メキシコ湾. On its own it appears in 湾内 "inside the bay" or 湾に面した〜. Smaller, narrow inlets are rather called 入江. Related is 湾岸 "bay coast" (湾岸戦争 "Gulf War"). Not to be confused with 椀/碗 (わん) "bowl".

examples[].german: Fishing boats were moored in the calm inlet.
A sandy beach with quiet waves lay hidden in a small cove.
It is said that this inlet was once a pirate hideout.
en.notes: 入江 is a small bay or arm of the sea reaching deep into the land, also on lakes. It sounds scenic and somewhat literary; it is found in travelogues and novels (静かな入江, 入江に船を泊める). For large, named bays, 湾 is used (東京湾). 入江 also occurs as a family name.

examples[].german: The Tsugaru Strait separates Honshu from Hokkaido.
The Kanmon Strait has fast tidal currents and is known as a difficult passage for ships.
I crossed the strait by ferry and returned from Kyushu to Honshu.
en.notes: 海峡 is a strait between two landmasses, mostly with a name in front: 津軽海峡, 関門海峡, ドーバー海峡, マラッカ海峡. Typical: 海峡を渡る, 海峡を隔てる, 海峡トンネル. Narrower sea passages are often called 水道 (豊後水道) or 瀬戸 (鳴門の瀬戸). Neutral, geographical.

examples[].german: The Japanese archipelago is located on the Pacific Ring of Fire.
This weekend, strong cold air will cover the whole Japanese archipelago.
The Kuril Islands stretch in a long line northeast from Hokkaido.
en.notes: 列島 is a long, elongated chain of islands lying in a row, above all in 日本列島 and 千島列島. In news and weather reports, 日本列島 often simply stands for "all of Japan": 寒波が日本列島を襲う, 列島各地で. To be distinguished from 諸島 "island group" (not necessarily in a line) and 群島 (closely clustered). Neutral to literary.

examples[].german: The Ogasawara Islands are registered as a World Natural Heritage site.
The Hawaiian Islands were formed by volcanic activity.
Because a typhoon is approaching the Amami Islands, ship sailings are being canceled one after another.
en.notes: 諸島 refers to a group of islands that belong together and almost always stands after a name: 小笠原諸島, 奄美諸島, ハワイ諸島, ガラパゴス諸島. 諸 means "various, several". Unlike 列島, the islands do not need to lie in a line. In everyday speech one says 島々 "the islands". Neutral, geographical.

examples[].german: Many imperial edicts were promulgated in the Meiji period.
French king Henry IV granted Protestants freedom of worship with the Edict of Nantes.
After the war, most imperial edicts were replaced by cabinet orders.
en.notes: 勅令 is an ordinance with the force of law issued by the emperor or monarch. In Japan they existed under the Meiji Constitution; many were issued without the consent of the parliament, and after 1947 they were replaced by 政令 ("cabinet orders"). For European history it is the usual translation of "edict": ナントの勅令. Distinguish 詔書 (imperial document, proclamation) and 勅語 (imperial address, e.g. 教育勅語).

examples[].german: A new environmental protection law was enacted.
The city enacted its own ordinance and banned smoking on the street.
"Mountain Day" is a newly established national holiday.
en.notes: 制定 is the formal enacting of laws, ordinances and statutes, but also the official establishment of holidays or symbols: 法律を制定する, 憲法の制定, 祝日を制定する. Transitive する-verb, in the news mostly passive. The stages of a law: 制定 "to enact", 改正 "to amend", 廃止 "to abolish"; 施行 is the entry into force. Not to be confused with 設定 "setting, configuring (e.g. on a device)".

examples[].german: The Tone River's drainage basin is the largest in Japan.
Because of the heavy rain, evacuation orders were issued to residents of the river basin.
In the Yellow River basin, civilization has flourished since ancient times.
en.notes: 流域 is the entire area drained by a river with its tributaries, and in a broader sense also the landscape along the river. Typical: 〜川流域, 流域面積 "area of the drainage basin", 流域の住民, 上流域/下流域. In everyday speech, one more often says 川沿い "along the river"; 流域 is factual and geographic, and is common in news about floods.

examples[].german: Unspoiled nature remains in the upper reaches of the river.
Salmon swim upstream to lay their eggs.
She was born into an upper-class family.
en.notes: 上流 is the upper course of a river or the direction "upstream": 川の上流, 上流へ向かう; counterparts are 中流 and 下流. In conversation one also hears 川上 (かわかみ). Figuratively, 上流 stands for the social upper class (上流階級, 上流社会); in business, 上流工程 refers to the early phases of a project.

examples[].german: A vast plain spreads across the lower reaches of the river.
When a dam releases water, the water level downstream can rise suddenly.
The hat that fell into the river was swept downstream in no time.
en.notes: 下流 (かりゅう) is the lower course of a river or "downstream": 下流へ流される, 下流域. The counterpart is 上流; colloquially also 川下 (かわしも). Figuratively, 下流 means "lower social class" (下流社会); this sounds derogatory and should be used with care. Do not read it as したながれ.

examples[].german: Many tributaries join the main stream.
This river is one of the tributaries of the Shinano River.
Heavy rain made a tributary overflow, and the surrounding fields were flooded.
en.notes: 支流 is a tributary that flows into a larger river; the counterpart is 本流 "main stream". Typical: 〜川の支流, 支流が本流に合流する. Figuratively, 支流 can also refer to a side branch of a school or movement, e.g. in art or martial arts. Objective, geographical.

en.meaning: confluence; to join up; to merge
examples[].german: A town developed at the confluence of two rivers.
I'll join you later, after I finish work.
When merging onto an expressway, it is important to match your speed.
en.notes: 合流 first of all means the flowing together of rivers (合流点 "confluence"), but in everyday speech it is very often used for people: 後で合流する "to join later", 駅で合流する. Intransitive する-verb: AがBに合流する or AとBが合流する. In traffic it means merging (合流車線), in politics the merger of parties. To be distinguished from 集合 "to gather at a meeting point".

examples[].german: The Nile Delta is world famous.
Hiroshima is a city that developed on the delta of the Ōta River.
Because deltas are low-lying, they are prone to storm surge damage.
en.notes: 三角州 is a river delta, that is, the usually triangular alluvial area at a river mouth where the river deposits sand and mud. 州 means "sandbar" here and is read す (cf. 中州, 砂州), not しゅう as in カリフォルニア州. The loanword デルタ (デルタ地帯) is synonymous. School geography, objective.

examples[].german: Alluvial fans are a landform suited to fruit growing.
The middle part of an alluvial fan is well drained, and the river water seeps underground.
In geography class, we explained how an alluvial fan forms using a diagram.
en.notes: 扇状地 is an alluvial fan: where a river emerges from the mountains onto the plain, it deposits gravel and sand in a fan shape (扇状 "fan-shaped"). In geography class, one distinguishes 扇頂, 扇央 and 扇端. The middle part is very permeable (水はけがよい) and suited to fruit growing; springs often emerge at the edge. A technical term of geography.

examples[].german: Floodplains have fertile soil and are used for agriculture.
Residential areas built on floodplains have a high flood risk.
Landforms such as natural levees and back marshes can be seen on floodplains.
en.notes: 氾濫原 is the flat valley floor next to a river that is regularly flooded at high water; 氾濫 means "flood, overflowing the banks", 原 "plain". Typical landforms within it are 自然堤防 "natural levee" and 後背湿地 "back marsh". A technical term from geography and flood control; in everyday speech one tends to say 浸水しやすい土地.

examples[].german: Fold mountains are formed by compression of the Earth's crust.
In the cliff along the road, you can see the strata folded greatly.
We experimented with clay to show the difference between folding and faulting.
en.notes: 褶曲 is the geological folding of rock layers by lateral pressure. As an intransitive する-verb: 地層が褶曲する; also 褶曲山脈 "fold mountains". To be distinguished from 断層 "fault", where the layers break instead of bending. 褶 is not a jōyō kanji, so it is also written しゅう曲. A purely technical term.

examples[].german: Japan is located where four plates meet.
The Pacific Plate is subducting beneath the North American Plate.
Large earthquakes tend to occur at plate boundaries.
en.notes: プレート has many meanings (name plate, license plate ナンバープレート, plate/dish, the home plate in baseball); in geography it is the tectonic plate. Mostly with names: 太平洋プレート, フィリピン海プレート, ユーラシアプレート, 北米プレート. Typical: プレートが沈み込む, プレートの境界, プレートテクトニクス. Neutral, familiar from textbooks and earthquake reports.

examples[].german: Many experts were involved in drafting the law.
The joint statement was drafted by representatives of both countries.
I was asked to draft the club's bylaws.
en.notes: 起草 is the drafting of an official text: 法案/条約/声明を起草する, 起草委員会 "drafting committee". Transitive する-verb. It stresses the first draft; the result is called 草案 "draft". For everyday drafts such as emails or essays, one says 下書き; 立案 is the planning of a measure. Formal language.

examples[].german: The Himalayas were uplifted by orogeny.
The Alps are gradually getting higher through orogeny that continues even now.
Shell fossils are found near the summit because the seabed was lifted up by orogeny.
en.notes: 造山運動 is mountain building (orogeny) through movements of the Earth's crust; 運動 means "movement" here, not "sport". Typical: 造山運動によって隆起する/形成される. The zones formed in the process are called 造山帯, e.g. 環太平洋造山帯 or アルプス・ヒマラヤ造山帯. A technical term of geology and school geography.

examples[].german: The uplift of the Earth's crust turned the seabed into dry land.
The coast rose by about two meters in the big earthquake.
A small bump formed on my skin, so I had it checked at a dermatologist.
en.notes: 隆起 is rising or bulging up, above all of land: 土地が隆起する, 地殻の隆起. The opposite is 沈降 "subsidence". As an intransitive する-verb it has no transitive counterpart; for "to lift up" one says 持ち上げる. Also used for bulges on the body (皮膚の隆起, 筋肉の隆起). Literary, in geology and medicine.

examples[].german: Subsidence of the ground enlarged the area of land below sea level.
The Seto Inland Sea is said to have been created by the sinking of land.
In the blood test, the erythrocyte sedimentation rate was checked.
en.notes: 沈降 has two technical meanings: the sinking of land (the opposite of 隆起) and the settling of particles in a liquid, for example 赤血球沈降速度 "erythrocyte sedimentation rate". Intransitive する-verb: 土地が沈降する. For the everyday sinking of the ground due to groundwater extraction, one usually says 地盤沈下. Literary and technical.

examples[].german: Depositional plains formed by rivers are suited to agriculture.
The Kanto Plain is the largest depositional plain in Japan.
In geography textbooks, plains are divided into depositional plains and erosional plains.
en.notes: 堆積平野 is a plain formed by sediments deposited by rivers or the sea; 堆積 means "deposition". The opposite is 侵食平野 "erosional plain". Depositional plains include 沖積平野 and 海岸平野; most of Japan's large plains are of this type. A technical term of school geography.

examples[].german: Limestone was dissolved, and karst topography was formed.
Akiyoshidai in Yamaguchi Prefecture is known as one of the largest karst landscapes in Japan.
Beneath karst topography, limestone caves often extend.
en.notes: カルスト地形 is a karst landscape, which forms when rainwater dissolves limestone (石灰岩). Typical forms are sinkholes (ドリーネ) and limestone caves (鍾乳洞). The best-known example in Japan is the plateau 秋吉台. Briefly, one also says just カルスト. A technical term of geography, but also familiar from travel guides.

examples[].german: A settlement has formed on the river terrace.
Walking along the river, you can clearly see the stair-like river terraces.
River terraces form through repeated land uplift and river erosion.
en.notes: 河岸段丘 are stair-like river terraces along a valley; they form when land rises and the river cuts down deeper again and again. The flat steps (段丘面) often carry settlements and fields; the steep edges are called 段丘崖. 河岸 is read かがん here; かし is the riverbank with a fish market (魚河岸). A technical term of geography.

examples[].german: A new island was born from the eruption of an undersea volcano.
The sunken ship still lies asleep on the deep seabed.
The Seikan Tunnel is a railway tunnel that runs under the seabed.
en.notes: 海底 is the seabed or sea floor: 海底に沈む, 深い海底. It very often stands before other nouns in the sense of "undersea": 海底トンネル, 海底ケーブル, 海底火山, 海底地震. To be distinguished from 海中 "in the sea, underwater" (the water column) and the more general 水底 "bottom of a body of water". Neutral.

examples[].german: The Japan Trench was formed by the subduction of the Pacific Plate.
The Mariana Trench is the deepest ocean trench in the world.
The earthquake that caused the Great East Japan Earthquake disaster occurred along the Japan Trench.
en.notes: 海溝 is an ocean trench, a long, very deep groove in the seabed where one oceanic plate dives under another. Mostly with names: マリアナ海溝, 日本海溝, 千島海溝. Less deep grooves of this kind are called トラフ (南海トラフ). 溝 means "ditch, groove" (cf. 溝 みぞ). A technical term, often in earthquake reports.

examples[].german: The continental shelf is known as a rich fishing ground.
Oil and natural gas may lie beneath the seabed of the continental shelf.
The two countries continue to negotiate over the boundary of the continental shelf.
en.notes: 大陸棚 is the shallow seabed that extends from the mainland to a water depth of about 200 m, before the steep 大陸斜面 "continental slope" begins. The word is encountered in geography, fishing and above all in maritime law: because of oil and gas deposits, the 大陸棚 often appears in the news alongside the 排他的経済水域 "exclusive economic zone". 棚 is read だな here with rendaku, as in 本棚. A purely technical term, not an everyday word.

examples[].german: The Maldives is an island nation made up of atolls.
Inside the atoll lies a calm lagoon.
If sea levels rise, the islands of low-lying atolls are at risk of being submerged.
en.notes: 環礁 is an atoll, a ring-shaped coral reef that encloses a lagoon (礁湖, ラグーン). Coral reefs in general are called サンゴ礁; 環 "ring" makes the shape clear. Beware of many homophones: 鑑賞 "appreciation (of art)", 干渉 "interference", 感傷 "sentimentality". Objective, geographical.

examples[].german: The overstepping of discretionary authority was judged unlawful.
The discussion strayed from the original topic.
His behavior deviates greatly from society's rules.
en.notes: 逸脱 is deviating from a norm, rule, role or a given framework: 本来の目的から逸脱する, 常識を逸脱した行動. Intransitive する-verb, mostly with から, in fixed combinations also with を (権限を逸脱する "to exceed one's authority"). It sounds formal and judgmental; for simple spatial deviation one says 外れる. In administrative law: 裁量権の逸脱・濫用 "exceeding and abuse of discretion".

examples[].german: The ship ran onto a hidden reef in the fog.
The negotiations between the two countries ran aground over the territorial issue.
Funds are not coming in, and the redevelopment plan in front of the station has hit a snag.
en.notes: 暗礁 is a reef or rock hidden just below the water surface that is dangerous for ships. It is most often encountered in the idiom 暗礁に乗り上げる, literally "to run onto a reef", figuratively "to come to a standstill, to get stuck", for instance in negotiations or projects. The running aground of a ship itself is called 座礁. Literary, very familiar from the news.

examples[].german: Amanohashidate is a scenic spot formed by a sandbar.
A sandbar closed off the bay, and a lake was formed.
I walked along the narrow path on the sandbar, beside a row of pine trees.
en.notes: 砂州 is a sandbar piled up by currents, which often grows from the coast into a bay and almost closes it off (spit); the most famous example is 天橋立. Read さす, not さしゅう; also written 砂洲. A sand island in the middle of a river is called 中州. A technical term of geography, but also found in travel guides.

examples[].german: Alluvial plains are formed by the depositional action of rivers.
Many of Japan's big cities are built on alluvial plains.
The ground of alluvial plains is soft, so liquefaction easily occurs during earthquakes.
en.notes: 沖積平野 is a young alluvial plain that rivers have built up in the most recent geological history (Holocene, formerly 沖積世). It includes 扇状地, 氾濫原 and 三角州. Its counterpart is the older, higher-lying 洪積台地. Since many of Japan's cities lie on it, it is vulnerable to flooding and soil liquefaction because of its soft ground. A technical term.

examples[].german: The Musashino Plateau is a typical example of a diluvial upland.
Diluvial uplands have firm ground, so they are relatively resistant to earthquakes.
Water was hard to obtain on diluvial uplands, so in the past there were mostly fields and coppice woodland.
en.notes: 洪積台地 is an upland made of deposits from the Pleistocene (formerly 洪積世) that lies somewhat higher than the surrounding 沖積平野. The ground is firm and well drained, but water used to be scarce there. A well-known example: 武蔵野台地. The term 洪積 is considered outdated in technical language (today 更新世, 段丘), but is still common in textbooks and place descriptions.

examples[].german: The Sanriku Coast is a typical example of a ria coast.
Because the bays of a ria coast are deep and intricate, tsunamis tend to become higher there.
In the calm bays of the ria coast, farming of oysters and wakame thrives.
en.notes: リアス式海岸 is a ria coast: river valleys have been drowned by the sea, creating a heavily indented, saw-toothed coast with deep bays. Well-known examples in Japan: 三陸海岸, 志摩半島, 若狭湾. The calm bays are suited to harbors and aquaculture, but amplify tsunamis. More recent textbooks also write リアス海岸.

examples[].german: The fjords of Norway were formed by glacial erosion.
During summer vacation, I took a cruise around the fjords.
Fjords were formed when seawater entered valleys carved by glaciers, whereas ria coasts formed when it entered valleys cut by rivers.
en.notes: フィヨルド is a fjord, a valley carved out by glaciers and later flooded by the sea, with steep walls. Known from Norway, New Zealand and Chile; there are none in Japan. In class it is often contrasted with the リアス式海岸, which arises from river valleys. A loanword from Norwegian, neutral.

examples[].german: The caldera of Mt. Aso boasts a size among the largest in the world.
Lake Toya is a caldera lake formed by a volcanic eruption.
There is a town inside the caldera, and many people live there.
en.notes: カルデラ is a technical word from Spanish or Portuguese ("cauldron") and refers to the large, usually round depression that forms when a volcano collapses in on itself after a gigantic eruption. It is much larger than an ordinary crater 火口; the surrounding ring wall is called 外輪山. If the depression fills with water, a カルデラ湖 forms, such as 洞爺湖 or 十和田湖. The word is written only in katakana.

examples[].german: The water of the crater lake is acidic from volcanic gases.
The climbers peered into the crater from the summit.
After the volcanic alert level was raised, entry to the area around the crater was restricted.
en.notes: 火口 is the opening of a volcano from which lava, gas and ash emerge, that is, the "crater"; synonymous but more technical is 噴火口. Typical combinations are 火口湖 "crater lake", 火口付近 and 火口周辺への立ち入り規制 in warning notices. A much larger collapse depression is called カルデラ. Beware of homophones: 河口 "river mouth" and 加工 "processing" are also read かこう; in the reading ひぐち, by contrast, 火口 means the point where a fire starts.

examples[].german: A lava plateau is a landform made of many layers of flowed-out lava piled on top of each other.
The Deccan Plateau in India is known as one of the world's leading lava plateaus.
In Iceland, a sparsely grassed lava plateau stretched on endlessly.
en.notes: 溶岩台地 is composed of 溶岩 "lava" and 台地 "plateau, tableland": a wide, flat upland that forms when fluid basalt lava flows out in large quantities and layers up one on top of another. It is a technical term of geography and geology. It is to be distinguished from 火山灰台地 such as the シラス台地 in Kyushu, which consists of ash instead of lava; 高原 is generally a "highland" with no statement about its origin.

examples[].german: A claim for state compensation was filed on the grounds of the administration's failure to act.
Leaving a child who should be protected unattended can be a crime of omission.
The distinction between acts and omissions is fundamental to criminal law.
en.notes: 不作為 is a legal technical term for failing to perform a required action - the counterpart of 作為 "active doing". Typical: 行政の不作為 "inaction of the authorities", 不作為犯 "crime of omission", 不作為による〜. In everyday life one says 何もしない or 放置する. Not to be confused with 無作為 "random" (無作為抽出 "random sampling").

examples[].german: A debris flow hit the settlement directly and caused enormous damage.
In heavy rain, people living along valleys should be on guard against debris flows.
Volcanic ash deposited by the eruption was washed away by rain and struck the village as a debris flow.
en.notes: 土石流 is a "debris flow": a water-saturated stream of earth, rubble and boulders that rushes through valleys at high speed during heavy rain or after volcanic eruptions. An older, popular term is 山津波. Unlike 地滑り, where a slope slides as a whole, in a 土石流 the material flows like a flood. Typical: 土石流が発生する, 土石流に巻き込まれる／のみ込まれる, 土石流に警戒する.

examples[].german: The erosive action of rivers forms V-shaped valleys.
The flow of a river has three actions: erosion, transportation and deposition.
The coastal cliff is gradually receding due to the erosive action of waves.
en.notes: 侵食作用 is the textbook term for the "eroding action" of flowing water, waves, wind or ice; 作用 means "action, process" here. In geography class it almost always appears in the triad 侵食作用・運搬作用・堆積作用 "erosion, transportation, deposition". Besides 侵食, the spelling 浸食 is also common. 侵食 alone can also mean "encroachment, intrusion" figuratively (市場を侵食する), whereas 侵食作用 refers only to the natural process.

examples[].german: Deposition forms a vast plain at the river mouth.
An alluvial fan is a landform created by the depositional action of a river emerging from the mountains.
Upstream of the dam, deposition advances and the storage capacity decreases.
en.notes: 堆積作用 is the "deposition" of sand, gravel and mud when water, wind or ice lose strength; it is the counterpart of 侵食作用 and follows transportation, 運搬作用. This process creates forms such as 扇状地 "alluvial fan" and 三角州 "delta". As a verb one says, intransitively, 土砂が堆積する; the deposited material is called 堆積物, and the rock formed from it 堆積岩. A technical expression from geography and geology.

examples[].german: In desert regions, landform change due to wind erosion is remarkable.
The rock shaped by wind erosion has taken on a mushroom-like form.
Windbreak forests were planted so that the topsoil of fields would not be lost to wind erosion.
en.notes: 風食 (older spelling 風蝕) is "wind erosion": wind carries away loose soil and grinds rock with the sand it carries, creating, for example, mushroom-shaped rocks. It forms a series with 水食 and 氷食. Not to be confused with 風化 "weathering", the disintegration of rock in place (figuratively also the "fading" of memories). According to dictionaries it is also possible as a する-verb, but in practice it is almost only a noun: 風食による, 風食を受ける.

examples[].german: A U-shaped valley was formed by glacial erosion.
A fjord is a landform where seawater has entered a valley formed by glacial erosion.
Traces of past glacial erosion remain in the Japanese Alps as well.
en.notes: 氷食 (also 氷蝕) is "glacial erosion", that is, the grinding and scooping out of the ground by a flowing glacier 氷河. Typical forms created by 氷食 are U字谷 "U-shaped valley", 圏谷 or カール "cirque", fjords フィヨルド and pointed peaks ホルン "horns". It belongs to the series 風食・水食・氷食 and is a purely technical term; it mostly appears with によって／による or as 氷食地形 "glacially shaped landscape".

examples[].german: Moraines are deposits transported by glaciers.
After the glacier retreated, a moraine containing large boulders was left behind.
This lake was formed when a moraine dammed a river.
en.notes: モレーン is the loanword for "moraine", the debris of rock fragments, gravel and sand that a glacier carries along and deposits. The Japanese technical word for it is 堆石 or 氷堆石 – not to be confused with the identically sounding 堆積 "deposition". A distinction is made, for example, between lateral moraines (側堆石) and terminal moraines (末端モレーン). Moraines can block valleys, so that a glacial lake 氷河湖 forms behind them.

examples[].german: The water of glacial lakes often looks bluish-white and cloudy because of fine rock powder.
Due to warming, there is a danger that a glacial lake will burst and the villages downstream will be hit by flooding.
North America's Great Lakes are also glacial lakes formed by the action of glaciers.
en.notes: 氷河湖 is a "glacial lake": a lake created by the work of a glacier – for example in a scooped-out basin, in a cirque or behind a blocking moraine. The suffix 湖 is read こ here, as in カルデラ湖 or 火口湖. Because of fine rock powder, the water is often milky turquoise. In the news the word often appears in connection with climate change: 氷河湖の決壊 "outburst of a glacial lake" threatens villages in the Himalayas.

examples[].german: A landslide formed a barrier lake.
Lake Chuzenji is a barrier lake formed when lava from Mt. Nantai dammed a river.
Because the barrier lake created by the earthquake risked bursting, evacuation orders were issued to residents.
en.notes: 堰止湖 (also written せき止め湖 or 堰き止め湖) comes from 堰き止める "to dam up" and refers to a naturally dammed lake: a landslide, lava flow or moraine blocks a river valley, and water collects behind it. Well-known examples are 中禅寺湖 and the Fuji Five Lakes. When such a lake forms freshly after an earthquake or heavy rain, the news often speaks of 天然ダム or 土砂ダム and warns of a dam break 決壊.

examples[].german: At a mid-ocean ridge, magma erupts and new crust is formed.
A long ridge runs north to south through the middle of the Atlantic.
Iceland is a rare place where an oceanic ridge appears above sea level.
en.notes: 海嶺 is generally an elongated "oceanic ridge", an undersea mountain range. In plate tectonics it mostly means the 中央海嶺 "mid-ocean ridge", where plates drift apart, magma rises and new oceanic crust forms. Its counterpart is the 海溝 "ocean trench", where a plate dives down again; individual undersea mountains are called 海山. The word belongs to the technical language of geology and oceanography.

examples[].german: Pursuing charges was passed over for lack of sufficient evidence.
The police plan to build a fraud case against the company president.
The driver was not arrested; the case against him was built while he remained at liberty.
en.notes: 立件 means that the police or prosecution prepare a case as a criminal matter, i.e. gather enough evidence to formally initiate proceedings. Typical: 〜を…の疑いで立件する, 立件を見送る "to refrain from pursuing charges". Transitive する-verb, news language. 逮捕 is arrest, 起訴 is the filing of charges; 立件 is possible even without an arrest (在宅のまま立件).

examples[].german: The Fossa Magna is a large rift zone that crosses the Japanese archipelago.
The East African Rift is also known as the cradle of humankind.
When a strip of land between faults sinks, a graben is formed.
en.notes: 地溝 is a "graben" or rift: an elongated strip of land that has sunk between two parallel faults 断層. The opposite, a block raised between faults, is called 地塁 "horst". The word is most often encountered in 地溝帯 "rift zone", for example 東アフリカ大地溝帯 "East African Rift"; lakes formed in a rift are called 地溝湖. The フォッサマグナ in central Japan is often described as a large rift.

examples[].german: A canal was built across the Isthmus of Panama.
Whereas a strait is a waterway connecting two seas, an isthmus is a narrow strip of land connecting two landmasses.
In ancient Greece, ships were transported overland across the Isthmus of Corinth.
en.notes: 地峡 is an "isthmus", a narrow strip of land that connects two larger landmasses and is bordered by sea on both sides. It is easily confused with 海峡 "strait" – exactly the reverse, a narrow waterway between two landmasses. 地峡 mostly stands after a proper name: パナマ地峡, スエズ地峡, コリントス地峡. Because a canal can be dug through an isthmus, it often appears together with 運河.

examples[].german: The Amami Islands belong to Kagoshima Prefecture and have a distinctive culture.
Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic state.
From the ship, we saw an archipelago made up of islands of all sizes.
en.notes: 群島 is an "island group", a cluster of islands lying close together. In proper names it competes with 諸島, the most common word for a group of islands (小笠原諸島), and 列島, which refers more to a long chain of islands (日本列島, 千島列島). A fixed Japanese name with 群島 is 奄美群島. In international law, an "archipelagic state" is called 群島国家, e.g. Indonesia or the Philippines.

examples[].german: The Pacific Ring of Fire is an area of active earthquake and volcanic activity.
The Trans-Pacific Partnership Agreement is abbreviated as TPP.
Countries around the Pacific Rim gathered and discussed trade.
en.notes: 環太平洋 means "around the Pacific" (環 "ring, to surround") and corresponds to the English "Pacific Rim". It almost never stands alone, but as a modifier: 環太平洋地域 "Pacific Rim region", 環太平洋の国々. The "Pacific Ring of Fire" is only the compound 環太平洋火山帯 (or 環太平洋造山帯 for the mountain-building belt). Known from economic policy is 環太平洋パートナーシップ協定, the TPP free trade agreement.

examples[].german: Large earthquakes tend to occur in subduction zones.
A subduction zone of plates extends off Japan's Pacific side.
Volcanoes line up in a row along the subduction zone.
en.notes: 沈み込み帯 is the "subduction zone": the area where an oceanic plate dives beneath another plate. The word is formed from 沈み込む "to sink down, dive" and 帯 "zone, belt"; less often one also says サブダクション帯. At the surface, an ocean trench 海溝 marks the zone, and volcanoes line up above it. Japan lies above several such zones, which is why large earthquakes of the 海溝型地震 type occur there.

examples[].german: Anticlinal structures are suitable for trapping oil.
The part where rock layers are bent upward like a mountain is called an anticline.
In the cross-section of the cliff, anticlines and synclines appeared alternately.
en.notes: 背斜 is a geological "anticline": a fold 褶曲 in which the rock layers are arched upward like a hump. Its counterpart, the downward-bent trough, is called 向斜 "syncline". It often appears in 背斜構造 "anticlinal structure" or 背斜軸 "anticlinal axis"; oil and natural gas often collect at the crest of such anticlines. Beware of homophones: 歯医者 "dentist" and 敗者 "loser" are also read はいしゃ.

examples[].german: Groundwater tends to collect at the bottom of a syncline.
The part of a stratum that bends downward like a valley is called a syncline.
A large synclinal structure is sometimes hidden beneath a basin.
en.notes: 向斜 is a geological "trough" (syncline): a fold in which the rock layers sag downward like a bowl. Its counterpart is the anticline 背斜; together they form a fold structure 褶曲. Common combinations are 向斜構造 and 向斜軸. Because water flows together in troughs, they often serve as groundwater reservoirs. Homophones such as 後者 "the latter" and 校舎 "school building" are also read こうしゃ.

examples[].german: The foundations of a skyscraper are built on hard bedrock.
The prime minister stressed that he would break through the "bedrock regulations".
I went to a bedrock bath on the weekend and had a really good sweat.
en.notes: 岩盤 is the solid "bedrock" beneath soil and rubble, on which, for example, skyscrapers, bridges or nuclear power plants are founded: 岩盤の上に建てる, 固い岩盤. Figuratively, 岩盤 is common in politics: 岩盤規制 refers to "entrenched regulations that are hardly ever broken open", and 岩盤支持層 to an "unshakable core base of voters". In everyday life it is also known from 岩盤浴, a wellness bath on heated stone slabs.

examples[].german: The Kanto loam layer is an aeolian deposit of volcanic origin.
China's Loess Plateau consists of thick aeolian deposits of sand and dust carried by the wind.
Aeolian deposits often have more uniform grain sizes than strata formed in water.
en.notes: 風成層 is an "aeolian deposit", that is, a layer of rock or soil formed from material carried by the wind: 風成 "formed by wind" + 層 "layer". It includes loess レス, dune sand and wind-blown volcanic ash such as the 関東ローム層. Its counterpart is the water-laid strata 水成層. A rare technical term from geology and soil science.

examples[].german: Fresh water and seawater mix near the river mouth.
The closer you get to the river mouth, the wider the river becomes.
Every winter, many migratory birds gather on the tidal flats at the river mouth.
en.notes: 河口 is the "river mouth", the place where a river flows into the sea or a lake. Common combinations are 河口付近, 河口域 and 河口堰 "estuary barrage". Careful: 火口 "crater" sounds exactly the same, and Lake Kawaguchi near Mount Fuji, 河口湖, is read not かこうこ but かわぐちこ. In everyday speech people often say more simply 川の河口 or 川が海に注ぐところ.

examples[].german: The prosecution decided not to indict.
The man was not indicted because of insufficient evidence.
After a settlement was reached with the victim, the case was dropped.
en.notes: 不起訴 is the prosecution's decision not to bring charges. Typical: 不起訴処分にする, 不起訴となる/になる. Reasons include 嫌疑不十分 "insufficient suspicion" and 起訴猶予 "forgoing indictment despite suspicion". The opposite is 起訴 "indictment". Against a 不起訴, one can apply for review to the 検察審査会. News language.

examples[].german: The brackish zone has a unique ecosystem.
Basket clams are mostly found in brackish water, where river water and seawater mix.
Eels travel upriver through the brackish zone.
en.notes: 汽水域 is the "brackish zone" where fresh water 淡水 and seawater 海水 mix, typically in river mouths and lagoons. 汽水 means "brackish water" and 域 "area, zone"; a brackish lake is a 汽水湖 such as 宍道湖 or 浜名湖. The word appears especially in ecology and fisheries, because typical species such as shijimi clams, eels and mullet live there. Compared with 河口, 汽水域 emphasizes the salinity rather than the place.

examples[].german: The Seto Inland Sea is a calm body of water dotted with many islands.
