The Ondo Strait is a narrow strait said to have been cut open by Taira no Kiyomori.
The tide flows fast through the narrow strait between the islands.
en.notes: 瀬戸 denotes a narrow "strait", often with strong currents, between two coasts or islands. As a general word people now usually say 海峡; 瀬戸 survives mainly in names, such as 瀬戸内海 "Seto Inland Sea" or 音戸の瀬戸. Derived words are 瀬戸際 "the critical moment, the brink" (瀬戸際に立たされる) and 瀬戸物 "porcelain, earthenware", named after the pottery town 瀬戸 in Aichi.

examples[].german: Sea cliffs are formed by the erosion of waves.
At the tip of the peninsula, sea cliffs more than a hundred meters high continue on.
Tours viewing the sea cliffs from a sightseeing boat are popular.
en.notes: 海食崖 is a steep coast washed out by the surf, that is, a cliff by the sea; literally "sea" + "eat away" + "cliff". The older spelling 海蝕崖 is also found, since 食 here stands for 蝕 "to eat away" (cf. 侵食/侵蝕). In everyday speech people simply say 崖 or 断崖; 海食崖 belongs to geology, geography class and travel guides, often together with 海食洞 "sea cave".

examples[].german: A sea cave was formed by wave erosion.
Italy's "Blue Grotto" is a typical example of a sea cave.
You can walk into the depths of the sea cave only at low tide.
en.notes: 海食洞 (also 海蝕洞) is a "sea cave": a cave in a cliff coast that waves have carved out by erosion 海食. It belongs to a series of technical terms for coastal landforms such as 海食崖 "sea cliff" and 海食台 "wave-cut platform". In everyday speech people simply say 洞窟 or 洞くつ; a famous example is the "Blue Grotto" on Capri, and in Japan, for instance, the caves of 江の島岩屋.

examples[].german: A sand spit is formed by sand deposited by coastal currents.
The Notsuke Peninsula in Hokkaido is known as one of the largest sand spits in Japan.
When a sand spit extends further and closes off a bay, it becomes a sandbar.
en.notes: 砂嘴 is a "sand spit": a narrow tongue of sand that a coastal current builds out into the sea from the shore; 嘴 means "beak", after its curved shape. If the spit keeps growing until it closes off a bay or reaches an island, it is called a 砂州 "sandbar", and a 潟湖 can form behind it. Well-known examples are the 野付半島 in Hokkaido and the peninsula of 三保の松原.

examples[].german: A lagoon has formed on the inner side of the sandbar.
Lake Saroma in Hokkaido is Japan's largest lagoon.
Many lagoons gradually become shallower from the sediment that flows in from rivers.
en.notes: 潟湖 is a "lagoon": a shallow body of water separated from the open sea by a sandbar 砂州 or a sand spit 砂嘴, often with brackish water. 潟 (かた／がた) on its own means tidal flat or lagoon and appears in names like 新潟 or 八郎潟. In everyday speech and travel guides the loanword ラグーン is more common; 潟湖 is the technical term. Japan's largest lagoon is the サロマ湖 in Hokkaido.

examples[].german: The reclaimed land of the Ariake Sea is used as vast farmland.
Hachirogata was drained, and rice is now grown on the broad reclaimed land.
In the Netherlands, a considerable part of the country is polder.
en.notes: 干拓地 is a "polder": land gained by diking a tidal flat, lagoon or shallow lake and pumping out the water (干拓する "to drain, reclaim"). It should be distinguished from 埋立地, new land created by filling in the sea with earth or refuse. Well-known Japanese examples are the former lake 八郎潟 in Akita and the polders on the 有明海; worldwide one thinks of the Netherlands. 干拓地 is mostly used as farmland, especially for rice.

examples[].german: A new city was built on the reclaimed land in Tokyo Bay.
Non-burnable waste is disposed of as landfill at the disposal site.
A residents' movement arose against the reclamation of the tidal flats.
en.notes: 埋立 "land reclamation, landfill" is the noun form of the transitive verb 埋め立てる (to fill in the sea, a swamp or pits with earth). Written out in full it is usually 埋め立て; the short form 埋立 without め is found mainly in compounds and official language: 埋立地 "reclaimed land", 埋立工事, 埋立処分 "landfill disposal". Besides land reclamation in the sea, it thus also means burying waste in landfills. Distinguish it from 干拓, land reclamation by diking and draining.

examples[].german: The indented coastline forms a natural harbor.
Nagasaki developed as a natural harbor with a deeply recessed bay.
Even without a breakwater, this natural harbor protects ships during typhoons.
en.notes: 天然港 is a "natural harbor", that is, a harbor that bays, peninsulas or offshore islands protect from wind and waves by nature, in contrast to the artificially built 人工港. In ordinary usage the phrase 天然の良港 "a good natural harbor" is heard even more often. Many such harbors lie on rugged ria coasts リアス海岸; Nagasaki and Sydney are classic examples.

examples[].german: If you are dissatisfied with a decision not to indict, you can file a petition with the Prosecution Review Commission.
The Prosecution Review Commission resolved that an indictment was warranted.
The members of the Prosecution Review Commission are citizens chosen by lot.
en.notes: 検察審査会 is a body of eleven citizens chosen by lot that examines, on request, whether the prosecution's decision not to indict (不起訴) was appropriate. Possible resolutions: 起訴相当 "indictment warranted", 不起訴不当 "non-indictment inappropriate", 不起訴相当. After a second 起訴相当, a 強制起訴 "compulsory indictment" follows. Typical: 検察審査会に申し立てる, 検察審査会が議決する.

examples[].german: The Tone River system is the main water source of the Kanto region.
Japan's large rivers are designated as Class A river systems managed by the state.
The main stream and its tributaries together are called one river system.
en.notes: 水系 is the "river system": a main stream 本流 with all its tributaries 支流, lakes and the associated catchment area. It typically follows a river name: 利根川水系, 淀川水系. In administrative language Japan divides its rivers into 一級水系 (managed by the state) and 二級水系 (managed by the prefectures). In addition, in medicine 水系 means "via water": 水系感染 "infection via drinking water".

examples[].german: Houses in the lowlands were flooded by the torrential rain.
The heavy rain caused above-floor flooding in many shops in the shopping street in front of the station.
A hole opened in the hull, and the ship began to take on water.
en.notes: 浸水 means that water enters houses, land or a ship; as an intransitive する-verb: 家が浸水する, 船が浸水する. In storm news, 床上浸水 "water above the floor" and 床下浸水 "water only under the floor" are fixed terms, as are 浸水被害 and 浸水想定区域 on hazard maps. Distinguish 冠水 (roads or fields are under water), 洪水 "flood" as an event and 氾濫 "overflowing of a river".

examples[].german: A retarding basin is a flood-control facility that prevents river flooding.
The Watarase Retarding Basin is known as the largest in Japan.
During the typhoon, river water flowed into the retarding basin, which is normally used as a park.
en.notes: 遊水地 (also 遊水池) is a "retarding basin": an area next to a river that is deliberately flooded during high water to store water temporarily and relieve the lower reaches. Outside flood periods it is often used as fields, a park, a sports ground or a wetland. The largest in Japan is the 渡良瀬遊水地. Related are 調整池 "detention pond" and ダム; the word belongs to the word field 治水 "river control, flood protection".

examples[].german: The development of cartography made accurate understanding of terrain possible.
I studied cartography at university and now work at a map-making company.
In cartography, a major challenge is how to depict the round Earth on a flat surface.
en.notes: 地図学 is "cartography" as a science: the study of how to measure the Earth's surface, represent it and translate it into maps, for example with various map projections 図法. For the practical activity people rather say 地図作成 or 地図作り. Closely related are 測量 "surveying" and, today, GIS 地理情報システム. The word is academic and appears mainly in university and specialist texts.

examples[].german: The narrower the spacing of the contour lines, the steeper the slope.
Before the climb, I checked the contour lines on the map to see how rugged the route was.
On the topographic map, a contour line is drawn every 10 meters.
en.notes: 等高線 is the "contour line" on a map, connecting points of equal elevation. People speak of 等高線を読む "reading contour lines" and 等高線の間隔 "contour spacing": the denser they are, the steeper the terrain. Formed on the same pattern 等〜線 "line of equal ..." are 等圧線 "isobar" on weather maps and 等温線 "isotherm". On the official 1:25,000 maps 地形図, they are spaced 10 meters apart.

examples[].german: Japan Standard Time is based on the meridian at 135 degrees east longitude.
The meridian passing through the Greenwich Observatory is called the prime meridian.
The clock tower of the Akashi Municipal Planetarium stands exactly on the meridian.
en.notes: 子午線 is the "meridian", a north-south line across the poles. The name comes from the old way of indicating direction with zodiac signs: 子 (rat) stands for north, 午 (horse) for south. In school geography and everyday speech the synonymous 経線 "line of longitude" is more common; 子午線 sounds more elevated and is usual in astronomy and timekeeping, for example 本初子午線 "prime meridian". The city of Akashi calls itself the "city of the meridian" because the meridian for Japan Standard Time runs through it.

examples[].german: In the Arctic, the midnight sun can be observed in summer.
The ice of the Arctic is melting rapidly due to global warming.
Rovaniemi in Finland is known as the town at the gateway to the Arctic.
en.notes: 北極圏 denotes both the "Arctic Circle" as a line (about 66.5° N) and, more often, the whole region north of it, that is, the "Arctic". 圏 means "sphere, realm", as in 首都圏 or 大気圏. Typical are 北極圏に入る, 北極圏の国々 and topics like 白夜, polar lights オーロラ and melting ice. Its counterpart is 南極圏; 北極 alone is the North Pole.

examples[].german: The westerlies have a great influence on Japan's weather.
Carried by the westerlies, yellow dust flies in from the Chinese mainland.
Because the westerlies meandered greatly, this summer saw record-breaking heat.
en.notes: 偏西風 are the "westerlies" of the middle latitudes, which blow steadily from west to east; that is why weather systems in Japan mostly approach from the west. Their strongest core at high altitude is the jet stream ジェット気流. In the news you often read 偏西風の蛇行 "meandering of the westerlies" as a cause of heat waves or cold snaps, and 偏西風に乗って when yellow dust 黄砂 or fine particulates are carried over from China.

examples[].german: Trade winds are constant winds that blow in the low latitudes near the equator.
In the age of sailing ships, the trade winds were an important source of power for ships crossing the Atlantic.
When the trade winds weaken, El Nino events are more likely to occur.
en.notes: 貿易風 is the "trade wind": a steady wind that blows from the subtropical high-pressure belts toward the equator, from the northeast in the Northern Hemisphere (北東貿易風) and from the southeast in the Southern Hemisphere (南東貿易風). The name is a calque of English "trade wind", because merchant sailing ships used it. Together with 偏西風, it belongs to the 恒常風 "permanent winds"; when it weakens, an El Nino event エルニーニョ現象 can arise.

examples[].german: The Asian monsoon has a great influence on agriculture.
In winter, the northwest monsoon brings heavy snow to the Sea of Japan side.
Because of the monsoon, the rainy season arrives in India in summer.
en.notes: 季節風 is a wind that changes direction with the season, that is, the "monsoon" (loanword モンスーン). For Japan, the winter monsoon is central: the 北西の季節風 from Siberia brings heavy snowfall to the Sea of Japan side and dry, clear weather to the Pacific side; in summer it blows humid from the southeast. Typical combinations are 季節風が吹く／強まる and 冬の季節風. In South and Southeast Asia it determines the rainy and dry seasons.

examples[].german: When a cold air mass and a warm air mass collide, a front forms.
The rainy-season front forms between the Okhotsk air mass and the Ogasawara air mass.
In winter, Japan is covered by a cold, dry Siberian air mass.
en.notes: 気団 is an "air mass": a large body of air with uniform temperature and humidity, named after its region of origin. For Japan's weather, school teaches mainly the シベリア気団 (winter, cold and dry), the 小笠原気団 (summer, hot and humid) and the オホーツク海気団. Where two air masses meet, a front 前線 forms, e.g. the rainy-season front 梅雨前線. The word is technical (meteorology).

examples[].german: When the Pacific high gains strength, it gets extremely hot.
Tomorrow, a high-pressure system will cover the country, and it will probably be sunny nationwide.
In spring, migratory highs and lows come alternately.
en.notes: 高気圧 is a "high-pressure area" that usually brings fine, dry weather. The most important phrase in the weather report is 高気圧に覆われる "to be under the influence of high pressure"; also 高気圧が張り出す "to extend" and 勢力を強める. Typical names are 太平洋高気圧 for the hot summer and 移動性高気圧 "migratory highs" in spring and autumn. Its counterpart is 低気圧.

examples[].german: A well-developed low-pressure system brought a rainstorm.
The typhoon moved north and changed into an extratropical cyclone.
Whenever a low approaches, I always get a headache.
en.notes: 低気圧 is a "low-pressure area" that brings clouds, rain and wind. Common are 低気圧が発達する "to intensify", 爆弾低気圧 "bomb cyclone" and 温帯低気圧 "extratropical cyclone", into which a typhoon turns on its way north. In everyday speech you often hear 低気圧で頭が痛い, because many people are sensitive to the weather. Colloquially and jokingly, 低気圧 also means "bad mood": 今日は部長が低気圧だ.

examples[].german: A winter-type pressure pattern brings heavy snow to the Sea of Japan side.
In summer, the pressure pattern is high in the south and low in the north, and muggy days continue.
If you look at the weather map, you can immediately tell the day's pressure pattern.
en.notes: 気圧配置 is the "air pressure distribution" or "weather pattern" as seen on the weather map 天気図. The best-known formula is 西高東低の冬型の気圧配置 (the winter-type pattern with high pressure in the west and low in the east), which brings Japan cold and, on the Sea of Japan side, snow; in summer, by contrast, 南高北低 prevails. In the weather report you often hear 冬型の気圧配置が強まる／緩む. A technical word, but generally known through weather forecasts.

examples[].german: This year's precipitation far exceeded the normal level.
Yakushima is one of the islands with the highest precipitation in Japan.
Torrential rain fell, with precipitation of over 100 millimeters in one hour.
en.notes: 降水量 is the "amount of precipitation", that is, rain, snow and hail together, given in millimeters (ミリ). Typical are 年間降水量, 降水量が多い／少ない and 例年を上回る／下回る. Do not confuse it with 降水確率 "probability of precipitation" from the weather report. In everyday speech, for rain people also simply say 雨量; 降水量 is the official and scientific term.

examples[].german: In the arid zone, annual precipitation is extremely low.
In the Koppen climate classification, the arid zone is divided into desert climate and steppe climate.
People in the arid zone have long practiced farming around oases.
en.notes: 乾燥帯 is the "arid zone" in the Koppen climate classification (ケッペンの気候区分), alongside 熱帯, 温帯, 冷帯（亜寒帯） and 寒帯. Here more water evaporates than falls as precipitation; it is subdivided into 砂漠気候 "desert climate" and ステップ気候 "steppe climate". The more general word for "dry region" is 乾燥地帯; 乾燥帯 is mainly a textbook term.

examples[].german: Most of Japan belongs to the temperate zone.
The temperate zone is characterized by clearly distinct seasons.
In temperate-zone forests, many trees shed their leaves in autumn.
en.notes: 温帯 is the "temperate zone" between the tropics and the polar regions, with mild temperatures and distinct seasons. It appears in 温帯気候, 温帯林 and 温帯湿潤気候, the climate of most of Japan. Weather reports also speak of 温帯低気圧 when a typhoon turns into an "extratropical low". The sequence of climate zones is 熱帯・亜熱帯・温帯・冷帯（亜寒帯）・寒帯.

examples[].german: Okinawa is classified as having a subtropical climate.
Mangrove forests can be seen on the subtropical islands.
It is also said that the climate of Tokyo is approaching the subtropics due to the effects of global warming.
en.notes: 亜熱帯 is the "subtropics" between the tropics and the temperate zone. The prefix 亜 means "sub-, next to, almost" and is also found in 亜寒帯 "subarctic zone" or 亜種 "subspecies". Common combinations are 亜熱帯気候, 亜熱帯植物 and 亜熱帯高気圧. In Japan, mainly Okinawa and the Ogasawara Islands count as subtropical; with climate change one also reads that Tokyo is becoming "more subtropical" 亜熱帯化.

examples[].german: In the tropics it is hot and humid all year round.
Tonight is another tropical night, and I can hardly sleep.
When I was a child, I kept tropical fish at home.
en.notes: 熱帯 refers to the tropical climate zone around the equator. Very common in compounds: 熱帯雨林 "tropical rainforest", 熱帯魚 "tropical aquarium fish" and 熱帯夜 "tropical night" (a night when the temperature does not fall below 25 °C - a standard term in Japanese summer weather reports). Attributively it takes の: 熱帯の植物. The series of climate zones is 熱帯・亜熱帯・温帯・亜寒帯・寒帯; Okinawa counts as 亜熱帯 "subtropics".

examples[].german: The polar zone includes vast areas where almost no trees grow.
Animals of the polar zone protect themselves from the cold with thick fat and fur.
In geography class, we learned the differences between the tropical, temperate and polar zones.
en.notes: 寒帯 is the cold climate zone of the polar regions, a technical term from geography and climatology (寒帯気候, 寒帯に属する). It is the counterpart of 熱帯; between them lie 温帯 and 亜寒帯 (e.g. Hokkaidō). In everyday speech one more often says 北極・南極 or 寒い地方. Not to be confused with the identically read 艦隊 "fleet" and 歓待 "warm hospitality".

examples[].german: The jury system is a feature of the American justice system.
The jury returned a verdict of not guilty for the defendant.
I was selected as a juror in the United States and went to the courthouse for a week.
en.notes: 陪審 refers to the jury system or the jury, especially in Anglo-American law: 陪審員 "juror", 陪審団 "the jury (as a group)", 陪審制 "jury system", 陪審の評決 "jury verdict". Japan had a jury system from 1928 to 1943; today the 裁判員制度 applies instead, in which lay people judge together with professional judges. Mostly in connection with foreign trials.

examples[].german: Permafrost extends beneath the tundra zone.
During the short summer, small flowers bloom all over the tundra.
Reindeer live on the tundra, eating moss.
en.notes: ツンドラ "tundra" is a loanword (via Russian) and is always written in katakana. It means the treeless cold steppe with mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs above permafrost (永久凍土). Typical combinations: ツンドラ地帯, ツンドラ気候. To the south it is followed by the タイガ "coniferous forest". In internet slang there is also ツンドラ as a pun on ツンデレ for a person who is merely cold and snippy - that is slang and not meant here.

examples[].german: The Siberian taiga is the largest forest region in the world.
The taiga has many conifers such as fir and spruce.
Forest fires in the taiga are getting bigger every year.
en.notes: タイガ (from Russian) is the boreal coniferous forest belt south of the tundra, mainly in Siberia, Scandinavia and Canada. It is a geography term; synonymous are 針葉樹林帯 or 北方林. Typical: シベリアのタイガ, タイガ地帯. Watch the long vowel: タイガー with ー is the "tiger".

examples[].german: Nomads live on the Mongolian steppe.
In regions with a steppe climate, there is little rain and hardly any trees grow.
From the train window, I gazed at the endless steppe.
en.notes: ステップ in the sense of "steppe" (from Russian степь) is a treeless grassland in a dry climate, for example in Mongolia or Kazakhstan. Careful: in everyday speech the homonym ステップ from English "step" is much more common (step, dance step, 次のステップ "the next step"). For clarity people therefore often say ステップ気候 or simply 草原. Distinction: サバンナ is tropical grassland with scattered trees.

examples[].german: A wide variety of wild animals live in the African savanna.
In the savanna, animals move around in search of water during the dry season.
Someday I would like to see a pride of lions in the savanna.
en.notes: サバンナ "savanna" is tropical grassland with scattered trees and a clear alternation of rainy and dry seasons, mainly in Africa. In geography books the spelling サバナ (サバナ気候) is often used; in everyday speech and animal programs people say サバンナ. Typical: サバンナの動物, サバンナに暮らす. In contrast to the ステップ, the savanna lies in the tropics and is not entirely treeless.

en.meaning: foot of a mountain; mountain base
examples[].german: Cows are grazing on the pasture that spreads out at the foot of the mountain.
I bought a ticket at the base station of the ropeway.
There are many tourist spots such as lakes and caves at the foot of Mt. Fuji.
en.notes: 山麓 is the written-language word for the foot of a mountain and appears in descriptions of places, tourism texts and the news (山麓の町, 富士山麓). In speech people rather say 山のふもと. 裾野, by contrast, emphasizes the widely spreading area around the mountain. For cable cars, the valley station is called 山麓駅 and the summit station 山頂駅.

examples[].german: The view from the summit was magnificent.
We finally reached the summit and all ate our lunch boxes together.
The weather looked likely to turn, so we gave up on aiming for the summit.
en.notes: 山頂 is the neutral standard word for the summit of a mountain. Typical combinations: 山頂に着く／到達する, 山頂を目指す, 山頂からの眺め. In speech you often also hear 頂上, which can additionally be used figuratively (e.g. 頂上会談 "summit meeting"); 山頂, by contrast, stays literally with the mountain. 頂 (いただき) is literary. The opposite is 山麓.

examples[].german: Climbing routes that traverse along the ridge are popular.
When we came out onto the ridge, the wind suddenly got stronger.
This ridge trail has a nice view and is easy to walk even for beginners.
en.notes: 尾根 is the elongated mountain ridge that separates two valleys; its counterpart is 谷 or 沢. Typical in hiking: 尾根を歩く, 尾根に出る, 尾根伝いに "along the ridge", 尾根道 "ridge trail". 稜線 means almost the same but emphasizes the visible line of the crest against the sky and is stylistically more elevated.

en.meaning: valley bottom; bottom of a gorge
examples[].german: A clear stream flows along the valley floor.
A car broke through the guardrail and plunged to the bottom of the valley.
When I looked down at the valley floor from the suspension bridge, my legs froze.
en.notes: 谷底 (with voicing: たにぞこ) is the deepest part of a valley or gorge. Common in accident reports: 谷底に転落する "to fall into the gorge"; also 谷底を見下ろす. For a figurative low point (poverty, despair) people rather say どん底; in economics people speak of 景気の谷.

examples[].german: This canyon was formed by millions of years of erosion.
We crossed the suspension bridge spanning the gorge.
In autumn, this gorge is crowded with tourists who come to see the autumn leaves.
en.notes: 峡谷 is a deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls, usually carved out by a river ("gorge, canyon"). It sounds rather written and appears in nature and travel descriptions and in proper names (黒部峡谷); the Grand Canyon is called グランドキャニオン or 大峡谷. The very common 渓谷 rather emphasizes a mountain valley with a clear stream; the boundary is fluid. 谷 is the general umbrella term.

examples[].german: The silhouettes of climbers walking along the ridgeline are beautiful.
The evening sun sank behind the western ridgeline.
When we came out onto the ridgeline, we could see Mt. Fuji in the distance.
en.notes: 稜線 is the line that a mountain ridge draws against the sky ("ridgeline, crest line"). The word is elevated and popular in mountain reports and landscape descriptions: 稜線を歩く, 稜線に出る, 夕日が稜線に沈む. Compared with 尾根, the terrain ridge itself, 稜線 emphasizes the line or silhouette. The kanji 稜 means "edge".

examples[].german: Small claims are heard in summary court.
For speeding, the summary court issued a fine order.
I took the dispute with my landlord over the deposit to summary court.
en.notes: 簡裁 is the short form of 簡易裁判所, Japan's lowest court for civil cases with a small amount in dispute (up to 1.4 million yen) and minor criminal cases; 少額訴訟 "small claims" are also handled there. The short forms 簡裁, 地裁, 高裁, 最高裁 and 家裁 are common in news and headlines, while formal texts use the full form. Note: it is read the same as 関西. "Summary court" is only a rough equivalent.

examples[].german: We pitched our tent in the saddle between two peaks.
The trail descends to the saddle and then climbs steeply again.
Saddles tend to be wind corridors, and the weather changes easily there.
en.notes: 鞍部 is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks, literally "saddle part" (鞍 = saddle) - that is, "mountain saddle, col". It is a technical word from geography and mountaineering. Climbers often say コル; in place names 〜乗越 (のっこし) appears; a pass over which a path or road leads is called 峠.

en.meaning: foot of a mountain; skirts; (fig.) broad base
examples[].german: A vast forest spreads out at the foot of Mt. Fuji.
The automobile industry has a broad base and supports many small and medium-sized companies.
I want to widen the base of the sport by opening classes for children.
en.notes: 裾野 literally means "hem field" (裾 = hem of a garment): the gently sloping plain at the foot of a mountain, classically 富士山の裾野. In contrast to 山麓 or ふもと, it emphasizes the wide expanse. Figuratively it means the broad base of something: 裾野が広い "to have a broad base" (for example an industry with many suppliers), 競技の裾野を広げる "to promote a sport at the grassroots".

examples[].german: The riverbed rose, and the flow of water changed.
Sediment has accumulated after heavy rain, and the riverbed is rising.
The drought continued, the river dried up, and the riverbed was exposed.
en.notes: 河床 "riverbed" is a technical word from geography, geology and hydraulic engineering (河床が上がる／下がる, 河床の掘削). In everyday speech people say 川底. The kanji 川床 or 河床 read かわどこ／かわゆか, by contrast, denote the summer dining terraces over rivers, for example in Kyoto. Note the reading: 床 here is しょう.

examples[].german: A lot of gravel has accumulated in the upper reaches of the river.
There is a thick gravel layer beneath this area.
The slopes of the volcano are covered with gravel, and hardly any plants grow.
en.notes: 砂礫 denotes a mixture of sand (砂) and small stones (礫) - "gravel, shingle, rubble". It is a technical word from geology, construction and geography: 砂礫層 "gravel layer", 砂礫地, 砂礫が堆積する. In everyday speech people say 砂利 (e.g. for gravel paths) or 小石. The kanji 礫 otherwise occurs almost only in technical words such as 礫岩 "conglomerate".

en.meaning: offshore waters; offshore, out at sea
examples[].german: A huge undersea mountain range exists offshore.
An earthquake occurred off the coast of Chiba Prefecture.
The fishing boat dropped its nets at a point ten kilometers offshore.
en.notes: 沖合 (also 沖合い) denotes the sea at some distance from the coast, "offshore, at sea". It is typical of news and of earthquake and weather reports: 〜の沖合で地震が発生, 沖合10キロ. 沖 alone is synonymous and more everyday; 沖合 emphasizes the area. It does not mean the high seas: for that there are 外洋 or 遠洋 (遠洋漁業), while 沖合漁業 is fishing between the coast and the high seas.

examples[].german: The waves are calm in an inner bay, making it suitable for aquaculture.
In an inner bay, seawater is slow to be exchanged, so red tides occur easily.
This harbor is in an inner bay, so ships can take shelter there even during typhoons.
en.notes: 内湾 is a bay cut deep into the land and almost closed off from the outside, with calm water ("inner bay"). The word is technical (geography, fisheries, environmental reports: 内湾の水質, 内湾漁業). Its opposites are 外洋 and 外海. Do not confuse it with 内海 (うちうみ／ないかい) "inland sea" as in the 瀬戸内海.

examples[].german: In the open sea, the tidal current is extremely fast.
It is dangerous to go out into the open sea in a small yacht.
As soon as we left the bay, the ship began to roll heavily in the swell of the open sea.
en.notes: 外洋 is the open sea beyond bays and coastal waters, with high waves ("open sea, high seas"). Typical: 外洋に出る, 外洋航海, 外洋のうねり. Its opposites are 内湾 and 沿岸. 遠洋 emphasizes the great distance from home (遠洋漁業), and 公海 is the international-law term for "international waters".

examples[].german: Gas fields can exist on the seabed of the continental shelf.
Because sunlight reaches the continental shelf, there are many kinds of fish.
Most of the East China Sea is a shallow continental shelf.
en.notes: 陸棚 (with voicing: りくだな) is the shallow sea floor down to a depth of about 200 m along the continents, "shelf, continental shelf". It is the technical short form of 大陸棚, which is much more usual in everyday speech and in international law (大陸棚の境界). Seaward follow the 大陸斜面 and finally the 大洋底.

examples[].german: Wide, flat abyssal plains stretch across the ocean floor.
The rocks of the ocean floor are much younger than those of the continents.
The ocean floor is born at mid-ocean ridges and slowly moves.
en.notes: 大洋底 is composed of 大洋 "ocean" and 底 "bottom" and in oceanography denotes the floor of the great oceans beyond the continental margin, mostly at a depth of 3,000 to 6,000 m. The division seen from land: 陸棚 → 大陸斜面 → 大洋底 (with 深海平原, 海山 and 海溝). In everyday speech people simply say 海底 or 深海の底.

examples[].german: The area around a seamount makes a rich fishing ground.
A research vessel examined in detail a seamount at a depth of 2,000 meters.
Northwest of the Hawaiian Islands, a chain of seamounts formed by sunken old volcanoes extends.
en.notes: 海山 read かいざん is a mostly volcanic mountain on the sea floor that does not reach the surface ("seamount"); with a flattened summit it is called 平頂海山. It is an oceanography term. Careful: the same kanji read うみやま mean "sea and mountains" and, figuratively, "immeasurable", for example in 海山の恩 "a deep debt of gratitude".

examples[].german: The imperial rescript on the end of the war was conveyed to the people.
The dissolution of the House of Representatives is carried out by an imperial edict.
When the Speaker read out the dissolution edict, the lawmakers shouted "banzai".
en.notes: 詔書 is a formal document in which the emperor publicly announces a declaration of intent. Historically well known are 終戦の詔書 (1945) and the New Year's rescript of 1946, the so-called 人間宣言. To this day, the dissolution of the lower house is carried out by a 解散詔書, which the Speaker of the House reads out. Distinguish: 勅令 is an ordinance with the force of law, 勅語 an oral address by the emperor.

examples[].german: If you are dissatisfied with a district court ruling, you can appeal to the high court.
The Tokyo District Court dismissed the plaintiff's suit.
Residents filed suit in district court seeking a halt to the construction.
en.notes: 地裁 is the short form of 地方裁判所, the court of first instance for most civil and criminal cases; every prefecture has one, Hokkaido four. Typical: 東京地裁, 地裁に提訴する, 地裁判決. Against a judgment, one appeals (控訴) to the 高裁 and then to the 最高裁 (上告). "District court" is an approximation. News language.

examples[].german: Installing ecological corridors makes animal movement possible.
A tunnel was built under the road to serve as an ecological corridor so animals can pass.
When a forest is fragmented, animals become isolated without ecological corridors.
en.notes: 生態回廊 is a strip of habitat (forest, hedgerow, river bank, green bridge) that connects separated protected areas so that animals can migrate and populations can exchange - "ecological corridor, habitat network". A technical term from nature conservation; synonymous are エコロジカル・コリドー and, for forest corridors of the Japanese forestry agency, 緑の回廊. Typical: 生態回廊を整備する／設ける. 回廊 alone is a roofed colonnade, for example in temples.

examples[].german: The environmental remediation of contaminated land takes many years.
At the former mine site, environmental restoration through tree planting is under way.
The company paid a large sum in compensation for the cost of environmental remediation.
en.notes: 環境修復 denotes the restoration of polluted or destroyed environment such as soil, waters and ecosystems ("environmental remediation"). It is a technical word in official and environmental texts: 環境修復に取り組む, 環境修復事業. Related are 環境再生, 土壌浄化 "soil remediation" and バイオレメディエーション (remediation with microorganisms). 修復 alone means "repair, restoration" (文化財の修復, 関係修復).

examples[].german: Naturalized plants are crowding out the growth of native species.
This dandelion blooming by the roadside is actually a naturalized plant.
When we surveyed the plants on the riverbank, nearly half were naturalized plants.
en.notes: 帰化植物 is a foreign plant species introduced by humans that reproduces independently in the wild ("naturalized plant, neophyte"). 帰化 actually means "naturalization" and is also used for people (日本に帰化する). The opposite term is 在来種 or 在来植物. Well-known examples are セイヨウタンポポ and セイタカアワダチソウ. For problematic species as a whole people say 外来種, and legally 特定外来生物.

examples[].german: Deciduous broadleaf forests are beautiful for their changes through the four seasons.
One of the world's largest beech deciduous forests remains in the Shirakami Mountains.
In winter, the deciduous forest loses its leaves, and the sun shines in even to the interior of the woods.
en.notes: 落葉広葉樹林 is composed of 落葉 "shedding leaves", 広葉樹 "broadleaf tree" and 林 "forest": a deciduous broadleaf forest that is bare in winter. In Japan it characterizes the cooler climate of Tohoku and Hokkaido, typically with ブナ "beech" and ナラ "oak". Its opposites are 照葉樹林 (evergreen, southwestern Japan) and 針葉樹林 "coniferous forest". It is a technical word from biology and geography; in everyday speech people simply say 林 or 森.

examples[].german: Mixed coniferous-broadleaf forests can be seen in the middle altitude zone.
Many of Hokkaido's forests are mixed coniferous-broadleaf forests.
There is a plan to plant broadleaf trees in artificial cedar plantations and convert them into mixed forests.
en.notes: 針広混交林 is a short form made of 針葉樹 "conifer", 広葉樹 "broadleaf tree" and 混交林 "mixed forest": a forest in which conifers and broadleaf trees grow together. It is typical of Hokkaido and of middle altitudes in the transition between deciduous and coniferous forest. The word comes from forestry and vegetation science; in forestry policy there is often talk of converting uniform cedar plantations into 針広混交林.

examples[].german: In the alpine zone, alpine plants grow beyond the tree line.
Plants that withstand harsh conditions, such as Siberian dwarf pine, grow in the alpine zone.
Because of the effects of global warming, the rock ptarmigan living in the alpine zone are declining.
en.notes: 高山帯 is the altitude zone above the tree line (森林限界) with krummholz such as ハイマツ, meadows and 高山植物 "alpine plants"; in central Japan it begins at about 2,500 m. The Japanese sequence of altitude zones is 丘陵帯・山地帯・亜高山帯・高山帯. It is a technical word from biology and geography; in everyday speech people rather say 高い山 or 高山.

examples[].german: The tree line varies with latitude and altitude.
Once we passed the tree line, the view suddenly opened up.
Above the tree line, there are almost no places to take shelter from lightning.
en.notes: 森林限界 is the limit in altitude (or latitude) above which no closed forests grow - the "tree line". Typical: 森林限界を超える, 森林限界より上. In the Japanese Northern Alps it lies at about 2,500 m, and in Hokkaido considerably lower. It matters in mountain hiking because above it you are exposed to wind, sun and thunderstorms without protection.

examples[].german: The vertical distribution of plants is influenced by temperature and precipitation.
If you climb Mt. Fuji, you can clearly see the vertical distribution of plants.
In this survey, the vertical distribution of deep-sea fish was recorded by water depth.
en.notes: 垂直分布 is the distribution of plants or animals by height above sea level (or by water depth) - "vertical distribution, altitudinal zonation". Its counterpart is 水平分布, the distribution by latitude. It is a technical word and a classic topic in Japanese biology classes (丘陵帯・山地帯・亜高山帯・高山帯).

examples[].german: The horizontal distribution of vegetation depends on latitude and the position on the continent.
Because the Japanese archipelago is long from north to south, differences in the horizontal distribution of plants are clear.
A question on the test asked us to explain the difference between vertical and horizontal distribution.
en.notes: 水平分布 is the distribution of organisms or vegetation by latitude, that is, from south to north - "horizontal distribution". In Japan it extends roughly from the subtropical forest of Okinawa to the coniferous forest of Hokkaido; temperature and precipitation are the main determinants. It is the counterpart to 垂直分布 and appears almost only in specialist texts and in teaching.

examples[].german: The high court overturned the district court's ruling.
The defense appealed the ruling to the high court, dissatisfied with the judgment.
The Osaka High Court upheld the first-instance ruling.
en.notes: 高裁 is the short form of 高等裁判所, the appellate court above the 地裁 and 家裁. Japan has eight 高裁 (Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Hiroshima, Fukuoka, Sendai, Sapporo, Takamatsu) with branches. Typical: 高裁に控訴する, 高裁判決, 一審判決を覆す/支持する "to overturn/uphold the first-instance ruling". News and legal language.

examples[].german: This waterfall has a drop of more than a hundred meters.
To see Niagara Falls, I went to the observation deck on the Canadian side.
In the snowmelt season, the waterfall pours down with a thunderous roar.
en.notes: 瀑布 is the Sino-Japanese, elevated word for "waterfall"; in everyday speech people say 滝. It appears in written descriptions and in some names, above all ナイアガラ瀑布 "Niagara Falls". The height of the fall is called 落差. The kanji 瀑 is rare and otherwise occurs in, for example, 瀑声 "roar of a waterfall".

examples[].german: The rapids in the gorge are known as a famous spot for river rafting.
A child was swept away by the rapids but was rescued safely.
Japan's rivers are said to be short and full of rapids.
en.notes: 急流 denotes fast, violent flowing water or a rushing stretch of river ("rapids, swift current"). Typical: 急流に流される "to be swept away by the current", 急流を下る, 急流下り. Japanese rivers are considered especially 急流 because of their shortness and gradient. 激流 is even more violent; 早瀬 more poetically denotes a shallow, fast-flowing spot.

examples[].german: Ayu fish swim up the rapids of the river.
The sound of the rapids echoed through the valley.
It is easy to lose your footing in rapids, so be careful when crossing the river.
en.notes: 早瀬 is a shallow river spot with a fast current (瀬 = shallow place in a river). Its counterpart is 淵, the deep, calm spot; rivers alternate between 瀬 and 淵. The word is elevated to literary and appears in nature and angling texts; more soberly, people say 急流 or 流れの速い所. Related is 浅瀬 "shoal".

en.meaning: deep pool in a river; (fig.) abyss
examples[].german: Large char lurk in the deep pools of the river.
He wandered on the brink between life and death after the accident.
When his company went bankrupt, he was left standing on the brink of despair.
en.notes: 淵 is a deep, calm spot in a river or lake, often looking dark ("deep pool"); its counterpart is 瀬, the shallow, fast-flowing spot. Figuratively it stands for an abyss: 絶望の淵 "abyss of despair", 生死の淵をさまよう "to hover between life and death". Do not confuse it with the identically read 縁 "rim" (眼鏡の縁).

examples[].german: Rivers flowing through plains meander repeatedly.
A drunken man was arrested for driving in a zigzag.
Because the westerlies are meandering greatly, this summer is unusually hot.
en.notes: 蛇行 literally means "snake walk" and denotes a snake-like back and forth, for rivers "meandering". As an intransitive する-verb: 川が蛇行する, 道が蛇行している. In the news you often see 蛇行運転 "weaving in a zigzag" (e.g. when drunk) and in the weather report 偏西風の蛇行 "meandering of the jet stream". When a river loop is cut off, an 三日月湖 "oxbow lake" is formed.

examples[].german: Natural levees formed along the river, and settlements were established there.
Natural levees are a little higher than their surroundings, so they are often used as fields.
According to the hazard map, this district is on a natural levee and is unlikely to be flooded.
en.notes: 自然堤防 is a low ridge along a river that forms when the river deposits sand on its banks during floods - a "natural levee". Because it lies somewhat higher and drier than its surroundings, settlements, roads and fields were traditionally laid out on it; behind it lies the lower 後背湿地. Its counterpart is the artificially built 堤防 "embankment". A technical word from geography and disaster prevention.

examples[].german: A back marsh spreads out behind the natural levee.
Because back marshes drain poorly, they have long been used as rice paddies.
Residential areas built on filled-in back marshes are prone to flooding during heavy rain.
en.notes: 後背湿地 is the low-lying, clayey wet lowland behind the natural levee (自然堤防): floodwater that overflows the levee remains standing here. In Japan it was traditionally used as rice paddy (水田); today built-up 後背湿地 are considered especially at risk of flooding and liquefaction (液状化). It is a technical word from geography and disaster prevention.

examples[].german: In dry regions, agriculture that depends on rainwater is practiced.
These terraced rice fields have no irrigation canal and grow rice with rainwater alone.
In front of the temple gate stands a rainwater barrel prepared for fires.
en.notes: 天水 literally means "heaven water" and means rainwater, especially as a water source. It is a technical word mainly in agriculture: 天水農業 "rain-fed agriculture", 天水田 "rice field irrigated only by rain". In everyday speech people say 雨水 (あまみず). A 天水桶 is a rain barrel that used to stand in front of houses and temples as a firefighting water supply.

examples[].german: Hydrology is the science that clarifies the mechanism of the water cycle.
I majored in hydrology in graduate school and am researching flood prediction.
From a hydrological point of view, forests play the role of natural dams.
en.notes: 水文学 "hydrology" is the science of the water cycle: precipitation, runoff, evaporation and groundwater. Note the reading: 文 is read もん here (as in 天文学), not ぶん. Derived are 水文観測 and 水文データ. Not to be confused with 水理学 "hydraulics", the study of the flow of water in engineering.

examples[].german: The Supreme Court delivered a landmark ruling.
The Supreme Court ruled the provision of this law unconstitutional.
The judgment became final at the Supreme Court, and the long trial was over.
en.notes: 最高裁 is the short form of 最高裁判所, Japan's Supreme Court in Tokyo. It is the court of last resort and also reviews the constitutionality of laws (違憲審査). Typical: 最高裁に上告する, 最高裁判決, 最高裁が〜を違憲と判断する, 最高裁長官 "Chief Justice of the Supreme Court". At House of Representatives elections, citizens also vote on its judges in the 国民審査.

examples[].german: Flood control projects greatly reduced flood damage.
Takeda Shingen put effort into flood control and had embankments built.
Torrential rains are increasing because of global warming, and conventional flood control measures are no longer sufficient.
en.notes: 治水 literally means "to tame the water" (治 = to govern) and covers flood protection and river regulation. Typical: 治水事業, 治水対策, 治水ダム. Often in the pair 治水と利水 (flood control and water use) or as 治山治水 (protection of mountain forests and rivers). Historically 治水 was regarded as a core task of rulers - famous is the embankment 信玄堤 of Takeda Shingen.

examples[].german: Dams have both flood control and water utilization functions.
Because of the drought, water use such as agricultural water has begun to be affected.
Even at water-supply dams, the water level is lowered in advance before heavy rain.
en.notes: 利水 is the use of river or reservoir water for drinking water, irrigation, industry and power generation ("water utilization"). It usually appears in a pair with 治水: multipurpose dams serve 治水・利水・発電. Typical are 利水ダム and 利水者 "water user". Not to be confused with 水利 (water supply, 水利権 "water right") - the same kanji in reverse order.

examples[].german: This region is blessed with abundant mineral resources.
Japan is poor in mineral resources and relies on imports for almost all of its oil.
Conflict with neighboring countries deepened over mineral resources.
en.notes: 地下資源 are raw materials from the subsurface such as ores, coal, oil and natural gas ("mineral resources"). Typical: 地下資源に恵まれる／乏しい, 地下資源を開発する. Japan is considered a 地下資源に乏しい国. 鉱物資源 means only mineral raw materials; 天然資源 is broader and includes forests, water and fish stocks.

examples[].german: The discovery of a new ore deposit revitalized the regional economy.
A new hydrothermal deposit was found on the seabed near Okinawa.
This ore deposit has a high gold content and is still being mined today.
en.notes: 鉱床 is a natural accumulation of useful minerals in rock that is worth mining ("ore deposit"). A technical word from geology and mining: 鉱床を発見する, 金の鉱床, 海底熱水鉱床 "hydrothermal deposit on the seabed". Related: 鉱山 "mine", 鉱脈 "ore vein". Beware of homophones such as 交渉 "negotiation" or 高尚 "refined" - context decides.

examples[].german: You can observe the structure of the strata from the outcrop on the riverbank.
At this outcrop, you can clearly see the fault that moved in the earthquake.
Road construction exposed a new outcrop, and fossils were found.
en.notes: 露頭 is a place where rock or rock layers are exposed uncovered at the surface (露 = to be exposed) - geologically an "outcrop". Typical: 露頭を観察する, 地層の露頭, 断層の露頭. Not to be confused with the identically read 路頭 in the phrase 路頭に迷う "to be left standing in the street, to become destitute".

examples[].german: Columnar jointing is formed by the cooling of lava.
At the cliffs of Tojinbo, you can see magnificent columnar jointing.
If the bedrock has many joints, landslides are likely to occur.
en.notes: 節理 denotes in geology regular cracks in rock along which the blocks have not shifted against each other ("joint, jointing"); when there is displacement, it is called 断層 "fault". Well known are 柱状節理 "columnar jointing" (e.g. at 東尋坊 or in the 玄武洞) and 板状節理. The rare meaning "reason, logic" (JMdict Sense 2) is not meant here.

examples[].german: Gneiss is a rock formed by metamorphism under high temperature and high pressure.
Gneiss is characterized by its white and black striped pattern.
Gneiss, one of the oldest rocks in Japan, is distributed in the Hida region.
en.notes: 片麻岩 "gneiss" is a metamorphic rock with striped banding of light and dark minerals. It forms under high pressure and high temperature, often from granite (花崗岩) or sedimentary rock. Related technical words: 変成岩 "metamorphic rock", 片岩 "schist" (e.g. mica schist). In Japan the rock is rare; well known is the 飛騨片麻岩 in central Japan.

examples[].german: We analyze international relations from a geopolitical perspective.
Oil prices soared as geopolitical risks heightened.
I am taking a lecture on geopolitics at university.
en.notes: 地政学 "geopolitics" studies how location and geography shape the politics and power of states. The derived 地政学的 is very common: 地政学的リスク "geopolitical risks" (a standard expression in business news), 地政学的な観点, 地政学上の要衝 "strategically important place". The word is matter-of-fact and elevated and appears mainly in the media, business and scholarship.

examples[].german: This regional gazetteer records the nature and culture of the region in detail.
In high school geography class, we studied the regional geography of Africa.
In the Edo period, domains in various places compiled regional gazetteers.
en.notes: 地誌 is the description of an area by nature, climate, population, economy and history, that is, "regional geography" (as a subject 地誌学, in contrast to systematic geography 系統地理). The word has nothing to do with the physical landform (地形); "topography" is therefore correct only in the old sense of "description of places". Historically, the regional descriptions compiled by domains and offices are also called 地誌; typical are 地誌を編纂する and 〜の地誌. Technical and written language.

examples[].german: The flora of this island has undergone its own evolution.
To investigate the flora of the high mountains, we conduct a survey every summer.
The flora of this region has changed greatly due to the invasion of alien species.
en.notes: 植物相 is the totality of plant species in an area, that is, the "flora" in the sense of a species list: 〜の植物相を調べる, 植物相が豊か. To be distinguished from 植生 "vegetation", which describes the actual plant cover and its structure. The counterpart for animals is 動物相, and both together are called 生物相. For gut flora people do not say 植物相 but 腸内細菌叢 or 腸内フローラ. Technical language of biology.

examples[].german: Divorce mediation is conducted at the family court.
The juvenile who committed shoplifting was referred to the family court.
If you want to change your name, you need the permission of the family court.
en.notes: 家裁 is the short form of 家庭裁判所, responsible for family matters such as divorce, inheritance and guardianship, as well as juvenile criminal cases (少年事件). Many family disputes first go through mediation (調停) there. Typical: 家裁に申し立てる, 家裁送致 "referral to family court" for juveniles. Note: it is read the same as 火災 "fire". News language.

examples[].german: The fauna of Australia differs greatly from that of other continents.
The fauna of caves is characterized by many creatures with degenerated eyes.
The researchers reconstructed the fauna of that time from fossils.
en.notes: 動物相 denotes the totality of animal species of an area or era, that is, the "fauna": 〜の動物相, 動物相が豊富だ, 当時の動物相を復元する. The counterpart is 植物相 "flora"; together they are called 生物相. The word is technical language of biology and paleontology; in everyday speech people simply say そこに住む動物 or 生き物.

examples[].german: A climax forest is the most stable vegetation under the climatic conditions of the region.
As succession progresses, the forest eventually reaches climax.
In the warm regions of Japan, forests of shii and kashi (evergreen oaks) form the climax.
en.notes: 極相 is in ecology the stable end stage of a succession, the "climax": 極相に達する, 極相林 "climax forest", 極相種. In Japan, evergreen forests of シイ and カシ form the 極相 in warm areas, and beech forests (ブナ) in cooler ones. For the high point of a story people never say 極相, but クライマックス or 山場. A purely technical term.

examples[].german: Primary succession on lava plateaus proceeds very slowly.
Primary succession begins when lichens and mosses settle on the rock.
Primary succession has also been observed on land left behind by a retreating glacier.
en.notes: 一次遷移 is primary succession: plants colonize a substrate without soil and without a seed bank, such as fresh lava or rock exposed by a glacier. It usually begins with lichens (地衣類) and mosses and takes very long. The counterpart is 二次遷移 on areas where soil has remained. 遷移 alone means "succession" in ecology; typical verbs are 一次遷移が進む／始まる／起こる. School biology and technical language.

examples[].german: Secondary succession in logged forests is relatively fast.
On land burned by a wildfire, secondary succession begins right away because the soil remains.
Fields that are no longer cultivated change from grassland to woodland through secondary succession.
en.notes: 二次遷移 is secondary succession: after a forest fire, clear-cutting or on abandoned fields, soil, seeds and roots remain, so recolonization proceeds much faster than in 一次遷移. Typical sequence: grasses, then shrubs, sun-loving trees (陽樹) and finally shade-tolerant trees (陰樹). Common combinations are 二次遷移が始まる／進む and 二次遷移によって〜になる. Technical language of ecology.

examples[].german: Pioneer species are the plants that first settle on wasteland.
After the eruption, pioneer species such as Japanese knotweed were the first to sprout.
Pioneer species grow quickly, but many of them have short lifespans.
en.notes: 先駆種 are pioneer species that are the first to colonize open or disturbed areas, e.g. ススキ, イタドリ or アカマツ. They grow fast, need a lot of light and are often short-lived, so they are displaced over the course of succession. Plants are mostly meant; in addition, パイオニア種 and パイオニア植物 are in use. Typical: 先駆種が侵入する／定着する. Technical language.

examples[].german: Sun trees are tree species that need plenty of sunlight.
Japanese red pine and white birch are typical sun trees.
When the forest matures and the forest floor becomes dark, the seedlings of sun trees no longer grow.
en.notes: 陽樹 are shade-intolerant (light-demanding) tree species: their seedlings need full sunlight and hardly grow in shade, but they grow fast on open ground. Typical examples in Japan are アカマツ, シラカバ and コナラ. Over the course of succession they are replaced by 陰樹 "shade-tolerant trees", whose seedlings survive in the dark forest. A term of school biology and forestry.

examples[].german: Shade-tolerant trees are trees with high shade tolerance that can grow even in shade.
In the later stage of succession, shade-tolerant trees take over from sun trees as the main players of the forest.
Beech and shii are typical shade-tolerant trees of Japan.
en.notes: 陰樹 are shade-tolerant tree species whose seedlings can grow even in the partial shade under the canopy, e.g. ブナ, シイ, カシ. For this reason they replace the 陽樹 over the course of succession and form the climax forest (極相林). Careful: the English "shade tree" in the sense of "a tree that provides shade" is not meant; that would be 緑陰樹 or simply 日陰を作る木. A technical term from biology and forestry.

examples[].german: The canopy of the tropical rainforest is a habitat for diverse organisms.
When a large tree falls and a gap opens in the canopy, light reaches the forest floor.
The researchers surveyed the canopy using a crane.
en.notes: 林冠 is the "canopy" of a forest, that is, the closed layer of tree crowns. The opposite term is 林床 "forest floor". Typical combinations: 林冠が閉じる "the canopy closes", 林冠ギャップ for a gap after a tree fall, 林冠を形成する. Technical language of ecology and forestry.

examples[].german: Sunlight enters the forest edge, and diverse plants grow there.
Many animals such as hares and foxes show themselves at the forest edge.
A new forest edge was created by road construction, and drying progressed even into the interior of the forest.
en.notes: 林縁 is the forest edge as an ecological transition zone between forest and open land; often 林縁部. It is brighter and richer in species there than in the forest interior, and typical belts of shrubs and climbers form (マント群落). The word is technical; in everyday speech people say 森のはずれ or 林の端.

examples[].german: Sparse forests spread across dry regions.
In the savanna, you can also see open woodland where trees grow sparsely in the grassland.
After the wildfire, that slope was reduced to sparse woodland.
en.notes: 疎林 is a light forest in which the trees stand far apart so that a lot of light falls on the ground; the opposite is 密林. It is found in dry regions, savannas or after fires and logging. The word is literary and technical; colloquially people say 木がまばらな林.

en.meaning: Legal Affairs Bureau (regional office of the Ministry of Justice; land and corporate registry office)
examples[].german: Real estate registration is done at the Legal Affairs Bureau.
Naturalization applications are accepted at the Legal Affairs Bureau.
I deposited my handwritten will with the Legal Affairs Bureau.
en.notes: 法務局 is the regional branch of the Ministry of Justice (法務省). For citizens, it is above all the office for register entries - land registry (不動産登記) and commercial register (商業登記) - and also for naturalization (帰化), human rights consultation and the custody of wills. Smaller offices are called 地方法務局, 支局 or 出張所. "Legal Affairs Bureau" is only a makeshift translation; functionally it corresponds to a land registry office and a company registry court.

examples[].german: Numerous unknown creatures live in the Amazon jungle.
The expedition kept walking through the jungle for days.
On the internet, the online shopping site Amazon is sometimes jokingly called "mitsurin".
en.notes: 密林 is a dense, hardly penetrable forest, especially the tropical jungle: アマゾンの密林, 密林に分け入る. The opposite is 疎林. In everyday speech ジャングル is more common; 密林 sounds more literary and adventurous. In internet slang, 密林 is also a joking name for the online retailer Amazon.

examples[].german: A vast wilderness spreads across Hokkaido.
The settlers cleared the wilderness and made fields.
Beware of the "wasteland scam" in which worthless land is sold at a high price.
en.notes: 原野 is wide, undeveloped and uncultivated land, mostly grassland, heath or moor, not dense forest: 広大な原野, 原野を切り開く "to clear wilderness". 荒野, by contrast, emphasizes desolation and dryness, and 荒れ地 fallow land. Also well known is 原野商法, the fraudulent sale of worthless plots in the wilderness. Literary, but common.

examples[].german: Peatlands are huge reservoirs of carbon dioxide.
In the production of Scotch whisky, peat is burned to dry the malt.
In the past, peat was dug out and used as fuel.
en.notes: 泥炭 is "peat", incompletely decomposed plant material from bogs; the peat bog is called 泥炭地. In connection with whisky and garden soil, the loanword ピート is usual (ピート香, ピートモス). The word element 炭 recalls that peat is a precursor of coal and served as fuel. Technical and neutral.

examples[].german: Mangrove forests play a role in protecting coastal ecosystems.
On Iriomote Island, tours paddling a canoe through the mangroves are popular.
Many mangroves were cut down to make shrimp farming ponds.
en.notes: マングローブ is not a single tree species but the collective name for salt-tolerant woody plants in the tidal zone of tropical and subtropical coasts; the forest is called マングローブ林. In Japan it grows in Okinawa and Amami, where the trees are called ヒルギ. It protects coasts from waves and serves fish as a nursery. Common: マングローブを植林する／伐採する.

examples[].german: Seaweed beds are important as spawning grounds for marine life.
Fishermen have been continuing to plant seaweed to restore the seaweed beds.
Reclamation has destroyed many of the seaweed beds in the bay.
en.notes: 藻場 are stands of seaweed or seagrass in shallow coastal water, such as アマモ場 (eelgrass meadow) or kelp forests of ホンダワラ, アラメ and カジメ. They are regarded as the "nursery of the sea" (海のゆりかご), because fish spawn and young fish grow up there. Their disappearance is called 磯焼け. Typical: 藻場を再生する／保全する, 藻場が失われる. Technical language of fisheries and marine ecology.

examples[].german: Rising seawater temperature is thought to be the cause of the loss of seaweed beds.
Sea urchins have eaten up the seaweed, and the barren coast is spreading.
Because of the loss of seaweed, hardly any abalone or turban shells can be caught anymore.
en.notes: 磯焼け literally means "burning of the rocky shore": the kelp forests (藻場) on rocky coasts disappear, leaving behind bare rock with a whitish crust. Causes are rising water temperatures and grazing by sea urchins (ウニ) or fish such as アイゴ. For coastal fisheries this is a serious problem, because abalone and turban shells lack food. Typical: 磯焼けが起きる／広がる／進む. Technical language, but common in the news.

examples[].german: Coral bleaching has been reported in various parts of the world.
When high seawater temperatures persist, coral bleaching is likely to occur.
When I dived, vast stretches of corals turned pure white by bleaching spread out before me.
en.notes: 白化現象 is a general term for turning white when pigment is lost, but it nearly always refers to coral bleaching, as in サンゴの白化現象. When the water temperature rises, corals expel their symbiotic algae and turn white; if this continues, they die. As a verb, people say サンゴが白化する. Less often it stands for albinism in animals or chlorosis in plants. Technical language, common in environmental news.

examples[].german: Degradation of grassland due to overgrazing is progressing.
In Mongolia, desertification is spreading because of overgrazing.
Some regions limit the number of livestock to prevent overgrazing.
en.notes: 過放牧 is composed of 過 "too much" and 放牧 "grazing of livestock": more animals graze than the vegetation can bear. It is typical in environmental texts on desertification, e.g. 過放牧による砂漠化, often in a series with 過耕作 "overuse of farmland" and 森林伐採 "deforestation". Grammatically it almost always stands as a noun with による or が原因で; the する-form is rare. Technical language of ecology and geography.

examples[].german: Salt damage from irrigation is causing farmland to deteriorate.
After the typhoon, the rice fields along the coast suffered salt damage.
If you live near the sea, protecting your car against salt damage is essential.
en.notes: 塩害 is damage caused by salt: either by seawater and salty sea air, for example to crops, power lines or cars after a typhoon, or by soil salinization through improper irrigation. Typical combinations are 塩害を受ける "to suffer salt damage", 塩害対策 "protection against salt damage" and 塩害による停電. Formed like 水害 "flood damage" and 冷害 "cold damage". Neutral, from agriculture, engineering and the news.

examples[].german: Continuous-cropping injury occurs when the same crop is grown repeatedly.
Tomatoes and eggplants are prone to continuous-cropping injury, so I change where I plant them every year.
Crop rotation is the basic method for preventing continuous-cropping injury.
en.notes: 連作障害 are the yield losses and diseases that occur when the same crop is grown year after year on the same plot (連作); causes are one-sided nutrient depletion and soil pests. The remedy is 輪作 "crop rotation". Especially susceptible are nightshades such as トマト, ナス and ジャガイモ. Typical: 連作障害が出る／起きる, 連作障害を防ぐ／避ける. Also common among hobby gardeners.

examples[].german: I applied for registration of the transfer of ownership.
After founding a company, you first have to register it.
Before buying the house, I checked the registry to confirm who the owner was.
en.notes: 登記 is the official entry of rights and facts into a public register, above all 不動産登記 (land registry) and 商業登記 (commercial register). Transitive する-verb: 〜を登記する; one applies for it with 登記を申請する at the 法務局. The extract is today called 登記事項証明書, formerly 登記簿謄本. Distinction: 登録 is general registration (membership, trademarks, vehicles), 届出 a notification or report.

examples[].german: Bioindicators are used to evaluate water quality.
Stonefly larvae are known as a bioindicator of clean rivers.
Using lichens as a bioindicator, we investigated air pollution in the city.
en.notes: 生物指標 denotes organisms whose presence or condition allows conclusions about the environment, for example insect larvae for water quality or lichens for air purity. Synonymous and at least as common is 指標生物; typical frames are 〜を生物指標とする and 〜の生物指標として用いる. The second element 指標 "indicator, index" also occurs in 経済指標 "economic indicator". Purely technical and written language.

examples[].german: An environmental impact assessment is required for large-scale development.
Environmental assessment procedures have begun for the planned construction of the wind power plant.
Residents are protesting that the content of the environmental impact assessment is inadequate.
en.notes: 環境アセスメント is the environmental impact assessment before large projects such as power plants, roads or airports. The official term is 環境影響評価 (the law: 環境影響評価法); the media also abbreviate it to 環境アセス. Typical combinations: 環境アセスメントを実施する／行う, 環境アセスメントの手続き, 環境アセスメントの対象になる.

examples[].german: Tighter emission regulations are having a big impact on industry.
Emission regulations for automobiles became stricter, and sales of diesel vehicles fell.
The government indicated a policy of easing emission regulations for factories.
en.notes: 排出規制 are legal limits on the output of exhaust gases, pollutants or greenhouse gases. Typical: 排出規制を強化する／緩和する, 排出規制が厳しくなる, 排出規制をクリアする. Concrete limit values are called 排出基準; for car exhaust, 排ガス規制 is common in colloquial speech. Language of administration, business and the news.

examples[].german: An environmental restoration project for the degraded wetland is under way.
Minamata City has drawn on its experience of pollution to pursue community building centered on environmental regeneration.
Citizen volunteers are working on restoring the environment of the river.
en.notes: 環境再生 means the restoration of a damaged environment, for example polluted rivers, destroyed wetlands or former industrial areas. Typical: 環境再生に取り組む, 環境再生事業, 環境再生プロジェクト. Close terms are 自然再生 (more about ecosystems) and 環境保全 "environmental protection", which preserves what exists instead of restoring what was destroyed. Language of officialdom and the media.

examples[].german: The airline introduced a carbon offset scheme.
More and more companies are carbon-offsetting the CO2 from business trips through donations to tree planting.
Some argue that we should first reduce emissions before relying on carbon offsets.
en.notes: カーボンオフセット means compensating for unavoidable CO2 emissions through climate protection projects such as reforestation or the purchase of certificates (カーボンクレジット). Related is カーボンニュートラル "carbon neutral", the goal of the offsetting. People say カーボンオフセットを導入する, occasionally also as a する-verb: 排出量をカーボンオフセットする. Language of business and the media.

examples[].german: The concept of green infrastructure is being incorporated into urban planning.
Parks that let rainwater soak into the ground are attracting attention as green infrastructure for flood control.
We should combine not only concrete embankments but also green infrastructure that makes use of wetlands.
en.notes: グリーンインフラ is the short form of グリーンインフラストラクチャー: nature and green spaces are deliberately used as infrastructure, e.g. parks and wetlands as rainwater retention and street trees against heat. The opposite term is グレーインフラ, classic concrete infrastructure such as embankments and canals. Typical: グリーンインフラを導入する／活用する. Language of administration and planning.

examples[].german: The ecosystem functions of forests include water source conservation and prevention of landslide disasters.
The invasion of alien species may impair native ecosystem functions.
The research team evaluated the ecosystem functions of the wetland and estimated their economic value.
en.notes: 生態系機能 are the processes that an ecosystem performs itself, such as nutrient cycles, water retention, soil formation or pollination. Closely related is 生態系サービス "ecosystem services", which emphasizes the benefit of these functions to humans. Typical: 生態系機能を維持する／損なう／評価する. Technical language of ecology and environmental policy.

examples[].german: Surveys of benthic organisms are used for water quality assessment.
Many benthic organisms such as polychaete worms and shellfish live in the mud of the tidal flats.
Bottom trawling does great damage to the benthic organisms on the seabed.
en.notes: 底生生物 are organisms that live on or in the bottom of seas, lakes and rivers, that is, the "benthos": shellfish, worms (ゴカイ), crustaceans or aquatic insect larvae. The loanword ベントス is a synonym. It is one of the three ecological groups of aquatic organisms, alongside 浮遊生物 "plankton" and 遊泳生物 "nekton". Because they are sedentary, they serve as indicators of water quality. Technical language.

examples[].german: Plankton forms the basis of the marine food chain.
Plankton cannot swim against the flow of water.
We scooped up seawater with a net and observed the plankton under a microscope.
en.notes: 浮遊生物 is the Sino-Japanese technical term for "plankton": organisms that drift in the water and cannot swim against the current. In everyday speech, and even in many specialist texts, プランクトン is much more common (植物プランクトン, 動物プランクトン). The opposites are 遊泳生物 "nekton" and 底生生物 "benthos". 浮遊 alone means "to float, to drift", as in 浮遊物.

examples[].german: Fish and dolphins are classified as nekton.
Nekton can move against ocean currents under their own power.
Jellyfish swim, but they cannot go against the current, so they are classed as plankton rather than nekton.
en.notes: 遊泳生物 are aquatic animals that can swim against currents under their own power, that is, the "nekton": fish, squid, whales, seals. ネクトン is a synonym. What matters is swimming strength, not swimming as such: jellyfish do swim but count as 浮遊生物. The third group is 底生生物 "benthos". Technical language.

examples[].german: The will was drawn up in the presence of a notary.
Documents to be used abroad sometimes require notarization.
I took the contract to the notary office and had it certified.
en.notes: 公証 is the official certification or recording that a document or fact is genuine. It rarely stands alone and mostly appears in compounds: 公証人 "notary", 公証役場 "notary office". The deed drawn up by a notary is called 公正証書, a notarial will 公正証書遺言; certifying private documents is called 認証. Technical language from law and administration.

examples[].german: The inflow of nutrient salts into the ocean can cause red tides.
In the winter sea, the upper and lower water mix well, and nutrient salts are supplied to the surface layer.
Sewage treatment has advanced so far that nutrient salts have decreased too much, and the fading of the color of nori seaweed has become a problem.
en.notes: 栄養塩 (also 栄養塩類) are the nutrients dissolved in water for algae and plankton, above all nitrogen, phosphorus and silicate compounds. Too much leads to 富栄養化 "eutrophication" and 赤潮 "algal bloom"; too little leads to nutrient deficiency in the sea. Typical: 栄養塩が供給される／不足する, 栄養塩濃度. Technical language of oceanography and fisheries.

examples[].german: Organic matter in the soil is essential for plant growth.
Organic matter such as food waste is decomposed by microorganisms.
Many compounds containing carbon are classified as organic matter.
en.notes: 有機物 is "organic matter", that is, carbon-containing material from living things such as fallen leaves, food scraps or compost; in chemistry also "organic compound" (有機化合物). The opposite term is 無機物. Typical: 有機物を分解する, 有機物を多く含む土. Not to be confused with 有機 in 有機野菜 or 有機栽培, where it means "organic, ecologically grown". School and technical language.

examples[].german: Decomposers convert organic matter into inorganic matter.
Water, table salt and metals are inorganic substances.
Unlike organic matter, inorganic matter does not give off carbon dioxide when burned.
en.notes: 無機物 is "inorganic matter": water, salts, metals, rocks and gases such as carbon dioxide. The opposite term is 有機物; decomposers convert 有機物 back into 無機物. In nutrition, minerals are by contrast called 無機質 or ミネラル. The adjective 無機質な is used figuratively for "cold, soulless" (無機質な部屋), 無機物 itself is not. School and technical language.

examples[].german: Material cycling in ecosystems maintains the Earth's environment.
Without decomposers, the material cycle of the ecosystem would come to a halt.
We need to reuse waste as resources and promote material cycling within society.
en.notes: 物質循環 is the "material cycle": elements such as carbon, nitrogen or phosphorus move between organisms, soil, water and air. Typical: 生態系における物質循環, 物質循環を担う. In environmental policy the word also stands for the circulation of raw materials and waste in society, related to 循環型社会 "recycling-oriented society". For the flow of energy, by contrast, people say エネルギーの流れ, because energy does not return.

examples[].german: Forests play an important role in the carbon cycle.
The massive consumption of fossil fuels is upsetting the balance of the Earth's carbon cycle.
Photosynthesis and respiration are two important processes that support the carbon cycle.
en.notes: 炭素循環 is the carbon cycle between atmosphere, organisms, ocean and rock. Important steps are 光合成 (uptake of CO2) and 呼吸 or 分解 (release). Typical: 炭素循環において, 炭素循環のバランスが崩れる, 地球規模の炭素循環. Technical language, common in climate reports.

examples[].german: Disruption of the nitrogen cycle is causing environmental problems.
Microorganisms in the soil play an important role in the nitrogen cycle.
Please do not add fish until the nitrogen cycle in the tank has stabilized.
en.notes: 窒素循環 is the cycle of nitrogen between air, soil, organisms and water: bacteria fix it, plants take it up, and it is released again during decomposition. Formed like 炭素循環 "carbon cycle" and 水循環 "water cycle"; typical are 窒素循環が乱れる and 窒素循環を担う微生物. The word also appears in aquarium keeping, when filter bacteria break down ammonia. Technical language of biology and environmental science.

examples[].german: The water cycle consists of the processes of evaporation, precipitation and runoff.
Forests store rainwater and have the function of stabilizing the water cycle.
Urbanization has paved the ground, and the balance of the water cycle is being upset.
en.notes: 水循環 is read みずじゅんかん, not すいじゅんかん. It means the water cycle made up of 蒸発 "evaporation", 降水 "precipitation", 浸透 "infiltration" and 流出 "runoff". In Japan the 水循環基本法 regulates the protection of this cycle, so the word also appears in official texts. Typical: 健全な水循環, 水循環を保つ.

examples[].german: Unlike the carbon and nitrogen cycles, the phosphorus cycle does not pass through the atmosphere.
The mining of phosphate rock and the heavy use of fertilizer are greatly changing the phosphorus cycle.
Seabird droppings carry phosphorus from the sea to the land and form part of the phosphorus cycle.
en.notes: リン循環 is the phosphorus cycle. Phosphorus is almost always written in katakana in Japan (リン, rarely 燐). Unlike the carbon and nitrogen cycles, there is no significant route through the atmosphere; phosphorus enters soil and waters through weathering of rock and ends up in marine sediment. Humans intervene strongly through リン鉱石 "phosphate rock" and fertilizers. Technical language.

examples[].german: Upwelling currents carry nutrient salts from the deep sea to the surface and form rich fishing grounds.
Upwelling occurs off Peru, so it is a good fishing ground for anchovies.
When El Nino occurs, upwelling weakens and catches decline.
en.notes: 湧昇 is oceanic "upwelling": cold, nutrient-rich deep water rises to the surface, often off west coasts such as Peru or California. Most often you hear 湧昇流 "upwelling current" or 湧昇域 "upwelling area"; 湧 is the same character as in 湧く "to well up". Careful, homophone: ゆうしょう is in everyday speech almost always 優勝 "championship". Technical language of oceanography.

examples[].german: Longshore currents transport sand and change coastal landforms.
When swimming in the sea, besides rip currents heading offshore, you also need to watch out for longshore currents flowing along the shore.
The construction of a breakwater changed the longshore current, and the sandy beach next door shrank.
en.notes: 沿岸流 is a current that runs parallel to the coast, on a large scale as a coastal current of the ocean, on a small scale as a longshore current in the surf zone. It transports sand and shapes beaches and sand spits (砂州, 砂嘴). Not to be confused with 離岸流, the dangerous rip current that pulls away from the shore into the open sea. Technical language, also generally known from swimming warnings.

examples[].german: The plaintiff gave a statement in court.
At the first hearing, the prosecution delivered its opening statement.
I asked my lawyer to draw up a written statement for me.
en.notes: 陳述 is the formal presentation of facts or views, especially in court or before an authority: 意見陳述 "statement of opinion (e.g. by the victim)", 陳述書 "written statement", 冒頭陳述 "opening statement of the prosecution". Transitive する-verb: 意見を陳述する. In everyday speech one says 述べる; 供述, by contrast, is the testimony of a suspect or witness to the police or in court.

examples[].german: Deep water is rich in nutrient salts.
In Muroto, Kochi Prefecture, drinking water and salt are made using deep ocean water.
Deep water is cold and contains almost no bacteria.
en.notes: 深層水 is cold deep water below the layer reached by light; the opposite term is 表層水. In Japan, 海洋深層水 is best known; it is pumped, for example, in 室戸 (Kochi) or Toyama and marketed as drinking water, salt or cosmetics. It is regarded as nutrient-rich, clean and low in germs. Neutral, common in advertising.

examples[].german: The Kuroshio is a warm current that flows along the Japanese archipelago.
Because of the warm current, this region is relatively warm even in winter.
The Tsushima Current is a warm current flowing north through the Sea of Japan and is also related to the heavy snowfall in winter.
en.notes: 暖流 is a warm ocean current that usually flows poleward from low latitudes; the opposite term is 寒流. The well-known 暖流 around Japan are the 黒潮 (日本海流) on the Pacific side and the 対馬海流 in the Sea of Japan. Typical: 暖流が流れる, 暖流の影響で暖かい. School geography vocabulary.

examples[].german: The Oyashio is a cold current flowing south from the north and forms rich fishing grounds.
Over a cold current, the air is cooled and fog forms easily.
The Peru Current is a cold current that flows north to near the equator.
en.notes: 寒流 is a cold ocean current that usually flows from high latitudes toward the equator; the opposite term is 暖流. Around Japan, 親潮 (千島海流) and the リマン海流 are the most important 寒流. Where 寒流 and 暖流 meet (潮目), rich fishing grounds arise; sea fog often forms over cold currents. School geography vocabulary.

en.meaning: current boundary; tide rip; (fig.) turning point
examples[].german: The current boundary where warm and cold currents collide becomes a good fishing ground.
After the debate, the tide of the election campaign turned, and the opposition candidate took the lead.
Veteran fishermen can tell the current boundary by the difference in the color of the sea.
en.notes: 潮目 is the visible boundary line where two ocean currents or water masses meet; plankton and fish gather there, hence good fishing grounds. Very common is the figurative use for a turning point in politics, business or competition: 潮目が変わる "the tide turns", 潮目を読む. Kun reading しおめ.

examples[].german: During the Jomon period, part of the Kanto Plain was under the sea because of marine transgression.
Shell mounds are found inland because, owing to the Jomon transgression, the coastline lay farther inland than it does now.
Examining the strata shows that marine transgression and regression were repeated many times in this region.
en.notes: 海進 is geological "transgression": the sea level rises or the land subsides, and the sea advances inland. The opposite term is 海退. Famous is the 縄文海進 about 6,000 years ago, when the sea reached far into what is now the Kanto region; that is why many shell mounds (貝塚) lie inland today. For the current rise in sea level people rather say 海面上昇. Technical language of geology and history.

examples[].german: During the Ice Age, marine regression made it possible to travel between continents on foot.
Through marine regression, the former seabed became dry land.
Coastal terraces are landforms created by uplift of the land or marine regression.
en.notes: 海退 is geological "regression": the sea retreats because sea level falls (e.g. in ice ages) or the land rises; former sea floor becomes land. The opposite term is 海進. In the ice ages, 海退 created land bridges, for example between Japan and the continent. Technical language of geology and Earth history.

examples[].german: Plants that can grow even in poor soil are being bred.
My grandfather spent decades turning barren land into rich fields.
It is good to plant legumes in poor soil to enrich it.
