en.notes: 健気 is a な-adjective for the brave, dutiful behavior of someone weaker despite difficult circumstances, typically of children, young people or even animals and plants: 健気な子, 健気に頑張る, 健気に咲く花. It stirs emotion and sympathy in the observer. For brave adults in danger, one rather says 勇敢 or 勇ましい.

examples[].german: An innocent smile soothes the heart.
Looking at my child's innocent sleeping face, I forget my fatigue.
Even though she is in high school, her face still retains a childlike innocence.
en.notes: あどけない is an い-adjective for the innocent, guileless aura of a small child, especially in the face and expression: あどけない笑顔, あどけない寝顔. For teenagers or adults, one often says あどけなさが残る "still looks childlike". Unlike 無邪気, which also describes childlike behavior, or 幼い, which just means "young, immature", あどけない is always affectionate and never pejorative in the sense of "naive".

examples[].german: I made an infuriating mistake.
Damn it, it started raining just as I was about to leave.
He watched his rival's success with bitter annoyance.
en.notes: 忌々しい (often いまいましい) expresses fierce annoyance at something one cannot change, almost like a curse: 忌々しい雨だ "this damned rain". Also typical are 忌々しいことに "annoyingly" and 忌々しそうに "with an irritated look". The kanji 忌 ("to avoid, taboo") recalls the older sense "ominous". Compared with 腹立たしい, 忌々しい is more emotional and bitter.

examples[].german: He lines up hollow excuses.
An apology without real feeling sounds hollow instead.
I'm thoroughly fed up with his empty flattery.
en.notes: 空々しい describes words or gestures that sound hollow and insincere because there is no real feeling behind them: 空々しいお世辞, 空々しい言い訳, 空々しく聞こえる. Related is 白々しい, which stresses more the brazenness with which someone obviously lies or feigns ignorance. 空々しい stresses emptiness; similar is 上辺だけの "merely superficial".

examples[].german: He was sentenced to two years in prison as an accessory.
Even someone who only acted as a lookout can be charged as an accessory.
The sentence for an accessory is lighter than that for the principal offender.
en.notes: 従犯 is, in Japanese criminal law, the accessory, that is, someone who merely assists another's crime without being a perpetrator himself; 幇助犯 is a synonym. The opposite is 正犯 ("principal offender"), the leader is called 主犯. The punishment of a 従犯 is reduced compared with that of a 正犯. A purely technical term from statutes, judgments and court reports.

examples[].german: I wish you would stop telling such obvious lies.
Although he had seen everything, he asked back with feigned innocence, "What do you mean?"
Please don't say something so hypocritical as "I'm rooting for you" now, of all times.
en.notes: 白々しい describes brazen, transparent insincerity: 白々しい嘘 "a bald-faced lie", 白々しいお世辞, or pretending not to know: 白々しく「知らない」と言う. Compared with 空々しい ("hollow, empty"), 白々しい is sharper and stresses the brazenness. Do not confuse it with the expression 白々と明ける (しらじらと) "dawn breaks, the sky grows light".

examples[].german: A heavy security presence has been put in place.
The trial began in a tense atmosphere.
It's just a minor examination, so don't put it in such grand terms.
en.notes: 物々しい describes something that looks intimidating or exaggerated because of its scale or severity. Most common in the news: 物々しい警備 "heavy security", 物々しい雰囲気 "tense, martial atmosphere". In everyday life it also means "exaggerated, blown up": 物々しい言い方, 物々しい格好. For merely "magnificent, impressive", 堂々とした or 立派 is more usual.

examples[].german: Everything is novel to a foreign child.
The village children looked at the foreign tourists with curiosity.
The first-time customer looked around the shop with curiosity.
en.notes: 物珍しい describes something that is new and unfamiliar to the observer and therefore arouses curiosity. Unlike 珍しい ("rare, unusual"), which states an objective rarity, 物珍しい stresses the subjective appeal of the unfamiliar. Very common are the adverbial forms 物珍しそうに / 物珍しげに ("(to look) with curiosity, with wonder") and the noun 物珍しさ, e.g. 物珍しさから "out of sheer curiosity". Slightly elevated, rather written tone.

examples[].german: There's no need to put it in such grandiose words.
The summit was held under heavy, showy security.
He makes a huge fuss even over trivial matters.
en.notes: 仰々しい means that something is presented in a more elaborate, solemn or dramatic way than the matter deserves: words, titles, packaging, a security presence. In everyday speech one usually says 大げさ ("exaggerated"); 仰々しい stresses more the pompous, blown-up quality and is pejorative. Adverbial: 仰々しく騒ぎ立てる "to make a big fuss". Also written 仰仰しい; "boastful" in the sense of showing off would rather be 自慢げ.

examples[].german: I can't be bothered to go out on rainy days.
As you get older, it becomes a chore to start something new.
I couldn't be bothered to write a reply and left the email for a whole week.
en.notes: 億劫 is a な-adjective that describes inner sluggishness: something seems so tedious that one cannot bring oneself to do it. Typical is the frame 〜のが億劫だ / 億劫になる, plus the verb 億劫がる. Whereas 面倒 ("troublesome, bothersome") judges the matter itself as laborious, 億劫 stresses one's own reluctance. Often written in kana as おっくう; the word comes from the Buddhist 億劫 ("an immeasurably long period of time").

examples[].german: The paperwork procedures are a terrible hassle.
On rainy days, going out is a pain.
He is fussy about small details and is a bit of a pain to deal with.
en.notes: 面倒臭い expresses that one finds something burdensome out of reluctance: 手続きが面倒臭い, 〜するのが面倒臭い. It is usually written 面倒くさい or めんどくさい; in speech the う is often dropped, and informally one also says めんどい. Compared with 面倒な "complicated, laborious", the word stresses one's own reluctance more and is more colloquial. Said of people, it means "tiring, difficult to deal with".

examples[].german: I'm not familiar with machines, so I don't know how to use it.
I'm out of touch with trends, so I can't keep up with what young people talk about.
Since graduating, my contact with my old friends has become sparse.
en.notes: 疎い usually takes に and means "to be unfamiliar with something, to know little about it": 機械に疎い, 流行に疎い, 世事に疎い. The older meaning "estranged, distant" lives on in 付き合いが疎くなる and in the proverb 去る者は日々に疎し ("out of sight, out of mind"); in everyday speech one rather says 疎遠になる for this. Compared with 詳しくない, 疎い sounds somewhat more elevated and is often self-deprecating.

examples[].german: I am proud of my son, who has grown up strong.
He lifted the heavy luggage with his tanned, sturdy arms.
The people in the disaster area live resiliently even amid hardship.
en.notes: 逞しい first describes physical strength (逞しい腕 "strong arms"), then also inner strength and resilience: 逞しく生きる "to live resiliently". For children, 逞しく育つ praises that they have become robust and independent. Set phrase: 想像を逞しくする "to let one's imagination run wild". Mostly written in kana, たくましい; unlike 強い, there is a note of appreciation for staying power.

examples[].german: I haven't done anything I have to feel guilty about.
You're looking away because you have something to hide, aren't you?
I feel a little guilty about having lied.
en.notes: やましい (mostly in kana; the kanji is rather 疚しい than 疾しい) denotes a guilty conscience because one has something to hide. Most common is the negation やましいことは何もない / していない "I have nothing to reproach myself for". Noun: やましさ. Close in meaning are 後ろめたい ("to feel guilty, to have a bad conscience") and 気がとがめる; "ashamed" in the sense of embarrassed would instead be 恥ずかしい.

examples[].german: Sentences are aggravated for repeat offenders.
To prevent reoffending, support after release from prison is indispensable.
He is a repeat thief; this was his fifth arrest.
en.notes: 累犯 is, in criminal law, a new offense within a certain period after serving a prison sentence; the punishment is then increased (累犯加重). A person who relapses in this way is a 累犯者. The more general 再犯 simply means "another offense, relapse" and is much more common in everyday life and the media, for example in 再犯防止.

examples[].german: I was filled with inconsolable sorrow.
My efforts went unrewarded, and I felt a dreary helplessness.
The news that young lives were lost in the accident is truly heartbreaking.
en.notes: やるせない (mostly in kana) describes a grief one cannot get rid of and is powerless against: sadness, frustration and helplessness at once. Literally about "there is no ford (瀬) to which one could send it". Typical are やるせない気持ち / 思い, often in the face of injustice, senseless loss or fruitless effort. Similar is 切ない, which sounds more yearning and wistful; やるせない stresses the lack of a way out.

examples[].german: We adapt to a rapidly changing society.
With meetings and business trips back to back, this week was a whirlwind.
The game unfolded at a dizzying pace, and I couldn't take my eyes off it until the end.
en.notes: 目まぐるしい literally means "so fast that it makes your eyes spin" and describes rapid, hard-to-follow changes or hectic goings-on. Very common adverbially: 目まぐるしく変わる / 変化する / 展開する. Attributively: 目まぐるしい一日 "a hectic day". Unlike 忙しい ("busy, having a lot to do"), 目まぐるしい stresses the pace and the constant change.

examples[].german: We will take care of it appropriately, so please rest assured.
The teacher arranged things so that I could retake the exam.
Thank you for your special consideration.
en.notes: 取り計らう means to handle a matter in the interest of those involved, or to arrange something so that it works out; typical is 〜ように取り計らう. The word sounds formal and occurs mainly in business and official language, often with keigo: 取り計らってくださる. The noun お取り計らい ("consideration, arrangement") is very common in thank-you formulas. More neutral are 手配する ("to arrange") or 処理する ("to deal with").

examples[].german: We suffered enormous damage from the typhoon.
Our company also incurred a large loss due to a business partner's bankruptcy.
I'd rather be excused from such a dangerous job.
en.notes: 被る (こうむる) means "to suffer or incur something (usually negative)": 被害 / 損害 / 損失 / 迷惑を被る. More rarely and in elevated language also something positive: 恩恵を被る "to receive benefits". Note: the same kanji is read かぶる ("to put on, to pull over", 帽子をかぶる); in combination with 被害 or 損害 it is always こうむる. Set phrase: 御免被る "I'd rather be excused, no thank you". Literary; in conversation one rather says 受ける.

en.meaning: to stagnate, to fall into arrears
examples[].german: If payments fall behind, it develops into a matter of trust.
Heavy snow held up distribution, and the shelves in the stores went empty.
The rent is three months in arrears.
en.notes: 滞る is intransitive and means that something that should flow or progress comes to a standstill: 仕事 / 物流 / 交通が滞る. For payments it means "to be in arrears": 家賃 / 支払いが滞る. The noun 滞り belongs with it; 滞りなく ("smoothly, without incident") is a set formula, e.g. 式は滞りなく終わった. Related is 停滞 ("stagnation").

examples[].german: We train talent who will shoulder the next generation.
She plays a central role in the project.
Tourism is an important industry that supports the economy of this region.
en.notes: 担う today means almost only figuratively "to bear responsibility, a role or a task": 役割 / 責任 / 未来を担う. Very common is 次世代を担う / 未来を担う ("who will carry the future") as a modifier before 人材 or 若者. The literal meaning "to carry on the shoulder" is rare; for that one says 担ぐ (かつぐ), which has the same kanji. The word sounds elevated and suits speeches, newspapers and corporate texts.

en.meaning: to be particular about, to insist on
examples[].german: He has a craftsman's temperament and is particular about details.
There's no point in dwelling on past mistakes forever.
This shop is popular for its ramen, made with great attention to the ingredients.
en.notes: こだわる (mostly in kana) takes に and carries two evaluations: negative "to get hung up, to cling to something" (過去にこだわる, 細かいことにこだわる), positive "to place special value on, to be uncompromising" (素材にこだわる). The positive reading is very common in advertising, also as the noun こだわり: こだわりの一品 "a product made with devotion". Unlike 気にする ("to worry"), it is about persistent adherence.

en.meaning: to hold back, to hesitate (out of consideration)
examples[].german: Wary of other people's eyes, they met in secret.
It is a story that one hardly dares to say in public.
They say "the hated child gets ahead in the world", and that person has become more and more powerful.
en.notes: 憚る means to avoid something out of consideration for others or out of reserve: 人目を憚る "to shun other people's eyes". Very common is the passive form: 口にするのも憚られる "one hardly dares to say it", as well as 〜を憚らず / 誰に憚ることなく "without any reserve". The second meaning "to throw one's weight around" is known almost only from the proverb 憎まれっ子世に憚る ("ill weeds grow apace"). Elevated, written tone; 遠慮する is the everyday equivalent.

en.meaning: to pine, to be lonely or miserable; (after a verb stem) longingly, impatiently (待ち侘びる)
examples[].german: The children are eagerly waiting for summer vacation to come.
Weary of city life, he returned to his hometown.
In a hermitage deep in the mountains, the old monk lived alone in solitude.
en.notes: 侘びる is a literary, today almost archaic verb: "to pine, to be lonely and miserable, to live a sad life (in a place)". It is alive mainly as the second element after a verb stem: 待ち侘びる "to wait longingly, impatiently for something" (〜を待ち侘びる) and 住み侘びる "to become weary of living in a place". Related are the adjective 侘しい ("dreary, lonely, shabby") and the aesthetic ideal 侘び寂び. Note: "to apologize" is written 詫びる (same reading わびる, お詫び).

examples[].german: You can't get promoted just by flattering your boss.
He thinks nothing of fawning on the powerful.
I don't like service that grovels to customers.
en.notes: へつらう (mostly in kana) means to ingratiate oneself with those more powerful through flattery and servility; it takes に: 上司に諂う, 権力に諂う. The intensified こびへつらう ("to kowtow, to ingratiate oneself") is very common. The word is clearly pejorative and rather written; neutral praise would be 褒める, and colloquially one says ごまをする.

examples[].german: Having a criminal record can be a disadvantage when looking for a job.
Even with a fine, a guilty verdict leaves you with a criminal record.
The arrested man had three prior convictions for theft.
en.notes: 前科 is an earlier criminal conviction: 前科がある, 前科がつく ("to get a criminal record"), counted with 犯: 前科三犯 ("three prior convictions"). The broader 前歴 also includes arrests or investigations without conviction. 前科者 for a person with a record sounds derogatory. Neutral to formal, common in the news and when talking about job hunting.

examples[].german: The costs have mounted beyond what was expected.
The hospital stay is dragging on, and the treatment costs are piling up.
I bought too many souvenirs, and my luggage has grown bulky.
en.notes: 嵩む is intransitive and means that something increases in volume or amount, especially costs and debts: 費用 / 出費 / 借金がかさむ. It usually suggests an undesired increase. From the base word 嵩 (かさ, "volume"), it also concerns bulky quantity: 荷物がかさむ. Mostly written in kana, かさむ; more neutral are 増える or 膨らむ.

en.meaning: to refrain from, to abstain from
examples[].german: Since it concerns personal information, I will refrain from commenting.
On the doctor's advice, I am abstaining from drinking for the time being.
Please refrain from non-essential, non-urgent outings.
en.notes: 差し控える is the formal variant of 控える and means to deliberately do without or hold back on something: コメント / 発言 / 外出を差し控える. Typical in press statements (コメントは差し控えさせていただきます "I would prefer not to comment on that") and announcements: お差し控えください "please refrain". In conversation, 控える or やめる is enough.

examples[].german: We will decide after taking the various circumstances into consideration.
Salary is determined taking experience and ability into account.
Considering the trend in prices as well, this price increase is unavoidable.
en.notes: 勘案 means weighing several factors against one another and including them in a decision; mostly as 〜を勘案する / 勘案して / 勘案した上で. It is a typical word of official, legal and business language. 考慮 ("consideration") is more general and also common in speech; 勘案 stresses adding up various circumstances. In everyday speech one says 考えに入れる.

examples[].german: Surplus funds will be allocated to capital investment.
I applied part of my bonus to repaying the loan.
Because a vacancy arose, staff were assigned from another department.
en.notes: 充当 means assigning or using money, resources or personnel for a specific purpose; frame: AをBに充当する. It is a word of financial and administrative language, e.g. 予算を人件費に充当する; in tax law also "to offset" (還付金を未納分に充当する). Close in meaning is 充てる (あてる), which is more common in normal usage.

examples[].german: I am dissatisfied with the inflexible rules.
A friend lent me 100,000 yen.
There is some leeway on the deadline.
en.notes: 融通 (ゆうずう, not ゆうつう) has two main meanings: "to lend or procure money or goods" as a する-verb (資金を融通する), and "flexibility, leeway", especially in 融通が利く / 融通が利かない ("to be flexible / stubborn, inflexible"). Said of people, 融通が利かない is a frequent reproach. Related: 融資 ("a bank loan"), 臨機応変 ("flexible according to the situation").

examples[].german: They plotted a rebellion.
Someone seems to be plotting a takeover of the company.
He planned a new business, but couldn't raise the funds.
en.notes: 企てる means to intend to carry something out according to plan, and often has a negative undertone: 反乱 / 陰謀 / 暗殺を企てる, 自殺を企てる "to attempt suicide". It is used neutrally for ventures: 新事業を企てる. The noun 企て means "plan, attempt". 企む (たくらむ) is always negative ("to hatch a scheme"), whereas 計画する is completely neutral.

examples[].german: There were people who mocked his failure.
Even when mocked for her poor clothes, she remained dignified.
"You can't even do that?" he said, laughing mockingly.
en.notes: 嘲る means to scornfully ridicule someone or something, often because of weakness or failure: 人の失敗を嘲る. Common are 嘲るように笑う "to laugh scornfully" and the passive 嘲られる. The noun is 嘲り, the Sino-Japanese word 嘲笑 (ちょうしょう). In everyday speech one rather says あざ笑う or バカにする; からかう, by contrast, is harmless, often friendly teasing.

en.meaning: to be absorbed in, to immerse oneself
examples[].german: She is absorbed in her research.
I got so absorbed in reading that I passed my stop.
When the child gets absorbed in a game, they don't answer even when called.
en.notes: 没頭する takes に and means to be so absorbed in an activity that one forgets everything around: 研究 / 仕事 / 読書に没頭する. Unlike 熱中する (to be enthusiastically involved), 没頭 stresses complete immersion; 専念する, by contrast, means to consciously devote oneself exclusively to one task. 夢中になる is the more colloquial equivalent.

en.meaning: to forge ahead, to press on
examples[].german: I will press on toward my goal.
Aiming for the championship, we will keep pushing forward as one team.
Without looking aside, he has pressed on along the path of research.
en.notes: 邁進する means to work steadfastly and with full force toward a goal. Typical frames are 〜に向かって邁進する, 〜の道を邁進する and the formula 一路邁進. The word is very formal and sounds like a speech, a New Year's address or a company statement, often with the humble form 邁進してまいります. In conversation one rather says 頑張る or 突き進む; 前進する, by contrast, is neutral "to move forward".

en.meaning: to discern, to know one's place, to be aware of
examples[].german: Behave with proper manners.
Speak with an awareness of your position.
Even small children know right from wrong.
en.notes: わきまえる (mostly in kana) means to know the difference between right and wrong and to act accordingly: 善悪をわきまえる. Even more common is the meaning "to know what is proper": 礼儀 / 立場 / 場所をわきまえる, in modern usage also TPOをわきまえる. The negation 立場をわきまえない is a reproach that someone forgets their place. 区別する, by contrast, is mere distinguishing without a moral undertone.

examples[].german: Programs supporting the rehabilitation of prisoners are being carried out.
He reflected on his past, reformed, and now works honestly.
The bankrupt airline applied for corporate reorganization proceedings.
en.notes: 更生 means that a person begins a new, orderly life after misconduct or crimes: 更生する, 更生を支援する, 更生施設. It is also used for the reorganization of a company, especially in 会社更生法 ("Corporate Reorganization Act"). Not to be confused with the homophones 更正 ("correction", e.g. of a tax assessment) and 厚生 ("welfare", as in 厚生労働省).

en.meaning: to endure; to bear; to hold back
examples[].german: I kept running, bearing the pain.
She held back her tears and continued her speech to the end.
When I saw the department head's bed hair during the meeting, I desperately tried to hold back my laughter.
en.notes: こらえる means to deliberately hold back an emotional or physical reaction: 涙をこらえる, 笑いをこらえる, 痛みをこらえる, 怒りをこらえる. Mostly written in kana, because 堪える is also read たえる "to endure, to withstand" and こたえる "to take a toll". Compared with 我慢する, こらえる is somewhat more literary and stresses suppression in the moment; 耐える describes more the longer endurance of hardship or pressure.

examples[].german: His ability surpasses that of his master.
I escaped the heat in the shade of a tree.
I dipped into my savings and somehow got through the emergency.
en.notes: 凌ぐ has two groups of meaning: "to surpass" (師匠を凌ぐ, 前年を凌ぐ売り上げ, 〜を凌ぐ人気) and "to ward off or get through something unpleasant": 暑さ / 寒さ / 雨露を凌ぐ, 飢えを凌ぐ, 急場を凌ぐ "to get through an emergency". The expression しのぎを削る ("to fight a hard contest") does not belong here etymologically (鎬). Often in kana; in everyday speech one says 超える or 耐える.

en.meaning: to come to nothing, to collapse
examples[].german: His dream was shattered.
He lost in the final, and the hope of winning the title was dashed.
Due to a lack of funds, the plan to build the new airport fell through.
en.notes: 潰える is a literary, intransitive verb: hopes, dreams and plans "burst, come to nothing"; originally also an army "being utterly defeated". Typical: 夢 / 望み / 野望 / 計画が潰える. The same kanji is used in つぶれる / つぶす ("to be crushed / to crush"), which are common in everyday speech. Neutrally one says 駄目になる or 失敗に終わる.

examples[].german: I press forward without flinching at difficulties.
I flinched for a moment at the other person's loud voice, but immediately talked back.
She stated her opinion without flinching even at criticism.
en.notes: ひるむ (mostly in kana) describes a brief recoil or being intimidated in the face of danger, pressure or a strong opponent; the trigger takes に: 相手の勢いに怯む. Very often negated: 怯まず / 怯むことなく "undaunted". Unlike ためらう ("to hesitate", out of indecision), ひるむ is a reaction out of fear; 臆する is more elevated and similar.

en.meaning: to lose heart, to give up
examples[].german: No matter how many times I fail, I don't lose heart.
During the long rehabilitation, my spirit nearly gave way many times.
"Don't lose heart!" the coach called out to the players.
en.notes: くじける (mostly in kana) means to lose courage after setbacks and buckle inwardly; the subject is the person or 心 / 気持ち. Very often negated (挫けない, 挫けずに) or as an exhortation 挫けるな. The transitive counterpart is 挫く: 足首を挫く ("to sprain one's ankle"), 出鼻を挫く ("to stop someone right at the start"). Unlike 諦める ("to give up", a decision), くじける describes a mental collapse.

en.meaning: to be filled with, to brim with
examples[].german: His face brims with confidence.
Ahead of the final, tension filled the venue.
In the snowmelt season, the river swells with water.
en.notes: みなぎる (often in kana) means that something fills a space or body to the brim: originally water swelling (川に水が漲る), today mostly strength, energy or mood: 体に力が漲る, 会場に緊張感が漲る. The force is the subject with が, and the place takes に; "he brims with ..." is thus 彼には自信が漲っている, not 自信に漲る. Similar: 満ちる, あふれる.

examples[].german: A good idea flashed into my mind.
During a walk, a way to solve the problem occurred to me.
Lightning flashed in the night sky.
en.notes: ひらめく (mostly in kana) first means "to flash briefly, to flare up" (稲妻が閃く) or "to flutter" (旗が閃く); but most often that an idea suddenly comes to one: アイデアが閃く, with the idea as subject. The noun 閃き means "flash of inspiration". Unlike 思いつく ("to come up with", also quite everyday), 閃く stresses the sudden, inspired quality.

examples[].german: That incident shook society.
When the child shook the branch, leaves fell.
Her singing voice moved the hearts of those who listened.
en.notes: 揺さぶる means to shake something vigorously back and forth (木を揺さぶる, 肩を揺さぶって起こす) and, figuratively, to shake people or systems: 心を揺さぶる ("to move deeply"), 社会 / 政界を揺さぶる. In sports and negotiations also "to unsettle the opponent". 揺する is similar but weaker; 揺らす is gentle rocking; the intransitive is 揺れる.

examples[].german: His speech stirred up the audience's emotions.
I stoked the fire in the fireplace to warm the room.
The opening of that novel arouses the readers' curiosity.
en.notes: 掻き立てる literally means "to stir up, to poke" (火を掻き立てる, to stoke a fire), and figuratively to awaken or fuel feelings and imagination: 好奇心 / 想像力 / 不安 / 食欲を掻き立てる. The object takes を; the word is neutral to positive ("to stimulate, to inspire"), whereas 煽る ("to incite, to egg on") is rather negative. Also written in kana, かきたてる.

examples[].german: You must not disregard other people's feelings.
I've been so caught up in work that I've neglected my family.
As a result of neglecting safety measures, a major accident occurred.
en.notes: ないがしろにする (mostly in kana) means to belittle and neglect something or someone who deserves attention: 家族 / 基本 / 安全 / 人の意見をないがしろにする. The expression is clearly reproachful. 無視する ("to ignore") is more direct, 軽視する ("to underestimate, to belittle") more literary; おろそかにする stresses negligence in duties.

examples[].german: After release on parole, one is placed under probation.
In a family court hearing, the youth was placed on probation.
During probation, you must meet with your probation officer every month.
en.notes: 保護観察 is the supervision of convicted persons or juveniles who are not in prison, for instance after parole or with a suspended sentence: 保護観察に付される, 保護観察処分, 保護観察中. They are looked after by full-time 保護観察官 and volunteer 保護司. The suspension of a sentence itself is called 執行猶予; 保護観察 is the supervision associated with it.

en.meaning: to consider, to take into account
examples[].german: I take the other person's position into consideration.
Out of consideration for the feelings of the disaster victims, the celebration was canceled.
Considering the future, we should take measures now.
en.notes: 慮る (おもんぱかる, also おもんばかる) means to carefully consider other people's situation or feelings, or future consequences: 相手の立場 / 気持ちを慮る, 将来を慮る. It is an elevated, literary word found mainly in newspapers and speeches; in everyday speech one says 気遣う, 配慮する or 考える. The て-form is common as a reason: 〜を慮って中止する "to cancel out of consideration for ...".

examples[].german: He is watching for an opportunity.
I peeked at the room through a gap in the door.
Watching their parents' expressions, the child timidly began to speak.
en.notes: うかがう in the spelling 覗う / 窺う (窺う is more usual, often also kana) means "to peek secretly, to observe" and "to lie in wait for an opportunity": 様子をうかがう, 機会 / チャンスをうかがう, 顔色をうかがう ("to read someone's expression, to defer to them"). Do not confuse it with the identically sounding humble 伺う ("to ask, to visit"). 覗く (のぞく) has the same kanji and means "to look in".

en.meaning: to look up to, to ask for (guidance)
examples[].german: I ask my teacher for guidance.
I lifted my face and looked up at the night sky.
She looks up to Professor Tanaka as her teacher for life.
en.notes: 仰ぐ literally means "to look upward" (空 / 天を仰ぐ, often as a gesture of despair or wonder). Figuratively: to revere someone (師と仰ぐ "to revere as a teacher") and to ask a higher authority for something: 指導 / 判断 / 指示 / 協力を仰ぐ, typical in business language. Do not confuse it with the homophone 扇ぐ ("to fan"). The word is elevated; in everyday speech one says 見上げる or お願いする.

en.meaning: to go back (in time); to trace back
examples[].german: The history of that temple goes back a thousand years.
I walked upstream along the river to near the waterfall.
This rule applies retroactively to April 1.
en.notes: さかのぼる (often in kana) means, spatially, "to go upstream" (川を遡る, with を for the route) and, temporally, "to go back, to date back": 〜に遡る / 〜まで遡る, e.g. その歴史は千年前に遡る. In administration and law, 〜に遡って適用する means "to apply retroactively". Although it takes を, it is intransitive; similar is 戻る, which however does not express tracing back.

en.meaning: to hold up, to hold over
examples[].german: He held up his hand to shield the sunlight.
Because it was cold, I warmed my hands by holding them over the stove.
At the ticket gate, you hold your IC card over the reader and pass through.
en.notes: かざす (almost always in kana) means to hold something up, or to hold it over or in front of something: 手をかざして日差しを遮る ("to hold a hand protectively over one's eyes"), 火に手をかざす ("to warm one's hands at the fire"). Very everyday today: カードやスマホを読み取り機にかざす. The direction takes に, the held object を. Unlike 持ち上げる ("to lift"), it is about holding something out in a direction.

en.meaning: to block; to stop up; to close
examples[].german: They blocked the road so that it was impassable.
The construction noise was so loud that I covered my ears without thinking.
When rainy days go on, I feel gloomy.
en.notes: 塞ぐ is transitive and means "to close off, to block, to cover": 穴 / 道 / 耳 / 目を塞ぐ. The intransitive counterpart is 塞がる: 道が塞がる, 手が塞がっている ("to have no hand free"). There is also the intransitive 気が塞ぐ ("to feel depressed"). Unlike 閉める ("to close", a door or window), the point is sealing or blocking an opening.

en.meaning: to be overturned, to be reversed
examples[].german: The ruling was overturned.
New evidence overturned the conventional wisdom.
A gust of wind capsized the small boat.
en.notes: 覆る is intransitive: something is knocked over or capsizes (船が覆る), but above all verdicts, decisions or previous certainties are overturned: 判決 / 定説 / 常識 / 結果が覆る. The transitive counterpart is 覆す (判決を覆す). Do not confuse it with 覆う (おおう, "to cover"), which has the same kanji. In everyday speech, for boats one rather says ひっくり返る or 転覆する.

en.meaning: to make a profit; to earn
examples[].german: He made a lot of money on stocks.
If you try to make money without effort, you'll get caught in a scam.
The two got married and had three children.
en.notes: 儲ける means "to make a profit, to earn (money)", usually with an undertone of business or speculation: 株 / 商売で儲ける. For wage labor one more often says 稼ぐ. The intransitive counterpart is 儲かる ("to pay off, to yield a profit": この商売は儲かる), and the noun is 儲け ("profit"). In elevated usage, 子供を儲ける means "to have children". Not to be confused with 設ける ("to set up, to establish").

examples[].german: I spent a lot of time on research.
I spent a whole day off tidying my room.
It is a waste to spend hours on pointless meetings.
en.notes: 費やす means to expend time, money, effort or words on something: AをBに費やす. It is neutral in itself, but in context can also express waste (無駄な会議に時間を費やす). 浪費する, by contrast, explicitly means "to waste", and 使う is the everyday "to use". Common phrases: 多くの年月を費やす, 言葉を費やす ("to use many words").

en.meaning: to do as one pleases, to indulge fully
examples[].german: He wields power at will.
He enjoyed the fame of a genius from a young age.
From the observation deck, you can take in the superb view of Mt. Fuji to your heart's content.
en.notes: ほしいままにする (mostly in kana, also 擅にする) means to possess or use something without restriction, as one pleases. Negative for power: 権力をほしいままにする ("to abuse power, to rule at will"); positive for fame or views: 名声をほしいままにする ("to enjoy undisputed fame"), 絶景をほしいままにする. Adverbial: ほしいままに振る舞う "to do as one pleases". Literary.

examples[].german: Lowering the age of application of the Juvenile Act is being debated.
Under the Juvenile Act, the real names of minor suspects are not reported.
The Juvenile Act was amended, and 18- and 19-year-olds became "specified juveniles".
en.notes: 少年法 is the Japanese law on delinquent juveniles; 少年 here legally means all persons under 20, boys and girls alike. It puts education and protective measures before punishment and in principle forbids publishing the names of juvenile offenders. Since the 2022 reform, 18- and 19-year-olds count as 特定少年 with stricter rules. Typical: 少年法の適用, 少年法改正, 少年法に守られる.

examples[].german: His expression clouded over.
The sun suddenly went behind clouds, and the wind turned cold.
The popularity of the former star has also been fading lately.
en.notes: かげる (also written 陰る, which is more common today) means that light fades: 日が翳る ("the sun disappears behind clouds"). Figuratively, a face darkens (表情が翳る) or something loses its luster: 人気 / 景気が翳る. Very common is the noun 翳り / 陰り: 景気に陰りが見える "the economy is showing signs of clouding over". Intransitive; similar is 曇る, which concretely means "to become cloudy".

en.meaning: to become gaunt, to be worn out
examples[].german: He had a face worn thin by illness.
Exhausted from nursing, my mother has become completely haggard.
The friend I met after a long time looked a little gaunt.
en.notes: やつれる (mostly in kana) describes someone who becomes thin and haggard-looking through illness, worry or exhaustion; often 顔がやつれる, やつれた顔, with the cause 〜でやつれる. Unlike 痩せる ("to lose weight, to become slim", neutral to positive), やつれる is always a sign of suffering. Similar: 憔悴する (literary), げっそりする (colloquial).

en.meaning: to play with, to toy with
examples[].german: You must not play with other people's feelings.
When she is nervous, she has a habit of fiddling with her hair.
Toyed with by fate, he was driven from his hometown.
en.notes: 弄ぶ literally means to play around with something in the hand (髪 / ペンを弄ぶ) and, figuratively, to treat people or feelings ruthlessly: 人の気持ちを弄ぶ. In the passive, 運命に弄ばれる ("to be buffeted by fate") is common in narratives. Unlike 遊ぶ ("to play", intransitive), 弄ぶ is transitive and mostly pejorative; colloquially one says いじる.

examples[].german: It is an act that deviates from the rules.
The conversation has strayed from the main topic, so let's get back to it.
He was disciplined for acting beyond the scope of his duties.
en.notes: 逸脱する means to deviate from a norm, rule or given framework: 〜から逸脱する (規則 / 本題 / 軌道から) or with を: 権限 / 職務の範囲を逸脱する ("to exceed one's authority"). The word is literary and sounds like law, administration or science. In conversation one says 外れる; for topics, colloquially 脱線する ("to digress").

en.meaning: to be fired up, to be stirred to action
examples[].german: His words fired me up.
The players were fired up by the audience's loud cheers.
Even as failures continued, I pulled myself together and kept studying for the exam.
en.notes: 奮い立つ describes someone inwardly summoning new courage and fighting spirit, "to feel roused, to catch fire". The trigger takes に: 言葉に奮い立つ, 声援に奮い立つ. The transitive counterpart is the causative 奮い立たせる, especially 自分を奮い立たせる "to rouse oneself". Rather elevated and narrative; in everyday speech one often says やる気が出る or 元気が出る.

examples[].german: I confided the secret to a friend.
Instead of worrying alone, I confided my anxieties to my family.
I confided to my boss that, in fact, I was thinking of quitting the company.
en.notes: 打ち明ける means to openly tell a trusted person something previously kept secret: 人に秘密・悩み・本心を打ち明ける. The person takes に, the content を or a quotation (〜と打ち明ける). Unlike 告白する (mainly a declaration of love or a confession of guilt) or 明かす (to reveal, also matter-of-fact: 正体を明かす), 打ち明ける stresses personal trust. Related is the noun 打ち明け話 "confidential disclosure".

examples[].german: We will stop the spread of the infection.
A quick repair limited the damage from the water leak.
To stem the exodus of young people, the town began subsidizing rent.
en.notes: 食い止める means to halt a negative development that is already under way and spreading: 被害・感染拡大・人口流出・値下がりを食い止める. Often with a limit: 被害を最小限に食い止める "to keep the damage to a minimum". 防ぐ is more general and often means preventing before something happens; 食い止める presupposes that the problem has already begun. There is no intransitive partner; potential and passive forms are common (食い止められない).

en.meaning: to block the way, to stand in the way
examples[].german: A major obstacle stood in the way.
A man spread his arms and blocked the exit.
In the final, last year's champion will stand in our way.
en.notes: 立ち塞がる literally means "to stand and block the way". Concretely, a person stands in someone's way (〜の前に立ち塞がる, 行く手に立ち塞がる); figuratively, obstacles, problems or opponents stand in the way (困難が立ち塞がる). The verb is intransitive, and the obstacle takes が. By comparison, 道を塞ぐ "to block the road" is transitive. Often also written 立ちふさがる.

en.meaning: to look squarely at, to fix one's gaze on
examples[].german: I make plans with an eye on the future.
I looked the other person straight in the eye and answered clearly.
Before talking about dreams, one should first face reality.
en.notes: 見据える has two uses: literally "to look at fixedly, steadily" (相手の目を見据える, 一点を見据える) and figuratively "to keep something firmly in view and factor it in" (将来・現実・次の選挙を見据える). Very common as 〜を見据えて "with a view to ..." or attributively 将来を見据えた計画. Compared with 見つめる (to gaze for a long time, often tenderly), it seems resolute and sober; the figurative meaning is typical newspaper and business language.

en.meaning: to think through, to get to the bottom of
examples[].german: I think the problem through thoroughly.
When we probed the cause to the bottom, we ended up at a lack of information sharing.
Ultimately, the problem is not money but time.
en.notes: 突き詰める means to think through or investigate a matter to the last point: 問題・原因・理論を突き詰める, 突き詰めて考える. Set phrases are 突き詰めれば and 突き詰めて言えば "in the end, at its core". 突き止める, by contrast, stresses finding out a concrete result (原因・犯人を突き止める), whereas 突き詰める is more the thorough thought process. For "to brood obsessively on one thought", 思い詰める is more usual.

examples[].german: The leaders signed the treaty.
The signing ceremony is scheduled to be held in Tokyo next month.
The two companies signed the merger agreement.
en.notes: 調印 is the solemn "signing" of a treaty or important agreement by both sides, originally with signature and seal. It is mostly used with に: 条約に調印する, less often 条約を調印する; also 調印式 "signing ceremony". For ordinary signatures on forms, one says 署名 or サイン, not 調印. For state treaties, 調印 is followed by 批准.

examples[].german: Fundamental human rights are guaranteed by the constitution.
One of the three principles of the Japanese Constitution is respect for fundamental human rights.
The bill was criticized for possibly infringing on fundamental human rights.
en.notes: 基本的人権 are the fundamental rights to which every person is entitled from birth; the Japanese Constitution names respect for them (基本的人権の尊重) as one of its three principles, alongside 国民主権 and 平和主義. Typical: 基本的人権を保障する, 基本的人権を侵害する. The shorter 人権 is more general and more everyday (人権問題, 人権侵害); 基本的人権 sounds like the constitution and school lessons.

en.meaning: to offer, to report, to request
examples[].german: He offered his cooperation.
I offered to guide a traveler who had lost his way.
If you find a lost item, please report it to a station attendant.
en.notes: 申し出る means to come forward on one's own with an offer, a request or a report to a person or the responsible office: 協力・寄付・辞退を申し出る, 係員に申し出る. The addressee takes に, the content を or a quotation (〜たいと申し出る). Very common in notices: お気軽にお申し出ください "please feel free to contact us". Unlike 申し込む (to sign up, to apply for participation), the focus is on putting forward an intention. Noun: 申し出 "offer, request".

en.meaning: to put together; to sum up; to bundle
examples[].german: I sum up the discussion and report to my boss.
Before the move, I packed my belongings together into one box.
The department head brought the talks between the two companies to a conclusion, and the contract was concluded.
en.notes: まとめる (the kanji 纏める are rare; it is almost always written in kana) means to bring scattered things into a whole: to bundle things (荷物をまとめる), to summarize content (意見・要点をまとめる), to bring negotiations to a conclusion (話・交渉をまとめる) and to hold a group together (チームをまとめる). The intransitive partner is まとまる (意見がまとまる "people come to an agreement"). まとめて also means "all at once, together" (まとめて払う); the noun まとめ means "summary".

en.meaning: to partition, to run, to take charge of
examples[].german: He is running the event.
I divided the room into two with a shelf.
He immediately wants to take charge of everything.
en.notes: 仕切る has two main meanings: spatially "to partition, to divide off" (部屋をカーテンで仕切る) and "to run, to organize, to be in charge" (会議・宴会・店を仕切る). The second is very common in colloquial speech; 仕切りたがる describes someone who always wants to be in charge of everything. More formal and stronger: 取り仕切る "to manage with full responsibility". Nouns: 仕切り "partition", 仕切り直し "fresh start" (originally from sumo).

en.meaning: to bring, to bring about, to cause
examples[].german: The typhoon caused great damage.
New technology has brought great changes to our lives.
The Portuguese brought firearms to Japan.
en.notes: もたらす (the kanji 齎す are hardly used) means "to bring with it, to bring about": 利益・変化・被害・幸運をもたらす; the target takes に (社会に影響をもたらす). It also means bringing news, techniques or cultural goods to a place. Literary-neutral and typical of news and factual texts; in everyday speech one rather says 〜につながる or 〜を起こす. Unlike 引き起こす (usually triggering something negative), もたらす can refer to the positive as well as the negative.

en.meaning: to talk round, to win over
examples[].german: He skillfully talked the other person around.
My child cleverly talked me round, and I ended up buying the toy.
I read the contract carefully so as not to be talked round by the salesperson.
en.notes: 丸め込む means to get someone to do something with clever words, often in a slightly unfair way: "to cajole, to talk round". Pattern: 人を丸め込む, very often in the passive 〜に丸め込まれる "to be talked into something". Colloquial and pejorative; neutral would be 説得する "to persuade", and very similar is 言いくるめる (stresses twisting of words). The literal meaning "to roll up and stuff in" is rare.

examples[].german: I gave a short speech to wrap up the meeting.
He closed his speech with words of thanks.
It was a game fitting to round off the year.
en.notes: 締め括る means to bring something to a proper, well-rounded end: 会議・スピーチ・一年を締め括る; the means takes で (感謝の言葉で締め括る). The noun 締め括り "conclusion" is common (締め括りの言葉 "closing words"). Unlike 終える (simply to finish), it stresses a summarizing, dignified ending. Very often also written 締めくくる; colloquially it is shortened to 締める (会を締める).

en.meaning: to be rooted in, to be based on
examples[].german: There is a culture rooted in tradition.
This festival is deeply rooted in the life of the region.
Discrimination is often rooted in ignorance.
en.notes: 根差す means "to have one's roots in something, to be based on something": 〜に根差す, mostly as 根差している or attributively (地域に根差した店 "a business rooted in the community"). Typical partners are 文化・伝統・生活・地域・経験, but also negatives like prejudice. Intransitive. 基づく "to be based on" (data, rules) is more factual; 根差す stresses grown, deep rootedness. Also written 根ざす.

examples[].german: I act in accordance with the law.
The match was conducted fairly and according to the rules.
The ceremony was held in accordance with old tradition.
en.notes: 則る means "to follow a rule or model" and appears almost only as 〜に則って "in accordance with" or attributively 〜に則った "in accordance with ...". Typical partners: 法律・規則・伝統・先例・作法. Very formal; in everyday speech one says 〜に従って, 〜に沿って or 〜に基づいて. Do not confuse it with the identically read 乗っ取る "to hijack, to take over".

examples[].german: You cannot go against fate.
When I was a child, I was always defying my parents.
Cycling against the wind is hard.
en.notes: 逆らう means "to set oneself against something"; the person, order or current takes に: 親・命令・流れ・時代に逆らう. It also works purely physically: 風・流れに逆らって進む "to move against the wind, against the current". Neutral and everyday; the opposite is 従う "to follow, to obey". 反抗する is stronger (open rebellion, e.g. by teenagers), 抵抗する emphasizes active resistance against pressure.

examples[].german: Freedom of speech is a pillar of a democratic society.
In that country, the freedom to criticize the government is restricted.
Even with freedom of speech, that doesn't mean you may hurt others.
en.notes: 言論の自由 is the freedom to express one's opinion in speech and writing. The Constitution speaks more broadly of 表現の自由 ("freedom of expression"), which also includes art and the press; for the press there is the separate 報道の自由. Typical combinations: 言論の自由を守る, 言論の自由が制限される/弾圧される. Often also used in discussions about the limits of free speech on the internet.

en.meaning: to be content with, to resign oneself to
examples[].german: He is resigned to the status quo.
He lost in the final and had to settle for second place.
He said he would accept the criticism without complaint.
en.notes: 甘んじる means to settle for something that is usually less than hoped: 〜に甘んじる (現状・二位・低い給料に甘んじる). Set phrase: 〜を甘んじて受ける "to accept something without complaint" (批判・罰を甘んじて受ける). Literary; variant 甘んずる. Do not confuse it with 甘える "to be indulged, to depend on others".

en.meaning: to hide on one's person, to muffle (steps)
examples[].german: I tucked the letter secretly into my pocket.
He entered the room with muffled footsteps.
She always keeps a charm hidden in her bag.
en.notes: 忍ばせる means to hide something discreetly on one's person: 〜に〜を忍ばせる (ポケットにナイフを忍ばせる). Set phrases are 足音を忍ばせる "to walk on tiptoe, softly" and 声を忍ばせる "to speak in a hushed voice". It is the causative form of 忍ぶ "to hide oneself". Rather literary; in everyday speech one says こっそり入れる or 隠す.

examples[].german: One cannot resist aging.
The protagonist kept resisting power until the end.
I couldn't resist the strong drowsiness and fell asleep in class.
en.notes: 抗う means "to brace against an overwhelming force, to resist": 〜に抗う; typical partners are 運命・時代の流れ・権力・老い・眠気・誘惑. Literary and expressive; in everyday speech one says 逆らう or 抵抗する. Often negated in the potential: 抗えない "irresistible, impossible to fend off". Also written in kana, あらがう.

en.meaning: to be associated with, to cling to
examples[].german: There are many legends associated with this castle.
Money-related trouble occurs even among family.
I heard stories about the war from my grandfather.
en.notes: まつわる (the kanji 纏わる are rare) is used almost only attributively as 〜にまつわる + noun: "connected with ..., surrounding ...", e.g. 城にまつわる伝説, お金にまつわる話. Compared with 〜に関する, it is more elevated and has the nuance of stories and memories that gather around something. The concrete meaning "to wind around something" is rare; for that one says まとわりつく.

examples[].german: You must not hesitate over a decision.
He seemed to hesitate to tell the truth.
If you have a problem, please consult us without hesitation.
en.notes: ためらう means to hesitate over an action out of uncertainty or inhibition, and it is almost always written in kana. Typical are 〜するのをためらう, 返事をためらう, 決断をためらう and, in the negative, ためらわずに "without hesitating". The Sino-Japanese word 躊躇(ちゅうちょ)する has the same meaning but is more literary. Compared with 迷う "to waver, to be unable to decide", ためらう stresses the inner shrinking back from taking the step.

examples[].german: The infectious disease is spreading.
A sense of powerlessness has spread through society.
It is difficult to change an organization in which misconduct is rampant.
en.notes: 蔓延する (literally "to spread like vines") describes the uncontrolled spread of something harmful: diseases and pests, but also corruption, drugs or moods (不信感が蔓延する). Intransitive: 〜が蔓延する, the space takes に (社会に蔓延する). Exclusively negative; neutral spreading is 広がる or 普及する. In official language and media also written まん延 (まん延防止等重点措置).

examples[].german: I explained in order to dispel the anxiety.
Seeing the demonstration dispelled my worry that it would be hard to operate.
The new president is trying to shake off the company's old image.
en.notes: 払拭する literally means "to wipe away" and is used figuratively for completely removing negative notions: 不安・疑念・不信感・悪いイメージを払拭する. Transitive with を; passive 不安が払拭される. Formal, typical of media, politics and business language; in everyday speech one says 不安をなくす or 消す. It is not used for physically wiping off dirt.

examples[].german: They smashed the enemy's defensive line.
In the factory, stones are crushed fine by machine.
The Japan national team crushed the powerhouse team 3-0.
en.notes: 粉砕する literally means "to smash into powder". Technically it stands for grinding and crushing (石・氷・ごみを粉砕する, 粉砕機 "crusher, mill"). Figuratively it means to defeat an opponent or resistance utterly (敵・野望・反対運動を粉砕する), forceful and often used in sports and combat rhetoric. Transitive; passive 粉砕される. More everyday is 砕く "to break, to crush".

examples[].german: It is a work in which many years of experience are condensed.
Years of gratitude were condensed into the short greeting.
On the surface of a cold glass, water vapor in the air condenses.
en.notes: 凝縮する means "to condense, to compress". Physically, gas turns into liquid (水蒸気が凝縮する). Figuratively very often in the passive: experiences, feelings or content are condensed into a small space (〜に〜が凝縮されている). It can be used both transitively (内容を凝縮する) and intransitively. Do not confuse it with 濃縮 "to concentrate, to thicken" (濃縮ジュース).

examples[].german: He hesitated before making the decision.
She hesitated for a moment, but then raised her hand and asked a question.
For months he wavered over whether he should change jobs.
en.notes: 逡巡する means "to hesitate, to waver indecisively" and is literary to bookish. Mostly without an object: 決断を前に逡巡する, 〜か逡巡する; as a noun in 逡巡の末 "after long hesitation". Everyday equivalents are ためらう and 迷う; 躊躇する means the same but is much more common.

examples[].german: The constitution guarantees freedom of association.
People can freely form political parties because freedom of association is recognized.
Under the military regime, freedom of assembly and association was taken away.
en.notes: 結社の自由 is the right to found and join associations such as parties, clubs or labor unions; Article 21 of the Japanese Constitution guarantees it together with freedom of assembly (集会の自由). 結社 alone means "association, society" and sounds formal or somewhat old-fashioned (秘密結社 "secret society"). Typical: 結社の自由を保障する, 結社の自由を奪う.

examples[].german: They denounce the politicians' corruption.
The citizens' group sharply denounced the company's discriminatory treatment.
At the meeting, he was called to account as the person responsible.
en.notes: 糾弾する means to publicly and sharply denounce misconduct or those responsible: 不正・汚職・差別を糾弾する, 責任者を糾弾する. Transitive, often with 厳しく; passive 糾弾される "to be pilloried". Stronger and more public than 非難する "to criticize, to blame"; 追及する stresses persistently pressing for responsibility. Formal, typical of the press and politics.

en.meaning: to detain, to restrain, to bind
examples[].german: The suspect was detained.
This contract binds both parties for three years.
The meeting dragged on, and I was tied up all day.
en.notes: 拘束する means to hold someone or restrict their freedom. In police use: 容疑者・身柄を拘束する "to take into custody" (the formal arrest is 逮捕する). Figuratively "to bind, to take up": contracts, rules or work tie someone down (時間を拘束される; 拘束時間 "total time on duty"). Transitive, often in the passive. 束縛する, by contrast, stresses more personal, emotional restriction (恋人を束縛する).

examples[].german: She begged for help.
With tears in his eyes, he begged for another chance.
The residents implored the city to halt the construction.
en.notes: 懇願する means "to ask earnestly and humbly, to implore". Pattern: 人に〜を懇願する or with a quotation 〜てくださいと懇願する. Much stronger than 頼む or お願いする. Similar are 嘆願する (a formal request, often written and from groups to authorities) and 哀願する (to plead piteously). Formal, literary.

examples[].german: This dictionary covers the entire vocabulary.
This guide covers all the procedures necessary for the application.
It was impossible to cover the entire exam range, so I studied only the important parts.
en.notes: 網羅する means "to cover without gaps, to include completely": 全分野・情報・必要事項を網羅する; adverbially 網羅的に "comprehensively, exhaustively". Typical of reference works, lists, manuals and exam material. Compared with 含む "to contain", it stresses completeness; someone who collects only a few examples is 網羅していない. Formal, common in factual and promotional texts.

en.meaning: to hold fast to, to maintain
examples[].german: I hold fast to my position.
The government stated that it would adhere to its existing policy.
Since its founding, this shop has kept to its tradition of handmade products.
en.notes: 堅持する means "to hold steadfastly to something": 方針・原則・立場・伝統を堅持する. Transitive. Very formal, typical of government and corporate statements. 維持する "to maintain" is more neutral and also usual for states; 固執する "to stick stubbornly" sounds obstinate and rather negative, whereas 堅持 sounds positive and principled.

en.meaning: to look on, to stand by
examples[].german: You must not just stand by and watch the problem.
The students who had looked on at the bullying also felt responsible.
He didn't join the discussion and merely looked on.
en.notes: 傍観する means to merely watch something without intervening, usually with a critical undertone ("doing nothing"). Pattern: 〜を傍観する, often ただ傍観する or 傍観している場合ではない "this is no time to stand by". Related are 傍観者 "uninvolved bystander" and 傍観者効果 "bystander effect". Unlike 見物する (to watch out of interest) or 見守る (to watch over benevolently), 傍観 stresses a lack of engagement.

examples[].german: There is a person operating behind the scenes.
Foreign spies seem to have been working in the shadows behind the incident.
On the internet, fraud groups are active behind the scenes.
en.notes: 暗躍する means to be active in secret, usually with dishonest aims: "to pull strings in the background, to work in the shadows". Intransitive: 〜が暗躍する, often with 裏で, 背後で or 陰で. Typical subjects are スパイ, 黒幕 or 詐欺グループ. Clearly negative and literary (press, crime fiction). The counterpart is 活躍する "to be successfully active, to distinguish oneself" (positive and public).

en.meaning: to rise to prominence, to emerge
examples[].german: A new power has emerged.
With the rise of young players, the veterans get fewer appearances.
Populism is on the rise in many places.
en.notes: 台頭する means that a new force gains importance and comes to the fore: 新興国・新勢力・若手・ナショナリズムが台頭する. Intransitive, often as 台頭してくる (increasingly); as a noun very common: 〜の台頭 "the rise of ...". Typical of business, political and sports reporting, neutral to slightly cautionary. Similar: 躍進する "to make great strides", 浮上する "to surface, to come into play". Older spelling: 擡頭.

en.meaning: to decline, to fall into decay
examples[].german: The empire's decline began.
The once-prestigious team has declined greatly in the past few years.
With the spread of smartphones, the company declined rapidly.
en.notes: 凋落する originally means "to wither" (leaves, flowers) and today mainly the decline of power, reputation or success: 帝国・名門・企業・人気が凋落する. Intransitive; very common as a noun 〜の凋落 or 凋落ぶり. Very formal and literary. Similar: 没落する (the fall of a family or class), 衰退する (gradual decline, e.g. of an industry or region).

en.meaning: to become tight; to be strained
examples[].german: The finances are tight.
The number of patients has risen sharply, and hospital beds are running short.
Because there was a risk that the power supply would be strained, people were urged to save electricity.
en.notes: 逼迫する describes a tight, strained situation with no room to spare: 財政・家計・医療・電力需給・病床が逼迫する. Intransitive, usually used as 逼迫している; the noun is 〜の逼迫. It is also used for situations that are coming to a head: 事態が逼迫する. Formal and typical of news reporting; often written ひっ迫. Similar is 切迫する (pressing in terms of time, imminent); in everyday speech people more often say 苦しい or 足りない.

examples[].german: The limitation period for claims for damages is three years.
Even after leaving the company, the right to claim unpaid overtime remains.
After discussions, he decided to waive his claim.
en.notes: 請求権 is the right to demand something from someone, mostly money: 損害賠償請求権, 代金請求権, 請求権を行使する/放棄する. It can lapse through the statute of limitations (請求権が時効で消滅する). The verb 請求する means "to demand, bill"; 権利 alone is more general, whereas 請求権 is the legal claim. Also well known in politics, for example in postwar compensation issues (個人の請求権).

en.meaning: to come to light; to be exposed; to reveal
examples[].german: The organization's problems came to light.
The recent disaster exposed the weakness of the town's disaster-prevention system.
He could not answer the reporters' questions and so revealed his lack of knowledge.
en.notes: 露呈する means that something hidden, usually negative, comes out into the open: 弱点・問題点・矛盾・準備不足が露呈する (intransitive). Used transitively, 〜を露呈する means "to reveal unintentionally" (知識不足を露呈する). Unlike 公開する or 明らかにする (to make public deliberately), it happens against one's will. Formal, typical of commentaries and reports; similar is 露見する "to be found out" (a lie, a crime).

examples[].german: The plan stalled.
The negotiations broke down halfway because the terms could not be agreed on.
Because of an injury, his athletic career was temporarily brought to a standstill.
en.notes: 頓挫する means that an ongoing project suddenly stalls or fails: 計画・交渉・事業・改革が頓挫する. Intransitive; the cause is marked with で (資金不足で頓挫する). It emphasizes a breakdown in the middle of the process (途中で頓挫する). Formal, typical of news. 挫折する, by contrast, refers more to personal failure and giving up a goal.

examples[].german: The government collapsed.
Because of a single lie, the trust between the two of them fell apart.
After the key players left, the team's defense collapsed.
en.notes: 瓦解する (literally "like roof tiles sliding down") means that a structure as a whole collapses as soon as one part gives way: 政権・組織・体制・信頼関係が瓦解する. Intransitive; used almost only for abstract structures, not for buildings (for those, use 崩れる or 倒壊する). 崩壊する is similar but more general and can also be used for concrete things. Formal, written language.

en.meaning: to be fed up; to recoil
examples[].german: I was fed up with his persistence.
Being made to listen to the same story every day, I really am fed up by now.
Put off by the crowds at the tourist spot, I went back to the hotel early.
en.notes: 辟易する means to have had enough of something and to shrink back from it inwardly: "to be annoyed, to be sick of it". Pattern: 〜に辟易する (しつこさ・長話・暑さに辟易する). Intransitive. A more elevated expression for うんざりする, which is more common in everyday speech; 閉口する is similar ("not knowing what to say anymore"). Occasionally written in katakana ヘキエキ for a lighter tone.

en.meaning: to toy with; to tease; to be tossed about
examples[].german: It was a life tossed about by fate.
The little boat was tossed about by the stormy waves.
The young boxer made a fool of the champion with his quick movements.
en.notes: 翻弄する means to toss someone or something about at will, to play with them. Very common in the passive: 運命・時代・波・噂に翻弄される "to become the plaything of ...". Active: 相手を翻弄する "to make a fool of the opponent, to run rings around them" (sports, negotiations); the means is marked with で. Transitive, literary and figurative. Similar is もてあそぶ "to play with something", often with feelings.

en.meaning: to run rampant; to be rife
examples[].german: There are areas where crime runs rampant.
Unscrupulous companies are running rampant, and harm to consumers is increasing.
In the Sengoku period, bandits ran rampant in every region.
en.notes: 跋扈する means that undesirable people or forces act unchecked and without consideration: "to run rampant, to take over". Intransitive, usually 〜が跋扈する; typical subjects are 盗賊・悪徳業者・偽物・犯罪・フェイクニュース. Often used in the intensified form 跳梁跋扈. Very much written language and pejorative. Difference: 蔓延する describes spreading (disease, mood), whereas 跋扈する describes the brazen activity of actors.

examples[].german: There were people who longed for freedom.
The team has craved a championship for years.
Walking on through the desert, they craved a single drop of water.
en.notes: 渇望する literally means "to desire thirstily" and describes a burning, long-unsatisfied longing: 自由・平和・愛情・勝利を渇望する. Transitive with を; also used as a noun, 〜への渇望. Stronger and more literary than 望む or 欲しがる. Similar are 切望する (to wish urgently, more matter-of-fact and formal) and 熱望する (to wish ardently).

en.meaning: to be evenly matched; to rival
examples[].german: The strength of the two sides is evenly matched.
The two sides were evenly matched in ability right to the end of the game.
Opinions for and against were evenly balanced, so no conclusion was reached.
en.notes: 拮抗する means that two sides are roughly equal in strength and balance each other: 実力・勢力・賛否が拮抗する; with a partner, AとBが拮抗する or AがBと拮抗する. Intransitive. Typical of sports, elections and polls (拮抗した試合 "a close, balanced match"); in medicine, 拮抗薬 "antagonist". Formal; in everyday speech people more often say 互角 or いい勝負.

examples[].german: There are companies that monopolize the market.
A small group of nobles had monopolized politics.
Whoever monopolizes information holds power.
en.notes: 壟断する goes back to an anecdote in Mencius: a merchant climbed a mound (壟断), surveyed the market and raked in all the profits. Hence "to seize profits or power for oneself, to monopolize": 利益・市場・政権を壟断する. Transitive and pejorative. Very rare and elevated written language; today people almost always say 独占する.

examples[].german: His words hint at something.
The opening scene of the film already hints at the ending.
I told myself that I would be all right.
en.notes: 暗示する means "to hint indirectly, to point to something": 結末・危険・将来を暗示する; things are often the subject (タイトルが内容を暗示している). The opposite is 明示する "to state explicitly". 示唆する is similar but more matter-of-fact (data suggest something), whereas 暗示 is more figurative and literary. In psychology: 暗示をかける "to suggest, to talk into", 自己暗示 "autosuggestion".

examples[].german: Registration of the transfer of ownership of the real estate was carried out.
Until the loan is paid off, ownership of the car rests with the loan company.
The siblings are fighting over ownership of their late father's land.
en.notes: 所有権 is legal ownership of a thing: 所有権を持つ/取得する/主張する, 所有権が移る, 所有権移転登記 ("land register entry of the transfer of ownership"). Legally it must be clearly distinguished from 占有 ("actual possession"): someone who rents a car has it in possession but is not the owner. For rights in intellectual works one says 著作権, not 所有権.

examples[].german: The survey results suggest that a problem exists.
The change in sales indicates a change in customers' tastes.
The teacher hinted that there is another way to solve it.
en.notes: 示唆する means "to point to, to suggest, to hint"; the subject is often data, results or experts: 可能性・存在・必要性を示唆する. It is a pointer, not proof; 証明する would be "to prove". Set phrase: 示唆に富む "insightful, thought-provoking". More matter-of-fact than 暗示する and typical of science, reports and news.

en.meaning: to ignore; to give the silent treatment
examples[].german: His proposal was ignored.
The company kept ignoring the employees' appeals.
The minister ignored the reporters' questions and left the hall.
en.notes: 黙殺する means to deliberately say nothing and not react to something: 意見・提案・抗議・批判を黙殺する; very often in the passive, 黙殺される. Stronger than 無視する: it emphasizes deliberate disregard, often by an authority or institution. Formal, typical of politics and the press; historically known through the Japanese government's reaction to the Potsdam Declaration in 1945.

en.meaning: to reject out of hand; to brush off
examples[].german: He rejected the other side's demand out of hand.
The president dismissed my plan as unrealistic.
The champion easily brushed aside the challenger.
en.notes: 一蹴する literally means "to kick away with one kick". Main meaning: to dismiss proposals, demands or criticism out of hand (要求・提案・批判を一蹴する), often with the reason as a quotation (〜と一蹴する). In sports also "to beat an opponent with ease". Transitive. Blunter and more dismissive than 断る or 拒否する; journalistic and formal. Do not confuse with 一周 "one lap" (same reading).

examples[].german: The man bullied the shop clerk by shouting at her.
It is power harassment when a boss yells at and threatens his subordinates.
A major power is intimidating a small country with its military might.
en.notes: 恫喝する means to intimidate someone with loud threats or a show of power: 部下・店員・相手国を恫喝する; the means is marked with で (大声で, 武力で). Transitive. Unlike 脅迫する (legal: threatening a concrete harm, blackmail), 恫喝 emphasizes shouting at someone and pressure from a position of superiority. Written language; in everyday speech people say 脅す.

examples[].german: There is a tendency to exclude heretics.
A movement to boycott foreign products arose.
He lost the factional struggle and was pushed out of the party.
en.notes: 排斥する means to deliberately shut out and keep away people, groups or things: 移民・異分子・外国製品を排斥する; the origin is marked with から (党から排斥される). Transitive, often in the passive. Similar are 排除する (more matter-of-fact "to remove, to exclude") and 追放する ("to banish, to expel"). Typical of political and historical contexts, e.g. 排斥運動 "boycott or exclusion movement".

en.meaning: to change over time; to undergo transition
examples[].german: Values change with the times.
Japanese honorific language has changed greatly from era to era.
In this exhibition you can trace how the town's appearance changed over time.
en.notes: 変遷 refers to gradual change over a long period, usually of eras, systems, language or values. It is written language and often appears as a noun: 〜の変遷をたどる "to trace the development of ..."; as an intransitive する-verb it is used as 時代とともに変遷する. Unlike 変化 "change" (neutral, also short-term), 変遷 emphasizes a succession of stages in history. In everyday speech people more often say 移り変わる.

en.meaning: to descend into dispute; to get out of hand (debate); to become entangled
examples[].german: The discussion got completely out of hand.
The meeting over the budget proposal descended into wrangling, and the conclusion was postponed to the next time.
The residents' briefing became heated over the problem of construction noise.
en.notes: 紛糾 describes a meeting, debate or negotiation getting out of control and bogged down through quarrels and conflicting positions. Typical are 会議が紛糾する, 議論が紛糾する, 審議が紛糾した; intransitive with が, the point of dispute is marked with をめぐって or で. Unlike 混乱 "confusion" (general, also for traffic or systems), 紛糾 is always about a dispute of opinion. Written language, frequent in news.

en.meaning: to become intricately tangled; to become complicated
examples[].german: Interests are intricately intertwined.
Right after the accident, information was confused and conflicting.
This novel interweaves several timelines, so it is a little hard to read.
en.notes: 錯綜 means that many threads, such as information, interests and relationships, run into one another and can hardly be untangled. Almost always in the state 錯綜している or attributively: 錯綜した情報 "conflicting, jumbled reports"; typical after accidents and disasters is 情報が錯綜する. 複雑 is the general "complicated"; 錯綜 emphasizes the tangle of many crossing elements. Written language.

examples[].german: The negotiations have been deadlocked for three months.
The front line stalled, and neither army could advance.
Even after the second half began, the game remained deadlocked.
en.notes: 膠着する means that a situation is stuck and no longer moving: in negotiations, war fronts, scores or debates. 膠 means "glue", so literally "to stick fast"; this basic meaning now appears only in technical texts, as does 膠着語 "agglutinative language". Intransitive, mostly in the form 膠着している; 膠着状態に陥る "to fall into a stalemate" is also very common. News-language, formal; in conversation people more often say 行き詰まる.

examples[].german: It is necessary to draw a strict line between public and private.
In reporting, facts and opinions must be strictly separated.
The court strictly distinguished between legal responsibility and moral responsibility.
en.notes: 峻別 means to keep two things sharply and uncompromisingly apart. Typical patterns are AとBを峻別する and the fixed combination 公私を峻別する "to strictly separate work and private life". Written language, frequent in legal, scholarly and ethical texts. More neutral are 区別する "to distinguish" and 分ける; 峻別 emphasizes that no mixing whatsoever is tolerated.

examples[].german: The unlawful occupant of the land was asked to leave.
To occupy a road for construction work, permission from the police and the city office is needed.
That company holds sixty percent of the domestic market.
en.notes: 占有 means to actually have something in one's control or to occupy a space for oneself: 土地を占有する, 不法占有, 占有権. Legally it is to be distinguished from ownership (所有); one can possess something without being the owner. In economics it appears in 市場占有率 ("market share", today often シェア). Not to be confused with 占領 ("military occupation").

en.meaning: to pity; to have compassion for
examples[].german: A heart that feels compassion for the weak is important.
The king took pity on the people suffering from hunger and distributed the rice in the storehouses.
His pride would not allow him to be pitied by others.
en.notes: 恤む (あわれむ) means "to pity, to have mercy", usually toward the weak or those in need: 弱者を恤む. The spelling with 恤 (cf. 救恤 "relief for the needy") is very rare and outside the Jōyō list; 哀れむ, 憐れむ or kana are usual. Transitive godan verb with を; the passive 恤まれる "to be pitied" is often felt to be insulting. Written language and somewhat old-fashioned; in everyday speech people say 同情する or かわいそうに思う.

examples[].german: He flaunts his own power.
The country displayed its military strength with a large military parade.
He rolled up his sleeve as if to show off his expensive watch.
en.notes: 誇示 means to demonstratively show off something, such as power, wealth or skill, so that others see it. Typical are 力を誇示する, 軍事力を誇示する, 存在感を誇示する. The word is written language and usually sounds critical. Unlike 自慢する "to boast, to brag" (mainly in words, everyday), 誇示 emphasizes display through deeds or objects.

examples[].german: He saw through his lie.
The master detective saw through the culprit's trick at a glance.
She had seen through the other party's true aim.
en.notes: 看破 means to see through a hidden truth, such as a lie, a trick or an intention, with a sharp eye. Typical objects are 嘘を看破する, 正体を看破する, 意図を看破する, トリックを看破する. Written language and somewhat literary; in everyday speech people say 見破る or 見抜く. 看破 emphasizes the mental sharpness of the one who sees through.

en.meaning: to evoke; to arouse; to call (attention) to
examples[].german: It is necessary to call people's attention to it.
The Meteorological Agency called for vigilance against heavy rain.
That photo evoked memories of my childhood.
en.notes: 喚起 means to call something up in others: attention, interest, memories, public opinion. Fixed phrases are 注意を喚起する "to warn, to urge caution" (as a noun 注意喚起 "warning notice"), 関心を喚起する, 世論を喚起する, 記憶を喚起する. Written language, typical of government agencies and news. Beware when listening: homophone 換気 "ventilation".

en.meaning: to seize control of; to have a firm grip on
examples[].german: He seized real power.
The new department head quickly got his subordinates under control.
It was reported that the military had taken control of the capital.
en.notes: 掌握 literally means "to hold in the palm of the hand": to have power, an organization or a situation firmly in one's grip. Typical are 実権を掌握する, 政権を掌握する, 部下を掌握する "to have one's people under control" and 状況を掌握する "to have the situation under control". Written language; more everyday is 握る (権力を握る). Do not confuse with 把握, which only means "to grasp, to understand", not to control.

en.meaning: unmoved; unconcerned (usually critical: 恬として恥じない "shameless")
examples[].german: Even when criticized, he remains completely unmoved.
Even when he breaks a promise, he feels not the slightest shame.
Some politicians use public funds privately and feel not the slightest shame about it.
en.notes: 恬として describes someone remaining completely unmoved where one would actually expect shame or pangs of conscience. It almost always appears in the phrase 恬として恥じない "not to be in the least ashamed, to be shameless", less often 恬として顧みない. It is written language and always sounds critical; for positive composure one says 平然と or 落ち着いて. The rare character 恬 belongs purely to reading vocabulary.

en.meaning: to become eager; to be feverishly intent
examples[].german: He is desperately intent on getting ahead.
The government is desperately trying to stop the fall of the yen.
He vehemently denied the rumor.
en.notes: 躍起になる means to go all out for something feverishly and doggedly, often under pressure or out of annoyance. Typical patterns are 〜に躍起になる, 〜しようと躍起になる and adverbial 躍起になって否定する "to deny vehemently". Usually slightly critical: the zeal seems exaggerated or desperate. More neutral is 熱心に; similar, but more petulant and childish, is むきになる.

examples[].german: It is necessary to overhaul the organization.
The new president largely replaced the management team.
The app's design was renewed and has become easier to use.
en.notes: 刷新 means to fundamentally renew a system, an organization or an appearance and to get rid of what has become stale. Typical objects are 組織を刷新する, 人事を刷新する, イメージを刷新する; as a noun 政治の刷新. Written language, frequent in business and politics. Unlike 改善 "to improve" (gradual) or 更新 "to update, to renew", 刷新 stands for a clear fresh start; a close synonym is 一新.

examples[].german: An atmosphere of unease pervades society.
After the war, a sense of emptiness had spread among the people.
A policy of avoiding any trouble has spread throughout the whole organization.
en.notes: 瀰漫 means that a mood or attitude spreads everywhere and permeates everything, almost always something negative such as unease, distrust or resignation. Pattern: 〜が社会に瀰漫する, mostly in the state 瀰漫している. Very much written and literary language; JMdict also lists the spelling 弥漫. In everyday speech people say 広がる, and for diseases and evils 蔓延する.

en.meaning: to enjoy to the fullest; to celebrate
examples[].german: Enjoy your youth to the fullest.
The war was over, and people reveled in their freedom.
Since retiring, my father has been enjoying a life devoted to his hobbies.
en.notes: 謳歌 literally means "to sing praises": to enjoy something beautiful to the fullest and, as it were, celebrate it. Typical objects are 青春を謳歌する, 自由を謳歌する, 人生を謳歌する, 平和を謳歌する. Elevated, but also common in newspapers and advertising. Unlike 楽しむ "to enjoy" (everyday, also for small things), 謳歌 stands for a comprehensive, happy state of life; 享受, by contrast, soberly emphasizes receiving benefits.

examples[].german: The way land encumbered with a usufructuary right may be used was disputed.
Superficies is a type of right of use that allows one to build a building on another person's land.
Even the owner cannot arbitrarily obstruct use by the holder of a usufructuary right.
en.notes: 用益権 is a right to use someone else's property, above all land, and draw income from it without being the owner. In Japanese civil law this covers the superficies right (地上権), the perpetual tenancy right (永小作権) and the easement (地役権), together called 用益物権. The counterpart is security rights (担保物権) such as the mortgage. A purely technical term from law and real estate.

examples[].german: Many politicians pander to the masses.
He just keeps currying favor with his boss and never states his own opinion.
I want to make works that do not pander to trends.
en.notes: 迎合 means to adapt to the opinions or tastes of others in order to please them, and is clearly pejorative. The target is marked with に: 大衆に迎合する, 世論に迎合する, 権力に迎合する, 時流に迎合する. Written language. Related are こびる "to ingratiate oneself" (more personal) and ご機嫌を取る; 迎合 emphasizes giving up one's own position.

en.meaning: to read (feelings); to empathize; to scoop up
examples[].german: To sense the other person's feelings.
I picked up on her unspoken feelings from her facial expression.
I scooped water out of the well and sprinkled it on the field.
en.notes: 汲み取る has two meanings: literally "to scoop or pump out a liquid" (水を汲み取る; hence 汲み取り式トイレ "pit toilet") and figuratively "to sensitively pick up feelings or intentions": 気持ちを汲み取る, 意図を汲み取る, 真意を汲み取る. The figurative meaning is the more common one today and suits a style of communication in which much remains unspoken. Close are 察する "to sense" and 汲む (気持ちを汲む); the spelling くみ取る is also widespread.

en.meaning: to announce; to pronounce; to hand down
examples[].german: The judge handed down the verdict.
He was suddenly given notice of dismissal by the company.
For abusive language during the match, the player was sent off.
en.notes: 言い渡す means to communicate a decision officially and from above, so that the recipient has to accept it. Typical are 判決を言い渡す "to pronounce a verdict", 解雇を言い渡す, 別れを言い渡す; the recipient is marked with に: 部下に異動を言い渡す. Often in the passive 〜を言い渡される. Unlike 伝える "to tell" (neutral) or 発表する "to announce" (public), 言い渡す emphasizes the speaker's authority.

en.meaning: to pin down; to track down
examples[].german: I pinned down the cause.
By going through the records, I found out why the package had not arrived.
From security camera footage, the police tracked down the culprit's whereabouts.
en.notes: 突き止める means to establish something hidden with certainty by persistent investigation. Typical objects are 原因を突き止める, 犯人を突き止める, 居場所や所在を突き止める, 正体を突き止める. It emphasizes the result of the search; the process itself is 調べる or 探る. Neutral, common in everyday speech as well as in the news; transitive with を.

en.meaning: to break through; to find a way out of
examples[].german: I am thinking of a measure to break the deadlock.
A new proposal broke the impasse in the talks.
To break out of the current state of continuing losses, the company moved into a new business.
en.notes: 打開 means to break open a stuck, hopeless situation through a new step. Typical objects are 局面を打開する, 現状を打開する, 難局を打開する, 行き詰まりを打開する; very common as a noun in 打開策 "way out, approach to a solution". Written language, especially in politics and business. Unlike 解決する "to solve", 打開 means overcoming the blockage, not necessarily the final solution.

en.meaning: to back (a candidate); to field; to install
examples[].german: To back a new leader.
The opposition fielded its own candidate in the gubernatorial election.
The retainers installed the young prince as ruler and seized power.
en.notes: 擁立 means to put someone forward as a candidate or leader while actively supporting him. Today mainly in politics: 候補者を擁立する "to field a candidate", 独自候補を擁立する.
