Historically it also means to raise a young heir to the throne. Written language; unlike 推薦する "to recommend", here the group putting the person forward carries the candidacy itself.

examples[].german: We held repeated negotiations with the other side.
The person in charge is negotiating the price with the business partner.
In the year-end budget negotiations, coordination between the ministries and the Ministry of Finance continued.
en.notes: 折衝 refers to hard-fought business, official or diplomatic negotiations in which interests are weighed against each other. Typical are 〜と折衝する, 折衝を重ねる, 予算折衝, 外交折衝. Written language; in everyday speech people say 交渉する. 折衝 emphasizes the back and forth until a compromise, often at working level between agencies or companies.

examples[].german: To enjoy the benefits of freedom.
We enjoy the convenience brought by the development of science and technology.
All citizens should equally enjoy the right to receive an education.
en.notes: 享受 means to receive and enjoy benefits, rights or comforts. Typical objects are 恩恵を享受する, 自由を享受する, 権利を享受する, 豊かさを享受する. Written language, frequent in essays, law and politics. Unlike 謳歌 (exuberant celebration), 享受 is sober: one comes to enjoy something that falls to one. Do not confuse with 甘受 "to accept something unpleasant".

en.meaning: to accept; to resign oneself to
examples[].german: There is nothing to do but accept the result.
As the person responsible, I intend to accept any criticism.
The workers who had long put up with low wages finally raised their voices.
en.notes: 甘受 means to accept something unpleasant, such as criticism, punishment or an unfavorable result, without protest, because one cannot change it or considers it justified. Typical are 批判を甘受する, 処分を甘受する, 運命を甘受する, often with 〜するしかない or 〜するつもりだ. Written language. Despite the character 甘 "sweet", nothing pleasant is meant; do not confuse with 享受, which receives something positive. More everyday are 受け入れる and 我慢する.

en.meaning: to take into account; to consider in light of
examples[].german: To judge in light of past experience.
In view of the seriousness of the situation, the tournament has been canceled.
Taking last year's reflections into account, we started preparing earlier this year.
en.notes: 鑑みる means to take something as a standard or lesson and judge accordingly. It appears almost only as 〜に鑑みて or, in writing, 〜に鑑み: 現状に鑑み, 事の重大さに鑑みて "in view of the seriousness of the matter". Very formal, typical of official letters, press releases and speeches; in everyday speech people say 〜を考えて or 〜を考慮して. The variant 〜を鑑みて is widespread but considered non-standard.

examples[].german: The employee's overstepping of authority was seen as a problem.
Signing a contract without the department head's permission is clearly an act exceeding one's authority.
I think it is overstepping for the vice chairman to decide in place of the chairman.
en.notes: 越権 is the exceeding of one's own powers and appears almost always as 越権行為 ("act in excess of authority"). It can also be used predicatively: それは越権だ ("that is not your place"). It fits civil servants as well as employees or volunteers who make decisions they are not responsible for. Related: 権限を超える, colloquially 出しゃばる ("to butt in").

en.meaning: to flutter; to sway; to yield
examples[].german: Her hair flutters in the wind.
He is a man who never yields to money or status.
Many lawmakers went over to the up-and-coming new party.
en.notes: 靡く has two meanings: literally "to wave in the wind, to flutter, to sway" (旗が風に靡く, 髪が靡く) and figuratively "to bow, to yield, to turn toward someone" (権力に靡く, 金に靡かない, 誘いに靡く). The trigger is always marked with に; the verb is intransitive. It is mostly written in kana, なびく. Figuratively it often sounds pejorative (opportunistic conformity) or romantic (giving in to someone's courtship).

en.meaning: to earn; to make money; to gain (time, points)
examples[].german: We need to buy time.
She earns her tuition with a part-time job.
Let's pick up a few bonus points in this stage.
en.notes: 稼ぐ primarily means "to earn money": 生活費を稼ぐ, アルバイトで稼ぐ, 稼いだお金. Figuratively it means "to get something for oneself": 時間を稼ぐ "to gain time", 点数を稼ぐ "to score points" (also in the sense of "to curry favor"). Transitive with を, neutral and everyday. In contrast to 儲ける "to make a profit" (more from business deals), 稼ぐ emphasizes one's own work; the noun is 稼ぎ "earnings".

examples[].german: The market has reached saturation.
If you keep dissolving salt in water, it eventually becomes saturated and stops dissolving.
Parking lots in the city center are almost completely full at midday on weekdays.
en.notes: 飽和 means that something has reached its capacity and can absorb nothing more. Originally a technical term of chemistry (飽和溶液 "saturated solution"), also used figuratively for markets, cities or amounts of information. Very common as a noun: 飽和状態, 飽和点; as a verb mostly in the state 飽和している. The opposite is 不飽和 (e.g. 不飽和脂肪酸 "unsaturated fatty acid"); in everyday speech people simply say いっぱいになる.

en.meaning: to use widely; to use for general purposes
examples[].german: This technology is widely used.
This is a standard part, so you can get it at any shop.
This software is highly versatile and is used in a wide range of industries.
en.notes: 汎用 means "usable for many purposes, universal". It lives almost exclusively as a noun or attribute: 汎用の部品, 汎用品 "standard article", 汎用機, 汎用性が高い "highly versatile", 汎用的な. As a verb, 汎用する appears only rarely, mostly in the passive in technical texts (汎用されている). The counterpart is 専用 "intended for one purpose only"; in everyday speech people say 幅広く使う instead of 汎用する.

en.meaning: to take into consideration; to make allowances
examples[].german: The sentence was reduced in consideration of the circumstances.
The defendant's circumstances leave room for mitigating circumstances.
The teacher took the reason for the lateness into account and let it go with a warning this time.
en.notes: 酌量 means to take special circumstances into account with goodwill, especially in determining a sentence. It is almost always found in the fixed compound 情状酌量 "consideration of mitigating circumstances": 情状を酌量する, 情状酌量の余地がある／ない. The character 酌 is the same as in 酌む "to empathize with (others' feelings)". Legal and written language; in everyday speech people say 考慮する or 事情を汲む.

en.meaning: to demand payment; to press (for payment)
examples[].german: To press for payment.
I received an email from the library demanding the return of a book.
When I was behind on my taxes, a demand notice came from the city hall.
en.notes: 督促 means to formally and emphatically remind someone of a due obligation, especially payments or returns. Typical are 支払いを督促する, 返済を督促する and the noun 督促状 "reminder letter". Official language of agencies, banks and companies. More everyday is 催促する "to press, to follow up", which also fits among friends; 督促 sounds official and strict.

examples[].german: To choose materials after careful selection.
I weighed several explanations carefully before reaching a conclusion.
He carefully weighed each and every word of his speech.
en.notes: 吟味 means to carefully examine the quality, content or suitability of something before choosing or deciding. Typical are 素材を吟味する, 内容を吟味する, 言葉を吟味する and 吟味された食材 "carefully selected ingredients" (popular in gastronomy and advertising). Elevated, but common. Unlike 検討する "to consider options" or 確認する "to check", 吟味 emphasizes weighing quality through examination.

en.meaning: to be well versed in; to be thoroughly familiar with
examples[].german: He is well versed in law.
I consulted someone who knows the local situation well.
We are looking for an interpreter fluent in three languages.
en.notes: 精通 means to know a field or certain circumstances thoroughly and in detail. The field is marked with に: 法律に精通する, 業界の事情に精通している, 〜に精通した人物. Mostly in the state 精通している or attributively 精通した; written language, frequent in résumés and personnel descriptions. Unlike 詳しい "to be knowledgeable" (everyday), 精通 sounds like real expertise; merely having heard of something (聞いたことがある) is not enough.

en.meaning: to foster; to cultivate; to create gradually
examples[].german: To build a relationship of trust.
We want to build momentum for supporting child-rearing across the whole community.
Through working together, a sense of unity was fostered in the team.
en.notes: 醸成 originally means "to let ferment, to brew" and today is used mainly figuratively: "to let a mood, trust or awareness arise gradually". Typical are 信頼関係を醸成する, 機運を醸成する, 雰囲気を醸成する, 一体感を醸成する. Written language, popular in politics and corporate texts; for actual beer or sake brewing, people say 醸造. The image of slow fermentation distinguishes it from 作る or 生み出す.

en.meaning: to sweep away; to eliminate completely
examples[].german: To eradicate wrongdoing.
In the stock clearance sale, winter wear is half price.
A single word from the manager swept away the team's anxiety.
en.notes: 一掃 means to remove something undesirable completely in one stroke. Typical objects are 不正を一掃する, 暴力団を一掃する, 不安を一掃する; in retail 在庫一掃セール "clearance sale". Written language, but also common in advertising. Unlike 取り除く, 一掃 emphasizes thoroughness and completeness. Do not confuse with the identically read adverb 一層 "even more".

en.meaning: delegation of authority; devolution of powers
examples[].german: Devolving powers from the central government to local governments is a challenge.
Since authority was delegated to subordinates, decisions are made faster.
Our company president really doesn't want to delegate authority.
en.notes: 権限委譲 means handing decision-making authority down to a lower level: in companies from the boss to employees (部下に権限委譲する), in politics from the state to prefectures and municipalities. In an administrative context the spelling 権限移譲 is often seen, with the same pronunciation. The opposite is centralization (中央集権); related is 地方分権 ("decentralization").

en.meaning: to look back; to reflect on the past
examples[].german: We need time to look back on our lives.
In his memoirs, the former prime minister looks back on the decisions he made at the time.
A retrospective of that painter is being held at the art museum.
en.notes: 回顧 means to look back on past times or events and consciously call them to mind. Typical are 人生を回顧する, 当時を回顧する as well as the nouns 回顧録 "memoirs" and 回顧展 "retrospective". Written language. Unlike 思い出す "to remember" (spontaneous, everyday), 回顧 is an orderly retrospective; 懐古, by contrast, emphasizes nostalgic longing.

examples[].german: To writhe in pain.
He was tormented alone by an unrequited love.
The sleeping kitten's face was so cute that I couldn't help swooning.
en.notes: 悶える means to writhe in physical pain or to suffer mental torment. The trigger is marked with に: 苦痛に悶える, 恋に悶える; intensified, 悶え苦しむ "to writhe in agony". Intransitive, rather literary. In colloquial and internet language it is also used jokingly for "to swoon with delight" (かわいすぎて悶える). More everyday are 苦しむ and 悩む.

en.meaning: to accept with detachment; to resign oneself
examples[].german: To accept one's fate with equanimity.
In his later years, he had a calm expression, as if he had come to terms with everything.
This work shows the author's serene, resigned outlook on life.
en.notes: 諦観 has two sides: originally (Buddhist) "to see clearly through the nature of things", today mostly "to accept one's fate calmly, to be serenely resigned". Typical are 運命を諦観する, 人生を諦観する as well as the noun forms 諦観の境地 "a state of serene resignation" and 諦観した態度. Very much written and literary language. Unlike 諦める "to give up" (everyday, often disappointed), 諦観 carries a note of serene insight.

en.meaning: to be at a loss; to be hard pressed
examples[].german: I was at a loss for an answer.
More and more people are falling into hardship due to unemployment.
Necessity is the mother of invention: only when I was cornered did a good idea come to me.
en.notes: 窮する means to get into a situation from which one sees no way out. The area is marked with に: 返答に窮する "to be at a loss for an answer", 説明に窮する, 生活に窮する "to fall into material hardship". Well known is the proverb 窮すれば通ず "necessity is the mother of invention". Written language; in everyday speech people say 困る.

examples[].german: An article appeared mocking his words and actions.
The prime minister's response was mocked by the opposition as "always a step behind".
That manga artist gained popularity with works that satirize the contradictions of society.
en.notes: 揶揄 means to make someone or something look ridiculous with mocking, ironic remarks. Typical in the media are 〜を揶揄する記事 and the passive 〜と揶揄される "to be mocked as ...". Written language; because of the difficult characters it is often written やゆ. More everyday are からかう "to tease" (mostly harmless) and 皮肉る "to jibe"; 揶揄 is often aimed at public figures or social conditions.

examples[].german: You must not miss a good opportunity.
His behavior is beyond the bounds of common sense.
Because of a mistake in the closing stages, the team missed out on the championship.
en.notes: 逸する has three meanings: "to miss an opportunity" (好機を逸する, 機会を逸する, 優勝を逸する), "to overlook, to omit" and "to deviate", above all in the fixed phrase 常軌を逸する "to go beyond all normal bounds". Transitive with を, written language. It conjugates as a する-verb of the special class: 逸した, 逸して. In everyday speech people say チャンスを逃す.

en.meaning: to result in; to come down to
examples[].german: The discussion came down to the same conclusion.
That the unreasonable plan ended in failure was the natural consequence.
The problem of the falling birthrate ultimately comes down to the question of how we work.
en.notes: 帰結 refers to the result that a train of thought or a development leads to logically. As a verb it is 〜に帰結する "to come down to ..."; very common is the noun in 当然の帰結 "the logical consequence" and 論理的帰結. Written language, typical of arguments and technical texts. Unlike 結果 "result", 帰結 emphasizes the inevitable logical follow-through; 結論 is the conclusion explicitly drawn.

examples[].german: To report facts in a distorted way.
He twisted his face in pain.
An overly strict home environment warped his character.
en.notes: 歪める is the transitive counterpart of 歪む "to warp, to bend": to bring something out of its proper shape. Concretely: 顔を歪める "to contort one's face" (from pain or disgust), 口元を歪める. Figuratively: 事実を歪める, 真実を歪める, 歴史を歪める "to falsify", also 性格を歪める. Neutral to written language; related noun 歪み "distortion".

en.meaning: to shun; to keep at a distance; to dislike
examples[].german: He is shunned by those around him.
Because he said nothing but correct things, he was disliked by his boss.
Some senior colleagues shun talented newcomers.
en.notes: 疎む means to find someone a nuisance and therefore avoid them or keep them at a distance. It is almost always used in the passive: 周囲から疎まれる, 上司に疎まれる "to be unpopular with the boss". Written language; more common is the adjective 疎ましい "annoying, unpleasant". Similar are 嫌う "to dislike" (more general) and 避ける "to avoid"; 疎む emphasizes cool distance. Related: 疎い "to be unfamiliar with", 疎遠 "estranged".

examples[].german: Residents filed a residents' audit request over the misuse of public funds.
Any resident of the city can file a residents' audit request, even alone.
Because the residents' audit request was rejected, the citizens' group went to court.
en.notes: 住民監査請求 is a procedure under the Local Autonomy Act: residents can ask their municipality's audit commissioners (監査委員) to investigate unlawful or inappropriate expenditures and to demand remedies. Any single resident can file one; typical is 住民監査請求を行う/起こす. If it fails, one can then bring a 住民訴訟.

examples[].german: Acts that trample on human rights are not permitted.
The country was overrun by enemy troops.
The powerhouse team ran roughshod over its lower-ranked opponent.
en.notes: 蹂躙 literally means "to trample underfoot" and refers to violently disregarding rights or overrunning a country. Typical are 人権を蹂躙する, 主権を蹂躙する, 国土が蹂躙される. Strongly written and emotional language, frequent in news and historical accounts; in sports also used hyperbolically for a crushing rout. More neutral are 侵害する "to infringe" (for rights) and 踏みにじる (same image, somewhat more everyday).

en.meaning: to run rampant; to be rife
examples[].german: Fraud is rampant on the Internet.
Illegal parking is rampant in this area.
At that time, corruption among officials was rampant.
en.notes: 横行 means that something bad, such as fraud, corruption or violence, spreads unchecked. Pattern: 〜が横行する, mostly in the state 横行している: 詐欺が横行する, 不正が横行する, 違法駐車が横行する. Written language, typical of news and always negative. Unlike 流行する "to be in fashion" (neutral) or 蔓延する (disease, evil), 横行 emphasizes the brazenness with which something happens with impunity.

en.meaning: to include; to contain; to encompass
examples[].german: This concept contains many meanings.
This plan involves many risks.
The new law also brings online transactions within the scope of regulation.
en.notes: 包含 means that something includes other things as a component. Pattern: AはBを包含する, 〜を包含した概念. Very much written language, typical of philosophy, law and science (in mathematics 包含関係 "inclusion relation"). In everyday speech people say 含む; 包括, by contrast, means "to cover comprehensively".

en.meaning: to abolish; to do away with
examples[].german: To abolish the old system.
More and more companies are doing away with empty formalities such as New Year's cards.
The shogun was deposed by his retainers.
en.notes: 廃する means to abolish an existing institution, rule or custom: 制度を廃する, 虚礼を廃する "to abolish empty formalities". Historically it also means "to depose a ruler". Written language; more usual are 廃止する (laws, institutions) and やめる. Do not confuse with the identically read 排する "to exclude, to push aside" (私情を排する).

en.meaning: to check; to hold in check; to restrain
examples[].german: To keep the opponent's moves in check.
The pitcher made several pickoff throws to the runner on first base.
The prime minister's remark is seen as aimed at checking calls for a tax increase.
en.notes: 牽制 means to keep an opponent from acting freely through threatening gestures, statements or maneuvers. Typical are 相手を牽制する, 〜の動きを牽制する, 互いに牽制し合う; in baseball, 牽制球 is the throw to a base that holds the runner. Frequent in political, business and sports reports; newspapers often write けん制. Unlike 阻止する "to prevent", 牽制 only aims to keep the other side in check.

examples[].german: To be concerned about the country's future.
Many experts are concerned that young people are reading less.
A poem survives that laments a hometown ravaged by war.
en.notes: 憂える means "to worry about, to be distressed over" and mostly concerns large, impersonal matters: 国の将来を憂える, 環境破壊を憂える, 少子化を憂える. It is transitive with を and is considerably more serious and literary than 心配する; unlike 悩む it is hardly about one's own problems but about the state of society. There is also the synonymous older form 憂う, for example in 憂うべき事態 "a worrying situation". The noun is 憂い or 憂え "worry", cf. 備えあれば憂いなし.

examples[].german: Measures to deter crime are needed.
The merits of deterrence by nuclear weapons are being debated.
It is thought that stricter penalties can deter drunk driving.
en.notes: 抑止 means to prevent something undesirable, such as crime, war or abuse, in advance through deterrence or countermeasures. Typical are 犯罪を抑止する, 戦争を抑止する and, very commonly, the noun 抑止力 "deterrent effect" (核抑止 "nuclear deterrence"). Written language, in politics and security debates. Unlike 抑制 "to curb, to hold down" (costs, appetite), 抑止 emphasizes prevention through deterrence.

examples[].german: The cells multiply rapidly.
In summer, bacteria multiply easily in food.
Convenience stores have sprung up like mushrooms in front of the station; there are now five of them.
en.notes: 増殖 means that cells or organisms multiply by division or reproduction: 細胞が増殖する, 細菌が増殖する, ウイルスが増殖する. Figuratively, and often ironically, also for things that spread uncontrollably (空き家が増殖する). Intransitive; technical in biology and medicine, otherwise written language. Unlike 増える "to increase", 増殖 emphasizes self-multiplication; 繁殖 refers more to the reproduction of animals and plants.

en.meaning: to grant; to confer; to assign
examples[].german: To grant authority.
New members will be granted 100 points.
Each product is assigned a number for management.
en.notes: 付与する is a formal administrative and technical word for "to allot, to confer (rights, status, points)". Typical: 権限を付与する, 資格を付与する, 番号を付与する; the recipient is marked with に (ユーザーに権限を付与する), very often in the passive: ポイントが付与される. In everyday speech people simply say 与える or あげる; the ceremonial presentation of titles or prizes is 授与する, the issuing of documents 交付する.

en.meaning: to follow; to carry on; to adopt
examples[].german: To follow the policy of one's predecessor.
The new model largely follows the design of the old model.
This year's school festival will also follow the usual way of previous years.
en.notes: 踏襲する means to take over and continue an existing course, precedent or style unchanged: 前例を踏襲する, 方針・路線を踏襲する, デザインを踏襲する. It is a written and news word; more neutral is 受け継ぐ "to inherit, to carry on", and for traditions or offices 継承する. Beware of a notorious reading mistake: the correct reading is とうしゅう, not ふしゅう.

examples[].german: The two parties concluded a pact on electoral cooperation.
The three exchanged a pledge to help one another for life.
The country that broke the pact lost the trust of its neighbors.
en.notes: 盟約 is a solemnly sworn "pact" or "covenant", an elevated, rather literary word. Typical combinations: 盟約を結ぶ "to conclude a pact", 盟約を交わす "to swear to one another", 盟約を破る "to break the pact". It emphasizes the mutual promise, whereas 同盟 denotes the alliance relationship resulting from it. In everyday speech, for promises one says 約束 or 誓い.

examples[].german: A residents' lawsuit led to the municipality's spending being found unlawful.
Before filing a residents' lawsuit, you must first file a residents' audit request.
In the residents' lawsuit, the former mayor was ordered to pay damages.
en.notes: 住民訴訟 is a lawsuit in which residents challenge in court unlawful expenditures or property transactions of their municipality. A prior 住民監査請求 is a prerequisite; only if that fails can one 住民訴訟を起こす/提起する. The plaintiff acts in the public interest, not because of damage to himself. Frequent in local news about mayors and subsidies.

en.meaning: to investigate thoroughly; to get to the bottom of
examples[].german: To get to the truth of the incident.
The opposition strictly called the minister to account for his responsibility.
The citizens' group demanded a thorough investigation into the misuse of subsidies.
en.notes: 糾明する means to investigate wrongdoing or guilt thoroughly and bring it to light: 責任を糾明する, 不正を糾明する, 真相を糾明する. It sounds accusatory; one calls someone to account. Do not confuse with the identically read 究明する, which means neutral research into causes (事故の原因を究明する); 究明 is used for accidents and scientific questions, 糾明 for scandals and questions of guilt. Written language, typical of news, parliament and the judiciary; older spelling 糺明.

examples[].german: To proclaim martial law.
In 1941, Japan declared war on the United States.
The new president declared war on pointless meetings.
en.notes: 布告する is the official "proclaiming, declaring" by a state or authority: 戒厳令を布告する. Today the word lives mainly in 宣戦布告 "declaration of war" (〜に宣戦を布告する), which is also used jokingly in a figurative sense ("to declare war on someone"). The promulgation of laws is 公布する, a general declaration 宣言する, an announcement 発表する.

en.meaning: to suppress; to subdue; to overpower
examples[].german: The rebellion was suppressed.
The police officer quickly overpowered the man holding a knife.
In the first half, the home team completely dominated midfield.
en.notes: 制圧する means to bring something completely under control by force or superiority: 反乱・暴動を制圧する, 首都を制圧する; the police 犯人を制圧する "overpower" a culprit; in sports also "to dominate" (中盤を制圧する). Putting down unrest is also specifically called 鎮圧する; 抑圧する is the political "oppressing" of people and sounds negative; 征服する "to conquer". Passive: 制圧される.

examples[].german: He exposed the wrongdoing.
A former employee revealed the company's inside story in a weekly magazine.
A friend exposed an embarrassing old story about me.
en.notes: 暴露する means to "reveal, spill" something hidden against the will of others: 秘密・不正・正体を暴露する; an exposé book is a 暴露本. Often in the passive (〜に暴露される). Neutral "to disclose" is 明かす, the formal reporting of abuses is 告発する, and colloquially people say ばらす. In technical texts 曝露 stands for "exposure" to harmful substances.

examples[].german: You should not pry into other people's private lives.
I'll refrain from asking about the reason.
The neighbor is nosy and asks who it is every time a visitor comes.
en.notes: 詮索する means to poke around and dig nosily into other people's affairs; the word is almost always pejorative: 他人の私生活を詮索する, あれこれ詮索する, 余計な詮索はしない. A nosy person is 詮索好き. Neutral investigating is 調べる or 調査する, covert spying out is 探る.

en.meaning: to be fixated on; to cling to; to be hung up on
examples[].german: You should not be hung up on form.
You can't move forward if you dwell on past failures.
Don't get caught up in the details; please look at the overall flow.
en.notes: 拘泥する is a written word for "to (excessively) fixate on something, to stick to something" and takes に: 形式に拘泥する, 細部に拘泥する, 過去に拘泥する. It is always negative and often appears negated (〜に拘泥せず). The everyday word is こだわる, which, however, can also mean positively "to be particular about" (素材にこだわる), which 拘泥する never does.

en.meaning: to reflect seriously; to repent deeply
examples[].german: To deeply reflect on one's own conduct.
As a company, we are reflecting deeply on this scandal.
The coach urged the players to reflect seriously.
en.notes: 猛省する is an intensified 反省する: "to take a hard look at oneself, to rethink one's conduct in a sharply self-critical way". Typical in official apologies (深く猛省しております) and in the phrase 猛省を促す "to urge someone to reflect seriously on their conduct". 後悔する, by contrast, is the mere feeling of regret, without the aspect of self-examination.

en.meaning: to decline firmly; to refuse stubbornly
examples[].german: He firmly declined to take the chairmanship.
However many times she was asked, she firmly refused any honorarium.
There are also athletes who declined the People's Honor Award.
en.notes: 固辞する means to "firmly decline" an offer or an honor despite repeated urging: 就任・受賞・謝礼を固辞する. It sounds politely modest, not hostile. Neutral declining is 辞退する, in everyday speech 断る; 拒否する is a blunt, confrontational "refusal".

en.meaning: to devote oneself; to dedicate oneself
examples[].german: To devote oneself to society.
She has devoted herself to community medicine for many years.
Thanks to my mother's devoted nursing care, my father got well.
en.notes: 献身する means to selflessly "devote, sacrifice oneself" to a cause or to people; it is intransitive: 〜に献身する or 〜のために献身する. Even more common than the verb is the adjective 献身的 (献身的な看護, 献身的に支える). 専念する only means "to concentrate entirely on something"; 尽くす is the more everyday "to do one's best for someone".

examples[].german: A countless number of stars could be seen.
An enormous amount of blood was left at the scene of the accident.
After the typhoon, vast amounts of trash were washed up on the shore.
en.notes: 夥しい describes an enormous number or quantity, often of something alarming: 夥しい数の〜, 夥しい量の血, 夥しい人出. It is a written word and is mostly written in kana, おびただしい. In a literary-ironic use it follows 〜こと: 不便なこと夥しい "extremely inconvenient". More sober are 無数の "countless" and 膨大な "huge (amounts of data, costs)".

examples[].german: Subsidies for agriculture were increased.
Using a city subsidy, we installed solar panels on the roof.
The company president was arrested for improperly receiving subsidies.
en.notes: 補助金 is a grant, mostly from the state or a local government, that covers part of the cost of a project: 補助金を出す/交付する, 補助金を受ける/申請する, 補助金の不正受給. 助成金 is similar and is often used for funding from foundations or in the employment field; 交付金 is more a general state allocation to municipalities. Neutral, very common in the news and everyday life.

examples[].german: I want to erase the abominable memory.
Ten years have passed since that dreadful incident.
An ominous legend has remained in the village since ancient times.
en.notes: 忌まわしい expresses strong abhorrence of something one would most like to forget or avoid, often with an undertone of ill omen: 忌まわしい事件, 忌まわしい記憶, 忌まわしい過去. The word is written language and weighty; in everyday speech people say 嫌な. For "ominous" alone, 不吉な is more usual.

examples[].german: Spirited shouts rang out.
The firefighters went bravely into the flames.
He talks big, but in reality he does nothing.
en.notes: 勇ましい means "brave, valiant", but it often also describes sound and bearing: "spirited, vigorous, stirring" (勇ましい行進曲, 勇ましい掛け声). Adverbially: 勇ましく戦う. Slightly ironic is 勇ましいことを言う "to talk big". 勇敢な, by contrast, soberly stresses the brave deed and is more formal.

examples[].german: The ceremony was held in a solemn atmosphere.
The priest offered a prayer in a solemn voice.
The mountaintop at dawn was wrapped in a solemn stillness.
en.notes: 厳か is a な-adjective for a "solemn, dignified" mood at ceremonies and rituals: 厳かな雰囲気, 厳かな声, 厳かに執り行う. Do not confuse with the same kanji in 厳しい "strict". 荘厳な "sublime, magnificent" describes buildings or music rather.

examples[].german: She has a cheerful personality.
My grandmother is always laughing cheerfully.
The cheerful singing voices of the children rang through the classroom.
en.notes: 朗らか describes a "cheerful, sunny" nature, laugh, or a clear, cheerful voice: 朗らかな人, 朗らかな性格, 朗らかに笑う. It sounds a bit more elevated than 明るい; 陽気な is more "exuberant, merry". Rarely, and in literary use, it also describes clear, beautiful weather.

examples[].german: A secret meeting was held.
Reading at night is my quiet pleasure.
The two lived quietly on the outskirts of town.
en.notes: 密やか is a literary な-adjective for "quiet, secret, inconspicuous": 密やかな楽しみ, 密やかな足音, 密やかに暮らす. It is often written in kana, ひそやか. Much more common in everyday speech is the related 密か (ひそかに "secretly"), and colloquially 内緒で.

examples[].german: The glossy black hair is beautiful.
Shiny cherries are lined up in front of the shop.
If you use this cream, your skin becomes glowing.
en.notes: 艶やか (つややか) describes a beautiful, healthy "gloss" of hair, skin, fruit or lacquer: 艶やかな黒髪, 肌が艶やかになる. Note: the same spelling read あでやか means "enchanting, glamorous" (of women or kimono); therefore it is often written in kana as つややか. More colloquial are つやつや and ぴかぴか.

examples[].german: He committed a despicable act.
Taking advantage of other people's weaknesses is a despicable way to act.
When it comes to food, my younger brother gets greedy.
en.notes: 卑しい is a sharp value judgment with several meanings: "base, mean" (卑しい行為, 卑しいやり方), "greedy" especially about food (食べ物に卑しい) and, obsolete, "of low social standing". 下品な refers more to vulgar manners, 卑怯な to cowardly, unfair behavior.

examples[].german: To avoid confusing expressions.
The names of the two stations are confusingly similar, and I took the wrong train.
Don't put it in a confusing way; say it clearly.
en.notes: 紛らわしい means "easily confused, misleading" because things resemble each other or something is ambiguous: 紛らわしい名前, 紛らわしい表現, 紛らわしい言い方. In conversation also as an annoyed exclamation: 紛らわしい！. ややこしい, by contrast, means "complicated, tangled", and 曖昧な "vague, unclear".

examples[].german: To endure harsh working conditions.
There are plants that can live even in the harsh environment of the desert.
This marathon has many hills and is a very grueling race.
en.notes: 過酷な describes conditions that are "harsh, merciless" beyond what is bearable: 過酷な労働, 過酷な環境, 過酷なレース, 過酷な試練. The variant 苛酷 emphasizes cruel treatment by people. 厳しい is the general, weaker "strict, severe"; 残酷な means morally "cruel".

examples[].german: He apologized with a contrite attitude.
Getting up early every morning to study, what a commendable attitude!
My brother, who is always complaining, said something admirable for once.
en.notes: 殊勝な praises behavior as "laudable, good, contrite", often about someone from whom one would not have expected it: 殊勝な心がけ, 殊勝な態度, 殊勝なことを言う. Because a judgment from above resonates in it, one does not say it about superiors, and it can sound ironic. 立派な and 感心な are more neutral words of praise.

examples[].german: The method of distributing local grants was reviewed.
The city built a new library with grants from the national government.
Towns with a power plant receive large grants every year.
en.notes: 交付金 is money that an authority, mostly the state, officially pays out to municipalities or institutions: 交付金を受ける, 国からの交付金, 地方創生交付金. 交付 means "to hand over officially" (as in 免許証の交付). Unlike a 補助金, which funds a certain share of costs, 交付金 often leave recipients more leeway. The large fiscal allocation to municipalities is, strictly speaking, called 地方交付税.

examples[].german: Human relationships are growing thin.
The air is thin on high mountains, so breathing becomes difficult.
The problem is that employees have little sense of crisis.
en.notes: 希薄な literally means "thin, diluted" (空気が希薄だ, 酸素が希薄) and figuratively "weakly developed, lacking": 人間関係が希薄だ, 危機感が希薄, 当事者意識が希薄. Mostly predicative with が ... 希薄だ or 希薄になる. The everyday words are 薄い and 乏しい "scanty"; the variant 稀薄 is rare.

examples[].german: He is the possessor of a rare talent.
It is a rare case for both husband and wife to live past one hundred.
He had the rare experience of seeing the Earth from space.
en.notes: 稀有な is a written word for "extremely rare, extraordinary", mostly positive or neutral: 稀有な才能, 稀有な例, 稀有な存在, 稀有な体験. It is also written 希有 and read けう (きゆう is rare). In everyday speech people say 珍しい; 稀な (まれな) is also elevated, but more common.

examples[].german: He made a considerable contribution.
We sincerely apologize for the great inconvenience this time.
His novels had a great influence on young writers.
en.notes: 多大な denotes a "considerable, great" amount of something abstract: 多大な貢献, 多大な影響, 多大な損害; very common in formal thank-you and apology formulas (多大なご支援, 多大なご迷惑をおかけしました). It is not used for concrete size (buildings, etc.). 莫大な emphasizes huge sums (莫大な費用), 甚大な serious damage.

examples[].german: To uphold lofty ideals.
Saving people at the risk of one's life is a noble act.
The view from the summit had a sublime beauty.
en.notes: 崇高な means "lofty, noble" and is used for ideals, goals and deeds: 崇高な理念, 崇高な使命, 崇高な精神, 崇高な行為. In aesthetics 崇高 is "the sublime". The word is elevated; 高尚な means rather "refined, cultured" (taste, hobbies) and can sound aloof, while 気高い is the native "noble, dignified".

examples[].german: Enormous damage occurred.
The damage to crops from the typhoon was enormous.
The scandal had a grave impact on the company's credibility.
en.notes: 甚大な denotes an "enormous, serious" extent, almost always of damage and negative consequences: 甚大な被害, 甚大な損害, 甚大な影響; also predicative, 被害は甚大だ. Typical of news about disasters. 多大な can also describe positive things (多大な貢献), 莫大な emphasizes huge sums of money.

examples[].german: I made a finely detailed model.
The ceiling of this temple is adorned with elaborate carvings.
His paper was highly rated for its meticulous analysis.
en.notes: 精緻な means "worked out down to the finest detail, precise" and praises both manual and intellectual work: 精緻な細工, 精緻な模型, 精緻な分析, 精緻な理論. It is a written word. 精密な emphasizes technical accuracy (精密機械), 緻密な careful, gapless planning (緻密な計画); in everyday speech people say 細かい.

examples[].german: To strive for concise writing.
Please explain the main points concisely.
His speech was concise and easy to understand.
en.notes: 簡潔な means "brief and to the point" and refers to language: 簡潔な文章, 簡潔な説明; very often adverbial: 簡潔に説明する, 簡潔にまとめる. Do not confuse with 簡単 "simple, easy" and 簡素 "plain, unadorned". In speech people also say 手短に "briefly"; the opposite is 冗漫.

examples[].german: He has tremendous mental toughness.
Spider silk is thin but extremely tough.
In preparation for disasters, we are building resilient infrastructure.
en.notes: 強靭な means "tough, resilient, durable" and applies to materials (強靭な繊維), the body (強靭な肉体) and the mind (強靭な精神力); in politics 国土強靭化 is "strengthening disaster resilience of the land". Spelling variants: 強靱, 強じん. 頑丈な "sturdy" describes objects rather, and 丈夫な is the everyday word.

examples[].german: Beware of ferocious animals.
This dog looks fierce but is gentle by nature.
Some kinds of sharks are ferocious.
en.notes: 獰猛な describes mainly animals as "aggressive, dangerously wild": 獰猛な犬, 獰猛な猛獣, 獰猛なサメ; figuratively also a fierce appearance (獰猛な顔つき). Because of the difficult kanji it is often written どう猛. Do not confuse with 野生の "wild (not domesticated)"; 凶暴な "violent" is also used for people.

examples[].german: A tragic accident occurred.
I want to convey the horrors of war to the next generation.
Yesterday's test results were dismal.
en.notes: 悲惨な means "tragic, shocking, wretched" for accidents and conditions: 悲惨な事故, 悲惨な状況, 戦争の悲惨さ. Colloquially and hyperbolically also "disastrous" (テストの結果は悲惨だった). 惨めな emphasizes personal humiliation ("pitiful"), 気の毒な sympathy ("pitiable").

examples[].german: The local government issued bonds for public works.
The company issued corporate bonds to raise funds for a new factory.
The city aims for fiscal management that does not rely on bond issuance.
en.notes: 起債 means taking on debt by issuing bonds, whether by the state, municipalities (地方債) or companies (社債): 起債する, 起債を行う, 起債額, 起債許可. The counterpart, repayment, is called 償還. A term from budget and financial reports; in everyday speech one simply says 借金をする.

examples[].german: He made a blatantly discriminatory remark.
When I asked him for a favor, he openly made a sour face.
This film contains explicit depictions, so it is not suitable for children.
en.notes: 露骨な means "unconcealed, blunt" and describes feelings or intentions that one tactlessly shows openly: 露骨な差別, 露骨に嫌な顔をする; for depictions also "explicit, suggestive" (露骨な描写). Almost always negative, very often adverbial 露骨に. あからさまな is similar, whereas 率直な "frank, honest" is positive.

examples[].german: To have a vigorous curiosity.
My son has a hearty appetite and eats three bowls of rice at every meal.
Supported by strong demand, sales are growing.
en.notes: 旺盛な means "vigorous, strong, full of ..." and is used with drives and energies: 旺盛な好奇心, 旺盛な食欲, 旺盛な需要. Very often placed after the noun in fixed combinations: 食欲旺盛, 好奇心旺盛, 元気旺盛 (好奇心旺盛な子ども). 盛んな describes brisk activities (スポーツが盛んだ), 活発な lively behavior.

examples[].german: Teamwork is an indispensable element.
Water is indispensable for life.
English ability is absolutely essential for this job.
en.notes: 不可欠な means "indispensable" and typically goes with 〜に(とって): 生命にとって不可欠だ, 成功に不可欠な条件. The intensified fixed phrase 必要不可欠 is very common. The word is formal; in conversation people say 欠かせない, and the weaker 必要な means "necessary".

examples[].german: Change is unavoidable.
If this continues, a price increase is unavoidable.
A conflict between the two countries is now seen as inevitable.
en.notes: 不可避な means "unavoidable" and is a written word from politics, business and science; mostly predicative (〜は不可避だ / 不可避である) or in 不可避と見られる. In conversation people say 避けられない; やむを得ない means "cannot be helped, out of necessity", and 必然的 "inevitable (logically necessary)".

examples[].german: To take an arrogant attitude.
His arrogant remark at the press conference drew criticism.
It is a presumptuous act that does not even fear the gods.
en.notes: 不遜な means "arrogant, presumptuous", especially toward superiors or what deserves respect: 不遜な態度, 不遜な発言; as a four-character compound 傲岸不遜. It is written language. 生意気な "cheeky, impertinent" is colloquial and mostly refers to younger people, 横柄な describes a condescending manner.

examples[].german: Wordy explanations should be avoided.
The middle part of this novel is so long-winded that I stopped reading partway.
I cut the wordy parts and made the article half as long.
en.notes: 冗漫な means "verbose, long-winded" and criticizes texts, speeches or films that are not tightened: 冗漫な文章, 冗漫な説明. It is a written word and the opposite of 簡潔な. 冗長な is very similar (in technology also "redundant"), and くどい is the colloquial "long-winded, repetitive".

examples[].german: Sloppy management led to the accident.
Because of the sloppy planning, the trip was a disaster.
The police's sloppy investigation is being criticized.
en.notes: 杜撰な means "sloppy, faulty" and criticizes above all organization and procedures: 杜撰な管理, 杜撰な計画, 杜撰な捜査, 杜撰な工事. It is mostly written in kana, ずさん, and is typical of news criticism. In everyday speech people say いい加減な or 雑な; 不注意 is an individual lapse of attention.

en.meaning: vivid; true to life; faithful to reality
examples[].german: The data clearly show the current situation.
His expression vividly told how the match had gone.
His fatigue is clearly visible on his face.
en.notes: 如実 means "in accordance with reality" and is practically used only adverbially as 如実に: 如実に示す, 如実に表す, 如実に物語る, 如実に現れる "to show clearly, to reflect without embellishment". The form 如実な is rare. It is a written word; in everyday speech people say はっきり or ありのままに.

examples[].german: We are facing a serious environmental problem.
Don't look so serious. It's not a big deal.
In rural areas, the shortage of doctors is becoming more serious.
en.notes: 深刻な means "serious, grave" and describes problems and situations: 深刻な問題, 深刻な影響, 深刻な状況; 深刻化する "to worsen". For people, 深刻な顔 means "a serious, worried expression". Common mistake: a serious attitude ("to study seriously") is 真剣, not 深刻. 重大な emphasizes the significance.

examples[].german: He made an earnest plea.
For the child-rearing generation, the shortage of nurseries is a pressing problem.
Since I started living alone, I keenly felt how much my family means to me.
en.notes: 切実な describes something that concerns one personally and directly: "pressing, earnest, painfully felt". Typical: 切実な願い, 切実な問題, 切実な訴え; adverbial 切実に感じる "to feel keenly firsthand". 深刻な rather assesses severity objectively, 緊急の urgency in terms of time.

examples[].german: The redemption of local bonds is putting pressure on finances.
The principal of this government bond will be redeemed in ten years.
With reimbursement-type payment, the medical costs come back later from insurance.
en.notes: 償還 is the scheduled repayment of bonds and loans: 国債を償還する, 償還期限 ("maturity"), 満期償還. In health care, 償還払い refers to reimbursement when you first pay yourself. 返済 is the general word for repaying private debts; 償還 sounds financial-technical and fits securities and public budgets.

examples[].german: Careless work is not acceptable.
Please do not handle the luggage roughly.
That argument is crudely grounded and lacks persuasiveness.
en.notes: 粗雑な means "rough, careless, unrefined" and refers to work, handling of things and arguments: 粗雑な仕事, 粗雑な作り, 粗雑に扱う, 粗雑な議論. In everyday speech people say 雑な. 杜撰な criticizes rather sloppy organization, and 粗末な means "poor, inferior" (粗末にする "to waste, to treat with disrespect").

examples[].german: Insidious bullying has become a problem.
I am troubled by malicious harassment on the Internet.
We passed through a sunless, damp back alley.
en.notes: 陰湿な describes malice that proceeds in a hidden, wearing way: "insidious, underhanded": 陰湿ないじめ, 陰湿な嫌がらせ, 陰湿なやり方. Literally it also means "shady and damp" (陰湿な場所). 陰険な characterizes rather a sly person, and 意地悪な is the everyday word for "mean".

examples[].german: The plans all failed.
My proposals were all rejected at the meeting.
It was a week in which every single weather forecast was wrong.
en.notes: 悉く means "every single one, completely" and is often used with negative outcomes: 悉く失敗する, 悉く却下される, 予想が悉く外れる. It is written language and mostly written in kana, ことごとく. Neutral are すべて and 全部; 軒並み emphasizes "across the board, on a broad front".

en.meaning: across the board; one after another
examples[].german: Corporate earnings worsened across the board.
Because of the typhoon, Shinkansen trains were canceled one after another.
Food prices have gone up across the board since April.
en.notes: 軒並み literally means "a row of houses" (軒 = eaves), but as an adverb it means "across the board, one after another, extensively": 軒並み値上がりする, 軒並み運休する, 業績が軒並み悪化する. Typical of business and transport news. 一斉に emphasizes simultaneity, 悉く exclusion of no exception.

en.meaning: one by one; in detail; point by point
examples[].german: To report the progress point by point.
My mother wants to check my every move.
We will keep you informed one by one as new information comes in.
en.notes: 逐一 means "one by one, point by point, without gaps" and stands before verbs of reporting and checking: 逐一報告する, 逐一説明する, 逐一チェックする, 逐一お知らせする. It is rather formal and matter-of-fact. The colloquial いちいち means the same, but often sounds annoyed ("every time, over every little thing").

en.meaning: all the more; even more so
examples[].german: If you fail, you should make all the more effort.
If it is going to rain, you had better leave all the earlier.
When I'm told to stop, I want to do it all the more.
en.notes: 尚更 means "all the more, even more so" and intensifies an inference: 〜なら尚更だ, それなら尚更, 止められると尚更やりたくなる. With a negative it means "even less". Mostly written in kana, なおさら. ましてや "let alone" introduces a more extreme case, and 余計に is colloquial and often negatively colored.

en.meaning: in rapid succession; one after another
examples[].german: Questions flew in rapid succession.
Bombarded with questions by the interviewer, my mind went blank.
That company is releasing new products one after another.
en.notes: 矢継ぎ早 comes from quickly nocking one arrow after another and means "in rapid succession, thick and fast". Most often with questions: 矢継ぎ早に質問する, 矢継ぎ早の質問; but also 矢継ぎ早に新製品を出す, 対策を打ち出す. More neutral are 次々に "one after another" and 立て続けに "in a row".

examples[].german: He was sharply criticized.
As a film critic, she is known for her scathing reviews.
My grandfather is kind, but he speaks bitingly about politics.
en.notes: 辛辣 means "biting, sharp-tongued" and refers to criticism and words: 辛辣に批判する, 辛辣な批評, 辛辣な皮肉, 辛辣な口調. A person who likes to talk like that has a 毒舌 "sharp tongue". 厳しく is more general "strictly"; 痛烈に emphasizes the force, 手厳しい the unforgiving nature.

en.meaning: not at all; (not) in the least
examples[].german: The situation is not improving at all.
Even though I'm taking medicine, my fever won't go down at all.
I don't mind at all.
en.notes: 一向に is almost always used with a negative and means "not at all, not in the least", often with the undertone that one is waiting in vain for a change: 一向に良くならない, 一向に連絡が来ない. The fixed phrase 一向に構わない means "I don't mind at all". Compared with 全然 and 少しも, 一向に sounds more like written language and emphasizes the absence despite expectation. The positive meaning "entirely" is obsolete.

examples[].german: The state's fiscal situation is steadily worsening.
Because the city's finances are tight, the library's opening hours were shortened.
Since we bought a car, our household finances are in dire straits this month.
en.notes: 財政 is primarily the public finances of the state and municipalities: 国の財政, 財政赤字, 財政難, 財政再建, 財政が厳しい. Half-jokingly it can also refer to the financial situation of a company or household (我が家の財政は火の車). Not to be confused with 経済 ("economy") or 金融 ("finance, banking"); for the private household budget one normally says 家計.

examples[].german: My physical condition is extremely good.
The department head is in an especially good mood today.
The new bakery has an excellent reputation.
en.notes: 頗る is an intensifying adverb meaning "extremely, decidedly" and stands before adjectives or expressions of state: 頗る元気, 頗る機嫌がいい, 頗る評判がいい. It sounds somewhat old-fashioned to elevated and is often used in a jokingly formal way; in everyday speech people more often say とても or すごく. It is mostly written in kana (すこぶる).

examples[].german: Rather than criticizing, we should cooperate.
Today is not so much cold as rather cool.
That failure turned out to be, if anything, a good experience.
en.notes: 寧ろ means "rather, instead" and, in a comparison, picks the more fitting or better of two possibilities; typical frames are AよりむしろB and AというよりむしろB. It often corrects an expectation: the failure was むしろ a good experience. Unlike かえって ("on the contrary, all the more", an unexpected opposite effect), むしろ expresses a weighing of options. Usually written in kana.

en.meaning: on the contrary; rather; all the more
examples[].german: I tried to help but ended up causing trouble instead.
Going by taxi actually took longer because of traffic.
Taking too much medicine is actually bad for the body.
en.notes: 却って describes a result that runs counter to what was intended or expected: you wanted to help and ended up doing harm, かえって. Typical after clauses with て, のに or たら. Unlike むしろ (a deliberate weighing, "rather"), かえって stresses the unexpected opposite effect. Usually written in kana; not to be confused with the verb 帰って.

en.meaning: for the most part; almost all
examples[].german: The work is mostly finished.
The moving boxes have mostly been put away.
After listening to the explanation, I was able to understand most of what was said.
en.notes: 粗方 means "for the most part, nearly" and describes that something is almost completely done or understood: あらかた終わった, あらかた片付いた. It is somewhat more colloquial than 大体 or ほとんど and is mostly written in kana. As a noun it denotes "the greater part": 客のあらかたが帰った.

examples[].german: Since this is my first time, please be lenient with me.
Since it is an old building, repairs cost money.
I may still be inexperienced in some respects, but I sincerely ask for your support.
en.notes: 何分 (なにぶん) is used mainly in polite speech as a reason and an apology: "since, after all", typically with ので: 何分初めてなので…. Second, it reinforces requests: 何分よろしくお願いいたします "I sincerely ask this of you". Not to be confused with 何分 (なんぷん) "how many minutes". Also intensified as 何分にも.

en.meaning: to the end; persistently; only; merely
examples[].german: I stick to my own opinion to the end.
This is only my personal opinion.
The time shown is only a rough guide.
en.notes: 飽くまで has two uses. First, "to the very end, persistently": あくまで反対する, あくまで戦う. Second, very common in modern everyday speech, as a limiting "only, merely": あくまで個人の意見です, あくまで目安です - one stresses that something is no more than that. Usually written in kana; also intensified as あくまでも.

examples[].german: Almost everyone agreed.
The homework is almost done.
I could hardly sleep last night because of worry.
en.notes: 殆ど means "almost, nearly": ほとんど終わった. With a negative it means "hardly": ほとんど寝ていない. As a noun with の it stands for "the majority, almost all": ほとんどの人. In everyday writing it is almost always written in kana; the kanji spelling is a typical reading exercise at N1 level.

examples[].german: Of course I'll help you.
"Are you coming along?" "Of course!"
He can speak not only English but also Chinese, of course.
en.notes: 勿論 means "of course, naturally" and stands alone as an answer (もちろん！) or before a statement. The pattern AはもちろんB(も) means "not only A, but of course B as well". In everyday writing it is almost always in kana; the kanji 勿論 are seen in older or formal texts. More polite in replies is もちろんです.

examples[].german: He kept looking at his watch.
A dog is barking incessantly in the middle of the night.
My mother earnestly urged me to study abroad.
en.notes: 頻りに describes an action that repeats conspicuously often ("constantly, incessantly"): しきりに時計を見る, 犬がしきりに吠える. With verbs such as 勧める, 頼む, 感心する it means "earnestly, insistently". It sounds somewhat more literary than 何度も or ずっと and is usually written in kana.

examples[].german: The result was unexpectedly good.
It was farther to the station than I expected.
The cleanup took surprisingly long.
en.notes: 思いの外 means "contrary to expectation, surprisingly" and expresses that something turns out differently (usually stronger or better) than thought: 思いの外簡単だった, 思いの外時間がかかった. In content it corresponds to 意外に or 予想以上に, but sounds somewhat more elevated. Literally "outside of what was thought"; with の it can also be used attributively: 思いの外の結果.

examples[].german: Securing funding for social security is considered urgent.
If taxes are cut, how will the lost revenue be made up?
The town uses an accommodation tax as a new source of revenue.
en.notes: 財源 is the source of money from which expenditures, especially public ones, are paid: 財源を確保する, 財源が不足する, 財源不足, 新たな財源. In political debates people often ask 財源はどうするのか ("How is this to be financed?"). 資金 is the money itself, 財源 the origin of the money. Formal, typical in politics and administration.

en.meaning: narrowly; barely; by the skin of one's teeth
examples[].german: He narrowly escaped disaster.
They narrowly won the final 1-0.
He narrowly won election in the last election.
en.notes: 辛くも means "narrowly, only just" and stands before verbs of succeeding or escaping: 辛くも勝つ, 辛くも逃れる, 辛くも当選する. It is written language and typical of news and sports reports; in conversation people more often say ぎりぎり or かろうじて. Do not confuse with 辛い (からい "spicy" / つらい "hard, painful").

examples[].german: The rumor spread instantly.
As soon as that new product went on sale, it sold out.
The sky grew dark, and in no time it was pouring.
en.notes: 忽ち means "in a flash, immediately" and describes a change that occurs very quickly and often without anyone doing anything: たちまち売り切れる, たちまち広まる. Unlike すぐに (also used for deliberate actions: すぐに行きます), たちまち describes processes rather than actions and sounds narrative. Usually written in kana.

en.meaning: in the end; after all; ultimately
examples[].german: In the end, effort is what counts.
In the final analysis, human beings cannot live alone.
His excuses are, in the end, nothing but an attempt to dodge responsibility.
en.notes: 畢竟 is an elevated, written adverb meaning "in the end, fundamentally" and introduces a summarizing conclusion, often at the start of a sentence followed by a comma. In content it corresponds to 結局 or つまり, but seems literary to archaic. Frequently combined with 〜にすぎない or 〜のだ.

examples[].german: To update information continuously.
Please report on progress as it develops.
Consecutive interpreting will be provided at the conference.
en.notes: 逐次 means "one after another, continuously, step by step" and describes that something happens continuously in individual steps: 逐次報告する, 逐次更新する. It is a formal word from administration, business and technology; in everyday language it corresponds to 順次 or その都度. Well-known compounds are 逐次通訳 "consecutive interpreting" and 逐次処理.

examples[].german: The news spread everywhere.
His name is known all over the world.
The government is striving to make sure the support reaches all citizens.
en.notes: 遍く is a written adverb meaning "everywhere, generally, without exception" and emphasizes that something reaches every part of an area: 遍く知られる, 遍く行き渡る. In everyday speech people more often say 広く or みんなに. Typical are verbs of spreading and being known; mostly written in kana.

examples[].german: It developed into a serious situation.
This is a serious problem that affects the company's credibility.
The falling birthrate is an alarming situation for the country.
en.notes: 由々しい means "serious, grave, alarming" and describes situations that can have serious consequences: 由々しい問題, 由々しい事態. Very common is the classical attributive form 由々しき: 由々しき事態. The word is formal and typical of news, speeches and editorials; more neutral are 深刻な or 重大な.

examples[].german: It takes about three hours.
Such a rough way of speaking is not at all like him.
I understood the gist of the story.
en.notes: 凡そ mostly means "about, approximately" before numbers: およそ三時間. With a negative or negatively valued expressions it means "(not) at all": およそ彼らしくない. As a noun it stands for "the essentials, the rough outline": 話のおよそは分かった. Compared with 約 and 大体, およそ sounds somewhat more elevated; usually written in kana.

examples[].german: Let's just try it anyway.
Anyway, I'm glad you're safe.
That shop is just really cheap.
en.notes: 兎に角 means "anyway, in any case" and sets aside secondary matters in order to get to the essential point or to action: とにかくやってみよう. Colloquially it also intensifies, "simply, really": とにかく安い. Close synonyms are ともかく (more common in Nはともかく "setting N aside") and いずれにしても. The kanji spelling 兎に角 is ateji and it is almost only written in kana.

en.meaning: going out of one's way; specially
examples[].german: Thank you for coming all this way.
I went out of my way to buy it, but it was sold out.
He deliberately badmouthed me so that I could hear it.
en.notes: 態々 means "specially, expressly, going to the trouble" and stands before an action that would not actually have been necessary. As thanks it is very common: わざわざありがとうございます. In a negative context it means "deliberately, needlessly": わざわざ聞こえるように言う. Distinction: わざと emphasizes only the intention (often malicious), わざわざ the unnecessary effort. Almost always written in kana.

examples[].german: Now that it has come to this, it can't be helped.
Because of the bad weather, cancellation is unavoidable.
If a promise were broken three times, it is understandable that she would be angry.
en.notes: 致し方ない is the polite, formal variant of 仕方がない: "it can't be helped, there is no other choice". 致す is the humble form of する. It is heard in business language and speeches, often as 致し方ありません or 致し方ないことです. For a justified reaction of others: 怒るのも致し方ない "it is understandable that ...".

examples[].german: Each ministry submitted its budget request for the next fiscal year.
The Ministry of Defense's budget request reached a record amount.
The deadline for budget requests is the end of August every year.
en.notes: 概算要求 is, in Japan's budget process, the preliminary budget request that each ministry submits to the Ministry of Finance by the end of August. The Ministry of Finance then examines the requests (査定), and in December the Cabinet approves the draft budget (予算案). Typical in the news: 概算要求を提出する, 概算要求額, 過去最大の概算要求.

en.meaning: needless to say; it goes without saying
examples[].german: It goes without saying that health is important.
Needless to say, talking during the exam is prohibited.
Not to mention English, he can also speak French.
en.notes: 言うまでもない means "it goes without saying, of course". At the end of a sentence: 〜のは言うまでもない. Adverbially at the start of a sentence: 言うまでもなく, "needless to say". The pattern Aは言うまでもなく、Bも means "not only A, but B all the more", similar to Aはもちろん. Neutral to formal; in conversation people also say もちろん.

en.meaning: nothing other than; none other than
examples[].german: The success is nothing other than the result of effort.
She was chosen for no other reason than that her ability was recognized.
If it's a request from you of all people, I can't refuse.
en.notes: 他ならない (mostly as Nに他ならない or 〜からに他ならない) emphatically asserts "is nothing other than, is solely". It is written language and typical of essays and speeches. The attributive form 他ならぬ means "none other than" or "precisely (this person)": 他ならぬあなたの頼みなら. Close in content: 〜そのものだ, 〜以外の何物でもない. Often in kana: ほかならない.

en.meaning: unbearable to; not worth; (with emotions) deeply, utterly
examples[].german: It was a sight too awful to look at.
The content of his speech was hardly bearable to listen to.
I cannot thank you enough for your support.
en.notes: After a verb of perception (見る, 聞く, 読む), に堪えない means "unbearable to, not worth": 見るに堪えない光景. After emotion nouns such as 感謝, 遺憾, 同情, by contrast, it means "extremely, cannot help but": 感謝に堪えません "I am deeply grateful". Both uses are written language and formal. Do not confuse with 絶えない "incessant" (笑顔が絶えない).

en.meaning: to be forced to; to have no choice but to
examples[].german: We were forced to change the plan.
Because of the typhoon, many flights were forced to be canceled.
Because of an injury, he was forced to retire.
en.notes: Nを余儀なくされる means "to be forced to N" by external circumstances, against one's will. N is usually a Sino-Japanese action noun: 中止, 変更, 撤退, 引退, 欠航. The pattern is very common in news. The active form Xが Yに Nを余儀なくさせる "X forces Y to N" is rarer. As an adverb: 余儀なく〜する.

en.meaning: in accordance with; based on; in keeping with
examples[].german: To take measures that suit reality.
Please report in line with the facts.
Explaining it using concrete examples makes it easier to understand.
en.notes: Nに即して means "in accordance with, in conformity with" and requires that one orient oneself by concrete facts or circumstances: 事実に即して, 実情に即して, 現実に即して. Before a noun the form is Nに即した: 現実に即した対策. It is formal and typical of reports and administrative language. For rules and laws, 則して (法律に則して) is written more often, or people say に従って.

en.meaning: based on; in light of; taking into account
examples[].german: To judge based on the survey results.
Learning from the previous time, we prepared early this time.
We have developed a new product that reflects customers' feedback.
en.notes: Nを踏まえて means "taking N into account, on the basis of N": results, experiences or opinions are taken as the starting point for a decision. Typical N are 結果, 経験, 反省, 意見, 現状. Before a noun: Nを踏まえた提案. Unlike に基づいて ("strictly relying on", e.g. data, laws), を踏まえて emphasizes incorporating N into one's own thinking. Formal, very common in business language.

en.meaning: prior to; in advance of; ahead of
examples[].german: Materials were distributed ahead of the meeting.
A preview screening was held prior to the film's release.
A moment of silence was offered before the match.
en.notes: Nに先立って means "before, in the run-up to" and indicates that something is done as preparation ahead of an important event: 開会に先立って, 発売に先立って. In writing also に先立ち, and before a noun に先立つ. It is more formal and ceremonial than 前に. The verb 先立つ alone can also mean "to die before someone" (親に先立つ).

en.meaning: without regard for; in disregard of
examples[].german: He helped someone regardless of the danger.
My father neglected his family and did nothing but work.
Some people make loud noise in the middle of the night, with no regard for those around them.
en.notes: Nを顧みず means "without regard for N"; ず is the classical negation (= 顧みないで). Typical N are 危険, 身の危険, 家庭, 周囲の迷惑. Depending on context it sounds heroic (危険を顧みず助ける) or reproachful (家庭を顧みず仕事ばかり). Do not confuse with 省みる "to reflect on oneself" (自らを省みる). Written language and formal.

en.meaning: as for ... (extreme case); when it comes to ... even
examples[].german: His grades were poor, and in math he even got a failing mark.
Everyone in my family is bad at mornings, and my father even sleeps until noon.
Few participants came, and as for young people, there was not a single one.
en.notes: Nに至っては picks out the most extreme case from a series of mostly negative examples: "and as for N, even ...". The preceding sentence often states the general situation, then the extreme case follows. Unlike neutral については or に関しては, に至っては carries a critical or surprised judgment. Do not confuse with に至るまで "all the way to".

en.meaning: combined with; together with; coupled with
examples[].german: Combined with the good weather, the holiday weekend left the tourist spots bustling with crowds.
His talent, coupled with effort, blossomed greatly.
Together with the beautiful night view, the food tasted even better.
en.notes: AがBと相まって means "A works together with B": two factors reinforce each other and jointly lead to a result. AとBが相まって is also possible. The result is usually an amplified effect, positive or negative. Formal and written language; often in kana, あいまって. Do not confuse with the verb 合う.

examples[].german: The opacity of special accounts is being criticized.
The national budget consists of the general account and special accounts.
The costs of earthquake reconstruction are managed in a special account.
en.notes: 特別会計 is a special account kept separately from the general account (一般会計) for particular purposes, such as pensions, energy or reconstruction: 年金特別会計, 復興特別会計. Because income and spending there are less visible, it is often criticized in Japan as opaque. Municipalities also keep 特別会計, for example for health insurance or water supply.

en.meaning: starting with; beginning with; kicking off with
examples[].german: A nationwide tour will be held, starting with Tokyo.
Starting with one person's remark, objections came out one after another.
Starting with this partnership, we plan to advance our overseas expansion.
en.notes: Nを皮切りに means "starting with N": N is the starting point of a whole series of similar events that follow and expand. Typical for tours, event series and business expansions. Also を皮切りとして, を皮切りにして. Unlike をはじめ (names a representative example), を皮切りに emphasizes the chronological sequence. Originally 皮切り refers to the first moxibustion treatment.

en.meaning: to accelerate; to spur on; to add fuel to
examples[].german: The weak yen accelerated the rise in prices.
The spread of social media is accelerating young people's drift away from print.
As the deadline approached, work picked up speed.
en.notes: 拍車 is the spur on a riding boot; Nに拍車をかける literally means "to give N the spurs" and means that a factor speeds up a development that is already underway. Often for negative trends (物価上昇, 過疎化, 少子化), but also neutral. Intransitive: Nに拍車がかかる "N speeds up". Formal, typical of news.

en.meaning: regardless of; in disregard of; heedless of
examples[].german: He pushed ahead with the plan regardless of opposition from those around him.
Heedless of his parents' worry, the son goes out partying every night.
In spite of the recession, long lines form at that shop every day.
en.notes: Nを余所に means "regardless of N, without caring about N": the acting person ignores the worries, expectations or opposition of others, or a development runs counter to the general situation. Typical: 親の心配をよそに, 周囲の期待をよそに, 不況をよそに. Mostly written in kana. Unlike にもかかわらず, をよそに emphasizes disinterest or indifference toward N.

examples[].german: That is utterly rude behavior.
Riding at night in the rain without a light is extremely dangerous.
Procedures at government offices are extremely complicated.
en.notes: 極まりない is attached to a noun or the stem of a な-adjective and means "extremely, beyond all measure": 失礼極まりない, 危険極まりない, 不愉快極まりない. It almost always intensifies negative evaluations and sounds formal and indignant. Synonymous is 極まる (失礼極まる). As an independent adjective it also means "boundless" (極まりない宇宙).

examples[].german: He is a person worthy of trust.
This is a proposal well worth considering.
There is no need to worry over such a trivial matter.
en.notes: V-るに足る or Nに足る means "to be worth, to be sufficient for": 信頼に足る人物, 検討するに足る提案. It is written language; in everyday speech people more often say 〜できる, 〜する価値がある. Very common is the fixed negation 取るに足らない "insignificant, trivial". 足る is an older form of 足りる.

en.meaning: undaunted by; in defiance of; regardless of
examples[].german: He pushed ahead undeterred by the criticism.
The runners ran through to the end, undaunted by the heavy rain.
Defying her illness, she continued to stand on stage.
en.notes: Nをものともせず means "unfazed by N, in spite of N": one does not let difficulties such as rain, injury or criticism stop one. It expresses admiration and usually describes others, not oneself. Distinction: をよそに emphasizes indifference, を顧みず disregard of a risk. Written language; almost always in kana.

examples[].german: I cannot hide my astonishment.
Hearing the victim's story, I could not hold back my tears.
I cannot help feeling anger at this ruling.
en.notes: Nを禁じ得ない means "cannot suppress N", that is, "cannot help feeling N". N is an emotion noun: 涙, 同情, 怒り, 驚き, 失望. It is very formal and written language and describes the speaker's own feelings. In everyday speech people say 〜ずにはいられない or simply 思わず泣いた. Also written 禁じえない.

examples[].german: I can't waste even a second.
I have no intention of paying even a single yen for such a bill.
No one, whoever they may be, is permitted to enter here.
en.notes: A counter with 一 + たりとも + negation means "not even a single ...": 一秒たりとも, 一円たりとも, 一日たりとも. It is more emphatic and formal than 一〜も. The classical phrase 何人たりとも (なんぴとたりとも) means "no one, whoever it may be". Almost always followed by a prohibition, an impossibility or a firm resolution.

en.meaning: even normally; as it is already
examples[].german: I'm already busy as it is, and now there's more work.
I went and put a big bookshelf in a room that was already small.
The station, which is crowded to begin with, is even more packed because of the holiday.
en.notes: ただでさえ means "already, even under normal circumstances". One names a situation that is already unfavorable and made worse by an additional factor; typical is ただでさえ〜のに: ただでさえ忙しいのに. A reproach or complaint often follows. Neutral, common in both speech and writing.

examples[].german: Carrying unused budget over to the next fiscal year was approved.
Looking at my household account book, there is a carryover of 30,000 yen from last month.
With this plan, unused data can be carried over.
en.notes: 繰越 is the carrying of a remaining or balance amount over into the next period: 翌年度への繰越, 前月からの繰越, 繰越金, also with vacation days or mobile data. The related verb is 繰り越す (transitive, "to carry over"), intransitive 繰り越される. As a noun it is mostly written without okurigana, 繰越, in forms and ledgers, and also 繰り越し in running text.

en.meaning: unique to; only possible with; characteristic of
examples[].german: A landscape unique to Kyoto spreads out before you.
This sweater has the warmth that only hand-knitting has.
Filleting a fish in an instant, that is truly a skill only a professional has.
en.notes: Nならでは(の) means "typical of N, possible only with N" and highlights a special, positive quality: 京都ならではの風景, プロならではの技. Before a noun it is ならではの, at the end of a sentence ならではだ. It is used only in praise, never for disadvantages. The older meaning "except, without" (Nならでは〜ない) is literary.

en.meaning: given that; since; because of the circumstance that
examples[].german: Since it was a holiday, the park was bustling.
Because a popular singer was coming, a long line had formed at the venue since morning.
As it was her first trip abroad, she was very excited.
en.notes: Nとあって or sentence+とあって means "since it is a case of ...": one names a special circumstance and a consequence that follows naturally from it, from an observer's viewpoint. Typical: 休日とあって, 人気歌手が来るとあって, 初めてとあって. It sounds like news or reportage style; the consequence is not a request or intention of the speaker. Related: とあれば "if it is a matter of ...".

en.meaning: with; by means of; (time) as of, with
examples[].german: We will close down as of today.
We will notify you of the result in writing at a later date.
He learned the fear of failure through personal experience.
en.notes: をもって is a formal expression that appears in kana more often than in the spelling を以て. It marks above all the means ("with, by": 書面をもって通知する, 身をもって知る "to learn from personal experience") and a point in time or an end ("with, as of": 本日をもって閉店, 以上をもって終了します); in elevated usage also a reason. In announcements, letters and notices it replaces the neutral で; in conversation it sounds stiff. Even more polite is をもちまして, typical of announcements.

en.meaning: unbecoming; unworthy of; ought not to be
examples[].german: That is conduct unbecoming of a teacher.
His remark was criticized as unworthy of a politician.
Bullying the weak is an unforgivable act.
en.notes: まじき is the attributive form of the classical auxiliary まじ "should not, must not". Almost always in Nにあるまじき N: "unworthy of N, unforgivable for N", e.g. 教師にあるまじき行為, 政治家にあるまじき発言. It expresses sharp moral condemnation and is very formal. Also with other verbs: 許すまじき行為 "an unforgivable act".

examples[].german: It became a problem that could not be handled.
He is impossible to deal with when he is drunk.
The puppy is at its mischievous stage and is completely unmanageable.
en.notes: 始末 means "settlement, taking care of" and 負えない "cannot bear"; 始末に負えない thus means "cannot be brought under control, hopeless". It often describes people or animals with troublesome behavior (酔うと始末に負えない) or hopelessly tangled problems. Very similar is 手に負えない; 始末に負えない sounds more exasperated. The spelling 始末に終えない is a common mistake.

en.meaning: to marvel; to be wide-eyed; astonishing (attributive)
examples[].german: He achieved astonishing growth.
The children stared wide-eyed at the sea they were seeing for the first time.
Everyone marvels at that craftsman's skill.
en.notes: 目を見張る literally means "to open one's eyes wide" and describes astonishment or admiration. As a verb it takes に or を: 美しさに目を見張る. It is very common attributively: 目を見張るような〜 / 目を見張るほどの〜 "astonishing, breathtaking", e.g. 目を見張る成長. Neutral to formal; not to be confused with 見張る on its own, "to keep watch".

en.meaning: to not make sense; to be incomprehensible
examples[].german: His explanation doesn't add up.
There are a few points that just don't make sense to me.
After reading it over many times, it finally clicked.
en.notes: 腑 means the innards, formerly regarded as the seat of understanding; 腑に落ちない means "doesn't quite make sense to me, isn't entirely clear to me". You have heard an explanation, but a remnant of doubt remains: どうも腑に落ちない. The positive form 腑に落ちる "to make sense, to click" is now common as well. Related: 納得できない, 釈然としない (more formal).

en.meaning: to touch the heart; to move deeply
examples[].german: Her speech touched people's hearts.
The words of the disaster victims moved many people.
This is a moving story about family bonds.
en.notes: 胸を打つ means "to move deeply, to touch the heart". The subject is the thing that moves (speech, story, words); the object, if any, is the person: 人々の胸を打つ. Passive: 胸を打たれる "to be deeply moved". Very common attributively: 胸を打つ物語. 心を打つ means the same; 感動させる sounds more matter-of-fact.

en.meaning: to be let down; to feel deflated
examples[].german: It was resolved so easily that I felt rather let down.
I had been told the interview would be tough, but it was so easy it was an anticlimax.
I had prepared with great enthusiasm, but the event was cancelled and I felt deflated.
en.notes: 拍子抜け describes the feeling when you have braced yourself for something difficult or exciting and it turns out far easier or more harmless: "anticlimax, to be let down". Literally "to fall out of the beat". As a する-verb: 拍子抜けした; attributively 拍子抜けするほど簡単. Unlike がっかり (disappointment at something bad), 拍子抜け leaves the feeling that your own tension was for nothing.

examples[].german: Strengthening the military alliance is being debated.
Japan and the United States are in an alliance relationship.
Small countries formed an alliance to stand up to a great power.
en.notes: 同盟 is an "alliance" between states, parties or groups: 同盟を結ぶ "to form an alliance", 同盟国 "ally", 軍事同盟, 日米同盟 "Japan-US alliance", 同盟関係にある "to be allied". 同盟する as a verb is possible but much rarer than 同盟を結ぶ. Do not confuse it with 連盟 "federation, league" as an organization (国際連盟 "League of Nations"); 盟約 is the sworn pact itself.

examples[].german: The accuracy of the accounts and cash handling was confirmed in the audit.
I keep a cash book to manage my monthly allowance.
When she was young, my mother worked as a bank teller.
en.notes: 出納 is read すいとう (not しゅつのう) and refers to receiving and paying out money, or to issuing and accepting items. Typical are 金銭出納帳 ("cash book"), 出納係 ("cashier", e.g. in a bank or agency) and 出納業務. A formal word from bookkeeping and administration; in everyday speech one says お金の出し入れ instead.

en.meaning: to hit the nail on the head
examples[].german: His remark hits the mark.
"That's a very pertinent question," the lecturer praised.
His explanation at the meeting missed the point.
en.notes: 的を射る literally means "to hit the target" (射る "to shoot with a bow") and means "to be to the point, accurate". It almost always evaluates statements: 的を射た意見・質問・指摘 or predicatively 〜は的を射ている. The common variant 的を得る is traditionally considered an error (a mix-up with 当を得る) and should be avoided in formal texts. The opposite is 的外れ "off the mark, beside the point".

en.meaning: to throw in the towel; to give up
examples[].german: Even the doctor gave up.
No matter how many times he was taught, he never remembered, so even the teacher finally gave up on him.
Even the repair company threw in the towel over this computer fault.
en.notes: 匙を投げる literally means "to throw away the spoon": originally it refers to a doctor who puts down his medicine spoon because he considers the patient incurable. Today it generally means "to give up on something or someone as hopeless", typically 医者も・先生も匙を投げた or 〜には匙を投げる. Unlike the neutral あきらめる, it stresses that someone capitulates after efforts of their own. Often written in kana as さじを投げる.

en.meaning: to be intolerable; to be beyond what can be overlooked
examples[].german: His behavior is intolerable.
His lateness lately is hardly acceptable any more.
The appalling manners of tourists have become a problem.
en.notes: 目に余る literally means "to exceed the eye": something is so bad that you can no longer overlook it, hence "intolerable, no longer acceptable". It almost always judges other people's behavior: 目に余る行為・態度・振る舞い or predicatively 〜は目に余るものがある. Unlike 我慢できない (personal feeling), it sounds like an objective, rather formal judgment from outside. The meaning "too much to see it all" is rare.

en.meaning: needless to say; better left unsaid
examples[].german: The result goes without saying.
He speaks English, needless to say, and also French and Chinese.
I carelessly said something that should have been left unsaid and made her angry.
en.notes: 言わずもがな is a classical form of "better not to say" and has two uses. Mostly it means "of course, not to mention", especially in the pattern AはBは言わずもがな、Cも… "A of course, but also C". With の before a noun, however, it means "what would better be left unsaid": 言わずもがなのことを言う "to say something superfluous or tactless". The expression is elevated and literary; in everyday speech people usually say もちろん or 言うまでもない.

examples[].german: I won't give in to any difficulty.
Violence is not permitted for any reason whatsoever.
Nobody knows what kind of person he actually is.
en.notes: いかなる is the elevated, literary counterpart of どんな and always stands directly before a noun. The most common use is the generalizing one with も・でも・にも: いかなる理由があっても "for whatever reason", いかなる困難にも "in the face of any difficulty". There is also the question use "what kind of …?" (いかなる人物か). The kanji spelling 如何なる is rare; kana is usual.

examples[].german: This year's students are excellent across the board.
Winters in this region generally have a lot of snow.
Reception of the new product is good across the board.
en.notes: おしなべて sums up a group: "on the whole, across the board". It stands before evaluative statements such as 高い, 良好だ, 優秀だ and refers to many individual cases at once. Equivalent in meaning but somewhat more common are 概して and 総じて; the neutral 一般に sounds less like a summing-up. Almost always written in kana; the kanji 押し並べて are rare.
