examples[].german: The girl's face turned red and her heart pounded.
With the stethoscope, I heard the baby's heartbeat.
You can feel the pulse of a new era in this city.
en.notes: 鼓動 is the "heartbeat" as a perceptible pounding, especially in excitement: 鼓動が高鳴る, 鼓動が速くなる. Medically and soberly, one speaks of 心拍 or 脈 "pulse"; onomatopoeically one says ドキドキする. Figuratively, 鼓動 can also mean the "pulsing" of an era or a city (新しい時代の鼓動). As a verb, 鼓動する is rare and literary.

en.meaning: to heal; to soothe; to quench
examples[].german: I soothed my travel fatigue by soaking in a hot spring.
I quenched my thirst with cold water.
Time should heal the wounds of the heart.
en.notes: 癒す (also 癒やす) means "to heal, to soothe, to quench" and is transitive: 疲れを癒す "to recover", 心の傷を癒す, のどの渇きを癒す "to quench thirst". It is mostly about exhaustion, emotional wounds or needs; the medical healing of an illness is rather 治す. The intransitive counterpart is 癒える "to heal over". The noun 癒し "relaxation, comfort" is very widespread (癒し系).

examples[].german: Ryota's face turned pale with anger.
When my mother heard the news of the accident, she turned deathly pale.
He lay in bed with a high fever and a pallid face.
en.notes: 蒼白 describes a face color that is ashen and pale from fright, fear or illness, and is written language. It almost always refers to the face: 顔面蒼白になる, 顔が蒼白になる, 蒼白な顔. In conversation one rather says 顔が青白い or 青ざめる "to turn pale"; paleness is expressed in Japanese with 青. For light skin as a beauty feature, 蒼白 is not appropriate; for that one says 色白.

en.meaning: warranty against defects; seller's liability for latent defects
examples[].german: The seller is subject to liability for defects.
A leaky roof was found in the house I bought, so I held the seller liable for defects.
With the civil code reform, liability for defects was replaced by liability for nonconformity to the contract.
en.notes: 瑕疵担保責任 is the seller's liability for hidden defects (隠れた瑕疵) of the item sold; 瑕疵 is the legal word for "defect". Typical: 瑕疵担保責任を負う, 〜を免責する, 瑕疵担保責任を追及する. Since the civil code reform of 2020, the institution is officially called 契約不適合責任; the old term, however, remains widespread in real estate and construction contracts and in common usage. Register: legal.

examples[].german: This man seems to have come from a country in the East.
There is a small mountain to the east of the village.
In the Christmas play, I played one of the Magi.
en.notes: 東方 is the written-language word for "east, eastern direction" (村の東方に "east of the village") and for the "Orient", for example in 東方の三博士 "the Magi (Wise Men from the East)" or 東方正教会 "Eastern Church". In everyday speech one simply says 東 or 東の方 (ひがしのほう). The counterpart is 西方.

examples[].german: The Japan national team won a narrow 2-1 victory after extra time.
The incumbent mayor narrowly beat the newcomer in the election.
Even if it was a narrow win, a win is a win.
en.notes: 辛勝 is a "narrow victory", literally "to win with difficulty"; as an intransitive する-verb the opponent takes に: 強豪に辛勝する. The word comes from sports and election reports. Opposites are 楽勝 "easy win", 圧勝 "landslide victory" and 惜敗 "narrow defeat". Colloquially one says ギリギリで勝つ or 辛くも勝つ.

examples[].german: Our company is enjoying great benefits from the weak yen.
All citizens have the right to enjoy freedom and equality.
Since retiring, my father has been enjoying a quiet life in the countryside.
en.notes: 享受 means "to enjoy, to come to enjoy something" and is a formal, transitive する-verb. Its objects are abstract things such as 恩恵, 権利, 自由, 豊かさ or 平和: 恩恵を享受する "to benefit from something". For personal enjoyment of food or leisure, use 楽しむ or 味わう. Do not confuse it with the identically read 教授 "professor".

examples[].german: Who do you think was the strongest hero in Japanese history?
Numerous bold heroes appear in "Romance of the Three Kingdoms".
My grandfather was a fearless type who didn't worry about small things.
en.notes: 豪傑 is a "hero, bold warrior": someone of great physical strength and fearlessness, especially in war stories such as 三国志. In contrast to 英雄 "hero" (great deeds, role model), 豪傑 emphasizes strength, daring and a generous, carefree nature. Today it is also used half-jokingly for people with a rough, carefree temperament (豪傑タイプ).

examples[].german: We can't say anything until we have performed an autopsy.
In science class we dissected a frog.
The book sharply dissects the problems of modern society.
en.notes: 解剖 means "dissection, autopsy" and is transitive: カエルを解剖する. Common are 司法解剖 "forensic autopsy", 病理解剖 and 解剖学 "anatomy". Figuratively it means a thorough "dissection, analysis" of a problem or work (社会を解剖する). For a doctor's examination of living patients, use 診察 or 検査, not 解剖.

examples[].german: You idiot! Watch where you're walking.
Because of jet lag I'm unbearably sleepy even during the day.
In manzai, the interplay between the boke and the tsukkomi is important.
en.notes: ぼけ (rarely 呆け, often ボケ) is first of all a term of abuse, "fool, idiot", particularly strong in the Kansai dialect (このボケ！). It also colloquially refers to declining mental faculties in old age; today the more respectful 認知症 is used for that. As a suffix it means "dazed from": 時差ぼけ "jet lag", 寝ぼけ. In 漫才, the ボケ is the comedian who talks nonsense and the ツッコミ is the one who corrects him.

examples[].german: Everyone was dumbfounded by her strange behavior.
I was stunned by how high the price was.
The match I had been looking forward to ended disappointingly quickly.
en.notes: 呆気 occurs practically only in two expressions and is usually written in kana: 呆気に取られる "to be dumbfounded, speechless" (frozen with surprise) and the adjective 呆気ない "disappointingly short, over all too quickly". The cause is marked with に: 彼の言葉に呆気に取られる. Similar is ぽかんとする; stronger is 唖然とする.

en.meaning: to be utterly appalled; to be flabbergasted
examples[].german: I was utterly appalled because the room was so dirty.
I was truly aghast at his irresponsible attitude.
I'm so appalled at such lack of common sense that I'm speechless.
en.notes: 呆れ返る is an intensification of 呆れる: "to be completely stunned, appalled", usually out of indignation or disgust at stupidity, impudence or sloppiness. The trigger is marked with に: 彼の態度に呆れ返る. Set phrase: 呆れ返って物も言えない "so appalled that one is lost for words". Intransitive; often written in kana as あきれ返る.

en.meaning: to busy oneself (for); to run around (on behalf of)
examples[].german: Our company president is busy scrambling to arrange funding.
He ran around tirelessly to support the disaster area.
Thanks to a friend's efforts, I found a job.
en.notes: 奔走 literally means "running around" and refers to working tirelessly for a goal, running everywhere and negotiating with many people. The goal is marked with に or 〜のために: 資金集めに奔走する. As a noun it also means the "mediation, efforts" of others: 友人の奔走で. Related is the saying 東奔西走. Literary; in everyday speech, 走り回る or 駆け回る is used.

en.meaning: duty of care of a good manager
examples[].german: Directors are subject to the duty of care of a good manager.
The shareholders sued the executives who had incurred losses through reckless investments for breach of the duty of care.
A rented room must be used in compliance with the duty of care.
en.notes: 善管注意義務 is the short form of 善良な管理者の注意義務, the duty of care of a "good manager" in civil law. It applies to everyone who looks after another's affairs or property: agents, custodians, tenants and above all board members of a company. It is stricter than the care applied to one's own affairs. Typical: 善管注意義務を負う／怠る, 善管注意義務違反. Register: legal.

examples[].german: I was drawn to that free-spirited personality.
She paints unique pictures with her unbridled imagination.
In my youth I lived a wild life without listening to my parents.
en.notes: 奔放 means "unrestrained, free and unconstrained": someone follows only their own impulses, without regard for conventions. It almost always appears in the combination 自由奔放 (な性格, に生きる). Depending on context it sounds positive (free-spirited, creative: 奔放な想像力) or negative (licentious, e.g. 恋愛に奔放). It is a な-adjective: 奔放な, adverbial 奔放に. わがまま, in contrast, emphasizes selfishness.

examples[].german: For some reason I feel more reassured by information I get from print media.
We are considering which medium to place the advertisement in.
Please save the data on an external storage medium.
en.notes: 媒体 is a "medium, carrier": on the one hand communication channels such as 紙媒体 "print media", 広告媒体, 電子媒体; on the other hand technical carriers such as 記録媒体 "storage medium", and physically the substance that transmits sound or heat. For "the media" as the press, メディア or マスコミ is usually used. Do not confuse it with 媒介 "mediation, transmission (e.g. of diseases)".

examples[].german: Thank you so much for taking the trouble to act as go-between at our wedding.
The two married through the matchmaking of their former university professor.
Recently there are more and more weddings without a go-between.
en.notes: 媒酌 refers to the role of the official matchmaker or go-between (仲人) at a traditional Japanese wedding. The person is called 媒酌人, which is more formal than 仲人 and typical of wedding speeches and invitation cards. Set phrases are 〜の媒酌で結婚する and 媒酌の労をとる ("to take on the role of go-between"); as a verb, 媒酌する is rarely used. Today many couples do without a 媒酌人 altogether.

examples[].german: Look, a yacht is sailing over there.
This ship sails with wind power alone, without an engine.
The training ship crossed the Pacific under sail.
en.notes: 帆走 is "sailing" in the sense of "traveling by sail power" and belongs to technical and written language (帆走訓練, 帆走中). Intransitive; the route traveled is marked with を: 太平洋を帆走する. In everyday speech, ヨットに乗る or セーリングする is more common. Related: 帆船 "sailing ship", 帆を張る "to set the sails".

examples[].german: My uncle repairs stringed instruments.
Violins and cellos are members of the string family.
The shamisen and koto are also counted as stringed instruments.
en.notes: 弦楽器 are all "stringed instruments", both bowed ones such as バイオリン and チェロ and plucked ones such as ギター, 琴 or 三味線. "Bowed string instrument" in the narrow sense is the technical term 擦弦楽器. The other groups are 管楽器 "wind instruments" and 打楽器 "percussion instruments". Related: 弦楽四重奏 "string quartet".

examples[].german: He composed a suite for orchestra.
There is an orchestral concert at the civic hall this weekend.
I play the cello in the university orchestra.
en.notes: 管弦楽 is "orchestral music", literally music for "pipes (winds) and strings". The word is formal and appears in titles of works (管弦楽のための〜) and concert programs. The orchestra itself is called 管弦楽団, but in everyday speech usually オーケストラ. Chamber music is 室内楽, a wind band is 吹奏楽.

examples[].german: The kindergarten children are doing action games to music.
At the sports day, the oldest class performed a dance.
This is nothing more than a play on words.
en.notes: 遊戯 is a formal word for "play, playing" (遊戯施設 "play facilities", 遊戯室 "playroom"). In everyday life it appears mainly as お遊戯: singing and movement games that kindergarten children perform to music. Figuratively, 〜の遊戯 means a mere "game, trifling". For ordinary playing, use 遊び/遊ぶ. Do not confuse it with 遊技 (gaming machines, pachinko).

examples[].german: Most students live on support from their parents.
Families in financial difficulty receive living assistance from the state.
Spouses are obliged to support each other.
en.notes: 扶助 is formal or legal "support, assistance", especially material help for people who cannot provide for themselves: 生活扶助 "living-expense assistance" under welfare, 相互扶助 "mutual aid", 扶助を受ける. 扶養, in contrast, means the duty to support dependents; in everyday speech, 援助, 支援 or simply 助け is used.

examples[].german: This is an immortal masterpiece.
He left enduring achievements in physics.
Through this discovery, her name became immortal.
en.notes: 不朽 means "imperishable, immortal" (literally "not rotting") and is used practically only attributively with の: 不朽の名作, 不朽の名曲, 不朽の功績, 不朽の名声. It is elevated and praising. Similar is 不滅 (不滅の記録 "eternal record"); the opposite, decay through age, is expressed by 老朽 or 朽ちる.

examples[].german: That building is quite dilapidated, so you'd better not go in.
Replacing the aging water pipes is urgent.
It was decided to rebuild the run-down school building.
en.notes: 老朽 refers to decay through age and today is used almost only for buildings, facilities and infrastructure, mostly as 老朽化 (する): 老朽化した橋, 老朽化が進む. As a prefix it appears in 老朽施設 or 老朽校舎. For people it is outdated. 劣化, in contrast, means general deterioration of material or quality.

examples[].german: Acts that violate the principle of good faith receive no legal protection.
Even though it was not written in the contract, a duty to explain was found based on good faith.
The unilateral breaking off of negotiations was judged a violation of good faith.
en.notes: 信義則 is the short form of 信義誠実の原則, the principle of good faith in the Japanese Civil Code (Art. 1, para. 2). Typical: 信義則に反する, 信義則違反, 信義則上の義務 (e.g. duties to inform or protect that are not in the contract). The same article contains the prohibition of 権利濫用. Register: legal, hardly used in everyday life.

examples[].german: I injured my spine in a traffic accident and was left paralyzed from the waist down.
Humans are a kind of vertebrate.
Next month I'm going to have surgery on my spine.
en.notes: 脊椎 is the medical term for the "spine, vertebral column" or a single "vertebra"; in everyday speech 背骨 is used. Important are 脊椎動物 "vertebrates" and 無脊椎動物 "invertebrates". Do not confuse it with 脊髄 "spinal cord", which runs inside the spine (脊髄損傷 "spinal cord injury").

examples[].german: Kanae has a very gentle, ladylike personality.
She walked gracefully in her kimono.
As a child I was often told to behave more demurely.
en.notes: しとやか (rarely 淑やか) describes "gentle, ladylike, gracefully reserved" behavior and is used almost only for women, usually with お: おしとやかな人, おしとやかにする. It sounds somewhat old-fashioned and carries traditional gender roles. 上品 "refined" is more general; 大人しい "quiet, well-behaved" emphasizes restraint without elegance.

examples[].german: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.
She has grown into a fine lady whom everyone admires.
This novel depicts the lives of ladies of high society.
en.notes: 淑女 is a "lady" in the sense of an educated, refined woman and is the counterpart of 紳士 "gentleman". It is most often heard in the form of address 紳士淑女の皆さん "ladies and gentlemen". Otherwise it sounds elevated to old-fashioned; in everyday speech, 女性 or レディー is used. In internet slang, 淑女 is used ironically for "perverted" women.

examples[].german: Regulations were introduced to prevent water pollution of the lake.
The river was polluted by the factory's wastewater.
The new prime minister promised to sweep away the corruption in politics.
en.notes: 汚濁 is "pollution, turbidity", above all of water; the fixed term is 水質汚濁 "water pollution" (law: 水質汚濁防止法). As an intransitive する-verb: 川が汚濁する. Figuratively it means moral "depravity, corruption" (政界の汚濁). 汚染 is the more general word, also for air, soil or radioactivity.

en.meaning: to make cloudy; to be evasive (in answering)
examples[].german: Faced with a question that hit the core of the matter, the president was evasive.
A child stirred the pond and made the water cloudy.
Since I was poorly prepared, I got by with some vague talk.
en.notes: 濁す is the transitive verb of 濁る "to become cloudy": literally "to make cloudy, to muddy" (水を濁す). Much more common is the figurative use: 言葉を濁す "to answer evasively, not to commit oneself" and お茶を濁す "to muddle through with a makeshift solution, to talk around something". The proverb 立つ鳥跡を濁さず urges one to leave a place clean.

examples[].german: I was nearly swallowed by the muddy torrent, but he saved me.
Because of the heavy rain, the river is flowing as a muddy torrent.
The muddy torrent swept the bridge away.
en.notes: 濁流 is a "muddy, raging flood", as rivers carry after heavy rain or typhoons: 濁流に飲み込まれる "to be swept away by the flood", 川が濁流となる. The opposite is 清流 "clear stream". The word is used mainly in news and narratives; in everyday speech, 泥水 or 増水した川 is used.

examples[].german: A decision was made not to prosecute.
Because it was his first offense and he was deeply remorseful, prosecution was suspended.
Unlike an acquittal, suspension of prosecution presupposes that there is suspicion of a crime.
en.notes: 起訴猶予 means that the public prosecutor "refrains from indictment" despite sufficient suspicion, for example because of triviality, a first offense or remorse. It is a form of 不起訴処分 and is expressed with 起訴猶予処分になる/とする. Do not confuse it with 執行猶予 "suspended sentence on probation" after a conviction or with 嫌疑不十分 "for lack of evidence".

examples[].german: Where did you get sulfuric acid?
When handling sulfuric acid in experiments, always wear safety goggles.
When diluting concentrated sulfuric acid, add it to water little by little.
en.notes: 硫酸 is "sulfuric acid"; 硫 stands for sulfur (硫黄), 酸 for acid. One distinguishes 濃硫酸 "concentrated" and 希硫酸 "dilute sulfuric acid"; salts are called 硫酸塩 (e.g. 硫酸銅). Other important acids are 塩酸 "hydrochloric acid" and 硝酸 "nitric acid".

examples[].german: Apparently he repeatedly stole to relieve stress.
The man was arrested on suspicion of theft.
Bicycle thefts are increasing in front of the station.
en.notes: 窃盗 is the legal and journalistic term for "theft" without violence (窃盗罪, 窃盗犯, 窃盗の容疑). With violence or threats it is 強盗 "robbery"; subtypes are 万引き "shoplifting", 空き巣 "burglary of an unoccupied home" or スリ "pickpocketing". In everyday speech, 盗む or 泥棒 is used; 窃盗する as a verb is rare.

examples[].german: We're supposed to have a gentlemen's agreement with those guys.
The two companies have a gentlemen's agreement not to poach each other's employees.
A gentlemen's agreement has no legal binding force.
en.notes: 紳士協定 is a "gentlemen's agreement": an unwritten arrangement based on mutual trust that is not legally binding. Typical verbs: 紳士協定を結ぶ, 守る, 破る. It is found in business (no poaching, no price wars), sports and diplomacy. A formal contract is 契約 or 協定.

examples[].german: The claim was not allowed under the doctrine of abuse of rights.
Demanding the demolition of a building over a slight encroachment across the boundary constitutes abuse of rights.
The company's dismissal was judged invalid as an abuse of rights.
en.notes: 権利濫用 refers to the exercise of a right that does exist, but so unreasonably that it is not protected; the Civil Code says in Art. 1, para. 3: 権利の濫用は、これを許さない. Typical: 権利濫用に当たる, 権利濫用として無効, 権利濫用の法理 (e.g. with dismissals: 解雇権の濫用). In newspapers also written 権利乱用. Register: legal.

examples[].german: Please buy some silk thread at the thread shop in Nishijin.
Silk thread has a gloss and is often used for kimono embroidery.
This region once prospered through the export of silk thread.
en.notes: 絹糸 "silk thread, silk yarn" has two readings: in everyday speech usually きぬいと, in technical language and industry (textiles, trade) rather けんし. It is used for sewing, embroidering and weaving fine fabrics such as kimonos. Not the same is 生糸 "raw silk", the yarn reeled directly from the cocoon; cotton thread is 綿糸.

examples[].german: Have you ever experienced sleep paralysis?
Sleep paralysis is said to occur easily when you are tired.
I was so frightened that I couldn't move, as if paralyzed.
en.notes: 金縛り is above all "sleep paralysis": you wake up but cannot move. One says 金縛りにあう (遭う); in folk belief it is often attributed to ghosts, medically it is called 睡眠麻痺. Figuratively, 金縛りにあったように describes freezing from fear or shock. Literally it means "bound with metal fetters".

examples[].german: In Westerns, there are often scenes where villains are hanged.
In medieval Europe, thieves were sometimes hanged.
If that gets out, you'll hang for it!
en.notes: 縛り首 is "death by the rope, hanging" as a punishment; literally "neck-binding". Typical: 縛り首にする/される. The word sounds archaic and appears in Western films, historical novels or translations. The legal technical term, also for the present-day death penalty in Japan, is 絞首刑.

examples[].german: I sewed it myself, so the seams are crooked.
The seam of my trousers has come apart.
The surgical stitches still hurt a little.
en.notes: ぬいめ "seam, stitch" is normally written 縫い目; the spelling 縫目 without い is rare. It refers to the seam on clothing (縫い目がほつれる "the seam comes undone"), individual stitches (縫い目が粗い/細かい) and also the surgical suture after an operation. Related are 縫う "to sew" and 継ぎ目 "joint, seam" in components.

examples[].german: Let me have that painter paint my portrait.
Portraits of historical figures are printed on banknotes.
Posting other people's photos online without permission can violate their portrait rights.
en.notes: 肖像 refers to the likeness of a specific person, usually as a painting, photo or sculpture. On its own it belongs more to elevated language (肖像を描く); in everyday life one almost always hears compounds such as 肖像画 "portrait painting" or 肖像写真 "portrait photo". An important legal term is 肖像権 "right to one's own image". For a quick photo of a face, 顔写真 is used rather than 肖像.

en.meaning: feudal lord; daimyo of a domain
examples[].german: I went to visit the grave of the domain lord.
Generations of domain lords lived in this castle.
The first domain lord is said to have devoted himself to flood-control works on the river.
en.notes: 藩主 is the lord of a 藩, that is, a feudal domain of the Edo period; essentially a Daimyō in his role as ruler of a territory. The word is a historical technical term and appears in history books, museums and castle tours: 〇〇藩の藩主, 初代藩主, 藩主の居城. 大名 emphasizes the rank as a feudal lord relative to the Shōgun, while 藩主 emphasizes rule over a specific territory.

en.meaning: record of a game; game record
examples[].german: Please teach me how to record a game.
Every evening I study by replaying professional game records on the board.
The game record of the Meijin title match was published online.
en.notes: 棋譜 is the written record of a game of shōgi, go or chess, move by move. One "keeps" it with 棋譜を付ける or 棋譜を取る; replaying a game on the board is called 棋譜を並べる or 棋譜並べ and is a classic training method. The word belongs to the technical language of board games; for musical notation, 楽譜 is used instead.

examples[].german: This scroll records the family's genealogy.
His works follow the lineage of Japanese naturalist literature.
This car is the latest model in a lineage of prestigious sports cars.
en.notes: 系譜 is first of all the family tree or genealogy of a family (一族の系譜, 家の系譜). Very often it is used figuratively for a line of tradition or development: 〜の系譜を引く "to stand in the tradition of ...", 〜の系譜に連なる. It sounds literary; the everyday word for a drawn family tree is 家系図.

en.meaning: chronological biography; chronology (of a person's life)
examples[].german: Could you make a chronology of this author's life?
The last volume of the complete works includes a detailed chronology.
On the wall of the exhibition room, the painter's chronology was displayed along with photographs.
en.notes: 年譜 is a chronological overview of a person's life and work, typically as a table at the end of a biography, a volume of collected works or in an exhibition: 作家の年譜, 年譜を作る, 年譜をたどる. For general timelines of historical events, 年表 is more usual; 年譜 is tied to a person (or institution).

examples[].german: I'm looking for a site where I can download sheet music for free.
She played the piece to the end without looking at the score.
Please adjust the height of the music stand before the performance.
en.notes: 譜面 is the music as it lies in front of you in concrete form: the sheet of music on the stand (譜面台). 楽譜 is the more general, somewhat more formal word for sheet music or scores. Typical are 譜面を読む, 譜面を見ながら弾く and 譜面なしで弾く "to play from memory". In rhythm games, the sequence of notes of a song is also called 譜面.

en.meaning: self-help (taking the law into one's own hands)
examples[].german: In Japanese law, self-help is in principle prohibited.
If a landlord arbitrarily locks out a tenant who is behind on rent, that is self-help.
Even if the money you lent is not returned, taking the other person's belongings on your own may be illegal as self-help.
en.notes: 自力救済 is the arbitrary enforcement of a claim without a court, for example when a landlord simply changes the lock over unpaid rent. In Japanese law the 自力救済の禁止 applies: self-help is permitted only in narrow exceptional cases, otherwise it can lead to damages. To be distinguished from 正当防衛 "self-defense" against a present attack. Typical: 自力救済に当たる, 自力救済は禁じられている. Register: legal.

examples[].german: He was exceptionally granted a pardon for his crime.
The monk exiled to an island was finally pardoned after ten years.
In celebration of the king's wedding, many prisoners were pardoned.
en.notes: 赦免 is the remission of a punishment or guilt by a higher authority, that is, a pardon. As a transitive する-verb: 罪人を赦免する, passive 赦免される; also 赦免状 "letter of pardon". The word sounds historical or legal-solemn; for present-day state amnesty, 恩赦 is mostly used, and for everyday forgiving, 許す.

examples[].german: Criminals must be punished without mercy.
We apologize for the inconvenience during construction and ask for your kind understanding.
The midsummer sun beat down mercilessly.
en.notes: 容赦 means leniency or sparing. Most often it appears negated: 容赦なく "mercilessly, ruthlessly", 容赦しない "to show no mercy", 情け容赦もない. In polite notices, one asks for understanding or pardon with ご容赦ください, for example for disruptions or mistakes. Positively and without negation it is rarely used outside this formula.

en.meaning: to pour (sake); to drink together; to take (feelings) into account
examples[].german: I drank sake late into the night with a friend I hadn't seen in a long time.
Taking her feelings into account, I did not ask anything further.
The department head took our circumstances into account and extended the deadline.
en.notes: 酌む originally means "to pour sake" or "to drink sake together", today mainly in 酒を酌み交わす "to drink together". The second, very common meaning is "to take someone's feelings or situation into account": 気持ちを酌む, 事情を酌む, 意を酌む. Not to be confused with the identically read 汲む "to draw water" - in the figurative meaning both spellings are used, but drawing water from a well is written only with 汲む. Pouring itself is usually called お酌をする or 注ぐ in everyday speech.

examples[].german: I was mistaken for the culprit and handcuffed.
The police officer put handcuffs on the suspect's wrists.
The handcuffs were finally removed once I entered the interrogation room.
en.notes: 手錠 means handcuffs; the standard verb is 手錠をかける "to put handcuffs on", passive 手錠をかけられる, and to remove them is 手錠を外す. Less often one hears 手錠をはめる. The word appears mainly in news, crime stories and police contexts. 錠 means "lock", hence also 南京錠 "padlock".

examples[].german: I can't swallow tablets, so I crush them before taking them.
Take one of these tablets three times a day after meals.
If you're not good with powdered medicine, they can switch you to tablets.
en.notes: 錠剤 is a tablet as a dosage form, in contrast to 粉薬 "powder", カプセル "capsule" or 水薬 "liquid medicine". One takes it with 飲む (錠剤を水で飲む); tablets are counted with 錠: 一回二錠. In everyday speech one often says simply 薬; 錠剤 emphasizes the form and often appears on package inserts and in the pharmacy.

examples[].german: I just get bored of things easily.
This design is simple, so you don't tire of it even after using it for a long time.
Having the same bento every day, you do get sick of it eventually.
en.notes: 飽き is the noun of 飽きる "to get tired of something" and refers to the weariness or boredom that sets in after a while. Typical are 飽きが来る "to get sick of it" and the praise 飽きが来ない "you never tire of it" (for design, taste, music). From the same root comes 飽きっぽい "quickly bored, lacking perseverance". For general boredom without prior excess, 退屈 is more usual.

en.meaning: persistently; to the end; only; merely
examples[].german: To be clear, this is only my personal opinion.
He persistently opposed the plan to the very end.
These figures are only a rough guide, so they may change somewhat.
en.notes: 飽くまでも is almost always written in kana (あくまでも, shorter あくまで). It has two meanings: "persistently, to the bitter end" (あくまでも反対する, あくまで戦う) and, very common in everyday speech, in a limiting sense "only, merely, after all", to qualify a statement: あくまでも個人的な意見ですが…, あくまで参考です. The translation "quite" fits neither meaning.

examples[].german: I try to eat chicken tenderloin as much as possible.
I wrote "300 grams of chicken" on my shopping list.
en.notes: 鶏肉 is read とりにく here and refers to chicken meat. とり肉 is a mixed spelling with hiragana for 鶏, which one may encounter in a simplified text, for example. 鶏肉のささみ are the tenderloins of the chicken breast. 食べるようにしています describes a habit kept up deliberately; できるだけ means "as much as possible" here, not a fixed amount of meat. The also attested reading けいにく is not the reading practiced on this card.

examples[].german: The price of chicken eggs has risen sharply over the past year.
This product contains chicken egg as part of its ingredients.
My son has an egg allergy, so we are careful when eating out.
en.notes: 鶏卵 is the formal word for "hen's egg" and appears in statistics, economic news, food labeling and allergy information (鶏卵アレルギー). In everyday speech one says simply 卵 or, for cooked eggs and on menus, often 玉子. Someone who says 鶏卵 in a supermarket sounds like a technical article.

examples[].german: I keenly felt how difficult it is to run a poultry farm.
After an outbreak of bird flu, a large number of chickens were culled at a nearby poultry farm.
My grandfather ran a small poultry farm in the countryside.
en.notes: 養鶏 is the keeping of chickens or poultry as an industry. It appears almost always in compounds: 養鶏場 "chicken farm", 養鶏業 "poultry industry", 養鶏農家 "poultry farmer". The pattern 養〜 "to raise" is also known from 養豚 "pig farming" and 養殖 "aquaculture". For keeping a few chickens in the yard, 鶏を飼う is more usual.

examples[].german: The court appointed a bankruptcy trustee.
The bankruptcy trustee sold the company's assets and distributed the proceeds to the creditors.
A lawyer well versed in insolvency proceedings took office as trustee.
en.notes: 管財人 is a person appointed by the court, mostly a lawyer, who administers another's assets. Most common are the 破産管財人 "bankruptcy trustee" in bankruptcy and the 更生管財人 in the 会社更生 reorganization procedure. Typical: 管財人を選任する, 管財人に就任する, 管財人の管理下に置かれる. To be distinguished from the 清算人, who handles a voluntary liquidation. Register: legal, business news.

examples[].german: After many experiences, my father arrived at a serene acceptance.
A deep, resigned serenity showed through the old monk's words.
She accepted her illness with equanimity and spent her remaining days in peace.
en.notes: 諦観 is a literary, Buddhist-tinged word with two meanings: "clear insight into the nature of things" and, more common today, the calm, composed acceptance of fate. Typical are 諦観に至る, 諦観の境地 and 諦観をもって受け入れる. Unlike the everyday 諦め "giving up", 諦観 carries a sense of calm and inner maturity, not defeat.

examples[].german: Riko appeared at the meeting place with Ryōichirō in a lapis-blue dress.
From the observation deck, we could see the sea shimmering deep blue.
These deep-blue glasses were each made by hand by a craftsman.
en.notes: 瑠璃色 is a deep, luminous blue with a slight violet tint, named after the semi-precious stone 瑠璃 "lapis lazuli". The word is poetic and is used for the sea, sky, glass, fabrics and bird plumage: 瑠璃色の海, 瑠璃色に輝く. In ordinary conversation one says simply 青 or 紺; 瑠璃色 sounds elevated and vivid.

examples[].german: Sugahara is a cool surname, don't you think?
Mr. Sugahara will be transferred to the Osaka branch from next month.
Is "菅原" read Sugahara or Sugawara?
en.notes: 菅原 is a Japanese family name, not general vocabulary. The usual reading is すがわら (known from the scholar 菅原道真); the reading すがはら occurs as a rarer variant. With names, you can never be sure of the reading from the kanji, so one politely asks: お名前は何とお読みすればいいですか. The character 菅 means "sedge, reed grass".

examples[].german: In Japanese trials, there is something called "extenuating circumstances".
The court took the defendant's upbringing into consideration and reduced the sentence.
The prosecution argued that it was a premeditated crime and there was no room for leniency.
en.notes: 酌量 means to take circumstances into account in a mitigating way when judging something. It appears almost always in the legal expression 情状酌量 "consideration of extenuating circumstances" and in 酌量の余地がある／ない "there is (no) room for leniency". As a transitive する-verb: 事情を酌量する. The kanji 酌 is the same as in 気持ちを酌む "to take feelings into account"; outside law and news the word sounds very formal.

examples[].german: This year is my grandfather's second death anniversary.
Relatives gathered for the first time in a long while for the memorial service marking six years since my mother's death.
Many families conclude the memorial services with the 33rd anniversary.
en.notes: 回忌 is a counter for the Buddhist memorial anniversaries of a deceased person and follows numbers: 三回忌, 七回忌, 十三回忌. Note the counting: the day of death itself counts as the first, so 三回忌 is the second anniversary and 七回忌 the sixth. Only the first anniversary has its own name, 一周忌. On these dates one holds a 法要 or 法事.

examples[].german: In the past, entering that mountain was considered taboo in this village.
This medicine is contraindicated for pregnant women.
That author is known for works that deliberately venture into society's taboos.
en.notes: 禁忌 is a taboo, that is, something forbidden for religious, social or moral reasons: 禁忌を犯す "to break a taboo", 禁忌とされる. In medicine it means a contraindication, for example on package inserts (禁忌, 併用禁忌 "must not be combined"). In everyday speech タブー is more usual; 禁忌 sounds written and technical.

examples[].german: In July there is a memorial service for the first anniversary of my wife's father's death.
My grandmother passed away, and time flies: next month will be the first anniversary.
What should one wear to a first-anniversary memorial service?
en.notes: 一周忌 is the first anniversary of a death and the accompanying Buddhist memorial service (一周忌の法要／法事). After that, counting continues with 回忌: the second anniversary is already 三回忌. Typical combinations are 一周忌を迎える and 一周忌を営む "to hold the memorial service". Until the 一周忌, one is considered in mourning (喪中) in Japan.

en.meaning: rice-planting girl; young woman who plants rice seedlings
examples[].german: In the past, women who planted rice seedlings in paddies were called "saotome" or "ueme".
At the rice-planting festival, women in kimono plant seedlings to the rhythm of songs.
Local elementary school children put on saotome costumes and tried rice planting.
en.notes: 早乙女 are the young women who set the seedlings in the field during traditional rice planting (田植え); さ (早) is the same prefix as in 早苗 ("rice seedling"), and 乙女 means "maiden". Today the word is alive mainly in folk customs and rice festivals, where 早乙女 plant in kimono and straw hats (菅笠). In older language it can mean "young girl" in general; 早乙女 is also a well-known family name.

examples[].german: Why is the Pacific War called the Greater East Asia War?
The word "Tōa" for East Asia often appears in prewar newspapers.
Korea's Dong-A Ilbo is a newspaper founded in 1920.
en.notes: 東亜 is an older, literary word for East Asia. Today 東アジア is normally used; 東亜 lives on mainly in the proper names of companies, universities and newspapers (e.g. the Korean newspaper 東亜日報) and in historical wartime terms such as 大東亜共栄圏 and 大東亜戦争. Because of this association, the word seems historical and partly politically loaded in modern texts.

examples[].german: Are you telling me to stay quiet after receiving an insult like this?
He made a remark in the meeting that insulted his subordinates, which became a problem.
With online slander on the rise, the insult offense has been made stricter.
en.notes: 侮辱 is an insult or humiliation that injures another person's honor. As a transitive する-verb: 人を侮辱する; from the victim's perspective 侮辱を受ける or 侮辱される; adjectivally 侮辱的な発言. Legally there is 侮辱罪 "insult (as a criminal offense)". In everyday speech, for milder mocking, 馬鹿にする is more usual; 侮辱 is more serious and more formal.

examples[].german: A company in financial difficulty applied for civil rehabilitation proceedings.
Civil rehabilitation is a procedure for rebuilding a company without dissolving it.
Because our business partner filed for civil rehabilitation, it has become difficult to collect payment.
en.notes: 民事再生 is the rehabilitation procedure under the 民事再生法: a struggling company (or an individual) continues to exist and restructures according to a plan, usually under its previous management. Typical: 民事再生法の適用を申請する, 民事再生を申し立てる, 民事再生手続き. In contrast, 破産 means dissolution and liquidation of the assets; 会社更生 is a stricter procedure for large stock companies. 倒産 is the general umbrella term for a company's bankruptcy.

examples[].german: It bothers me that the floor is a little uneven.
The mountain path was bumpy and very hard to ride on by bicycle.
The tall man and the petite woman are a well-known mismatched pair at work.
en.notes: 凸凹 (usually written でこぼこ) describes an uneven, bumpy surface: でこぼこ道, 道がでこぼこしている, as an adjective でこぼこな／でこぼこの. Figuratively it denotes unevenness or imbalance, e.g. in performance or in 凸凹コンビ "mismatched duo". The same kanji are also read おうとつ in technical usage ("projections and depressions") - that is a different, written word.

en.meaning: to be dented; to feel down
examples[].german: I'm feeling down because of a breakup.
I was hit in the parking lot, and the car door got dented.
Don't be so down. Next time it will surely go well.
en.notes: 凹む (usually written へこむ) first means "to be pressed in, to get a dent": 車のドアが凹んだ. Very common in colloquial speech is the figurative meaning "to be dejected, to feel down", often with で for the reason: 失恋で凹む, 上司に怒られて凹んでいる. It is intransitive; the transitive counterpart is 凹ませる "to dent, to pull in" (お腹を凹ませる). The opposite in the literal sense is 出っ張る "to stick out".

examples[].german: I want to choose my spouse only after careful consideration.
Our shop uses only vegetables from carefully selected growing regions.
We need to scrutinize the content of the proposal once more.
en.notes: 吟味 means to examine something carefully and select the best, with emphasis on quality: 材料を吟味する, 内容をよく吟味する. Typical in restaurant advertising (吟味した素材 "carefully selected ingredients") and for decisions one does not want to make hastily. In contrast to 検査 "technical inspection" or 審査 "assessment by an authority", 吟味 is about critical weighing. Transitive する-verb.

examples[].german: We submitted our marriage registration to the municipal office.
The two have lived together for a long time but are not in a legal marital relationship.
The debate continues over whether to recognize marriage between same-sex couples.
en.notes: 婚姻 is the legal term for marriage or the contracting of marriage and appears in laws, forms and news: 婚姻届 "marriage registration (at the office)", 婚姻関係 "marital relationship", 婚姻率 "marriage rate". In Japan one is legally married as soon as the 婚姻届 is accepted; a wedding ceremony is not necessary for this. In everyday speech one says 結婚; 婚姻 sounds official.

examples[].german: US forces are stationed over there.
A summer festival is held every year at the Self-Defense Forces garrison.
The unit was stationed for six months in a town near the border.
en.notes: 駐屯 means that troops are stationed at a place and take up quarters there. It is an intransitive する-verb: 部隊が〜に駐屯する, 〜に駐屯している. Very common is 駐屯地 "garrison, barracks", especially for sites of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (陸上自衛隊〇〇駐屯地). For the active "to station troops", 駐留させる or 配備する is more usual.

examples[].german: The happy events of close friends make me as happy as if they were my own.
When replying to a wedding invitation, etiquette is to affix a stamp for celebratory occasions.
To celebrate the joyous event in the imperial family, commemorative events were held in various places.
en.notes: 慶事 is a formal word for a joyful, festive event such as a wedding, birth or anniversary. Its counterpart is 弔事 "bereavement"; together they form 慶弔. It appears in questions of etiquette (慶事のマナー, 慶事用の切手), in news about the imperial family (皇室の慶事) and in letters. In conversation one says おめでたいこと or おめでた instead.

examples[].german: Benkei and Ushiwakamaru fought at Kiyomizu Temple.
I banged my shin against the table leg and instinctively crouched down in pain.
Our son is a lion at home but quiet at school.
en.notes: 弁慶 is 武蔵坊弁慶, the legendary warrior monk of the 12th century who, according to legend, lost a duel to the young 牛若丸 (later 源義経) and then served him faithfully. By extension, 弁慶 stands for a "strongman" and appears in many expressions: 弁慶の泣き所 ("shin; Achilles' heel"), 内弁慶 ("strong at home, timid outside"), 弁慶の立ち往生 ("to die standing; to be unable to go forward or back"). 弁慶 also refers to a perforated bamboo stand for kitchen utensils and, as a short form of 弁慶縞, a checkered pattern.

examples[].german: To express our congratulations, cheers!
Events celebrating the new emperor's accession were held throughout the country.
With the hundredth anniversary of its founding, the town is wrapped in a celebratory mood.
en.notes: 慶祝 means to celebrate a joyous event solemnly or to congratulate on it, mostly on a public or official level: 慶祝行事 "celebration event", 慶祝ムード, 〜を慶祝する. The word is very formal and belongs to speeches, commemorative volumes and news. For personal congratulations, お祝い or 祝う is used.

en.meaning: joys and sorrows; weddings and funerals
examples[].german: Do you have formal wear for weddings and funerals?
For my grandmother's funeral, I applied to the company for ceremonial leave.
How to wrap money for celebrations and condolences differs slightly from region to region.
en.notes: 慶弔 combines joyful (慶) and sad (弔) occasions, that is, weddings and births as well as deaths. The word appears mainly in compounds from the world of companies and etiquette: 慶弔休暇 "special leave for a wedding or bereavement", 慶弔費 "payments for celebrations and condolences", 慶弔電報. On its own it is hardly used in conversation.

examples[].german: Suspicions of political manipulation by a foreign country have surfaced.
The children enjoyed making crafts with paper and wood.
Behind-the-scenes maneuvering targeted opposition lawmakers to get the bill passed.
en.notes: 工作 has three meanings; the context decides. In everyday life it is "crafts, handiwork": 夏休みの工作, the school subject 図画工作 (short 図工). Technically it stands for "machining, manufacture" as in 工作機械 "machine tool". Politically it means covert influence: 政治工作, 裏工作 "behind-the-scenes machinations", 工作員 "agent". The more neutral 根回し is an informal preliminary understanding, not an intrigue.

examples[].german: A large company filed for corporate reorganization proceedings.
Japan Airlines applied for corporate reorganization under the Corporate Reorganization Act in 2010.
If you choose corporate reorganization rather than bankruptcy, you can aim for rebuilding while continuing the business.
en.notes: 会社更生 is the court-supervised reorganization procedure for (mostly large) stock companies under the 会社更生法, comparable to Chapter 11 in the U.S. The company is not broken up as in 破産, but continues under a 管財人 appointed by the court; the old management usually steps down. For smaller firms there is the 民事再生. Typical in the news: 会社更生法の適用を申請する, 会社更生手続き.

examples[].german: I suffered the pain of a broken heart.
Hit by the recession, a long-established inn went through the bitter experience of bankruptcy.
The team that was a title favorite suffered the unexpected misfortune of being eliminated in the qualifiers.
en.notes: 憂き目 is a bitter, painful experience that befalls someone. It appears almost always in the set phrases 〜の憂き目に遭う or 〜の憂き目を見る, with the misfortune before it: 倒産の憂き目, 落選の憂き目, リストラの憂き目. The word is literary and common in news and sports reports; in conversation one says つらい目に遭う instead.

examples[].german: It is a clumsy piece of writing, but please read it if you like.
No one will be convinced by such a childish excuse.
That painter's pictures look crude at first glance, but they have a strange charm.
en.notes: 稚拙 describes something as clumsy and childishly immature, especially texts, drawings, arguments or techniques: 稚拙な文章, 稚拙な言い訳. As a な-adjective it is rather disparaging, but it is often said modestly about one's own work (稚拙な文章ですが…). In contrast to 下手 "bad, unskilled", 稚拙 emphasizes immaturity; in art it can also mean positively "naive, unaffected".

examples[].german: How did the mock exam results turn out?
At the school festival, our class is running a yakisoba stall.
A law student played the role of defense lawyer in a mock trial.
en.notes: 模擬 means "imitation, simulation" and appears almost only as the first element of compounds denoting a practice or trial version: 模擬試験 (short 模試) "mock exam", 模擬店 "food stall at a school festival", 模擬裁判 "mock trial", 模擬授業 "demonstration lesson". On its own or as a する-verb it is rarely used; for "to simulate", シミュレーションする is more usual.

examples[].german: The tank was camouflaged with tree branches and could not be seen from a distance.
To deceive the enemy, the ship was disguised as a fishing boat.
The entire position is covered with camouflage netting.
en.notes: 擬装 means to disguise something so that it looks like something else, especially in the military sense: 車両を木の枝で擬装する, 擬装網 "camouflage net". The homophonous spelling 偽装 is much more common today for deception and fraud: 食品偽装 "food fraud", 偽装結婚 "sham marriage". Both are transitive する-verbs; 擬装 seems more technical-military, 偽装 more criminal.

en.meaning: legal profession; legal practitioners (judge, prosecutor, lawyer)
examples[].german: What made you decide to aim for a legal career?
He passed the bar exam and entered the legal profession.
This ruling sparked major debate even in legal circles.
en.notes: 法曹 refers to the professional group of legal practitioners, that is, judges, prosecutors and lawyers, together called 法曹三者. Typical are 法曹界 "legal world", 法曹資格 "qualification to practice law" and 法曹を目指す "to aim for a legal career". Not everyone with a law degree is 法曹; for that one must pass the 司法試験. The word is formal and appears mainly in education and judicial contexts.

en.meaning: not having been in touch for a long time; long time no see
examples[].german: It has been such a long time since we last met.
I apologize very much for not having been in touch for such a long time.
I've been so busy that I haven't been to the gym at all lately.
en.notes: ご無沙汰 means not having contacted or visited someone for a long time; with it, one apologizes, so to speak, for one's own silence. The fixed polite formula is ご無沙汰しております - toward superiors, customers and in letters or emails; among friends one more often says 久しぶり. Also written 御無沙汰. Colloquially it is also used figuratively for places or activities: ジムにはご無沙汰だ "I haven't been to the gym in ages".

examples[].german: Not all Roma are poor, wandering people.
People who had lost their homeland in the war roamed from place to place for years.
The samurai who had lost his lord set out on a wandering journey.
en.notes: 流浪 is aimless wandering without a fixed residence, often involuntary, for example after being driven out: 国を追われて流浪する, 流浪の旅, 流浪の民 "wandering people". The word is literary and suggests homelessness and hardship. 放浪 is similar but emphasizes free, often self-chosen roaming; 流浪 has a heavier, fateful tone. Intransitive する-verb.

examples[].german: At that time I drifted from place to place as if fleeing.
In his youth, he wandered around Asia with just a backpack.
Our cat has a tendency to roam and sometimes doesn't come home for two or three days.
en.notes: 放浪 is wandering without a fixed goal or residence: 各地を放浪する, 放浪の旅, 放浪生活. It can sound romantically free (artists, globetrotters); hence 放浪癖 "wanderlust, tendency to roam". Compared to 流浪 it is less fateful; for mere strolling around town, ぶらぶらする or 散策 is more usual. Intransitive する-verb; the area roamed is marked with を.

examples[].german: Right after the war ended, many vagrants slept at the stations.
The novel's protagonist was a former nobleman who had been reduced to living as a vagrant.
Today people often say "homeless" rather than "furōsha".
en.notes: 浮浪者 refers to a vagrant, that is, someone without a fixed residence or regular work. The word is considered derogatory today and is avoided in the media; neutral terms are ホームレス or, officially, 路上生活者. 浮浪者 is therefore found mainly in older texts, novels and historical accounts, for example about the postwar period.

en.meaning: liquidation; settlement (of debts); breaking with the past
examples[].german: The liquidation procedure of the dissolved corporation is progressing.
He settled all his debts and started a new life.
To leave her past behind, she left her hometown.
en.notes: 清算 has three meanings: to settle debts or accounts finally (借金を清算する), to dissolve and wind up a company (会社の清算, 清算人), and, figuratively, to draw a line under something (過去を清算する, 関係を清算する). Transitive する-verb: 〜を清算する. Not to be confused with the identically read 精算 "exact settlement", for example when paying the fare difference at a 精算機 "fare adjustment machine". Register: neutral to formal.

examples[].german: The blue Earth floated in the pitch-black darkness.
Her jet-black hair shone in the moonlight.
This vessel has a pattern painted in gold on a deep black ground.
en.notes: 漆黒 is a deep, glossy black like lacquer (漆 "urushi lacquer"). It is used attributively with の: 漆黒の闇, 漆黒の髪, 漆黒の夜空. The word is literary and vivid; in everyday speech 真っ黒 "completely black" is used. Unlike 真っ黒, which can also mean "dirty" or "sunburned", 漆黒 always describes a beautiful, rich black.

examples[].german: The reef was reclaimed and turned into an artificial island.
On a stormy night, a cargo ship ran aground on a reef.
Around this reef there are many fish, so it is popular with anglers.
en.notes: 岩礁 is a rocky reef, that is, rocks lying just below or above the water surface that are dangerous for ships. Typical is 岩礁に乗り上げる "to run aground on a reef". For coral reefs, サンゴ礁 is used; 暗礁 is a hidden reef under water and appears figuratively in 暗礁に乗り上げる "to run into a deadlock". 岩礁 is a plain, rather written term from seafaring and geography.

en.meaning: root of evil; seed of future trouble
examples[].german: If possible, I would like to avoid leaving behind seeds of future trouble.
A hasty decision could end up sowing seeds of trouble for the future.
To cut off the root of the incident, the system itself should be reviewed.
en.notes: 禍根 is the root of a future disaster, that is, a cause that will bring trouble later. It appears almost always in 禍根を残す "to sow the seed of future trouble" (often 将来に禍根を残す) and 禍根を断つ "to strike the evil at its root". The word is written-style and typical of politics, editorials and negotiations; in conversation one says 後で問題になる instead.

examples[].german: We escaped the ravages of the war and were evacuated to the countryside.
Many citizens were caught up in the war and lost their homes.
This temple miraculously escaped the destruction of war.
en.notes: 戦禍 refers to the devastation and suffering caused by a war. Typical combinations: 戦禍を逃れる "to escape the turmoil of war", 戦禍に巻き込まれる "to be drawn into the war", 戦禍を被る "to suffer from the war". It is a written word from news and historical accounts; 戦災 emphasizes more the concrete material damage (戦災孤児).

en.meaning: critical condition; on the verge of death
examples[].german: I got a phone call saying my father is in critical condition.
My grandmother fell into critical condition, and the whole family gathered at the hospital.
Upon receiving the news of his critical condition, he hurriedly jumped on the Shinkansen.
en.notes: 危篤 refers to the critical condition of a sick person who could die at any moment. Typical: 危篤だ, 危篤状態に陥る, 危篤の知らせを受ける. It is a noun (with だ or の), not an adjective. In contrast to 重体 "seriously injured / in serious condition", which is often used after accidents, 危篤 signals that death is imminent - the family is then summoned immediately.

examples[].german: Break spinning is a spinning method specific to synthetic fibers and is not spinning from cotton.
In the Meiji era, the spinning industry supported Japan's modernization.
My grandmother worked in a spinning mill when she was young.
en.notes: 紡績 is the industrial spinning of fibers such as cotton or wool into yarn; the corresponding verb is 紡ぐ ("to spin"). The word is encountered mainly in business and history: 紡績業, 紡績工場, 紡績会社, 紡績機. To be distinguished are 製糸 (producing raw silk from cocoons) and 織物 or 機織り (weaving). In the Meiji era, cotton spinning was an engine of industrialization; company names like 東洋紡 still carry the short form 紡.

examples[].german: After the war, Japan's textile industry recovered mainly around cotton spinning and weaving and synthetic fibers.
I hear my grandmother worked in a spinning and weaving mill when she was young.
In the Meiji era, the textile industry supported Japan's modernization.
en.notes: 紡織 combines spinning (紡) and weaving (織) and refers to textile manufacturing as a branch of industry. It is a technical word from business and history: 紡織業, 紡織工場, 綿紡織 "cotton spinning and weaving". 紡織 played a central role in Japan's modernization; in everyday speech one talks more of 繊維産業 or 織物.

examples[].german: It's obvious that you have an ulterior motive of getting some leftovers if possible.
Suddenly being nice like that, he must have some scheme.
I knew from the start the other side's scheme of trying to beat the price down.
en.notes: 魂胆 is a hidden, usually self-serving plan; an ulterior motive that one imputes to others. Typical and derogatory: 魂胆がある, 何か魂胆があるに違いない, 魂胆が見え見えだ／見え透いている. It is used almost only about others, not about oneself. More neutral are 下心 "ulterior motive (often romantic)" or 狙い "aim, intention".

examples[].german: Gallbladder inflammation is in most cases caused by gallstones.
My father had surgery for gallstones and was in the hospital for a week.
If you keep eating greasy food, you apparently develop gallstones more easily.
en.notes: 胆石 is a gallstone (胆 "gall", 石 "stone"). Typical are 胆石ができる "gallstones form", 胆石の手術 and 胆石症 "gallstone disease". Similarly formed are 尿路結石 and 腎臓結石 "kidney stone". The word is medical but also common in everyday speech when talking about illnesses.

examples[].german: There is a card game app in which E. coli is personified as a pretty girl.
E. coli was detected in the well water.
E. coli can be present on hands that have touched raw meat.
en.notes: 大腸菌 is the intestinal bacterium Escherichia coli, literally "large-intestine bacterium". It is typical in news about hygiene and food: 大腸菌が検出される "E. coli is detected", 大腸菌に汚染される; in water testing one speaks of 大腸菌群 "coliforms", and in food poisoning of 腸管出血性大腸菌 (e.g. O157). Bacteria in general are called 細菌 or colloquially 菌 or バクテリア.

examples[].german: Disciplinary action was taken on the basis of the ministry's internal rules.
Under our internal rules, we are not allowed to accept gifts from business partners.
The selection criteria are set in the university's internal rules and are not made public.
en.notes: 内規 are the internal rules of an organization, often unpublished or even unwritten. Typical: 内規で定める, 内規に従う／違反する, 社の内規. Unlike 規則 or 規約, 内規 sounds "in-house" and is sometimes criticized for a lack of transparency. The legally required set of rules for employees is called 就業規則. Register: formal.

examples[].german: On this blog, I'll introduce my favorite anime and manga, focusing on moe types.
In Akihabara there are many shops selling moe merchandise.
He is the type who gets infatuated with characters who wear glasses.
en.notes: 萌え is otaku slang for tender enthusiasm for (mostly cute) anime and manga characters; as an exclamation 萌え～! "how cute!", as a verb 〜に萌える "to be smitten with something". Common in compounds such as 萌えキャラ, 萌え系, 萌えグッズ. Originally 萌え or 萌える literally means "sprouting, budding" (cf. 萌え出る); today the slang word seems somewhat out of fashion, and younger fans rather say 推し or 尊い.

examples[].german: I think it's a very universal theme.
A parent's love for their child is universal, regardless of era or country.
The laws of science are thought to hold universally.
en.notes: 普遍的 is a な-adjective: 普遍的な価値 "universal value", 普遍的に成り立つ "to hold universally". It emphasizes that something applies to all times, places and people, often in discussions of philosophy, art and science; the opposite is 特殊 "special" or 個別的. Do not confuse it with 一般的 "generally common, widespread", which describes only frequency. The corresponding noun is 普遍性 "universality".

en.meaning: all at once; at one time
examples[].german: Even if you tell me so many different things at once, I can't understand.
Don't try to finish all your homework at once; do a little every day.
When I washed my face with cold water, my drowsiness vanished all at once.
en.notes: 一遍に means "everything at once, in one go" and is usually written in kana as いっぺんに; it is somewhat more colloquial than 一度に or 同時に. It is typical with things that pile up: 一遍に片付ける, 一遍に言われても困る. It also means "suddenly, instantly": 眠気が一遍に吹き飛ぶ. Do not confuse it with 一遍 without に ("once", e.g. 一遍読んだ).

examples[].german: Do not cross the tracks while the crossing gate is down.
After the train passed, the gate went up.
At the parking lot exit, the barrier won't go up unless you pay the fee.
en.notes: 遮断機 is the barrier at a railroad crossing (踏切), literally "blocking machine"; barriers at toll gates and parking lots are also called this. One says 遮断機が下りる (also written 降りる) "the barrier comes down" and 遮断機が上がる "goes up". The crossing itself is 踏切, and the warning device with bell and flashing light is 警報機. The verb 遮断する generally means "to block off, to cut off".

examples[].german: Next year, an event commemorating the 1300th anniversary of the relocation of the capital will be held.
In 794, Emperor Kanmu moved the capital to Heian-kyō.
Relocating the capital's functions was discussed, but it never came to an actual move of the capital.
en.notes: 遷都 is the relocation of the capital, especially in Japanese history: 平城京に遷都する, 平安遷都 (794). As an intransitive する-verb, the destination is marked with に or へ. The word is written-style and historically tinged; for present-day plans to relocate government functions, 首都移転 or 首都機能移転 is more usual. 都 means "capital" here, 遷 "to move".

examples[].german: This is the birthplace of Japanese dairy farming.
Hokkaido is a region where dairy farming thrives.
My grandfather runs a dairy farm on a ranch.
en.notes: 酪農 is dairy farming, that is, keeping cows to obtain milk, butter and cheese; 酪 stands for dairy products. Typical combinations: 酪農が盛んだ "dairy farming is widespread", 酪農を営む "to run a dairy farm", 酪農家 "dairy farmer". The umbrella term for livestock farming in general (including meat) is 畜産, and grazing livestock on pasture is 牧畜.

examples[].german: Himalayan cedars do not bear female flowers until they are over 30 years old.
The female flower of a cucumber has a small swelling that looks like a tiny fruit.
For pumpkins, pollen from the male flower is applied to the female flower to pollinate it.
en.notes: 雌花 is a female (pistil-bearing only) flower; its counterpart is 雄花 "male flower". In compounds 雌 is read め (雌花, 雌しべ "pistil"), on its own めす. One says 雌花が咲く or 雌花をつける "to bear female flowers". The word appears mainly in vegetable growing (cucumbers, pumpkins) and in botany.

examples[].german: Do you all know who composed this poem?
The pilgrims walked along the mountain path chanting their pilgrim hymns.
At the poetry gathering, each participant's poem was presented.
en.notes: 詠歌 is an elevated, rather classical word for a (waka) poem, especially a tanka, or the composing itself; the corresponding verb is 詠む "to compose poetry". Today it is encountered mainly in 御詠歌 (ご詠歌), the Buddhist pilgrim songs sung with small bells on pilgrimages such as the 33 temples of Saigoku. In everyday speech, for poems one says 和歌, 短歌 or simply 歌.

examples[].german: I was moved to admiration by the beauty of the sunset seen from the summit of that mountain.
The classical "keri" can also carry an exclamatory meaning.
He involuntarily cried out in admiration, "How beautiful!"
en.notes: 詠嘆 is a deeply felt exclamation of admiration or emotion, such as "Ah, how beautiful!". As an intransitive する-verb, the trigger is marked with に: 美しさに詠嘆する; more common, however, are 詠嘆の声 and 詠嘆を込めて. The word is very often encountered in classical-language grammar: 詠嘆の助動詞「けり」, 詠嘆の終助詞「かな」. In everyday speech 感嘆 or 感動する is more usual.

examples[].german: I carry out my work in accordance with the job regulations.
An employee was disciplined for violating the job regulations.
I read the job regulations of the new department and confirmed my authority.
en.notes: 職務規程 is a written set of rules that defines tasks, authority and conduct at work, e.g. the 職務権限規程 "authority regulations" in companies or the 弁護士職務基本規程 for lawyers. 規程 denotes the whole set of rules as a document, whereas the identically read 規定 is a single provision. Typical: 職務規程に従う／違反する, 職務規程を定める. Register: formal, administrative language.

en.meaning: sal tree; Japanese stewartia; Sara (given name)
examples[].german: Sara and I exchanged a nod and parted.
The color of the sal flowers reveals the truth that the prosperous must decline.
Stewartia flowers were blooming in the temple garden.
en.notes: In the dictionary, 沙羅 refers to the Indian sal tree under which the Buddha is said to have died; 沙羅双樹 from the opening of the 平家物語 is famous. Since the sal tree does not grow in Japan, the Japanese stewartia (ナツツバキ) is called 沙羅 or 沙羅の木 there; it blooms in early summer in many temple gardens. 沙羅 (さら) is also a popular girl's name.

examples[].german: Excuse me, sir, you've dropped your wallet!
In the period drama, there was a scene in which a townsman stopped a samurai by calling, "Excuse me, honorable samurai!"
"Moshimoshi" is said to be a shortened form of "mōshi mōshi".
en.notes: 申し申し is an archaic call for addressing or stopping someone: "Excuse me!, You there!", literally the doubling of 申す "to say". Today it is heard only in samurai dramas (時代劇) or rakugo. The telephone もしもし developed from it; but nobody says 申し申し on the phone, and businesses answer with their name rather than with もしもし anyway.

examples[].german: Who do you think will be chosen as head of the next cabinet?
The election to designate the prime minister was held in the Diet.
In a coalition government, the key question is which party's leader becomes prime minister.
en.notes: 首班 today refers almost only to the head of government, that is, the prime minister as head of the cabinet. The most important combination is 首班指名 "designation of the prime minister by the parliament", also 内閣の首班 and 首班に選ばれる. The word is political and written-style; for a leader in general one says リーダー or 指導者, and for the top of the class 首席.

examples[].german: I do research in anatomy at university.
Medical students learn the structure of the human body in anatomy class.
That painter studied anatomy in order to depict people accurately.
en.notes: 解剖学 is anatomy as the science of body structure; 解剖 on its own is the dissection itself (解剖する, 司法解剖 "forensic autopsy"). One says 解剖学を学ぶ／研究する, 人体解剖学, and as an adjective 解剖学的な. Do not confuse it with 生理学 "physiology", which studies the functions of the body.

examples[].german: She was harboring the criminal.
The company president was arrested on suspicion of concealing company assets.
After the war, hoarded military supplies flowed into the black markets.
en.notes: 隠匿する is a legal, written-style transitive verb (X を隠匿する) for hiding things or people, mostly in connection with wrongdoing: 財産を隠匿する, 隠匿物資 "hoarded goods". In everyday speech one simply says 隠す. To be distinguished is 隠蔽 "to cover up" (facts, scandals: 事実を隠蔽する); hiding a perpetrator is called 犯人蔵匿 in criminal law.

examples[].german: I sent in a letter anonymously.
Even anonymous posts on the internet carry responsibility.
The donor wishes to remain anonymous.
en.notes: 匿名 means appearing without a (real) name: 匿名で "anonymously", 匿名の手紙 "anonymous letter", 匿名希望 "wishes to remain anonymous", 匿名性 "anonymity (e.g. online)". The opposite is 実名 "real name"; a self-chosen name is 仮名 (かめい) or ペンネーム. Do not confuse it with 無名 "unknown, nameless" (無名の画家).

examples[].german: When I counted the squares, there were 400 in total.
I carefully wrote one character in each square of the manuscript paper.
Please write the postal code in the boxes on the application form.
en.notes: 升目 is a single square in a grid, such as on graph paper, on Japanese manuscript paper (原稿用紙) or in form fields; today it is mostly written マス目, more rarely 枡目. Typical: 升目に書く／記入する, 升目を埋める. Originally 升 is a wooden measure for rice, hence also the old meaning "measure, quantity".

examples[].german: My uncle is a singing accordion player.
My grandmother was cooking in the kitchen while singing folk songs.
At the Bon dance, everyone formed a circle, singing and dancing.
en.notes: 唄う is a spelling variant of 歌う "to sing". 唄 is preferred for traditional Japanese songs such as 民謡, 長唄 or 小唄 and when a folksy, heartfelt tone is meant; the standard in school and everyday life is 歌う. Not to be confused with 謳う ("to extol; to stipulate explicitly", e.g. 憲法に謳われた権利). Construction as with 歌う: 民謡を唄う, 〜を唄いながら.

examples[].german: I've started going to a nagauta class.
In kabuki dances, nagauta is played as accompaniment.
My grandmother has been learning nagauta and shamisen since she was young.
en.notes: 長唄 is a genre of shamisen vocal music that arose in Edo in the early 17th century as accompaniment for kabuki dance. One speaks of 長唄を習う, 長唄の師匠, 長唄三味線. The character 唄 instead of 歌 is used for traditional songs sung to the shamisen; shorter forms are called 小唄 and 端唄, folk songs 民謡.

examples[].german: A mine tunnel has been dug 20 meters underground.
In a cave-in accident, workers were trapped in the tunnel.
There are tours where you can see the tunnels of a closed mine.
en.notes: 坑道 is an underground passage in mining, that is, a tunnel or shaft; 坑 means "pit" (cf. 炭坑 "coal mine"). Typical: 坑道を掘る, 坑道に閉じ込められる, 坑道の入口. For traffic tunnels, トンネル is used. Beware of the homophones 行動 "action" and 講堂 "auditorium".

en.meaning: service discipline; code of conduct for employees
examples[].german: Public employees must comply with the rules of service discipline.
A police officer received a pay cut for violating service discipline.
The code of conduct in the work rules also prohibits side jobs.
en.notes: 服務規律 are the rules of conduct for civil servants and employees on duty: punctuality, confidentiality, prohibition of side jobs, appropriate demeanor. In companies, 服務規律 usually forms a separate chapter of the 就業規則. Typical: 服務規律を守る／遵守する, 服務規律違反, 服務規律の徹底. While 職務規程 regulates tasks and authority, 服務規律 is about behavior. Register: formal.

examples[].german: I hear the groom ran away from the wedding hall!
The bride and groom had their picture taken side by side.
As the groom's father, I would like to say a few words of greeting.
en.notes: 花婿 is the bridegroom, paired with 花嫁 "bride". At weddings and in speeches, 新郎 (with 新婦) is the more formal choice: 新郎新婦のご入場. 婿 on its own means "son-in-law" or a man who marries into his wife's family (婿入り, 婿養子).

examples[].german: I intend to make my son-in-law president eventually.
On days off, I often go fishing with my son-in-law.
My son-in-law's family home is in Kyushu, so we can't see each other often.
en.notes: 娘婿 is the husband of one's own daughter, that is, the son-in-law from the parents' point of view; more neutral but longer is 義理の息子. If he marries into the wife's family and takes her name, he is a 婿養子. The counterpart from the parents' point of view is the daughter-in-law 息子の嫁.

examples[].german: Please explain the widow's deduction to me in detail.
Widows who lost their husbands in the war were forced to lead hard lives.
Legally, "widows" also include divorced women who have not remarried.
en.notes: 寡婦 is a written-style, official term for a widow, in law also for a divorced woman who has not remarried; the tax term 寡婦控除 is well known. In everyday speech one says 未亡人 (now sometimes felt to be inappropriate) or the circumlocution 夫を亡くした女性; 後家 and やもめ are outdated. A widower is called, with the same reading, 寡夫 (かふ).

examples[].german: The shop's interior is designed with the image of a sailing ship.
A large sailing ship was moored in the harbor.
In the Age of Discovery, European sailing ships crossed the seas of the whole world.
en.notes: 帆船 is a sailing ship; 帆 (ほ) is the sail, 帆を張る "to set the sails". It contrasts with 汽船 "steamship"; small recreational sailboats are usually called ヨット. Besides はんせん there is the rarer reading ほぶね. Typical are 帆船が停泊する and 帆船模型 "sailing ship model".

examples[].german: This tree is just right for a mast.
The mast broke in the storm.
A sailor climbed the mast and searched for a distant island.
en.notes: 帆柱 is the mast of a sailing ship, to which the sail (帆) is attached; the reading ほばしら follows 帆 ほ and 柱 はしら. Today the loanword マスト is more common; 帆柱 seems traditional and suits old ships or literature. Typical: 帆柱が折れる, 帆柱に登る, 帆柱を立てる.

examples[].german: The packaging of budget versions of games looks so cheap, doesn't it?
This store sells brand-name goods at low prices.
Even a budget smartphone model is enough for everyday use.
en.notes: 廉価 is a written-style, commercial word for a "low, inexpensive price". It mostly appears as a noun: 廉価で販売する "to sell cheaply", 廉価版 "budget edition", 廉価モデル, 廉価品; as a な-adjective (廉価な商品) it is rarer. In everyday speech one says 安い, and in advertising and business also 安価 or 低価格. 廉 means "cheap" here (but cf. 清廉 "honest, upright").

examples[].german: I play the violin in a small orchestra.
The city orchestra gives a concert every Christmas.
I got tickets for the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra's concert in Japan.
en.notes: 管弦楽団 is an orchestra, literally a "wind-and-string music group" (管 wind instruments, 弦 stringed instruments). In everyday speech one usually says オーケストラ; 管弦楽団 appears mainly in ensemble names such as 〜フィルハーモニー管弦楽団 or 〜室内管弦楽団, alongside 〜交響楽団 "symphony orchestra". A wind band without strings is called 吹奏楽団, and orchestral music in general 管弦楽.

examples[].german: In a foreign land, my longing for my mother only grows.
She put her deep affection for her late teacher into a letter.
The boy secretly yearned for an older woman.
en.notes: 思慕 is a literary term for deep, yearning affection for someone who is distant, deceased or revered. Typical are 〜への思慕, 思慕の念を抱く, 思慕が募る; as a transitive する-verb: 母を思慕する. The character 慕 is also found in the more common verb 慕う "to be attached to, to adore"; romantic love is rather 恋慕, and in everyday speech one says 恋しい or 会いたい.

en.meaning: deeply moving; filled with deep emotion (in retrospect)
examples[].german: Having something I wrote published for the first time is, of course, deeply moving.
Visiting my old school for the first time in twenty years was deeply moving.
When I think of the ten years until this bridge was completed, I am deeply moved.
en.notes: 感慨深い is an い-adjective for the moved, reflective feeling when looking back on past time, hardships or memories. Very typical is the phrase 感慨深いものがある; related is 感慨にふける "to sink into reminiscence". Unlike 感動的 "moving" (a film, a speech), it usually describes one's own emotion at a milestone, for example a graduation, reunion or anniversary.

examples[].german: Disciplinary action was taken against the employee who caused the scandal.
The teacher who drove drunk received disciplinary action.
There are four types of disciplinary action for public employees: dismissal, suspension, pay cut and reprimand.
en.notes: 懲戒処分 is formal disciplinary action against civil servants or employees. For civil servants there are four levels: 戒告 "reprimand", 減給 "pay cut", 停職 "suspension" and 免職 "dismissal"; companies also have, among others, 譴責 and 懲戒解雇. Mere admonitions such as 訓告 or 厳重注意 do not count. Typical: 懲戒処分を受ける／下す, 懲戒処分とする. Register: administrative and news language.

examples[].german: That's a prank that's popular among kids right now.
When I was a child, I often played pranks on my friends and got scolded.
A prank call came in the middle of the night.
en.notes: いたずら is a "prank, mischief", especially by children: いたずらをする, 〜にいたずらする "to play a prank on someone". As a na-adjective, いたずらな means "naughty, mischievous"; common compounds are いたずら電話 "prank call" and いたずら書き "scribbling". It can also mean unauthorized fiddling with objects (火でいたずらする), and in the news it is a euphemism for sexual assault. Almost always written in kana; 悪戯 is seen mainly in novels.

examples[].german: I only wrote it for fun, yet it won a prize.
What I said as a mere joke hurt her deeply.
That the two met again was truly a trick of fate.
en.notes: 戯れ is the noun of 戯れる ("to play, frolic; to dally") and means "play, jest, whim". It is written-literary; in everyday speech one says 冗談 or 遊び. Common is the adverbial 戯れに ("for fun, on a whim"), as well as 戯れの恋 ("a flirtation") and 運命の戯れ ("a trick of fate"). Related, but derogatory, is 戯言 (たわごと) "nonsense, silly talk".

examples[].german: My older sister was brutally tortured by the mafia.
Confessions obtained through torture are not accepted as evidence.
Being made to wait an hour in this heat is sheer torture.
en.notes: 拷問 is torture, especially to extort a confession or information. Typical combinations: 拷問を受ける "to be tortured", 拷問を加える, 拷問にかける. Colloquially it is used figuratively: まるで拷問だ "it's pure torture". Do not confuse it with 尋問 "interrogation" or 虐待 "abuse (e.g. of children)".

examples[].german: There is a strange rumor going around about a certain private high school.
A popular singer's drama was filmed at an undisclosed location in Tokyo.
The other day I had the chance to have a meal with the president of a certain major company.
en.notes: 某 (ぼう) is placed before a noun when one deliberately does not name something: 某所 "a certain place", 某氏 "a certain gentleman", 某社, 某大学, 某日. After a family name it means "a certain ..." (山田某). It is typical of news and written language, but is also used jokingly on blogs; more neutral is ある (ある日, ある会社). The kun reading なにがし (山田なにがし) is old-fashioned.

en.meaning: to die in the line of duty
examples[].german: That detective was hit by bullets and died in the line of duty.
A ceremony was held to mourn the firefighter who died on duty while fighting a fire.
The families of those who die in the line of duty receive compensation from the state.
en.notes: 殉職する is an intransitive する-verb: to lose one's life in the line of duty, especially of police officers, firefighters, soldiers or rescue workers. Typical: 職務中に殉職する, 殉職者, 殉職警察官. Related but different are 戦死 "to fall in war", 殉教 "martyrdom (for one's faith)" and 殉死 "to follow one's lord in death". The word has a respectful, honoring tone.

examples[].german: When two butts have accumulated, please replace the ashtray right away.
Throwing away cigarette butts is prohibited by ordinance.
While cleaning the park, we picked up lots of cigarette butts.
en.notes: 吸い殻 is a cigarette butt, from 吸う "to smoke" and 殻 "shell, husk"; it is counted with 本 and is also written 吸殻. Typical: タバコの吸い殻, 吸い殻を捨てる, 吸い殻入れ, and the prohibited ポイ捨て "careless littering". The ashtray is called 灰皿.

examples[].german: As much as one to two liters of gastric juice are secreted per day.
When you are nervous, adrenaline is secreted.
The sweat glands that secrete sweat are distributed over the whole body.
en.notes: 分泌 means "secretion" by glands and organs; in medicine the reading ぶんぴ is also heard. It is both transitive and intransitive: 汗を分泌する, 胃液が分泌する, but most often in the passive 〜が分泌される. Compounds: 分泌物 "secretion", 内分泌 "internal secretion, endocrine". Note: in 泌尿器 the same character 泌 is read ひ.

examples[].german: I am going to be hospitalized for a disease of the urinary organs.
Just to be safe, I had an examination in urology.
As you get older, urinary problems tend to increase.
en.notes: 泌尿器 are the organs that produce and drain urine: kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra; 泌 "to secrete" is read ひ here (unlike in 分泌 ぶんぴつ), and 尿 is "urine". The word is most often encountered in 泌尿器科 "urology, urology department". Typical are 泌尿器の病気 and 泌尿器系.

examples[].german: We went down the mountain stream while rafting.
Stream fishing, I caught three char.
We enjoyed camping while listening to the murmur of the mountain stream.
en.notes: 渓流 is a mountain stream flowing through a narrow valley (渓); one thinks of clear, fast water between rocks. Typical are 渓流釣り "stream fishing (for char, trout)", 渓流沿いの道 and 渓流のせせらぎ "the murmur of the stream". The valley itself is 渓谷; a brook in the lowlands is more likely 小川, and a clear river 清流.

examples[].german: The sound of him eating potato chips is noisy and irritating.
Please don't make noise at night.
en.notes: 煩い is read うるさい here and is mostly written in hiragana too. It describes disturbing noise and can also express that something gets on one's nerves. As an i-adjective it becomes うるさくて before て and うるさくしないで in a negative request. A bare うるさい shouted on its own can sound very harsh.

examples[].german: An admonition was given for the minor violation.
The boss gave an admonition to the employee who was repeatedly late.
My grandfather's admonitions stay in my heart even now.
en.notes: 訓戒 is an instructive admonition so that someone does not repeat a mistake. In civil service law, 訓戒 (similarly 訓告) is not a formal disciplinary punishment for civil servants but a step below 戒告; in some company work rules, however, it is a sanction level of its own. Outside work it can also mean the "admonishing lessons" of elders. Typical: 訓戒を与える／受ける, 訓戒処分. Register: formal.

examples[].german: The cumbersome procedures irritate me.
Because managing the documents had become too cumbersome, we introduced a system.
So that the explanation would not get too convoluted, I summarized only the main points.
en.notes: 煩雑 is a な-adjective for things that are cumbersome and troublesome because of many details: 煩雑な手続き, 煩雑な事務作業, 手続きが煩雑になる. It is also written 繁雑 with the same meaning. In contrast to 複雑 "complicated (in structure)", 煩雑 emphasizes the effort and annoyance; colloquially one says 面倒 or ややこしい.

examples[].german: I escaped my hectic daily routine and came to Hawaii.
Lost in the bustle of the year-end, I failed to write my New Year's cards.
Even while living busy days, I value time with my family.
en.notes: 煩忙 means "very busy, rushed", as a noun or な-adjective: 日々の煩忙, 煩忙な日々. The word is rare and written-style; much more common is the homophone 繁忙 (繁忙期 "peak season", 繁忙を極める). In everyday speech one says 忙しい, and in business letters 多忙 (ご多忙のところ).

examples[].german: In summer, I read in a quiet lodge by the lakeside.
While strolling along the lakeshore, I watched the sunrise.
