The campground by the lake is lively with families on weekends.
en.notes: 湖畔 is the lakeshore or the area right at the lake; 畔 means "edge, bank". Typical are 湖畔の宿／ホテル, 湖畔に建つ, 湖畔を散歩する. In parallel there is 河畔 "riverbank"; by the sea one says 海辺 or 海岸. Literary-soft is 湖のほとり.

examples[].german: Dysentery bacteria were detected in five people in total, men and women.
I drank unboiled water while traveling and caught dysentery.
In Japan in the past, dysentery was a life-threatening infectious disease.
en.notes: 赤痢 is dysentery, an intestinal infection with bloody diarrhea: 赤 "red" and 痢 "diarrhea" (cf. 下痢). One distinguishes 細菌性赤痢 and アメーバ赤痢; the pathogen is called 赤痢菌 (Shigella, named after the Japanese 志賀潔). Typical: 赤痢にかかる "to contract dysentery", 赤痢菌が検出される.

examples[].german: Is this seaweed edible?
Seaweed is rich in minerals and dietary fiber.
Japanese people have eaten seaweed such as wakame and kombu since long ago.
en.notes: 海藻 is the general term for marine algae or seaweed, such as わかめ, 昆布, ひじき, もずく or 海苔. The identically pronounced 海草 actually refers to seagrass (flowering plants in the sea); in everyday speech the two are often confused, but for edible ones 海藻 is correct. Typical: 海藻サラダ, 海藻類, 海藻を食べる.

examples[].german: If you have an easy and delicious recipe for chicken nanban, please tell me.
In the 16th century, nanban trade with the Portuguese began.
At the soba restaurant, I ordered duck nanban.
en.notes: 南蛮 was originally a derogatory Chinese term for "barbarians of the south"; in Japan from the 16th century it referred to the Portuguese and Spanish who came via Southeast Asia: 南蛮人, 南蛮貿易, 南蛮文化. Today it is encountered mainly in cooking: dishes with chili and leek or in a spicy vinegar marinade are called 〜南蛮 (鴨南蛮, カレー南蛮, チキン南蛮, 南蛮漬け); regionally 南蛮 also simply means "chili".

examples[].german: Those guys keep committing atrocities there.
The barbaric destruction of cultural property drew condemnation from around the world.
The rowdy behavior of drunken tourists is troubling local residents.
en.notes: 蛮行 is a barbaric, brutal act; the word appears mainly in news and commentary: 蛮行を働く／繰り返す, 〜という蛮行に非難が集まる. The matching adjective is 野蛮 "barbaric". In contrast to 暴行 "act of violence, assault" (legal), 蛮行 emphasizes moral condemnation; serious atrocities are also called 残虐行為.

examples[].german: The New Year's card said "Happy New Year".
Happy New Year. Thank you very much for all your help over the past year.
For New Year's cards to superiors, four-character greetings like 「謹賀新年」 are suitable.
en.notes: 謹賀新年 is a written New Year formula for New Year's cards (年賀状) and notices, literally "respectfully congratulate on the new year"; it is not spoken, and verbally one says あけましておめでとうございます. As a four-character formula, it is considered polite even toward superiors, while short formulas like 賀正 or 迎春 are used more among equals. Doubling up, such as 謹賀新年 next to あけましておめでとう on the same card, is considered stylistically unattractive.

examples[].german: Father beat my younger brother mercilessly.
That teacher points out students' mistakes without mercy.
The midsummer sun beats down mercilessly.
en.notes: 容赦なく is the adverbial form of 容赦ない "merciless, ruthless"; 容赦 means "leniency, pardon" (cf. the polite ご容赦ください "please be lenient"). It describes people (容赦なく批判する) as well as forces of nature or time (日差しが容赦なく照りつける). Intensified: 情け容赦なく. Do not confuse it with 遠慮なく "without reserve, freely", which is meant positively.

examples[].german: The president's passing is a really big shock.
In mourning the passing of your esteemed father, I offer my heartfelt condolences.
The former prime minister passed away last night at the age of eighty-nine.
en.notes: 逝去 is a respectful (尊敬語) expression for the death of another, usually esteemed person: ご逝去, 逝去される. It appears in letters of condolence and obituaries, never for members of one's own family or company when speaking to outsiders; for those one uses 死去 or 他界. Neutral in the news is 死去, and in everyday speech 亡くなる.

examples[].german: A reprimand was issued for neglect of duty.
The city gave a reprimand to the employee who had repeatedly been absent without notice.
The city sent the owner of the vacant house a formal warning demanding demolition.
en.notes: 戒告 is the mildest formal disciplinary punishment for civil servants: responsibility is established in writing, without direct effects on pay, but promotion and bonus may suffer. To be distinguished from 訓告／訓戒, which are not formal punishments. In administrative enforcement law, 戒告 also means the formal warning before a substitute execution (代執行). Typical: 戒告処分を受ける, 〜を戒告とする. Register: administrative language.

examples[].german: After making such a spectacle of yourself, how can you go to work with such a calm face?
I got drunk and made a fool of myself in front of my boss.
The string of errors late in the match was a disgrace unworthy of a title favorite.
en.notes: 醜態 is shameful, embarrassing behavior that others witness: 醜態を演じる and 醜態をさらす "to make a fool of oneself". It is often about drunkenness, outbursts of anger or a disastrous failure in public. Similar but different is 失態 "blunder, failure (at a task)"; 醜態 emphasizes the undignified picture one presents.

examples[].german: Who spread such a baseless scandal?
A scandal involving the minister was reported in a weekly magazine.
As the scandal spread, he had no choice but to resign as chairman.
en.notes: 醜聞 is a written-style word for "scandal, scandalous news", literally "ugly report". In everyday speech and in the media one usually says スキャンダル; 醜聞 seems elevated or journalistic. Typical: 醜聞が広まる, 醜聞を流す ("to spread"), 政界の醜聞. For misconduct in companies or government offices, 不祥事 is the usual word.

en.meaning: kowtow; bowing with the forehead to the ground
examples[].german: The kowtow is a Chinese form of obeisance similar to Japan's dogeza.
The envoy kowtowed before the emperor.
He prostrated himself and begged for forgiveness.
en.notes: 叩頭 is the kowtow: kneeling and bowing so low that the forehead touches the ground, originally a gesture of homage at the Chinese imperial court (三跪九叩頭). As an intransitive する-verb: 皇帝の前で叩頭する, 叩頭して許しを請う. The word is written-historical; the Japanese counterpart, bowing on the knees with the head to the floor, is called 土下座, and an ordinary bow お辞儀.

examples[].german: What the leader says is absolute.
The heads of the party's factions gathered and discussed the next candidate for party president.
He came to be regarded as a leader of the business world at a young age.
en.notes: 領袖 refers to the leader of a group, today almost only in politics: 派閥の領袖 "head of a party faction", 党の領袖. Literally, 領 "collar" and 袖 "sleeve" are the most conspicuous parts of a garment, hence the meaning "outstanding person". The word is written-style; in general one says リーダー or 指導者, and the party chairman is called 党首.

examples[].german: Pluto's orbit is an elongated ellipse, and it takes about 250 years to go around the Sun once.
In 2006, Pluto was reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet.
A space probe approached Pluto for the first time and photographed its surface.
en.notes: 冥王星 is Pluto; the name literally means "star of the king of the underworld" (冥王), corresponding to the Roman god Pluto. Since 2006 it is no longer regarded as a planet (惑星) but as a dwarf planet (準惑星); one says, for example, 冥王星が惑星から外された. The planet names follow the same pattern with 星: 水星, 金星, 火星, 木星, 土星, 天王星, 海王星.

examples[].german: Only the souls of the dead can enter the underworld.
In Greek mythology, Hades rules the underworld.
The hero of the story descended into the underworld to bring back his late wife.
en.notes: 冥界 is the world of the dead, the underworld; 冥 means "dark, of the other world". The word is written-style and appears in mythology, fantasy and religion: 冥界の王, 冥界へ下る. Colloquially one says あの世; in Japanese myth the underworld is called 黄泉; 地獄, in contrast, is hell as a place of punishment. The same character appears in ご冥福をお祈りします "May he/she rest in peace".

en.meaning: the realm of the dead; the next world
examples[].german: No matter how much money you earn, you can't take it with you to the next world.
Seeing my granddaughter in her wedding dress gave me a fine memory to take to the grave.
People in the past believed that the dead crossed a river and went to the netherworld.
en.notes: 冥土 (also written 冥途) is a Buddhist-tinged, elevated word for the "realm of the dead" to which the soul travels after death; one goes 冥土へ or arrives in 冥土. A very common phrase is 冥土の土産, a last fine experience that one "takes to the grave", often said jokingly by older people. In everyday speech one rather says あの世; 地獄 and 天国, in contrast, denote hell and heaven as places of punishment and reward respectively.

en.meaning: to drink together; to exchange cups of sake
examples[].german: Do you remember drinking sake together here that day?
Drinking sake with a friend I hadn't seen in a long time, we chatted happily about old times.
After the negotiations were concluded, the presidents of the two companies exchanged cups.
en.notes: 酌み交わす is composed of 酌む "to pour" and 交わす "to exchange": people pour for each other and drink together. Typical are 酒を酌み交わす and 杯を酌み交わす, usually with 〜と for the drinking partner. Unlike the neutral 一緒に飲む, the word emphasizes familiarity, friendship or reconciliation and sounds elevated to literary. The background is the custom of not pouring for oneself but for the other person (お酌をする).

en.meaning: to compose poetry; to write verse
examples[].german: This is a love poem he wrote for his girlfriend.
Since ancient times, many poets have sung of the beauty of Mount Fuji.
This poem expresses the sorrow of having left one's hometown.
en.notes: 詠う is one of the spellings of うたう and is used for celebrating a theme in a poem: 恋を詠う, 自然の美しさを詠う. For ordinary singing one writes 歌う, for "to extol, to stipulate explicitly" (e.g. in a law) 謳う. Not to be confused with 詠む (よむ), which refers to composing a specific poem: 俳句を詠む, 短歌を詠む. 詠う is literary and appears mainly in texts about literature.

examples[].german: This is the story of a certain Yamada.
Yesterday I got a call from a man named Suzuki or something.
I intend to pay the students who helped some token of thanks.
en.notes: 某 read as なにがし follows a family name and means "a certain ..." when one does not know or does not want to give the full name: 山田某. The word sounds old-fashioned to literary. In なにがしか(の) "a certain amount, some" it is almost always written in kana: なにがしかのお礼. As a prefix, in contrast, 某 is read ぼう (某国, 某所, 某氏); in historical dramas, なにがし can also mean "I" humbly.

examples[].german: A pay cut was imposed to take responsibility for the scandal.
If you are late often, you may get a pay cut.
Because of deteriorating business performance, all employees received a uniform 10 percent pay cut.
en.notes: 減給 is a pay cut, both as disciplinary punishment (減給処分, for civil servants up to one fifth for at most one year) and for economic reasons. Typical: 減給になる／となる, 減給される, 減給処分を受ける. Similar is 減俸, which is more used for executives and athletes; 減額 is a general "reduction of an amount". Register: neutral to formal.

examples[].german: I teach in a certain country that sends many international students to Japan.
There is a suspicion that the intelligence agency of a certain country was involved in the case.
On the program, he was introduced only as "the president of a certain country".
en.notes: 某国 refers to a country whose name one deliberately does not mention, for example out of diplomatic consideration, to protect sources or because it is obvious to the reader anyway. The word is typical of news, reports and insinuations: 某国の情報機関, 某国の大統領. In fictional stories, where a country simply remains unspecified, the neutral ある国 is more usual. Formed in the same way are 某所, 某氏, 某社 and 某日.

en.meaning: a certain place; an undisclosed location
examples[].german: I went to an event held at a certain place in Tochigi Prefecture.
The culprit is believed to be hiding somewhere in Tokyo.
Filming of the new movie is proceeding in strict secrecy at an undisclosed location.
en.notes: 某所 is a "certain place" whose exact location is kept secret. Typical are phrases like 都内某所 "somewhere in Tokyo" or 県内某所, often in news, secret film shoots or events. On social media, 某所 is also used with a wink when everyone guesses which place is meant. Without any intent to conceal, one simply says ある場所 or どこか.

examples[].german: I met one of the judges.
According to a person connected with the matter, the plan has already been cancelled.
The article avoided the real name and wrote only "a person from Company A".
en.notes: 某氏 means "Mr./Ms. X": a specific person whose name one deliberately does not give. Because of 氏 it sounds polite and matter-of-fact; it is typical of newspaper articles, reports and anonymized sources: 関係者の某氏. If the person is truly unknown, such as a perpetrator, one says 何者か; neutral for "someone" is ある人. Pronounced the same but unrelated is 帽子 "hat".

en.meaning: a series; a chain (of related things)
examples[].german: We are investigating a series of related problems.
We automated the whole sequence of work.
The whole series of incidents is believed to be the work of the same person.
en.notes: 一連 almost always appears as 一連の before a noun and groups things into a "connected series": 一連の事件, 一連の流れ, 一連の騒動, 一連の作業. In contrast to いくつかの, it emphasizes the internal connection or fixed sequence. It is especially common in news when several incidents are presented as belonging together.

examples[].german: The participation fee is a flat 1,000 yen.
We applied a uniform standard to all schools.
The company raised all employees' salaries uniformly by three percent.
en.notes: 一律 means "the same for everyone, across the board, without distinction". It is used adverbially as 一律に (一律に値上げする), attributively as 一律の (一律の基準) or directly before amounts: 一律千円. Criticism is often implied when individual differences are ignored: 一律に禁止するのはおかしい. Related are 均一 (uniform price, e.g. 百円均一) and 一様 (uniform in appearance or condition).

examples[].german: There are no additional charges whatsoever.
I have had nothing whatsoever to do with that matter.
My father left everything about the household to my mother.
en.notes: 一切 has two uses: as an adverb with a negative it means "not at all, none whatsoever" and is stronger and more formal than 全然 - typical on signs and in statements: 一切お断り, 一切関係ない. As a noun it means "everything, all": 財産の一切, 一切を任せる; intensified also 一切合切. Do not confuse it with 一切れ (ひときれ) "one piece".

examples[].german: We changed part of the plan.
Please give me one copy of the materials.
Because of the typhoon, power outages continue in some areas.
en.notes: 一部 (いちぶ) first of all means "a part": 計画の一部, 一部の人 "some people", 一部の地域 "some areas". As a counter for printed matter it means "one copy": 資料を一部, 二部 and so on. In contrast to 全部, it denotes only a portion; 一部分 is a somewhat more concrete "section". A well-known phrase: 一部始終 "the whole course of events from beginning to end".

examples[].german: I have no objection to this proposal.
At the meeting, we also listened to dissenting opinions.
No one is likely to dispute that he is an excellent player.
en.notes: 異論 is a "dissenting opinion" or an "objection". Typical combinations: 異論はない (no objections), 異論が出る, 異論を唱える (to object). It sounds matter-of-fact to formal and suits meetings and debates. 反論 is a concrete counterargument to a statement, and 異議 a formal objection (異議あり in meetings or in court).

examples[].german: Please give me a breakdown of the costs.
I summarized the breakdown of participants in a table.
The invoice didn't have a breakdown written on it, so I inquired.
en.notes: 内訳 is the "breakdown" of a total sum or total number into its items: 費用の内訳, 売上の内訳, 内訳は次の通りです. It is read with the kun reading うちわけ. 明細, in contrast, is the detailed itemized list as a document (給与明細 "payslip"); 内訳 emphasizes more what the whole is made up of, and is also used for groups of people.

examples[].german: You must not put off important problems.
We put off the tidying up and had a meal first.
When I'm busy, I easily end up putting my own health last.
en.notes: 後回し means "to put off until later, to put at the back of the line" and almost always appears as 後回しにする (active) or 後回しになる (it turns out that way). It concerns the order of tasks, not a new date. For the official postponement of an appointment one says 延期, and for putting off unpleasant problems, especially in politics, 先送り.

examples[].german: He received a six-month suspension for misconduct.
After the abuse of power against his subordinates was established, the section chief was suspended for three months.
No salary is paid during a suspension.
en.notes: 停職 is a temporary suspension from duty as a disciplinary penalty; for civil servants it lasts from one day to one year, without pay. Typical: 停職処分, 停職〇か月, 停職中. Do not confuse it with 休職 "leave of absence" (e.g. because of illness, not a penalty); in companies 停職 roughly corresponds to 出勤停止. Register: administrative and news language.

examples[].german: I review vocabulary in between work.
I went out shopping during a break in the rain.
Squeezing it in between childcare, I keep studying for a qualification.
en.notes: 合間 is the short "interval" between two phases of an activity or event: 仕事の合間に, 雨の合間, CMの合間. Very idiomatic is 合間を縫って "to squeeze in time in between". In contrast to 休憩 (official break), 合間 emphasizes the gap that one uses on the side; for spatial gaps one mostly uses 隙間.

examples[].german: I admitted my mistake and apologized.
I will make sure not to repeat the same mistake.
In my youth, I made a grave mistake.
en.notes: 過ち is a "mistake" with weight: a misstep with consequences or a moral dimension. Typical are 過ちを犯す, 過ちを認める, 過ちを繰り返す. For everyday slips one says 間違い or ミス, and for factual errors in texts and judgments 誤り. 過ち sounds serious and rather written-style, for example in confessions or historical retrospectives.

examples[].german: On the day I forgot my umbrella, it rained, sure enough.
The popular restaurant was full, as expected.
I didn't study at all, and, sure enough, I failed the exam.
en.notes: 案の定 means "as expected, sure enough" and confirms a supposition, mostly a fear that then actually comes true. It stands as an adverb at the beginning of a sentence or before the predicate, often with a comma. 予想通り is more neutral and can also introduce something positive; やっぱり is more colloquial and broader. Literally: 案 "supposition" + 定 "certainty".

examples[].german: We are putting effort into developing young talent.
We will create a system in which the whole community nurtures children.
At this facility, fish that are feared to be going extinct are being raised.
en.notes: 育成 is the systematic "bringing up, fostering" of people or abilities and is a transitive する-verb: 人材を育成する, 後継者の育成. It is also used for raising plants and animals (稚魚の育成) and is known from 育成ゲーム. 養成 denotes targeted vocational training (教員養成), and 育てる is the everyday "to raise"; 育成 sounds official or like companies and administration.

en.meaning: to catch; to take in; to take seriously
examples[].german: We took the customers' criticism seriously.
I caught the incoming ball with both hands.
I still can't come to terms with the sudden parting.
en.notes: 受け止める literally means "to catch something coming at you" (ボールを受け止める) and figuratively "to take in, to take seriously, to process": 批判を真剣に受け止める, 現実を受け止める. The passive 受け止められる describes how something is received: 好意的に受け止められた. 受け入れる, in contrast, means "to accept, to agree to", and 受け取る "to receive" or "to interpret". There is no intransitive counterpart.

examples[].german: We accept applications until the end of the month.
We also accept questions by phone.
I have a fever, and my body won't keep food down.
en.notes: 受け付ける means to officially "accept" applications, orders or inquiries: 申し込みを受け付ける, 予約は電話で受け付けております. The noun 受付 refers to the acceptance and the reception desk. In the negative it also means "cannot tolerate, will not admit": 体が食べ物を受け付けない, 人の意見を受け付けない. 受け取る, in contrast, is simply receiving an object.

examples[].german: We cut off the discussion because time ran out.
The company discontinued production of that product.
Because of low ratings, the drama was cancelled after three months.
en.notes: 打ち切る means to "break off" or "discontinue" something in progress, either early or for good: 議論を打ち切る, 交渉を打ち切る, 支援を打ち切る. The passive and the noun 打ち切り are very common, for example when a series is taken off the air: 番組が打ち切りになる. 中止 means more "to call off" (often before something begins), and 中断 means "to interrupt" with a possible resumption.

examples[].german: The mayor explained his policy at a press conference.
The content of the press conference appeared in the newspaper.
The prime minister met with the US president, who was visiting Japan.
en.notes: 会見 is an official meeting or a press conference. The most common form is 記者会見 (often shortened to 会見): 会見を開く, 会見に臨む. As an intransitive する-verb it refers to a formal meeting of high-ranking people: 首相と会見する. 面会 is a visit (hospital, prison), 面接 is a job interview, and インタビュー is an interview with individuals.

examples[].german: Next month we will hold an international conference.
The tournament will be held even if it rains.
The host city of the next Olympics was announced.
en.notes: 開催 is the formal word for "organizing, holding" conferences, trade fairs, tournaments or festivals. As a transitive する-verb: 会議を開催する; the passive 開催される "to take place" is very common. Related words include 開催地 (venue), 開催国 and 開催中. In everyday speech people say the simpler 開く or 行う; 催す is literary.

examples[].german: The travel schedule has been finalized.
I will contact you once the amount is settled.
The tax return must be filed by March 15 every year.
en.notes: 確定 means "to fix definitively" or "to be settled" and, as a する-verb, is both transitive and intransitive: 日程を確定する / 日程が確定する. It is common in administration and online forms (確定ボタン, 注文確定) as well as in 確定申告 "income tax return". 決定 stresses the decision itself, 確定 stresses that nothing will change anymore; 確認 only means "to check, to confirm".

en.meaning: appeal to the highest court; final appeal
examples[].german: The appeal to the Supreme Court was granted.
The defense appealed to the Supreme Court, dissatisfied with the second-instance ruling.
The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, and the judgment became final.
en.notes: 上告 is the legal remedy against a second-instance judgment, usually to the Supreme Court 最高裁: 最高裁に上告する, 上告審, 上告を棄却する "to dismiss the appeal". Distinguish 控訴, the "appeal" against a first-instance judgment; the umbrella term for both is 上訴. Someone who does not accept a verdict typically files 判決を不服として上告する.

en.meaning: dismissal from office; removal from office
examples[].german: The disciplinary dismissal cost him his status as a civil servant.
The employee who had embezzled public funds was dismissed from service as a disciplinary measure.
In the course of the reorganization, some employees were dismissed for official reasons.
en.notes: 免職 is dismissal from a public office. 懲戒免職 is the most severe disciplinary penalty (usually without a pension), 分限免職 is a dismissal without punitive character, e.g. due to inability to work or job cuts, and 依願免職 is a dismissal at one's own request. In private companies one says 解雇 or 懲戒解雇. Typical: 免職になる／となる, 免職される. Register: administrative and news language.

examples[].german: We reviewed our household budget and cut spending.
Rising prices are putting a strain on the household budget.
My mother keeps her household account book every evening.
en.notes: 家計 means the finances of a private household, that is, the family's income and expenses. Typical phrases: 家計が苦しい, 家計を支える, 家計を圧迫する, 家計を見直す; a household account book is 家計簿 (家計簿をつける). 生計 is "livelihood" (生計を立てる), and 予算 is a planned budget, also for companies or states.

examples[].german: Please write the main points as a list.
A bullet-point list makes it easier to check the content.
Let's summarize the text on the slides in short bullet points.
en.notes: 箇条書き is a presentation in individual points, that is, a bullet list instead of running text (文章). Typical: 箇条書きにする, 箇条書きで書く, 要点を箇条書きにまとめる. 箇条 means "item, article" - the same 条 as in legal articles (第一条). It is very common in office and school life, for example for minutes, presentation slides and application documents.

examples[].german: I took out insurance before the trip.
A new member joined the union.
This service now has over a million subscribers.
en.notes: 加入 is the formal word for "joining, signing up for" and an intransitive する-verb used with に: 保険に加入する, 組合に加入する, 年金に加入する, 条約に加入する. A person who has joined is a 加入者 (insured person, subscriber, member). For associations and clubs people prefer 入会 or 入部, for taking part in events 参加; states usually join organizations with 加盟 (国連に加盟する).

examples[].german: I forgot to ask about the most important thing.
What matters is to keep at it.
The party has already started, but the guest of honor, of all people, hasn't arrived yet.
en.notes: 肝心 refers to "the crucial thing, what really matters" - the core of a matter. It is used as a な-adjective (肝心なこと, 〜が肝心だ) and very often as 肝心の + noun: 肝心の本人がいない "the main person, of all people, is missing". Literally "liver and heart", i.e. vital organs; hence also the intensified form 肝心要. 大切 and 重要 are more general, while 肝心 often stresses that precisely the most important thing is missing or going wrong. Alternative spelling: 肝腎.

examples[].german: Many experts are involved in the plan.
He was not involved in this decision.
The police believe a former employee was involved in the case and are investigating.
en.notes: 関与 is the factual "involvement" in a matter and an intransitive する-verb with に: 計画に関与する. It is often about entanglement in scandals, crimes or political decisions: 事件への関与を否定する. 参加 is active participation in an event, and 関わる is the everyday "to have to do with something"; 関与 sounds sober, legal or journalistic.

examples[].german: We carried out the ceremony according to the usual customs.
Old conventions need to be reconsidered.
At this company, it is customary for new employees to give a speech at the year-end party.
en.notes: 慣例 is a practice, often unwritten, that has arisen through repetition within an organization or at ceremonies. Typical: 慣例に従う, 慣例を破る, 慣例により, 〜のが慣例になっている. 習慣 is more a personal habit, 慣習 is a social custom, and 前例 is a precedent. 慣例 sounds formal and is common in administration, politics and corporate culture.

examples[].german: The result matched our expectations.
The interests of both sides coincide.
No one met the application requirements.
en.notes: 合致 means "to agree, to correspond" and is an intransitive する-verb with と or に: 予想と合致する, 条件に合致する, 目的に合致する. It sounds more formal than the more common 一致 and often stresses that something meets criteria or requirements. In everyday speech people simply say 合う (条件に合う). The pronunciation has a geminate consonant: がっち.

examples[].german: I practice listening comprehension every day.
We questioned the residents in person.
In the exam, each listening passage is played twice.
en.notes: 聞き取り has two meanings: in language classes "listening comprehension" (聞き取りの練習, 聞き取り問題) and, in administration or research, "oral questioning" to gather information (聞き取り調査, 関係者から聞き取りを行う). The related verb is 聞き取る "to catch, to make out". Among learners リスニング is also common; a police interrogation, by contrast, is called 事情聴取.

examples[].german: Please submit the documents by the deadline.
The payment due date is approaching.
I voted early and cast my ballot last week.
en.notes: 期日 is a fixed, agreed-upon day, especially a submission or payment deadline: 期日までに提出する, 期日を守る, 支払期日. Also well known is 期日前投票 "early voting". 期限 stresses the time limit as a span and its expiry (期限切れ), 締め切り is the cut-off for submissions or editorial deadlines, and 日付 is only the date on a document. 期日 sounds formal and official.

examples[].german: I am filing the application in accordance with company regulations.
The hours of use are set by a regulation.
Please register only on the prescribed form.
en.notes: 規定 is a concretely established "provision, regulation" in laws, statutes or company rules: 規定に従う, 規定により, 規定の用紙 "prescribed form". As a transitive する-verb it means "to stipulate, to prescribe", often in the passive: 法律で規定されている. 規則 are general rules of conduct, 規約 are rules agreed between parties (e.g. terms of use), and 規制 is a restrictive regulation.

en.meaning: economic crisis; financial panic; panic; terror
examples[].german: The Great Depression had a serious impact on many countries.
The run on the banks developed into a financial panic.
At the sudden sound of an explosion, panic broke out among the passengers.
en.notes: 恐慌 has two meanings: generally "panic, terror" (恐慌をきたす, 恐慌状態に陥る) and, in economics, a severe crisis with bank collapses and company bankruptcies, e.g. 世界恐慌 (from 1929), 金融恐慌, 昭和恐慌. 恐慌 is much stronger than 不況 "recession, slump" or, colloquially, 不景気. In everyday speech, one usually says パニック for panic. Register: formal, history and economics.

en.meaning: set of rules; terms of use
examples[].german: Please read the terms of use before registering.
With the members' consent, we amended the rules.
Accounts that violate the terms of use will be deleted.
en.notes: 規約 are written rules that members or users agree to - the bylaws of an association or the terms of use of a service (利用規約). Typical: 規約に同意する, 規約に違反する, 規約を改正する. 規定 is a single provision, 規則 is a general rule; treaties between states are called 条約.

examples[].german: A deviation of this size is acceptable.
The noise exceeds the permissible range.
How many mistakes to tolerate from one's staff is a difficult question.
en.notes: 許容 means "to tolerate, to accept as still permissible" and is a transitive する-verb: 誤差を許容する. It is very common in compounds such as 許容範囲 (tolerance range), 許容量 and 許容できない. It sounds objective to technical; in everyday speech people say 許す. 許可, by contrast, is official permission, and 容認 is the (often reluctant) acceptance of an attitude or action.

examples[].german: Let's move on to the next agenda item.
We put the budget review on the agenda.
Environmental issues came onto the agenda in parliament.
en.notes: 議題 is the topic discussed at a meeting, that is, an "agenda item". Typical: 議題に移る, 議題に加える, 議題にする, 議題に上がる (to come up on the agenda). 話題, by contrast, is an everyday topic of conversation, and 議案 is a formal motion or bill that is voted on. The whole agenda is called 議事日程.

examples[].german: I left the repair to a specialist firm.
I got quotes from several providers.
Beware of inflated bills from unscrupulous companies.
en.notes: 業者 is a commercial provider or specialist firm that you hire or buy from: 引っ越し業者, 清掃業者, 業者に頼む. The word sounds somewhat impersonal and can have a negative tone in combinations such as 悪質な業者 or 悪徳業者. From a company's point of view, 同業者 means "competitor in the same industry". More neutral words are 会社 or 専門店.

examples[].german: I was briefed on my duties.
We are considering how to make our workflows more efficient.
We have closed for today.
en.notes: 業務 means the work duties and ongoing operations of a company or government office. It is more businesslike than 仕事 and appears in many compounds: 業務内容, 通常業務, 業務時間, 業務提携; 業務用 means "for commercial use". On signs and in announcements you read, for example, 本日の業務は終了しました.

examples[].german: The two of them give conflicting accounts.
We had misunderstood each other about the meeting place and so missed each other.
The president and his deputy disagree over the future course.
en.notes: 食い違う is intransitive and means "to not fit together, to diverge" - originally of seams or gears, today mostly of statements, opinions and figures: 話が食い違う, 意見が食い違う, 証言が食い違う. The noun is 食い違い. 異なる only neutrally means "to be different", and 矛盾する means "to contradict logically"; 食い違う stresses that two versions that should agree do not.

examples[].german: The progress after the operation is good.
An hour has passed since the start.
I will briefly report on the situation so far.
en.notes: 経過 has two main meanings: the passing of time (一時間が経過する, 経過時間) and the course of a development (手術後の経過, 経過報告, 経過観察). As a する-verb it is mostly intransitive. In everyday speech people prefer 経つ for time; 過程 stresses the individual stages of a process, while 経過 stresses the progression over time. Typical for medicine, reports and announcements.

examples[].german: The new rule reduces the burden.
This tool makes the work easier.
A reduced tax rate applies to food.
en.notes: 軽減 means "to reduce, to alleviate, to relieve", especially of burdens, pain, damage or costs: 負担を軽減する, 負担軽減, 痛みの軽減. As a する-verb it is mostly transitive. Well known is 軽減税率 "reduced tax rate". 削減 is cutting an amount (costs, staff), 緩和 is easing rules or tensions; 減らす is the everyday word.

examples[].german: We checked the applicants' backgrounds.
She has experience of working abroad.
It turned out that he had joined the company by falsifying his background.
en.notes: 経歴 is a person's, especially professional, "career history" - education, positions held, experience: 経歴を確認する, 〜した経歴がある, 華やかな経歴. The document itself is called 履歴書; 学歴 is only the educational path, 職歴 the job history. Giving false information on a résumé is called 経歴を偽る or 経歴詐称.

examples[].german: I gave my opinion from a professional standpoint.
We are reviewing the plan from a safety perspective.
From a medical standpoint, this method is not recommended.
en.notes: 見地 is a written-language word for "standpoint, viewpoint" and almost always appears as 〜の見地から or 〜的見地から: 専門的な見地から, 医学的見地から, 安全の見地から. In everyday speech people prefer 観点 or 視点; 立場, by contrast, is one's own role or position. 見地 sounds objective and official and suits expert opinions, statements and reports.

examples[].german: In boom periods, employment tends to increase.
The semiconductor industry is enjoying an unprecedented boom.
Even if the boom continues, wages hardly rise.
en.notes: 好況 denotes a good economic situation, a boom; the opposite is 不況. It sounds more literary than 好景気 or 景気がいい. Typical: 好況が続く, 好況に沸く "to boom", 好況期, 空前の好況. For a single business that is doing well, one does not say 好況 but 繁盛する. Register: economic and news language.

examples[].german: I compared the translation with the original.
Since the meaning is unclear, I will check the original text.
Please copy quotations from the original unchanged.
en.notes: 原文 is the "original text" before a translation, summary or adaptation: 原文と比べる, 原文を確認する, 原文に忠実な翻訳. 原文のまま means "word for word as in the original", for example with quotations. 原作, by contrast, is the original work that gets adapted or filmed, 原稿 is a manuscript, and 本文 is the main text of a document.

examples[].german: We answer questions on an individual basis.
The circumstances of each case must be taken into account.
My son gets one-on-one lessons at cram school.
en.notes: 個別 means "individual, separately for each" and appears as 個別に (adverbial) or 個別の (attributive): 個別に対応する, 個別の事情. Common compounds are 個別指導 (one-on-one tutoring), 個別面談 and 個別包装. The opposite is 一括 or 全体; in everyday speech people often say the simpler 別々に. 個々 stresses "each single one", 個人 the individual person.

examples[].german: Lack of information lies at the root of the problem.
This discovery fundamentally changed previous ways of thinking.
A deep longing for peace underlies his works.
en.notes: 根底 is the deepest "foundation" or the real origin of something abstract. Typical: 〜の根底にある "to lie at the root of ..." and 根底から "from the ground up" (根底から覆す, 根底から揺るがす). 根本 is similar but more common as the adjective 根本的; 基礎 and 土台 are rather concrete or technical foundations. 根底 belongs to written language.

examples[].german: Let's be careful not to confuse similar words.
Facts and opinions are being mixed together.
Taking the company car on a family vacation is mixing business with private matters.
en.notes: 混同 means failing to keep two different things apart or mixing them up; as a transitive する-verb: AとBを混同する, AをBと混同する. Fixed phrase: 公私混同 "mixing of official and private matters", for example the private use of company resources. 間違える is the everyday "to mix up", and 混乱 means "confusion, disorder" as a state.

examples[].german: I will do my best to solve the problem.
That is the best method at present.
Together with the family, we considered what would be best for the patient.
en.notes: 最善 is "the best possible" in the sense of the best course of action: 最善を尽くす "to do one's best", 最善の方法, 最善策. The second-best solution is 次善の策. 最良 refers more to the best quality (最良の日), and 最高 means the highest or, colloquially, "awesome". 最善 sounds serious and suits promises, decisions and official statements.

examples[].german: The standards are set by law.
I set a goal and kept working toward it.
The cat fixed its eyes on its prey and froze.
en.notes: 定める means "to establish, to determine", especially rules, standards, goals and limits: 法律で定める, 〜と定められている (typical of legal texts), 目標を定める. The idiom 狙いを定める means "to take aim at". The intransitive counterpart is 定まる (方針が定まる). 決める is the everyday "to decide"; 定める sounds more formal and stresses a binding determination.

examples[].german: You must not impose your views on others.
The residents were forced to live a long time in emergency shelters.
Pressuring subordinates to drink is harassment.
en.notes: 強いる means "to force someone to do something, to impose something on someone"; pattern: 人に〜を強いる. The passive 〜を強いられる "to be forced to ..." is very common, for example 苦戦を強いられる "to be forced into a hard fight" or 我慢を強いられる. Despite the ending -iru, it is an ichidan verb (強いて, 強いない); the form 強いて as an adverb means "if one must" (強いて言えば). Compared with 強制する, 強いる is somewhat more literary; in everyday speech people prefer 無理にさせる.

examples[].german: Experience abroad broadened my horizons.
We also take long-term effects into account.
At high speed, the field of vision narrows.
en.notes: 視野 literally means the "field of view" of the eyes (視野が狭くなる), but it is used even more often figuratively for the mental "horizon": 視野を広げる "to broaden one's horizons", 視野が狭い "to be narrow-minded", 広い視野を持つ. The fixed phrase 〜を視野に入れる means "to take something into consideration, to have something in view" (e.g. 将来の留学を視野に入れる). For plain visibility in fog or rain, people prefer 視界.

examples[].german: We tallied the survey responses.
We will announce the tally results tomorrow.
I add up the sales every month and report to the department manager.
en.notes: 集計 means "adding up, tabulating" numbers, votes or answers; as a transitive する-verb: 票を集計する, アンケートを集計する. Typical compounds are 集計結果 "tabulation result" and 集計表 "summary table". Unlike 計算 ("calculating" in general), 集計 stresses gathering many individual values into a total or overview; 合計, by contrast, is only the grand total itself.

en.meaning: main body; acting subject; main component
examples[].german: The residents themselves carry out the activities.
I switched to a diet that is mainly plant-based.
We aim for lessons in which children can learn independently.
en.notes: 主体 refers to the "bearer" or "acting subject" of something as well as the "main component". Typical frames: 〜が主体となって "with ... taking the lead", 〜を主体とする "consisting mainly of ...". The derivative 主体的 "independent, on one's own initiative" (主体的に行動する) and 主体性 "initiative" are very common. Do not confuse it with 主催 "organizer": 主体 stresses who acts actively or forms the core.

examples[].german: Regulation of financial institutions was tightened.
The Bank of Japan indicated that it will continue its monetary easing policy.
My older brother has worked in the financial industry since leaving university.
en.notes: 金融 refers to the money and credit system as a whole and mostly appears in compounds: 金融機関 "financial institution", 金融市場, 金融政策 "monetary policy", 金融危機, 金融緩和 "monetary easing" and 金融引き締め "tightening". As a modifier it also works with の (金融の専門家). It is to be distinguished from 財政 "public finances, government budget"; 経済 is the economy in general. Matter-of-fact news and technical language.

examples[].german: I don't know where the documents are.
It must be clarified who is responsible.
Please enter the address of the company's head office on the application form.
en.notes: 所在 is "the place where something or someone is", the "whereabouts". It is a formal word: 所在が分からない, 所在不明 "whereabouts unknown", 所在地 "location, address" (e.g. of a company). Figuratively, 責任の所在 asks "with whom the responsibility lies". In everyday speech people say the simpler どこにあるか or 居場所 (for people). The adjective 所在ない, by contrast, means "bored, idle".

examples[].german: Please fill out the designated form.
I completed the prescribed procedure.
Please return it to its designated place after use.
en.notes: 所定 means "prescribed, designated for that purpose" and is practically always used as 所定の before a noun: 所定の用紙 "the designated form", 所定の場所, 所定の手続き, 所定の時間. It is typical of instructions at government offices, companies and notices. Compared with 規定 (the rule itself), 所定 stresses that something has already been determined; in everyday speech people say the simpler 決められた.

examples[].german: The effect lasts a long time.
To stay focused, you also need breaks.
What can we do for a sustainable society?
en.notes: 持続 means that a state or effect "continues, lasts". As an intransitive する-verb: 効果が持続する; maintaining something by someone is usually expressed with 持続させる. Very common is 持続可能 "sustainable" (持続可能な社会, SDGs). Unlike 継続 (deliberately continuing an activity), 持続 stresses that something endures over time; 維持 means "to maintain a state".

examples[].german: I declined to take part for personal reasons.
He turned down the award.
Because I was accepted by my preferred company, I turned down the other offers.
en.notes: 辞退 means to politely "decline" something offered to oneself or to "waive" it: 参加を辞退する, 受賞を辞退する, 内定を辞退する "to turn down a job offer". It is used with を and sounds formal and modest. Unlike 断る ("to refuse" in general, also other people's requests), 辞退 refers to honors, posts, participation or gifts; 遠慮 is rather a polite holding back.

examples[].german: The price increase has raised the actual burden.
We give more weight to content than to form.
This plan can be used practically for free.
en.notes: 実質 is the "actual content, the substance" as opposed to outward form (形式) or name (名目). Often used as 実質的な "actual, de facto" and adverbially as 実質 or 実質的に "practically, effectively": 実質無料, 実質値上げ "hidden price increase". In economics it stands for "real" as opposed to "nominal": 実質賃金, 実質GDP.

examples[].german: We use local ingredients.
After graduating, I want to return to my hometown.
I was taken to a restaurant that only the locals know.
en.notes: 地元 is the "home area" where one grew up or lives, and as 地元の also "local, regional" from the viewpoint of a particular place: 地元の人, 地元の食材, 地元企業, 地元の警察. 地元に帰る means "to return to one's hometown". Unlike 故郷 or ふるさと, which emotionally refer to one's birthplace, 地元 is matter-of-fact and everyday; 現地, by contrast, means "on the spot" in a foreign place.

examples[].german: I worked in the field of education for many years.
We support people working in medical professions.
My grandfather worked in agriculture for sixty years.
en.notes: 従事 means "to be professionally active in a field"; the field is marked with に: 農業に従事する, 医療に従事する. It is a formal word from résumés, statistics and news (医療従事者 "medical personnel"). Close in meaning is 携わる (〜に携わる), which sounds a bit more personal; in everyday speech people simply say 〜の仕事をしている.

examples[].german: Two appointments overlap.
I cleaned up duplicate information.
Please do not register twice for the same course.
en.notes: 重複 means "duplication, overlap"; as an intransitive する-verb: 予定が重複する, データが重複している. The traditional reading is ちょうふく, but in everyday speech じゅうふく is heard at least as often; both are now considered correct. Often used adverbially as 重複して "twice over" (重複して申し込む) and in 重複を避ける. For overlapping appointments in time, 重なる is also very common.

examples[].german: I listened to the residents' urgent requests.
The labor shortage is a pressing problem.
Since I started living alone, I keenly feel how important cooking is.
en.notes: 切実 describes something that "affects one directly and deeply": a "pressing" problem or an "earnest, urgent" wish. Typical are 切実な問題, 切実な願い, 切実な声 and adverbially 切実に感じる/訴える. Unlike 緊急 ("urgent" in the sense of hurried), 切実 stresses personal concern and seriousness, not haste.

examples[].german: We won't give up just because there is no precedent.
I based my decision on earlier cases.
Once you allow an exception, it becomes a precedent.
en.notes: 前例 is a "precedent, previous example". Typical are 前例がない/前例のない "unprecedented", 前例を作る "to set a precedent" and 前例になる; 前例に従う or 前例を参考にする means to follow earlier cases. 前例主義 criticizes rigid adherence to what has been done before. Since 前 already contains "earlier", 過去の前例 is considered redundant.

examples[].german: Speculative trading caused the bubble.
Many people also buy and sell stocks in the short term for speculative purposes.
Speculation in land drove up land prices.
en.notes: 投機 is "speculation": one buys stocks, land or commodities in order to profit from price fluctuations in the short term. Typical are 投機的な取引, 投機目的, 投機マネー and 投機に走る. In contrast, 投資 denotes a longer-term, value-oriented "investment"; 投機 therefore often sounds critical. Do not confuse it with the identically read 投棄 ("illegal dumping", e.g. 不法投棄).

examples[].german: We discussed the future of the school.
Efforts to preserve the tradition continue.
After continued losses, the company's survival is at stake.
en.notes: 存続 is the "continued existence" of an institution, company, tradition or species. Typical: 〜の存続が危ぶまれる "the continued existence is in danger", 存続を求める, and for actively preserving 存続させる. As a する-verb it is mostly used intransitively (制度が存続する). Compared with 継続 ("continuation of an activity"), 存続 is about continuing to exist at all, often in the face of impending closure.

examples[].german: He carried out the investigation alone.
One company alone cannot realize this plan.
On the final day, the player took sole possession of the lead.
en.notes: 単独 means "alone, independent, without other participants". Mostly as 単独で (単独で行動する) or as a prefix in compounds: 単独行動, 単独犯 "lone offender", 単独事故 "single-vehicle accident", 単独首位 "sole lead". It is more businesslike than 一人で and can also be applied to companies, states or parties (一社単独, 単独政権).

examples[].german: We are facing a major challenge.
Faced with reality, my view changed.
It is precisely in a crisis that staying calm matters.
en.notes: 直面 means "to face something directly"; almost always in the pattern 〜に直面する with difficult things: 問題, 危機, 困難, 現実, 死. It is an intransitive する-verb, and the thing faced takes に, not を. Compared with 向き合う ("to consciously confront something"), 直面 describes more the situation one gets into; in everyday speech people also say 〜にぶつかる.

examples[].german: Normally it arrives within two days.
Normal business hours apply again from tomorrow.
Students get in at half the regular price.
en.notes: 通常 means "usual, normal, regular". As an adverb it stands alone or with は (通常は二日で届く), before nouns as 通常の or directly in compounds: 通常料金, 通常営業, 通常国会. 通常通り means "as usual". It is more formal than 普通 and typical of business notices, manuals and news; in conversation 普通 or いつも sounds more natural.

examples[].german: Please show an ID at the entrance.
The company has put forward new terms.
Please explain using concrete examples.
en.notes: 提示 means to "show" something (ID, ticket) or to "present, put forward" (conditions, a plan, an example): 身分証を提示する, 条件を提示する, 例を提示する. The difference from 提出 is important: with 提出 you hand in a document and it stays with the recipient, whereas with 提示 you merely show it. 提示 is formal; in conversation people say 見せる.

examples[].german: Take breaks as needed if you feel tired.
We adjust the content as appropriate to the situation.
Taste it and add salt to taste.
en.notes: 適宜 means "as needed, depending on the situation, at one's own discretion" and usually stands directly before the verb as an adverb: 適宜休憩を取る, 適宜変更する. Common in manuals, work instructions and recipes (塩 適宜 "salt to taste"). Do not confuse it with 適当: that can also mean "suitable", but in everyday speech also "sloppy, any old way", whereas 適宜 always stays neutral and businesslike.

examples[].german: I don't have the documents at hand, so I can't check.
Please keep important documents with you.
My hand slipped and I cut my finger.
en.notes: 手元 is the area "right at hand": 手元にある "to be at hand", 手元に置く "to keep within reach". In presentations you often hear お手元の資料をご覧ください "Please look at the materials in front of you". 手元 can also mean the movement of the hands (手元が狂う "the hand slips") and available money (手元資金). Unlike 近く, 手元 stresses that one can reach for it immediately.

examples[].german: We invested capital in the new business.
Please insert coins into the machine.
Next month we will launch a new product on the market.
en.notes: 投入 literally means "to throw in" (coins, ballots: 硬貨を投入する) and figuratively "to commit, to pour in" money, personnel or effort: 資金を投入する, 人員を投入する. It also means to bring a product to market (市場に投入する). Unlike 投資 ("to invest" with an expectation of profit), 投入 stresses the commitment of resources for a goal. The target takes に.

examples[].german: This qualification is treated as equivalent to a university degree.
The prices differ, but the performance is equivalent.
As for salary, I would like at least as much as at my previous company.
en.notes: 同等 means "equivalent, of equal rank" and is usually used with と: 〜と同等の (rights, performance, degree), 〜と同等に扱う "to treat equally", 同等以上 "equal or better". Compared with 同じ ("the same"), it concerns equal value or rank, not identity. 対等, by contrast, stresses the equal standing of partners (対等な関係).

examples[].german: We toured the building from the inside.
We need to discuss the matter thoroughly internally.
Internal information has leaked to the outside.
en.notes: 内部 is the "inside" of an object or building and, especially often, the "internal" side of an organization; its opposite is 外部. Typical: 建物の内部, 内部情報, 内部告発 "whistleblowing", 内部で検討する "to examine internally". In everyday speech, for rooms people prefer 中; 内側 stresses the inner side of a surface. For one's own company, 社内 is also common.

examples[].german: Devise a strategy to maximize profit.
Companies should not pursue profit alone.
In economics class we learned about the relationship between profit and costs.
en.notes: 利潤 is profit in the economic, rather abstract sense, e.g. in 利潤を追求する "to pursue profit" or 利潤の最大化. In business reports and everyday speech one usually says 利益 (with indicators such as 営業利益), colloquially 儲け "earnings, profit". 利潤 sounds theoretical and is often used critically when companies chase only profit.

examples[].german: I obtained the necessary documents.
This book is now hard to get.
The police have received new information about the case.
en.notes: 入手 means "to get into one's hands, to obtain"; as a transitive する-verb: 情報を入手する, チケットを入手する. 入手困難 "hard to obtain" and 入手方法 are common. It is more formal than 手に入れる and neutral about the means: 購入, by contrast, explicitly means "to buy", and 取得 means "to acquire (officially)", for example a license.

examples[].german: Please feel free to speak up at the meeting.
His remark triggered the discussion.
The minister's inappropriate remark is causing an uproar.
en.notes: 発言 is a "remark" or "contribution", especially in meetings, debates or in public: 会議で発言する, 大臣の発言, 発言を撤回する "to retract a remark". Related are 発言権 "right to speak" and 発言力 "influence in discussions"; a careless remark is a 失言. For everyday talking people simply say 言う or 話す; 発言 stresses taking the floor within a setting.

examples[].german: A small mistake caused a serious accident.
The remark triggered a heated debate.
It is hard to pick up a fallen motorcycle by yourself.
en.notes: 引き起こす mostly means "to cause, to trigger" - almost always with undesirable consequences: 事故を引き起こす, 混乱を引き起こす, 議論を引き起こす. It sounds stronger and more formal than 起こす. The literal meaning "to pick up something that has fallen over" (倒れた自転車を引き起こす) also exists. For positive results, もたらす fits better. The intransitive counterpart is simply 起こる.

examples[].german: With insufficient preparation, failure is inevitable.
This change is an inevitable consequence of social development.
Perhaps the meeting of the two was not chance but fate.
en.notes: 必然 is "the necessary, the inevitable"; its opposite is 偶然 "chance". As a predicate: 失敗は必然だ; before nouns mostly 必然的な結果, adverbially 必然的に "inevitably". The contrast 偶然ではなく必然 "not chance but destiny" is popular. In everyday speech people often say 当然 ("naturally"), but 必然 stresses logical-causal necessity, not expectedness.

examples[].german: We divided the work among several people in charge.
By staggering the times, we avoid crowding.
To spread the risk, I invest in several companies.
en.notes: 分散 means "to distribute, to scatter, to disperse"; its opposite is 集中. As a する-verb it is transitive (リスクを分散する, 作業を分散する) as well as intransitive (人口が分散する, 注意が分散する "attention is scattered"). Typical expressions are リスク分散, 分散投資 and 分散登校. In statistics, 分散 means "variance". Compared with 分ける ("to divide"), 分散 stresses spreading across many places.

examples[].german: We put the agreement in writing.
We keep important documents in a safe place.
We will send you the answer to your question in writing.
en.notes: 文書 is a "document, written paper" as an object, especially in the official sense: 公文書 "official document", 文書で回答する "to answer in writing", 文書化 "to put in writing". Do not confuse it with 文章 (ぶんしょう) "text, prose", which is about the wording. 書類 refers more to concrete papers and forms in a folder; 文書 is more general and more formal.

examples[].german: I repay the borrowed money every month.
I drew up a repayment plan.
I still have to pay off the home loan for ten more years.
en.notes: 返済 is the "repayment" of borrowed money, loans or debts: 借金を返済する, ローンの返済, 返済期限 "repayment deadline". In everyday speech people simply say お金を返す. Do not confuse it with 返却 (return of objects, e.g. books) and 返金 (refund of a purchase price by the seller).

examples[].german: I am waiting for an answer to the question.
I could not answer right away.
In the job interview, I was asked a question I had no answer to.
en.notes: 返答 is an "answer, reply" to a question, inquiry or request: 返答する, 返答に困る "to not know what to answer", 返答を待つ. In everyday speech 返事 is more usual (also for letters and emails); 回答 is the formal answer to an inquiry or survey, and 答え is the solution to a question or task. 返答 sounds somewhat more formal than 返事.

examples[].german: If you leave the problem alone, it will get worse.
Please do not leave bicycles standing in the street.
Never leave children alone in a car.
en.notes: 放置 means to "leave lying, leave to itself" something one should take care of - usually with criticism: 問題を放置する, 自転車を放置する, 放置自転車 "illegally parked bicycles". In conversation people prefer 放っておく or ほったらかす. Unlike そのままにする ("to leave as is", neutral), 放置 stresses neglect of a duty.

examples[].german: Read the passage and answer the questions.
The detailed explanation is in the main text.
I forgot to write my name in the body of the email.
en.notes: 本文 is the "main text" of a book, article or letter as opposed to the title, subject line, footnotes or appendix; for emails it is the "body" (メールの本文). In exams, 本文 stands for "the text at hand" (本文の内容と合うもの). Do not confuse it with 文章 ("text, wording" in general) and 本題 ("the actual topic").

examples[].german: I chose a financial product with a principal guarantee.
This investment fund carries the risk that you get back less than you paid in.
Every month I repay not only the interest but also a little of the principal.
en.notes: 元本 is the amount originally deposited or borrowed, from which interest and returns are calculated: "capital, principal". Typical are 元本保証 "principal guarantee", 元本割れ "falling below the amount paid in" (a loss on funds) and 元本を返済する. For loans one also says 元金, hence 元利 "principal and interest"; the counterpart is 利息 or 利子 "interest". Language of finance and law.

examples[].german: Please let us know the number of people beforehand.
I had researched beforehand, so I didn't get lost.
If you tell me in advance, I'll pick you up at the station.
en.notes: 前もって means "in advance, beforehand" and stands before a verb, often together with 〜ておく: 前もって調べておく, 前もって知らせる. It is neutral to slightly colloquial; synonymous but more formal are あらかじめ and 事前に (事前に連絡する). It is usually written in mixed kana and kanji as 前もって.

en.meaning: to fill; to satisfy; to meet
examples[].german: I meet all the application requirements.
Please fill the container with water.
I satisfied my hunger with a hot soup.
en.notes: 満たす means "to fill" (容器を水で満たす) and figuratively "to fulfill, to satisfy": 条件を満たす "to meet conditions", 基準を満たす, お腹を満たす "to satisfy one's hunger", 欲求を満たす. The intransitive counterpart is 満ちる "to be full, to be filled" (自信に満ちる). The passive 満たされる also means "to feel fulfilled". The phrase 〜に満たない "less than" comes from the related 満つ.

examples[].german: Let's start with problems from everyday life.
If you have trouble, talk to someone close to you.
The smartphone is now our most familiar everyday tool.
en.notes: 身近 means "close to one's own life, familiar, everyday" - both spatially and personally: 身近な人 "people in one's own circle", 身近な問題, 身近に感じる "to feel close". As a na-adjective: 身近な, 身近に. Unlike 近く (purely spatial) and 親しい ("closely befriended"), 身近 stresses that something belongs to one's own daily life. The kana spelling is みぢか, not みじか.

examples[].german: The date of the next meeting has not been decided yet.
The number of participants is still open, so I can't make a reservation.
The release date of the new title has not been decided; we will inform you once it is.
en.notes: 未定 means "not yet determined, open" and usually appears as the predicate 〜は未定です or as 未定の. Typical for announcements and plans: 日程未定, 発売日は未定, 詳細は未定. The prefix 未 means "not yet" (cf. 未定, 未完成, 未経験). The opposite is 決定 or 確定; in conversation people also say まだ決まっていない.

examples[].german: Please do not take photos without permission.
He stayed away from work without notice.
Redistributing the images on this website without permission is prohibited.
en.notes: 無断 means "without permission" or "without prior notice". It appears as 無断で before an action (無断で休む) or as a prefix in fixed terms: 無断欠勤 "unexcused absence", 無断駐車, 無断転載禁止 "reprinting without permission prohibited". The tone is always critical. More neutral would be 許可なく or 連絡せずに.

examples[].german: We are searching for new ways to solve it.
We explored possibilities for cooperation with the region.
I am still looking for my path for after graduation.
en.notes: 模索 means to "feel one's way, search for a solution" when the answer is still unclear: 解決策を模索する, 方向性を模索する, 模索が続く. Well known is the four-character idiom 暗中模索 "groping in the dark". Unlike 探す (searching for something concrete), it concerns abstract ways and possibilities; 試行錯誤, by contrast, stresses trying things out by trial and error. Typical of news and reports.

examples[].german: She is one of the leading candidates.
A plausible explanation of the cause of the accident was presented.
The police have found a promising lead on the culprit.
en.notes: 有力 means, on the one hand, "influential, powerful" (有力者, 有力企業), and on the other "promising, convincing": 有力な候補, 有力な説, 有力な手がかり "a promising lead". The passive 有力視される means "to be considered promising". Do not confuse it with 有能 ("capable, competent"), which refers to personal competence, not to power or likelihood.

examples[].german: We collected the users' requests.
The residents are calling for improvements to the road.
At our customers' request, we extended the opening hours.
en.notes: 要望 is a "wish, request" addressed to an organization or those in charge: 要望を出す, 要望に応える, お客様のご要望. As a する-verb: 改善を要望する. It is stronger than 希望 (a personal wish) but less demanding than 要求 ("demand", often with pressure). For a concrete request to do something, people say 依頼.

examples[].german: There is room for improvement in this plan.
There is no doubt about this result.
There is no room left in the parking lot for another car.
en.notes: 余地 literally means "free space", but is mostly used figuratively for "leeway, room for something". Typical frames: 〜の余地がある/ない - 改善の余地 "room for improvement", 疑いの余地はない "there is no room for doubt", 選択の余地がない "to have no choice", 議論の余地 "open to debate". Also with a verb: 入る余地がない "no room to get in". Compared with スペース or 空き, 余地 stresses the possibility of still fitting something in or doing something.

examples[].german: We received approval for the schedule change.
Please understand that a reply may take some time.
The department manager agreed to my proposal.
en.notes: 了承 means "to take note of and agree": 了承を得る "to obtain approval", 提案を了承する. Very common in notices is ご了承ください "We ask for your understanding" - one announces something the reader has to accept. Compared with 承認 (official approval), 了承 is less formal; 了解 is more a brief "understood" among equals, and 承知 is the humble form (承知しました).

examples[].german: A cut in interest rates is expected to stimulate consumption.
The interest rate on this time deposit is 0.3 percent per year.
Before taking out a home loan, I compared the interest rates of the banks.
en.notes: 利率 is the interest rate as a percentage, especially for loans, bonds and savings: 利率が高い／低い, 利率を引き上げる／引き下げる, 年利率. The more common, more general word for "interest (level)" is 金利 (金利が上がる, 低金利); 利息 and 利子, on the other hand, denote the amount of interest actually paid. 利率 sounds somewhat more technical and often appears in contract documents.

examples[].german: I combine work and study.
We aim to achieve both safety and comfort.
Balancing child-rearing and a career is not easy.
en.notes: 両立 means that two things are "compatible with each other" or are both realized at the same time: AとBが両立する (intransitive) or AとBを両立させる; in everyday speech you also hear AとBを両立する. Classic themes are 仕事と家庭の両立, 勉強と部活の両立 and 経済と環境の両立. 両立しない means "incompatible". Compared with 共存 ("coexistence"), 両立 stresses successfully balancing the two.

examples[].german: I put a lot of work in until it was finished.
This method saves time and effort.
He spares no effort for the team.
en.notes: 労力 is the "work and effort" one puts into something: 労力を費やす, 労力がかかる, 労力を惜しまない "to spare no effort", 時間と労力. Unlike 努力 ("effort, striving" as a positive attitude), 労力 refers more to the labor expended as a cost factor; 手間 is the bothersome time and effort on a small scale. 労働力, by contrast, means the "labor force" of a society.

examples[].german: I thought carefully about my future.
Let's discuss it calmly next time.
You let it simmer over low heat for an hour.
en.notes: じっくり (also じっくりと) means "calmly and thoroughly", without haste and with full attention: じっくり考える, じっくり話し合う, じっくり読む, and in cooking じっくり煮込む "to simmer for a long time". Unlike ゆっくり ("slowly, leisurely"), じっくり stresses care and depth; しっかり means more "properly, firmly". Typical of conversation, advertising and recipes.

examples[].german: I was sure that today was a day off.
Since he came, I assumed there was a meeting.
I was sure I would be scolded, but I was praised instead.
en.notes: てっきり expresses that one "was firmly convinced" - and was mistaken. It almost always appears with 〜と思っていた/〜と思った; the correction often follows with のに, けど or 〜たら: てっきり〜と思ったら, 違った. Unlike きっと (a conjecture about the future), てっきり looks back on a wrong assumption. Spoken language, written in kana without kanji.

examples[].german: I will reply by Friday at the latest.
We have to leave by eight at the latest.
Please take your seat at least ten minutes before the performance starts.
en.notes: 遅くとも means "at the latest" and stands before a time expression with までに or には: 遅くとも金曜日までに, 遅くとも八時には. It is somewhat more literary; in conversation people often say 遅くても. The counterpart is 早くとも/早くても "at the earliest". For deadlines in official and business language, 〜までに必ず is also common.

examples[].german: I combine two methods when studying.
Combine the colors as you like.
Because of the draw, two strong teams meet already in the first round.
en.notes: 組み合わせる means to "combine, put together" several elements: 色を組み合わせる, AとBを組み合わせる. The noun 組み合わせ means "combination" and, in tournaments, also "pairing"; accordingly the verb can mean "to draw against each other". Unlike 合わせる ("to put together, to match"), 組み合わせる stresses deliberately assembling different parts into a whole. Ichidan verb.

examples[].german: I built breaks into the schedule.
We are integrating a new feature into the product.
These costs are already included in the budget.
en.notes: 組み込む means to insert something as a fixed component into a larger whole: AをBに組み込む ("to build A into B"), for example breaks into a schedule, costs into a budget or a function into a device. There is no separate intransitive counterpart; the passive 組み込まれる ("to be built in") is used. The noun 組み込み stands in technology for "embedded" (組み込みソフト). 取り入れる stresses adopting ideas from outside, 含める mere inclusion in a count.

examples[].german: Through the discussion, I deepened my understanding.
We would like to intensify exchange with the region.
His vague explanation only strengthened the police's suspicion.
en.notes: 深める is the transitive verb of 深い and is used almost only for abstract things: 理解を深める, 知識を深める, 交流を深める, 絆を深める, but also negatively 疑いを深める ("to strengthen suspicion"). The intransitive counterpart is 深まる (理解が深まる, 秋が深まる). For a concrete hole or basin, people prefer 深くする or 掘り下げる. The tone is neutral to slightly literary.

en.meaning: to reveal; to disclose; to spend (the night)
examples[].german: He revealed the real reason for the first time.
I spent the night talking with a friend.
In the end, the magician revealed how the trick works.
en.notes: 明かす has two main uses: revealing something hidden, typically with 秘密, 本当の理由, 正体, 胸の内 or 手品の種 as the object; and 夜を明かす or 一夜を明かす for "to spend the night (awake)". 打ち明ける stresses confiding in someone, 明らかにする the factual clarification of facts, and ばらす is colloquial blabbing. Do not confuse it with the intransitive 明ける (夜が明ける "day breaks").

examples[].german: His effort deserves praise.
This proposal is worth considering.
His testimony is not credible.
en.notes: 値する almost always appears in the frame "noun + に値する": 賞賛に値する, 注目に値する, 一読に値する, 検討に値する; negated 信用に値しない ("not trustworthy"). It is intransitive and elevated, written-language; in everyday speech people prefer 〜の価値がある or 〜する価値がある. It conjugates like する (値します, 値しない) and is often used attributively before a noun (検討に値する提案).

examples[].german: The household savings rate is falling year by year.
I decided to put half of my bonus into savings.
It is better to save from a young age to prepare for old age.
en.notes: 貯蓄 is saving or the accumulated assets in a factual, economic sense, also as a する-verb (老後のために貯蓄する). Common: 貯蓄率 "savings rate", 貯蓄に回す "to put aside as savings", 貯蓄から投資へ. In everyday speech one usually says 貯金 or 貯金する; 貯蓄 is broader, also covering insurance and securities, and sounds more formal. 預金 is specifically a bank deposit.

en.meaning: to value; to attach importance to
examples[].german: This company places great value on experience.
It is important to respect the other person's opinion.
In the tea ceremony, great importance is placed on etiquette.
en.notes: 重んじる means to attach great weight to something or some value: 伝統を重んじる, 礼儀を重んじる, 経験を重んじる, 和を重んじる. It is more formal than 大切にする; for other people's opinions or rights, 尊重する is even more common. The opposite is 軽んじる ("to belittle"). The literary variant 重んずる means the same.

examples[].german: The author has not published her real name.
Please use your real name for the application.
This singer's real name is surprisingly ordinary.
en.notes: 本名 (read ほんみょう) is a person's real, official name, as opposed to 芸名 ("stage name"), ペンネーム, 偽名 ("false name") or 通称 ("commonly used name"). Typical are 本名を明かす, 本名を公表する and 本名で活動する. On forms, 氏名 is usually used instead; 本名 stresses that there is also another name.

examples[].german: I put my work history in my résumé.
You can view your past purchases.
I deleted the browser history on the computer.
en.notes: 履歴 refers, on the one hand, to a personal career history, above all in the compound 履歴書 ("résumé"); for the career itself people mostly say 経歴, 学歴 or 職歴. Today 履歴 is mainly encountered as stored history: 閲覧履歴, 検索履歴, 通話履歴, 購入履歴, 変更履歴. Fitting phrases are 履歴を確認する, 履歴を消す and 履歴が残る.

examples[].german: We conducted a user survey.
We use the survey results for improvements.
Please fill out our short questionnaire before you leave.
en.notes: アンケート (from French "enquête") is a written questionnaire or a survey of customers, users or participants. The organizer says アンケートを取る or アンケートを実施する, the respondents アンケートに答える or, politely, アンケートにご協力ください. For representative opinion polls in politics and the media, people say 世論調査 instead. アンケート用紙 and アンケート調査 are also common.

examples[].german: We value communication in the workplace.
Language is not the only means of communication.
To keep talking as a family, we eat together every evening.
en.notes: コミュニケーション in Japanese refers mainly to interpersonal exchange and getting along with one another, less to technical transmission (for that, 通信). Typical are コミュニケーションを取る ("to communicate"), コミュニケーション不足 and コミュニケーション能力 (colloquially shortened to コミュ力). More formal is 意思疎通 ("mutual understanding").

examples[].german: I was asked for a comment on the article.
I received concrete feedback and revised the text.
The video received many comments.
en.notes: コメント is a short remark, note or statement and can also be used as a する-verb: 〜についてコメントする. Typical are コメントを求める, コメントを書く/残す, SNSのコメント欄 and the refusal ノーコメント ("no comment"). 感想 is a personal impression and 意見 an opinion; コメント stresses brief feedback on something specific.

examples[].german: Work came to a standstill because of a machine malfunction.
We are reviewing the contract to avoid problems.
I got into trouble with the neighbor because of the noise.
en.notes: トラブル covers technical malfunctions (機械のトラブル), disputes (近所トラブル, 金銭トラブル) and, in cosmetics, complaints (肌トラブル). Typical are トラブルが起きる, トラブルを起こす, トラブルになる and トラブルに巻き込まれる. 問題 is more general (also exam questions), and 故障 means only a device's breakdown. For "I'm in trouble" people don't say トラブル but 困っている.

examples[].german: These two words differ in nuance.
Subtle nuances are hard to convey in translation.
It wasn't supposed to sound angry.
en.notes: ニュアンス is the fine shade of meaning or undertone of an utterance. Typical are ニュアンスが違う, 微妙なニュアンス, ニュアンスを伝える/つかむ and "〜というニュアンスで言う" ("to mean something in the sense of ..."). 意味 is the basic meaning, 含み the hidden implication; ニュアンス stresses the difference between similar expressions.

examples[].german: I left a message on the answering machine.
This work conveys a strong message.
I sent my friend a message on his mobile phone.
en.notes: メッセージ is both a concrete message (メッセージを送る, メッセージを残す, via a chat app or answering machine) and the message conveyed by a work or speech (作品に込められたメッセージ, メッセージを発信する). 伝言, by contrast, is a message passed on orally via a third person, and メール specifically an email.

examples[].german: I attend class online.
Registration is also possible online.
Let's hold next week's meeting online instead of in person.
en.notes: オンライン is used adverbially with で (オンラインで申し込む, オンラインで受講する) or as a modifier before nouns: オンライン会議, オンライン授業, オンラインショップ. Opposites are オフライン and, for meetings and classes, 対面 ("in person"). A verb オンラインする does not exist; people say, for example, オンラインにする or オンラインで行う.

examples[].german: Funds were raised through a third-party allotment capital increase.
A major trading company underwrote the capital increase of the struggling airline.
To secure funds for the construction of the new factory, a capital increase is planned for next year.
en.notes: 増資 is the increase of a company's share capital, usually by issuing new shares; as a する-verb 増資する. Typical compounds: 第三者割当増資 "capital increase by allotment to third parties", 公募増資 "capital increase by public offering"; whoever takes up the new shares 増資を引き受ける. The opposite is 減資; raising money in general is called 資金調達. Purely the language of business and news.

examples[].german: Please give me a hint for the solution.
A friend's words gave the decisive inspiration.
This product was developed with nature as its model.
en.notes: ヒント is a hint that helps you find the solution yourself: ヒントを出す/あげる, ヒントをもらう. In a broader sense it is a suggestion or inspiration: 〜のヒントになる, 〜からヒントを得る. 手がかり is more a trace in an investigation, コツ a practical trick, and アドバイス direct advice.

examples[].german: I missed the right moment to ask.
The call came at exactly the right moment.
We had bad timing - the shop had just closed.
en.notes: タイミング is the (right) point in time for an action: タイミングがいい/悪い, タイミングが合う, タイミングを逃す, タイミングを見計らう, いいタイミングで. Unlike 時期 ("period, phase"), it concerns the exact moment; チャンス stresses the favorable opportunity itself. Bad timing is expressed with タイミングが悪い.

examples[].german: I compiled the materials into a single file.
I opened the old file and checked the contents.
Please bring the documents in a clear file folder.
en.notes: ファイル is both a computer file (ファイルを開く, ファイルを保存する, 添付ファイル) and a folder or binder for papers (クリアファイル "clear file folder"). As a する-verb, ファイルする means "to file away". For the folder on a computer one says フォルダ, not ファイル.

examples[].german: I left the room key at the front desk.
If you have any trouble, please contact the front desk.
I asked the front desk for a wake-up call.
en.notes: In daily life フロント is above all the hotel front desk: フロントに預ける, フロントに電話する, フロントで聞く. For the reception in companies, clinics or hospitals, one says 受付 instead. In addition, フロント also means "front" (weather front, front side, e.g. フロントガラス "windshield") and, in sports, the management of a club.

examples[].german: I don't remember the address for sure, so I'll check it again.
The meeting ended without clarifying who is responsible.
Don't be evasive; please say it clearly.
en.notes: あやふや is a na-adjective: あやふやな記憶, 記憶があやふやだ. It describes above all uncertain memories, knowledge, answers or attitudes that cannot be relied on. あやふやにする means to deliberately leave something unresolved. 曖昧 is broader and can also mean an ambiguous wording; あやふや is somewhat more colloquial and stresses the lack of firmness.

examples[].german: The lawyer took on the defendant's defense.
Only she defended me when everyone was blaming me.
There is no room for defending his behavior.
en.notes: 弁護 is defense in court (弁護士 "lawyer", 弁護人 "defense counsel"), but also standing up for someone in everyday life: 友人を弁護する "to take a friend's part". Fixed phrases are 弁護を引き受ける/依頼する, 自己弁護 ("self-justification") and 弁護の余地がない ("indefensible"). 擁護 means rather defending rights or principles (人権擁護); colloquially, for standing up for someone, one often says かばう.

examples[].german: A capital reduction was carried out to eliminate the accumulated deficit.
In the restructuring plan, the capital was reduced by 100%, and the existing shares lost their value.
More and more companies are reducing their share capital to 100 million yen or less in order to ease their tax burden.
en.notes: 減資 is the reduction of share capital; as a する-verb 減資する. It often serves to offset accumulated losses on the books, or to qualify as a small business for tax purposes with smaller capital. Collocations: 減資を行う／実施する, 100％減資 (complete reduction, in which the old shares become worthless). Opposite: 増資. Technical language from corporate law and business news.

examples[].german: Transactions with affiliated companies are conducted at fair prices.
After retiring, my father works at an affiliate of his former company.
Subsidiaries and affiliated companies are treated differently in the financial statements.
en.notes: 関連会社 is, in accounting law, a company in which a firm holds a significant stake without controlling it (usually about 20-50%): an "associate company". To be distinguished from it are 子会社 "subsidiary" (control) and 親会社 "parent company". In everyday speech, however, any firm of the same corporate group is often loosely called 関連会社 or グループ会社. Here 会社 is read がいしゃ.

examples[].german: Strengthen group management by shifting to a holding company structure.
The two companies merged their management and established a new holding company.
The supermarket came under the umbrella of the holding company of a major retail group last year.
en.notes: 持株会社 is a company whose main purpose is to hold shares of other companies and control them: a "holding". In company names it now often appears as 〜ホールディングス; 純粋持株会社 only holds stakes, 事業持株会社 additionally runs its own business. Typical: 持株会社を設立する, 持株会社体制に移行する, 持株会社の傘下に入る. 持株 alone is "share ownership" (持株比率 "shareholding ratio").

examples[].german: New directors were elected at the shareholders' meeting.
Heads of state and government gave speeches at the UN General Assembly.
The general meeting of our apartment building's management association is held every May.
en.notes: 総会 is the assembly of all members of an organization, which decides on important matters. Mostly in compounds: 株主総会 "general shareholders' meeting", 国連総会 "UN General Assembly", 定期総会 and 臨時総会, in schools 生徒総会. Verbs: 総会を開く／開催する, 総会で承認される／決議する. An ordinary meeting is 会議 or 集会; 総会 emphasizes that all members take part with voting rights.

en.meaning: articles of incorporation; articles of association
examples[].german: A resolution of the shareholders' meeting is required to amend the articles of incorporation.
To establish a company, you must first draw up the articles of incorporation.
You cannot start a business that is not listed in the articles of incorporation.
en.notes: 定款 are the articles of association of a legal entity (stock company, foundation, association), which set out its purpose, name, seat and organs. Typical: 定款を作成する, 定款を変更する, 定款に定める "to stipulate in the articles", 定款の認証 (notarial certification at founding). Pre-formulated customer terms, on the other hand, are called 約款, and the rules of an association or service are often 規約. Purely legal, formal language.

examples[].german: I signed the contract after thoroughly checking the insurance terms.
You cannot use this service unless you agree to the terms and conditions.
Damage to luggage is compensated in accordance with the carriage terms.
en.notes: 約款 are the pre-formulated contract terms of a company, identical for all customers: "standard terms and conditions", for insurance "insurance terms". Typical: 保険約款, 運送約款, 約款に同意する, 約款に基づいて. A single clause is called 条項. While 定款 is the internal charter of a company, 約款 governs the relationship with customers; for online services one usually reads 利用規約 "terms of use". Formal legal and business language.

examples[].german: Business sentiment has improved and companies' capital investment is picking up.
