The business conditions of small and medium-sized enterprises remain difficult.
The chamber of commerce and industry announced the results of its regional business conditions survey.
en.notes: 景況 is the general business or economic situation and occurs almost only in business reports. Very common is 景況感 "economic sentiment, business climate", that is, how companies judge the situation, as well as 景況調査 "business conditions survey". In everyday speech one says 景気 (景気がいい／悪い); 景況 is the formal, analytical counterpart and is more often associated with 厳しい, 改善する or 悪化する.

examples[].german: Monetary tightening was carried out to curb inflation.
Rapid inflation made life hard for the people.
Inflation is the phenomenon of prices rising continuously.
en.notes: インフレーション is the long form; in news and conversation people almost always say the short form インフレ (インフレが進む, インフレ率, インフレ対策). The long form sounds textbook-like and appears in definitions or technical texts, also in cosmology (インフレーション理論). The opposite is デフレーション／デフレ; a mere price rise is called 物価上昇, and inflation with a stagnating economy スタグフレーション.

examples[].german: The public is angry about political corruption.
When the storage temperature is high, food spoils more easily.
It is said that absolute power inevitably corrupts.
en.notes: 腐敗 has two meanings: literally "rot, spoilage" of food or organic material, and figuratively "corruption, moral decay" of politics, organizations or society. As a する-verb it is intransitive: 食品が腐敗する, 権力は腐敗する. In everyday speech, for spoiled food one rather says 腐る; 汚職 denotes concrete cases of bribery, whereas 腐敗 is the state of a whole system (政治の腐敗).

examples[].german: The oral hearing is scheduled for next week.
In the closing argument, defense counsel pleaded for the defendant's innocence.
My younger sister won the high school speech contest.
en.notes: 弁論 is presenting and justifying a standpoint. In court, 口頭弁論 means "oral hearing" and 最終弁論 the defense's "closing argument"; the prosecution's counterpart is 論告. Outside court it is known from 弁論大会 "speech contest" and 弁論部 "debate club" at schools. 討論 and 議論 mean "discussion" among several people, 演説 a public "speech".

examples[].german: Policies to escape deflation are called for.
If deflation continues, it becomes hard for companies to grow their sales.
Japan has suffered from deflation for a long time.
en.notes: デフレーション is the long form; the short form デフレ is usual, e.g. in デフレ経済, デフレスパイラル and above all デフレから脱却する "to overcome deflation", a perennial theme of Japanese economic policy since the 1990s. Opposite: インフレーション／インフレ. Deflation is a price phenomenon and not the same as 不況 "recession", even though the two often occur together.

examples[].german: The telecommunications industry is in a state of oligopoly by a few companies.
The smartphone OS market is increasingly dominated by two companies.
In an oligopolistic market, price competition is unlikely to occur.
en.notes: 寡占 denotes a market dominated by a few large suppliers: an "oligopoly". Typical: 寡占状態, 寡占市場, 寡占化が進む; as a transitive する-verb 上位三社が市場を寡占する. To be distinguished from it is 独占 "monopoly" (a single supplier). The kanji 寡 means "few" as in 寡黙 "taciturn". Technical and news language.

examples[].german: As competition intensifies, small and weak companies are being weeded out.
Shops that cannot adapt to changing times will sooner or later be weeded out.
The giraffe's long neck is often explained as the result of natural selection.
en.notes: 淘汰 means that what is weak or useless is sorted out and only the capable remains. Mostly passive: 淘汰される "to be pushed out, weeded out", e.g. 市場から淘汰される; also 淘汰が進む. In biology there is 自然淘汰 "natural selection" (also 自然選択). The tone is sober and harsh; for dismissing individual employees one rather says 解雇 or リストラ.

examples[].german: Entry from other industries is intensifying competition in the industry.
A major IT company announced that it will enter the electric power business.
This industry has high barriers to entry, so new entry is difficult.
en.notes: 参入 is entry into a market or industry; an intransitive する-verb with に: 市場に参入する. Common: 新規参入 "new entry, new entrant", 参入障壁 "market entry barrier"; the opposite is 撤退する "to withdraw". Do not confuse it with 参加 "to take part" (in events) or 加入 "to join" (insurance, club). The old meaning "to appear at court" is rare today.

examples[].german: The policy is to wind up unprofitable divisions.
At this price it is not profitable, so we have no choice but to raise prices.
That restaurant serves cheap meals to local children, disregarding profit.
en.notes: 採算 is the calculation of whether something is financially worthwhile: "profitability". Almost always in set phrases: 採算が取れる／合う "to pay off", 採算が取れない／合わない, 採算を度外視して "without regard for profit", 不採算部門 "unprofitable division", 採算性. A pure profit amount would be 利益; 採算 emphasizes the balance of costs and returns. Neutral, also used orally in business.

examples[].german: Operating profit hit a record high.
Due to soaring raw material costs, operating profit fell by 20% from the previous year.
Sales grew, but with rising advertising costs operating profit was flat.
en.notes: 営業利益 is the profit from the core business: sales minus cost of goods sold (売上原価) and selling, general and administrative expenses (販売費及び一般管理費). In the Japanese income statement it follows 売上総利益 "gross profit" and comes before 経常利益 and 純利益. Common: 営業利益率 "operating margin", 営業利益が増える／減る; an operating loss is called 営業損失 or 営業赤字.

examples[].german: Net profit rose sharply, and the share price went up as well.
With the addition of gains from the sale of a factory, net profit doubled from the previous year.
Even if sales are strong, only a small net profit remains after paying taxes and interest.
en.notes: 純利益 is the profit left after deducting all costs, extraordinary items and taxes: "net profit, net income"; formally in full 当期純利益. In the news 最終利益 or 最終損益 is often used with the same meaning, and a loss is called 純損失 or 最終赤字. Colloquially, gross profit is spoken of as 粗利; 純利益 is the figure at the very bottom of the income statement.

examples[].german: Record the depreciation expense of the equipment.
Computers are generally depreciated over four years.
Even a fully depreciated machine can still be used well.
en.notes: 減価償却 is the accounting allocation of the acquisition cost of durable assets such as machines, buildings or vehicles over their useful life (耐用年数): "depreciation". Typical: 減価償却費 "depreciation expense", 減価償却する, 減価償却が終わる, 定額法／定率法 "straight-line／declining-balance method"; in everyday office speech often just 償却. Unlike 値下がり (price decline on the market), it is a purely accounting term.

examples[].german: Knowledge of double-entry bookkeeping is essential for accounting staff.
Thinking it would help in job hunting, I obtained a bookkeeping certificate.
Even for a small shop, it is useful to know the basics of bookkeeping.
en.notes: 簿記 is the technique or subject of bookkeeping, that is, the systematic recording of all business transactions. Typical: 複式簿記 "double-entry bookkeeping", 単式簿記, 簿記を習う／勉強する, 簿記の資格 or 簿記検定 (a very widespread professional qualification). The concrete keeping of books is rather 帳簿をつける. 会計 is accounting in general, 経理 bookkeeping as an activity or department in a company.

examples[].german: The prosecutor demanded a severe penalty in the closing argument.
The closing argument and sentencing request are scheduled for the next trial session.
In its closing argument, the prosecution pointed out that the defendant showed no sign of remorse.
en.notes: 論告 is the "prosecution's closing argument" in a criminal trial, in which it summarizes the evidence. It almost always occurs together with the sentencing request as 論告求刑. The defense's counterpart is 最終弁論. The word belongs to the technical language of the judiciary and court reporting and does not occur in everyday life.

examples[].german: The company's financial situation can be read from the balance sheet.
On the left side of the balance sheet, assets are listed; on the right, liabilities and net assets.
At closing time, I prepared the balance sheet and submitted it to the tax office.
en.notes: 貸借対照表 is a company's balance sheet as of a reporting date: on the left the assets (資産), on the right the liabilities (負債) and equity (純資産). In practice one often says バランスシート or just B/S. Together with 損益計算書 and キャッシュフロー計算書 it forms the 財務諸表 "financial statements". Typical: 貸借対照表を作成する, 貸借対照表に計上する. Technical language of accounting.

en.meaning: income statement; profit and loss statement
examples[].german: Analyze business performance based on the income statement.
Looking at the income statement, you can see that sales have increased but profit has decreased.
Whereas the balance sheet shows the financial position at a single point in time, the income statement shows the business results over a given period.
en.notes: 損益計算書 is the income statement (profit and loss statement), in practice also called P/L. For a period it shows sales, costs and the profit levels 売上総利益 → 営業利益 → 経常利益 → 当期純利益. Whereas 貸借対照表 shows the position at a reporting date, 損益計算書 describes the result of a period. Typical: 損益計算書を作成する／読む. Technical language of accounting.

examples[].german: Cash flow has worsened, and the company is facing a management crisis.
Because a business partner went bankrupt, payments are late and we are struggling with cash flow.
The president racks his brains every month over how to manage the cash flow.
en.notes: 資金繰り is the ongoing juggling of incoming and outgoing payments so that a firm stays solvent at all times: "liquidity planning, cash position". Typical: 資金繰りが苦しい／厳しい／悪化する, 資金繰りに困る, 資金繰りに行き詰まる (often a precursor to insolvency), 資金繰りをつける. 繰り comes from 繰る "to handle one after another" and is read ぐり here. To be distinguished from 資金調達, the raising of new capital.

examples[].german: He is busy running around raising funds for the new business.
The venture company succeeded in raising funds through crowdfunding.
Besides bank loans, issuing bonds is also one means of raising funds.
en.notes: 資金調達 is the procurement of capital, for example through bank loans (融資), new shares (増資), bonds (社債) or クラウドファンディング. Typical: 資金調達を行う, 資金調達に成功する／苦労する, 資金調達の手段. As a verb one usually says 資金を調達する. Unlike 資金繰り, which concerns ongoing solvency, this is about raising money for projects. Business and news language.

en.meaning: capital investment; investment in plant and equipment
examples[].german: Increase capital investment to expand production capacity.
Because the economic outlook is uncertain, many companies are holding back on capital investment.
As the factory has aged, large-scale capital investment has become unavoidable.
en.notes: 設備投資 is investment in physical assets such as factories, machines or IT systems: "capital investment". As 民間設備投資 (private capital investment) it is an important economic indicator. Typical: 設備投資を増やす／抑える／控える, 設備投資が活発になる, 設備投資額. 投資 alone also covers financial investments such as stocks; 研究開発投資 is spending on research and development.

examples[].german: Weak domestic demand is a drag on economic growth.
The government announced tax cuts to boost domestic demand.
Domestically oriented companies such as railways and retailers are hardly affected by a strong yen.
en.notes: 内需 is the short form of 国内需要, demand within the country through consumption and investment: "domestic demand". Typical: 内需拡大, 内需主導の成長, 内需が低迷する／回復する, 内需型企業 "companies oriented toward the domestic market". The counterpart is 外需 "foreign demand". A word of economic news and statistics.

examples[].german: A shift away from an economic structure dependent on external demand is called for.
With the slowdown in the global economy, external demand collapsed and the results of export companies worsened.
Growth in this period was supported more by external demand than by domestic demand.
en.notes: 外需 is demand from abroad, essentially for exports: "foreign demand". Typical: 外需依存, 外需頼み, 外需主導, 外需が落ち込む／伸びる; in GDP statistics 外需 denotes the contribution of net exports. The counterpart is 内需. Formal economic language.

examples[].german: Banks were nationalized during the financial crisis.
The government plans to temporarily nationalize the bankrupt power company.
In that country, the oil industry was first nationalized and later privatized again.
en.notes: 国有化 is the transfer of companies, land or resources into state ownership: "nationalization". As a transitive する-verb: 銀行を国有化する, passive 国有化される. The opposite is 民営化 "privatization". 国営 means "state-run" (国営企業), 国有 "state-owned" (国有地). Formal language from politics and economics.

examples[].german: Deregulation has created new business opportunities.
To increase the number of foreign tourists, the government is easing visa regulations.
Deregulation intensified competition, and airfares fell.
en.notes: 規制緩和 is composed of 規制 "regulation" and 緩和 "easing" and means the dismantling of government rules: "deregulation". Typical: 規制緩和を進める, 規制緩和によって, 規制緩和策; as a verb form one usually says 規制を緩和する. The opposite is 規制強化. A common buzzword in politics and economic news.

examples[].german: It is important to develop products with high added value.
We process local fruit into jam and sell it with added value.
In many European countries, the value-added tax rate is around twenty percent.
en.notes: 付加価値 is the value additionally added to a product or service: in economics "value added", in marketing "added value". Typical: 付加価値が高い, 高付加価値の製品, 付加価値を高める／つける. In tax terms: 付加価値税 "value-added tax"; in Japan the corresponding tax is called 消費税. Neutral, very common in business and advertising.

examples[].german: The prosecution sought ten years' imprisonment for the defendant.
The verdict was two years lighter than the sentence sought.
A fine of 500,000 yen was requested.
en.notes: 求刑 is the prosecution's "sentencing request": 被告に懲役〜年を求刑する, often as 論告求刑. The verdict is measured against it: 求刑通り "as requested", 求刑を上回る／下回る判決. The actual determination by the court is called 量刑. Since 2025, imprisonment is officially called 拘禁刑; in older texts one still reads 懲役 and 禁錮.

examples[].german: Policies adapted to each phase of the business cycle are necessary.
The construction industry is easily affected by the business cycle.
Seen from the business cycle, one can say that we have now entered the recovery phase.
en.notes: 景気循環 is the recurring alternation of upswing (好況) and downswing (不況) with phases such as 回復, 拡張 and 後退: "business cycle". Typical: 景気循環の局面, 景気循環の影響を受ける, 景気循環株 "cyclical stocks". 景気 alone is the current economic situation (景気がいい); 景気循環 emphasizes the ups and downs over years. Technical language of economics.

examples[].german: This year's economic growth rate is forecast at two percent.
During Japan's period of high economic growth, the growth rate sometimes exceeded ten percent a year.
The economic growth rate of emerging countries tends to be higher than that of developed countries.
en.notes: 経済成長率 is the percentage change in economic output, usually GDP compared with the previous year; one distinguishes 実質経済成長率 "real" and 名目経済成長率 "nominal". Typical: 経済成長率が鈍化する／プラスに転じる／マイナスになる, 経済成長率の見通しを上方修正／下方修正する. In context, the short 成長率 is often enough. News and technical language.

examples[].german: Gross domestic product rose only slightly compared with the previous year.
Gross domestic product is the total of the value added generated domestically in a given period.
In this island nation, tourism accounts for nearly half of gross domestic product.
en.notes: 国内総生産 is the official term for gross domestic product, that is, the value of all goods and services produced domestically. In news and conversation people almost always say GDP; one distinguishes 実質 "real" and 名目 "nominal". To be distinguished from it are 国民総生産 (GNP) and 国民総所得 (GNI), which measure the income of residents. Formal, rather written technical language.

examples[].german: It is necessary to formulate a long-term business strategy.
The new president thoroughly revised the business strategy right after taking office.
I majored in business strategy in graduate school and now work as a consultant.
en.notes: 経営戦略 is the long-term strategy with which a company wants to reach its goals and hold its own in competition. Typical: 経営戦略を立てる／策定する／見直す. 経営 means "business management"; related are 経営方針 "management policy" and 経営計画 "concrete business plan with figures". Also used as a field of study and consulting. Business language.

examples[].german: Spread risk through diversification of the business.
That railway company has diversified its business into real estate, department stores and more.
Diversification was pushed too hastily, the core business was neglected, and results worsened.
en.notes: 多角化 means that a company moves into new business fields: "diversification". Typical: 事業の多角化, 多角化経営, 多角化を進める／図る; as a する-verb 事業を多角化する. To be distinguished from it is 多様化 "variety, diversification" in general (価値観の多様化); spreading financial investments is called 分散投資. Business and news language.

examples[].german: Moves toward industry restructuring are accelerating.
Due to the declining birthrate, the city's elementary schools will be reorganized.
The new department head reorganized the sales department into three teams.
en.notes: 再編 is the reorganization of organizations, industries or systems: "restructuring, reorganization". As a transitive する-verb: 組織を再編する, passive 再編される. Typical: 業界再編, 組織再編, 政界再編, 再編が進む. Unlike リストラ, which mainly means job cuts, 再編 emphasizes putting units together anew, for example through mergers or consolidations.

en.meaning: spin-off into a subsidiary; company split
examples[].german: Improve management efficiency by spinning off business divisions into separate companies.
The company announced that it will spin off its game business next April.
Even after the spin-off, employees' salaries and treatment remained unchanged.
en.notes: 分社化 means separating a business division from the company and continuing it as an independent company, usually as a subsidiary: a "spin-off". As a する-verb: ゲーム事業を分社化する, passive 分社化される. To be distinguished from it is 子会社化, in which an existing firm is made a subsidiary through acquisition; 会社分割 is the legal technical term for the split. Business and news language.

examples[].german: Thousands were laid off in a large-scale restructuring.
My father was laid off at fifty in a round of job cuts and was forced to change jobs.
As rumors of layoffs spread, the mood inside the company has darkened.
en.notes: リストラ is the short form of リストラクチャリング "restructuring", but in Japanese it mainly means job cuts and layoffs. The firm リストラする (社員をリストラする); those affected are リストラされる or リストラにあう. It sounds softer and more everyday than 解雇 "dismissal" or, colloquially, クビ. For neutral reorganization without job cuts, one rather says 再編 or 構造改革.

examples[].german: Significant cost reductions were achieved by streamlining operations.
We digitized paper procedures and streamlined the office work.
He tried to rationalize his failure as "just bad luck".
en.notes: 合理化 means, in a business context, making processes more efficient and cheaper: "rationalization"; transitive する-verb: 業務を合理化する. Typical: 業務の合理化, 合理化を進める／図る, 合理化策; in the past often associated with job cuts. 効率化 "increasing efficiency" is very similar but more neutral. In psychology, 合理化 also means "to talk oneself into something, to justify" (自分の失敗を合理化する).

examples[].german: The transformation of the industrial structure is progressing.
The industrial structure of this town changed greatly after the coal mine closed.
Japan's industrial structure has shifted from being manufacturing-centered to service-centered.
en.notes: 産業構造 denotes the composition of an economy by its sectors, such as 第一次産業 (agriculture, fishing), 第二次産業 (industry) and 第三次産業 (services). Typical: 産業構造の転換／変化, 産業構造が変わる, 産業構造の高度化. In reference to a region one also speaks of 地域の産業構造. Technical language from economics and politics.

examples[].german: Lay judges take part in the sentencing decision.
The defense appealed, arguing the sentence was too heavy.
The reasons for the sentence were explained in detail in the written judgment.
en.notes: 量刑 is the "sentencing" by the court, i.e. the decision on the type and level of punishment. Typical: 量刑が重い／軽い, 量刑の判断, 量刑の理由, 量刑不当 "unreasonable sentence" as a ground for appeal. By contrast, 求刑 is the prosecution's request and 判決 the verdict as a whole. Since the introduction of lay judges 裁判員, the word is also frequently used in the news.

examples[].german: The automobile industry is one of Japan's key industries.
In this region, agriculture and fishing have long been the key industries.
The slump in the steel industry, the key industry, is affecting the economy of the whole town.
en.notes: 基幹産業 is an industry that forms the backbone of a national or regional economy: a "key industry". 基幹 means "mainstay, core" as in 基幹システム or 基幹病院. Typical: 〜の基幹産業, 地域の基幹産業, 基幹産業として発展する. 主要産業 "major industry" is similar but weaker; 成長産業 and 新興産業 are industries of the future. Formal language.

examples[].german: More and more companies are looking to move away from declining industries.
The once-thriving coal industry became a declining industry with the energy transition.
Even in an industry said to be in decline, survival is possible with ingenuity.
en.notes: 斜陽産業 literally means "industry of the setting sun" (斜陽 "evening sun") and denotes an industry in decline: a "shrinking industry". The image was popularized by the novel 『斜陽』 by 太宰治; also 斜陽化 "decline". The opposites are 成長産業 and 新興産業. The expression is judgmental and can sound disparaging to those affected; news and business language.

examples[].german: Emerging IT-related industries are contributing to job creation.
The government is putting effort into nurturing emerging industries.
The space business is one of the most closely watched emerging industries right now.
en.notes: 新興産業 are newly emerging, rapidly growing industries: an "emerging industry". 新興 means "newly arising, emerging" as in 新興国 "emerging country", 新興企業 "young company, start-up" or 新興住宅地 "new housing development". Typical: 新興産業の育成, 新興産業が台頭する. Closely related is 成長産業; the opposite is 斜陽産業. Formal economic language.

en.meaning: keiretsu; corporate group; series; sequence; affiliated (to a group)
examples[].german: The review of keiretsu relationships is progressing.
This restaurant is affiliated with that hotel, so the service is good.
If you arrange the data in time series, you can see the changes well.
en.notes: 系列 generally means "series, sequence, related line" (時系列 "time series"). In a business context it denotes the Japanese keiretsu: corporate groups linked by mutual shareholdings and fixed supplier relationships, for example a car maker and its suppliers. Very common in 系列会社, 系列店 "affiliated branch" and with television stations (〜系列の局 "station of the ... network"). Neutral; compare 関連会社 and グループ.

examples[].german: Companies are required to strengthen their compliance systems.
A compliance violation by a business partner came to light, and we terminated the contract.
Compliance is so strict on TV these days that you can't make programs like the old ones.
en.notes: コンプライアンス in Japanese companies mainly means 法令遵守 "observance of laws", in a wider sense also of rules, ethics and social norms. Typical combinations: コンプライアンスを徹底する "to enforce compliance thoroughly", コンプライアンス違反 "compliance violation", コンプライアンス研修, コンプライアンス意識. Colloquially it is shortened to コンプラ, for example when saying that television has to be more careful nowadays.

examples[].german: The improvement of corporate governance had a positive effect on the share price.
After a series of scandals, the company was criticized for governance that is not functioning.
Governance reforms are also being pushed forward at national universities.
en.notes: ガバナンス denotes the steering and control of an organization, not operational management (for that, 経営). It most often appears in コーポレートガバナンス, in Japanese 企業統治. Typical: ガバナンスを強化する "to strengthen governance", ガバナンスが効いている／機能している "oversight is working", ガバナンスの欠如 "lack of oversight". It is also applied to states, universities or IT (ITガバナンス).

examples[].german: The increase in exports contributed greatly to GDP growth.
This study contributed to the establishment of a new treatment.
I want to train people who can contribute to the development of the region.
en.notes: 寄与 means "contribution" and is almost always used as an intransitive する-verb with に: XがYに寄与する "X contributes to Y". It sounds literary and often appears with causes and factors (exports, research, measures). 貢献 is very similar but rather emphasizes the meritorious effort of people (社会に貢献する); in everyday speech one simply says 役に立つ. In statistics, 寄与度 is the "contribution to growth".

examples[].german: The multiplier effect of public investment is declining.
Some economists claim that public works have a larger multiplier effect than tax cuts.
Tourists' spending spreads through the entire regional economy via the multiplier effect.
en.notes: 乗数効果 (乗数 "multiplier" + 効果 "effect") is a concept of macroeconomics: additional spending, such as government investment, raises national income by a multiple. Typical are 乗数効果が大きい／小さい, 乗数効果が低下する and 財政支出の乗数効果. Do not confuse it with 相乗効果 "synergy effect", which is also used in everyday speech for things that reinforce each other.

examples[].german: An increase in disposable income leads to expanded consumption.
Due to higher social insurance burdens, the disposable income of young households is decreasing.
Even if salaries rise, if prices rise too, real disposable income does not increase.
en.notes: 可処分所得 literally means "income that one can dispose of" (可処分 "disposable"): income after deduction of taxes and social contributions. It is a technical word from statistics and economic policy; in everyday speech one talks of 手取り "take-home pay". Typical: 可処分所得が増える／減る／伸び悩む, 世帯の可処分所得, 実質可処分所得 "real disposable income".

examples[].german: The purchasing power of emerging countries is rising rapidly.
Because of the weak yen, the purchasing power of Japanese people abroad has fallen.
Compared by purchasing power parity, the difference in living standards between the two countries is not so large.
en.notes: 購買力 is the "purchasing power" of individuals, households or whole countries; 購買 is the formal word for "purchase". Typical: 購買力が高い／低い, 購買力が高まる／落ちる／低下する. The technical term 購買力平価 means "purchasing power parity". Do not confuse it with 購買意欲 "desire to buy": 購買力 is the ability, 購買意欲 the willingness.

examples[].german: The execution was carried out by order of the Minister of Justice.
A sentence with a suspended execution was handed down to the defendant.
The party's executive leadership resigned en masse after the election defeat.
en.notes: 執行 is the "enforcement" or "execution" of something legally or officially decided: 刑を執行する, 死刑の執行, 強制執行 "compulsory enforcement", 予算の執行. Very common is 執行猶予 "suspension of sentence". 執行部 also denotes the leadership of a party or union, 執行役員 a senior executive officer. 実行 is general "carrying out" of a plan, 実施 the "implementing" of a measure.

examples[].german: Pricing is done by analyzing the price elasticity of demand.
Build flexibility into the use of the budget.
This material has excellent elasticity, so you hardly tire even when sitting for a long time.
en.notes: 弾力性 is "elasticity" as a property: physically in materials, in economics as 価格弾力性 "price elasticity" or 所得弾力性, e.g. 需要の弾力性が大きい／小さい. Figuratively it means "leeway, flexibility" of rules or budgets (弾力性を持たせる); the adjective 弾力的 (弾力的に運用する) is more common for this. For mental flexibility one rather says 柔軟性.

examples[].german: Promote technological innovation to strengthen international competitiveness.
The strong yen reduced the price competitiveness of export companies.
For regional universities to survive, they need their own competitive strengths.
en.notes: 競争力 is the "competitiveness" of companies, products, countries or institutions. Typical combinations: 競争力がある／ない, 競争力を高める／強化する／失う, 競争力が低下する. Common compounds are 国際競争力 "international competitiveness" and 価格競争力 "price competitiveness"; attributively one says 競争力のある製品 "a competitive product".

examples[].german: Profit margins are falling because of excessive competition.
The convenience store industry has fallen into cutthroat competition.
Many shops were driven to close by cutthroat competition in a price-cutting war.
en.notes: 過当競争 is "excessive, ruinous competition" in which too many suppliers fight over the same market until hardly any of them make a profit. 過当 means "beyond the appropriate measure". Typical combinations are 過当競争に陥る, 過当競争が激化する and 過当競争を招く. The neutral 競争激化 only describes tougher competition, without the negative judgment "harmful". Business language.

examples[].german: Earnings worsened after being drawn into price competition.
Price competition over lunch boxes is intensifying in the convenience store industry.
Our company avoids price competition and aims to compete on quality.
en.notes: 価格競争 is competition on price, often in the sense of a "price war". Typical: 価格競争が激しい／激化する, 価格競争に巻き込まれる "to be drawn into a price war", 価格競争に陥る, 価格競争を避ける. More colloquial are 値下げ競争 and 安売り競争. Do not confuse it with 価格競争力 "price competitiveness".

examples[].german: Work out a sales strategy to expand market share.
The company boasts a domestic market share of about 40 percent.
Market share is falling year by year because of the entry of foreign manufacturers.
en.notes: 市場占有率 is the formal expression for "market share"; 市場 is read しじょう here (market in the economic sense), not いちば "marketplace". In the media and in companies, the loanword シェア (市場シェア) is now more common. Typical: 市場占有率が高い, 市場占有率を拡大する／伸ばす, 〜%の市場占有率を誇る "to boast a market share of ...".

examples[].german: There are few new companies because barriers to entry are high.
Deregulation lowered barriers to entry, and many start-ups were born.
The major companies use their patents as a weapon to build barriers to entry.
en.notes: 参入障壁 is composed of 参入 "market entry" and 障壁 "barrier" and denotes everything that makes it harder for new suppliers to enter: high initial investment, licenses, patents or strong brands. Typical: 参入障壁が高い／低い, 参入障壁を築く／設ける, 参入障壁を下げる／取り除く. Related is 新規参入 "new entrant, market entry".

examples[].german: Make use of economies of scale to reduce costs.
The larger the production volume, the more economies of scale come into play and the lower the cost per unit.
The two banks merged in pursuit of economies of scale.
en.notes: 規模の経済 translates "economies of scale": as production volume grows, unit costs fall. 経済 here means "economy, saving", not "the economy". Typical: 規模の経済が働く "economies of scale take effect", 規模の経済を活かす／追求する. In business language one often says the pseudo-loanword スケールメリット; the counterpart in theory is 範囲の経済 "economies of scope".

examples[].german: The effects of positive externalities from industrial clustering are recognized.
That land prices around a station rise when it is built is a typical example of a positive externality.
Pollution from factory smoke is not called a positive externality but a negative externality.
en.notes: 外部経済 is a technical term of economics: a positive side effect of economic activity that benefits third parties without their paying for it (e.g. rising land values because of a new station). The opposite, that is, negative effects such as environmental pollution, is called 外部不経済. The neutral umbrella term for both is 外部性 or 外部効果.

examples[].german: The economic levels of the individual countries tend to converge.
The discussion eventually converged on two proposals.
The similar body shapes of dolphins and fish are an example of convergent evolution.
en.notes: 収斂 is a literary word for "convergence, coming together", often also written 収れん. As an intransitive する-verb it takes に: Yに収斂する "to converge on Y, to settle on Y", e.g. for economic data, opinions or in biology (収斂進化 "convergent evolution"). The close synonym 収束 is more common in mathematics and everyday speech and also means "subsiding, containment" (感染の収束). In addition, 収斂 means "astringent" as in 収れん化粧水.

examples[].german: The income redistribution function should be strengthened.
Inequality is reduced to some extent by income redistribution through taxes and social security.
The ruling and opposition parties are at odds over the redistribution of wealth.
en.notes: 再分配 is the "redistribution" of income or wealth, usually through taxes and social benefits: 所得の再分配, 所得再分配, 富の再分配. It appears mainly as a noun, less often as 再分配する. The very similar 再配分 is also used, especially for the reallocation of resources or budgets (資源の再配分).

examples[].german: The man received a ten-day detention sentence for violating the Minor Offenses Act.
Detention is a short sentence of at least one day and under thirty days.
Detention is considered a lighter punishment than a fine.
en.notes: 拘留 is a separate, very light penalty in Japanese criminal law: detention of one to at most 29 days, for example for violations of the Minor Offenses Act 軽犯罪法 (拘留又は科料). It is regarded as milder than a fine 罰金. The identically read 勾留, by contrast, is pretrial detention of suspects; newspapers correctly write 勾留 for that, even though in everyday life the two are confused.

examples[].german: The progressive tax system contributes to correcting income inequality.
Since Japan's income tax is progressive, the higher the income, the higher the tax rate.
Calls for stronger progressive taxation of the wealthy are growing louder.
en.notes: 累進課税 consists of 累進 "rising step by step" and 課税 "taxation": the higher the income, the higher the tax rate. Typical combinations are 累進課税制度, 累進税率 and 累進課税を強化する. The opposite is a regressive effect (逆進性), in which low earners are burdened proportionally more; a uniform rate is called 比例税 or 一律の税率.

examples[].german: There is criticism that the consumption tax is regressive.
A reduced tax rate is applied to food to ease regressivity.
The tobacco tax places a larger share of the burden on low-income earners and is said to be strongly regressive.
en.notes: 逆進性 (逆進 "advancing in reverse" + 性 "-ity") describes the regressive effect of a levy: low earners bear a higher burden in proportion to their income. The word comes up mainly in the debate on the consumption tax: 消費税の逆進性, 逆進性がある／強い, 逆進性を緩和する "to ease the regressive effect". The opposite is 累進性 "progressivity".

examples[].german: Make investment decisions after scrutinizing the financial statements.
Listed companies are obliged to publish their financial statements.
If you know how to read financial statements, you can tell the health of a company.
en.notes: 財務諸表 (諸表 "the various statements") is the collective term for a company's financial reports, above all 貸借対照表 "balance sheet", 損益計算書 "income statement" and キャッシュ・フロー計算書. Typical: 財務諸表を作成する／開示する／公表する／分析する, 財務諸表を読む. In everyday speech one also says 決算書.

examples[].german: The decline in the equity ratio is increasing management risk.
Banks must secure a certain amount of equity.
It is difficult to finance capital investment with equity alone.
en.notes: 自己資本 is "equity" as opposed to 他人資本 "borrowed capital" (i.e. 負債, debt). Very common are the compounds 自己資本比率 "equity ratio" and 自己資本利益率 "return on equity (ROE)". On the balance sheet, the corresponding item is now usually called 純資産 "net assets".

examples[].german: Dependence on borrowed capital is too high.
Equity and borrowed capital together are called total capital.
Bank loans count as borrowed capital.
en.notes: 他人資本 is a term from bookkeeping and business administration: "borrowed capital", that is, money a company has received from third parties and must repay (loans, bonds, liabilities). The counterpart is 自己資本 ("equity"); together the two make up 総資本. On balance sheets it is mostly called 負債. 他人 has nothing personal here, but means "from outside".

examples[].german: Increase current assets to secure short-term solvency.
Cash, accounts receivable and inventory are included in current assets.
Current assets greatly exceed current liabilities, and the finances are stable.
en.notes: 流動資産 are "current assets": assets that turn into cash within a year, such as 現金, 預金, 売掛金 "receivables" and 在庫 "inventory". The counterpart is 固定資産 "fixed assets". For liquidity analysis they are compared with 流動負債; the ratio of the two is called 流動比率.

examples[].german: The appraised value of the fixed assets was reviewed.
When you buy a house, you have to pay fixed asset tax every year.
A factory's machinery and land are recorded as fixed assets.
en.notes: 固定資産 are "fixed assets": assets used over the long term, such as 土地 "land", 建物 and 機械 (有形固定資産) as well as software or patents (無形固定資産). The counterpart is 流動資産. Even outside bookkeeping, every homeowner knows the word from 固定資産税, the annual "property tax".

examples[].german: The repayment deadline for the current liabilities is approaching.
Accounts payable and short-term loans are classified as current liabilities.
If current liabilities exceed current assets, cash flow may become difficult.
en.notes: 流動負債 are "current liabilities", that is, debts that fall due within a year: 買掛金 "accounts payable", 短期借入金 "short-term loans", 未払金. The counterpart is 固定負債. If they exceed 流動資産, a bottleneck in 資金繰り "cash flow management" threatens.

examples[].german: Reduce long-term liabilities to improve the financial structure.
Bonds and long-term loans count as long-term liabilities.
Because the construction funds for the new factory were raised through long-term borrowing, long-term liabilities have swelled.
en.notes: 固定負債 are "long-term liabilities" that fall due only after more than a year, e.g. 社債 "bonds", 長期借入金 "long-term loans" or pension provisions. The counterpart is 流動負債. Typical: 固定負債が膨らむ／増える, 固定負債を減らす.

examples[].german: Disclose the performance of the entire group in consolidated financial statements.
In the company's consolidated results for the current term, net profit hit a record high.
It is in the red on a standalone basis, but it secured a profit in the consolidated results.
en.notes: 連結決算 are the "consolidated financial statements" that present parent and subsidiary companies (連結子会社) as one unit. The counterpart is 単体決算 or 個別決算 "standalone statements". In business news one often reads 連結決算で過去最高益 "record profit in the consolidated results". 決算 alone means "closing of accounts, financial statements".

examples[].german: Unjust physical restraint is a violation of human rights.
This job has long bound hours when travel is included.
The police took into custody the man who was at the scene.
en.notes: 拘束 means "restraint, restriction of freedom", in a broader sense "binding". With the police: 身柄を拘束する "to take into custody", which need not yet be a formal arrest 逮捕. In working life, 拘束時間 is the time one is tied up including breaks and commuting; 法的拘束力 means "legally binding force". 束縛 means rather personal constraint, for example in a relationship.

examples[].german: Companies' retained earnings hit a new record high.
The labor union demanded that retained earnings be used for wage increases.
Many companies build up their retained earnings to prepare for a recession.
en.notes: 内部留保 are the "retained earnings" kept within the company, not paid out as dividends. The word is politically charged: companies are criticized for 内部留保をため込む "hoarding reserves" instead of using them for wages or investment (賃上げに回す). Other combinations: 内部留保を厚くする "to build up", 内部留保を取り崩す "to draw down".

examples[].german: The unrealized gains on held shares increased significantly.
Because share prices rose, the shares I hold show an unrealized gain of 100,000 yen.
I sold while I still had an unrealized gain and locked in the profit.
en.notes: 含み益 (含み "what is contained, hidden" + 益 "profit") is the paper gain on stocks, real estate etc. whose market value is above the purchase price while one has not yet sold them. Typical: 含み益が出る／膨らむ, 含み益を抱える; it is realized by selling (利益を確定する). The opposite is 含み損. Companies use the word just as private investors do.

examples[].german: Unrealized losses on real estate are weighing on management.
The shares I bought have fallen in price, and I am sitting on an unrealized loss.
Before the unrealized loss grew further, I made up my mind and cut my losses.
en.notes: 含み損 is the "paper loss": the market value of held shares or real estate is below the purchase price, but the loss has not yet been realized by selling. Typical: 含み損を抱える "to sit on paper losses", 含み損が膨らむ, 含み損が経営を圧迫する. Someone who sells at a loss to avoid worse does 損切り. The opposite is 含み益.

examples[].german: The allowance for doubtful accounts was increased.
A bonus provision was recorded in preparation for the summer bonus.
Since losing in court is likely, a provision was set aside against the loss.
en.notes: 引当金 is a "provision" on the balance sheet for future expenses or losses that are already foreseeable. Common types: 貸倒引当金 "for bad debts", 退職給付引当金 "for pensions", 賞与引当金 "for bonuses". Typical verbs: 引当金を計上する／積む／積み増す "to set up, to increase" and 引当金を取り崩す "to release". In bookkeeping it is written without okurigana, although the verb is 引き当てる.

examples[].german: Accelerate the write-off of non-performing loans.
Computers are depreciated over four years.
One month's worth of the deposit is retained, so it is not returned when you move out.
en.notes: 償却 is a transitive する-verb of bookkeeping: "to depreciate" (spread the loss in value of assets over the years, mostly as 減価償却) and "to write off" (不良債権を償却する "to write off bad loans"). The meaning "redemption, repayment" also exists, but for bonds one usually says 償還. In everyday life one meets the word in rental contracts: 敷金償却 is the part of the deposit that is not refunded.

examples[].german: The amount recorded as an extraordinary loss is enormous.
The company posted a loss for the third consecutive term.
The construction cost of the new library was included in next year's budget.
en.notes: 計上 means "to enter an amount in the accounts, to book, to report" and is a transitive する-verb. Typical patterns: XをYとして計上する "to book X as Y", 赤字／利益／損失を計上する "to report a loss/profit", 予算に計上する "to include in the budget". It is very often used in the passive (計上される). For private household account books, one says 家計簿につける instead.

examples[].german: The rules on timely disclosure must be observed.
I asked the hospital for disclosure of my medical records.
The company should promptly disclose information about the accident.
en.notes: 開示 is the "disclosure" of information or documents, mostly to those entitled to it or on the basis of an obligation: 情報を開示する, 情報開示, 決算を開示する, 適時開示 "timely disclosure". With 開示請求 one requests access, for example to one's own personal data or government records. 公開 generally means "make public", 公表 "announce publicly"; 開示 emphasizes releasing information that had been withheld until then.

examples[].german: Trade secrets are protected by the Unfair Competition Prevention Act.
Selling goods that imitate the logo of a famous brand constitutes unfair competition.
Acquiring a domain name similar to another company's trademark can also constitute unfair competition.
en.notes: 不正競争 (不正 "illegitimate" + 競争 "competition") is a legal term and appears mostly in 不正競争防止法 "Unfair Competition Prevention Act" or 不正競争行為. It covers, for example, the theft of trade secrets, imitation of well-known brands or misleading labeling. To be distinguished from 過当競争 "excessive (but legal) competition"; the opposite is 公正な競争.

examples[].german: The protection of intellectual property rights has become an international issue.
To protect our intellectual property, we file patents for all new technologies.
Using other people's works without permission can be an infringement of intellectual property.
en.notes: 知的財産 (知的 "intellectual" + 財産 "property, assets") is "intellectual property"; in companies and the media it is often abbreviated to 知財 (知財部 "patent department"). The rights to it are called 知的財産権, e.g. 特許権, 著作権 and 商標権. Typical: 知的財産を守る／保護する／侵害する, 知的財産戦略.

examples[].german: The judge ordered the suspect's detention.
The prosecution requested an extension of the detention.
The suspect was indicted the day before the detention deadline.
en.notes: 勾留 is the "pretrial detention" a judge orders for suspects or defendants. After the arrest 逮捕 (at most 72 hours), ten days follow at first, which can be extended by another ten: 勾留延長, 勾留期限. It is mostly used in the passive (勾留される) or as a noun. Do not confuse it with the identically read 拘留, a short prison sentence.

examples[].german: Fiscal stimulus during a recession phase is being discussed.
Concern is spreading that the US economy will fall into a recession.
Because of the downturn, job offers decreased and job hunting became harder.
en.notes: 景気後退 (景気 "economy" + 後退 "decline") is an "economic downturn" or "recession", that is, a phase. Typical: 景気後退に陥る／入る, 景気後退局面, 景気後退の懸念 "recession worries". The loanword リセッション is synonymous; 不況 and colloquially 不景気 describe more the state of the slump. Opposites: 景気回復 "recovery", 景気拡大 "expansion".

examples[].german: Large-scale economic stimulus measures were announced.
The government is considering a stimulus package centered on tax cuts.
There is also criticism that the effect of stimulus measures is only temporary.
en.notes: 景気刺激策 (景気 "economy" + 刺激 "stimulus" + 策 "measure") is an "economic stimulus program", for example tax cuts, public works or cash payments to citizens. Typical verbs: 景気刺激策を打ち出す "to announce", 講じる "to take", 実施する. In Japanese news such a package is often called, more neutrally, 経済対策, e.g. 総合経済対策.

examples[].german: Large-scale monetary easing supported the economic recovery.
The Bank of Japan maintained its policy of continuing monetary easing.
Monetary easing weakened the yen, and the prices of imported goods rose.
en.notes: 金融緩和 is "monetary easing": the central bank lowers interest rates or increases the money supply to stimulate the economy. Typical: 金融緩和を行う／続ける／拡大する／縮小する, 金融緩和策, 大規模金融緩和. The opposite is 金融引き締め; a special form is 量的緩和. 緩和 alone means "easing", cf. 規制緩和 "deregulation".

examples[].german: Monetary tightening was carried out as a measure against inflation.
Monetary tightening raised mortgage interest rates, and fewer people bought homes.
Markets are wary that abrupt monetary tightening will cool the economy.
en.notes: 金融引き締め is "monetary tightening", usually through interest rate hikes (利上げ) or a reduction of the money supply, in order to curb inflation. Typical: 金融引き締めに転じる "to switch to", 金融引き締めに踏み切る, 金融引き締めを強化する. The verb behind it is 引き締める "to tighten, to draw tight" (also 気を引き締める "to pull oneself together"); in official texts also written 金融引締め. Opposite: 金融緩和.

examples[].german: The central bank indicated its intention to continue its quantitative easing policy.
In 2001, Japan became the first country in the world to introduce quantitative easing.
When quantitative easing began to be scaled back, stock prices fell sharply.
en.notes: 量的緩和 is "quantitative easing": the central bank buys government bonds and other securities on a large scale to increase the money supply when interest rate cuts are no longer possible. Typical: 量的緩和を導入する／拡大する／縮小する／終了する. From 2013, the Bank of Japan pursued the so-called 量的・質的金融緩和. 金融緩和 is the umbrella term; the winding down is called 量的緩和の縮小 or テーパリング.

examples[].german: The raising of the official discount rate affected the market.
The cut in the discount rate made it easier for companies to borrow funds.
In 2006, the official discount rate was renamed "the basic discount rate and basic loan rate".
en.notes: 公定歩合 was for a long time the most important policy interest rate of the Bank of Japan, at which it lent money to banks. Since 2006 it has officially been called 基準割引率および基準貸付利率, and the policy rate target is now a different rate; the word is therefore found mainly in historical contexts or older texts. 歩合 means "rate, percentage" (also 歩合制 "commission basis"). Typical: 公定歩合を引き上げる／引き下げる.

examples[].german: The negative interest rate policy is squeezing banks' earnings.
The Bank of Japan introduced negative interest rates in 2016 and lifted them in 2024.
Because of negative interest rates, mortgage rates fell to record lows.
en.notes: マイナス金利 (マイナス "minus" + 金利 "interest") is the "negative interest rate": banks pay interest on deposits at the central bank instead of receiving it. The Bank of Japan introduced the マイナス金利政策 in 2016 and ended it in 2024. Typical: マイナス金利を導入する／解除する, マイナス金利の影響. Related: ゼロ金利 "zero interest rate".

en.meaning: fiscal stimulus; expansion of government spending
examples[].german: Support the economy through large-scale fiscal stimulus.
While some call for fiscal stimulus, others worry about a growing budget deficit.
For reconstruction after the disaster, the government went ahead with fiscal stimulus on an unprecedented scale.
en.notes: 財政出動 denotes the use of additional government spending to support the economy, for example through public works or subsidies. 出動 actually means "to turn out" (like the fire brigade or troops) and sounds like an emergency deployment. Typical: 財政出動を行う／求める, 大規模な財政出動, 財政出動に踏み切る. Opposites are 財政再建 "fiscal consolidation" and 緊縮財政 "austerity"; government spending in general is called 財政支出.

examples[].german: Corporate tax revenue increased significantly.
Thanks to the economic recovery, the state's tax revenue hit a record.
In towns with a shrinking population, the shortage of tax revenue is serious.
en.notes: 税収 is "tax revenue" from the point of view of the state or a municipality; what a citizen pays, on the other hand, is 税金. Typical: 税収が増える／減る／落ち込む, 税収が過去最高を更新する, 税収不足 "tax shortfall", 法人税収. Total government revenue including borrowing is called 歳入.

examples[].german: The massive issuance of government bonds is one cause of worsening public finances.
Government bonds for individuals are a safe investment with no worry of losing principal.
The yield on long-term government bonds rose.
en.notes: 国債 is the "government bond" of the central government and, in a wider sense, the national debt. Typical: 国債を発行する／購入する／償還する, 赤字国債 "deficit bonds", 国債の利回り "yield", 個人向け国債 "government bonds for individual investors". Careful when listening: it sounds exactly like 国際 "international". 公債 is the umbrella term that also includes local government bonds (地方債).

examples[].german: The defense counsel applied for bail.
He paid the bail and was released.
The court did not grant bail, citing a risk of flight.
en.notes: 保釈 is "release on bail"; in Japan it is possible only after indictment 起訴, not during the pretrial detention before it. Typical: 保釈を請求する, 保釈を認める／却下する, 保釈金 "bail money", 保釈中 "out on bail", 被告が保釈される. General "releasing" is 釈放, early release from prison is 仮釈放.

examples[].german: The outstanding balance of public bonds reached a record high.
More than 30 percent of next year's budget depends on public bonds.
As debt service costs grow, the money available for other policies is shrinking.
en.notes: 公債 is the umbrella term for "public bonds" or public debt: government bonds (国債) and local government bonds (地方債). The word is common mainly in budget and statistics terms: 公債残高 "outstanding debt", 公債依存度 "share of debt financing in the budget", 公債費 "debt service". In everyday speech one rather says 国債 or simply 国の借金.

examples[].german: Funds for capital investment were raised by issuing corporate bonds.
Unlike stocks, with corporate bonds the principal is returned at maturity.
Due to worsening results, the rating of that company's bonds was lowered.
en.notes: 社債 is a "corporate bond": a company borrows money from investors and repays it with interest. Unlike 株式 "shares", it is debt capital. Typical: 社債を発行する／引き受ける／償還する, 社債の格付け "rating", 転換社債 "convertible bond". Compare 国債 (state) and 地方債 (local governments).

examples[].german: The dishonoring of the bills triggered a chain of bankruptcies.
We issued a promissory note to our business partner.
As a souvenir, I received a yokozuna's handprint.
en.notes: 手形 is above all a "bill of exchange": 約束手形 (promissory note) and 為替手形 (draft). One says 手形を振り出す "to issue", 手形を割り引く "to discount"; if it is not honored, this is called 不渡り, which often means the end for companies. In Japan, paper bills are increasingly being replaced by electronic procedures. Literally, 手形 is also a "handprint", such as the signed handprints of sumo wrestlers. 空手形 figuratively means "empty promise".

examples[].german: I wrote a check and paid the amount with it.
I cashed the check I received at the bank.
In Japan, individuals almost never use checks.
en.notes: 小切手 is the "check"; it is read こぎって with a voiced ぎ, not to be confused with 切手 "postage stamp". Writing a check is colloquially 小切手を切る, formally 小切手を振り出す; cashing it is 小切手を現金化する or 現金に換える. In Japan, individuals hardly use checks, but they still occur in business dealings.

examples[].german: Large profits were made by trading securities.
Listed companies must submit a securities report every year.
Banks invest part of their surplus funds in securities.
en.notes: 有価証券 (有価 "having value" + 証券 "certificate, instrument") is the legal and accounting term for "securities" such as stocks, bonds and investment fund units. Very common is 有価証券報告書, the mandatory annual report of listed companies (short 有報). Typical: 有価証券を保有する／売却する, 有価証券の売買. In everyday speech one rather says 株 or 証券.

examples[].german: Hedge risk with futures trading.
The price of crude oil futures soared more than 5 percent in a single day.
That team succeeded by betting early on unknown young players.
en.notes: 先物 (先 "future" + 物 "goods") denotes "futures": buying or selling at a price fixed today for a later date. Typical: 先物取引, 先物市場, 原油先物, 日経平均先物. The opposite is 現物 "spot goods". Figuratively, 先物買い means "betting early on future potential", for example on young talents.

examples[].german: I entrust my assets to a trust bank and have it manage them.
I put 10,000 yen into an investment trust every month.
A government that received the people's mandate in the election has a responsibility to live up to it.
en.notes: 信託 (信 "trust" + 託 "to entrust") is a "trust": assets are transferred to someone for management for the benefit of a beneficiary. Common in compounds: 信託銀行 "trust bank", 投資信託 (short 投信) "investment fund", 家族信託. As a transitive する-verb (XをYに信託する) it is very formal; in everyday speech one says 預ける or 任せる. Politically, 国民の信託 stands for the "mandate of the people".

examples[].german: The securities firm handled the underwriting of the corporate bonds.
For the management turnaround, the business partner's bank became the subscriber of the new shares.
At the post office counter, parcels are accepted until 7 p.m.
en.notes: 引受 is the noun of 引き受ける "to take over, to take on". In finance, it denotes the taking over of a securities issue by a bank or securities firm (underwriting): 引受業務, 引受手数料, 引受先 "taker (e.g. of the new shares in a capital increase)". Further technical meanings are the acceptance of a bill of exchange (手形の引受) and the acceptance of postal items (郵便物の引受). In everyday writing it is mostly 引き受け with okurigana; the short spelling 引受 is typical of technical language, forms and compounds.

examples[].german: Funds were raised through the issuance of new shares.
Could you issue me a receipt, please?
This magazine is published on the tenth of every month.
en.notes: 発行 is a transitive する-verb: 株式・社債・紙幣を発行する "to issue, to float", but also 領収書・パスポート・証明書を発行する "to issue (a document)" and 雑誌・新聞を発行する "to publish". In the passive one says 新株が発行される. For books, 出版 "to publish" is more usual; 発行 emphasizes the formal act of issuing, for example with magazines and documents. Not to be confused with the identically read 発効 "coming into force" and 発酵 "fermentation".

examples[].german: The spread of electronic payment is progressing.
I paid the amount by credit card.
We have to complete settlement with our business partners by the end of the month.
en.notes: 決済 means the settling of a payment or the processing of a transaction; as a transitive する-verb: 代金をカードで決済する. Typical compounds are 電子決済, キャッシュレス決済, スマホ決済, 決済手段 and 決済日. In everyday speech one usually says simply 払う or 支払い; 決済 sounds more technical and is common in online shops and in business. Beware of the homophone 決裁 "approval by a superior" (部長の決裁を仰ぐ).

examples[].german: Parole was granted for his model-prisoner conduct.
Even those serving life sentences may be paroled if they meet the conditions.
The man committed another crime while on parole.
en.notes: 仮釈放 is the early "conditional release" of a prisoner under conditions and supervision; in the news it is also called 仮出所. It is mostly used in the passive or as a noun: 仮釈放される, 仮釈放が認められる, 仮釈放中. Do not confuse it with 保釈 "release on bail" before the verdict, or with 執行猶予, where one does not have to go to prison at all. 釈放 alone is the general "release".

examples[].german: Sudden fluctuations in the exchange rate are affecting corporate performance.
Before exchanging money, I checked today's exchange rate.
The exchange rate at banks in the city is better than at the airport.
en.notes: 為替レート is the everyday expression for the exchange rate; in news and technical texts one also hears 為替相場 or, specifically, 円相場. 為替 alone means "foreign exchange, money transfer" and has the irregular reading かわせ. Typical combinations: 為替レートが変動する, 為替レートを確認する, 有利な為替レートで両替する. A rising yen is called 円高, a falling one 円安.

examples[].german: Commemorative coins are produced at the mint.
At the mint in Osaka, a cherry blossom walk-through is held every spring.
Japan's minting technology is highly regarded for its protection against counterfeiting.
en.notes: 造幣 means the minting or production of coin money and occurs almost only in compounds, above all in 造幣局, Japan's state mint, based in Osaka. Other combinations are 造幣技術 and 造幣事業. Banknotes are not printed by the 造幣局 but by the 国立印刷局. The word is literary; in everyday speech one rather says 硬貨を作る or 貨幣の製造.

examples[].german: The yield on government bonds hit a record low.
The yield on this investment fund is about three percent a year.
It is dangerous to choose a product based only on the height of its yield.
en.notes: 利回り is the yield, that is, the annual return in relation to the capital invested, usually in percent: 利回りが高い・低い, 利回りが上昇する, 配当利回り "dividend yield", 国債の利回り. To be distinguished from it are 金利 or 利率 "interest rate" and 利息・利子 "interest as an amount". For bonds, price and 利回り move in opposite directions. The spelling with okurigana り is standard.

examples[].german: The investment results of the pension fund have worsened.
Rules should be applied flexibly depending on the situation.
The new system goes into operation next month.
en.notes: 運用 means to put something to practical use and handle it; as a transitive する-verb: 資金・資産を運用する "to invest and manage money", 規則・法律を運用する "to apply, implement rules" and システムを運用する "to operate a system". To be distinguished from it are 利用 "to use", 適用 "to apply a rule to a case" and 応用 "to transfer knowledge to something new". Common in 資産運用, 運用成績 and 運用開始.

examples[].german: Risk management in derivatives trading is important.
Some banks have suffered huge losses on derivatives.
It is said to be dangerous for individual investors to get involved in derivatives.
en.notes: デリバティブ are financial products whose value is derived from an underlying asset such as stocks, interest rates or currencies; the Japanese technical term is 金融派生商品. Typical combinations: デリバティブ取引, デリバティブ商品, デリバティブで損失を出す. Derivatives include 先物 "futures", オプション and スワップ, among others. The word belongs to business and news language.

examples[].german: Stock options are granted to executives.
The car navigation system is an option and costs extra.
I bought put options to hedge against falling share prices.
en.notes: オプション has two areas of use. In everyday life it is an extra that can be chosen for an additional charge, for example on cars or trips: オプションで付ける, オプション料金, オプショナルツアー. In finance it is the right to buy or sell an underlying asset at a fixed price: コールオプション, プットオプション, ストックオプション, オプション取引. For "choice, alternative" in the general sense one usually says 選択肢.

examples[].german: Avoid the risk of floating interest rates through an interest rate swap.
The central banks of both countries concluded a currency swap agreement.
By swapping floating rates for fixed rates, payment amounts were stabilized.
en.notes: スワップ is in finance an exchange transaction in which two parties swap payment streams: 金利スワップ "interest rate swap", 通貨スワップ "currency swap" (also as an agreement between central banks). As a する-verb: 変動金利を固定金利にスワップする. In foreign exchange trading one also knows the スワップポイント (interest rate differential). For ordinary "swapping" in everyday life, one says 交換する or 取り替える, not スワップ.

examples[].german: Use futures trading to hedge exchange rate risk.
I chose an investment fund with currency hedging.
As a hedge against risk, we have contracts with multiple suppliers.
en.notes: ヘッジ is protection against the risk of loss; as a transitive する-verb: 為替リスクをヘッジする. Common combinations are 為替ヘッジ, ヘッジ付き "currency-hedged" and ヘッジファンド. In business Japanese, リスクヘッジ has also become established in the general sense of "precaution against risks", for example with suppliers or personnel. For funds one distinguishes 為替ヘッジあり "with currency hedging" and 為替ヘッジなし "without".

examples[].german: Arbitrage trades exploiting price differences between markets are being carried out.
Price differences are quickly eliminated by arbitrage.
High-speed computer-driven arbitrage is increasing.
en.notes: 裁定取引 is arbitrage: one exploits price differences of the same good between markets by buying cheap and selling dear at the same time. 裁定 actually means "decision, arbitral ruling"; an arbitration proceeding in the legal sense, however, is called 仲裁. In stock exchange jargon one also hears アービトラージ or the shortened 裁定, e.g. 裁定買い・裁定売り. The word is technical language.

examples[].german: The prime minister took command of the disaster response.
The manager's tactics paid off brilliantly, and the team won a comeback victory.
Mother ran all the wedding preparations.
en.notes: 采配 was originally the tasseled baton with which a commander directed his troops; from this came the meaning "direction, command". It almost always appears in the phrase 采配を振る or 采配を振るう ("to take command, pull the strings"). It is very common in sports for a coach's decisions: 監督の采配, 采配ミス, 采配が当たる. Somewhat elevated, but also used jokingly in everyday life.

examples[].german: An amnesty was implemented upon the emperor's accession.
He was released from prison after receiving a pardon.
Some criticize that pardons run counter to the separation of powers.
en.notes: 恩赦 is the umbrella term for "pardon" and "amnesty" by the executive: in Japan the cabinet decides and the emperor attests. Types are 大赦 (amnesty for whole groups of offenses), 特赦 (pardon of individuals), 減刑, 刑の執行の免除 and 復権. Typical: 恩赦を受ける, 恩赦が実施される, 恩赦で釈放される. General amnesties are often granted on state occasions such as an accession to the throne; critics see this as an interference with the judiciary.

examples[].german: Losses from margin trading are mounting.
With margin trading, you can trade up to about three times your own capital.
Beginners should not start margin trading right away.
en.notes: 信用取引 is securities trading on credit: one deposits collateral with the broker (委託保証金) and borrows money or shares in order to trade more than one's own capital allows. Buying on credit is 信用買い, short selling 信用売り or 空売り; if the price falls sharply, a 追証 "margin call" threatens. In contrast stands 現物取引 "cash trading with one's own money". The general term "credit transaction" outside the stock market is rather 掛け取引.

examples[].german: Short-selling restrictions prevented a sharp fall in share prices.
Expecting the price to fall, he sold the stock short.
You lose on a short sale when the share price rises contrary to expectations.
en.notes: 空売り (read から, not くう) is "short selling": one sells borrowed shares in the expectation of falling prices and buys them back more cheaply later (買い戻し). As a する-verb the security takes を: 株を空売りする. Common combinations: 空売り規制, 空売り比率, 空売りを仕掛ける. The counterpart is 空買い. A technical word from the stock market and business news.

examples[].german: Price manipulation by speculators has become a problem.
A fierce speculative battle was fought between the two groups.
In Noh, the role of the protagonist is called shite.
en.notes: 仕手 literally means "the one who acts". On the stock exchange it denotes big speculators who deliberately move individual share prices with a lot of capital; mostly in compounds such as 仕手筋 "speculator circles", 仕手株 and 仕手戦 "speculative battle". In Noh theater, 仕手 is the main role, usually written in katakana シテ; the supporting role is called ワキ. The stock market sense has a negative tint and belongs to the business press.

examples[].german: Market manipulation is prohibited under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act.
The surveillance commission filed a criminal complaint against an individual investor on suspicion of market manipulation.
Moving the share price with fake large orders also constitutes market manipulation.
en.notes: 相場操縦 is the legal technical term for market manipulation, that is, artificially influencing prices, for example through fake orders or collusive trades; 相場 "market price, quotation" + 操縦 "to steer". It is prohibited under the 金融商品取引法 (until 2007, the 証券取引法). In the press and in everyday speech 株価操作 is more common. Spreading false rumors to influence prices is legally a separate offense called 風説の流布.

examples[].german: Prosecution of insider trading is being stepped up.
Trading your own company's shares using undisclosed information constitutes insider trading.
A former executive was arrested on suspicion of insider trading.
en.notes: インサイダー取引 is trading in securities by exploiting non-public company information (未公表の重要事実); the statute speaks of 内部者取引. Typical combinations: インサイダー取引の疑いで逮捕される, インサイダー取引を摘発する, インサイダー取引規制. In Japan it is also punishable to pass such information on to others in order to encourage them to trade.

examples[].german: It has become one of the world's top companies by market capitalization.
Market capitalization is calculated by multiplying the share price by the number of issued shares.
Because of the sharp fall in share prices, market capitalization shrank by one trillion yen in a single day.
en.notes: 時価総額 is the market capitalization or market value of a company: share price x number of issued shares. 時価 means "current market price" (on a sushi restaurant menu also "market price of the day"), 総額 "total amount". Typical are 時価総額ランキング, 時価総額が〜兆円に達する and 時価総額で世界一. The term is also used for entire markets, e.g. 東証の時価総額.

examples[].german: The stock index hit a new year-to-date high.
TOPIX is one of the leading stock indexes of Japan.
I save into a fund tracking a stock index every month.
en.notes: 株価指数 is a "stock index" that summarizes the price movement of many shares in a single number. The best known in Japan are 日経平均株価 and TOPIX (東証株価指数). Typical verbs: 株価指数が上昇する/下落する, 高値を更新する; 株価指数に連動する means "tracking an index" (index fund). 指数 alone also means "index" in general (物価指数) or, in mathematics, "exponent".

en.meaning: trading volume; yield, harvest amount; output (piecework)
examples[].german: Trading volume surged, indicating a lively market.
Thanks to good weather this year, the rice harvest exceeded the average year.
In this factory, wages are paid by piecework.
en.notes: 出来高 is the quantity actually achieved: on the stock exchange the trading volume, that is, the number of shares traded (出来高が増える・膨らむ・細る), in agriculture the harvest amount (米の出来高). With 払い or 制 it denotes performance-based or piece-rate pay: 出来高払い, 出来高制. To be distinguished from trading volume is 売買代金, the turnover in money.

examples[].german: The movement of high-priced stocks has a large influence on the index.
With high-priced stocks, even a single trading unit can cost several million yen.
Today high-priced stocks were bought, pushing up the Nikkei average.
en.notes: 値嵩株 are shares with a high price per unit; 値 "price" + 嵩 "bulk, volume" (cf. 値が嵩む "to become expensive"). Because the Nikkei 225 is price-weighted, a few 値嵩株 move the index particularly strongly. The opposite is 低位株 "low-priced stocks". Note: 値嵩株 says nothing about the quality of the company; first-class blue chips are called 優良株.

examples[].german: Build a portfolio centered on blue-chip stocks.
For long-term investing, blue chips with stable results are recommended.
Even in a recession, blue chips are relatively unlikely to fall in price.
en.notes: 優良株 are shares of solid, profitable large companies, that is, blue chips; 優良 means "excellent, first-class" (cf. 優良企業, 優良ドライバー). In stock market jargon one also hears ブルーチップ or 主力株. Not to be confused with 値嵩株, which only means a high price per share, and with the risky 仕手株. Typical: 優良株に投資する, 優良株中心のポートフォリオ.

examples[].german: A special pardon for political prisoners was issued.
On National Foundation Day, some prisoners were released under a special pardon.
When someone receives a special pardon, the effect of the guilty verdict is lost.
en.notes: 特赦 is a form of 恩赦: the "special pardon" of specific persons, through which a guilty verdict loses its effect. By contrast, 大赦 covers all offenders of certain types of offense at once. In foreign news, 特赦 is also used for mass pardons, for example when a state frees prisoners on its national day. Patterns: 特赦を受ける, 特赦で釈放される, 特赦が発令される.

examples[].german: I got involved in speculative stocks and lost a lot.
Speculative stocks often soar in a short time and then plunge.
Tips on speculative stocks are circulating on online message boards.
en.notes: 仕手株 are shares deliberately driven up by big speculators (仕手筋); mostly small, thinly traded stocks with extreme price swings. The phrase 仕手株に手を出す "to get involved in speculative stocks" is typical and sounds like a warning. The opposite term is 優良株. Similar but more neutral is 投機株 "speculative stock".

examples[].german: I applied for the lottery for IPO shares.
The company plans to go public next March.
The newly listed stock traded at twice the offering price on the first day.
en.notes: 新規公開 is the short form of 新規株式公開, the IPO; in the media one often also reads simply IPO. Shares from an IPO are called 新規公開株; in Japan their allocation to individual investors is often done by lottery (抽選). As a する-verb: 株式を新規公開する. Closely related is 新規上場, which emphasizes admission to exchange trading. Outside the financial world, 新規公開 can also simply mean "first release" (e.g. of a website).

examples[].german: The company achieved a listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Listed companies are obliged to publish their financial results.
Once listed, a company's name recognition and credibility both rise.
en.notes: 上場 is the listing on a stock exchange; as a する-verb: 会社が東証に上場する "to go public" or 株式を上場する. Typical are 上場企業 "listed company", 上場を果たす, 上場を目指す and 東証プライム市場に上場. The second meaning "to stage a play" is rare and formal; for that one normally says 上演. The opposite is 上場廃止.

examples[].german: It was delisted because of deteriorating business conditions.
Once a delisting is decided, the stock is designated as a security on liquidation watch.
Some companies choose to delist voluntarily through a management buyout.
en.notes: 上場廃止 is the removal of a stock from exchange trading (delisting). Usual are 上場廃止になる・となる, 上場廃止が決まる and 上場廃止基準. Before delisting, a stock in Japan is classified as 整理銘柄 and is still traded for a while. Besides forced delisting due to bankruptcy or violations, there is voluntary delisting, for example after a takeover by management (MBO) or a parent company.

en.meaning: public call for applications; public offering (securities)
examples[].german: Funds were collected widely through a public-offering capital increase.
It was decided to hold a public call for names for the city's new mascot.
This university hires faculty through open recruitment.
en.notes: 公募 first means "to invite publicly, to seek publicly"; as a transitive する-verb: 作品・職員・名前を公募する, 公募で選ぶ. In finance it is the public offering of securities to a broad circle of investors: 公募増資, 公募価格, 公募投信. The opposite term is 私募 "private placement". In contrast to the general 募集 "to recruit, to seek", 公募 emphasizes the public call, open to everyone.

examples[].german: Funds were raised from institutional investors by issuing privately placed bonds.
Privately placed funds are not sold to ordinary individual investors.
With a private placement instead of a public offering, the issuance procedure becomes simpler.
en.notes: 私募 is a private placement: securities are not offered publicly but only to a small circle or professional investors. Typical in compounds such as 私募債, 私募ファンド and 私募投信. The opposite term is 公募. Because the strict disclosure obligations of a public offering do not apply, the procedure is simpler; in return, the securities are usually not accessible to ordinary individual investors.

examples[].german: The rating agency announced a downgrade of the government bonds.
The higher a company's rating, the lower the interest rate at which it can borrow money.
The restaurant earned three stars in the Michelin rating.
en.notes: 格付け is classification by rank or quality; as a transitive する-verb: 〜を格付けする. In finance it means the rating of bonds, countries or companies by 格付け機関・格付け会社 "rating agencies": 格付けが高い・低い, 格付けを引き下げる. It is also used for rankings of all kinds, such as the stars of the Michelin Guide. Upgrade and downgrade are called 格上げ and 格下げ; the spelling 格付 without け occurs in technical texts.

examples[].german: The downgrade caused the yield on corporate bonds to soar.
The company was downgraded by two notches because of worsening results.
I can't accept being demoted from department head to section chief.
en.notes: 格下げ is a lowering in rank or rating; mostly passive: 〜が格下げされる, with the target in に (BBBに格下げ) or the extent (一段階格下げ). In finance it refers to ratings, in general to status and standing. For the demotion of people at work, 降格 is the usual, more factual term; 格下げ sounds more like an insult here. Opposite: 格上げ.

examples[].german: Following the upgrade, the share price rose.
The main hall of this temple was upgraded to a national treasure.
The tournament was upgraded to an international competition this year.
en.notes: 格上げ is a raising in rank or rating, mostly passive: 〜に格上げされる. Besides ratings in finance (格付けの格上げ), it is used for status upgrades of all kinds: cultural properties, competitions, government agencies (庁から省への格上げ). For promotions of people, one says 昇進 or 昇格 instead. Opposite: 格下げ.

examples[].german: Hedge funds exert a great influence on the market.
Every month I put 10,000 yen into an index fund.
An investment fund acquired the long-established ryokan.
en.notes: ファンド is a fund, that is, a pool of investors' money that is professionally invested: 投資ファンド, ヘッジファンド, インデックスファンド, 買収ファンド. For funds sold to the public, the formal term is 投資信託; in everyday speech, however, many people simply say ファンド. In the news, ファンド often denotes activist or takeover funds that buy companies. A charitable fund or foundation, on the other hand, is rather 基金.

examples[].german: A reduction of the sentence was granted on appeal.
Many citizens signed a petition seeking a reduced sentence.
His death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
en.notes: 減刑 is "commutation", the reduction of a penalty already imposed or requested. It is done by a higher court or as a form of 恩赦. The passive and the noun are typical: 減刑される, 減刑が認められる, 減刑を求める嘆願書 "petition for clemency". Do not confuse it with 減軽, the statutory mitigation of punishment at sentencing, for example because of diminished responsibility.

examples[].german: Diversified investing is done through investment trusts.
An investment trust was recommended to me at the bank counter.
With investment trusts, the principal is not guaranteed.
en.notes: 投資信託 is the investment fund for the general public: the money of many investors is pooled and invested by a fund company (運用会社). The usual short form is 投信. It is sold through banks and securities firms; typical combinations are 投資信託を購入する, 投資信託を積み立てる and 投資信託の基準価額 "net asset value". Colloquially, people often simply say ファンド.

examples[].german: The stock exchange temporarily suspended trading.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange is located in Kabutocho in Nihonbashi.
To be listed on a stock exchange, a company must pass a strict examination.
en.notes: 証券取引所 is the securities exchange; 証券 "securities" + 取引所 "trading place". The best known is the 東京証券取引所, short 東証, in the Kabutocho district of Nihonbashi. In the news it is often shortened to 取引所. The ending 所 is mostly read じょ here, but one also hears しょ. Typical: 証券取引所に上場する, 証券取引所が取引を停止する.

en.meaning: execution (of an order); agreement; contractual stipulation
examples[].german: The order was executed and the share trade was completed.
Payment of the purchase price is two business days after the trade date.
Loan interest is calculated based on the agreed interest rate.
en.notes: 約定 is a formal expression for "agreement, contractual stipulation": 約定書, 約定利率, 〜を約定する. In securities trading it means the execution of an order, that is, the completion of the trade; then intransitive: 注文が約定する. Important terms are 約定日 "trade date" and 約定価格 "execution price". In everyday speech one says 契約 for contracts and 約束 for promises.

examples[].german: Place a limit order and wait for a trade at the desired price.
I placed a buy order with a limit of 1,000 yen.
The share price did not fall to the limit, so the order was not filled.
en.notes: 指値 is the limit price set by the investor; literally "designated price". Mostly in 指値注文 "limit order" or 〜円の指値で買う・売る. If the price is not reached, the trade does not take place. The opposite term is 成行 "market order, at best". The spelling 指し値 also occurs.

en.meaning: market order; course of events; development
examples[].german: It was executed immediately with a market order.
If you sell at market, you sometimes get filled at a lower price than expected.
All we can do now is watch how things develop.
en.notes: 成行 has two meanings. On the stock exchange it is the short form of 成行注文 "market order": the order is executed immediately at the current price (成行で買う・売る); the opposite term is 指値. In general, なりゆき means "course, development, outcome" and is then mostly written 成り行き: 事の成り行き, 成り行きに任せる "to let things take their course".

examples[].german: The market was lively, with a trading value of over one trillion yen.
Trading volume and trading value are yardsticks of how lively a market is.
Of the purchase price of the land, ten percent was paid as a deposit at the time of contract.
en.notes: 売買代金 is the monetary amount of a purchase or sale. On the stock exchange it denotes the trading value in yen, in contrast to 出来高, the number of shares traded; both are considered yardsticks of market activity. In contracts, for example for real estate, 売買代金 is simply the purchase price. Typical: 売買代金が膨らむ, 売買代金が〜兆円を超える.

en.meaning: last trading day of the year
examples[].german: On the last trading day of the year, the Nikkei average hit a new year-to-date high.
This year's last trading day is on December 30.
Between the last trading day of the year and the first of the new year, stock trading is closed.
