en.notes: 大納会 is the last trading day of the year on the stock exchange, normally December 30 in Japan; the counterpart is 大発会, the first trading day in January. Typical: 大納会を迎える, 大納会の終値 "the year's closing price". 納会 alone generally denotes the last meeting or celebration of a year or season. The word occurs almost only in business news.

en.meaning: first trading day of the year
examples[].german: On the first trading day of the year, trading began in a celebratory mood.
It is customary for women in formal kimono to attend the first trading day of the year.
The Nikkei average on the first trading day of the year rose for the first time in three years.
en.notes: 大発会 is the first trading day of the year on the Japanese stock exchanges, usually in early January; the counterpart on the last trading day of the year is called 大納会. At the Tokyo exchange there is a ceremony for it, at which women in formal kimono traditionally appear. In the news, reports focus mainly on the price movement: 大発会の日経平均. The word is stock market jargon and hardly used otherwise.

examples[].german: The right to convert the convertible bond into shares was exercised.
With a convertible bond, you can swap into shares when the price rises and make a profit.
To raise funds, the company announced it would issue convertible bonds.
en.notes: 転換社債 is the convertible bond: a corporate bond that the holder can exchange for shares at a fixed price; 転換 "conversion" + 社債 "corporate bond". Legally it is now called 転換社債型新株予約権付社債, but in practice people continue to speak of 転換社債 or, in short, CB. Typical: 転換社債を発行する, 株式に転換する.

examples[].german: Subordinated bonds have a high yield but also a high risk.
If the company goes bankrupt, subordinated bonds are repaid after other debts.
The bank issued subordinated bonds to increase its equity.
en.notes: 劣後債 is a subordinated bond: in case of insolvency it is served only after the other liabilities; 劣後 means "to rank behind, to be subordinate". In compensation it offers higher interest. Banks often issue 劣後債 because they are partly counted as equity. Related: 劣後ローン "subordinated loan"; opposite term 優先 "senior, preferential".

examples[].german: A judgment of dismissal was issued because the statute of limitations had run.
Because of an amnesty, the case was dismissed.
At the retrial, a dismissal rather than an acquittal was pronounced, and the bereaved family expressed dissatisfaction.
en.notes: 免訴 is, in criminal proceedings, a judgment that ends the proceedings without deciding on guilt or innocence, for example because of the statute of limitations, amnesty (大赦) or an already final decision in the same matter. It is therefore not an acquittal 無罪. Distinguish 公訴棄却 (dismissal due to procedural defects) and 不起訴 (the prosecution does not file charges at all). Typical: 免訴の判決, 免訴となる.

examples[].german: You should fully understand the risks of structured bonds before investing.
An elderly customer who bought a structured bond on the bank's recommendation suffered a large loss.
Depending on the conditions, structured bonds can fall well below the amount invested.
en.notes: 仕組債 is a structured bond with built-in derivatives, so that interest and repayment depend on share prices, indexes or exchange rates. Also written 仕組み債. The often high interest is tempting, but considerable losses of capital threaten. In Japan, the sale to elderly retail customers came under criticism from the financial regulator.

examples[].german: The interest on the coupon bond is paid every six months.
I bought a ten-year interest-bearing government bond.
If you hold a coupon bond to maturity, you receive the face value and the interest.
en.notes: 利付債 is a bond with regular interest payments (coupon bond); 利 "interest" + 付 "provided with" + 債 "bond". The interest is usually paid semiannually; at maturity the face value is returned. The opposite term is 割引債 "zero-coupon bond". A well-known example: 利付国債 "interest-bearing government bond" such as the ten-year 10年利付国債.

en.meaning: face value; par value; gross amount (salary)
examples[].german: Government bonds for individuals can be bought from a face value of 10,000 yen.
You shouldn't take his flattery at face value.
On paper my monthly salary is 300,000 yen, but my take-home pay is about 240,000.
en.notes: 額面 is the amount printed on a security, coin or banknote, the face value; the opposite is 時価 "market value". Very common is the figurative phrase 額面通りに受け取る "to take at face value". For salary, 額面 denotes the gross amount, in contrast to 手取り "net". Par-value shares no longer exist in Japan since 2001, but for bonds the 額面 is central.

examples[].german: I closed the time deposit that had reached maturity.
When the insurance matures, you can receive the maturity benefit.
He served his sentence to the full term and was released.
en.notes: 満期 is the end of a fixed term: for time deposits, bonds and insurance the maturity (満期を迎える, 満期になる, 満期日), for insurance also 満期保険金 "maturity benefit". For prison sentences it means serving the full sentence: 満期出所. For contracts or deadlines in general, one rather says 期限が切れる or 満了.

examples[].german: Taking advantage of low interest rates, the corporate bonds were redeemed early.
With early repayment, the investor misses out on the interest they had expected.
An investment trust whose assets had shrunk will be redeemed early.
en.notes: 繰上償還 is early repayment or redemption before the scheduled date; 繰上 "to move up" + 償還 "repayment, redemption". It concerns bonds that the issuer buys back earlier, and investment funds that are dissolved early because their volume is too small. For private loans such as mortgages, one says 繰上返済 instead. The spellings 繰り上げ償還 and 繰上げ償還 also occur.

examples[].german: If a bill is dishonored twice, banking transactions are suspended.
A business partner dishonored a bill, and we could no longer collect our receivables.
The check bounced because of insufficient funds in the account.
en.notes: 不渡り denotes the non-payment of a bill of exchange or check for lack of funds. Typical are 不渡りを出す "to let a bill bounce", 不渡りになる and 不渡り手形. Anyone who has 不渡り twice within six months is excluded from banking transactions (銀行取引停止処分), which for companies practically means bankruptcy. The word therefore often appears in the news in connection with insolvencies.

en.meaning: bank run; run on a bank
examples[].german: Rumors of financial trouble triggered a run on the bank.
A false report spread online, and it turned into a bank run, with customers storming the counters.
The deposit insurance system also serves to prevent bank runs.
en.notes: 取り付け騒ぎ is a bank run: fearing a bankruptcy, customers rush to a bank to withdraw their deposits. 取り付け here means mass withdrawal, and 騒ぎ means "uproar". Typical: 取り付け騒ぎが起きる・起こる. Do not confuse it with 取り付け "mounting, installation" from 取り付ける. Rumors or false reports often set off the rush.

examples[].german: Under the deposit insurance system, deposits are protected up to a certain amount.
Even if a bank fails, principal up to ten million yen and its interest is protected by deposit insurance.
Foreign currency deposits are not covered by deposit insurance.
en.notes: 預金保険 is deposit insurance, which protects bank deposits in the event of a bank failure; in Japan it is run by the 預金保険機構. Up to 10 million yen of principal plus interest is protected per person per bank; the limited payout is called ペイオフ. Not protected are, among other things, foreign currency deposits. Mostly used in 預金保険制度 or 預金保険の対象.

examples[].german: Disposing of non-performing loans is a challenge for bank management.
After the collapse of the bubble, many banks were left holding huge amounts of bad debt.
The non-performing loan ratio fell, and the banks' management became sound again.
en.notes: 不良債権 are non-performing or bad loans whose repayment has become uncertain; 不良 "bad, defective" + 債権 "claim, receivable". The word is closely tied to the Japanese banking crisis after the burst of the bubble economy. Typical: 不良債権を抱える, 不良債権処理 "disposal of bad loans", 不良債権比率. Do not confuse it with 債券 "bond", which is read the same way.

examples[].german: The court dismissed the plaintiff's claim.
The high court dismissed the defendant's appeal.
The null hypothesis was rejected at the 5% significance level.
en.notes: 棄却 is the "dismissal" of a motion after examination on the merits: 請求を棄却する, 控訴棄却, 上告を棄却する. The important counterpart is 却下, rejection on formal grounds without examining the matter, so to speak turning someone away at the door. In statistics, 棄却 means "to reject": 帰無仮説を棄却する "to reject the null hypothesis". In everyday speech, for "to decline" one rather says 断る or 拒否する.

examples[].german: The calling in of loans left the company's cash flow in a bind.
In a recession, more and more small and medium-sized businesses suffer from banks calling in their loans.
The government asked the banks not to withhold new loans or call in existing ones.
en.notes: 貸し剥がし refers to a bank demanding early repayment of loans already granted, or refusing to renew them; literally something like "lend and strip away". Distinguish it from 貸し渋り "reluctance to lend", where new loans are refused; in the press the two often appear together (貸し渋り・貸し剥がし). It is a critical buzzword from business journalism and politics, coined during the banking crisis of the late 1990s; typical are 貸し剥がしに遭う and 貸し剥がしに苦しむ. Also often written 貸しはがし.

examples[].german: We tighten credit screening to reduce the risk of bad debt.
The payment could not be processed because the credit card limit was exceeded.
For new business partners, the person in charge of credit management first checks their financial condition.
en.notes: 与信 is the technical term for granting credit to a customer or business partner, including payment terms in trade and card limits. It appears almost always in compounds: 与信審査 "credit screening", 与信枠 or 与信限度額 "credit limit", 与信管理 "credit risk management". Unlike 信用 "trust, creditworthiness" and 融資 "financing, a concrete loan", 与信 means the extending of credit as a process or framework. Rare in everyday life, but standard in banks, accounting and sales.

examples[].german: A default occurred and the company's credibility collapsed.
There are fears that the country's government bonds may go into default.
Missing the delivery deadline counted as non-performance, and damages were demanded.
en.notes: 債務不履行 means that an obligation is not fulfilled. In finance this is a "default", often also called デフォルト: 債務不履行に陥る, 債務不履行を起こす. In civil law it means "non-performance" of a contract in general, e.g. late delivery, and gives rise to 損害賠償 ("damages"). 不履行 alone also appears in 契約不履行 or 約束の不履行.

examples[].german: The decline in the credit rating increased funding costs.
A major rating agency lowered the credit rating of Japanese government bonds by one notch.
Before buying corporate bonds, check the issuing company's credit rating.
en.notes: 信用格付け is the credit rating that rating agencies (格付け会社) assign to countries, companies or bonds. In the news it is often shortened to 格付け; downgrading and upgrading are 格付けを引き下げる/引き上げる, or 格下げ/格上げ for short. For the creditworthiness of private individuals, one more often says 信用情報 or 信用スコア. The spelling 信用格付 without け also occurs in technical texts.

examples[].german: Market liquidity declined, making trades harder to execute.
The central bank supplied the market with large amounts of liquidity.
Real estate is less liquid than stocks and cannot be turned into cash right away.
en.notes: In finance, 流動性 means "liquidity": how easily an asset can be converted into money, or how actively a market is traded: 流動性が高い/低い, 流動性を供給する (central bank), 流動性リスク. For a company's ability to pay in everyday terms, one more often says 資金繰り; 流動性 is the technical term. Outside finance it means "fluidity, mobility", e.g. 雇用の流動性 "labor market mobility".

examples[].german: The bank's capital adequacy ratio is below the international standard.
Companies with a high equity ratio are said to withstand recessions well.
Through a capital increase, the equity ratio was raised to thirty percent.
en.notes: 自己資本比率 is the share of equity (自己資本) in total capital; the counterpart of equity is 他人資本 "borrowed capital". For companies a high ratio is seen as a sign of stability (自己資本比率が高い); for banks it is internationally regulated as a capital requirement (BIS規制). Typical verbs: 自己資本比率を引き上げる, 〜が基準を下回る. A purely technical term from balance sheets and banking supervision.

examples[].german: Companies with capital of 100 million yen or more are covered.
This company was founded with a capital of only one million yen.
To expand the business, the capital was increased to 300 million yen.
en.notes: 資本金 is the capital registered in a company's commercial register, i.e. its stated capital or share capital: 資本金〇〇円の会社. Increase and reduction are 増資 and 減資. Distinguish it from 資本 "capital" as a general economic concept and 資金 "funds, money" for a specific purpose. Laws and subsidy programs often define small and medium-sized enterprises by their 資本金.

examples[].german: There is an obligation to set aside legal reserves.
The company sets aside part of its profits as reserves.
To cover the deficit, the reserves had to be drawn down.
en.notes: 準備金 are "reserves" that a company, bank or organization sets aside for future purposes. In Japanese company law one distinguishes 資本準備金 and 利益準備金, together 法定準備金. Typical verbs: 準備金を積み立てる, 準備金を取り崩す ("to draw down"). Similar but more general is 積立金; 引当金, by contrast, are provisions for expected costs.

examples[].german: Dividends are paid out of the carried-over surplus.
The shareholders' meeting resolved to pay a dividend out of surplus.
Part of the previous year's surplus will be used to repay debt.
en.notes: On the balance sheet, 剰余金 is the part of equity that exceeds the 資本金; one distinguishes 資本剰余金 "capital surplus" and 利益剰余金 "retained earnings". Dividends are paid out of the 剰余金 (剰余金の配当). In the national budget it means the surplus after the close of the fiscal year (決算剰余金). For an everyday "surplus", one more often says 余り or 黒字.

examples[].german: In the labor-management dispute, the labor relations commission stepped in to mediate.
My wife filed for divorce mediation at the family court.
The talks did not come together, and the mediation ended without agreement.
en.notes: 調停 is "mediation" or "conciliation": a neutral third party intermediates, and the parties agree by giving way to each other. Especially well known is 離婚調停 before the family court; also 調停を申し立てる, 調停委員, 調停が成立する／不成立に終わる, 調停に入る. In 仲裁 (arbitration), by contrast, an arbitrator decides bindingly; 和解 is the "settlement" reached.

examples[].german: Reducing tax collection costs is a challenge for administrative reform.
Farmers in the Edo period suffered under harsh tax collection.
The state is trying to make tax collection more efficient through digitalization.
en.notes: 徴税 is the collection of taxes by the state. Distinguish 課税 "taxation, imposing a tax", 徴税 "actually collecting" and 納税 "paying taxes" by the citizen. Typical are 徴税権, 徴税コスト, 徴税を強化する; the verb 徴税する exists, but 税を徴収する is more common. A formal word from administration, history and politics.

examples[].german: The repayment plan was approved at the creditors' meeting.
The company went bankrupt, and creditors flooded into the office.
Without the creditors' consent, a reduction of the debt is not permitted.
en.notes: 債権者 is the "creditor", i.e. a person who holds a claim (債権); the counterpart is 債務者 "debtor". Beware of the homophone 債券 "bond, security" - 債権 is the claim, 債券 the traded paper. Typical combinations are 債権者集会 "creditors' meeting", 債権者に返済する, 債権者の同意. Legal and economic register; in casual speech one more often says 貸した人 or 貸し手.

examples[].german: The debtor's ability to repay is carefully examined.
The debtor fell three months behind on repayment, so we sued in court.
A consultation desk was set up to support people with multiple debts.
en.notes: 債務者 is the "debtor", i.e. a person who has an obligation (債務); the counterpart is 債権者 "creditor". 債務 is more legal and broader than 借金 "monetary debt": in law it can be any duty to perform. Common are 多重債務者 "over-indebted person with several lenders" and 債務者が返済を滞らせる. In everyday speech one more often says 借りた人 or 借り手.

examples[].german: Foreign exchange reserves reached a record high.
The government drew down part of its foreign exchange reserves to intervene by buying yen.
Countries with small foreign exchange reserves easily fall into currency crises.
en.notes: 外貨準備 are the foreign exchange reserves that the state and central bank hold in foreign currency; the amount is called 外貨準備高. They serve mainly for interventions in the currency market and as a buffer in currency crises: 外貨準備を取り崩す "to draw on the reserves", 外貨準備が減少する. 外貨 alone simply means "foreign currency", e.g. in the private 外貨預金 "foreign currency account". A technical term from business news.

examples[].german: Currency intervention was carried out against the sharp rise of the yen.
The Ministry of Finance decided to intervene in the currency market to halt the yen's decline.
In the market, wariness of currency intervention is growing.
en.notes: 為替介入 is the authorities' intervention in the foreign exchange market; in Japan the Ministry of Finance decides and the Bank of Japan carries it out. One says 為替介入を行う/実施する or 為替介入に踏み切る "to decide to intervene"; depending on direction 円買い介入 or 円売り介入, and together with other countries 協調介入. Note the special reading 為替 = かわせ. A technical term from business news.

examples[].german: The increase in the money supply is raising inflationary pressure.
The Bank of Japan tried to stimulate the economy by increasing the money supply.
The growth of the money supply has slowed compared with the previous year.
en.notes: 通貨供給量 is the "money supply", i.e. the money in circulation. Officially the statistic is now called マネーストック (formerly マネーサプライ); 通貨供給量 is the Japanese paraphrase used in news and textbooks. Typical are 通貨供給量を増やす/絞る and 通貨供給量の伸び. Distinguish it from マネタリーベース "monetary base", the money provided directly by the central bank.

examples[].german: Short-term interest rates are steered through open market operations.
The Bank of Japan bought large amounts of government bonds in open market operations.
On the economics exam there was a question asking to explain how open market operations work.
en.notes: 公開市場操作 refers to the buying and selling of securities, mainly government bonds, by the central bank in order to steer the money supply and short-term interest rates. In the news and in the market it is usually shortened to オペ: 買いオペ "buying operation" (money is supplied), 売りオペ "selling operation" (money is withdrawn). The full term is typical of textbooks and official texts.

examples[].german: Changes to the reserve requirement ratio are used as a tool of monetary policy.
China's central bank announced a cut in the reserve requirement ratio.
If the reserve requirement ratio is raised, the money banks can lend decreases.
en.notes: 預金準備率 is the "reserve requirement ratio": the share of deposits that banks must hold with the central bank. Technically it is also called 準備率 or 支払準備率 in Japan. Typical are 預金準備率を引き上げる/引き下げる; a cut frees up more money for lending. The Bank of Japan has hardly used this instrument for a long time; in the news it appears mainly in connection with China's central bank.

examples[].german: Coordination between fiscal and monetary policy is important.
To stimulate the economy, the government adopted a fiscal policy of increasing public works.
Debt has grown so much that there is no room for an expansionary fiscal policy.
en.notes: 財政政策 is the government's fiscal policy: steering the economy through public spending and taxes. Its counterpart is 金融政策 "monetary policy" of the central bank. Typical expressions: 財政政策をとる, 積極財政 "expansionary fiscal policy" vs. 緊縮財政 "austerity", 財政出動 "government spending program". 財政 alone means "public finances", e.g. 財政赤字 "budget deficit".

examples[].german: The total of the general account has exceeded 100 trillion yen.
The Cabinet approved the draft general account budget for the next fiscal year.
Social security costs account for about one third of the general account expenditure.
en.notes: 一般会計 is the "general account", i.e. the core budget of the state or a municipality, from which regular expenses are paid. Alongside it there are 特別会計 "special accounts" for specific purposes such as pensions or government debt. Typical are 一般会計予算, 一般会計の歳出 "expenditure" and 歳入 "revenue". For a company's bookkeeping, one says 経理 or 会計 instead.

examples[].german: Government bonds that have reached maturity are refinanced.
This corporate bond matures in ten years.
Repayment became difficult, so we negotiated an extension of the redemption deadline with the bank.
en.notes: 償還期限 is the deadline by which a bond or loan must be repaid - for bonds, the "maturity". 償還 means "redemption, repayment" and is used mainly for bonds and public loans. Typical are 償還期限を迎える, 償還期限が到来する and 償還期限を延長する. Similar is 満期 "maturity, expiry", which also applies to savings contracts and insurance; for ordinary loans one more often says 返済期限.

examples[].german: Public funds were injected into the bank that had fallen into a management crisis.
As long as public funds are used, there is a responsibility to explain properly how they are spent.
Most of the cost of this research is covered by public funds.
en.notes: 公的資金 are "public funds", i.e. money from taxes or government budgets. Especially well known is the phrase 公的資金を注入する/投入する for the state bailout of banks or companies. The opposite is 民間資金 ("private funds"). 公金 specifically means money managed by public bodies (公金横領 "embezzlement of public funds"). The language of politics and business news.

examples[].german: The credit creation function of banks supports economic growth.
As deposits and lending are repeated, credit creation occurs.
When lending decreases, the effect of credit creation also weakens.
en.notes: 信用創造 describes how commercial banks create additional book money through lending: a loan is deposited again, lent out again, and so the money supply multiplies. 信用 here means "credit", not "trust". The term comes from economics and textbooks, often as 信用創造機能 or 信用創造のしくみ. Neutral and technical; hardly used in everyday life.

examples[].german: The decline in the financial intermediation function is seen as a problem.
Banks play the role of financial intermediation, lending money collected from depositors to companies.
Regional banks are required to strengthen their financial intermediation function that supports the local economy.
en.notes: 金融仲介 is the intermediary role of banks and other institutions between savers who invest money and companies or households that need money. It mostly appears in 金融仲介機能 or 金融仲介機関. Banks provide 間接金融 "indirect financing", while in 直接金融 companies finance themselves directly in the market via stocks and bonds. 仲介 alone means "mediation, brokering", e.g. 不動産の仲介 for a real estate agent.

examples[].german: There is an obligation to explain sufficiently the risks of complex financial products.
At the bank counter, I was recommended a financial product without a principal guarantee.
I am unsure which financial product I should invest in to prepare for retirement.
en.notes: 金融商品 is the collective term for financial products such as stocks, bonds, investment trusts (投資信託), deposits or insurance; 商品 here means "product", not "goods". Typical combinations: 金融商品を販売する/購入する, 金融商品に投資する, and the 金融商品取引法 "Financial Instruments and Exchange Act". Important in consultations is the risk of 元本割れ "loss of the invested capital". Neutral, common in banking and consumer contexts.

examples[].german: The global financial crisis spilled over into the real economy as well.
To prevent a financial crisis, the central banks of various countries jointly supplied funds.
My father lost his job during the financial crisis, and the family had a hard time.
en.notes: 金融危機 is a "financial crisis" in which banks and credit markets begin to wobble. Typical are 金融危機が起きる/発生する, 金融危機に陥る and 金融危機を乗り切る; the 2008 crisis is called 世界金融危機 or リーマン・ショック. Distinguish 通貨危機 "currency crisis", 財政危機 "government fiscal crisis" and the broader 経済危機 "economic crisis".

examples[].german: The patient died due to the doctor's negligence.
The fault ratio for the accident was determined to be eight to two.
The driver was arrested on suspicion of causing death by negligent driving.
en.notes: Legally, 過失 is "negligence": damage resulting from lack of care, not from intent. Important combinations: 過失致死 "negligent homicide", 業務上過失, 重過失 "gross negligence" and, for traffic accidents, 過失割合 "fault ratio". The opposite is 故意 "intent". For everyday mistakes one says ミス or 失敗; 過失 sounds legal.

examples[].german: The collapse of the real estate bubble dealt a serious blow to the economy.
I hear that during the bubble years they went out drinking almost every night on company expenses.
Some people worry that the sharp rise in stock prices is a bubble.
en.notes: Economically, バブル is a "speculative bubble": 不動産バブル, ITバブル; it bursts with バブルがはじける or バブルが崩壊する. Without any addition, バブル in Japan usually means the bubble economy of the late 1980s to early 1990s (バブル経済, バブル期): バブルの頃, バブル世代. For an actual soap or air bubble one more often says 泡; バブル is used for that only in loanwords such as バブルバス.

examples[].german: The policy is to expand investment and lending overseas.
The government used the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program to push forward the development of regional airports.
That bank is increasing its investment and lending in the renewable energy sector.
en.notes: 投融資 combines 投資 "investment, equity stake" and 融資 "lending" in one word: money is partly put in as capital and partly lent. Typical for the state, development banks and corporate groups: 投融資を行う, 投融資を拡大する, 海外投融資. A fixed term is 財政投融資, the government's investment and loan program, often called the "second budget". Written and technical language.

examples[].german: The international framework for combating money laundering is being strengthened.
A yakuza group is suspected of laundering money through shell companies.
When I tried to send a large sum of cash at the bank, I was asked the purpose in order to prevent money laundering.
en.notes: 資金洗浄 is the formal, legal word for "money laundering"; in the media and everyday speech one hears マネーロンダリング or shortened マネロン more often. Typical are 資金洗浄を行う, 資金洗浄に関与する and 資金洗浄対策 or 資金洗浄防止 "anti-money-laundering measures". 洗浄 literally means "washing, rinsing", as in 胃洗浄 "stomach pumping".

examples[].german: The development of fintech is transforming financial services.
A friend from university started a fintech company.
Regional banks, too, are making use of fintech so that people can open an account on their smartphones.
en.notes: フィンテック is formed from "finance" and "technology" and means financial services using digital technology, such as smartphone payments, robo-advisors or crypto-assets. It is written in katakana, and in technical texts also as FinTech. Typical are フィンテック企業 "fintech company" and フィンテックを活用する. A neutral term from the business press and the corporate world.

examples[].german: The spread of electronic money is reducing cash transactions.
At convenience stores, I often pay with transit-type electronic money.
My electronic money balance was too low, so I topped it up at the station.
en.notes: In Japan, 電子マネー mainly means rechargeable prepaid systems on IC cards or smartphones, such as Suica, PASMO, nanaco or WAON: 電子マネーで払う, 電子マネーにチャージする "to top up", 電子マネーの残高 "balance". Strictly speaking, credit cards and QR code payments do not count; all of them together are called キャッシュレス決済. Neutral and everyday.

examples[].german: The share of cashless payments is rising year by year.
This shop is completely cashless; cash cannot be used.
The government is promoting the shift to cashless payments in tourist areas.
en.notes: キャッシュレス "cashless" usually stands directly before a noun: キャッシュレス決済 "cashless payment", キャッシュレス社会; with 化 it forms キャッシュレス化 "shift to cashless payment". Adverbially one says キャッシュレスで払う; キャッシュレスな店 is possible but less common. The counterpart is 現金払い "cash payment". Neutral, very common in daily life and politics.

examples[].german: The digitalization of customs clearance procedures is being advanced.
Customs clearance of the imported parts took a long time, and production was delayed.
The package cleared customs yesterday and is due to arrive tomorrow.
en.notes: 通関 is the "customs clearance" of goods on import or export: 通関手続き, 通関業者 "customs broker", 通関書類. As an intransitive する-verb: 荷物が通関する "the shipment clears customs". Do not confuse it with 税関 "customs office, customs authority": 税関 is the agency, 通関 the process. For travelers at the airport one more often speaks of 税関検査.

examples[].german: The cargo is received upon presentation of the bill of lading.
At the port, the work of unloading the ship's cargo with cranes continued.
Part of the cargo fell into the sea in the storm.
en.notes: 船荷 is goods transported by ship, the "ship's cargo"; 船 is often read ふな in compounds, as in 船便. The word is technical and appears above all in 船荷証券 "bill of lading". One says 船荷を積む/降ろす. More general are 積み荷 "load" (for any vehicle) and 貨物 "freight, cargo".

examples[].german: The consignee checks the condition of the cargo.
At the warehouse, goods receiving is finished in the morning before shipping work begins.
The box was torn when the goods were received, so I took a photo.
en.notes: 荷受 is the "acceptance of goods", i.e. goods receiving in logistics and trade. It mostly appears in compounds: 荷受人 "consignee" (counterpart 荷送人 "consignor"), 荷受け場 "receiving area". In general text 荷受け with け is more often written; the form without okurigana is common in forms and technical texts. At wholesale markets, the wholesalers who take over goods from producers are also called 荷受.

examples[].german: The broker mediates between producers and retailers.
Before the war, my grandfather ran a rice brokerage.
At the market auction, the brokers call out one bid after another.
en.notes: 仲買 is intermediary trade or brokerage, where someone buys between seller and buyer and resells; the person is called 仲買人. The word has a traditional ring and is met mainly in connection with markets, auctions and historical contexts (米の仲買); at today's wholesale markets the official term is 仲卸. For modern brokering in general, one uses 仲介 or ブローカー.

examples[].german: It was proven that the crime was committed intentionally.
He didn't deliberately hit the other player with the ball.
The severity of the crime changes depending on whether it was intentional or negligent.
en.notes: 故意 is legally "intent", the conscious bringing about of a result, with the opposite 過失 "negligence". Adverbially 故意に means "intentionally, on purpose", for example with a deliberate foul in sports. Technical term: 未必の故意 "conditional intent (dolus eventualis)". In everyday speech, instead of 故意に one rather says わざと, in factual language 意図的に. Do not confuse it with the identically read 恋 "love".

examples[].german: A stocktake is carried out at the end of the period to confirm inventory.
In the year-end stocktake, the books and the actual stock did not match.
Before changing jobs, I tried taking stock of my own skills.
en.notes: 棚卸 is the "stocktaking": at the end of a period the stock of goods is counted and valued (棚卸をする, 棚卸資産 "inventories" on the balance sheet). It is more often written 棚卸し or たな卸し. Figuratively, one now says スキルの棚卸し or キャリアの棚卸し for "taking stock of one's own skills"; the older meaning "listing someone's faults" has become rare.

examples[].german: Price negotiations with the suppliers are struggling.
Because of the weak yen, the purchase price of imported goods has gone up, and we have no choice but to raise prices.
The head chef goes to the market every morning to buy fish.
en.notes: 仕入 is the purchase of goods or materials for resale or production. In running text one mostly writes 仕入れ; the verb is the transitive ichidan verb 仕入れる; without okurigana it appears mainly in compounds and in bookkeeping: 仕入先 "supplier", 仕入値 "purchase price". Unlike 購入 "purchase" in general, 仕入 always concerns business purchasing of goods; 調達 "procurement" is broader.

examples[].german: An accounting standard that values assets at market value was introduced.
The sea urchin at this restaurant is marked "market price", so I don't know how much it costs.
The company's market capitalization has exceeded one trillion yen.
en.notes: 時価 is the current market or daily value: 時価で評価する "to value at market value", 時価総額 "market capitalization". Opposites are 簿価 "book value" and 定価 "list price". At sushi restaurants, expensive fish are often marked only 時価 "market price" instead of a price - notorious because you only learn the amount at the register.

examples[].german: The surge in crude oil prices is a factor in rising prices.
As a wedding gift of money, 30,000 yen is the going rate for a friend.
It is a well-known fact that summer vacation homework is done on the last day.
en.notes: 相場 is first of all the "market price, quotation": 為替相場 "exchange rate", 株式相場, 相場が上がる/下がる. It also denotes the "customary amount", for example for monetary gifts: ご祝儀の相場は三万円. The fixed phrase 〜と相場が決まっている means "it is generally taken for granted that ...". 相場を張る "to speculate" is rather old-fashioned. Unlike 値段 "price of an item", 相場 always means a generally valid market value or yardstick.

examples[].german: I brought the documentary bill to the bank and asked them to purchase it.
The exporter collects payment through a documentary bill of exchange with attached shipping documents.
In the trade practice class, we had the mechanism of documentary bills explained with a diagram.
en.notes: 荷為替 is a term from foreign trade financing: the exporter draws a bill of exchange (為替手形) on the importer, attaches the shipping documents such as 船荷証券 and 保険証券, and has his bank purchase it - this is the 荷為替手形 "documentary bill". It is often combined with a 信用状 "letter of credit". The reading is にがわせ with voiced が. A purely technical term.

examples[].german: We open a letter of credit to guarantee settlement of the trade payment.
Since it was a new business partner, we made settlement by letter of credit a condition.
The payment was refused because the entries in the documents did not match the terms of the letter of credit.
en.notes: 信用状 is the "letter of credit", in practice often written L/C: the importer's bank commits to pay against presentation of the prescribed documents. Typical: 信用状を開設する "to open a letter of credit", 信用状を発行する, 信用状の条件, 信用状付き取引. 状 here means "letter, document", as in 招待状. A purely technical term of foreign trade.

examples[].german: A bill of lading is a negotiable instrument representing ownership of the cargo.
After loading the cargo onto the ship, the shipping company issues a bill of lading.
The bill of lading arrived late, so we couldn't collect the cargo at the port.
en.notes: 船荷証券 is the "bill of lading" (often written B/L). The shipping company issues it after loading; it confirms receipt of the goods and documents the right to delivery, so it is a negotiable instrument (有価証券). Typical: 船荷証券を発行する/提示する/裏書する. For air freight there is instead the 航空運送状 (air waybill), which is not a negotiable instrument.

examples[].german: The insurance policy is attached to the export documents.
When reporting an accident, please tell us your insurance policy number.
I keep my life insurance policy carefully in a safe.
en.notes: 保険証券 is the "insurance policy", the document by which the insurer confirms the contract - for life, car or cargo insurance. In foreign trade it is one of the shipping documents in CIF transactions. Do not confuse it with 保険証, the health insurance card. Typical: 保険証券番号, 保険証券を保管する/紛失する.

examples[].german: The trade balance fell into deficit.
Exports grew thanks to the weak yen, and the trade balance turned to a surplus for the first time in three years.
Rising energy prices are worsening the trade balance.
en.notes: 貿易収支 is the "trade balance": exports of goods minus imports of goods. Typical are 貿易収支が黒字/赤字になる, 赤字に転落する, 改善する/悪化する; one also says 貿易黒字 and 貿易赤字 for short. The trade balance is part of the broader 経常収支 "current account", which also includes services and investment income. 収支 alone means "income and expenditure".

examples[].german: Debate continues over the scope of application of the conspiracy law.
The man conspired with a former colleague to embezzle company funds.
The police are investigating on the belief that there was a conspiracy between the two.
en.notes: 共謀 is the "joint planning" of a crime, i.e. conspiracy or complicity. Typical: Aと共謀して〜する, 共謀の疑い, 共謀共同正犯 "joint principal by agreement" and 共謀罪, which was controversially introduced in 2017 as "preparation of terrorist offenses". 陰謀, by contrast, is a large-scale "plot", 結託 joint collusion; colloquially one says ぐるになる.

examples[].german: The current account surplus is shrinking.
Even with a trade deficit, Japan's current account is in surplus because of its large investment income from abroad.
The service balance improved with the increase in tourists, and the current account surplus widened.
en.notes: 経常収支 is the "current account": it comprises 貿易収支 "trade balance", サービス収支 "services balance" and the primary and secondary income (所得収支). Japan often has a current account surplus despite a trade deficit, because its investment income from abroad is high. Typical: 経常収支が黒字/赤字, 黒字幅が拡大/縮小する. 経常 means "ordinary, recurring", as in 経常利益.

examples[].german: Developments in the capital account affect exchange rates.
With more acquisitions of foreign companies, a major change was seen in the capital account.
In the textbook, the balance of payments is explained as divided into the current account and the capital account.
en.notes: 資本収支 is the "capital account", i.e. cross-border capital flows such as direct investment and securities purchases. Together with the 経常収支 it forms the classic breakdown of the balance of payments. In official Japanese statistics it was replaced in 2014 by 金融収支 "financial account" and 資本移転等収支; in textbooks and older texts, however, 資本収支 is still common.

examples[].german: Maintaining balance in the balance of payments is the foundation of economic stability.
The Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan publish balance of payments statistics every month.
The balance of payments is a record of all the transactions a country has carried out with foreign countries.
en.notes: 国際収支 is the "balance of payments": the overall account of all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world. It is divided into sub-accounts such as 経常収支 "current account" and 金融収支 or, formerly, 資本収支 "capital account". Typical are 国際収支統計 and 国際収支の均衡. 収支 alone means "income and expenditure", e.g. 家計の収支.

examples[].german: Trade friction between the two countries is becoming serious.
In the 1980s, the Japan-US trade friction over semiconductors became a major problem.
To avoid trade friction, that automaker started local production.
en.notes: 貿易摩擦 is "trade tension" between countries, triggered by trade imbalances, tariffs or import restrictions. Typical: 貿易摩擦が起きる/激化する/深刻化する, 貿易摩擦を解消する. Historically well known is the 日米貿易摩擦 of the 1980s over cars and semiconductors. An escalation to mutual punitive tariffs is called 貿易戦争 "trade war". 摩擦 literally means "friction", also used figuratively in 文化摩擦.

examples[].german: The rise of protectionism is becoming a risk for the world economy.
In a recession, countries easily lean toward protectionism.
To protect domestic farmers, the government has pursued a protectionist policy of imposing high tariffs on imported rice.
en.notes: 保護貿易 is a trade policy that protects domestic industry from foreign competition through tariffs, import quotas or subsidies; the opposite is 自由貿易 "free trade". The attitude behind it is called 保護貿易主義 "protectionism". Typical are 保護貿易政策 and 保護貿易に傾く/転じる. Technical language, common in business news and in civics class.

examples[].german: Promoting free trade contributes to economic development.
Japan has concluded free trade agreements with many countries.
We debated protectionism versus free trade in class.
en.notes: 自由貿易 is trade without tariffs, quantity restrictions or other government intervention; the opposite is 保護貿易 "protectionism". Typical combinations are 自由貿易を推進する "to promote free trade", 自由貿易体制 "free trade regime" and above all 自由貿易協定 "free trade agreement" (FTA). Attributively it takes の; the word belongs to the language of newspapers, politics and economics.

examples[].german: The two countries agreed to remove trade barriers.
High tariffs are a typical trade barrier.
The complicated inspection system has effectively become a trade barrier.
en.notes: 貿易障壁 are "barriers to trade" that make international movement of goods more difficult. One distinguishes 関税障壁 (tariffs) and 非関税障壁 (e.g. quotas, strict standards, complicated inspection procedures). Typical verbs: 貿易障壁を撤廃する/取り除く, 貿易障壁を設ける, 貿易障壁が高い. The word belongs to the language of economic policy and the news; 障壁 alone means "barrier, obstacle" (言葉の障壁).

examples[].german: Anti-dumping duties were imposed on dumped exports.
An investigation began on the grounds that Chinese steel is being dumped.
Underbidding in public works contracts has become a problem.
en.notes: ダンピング refers to selling goods below the production cost or domestic price, especially in exports, in order to drive competitors out of the market; the official Japanese term for it is 不当廉売. Fixed combinations are 反ダンピング関税 (also アンチダンピング関税) "anti-dumping duty" and, domestically, ダンピング受注 "accepting orders at dumping prices" in tenders. Unlike the neutral 安売り "cheap sale", ダンピング implies unfair intent. Rarely also used as a する-verb (ダンピングする).

examples[].german: Safeguard measures were invoked in response to the surge in imports.
Because beef imports suddenly increased, the safeguard was triggered.
The government said it would judge carefully whether to invoke the safeguard.
en.notes: セーフガード is above all the WTO's trade-law safeguard clause, under which a country may temporarily raise tariffs or limit quantities when imports suddenly rise sharply; the official term is 緊急輸入制限. The fixed verb for it is 発動する: セーフガードを発動する "to invoke the safeguard", passive セーフガードが発動される. In other fields (IT, finance), セーフガード can mean "safeguard, protective mechanism" in general.

en.meaning: place of origin; country of origin
examples[].german: Submission of a certificate of origin is required.
The tomato is said to originate from South America.
I checked the country-of-origin label on the meat at the supermarket.
en.notes: 原産地 is the place or country where something originally comes from: for plants and animals the natural homeland (トマトの原産地は南米), for goods the place of manufacture or production. On foods one reads 原産地表示 "origin labeling"; when a country is explicitly meant, one says 原産国 "country of origin". The simple 産地 refers more to the present growing or production area (りんごの産地), whereas 原産地 stresses the origin.

examples[].german: The budget proposal was passed unanimously.
Shareholders can exercise their voting rights at the general meeting of shareholders.
A resolution requires the approval of a majority of those present.
en.notes: 議決 is the formal decision-making of a body such as a parliament, town council or general meeting after deliberation; as a する-verb it is transitive: 予算案を議決する. The result can be 可決 ("approved") or 否決 ("rejected"); 決議 means rather the resolution that has been adopted. Important compounds: 議決権 ("voting right", e.g. of shareholders) and 議決機関 ("decision-making body").

examples[].german: He was indicted for instigating murder.
He is suspected of having instigated a subordinate to destroy evidence.
The instigator is also subject to the same penalty as the principal offender.
en.notes: 教唆 is "instigation": inducing someone to commit a crime. Patterns: 人に犯罪を教唆する, 殺人教唆, 自殺教唆, 教唆犯 "instigator". Under Japanese law, the instigator faces the same punishment as the principal offender 正犯, while aiding and abetting 幇助 is punished more leniently. In everyday speech one says そそのかす; 扇動 is the inciting of a crowd.

examples[].german: Negotiations to revise the bilateral commercial treaty have begun.
At the end of the Edo period, Japan concluded commercial treaties with Western countries.
Revising the unequal commercial treaties was a major task for the Meiji government.
en.notes: 通商条約 is a formal treaty between states on trade and navigation; 通商 is the formal word for trade between countries, 条約 a treaty under international law. One says 通商条約を結ぶ／締結する, 改正する "to revise". The word is especially well known from history (the 日米修好通商条約 of 1858, the "unequal treaties"); for modern arrangements one hears 貿易協定 or 経済連携協定 more often.

examples[].german: Tariff rates are applied based on the principle of most-favored-nation treatment.
The two countries agreed to grant each other most-favored-nation treatment.
Joining the WTO makes it possible to receive most-favored-nation treatment.
en.notes: 最恵国待遇 literally means "treatment of the most favored nation": a state must grant trade advantages that it gives to one country to all treaty partners equally. It is a basic WTO principle; typical combinations are 最恵国待遇を与える "to grant", を受ける "to receive" and 最恵国待遇の原則. The counterpart for equal treatment with domestic persons is 内国民待遇. Purely technical language from trade law and the news.

examples[].german: Preferential tariffs are applied to imports from developing countries.
Imports from this country are no longer eligible for the preferential tariff.
With a certificate of origin, you can import at the preferential tariff.
en.notes: 特恵関税 is a reduced preferential tariff that a country grants to certain partners, above all developing countries under the 一般特恵関税制度 (GSP). Watch the reading: 特恵 is read とっけい. Typical are 特恵関税を適用する／が適用される and 特恵関税の対象（外）になる. Unlike 最恵国待遇, which treats all partners equally, 特恵関税 deliberately favors individual countries.

examples[].german: With the entry into force of the economic partnership agreement, tariffs will be abolished in stages.
Thanks to the economic partnership agreement between Japan and the EU, wine can now be bought cheaply.
Under the economic partnership agreement, nurse candidates are accepted from Indonesia.
en.notes: 経済連携協定 (EPA) goes beyond a pure free trade agreement (自由貿易協定, FTA): besides reducing tariffs, it also regulates investment, services, intellectual property and the movement of people. 連携 means "cooperation, linkage". Typical are 経済連携協定を締結する／結ぶ, が発効する "takes effect" and ～に基づいて. The media mostly use the abbreviation EPA.

examples[].german: The multilateral negotiations dragged on and no agreement was reached.
In multilateral negotiations, it is difficult to reconcile the interests of all countries.
The government's policy is to aim for a solution in multilateral negotiations rather than bilaterally.
en.notes: 多国間交渉 are negotiations in which many states take part at the same time, such as the WTO trade rounds; the counterpart is 二国間交渉 "bilateral negotiations". Typical verbs are 多国間交渉に臨む "to enter negotiations", が難航する "stall", が決裂する "break down" and がまとまる "come to a conclusion". The word belongs to the language of politics and the news; 多国間 alone means "multilateral" (多国間協定, 多国間主義).

examples[].german: Investment protection is guaranteed under the bilateral agreement.
The two countries concluded a bilateral agreement on fisheries.
The working holiday program began through a bilateral agreement.
en.notes: 二国間協定 is an agreement between exactly two states; the counterpart is 多国間協定. In newspapers it is often written 2国間協定. 協定 is used more for concrete arrangements in a specific field (fisheries, air traffic, investment), 条約 for formal treaties between states. Typical: 二国間協定を結ぶ／締結する, ～に基づいて, により.

examples[].german: Export controls on advanced technology are being tightened.
Export controls on semiconductor materials worsened relations between the two countries.
Because of the poor harvest, the government decided to restrict rice exports.
en.notes: 輸出規制 covers all government restrictions on exports, such as licensing requirements for security-relevant technology or export bans during shortages. Typical verbs are 輸出規制を強化する "to tighten", を緩和する "to relax", をかける／課す and に踏み切る "to decide to ...". 規制 is broader than 制限 "limitation"; the counterpart is 輸入規制. Voluntary restrictions are called 輸出自主規制.

examples[].german: The dispute over import restrictions on agricultural products continues.
The government abolished the import restrictions on beef in stages.
When import restrictions are imposed, domestic prices tend to rise.
en.notes: 輸入制限 is the limiting of imports, for example through quantity quotas (輸入割当), bans or safeguard clauses (セーフガード). Typical verbs are 輸入制限を設ける／かける, を撤廃する "to abolish", を緩和する "to relax"; intransitive 輸入制限がかかる. 輸入規制 is somewhat broader and also includes health and safety requirements.

examples[].german: The import volume is restricted by the import quota system.
This company receives an import quota from the government every year.
The partner country asked us to expand the import quota.
en.notes: 輸入割当 is an import quota: the state decides what quantity of a good may be imported and allocates it to importers. The spelling varies between 輸入割当, 輸入割当て and 輸入割り当て; in official documents 輸入割当 (IQ) is usually used. Typical are 輸入割当を受ける "to receive a quota", 輸入割当制度 and 輸入割当の枠 "quota framework".

en.meaning: aiding and abetting; assistance (to a crime)
examples[].german: He may be punished for aiding a crime.
A doctor was charged with assisting a suicide.
The sentence for an accomplice is lighter than for the principal offender.
en.notes: 幇助 is "aiding and abetting" a crime, i.e. supporting the perpetrator without being a perpetrator oneself: 犯罪を幇助する, 自殺幇助 "assisted suicide", 幇助犯 "accomplice". Because 幇 is not a standard kanji, newspapers mostly write ほう助. The accomplice's penalty is mitigated compared with that of the principal offender 正犯; with instigation 教唆 this is not so.

examples[].german: The strict application of the rules of origin is affecting trade.
We import many parts from third countries, so we cannot meet the rules of origin.
The rules of origin differ for each agreement, so the staff in charge are confused.
en.notes: 原産地規則 are the rules of origin of a trade agreement: they determine when a good counts as a product of a treaty country and so receives tariff benefits, for example through a minimum share of domestic value added. The typical verb is 原産地規則を満たす "to meet"; also 原産地規則が厳しい／異なる. Technical language from customs and foreign trade.

examples[].german: Trade policy is drafted based on the trade statistics.
According to the trade statistics released by the Ministry of Finance, there was a trade deficit last month.
For my graduation thesis, I looked up the trade statistics of the past twenty years.
en.notes: 貿易統計 are the official statistics on imports and exports; in Japan the Ministry of Finance (財務省) publishes them monthly. Typical frames are 貿易統計によると "according to the trade statistics", 貿易統計を発表する／公表する and 貿易統計に基づいて. In the news, terms such as 貿易黒字 "trade surplus" and 貿易赤字 "trade deficit" usually follow.

examples[].german: The economic structure that depends on processing trade needs to be reviewed.
Japan, with few resources, achieved economic growth through processing trade.
Processing trade means importing raw materials, processing them into products, and exporting them.
en.notes: 加工貿易 refers to the trade model of importing raw materials, processing them into finished goods at home and exporting those. The word is known from Japanese school lessons, because it long counted as the foundation of the economy of resource-poor Japan. Typical are 加工貿易で発展する／成長する and 加工貿易に依存する. Do not confuse it with 中継貿易, where goods are resold without processing.

examples[].german: Singapore developed as a base for entrepot trade.
The Ryukyu Kingdom flourished on entrepot trade linking China and Southeast Asia.
Hong Kong is still an important port for entrepot trade.
en.notes: 中継貿易 is transit or intermediary trade: goods are brought into a country and resold unprocessed to a third country; 中継 means "relaying, relay". Typical are 中継貿易で栄える "to flourish through entrepot trade" and 中継貿易の拠点／港. Classic examples are Singapore, Hong Kong and the historical Ryukyu Kingdom. Unlike 加工貿易, no processing takes place.

examples[].german: Costs are reduced through commissioned processing overseas.
Our company takes on commissioned processing of parts from major manufacturers.
In commissioned processing, the client supplies the raw materials.
en.notes: 委託加工 is contract processing: the client (依頼主) supplies raw materials or parts, another company processes them for a processing fee (加工賃) and delivers the result back. Typical are 委託加工を請け負う "to take on", 委託加工に出す "to put out for contract processing" and 委託加工貿易 for cross-border manufacturing. 外注 "outsourcing" is more general and covers any kind of subcontracting.

examples[].german: General trading companies are actively investing in resource development.
My older brother works at a trading company and often goes on business trips abroad.
A small specialized trading company imports furniture from Europe.
en.notes: 商社 is a trading house that mediates import, export and trade in goods; a typically Japanese form of enterprise. A distinction is made between 総合商社 "general trading company" (large conglomerates with business from raw materials to foodstuffs) and 専門商社 "specialized trading company" for particular industries. Typical: 商社に勤める "to work at a trading company", 商社マン "trading company employee". A neutral term in everyday use.

examples[].german: We will build a sales network nationwide and expand our market share.
That company has a sales network all over Asia.
A small local sake brewery expanded its sales network using the internet.
en.notes: 販売網 is a company's sales network made up of branches, dealers and sales channels; 網 means "net". Typical verbs are 販売網を築く／構築する "to build", を広げる "to expand" and を持つ. Related words are 販路 "sales channel, outlet" (販路を開拓する) and 流通網 "distribution network", which stresses logistics more.

examples[].german: The disruption of the supply network hindered production activity.
Because of the semiconductor shortage, global supply chains were thrown into confusion.
The government indicated a policy of bringing supply chains for important goods back to Japan.
en.notes: 供給網 is the Japanese word for supply chain or supply network, i.e. the chain from raw material suppliers through manufacturers to retail. In newspapers it often has the same meaning as the loanword サプライチェーン, which is more common in companies. Typical combinations are 供給網が寸断される "is cut off", が混乱する and 供給網を見直す／強化する.

examples[].german: Risk is spread by diversifying the supply chain.
During the COVID pandemic, many companies reviewed their supply chains.
Our company set a goal of reducing carbon dioxide emissions across the entire supply chain.
en.notes: サプライチェーン is the loanword for the supply chain from raw material procurement to the end customer; its Japanese counterpart 供給網 sounds more official. Very common in business language, also in compounds such as サプライチェーン・マネジメント (SCM). Typical verbs are サプライチェーンを見直す "to review", を強化する and が寸断される. It is written with or without a middle dot (サプライ・チェーン).

examples[].german: Crude oil trading is active on the commodity futures market.
He incurred large losses in commodity futures trading.
Please be careful about telephone solicitations for commodity futures.
en.notes: 商品先物 are futures contracts on commodities such as oil, gold or grain; 商品 here means "commodity" in the exchange sense, 先物 "futures contract". It mostly appears in compounds: 商品先物取引 "commodity futures trading", 商品先物市場 "commodity futures market". The counterpart is 金融先物 "financial futures". Because of the high risk, the word is often associated for private individuals with aggressive sales calls (勧誘).

examples[].german: Self-defense was recognized and he was acquitted.
Because the other person had hit him first, he claimed self-defense.
Because the counterattack went too far, it was ruled excessive defense rather than self-defense.
en.notes: 正当防衛 is "self-defense": defending against an imminent unlawful attack, which goes unpunished. Literally, 正当 means "justified" and 防衛 means "defense". Typical: 正当防衛が認められる／成立する, 正当防衛を主張する. If the defense goes too far, it is called 過剰防衛 "excessive self-defense". To be distinguished from this is 緊急避難, where a danger is averted at the expense of an uninvolved third party.

examples[].german: Sign the written agreement to finalize the terms of the transaction.
When I took out the loan, I submitted a bank transaction agreement.
Please read the contents of the agreement carefully before you put your seal on it.
en.notes: 約定書 is a written agreement recording the terms of a transaction; 約定 (やくじょう) means "agreement, arrangement" and, in securities trading, also "execution of an order". The word is clearly more formal and rarer than the general 契約書 "contract" and appears mainly in fixed expressions such as 銀行取引約定書 or 約定書を交わす "to exchange an agreement".

examples[].german: The transparency of non-competitive contracts should be increased.
The construction work was ordered by non-competitive contract, without a tender.
For small-value purchases, non-competitive contracts are permitted.
en.notes: 随意契約 is a term from public procurement: an agency awards a contract directly to a chosen partner without a tender; 随意 means "at will, at one's discretion". The counterpart is 競争入札 or 一般競争入札 "open competitive bidding". Typical are 随意契約を結ぶ and 随意契約で発注する; in the news it often appears in connection with a lack of transparency. Short form in bureaucratic jargon: 随契.

examples[].german: Goods are delivered cash on delivery.
As a payment method, you can choose credit card or cash on delivery.
With cash on delivery, a separate fee is charged.
en.notes: 代金引換 is payment by cash on delivery: the recipient pays for the goods to the delivery person upon delivery. In everyday speech one almost always says the short form 代引き（だいびき）; 代金引換 appears more in order forms and terms of business. Typical are 代金引換で送る／支払う and 代金引換手数料 "cash-on-delivery fee". Do not confuse it with 着払い, where the recipient pays only the shipping costs.

examples[].german: The collection rate on credit sales is declining.
Liquor stores in the old days sold on credit to regular customers.
We do not accept credit sales at our store.
en.notes: 掛け売り is selling on credit or "on account": the customer takes the goods right away and pays later, for example at the end of the month. 掛け here stands for "credit, running a tab"; the outstanding claim is called 売掛金, and the buyer's side 掛け買い. The opposite is 現金売り "cash sale". Also written 掛売り; possible as a する-verb (掛け売りする). Colloquially one says ツケで売る.

examples[].german: We ask for prepayment on the first transaction.
At this language school, tuition is paid three months in advance.
I asked the president whether I could get part of my salary paid in advance.
en.notes: 前払い is payment in advance, before goods are delivered or a service is provided; the opposite is 後払い. As a する-verb: 授業料を前払いする. Fixed combinations are 前払い金 "advance payment, down payment", 前払い制 and 前払いをお願いする. In formal texts 前納 is also used. For salary one speaks of 給料の前払い "salary advance".

examples[].german: Expensive items can be purchased in installments.
I bought the computer in 12 installments.
Paying in installments may incur fees.
en.notes: 分割払い is payment in installments; the opposite is 一括払い. Typical are 分割払いで買う, 分割払いにする and phrases like 12回の分割払い "in twelve installments"; one also says 分割で払う for short. With credit cards, one chooses at the register between 一回払い, 分割払い and リボ払い (revolving payment). Installment payments often come with fees (手数料).

examples[].german: A discount is applied for payment in full.
"Would you like to pay in a single payment?"
I don't have enough savings to buy a car in one lump sum.
en.notes: 一括払い means paying the entire amount at once; the opposite is 分割払い. With credit cards it is also called 一回払い: the amount is charged in full on the next statement, so it is not necessarily paid "immediately". Typical are 一括払いで買う／支払う and 一括払いにする. 一括 alone means "bundled together, in one piece" (一括購入, 一括処理).

examples[].german: The upper limit of real estate brokerage fees is set by law.
When I rented the room, I paid a brokerage fee equal to one month's rent.
This site is popular because it has no brokerage fee.
en.notes: 仲介手数料 is the fee an intermediary receives for bringing a deal about, most commonly the agent's commission when renting or buying real estate. For rental apartments in Japan, it is limited by law to one month's rent (plus tax). Typical are 仲介手数料を払う, がかかる and 仲介手数料無料 "no brokerage fee". 仲介 means "mediation", 手数料 "fee".

examples[].german: Warehouse storage fees are rising and have become a factor in higher costs.
After I left my luggage for a week, I was charged a storage fee.
If pickup is delayed, a storage fee is charged for each day.
en.notes: 保管料 is the fee for keeping items in storage, such as goods in a warehouse, luggage, vehicles or documents; -料 forms fee words, as in 使用料 or 入場料. Typical are 保管料がかかる "a storage fee is charged", 保管料を払う／請求する. In warehousing it appears alongside 荷役料 "handling fee". The related verb is 保管する "to keep, to store".

examples[].german: The key issue was whether the requirements of necessity were met.
The nearby park is designated as an emergency evacuation site.
This tax cut is an emergency measure to support the economy.
en.notes: 緊急避難 literally means "emergency escape". In criminal law it is "justifiable necessity": one averts an acute danger and thereby harms the legal interests of an uninvolved person, for example by entering someone else's house while fleeing a fire. In disaster management it means "emergency evacuation": 指定緊急避難場所 "designated emergency evacuation site". Figuratively, 緊急避難的な措置 stands for an "emergency measure, stopgap solution".

examples[].german: Port cargo handling work is being automated.
Because of the typhoon, cargo handling at the port stopped temporarily.
At the warehouse, loading and unloading is done using forklifts.
en.notes: 荷役 is the loading and unloading of freight, especially in ports, on ships and in warehouses; it is read にやく. Typical are 荷役作業 "cargo handling work", 荷役業者, 荷役機械 and 荷役を行う. As an intransitive する-verb (荷役する) it is rare. Do not confuse it with 荷造り "packing" or 荷物 "luggage"; 荷役 is a technical word from logistics and shipping.

examples[].german: We entrusted the import procedures to a customs broker.
The customs broker prepared the documents, so the procedures were finished quickly.
If you want to work at a customs brokerage, a customs specialist qualification gives you an edge.
en.notes: 通関業者 is a licensed customs service provider who handles customs declarations and other formalities on behalf of importers and exporters; they are often freight forwarders. Licensing is governed by the 通関業法, and the qualified specialist within the firm is called 通関士. Typical are 通関業者に依頼する／委託する. 通関 means "customs clearance", 業者 "tradesperson, firm".

examples[].german: Cargo is temporarily stored in a bonded warehouse.
Imported cargo is kept in a bonded warehouse until the customs duty is paid.
Wine is stored duty-free in the bonded warehouse at the airport.
en.notes: 保税倉庫 is a bonded warehouse in which imported goods may be stored without duty until they are imported or re-exported; 保税 means "under customs bond, duty suspended". The umbrella term for such areas is 保税地域. Typical are 保税倉庫に保管する／搬入する. A technical word from customs and logistics.

en.meaning: free trade area; free trade zone
examples[].german: The establishment of the free trade area has stimulated trade within the region.
In the ASEAN Free Trade Area, tariffs within the region have fallen to almost zero.
In Okinawa, there is a free trade zone where companies can import raw materials without tariffs.
en.notes: 自由貿易地域 has two meanings: a free trade area between several states that abolish tariffs among themselves (ASEAN自由貿易地域), and a designated area within a country into which goods may be imported duty-free and processed (as in Okinawa). Unlike a 関税同盟 "customs union", in a free trade area each country keeps its own external tariffs. Typical: 自由貿易地域を設ける／設立する.

examples[].german: Foreign companies are being invited to the special economic zone.
Shenzhen was designated a special economic zone in 1980 and developed rapidly.
In special economic zones, preferential treatment in taxes and regulations is available.
en.notes: 経済特区 (short for 経済特別区) is a special economic zone in which taxes, tariffs and regulations are relaxed to attract investment; Shenzhen in China is famous. Typical combinations are 経済特区に指定する／される, 経済特区を設ける and 企業を誘致する "to attract companies". In Japan, similar arrangements are more often called 構造改革特区 or 国家戦略特区; in general it is shortened to 特区.

examples[].german: The increase in foreign direct investment is affecting domestic employment.
The company is building factories in Vietnam and expanding its direct investment.
To attract direct investment from abroad, the government lowered the corporate tax.
en.notes: 直接投資 is investment by which one founds a company abroad or takes a stake that gives influence over management, for example by building factories. Common are 海外直接投資 / 対外直接投資 "outward direct investment" and 対内直接投資 "inward direct investment" (FDI). The opposite term is 間接投資 (portfolio investment). Typical: 直接投資を拡大する／呼び込む.

examples[].german: Take part in the growth of emerging economies through portfolio investment.
Acquiring shares without involvement in management is classified as portfolio investment.
With indirect investment through investment trusts, you can start with a small amount.
en.notes: In economics, 間接投資 refers to investment in foreign stocks or bonds without influence on management, i.e. portfolio investment (also 証券投資); the opposite term is 直接投資. In retail-investor jargon, 間接投資 also means investing through funds (投資信託) instead of buying individual stocks directly. Typical: 間接投資を通じて, 間接投資に分類される.

examples[].german: Set up a local subsidiary and enter the overseas market in earnest.
He was posted to the Thai local subsidiary as its president.
Unlike a branch, a local subsidiary is an independent company under local law.
en.notes: 現地法人 is a company of a foreign firm established under the law of the host country, usually a subsidiary. Unlike a 支店 "branch" or a 駐在員事務所 "representative office", it is an independent legal entity. Typical are 現地法人を設立する, 現地法人に赴任する "to be posted to the overseas subsidiary" and a country name in front (タイの現地法人).

examples[].german: Share the risks through a joint venture with a local company.
The two companies announced that they would launch a joint venture for batteries.
Because of differences in management policy, the joint venture was dissolved after three years.
en.notes: 合弁事業 is a joint venture in which two or more companies pool capital; 合弁 means "joint capital participation". The company founded for it is called 合弁会社. Typical verbs are 合弁事業を立ち上げる "to launch", を解消する "to dissolve" and 合弁で設立する. In business language ジョイントベンチャー (JV) is also common.

examples[].german: Protecting intellectual property rights is an important issue in international trade.
The company was sued for infringing another company's intellectual property rights.
Patents and copyrights are typical examples of intellectual property rights.
en.notes: 知的所有権 are rights to intellectual creations such as patents (特許権), copyrights (著作権) and trademark rights (商標権). Today the official standard term is 知的財産権, shortened to 知財; 知的所有権 is the older translation, but it is still found in texts on international trade. Typical verbs are 知的所有権を侵害する "to infringe" and を保護する "to protect".

examples[].german: The prosecutor filed an indictment.
The statute of limitations for murder was abolished in 2010.
The court dismissed the prosecution because of a procedural illegality.
en.notes: 公訴 is the "public prosecution" brought by the public prosecutor's office in criminal proceedings: 公訴を提起する is the formal variant of 起訴する. Important terms are 公訴時効 "statute of limitations (for prosecution)" and 公訴棄却 "dismissal of the prosecution for procedural defects". Careful when listening: the identically pronounced 控訴 means "appeal" against a judgment. In everyday speech one almost always says 起訴.

examples[].german: Measures to stop the distribution of counterfeit goods are being strengthened.
The designer bag I bought online turned out to be a counterfeit.
A large quantity of counterfeit goods was found at customs and confiscated.
en.notes: 模倣品 are imitations that copy the design, brand or styling of an original product. In official texts it often appears as the pair 模倣品・海賊版 "counterfeits and pirated copies"; 偽造品 stresses the criminal forgery, and colloquially one says 偽物 or コピー商品. Typical are 模倣品が出回る "are in circulation", 模倣品を取り締まる and 模倣品対策.

examples[].german: Parallel-imported goods can be obtained more cheaply than genuine authorized products.
Parallel-imported goods may not be covered by the manufacturer's warranty.
That store parallel-imports foreign brand cosmetics and sells them cheaply.
en.notes: 並行輸入 is the import of genuine brand goods bypassing the official distribution channels (正規代理店); the goods imported this way are called 並行輸入品, as opposed to 正規品. They are not counterfeits (模倣品), but warranty and customer service may be limited. As a transitive する-verb: 化粧品を並行輸入する.

examples[].german: Import semi-finished products and carry out the final processing in Japan.
Stock of semi-finished products increased until the warehouse was full.
In this factory, semi-finished products are assembled into finished products.
en.notes: 半製品 are semi-finished goods: products that have gone through part of manufacturing and are to be processed further, but can also be sold as such. In accounting they are distinguished from 仕掛品 "work in process", which are not yet saleable. The sequence is 原材料 → 半製品 → 製品／完成品. A technical word from industry and accounting.

examples[].german: Exhibit at an international trade fair and introduce new products.
A furniture trade fair will be held in Tokyo next month.
We started doing business with a company we met at the trade fair.
en.notes: 見本市 is a trade fair where companies exhibit products to business customers; note the reading みほんいち. Typical are 見本市に出展する "to exhibit", 見本市が開かれる／開催される and 国際見本市. In current usage 展示会 and トレードショー are also common; 博覧会, by contrast, means a large exhibition for the general public (expo).

examples[].german: Send a product sample and have them confirm the quality.
When I requested a product sample, it arrived the next day.
We displayed product samples at the trade fair booth.
en.notes: 商品見本 is a product sample that is sent or shown to customers or dealers to check quality and appearance. In everyday speech one usually just says サンプル or 見本; 商品見本 sounds more businesslike. Typical verbs are 商品見本を送る／送付する, を請求する "to request" and を並べる "to display". Free samples for end customers are more often called 試供品.

examples[].german: Thorough quality control is the foundation of trust.
To ensure strict quality control, we inspect every product.
My older sister works in the quality control department of a food manufacturer.
en.notes: 品質管理 is quality control or quality management in production, QC in English. Typical combinations are 品質管理を徹底する "to carry out thoroughly", を強化する and 品質管理部 "quality control department". Related is 品質保証 "quality assurance" (QA), which stresses the guarantee to the customer more. Neutral; commonplace in industry and the food sector.

examples[].german: The speed of complaint handling affects customer satisfaction.
The customer at the next table complained that there was a hair in the food.
The same complaint about the new product has come in from customers many times.
en.notes: In Japanese, クレーム almost always means a customer complaint, often with a demand for replacement - not a legal "claim" as in English (for that: 請求, 損害賠償請求). Typical are クレームをつける "to complain", クレームが来る/入る and クレーム対応 "complaint handling"; someone who constantly complains without justification is a クレーマー. More neutral and general is 苦情 (also for noise among neighbors), stronger is 抗議 "protest".

examples[].german: The delay in delivery was exempted from liability under the force majeure clause.
Delays caused by typhoons are force majeure and therefore not eligible for compensation.
Since the child suddenly ran out into the road, that accident was unavoidable.
en.notes: 不可抗力 is "force majeure": an event that cannot be prevented despite all care (natural disasters, war, strikes). In contracts it appears in 不可抗力条項 "force majeure clause" and in phrases like 不可抗力による損害 or 不可抗力の場合は免責とする. In everyday speech too, one says 〜は不可抗力だった "that could not be helped" to clear someone of blame. 天災, by contrast, refers to the natural disaster itself. Register: written/legal, slightly elevated in daily life.

examples[].german: Pay royalties for the use of the patent.
Franchisees pay 5% of their sales to headquarters every month as royalties.
If you use that character on your products, royalties will be incurred.
en.notes: ロイヤルティー is the license fee for using patents, trademarks, characters or a franchise system: ロイヤルティーを支払う/受け取る, ロイヤルティーが発生する "royalties are incurred". The spelling varies widely; ロイヤリティー is at least as common. Note: the same katakana form also means "loyalty" (顧客ロイヤルティー "customer loyalty") - context decides. Japanese equivalents are 使用料 or 特許料; authors' royalties for books are called 印税.

examples[].german: Seek overseas expansion by granting technology licenses.
The license for this software has expired, so I have to renew it.
I got my diving license in Okinawa.
en.notes: ライセンス is a license in the broad sense: for software, patents, trademarks (ライセンス契約, ライセンス料, ライセンスを取得する/供与する "to obtain/grant", ライセンスが切れる "to expire"). Colloquially also for private certificates such as a diving license. Official permits, by contrast, are usually called 免許 (運転免許 "driver's license") or 許可, and professional qualifications 資格. Register: neutral, especially in business and IT.

examples[].german: This problem should be settled in a civil trial.
The police did not act, citing the principle of non-intervention in civil matters.
No charges were filed in the criminal case, but the bereaved family sought damages in a civil suit.
en.notes: 民事 refers to everything belonging to civil law, i.e. disputes between private persons or companies: 民事裁判, 民事訴訟, 民事事件, 民事責任. The opposite term is 刑事 "criminal". Well known is 民事不介入, the principle that the police do not interfere in private legal disputes. One often reads that someone was not prosecuted criminally, but that damages are being demanded 民事で (in a civil suit).

examples[].german: The store network was expanded rapidly using the franchise model.
He quit his company and joined a convenience store franchise.
Before signing a franchise contract, it is better to check carefully what support the headquarters provides.
en.notes: フランチャイズ refers to the franchise system: the headquarters (本部) provides the brand and know-how, and the franchisee (加盟店, オーナー) pays fees. Typical: フランチャイズ契約, フランチャイズ店, フランチャイズ方式, 〜のフランチャイズに加盟する "to become a franchisee of ..."; abbreviated FC in technical texts. In sports, フランチャイズ also refers to a pro team's home location, though in everyday speech 本拠地 is more commonly used for that.

examples[].german: We acquired the exclusive sales rights in Japan.
The company holds the exclusive domestic sales rights for a certain Italian luxury wine.
The contract says we lose the exclusive sales rights if we fail to achieve our sales targets.
en.notes: 独占販売権 consists of 独占 "monopoly, exclusivity" and 販売権 "sales right": the exclusive right to sell a product in a territory. Typical: 〜の独占販売権を取得する/持つ/与える/失う, often with a territory such as 日本における/国内の. The holder is frequently a 総代理店. The counterpart is a non-exclusive sales right (非独占の販売権). Register: contract and business language.

examples[].german: Develop business as the sole agent for the Asian region.
These watches are imported through the Japanese sole agent of a Swiss manufacturer.
For repair requests, please contact the support desk of the sole agent.
en.notes: 総代理店 consists of 総 "general, overall" and 代理店 "agency, agent": the company that a (usually foreign) manufacturer appoints as sole general representative for a country or region, often with 独占販売権. Below it stand ordinary 販売代理店 or 特約店. On packaging and websites one often reads 日本総代理店 or 輸入総代理店. Register: business language.

examples[].german: The expansion of e-commerce is affecting conventional retail.
Using e-commerce, we sell our products to customers overseas as well.
In e-commerce, protecting personal information is a major issue.
en.notes: 電子商取引 is the technical term for "e-commerce", i.e. trade over the internet between companies or with end customers. In official and business texts the abbreviation EC or eコマース often appears; in everyday speech one simply says ネット通販 or ネットショッピング. Typical combinations: 電子商取引の市場規模, 電子商取引を利用する, 電子商取引の拡大. 商取引 alone means "commercial transaction".

examples[].german: Cross-border trade over the internet is increasing.
In cross-border transactions, you need to check tariffs and delivery times in advance.
Regulation of cross-border cryptoasset transactions is being tightened in many countries.
en.notes: 越境取引 combines 越境 "crossing a border" with 取引 "deal, transaction": cross-border transactions, especially in online commerce (越境EC "cross-border e-commerce") and in finance (越境取引の規制). On its own, 越境 often means illegally crossing a border, but in compounds it is neutral. More general are 国際取引 or 貿易 "foreign trade". Register: press and technical language.

examples[].german: Modernizing the wholesale market has become an issue.
At the Toyosu wholesale market, tuna auctions are held every morning.
Chefs go to the wholesale market from early morning in search of fresh vegetables.
en.notes: 卸売市場 is the wholesale market where producers, wholesalers (卸売業者) and intermediate wholesalers (仲卸) trade fish, vegetables, fruit or flowers; the 中央卸売市場 in 豊洲 (formerly 築地) is well known. 市場 is read しじょう here, but in everyday speech one often says simply 市場（いちば） or 魚市場. The counterpart of wholesale 卸売 is retail 小売.

examples[].german: The auction of marine products takes place early in the morning.
At the first auction of the New Year, a single tuna fetched over 100 million yen.
The intermediate wholesaler carried the sea urchin he had just won at auction into his shop.
en.notes: 競り is the auction customary at fish and vegetable markets; also written せり or セリ. Typical: 競りにかける "to auction", 競りが行われる, 競り落とす "to win at auction" and 初競り, the first auction of the year, often with spectacular tuna prices. For art, online or forced auctions, one more often says オークション or 競売（きょうばい）. The underlying verb 競る means "to compete, to outbid each other".

examples[].german: Cut out the middlemen and reduce distribution costs.
Since no middleman is involved, you can buy directly from the farmer cheaply.
Because several intermediary companies are involved, the wages of workers on site are low.
en.notes: 中間業者 are the firms between manufacturer and end customer, i.e. middlemen.
