The word mostly appears in connection with cost cutting: 中間業者を排除する/通さない/省く, colloquially 中抜き "cutting out the middleman", and 中間マージン "middleman margin". 仲介業者 is more of a broker (e.g. in real estate), and ブローカー often sounds derogatory. Register: neutral to written.

examples[].german: It is cheaper to buy from the manufacturer's direct sales site.
This farm sells the apples it harvests directly to consumers.
Since switching to direct sales, the profit margin has improved greatly.
en.notes: 直販 is the short form of 直接販売: manufacturers or producers sell directly to customers without wholesale and retail. Typical: 直販サイト "manufacturer's online shop", 直販店, 産地直販, also as a する-verb: 野菜を直販する. Very similar is 直売, which you know especially from farm stands (直売所); 通販, by contrast, refers to the mail-order channel, not the seller.

examples[].german: Mail-order sales are increasing year by year.
My grandmother bought an exercise machine through TV shopping.
Be careful: the cooling-off system does not apply to mail-order sales.
en.notes: 通信販売 is mail order: ordering by catalog, telephone, television or internet, with delivery to your home. In daily life one almost always uses the short form 通販 (ネット通販, テレビ通販, 通販で買う); the full form appears in legal texts and formal notices. Important: in Japan no statutory right of withdrawal (クーリング・オフ) applies to 通信販売 - unlike with 訪問販売; the seller's return policy is what counts.

examples[].german: An investigation was opened as a criminal case.
A detective went around the neighborhood to question people.
Children under fourteen are not held criminally responsible.
en.notes: 刑事 has two meanings. As a prefix it means "criminal, criminal-law": 刑事事件, 刑事裁判, 刑事責任, as opposed to 民事 "civil". In everyday life, however, 刑事 is above all the "detective", the plainclothes investigator, known from 刑事ドラマ "crime series"; as a form of address one hears 刑事さん. The uniformed police officer, by contrast, is called 警察官 or colloquially お巡りさん.

examples[].german: Consumer protection in door-to-door sales has been strengthened.
I was made to buy an expensive water purifier from a door-to-door salesperson.
I put a sticker on the front door saying no door-to-door sales.
en.notes: 訪問販売 is selling at the customer's door or in the customer's home, a legal term in the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions (特定商取引法), for which a cooling-off right (クーリング・オフ) applies. Typical: 訪問販売員, 悪質な訪問販売, 訪問販売を断る, and on door signs 訪問販売お断り. Do not confuse it with 直販 "direct sales" by the manufacturer or 通信販売 "mail-order sales".

examples[].german: Reduce inventory risk through the consignment sales model.
A neighborhood general store sells my handmade accessories on consignment.
Since it is consignment, unsold items can be returned.
en.notes: 委託販売 is selling on consignment: the owner (委託者) leaves goods with a dealer who sells them for a commission; unsold goods are returned, and the inventory risk stays with the owner. Typical: 委託販売で売る, 〜を委託販売してもらう, 委託販売契約, 委託販売手数料. Common in bookselling, at second-hand shops and for handmade goods. The opposite term is 買い取り "purchase on one's own account".

examples[].german: Resale price maintenance is in principle prohibited under the Antimonopoly Act.
Books and newspapers are an exception, and resale price maintenance is permitted.
If a manufacturer forbids retailers to discount, it may amount to resale price maintenance.
en.notes: 再販売価格維持 is a term from competition law: the manufacturer dictates the resale price to the dealer (vertical price fixing). In Japan this is in principle prohibited under the 独占禁止法; exceptions apply to books, newspapers and sound recordings (再販制度, 再販 for short). Common phrases: 再販売価格維持行為, 再販売価格の拘束. Register: very formal, legal.

examples[].german: The sales promotion campaign increased sales by twenty percent.
To promote sales, we held a tasting event at the store.
Next term, the sales promotion budget will be cut and the money diverted to advertising.
en.notes: 販売促進 is sales promotion in marketing: promotions, coupons, samples, tastings, displays. In everyday business one almost always hears the short form 販促 (販促品 "promotional items", 販促キャンペーン); the full form appears more in texts, e.g. 販売促進費, 販売促進活動, 〜の販売促進を図る. In Japanese, 販促 is usually distinguished from 広告 "advertising in media"; as a loanword プロモーション is also common.

examples[].german: Develop new sales channels overseas.
As a result of expanding our sales channels through online shopping, orders now come in from all over the country.
After losing a major customer, securing sales channels became urgent.
en.notes: 販路 is the sales channel or sales market through which a company sells its goods. Fixed combinations: 販路を開拓する "to open up", 販路を拡大する/広げる, 販路を確保する, 新たな販路, 海外販路. 流通経路, by contrast, means the whole distribution chain from manufacturer to customer, and 市場 the market as a whole. Register: business language, frequent in the news.

examples[].german: The opening of a large store changed the surrounding trade area.
The trade area of a convenience store is generally said to be about a 500-meter radius.
Before opening, we surveyed the population and competing stores in the trade area.
en.notes: 商圏 is the catchment area of a shop or town, i.e. the area customers come from. Typical: 商圏が広い/狭い, 商圏人口, 商圏を分析する/調査する, 〜を商圏とする, 半径〜キロの商圏. Do not confuse it with 商店街 "shopping street" or the identically read 商権 "commercial rights". Register: technical language from retail and site planning.

en.meaning: terms of trade; terms and conditions of a deal
examples[].german: Both sides agreed on the terms of the transaction.
A new supplier offered us more favorable terms.
It is prohibited to impose one-sidedly unfavorable terms on subcontractors.
en.notes: 取引条件 are the conditions of a specific deal: price, payment terms (支払条件), delivery date (納期), quantities. Typical: 取引条件を提示する/交渉する/見直す/変更する, 有利な/不利な取引条件. The "general terms and conditions" as standard text, by contrast, are called 約款 or 利用規約; 契約条件 stresses the contract clauses. Register: business language.

examples[].german: The bilateral trading volume has set a new record.
Due to the weak yen, currency trading volume surged this month.
Business volume with the major supermarket chain accounts for thirty percent of our sales.
en.notes: 取引高 (with voiced だか) is the trading or business volume between partners, countries or in a market: 取引高が増える/減る, 取引高が過去最高を更新する, 〜との取引高. Similar is 取扱高 "handled volume". For the trading volume of individual stocks, one more often says 出来高 (number of shares) or 売買代金 (value). Register: business and press language.

examples[].german: The granting of rebates can become a breeding ground for improper transactions.
Stores that achieve their annual sales target are paid a rebate by the manufacturer.
It came to light that the person in charge had been receiving kickbacks from a contractor.
en.notes: リベート has two sides: legitimate is the after-the-fact rebate a manufacturer pays to dealers depending on sales volume (formally 販売奨励金); in scandal reports, however, it means "bribe, kickback" (リベートを受け取る/渡す). Unlike 値引き or 割引, it is not a price reduction at purchase but a later payment. Register: business language, negative in the second sense.

examples[].german: Pass the rise in raw material costs on to the selling price.
All selling prices in our store include tax.
If the yen stays weak, we will have no choice but to review the selling prices of imported goods.
en.notes: 販売価格 is the price at which a product is sold. Distinguish 定価 "fixed list price", 希望小売価格 "suggested retail price", 仕入れ価格 "purchase price" and the colloquial 売値. Typical: 販売価格を設定する/引き上げる/改定する/見直す, 〜を販売価格に転嫁する "to pass on to the selling price". Register: business language, also on price tags and notices.

examples[].german: The residents filed an administrative lawsuit and demanded that the permit be revoked.
It is not easy to bring an administrative lawsuit against the state.
Plaintiffs rarely win in administrative lawsuits.
en.notes: 行政訴訟 is a lawsuit against actions of the state or an authority, for example to have a permit or an administrative decision revoked; it is regulated in the 行政事件訴訟法. Typical: 行政訴訟を起こす／提起する, 国を相手に行政訴訟. Alongside 民事訴訟 "civil lawsuit" and 刑事訴訟 "criminal trial", it is the third major type of proceeding. For citizens, such suits are considered difficult to win.

examples[].german: Review the wholesale price between manufacturers and wholesalers.
Although the wholesale price has gone up, the in-store price has been left unchanged.
In exchange for buying in bulk, we got them to lower the wholesale price.
en.notes: 仕切り価格 (also 仕切価格) is an industry term for the price at which the manufacturer supplies the wholesale trade, or the wholesaler supplies the retailer - the transfer price to the trade. 仕切り comes from 仕切る "to settle accounts". The difference between 仕切り価格 and the shop price is the dealer's margin (マージン). Closer to everyday speech is 卸値 "wholesale price"; an intra-group "transfer price", on the other hand, is called 移転価格.

examples[].german: They announced a policy of keeping the suggested retail price unchanged.
I was able to buy this camera for as much as 20,000 yen below the suggested retail price.
The suggested retail price is the guideline price a manufacturer gives to retailers.
en.notes: 希望小売価格 is the manufacturer's "suggested retail price"; in full it is often メーカー希望小売価格. Retailers like to advertise discounts from it: 希望小売価格の3割引き. Typical verbs: 希望小売価格を設定する/据え置く/改定する. When a manufacturer gives up making a suggestion, it is called オープン価格. 小売 (こうり) means "retail".

examples[].german: The manufacturer's suggested retail price was abolished, and they moved to open pricing.
This product has an open price, so the price differs from store to store.
Many home appliances are sold at open prices.
en.notes: オープン価格 means that the manufacturer states no recommended selling price and each retailer sets the price freely. This is especially common for electronics and home appliances in Japan; in catalogs it then simply says 価格：オープン. The counterpart is (メーカー)希望小売価格. Typical: オープン価格に移行する, オープン価格で販売する. It does not mean "an open, negotiable price".

examples[].german: Improve cash flow by shortening the collection period for accounts receivable.
A client went bankrupt, and we can no longer collect the accounts receivable.
At the end of the month, I check the accounts receivable balance to make sure no invoice has been missed.
en.notes: 売掛金 is an accounting term: money that customers still owe after a sale on credit (掛け売り) - accounts receivable. The counterpart is 買掛金 "accounts payable". Typical: 売掛金を回収する "to collect", 売掛金の回収期間, 未回収の売掛金, 売掛金が焦げ付く "to become uncollectible". 掛け alone means "on credit" (掛けで買う). Register: accounting.

examples[].german: Extend the payment term of accounts payable to give cash flow some breathing room.
We pay our accounts payable all together at the end of the month.
As purchasing increased, the accounts payable on the balance sheet also swelled.
en.notes: 買掛金 is the counterpart of 売掛金: amounts a company still owes its suppliers after a purchase on credit (掛けで仕入れる) - accounts payable. Typical: 買掛金を支払う/決済する, 買掛金の支払期限, 買掛金が膨らむ. Other outstanding payments, for example for equipment, are called 未払金, and bank loans 借入金. Register: accounting.

examples[].german: Raise the inventory turnover rate and run the business efficiently.
This shop has a high turnover at lunch, so it makes a profit even at low prices.
To raise the turnover of the parking lot, the daily maximum fee was abolished.
en.notes: 回転率 indicates how often something "turns over" in a period: in business administration 在庫回転率 "inventory turnover" and 資本回転率, and in restaurants and parking lots how often seats or spaces are refilled (客席回転率). Typical: 回転率が高い/低い, 回転率を上げる/高める. Colloquially 回転 is often enough: この店は回転が速い. Register: technical, but also common in everyday speech.

examples[].german: Dispose of slow-selling items early to reduce inventory costs.
We identified the slow sellers from POS data and removed them from the shelves.
Even a product that was a hot seller quickly becomes a slow seller once the fad is over.
en.notes: 死に筋 is retail jargon for items that hardly sell - literally something like "dead line", where 筋 means "type, line". The opposite is 売れ筋. Typical: 死に筋商品, 死に筋をカットする/外す/洗い出す, often in connection with checkout data. More neutral are 不人気商品 or 売れ行きの悪い商品; 売れ残り, by contrast, are concrete leftover items. Register: retail jargon, sounds somewhat harsh.

examples[].german: Expand the lineup of best-selling products.
I asked the clerk what is selling well right now before choosing.
That rice cooker took first place in the online shop's best-seller ranking.
en.notes: 売れ筋 are the items that are currently selling well (売れる + 筋 "line, type"). Typical: 売れ筋商品, 売れ筋ランキング, and in a shop 今の売れ筋はどれですか. The opposite is 死に筋. Similar are 人気商品 and ヒット商品; ベストセラー is used mainly for books. Register: neutral, very common in shops and online stores.

examples[].german: A wide product selection is the key to attracting customers.
This bookstore has a good selection of specialist books, so I often use it.
The supermarket in front of the station has a small selection, and I can hardly find what I want.
en.notes: 品揃え is the assortment or selection of goods in a shop; also written 品ぞろえ. Typical: 品揃えが豊富だ/いい/少ない, 品揃えを充実させる/増やす, 〜の品揃えが自慢だ. It does not fit for a range of options one chooses between in general - for that one says 選択肢. Register: neutral, very common in daily life.

examples[].german: Optimizing shelf allocation contributes to higher sales.
In line with the spring new products, we changed the shelf allocation in the beverage section.
Manufacturers' sales reps negotiate over shelf allocation so that their products are placed at eye level.
en.notes: 棚割り (also 棚割) is retail jargon for shelf planning: which products stand on which shelf, in what quantity and at what height - places at eye level count as the ゴールデンゾーン "golden zone". Typical: 棚割りを変更する/見直す/作成する, 棚割り表 "planogram". The display itself is called 陳列. Manufacturers negotiate with retailers for good spots in the 棚割り.

examples[].german: The date of entry into force was set by cabinet order.
Yokohama is one of the government-designated cities.
The government amended the ordinance and eased the regulations.
en.notes: 政令 is a "government ordinance" issued by the Cabinet to implement a law. The order of rank is 法律 (from the Diet) > 政令 (Cabinet) > 省令 (an individual ministry); 条例 are local regulations of local governments. Typical: 政令で定める, 政令を改正する. Very common is 政令指定都市, a "large city designated by government ordinance" with extended powers, such as Yokohama or Osaka.

examples[].german: The consumer price index rose compared with the previous year.
The consumer price index is released every month by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.
Pension payments are revised every year based on the consumer price index and other factors.
en.notes: 消費者物価指数 is the consumer price index (物価 "price level", 指数 "index"), often simply CPI in the news. In Japan it is published monthly by the 総務省; the core measure of inflation is the index 生鮮食品を除く総合 (all items excluding fresh food). Typical: 消費者物価指数が上昇する/下落する, 前年同月比〜％上昇. For prices between companies there is the 企業物価指数 (formerly 卸売物価指数). Register: business and press language.

examples[].german: Trends in the wholesale price index lead consumer prices.
In Japan, the wholesale price index was renamed the corporate goods price index in 2002.
Following high crude oil prices, the wholesale price index rose sharply.
en.notes: 卸売物価指数 is the wholesale price index, which measures prices in trade between companies; it is regarded as a leading indicator for consumer prices (消費者物価指数). In Japan the Bank of Japan renamed it 企業物価指数 in 2002, so the old name now appears mainly in older texts or for other countries. Typical: 卸売物価指数が上昇する, 〜の動向. Register: economic technical language.

examples[].german: Japan's own distinctive business practices are keeping foreign companies from entering.
Moves have emerged to review the industry practice of free returns.
The Fair Trade Commission called for correction of business practices that lead to bullying of subcontractors.
en.notes: 商慣行 are the business practices actually followed in an industry or country. The word often appears critically: 不透明な商慣行, 商慣行を見直す/改める/是正する, 日本独自の商慣行. The nearly synonymous 商慣習 stresses the traditional custom and is also a legal term (商慣習法 "commercial customary law"). Register: business and press language.

examples[].german: Differences in commercial customs can become a barrier to international trade.
In Japan, there is a commercial custom of sending gifts to business partners at midsummer and year-end.
Where the contract has no provision, judgment is made in accordance with commercial custom.
en.notes: 商慣習 is commercial custom, i.e. what customarily applies in trade even without a written rule. Legally it matters because contracts are interpreted according to 商慣習 where there are gaps (商慣習法 "commercial customary law"). Typical: 商慣習の違い, 商慣習に従う, 〜という商慣習がある. The nearly synonymous 商慣行 stresses the lived, often criticized practice. Register: written, business and law.

examples[].german: Reduce costs by shortening the distribution channel.
The police are investigating the distribution channels of counterfeit brand goods.
Foods whose distribution path from the place of origin to the store is clear tend to earn consumers' trust.
en.notes: 流通経路 is the path of a product from the manufacturer through wholesale (卸) and retail (小売) to the consumer. Typical: 流通経路を短縮する/確保する/把握する, 複雑な流通経路; also for smuggled or counterfeit goods: 偽造品の流通経路を調べる. A synonym is 流通チャネル; 販路 means more narrowly the sales channel from the seller's point of view. Register: business language.

examples[].german: The spread of e-commerce is causing a distribution revolution.
The appearance of supermarkets brought a distribution revolution to Japan.
Direct sales that bypass wholesalers were a kind of distribution revolution.
en.notes: 流通革命 is a fundamental upheaval of the distribution channels between manufacturer and consumer. 流通 here means "distribution, movement of goods" (wholesale, retail, logistics). The term became popular in Japan in the 1960s, when supermarkets bypassed traditional wholesalers; today it is often used for online commerce and direct sales. Typical: 流通革命が起きる/を引き起こす/をもたらす.

examples[].german: Improving the efficiency of international logistics is the key to global competition.
During the COVID pandemic, congestion at ports threw international logistics into great disarray.
After graduating from university, I got a job at an international logistics company.
en.notes: 国際物流 is international logistics: transport, storage, customs clearance and documents across borders. 物流 refers to the physical flow of goods, whereas 流通 means the whole distribution including trade. Typical: 国際物流会社, 国際物流網, 国際物流の混乱/効率化; service providers are often called フォワーダー "forwarders". Register: business language.

examples[].german: Demand for container shipping is increasing worldwide.
Colorful containers were piled high at the port.
Until the move, I am keeping my furniture in a rented container.
en.notes: コンテナ (also コンテナー) is above all the standardized freight container: コンテナ船, コンテナ輸送, コンテナターミナル, コンテナを積む/降ろす; counted with 本 or 個. There are also rental storage containers (トランクルーム, レンタルコンテナ) and, in IT, software containers. An ordinary household "container", by contrast, is called 容器 or 入れ物.

examples[].german: Use consolidated shipping to transport small cargo.
If you have little cargo, consolidated shipping is cheaper than chartering a whole container.
This truck can carry frozen food and room-temperature goods together.
en.notes: 混載 means loading goods from different shippers (or of different kinds) together in one container, truck or aircraft - consolidated shipment. Typical: 混載便, 混載貨物, 混載輸送, as a する-verb 荷物を混載する. The opposite is a full load or charter (貸切, チャーター便). For small quantities 混載 is cheaper, but often takes longer. Register: logistics terminology.

examples[].german: Deliver the cargo to the port by the shipping deadline.
Once loading is done, please send the shipping documents to the buyer right away.
At Yokohama port, I watched cars for export being loaded onto a ship.
en.notes: 船積み (also 船積) is the loading of goods onto a ship for shipment; as a transitive する-verb: 貨物を船積みする. Typical in foreign trade: 船積み書類 "shipping documents", 船積み港, 船積み日, 船積み期限. The opposite is unloading the cargo: 荷揚げ, 陸揚げ or 揚げ荷. More general is 積み込み "loading" of vehicles of any kind. Register: trade and logistics language.

examples[].german: Detailed standards are specified in the ministerial ordinance.
The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare amended its ordinance and revised the standards.
The detailed procedures are written not in the law but in a ministerial ordinance.
en.notes: 省令 is a "ministerial ordinance" issued by an individual ministry 省, e.g. 厚生労働省令. In the hierarchy of norms it ranks below 法律 and 政令 and usually regulates technical details and procedures: 省令で定める, 省令を改正する. For regulations of agencies and similar bodies, one says 規則; 通達 are internal administrative instructions without the force of law.

examples[].german: Unloading work was delayed by the weather.
The quantity of discharged cargo did not match the entry on the bill of lading.
Damaged boxes were found among the unloaded cargo, so we contacted the insurance company.
en.notes: 揚げ荷 (also 揚荷) is port terminology: the cargo unloaded ("discharged") from a ship, or the unloading itself; 揚げる here means "to bring ashore". The counterpart is 積み荷 "loaded cargo". Typical: 揚げ荷作業, 揚げ荷役. In general usage 荷揚げ (also on construction sites) and 陸揚げ are much more common. Register: technical language.

examples[].german: The volume of air cargo handled is increasing.
The parts were urgent, so we sent them by air cargo rather than by sea.
Imported goods are inspected at the air cargo terminal at Narita Airport.
en.notes: 航空貨物 is air cargo, i.e. goods carried by aircraft, as opposed to passengers (旅客). Typical: 航空貨物で送る, 航空貨物便, 航空貨物運賃, 航空貨物ターミナル. Air cargo is fast but more expensive than sea freight (海上輸送, 船便). For parcels and letters, one simply says 航空便 "airmail" in everyday speech. Register: logistics and trade language.

examples[].german: Sea transport is suited to bulk transport.
Sea transport takes time, but it is much cheaper than air freight.
With the canal blocked, global sea transport was greatly affected.
en.notes: 海上輸送 is the transport of goods by ship over the sea. It is slow but cheapest for large quantities; its counterparts are 航空輸送 and 陸上輸送. Typical: 海上輸送のコスト/ルート, 海上輸送が滞る, as a する-verb 原油を海上輸送する. The shipping industry is called 海運; for parcels in everyday speech one says 船便. Register: business and press language.

examples[].german: Improving the land transport network raises logistics efficiency.
Containers that arrive at the port are carried by land transport to factories inland.
Costs of land transport are rising because of a shortage of drivers.
en.notes: 陸上輸送 is transport over land by truck or rail, as opposed to 海上輸送 and 航空輸送. The short form 陸送 is met especially in vehicle transfers (陸送会社). Typical: 陸上輸送網, 陸上輸送のコスト, 陸上輸送に切り替える. Do not confuse it with 陸上 in the sense of "track and field" (陸上競技). Register: business and logistics language.

examples[].german: Achieve efficient delivery through multimodal transport.
With multimodal transport combining sea and rail, goods reach Europe in about twenty days.
In multimodal transport, a single operator takes responsibility for the entire route.
en.notes: 複合輸送 (複合 "combined, composite" + 輸送) refers to transport in which several modes such as ship, rail, truck or aircraft are combined, usually under a single contract and one responsible company (国際複合輸送, 複合一貫輸送). Related is モーダルシフト "modal shift", the shift from trucks to rail or ships. Register: logistics terminology.

examples[].german: Conclude a charter contract and transport large quantities of crude oil.
Our own ships were not enough, so we chartered a freighter from a foreign shipping company.
Charter rates rose sharply because of higher fuel prices.
en.notes: 傭船 is the chartering of a ship, or the chartered ship itself. Since 傭 is not a jōyō kanji, 用船 is often written instead. Typical: 傭船契約 "charter contract" (定期傭船 "time charter", 航海傭船 "voyage charter"), 傭船料 "charter rate", as a する-verb 貨物船を傭船する. In everyday speech, for example for buses or flights, one says チャーター. Register: shipping terminology.

examples[].german: Take out marine insurance to prepare for risks during transport.
Under CIF terms, the seller arranges the marine insurance.
Marine insurance is said to have developed from the coffeehouses of London.
en.notes: 海上保険 is marine insurance; it covers ships (船舶保険) and above all cargo at sea (貨物海上保険). Typical: 海上保険に加入する, 海上保険を付ける/掛ける, 海上保険料. In foreign trade the delivery terms determine who takes it out - under CIF, the seller. 貨物保険 also covers air and land transport, and 損害保険 is the umbrella term "property and casualty insurance". Register: technical language.

examples[].german: Check the insurance terms of the cargo insurance.
The goods got wet in transit, so we were compensated under the cargo insurance.
When sending expensive artworks, we always take out cargo insurance.
en.notes: 貨物保険 is transport or freight insurance for goods in transit, whether by ship, plane or truck. Typical phrases: 貨物保険を掛ける/付ける, 貨物保険で補償される, 貨物保険の付保条件; 付保 is the formal word for "providing insurance cover". Unlike 海上保険, it does not cover the ship itself, but it does cover land and air transport as well. Register: trade and insurance language.

examples[].german: The consignee presents the documents when taking delivery of the cargo.
Please write the addresses of the shipper and the consignee correctly on the waybill.
Because the consignee was absent, the cargo is being kept in the warehouse.
en.notes: 荷受人 (荷 "cargo" + 受ける + 人) is the recipient of a shipment, as named on the waybill (送り状) or bill of lading (船荷証券). The counterpart is 荷送人 "shipper"; 荷主 is the client or owner of the goods. In everyday speech, for parcels and mail one more often says 受取人 or お届け先. Register: technical and form language.

examples[].german: The shipper is responsible for preparing the export documents.
Please write the addresses of the shipper and the consignee correctly on the waybill.
If the package cannot be delivered, it will be returned to the sender.
en.notes: 荷送人 (also 荷送り人) is the "sender" of a freight or parcel shipment, especially in logistics, insurance and foreign trade; its counterpart is 荷受人 ("consignee"). 荷主 similarly refers to the owner or client of the cargo. On letters and in everyday speech, 差出人 or 送り主 is used instead. Typical on forms: 荷送人の住所・氏名.

en.meaning: scrapping of a bill; bill's rejection
examples[].german: With the end of the session, the bill was scrapped.
The opposition protested, demanding the bill's withdrawal.
Due to a lack of budget, the plan for the new park was scrapped.
en.notes: 廃案 is a bill or plan that has been discarded or lapses without a decision. In the Japanese parliament, bills not passed by the end of the session automatically become 廃案, unless they are referred to 継続審議 ("continued deliberation"). Typical: 廃案になる/となる, 廃案に追い込む, 廃案を求める. Also outside politics for dropped projects: 企画が廃案になる.

examples[].german: A directive was issued to all government ministries and agencies.
A circular on cost reduction arrived from the head office to all branches.
The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology issued a notice to all schools, calling for heatstroke countermeasures.
en.notes: 通達 is an official "instruction" or "circular" from a higher to subordinate bodies, for example from a ministry to authorities and schools: 通達を出す, 通達に従う, 国税庁の通達. In companies, too, communications from the head office to branches are called 通達. A general notice to citizens is rather called 通知, a simple notification 連絡. The old meaning "to be well versed in" is rare today.

examples[].german: Ask a freight forwarder to handle customs clearance.
We leave the export paperwork to a freight forwarder we have worked with for a long time.
I asked the forwarder to secure us one container slot on next week's ship.
en.notes: 乙仲 is an abbreviation of 乙種海運仲立業, a former legal category, and is still common in port and foreign-trade jargon: it means the sea freight forwarder who handles booking, documents and customs clearance. Outsiders more often say 海貨業者, 通関業者 or フォワーダー. Typical: 乙仲に依頼する/頼む/任せる. Register: industry jargon.

examples[].german: Export proceeds are collected by bill of exchange.
The exporter drew a bill of exchange based on the letter of credit.
Since the bank had accepted the bill of exchange, it was certain that it would be paid on the due date.
en.notes: 為替手形 is a drawn bill of exchange (draft): the drawer instructs a third party (usually a bank or the buyer) to pay a beneficiary. Typical verbs: 為替手形を振り出す "to draw a bill", 為替手形を引き受ける "to accept", 為替手形で回収する "to collect by bill of exchange". In foreign trade it appears mainly as 荷為替手形 together with a letter of credit (信用状). Do not confuse it with 約束手形, where the drawer himself promises payment. 為替 has the irregular reading かわせ.

examples[].german: It has become standard business practice to make payments by promissory note.
The promissory note we received from our business partner was dishonored.
Our cash flow is so tight that we cannot prepare the cash by the due date of the promissory note.
en.notes: 約束手形 is the promissory note: the drawer himself promises to pay a sum on a set day. In the Japanese business world, 手形 alone usually means exactly this note; the short form is 約手. Typical are 約束手形を振り出す "to issue", 手形が落ちる "is honored" and 手形が不渡りになる "bounces" - bouncing twice effectively means bankruptcy. By contrast, with a 為替手形 the drawer instructs a third party to pay. Paper notes in Japan are increasingly being replaced by electronically recorded claims (でんさい).

examples[].german: A bill can be transferred to a third party by endorsement.
An endorsement is needed to cash this check.
The new research results ended up backing his theory.
en.notes: 裏書 (also 裏書き) literally means "writing on the back": by signing the back of a bill or check, one transfers it to someone else (手形に裏書する, 裏書して譲渡する). As a する-verb it is transitive. Figuratively, 〜を裏書きする in elevated language means "to confirm, to substantiate": 事実が証言を裏書きする. In this sense 裏付ける and 裏付け are much more common in everyday speech.

examples[].german: Secure working capital by turning bills into cash through discounting.
If a discounted bill is dishonored, the company must buy it back from the bank.
The balance of discounted bills is also noted in the financial statements.
en.notes: 割引手形 is a bill that a company has converted into cash at the bank before maturity, minus interest. The procedure itself is called 手形割引 or 手形を割り引く; 割引手形 refers to the instrument, or to the stock of such bills on the balance sheet. If a discounted bill is dishonored, the company remains liable and has to buy it back (買い戻す) from the bank. A purely technical term from accounting and banking.

examples[].german: We proposed a change in payment terms to our business partner.
Our payment terms are closing at the end of the month, payment at the end of the following month.
Please state not only the price but also the payment terms in the quotation.
en.notes: 支払条件 (also 支払い条件) are the payment terms of a contract: due date, payment period, installments, cash discount. Typical: 支払条件を提示する, 支払条件を交渉する, 支払条件を変更する. A very Japanese formula is 月末締め翌月末払い "closing at the end of the month, payment at the end of the following month". Distinguish from 支払方法 "method of payment" (transfer, cash, card): 条件 mainly concerns timing and modalities.

examples[].german: Please check the delivery terms in the contract.
The delivery term for this transaction is FOB.
The delivery terms determine who pays the freight and insurance.
en.notes: 引渡条件 (also 引渡し条件 or 引き渡し条件) are the "delivery terms" of a sales or trade contract: when and where the goods are handed over and who bears freight, insurance and risk. In foreign trade they are usually fixed with the Incoterms (インコタームズ), such as FOB or CIF. 引き渡し alone means "handover", and in law also the "extradition" of a suspect. Typical: 引渡条件を確認する/取り決める.

examples[].german: Freight rates are soaring due to a shortage of shipping space.
We secured shipping space early in preparation for the peak season.
The grounded ship had a large hole in its hull.
en.notes: 船腹 literally means "ship's belly", i.e. the side of the hull. In trade and logistics it mainly stands for available shipping space or tonnage: 船腹を確保する "to book cargo space", 船腹不足 "shortage of cargo space", 船腹過剰 "overcapacity", 船腹量 "tonnage". The physical hold inside a ship is more often called 船倉. A word of technical and business language.

examples[].german: The ship is moored at the port and the cargo is loaded and unloaded.
In preparation for the typhoon, the fishing boats were moored securely.
A retired sailing ship is moored at the quay as a museum.
en.notes: 係留 (older spelling 繋留, often written けい留 in regulations) means "to make fast with lines": 船を岸壁に係留する, very often in the passive 係留されている. Unlike 停泊 "to lie at anchor, to be in port", 係留 emphasizes the tying up. Balloons (係留気球) and, in ordinances, leashed dogs can also be 係留. Written and technical; in everyday speech one more often says つなぐ.

examples[].german: The written judgment was published and sparked discussion among legal experts.
The presiding judge read out the judgment.
The written judgment was over a hundred pages long.
en.notes: 判決文 is the written judgment with operative part and reasoning, whereas 判決 means the judgment as a decision. One says 判決文を読み上げる, 判決文の要旨 "summary of the judgment" or 判決文が公開される. The operative part of the judgment is called 主文; in death sentences it is often read out only after the reasoning (主文後回し). The reasoning alone is called 判決理由.

examples[].german: Imported plants are inspected under the Plant Protection Act.
If you bring seedlings in from abroad, you must have them inspected at a plant protection station.
The plant quarantine system was strengthened to prevent the entry of new pests.
en.notes: 植物防疫 is state plant protection against pests and plant diseases: both import inspection of plants (植物検疫) and control measures inside the country. The word appears almost only in fixed combinations such as 植物防疫法 "Plant Protection Act", 植物防疫所 "plant protection station" (at ports and airports) and 植物防疫官. 防疫 alone means epidemic prevention in general. Official language.

en.meaning: certificate of origin; proof of origin
examples[].german: A certificate of origin is required to apply the preferential tariff.
We obtained a certificate of origin from the chamber of commerce.
Due to an error in the certificate of origin, customs clearance was delayed.
en.notes: 原産地証明 is proof of the country in which goods were produced; the document itself is precisely called 原産地証明書. It is needed for preferential tariffs from free trade agreements (特恵関税, EPA) and in Japan is usually issued by the chamber of commerce (商工会議所). Typical: 原産地証明を取得する, 発給する, 提出する. To be distinguished from 原産地表示, the indication of origin on the label.

examples[].german: The commercial invoice lists the product details and prices.
Customs clearance requires the submission of the commercial invoice and the bill of lading.
The amount on the commercial invoice did not match the amount in the letter of credit.
en.notes: 商業送り状 is the formal official term for the commercial invoice in exports (description of goods, quantity, price, delivery terms). In practice one usually says インボイス or 商業インボイス. 送り状 alone is ambiguous: it can also mean the waybill or shipping label of a parcel service (宅配便の送り状). Typical: 商業送り状を作成する, 〜に記載する, 船荷証券と一緒に提出する.

examples[].german: Ship the cargo with shipping marks attached.
The marking had almost faded, so we couldn't tell which shipment it was.
Shipping marks must match the entries in the shipping documents.
en.notes: 荷印 are the markings on crates and cartons in shipping: consignee abbreviation, port of destination, case number, etc. One says 荷印を付ける or 荷印を表示する; in practice it is often also called ケースマーク or シッピングマーク. The details must match the shipping documents so that the shipment can be identified unambiguously. A purely technical logistics term.

examples[].german: Pool packages at the collection center and deliver them efficiently.
I requested a parcel pickup for the afternoon.
The agricultural cooperative collects rice from local farmers.
en.notes: 集荷 is the collecting of cargo: on the one hand, the pickup of parcels by a courier service (集荷を依頼する, 集荷に来てもらう), on the other hand the purchasing and collecting of agricultural products, for example by a cooperative (米を集荷する). Opposite terms are 出荷 "shipment" and 配達 "delivery"; together they are called 集配. Neutral, and very common in everyday parcel shipping.

examples[].german: Estimate the transport costs to the destination.
Depending on the destination, some items require an export license.
I wrote Hamburg in the destination field of the bill of lading.
en.notes: 仕向地 (also 仕向け地) is the destination or destination country of a shipment of goods in foreign trade; likewise 仕向港 "port of destination" and 仕向国. It appears mainly in documents, contracts and export controls. In everyday speech one says 目的地 or 届け先. Do not confuse it with the verb 仕向ける "to induce someone to do something".

examples[].german: Transshipment at a transit port increases the transport time.
Transshipment is prohibited under the letter of credit.
The cargo will be transshipped in Singapore and then transported to Europe.
en.notes: 積替え (usually written 積み替え) is the reloading of cargo from one means of transport to another, for example at a transit port. The related verb is transitive: 荷物を積み替える. Letters of credit often specify whether 積替え is allowed (積替え可) or prohibited (積替え禁止). The spelling without み (積替え) is typical of technical and form texts.

examples[].german: Demurrage was incurred due to delays in cargo handling.
Demurrage is set in the contract as a daily amount.
Unloading was delayed by port congestion, and the shipper ended up bearing the demurrage.
en.notes: 滞船料 is demurrage in maritime freight law: if the charterer needs longer than the agreed laytime for loading or unloading, he pays the shipowner a daily rate. Typical: 滞船料が発生する, 滞船料を支払う, 滞船料を負担する. The counterpart for faster work is 早出料. For containers, people nowadays mostly say デマレージ.

examples[].german: Cargo handling was completed ahead of schedule, and despatch money was paid.
Despatch money is generally half of the demurrage.
Because the charter agreement had no provision for despatch money, the negotiations dragged on.
en.notes: 早出料 is despatch money: if loading or unloading is faster than agreed, the shipowner pays the charterer a bonus for the time saved. It is the counterpart to 滞船料 "demurrage" and is usually half of its daily rate. In maritime trade it is read はやでりょう (not そうしゅつりょう); 早出 alone means "early start of work, early shift" in everyday speech. A purely technical term.

examples[].german: A short shipment occurred, and the delivery date was delayed.
For the portion of short shipment below the contract quantity, dead freight must be paid.
Due to a port strike, part of the cargo was not loaded.
en.notes: 不積み refers in the sea freight business to the case where the contractually promised cargo is not loaded, wholly or partly. For the unused cargo space the charterer owes the shipowner dead freight, in Japanese 不積運賃. Typical: 不積みが発生する, 一部が不積みとなる. For cargo or passengers that simply no longer fit on board, the general-language word is 積み残し. A rare technical term.

examples[].german: Greater efficiency in administrative agencies is being demanded.
This information is shared among administrative agencies.
Courts are not administrative agencies but judicial organs.
en.notes: 行政機関 is the collective term for state "administrative agencies" such as ministries, offices and agencies, and in a wider sense also local government administrations. It stands in contrast to 立法機関 (parliament) and 司法機関 (courts). In everyday speech, one says 役所 or 市役所 for the local office, and in the news 官庁 or 省庁 for the ministries; 当局 means "the authorities concerned".

examples[].german: Overloading is prohibited for safety reasons.
An overloaded truck was cracked down on on the expressway.
Overloading of the ship is thought to be the cause of the capsizing accident.
en.notes: 過積み means "overloading", i.e. more cargo than permitted. The word is rather rare; the standard in law, media and police language is 過積載 (e.g. 過積載のトラック, 過積載で取り締まられる). Both typically appear with 禁止, 取り締まり or as an accident cause (事故の原因). To load a vehicle too heavily is 積みすぎる or 積み過ぎる.

examples[].german: No customs duties are imposed within a bonded area.
The imported parts are stored in a bonded warehouse before customs clearance.
The cargo was transported in bond to another port.
en.notes: 保税 means "under customs supervision, not yet cleared": goods are stored or transported without duty having been paid yet. The word appears almost only as the first element of compounds: 保税地域 "bonded area", 保税倉庫 "bonded warehouse", 保税運送 "transport in bond", 保税工場. Standing alone it occurs in 保税のまま "still uncleared". Customs and logistics technical language.

examples[].german: In 1971, the United States imposed a flat 10% surcharge on imports.
The Fair Trade Commission ordered the companies that formed the cartel to pay a surcharge.
Many companies self-report violations to escape the surcharge.
en.notes: 課徴金 is a levy imposed by the state that is not counted as a tax. Today it mainly means the fine imposed by the competition authority (公正取引委員会) in cartel cases: 課徴金納付命令, 課徴金を課す, 課徴金減免制度 "leniency program". There is also the 輸入課徴金 "import surcharge". Unlike 罰金, it is an administrative sanction, not a criminal penalty. Official and press language.

examples[].german: Impose a countervailing duty on subsidized export goods.
The government decided to impose countervailing duties on foreign steel.
To impose a countervailing duty, it must be proven that subsidies are harming the domestic industry.
en.notes: 相殺関税 is the countervailing duty against subsidized imports: it offsets the price advantage that foreign producers gain through state aid. Typical: 相殺関税を課す, 相殺関税を発動する. To be distinguished from 反ダンピング関税 (against selling below value) and 報復関税 (retaliation). Note the reading: 相殺 is read そうさい here, not そうさつ.

examples[].german: The exchange of retaliatory tariffs worsened the economic relations between the two countries.
If the other country imposes retaliatory tariffs, a blow to exporters is unavoidable.
The president dangled the threat of retaliatory tariffs to gain an advantage in the negotiations.
en.notes: 報復関税 is a retaliatory or punitive tariff that a state imposes in response to trade measures by another. Typical: 報復関税を発動する, 報復関税を課す, 報復関税の応酬 "tit-for-tat tariffs", 報復関税をちらつかせる "to threaten tariffs". Unlike 相殺関税, it is not directed against subsidies but is politically motivated. Common in news about trade wars (貿易戦争).

en.meaning: ad valorem duty; ad valorem tax
examples[].german: An ad valorem duty is levied at a fixed percentage of the product price.
Most of Japan's import tariffs are ad valorem, and the rate is expressed in percent.
The consumption tax is also proportional to the price, so it is a kind of ad valorem tax.
en.notes: 従価税 is a levy based on the value (price) of the goods and expressed as a percentage, that is, an ad valorem duty or tax. The counterpart is 従量税, which is calculated by quantity or weight. 従 means "according to, following" here: "tax according to the price". Most import tariffs, and also the consumption tax, are 従価税. Technical language of tax and customs theory.

examples[].german: A specific duty is levied based on the quantity or weight of the goods.
Alcohol and tobacco taxes are specific taxes levied according to quantity.
With a specific tax, the tax amount does not change even if the price falls.
en.notes: 従量税 is a levy calculated by the quantity, weight or volume of the goods (e.g. yen per kilogram or liter), regardless of price. The counterpart is 従価税, which is based on value. In Japan, for example, alcohol and tobacco taxes are 従量税. When prices fall, a specific duty has a relatively stronger effect, because the amount stays the same. Technical language of tax and customs theory.

examples[].german: Check the applicable tariff rate based on the tariff schedule.
I looked up the tariff number of the imported product in the tariff schedule.
The tariff schedule is revised every year, so please check the latest edition.
en.notes: 関税率表 is the customs tariff: the official list that assigns a duty rate to each commodity number (HSコード or 統計品目番号). In Japan, the currently valid version is called 実行関税率表; it contains, among other things, the general rate (基本税率), the WTO rate and the rates from free trade agreements. Typical: 関税率表で調べる, 関税率表に基づく, 関税率表を改正する. Technical language of customs and foreign trade.

examples[].german: The export-import bank supports trade finance.
The former Export-Import Bank of Japan is the predecessor of today's Japan Bank for International Cooperation.
We borrowed the funds for the plant export from the export-import bank.
en.notes: 輸出入銀行 is a state export credit bank that promotes exports, imports and overseas investment with loans and guarantees. Usually a country name precedes it: 米国輸出入銀行 "Export-Import Bank of the United States". The former 日本輸出入銀行 was merged in 1999 with a development fund to form today's 国際協力銀行 (JBIC). Reading: 輸出入 = ゆしゅつにゅう, not ゆしゅついり.

examples[].german: Take out trade insurance to prepare for the risks of overseas transactions.
There was a coup in the partner country, but most of the loss was covered by trade insurance.
We took out trade insurance in case the importer fails to pay.
en.notes: 貿易保険 insures exporters and investors against risks that ordinary insurance does not cover: the buyer's default, war, foreign exchange restrictions in the partner country. In Japan, it is mainly offered by the state-run 日本貿易保険 (NEXI). Typical: 貿易保険をかける, 貿易保険に加入する, 貿易保険でカバーする. Do not confuse it with cargo insurance for the goods themselves (貨物海上保険).

examples[].german: A restructuring of the central government agencies was carried out.
Central government ministries are concentrated in Kasumigaseki.
After graduating from university, he took a job in a government office.
en.notes: 官庁 denotes state "government offices", especially the ministries: 中央官庁 are the central agencies in Tokyo's government district Kasumigaseki, 官庁街 a government quarter. Very common is 官公庁 for national and local government offices together. In everyday speech 役所 is used for the local office; 行政機関 is the legal collective term. The word sounds somewhat formal and slightly bureaucratic.

examples[].german: The government is pushing ahead with opening the market for agricultural products.
Japan has been strongly urged by other countries to open its market.
Market opening has increased cheap imports.
en.notes: 市場開放 is the opening of a domestic market to foreign goods, services or companies, for example by lowering tariffs and import restrictions. Typical: 市場開放を求める/迫る/進める, 農産物の市場開放. Related are 自由化 ("liberalization", e.g. 米の自由化) and 規制緩和 ("deregulation"); the opposite is 保護主義. 市場 is read しじょう here; いちば is a concrete marketplace.

examples[].german: New companies are entering the market one after another.
Regulations are strict, so the hurdles for market entry are high.
There are laws that restrict the market entry of foreign companies.
en.notes: 市場参入 is a company's "market entry" into a new market or industry. As a verb, one usually says 市場に参入する (参入 is intransitive), less often 市場参入する. Related terms: 新規参入 ("new entrant"), 参入障壁 ("barrier to entry"), and as the opposite 撤退 ("withdrawal from the market"). By contrast, 市場開放 means the opening of a market by the state.

examples[].german: With the progress of the international division of labor, countries' mutual dependence is deepening.
An international division of labor has become established in which parts are made in Asia and assembled in Europe.
The pandemic revealed the weaknesses of the international division of labor.
en.notes: 国際分業 is the international division of labor: each country specializes in certain goods or production stages and exchanges through trade. Typical: 国際分業が進む / 進展する, 国際分業体制, 国際分業に組み込まれる. Subtypes are 垂直分業 (raw materials for finished goods, or production stages) and 水平分業 (finished goods for finished goods). Economic language, common in newspapers and textbooks.

examples[].german: Trade patterns are determined based on comparative advantage.
Ricardo explained the benefits of free trade with the theory of comparative advantage.
This country has a comparative advantage in labor-intensive products.
en.notes: 比較優位 is comparative advantage in Ricardo's sense: a country should produce what it makes relatively most cheaply compared with other goods, even if another country can make everything more cheaply. Typical: 〜に比較優位がある, 比較優位を持つ, 比較優位に基づく. To be distinguished from 絶対優位 "absolute advantage". A technical term of economics, also used figuratively in the business press.

examples[].german: The deterioration in the terms of trade is having a negative impact on the economy.
Due to soaring crude oil prices, the terms of trade of Japan, which imports resources, worsened.
The terms of trade are expressed as the ratio of export prices to import prices.
en.notes: 交易条件 are the terms of trade: the ratio of a country's export prices to its import prices. If import prices (for oil, say) rise more than export prices, 交易条件が悪化する; in the opposite case, 改善する. 交易 is an older word for the exchange of goods and survives mainly in this technical term and in historical contexts (南蛮交易); in the modern sense one otherwise says 貿易.

examples[].german: Capital movements are regulated under the Foreign Exchange Control Act.
The country tightened its foreign exchange controls following the currency crisis.
Because of strict foreign exchange controls, we could not remit the profits to the home country.
en.notes: 外国為替管理 is state control of foreign exchange and capital transactions, e.g. permission requirements for transfers abroad or fixed exchange rates. Typical: 外国為替管理を強化する / 緩和する / 撤廃する; shorter, 為替管理. In Japan this was governed by the 外国為替管理法, which was liberalized in 1998 into the 外国為替及び外国貿易法 (short: 外為法). Technical language of economics and law.

examples[].german: Maintaining the multilateral trading system is essential for the stability of the world economy.
The Uruguay Round is one of the multilateral trade negotiations.
There is concern that an increase in bilateral agreements will weaken the framework of multilateral trade.
en.notes: 多角的貿易 (also 多角貿易) is multilateral trade, that is, trade under common rules among many countries rather than only between two partners (二国間). It almost always appears in fixed combinations: 多角的貿易体制 "multilateral trading system" (GATT/WTO) and 多角的貿易交渉 "multilateral trade round" such as the Uruguay Round. Language of politics, diplomacy and the business press.

examples[].german: The horizontal division of labor among developed countries is expanding.
In the smartphone industry, a horizontal division of labor is advancing in which different companies handle design and manufacturing.
The structure of the semiconductor industry has changed from vertical integration to a horizontal division of labor.
en.notes: 水平分業 is the horizontal division of labor. In trade theory it means the exchange of finished goods between countries at a similar level of development; in the business world, the splitting of value creation among specialized firms, for example development at one and manufacturing at another. Opposite terms: 垂直分業 or, at the company level, 垂直統合 "vertical integration". Typical: 水平分業が進む, 水平分業型のビジネスモデル.

examples[].german: The vertical division of labor between developed and developing countries is changing.
In the past, a vertical division of labor in which raw materials were imported and products exported was common.
The vertical division of labor of the colonial era is said to have hindered the industrialization of developing countries.
en.notes: 垂直分業 is the vertical division of labor: countries or firms take on different stages of the same value chain. The classic pattern is "developing countries supply raw materials, industrial countries supply finished goods"; today it also covers the distribution of parts manufacturing and final assembly among different countries. The opposite term is 水平分業. Typical: 垂直分業から水平分業へ, 垂直分業の構造.

examples[].german: Cooperation between ministries and agencies was strengthened.
The policy will be decided after consulting the relevant ministries and agencies.
In 2001, the central ministries and agencies were extensively reorganized.
en.notes: 省庁 is the collective term for the central government bodies: the ministries (〜省 like 財務省) and the agencies attached to them (〜庁 like 気象庁 or 金融庁). Typical are 中央省庁 "central ministries and agencies", 関係省庁 "the ministries concerned", 省庁間 "between ministries" and 省庁再編 "reorganization of the ministries" (major reform in 2001). In press jargon, 霞が関 often stands for the ministerial bureaucracy. The word belongs to the language of news and administration.

examples[].german: Liberalizing foreign trade promotes economic growth.
In the Edo period, foreign trade was largely limited to Nagasaki.
For the island nation of Japan, foreign trade is the lifeline of the economy.
en.notes: 外国貿易 is foreign trade, that is, the exchange of goods with other countries. In present-day Japanese, 貿易 alone usually suffices, since it already means "foreign trade" by itself; 外国貿易 sounds formal and appears mainly in laws (外国為替及び外国貿易法), statistics and historical texts, or in contrast to 内国貿易 "domestic trade". Typical: 外国貿易の自由化, 外国貿易に依存する.

examples[].german: Revitalizing domestic trade contributes to the development of regional economies.
In economics, trade within a country is called domestic trade and cross-border trade is called foreign trade, to distinguish them.
In the Meiji period, domestic trade expanded rapidly with the opening of the railways.
en.notes: 内国貿易 is domestic trade, that is, trade within a country's borders, and is the counterpart of 外国貿易. The word is rare today and sounds technical or historical; in contemporary language one more often says 国内取引, 国内商業 or 国内流通. It is found mainly in economics textbooks and in texts on economic history.

examples[].german: Compensation trade is a form of transaction that does not involve cash.
A compensation trade deal was made: equipment was supplied, and payment was recovered with products made at that factory.
In transactions with countries short of foreign currency, compensation trade is sometimes chosen.
en.notes: 補償貿易 is a form of compensation deal: a supplier provides machines or an entire plant and is paid not in foreign currency but with the products made there (buy-back). The term became known mainly through trade with China in the 1970s and 80s. Related are バーター貿易 "barter trade" and カウンタートレード as the umbrella term. Technical language of foreign trade.

examples[].german: An axiom is a basic proposition accepted without proof.
In mathematics, theorems are proven on the basis of a few axioms.
That everyone eventually dies is a sort of axiom nobody questions.
en.notes: 公理 is an "axiom" in mathematics and logic: a basic assumption presupposed without proof, from which 定理 ("theorems") are derived. To be distinguished from 定義 ("definition") and 原理 ("principle"). Outside technical language, 公理 also means a generally accepted, self-evident truth, as in …は公理のようなものだ. Typical: 公理を立てる, 公理系 ("axiom system").

examples[].german: Please judge the truth or falsity of this proposition logically.
The proposition "all birds can fly" is false because of the existence of penguins.
Cost reduction has become the top priority for management.
en.notes: 命題 is, in logic and philosophy, a statement that can be true or false: 命題が真である / 偽である, 命題の逆・裏・対偶 "converse, inverse, contrapositive". It also means "task, central challenge", especially in 至上命題 "top priority", which is very common in business and politics (originally 至上命令). Written language; in everyday speech one more often says 主張 or 説 for assertions.

examples[].german: We collected data to verify the theory.
A field trial of self-driving buses has started in the city.
This study demonstrated empirically that exercise improves memory.
en.notes: 実証 means "to demonstrate through facts, data or experiments"; as a する-verb it is transitive: 仮説を実証する, 効果が実証される. Common are 実証的 "empirical", 実証研究 and 実証実験 "pilot test, field test" (e.g. for new technology). To be distinguished: 証明 is more general and also mathematical, 立証 emphasizes proving in court or against doubts, 検証 is checking. Written and scientific language.

examples[].german: A single counterexample can overturn a hypothesis.
The defense presented evidence to the contrary against the prosecution's claims.
Popper considered falsifiability to be the very condition of science.
en.notes: 反証 is counter-evidence, that is, proof that refutes a claim or hypothesis. Typical: 反証を挙げる / 示す, 反証となる, 反証が見つかる; as a する-verb it is transitive (仮説を反証する), but less common. Important in the philosophy of science: 反証可能性 "falsifiability" (Popper). To be distinguished from 反論 "verbal objection": 反証 is a piece of evidence, not an argument. Academic and legal language.

examples[].german: A conclusion was drawn based on logical inference.
Inferring from the limited data, sales will probably keep growing next year.
Inference using trained AI models can also be run on a smartphone.
en.notes: 推論 is inferential thinking, or a conclusion obtained from it: 推論する (transitive), 推論を立てる, 〜から推論する, 論理的な推論. To be distinguished from 推測 "conjecture" (less rigorous) and 推理 "deduction by piecing clues together", typical of criminal cases. In AI, 推論 is the technical term for inference, that is, applying a trained model. Written, academic language.

examples[].german: The inductive method derives general laws from individual cases.
From many observations, a general tendency was found by induction.
Conclusions obtained inductively may be overturned by new cases.
en.notes: 帰納 is induction: reasoning from the particular case to the general. It appears almost always in 帰納法 "inductive method" or 帰納的 "inductive"; 帰納する exists but is rarer. The opposite term is 演繹 "deduction". Beware of the homophone 機能 "function" - in writing the kanji distinguish them clearly. Academic language.

examples[].german: In deductive reasoning, the conclusion follows necessarily from the premises.
A mathematical proof is the work of deducing theorems from axioms.
The master detective deductively identified the culprit from a few clues.
en.notes: 演繹 is deduction: reasoning from general premises compellingly to the particular case. Common in 演繹法, 演繹的 "deductive" and as a transitive する-verb: 公理から定理を演繹する. The opposite term is 帰納 "induction". The second kanji 繹 hardly occurs in other words; the reading is えんえき. Academic language; in everyday speech, 導き出す is more usual.

examples[].german: Representatives from all the prefectures of the country gathered.
I looked up the population ranking by prefecture.
Japan has forty-seven prefectures.
en.notes: 都道府県 combines the 47 prefectures of Japan, naming all four types: 1 都 (東京都), 1 道 (北海道), 2 府 (大阪府, 京都府) and 43 県. The word is found mainly in statistics and administrative language: 都道府県別 "by prefecture", 都道府県知事 "prefectural governor", 都道府県庁所在地 "prefectural capital". The level below is the 市町村; together they form the 地方自治体 "local governments".

examples[].german: The synthesis of organic compounds requires advanced techniques.
I combined two photos to make a single landscape photo.
This car navigation system gives directions with a synthesized voice.
en.notes: 合成 means "to put together from several parts into something new", as a transitive する-verb: 化合物を合成する, 画像を合成する. Typical compounds: 合成樹脂 "synthetic resin", 合成繊維 "synthetic fiber", 合成音声 "synthetic voice", 合成写真 "photo montage", 光合成 "photosynthesis". The opposite term is 分解 "decomposition". Neutral, equally common in technology and everyday speech.

examples[].german: The technology for extracting active ingredients from plants has advanced.
The survey subjects were a thousand people randomly selected from the voter register.
I extracted only the data matching the conditions and compiled it into a table.
en.notes: 抽出 means "to pull out": chemically, to extract a substance (植物から成分を抽出する), but also to filter out data (条件に合うデータを抽出する) and, in statistics, to draw a sample, especially in 無作為抽出 "random sampling". As a する-verb it is transitive. For extracting mineral resources, one says 採掘 or 採取 instead. Technical and written language, very common in IT.

examples[].german: Pure substances are separated from mixtures by distillation.
Please use distilled water for the experiment.
Whisky and shochu are distilled spirits made by distilling fermented drinks.
en.notes: 蒸留 is distillation: vaporizing a liquid and condensing the vapor again in order to separate substances. As a する-verb it is transitive: 海水を蒸留する. Well-known compounds are 蒸留水 "distilled water" and 蒸留酒 "spirits", as opposed to 醸造酒 "brewed / fermented drinks" such as beer or sake. On whisky labels one often still finds the older spelling 蒸溜, e.g. in 蒸溜所 "distillery".

examples[].german: We observed the process of the chemical reaction in detail.
Customers' reaction to the new product was excellent.
Even when his name was called, the patient did not respond.
en.notes: 反応 is any reaction: chemical (化学反応), physical (アレルギー反応, 陽性反応 "positive test result") and social (客の反応, 反応が鈍い "barely reacts"). As a する-verb it is intransitive with に: 刺激に反応する, 名前に反応する. Unlike 返事 "reply", it is not about answering back but about the effect of a stimulus. Neutral and very common.

examples[].german: When iron oxidizes, rust forms.
If you leave a cut apple out, it oxidizes and turns brown.
This wine contains antioxidants.
en.notes: 酸化 refers to chemical "oxidation"; as a する-verb it is mostly intransitive: 鉄が酸化する "iron oxidizes". To stress the causing of it, one says 酸化させる. The opposite term is 還元 "reduction"; together, 酸化還元反応 "redox reaction". In everyday life it turns up with food: 酸化した油 "rancid oil", 酸化防止剤 "antioxidant" on ingredient lists.

examples[].german: Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons.
The goal is to give the research results back to the local community.
If you pay with this card, five percent is returned to you as points.
en.notes: 還元 has two fields of use: in chemistry, "reduction" as the counterpart of 酸化; in everyday life, "giving back" profit or benefit to others. The latter typically uses the transitive pattern AをBに還元する: 利益を社会に還元する, 成果を地域に還元する. Very common today is ポイント還元 "rebate in points" when paying. In the sense of "tracing back to something fundamental" it is likewise 〜に還元する: 問題を個人の責任に還元する.

examples[].german: Sugar dissolves easily in water.
Please dissolve the powder in water before taking it.
At the factory, scrap iron is melted at high temperature to make new steel.
en.notes: 溶解 is the technical term for a substance "dissolving" in a liquid and sounds much more formal than the everyday verb 溶ける; as a する-verb it is mostly intransitive: 砂糖が水に溶解する, with the solvent marked by に. Transitively, one often says 溶解させる. It also refers to the melting of metal (溶解炉 "melting furnace"). Beware of the homophone 妖怪 "ghost, demon".

examples[].german: The temperature at which a liquid solidifies into a solid is called the freezing point.
At a wound, the blood coagulates and the bleeding stops.
Tofu is made by adding nigari to soy milk to make it coagulate.
en.notes: 凝固 refers to a liquid becoming solid, whether by cooling or by coagulation as with blood: 血液が凝固する. It is an intransitive する-verb in a technical style; in everyday speech one more often says 固まる or, for water, 凍る. Typical compounds are 凝固点 "freezing point, solidification point" and 血液凝固 "blood coagulation". The opposite term is 融解 "melting".

examples[].german: The melting point of metals varies greatly depending on the type.
Because tungsten has a very high melting point, it was used for light bulb filaments.
Chocolate's melting point is close to body temperature, so it melts right away in your mouth.
en.notes: 融点 is the "melting point", the temperature at which a solid becomes liquid (融解する). Typical: 融点が高い・低い, 融点に達する. The counterpart is 凝固点 "freezing point"; for water both are at 0 °C. Do not confuse it with 沸点 "boiling point". Purely technical; in everyday speech it is paraphrased as 溶ける温度.

examples[].german: The number of municipalities decreased due to municipal mergers.
How to put out garbage differs depending on the municipality.
After moving, you submit a move-in notification at the office of your new municipality.
en.notes: 市町村 refers to the municipalities of the lowest administrative level: 市 "city", 町 "town" and 村 "village". Forms usually say 市区町村, because the 23 special wards (区) of Tokyo are included as well. Common combinations are 市町村合併 "municipal merger", 市町村長 "mayor" and 〜は市町村によって異なる "differs from municipality to municipality". The higher level is the 都道府県.

examples[].german: The boiling point of water is 100 degrees Celsius at standard pressure.
On a mountaintop the boiling point drops, so water does not reach 100 degrees.
Our department head has a low boiling point and starts yelling right away.
en.notes: 沸点 is the "boiling point": 沸点が高い・低い, 沸点に達する; the related verb is 沸騰する "to boil". Colloquially, 沸点が低い is also used figuratively for people who quickly get angry ("to have a short fuse"). Do not confuse it with 融点 "melting point".

examples[].german: The density of a substance is defined as mass per unit volume.
Tokyo has an extremely high population density.
It was a short training course, but it was three very intense days.
en.notes: 密度 is "density" in physics (mass per volume), but it is just as often used figuratively: 人口密度 "population density", 密度の濃い時間 "intense, substantial time". Typical: 密度が高い・低い, 密度が濃い. Related is the adjective 密 "dense, close", but 密度 always refers to a measurable or comparable quantity.

examples[].german: It has been proven that mass and energy are equivalent.
On the Moon you become lighter, but your mass does not change.
Some black holes have a mass millions of times that of the Sun.
en.notes: 質量 is the "mass" of a body in physics and is clearly distinguished from 重さ or 重量 "weight": on the Moon the weight changes, but the 質量 stays the same. Typical: 質量が大きい, 質量保存の法則 "law of conservation of mass". Rarely it also means "quality and quantity". In everyday speech, 重さ is almost always said instead of 質量.

examples[].german: The law of universal gravitation was discovered by Newton.
The ebb and flow of the tides is caused mainly by the Moon's gravitational pull.
An attractive force acts between the north and south poles of a magnet.
en.notes: 引力 is in general the "attractive force" between bodies; 万有引力 is gravitation in the Newtonian sense. Distinctions: 重力 "gravity" is the force that pulls downward on Earth, 磁力 the magnetic force; the opposite is 斥力 "repulsive force". Typical: 引力が働く, 月の引力. Figuratively, 引力 can also mean a person's attractiveness, but one usually says 魅力 for that.

examples[].german: Visible light is a kind of electromagnetic wave.
A microwave oven heats food using electromagnetic waves.
To prevent electromagnetic waves from affecting medical equipment, the use of mobile phones is restricted in hospitals.
en.notes: 電磁波 is the "electromagnetic wave", an umbrella term for radio waves, microwaves, light, X-rays, etc. In technical explanations it often appears in the pattern 〜は電磁波の一種だ; in everyday life it comes up mainly regarding mobile phones, microwave ovens and health questions: 電磁波を出す, 電磁波の影響. Unlike 音波 "sound wave", it needs no medium.

examples[].german: A photon is the smallest unit of light energy.
When an atom absorbs a photon, the electron moves to a higher energy state.
A solar cell is a device that converts the energy of photons into electricity.
en.notes: 光子 is the "photon", the quantum of light; in technical jargon the loanword form フォトン is also common. The word belongs almost exclusively to physics and technology: 光子を放出する・吸収する, 光子のエネルギー. Beware of homophones: こうし is also 講師 "lecturer", 格子 "lattice" and 子牛 "calf"; as a girl's given name, 光子 is usually read みつこ.

examples[].german: Quantum mechanics is a theory that describes the microscopic world.
Quantum computers may be able to solve problems that conventional computers cannot.
In the quantum world, our common sense does not apply.
en.notes: 量子 "quantum" hardly ever stands alone but almost always in compounds: 量子力学 "quantum mechanics", 量子論 "quantum theory", 量子コンピューター, 量子もつれ "entanglement". As a modifier it is placed directly in front or linked with の (量子の世界). Beware of the homophones 漁師 "fisherman" and 猟師 "hunter", which are also read りょうし.

examples[].german: Radioactive isotopes are also used for medical diagnosis.
By examining carbon isotopes, the age of fossils can be estimated.
Hydrogen has three isotopes.
en.notes: 同位体 "isotope" refers to atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons; アイソトープ is used with the same meaning. Common combinations: 放射性同位体 "radioisotope", 安定同位体 "stable isotope", 炭素の同位体. The word is purely technical and is usually attached to an element with 〜の同位体.

examples[].german: The effects of radioactive contamination continue over the long term.
After the accident, residents measured the radioactivity around their homes.
News broke that radioactivity had leaked at the nuclear power plant.
en.notes: 放射能 is, strictly speaking, "radioactivity", that is, the property of a substance to emit radiation; the radiation itself is called 放射線, the radiating substance 放射性物質. In colloquial speech, however, 放射能 is often used for all three, as in 放射能漏れ "leak of radioactivity". Typical are 放射能汚染 "radioactive contamination" and 放射能を測る.

examples[].german: Nuclear fission reactions release enormous energy.
Nuclear power plants use the heat produced by the fission of uranium.
In cell division, nuclear division occurs first, and then the cytoplasm divides.
en.notes: 核分裂 "nuclear fission" is the process on which nuclear power plants (原子力発電) and the atomic bomb are based. Typical: 核分裂反応, 核分裂を起こす, ウランの核分裂. The opposite term is 核融合 "nuclear fusion". In biology, 核分裂 can also mean the division of the cell nucleus; the division of the whole cell is called 細胞分裂.

examples[].german: Government authorization is required to start a business.
The permit procedure took as long as six months.
Government offices hold strong influence over the industry through their authority to grant permits.
en.notes: 許認可 is a contraction of 許可 "permission" and 認可 "official approval" and refers collectively to all authorizations that an authority must grant. Typical: 許認可を得る/取る "to obtain permits", 許認可を申請する, 許認可権 "authority to grant permits", 許認可手続き. It is purely an administrative and newspaper word; it is hardly used as a する-verb, and for a concrete "to approve" one says 許可する or 認可する.

examples[].german: Nuclear fusion is expected to be the energy source of the next generation.
The Sun shines thanks to the nuclear fusion of hydrogen.
Many challenges remain before fusion power generation can be put to practical use.
en.notes: 核融合 "nuclear fusion" is the merging of light atomic nuclei, as in the interior of the Sun. Typical phrases: 核融合反応, 核融合発電 "fusion power", 核融合炉 "fusion reactor", 核融合を起こす. The counterpart is 核分裂 "nuclear fission". Note: 融合 alone means "merging" in general (文化の融合); company mergers, on the other hand, are called 合併.

examples[].german: The loudness of a sound is proportional to the amplitude of the wave.
When the amplitude of a pendulum is small, its period is nearly constant regardless of amplitude.
According to the seismograph record, the amplitude of the shaking suddenly increased.
en.notes: 振幅 is the "amplitude", the maximum displacement of an oscillation or wave: 振幅が大きい・小さい, 振り子の振幅, 波の振幅. The word is technical; for everyday fluctuations (prices, moods) one more often says 振れ幅 or 変動幅. Do not confuse it with 周期 "period" and 振動数 "frequency".

examples[].german: Resonance phenomena are observed in various fields of physics.
The body of a guitar amplifies the sound of the strings through resonance.
Many young people resonated with her appeal for environmental protection.
en.notes: In physics, 共鳴 is "resonance", the sympathetic vibration of a body (共鳴する, 共鳴現象, 共鳴箱 "resonance box"). At least as common is the figurative meaning "to find a response, to sympathize with someone's ideas" in the pattern 〜に共鳴する: 彼の考えに共鳴する. Unlike 共感 "empathy, feeling along with", 共鳴 emphasizes agreement with views or goals. Intransitive する-verb; transitively, 共鳴させる.

examples[].german: Refraction occurs when light passes through a prism.
A straw in water looks bent because light is refracted.
His works show the twisted feelings of his boyhood.
en.notes: In optics, 屈折 is the "refraction" of light (光が屈折する, 屈折率 "refractive index"). The basic meaning is "bending, a bend", and figuratively 屈折した describes a psyche or feelings that are not straightforward: 屈折した感情, 屈折した性格 "warped, twisted". In grammar it means "inflection" (屈折語 "inflecting language"). As a する-verb it is intransitive.

examples[].german: The diffraction phenomenon is important evidence of the wave nature of waves.
The reason you can hear voices beyond a wall is that sound waves diffract.
We examined the crystal structure using X-ray diffraction.
en.notes: 回折 "diffraction" describes how waves travel around obstacles or through narrow slits into the shadow region. Typical: 回折する, 回折現象, X線回折 "X-ray diffraction". Purely technical; to be distinguished from 屈折 "refraction" (change of direction on passing into another medium) and 反射 "reflection". Do not confuse it with the homophone 解説 "commentary, explanation".

examples[].german: When two waves overlap, interference fringes appear.
My mother meddles in my friendships at every turn.
One should not interfere in the internal affairs of other countries.
en.notes: In everyday speech, 干渉 mainly means "interference" in other people's affairs, usually negative: 〜に干渉する, 内政干渉 "interference in internal affairs", 過干渉 "excessive interference" (e.g. by parents). In physics it is the "interference" of waves (干渉縞 "interference fringes", 電波干渉). More neutral is 介入 "intervention"; colloquially one says 口出しする "to butt in".

examples[].german: A polarizing filter lets through only light of a specific direction.
Wearing polarized sunglasses reduces reflections on the water surface, making fish easier to see.
Polarizing plates are used in LCD screens.
en.notes: 偏光 is "polarized light" or the "polarization" of light. In everyday life it appears mainly in 偏光サングラス "polarized sunglasses", 偏光フィルター and 偏光板 "polarizing film" in displays. Do not confuse it with the homophones 変更 "change" and 偏向 "bias" (偏向報道 "biased reporting").

examples[].german: Fluorescent substances absorb ultraviolet light and emit visible light.
I drew lines over the important parts with a highlighter.
We replaced the fluorescent lights in the office with LEDs.
en.notes: 蛍光 "fluorescence" (literally "firefly light") is known mainly from everyday compounds: 蛍光灯 "fluorescent lamp", 蛍光ペン "highlighter", 蛍光色 "neon color". In technical use: 蛍光を発する, 蛍光物質. To be distinguished is 燐光 "phosphorescence", which keeps glowing after the light source is switched off.

examples[].german: Radiation harms health if it is not properly controlled.
My grandfather is receiving radiation therapy for cancer.
The amount of radiation received in an X-ray examination is very small.
en.notes: 放射線 is "radiation" in the sense of ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma, alpha and beta rays). Typical: 放射線を浴びる "to be exposed to radiation", 放射線量 "radiation dose", 放射線治療 "radiation therapy". Distinction: 放射能 is the ability of a substance to emit 放射線. For heat or solar radiation, one does not use 放射線 but 熱放射 or 日射.

examples[].german: Electrons are elementary particles with a negative charge.
Charges of the same kind repel each other.
Hair rubbed with a plastic sheet picks up an electric charge and stands on end.
en.notes: 電荷 is the "electric charge" of a particle or body: 正の電荷・負の電荷, 電荷を帯びる "to be charged", 電荷を持つ. It is a purely technical term; in everyday speech one more often says 静電気 "static electricity". Do not confuse it with the homophone 殿下 "His/Her Highness" (form of address for princes) or with 充電 "charging a battery".

examples[].german: Accounting fraud was uncovered in the financial audit.
We are audited every year by an external audit firm.
The corporate auditor audits the business conduct of the directors.
en.notes: 監査 is the examining control of accounts or management, especially in companies and organizations: 会計監査 "financial audit", 内部監査 "internal audit", 監査法人 "audit firm", 監査役 "corporate auditor". One says 監査を受ける "to be audited" and 〜を監査する "to audit". To be distinguished are 検査 "examination, inspection" (of things, health) and 審査 "screening, review" (of applications, candidates); the state audit of the budget is called 会計検査.

examples[].german: The potential difference is the driving force for electric current.
Nerve cells transmit signals through changes in membrane potential.
In circuits, the potential of the ground is often taken as the reference zero.
en.notes: 電位 is the "electric potential" at a point; the difference between two points, 電位差 "potential difference", corresponds to electric voltage (電圧). Typical: 電位が高い・低い, in biology 膜電位 "membrane potential". Purely technical; in everyday speech one says 電圧.

examples[].german: Electrical resistance depends on the material and length of the conductor.
The culprit was arrested without resisting.
I still feel a bit reluctant about having a meal alone with someone I don't know.
en.notes: 抵抗 is first of all "resistance" against pressure or force: 〜に抵抗する, 抵抗運動 "resistance movement". Very common is the psychological meaning 〜に抵抗がある "to have reservations, to feel reluctant", e.g. 人前で話すのに抵抗がある. In physics and engineering it refers to air or frictional resistance (空気抵抗) and electrical resistance, also the component. Similar is 反抗, which rather means defiant rebellion against parents or teachers.

examples[].german: Copper is widely used as an excellent conductor.
The human body is also a conductor, so you can get an electric shock.
Because of the semiconductor shortage, car production is delayed.
en.notes: 導体 is a "conductor" of electricity or heat: 電気の導体, 良導体 "good conductor". The opposite term is 絶縁体 "insulator"; in between lies 半導体 "semiconductor", which appears even more often than 導体 itself in business news. The matching verb is 電気を通す "to conduct electricity"; a person as a "leader", on the other hand, is called 指導者 or 責任者.

examples[].german: Rubber is an insulator that does not conduct electricity.
Electric wires are covered with an insulator, so you will not get a shock when you touch them.
Pure water is almost an insulator, but it conducts electricity when impurities are mixed in.
en.notes: 絶縁体 is an "insulator", a substance that does not conduct electricity (or heat), such as rubber, glass or plastic. The opposite term is 導体 "conductor". The base word 絶縁 means "insulation" (絶縁テープ "insulating tape"), but figuratively also "breaking off a relationship": 親と絶縁する "to cut ties with one's parents".
