For thermal insulation of a house, one more often says 断熱材.

examples[].german: In the superconducting state, electrical resistance becomes zero.
The maglev train floats its car body using the force of superconducting magnets.
If a substance that shows superconductivity at room temperature were found, the world would change greatly.
en.notes: 超伝導 "superconductivity" is the state in which a material has no electrical resistance at very low temperature. 超電導 is an equivalent spelling, especially in engineering (超電導リニア). Typical: 超伝導状態, 超伝導体 "superconductor", 超伝導磁石, 超伝導を示す. Purely technical.

examples[].german: The law of inertia is a basic principle of the motion of bodies.
When the train suddenly stops, your body nearly falls forward because of inertia.
Even after the engine was turned off, the boat kept moving for a while by inertia.
en.notes: 慣性 is the "inertia" of a body, its tendency to stay at rest or in motion: 慣性の法則 "law of inertia", 慣性が働く, 慣性で進む "to keep moving by inertia". For a person's "carrying on out of habit", 惰性 is used instead (惰性で続ける). Beware of homophones: 完成 "completion", 歓声 "cheer", 感性 "sensibility".

examples[].german: The acceleration of a freely falling object is about 9.8 meters per second squared.
When a car starts off abruptly, the occupants feel a strong acceleration.
The number of internet users is growing at an accelerating pace.
en.notes: 加速度 is "acceleration" as a physical quantity (change of velocity per time): 加速度が大きい, 重力加速度 "gravitational acceleration". The process of speeding up, by contrast, is 加速 (加速する). Figuratively, 加速度的に "at an increasing pace, rapidly" is very common: 加速度的に増える.

examples[].german: A device that uses centrifugal force to separate substances is called a centrifuge.
The washing machine uses centrifugal force to spin the water out of the laundry.
On sharp curves, centrifugal force acts and your body is pushed outward.
en.notes: 遠心力 "centrifugal force" is the outward-acting force in a rotating motion: 遠心力が働く・かかる. The opposite term is 求心力 "centripetal force", which figuratively also means the "cohesion, binding power" of a leader (首相の求心力が低下する). The device is called 遠心分離機 "centrifuge".

examples[].german: Without frictional force, we couldn't even walk.
On rainy days, the friction of the road surface decreases, so the brakes are less effective.
When you wax a floor, friction decreases and it becomes slippery.
en.notes: 摩擦力 is the "frictional force" between two surfaces: 摩擦力が働く, 摩擦力が大きい・小さい, 摩擦力を減らす. Often plain 摩擦 "friction" suffices, which figuratively also means "friction, tension" (貿易摩擦 "trade friction"); 摩擦力, by contrast, is always meant physically.

examples[].german: An elastic body returns to its original shape when the external force is removed.
Natural rubber is a material rich in elasticity.
If you pull a spring beyond its elastic limit, it will no longer return to its original shape.
en.notes: 弾性 is "elasticity", the ability of a material to return to its original shape after deformation: 弾性がある, 弾性に富む, 弾性体, 弾性限界 "elastic limit". The word is technical; in everyday speech one more often says 弾力 (弾力のある肌 "firm, springy skin"). Note: the homophone 男性 "man" sounds exactly the same; context decides.

examples[].german: The Board of Audit examined how public funds were used.
The city underwent an audit concerning the use of subsidies.
Inappropriate expenditure was pointed out in the audit.
en.notes: 会計検査 in Japan is above all the examination of state revenue and expenditure by the 会計検査院 "Board of Audit"; municipalities and recipients of subsidies must also undergo an audit (会計検査を受ける). For audits in private companies, on the other hand, one says 会計監査. It often appears with 指摘 "pointing out": 会計検査で〜が指摘された. A technical term from administration and the news.

examples[].german: Honey has a very high viscosity compared to water.
When it gets cold, the viscosity of engine oil increases.
Volcanic lava flows very differently depending on its viscosity.
en.notes: 粘性 "viscosity" describes how thickly a liquid flows: 粘性が高い・低い, 粘性のある液体. It is technical; in everyday speech one says 粘り気がある or, onomatopoeically, ねばねばする. The related technical term 粘度 denotes the measured viscosity value, for example for motor oil.

examples[].german: Gas molecules spread out evenly by diffusion.
The false rumor spread across social media in no time.
The scent of the aroma oil placed in the room slowly spreads.
en.notes: 拡散 means "spreading, dissemination" and in physics "diffusion"; as a する-verb it is mostly intransitive (においが拡散する), but today it is also transitive: 情報を拡散する "to spread information on social media", 拡散希望 "please share". Other combinations: 核拡散 "nuclear proliferation", 光の拡散. To be distinguished is 普及, the positive spread of technology or goods.

examples[].german: A certain symmetry can be seen in the crystal structure.
The human face is not perfectly symmetrical left to right.
This garden is designed symmetrically around the pond.
en.notes: 対称 is "symmetry": 左右対称 "mirror-symmetric", 点対称 "point-symmetric", 対称的な形; the property is called 対称性. Beware of three often confused homophones: 対象 "object, target group" (子どもを対象にする), 対照 "contrast, comparison" (対照的な性格) and 対称 "symmetry". The rare meaning "second person" (grammar) plays hardly any role in everyday life.

examples[].german: When the phases of two waves are shifted, the interference weakens.
Noise cancelling works by countering noise with sound in opposite phase to cancel it out.
I took a lecture on topology at university.
en.notes: 位相 denotes in physics the "phase" of an oscillation or wave: 位相がずれる "to be out of phase", 位相差 "phase difference", 逆位相 "opposite phase". In mathematics it stands for "topology" (位相幾何学, 位相空間), in linguistics for language variants by group or situation (位相語). Purely technical; the phases of the moon are called 月の満ち欠け in everyday speech.

examples[].german: This function approaches the x-axis asymptotically but never crosses it.
A hyperbola has two asymptotes.
As the sample size increases, the estimate gradually approaches the true value.
en.notes: 漸近 means "to approach gradually (arbitrarily closely)", mainly in mathematics: a curve approaches a straight line ever closer without reaching it (〜に漸近する). The line itself is called 漸近線 "asymptote"; adverbially there is 漸近的に "asymptotically", e.g. in statistics. The character 漸 "gradually" is known from 漸次 and 漸く (usually written ようやく). Outside technical language it is practically unused.

examples[].german: Using differentiation, you can find the rate of change of a function.
Differentiating this expression with respect to x gives 2x.
In high school, I was bad at calculus.
en.notes: 微分 is "differentiation, derivative" and, as a subject, "differential calculus": 微分係数 "differential coefficient", 導関数 "derivative function". As a する-verb it is transitive: 〜をxで微分する "to differentiate with respect to x". Together with 積分 it forms 微分積分 (short: 微積) "calculus", a classic subject of upper secondary school and the first year of university.

examples[].german: I calculated a definite integral to find the area.
Integrating velocity over time gives the distance traveled.
Integrals are more troublesome to calculate than derivatives.
en.notes: 積分 is "integration" or, as a subject, "integral calculus"; the result, the "integral", is also called 積分. Typical: 定積分 "definite integral", 不定積分 "indefinite integral". As a する-verb it is transitive: 〜をxで積分する "to integrate with respect to x". Together with 微分 it forms 微分積分 "calculus".

examples[].german: In quantum mechanics, the position of a particle can only be predicted probabilistically.
Tomorrow the chance of precipitation is seventy percent.
The probability of winning first prize in the lottery is close to zero.
en.notes: 確率 is "probability", both mathematically and in everyday use: 確率が高い・低い, 〜する確率, 降水確率 "chance of rain", 確率は五分五分 "fifty-fifty". Adverbial: 確率的に "probabilistically". Distinguish 可能性 "possibility", which does without a numerical value; with 確率 one thinks of percentages or fractions.

examples[].german: The Avogadro constant is a fundamental constant in chemistry.
In the following expression, let a and b be constants and x a variable.
A reduction in the number of Diet seats is being discussed in the Diet.
en.notes: In mathematics and science, 定数 is a "constant" (opposite term 変数 "variable"), e.g. プランク定数. In politics and administration it denotes a "fixed number": 議員定数 "number of parliamentary seats", 定数割れ "falling below the fixed number", 定数を削減する. Do not confuse it with 定員 "maximum permitted number (of people, seats)" for buses or courses.

examples[].german: Describe the position of an object in a three-dimensional coordinate system.
Find the coordinates of point A on the graph.
The rescue team set out based on the coordinates sent from the missing person's smartphone.
en.notes: 座標 are "coordinates", numerical specifications of a position: 座標を求める, x座標・y座標, 座標軸 "coordinate axis", 座標系 "coordinate system". It is also used for location data on maps or via GPS (緯度と経度の座標). Figuratively, in literary use it can mean "point of orientation" (人生の座標).

examples[].german: The role of the legislature is to enact laws.
The Diet is the sole legislative organ of the state.
Legislation to protect personal information is urgently needed.
en.notes: 立法 is lawmaking, one of the three powers of state alongside 行政 ("executive") and 司法 ("judiciary"). Typical compounds: 立法府 ("legislature, parliament"), 立法権, 立法機関, 議員立法 ("legislation initiated by members of parliament"). As a する-verb it is rare; one rather says 法律を制定する or 立法化する ("to put into law"). Literary, typical of politics and law.

examples[].german: Work on compiling next fiscal year's budget has begun.
The Ministry of Finance is pushing ahead with budget compilation toward the end of the year.
In the city's budget compilation, welfare spending became the focus.
en.notes: 予算編成 is the drawing up of the budget plan; at the national level, the 財務省 prepares the draft, which the Cabinet approves at the end of the year, but prefectures and municipalities also carry out 予算編成. Typical combinations: 予算編成方針 "budget guidelines", 予算編成作業, 予算編成を進める. As a verb one does not say 予算編成する, but 予算を編成する.

examples[].german: String theory assumes space with ten or more dimensions.
That player plays on a different level from other players.
He apparently is only interested in two-dimensional characters.
en.notes: 次元 is the "dimension" in mathematics and physics: 三次元 "three-dimensional", 四次元. In everyday speech the figurative use as "level, plane" is very common: 次元が違う "to play in a completely different league", 次元の低い話 "talk at a low level", 別次元 "a completely different dimension". In pop culture, 二次元 stands for anime and manga characters, 三次元 for real people.

examples[].german: Sound does not travel in a vacuum.
I vacuum-packed the meat and froze it.
After the dictator's death, a power vacuum arose in the country.
en.notes: 真空 is the "vacuum", airless space: 真空状態, 真空中で, 真空パック "vacuum packaging", 真空管 "vacuum tube". Figuratively it denotes an emptiness, especially a "power vacuum" (権力の真空, 政治的真空). In everyday life the word is mainly encountered with vacuum-packed foods.

examples[].german: No more solute can dissolve in a saturated solution.
The smartphone market is already saturated.
Because of the increase in tourists, the accommodations in this town are full.
en.notes: 飽和 is "saturation": chemically 飽和溶液 "saturated solution", physically 飽和水蒸気量 "saturation vapor content". Very common is the figurative use for markets, cities or capacities that are "full": 市場が飽和する, 飽和状態 "state of saturation". As a する-verb it is intransitive. For being full after a meal, one says 満腹 instead.

examples[].german: A precipitate was formed by the chemical reaction.
The pulp settles at the bottom, so please shake well before drinking.
At the water treatment plant, the mud is first allowed to settle, and then the water is filtered.
en.notes: 沈殿 denotes the "settling" of solid particles in a liquid and the resulting "precipitate, sediment": 沈殿する, 沈殿物, 沈殿が生じる. In everyday life it turns up with drinks (底に沈殿する) and in water treatment. The older spelling 沈澱 still occurs. As a する-verb it is intransitive, transitively 沈殿させる; "precipitation" in the sense of rain, on the other hand, is 降水.

examples[].german: Impurities can be removed by filtration.
The kidneys filter the blood and produce urine.
The aquarium water is kept clean by a filtration device.
en.notes: 濾過 is "filtration", the filtering out of solids: 〜を濾過する, 濾過装置. Because 濾 is not a Jōyō kanji, it is usually written ろ過 today. In everyday speech, for coffee or broth one more often says こす "to strain" or フィルターを通す. It is also known from medicine: 腎臓が血液を濾過する "the kidneys filter the blood".

examples[].german: Sodium chloride has a cubic crystal structure.
Snow crystals are hexagonal.
This work is the crystallization of her ten years of effort.
en.notes: 結晶 is the technical term for "crystal" and "crystallization"; as an intransitive する-verb: 塩が結晶する. Common combinations are 結晶構造, 結晶化 and 雪の結晶 "snow crystal". Figuratively, it denotes the "fruit" of long effort: 努力の結晶, 汗の結晶, and 愛の結晶 poetically stands for a shared child. The mineral "rock crystal" is called 水晶 instead.

examples[].german: Anti-rust treatment is applied to prevent metal corrosion.
Near the sea, car parts corrode easily.
The old water pipes corroded, and a leak occurred.
en.notes: 腐食 (older spelling 腐蝕) refers to the chemical decomposition of material, above all the "corrosion" of metals: 金属が腐食する (intransitive), less often transitive 酸が金属を腐食する. In everyday speech, for iron one more often says 錆びる ("to rust"), for food 腐る ("to spoil"). Technical terms include 腐食防止, 耐腐食性 and, in art, 腐食銅版画 ("etching"). For erosion by water or wind, 浸食 is used instead.

examples[].german: Water is known as the most common solvent.
In salt water, water is the solvent and salt is the solute.
This substance does not dissolve in water, but dissolves well in organic solvents.
en.notes: 溶媒 is the "solvent" in which a substance (溶質) is dissolved; together they form the solution (溶液). Typical combinations are 有機溶媒 "organic solvent" and 溶媒に溶かす "to dissolve in a solvent". The word belongs to the technical language of chemistry; for technical solvents such as thinner in everyday life, one more often says 溶剤 or シンナー.

examples[].german: The higher the concentration of the solute, the higher the osmotic pressure.
In sugar water, sugar is the solute.
When the temperature drops, the solute that can no longer stay dissolved comes out as crystals.
en.notes: 溶質 is the "solute" of a solution and the opposite term to 溶媒 "solvent". Typical are 溶質の濃度 "concentration of the solute" as well as 溶質が溶ける or 溶質が析出する "the solute precipitates". It is a purely technical word from chemistry class and practically never occurs in everyday life.

examples[].german: Industrially important substances are produced using catalytic reactions.
Car exhaust gases are converted into harmless substances by catalytic reactions.
Many catalytic reactions in the body are driven by enzymes.
en.notes: 触媒反応 is composed of 触媒 "catalyst" and 反応 "reaction". Typical verbs are 触媒反応が起こる/進む and 触媒反応を利用する; no する-verb is formed from it. While 触媒 alone is also used figuratively as a "catalyst for change", 触媒反応 remains a technical term of chemistry and biochemistry (enzymes are 生体触媒).

examples[].german: Most of the annual revenue is covered by tax receipts.
Due to the economic downturn, national revenue has fallen sharply.
The balance between the city's revenues and expenditures has been upset.
en.notes: 歳入 is the annual income of a state or municipality in its budget; the counterpart is 歳出 ("budget expenditure"). Typical combinations: 歳入が増える/減る, 歳入不足, 歳入を見込む, 国の歳入. For individuals or companies one says 収入 or 売上, not 歳入. 税収 means only the tax revenue, which makes up the largest part of 歳入.

examples[].german: Water can be decomposed into hydrogen and oxygen by electrolysis.
Sports drinks contain electrolytes.
In this factory, chlorine is produced by electrolyzing salt water.
en.notes: 電解 is the short form of 電気分解 "electrolysis"; in school lessons and everyday speech, the full 電気分解 is mostly used. The short form lives on mainly in compounds: 電解質 "electrolyte" (also on sports drinks), 電解液 "electrolyte solution", 電解コンデンサー. As a transitive する-verb: 水を電解する "to electrolyze water".

examples[].german: Acids ionize in water and release hydrogen ions.
The stronger an acid is, the more it ionizes in aqueous solution.
The ionosphere reflects shortwave radio waves.
en.notes: 電離 refers to a substance breaking up into ions, especially electrolytic dissociation in solution; as an intransitive する-verb: 塩化ナトリウムが水中で電離する. Besides the more general loanword イオン化, 電離 is the classic technical term. Important compounds are 電離度 "degree of dissociation", 電離層 "ionosphere" and 電離放射線 "ionizing radiation".

examples[].german: When an acid and a base react and neutralization occurs, salt and water are produced.
Antacids neutralize stomach acid and relieve heartburn.
Acidic soil in the field is neutralized with lime.
en.notes: 中和 is the "neutralization" of acid and base; the result is salt and water. As a する-verb it is intransitive (酸とアルカリが中和する) and often also transitive (胃酸を中和する "to neutralize stomach acid"). Figuratively it means "to render harmless, to balance out", as in 毒を中和する or 中和剤 "neutralizing agent". In everyday life one encounters the word with medicines, garden lime or cleaning agents.

examples[].german: Human cells have forty-six chromosomes.
Sex is determined by the combination of the X and Y chromosomes.
Down syndrome occurs when there is one extra copy of chromosome 21.
en.notes: 染色体 literally means "stainable body" and is the "chromosome". It is counted with 本 (四十六本) or in pairs with 対 (二十三対). Common compounds are 性染色体 "sex chromosome", X染色体 and 染色体異常 "chromosomal abnormality". Not to be confused with 遺伝子 "gene", which is a section on the chromosome.

examples[].german: Mutation is one of the driving forces of evolution.
Viruses mutate repeatedly, and their properties change.
Both his parents are bad at sports, yet their son is a fast runner, like a mutation.
en.notes: 突然変異 literally means "sudden change" and is the biological term for "mutation"; as an intransitive する-verb: 遺伝子が突然変異する. In technical language, for example about viruses, plain 変異 is often used (変異株 "virus variant"). Colloquially it is used jokingly for someone who totally "takes after no one": 突然変異みたいな天才.

examples[].german: The population density varies depending on environmental factors.
The deer population on this island grew rapidly because there are no natural predators.
In forests divided by roads, frog populations become isolated.
en.notes: 個体群 is the ecological technical term for "population": all individuals (個体) of a species in a certain area. Typical are 個体群の密度 and 個体群が増える/減る. In everyday speech one more often says 個体数 "number of individuals" or 群れ "herd, flock". For the human population, 人口 is used, not 個体群.

examples[].german: Living things win the struggle for survival by adapting to their environment.
Six months after starting to study abroad, I was finally able to adapt to life there.
Children adapt to a new environment faster than adults.
en.notes: 適応 is "adaptation" to the environment or circumstances; as an intransitive する-verb with に: 環境に適応する, 新しい職場に適応する. Common compounds are 適応力 "adaptability" and 適応障害 "adjustment disorder". 順応 is very similar, but emphasizes gradual getting used to something (目が暗さに順応する). Not to be confused with 適用 "to apply (a rule)".

examples[].german: In experiments, several assumptions are set up and tested.
I can't answer hypothetical questions.
Let's assume a hundred customers come per day and calculate the sales.
en.notes: 仮定 is an "assumption" that one provisionally treats as given; as a transitive する-verb mostly with と: 〜と仮定する "assuming that ...". Typical are 仮定に基づく, 仮定を設ける and 仮定の話 "a hypothetical question". 仮説, by contrast, is a scientific hypothesis meant to be tested, and 前提 the "premise" on which something is built. In grammar, the conditional form is called 仮定形.

examples[].german: Living things have mechanisms to maintain internal homeostasis.
In this department, a shortage of staff continues on a constant basis.
It is a problem that overtime has become the norm.
en.notes: 恒常 means "constancy, steadiness" and almost never stands alone. As an adjective one uses 恒常的な/恒常的に "constant, permanent"; in addition there are 恒常性 "homeostasis" and 恒常化する "to become the norm". The word is written and technical; in everyday speech one says いつも, 常に or ずっと.

examples[].german: Further experiments are needed to prove the validity of this theory.
The prosecution was unable to prove the defendant's crime.
It is difficult to prove a causal relationship between factory wastewater and health damage.
en.notes: 立証 is the "proof" of a fact with evidence; as a transitive する-verb: 無罪を立証する, 因果関係を立証する. It is especially common in law (立証責任 "burden of proof"). 証明 is more general and usual for mathematical proofs, 実証 emphasizes empirical confirmation through experiments, 論証 logical argumentation.

en.meaning: annual expenditure (of a government); government spending
examples[].german: Social security costs are the largest item of government spending.
The government is working on cutting expenditure.
Revenue falls far short of expenditure, and the deficit continues.
en.notes: 歳出 is the expenditure of a fiscal year by the state or a local government; the counterpart is 歳入 "budget revenue". Typical: 歳出削減 "expenditure cuts", 歳出拡大, 歳出規模 "expenditure volume", 歳出総額. For expenditure of companies or individuals one uses 支出 or 出費, not 歳出. A word from budget and economic reports.

examples[].german: A detailed discussion was carried out based on the experimental results.
Write the report in the order of purpose, method, results and discussion.
This paper examines the causes of the declining birthrate from an economic perspective.
en.notes: 考察 is the thorough thinking through and investigation of a topic; as a transitive する-verb: 原因を考察する. Typical are 考察を加える and 考察を深める. In lab reports and theses, the section following the results, the "discussion", is called 考察. 検討, by contrast, is examining and weighing with a decision in view, and 観察 is mere "observation".

examples[].german: It was shown through rigorous argumentation that this theorem holds.
His claim is interesting, but the argumentation is insufficient.
Based on historical sources, the author demonstrates that the theory is mistaken.
en.notes: 論証 is logical "demonstration" through arguments; as a transitive する-verb: 〜を論証する, 〜ことを論証する. Typical are 論証が不十分だ and 厳密な論証. 立証 emphasizes proof with evidence (e.g. in court), 実証 confirmation by experiments; for mathematical proofs, 証明 is the usual word. The word is academic and written.

examples[].german: A new asteroid was discovered through astronomical observation.
Today Tokyo recorded its highest temperature since records began.
The notion that the economy will recover soon is nothing but wishful thinking.
en.notes: 観測 is measuring observation of natural phenomena, mostly with instruments: 天体観測, 気象観測, 地震を観測する. Frequent in weather reports: 観測史上最高 "highest value since records began". 観察, by contrast, is close looking, such as at plants in class. Figuratively, 観測 means "assessment, forecast", especially in 希望的観測 "wishful thinking".

examples[].german: In statistics, the characteristics of the population are estimated from a sample.
For my summer vacation homework, I made an insect specimen collection.
A dinosaur skeleton specimen is on display at the museum.
en.notes: 標本 is a preserved "specimen" for collections and teaching (昆虫標本, 骨格標本) and, in statistics, the "sample" (標本調査). Figuratively it denotes a typical model example: 彼は真面目人間の標本だ. サンプル is the more general loanword, also for product samples, and 検体 the medical test sample.

examples[].german: Chemical analysis requires the use of high-purity reagents.
When the reagent was added, the color of the solution turned blue.
Please do not pour used reagents down the sink, but put them in the designated containers.
en.notes: 試薬 is a "reagent", that is, a chemical with which one detects or tests something. Typical are 試薬を加える, 試薬瓶 and 検査試薬 (e.g. in rapid tests). 薬品 is the general expression for "chemicals", while 薬 usually refers to medicines. The word belongs to lab and technical language.

examples[].german: We are studying tissue regeneration through cell culture.
Bacteria taken from the patient are cultured to find the cause.
The day when cultured meat lines supermarket shelves may be near.
en.notes: 培養 is the cultivation of microorganisms, cells or tissue under controlled conditions; as a transitive する-verb: 細菌を培養する. Typical compounds are 細胞培養, 培養液 "culture medium" and 培養肉 "lab-grown meat". For growing plants one usually says 栽培, for fish farming 養殖; in the figurative sense of "fostering abilities", 培養 is rare, where 養う or 育む are more usual.

examples[].german: We examined the validity of the theory with a virtual experiment on a computer.
The price of cryptocurrencies can fluctuate greatly in a single day.
With the goggles on, you can walk around freely in virtual space.
en.notes: 仮想 means "imagined, assumed" and today mainly "virtual". It mostly stands as the first element of compounds: 仮想現実 "virtual reality", 仮想空間, 仮想通貨 "cryptocurrency", 仮想敵国 "hypothetical enemy state". Attributively one uses 仮想の or 仮想的な; the する-verb 仮想する "to imagine, to suppose" is rare. 仮定, by contrast, is an assumption in an argument, 空想 a fantasy or daydream.

examples[].german: Collect a specimen and analyze its components.
As the specimen for the PCR test, mucus from the back of the nose is collected.
A wrong diagnosis was made because of a mix-up of specimens.
en.notes: 検体 is the "specimen" in medicine and the lab, e.g. blood, urine or a swab: 検体を採取する, 検体を提出する, 検体検査. 標本, by contrast, is a preserved preparation, and サンプル is the general word for "sample". Careful when listening: 献体 (same reading) is the "body donation" for medical education.

examples[].german: Measurements always involve error, so statistical processing is necessary.
A difference of about a thousand yen is within the margin of error.
This watch deviates by only a few seconds a month.
en.notes: 誤差 is the unavoidable "deviation" between a measured or calculated value and the true value, not an "error" in the sense of a mistake (for that: 間違い, ミス). Typical are 誤差が出る/生じる, 誤差を小さくする and 誤差の範囲内 "within the margin of error". Colloquially, one says 「そのくらいは誤差だ」 for "that is negligible".

examples[].german: Standard deviation is an indicator of the dispersion of data.
This high school is famous for its high academic standing.
Square the deviations from the mean and add them up.
en.notes: 偏差 is the "deviation" of a value from the mean or target value. Best known are 標準偏差 "standard deviation" and 偏差値, the standardized score by which schools and universities in Japan are ranked (偏差値が高い). Unlike 誤差 (measurement inaccuracy), 偏差 describes a systematic difference or dispersion; colloquially one says ずれ.

examples[].german: Use regression analysis to predict data trends.
Among young people recently, a return to the retro culture of the Showa era can be seen.
Salmon return to the river where they were born to spawn.
en.notes: 回帰 first means "return, recurrence" to a starting point; as an intransitive する-verb with に: 原点に回帰する "to return to one's roots", サケが生まれた川に回帰する. In statistics it is "regression" (回帰分析, 回帰直線), and in geography it is part of 北回帰線 "Tropic of Cancer". 復帰, by contrast, is a return to a former place, such as 職場復帰.

examples[].german: Apply temperature correction to the measured values to obtain accurate results.
The government drew up a supplementary budget for economic stimulus.
You should adjust the brightness of this photo a little.
en.notes: 補正 is the subsequent correcting or adjusting of a value so that it is right; as a transitive する-verb: データを補正する, 写真の色を補正する. Very common is 補正予算 "supplementary budget"; in fashion there is 体型補正 "figure-shaping". 修正 and 訂正 correct mistakes (訂正 mainly in texts), 較正 is the calibration of a measuring instrument.

examples[].german: If the discrepancy between the theoretical and measured values is large, the hypothesis is reviewed.
The politicians' statements are out of touch with the public's sentiment.
Many new employees are troubled by the gap between ideal and reality.
en.notes: 乖離 refers to the gaping apart of two things that should actually agree; as an intransitive する-verb: AとBが乖離する, 現実から乖離する. Typical are 理想と現実の乖離 and 民意との乖離. The word is written; in everyday speech one says ずれ, 差 or 隔たり. Since 乖 is not a Jōyō kanji, newspapers sometimes write かい離.

examples[].german: Determine whether the infinite series converges.
The disturbance is finally subsiding.
The government is aiming to bring the situation under control early.
en.notes: 収束 is "convergence" in mathematics (級数が収束する) and the focusing of light in optics. In the news it usually means that a crisis or unrest "subsides, comes under control": 事態が収束する, 混乱を収束させる, 収束に向かう. Do not confuse it with the identically read 終息 "complete end" (e.g. of an epidemic). The opposite term in mathematics is 発散.

examples[].german: Because this series diverges, its sum cannot be defined.
I relieved my stress by singing at karaoke.
When you exercise, the body gives off heat.
en.notes: 発散 means "to give off outward, to emit": 熱を発散する, においが発散する. In everyday life it is known mainly from ストレスを発散する and ストレス発散 "stress relief", that is, letting out pent-up feelings. In mathematics it is the "divergence" of a series, the opposite term to 収束. It is used both transitively and intransitively.

examples[].german: A reflux condenser is used to prevent evaporation of the solvent.
If the profits of overseas subsidiaries flow back into the country, it will also have a positive effect on the economy.
When the return flow of blood to the heart worsens, the legs swell easily.
en.notes: 還流 is "flowing back" to the starting point; as an intransitive する-verb: 〜に還流する. In the lab, 還流冷却器 "reflux condenser" is known; in business 資金の還流 "return flow of capital"; in medicine 静脈還流 "venous return". 逆流, by contrast, is flowing in the wrong direction, and the identically read 環流 denotes a circulating current.

en.meaning: evaporation, vaporization; vanishing without a trace (colloquial)
examples[].german: I studied the phenomenon of molecules evaporating from the surface of a liquid.
In summer, puddles evaporate quickly.
My father left behind debts and vanished without a trace.
en.notes: 蒸発 is the "evaporation" or "vaporization" of a liquid; as an intransitive する-verb: 水が蒸発する, transitive with 蒸発させる. 沸騰, by contrast, is "boiling", 気化 the general technical term for the transition to gas. Colloquially, 蒸発 also means that a person "disappears without a trace", for example to escape debts or family.

en.meaning: sublimation; sublimation (elevation to a higher level)
examples[].german: Dry ice sublimates and turns directly into gas.
The reason ice left in the freezer for a long time gets smaller is that sublimation is occurring.
He transformed the pain of his heartbreak into a masterpiece of a song.
en.notes: 昇華 is "sublimation" in chemistry, the direct transition from solid to gas: ドライアイスが昇華する. In psychology it means the sublimation of drives, and figuratively the raising of something to a higher level, mostly in the pattern AをBに昇華させる: 悲しみを芸術に昇華させる. This figurative use is elevated written language and common in reviews and interviews.

examples[].german: When water vapor is cooled, it condenses into water droplets.
The director's thoughts are condensed into two hours in this film.
Dried tomatoes have a concentrated umami and a rich flavor.
en.notes: 凝縮 is physically the "condensation" of gas into liquid: 水蒸気が凝縮する. The fogging up of windows, however, is called 結露 in everyday speech. Very common is the figurative sense "to condense, to concentrate", mostly in the passive: うまみが凝縮されている, 魅力が凝縮された一冊. It is used both transitively and intransitively.

examples[].german: Activated carbon has the ability to adsorb harmful substances.
If you put charcoal in the refrigerator, it absorbs odors.
An octopus clings firmly to rocks with its suckers.
en.notes: 吸着 is "adsorption" in chemistry: substances accumulate on a surface, e.g. with 活性炭 or 吸着剤. In everyday speech it also means "to cling by suction, to adhere" (吸盤で吸着する). Although JMdict lists it as intransitive, 〜を吸着する ("to adsorb something") is very common. 吸収, by contrast, is "absorption", taking up into the interior.

examples[].german: The boundaries of the electoral districts were reviewed.
He ran from his home electoral district.
In a single-member district, only one person can win.
en.notes: 選挙区 is the electoral district in which candidates run. In the Japanese House of Representatives, one distinguishes 小選挙区 "single-member district" and 比例代表 "proportional representation"; the redrawing of boundaries is called 区割り. Typical are 地元の選挙区 "home district", 〜区から立候補する/出馬する and 選挙区を回る "to tour the district". The word 区 alone, by contrast, usually means "city ward".

examples[].german: X-rays have the property of penetrating matter.
These curtains let almost no light through.
I use an image with a transparent background for the logo.
en.notes: 透過 is the "penetration" or "letting through" of light, radiation or substances: 光を透過する, X線が透過する. Important compounds are 透過率 "transmittance" and 透過性. 透明, by contrast, describes the property "transparent", and 浸透 the slow penetration of liquid. In image editing, 透過 means "transparent background" (透過PNG).

examples[].german: The sky is blue because of the scattering of light in the atmosphere.
Car parts were scattered all over the accident site.
Strong winds have scattered trash all over the park.
en.notes: 散乱 is physically the "scattering" of light or particles (光の散乱). In everyday speech it means that things "lie scattered about": 床にごみが散乱している, 書類が散乱する; it is intransitive. For a messy room, one colloquially says 散らかっている instead, and 拡散 is "spreading" (e.g. of posts on social media).

examples[].german: When electrons are excited, they transition to a higher energy level.
Lasers use the mechanism by which excited atoms emit light.
Fluorescent substances emit light when excited by ultraviolet light.
en.notes: 励起 is a technical term of physics and chemistry for the "excitation" of atoms, molecules or electrons to a higher energy level. Typical are 励起状態 "excited state" (opposite term 基底状態 "ground state") and the passive form 励起される. The figurative sense "to enliven" is very rare. Despite the shared kanji, it has nothing to do with 励ます "to encourage".

examples[].german: When an electron moves from a higher energy level to a lower one, light is emitted.
When you press this button, it moves on to the next screen.
On land after a forest fire, the vegetation gradually shifts from grassland to forest.
en.notes: 遷移 is a technical word for the "transition" from one state to another, mainly in physics, chemistry and computer science: 状態遷移, 画面遷移 ("screen transition" in apps), 遷移金属 ("transition metals"), electron transitions between energy levels. In ecology 遷移 means "succession" (植生の遷移). As a verb it is intransitive: AからBへ遷移する. For states of matter one says 相転移 or, specifically, 融解, 蒸発; in everyday speech 移り変わる or 変わる suffices.

examples[].german: The radiant energy from the Sun warms the Earth.
Because of radiant heat from the asphalt in summer, it is very hot near the ground.
Radiant heating produces no air movement, so dust is not stirred up.
en.notes: 輻射 is an older technical term for "radiation", especially thermal radiation. Because 輻 is not a Jōyō kanji, textbooks today mostly say 放射 (放射熱, 放射エネルギー). 輻射 is still alive in 輻射熱 "radiant heat" and 輻射式暖房 "radiant heating". It has nothing to do with radioactivity (放射線, 放射能) in everyday speech.

examples[].german: Metals are substances with high thermal conductivity.
Copper pots conduct heat well, so food is less likely to cook unevenly.
Cups made of material with poor heat conduction are easy to hold even with hot drinks in them.
en.notes: 熱伝導 is "heat conduction", one of the three kinds of heat transfer alongside 対流 "convection" and 放射 "radiation". It is most often encountered in 熱伝導率 "thermal conductivity" and in phrases like 熱伝導がよい/悪い. It is a pure noun; as a verb one says 熱が伝わる or 熱を伝える.

examples[].german: Atmospheric convection shapes weather patterns.
When you heat the water in a pot, convection occurs and the whole thing warms up.
Airplanes fly in the upper part of the troposphere.
en.notes: 対流 is "convection", that is, heat transport by flowing liquids or gases. Typical are 対流が起こる/生じる and 対流式ストーブ. In meteorology 対流圏 "troposphere" is important; strong rising air currents form thunderclouds (積乱雲). Alongside 伝導 "conduction" and 放射 "radiation", it is one of the three kinds of heat transfer.

examples[].german: The entropy of an isolated system increases over time.
In information theory, entropy expresses the uncertainty of information.
No matter how many times I tidy up, the entropy of my room only increases.
en.notes: エントロピー is, in thermodynamics, the measure of the disorder of a system; according to the second law, it does not decrease in an isolated system (孤立系): エントロピー増大の法則. In information theory it denotes uncertainty or information content. Typical: エントロピーが増大する/減少する. Half jokingly, the word is also used in everyday speech for increasing chaos.

examples[].german: Inspired by previous research, I planned a new experiment.
Spurred by my friend's success, I also started studying English.
A single small incident triggered massive demonstrations.
en.notes: 触発 means that something gives an impetus or sets something off. Most common is the passive 〜に触発される "to be inspired, spurred on by something"; actively it means "to trigger": 事件が暴動を触発する. The basic sense "ignition by touch" is found in 触発機雷 "contact mine". 刺激を受ける is similar but more general; 触発 emphasizes that one's own activity arises from it.

examples[].german: Solve complex equations using numerical analysis.
By analyzing the surveillance camera footage, the culprit was identified.
At university, the analysis course was the hardest.
en.notes: 解析 is a systematic, mostly technical or computational "analysis" of data and structures; as a transitive する-verb: データを解析する. Typical are 遺伝子解析, 画像解析, 数値解析 and, in computer science, 構文解析 "parsing"; 解析学 is the mathematical subject "analysis". 分析 is more general and is also used for markets, politics or psychology.

examples[].german: Rural areas have been regarded as the electoral stronghold of conservative parties.
The parties competed over the large pool of voters in urban areas.
The opposition is trying to break into the ruling party's strongholds.
en.notes: 票田 literally means "vote rice field": an area or group from which a party reliably "harvests" votes. Typical are 大票田 "large voter reservoir" (e.g. big cities), 票田を固める "to secure the core electorate", 票田を切り崩す "to break into rivals' strongholds" and 〜の票田とされる. A word of political reporting, rather written.

examples[].german: We performed hypothesis testing and confirmed a statistically significant difference.
In hypothesis testing, you first set up a null hypothesis and an alternative hypothesis.
Use hypothesis testing to check whether the new drug is effective.
en.notes: 仮説検定 is statistical "hypothesis testing". One sets up a 帰無仮説 "null hypothesis" and a 対立仮説 "alternative hypothesis" and checks with a 有意水準 "significance level" whether the null hypothesis is rejected. Concrete procedures are called 検定 for short (t検定, カイ二乗検定); in everyday speech, however, 検定 alone also means "exam, certificate" (漢字検定). The usual phrase is 仮説検定を行う.

examples[].german: If the null hypothesis is rejected, the alternative hypothesis is supported.
Since the p-value was smaller than 0.05, the null hypothesis was rejected.
The null hypothesis of this experiment is that "the new fertilizer has no effect".
en.notes: 帰無仮説 is the "null hypothesis"; 帰無 literally means "to return to nothing", because it is set up in the expectation of rejecting it. The fixed verbs are 帰無仮説を棄却する "to reject" and 帰無仮説を採択する "to accept" or 棄却できない. The opposite term is 対立仮説 "alternative hypothesis". A purely technical statistics term.

examples[].german: A statistically significant difference was found.
The incidence rate among smokers was significantly higher than among non-smokers.
No significant difference was seen between the two groups.
en.notes: 有意 means "significant" in statistics and is used as a な-adjective: 有意な差, 有意に高い. Important compounds are 有意差 "significant difference" and 有意水準 "significance level". The meaning "intentional" is rare. Do not confuse it with the everyday word 有意義 "meaningful, worthwhile" (有意義な時間).

examples[].german: The exact content of a substance is measured by quantitative analysis.
It is better to set goals as quantitatively as possible.
It is not easy to quantify customer satisfaction.
en.notes: 定量 literally means "fixed quantity"; in science and business, however, it appears almost only as a first element with the meaning "quantitative": 定量分析, 定量的な評価, 定量化する "to quantify". The opposite term is 定性 "qualitative". For the dose of medicines, 用量 is used instead.

examples[].german: Qualitative analysis is a technique for identifying the types of substances.
Not only the numbers from questionnaires but also qualitative information from interviews is important.
This test strip can only be used for qualitative tests and cannot tell you the concentration.
en.notes: 定性 means "qualitative" and never stands alone, only as a first element: 定性分析, 定性調査, 定性的な情報. It is the opposite term to 定量 "quantitative": 定性 asks "what/what kind", 定量 "how much". Beware when listening: 訂正 "correction" is read ていせい in exactly the same way.

examples[].german: The unknown compound was identified using mass spectrometry.
I looked up the collected insects in a field guide and identified the species.
The identity of the body was established through DNA analysis.
en.notes: 同定 is the technical "identification" or "determination", that is, establishing which species, substance or person something is; as a transitive する-verb: 化合物を同定する, 種を同定する. It belongs to biology, chemistry and forensics. In everyday speech and in the news, 特定する is mostly used (犯人を特定する); 識別 is mere "distinguishing".

examples[].german: Measuring instruments need to be calibrated regularly.
A scale will not give correct values unless it is calibrated before use.
We have a specialist institution carry out the calibration of the radiation measuring devices.
en.notes: 較正 is the "calibration" of measuring instruments against a standard; as a transitive する-verb: 機器を較正する, plus 較正曲線 "calibration curve". 校正 is often written for this too, but it mainly means "proofreading". In engineering the loanword キャリブレーション is also common. Do not confuse it with 補正, the correcting of the measured values themselves.

examples[].german: Mosquitoes are insects that act as vectors of malaria.
This disease is transmitted by ticks.
Through language, people share their thoughts.
en.notes: 媒介 is the "mediating" between two things or the "transmission" of pathogens; as a transitive する-verb: 蚊が病気を媒介する, often in the passive 〜によって媒介される. Abstractly one says 〜を媒介として "mediated by, through". 仲介, by contrast, is business brokerage (不動産の仲介), and 媒体 is the "medium" in the sense of a data carrier or the press.

examples[].german: Thanks to the surface tension of water, small insects can float on the water surface.
Water droplets become round because surface tension acts.
Detergent has the effect of lowering the surface tension of water.
en.notes: 表面張力 is the physics term for the "surface tension" of liquids. Typical are 表面張力が働く ("surface tension acts"), 表面張力が大きい／小さい, and 表面張力で〜 or 表面張力によって〜 for the cause. It explains, for example, round water droplets or insects on water; detergent 表面張力を下げる ("lowers the surface tension").

examples[].german: Through capillary action, plants draw water up from their roots.
A towel soaking up water is also an example of capillary action.
If you stand a thin glass tube in water, the water rises in it by capillary action.
en.notes: 毛管現象 is the technical term for "capillary action": liquid rises on its own in narrow tubes, pores or fibers. The long form 毛細管現象 means the same and is at least as common. Typical frames are 毛管現象によって〜 and 毛管現象で水が上がる／吸い上げられる. The term explains everyday things such as an absorbent towel or a candle wick.

examples[].german: The candidates' vote counts were announced.
She was elected with a much higher share of the vote than last time.
The candidate received about 30,000 votes.
en.notes: 得票 are the votes that a candidate or party receives, not to be confused with 投票 "casting a vote, voting". Most common in compounds: 得票数 "number of votes", 得票率 "share of the vote". As a する-verb one says 〜票を得票する "to receive ... votes"; more colloquial is 〜票を取る or 〜票を獲得する.

examples[].german: Water has a high specific heat capacity, so it heats up and cools down slowly.
Sand has a low specific heat capacity, so it gets hot quickly during the day.
The difference in specific heat between land and sea produces the sea breeze.
en.notes: 比熱 means "specific heat capacity", i.e. the amount of heat needed to raise 1 g of a substance by 1 °C. One says 比熱が大きい／高い or 比熱が小さい／低い. Do not confuse it with 熱容量 ("heat capacity" of a whole body) - 比熱 always refers to a unit of mass. Typical in physics lessons and climatology, for example in the contrast between land and sea.

examples[].german: Latent heat is absorbed when ice melts.
When sweat evaporates it takes away latent heat, so the body cools down.
Typhoons use the latent heat of water vapor evaporated from the sea as their energy source.
en.notes: 潜熱 is "latent heat" (heat of transformation), which is absorbed or released during phase changes such as melting or evaporation without a change in temperature. Typical combinations: 潜熱を吸収する／放出する, 融解潜熱 ("heat of fusion"), 蒸発潜熱 ("heat of vaporization"). The opposite term is 顕熱 ("sensible heat"). Purely technical; the figurative meaning "hidden heat" is rare.

examples[].german: The second law of thermodynamics states that entropy increases.
I am taking a lecture on thermodynamics at university.
A perpetual motion machine is considered thermodynamically impossible.
en.notes: 熱力学 is "thermodynamics" as a branch of physics. It often appears in fixed combinations: 熱力学第一法則／第二法則 ("first/second law of thermodynamics"), 熱力学的に ("thermodynamically"), 熱力学温度. It is built from 熱 ("heat") and 力学 ("mechanics"), like 流体力学 or 量子力学. Technical language from university study and engineering.

examples[].german: Fluid mechanics is the science that studies the motion of liquids and gases.
The shape of the Shinkansen's nose is designed based on fluid mechanics.
How an airplane flies can be explained by fluid mechanics.
en.notes: 流体力学 is "fluid mechanics" or "fluid dynamics", the study of the motion of liquids and gases (流体 = "fluid"). Typical: 流体力学に基づいて設計する, 流体力学的な観点から, 計算流体力学 ("computational fluid dynamics, CFD"). Related terms from the same field are 乱流, 層流 and 渦. Technical language from engineering, meteorology and physics.

examples[].german: Turbulence easily occurs in fluids flowing at high speed.
When the river's flow gets faster, it changes from laminar to turbulent flow.
Turbulence forms behind a car and causes air resistance.
en.notes: 乱流 is "turbulent flow" in liquids or gases, the opposite of 層流 ("laminar flow"). Typical are 乱流が発生する／生じる and 層流から乱流に変わる. For turbulence on an airplane, everyday speech usually says 乱気流 - 乱流 is the more general technical term. It is not used in the figurative sense ("political turbulence"); there 混乱 or 波乱 fit.

examples[].german: In laminar flow, the fluid flows in an orderly way.
If you let water run gently from a faucet, it becomes laminar and looks like a transparent rod.
In clean rooms, air is passed through in laminar flow to keep out dust.
en.notes: 層流 is "laminar flow", in which a fluid moves in orderly, parallel layers (層 = "layer"). The opposite term is 乱流. Typical: 層流になる, 層流を保つ, 層流から乱流へ移る. Purely technical; the word is encountered for example in clean-room ventilation or airfoils (層流翼).

examples[].german: I analyzed the structure of the vortices forming in the fluid.
Large whirlpools can be seen in the Naruto Strait.
When the victory was decided, the venue was engulfed in a whirl of excitement.
en.notes: 渦 is a "vortex" or "whirlpool" in water, air or smoke. Typical phrases: 渦を巻く ("to swirl, to spiral"), 渦ができる, 渦に巻き込まれる ("to get caught in a whirlpool"). Figuratively it stands for a whirl of events or emotions: 混乱の渦, 興奮の渦, plus 渦中 ("in the midst of events"). The 渦潮 ("tidal whirlpools") of Naruto are well known.

examples[].german: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem shows the relationship between fluctuation and dissipation.
This arm swings left and right, driven by a motor.
We installed a device that reduces the rolling of the ship.
en.notes: 揺動 is a technical term of written language for "swaying, swinging back and forth". In engineering it describes a pendulum or swiveling motion (揺動運動, 揺動する), in physics the "fluctuation" of a quantity, especially in 揺動散逸定理 ("fluctuation-dissipation theorem"). In everyday speech and popular physics, 揺れ or 揺らぎ is usually used instead, e.g. 量子揺らぎ ("quantum fluctuation").

examples[].german: The composition is investigated by analyzing the absorption spectrum of the elements.
When sunlight passes through a prism, it splits into a rainbow-like spectrum.
A star's temperature can be determined from its spectrum.
en.notes: スペクトル (from French spectre) is the "spectrum" in physics and chemistry: light, radiation or a signal broken down by wavelength or frequency. Common compounds: 吸収スペクトル, 発光スペクトル, 周波数スペクトル, スペクトル分析. For "spectrum" in the figurative sense ("a broad spectrum of opinions"), one usually uses 幅広い or 範囲; the English form スペクトラム appears mainly in technical terms such as 自閉スペクトラム症.

examples[].german: Nanoscale structures are observed with an electron microscope.
Viruses are so small that they can only be seen with an electron microscope.
This research institute has three electron microscopes.
en.notes: 電子顕微鏡 is the "electron microscope", as opposed to the 光学顕微鏡 ("optical microscope"). In professional circles it is abbreviated to 電顕; one distinguishes 走査型電子顕微鏡 (SEM) and 透過型電子顕微鏡 (TEM). Typical frames: 電子顕微鏡で観察する／撮影する, 電子顕微鏡写真 ("electron micrograph"). The devices are counted with 台.

en.meaning: official announcement; public notice (of an election)
examples[].german: The official announcement day of the election was decided.
The House of Representatives election was officially announced, and the campaign began.
The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism announced this year's official land prices.
en.notes: 公示 is an official public announcement. In election law, it refers specifically to the official proclamation of elections to the House of Representatives and House of Councillors; the official campaign begins afterward. For local and prefectural elections, 告示 is said instead. Other fixed combinations: 公示日 "announcement day", 公示地価 "officially announced land price". Mostly in the passive: 〜が公示される.

examples[].german: Spectroscopy is widely used for analyzing the composition of substances.
With a prism, you can split sunlight into its spectrum.
They split the light of a star into its spectrum to investigate its components.
en.notes: 分光 means the splitting of light into its spectrum, for example with a prism or grating: 光を分光する. The method or science is called 分光法 or 分光学 ("spectroscopy"), the device 分光器 ("spectroscope"), the analysis 分光分析. The word on its own is found almost only in physics, chemistry and astronomy; in everyday speech one would rather say 虹のように光を分ける.

examples[].german: I cut the specimen into thin slices and observed it under a microscope.
We collected river water as a sample and analyzed the water quality.
Samples of lunar rock are on display at the museum.
en.notes: 試料 is the "sample" or "test material" in laboratories, analysis and materials testing: 試料を採取する ("to take a sample"), 試料を分析する, 血液試料. Do not confuse it with the identically read 資料 ("documents, materials, data") and 飼料 ("animal feed") - in speech only the context clarifies. In medical practice, 検体 is preferred for blood or urine samples, and colloquially also サンプル.

examples[].german: The cross-linking reaction of polymers increases the strength of the material.
Construction of a bridge connecting the island and the mainland has begun.
This research aims to bridge theory and practice.
en.notes: 架橋 has two specialist fields: literally "bridge building" (橋を架ける), e.g. 架橋工事, and in chemistry the "cross-linking" of polymer chains (架橋反応, 架橋剤, 架橋する). Figuratively it also means "building a bridge" between two fields, e.g. 理論と実践の架橋. The word is technical written language; in everyday speech one simply says 橋を架ける for building a bridge and 橋渡し(をする) for "to mediate".

examples[].german: Integrated circuits carry billions of transistors.
A smartphone contains many small integrated circuits.
He designs integrated circuits at a semiconductor manufacturer.
en.notes: 集積回路 is the "integrated circuit" (IC), i.e. many electronic components on one semiconductor chip. In everyday speech one usually says IC or ICチップ, and LSI (大規模集積回路) for very large circuits. Typical: 集積回路を設計する／製造する, 集積回路の集積度 ("integration density"). 集積 means "accumulation, integration", 回路 "circuit" - cf. 電子回路.

examples[].german: The temperature is kept constant by feedback control.
The brakes failed and the car went out of control.
It is not easy to control feelings of anger.
en.notes: 制御 is the "control, regulation" of machines and systems: 制御する, 自動制御, 温度制御, 制御装置, 制御不能 ("out of control"). Figuratively also used for reining in emotions or people (感情を制御する), although コントロールする or 抑える sounds more everyday there. Distinction: 管理 is "administration, management", 操作 is "operation" by a human - 制御 stresses the deliberate steering of a process. Transitive する-verb with を.

examples[].german: Precise measurement technology is the foundation of quality control.
I measure my daily step count with this app.
The time is measured automatically at the moment of crossing the finish line.
en.notes: 計測 is "measuring, measurement" with instruments, especially when exact numerical values are recorded: 計測する, 計測器 ("measuring instrument"), 計測技術, 計測データ. Compared with the general 測定, 計測 sounds somewhat more technical and is often used for continuous or automatic measurements (タイムを計測する, 歩数を計測する). In everyday speech one simply says 測る／計る. Transitive する-verb with を.

examples[].german: Manufacturing precision machinery requires advanced technical skill.
An abnormality was found at my health checkup, so I am going to have a detailed examination.
This watch is made extremely precisely.
en.notes: 精密 is a な-adjective or noun for "precise, very exact, down to the detail". It often stands as a modifier before nouns: 精密機械 ("precision machine"), 精密検査 ("thorough medical examination"), 精密な地図／計算. Compared with 正確 ("correct, error-free"), 精密 stresses fineness and level of detail; the similar 緻密 is used more for plans and thinking. Adverbially: 精密に作る／調べる.

examples[].german: Casting technology has been used for metalworking since ancient times.
The Great Buddha of Nara was cast in bronze.
In the Edo period, coins were cast in many places.
en.notes: 鋳造 is the "casting" of metal into a mold (鋳型): 鋳造する, 鋳造品 ("casting, cast part"), 鋳造所 ("foundry"). Historically it also stands for minting coins: 貨幣を鋳造する. Its counterpart in metal forming is 鍛造 ("forging") - the kanji 鋳 ("to cast") and 鍛 ("to forge") are easily confused. The related simple verb is 鋳る (いる), known from 鋳物 ("cast goods").

examples[].german: Arc welding is a technique for joining metals at high temperature.
My father works as a welder at a small town factory.
I had the broken metal fitting on the gate welded and repaired.
en.notes: 溶接 is "welding", i.e. joining metal parts by melting them: 溶接する, 溶接工 ("welder"), 溶接機, 溶接部 ("weld"). Typical methods: アーク溶接 ("arc welding"), ガス溶接, スポット溶接. To be distinguished from はんだ付け ("soldering") and 接着 ("gluing"). Transitive する-verb: AとBを溶接する or AをBに溶接する.

examples[].german: Grinding lenses requires high precision.
I had the surface of my teeth polished at the dentist.
When a rough stone is polished, it becomes a beautiful gem.
en.notes: 研磨 means "grinding, polishing" of surfaces such as lenses, metal, teeth or gemstones: 研磨する, 研磨剤 ("abrasive, polishing agent"), 研磨機. It is more technical than 磨く; in everyday speech one says 包丁を研ぐ ("to sharpen a knife") or 靴を磨く. In elevated language, 研磨 can also mean "honing" one's own skills, but 研鑽 or 切磋琢磨 are more usual for that.

examples[].german: A new lawmaker ran for party leader.
Is there anyone who will run for class representative?
This city is bidding to host the Olympics.
en.notes: 立候補する is intransitive; the office or election takes に: 選挙に立候補する, 市長に立候補する. It is also used loosely for "to volunteer" (学級委員に立候補する) and for cities bidding as host (開催地に立候補する). In the press, 出馬する often appears as a synonym. The person is called 候補者 or 立候補者; if one is proposed by others, that is 推薦.

examples[].german: In machining, unnecessary portions are removed with a cutting tool.
When the blade of a cutting tool wears out, machining accuracy drops.
Smartphone cases are made by machining aluminum blocks.
en.notes: 切削 is "machining", i.e. the chip-removing processing of metal, wood or plastic with cutting tools (turning, milling, drilling). Typical: 切削加工, 切削工具, 切削油 ("cutting oil"), 切削する. Purely technical language of manufacturing engineering; everyday "to cut" is 切る, "to shave off, to plane" is 削る. Related are 研削 ("grinding") and 掘削 ("excavation, drilling" in earthworks).

examples[].german: Cylindrical parts are machined using a lathe.
My grandfather worked as a lathe operator for forty years.
The factory introduced two NC lathes.
en.notes: 旋盤 is the "lathe": the workpiece rotates while a fixed cutting tool removes material. Typical: 旋盤で削る／加工する, 旋盤工 ("lathe operator"), NC旋盤 ("CNC lathe"). To be distinguished from the フライス盤 ("milling machine"), in which the tool rotates. The machines are counted with 台.

examples[].german: Numerically controlled machine tools can manufacture parts with complex shapes.
Orders for machine tools have increased greatly compared with the previous year.
There are many factories in this town that make parts for machine tools.
en.notes: 工作機械 is the umbrella term for "machine tools", i.e. machines that process metal and other materials - e.g. 旋盤, フライス盤 or ボール盤. Typical: 工作機械メーカー, 数値制御工作機械 or NC工作機械, 工作機械の受注. Do not confuse it with 工具 ("hand tool") or 機械工作 ("machining" as an activity). Japan is among the largest manufacturers, so the word often appears in business news.

examples[].german: Hydraulic cylinders can generate great force.
A hydraulic excavator is digging soil at the construction site.
If the oil pressure warning light comes on, please stop the car immediately.
en.notes: 油圧 literally means "oil pressure" and in engineering stands for power transmission with oil, i.e. "hydraulics": 油圧シリンダー, 油圧ショベル ("hydraulic excavator"), 油圧式ブレーキ. In cars, 油圧 also means engine oil pressure (油圧計, 油圧警告灯). The pressure of other liquids is generally called 液圧, of water 水圧; the pneumatic counterpart is 空気圧.

examples[].german: Pneumatic equipment uses compressed air as its power source.
This robot hand is operated by air pressure.
Compared with hydraulics, pneumatics produces less force but moves faster.
en.notes: 空圧 is the engineering short form of 空気圧 and stands for "compressed air, pneumatics": 空圧機器, 空圧シリンダー, 空圧で動く. It is the counterpart to 油圧 ("hydraulics") - pneumatics is faster and cleaner, but weaker. In everyday speech, tire pressure is 空気圧 (タイヤの空気圧) and atmospheric air pressure is 気圧; 空圧 remains technical language.

examples[].german: Rotary motion is transmitted by the meshing of gears.
When I opened the old clock, it was full of small gears.
Sometimes I feel that I am just one cog in the company's machine.
en.notes: 歯車 is the "gear, cogwheel": 歯車が噛み合う ("the gears mesh"), 歯車が回る. Figuratively it denotes a "cog in the machine" of an organization, often with a resigned undertone: 会社の歯車にすぎない. If a previously smooth process goes awry, one says 歯車が狂う. In engineering, ギア is also used for gears and gear stages.

examples[].german: Proper lubrication extends the life of machines.
I oiled the bicycle chain.
With her cheerful personality, she is like the lubricant of the workplace.
en.notes: 潤滑 means "lubrication" and, more generally, "smoothness (absence of friction)": 潤滑油 ("lubricating oil"), 潤滑剤 ("lubricant"), 潤滑不良. The figurative use of 潤滑油 for a person or thing that makes cooperation easier is very common: 彼はチームの潤滑油だ. For "smooth" in the sense of processes, on the other hand, one usually says 円滑な (円滑に進む), not 潤滑な.

examples[].german: This material has excellent durability.
An endurance test was carried out on the new car.
An eight-hour endurance race is held at Suzuka.
en.notes: 耐久 means "endurance, durability" and almost never stands alone, but in compounds: 耐久性 ("durability, longevity"), 耐久力 ("stamina, resilience"), 耐久テスト ("endurance test"), 耐久レース ("endurance race"), 耐久消費財 ("durable consumer goods"). Typical is 耐久性に優れる／が高い. For a person's athletic stamina, 持久力 is more common.

examples[].german: Heat-resistant alloys are used for jet engine parts.
Containers made of heat-resistant glass can be used in the microwave too.
The heat resistance temperature of this plastic is 100 degrees.
en.notes: 耐熱 means "heat-resistant" and usually stands as a prefix or with の before nouns: 耐熱ガラス, 耐熱容器, 耐熱性, 耐熱温度 ("maximum heat-resistance temperature"). In daily life it is often seen on kitchen utensils and packaging, e.g. 耐熱温度120℃. It belongs to the series 耐水 ("waterproof"), 耐震 ("earthquake-resistant"), 耐火 ("fireproof") - 耐火 stresses fire, 耐熱 high temperatures.

examples[].german: The candidate traveled around the whole country campaigning.
The prime minister gave a speech in Osaka, a stop on his campaign tour.
The party leader set off on a campaign tour of the regions.
en.notes: 遊説 is read ゆうぜい, not ゆうせつ. It refers to a politician traveling around to give speeches in various places, especially during a campaign. Typical: 各地を遊説する, 遊説して回る, 遊説先 "stop on a campaign tour", 全国遊説, 地方遊説. A single speech on the street is called 街頭演説.

examples[].german: Stainless steel is a metal with high corrosion resistance.
Near the sea, you need to use materials with high corrosion resistance.
Titanium is light and highly corrosion-resistant.
en.notes: 耐食 means "corrosion-resistant" and is purely materials-science terminology. It almost always appears in compounds: 耐食性 ("corrosion resistance"), 耐食性が高い／に優れる, 耐食合金, 耐食鋼. The spelling 耐蝕 also occurs. In everyday speech one would rather say 錆びにくい ("hardly rusts"); active "corrosion protection" is 防食 or 防錆.

examples[].german: Forging makes the internal structure of the metal dense.
Japanese swords are forged by hammering iron over and over.
Forged parts are stronger than cast parts.
en.notes: 鍛造 is "forging": metal is heated and shaped by hammering or pressing, which makes it denser and stronger. As a する-verb it is transitive: 鉄を鍛造する. The contrast with 鋳造 ("casting"), in which liquid metal is poured into a mold, is important. Typical: 鍛造品, 鍛造部品, 鍛造ホイール, 刀の鍛造. The related verb is 鍛える ("to forge; to train").

examples[].german: Quenching greatly increases the hardness of steel.
In a Japanese sword, quenching makes only the edge hard.
You heat the steel to over 800 degrees, then cool it rapidly in water to quench it.
en.notes: 焼入れ is the "hardening" (quenching) of steel: the metal is heated strongly and then cooled quickly in water or oil. Also written 焼き入れ; as a verb 焼入れする or 焼きを入れる. It is usually followed by 焼戻し ("tempering") to reduce brittleness. Colloquially, 焼きを入れる also means "to straighten someone out, to give someone a good talking-to".

examples[].german: Tempering improves the brittleness left after quenching.
The hardness and toughness of steel change depending on the tempering temperature.
Quenched blades are always tempered before being finished.
en.notes: 焼戻し is the "tempering" of hardened steel: after 焼入れ, the metal is heated again to a moderate temperature to reduce brittleness and stress and gain toughness. Also written 焼き戻し; verb: 焼戻しする. Do not confuse it with 焼なまし or 焼鈍 ("annealing"). The four basic heat-treatment processes are 焼入れ・焼戻し・焼なまし・焼ならし.

examples[].german: Annealing is a heat treatment that removes internal stress in metal.
Copper wire hardened by cold working is annealed to soften it.
Steel sheets are cooled slowly in an annealing furnace.
en.notes: 焼鈍 is the written technical term for the "annealing" (soft annealing) of metal: it is heated and cooled slowly so that it becomes softer and internal stresses disappear. In the workshop one usually says 焼なまし (also written 焼鈍し); しょうどん is the Sino-Japanese reading used in technical texts and in compounds such as 焼鈍炉 ("annealing furnace"). The counterpart is 焼入れ, which makes metal hard.

examples[].german: Rolling makes the thickness of the metal plate uniform.
Aluminum foil is made by rolling aluminum thin.
The steelworks does both hot rolling and cold rolling.
en.notes: 圧延 is the "rolling" of metal between rotating rolls to shape it into sheets, plates or profiles: 圧延する, 圧延機 ("rolling mill"), 熱間圧延 ("hot rolling"), 冷間圧延 ("cold rolling"), 圧延鋼板. Technical language of the steel and aluminum industries. Related forming processes are 鍛造 ("forging"), 押出し ("extrusion") and 引抜き ("drawing").

examples[].german: Thin metal wire is produced by drawing.
Copper wire is made thinner by repeating the drawing many times.
Because a rival company poached them, three capable employees quit.
en.notes: 引抜き literally means "pulling out". In metalworking it is the "drawing" of wire, pipes or rods through a die, which reduces the cross-section: 引抜き加工, 引抜き管. Far more common in everyday life is the meaning "poaching" of staff or players: ライバル会社による引き抜き. In this meaning it is usually written 引き抜き; the corresponding verb is 引き抜く ("to pull out; to poach").

examples[].german: Metal sheets are formed into the specified shape by press working.
Car bodies are formed with large presses.
The company issued a press release about the new product.
en.notes: プレス in engineering means the "pressing, stamping" of sheet metal and also the "press" as a machine: プレス加工, プレス機, プレス金型, プレスする. In manufacturing, プレス加工 is so common that プレス alone often means this process. In everyday speech the word has other meanings: the "press" as media (プレスリリース, プレス発表) and the pressing of clothes (ズボンをプレスする).

examples[].german: Electrical discharge machining can precisely machine even hard materials.
Fine contours of molds are finished by electrical discharge machining.
With a wire EDM machine, even complicated shapes can be cut accurately.
en.notes: 放電加工 is "electrical discharge machining" (EDM): material is removed by electrical discharges (放電) between an electrode and the workpiece. This allows precise machining even of very hard, conductive materials such as hardened steel, for example when making 金型. Typical: 放電加工機, ワイヤー放電加工 ("wire EDM"), 形彫り放電加工 ("sinker EDM"). Purely technical language.

examples[].german: Laser machining is suited to fine cutting and marking.
I had my name engraved on a leather wallet by laser.
This factory cuts thin steel plates with a laser machine.
en.notes: レーザー加工 is "laser machining" with focused laser light: cutting (レーザー切断), welding (レーザー溶接), drilling and marking (レーザーマーキング). It works contact-free and very finely and is used for sheet metal, electronics and even personalized gift items. In industrial standards, the spelling レーザ without the long-vowel mark is also common. Typical: レーザー加工機, レーザー加工で切る／彫る.

examples[].german: The independence of the judiciary is the foundation of democracy.
He passed the bar examination on his third attempt.
This matter was ultimately left to the judgment of the judiciary.
en.notes: 司法 is the administration of justice, or the judiciary as a branch of state power, exercised by the courts. Frequent combinations: 司法の独立, 司法権, 司法制度, 司法の場で争う ("to contest in court"). Well-known compounds are 司法試験 ("bar examination") and 司法書士 ("judicial scrivener"). Counterparts in the system of separation of powers are 立法 and 行政.

examples[].german: The prime minister consulted the advisory council on system reform.
This committee was established as an advisory body to the prime minister.
At the mayor's request, the council began deliberations.
en.notes: 諮問 is the formal request by an authority or official to an advisory body for an opinion: AがBに〜を諮問する. The answer to it is called 答申; the body consulted is a 諮問機関, often a 審議会. A purely administrative word; in everyday speech one says 相談する or 意見を求める.

examples[].german: Many plastic products are made by injection molding.
The parts of this toy are made in large quantities at once by injection molding.
In injection molding, the temperature control of the mold greatly affects quality.
en.notes: 射出成形 is "injection molding": molten plastic is injected (射出) under high pressure into a 金型 and shaped (成形) there. Typical: 射出成形機, 射出成形品, 射出成形で作る. The spelling 射出成型 also occurs, but 成形 is the usual form. Related processes are 押出成形 ("extrusion") and ブロー成形 ("blow molding").

examples[].german: Precision molds determine the quality of the product.
It takes several months to make a new die.
Plastic cups are made by putting molten resin into a mold.
en.notes: 金型 is a "metal mold" or "die" in the sense of manufacturing engineering: stamping and pressing dies as well as die-casting and injection molds. Typical: 金型を作る／設計する, 金型メーカー, プレス金型, 射出成形用金型. The reading is かながた, not きんがた. The more general term is 型 ("mold, form"); 鋳型 is specifically the casting mold in 鋳造.

examples[].german: Corrosion resistance is improved by surface treatments such as plating.
This frying pan has a surface treatment that resists burning on.
Before painting, the surfaces of the parts are thoroughly treated.
en.notes: 表面処理 is the "surface treatment" of materials to improve corrosion protection, hardness, appearance or adhesion. It includes メッキ ("plating"), 塗装 ("painting"), アルマイト ("anodizing"), 蒸着 or 溶射. Typical: 表面処理を施す, 表面処理加工, 表面処理技術. Technical language of the metal, plastics and electronics industries, but also found in product descriptions.

examples[].german: A protective coating is applied to prevent metal deterioration.
A thin oxide film forms on the surface of aluminum and prevents rust.
Wax is used to form a coating on the car body.
en.notes: 被膜 is a thin "coating, layer, film" covering a surface: 保護被膜, 酸化被膜 ("oxide layer"), 被膜を形成する／施す. In biology it also means "capsule, envelope". The identically read 皮膜 is very similar and is also used for coatings; in engineering both occur. More everyday are コーティング and 膜.

examples[].german: A technique for forming thin films by vacuum deposition was developed.
The inside of a potato chip bag is vapor-coated with aluminum.
An anti-reflection coating is vapor-deposited on camera lenses.
en.notes: 蒸着 is "vapor deposition": a material is evaporated in a vacuum and condenses as a thin layer on a surface. Typical: 真空蒸着, 蒸着膜, アルミ蒸着, 蒸着する／蒸着される. It is found in mirrors, lens coatings, semiconductors and snack packaging. In pop culture, 蒸着 is known as the transformation call from the series 宇宙刑事ギャバン.

examples[].german: Thermal spraying forms a wear-resistant coating on the surface of parts.
Zinc is thermally sprayed onto the steel frame of the bridge to prevent rust.
The turbine blades are thermally sprayed with ceramic.
en.notes: 溶射 is "thermal spraying": metal, ceramic or the like is melted and sprayed as a fine jet onto a surface, where it forms a protective layer. Typical: 溶射皮膜, プラズマ溶射, 溶射する, 溶射加工. It is used for wear, heat and corrosion protection, e.g. on turbine blades or bridges. Do not confuse it with 溶接 ("welding") - only the first kanji 溶 ("to melt") is the same.

examples[].german: Internal defects in parts are detected by non-destructive testing.
Airplanes undergo non-destructive testing regularly.
We examined the concrete of the old tunnel by non-destructive testing.
en.notes: 非破壊検査 is "non-destructive testing": components are examined without being taken apart or damaged - for example with 超音波, X-rays, magnetic particles or penetrants. The word is composed of 非 ("non-"), 破壊 ("destruction") and 検査 ("inspection"). Typical for aircraft, bridges, pipelines and power plants: 非破壊検査を行う／実施する. In technical language also 非破壊試験.

examples[].german: Ultrasound is used to detect cracks inside metal.
I had an ultrasound examination at the hospital and gallstones were found.
Bats emit ultrasound to sense their surroundings.
en.notes: 超音波 is "ultrasound", i.e. sound above the range of human hearing. In everyday life it is encountered mainly in medicine: 超音波検査 ("ultrasound examination"), colloquially エコー (エコー検査). Other combinations: 超音波洗浄機 ("ultrasonic cleaner"), 超音波を出す／当てる. Do not confuse it with 超音速 ("supersonic speed").

examples[].german: Various sensors collect environmental data in real time.
The entrance light comes on automatically with a motion sensor.
I put my finger on the fingerprint sensor to unlock my smartphone.
en.notes: センサー is a "sensor, detector" and is very common in daily life as well as in engineering: 人感センサー ("motion sensor"), 温度センサー, 指紋センサー, センサーが反応する／作動する. A lamp with a motion detector is called a センサーライト. In technical standards the spelling センサ without the long-vowel mark is also found. The Japanese technical word 検出器 ("detector") is more formal and less common.

examples[].german: A piezoelectric transducer converts vibrations into electrical signals.
An A/D converter changes analog signals into digital signals.
To connect an old game console to a TV, you need a video signal converter.
en.notes: 変換器 is a technical device that converts a quantity or signal into another form: "transducer, converter". Typical in compounds: AD変換器 ("A/D converter"), 圧電変換器, 周波数変換器. In everyday speech one often says コンバーター or 変換アダプター; when traveling, the device for voltage is called 変圧器 ("transformer"). The corresponding verb is 変換する ("to convert").

examples[].german: The council submitted a report on education reform.
The council plans to compile its final report within the year.
The committee recommended to the minister that the system be abolished.
en.notes: 答申 is the reply of an advisory body to a 諮問, i.e. the official report or recommendation to the authority that made the request. Typical: 答申を出す/提出する/まとめる, 中間答申 "interim report", 最終答申 "final report", 〜に〜を答申する. A formal administrative word; a general report is 報告.

examples[].german: A weak signal is amplified to a size that can be processed.
The guitar's sound is amplified by the amp and comes out of the speaker.
Rumors on the internet amplified people's anxiety.
en.notes: 増幅 is the "amplification" of a signal or vibration: 信号を増幅する, 増幅器 ("amplifier", in everyday speech アンプ), 増幅回路. Figuratively it is often used for feelings or problems that build up: 不安が増幅する, 誤解を増幅させる. It is used transitively (〜を増幅する) and intransitively (〜が増幅する). Distinction: 強化 is "strengthening" in the sense of building up (警備を強化する), not of signals.

examples[].german: Frequency modulation is a communication method that is resistant to noise.
The culprit called with a modulated voice.
I felt something off in my body recently, so I went to the hospital.
en.notes: 変調 has two faces: in engineering it is the "modulation" of a signal (振幅変調 AM, 周波数変調 FM); 変調する is transitive there (信号を変調する). In everyday life, on the other hand, it means a "disturbance, irregularity" in the normal state, mainly in fixed phrases such as 体調に変調を来す "to get thrown off in terms of health" or 変調を感じる. The counterpart in engineering is 復調 "demodulation".

examples[].german: The receiver demodulates the modulated signal to extract the original information.
The ace, back from injury, is finally showing signs of regaining form.
Thanks to the recovery in exports, the economy is gradually rebounding.
en.notes: 復調 is "demodulation" in engineering, the counterpart to 変調: 信号を復調する. The word is read far more often in sports and economic news in the sense of "getting back into form, recovering": エースが復調する, 景気が復調する. In this meaning 復調する is intransitive; 回復 is more general (also illness), while 復調 stresses the return to one's usual performance.

examples[].german: Security is ensured by encrypting communication data.
Let's save important files in encrypted form.
All messages in this app are encrypted.
en.notes: 暗号化 is "encryption", from 暗号 "code, cipher" and the suffix 化 "-ization". As a する-verb it is transitive: データを暗号化する; the state is 暗号化されている. The counterpart is 復号 or 復号化 "decryption with the key", while 解読 means cracking a code without the key. Related: 暗号資産 "cryptocurrency".

examples[].german: The ciphertext is decrypted using the correct key.
I forgot the password, so I cannot decrypt the file.
A method that uses the same key for encryption and decryption is called symmetric-key cryptography.
en.notes: 復号 is the technical word for "decryption, decoding" with the matching key: 暗号文を復号する. In everyday IT speech one also hears 復号化, analogous to 暗号化, although specialists often prefer the shorter 復号. Do not confuse it with 解読, the deciphering or cracking of a code without the key (暗号を解読する), nor with the identically read 複合 "combination, complex".

examples[].german: Data transmission over optical fiber is fast and has high capacity.
The drawback of this old standard is its slow transmission speed.
Footage of the final was transmitted around the world via satellite.
en.notes: 伝送 is a technical term for the "transmission" of signals, data or energy over lines and by radio: データ伝送, 伝送速度, 伝送路. As a する-verb it is transitive (映像を伝送する). In contrast, 伝達 means the passing on of information between people (情報を伝達する), and 送信 the sending of a message or signal.

examples[].german: Optical fiber is a technology that forms the backbone of communications infrastructure.
Since optical fiber was laid in our apartment building, the internet has become much faster.
An optical fiber is made of glass about as thin as a hair.
en.notes: 光ファイバー is "optical fiber", a hair-thin light guide made of glass or plastic; in standards and technical texts the short spelling 光ファイバ without the long-vowel mark is common. For a home fiber internet connection one usually says 光回線 or simply 光 (光にする "to switch to fiber"). Typical combinations: 光ファイバーケーブル, 光ファイバー通信.

examples[].german: Developing cloud infrastructure supports digital transformation.
First, I want to find a job and solidify the foundation of my life.
This party has a strong base of support in rural areas.
en.notes: 基盤 is the supporting "foundation, base" of something larger: 生活の基盤, 経営基盤, 支持基盤 "base of support", in IT also "platform, infrastructure" (クラウド基盤). Typical verbs are 基盤を築く, 基盤を固める, 基盤となる. 基礎 is rather the groundwork on which one builds (基礎知識), while 基盤 emphasizes the stable base of a system. The circuit board is usually written 基板.

examples[].german: I implemented the new algorithm in the software.
This feature is scheduled to be implemented in the next update.
At the factory, we automated the process of mounting parts onto circuit boards.
en.notes: 実装 means "implementation" in software (機能を実装する "to build in a function") and in electronics the "mounting, assembly" of components on a circuit board (部品を基板に実装する). As a する-verb it is transitive, often with に for the target. 導入, in contrast, is the introduction of a system in an organization; in politics and research one has recently also heard 社会実装 "putting into practice in society".
