examples[].german: Embedded systems are widely used, from home appliances to cars.
Job openings for embedded engineers are increasing year by year.
If you use the spreadsheet's built-in functions, you can get the total right away.
en.notes: 組込み is the noun form of 組み込む "to build in, to incorporate" and in IT stands mostly before nouns in the sense of "embedded, built-in": 組込みシステム "embedded system", 組込み関数 "built-in function", 組込みエンジニア. The spelling varies: 組込み is usual in technical terms, otherwise mostly 組み込み. For hardware permanently built into a device, one rather says 内蔵 (カメラ内蔵).

examples[].german: The National Personnel Authority recommended a pay raise for civil servants.
The administration formally ordered the offending company to make improvements.
The expert committee recommended discontinuing use of the drug.
en.notes: 勧告 is an official recommendation or call to do something, usually issued by an authority or a body. It is often not legally binding, but carries considerably more weight than 助言 "advice" or アドバイス. Typical: 〜を勧告する, 〜するよう勧告する, 勧告に従う, 改善勧告, 人事院勧告 (annual pay recommendation for civil servants).

examples[].german: Updating the firmware improves the device's performance.
Do not turn off the router's power during the update. The firmware may be corrupted.
Because of a firmware bug, the printer no longer starts up.
en.notes: ファームウェア is "firmware", the control software permanently stored in a device (router, printer, camera). It is updated with ファームウェアを更新する or ファームウェアをアップデートする. Besides ファームウェア, the spelling ファームウエア also occurs. To be distinguished from ソフトウェア (application programs) and ハードウェア (the devices themselves).

examples[].german: We increase the redundancy of the system to prepare for failures.
This data center ensures redundancy of its power supply.
Language is redundant, so the meaning gets across even if you miss a little.
en.notes: 冗長性 is "redundancy". The base word 冗長 is negative in everyday speech: 冗長な文章 is a "long-winded, verbose text". In engineering, however, 冗長性 is positive: extra reserves that step in when something fails (冗長性を確保する, 冗長性を高める); creating such reserves is called 冗長化. In language and information theory, too, one speaks of the 冗長性 of a message.

examples[].german: We distribute the server load to improve stability.
Please choose exercises that do not put strain on your knees.
More and more people are choosing products with a low environmental impact.
en.notes: 負荷 is the "load, burden" acting on a system, a machine or the body. Typical are 負荷がかかる (intransitive) and 負荷をかける (transitive), plus 負荷が大きい/小さい, 環境負荷 "environmental impact" and 負荷テスト "load test". 負担, on the other hand, is the (financial or emotional) burden a person bears (費用を負担する); 負荷 sounds more technical.

examples[].german: Measures against static charge are essential in semiconductor factories.
In winter the air is dry, so clothes easily build up static.
When you rub a plastic pencil board, it becomes charged and attracts hair.
en.notes: 帯電 is the technical word for "electric (mostly static) charge"; as a する-verb it is intransitive: 静電気で帯電する. In everyday speech one rather says 静電気 ("static electricity", 静電気が起きる). Common combinations are 帯電防止 "antistatic" (帯電防止スプレー) and 帯電しやすい素材.

examples[].german: High-performance CPUs require an efficient heat dissipation design.
If you use a laptop on a futon, heat dissipation doesn't work well.
This heater has high heat-radiation efficiency, so the room warms up quickly.
en.notes: 放熱 means "heat dissipation, heat release": a component or device gives off heat to its surroundings. As a する-verb it is intransitive; typical are 放熱性, 放熱設計, 放熱板 "heat sink" and 放熱ファン. 発熱 is the generation of heat, 冷却 active cooling, 排熱 waste heat or its removal to the outside.

examples[].german: Feedback control guarantees the stability of the system.
I got feedback on my proposal from my boss.
We make use of customer feedback in developing new products.
en.notes: フィードバック in control engineering is "feedback" in the sense of a loop (フィードバック制御 "control with feedback"). In working life, however, the meaning "response, feedback" is far more common: フィードバックをもらう, 部下にフィードバックする, お客様のフィードバックを生かす. The acoustic squeal of a microphone feeding back is usually called ハウリング in Japanese.

examples[].german: Expanding the bandwidth has made high-capacity communication possible.
Streaming high-quality video requires sufficient bandwidth.
Please turn off your camera during the meeting to save bandwidth.
en.notes: 帯域幅 is the "bandwidth" of a frequency range or a data connection. In everyday IT speech one often says the shorter 帯域 (帯域が足りない "not enough bandwidth") or simply バンド幅. Typical are 帯域幅を確保する and 帯域幅を消費する. Not to be confused with 幅 alone, which means any spatial width.

examples[].german: Distributed processing allows large-scale data analysis to be done efficiently.
As traffic increased, we switched from a single server to distributed processing.
Disease research advanced through distributed processing using volunteers' PCs around the world.
en.notes: 分散処理 is "distributed processing": a task is split among several computers on a network. The opposite is 集中処理 (everything on one central computer). 並列処理, by contrast, stresses simultaneous computation, also within a single computer. One says 分散処理する or 分散処理を行う; related is 負荷分散 "load balancing".

examples[].german: We use parallel processing to dramatically increase computation speed.
GPUs are good at processing simple calculations in parallel.
The human brain processes information from the eyes and ears in parallel.
en.notes: 並列処理 is "parallel processing": several computation steps run at the same time on several cores or processors. Specialists distinguish 並列 (truly simultaneous) from 並行 (concurrent, interleaved); in everyday speech this blurs. The opposite is 逐次処理 "sequential processing". Figuratively one also says that the brain 並列処理する much information.

examples[].german: Server virtualization makes efficient use of hardware resources.
With virtualization software, you can run multiple operating systems on one PC.
We virtualized the desktops so that people can work in the same environment from home too.
en.notes: 仮想化 is "virtualization": physical resources such as servers, storage or desktops are reproduced by software. As a する-verb it is transitive (サーバーを仮想化する). The base word 仮想 "virtual, hypothetical" is known from 仮想現実 "virtual reality", 仮想通貨 and 仮想マシン.

examples[].german: The minister issued a directive to the department in charge.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs instructed the ambassador to suspend the negotiations.
This regulation is established as an internal directive of the ministry.
en.notes: 訓令 is an instruction that a superior authority addresses to subordinate bodies or officials; it takes effect only within the administration, not toward citizens. In diplomacy, it refers to the government's instructions to an envoy. The word is also known from 訓令式, the officially established romanization system (e.g. si instead of shi). Formal and rare outside administration and diplomacy; more general are 指示 or 命令.

examples[].german: Quantum computers take on problems that conventional computers cannot solve.
If quantum computers become practical, today's encryption might be broken.
That company is investing huge sums in developing quantum computers.
en.notes: 量子コンピューター is the "quantum computer", which computes with quantum bits (量子ビット). In technical texts the spelling without the long-vowel mark, 量子コンピュータ, is common. Typical combinations: 量子コンピューターの実用化 "practical use", 量子コンピューターを開発する. In contrast, conventional computers are called 古典コンピューター or simply 従来のコンピューター.

examples[].german: Deep learning has revolutionized image recognition and natural language processing.
Deep learning requires large amounts of data and computing resources.
This semester I'm taking a lecture on deep learning at university.
en.notes: 深層学習 is the Japanese technical term for "deep learning", a subfield of machine learning (機械学習) with multilayer neural networks (ニューラルネットワーク). In the media and in practice, the loanword ディープラーニング is heard at least as often; 深層学習 sounds somewhat more formal and likes to appear in textbooks and official texts.

examples[].german: Machine learning algorithms learn patterns from data.
Machine learning is used to detect spam email.
If you want to study machine learning, you should first solidify the basics of statistics.
en.notes: 機械学習 is "machine learning": computers learn patterns from data instead of being hard-coded. It is a subfield of 人工知能 (AI) and in turn includes 深層学習. Typical combinations: 機械学習モデル, 機械学習を使う, 機械学習で予測する. The loanword マシンラーニング exists too, but is rarer than 機械学習.

examples[].german: With the development of robotics, industrial robots have become widespread.
My older brother is majoring in robotics at university.
Asimov set out the "Three Laws of Robotics" in his novels.
en.notes: ロボット工学 is "robotics", from ロボット and 工学 "engineering" (as in 機械工学, 電子工学). One studies it (ロボット工学を専攻する) or does research in it; the loanword ロボティクス is also used, mainly in company names and specialist circles. Well known is Asimov's ロボット工学三原則 "the Three Laws of Robotics".

examples[].german: Thanks to autonomous control technology, drones automatically avoid obstacles.
The probe landed under autonomous control, without waiting for instructions from Earth.
In this warehouse, autonomously controlled robots carry the packages.
en.notes: 自律制御 is "autonomous control": a vehicle or robot perceives its surroundings and decides for itself, without human remote control. Do not confuse it with the identically read 自立 "independence, self-reliance" (経済的に自立する); 自律 stresses self-governance by one's own rules. 自動制御 is more general "automatic control" according to fixed specifications. Typical: 自律制御で飛行する, 自律制御システム.

examples[].german: A gearbox is a device that optimizes the efficiency of power transmission.
On a bicycle, the chain plays the role of power transmission.
If you reduce power transmission losses, fuel economy improves.
en.notes: 動力伝達 is the "power transmission" from the engine to wheels or tools, from 動力 "driving force" and 伝達 "transmission, conveyance". The word appears mainly in mechanical-engineering and vehicle texts: 動力伝達装置, 動力伝達機構, 動力伝達の効率. The components for it are e.g. 歯車, チェーン, ベルト and 変速機; the loanword for the whole drivetrain is パワートレイン.

examples[].german: Abnormal vibration of a machine may be a sign of impending failure.
My phone was in silent mode, so I didn't notice it vibrating.
The period of a pendulum's oscillation is determined by the length of the string.
en.notes: 振動 is an "oscillation, vibration" of machines, pendulums, phones or strings; as a する-verb it is intransitive: 機械が振動する. In everyday speech, for noticeable shaking one rather says 揺れ/揺れる. Do not confuse it with the identically read 震動, which stands for shocks such as in earthquakes. Typical: 振動が伝わる, 振動を抑える, 振動数 "frequency".

examples[].german: If resonance occurs at a structure's natural frequency, it can lead to destruction.
During the spin cycle the washing machine went into resonance, and even the floor shook.
Soldiers break step when crossing a bridge in order to avoid resonance.
en.notes: 共振 is mechanical or electrical "resonance": a body vibrates along when an external vibration hits its natural frequency. One says 共振が起きる/発生する or 共振する (intransitive). For sound and, figuratively, "to find resonance, to sympathize", 共鳴 is used instead (彼の考えに共鳴する); 共振 remains almost always technical and physical.

examples[].german: Shock absorbers are designed taking the damping characteristics of vibrations into account.
Radio waves attenuate the farther the distance.
The sound of the bell gradually faded until it could no longer be heard.
en.notes: 減衰 means "damping, attenuation, decay" of a quantity such as a vibration, signal or sound; as a する-verb it is intransitive: 信号が減衰する. Typical are 減衰特性, 減衰率 and 減衰が大きい. 減少, on the other hand, is a decrease in a number or amount (人口が減少する), and 衰退 the decline of an industry or culture.

examples[].german: The stress applied to the part is analyzed with the finite element method.
Stress tends to concentrate around holes.
Changes in temperature cause stress in the rails.
en.notes: 応力 is the "mechanical stress" in mechanics and materials science, i.e. the internal force per unit area in a loaded component. Typical are 応力がかかる/生じる, 応力集中 "stress concentration" and 引張応力/圧縮応力. Do not confuse it with 圧力 "pressure" or with ストレス, which in everyday speech means mental strain.

examples[].german: The extent of the administration's discretionary authority became an issue.
We will leave the details to the discretion of the person in charge.
Under the discretionary work system, you can decide your working hours yourself.
en.notes: 裁量 is the latitude to decide by one's own judgment. Typical: 〜の裁量に任せる/委ねる "to leave to someone's discretion", 〜の裁量で決める, 裁量権 "discretionary authority", 自由裁量 "free discretion" and 裁量労働制 "discretionary work system". As a する-verb it is rare. The word comes from administration and law, but is also common in working life.

examples[].german: Stress causes strain in the material.
This speaker has little sound distortion even at high volume.
The strains of rapid economic growth appeared in the form of pollution.
en.notes: 歪み (ひずみ) is technically the "strain, deformation" of a material under stress and in acoustics the "distortion" of a signal (音のひずみ). Figuratively it denotes "imbalances, distortions" in society or the economy (社会のひずみ). It is usually written in kana. The same written form can also be read ゆがみ, which rather means visible bending or distortion (顔のゆがみ, 画像のゆがみ).

examples[].german: A tiny crack can become the starting point of fatigue failure.
The earthquake caused a large crack in the wall of the building.
That one remark caused a rift in the two's friendship.
en.notes: 亀裂 is a "crack, fissure" in walls, roads, ice or material; the basic phrases are 亀裂が入る or 亀裂が生じる. Figuratively it describes a "rift" in relationships or organizations: 二人の関係に亀裂が入る. In everyday speech, for small cracks one rather says ひび (ひびが入る); 亀裂 sounds more literary and often larger.

examples[].german: Materials with high toughness are strong against impact.
Glass is hard but has low toughness, so it breaks easily under impact.
Steel whose toughness does not easily drop even at low temperatures is used for bridges in cold regions.
en.notes: 靭性 is the "toughness" of a material, i.e. its ability to absorb energy without breaking. The standard spelling is 靱性; 靭性 is the widespread variant. The distinction is important: 硬度 "hardness" and 強度 "strength" are different things; the opposite term is 脆性 "brittleness". Typical: 靭性が高い/低い, 破壊靭性.

examples[].german: Diamond has the highest hardness of all natural minerals.
The water in this area has high hardness, so soap does not lather easily.
The hardness of pencil leads is indicated by symbols such as H and B.
en.notes: 硬度 is the "hardness" of a material (モース硬度, ビッカース硬度) and also "water hardness" (硬度の高い水 = 硬水, opposite 軟水). One says 硬度が高い/低い and 硬度を測る. To be distinguished from 強度 "strength, load capacity" and 靭性 "toughness": a material can be very hard and yet brittle.

examples[].german: Carbon fiber is a material with very high tensile strength.
The test piece is pulled from both ends to measure its tensile strength.
Steel with high tensile strength is used for crane cables.
en.notes: 引張強度 is "tensile strength", i.e. the maximum tensile stress a material withstands before it tears. In technical texts 引張 is written without okurigana; in standards the quantity is usually called 引張強さ, formerly also 抗張力. Counterparts are 圧縮強度 "compressive strength" and せん断強度 "shear strength". Typical: 引張強度が高い, 引張強度を測定する.

examples[].german: Concrete shows strong resistance to compressive force.
Please compress the file before sending it by email.
Due to budget constraints, the construction period was shortened from six months to three.
en.notes: 圧縮 means "compression" (gas, air, concrete under pressure) and, in IT, "data compression": ファイルを圧縮する, counterpart 解凍 or 展開 "to unpack". Figuratively it also means "to cut back, to tighten": 予算を圧縮する, 日程を圧縮する. As a する-verb it is transitive. In construction, 圧縮力 "compressive force" is the opposite of 引張力 "tensile force".

examples[].german: Shear force acts on bolted joints.
The earthquake's shaking caused shear failure in the columns.
Scissors are a tool that shears paper with two blades.
en.notes: 剪断 is "shear" in mechanics: two forces act in parallel but offset from each other, as with scissors. Since 剪 is not a Jōyō kanji, textbooks and standards usually write せん断 (せん断力, せん断破壊, せん断応力). As a する-verb it is transitive. Counterparts are 引張 "tension" and 圧縮 "compression".

examples[].german: The deflection of the beam is calculated to produce a safe design.
I stuffed in too many books, and the shelf board has started to sag.
From how much the fishing rod bends, you can roughly tell the size of the fish.
en.notes: 撓み (たわみ) is the "deflection" of a beam, board or rod under load; the corresponding verb is 撓む "to bend, to give way" (intransitive). The kanji is rare, so it is usually written たわみ. Typical: たわみが生じる/出る, たわみを計算する, たわみ量. Unlike 曲がり, with たわみ the deformation is usually elastic and returns after the load is removed.

examples[].german: The tightening torque of bolts is controlled to the specified value.
Electric cars can produce large torque from the moment they start moving.
After changing the tires, please tighten the nuts with a torque wrench.
en.notes: トルク is "torque", i.e. the force with which something is turned about an axis. Typical are トルクが大きい/強い, トルクを出す, 最大トルク, 締め付けトルク "tightening torque" and トルクレンチ "torque wrench". In a car context, トルク (pulling force) is distinguished from 馬力 "horsepower, output".

examples[].german: The engine's rotation speed is kept within the optimal range.
If the rpm gets too high, it damages the engine.
If you lower the spin speed, clothes wrinkle less easily.
en.notes: 回転数 is the "rotational speed" or "number of revolutions" of a motor, wheel, hard disk or spin drum, usually given per minute (毎分〜回転, rpm). Typical: 回転数が上がる/下がる, 回転数を上げる/抑える, エンジンの回転数. 回転 alone is the rotation itself; 速度 would be the speed of the vehicle.

examples[].german: This case falls under the jurisdiction of the Metropolitan Police Department.
That matter is outside our jurisdiction, so please go to another counter.
The tax return is submitted to the tax office with jurisdiction over your address.
en.notes: 管轄 is the jurisdiction of an authority, court or police, often for a particular area: 〜の管轄だ, 〜の管轄に属する, 管轄外 "outside one's jurisdiction", 管轄区域, 〜を管轄する税務署/警察署. Related is 所管, which rather stresses the subject-matter responsibility for a field of tasks (e.g. of a ministry). In everyday speech one often hears うちの管轄じゃない "that's not our department".

examples[].german: A liquid cooling system manages the temperature of high-performance processors.
Water for cooling the reactor ran short because of the accident.
The two do nothing but fight, so they need a bit of a cooling-off period.
en.notes: 冷却 is "cooling" in technical contexts: 冷却装置, 冷却水, 水冷/空冷による冷却 ("cooling by water or air"). As a する-verb it is both transitive and intransitive (エンジンを冷却する / 冷却される). Figuratively it means a "cooling off" between people or states, e.g. 冷却期間 "cooling-off period". In everyday speech, for drinks or food one simply says 冷やす.

examples[].german: Improving the engine's intake efficiency increases power.
If the air intake gets clogged with dust, the air conditioner works worse.
In deep breathing, it is good to make the exhalation slower and longer than the inhalation.
en.notes: 吸気 is the "intake" of air in engines and devices (吸気口 "air intake", 吸気効率) and in medicine "inhalation" or the inhaled air. The counterpart in engineering is 排気 "exhaust", in breathing 呼気 "exhalation, exhaled air". In everyday speech, for breathing in one simply says 息を吸う.

examples[].german: Lithium-ion storage batteries are the core technology of electric vehicles.
We installed a home storage battery in preparation for power outages.
Electricity generated during the day is stored in the battery and used at night.
en.notes: 蓄電池 is a "storage battery, rechargeable battery", i.e. a store of electrical energy (蓄 "to store" + 電池). In everyday speech, for phones and cars one rather says バッテリー, for small rechargeables 充電池. 蓄電池 is heard mainly with power storage for homes and grids: 家庭用蓄電池, 蓄電池に電気をためる. The opposite term is 一次電池 "non-rechargeable battery".

examples[].german: The conversion efficiency of solar cells improves year by year.
This calculator runs on a solar cell, so there's no need to replace batteries.
Satellites get their power from solar cell panels.
en.notes: 太陽電池 is the "solar cell", which converts light directly into electricity. The whole module on the roof is usually called 太陽光パネル or ソーラーパネル, and power generation as a whole 太陽光発電. Although 電池 is in the name, a solar cell does not store electricity. Typical: 太陽電池で動く, 太陽電池の変換効率.

examples[].german: A fuel cell is a device that generates electricity from hydrogen and oxygen.
Fuel cell vehicles emit only water while driving.
In our house, a home fuel cell generates electricity and supplies hot water at the same time.
en.notes: 燃料電池 is the "fuel cell", which generates electricity through a chemical reaction of hydrogen and oxygen. Important combinations are 燃料電池車 "fuel cell vehicle" and 家庭用燃料電池, which in Japan supplies electricity and hot water at once. Unlike 蓄電池, it is not charged but supplied with fuel.

examples[].german: High-voltage transmission makes long-distance power transport possible.
A typhoon cut the power lines, and a wide area lost power.
Due to construction work, power transmission will be temporarily suspended during the morning.
en.notes: 送電 is the "transmission of electricity" from the power plant via high-voltage lines; as a する-verb transitive/intransitive (電力を送電する, 送電を止める). Typical: 送電線 "power line", 送電網 "power grid", 送電を再開する. The chain consists of 発電 "generation", 送電 "transmission" and 配電 "distribution to households"; the everyday opposite of 送電 is 停電 "power outage".

examples[].german: Voltage is stepped up and down with transformers to transmit power efficiently.
When using Japanese appliances abroad, a transformer may be necessary.
Electricity is sent to each household from the transformer on top of the utility pole.
en.notes: 変圧器 is the "transformer", which raises or lowers alternating voltage (電圧を上げる/下げる); colloquially also トランス. In a travel context, the voltage converter for electrical appliances abroad is also called 変圧器 - not to be confused with a mere plug adapter (変換プラグ). Typical: 変圧器を通す, 変圧器が必要だ.

examples[].german: A rectifier is an electronic component that converts alternating current to direct current.
I built a circuit that rectifies alternating current using diodes.
This fan straightens the airflow to deliver a gentle breeze.
en.notes: 整流 means "rectification" in electrical engineering, i.e. the conversion of alternating current (交流) into direct current (直流): 交流を整流する. The device is called 整流器, and the diode acts as a 整流素子. In fluid engineering, 整流 also denotes "straightening" an air or water flow to avoid eddies. As a する-verb it is transitive.

examples[].german: Proper grounding is essential to prevent electric shock accidents.
Please be sure to ground the washing machine before using it.
This tire has a wide contact patch, so it does not slip easily even on rainy days.
en.notes: 接地 is "grounding" (earthing) in electrical engineering; in everyday speech it is mostly called アース (アース線をつなぐ). As a する-verb: 機器を接地する. The second meaning is "ground contact": 接地面 "contact patch" of a tire, or the touchdown of an airplane or a foot while running. 着地, in contrast, stresses landing after a jump.

examples[].german: High-voltage components need sufficient insulation treatment.
The insulation of the electric wire deteriorated and caused a short circuit.
He has cut ties with his father and hasn't seen him for ten years.
en.notes: 絶縁 has two meanings: technically electrical or thermal "insulation" (絶縁体 "insulator", 絶縁テープ, 絶縁処理), and in everyday life the "severing of ties, break in relations": 親と絶縁する, 絶縁状 "letter by which one ends a relationship". In the second sense the other party takes と. For the thermal insulation of houses, 断熱 is usually said; 隔離 is the isolation of people, for example during illness.

examples[].german: This field is under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare.
The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology is in charge of this law.
For details, please inquire at the competent government office.
en.notes: 所管 is the subject-matter responsibility of an authority for a law, a task or an institution: 〜省の所管である, 〜を所管する, 所管官庁 "competent authority", 所管事項. Unlike 管轄, which is often thought of spatially (the territory of a court or police station), 所管 is about departments and subject areas. A formal administrative word.

examples[].german: Pathological examination confirms tissue abnormalities at the microscopic level.
My older sister works as a pathologist at a university hospital.
Bullying is said to be one of the pathologies of modern society.
en.notes: 病理 is "pathology", the study of the causes and processes of diseases. It often appears as a first element: 病理学 (the field), 病理検査, 病理医, 病理解剖. Figuratively, media and sociology speak of 社会の病理 "pathological phenomena of society". To be distinguished from 病状 "a patient's condition".

examples[].german: An antigen test can quickly confirm the presence of a virus.
An immune response occurs when antigens and antibodies bind.
I took an antigen test before my trip, and it was negative.
en.notes: 抗原 is the technical term for "antigen", a substance against which the body forms an immune response; its counterpart is 抗体 ("antibody"), together in the expression 抗原抗体反応. Since the Covid era, 抗原検査 ("rapid antigen test") has also become common in everyday life, usually in contrast to PCR検査. For allergies, one speaks of the 抗原 as the trigger, colloquially more often アレルゲン.

examples[].german: Benign tumors do not metastasize and are rarely life-threatening.
I was relieved to learn from the test results that the polyp was benign.
We will take part of the tissue and test it to find out whether it is benign or malignant.
en.notes: 良性 means "benign" in the medical sense and is used mainly with tumors, polyps or cysts: attributively as 良性の腫瘍 or directly as the compound 良性腫瘍, predicatively as 良性だ／良性です. The opposite is 悪性, and in a diagnostic conversation the question 良性か悪性か often comes up. For a good-natured character, 良性 is not used; one uses 人がいい or 善良な.

examples[].german: Malignant tumors tend to invade the surrounding tissue.
When we were told that my father's tumor was malignant, the whole family was shocked.
Prices are rising sharply, and concern about vicious inflation is growing.
en.notes: 悪性 means "malignant" and is the opposite of 良性; 悪性腫瘍 is the formal term for cancer, plus 悪性リンパ腫 or 悪性貧血. Outside medicine it describes things that spread badly, such as 悪性インフレ ("runaway inflation"). Do not confuse it with 悪質な, which describes malicious human actions (悪質な詐欺 "vicious fraud").

examples[].german: Cancer cells metastasize to other organs through the blood.
The test results showed that the cancer had not spread to the lymph nodes.
A metastasis to the liver was found, so the treatment plan was changed.
en.notes: 転移 is medically "metastasis": as an intransitive する-verb がんが肺に転移する, as a noun 肺への転移, 転移がある, 遠隔転移 ("distant metastasis"). Do not confuse it with the reversed 移転 ("relocation" of an office or shop). In specialist fields, 転移 has other meanings such as 相転移 ("phase transition"), transfer of learning, or transference in psychoanalysis.

examples[].german: We examine whether the tumor has infiltrated the surrounding tissue.
Surgery revealed that the cancer had invaded as far as the muscle layer.
An infiltrate was seen in the lung on the X-ray.
en.notes: 浸潤 is "infiltration" in medicine: a tumor grows into neighboring tissue (〜に浸潤する), in contrast to 転移, the spread to distant organs. In X-ray findings one encounters 浸潤影 ("infiltrate, shadowing"). Originally the word means "soaking through with liquid" and, figuratively, the gradual penetration of ideas into society, but that is literary; in everyday speech one says 浸透 for it.

examples[].german: A skilled surgeon performed the operation and made the highly difficult surgery a success.
The hospital director will perform this surgery himself.
The day before the surgery, I received a detailed explanation from the operating surgeon.
en.notes: 執刀 literally means "to hold the knife" and denotes that a doctor operates as the responsible surgeon: 医師が執刀する, 〇〇医師の執刀で手術が行われる, plus 執刀医 ("operating surgeon"). The general word is 手術する; the patient, on the other hand, says 手術を受ける, never 執刀. The word belongs to the medical and journalistic register.

examples[].german: General anesthesia is an indispensable procedure in major surgery.
I had anesthesia at the dentist, so it didn't hurt at all.
Pain comes when the anesthesia wears off, so please take the painkiller.
en.notes: 麻酔 covers both "general anesthesia" and local "numbing": 全身麻酔 ("general anesthesia") and 局所麻酔 ("local anesthesia"). Typical combinations are 麻酔をかける／麻酔をする, 麻酔が効く ("takes effect"), 麻酔が切れる ("wears off") and 麻酔から覚める ("to wake up from anesthesia"). The specialist is called 麻酔科医. The word is also perfectly normal in everyday life at the dentist.

examples[].german: The wound is carefully sutured to reduce the risk of infection.
The doctor closed the wound on the forehead with five stitches.
The stitches will be removed after one week.
en.notes: 縫合 is the medical word for sewing up a wound or tissue: 傷口を縫合する, 縫合糸 ("suture material"), 縫合不全 ("suture failure"). In everyday speech one simply says 縫う, especially with a stitch count: 三針縫った. The removal of the stitches afterwards is called 抜糸. For sewing clothes, only 縫う is used, never 縫合.

examples[].german: As first aid for external injuries, one first stops the bleeding.
I pressed hard on the wound with gauze and stopped the bleeding.
The bleeding was so severe that it could not be stopped for a long time.
en.notes: 止血 is the "stopping of bleeding": 止血する, 止血を行う, 止血剤 ("hemostatic agent"), 止血帯 ("tourniquet"). In first aid, 圧迫止血 ("stopping bleeding by pressure") is a fixed term. In everyday speech one rather says 血を止める or intransitively 血が止まる; 止血 sounds medical and technical.

examples[].german: A department to oversee the entire project was established.
The head of sales supervises all the branches in the country.
Each ministry is placed under the overall control of the Cabinet.
en.notes: 統轄 means to direct and supervise several subordinate units as a whole: 〜を統轄する, 〜の統轄の下に置く. The spelling 統轄 is typical of legal and administrative texts; in general usage and in companies, 統括 is usually written, which can mean both "to bring together" and "to direct" (統括部長 etc.). In conversation, the word sounds very formal.

examples[].german: An emergency transfusion was performed on the patient with heavy bleeding.
Before the surgery, I was told that a blood transfusion might become necessary.
Some patients refuse blood transfusions for religious reasons.
en.notes: 輸血 is the "blood transfusion": 患者に輸血する, 輸血を受ける, 輸血用血液. The counterpart on the donor side is 献血 ("blood donation"), which is often confused in everyday life. In informed-consent discussions one hears 輸血が必要になる場合がある; refusal for religious reasons is called 輸血拒否.

examples[].german: Organ transplantation is the last hope for patients with end-stage organ failure.
I am going to receive a kidney transplant from my older brother.
When spring comes, I will transplant the seedlings to the field.
en.notes: 移植 is transitive: 臓器を移植する, the recipient says 移植を受ける; plus 臓器移植, 骨髄移植, 移植手術 and ドナー ("donor"). Originally it means the transplanting of plants (苗を移植する), for which 植え替える is also said in everyday speech. In IT, 移植 also stands for porting software to another platform.

examples[].german: Rejection after an organ transplant is suppressed with immunosuppressants.
The transplanted kidney suffered a rejection reaction.
The new evaluation system provoked strong resistance from employees.
en.notes: 拒絶反応 is the body's "rejection reaction" against a transplant: 拒絶反応が起きる／出る, 拒絶反応を抑える (e.g. with 免疫抑制剤). Figuratively it denotes a violent, almost instinctive rejection of ideas or changes: 〜に拒絶反応を示す. The figurative use is common in newspapers and conversation.

examples[].german: Pharmacology studies the effects of drugs on living organisms.
The pharmacological action of this ingredient has not yet been fully elucidated.
Research that scientifically verifies the pharmacological effects of Kampo medicines is progressing.
en.notes: 薬理 denotes how a drug acts in the body and occurs almost only in compounds: 薬理作用 ("pharmacological action"), 薬理効果, 薬理学 ("pharmacology" as a subject). On its own it is rare, e.g. in lecture titles. Do not confuse it with 薬学 ("pharmacy", the course of study of pharmacists) or the more everyday 薬効 ("efficacy of a medicine").

examples[].german: Bacterial infections are treated by administering antibiotics.
Because the pain was severe, the patient was given a painkiller.
This drug is not approved for administration to children.
en.notes: 投与 is the technical word for "administering" a medication: 患者に薬を投与する, where the recipient takes に; plus 投与量 ("dose"), 経口投与 ("oral administration"), 静脈内投与. In everyday speech one says 薬を出す, 飲ませる or 注射を打つ instead. Similar is 投薬 ("medication"), which refers more to giving drugs as a form of treatment.

examples[].german: A pharmacist dispenses medication based on the prescription.
I got a prescription at the hospital and picked up the medicine at a nearby dispensing pharmacy.
Dispensing takes time, so please wait a moment.
en.notes: 調剤 is the compounding and handing out of medicines according to a prescription, the work of the 薬剤師: 処方箋に基づいて調剤する. The doctor 処方する ("prescribes"), the pharmacist 調剤する. A pharmacy that fills prescriptions is called 調剤薬局, as opposed to a drugstore (ドラッグストア) with over-the-counter products.

examples[].german: Please take this medicine orally three times a day after meals.
Please tell me if you are currently taking any medicine.
I was prescribed one oral medicine and one ointment.
en.notes: 内服 is "internal use", i.e. taking a medicine by mouth: 薬を内服する, 内服薬. It sounds medical and formal and appears on package inserts or in doctors' questions; patients themselves say 薬を飲む. The opposite is 外用 ("external use"); a medicine only as needed is called 頓服.

examples[].german: External medicines are applied directly to the skin.
This ointment is for external use only. Do not put it in your mouth.
For my lower back pain, I was prescribed a medicated patch as an external medicine.
en.notes: 外用 means "external use" and appears mainly in 外用薬, 外用剤 or the warning 外用のみ ("for external use only"). The opposite is 内服. In everyday speech one speaks more concretely of 塗り薬 ("ointment") or 貼り薬／湿布 ("patch, compress").

examples[].german: If this disease is detected early, the prognosis is good.
The doctor told us that my father's illness has a grim prognosis.
The new treatment has greatly improved patients' prognosis.
en.notes: 予後 is the medical "prognosis", i.e. the expected further course of a disease: 予後が良い／悪い, 予後良好, 予後不良. It is not used for weather, the economy or elections; there one says 予報, 予測 or 見通し. The older meaning "recovery after an illness" is rare today.

examples[].german: Chemotherapy has put the cancer into remission.
After his leukemia went into remission, he returned to work for the first time in three years.
Depression can alternate between remission and relapse.
en.notes: 寛解 is "remission": the symptoms have disappeared or declined markedly, but a return is possible. It is therefore deliberately distinguished from 完治 ("complete cure"). Typical are 寛解する, 寛解状態, 寛解期, 完全寛解; the word is used for cancer, leukemia, autoimmune and mental illnesses.

examples[].german: The new ambassador to Japan took up his post.
I applied for a visa at the embassy.
A popular actress was appointed tourism goodwill ambassador.
en.notes: 大使 is the ambassador, the highest diplomatic representative of a state; the embassy is called 大使館. The country is indicated with 駐〜: 駐日大使 "ambassador to Japan", 駐米大使 "ambassador to the USA"; formally 特命全権大使. Below it in rank stands the 公使 "minister (envoy)", while 領事 handles consular duties. Figuratively there are 親善大使 "goodwill ambassador" or 観光大使.

examples[].german: Even after treatment, regular checkups are done to monitor for recurrence.
My back pain has come back, and I have started going to the hospital again.
To prevent a recurrence of the same accident, we reviewed the work procedures.
en.notes: 再発 is intransitive: 病気が再発する ("occurs again"). Besides illnesses it often appears with accidents, mistakes and scandals, especially in the fixed phrase 再発防止 ("prevention of recurrence") in apologies and reports. Do not confuse it with 再発行 ("reissuing" of a card or document).

examples[].german: Complications of diabetes include kidney damage and retinopathy.
Surgery carries the risk of complications such as infection.
Elderly people easily develop complications such as pneumonia from influenza.
en.notes: 合併症 is a "complication" in the medical sense, i.e. an additional disease resulting from an illness or procedure: 〜の合併症, 合併症を起こす／引き起こす, 合併症のリスク. It is not used for complications in projects or in life; there one uses 問題, トラブル or 面倒なこと. The word 合併 alone means "merger" (会社の合併).

examples[].german: The patient's medical history is taken in detail to decide the treatment plan.
Please fill in your medical history and any allergies on the questionnaire.
My father has a history of heart disease, so he gets checked every year.
en.notes: 既往歴 is the list of a patient's earlier illnesses, i.e. the "medical history": 〜の既往歴がある, 既往歴を聴取する. A single earlier illness is called 既往症, the illnesses in the family 家族歴. In everyday speech one rather says 病歴 or 前に〜をしたことがある.

examples[].german: The patient's subjective symptoms are grasped through the medical interview.
Please fill out the medical questionnaire at reception and then wait.
In the interview, I was asked since when I had had a cough.
en.notes: 問診 is the doctor's questioning of the patient about complaints and history, the first step of the examination (診察). It includes 問診票 ("medical questionnaire") and 問診する. It forms a series with 視診 ("inspection"), 触診 ("palpation"), 聴診 ("auscultation") and 打診 ("percussion"). 問診 is the conversation itself, 既往歴 its content.

examples[].german: Abnormalities in the abdomen are confirmed by palpation.
The doctor palpated my abdomen to locate the painful spot.
It is recommended to perform a breast self-exam once a month.
en.notes: 触診 is the doctor's "palpation" with the hands: おなかを触診する, 触診で〜が分かる. It belongs to the series 問診, 視診, 触診, 聴診. Also well known is 自己触診 ("self-examination"), e.g. for breast cancer screening. In everyday speech one simply says 触る or 押さえてみる.

examples[].german: Heart and breath sounds are checked with a stethoscope.
Auscultation revealed a murmur in the heart.
I will listen to your back, so please lift your shirt a little.
en.notes: 聴診 is the "listening" to the heart, lungs or intestines with the 聴診器 ("stethoscope"): 胸を聴診する, 聴診器を当てる. It belongs to the series 問診, 触診, 聴診. In everyday speech the process is rather described as 胸の音を聞く; 聴診 itself is medical vocabulary.

examples[].german: Percussion is used to infer abnormalities in the chest cavity.
The doctor percussed the patient's abdomen with his fingers.
My department head sounded me out about a transfer to Osaka next month.
en.notes: 打診 has two meanings. Medically it is "percussion": the doctor taps the chest or abdomen to recognize changes from the sound (胸部を打診する). Much more common, however, is the figurative meaning "to sound out, to inquire non-bindingly": 〜に出演を打診する, 意向を打診する, 異動を打診される. With it one asks cautiously before an official offer is made. As a する-verb it is transitive.

examples[].german: A biopsy is performed to examine the nature of the tumor.
It takes about a week until the biopsy results come out.
During the gastroscopy, a biopsy was also taken just in case.
en.notes: 生検 is the short form of 生体組織検査 and means "biopsy", i.e. the taking and examination of tissue: 生検を行う／実施する, 生検を受ける, 生検の結果, 針生検 ("needle biopsy"). It is technical language; doctors often explain it to patients in other words: 組織を少し取って調べる. Typically, 生検 clarifies whether a finding is 良性 or 悪性.

examples[].german: Abnormalities inside the digestive tract are observed by endoscopy.
With surgery using an endoscope, the wound can be kept small.
The day before a colonoscopy, please eat easily digestible food.
en.notes: 内視鏡 is the "endoscope"; the examination is called 内視鏡検査 ("endoscopy"), e.g. 胃の内視鏡検査 or 大腸内視鏡検査. In everyday speech, a gastroscopy is usually called 胃カメラ. 内視鏡手術 means minimally invasive procedures; the device is inserted: 内視鏡を入れる／挿入する.

examples[].german: The condition of the blood vessels is checked with a contrast-enhanced CT scan.
When the contrast agent is injected, your body may feel a little warm.
An angiogram was performed using a catheter to examine the blood vessels of the heart.
en.notes: 造影 is the imaging of vessels or organs with the help of a contrast agent in X-ray, CT or MRI. The word appears almost only in compounds: 造影剤 ("contrast agent"), 造影CT, 造影検査, 血管造影 ("angiography"). Before such examinations, patients are asked about allergies to 造影剤.

examples[].german: Protection services for Japanese nationals abroad are carried out at the consulate.
I had lost my passport, so I consulted the consulate.
He took up his post as consul general in New York.
en.notes: 領事 is the consul who, abroad, mainly handles administrative tasks for his own country's citizens (passports, visas, help in emergencies). Common are 領事館 "consulate", 総領事 "consul general", 総領事館 and 在〜総領事館. In contrast to the 大使 "ambassador", who represents the state politically in the capital, consulates are often located in large cities outside the capital.

examples[].german: Diagnostic imaging technologies such as MRI and CT are advancing.
Diagnostic imaging found no fracture.
Attempts to reduce missed findings by doctors through AI-based diagnostic imaging are progressing.
en.notes: 画像診断 is "diagnostic imaging", i.e. the assessment of X-ray, CT, MRI or ultrasound images (レントゲン, CT, MRI, エコー). 画像検査 refers more to taking the images themselves, 画像診断 to their interpretation by specialist physicians (放射線科医, 画像診断医). The phrase 画像診断の結果 is common; recently also AIによる画像診断.

examples[].german: A lesion in the organ was identified on imaging.
A small lesion was found in the stomach during the endoscopy.
Since the lesion covers a wide area, it is difficult to remove all of it by surgery.
en.notes: 病変 denotes a "pathological change" or "lesion" in tissue, often before it is determined which disease is involved: 病変が見つかる／認められる, 病変の範囲, 前がん病変, 皮膚病変. It is not the same as 病気 ("illness") or 病状 ("condition of a disease"). The word belongs in medical findings and conversations with doctors.

examples[].german: The tissue became necrotic because blood flow was cut off.
Due to severe frostbite, his toes became necrotic.
After a venomous snake bite, the tissue around the wound can die.
en.notes: 壊死 is the "dying off" of body tissue, necrosis. The reading え is unusual, since 壊 is otherwise mostly read かい. As a する-verb it is intransitive: 組織が壊死する, also 壊死に陥る. Causes include circulatory disorders, frostbite or poisons. Related is 壊疽 ("gangrene"); in everyday speech one says, simplified, 組織が死ぬ.

examples[].german: Ischemia of the heart muscle is the cause of angina pectoris.
If the ischemic state continues for a long time, the tissue becomes necrotic.
My father has ischemic heart disease and goes to the hospital regularly.
en.notes: 虚血 is "ischemia", reduced blood supply to a tissue, usually due to narrowed or blocked vessels. Common in 虚血性心疾患 ("ischemic heart disease": 狭心症 and 心筋梗塞), 脳虚血 and 一過性脳虚血発作. Do not confuse it with 貧血, which means "anemia" or, colloquially, a fainting spell.

examples[].german: When a thrombus blocks a cerebral blood vessel, it causes a cerebral infarction.
If you sit on a plane for a long time, a blood clot can form in your leg.
I take a blood-thinning medicine to prevent blood clots.
en.notes: 血栓 is a "blood clot" (thrombus) that forms in a vessel: 血栓ができる, 血栓が詰まる, 血栓を溶かす, 血栓症. It is well known through the エコノミークラス症候群 ("economy class syndrome") after long sitting. If a clot detaches and blocks a vessel elsewhere, it is called 塞栓; the resulting tissue death is a 梗塞 (脳梗塞, 心筋梗塞).

examples[].german: Pulmonary embolism is a disease in which a venous thrombus blocks the pulmonary artery.
A blood clot can travel with the bloodstream and cause an embolism in another place.
To stop the bleeding, arterial embolization was performed with a catheter.
en.notes: 塞栓 is actually the "embolus", a plug of clot, air or fat that travels with the blood and blocks a vessel; the clinical picture "embolism" is called 塞栓症 (肺塞栓症, 脳塞栓症). Unlike 血栓, the blockage does not form at the site. 塞栓術 is deliberate "embolization", e.g. to treat bleeding or tumors.

examples[].german: Depending on the type of arrhythmia, it can be life-threatening.
Recently my pulse sometimes skips, so I had it checked, and it was a mild arrhythmia.
Stress and lack of sleep can also trigger arrhythmia.
en.notes: 不整脈 is "arrhythmia" (heart rhythm disorder): 不整脈がある／出る／見つかる. It includes e.g. 頻脈 ("pulse too fast"), 徐脈 ("pulse too slow") and 心房細動 ("atrial fibrillation"). Patients often describe the feeling colloquially as 脈が飛ぶ ("the pulse skips") or ドキドキする.

examples[].german: Improving lifestyle habits is important for patients with chronic heart failure.
My grandfather died of heart failure.
If heart failure worsens, you get out of breath after walking just a little.
en.notes: 心不全 is "heart failure": the heart no longer pumps enough blood. One distinguishes 慢性心不全 and 急性心不全; in obituaries one often reads 心不全で死去. The pattern 〜不全 ("failure, insufficiency") recurs in 腎不全, 呼吸不全 and 多臓器不全. Do not confuse it with 心筋梗塞 ("heart attack").

examples[].german: When chronic kidney failure progresses, dialysis treatment becomes necessary.
Quite a few people develop kidney failure because of diabetes.
Acute kidney failure often resolves if treated early.
en.notes: 腎不全 is "kidney failure"; 腎 is the technical syllable for "kidney" (腎臓, 腎機能). One distinguishes 急性腎不全, which is often curable, and 慢性腎不全, which in the final stage (末期腎不全) requires 透析 or a 腎移植. Typical verbs are 腎不全になる and, more formally, 腎不全に陥る.

en.meaning: sub-, secondary, subordinate (prefix, e.g. 亜熱帯, 亜種, 亜流)
examples[].german: Okinawa has a subtropical climate and is warm even in winter.
A rare subspecies of bird lives on this island.
His works were judged to be merely imitations of a famous painter.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese prefix of technical and written language meaning "sub-, secondary, subordinate": 亜熱帯 ("subtropics", separate card), 亜種 ("subspecies"), 亜寒帯 ("subarctic zone"). In chemistry it marks a lower oxidation state (亜硫酸 "sulfurous acid"), and 亜流 means pejoratively "epigone, mere imitation". Alone, 亜 also stands as an abbreviation for Asia, e.g. in 東亜.

examples[].german: The child put his shoes on the wrong feet.
Although I had warned him, I was the one who got scolded instead.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun: the order or sides are swapped: 靴を左右あべこべに履く. Colloquial; the more neutral word is 逆.

examples[].german: The store's takings today came to 100,000 yen.
Let's finish this job at five o'clock.
en.notes: Versatile noun: rise (物価の上がり), takings (店の上がり) and completion (仕事の上がり). As a suffix also "fresh after": 雨上がり (after the rain), 病み上がり.

en.meaning: to pounce on someone's slip of the tongue; to nitpick
examples[].german: Stop holding every little slip against others.
The discussion degenerated into mutual nitpicking.
en.notes: From wrestling: grabbing the opponent's raised leg. It means to seize on someone's small slip of the tongue or wording error instead of engaging with the content.

en.meaning: mutual, together; formally intensifying (prefix, e.g. 相次ぐ, 相変わらず, 相成る)
examples[].german: Recently, big earthquakes have been occurring one after another.
I hadn't seen him in a long time, but he was as lively as ever.
Our store has closed as of today.
en.notes: A prefix before verbs and in set words that expresses reciprocity or simultaneity: 相次ぐ "to happen one after another", 相変わらず "as always", 相対する "to face each other". In 相成る or 相済まない, it merely gives the sentence a solemn, formal tone. Not productive; the Sino-Japanese reading そう (相談, 相当) is a different use of the character, and 相手 (あいて) is learned as a word of its own.

examples[].german: The two have been close for a long time.
Even in the relationship between boss and employee, I say what needs to be said.
en.notes: The relationship between two people: 親しい間柄 (close relationship), 親子の間柄.

examples[].german: The saleswoman there is always friendly.
He isn't very sociable, but he works carefully.
en.notes: An affable, friendly manner: 愛想がいい (friendly), 愛想が悪い (unfriendly). Also read あいそう. Idiom: 愛想が尽きる (to be fed up).

en.meaning: only between the parties involved, in private
examples[].german: The shares were not sold through the exchange but in a direct transaction between the parties.
The price was set not by the market but directly between the parties involved.
en.notes: A rare, independent reading of 相対: "only between the parties involved, without third parties". Today it survives almost only in compounds such as 相対取引 "direct (off-exchange) trading between two parties" or 相対売買 and in 相対で決める "to settle between themselves". The usual reading そうたい (own card) means "relative" (相対的, opposite 絶対); which reading is meant becomes clear from the context, and in trade and negotiation it is mostly あいたい.

en.meaning: to get a taste for it (after an initial success)
examples[].german: Since winning the lottery once, he has gotten a taste for it and buys tickets every week.
Once a crow has found food in the garbage, it keeps coming back.
en.notes: After an initial success or advantage, one wants to try the same thing again - often with a slightly negative undertone (greed, recklessness). Often also written in kana: 味をしめる.

examples[].german: This wine has a full-bodied flavor.
Old streets have a charm all their own.
en.notes: Flavor (深い味わいのコーヒー) and, figuratively, the special charm of something: 味わいのある文章.

examples[].german: I scrubbed myself thoroughly clean in the bath.
Grime clings to the collar of the shirt worn for a long time.
en.notes: Dirt that accumulates on skin or objects: 垢を落とす (to wash thoroughly). Homophone: 赤 (red).

examples[].german: Lions and tigers are classified in the subfamily Pantherinae.
In taxonomy, a subfamily is sometimes established between the family and the genus.
A new subfamily was established for this fossil insect.
en.notes: Taxonomic term for the rank between 科 "family" and 属 "genus", usually attached directly to an animal or plant name in katakana: ネコ亜科, ヒト亜科. Formed analogously are 亜目 "suborder" and 亜種 "subspecies". Outside biology the word hardly occurs; do not confuse it with the homophones 赤 "red" and 垢 "dirt".

examples[].german: In the evening sun, the temple roof shone copper-colored (あかがねいろ).
The copper (あかがね) bell of the mountain temple echoed through the quiet valley.
In the past, gold, silver and copper were called "kogane", "shirogane" and "akagane".
en.notes: あかがね "red metal" is the old native Japanese reading of 銅 and belongs to the series こがね (gold), しろがね (silver) and くろがね (iron). Today it appears almost only in literature, poems and color words such as あかがね色 "copper-colored"; in everyday use, technology and medals, 銅 is always read どう (separate card), e.g. 銅メダル. Because the reading cannot be seen from the kanji, furigana or hiragana is often added.

examples[].german: When she was praised, she blushed slightly.
In the evening, the western sky turned red.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: 顔が赤らむ (to blush), 空が赤らむ (the sky turns red). Somewhat more literary than 赤くなる.

examples[].german: This medal is proof of his efforts.
I gave him a ring as a token of friendship.
en.notes: Elevated word for proof or sign, often emotional: 愛の証 (token of love), 努力の証. More everyday: 証拠.

en.meaning: vacant, unused room; room for rent
examples[].german: Is there a vacant room at this inn tonight?
The landlord decided to rent out the vacant room on the second floor to a student.
en.notes: 空き間（あきま）denotes a room that is currently not in use or has no tenant yet. You can ask 空き間があるか or 空き間を貸す. The rarer writing 空間 has the same reading あきま here; the ordinary 空間（くうかん）, by contrast, means "space" in the general sense. In present-day daily life, 空き部屋 and 空室 are often more common.

examples[].german: He did not give up and kept trying again and again.
Because I gave it my all, I can accept even a defeat.
en.notes: Noun of 諦める: 諦めが早い (to give up quickly), 諦めがつく (to be able to come to terms with it).

examples[].german: My grandmother did not want to move house on an unlucky day.
We looked at the calendar and set the wedding date so as to avoid an unlucky day.
I was told that today is an unlucky day, so it is better not to start anything new.
en.notes: 悪日 denotes, according to the traditional calendar or folk belief, an unlucky day on which one avoids important undertakings such as moving or weddings; the opposite is 吉日 "lucky day". Besides あくび, the reading あくにち is also used. The word sounds exactly like あくび "yawn" (separate card), which only context distinguishes; today it is encountered mainly in calendar and fortune-telling texts.

examples[].german: Cheating elderly people is an unscrupulous method.
This dress is a garish color and too eye-catching for me.
en.notes: Mostly "unscrupulous, cunning": あくどい商売 (shady business). More rarely "loud, garish" of colors or flavor. Also written 悪どい.

examples[].german: Today is an unlucky day, so let's move next week.
My grandmother chose the wedding date by the calendar so as to avoid unlucky days.
en.notes: A day that is inauspicious according to the calendar or fortune-telling, on which people avoid weddings, moves or starting a business; the opposite of 吉日 ("lucky day"). あくにち is the usual reading; the secondary reading あくび has its own card but is rare, also because あくび otherwise means "yawn" (欠伸).

examples[].german: On the morning of the next day, he left the house early.
The following year, the two of them married.
en.notes: A prenominal word (連体詞) used only before time expressions: 明くる日 (the next day), 明くる朝, 明くる年. Written language; in everyday speech people prefer 次の日 or 翌日.

examples[].german: Since the light turned green, I hit the gas.
An accident occurred because the accelerator and brake were mixed up.
en.notes: The gas pedal in a car: アクセルを踏む (to step on the gas). Counterpart: ブレーキ. Figuratively also "to push something forward".

examples[].german: He is an amateur, but has the skill of a professional.
I entered a photo contest for amateurs.
en.notes: Someone who does something not as a profession; short form アマ. Opposite: プロ.

examples[].german: The weather in the mountains changes quickly, so let's take rain gear.
Rain gear is on the packing list for the school trip.
en.notes: Generic term for umbrella, raincoat and rain boots: 雨具を持参してください.

examples[].german: I cooked a mild curry for the kids.
This sake is sweet and easy to drink.
en.notes: A mild flavor profile, for example for curry or sake: 甘口のカレー. Opposite: 辛口 (hot, dry).

examples[].german: The Kojiki begins with the story of the beginning of heaven and earth.
The poets of old prayed to the gods of heaven and earth for peace in the land.
The poet sang that all living things between heaven and earth share the same life.
en.notes: Old Japanese reading of 天地 with the same basic meaning "heaven and earth, the whole world" as 天地/てんち (separate card). あめつち is found almost only in classical poetry, in myths such as the 古事記, and in deliberately archaizing language, often referring to the gods of heaven and earth. In present-day use and in phrases such as 天地の差 or 天地無用, it is always read てんち.

examples[].german: A hint of the ending is hidden at the beginning of the novel.
He is the type who is easily influenced (susceptible to suggestion).
Before the match, I told myself through self-suggestion, "I can definitely win."
en.notes: Noun of the verb 暗示する (separate card): an indirect hint or a hidden clue, as opposed to 明示 "explicit statement". In psychology it means "suggestion": 暗示にかかる "to be influenced", 暗示をかける "to suggest", 自己暗示 "self-suggestion". More elevated than ヒント, typical in texts about literature, psychology and advertising.

en.meaning: to worry about; to think up
examples[].german: Mother is always worried about her son who lives far away.
He devised a plan to solve the problem.
en.notes: Literary Ichidan verb: to worry (身を案じる = to be anxious about someone's welfare) or to devise a plan (一計を案じる). Also 案ずる.

examples[].german: In response to the audience's calls for an encore, she sang one more song.
There were two encores at the end of the concert.
en.notes: An encore at a concert; the audience calls out "アンコール!". Also the rerun of a popular program.

examples[].german: The doctor told me to rest for a week.
After the operation, my father needs strict bed rest.
en.notes: Physical rest for recovery: 安静にする (to rest), 絶対安静 (strict bed rest).

examples[].german: Starting next month, the hourly wage will go up.
This photo is a close-up of a flower.
en.notes: Mostly as a suffix or with する: 給料アップ (pay raise), 売り上げがアップする. In film also a close-up (顔のアップ). Opposite: ダウン.

examples[].german: This problem calls for a different approach.
The approach from the station to the museum runs along an avenue of cherry trees.
en.notes: An approach to tackling a problem (新しいアプローチ); as the verb アプローチする also "to approach someone" or "to make advances toward someone". In golf, the approach shot.

examples[].german: Oh, it's already this late! I have to go home.
Oh, Mr. Tanaka, long time no see!
en.notes: Exclamation of surprise, used more by women: あら、もうこんな時間. Do not confuse it with あら (flaw, defect) or the fish アラ.

examples[].german: Arabic is spoken in the Arab countries.
He is researching Arab culture.
en.notes: The Arabs and the Arab countries, often in compounds: アラブ諸国 (Arab states), アラブ人. Also a horse breed.

examples[].german: The taxi drove so roughly that I was scared.
He speaks roughly, but is basically good-natured.
en.notes: い-adjective: rough behavior (荒っぽい運転 = reckless driving) or coarse, careless work (仕事が荒っぽい).

examples[].german: A dispute broke out between the siblings over the land.
The fight for the league championship lasted until the end.
en.notes: Noun of 争う: dispute (争いが起きる) and competition (首位争い = fight for first place).

en.meaning: to be commonplace; to be ordinary
examples[].german: That is a perfectly ordinary story, the kind you hear everywhere.
Even with ordinary ingredients, you can make delicious food.
en.notes: Ichidan verb, used almost only attributively in the form ありふれた: ありふれた話 (a commonplace story). Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: Please tell it exactly as it happened.
It is important to accept yourself as you are.
en.notes: The way something actually is, without embellishment: ありのままを話す, ありのままの自分. Mostly in kana.

examples[].german: After the typhoon, the town presented a terrible sight.
Because you never tidy up, the room looks like this.
en.notes: State, often negative or reproachful: 何だこの有様は (What kind of state is this!). Also written 有り様.

examples[].german: Soapy water is alkaline.
When you mix an acid and an alkali, they neutralize each other.
en.notes: Chemistry: base, alkali. アルカリ性 (alkaline, basic); opposite: 酸 or 酸性.

examples[].german: The color of the curtains has faded in the sun.
The memory of that day has not faded to this day.
en.notes: Intransitive ichidan verb: colors fade (色が褪せる), and memories fade too. Often 色褪せる. Homophone: 焦る (to hurry, to be nervous).

examples[].german: I'm afraid I cannot take part this time; I ask for your understanding.
If all seats are taken, we may have to turn you away. Please understand.
en.notes: A polite formula used when one has to decline a request or communicate something unpleasant; often at the end: 悪しからずご了承ください. Mostly in kana: あしからず.

examples[].german: I want to see that movie too.
I'll cook today, okay?
en.notes: あたし is a colloquial first-person pronoun, especially in everyday speech with a feminine flavor. It is usually written in kana; the kanji writing 私 can also have this reading. For formal conversation, わたし is the more common choice. In the first example, も means "also". In the second, が highlights who is cooking today; the final ね seeks agreement. The readings わたし and わたくし are covered in their own entries.

en.meaning: aim; hope, prospect; reliance; (suffix, usually 宛/宛て) addressed to
examples[].german: On days off, I like to wander around the city aimlessly.
You can't rely on his promises.
Please send these documents to the personnel department.
en.notes: 当て stands for "aim" and "expectation, something one counts on", almost only in fixed phrases: 当てもなく "aimlessly", 当てが外れる "for expectations not to be met", 当てにする "to rely on", 当てにならない "unreliable". For a concrete goal or purpose, people otherwise say 目的 or 目当て. As a suffix after names or companies, あて means "addressed to": 田中様宛ての手紙, 会社宛てに送る; in this sense it is written 宛 or 宛て, never 当て (cf. 宛先 "recipient, address").

examples[].german: This is a letter I wrote to my teacher.
Who is this message addressed to?
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb: to address a letter to someone: 母に宛てた手紙. Homophones: 当てる (to hit), 充てる (to allocate).

en.meaning: hour, time (mostly in compounds, e.g. ラッシュアワー, ハッピーアワー, キロワットアワー)
examples[].german: I leave home early to avoid the morning rush hour.
This bar has a happy hour from five to seven, and beer is half price.
This refrigerator's annual power consumption is about 300 kilowatt-hours.
en.notes: Loanword from English "hour" that occurs almost only in compounds: ラッシュアワー "rush hour" (separate card), ハッピーアワー or the unit キロワットアワー "kilowatt-hour". It hardly stands alone; the normal hour as a unit of time is 時間, the time of day 〜時.

en.meaning: joining together, combination; facing each other (mostly in compounds)
examples[].german: If you put two mirrors facing each other, you can see the back of your own hair.
On the train, I sat directly facing a stranger.
I sent an assortment of sweets as a year-end gift.
en.notes: Noun of the verb 合わせる (separate card): the joining or facing of two things. On its own it is rare; it is mostly the first or last element of compounds: 合わせ鏡 "two mirrors facing each other", 向かい合わせ "facing each other", 背中合わせ "back to back", 詰め合わせ "assortment" or 打ち合わせ "meeting" (separate card). Do not confuse it with the homophone 袷 "lined kimono".

en.meaning: to put together; to adjust; to match up
examples[].german: We all joined forces and overcame the difficulties.
I quietly put my hands together in front of the temple.
en.notes: Godan variant of 合わせる, a bit more colloquial: 手を合わす (to put one's hands together), 力を合わす (to join forces), 時計を合わす (to set a clock).

examples[].german: Because of the typhoon, it is doubtful whether the tournament can take place.
The people around him doubted the success of the plan.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb of written language: to have doubts about whether something will succeed: 成功を危ぶむ声. Often in the passive: 開催が危ぶまれる.

en.meaning: to err; to make a mistake
examples[].german: I made the wrong decision and suffered a big loss.
False information spreads on the internet.
en.notes: Godan verb: to do something wrongly: 判断を誤る (to misjudge). Often attributive: 誤った情報 (false information). Homophone: 謝る (to apologize).

examples[].german: This book describes the company's fifty-year history.
He was tired and stopped walking.
en.notes: Elevated noun: step (歩みを止める) and, figuratively, the history or development of something: 会社の百年の歩み.

en.meaning: to walk; to tread (a path in life)
examples[].german: The two decided to go their separate ways.
She walked the path of a doctor throughout a long life.
en.notes: Elevated godan verb; in everyday speech 歩く. Mostly figurative: 人生を歩む, 別々の道を歩む (to go separate ways).

en.meaning: hamlet, district (subdivision of a village, in addresses)
examples[].german: My grandfather's house address is "Nakano Village, Ōaza Yamada, Aza Uehara".
In this village, each district puts out its own festival float.
Because of land readjustment, the old aza names disappeared from the map.
en.notes: Designation for a district or section within a municipality, today mainly in rural addresses: 大字 "larger district" and 小字 "small section name", often also simply 字 before the name. It is written the same as 字/じ "character" (separate card), but is a completely different word; in addresses it is always read あざ. In everyday speech 地区 or 集落 is used instead.

examples[].german: It is not good to mock other people's mistakes.
Although those around him jeered at him, he did not give up his dream.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to laugh at someone contemptuously: 人の失敗をあざ笑う. Kanji also 嘲笑う.

examples[].german: After work, I had a drink at the hotel bar.
She cleared the two-meter bar with ease.
en.notes: Establishment: ホテルのバー (hotel bar). In sports: バーを越える (to clear the bar).

examples[].german: This microscope can raise the magnification up to 1,000 times.
Popular universities have high competition ratios in entrance exams.
en.notes: Optics: 倍率の高い望遠鏡 (a high-magnification telescope). For entrance exams: 倍率が高い (many applicants per place), 倍率十倍 (ten applicants per place).

examples[].german: He always wears his company badge on his chest.
The children collect pin badges of their favorite characters.
en.notes: バッジをつける (to wear a badge). 議員バッジ = a legislator's badge.

examples[].german: The old building was demolished in an instant by blasting.
The bridge was blown up, and the road to the town was cut off.
en.notes: 爆破する (to blow up): ビルを爆破する. Also 爆破予告 (bomb threat).

en.meaning: format, size (of paper or books) (suffix, e.g. A4判, B5判)
examples[].german: Please print this document on A4-size paper.
The new magazine is B5 size and easy to carry around.
I had the vacation photo enlarged to A3.
en.notes: Stands as a suffix after paper and book formats: A4判 (エーよんばん), B5判, A3判; also 大判 (おおばん) "large format". Common in offices and publishing; in conversation people often say just A4. Do not confuse it with 判/はん "stamp, seal" (separate card): same spelling, but different reading and meaning.

examples[].german: His works are loved by everyone across the ages.
Peace is the wish of all people.
Before the law, all people must be equal.
en.notes: A rarer, elevated alternative reading of 万人 with the same meaning "all people". The standard reading is ばんにん (separate card), which you hear practically always in fixed expressions such as 万人向け and 万人受け; ばんじん appears mainly in solemn or older written language (万人の願い). Do not confuse it with 一万人 (いちまんにん) "ten thousand people".

en.meaning: last years of one's life, twilight years
examples[].german: In his later years, the painter lived quietly in his home village.
This is a novel the writer wrote late in life.
en.notes: The late years of a life, especially of well-known people: 晩年の作品 (late work).

examples[].german: She is an all-round athlete and shines in every sport.
Money is not omnipotent.
en.notes: Often with の or as a first element: 万能ナイフ (all-purpose knife), 万能薬 (cure-all). スポーツ万能 = good at all sports.

en.meaning: to scatter, strew; to distribute (money, flyers) in large quantities
examples[].german: The child scattered the beans from the bag all over the floor.
Someone in front of the station was handing out election flyers in bulk.
en.notes: Usually in kana, also written ばら撒く. Figuratively often pejorative: 税金をばらまく (to hand out tax money indiscriminately); hence ばらまき (indiscriminate handouts).

en.meaning: to be worn out, to be utterly exhausted
examples[].german: The heat has worn me out, and I don't feel like doing anything.
I ran out of steam in the middle of the marathon and walked.
en.notes: Colloquial, often with heat or sports. Related: 夏ばて (exhaustion from summer heat).

examples[].german: He swung the bat with all his might.
I bought a new bat and practice swinging every day.
en.notes: Mainly the baseball bat: バットを振る (to swing the bat), 素振り (practice swings without a ball).

examples[].german: Startled by a noise, the cat leapt up in a flash.
When the alarm clock rang, he threw back the futon and got up in one motion.
The rumor spread through the whole town in an instant.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic adverb for a sudden, forceful movement, often with verbs such as 飛び上がる, 跳ね上げる or 広がる. It is the voiced, more forceful counterpart to ぱっと, which seems lighter and quicker. It has nothing to do with the loanword バット "bat" (separate card).

examples[].german: This movie is based on a real incident.
Using the village at the foot of the mountain as our base, we climbed the mountain every day.
en.notes: 〜をベースにする (to build on ..., to base on ...). Same sound: ベース (bass, bass guitar). In baseball: base.

examples[].german: The city makes various accommodations for the elderly.
For convenience, we divided the participants into three groups.
en.notes: 便宜を図る (to accommodate someone, to provide favors), 便宜上 (for convenience's sake).

examples[].german: He made no excuses for being late.
There is no excuse for this mistake.
en.notes: 弁解する (to justify oneself), 弁解の余地がない (inexcusable). More everyday: 言い訳.

en.meaning: the best, one's best; best possible
examples[].german: Whatever the result, I want to do my best.
In the current situation, I think this is the best choice.
en.notes: ベストを尽くす (to do one's best), 自己ベスト (personal best). Same sound: ベスト (vest).

examples[].german: Her first novel became a bestseller.
This month's bestsellers are lined up in the bookstore at the station.
en.notes: ベストセラーになる (to become a bestseller). A long-running bestseller: ロングセラー.

examples[].german: He started his own business right after graduating from university.
On business trips, I stay at the business hotel in front of the station.
en.notes: Often in compounds: ビジネスマン (businessman), ビジネスホテル (simple hotel for business travelers), ビジネスクラス. More general: 仕事, 商売.

examples[].german: I came in last in the race at the sports day.
He ranked last in his class, but now works as a doctor.
en.notes: Colloquial: びりになる (to come in last). Neutral: 最下位.

examples[].german: A trace amount of lead was detected in the tap water.
This medicine is strongly effective even in tiny amounts.
en.notes: Often 微量の〜: 微量の放射性物質 (a trace of radioactive material), 微量の毒 (a trace of poison). Opposite: 大量.

examples[].german: With a smile on her lips, she nodded quietly.
The woman in the painting wears a gentle smile.
en.notes: Written style: 微笑を浮かべる (to have a smile on one's face). Everyday: 微笑み (ほほえみ), verb 微笑む.

examples[].german: The sudden rain left my clothes soaking wet.
When I ran home, my shirt was drenched with sweat.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic; mostly with 濡れる, with だ, or in 汗びっしょり (drenched in sweat). Similar: ずぶ濡れ.

examples[].german: Several countries boycotted the tournament.
The students boycotted classes in protest against the tuition increase.
en.notes: ボイコットする (to boycott): 授業をボイコットする, 大会をボイコットする.

examples[].german: When I finish my studies abroad, I intend to return to my home country and become a teacher.
She treated her friends to dishes from her home country.
en.notes: The country where one was born and raised, mainly from the viewpoint of people abroad: 母国に帰る (to return to one's home country). Cf. 母国語 (native language).

examples[].german: I visited my old school for the first time in ten years since graduating.
The baseball team of my old school will take part in Koshien.
en.notes: The school or university one attended oneself: 母校を訪ねる (to visit one's old school). Also used for elementary and high schools, not only for universities.

examples[].german: The voltage of household outlets in Japan is 100 volts.
This charger supports up to 240 volts.
en.notes: Unit of electrical voltage: 百ボルト. In Japan, household outlets supply 100 volts. A different word that sounds the same: ボルト (bolt).

en.meaning: gradually; little by little; it's about time (to do something)
examples[].german: An hour after opening, customers gradually started to come in.
It's already late, so shall we start heading home?
en.notes: Like ぼちぼち: slowly but steadily (ぼつぼつ客が来始めた) or "about time" when it is becoming time for something: ぼつぼつ帰ろうか. As a noun also "dots, pimples".

examples[].german: Citizens angered by the sudden rise in prices started a riot.
The police put down the riot by evening.
en.notes: A violent uprising of a crowd: 暴動が起きる (a riot breaks out), 暴動を鎮める (to put down a riot).

examples[].german: Debate continues in the Diet about the nation's defense.
The champion successfully defended his title for the third time.
en.notes: 防衛する (to defend), 防衛費 (defense spending), 正当防衛 (self-defense). In sports: タイトルを防衛する (to defend a title).

examples[].german: Because of the typhoon, a violent wind began to blow from the evening.
Because of the storm, all afternoon flights were cancelled.
en.notes: Very strong wind, mainly in weather reports: 暴風警報 (storm warning), 暴風雨 (storm with wind and rain). In everyday speech, 強い風 or 嵐 is more usual.

en.meaning: beginning; opening (of a speech or text)
examples[].german: At the start of the meeting, the company president gave a greeting.
The opening sentence of the novel was very impressive.
en.notes: The beginning of a text, speech or meeting: 冒頭で述べたように (as mentioned at the beginning). Homophone: 暴騰 (sharp price surge).

examples[].german: Without my glasses, the letters blur and I can't read them.
The photo came out blurry because my hand moved.
en.notes: Intransitive: outlines, images or memories become indistinct: 写真がぼやける, 記憶がぼやける.

en.meaning: to grumble; to complain; to whine
examples[].german: My father is grumbling that prices are far too high these days.
Stop grumbling all the time and help out a little.
en.notes: Colloquial: to complain under one's breath in a rather resigned way, often about trifles: 仕事が多いとぼやく (to grumble about having too much work).

en.meaning: spots, patches (esp. in fur, e.g. ぶち猫 spotted cat)
examples[].german: Our cat is a black-and-white spotted one.
I saw a dog with brown patches in the park.
That cow has big spots on its body.
en.notes: Refers to spots in the fur of animals, especially in ぶち猫 "spotted cat" or 白黒のぶちの犬; ブチ is a popular name for spotted pets. Mostly in kana. The kanji spelling 斑 is mostly read まだら (separate card): まだら "mottled, uneven" is more general and also applies to patterns, colors or snow.

examples[].german: The hand-me-down trousers from my older brother are baggy.
Because I lost weight, my old suit has become baggy.
My daughter wears an oversized sweater on purpose.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic word for clothes or shoes that are too big and flap around: ぶかぶかのズボン, 靴がぶかぶかだ, ぶかぶかになる. The opposites are きつい "tight" and ぴったり "a perfect fit". Colloquial and mostly in hiragana, more rarely ブカブカ; the meaning "bulging, warped" is rare.

examples[].german: He is brusque, but actually a nice person.
The salesperson answered me curtly, and I felt a bit uncomfortable.
en.notes: な-adjective: ぶっきらぼうな返事; adverbially ぶっきらぼうに答える. It describes an unfriendly, terse way of speaking, often without ill intent.

examples[].german: For a first visit, sweets are a safe choice as a gift.
He handles any job competently without mistakes.
en.notes: The choice where you can't go wrong: 無難な色 (an unobtrusive color). 〜ほうが無難だ = it is safer to ...

examples[].german: When adding fractions, first make the denominators the same.
The denominator of three quarters is four.
en.notes: Mathematics; opposite: 分子 (numerator). Fraction: 分数.

examples[].german: This factory makes products with a finely divided labor system.
In our household, my spouse and I divide up the housework.
en.notes: 分業する (to divide the work), 分業制 (division-of-labor system). Related: 国際分業 (international division of labor).

examples[].german: Valuable cultural properties were lost in the fire.
Many nationally designated Important Cultural Properties remain in this temple.
en.notes: Legally protected cultural properties: 重要文化財, 無形文化財 (intangible cultural property). World Heritage: 世界遺産.

examples[].german: Profits are distributed according to the amount invested.
The siblings fought over the division of the inheritance.
en.notes: 分配する (to distribute, to divide): 利益を分配する. Related: 配分, 再分配.

examples[].german: You must not behave rudely toward customers.
Please forgive my rudeness the other day.
en.notes: 無礼な態度 (insolent behavior); stronger than 失礼. Polite: 先日はご無礼しました. 無礼講 = a party where differences in rank don't matter.

examples[].german: The bull market continues in the stock market.
A bulldozer was pushing earth at the construction site.
A friend has started keeping a French bulldog.
en.notes: On the stock exchange, ブル stands for rising prices (ブル相場 "bull market", opposite ベア相場); in general Japanese 強気相場 is said instead. It is also the short form of ブルドーザー "bulldozer" and ブルドッグ "bulldog" (e.g. フレンチブル). Do not confuse it with ブルー "blue".

examples[].german: She was wearing a blue dress.
On Monday mornings I somehow feel blue.
en.notes: Color: ライトブルー (light blue), ネイビーブルー (navy blue). Colloquial: ブルーな気分 (a gloomy mood).

examples[].german: The two countries should solve the problem through talks, not by force of arms.
An armed clash occurred near the border.
en.notes: 武力衝突 (armed clash), 武力行使 (use of armed force).

en.meaning: goods, product; stuff, (stolen) goods (colloquial, often ブツ); -item, -matter (suffix, e.g. 印刷物)
examples[].german: Carrying dangerous items onto the aircraft is prohibited.
Please distribute the printed materials for the meeting in advance.
The detectives finally found out where the goods were hidden.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 物, mainly as a suffix in technical words: 危険物, 印刷物, 郵便物, 農産物. On its own, ぶつ is slang from crime stories and police jargon for stolen goods, drugs or "the stuff", and is then usually written ブツ. In everyday speech "thing" is もの (separate card); the verb ぶつ "to hit" is a different word.

examples[].german: The minister's remarks are causing controversy.
The film caused controversy because of its many violent scenes.
en.notes: Almost only in 物議を醸す (to cause a stir, to spark controversy).

examples[].german: There was a report that someone had seen a glowing object in the sky.
Most objects expand when heated.
en.notes: Neutral and factual word for an object, especially in physics and reports: 未確認飛行物体 (UFO). Everyday: 物.

examples[].german: Camping is quite a boom right now.
Once the boom passed, hardly any customers came to the shop.
en.notes: 〜ブーム: 健康ブーム (health craze), ブームになる (to become popular), ブームが去る (the craze is over).

examples[].german: On snowy days I go out in boots that don't slip easily.
It took a while to take off my boots in the entryway.
en.notes: ロングブーツ (long boots), レインブーツ (rain boots). Rubber boots are also called 長靴.

examples[].german: The buzzer for the end of the exam sounded.
Elementary school children have a security alarm attached to their school backpacks.
en.notes: ブザーが鳴る (the buzzer sounds). 防犯ブザー = personal safety alarm that many Japanese schoolchildren carry.

examples[].german: The chime signaling the end of class rang.
