I rang the doorbell, but no one came out.
en.notes: The chime at schools and stations; also the doorbell (玄関のチャイム).

examples[].german: Ladies and gentlemen, please be seated.
When the teacher came in, the students quietly sat down.
en.notes: Formal for 座る. In class: 起立、礼、着席 (stand, bow, sit).

examples[].german: These sweets are artificially colored.
We recreated the old townscape by coloring black-and-white photographs.
en.notes: Adding color to food, photos, or materials; 着色料 (coloring agent), 無着色 (no added coloring). As a verb 着色する.

examples[].german: Is it okay if I change the channel?
She runs a cooking video channel.
en.notes: A TV channel, now also a video channel (動画チャンネル). The spelling チャネル is mainly used in technical contexts (販売チャネル sales channel).

examples[].german: The family always gathers in the living room to watch TV.
The program became popular in living rooms across the country.
en.notes: The traditional family room; figuratively, TV viewers at home: お茶の間の人気者.

examples[].german: For a change of mood, I changed my hairstyle.
After the third out, the teams switched sides.
en.notes: Colloquial for "change" (イメージチェンジ, short イメチェン); in baseball, the switch between batting and fielding teams. More neutral: 変更, 交代.

examples[].german: The baby is nursing at its mother's breast.
The work of milking cows starts early in the morning.
en.notes: Mother's milk or animal milk, and also the breast. Homophone: 父 (father). As an everyday drink: 牛乳, ミルク.

examples[].german: When I think of my parents in my hometown, my heart grows warm.
I wrote a letter to my parents, who live far away.
Many of the songs of the frontier guards sing of parting from father and mother.
en.notes: The native Japanese reading ちちはは is literary and emotional, e.g. in poems or letters about one's hometown (故郷の父母). The same spelling is read ふぼ in factual texts and administrative language (separate card, e.g. 父母会, 父母の同意). In everyday speech 両親 (りょうしん) or 父と母 is said. Without furigana, 父母 is mostly to be read ふぼ.

en.meaning: to alter; to break (a promise); to sprain, to crick
examples[].german: He is not the kind of person to break a promise.
I lifted a heavy load and strained a muscle in my neck.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 違う: to make something different (色を違える), to break a promise (約束を違える), to sprain or crick (筋を違える). Common in compounds: 間違える, 寝違える.

examples[].german: The two pledged eternal love to each other.
With a firm promise to meet again, the two parted.
en.notes: Literary/formal: to pledge lasting fidelity, love, or a reunion. Noun: 契り (pledge, vow). Homophone: 千切る (to tear off).

examples[].german: The strength of this team lies in its teamwork.
Teamwork is important in the workplace.
en.notes: Cooperation within a group: チームワークがいい (to work well together).

examples[].german: She glanced at me.
I have caught a snippet of that rumor.
en.notes: Only very briefly or in passing: ちらっと見る, ちらっと聞く. Similar: ちらりと; repeated: ちらちら.

examples[].german: Dust had piled up on the shelf.
Many a little makes a mickle.
en.notes: Fine dust; the proverb 塵も積もれば山となる (even small things add up). In daily life usually ほこり or ごみ.

examples[].german: You can sense intelligence in the way she speaks.
It is important to cultivate both intellect and sensibility.
en.notes: The ability to think and judge, often as a character trait (知性のある人). Cf. 知能 (measurable intelligence).

examples[].german: He has an intellectual air about him.
Reading satisfies intellectual curiosity.
en.notes: Relating to the intellect or seeming intelligent: 知的な人, 知的財産 (intellectual property).

en.meaning: to pamper, to spoil, to fawn over (ちやほやする)
examples[].german: She grew up fussed over by everyone around her from childhood.
If you fawn over newcomers too much, it doesn't do them any good.
When his popularity declined, the people who had been fawning over him drifted away.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic word, almost always as ちやほやする or in the passive ちやほやされる "to be doted on, courted". It sounds slightly derogatory: someone gets excessive attention and flattery, often because of looks or success. 甘やかす (あまやかす), by contrast, means indulgent spoiling, typically of children. Mostly written in hiragana.

en.meaning: (written) work, book; written by (suffix after author names, e.g. 夏目漱石著)
examples[].german: This book is "Kokoro" by Natsume Soseki.
This book is by the economist Tanaka and was written over ten years.
The reference list says "Ichiro Yamada, 2020".
en.notes: 著 appears mainly as a suffix after an author's name and means "written by" (山田太郎著); as a noun "work" it appears in 〜の著 ("a work by ..."). In everyday speech, for an author's book 著書 (ちょしょ, separate card) or 作品 is said; 著 is typical of bibliographic information, book covers and reviews. For translations, 訳 ("translated by") often stands next to 著.

examples[].german: My intuition told me this person could be trusted.
When in doubt, trust your own intuition.
en.notes: Grasping something spontaneously without reasoning; 直感的 (intuitive). In philosophy also written 直観.

examples[].german: He comes to visit every now and then.
I come to this shop quite often.
en.notes: Colloquial for "often, every now and then"; similar to ときどき, よく.

examples[].german: A renowned writer came to give a lecture.
She is an internationally renowned scientist.
en.notes: More formal than 有名: 著名な作家, 著名人 (prominent figures).

examples[].german: His books have been translated into many languages.
I read my professor's new book.
en.notes: A book someone wrote themselves. Cf. 著者 (author).

examples[].german: Yogurt is said to be good for the intestines.
My bowels were bothering me, so I went to the hospital.
en.notes: 大腸 (large intestine), 小腸 (small intestine), 腸内環境 (gut environment). Homophone: 蝶 (butterfly).

en.meaning: clanging, clashing (sword blows, axe strokes, go stones)
examples[].german: From deep in the mountains came the sound of wood being chopped.
The two lawmakers engaged in a heated debate in the Diet.
In the quiet tatami room, only the clack of go stones can be heard.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic adverb for repeated hard striking: swords meeting, axe blows when felling trees, the clack of go stones; usually with と (丁々と). Literary, and today known mainly from the four-character compound 丁々発止 ("heated exchange of blows", also in debates). Do not confuse it with the homophone 蝶々 ("butterfly").

en.meaning: very long and large; immense; huge (na-adj.)
examples[].german: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge is one of the longest and grandest suspension bridges in the world.
That novel is a monumental work of ten volumes in all.
It is impossible to read such a long, voluminous report in one night.
en.notes: 長大 is a literary na-adjective that mainly stresses great length: 長大な橋, 長大な小説, 長大な報告書. 巨大 (own card), on the other hand, means enormous size or mass in general. The identically read 頂戴 "to receive; give me" is a completely different word; in conversation one usually says とても長い or 大きい instead of 長大.

en.meaning: handy, useful; to find useful, to prize
examples[].german: I make good use of the handy goods from the 100-yen shop.
Because he speaks English, he is highly valued at the office.
en.notes: Mostly 重宝する (to find handy) or 重宝される (to be in great demand); also 重宝な (handy). With the reading じゅうほう: a precious treasure.

examples[].german: Dogs have sharper hearing than humans.
Hearing impairment remained after the accident.
en.notes: One of the five senses; cf. 視覚 (sight), 嗅覚 (smell), 味覚 (taste), 触覚 (touch).

examples[].german: The head of the Meteorological Agency held a press conference.
The US Secretary of State has arrived in Japan.
en.notes: Head of an agency (庁), e.g. 気象庁長官; also the title for US cabinet secretaries: 国務長官 (Secretary of State).

examples[].german: You need to remove the bones from this fish before cooking it.
The cooking time is about twenty minutes.
en.notes: Matter-of-fact word for cooking/preparing food, as in recipes and occupations: 調理師 (licensed cook), 調理器具 (cooking utensils). As a verb 調理する.

examples[].german: The doctor placed the stethoscope on the chest.
You listen to the heartbeat with a stethoscope.
en.notes: From 聴診 (auscultation) + 器 (instrument).

examples[].german: There is a small temple halfway up the mountain.
Fog set in when we had climbed halfway up.
en.notes: The middle of a slope, usually of a mountain: 山の中腹 (also 丘の中腹).

examples[].german: The gymnast landed a beautiful somersault.
The airplane performed a loop in the sky.
en.notes: A flip in the air (gymnastics) or a loop (aircraft); 後方宙返り (backflip).

examples[].german: In central Tokyo, the daytime population is very large compared with the nighttime population.
While working, he attended not the daytime division of the university but the evening division.
This high school also has a daytime part-time course.
en.notes: The Sino-Japanese reading ちゅうかん appears almost only in official and technical compounds, mostly as the counterpart to 夜間 (やかん): 昼間人口 "daytime population", 昼間部 "daytime division", 昼間定時制. Alone and in everyday speech, 昼間 is always read ひるま (separate card). Do not confuse it with the homophone 中間 "middle".

examples[].german: The soccer match is broadcast on TV.
We'll bring you a live report from the scene.
en.notes: Broadcasting a program, especially live: 生中継 (live broadcast). Also an intermediate stop: 中継地点. As a verb 中継する.

examples[].german: After being kept waiting for a whole hour, he was thoroughly irritated inside.
My father left the room in a huff without saying a word.
en.notes: Refers to anger that one does not show openly but carries around inside; mostly used as 中っ腹になる or 中っ腹で (annoyed, huffy). Somewhat old-fashioned and found mostly in novels; also read ちゅっぱら. In everyday speech people more often say むっとする or 腹が立つ.

examples[].german: A referee must always be neutral.
That country remained neutral during the war.
en.notes: Neutrality of states or persons: 中立を保つ, 中立的な立場. 永世中立国: a permanently neutral state (e.g. Switzerland).

examples[].german: The examination found a fracture in the middle finger of the right hand.
The patient is complaining of pain in the joint of the middle finger.
We will check the middle toe of the left foot on the X-ray.
en.notes: ちゅうし is the Sino-Japanese reading of 中指 and occurs almost only in medicine, anatomy and technical texts, for example in doctors' reports or X-ray findings. In everyday life, 中指 is always read なかゆび (own card); in conversation you should use that reading. 中止 "cancellation" sounds the same, and only the context tells them apart.

examples[].german: I was subjected to baseless slander online.
Remarks that slander others are not acceptable.
en.notes: Damaging someone's reputation with false claims; 誹謗中傷 (slander and abuse, especially online). As a verb 中傷する.

examples[].german: I bought a dozen pencils.
I ordered two dozen eggs.
en.notes: Twelve pieces: 一ダース = 12. Attached directly to the number like a counter. The rare kanji spelling is 打.

examples[].german: The hand-me-down trousers from my older brother are baggy.
From lack of exercise, the flesh on my belly has become flabby.
He pours sauce all over his tonkatsu.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic word, mostly for clothing that is too loose: だぶだぶのズボン, このシャツはだぶだぶだ. With する it describes flabby flesh or sloshing liquid; as an adverb also "generously" when pouring (ソースをだぶだぶかける). ぶかぶか stresses more "too big" (also for shoes), だぼだぼ is a close variant. Mostly in hiragana, ダブダブ for emphasis.

examples[].german: The typhoon dealt a heavy blow to agriculture.
He is a player who is good at batting.
en.notes: Literally a blow, mostly figurative: severe damage (経済的打撃). In baseball: batting (打撃力 hitting power).

examples[].german: Please collect a stool sample for the test.
It is proper etiquette for dog owners to take their dogs' feces home.
en.notes: Neutral, medical word; childish/colloquial うんち. Counterpart: 小便 (urine). Homophone: 代弁.

examples[].german: I conveyed our opinion to the president, speaking for the employees' feelings.
This song speaks for the true feelings of young people.
en.notes: Voicing other people's opinions or feelings in their place; as a verb 代弁する. 代弁者: spokesperson. Homophone: 大便.

examples[].german: The rain ruined our trip.
With one unnecessary remark, I spoiled the lovely atmosphere.
en.notes: Mostly 台無しになる (to be ruined) or 台無しにする (to ruin, to spoil).

en.meaning: to be titled, to bear the title
examples[].german: A lecture titled "The City of the Future" was given.
He wrote a poem titled "Spring".
en.notes: Almost always as 「…」と題する/と題した: "titled ...". Literary.

examples[].german: Both countries are aiming to break the deadlock in the negotiations.
The government put forward measures to overcome the recession.
Bold reforms are needed to break through the current situation.
en.notes: Formal noun for breaking open a stalled situation, typical in politics and economics: 局面の打開, 現状打開, 打開策 "approach to a solution". The verbal use is taught by the separate card 打開する. Unlike 突破 (とっぱ), which means forcibly breaking through or exceeding a mark, 打開 is about a new way out of a dead end.

examples[].german: The protracted wage negotiations finally reached a settlement.
The settlement amount in this year's spring wage talks exceeded last year's.
The two companies continue talks aiming for an early agreement.
en.notes: Formal noun for the successful conclusion of negotiations, especially in wage and trade talks: 交渉が妥結に至る, 早期妥結, 妥結額 "agreed pay raise". The verbal use is taught by the card 妥結する. 妥協 (だきょう) is the mutual giving way itself, 妥結 the resulting outcome; the opposite is 決裂 "breakdown".

examples[].german: The principal stepped up onto the platform and gave a speech.
He made his debut on the literary scene in his twenties.
en.notes: A raised surface for speakers (壇上 on the platform, 教壇 teacher's lectern); as a suffix the professional world: 文壇 (literary world), 画壇 (art world).

examples[].german: He declared, "We will definitely win."
I can't say for certain that it's right.
en.notes: Asserting something with certainty; as a verb 断言する. Often negated: 断言できない.

examples[].german: The whole class pulled together and won the choral competition.
Now more than ever, the nation needs unity.
en.notes: Banding together for a common goal; as a verb 団結する (to stand together).

examples[].german: You can see the annual rings in the cross section of a tree.
This novel depicts one facet of modern society.
en.notes: A cut surface (断面図 cross-section drawing); figuratively a slice or aspect: 社会の一断面.

examples[].german: Dump trucks are constantly going in and out of the construction site.
My father works as a dump truck driver.
en.notes: Short for ダンプカー (dump truck, a Japanese coinage).

examples[].german: It may be superfluous, but let me add one more thing.
The last explanation was perhaps unnecessary.
en.notes: From a Chinese anecdote: in a snake-drawing contest, the one who adds feet to the snake loses. Often used as a modest introduction: 蛇足ですが... ("Just a small, perhaps superfluous addition ...").

en.meaning: to escape, to get out (of a situation), to overcome
examples[].german: The patient has finally passed the danger point.
The economy is gradually emerging from the slump.
en.notes: Literary: to get out of a crisis, danger or phase (危機を脱する). Colloquial: 抜け出す.

examples[].german: He left the labor union last year.
The country announced its withdrawal from the international treaty.
en.notes: Leaving an organization, party, band or treaty; as a verb 脱退する. Opposite: 加入, 加盟.

examples[].german: "It's started to rain." "Then let's go by taxi."
You don't want to go? Then you don't have to come along.
en.notes: Colloquial sentence opener that picks up on what was said. More polite: でしたら; neutral: それなら.

en.meaning: decline, reduction; knockdown (boxing); being laid up (due to illness)
examples[].german: I went down with a cold and stayed in bed for three days.
This month, sales have fallen sharply.
en.notes: A versatile loanword: decline (給料ダウン), a knockdown in boxing, being laid up with illness or exhaustion (風邪でダウン). Opposite: アップ.

examples[].german: A huge building has gone up in front of the station.
Hey, your voice is too loud. Everyone is looking.
en.notes: Colloquial for 大きい, often emphatic: でかい家, 声がでかい (to be loud). Avoid in formal speech.

examples[].german: I have a pimple on my face and don't want to see anyone.
The lump on my back wouldn't heal, so I went to a dermatologist.
en.notes: Everyday word for a swelling or pimple on the skin: 顔に出来物ができる. Often in kana: できもの.

en.meaning: to come out completely; to be fully expressed
examples[].german: In the meeting, a conclusion was drawn only after everyone's opinions had been fully voiced.
Since all the beans in the box had come out, I closed the mouth of the bag.
en.notes: 出切る means that everything comes out or is completely put forward: 意見が出切る means that all opinions have been expressed. The verb describes the process with が; it is an intransitive Godan verb. Its forms are できります, できって and できった. This distinguishes it from 出来る "can, to be made" with できます and できた. The statement refers to complete coming-out, not in general to every form of shortage of goods.

examples[].german: I helped decorate the cake for my daughter's birthday.
The Christmas decorations made the shop look festive.
en.notes: Decoration, especially of cakes and rooms: デコレーションケーキ (decorated cake). More general: 飾り, 装飾.

en.meaning: to run into; to come across
examples[].german: I bumped into an old girlfriend at the station.
If you come across a bear on a mountain trail, don't run away.
en.notes: To meet someone or something unexpectedly, often something unpleasant: 事故に出くわす, 熊に出くわす. More colloquial than 出会う.

examples[].german: Many customers gathered for the demonstration of the new product.
Citizens held a demonstration against nuclear power.
en.notes: In both senses usually shortened to デモ in daily life; the long form is more formal.

examples[].german: A beautiful countryside stretched out outside the window.
I long for a quiet life in the countryside after retirement.
en.notes: Elevated word for rural scenery: 田園風景 (pastoral scenery), 田園都市 (garden city). Everyday: 田舎.

examples[].german: I quit my job, so I'm starting from scratch.
If the person in charge is absent, I'll have to come back another time.
en.notes: To start over from the beginning (一からの出直し) or to come by again later. Verb: 出直す.

examples[].german: Could I leave a message for Mr. Tanaka?
I wrote down my mother's message on a note and left it on the desk.
en.notes: A message that one asks someone to pass on: 伝言をお願いできますか (Could you pass on a message?). 伝言を残す = to leave a message.

examples[].german: The introduction of firearms greatly changed the way war was fought in Japan.
This house has a sword handed down from the ancestors.
en.notes: 1) Introduction from abroad: 仏教の伝来 (the introduction of Buddhism). 2) Handing down through generations: 先祖伝来の刀 (a sword handed down from ancestors).

en.meaning: electric wire; power line; telephone line
examples[].german: Several crows are perched on the power line.
The typhoon snapped the power lines, and the whole town lost power.
en.notes: Especially the overhead lines on poles along streets: 電線にカラスがとまっている. Homophone: 伝染 (contagion).

examples[].german: In art class, we drew a sketch of an apple.
A painter makes many sketches before the actual painting.
en.notes: From French dessin: a preliminary drawing, usually in pencil or charcoal, also as an exercise in art class.

examples[].german: I like the simple design of this smartphone.
She designs and makes her own clothes.
en.notes: Design of products, clothing or graphics; as a verb デザインする. デザイナー = designer.

examples[].german: The schedule says: "Information session on Saturday the tenth."
This shop is open on Saturdays and Sundays too.
en.notes: 土 is, in calendars, schedules and opening hours, the short form of 土曜日, Saturday. After a date, a parenthesis such as （土） gives the day of the week; in 土・日 Saturday and Sunday are listed together. The short form is read ど, the full weekday name どようび. The identically written word 土（つち） for soil has a different meaning and reading here.

examples[].german: My older brother is studying civil engineering at university.
Because of civil engineering works, the road will be closed for a while.
en.notes: Construction of roads, bridges, dams, etc.: 土木工事 (civil engineering works), 土木工学 (civil engineering). Cf. 建築 (building construction, architecture).

en.meaning: foundation; base; (adverb) in the first place
examples[].german: If a house's foundation is solid, it will withstand earthquakes too.
Learning that in one week is impossible in the first place.
en.notes: The foundation of a building; figuratively a basis (成功の土台). As a colloquial adverb "fundamentally, anyway", usually with a negative statement: 土台無理な話だ (impossible from the start).

examples[].german: He is a matter-of-fact person who strictly separates work from private life.
Moisturizing cream is indispensable for dry skin.
en.notes: Literally dry (ドライな肌), but mostly figurative: rational and unsentimental (ドライな性格, ドライに割り切る). Can come across as cold.

examples[].german: We had lunch at a roadside restaurant along the national highway.
On my trip to America, I watched a movie at a drive-in theater for the first time.
en.notes: In Japan usually a roadside stop on national roads with a restaurant and parking lot; on expressways it is called サービスエリア. Also drive-in facilities such as a drive-in theater.

examples[].german: You should take this coat to the dry cleaner's.
I had my suit dry-cleaned.
en.notes: Cleaning with solvents instead of water, e.g. for suits and coats. The shop is called クリーニング屋.

en.meaning: well now, let me see; all right then
examples[].german: Well now, let me see, show me the photo.
"I think I have a fever." "Let me see," said my mother, putting her hand on my forehead.
en.notes: Interjection used when one wants to look at or check something: どれどれ、見せてごらん. Almost always in kana; the spelling 何々 is usually read なになに.

examples[].german: I drilled a hole in the wall with a drill.
My son does one page of a kanji drill book every morning.
en.notes: Tool: 電動ドリル (electric drill). At school: 計算ドリル / 漢字ドリル (practice book for arithmetic / kanji).

en.meaning: local product of a country or region
examples[].german: In the Edo period, silk was an important product of this region.
Old records describe in detail the products of each province.
en.notes: どさん is the Sino-Japanese reading of 土産 and means "product of a country or region"; it appears almost only in historical or very formal texts. In ordinary text, 土産 is always read みやげ "souvenir, gift brought back" (separate card), so you can recognize どさん only from context or reading aids. Today, for regional products people usually say 特産品 or 名産.

examples[].german: In the evening, I took a walk along the river embankment.
There is a danger that the embankment will collapse due to the heavy rain.
en.notes: A raised earthen bank, especially along rivers: 川の土手 (river embankment), where people often take walks.

examples[].german: This dog has a long body and short legs.
Lately my waistline has been getting bigger.
en.notes: The body without head and limbs: 胴が長い. 胴回り = waist or girth measurement. In kendo, also the chest protector.

examples[].german: If you only go along with the opinions around you, you can't grow.
We discussed the pressure to conform in Japanese society.
en.notes: To fall in line with others' opinions or behavior: 〜に同調する; 同調圧力 (peer pressure, pressure to conform).

examples[].german: He gave a confident speech in front of everyone.
You haven't done anything wrong, so you can hold your head high.
en.notes: As 堂々と (confidently, without hiding) or 堂々たる / 堂々とした (imposing, magnificent). Cf. 正々堂々 (fair and square).

examples[].german: Please enclose a photo with your résumé.
Please fill in the enclosed form and send it back.
en.notes: Putting something into a letter or package: 写真を同封する; in business letters: 資料を同封いたします (I am enclosing the materials).

examples[].german: More than a hundred police officers were mobilized for the search.
The film drew a large audience in the month after its release.
en.notes: Gathering people or resources for a purpose: 警官を動員する; 観客動員数 (attendance figures). Historically also military mobilization.

examples[].german: He and I were in the same class in elementary school.
I was invited to a former classmate's wedding.
en.notes: Mostly in 同級生 (classmate, schoolmate of the same year). On its own, e.g.: 彼とは同級だった (we were in the same class).

examples[].german: I just barely made the last train.
Isn't there something that can be done about this problem?
en.notes: Barely, just about: どうにか間に合った (just made it). どうにかする (to do something about it), どうにかなる (it will work out somehow). Similar: なんとか.

examples[].german: This ship moves using the wind as its power source.
In factories of the past, the water wheel was used as motive power.
en.notes: Power that drives machines: 動力源 (power source). Also figuratively a driving force.

examples[].german: They are like-minded people who share the same dream.
We are recruiting people to join our environmental protection activities.
en.notes: People with the same goals or convictions: 同志を募る (to recruit comrades). In political movements, "comrade". Homophone: 同士 (among each other).

examples[].german: Since we're neighbors, we often eat together.
Please form groups with people you like.
en.notes: Mostly a suffix: 友達同士 (among friends), 男同士 (among men), 似た者同士 (two of a kind). Homophones: 同志 (comrade), 動詞 (verb).

examples[].german: In sports photography, it is important to capture the athletes' dynamic moments.
We need to see society not as static but as dynamic.
en.notes: Technical and elevated; opposite: 静的 (static). 動的なウェブページ (dynamic web page).

en.meaning: momentary lapse of memory; blanking out
examples[].german: Even though I know the person well, I blanked on their name.
I was so nervous that I blanked, and my own phone number wouldn't come to me.
en.notes: Mostly ど忘れする: something you actually know well suddenly won't come to mind. Also written 度忘れ.

en.meaning: layer; fold (counter with native Japanese number forms)
examples[].german: Because it was cold, I slept with the blanket doubled.
The cherry trees in the garden have single-petaled blossoms and double-petaled blossoms.
en.notes: 重（え）counts layers with the native Japanese number forms: 一重（ひとえ）、二重（ふたえ）、三重（みえ）. For fabrics, 二重に重ねる describes two layers lying on top of each other; for flowers, 八重（やえ）denotes many layers of petals. The reading え cannot simply be attached to arbitrary Sino-Japanese numbers.

examples[].german: The monks held a service at the temple and prayed for the deceased.
An old record says that villagers gathered at the festival gathering.
en.notes: The reading え belongs mainly to older texts about Buddhist ceremonies or festivals. 会を設ける there means holding a gathering. A present-day meeting or club is usually 会（かい）; for "understanding", this independent reading え is not suitable.

examples[].german: A ray was swimming leisurely in the large tank at the aquarium.
In the shallows, be careful not to be stung by the barb on a ray's tail.
At the izakaya, I drank beer with dried ray fin as a snack.
en.notes: Animal names such as エイ "ray" are mostly written in katakana, just like サメ "shark" (separate card); the kanji 鱝, 鱏 or 海鷂魚 are rare and hardly used anymore. Well known is エイヒレ, dried ray fin eaten as a snack with beer. It sounds the same as the pronunciation of the letter A (エイ/エー), but context always makes it clear.

examples[].german: Every morning I read an English-language newspaper to study English.
Please combine letters and numbers in your password.
en.notes: Letters of the Latin alphabet, often in 英字新聞 (English-language newspaper).

examples[].german: We screened an old film with an old projector.
When the screening started, the hall fell quiet.
en.notes: Projecting films or images: 映写機 (projector), 映写室 (projection room).

examples[].german: Liquid is leaking from the container.
Dilute this liquid ten times with water before use.
en.notes: Liquid, often in compounds: 消毒液 (disinfectant), 血液 (blood). Homophone: 駅.

examples[].german: In class, we looked into why the Bunroku Campaign began.
After the Keicho Campaign, relations between the two countries gradually changed.
en.notes: 役（えき）appears especially in historical war names such as 文禄の役 and 慶長の役. の links the name with 役; an everyday "task" or a theater role, by contrast, is 役（やく）. For a present-day war, 戦争 is the usual general term.

examples[].german: The two dancers on the stage were competing in their respective charms.
Her alluring figure captivated the audience of the old film.
en.notes: 艶（えん）sounds literary and describes alluring, often sensuous beauty. As a noun it can appear in 艶を競う; as a な-adjective it connects to a noun, for example 艶な姿. The gloss of a surface is usually expressed with the other reading 艶（つや）.

en.meaning: fate-linked bond; connection; opportunity to get acquainted
examples[].german: That we met again on a trip must be some kind of destiny.
My father worked there, so I also have a connection to this town.
At this gathering, I was fortunate to make a good acquaintance.
en.notes: 縁（えん）can mean a fateful encounter or the bond between people. 何かの縁ですね judges an encounter to be a kind of destiny; 縁がある says that there is a connection or contact with someone or something. ご縁 adds the polite prefix ご. When getting acquainted, 縁 means an occasion from which a relationship arises, not just any chance. 縁（ふち）meaning edge has a different reading.

examples[].german: When an acid reacts with a base, a salt may form.
In the experiment, we extracted crystals of a salt dissolved in water.
en.notes: In chemistry, 塩（えん）denotes a class of substances that includes, for example, sodium chloride and calcium sulfate. So it is not only about edible table salt. For food, 塩 is usually read しお; in a chemical context, 塩の結晶 and 塩が生成する can have the reading えん.

examples[].german: The traveler sat down in the shade of the trees in the garden.
When this garden was built, a promenade was laid out around the pond.
en.notes: As an independent word, 園（えん）is a rare, rather literary term for a landscaped garden or park. In a description, 園の木陰 or 園を歩く may appear. In everyday use 庭園 or 公園 are clearer; the meaning learned here does not refer to an abbreviated kindergarten facility.

examples[].german: At this orchard, apples are harvested in autumn.
If you're going to the station, cutting through the park is a shortcut.
en.notes: The ending 園（えん）denotes a landscaped area in compounds: 農園 is an agricultural operation with cultivated land, 公園 a public park. The particle stands after the whole word, for example 農園で or 公園を. As an ending, 園 is attached directly to the preceding part of the word.

examples[].german: My older brother works as an engineer at an IT company.
This engineer designed the new machine.
en.notes: Often used for IT professionals: システムエンジニア (SE). More formal: 技術者.

en.meaning: to play (a role); to commit (a blunder)
examples[].german: She played the role of a doctor in the film.
He made a blunder at an important meeting.
en.notes: To play a role: 主役を演じる. Figuratively "to make a blunder": 失態を演じる. Literary variant: 演ずる (N3).

examples[].german: She turned down the invitation in a roundabout, polite way.
Japanese has many indirect ways of saying things.
en.notes: な-adjective: to express something politely and indirectly: 婉曲に断る (to decline indirectly), 婉曲な言い方 (a roundabout way of putting it).

examples[].german: Thank you for coming from so far away.
My grandmother lives far away, so I rarely get to see her.
en.notes: Formal: 遠方から (from far away), 遠方に住む (to live far away). More everyday: 遠く.

examples[].german: The staging of this play was very innovative.
I left the arrangements for the wedding to a friend.
en.notes: As a verb 演出する: to stage a play, film or event. The person is called 演出家 (director, especially in theater).

examples[].german: She always wears elegant clothes.
The hotel lobby was very elegant.
en.notes: な-adjective: エレガントなドレス. Somewhat more refined than 上品.

examples[].german: The collar of the shirt is dirty.
Because it was cold, I turned up my coat collar.
en.notes: Collar of a garment. Idiom: 襟を正す (to straighten up, to adopt a serious attitude).

examples[].german: The fighting spirit of never giving up until the end led to victory.
I called out "Fight!" to my friend before her exam.
en.notes: As a cheer: ファイト！ (Let's go!, You can do it!). ファイトがある = to have fighting spirit. Also "fight" in boxing.

examples[].german: We ran out of coffee filters, so I went to buy some.
Applying a filter to a photo changes its mood.
en.notes: Coffee, air, or camera filter; also image filters in apps: フィルターをかける (to apply a filter).

examples[].german: The coach corrected my batting form.
Please send inquiries via the form on our website.
en.notes: Mainly body posture and technique in sports: 投球フォーム (pitching form). In IT: 入力フォーム (input form). Same spelling: フォーム (foam, e.g. シェービングフォーム).

examples[].german: First, he advanced one pawn one square.
He dropped the captured pawn onto the board as his own piece.
When a pawn enters the enemy camp, it can promote to a tokin.
en.notes: Short form of 歩兵 (ふひょう), the weakest shogi piece, which moves only one square forward and is promoted to と金 in the enemy camp. Phrases: 歩を突く "to advance a pawn", 歩を打つ "to drop a captured pawn". In Western chess, ポーン is said more. Same spelling as 歩/ほ "step" (separate card), but a different reading.

examples[].german: I felt pity for the small child living apart from his family.
A neighbor took in the pitiable dog that its owner had abandoned.
en.notes: 不憫（ふびん）describes someone whose situation arouses pity. With 不憫に思う you say that you feel sorry for someone; before a noun it takes な. The rare older writing 不便 can also be read ふびん. Today, however, 不便 is usually read ふべん and means "inconvenient, awkward", so 不憫 is clearer for this meaning.

examples[].german: The departure of the plane was delayed due to engine trouble.
That player has been in a slump the whole season.
en.notes: 体の不調 (physical ailments), エンジンの不調 (engine trouble), 交渉が不調に終わる (negotiations fail). Opposite: 好調.

examples[].german: He listened to the teacher with a dissatisfied look.
The defendant did not accept the verdict and filed an appeal.
en.notes: 不服そうな顔 (dissatisfied look). Legal: 判決を不服として控訴する (to appeal against a verdict).

examples[].german: The wealthy man donated much of his fortune to charities.
He succeeded in business and became rich within a single generation.
en.notes: 大富豪 (multimillionaire). More everyday: 金持ち. Similar sound: 符号 (sign, code).

examples[].german: The new design was unpopular among customers.
The price increase met with disapproval from users.
en.notes: 不評を買う (to meet with disapproval), 〜は不評だ (is poorly received). Opposite: 好評.

examples[].german: I was startled when someone suddenly called my name from behind.
The opposing team attacked, catching us off guard.
en.notes: Mostly 不意に (suddenly) or 不意を突く / 不意を打つ (to take by surprise): 不意を突かれる = to be taken by surprise.

examples[].german: The weather was unsettled this summer, and vegetable prices rose.
The weather tends to be unsettled at the change of seasons.
en.notes: Mainly 天候不順 (unsettled weather) and 生理不順 (irregular periods). Similar sound: 不純 (impure).

en.meaning: to age, grow old (especially in appearance)
examples[].german: My father has aged a lot in the past few years.
He looks older than his age.
en.notes: Especially in appearance: 年の割に老けて見える (to look older than one's age). Same sound: 更ける (night: to grow late), 耽る (to indulge).

en.meaning: to indulge in, be absorbed in
examples[].german: On days off, I spend the whole day absorbed in reading.
She was lost in thought, looking out the window.
en.notes: Mostly 〜に耽る, often in kana ふける: 読書に耽る (to be absorbed in reading), 物思いに耽る (to be lost in thought). Also slightly negative: 遊びに耽る (to indulge in pleasures).

examples[].german: After fifty years, the town's traditional festival was revived.
The athlete who came back from an injury won a brilliant victory.
en.notes: 復活する = to come back to life, to return: 古い祭りが復活する (an old festival is revived). Religious: キリストの復活 (the resurrection of Christ).

examples[].german: At Setsubun, people scatter beans while saying "Demons out, good fortune in!"
They say good fortune comes to those who laugh, so let's always smile.
en.notes: Mainly in fixed phrases: 鬼は外、福は内 (the call when throwing beans at 節分), 笑う門には福来たる (good fortune comes to the house that laughs). General: 幸せ, 幸運.

examples[].german: Several causes combined, and the accident occurred.
A complex housing a cinema and shops has been built in front of the station.
en.notes: Often as a first element: 複合語 (compound word), 複合施設 (multi-use complex). 複合する = to combine, to merge.

examples[].german: She sent a letter to her distant lover.
A love letter from my grandmother was found in an old box.
The nobles of the Heian period exchanged letters with poems attached.
en.notes: Elevated, literary word for "letter, message" and "writings, books"; in everyday speech 手紙 is said. It lives on in compounds such as 恋文 (こいぶみ) "love letter". Same spelling as 文/ぶん "sentence, text" (separate card): ぶん is the neutral word for sentences and texts, ふみ belongs to poetic or archaic style.

examples[].german: This dish uses plenty of seasonal vegetables.
The windows are large, and plenty of light enters the room.
en.notes: Mostly adverbial as ふんだんに: 材料をふんだんに使う (to use ingredients lavishly).

examples[].german: This medicine is a powder; please dissolve it in water before drinking.
I ground green tea into powder and mixed it into the sweets.
en.notes: 粉末状 (powdery), 粉末ジュース (powdered drink mix). More everyday: 粉.

examples[].german: I struggle every day with the unfamiliar task of raising a child.
Despite the players' strenuous efforts, the team lost.
en.notes: 奮闘する (to exert oneself to the utmost), 孤軍奮闘 (to fight all alone).

en.meaning: unsteady, staggering, dizzy; indecisive, wavering; aimlessly (wander about)
examples[].german: I have a fever and my head is spinning.
I had nothing to do, so I wandered aimlessly around the station.
He is always wavering in his thinking and cannot make up his mind.
en.notes: Mimetic word for unsteady swaying, mostly used with する or だ: 熱でふらふらする "to reel from a fever", 疲れてふらふらだ "to be completely exhausted". With と it also means "to wander around aimlessly" (ふらふらと歩き回る) or, figuratively, "to be indecisive". Unlike ぐらぐら (objects wobbling), ふらふら describes mainly people and their gait or attitude.

examples[].german: The negotiations broke down, and we were back to square one.
In sugoroku, I landed on the "Back to start" square.
en.notes: Mainly 振り出しに戻る (to start again from zero; like "back to start" in a board game). In banking also: issuance (of a bill).

examples[].german: As a child I always looked forward to the freebies that came with magazines.
The detailed data is in the book's appendix.
en.notes: A supplement to magazines (e.g. small gifts in children's magazines) or an appendix of a book: 巻末付録.

examples[].german: She was crying with her shoulders shaking.
He protested, his voice trembling with anger.
en.notes: Transitive: 声を震わせる (to speak with a trembling voice), 肩を震わせて泣く (to cry with shaking shoulders). Intransitive: 震える.

examples[].german: Seawater has more buoyancy than fresh water, so the body floats more easily.
A ship floats on water thanks to buoyancy.
en.notes: Physics: 浮力が働く (buoyancy acts). Related: 浮く (to float).

examples[].german: If you find a suspicious package, please tell the station staff.
In the middle of the night, a suspicious person was loitering in front of the house.
My mother found what the caller said suspicious.
en.notes: Denotes something that seems strange or suspicious; also as a na-adjective (不審な荷物) and in 不審者 "suspicious person", 挙動不審 "suspicious behavior", 不審に思う "to find strange". Two homophones: 不信 "distrust" is directed against a person or institution (不信感), 不振 "slump, weakness" concerns performance or business (食欲不振).

examples[].german: Three people were injured in this accident.
He injured his leg during the match and left the field midway.
en.notes: Formal, mainly in news: 負傷する (to be injured), 負傷者 (injured person). Everyday: けが.

examples[].german: He complained that the company had treated him unfairly.
This price is unreasonably high compared to the quality.
en.notes: na-adjective: 不当な扱い (unfair treatment), 不当解雇 (unjustified dismissal). Opposite: 正当.

en.meaning: France (abbr.), French (mainly in newspapers and compounds: 日仏, 仏語, 仏大統領)
examples[].german: The Japan-France summit meeting was held in Tokyo.
The French president came to Japan for a three-day visit.
She majors in French literature at university.
en.notes: 仏 with the reading ふつ is the short form of 仏蘭西 and stands for "France" or "French", almost only in headlines, tables and compounds such as 日仏, 英仏, 仏語 or 仏文学. In spoken everyday language, フランス is always used. The same kanji with the reading ほとけ (separate card) is a completely different word: "Buddha" or "the deceased".

en.meaning: seal, closure (of a letter or package)
examples[].german: After finishing the letter, I sealed the envelope.
Unopened goods can be returned.
en.notes: 封をする (to seal), 封を切る / 封を開ける (to open, break the seal). Envelope: 封筒.

en.meaning: natural features, climate and landscape (of a region)
examples[].german: The natural conditions of this region are well suited to rice cultivation.
A unique culture developed under the harsh natural conditions.
en.notes: Climate, soil, and landscape as living conditions: 日本の風土に合った家 (a house suited to Japan's climate). Figuratively also 企業風土 (corporate culture).

en.meaning: manners and customs, way of life (of an era)
examples[].german: This picture depicts the way of life of the common people in the Edo period.
The customs of an era show in its clothing and speech.
en.notes: E.g. 江戸時代の風俗 (way of life in the Edo period), 風俗画 (genre painting). Note: on its own, 風俗 in present-day everyday use is often a euphemism for the sex trade; for customs, 風習 is also used neutrally.

examples[].german: The person in charge is currently away.
A package arrived while I was out.
en.notes: Formal: 不在にしております (is currently away). 不在通知 / 不在票 = notice card left when a delivery is made in one's absence.

en.meaning: stocky, robust; firm, tight; shrewd, calculating
examples[].german: He has a sturdy build, just as you'd expect of a rugby player.
The two exchanged a firm handshake.
The company made a good profit in the year-end sales season.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic word for something robust and firmly put together: がっちりした体格 "strong build", がっちり握手する "to shake hands firmly", がっちり守る "to defend tightly". Unlike がっしり, it additionally has the colloquial meaning "shrewd in business, calculating" (がっちり稼ぐ "to make good money", がっちりした人 "a calculating person"). Often also written in katakana ガッチリ.

examples[].german: I exchanged yen for foreign currency at the airport.
Tourism is an important earner of foreign currency for the country.
en.notes: 外貨を稼ぐ (to earn foreign currency), 外貨預金 (foreign-currency deposit).

examples[].german: In the first class, I will give an overview of this field.
At the beginning of the report there is an outline of the plan.
en.notes: Often in book titles: 日本史概説 (Outline of Japanese History). As a verb 概説する.

examples[].german: The foreign ministers of the two countries held talks in Tokyo.
The new foreign minister visited the United States right after taking office.
en.notes: Short form used in the news for 外務大臣.

en.meaning: to harm; to impair; to offend
examples[].german: I damaged my health by working too much.
My remark seems to have put him in a bad mood.
en.notes: Literary: 健康を害する (to harm one's health), 気分を害する (to offend someone; to be offended).

examples[].german: With the election approaching, candidates are giving speeches on the street.
In front of the station, we appealed for donations on the street.
en.notes: 街頭で (out on the street): 街頭演説 (street speech), 街頭インタビュー (street interview). Homophone: 街灯 (street lamp).

examples[].german: At the news that he had failed, he slumped his shoulders in disappointment.
After losing the match, the players were dejected.
en.notes: With する or と: がっくりする, がっくりと肩を落とす (to slump one's shoulders in disappointment). Similar: がっかり.

examples[].german: This material gives the acceleration of the earthquake in gal.
The acceleration measured in the experiment was one hundred gal, that is, one meter per second squared.
en.notes: ガル is the unit of acceleration, the gal. One gal equals one centimeter per second squared (1 cm/s²). The unit appears, for example, in measurements of gravitational acceleration or of the acceleration of earthquake motion. A number stands directly before it: 百ガル. A gal value is not a magnitude and cannot be converted into a Japanese seismic intensity level 震度 without further information. The similar-sounding がる, a verb-forming suffix, belongs to a different entry.

examples[].german: With these glasses, it is hard to read distant letters.
The lenses of the new glasses are lighter than the previous ones.
en.notes: 眼鏡 is read がんきょう here and means eyeglasses. The usual everyday reading is めがね; がんきょう appears in technical terms such as 眼鏡店 and in older descriptions. Both readings can refer to the same vision aid. This card practices the actual object, not the figurative sense of judgment in 人を見る眼鏡. In がんきょう, きょ and the following う form the long sound kyō; you do not pronounce four separate syllables.

en.meaning: first year (of an era); inaugural year
examples[].german: My daughter was born in the first year of Reiwa.
This year will probably be the first year of a new era for this industry.
en.notes: The first year of a Japanese era: 令和元年 (2019). Figuratively the year something begins: 電気自動車元年 (the first year of electric cars).

examples[].german: The rocks in this region were formed by volcanic activity.
The probe brought back rock from the moon.
en.notes: Technical word for rock (geology); in everyday speech usually 岩 (boulder) or 石 (stone).

examples[].german: I submitted my application for admission to the university.
The deadline for the application is next Friday.
en.notes: A written application, especially the application to a school or university: 願書を出す (to apply).

examples[].german: The receipt had only the month and day written on it.
Please don't forget to fill in the date field on the application form.
en.notes: Mainly on forms and in documents. Read つきひ, 月日 means "the time that passes".

en.meaning: sturdy, stocky, solidly built; firmly (がっしりした体)
examples[].german: He has a sturdy build.
This desk is old, but it is solidly built and durable.
My father gripped my hand firmly.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic word for a strong, broad physique or a heavy, solid construction; mostly as がっしりした + noun (がっしりした体格) or がっしりしている. With と as an adverb it describes a firm grip (がっしりと握る). The similar がっちり also means "robust, firm", but can additionally mean "shrewd in business, calculating"; がっしり emphasizes more the massive, stable build.

examples[].german: That rakugo storyteller has honed his craft for many years.
Our dog can do simple tricks.
en.notes: Skill acquired through practice, especially in entertainment and the performing arts: 芸を磨く, 犬に芸を教える. Proverb: 芸は身を助ける.

en.meaning: original, primordial, raw, proto- (prefix, e.g. 原材料, 原日本人)
examples[].german: Because of rising raw material prices, the prices of goods have also gone up.
I want to read the original work, not a translation.
There are various theories about the origin of the proto-Japanese.
en.notes: Prefix meaning "original, primordial, raw": 原材料 "raw materials", 原作 "original work", 原文 "original text", 原日本人 "proto-Japanese". Do not confuse it with the identically sounding prefix 現〜 "current" (現会長 "the current chairman"): 原〜 points to the origin, 現〜 to the present state. Read on its own, 原 means はら "field, plain" (separate card).

en.meaning: the actual site; on the spot; local
examples[].german: A reporter is reporting live from the scene.
When traveling, I want to eat the local food.
en.notes: The actual place where something happens or that one visits: 現地時間 (local time), 現地の人 (locals).

examples[].german: The car in the accident was no longer recognizable.
What is the base form of this verb?
en.notes: The original shape of something (原形をとどめない = to be unrecognizable) and, in grammar, the base form of a word. Homophone: 原型 (prototype, model).

examples[].german: Under the current system, this application is not possible.
The current fees will remain unchanged until April next year.
en.notes: What is currently in force or in use: 現行の制度 (current system), 現行法 (current law). Homophone: 原稿 (manuscript).

examples[].german: In a democracy, freedom of speech must be protected.
One should resist with words, not with violence.
en.notes: Public expression of opinions in speech and writing; mainly in 言論の自由 (freedom of speech).

examples[].german: I wrote a kanji wrong and lost two points.
I lost points for a false start.
en.notes: Deduction of points in exams, competitions or evaluations; as a verb 減点する. Homophone: 原点.

examples[].german: When we get stuck, let's go back to the starting point and think again.
The origin of a graph is the point where the two axes cross.
en.notes: The original starting point (原点に戻る = to return to one's roots) and, in mathematics, the coordinate origin.

examples[].german: I took my trip photos in for developing.
In the old days, it took a few days to develop photos.
en.notes: The developing of photographic film; as a verb 現像する. In digital photography also the processing of RAW files.

examples[].german: I bought the car in monthly installments over three years.
I haven't paid this month's installment yet.
en.notes: Payment in monthly installments: 月賦で買う (to buy on installments). Today often ローン or 分割払い. Homophone: げっぷ (burp).

examples[].german: Piano lessons cost 8,000 yen a month.
I put the monthly tuition in an envelope and handed it to the teacher.
en.notes: Monthly fee for private lessons, tutoring or courses (piano, dance, juku).

examples[].german: After his illness, he became gaunt and thin.
I was discouraged when I saw the mountain of homework.
en.notes: Describes someone who has lost a lot of weight (げっそり痩せる) or is completely disheartened (話を聞いてげっそりする).

en.meaning: guest (on a show or at an event)
examples[].german: Today's guest on the program is a famous author.
Guests from overseas were invited to the event.
en.notes: An invited guest on TV, radio, or at events: ゲスト出演 (guest appearance). A guest in one's own home is called 客 or お客さん.

examples[].german: On the school trip we toured the National Diet Building.
Demonstrators had gathered in front of the parliament building.
en.notes: The assembly building of a parliament; in Japan especially the 国会議事堂 in Tokyo.

examples[].german: Suspicions over political donations surfaced regarding the minister.
He desperately tried to clear the suspicions against him.
en.notes: Suspicion of wrongdoing, especially in politics and the press: 汚職疑惑, 疑惑を晴らす (to clear suspicion).

examples[].german: The president was surrounded by many bodyguards.
The police escorted the team bus.
en.notes: To accompany and protect people or transports; also the guards themselves. As a verb 護衛する.

examples[].german: Please look up words and phrases you don't know in a dictionary.
Please enter the words you want to search for.
en.notes: Words and expressions in a text: 語句の意味を調べる (to look up the meaning of words and phrases). Homophone: ごく (extremely).

examples[].german: Look, look out the window. It's snowing.
Think about it once more by yourself.
en.notes: A gentle request from an older person to a younger one: "Look!" After the て-form: 〜てご覧なさい (try doing ...). Shorter: ご覧.

examples[].german: When the air-raid siren sounded, people fled into the air-raid shelter.
The soldiers hid in the trench.
In the Yayoi period, moated settlements surrounded by a ditch were built.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 濠/壕 "ditch": 濠 refers more to a water-filled castle moat, 壕 to a dug-out trench or shelter, e.g. 塹壕 "trench" and 防空壕 "air-raid shelter". Standing alone, 濠 is mostly read ほり (card 堀/ほり); ごう appears mainly in compounds such as 環濠 and in texts about war and fortification. Do not confuse it with 業/ごう "karma" or 号/ごう "number".

examples[].german: This matter will be decided by joint deliberation of the committee members.
Three judges deliberated together and delivered the verdict.
en.notes: Deliberation by several people to decide together: 合議制 (collegiate system), 合議の上で決める (to decide after joint deliberation).

examples[].german: Spending a million yen in one evening is quite a tremendous thing.
Paying all employees a double bonus - the president really is generous, isn't he?
Magnificent festival floats paraded through the town.
en.notes: Colloquial, somewhat old-fashioned na-adjective for "magnificent, tremendous, splendid", often admiring or slightly ironic about generous, lavish deeds (豪儀な話, 豪儀なものだ). Written 豪儀, 豪気 or 強気; the spelling 強気 is easily confused with 強気/つよき "confident, bold" (separate card), which is a different word. It shares only the sound with 合議/ごうぎ "consultation".

examples[].german: Her grades stand out far above the rest of the class.
In math class we learned the definition of a group.
en.notes: A set of similar things; used almost only in the phrase 群を抜く (to stand out) and as a mathematical term. Homophones: 軍, 郡.

examples[].german: Countries are building up their armaments.
Reducing armaments was discussed at the conference.
en.notes: A state's military equipment: 軍備を増強する (to build up arms), 軍備縮小 (arms reduction).

examples[].german: Military tension is rising between the two countries.
He is a journalist who knows a lot about military matters.
en.notes: Everything concerning the military: 軍事力 (military power), 軍事基地 (military base).

examples[].german: There is still a photo of my grandfather in his youth in military uniform.
Old military uniforms were prepared for the film shoot.
en.notes: The uniform of soldiers.

examples[].german: I tried putting the change in sales into a graph.
Looking at this graph, you can see that the population is decreasing.
en.notes: Graphic representation of numbers: 棒グラフ (bar chart), 円グラフ (pie chart), 折れ線グラフ (line graph).

examples[].german: I went to the interview wearing a gray suit.
That method is said to be legally gray.
en.notes: The color gray (also 灰色). Figuratively: グレーゾーン (gray area).

en.meaning: firmly; with force; much more; deeply (moved)
examples[].german: With repeated practice, his playing has improved markedly.
Reading that letter, I was deeply moved.
en.notes: Several uses: with a jerk or firmly (ぐっと引く), considerably more (ぐっと良くなる), deeply moved (胸にぐっと来る).

examples[].german: We turned the game around in the last minute and won.
In this experiment the rotation of the motor is reversed.
en.notes: A situation turns around, especially in sports: 逆転勝ち (comeback win), 形勢が逆転する.

examples[].german: This jade glows a deep green when polished.
The craftsman carved a small jade stone and made it into an ornament for an obi.
Check the squares where your king can escape.
Before chasing the opponent's king, I think about the safety of my own king.
en.notes: 玉（ぎょく）means a precious stone, especially jade, and in shogi the king piece. In the game it is a short form of 玉将（ぎょくしょう）; for a piece of jewelry, the context decides the gemstone meaning. The usual reading たま for a ball or sphere cannot be used here.

examples[].german: I spent the summer vacation in a small fishing village.
In that fishing village, boats put out from early in the morning.
en.notes: A village whose inhabitants live mainly from fishing. Compare 農村 (farming village).

examples[].german: The blade of the kitchen knife has chipped.
Please be careful not to touch the blade.
en.notes: 包丁の刃 (knife blade), 刃が欠ける (the blade gets chipped). Not to be confused with 歯 (tooth) and 葉 (leaf), which have the same reading.

examples[].german: The meeting split into two factions, and the debate continued.
Monet is a leading painter of Impressionism.
en.notes: Free-standing e.g. in 二つの派に分かれる (to split into two camps). Very common as a suffix: 賛成派 / 反対派 (supporters / opponents), 印象派 (Impressionism).

en.meaning: to peel off, to come off; to fade
examples[].german: The paint on the old wall is peeling off in many places.
I've washed the shirt so many times that the print has started to come off.
en.notes: Intransitive counterpart of 剥ぐ: ペンキが剥げる (the paint peels off). Figuratively: 化けの皮が剥げる (the mask falls off). Not to be confused with 禿げる (to go bald), which has the same reading.

en.meaning: to tear off, to peel off, to strip
examples[].german: I tore the old posters off the wall.
With practiced hands, the hunter skinned the deer.
en.notes: Transitive: 皮を剥ぐ (to strip off the skin), ポスターを剥ぐ. Figuratively also 地位を剥ぐ (to strip someone of rank). Intransitive counterpart: 剥げる.

en.meaning: Dear Sir or Madam (formal letter salutation)
examples[].german: A letter begins with "Haikei" and ends with "Keigu".
Dear Sir or Madam, in this warm spring season, we are pleased that you continue to thrive.
en.notes: Formal opening phrase of a letter; the corresponding closing phrase is 敬具. A seasonal greeting usually follows. Not to be confused with 背景 (background), which has the same reading.

examples[].german: On this keyboard, the key layout is different from usual.
In the program, the data is stored in an array.
en.notes: In general: キーの配列 (key layout), 五十音順に配列する (to arrange in Japanese syllabary order). In computing: 配列 = array.

examples[].german: After the defeat in the war, Japan suffered from a severe food shortage.
The manager took responsibility for the defeat and resigned.
en.notes: Historically mainly Japan's defeat in the war in 1945: 敗戦後の日本. Also in sports: 敗戦の責任 (responsibility for the defeat).

examples[].german: Excuse me, may I borrow your pen?
On this matter, I would like to ask for everyone's advice.
en.notes: Humble form of 借りる: 拝借する. Polite request: お知恵を拝借したい (I would like to ask for your advice).

en.meaning: to flick, to snap away; to repel, to make bead off
examples[].german: When I flicked the marble with my finger, it rolled to the edge of the desk.
This fabric repels water well, so it is used for rain gear.
en.notes: はじく means to hit or snap something away with a quick spring-like motion, for example flicking a marble with a finger. The moved object takes を. With a material, 水をはじく means that it repels water or makes it bead off. The transitive Godan verb forms はじきます, はじいて and はじいた. For playing piano or guitar, 弾く／ひく is the usual reading; this card practices flicking and repelling.

en.meaning: to be bashful, to blush shyly
examples[].german: The girl hid shyly behind her mother.
Praised, she looked down bashfully.
en.notes: Intransitive, rather literary: 恥じらうように (bashfully). Noun: 恥じらい (shyness, bashfulness).

en.meaning: to plan, to attempt; to strive for, to work toward
examples[].german: The government is trying to bring about an economic recovery.
The two companies tried to resolve the problem through talks.
en.notes: Transitive, mostly with abstract nouns: 解決を図る (to seek a solution), 便宜を図る (to show accommodation). Other はかる: 測る (to measure), 量る (to weigh), 計る (to time).

examples[].german: The culprit finally confessed everything.
To be honest, I haven't finished my homework yet.
en.notes: Mostly 白状する (to confess): 罪を白状する. Also everyday: 正直に白状すると (to be honest, I have to confess). Not to be confused with 薄情 (heartless), which has the same reading.

examples[].german: Early in the morning, I took a walk on the beach.
Fishermen are drying their nets on the beach.
en.notes: A sandy shore by the sea; 浜辺 and 海岸 are more everyday. Common in place names (横浜).

examples[].german: This dictionary has gone through many editions and is still used by many people today.
The new edition corrects the errors of the old one.
en.notes: Also as a counter: 第3版 (3rd edition). 最新版 (latest version), 日本語版 (Japanese edition). 版を重ねる = to go through many editions.

examples[].german: The students split into five groups and explored the town.
I prepared the presentation together with the people in my group.
en.notes: A small working group at school, work, or in administration: 班に分かれる (to split into groups), 班長 (group leader). As a suffix: 救護班 (rescue squad).

examples[].german: Please put your seal on the document here.
Before stamping the contract, I checked its contents carefully.
en.notes: 判を押す = to stamp, to confirm with a name seal; colloquially はんこ. Idiom: 判で押したような (always the same, stereotyped). With the reading ばん, 判 stands for paper sizes (A4判).

examples[].german: The wind blew, and cherry blossom petals fluttered down.
Petals are floating on the surface of the pond.
en.notes: 桜の花びら (cherry blossom petals), 花びらが散る (petals fall). The spelling 花弁 is also read はなびら or, in technical contexts, かべん.

examples[].german: Please hang your coat on a hanger.
I dried the shirts hanging on the hangers.
en.notes: Clothes hanger (from English hanger). Pronounced the same but separate words: ハンガー "aircraft hangar" and ハンガー "hunger" (in ハンガーストライキ, hunger strike).

examples[].german: In the second half, the opposing team began its counterattack.
He immediately hit back against the harsh criticism.
en.notes: 反撃する = to strike back; also in sports and debates: 反撃に出る (to go on the counterattack).

examples[].german: You can't keep up this job with a half-hearted attitude.
Today's heat is insane.
en.notes: As a na-adjective: 半端な気持ち (half-hearted attitude); intensified as 中途半端. Colloquially 半端じゃない (also ハンパない) = unbelievable, insane.

examples[].german: Peasants suffering under heavy taxes rose in revolt.
The revolt was suppressed within a few days.
en.notes: 反乱を起こす (to start a revolt), 反乱軍 (rebel army). Similar sound: 氾濫 (flood).

en.meaning: to be contrary to, violate; contrary to
examples[].german: Using other people's works without permission violates the law.
Contrary to most expectations, a newcomer won the award.
en.notes: Written style, mostly 〜に反する / 〜に反して: 規則に反する (to violate the rules), 予想に反して (contrary to expectations; also a grammar pattern 〜に反して).

examples[].german: I slammed the door in anger.
I couldn't suppress my anger at his rude attitude.
en.notes: Noun of 腹が立つ (to get angry). Common in 腹立ちまぎれに (in anger, in a fit of rage).

en.meaning: anxious, nervous, in suspense (ハラハラする); (leaves, tears) falling softly, fluttering down
examples[].german: The game kept us on the edge of our seats until the very end.
The mother watched her child climbing the tree with her heart in her mouth.
Cherry blossom petals are fluttering down softly.
en.notes: ハラハラする describes the anxious tension felt when watching someone or waiting for an outcome (ハラハラさせる "to keep in suspense"). Unlike ドキドキ (vocab-n4:1251), which means a pounding heart from excitement or love, ハラハラ is about worry that something will go wrong. With と and usually in hiragana, はらはら depicts blossoms, leaves or tears falling softly.

examples[].german: As a child I played baseball every day in the nearby field.
This used to be an open field, but now an apartment building stands here.
en.notes: Colloquial for an open, usually grassy area, often a children's playground. Neutral: 野原.

examples[].german: The water pipe burst because of the cold.
I put too much air into the balloon and made it burst.
en.notes: 破裂する = to burst, rupture: 水道管が破裂する (the water pipe bursts). Figuratively: 交渉が破裂する (negotiations break down), today usually 決裂.

en.meaning: posted notice, bill, sign stuck on a wall
examples[].german: A sign saying "Closed today" was posted on the shop door.
I put up posters looking for the lost cat on utility poles in the neighborhood.
en.notes: A notice stuck to a wall or door with a message; also written 貼り紙. 張り紙禁止 = post no bills.

examples[].german: The package was damaged during delivery.
The file is corrupted and won't open.
en.notes: 破損する (to be damaged): 荷物が破損する. Also for data: ファイルの破損.

examples[].german: A fire broke out near the station this morning.
When the motor runs, heat is generated.
en.notes: Mostly 発生する (to occur, to arise): 事故が発生する, 火災が発生する, 熱が発生する. Frequent in news reports.

examples[].german: He always takes a cynical stance and never takes anything seriously.
Please cut the long green onion diagonally and put it in the pot.
My house is diagonally across from the post office.
en.notes: 斜 "slanting" is rare as an independent word and appears almost only in fixed phrases: 斜に切る "to cut diagonally" (cooking), 斜に構える "to adopt a cynical, detached attitude" (also read しゃに構える) and in the compound 斜向かい "diagonally opposite". In everyday speech one says 斜め/ななめ (separate card), e.g. 斜めに切る. Not to be confused with the homophone 蓮 "lotus".

examples[].german: My grandmother used to weave on a loom at home.
At the village museum, you can see demonstrations using an old loom.
en.notes: 機を織る (to weave on a loom), 機織り (weaving). The same kanji is read き (machine, opportunity); the reading はた applies only to the loom.

examples[].german: Wide farmland stretches across this area.
The city plans to convert part of the farmland into residential land.
en.notes: Written-language term for (dry) field land as opposed to rice paddies (水田), common in news, statistics and administrative texts (畑地を宅地に転用する). In everyday speech people simply say 畑/はたけ; 田畑/たはた covers both rice paddies and dry fields. It sounds the same as 二十歳/はたち "twenty years old", which is distinguished only by context.

examples[].german: I will find you even if I have to go to the ends of the earth.
I wonder what the edge of the universe is like.
en.notes: Noun of 果てる: 地の果て (the end of the earth), 宇宙の果て. Set phrase: 挙げ句の果てに (on top of everything, in the end).

en.meaning: first, the first ever, for the first time
examples[].german: She became Japan's first female astronaut.
The team won its first title since the club was founded.
en.notes: Free-standing mainly as 初の (first): 日本初の (Japan's first), 史上初 (first in history). As a first element: 初雪 (first snow), 初恋 (first love).

examples[].german: My father fell ill at fifty and lived through a long struggle with the disease.
Even after infection, the disease does not necessarily break out right away.
en.notes: 発病する (to fall ill): 感染してから発病するまで (from infection until the onset of the disease).

examples[].german: This child is developing well and is taller than children of the same age.
Insufficient nutrition affects children's growth.
en.notes: Mainly for children, animals and plants: 発育がいい / 発育が遅れる; 発育する.

en.meaning: to move up, bring forward; to speed up
examples[].german: It looked like rain, so we moved the departure up by an hour.
Could we move the start of the meeting up a little?
en.notes: Transitive: 予定を早める (to move an appointment forward), 死期を早める (to hasten death). Intransitive: 早まる. For speed (to quicken one's pace), 速める is usually written.

en.meaning: to let grow (beard, hair); to let (weeds) run wild
examples[].german: My father recently started growing a beard.
The garden of the vacant house is left as it is, with weeds growing freely.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 生える (to grow): ひげを生やす (to grow a beard). Also for plants one lets grow unchecked: 雑草を生やしたままにする.

examples[].german: This room is twenty square meters.
The square of five is twenty-five.
en.notes: Area units: 平方メートル (square meter), 平方キロメートル (square kilometer). Mathematics: 平方根 (square root).

examples[].german: The typhoon has passed, and the trains are running as usual.
In a match, it is important to keep a calm mind.
According to the examination, the blood pressure was within the normal range.
en.notes: Formal word for the normal, usual state, often in notices and announcements: 平常通り "as usual", 平常運転 "regular service", 平常心 "composure, inner calm". With の before nouns: 平常の業務. In conversation 普段 or いつも is said more; 日頃, by contrast, stresses habit over a longer period. Opposite: 異常 "abnormal".

en.meaning: to be at a loss; to be fed up with, hardly able to bear
examples[].german: I'm fed up with the heat that goes on every day.
I'm so tired of the noise from the house next door that I'm thinking of moving.
en.notes: Mostly 〜に閉口する: 暑さに閉口する (to groan under the heat). Literally "to close one's mouth", i.e. to be left speechless by annoyance. Similar sound: 平行, 並行.

en.meaning: left-hand radical of a kanji (e.g. にんべん, さんずいへん)
examples[].german: The left component of the character 休 is the person radical.
The left component of 海 and 池 is the water radical.
Many kanji are made by combining a left component and a right component.
en.notes: Technical term of kanji study for the left component of a character, often as a suffix -へん/-べん: 人偏 (にんべん), 木偏 (きへん), 糸偏 (いとへん). The counterpart is 旁 (つくり), the right component; on top is 冠 (かんむり). In teaching it is often written in kana. Do not confuse it with the identically read 辺, 変, 〜編 and 〜遍 (separate cards).

en.meaning: edge, brink, bank; hem, brim; border (e.g. of a tatami)
examples[].german: Stepping on the border of a tatami mat is considered bad manners.
My mother sewed a small ribbon onto the brim of the hat.
The children sat on the bank of the river, dipping their feet in the water.
en.notes: Refers to a narrow, strip-like edge: the cloth border of a tatami mat (畳の縁), the brim of a hat, a hem, or the edge of a path or river. Often written in kana as へり. 縁/ふち is the more general word for the edge or rim of round things (眼鏡の縁, 崖の縁); 縁/えん, on the other hand, means "fateful bond, relationship".

examples[].german: Humble language is a form of expression in which one humbles oneself to elevate the other person.
He treats everyone with a humble attitude.
en.notes: Usually in kana. The basic idea of humble language (謙譲語): one lowers oneself to honor the other person.

en.meaning: (time) to pass; to go through, pass via; to experience
examples[].german: After ten years, the bridge was finally completed.
This plan was decided after many discussions.
en.notes: Written style, mostly 〜を経て: 長い年月を経て (after many years), 大阪を経て (via Osaka), 審査を経て (after screening). Same sound: 減る (to decrease).

examples[].german: We will pay the transportation costs for those who come for an interview.
Living costs are high in Tokyo.
en.notes: Suffix for types of costs: 交通費 (transportation costs), 生活費 (living costs), 会費 (membership fee). In general: 費用 (cost).

examples[].german: Company employees become insured persons under health insurance.
In Japan, from the age of 25 you have the right to stand for election to the House of Representatives.
en.notes: Turns a noun of action into the party that undergoes or receives something: 被保険者 (insured person), 被選挙権 (right to stand for election), 被害 (damage suffered).

examples[].german: Sparks flew from the power line and for a moment the area lit up.
In the final, the two aces fought a fierce duel.
en.notes: 火花が散る (sparks fly). Figuratively: 火花を散らす (to fight a fierce contest).

examples[].german: The glass I dropped got a crack.
The incident put a crack in the two's friendship.
en.notes: Usually in kana. ひびが入る (to crack); figuratively: 友情にひびが入る (the friendship develops a rift). Same sound: 日々 (the days).

en.meaning: the days; daily, day by day
examples[].german: Small daily efforts lead to great results.
I still often think back on the days when I studied abroad.
en.notes: Somewhat more formal than 毎日: 日々の暮らし (daily life), 日々努力する (to make an effort day after day). Same sound: ひび (crack).

examples[].german: The two have not yet decided the date of the wedding.
Please let me know right away once the date of the move is set.
en.notes: The date for an event: 結婚式の日取りを決める. More general, also for the course of events: 日程.

examples[].german: Oil has a lower specific gravity than water, so it floats on water.
This university places more emphasis on teaching than on research.
en.notes: Physics: 比重が大きい (has a higher specific gravity). Figuratively: 〜に比重を置く (to place emphasis on ...).

en.meaning: waiting room, green room (before a performance)
examples[].german: Performers, please wait in the waiting room until the show.
Before the wedding, the bride changed in the waiting room.
en.notes: A room where one waits before a performance, ceremony, or exam, e.g. for speakers, performers, or brides and grooms. Also written 控室.

examples[].german: There's no need to be so pessimistic just because you failed once.
After hearing the doctor's explanation, he despaired about his illness.
en.notes: 悲観する = to be pessimistic, to despair: 将来を悲観する. Adjective: 悲観的 (pessimistic); opposite: 楽観.

en.meaning: to pull up, salvage; to raise (prices, taxes); to withdraw, pull out
examples[].german: The government plans to raise the consumption tax next year.
The car that had fallen into the sea was hauled up with a crane.
en.notes: Transitive: 沈没船を引き上げる (to salvage a sunken ship), 税率を引き上げる (to raise the tax rate), 部隊を引き上げる (to withdraw troops). For "to withdraw, return home" 引き揚げる is also used. Opposite when raising: 引き下げる.

en.meaning: to lower, reduce; to withdraw (a motion, demand)
examples[].german: It was decided to lower mobile phone fees.
Because there was a lot of opposition, he withdrew his proposal.
en.notes: Transitive: 料金を引き下げる (to lower fees), 要求を引き下げる (to withdraw a demand). Opposite: 引き上げる.

en.meaning: to take back, pick up, take over; to take in (a person, animal)
examples[].german: The retailer took back the old refrigerator.
After her parents died, she was taken in by her grandmother.
en.notes: 不用品を引き取る (to take back unwanted items), 子どもを引き取る (to take a child in). Euphemism: 息を引き取る = to pass away.

en.meaning: to drag, trail; to drag out, be unable to shake off
examples[].german: I dragged the heavy suitcase up the slope.
Dragging his injured leg, he ran all the way to the finish line.
en.notes: 足を引きずる (to drag a leg, to limp). Figuratively: 過去を引きずる (to be unable to let go of the past). Also written 引き摺る.

en.meaning: to hang, throw on (clothes); to snag, catch; to knock back (a drink)
examples[].german: Before going out, I threw on a jacket.
My sweater snagged on a nail and now there's a hole.
en.notes: Transitive: 上着を引っ掛ける (to throw on a jacket), 釘に服を引っ掛ける (to snag one's clothes on a nail). Colloquial: 一杯引っ掛ける (to have a quick drink). Intransitive: 引っ掛かる.

examples[].german: The cat scratched my hand and it bled.
The dog scratched at the door and left marks.
en.notes: To scratch with claws or fingernails: 猫に引っ掻かれる (to be scratched by a cat). For scratching an itch, かく is usually used.

examples[].german: Some children turn to delinquency because of family problems.
Adults in the neighborhood make patrols to prevent juvenile delinquency.
en.notes: Mainly of young people: 非行に走る (to go astray), 非行少年 (juvenile delinquent). Similar sound: 飛行 (flight).

examples[].german: I touched something in the dark room and involuntarily screamed.
A woman's scream could be heard from far away.
en.notes: 悲鳴を上げる (to scream; figuratively also: to cry out under overload). 嬉しい悲鳴 = "joyful scream", complaining about too much success or work.

examples[].german: In the nest, baby swallows are waiting for food.
On March 3rd, people display hina dolls and celebrate the growth of girls.
en.notes: Often also in kana ひな. The dolls for the Girls' Festival on March 3rd are called 雛人形; the festival itself ひな祭り.

examples[].german: The cat is sleeping comfortably in the sun.
Laundry dries better if you hang it in the sun.
en.notes: 日向で (in the sun), 日向ぼっこ (sunbathing, basking in the sun). Opposite: 日陰 (shade).

examples[].german: As a child he was frail, so he started swimming.
This report is based on poor data and is not convincing.
en.notes: na-adjective: 貧弱な体 (frail body), 貧弱な知識 (meager knowledge).

en.meaning: Hinomaru, the Japanese national flag; red sun disc
examples[].german: When the Japanese flag was raised at the award ceremony, the athlete shed tears.
Fans along the street cheered, waving small Japanese flags.
en.notes: The white flag with a red disc; official name 日章旗. 日の丸弁当 = rice with a single pickled plum in the middle.

examples[].german: Koshihikari is the most widely grown rice variety in Japan.
This farm grows many different varieties of apples.
en.notes: For plants and animals: 米の品種 (rice variety), 品種改良 (breeding of new varieties).

examples[].german: I arranged the food on a flat plate.
Put simply, this plan was a failure.
en.notes: i-adjective: 平たい皿 (flat plate). Figuratively: 平たく言えば (put simply).

examples[].german: The rumor spread throughout the whole school in no time.
Thanks to the internet, this word has spread among young people.
en.notes: Intransitive; transitive: 広める. うわさが広まる (a rumor spreads). For spatial expansion, 広がる is more common.

examples[].german: Shall we have lunch soon?
I was so busy that I didn't even have time for lunch.
en.notes: Casual (飯 = meal, rough); neutral: 昼ご飯, お昼.

examples[].german: The president's schedule is entirely managed by his secretary.
After graduating from university, she worked as a secretary to a Diet member.
en.notes: Personal assistant to an executive or politician: 社長秘書, 議員秘書. General office worker: 事務員.

examples[].german: I studied single-mindedly every day in order to pass.
Without saying anything, he just kept bowing his head.
en.notes: Usually in kana. Totally focused on one thing: ひたすら待つ (to just wait), ひたすら謝る (to apologize over and over).

en.meaning: single, single-layered; (flower) single-petaled; (eyelid) without a crease
examples[].german: This cherry tree has single-petaled blossoms and blooms earlier than the double-flowered Yae cherry.
My eyelids have no crease, so my eyes look small, which bothers me.
en.notes: Opposite: 二重 (ふたえ, e.g. 二重まぶた = eyelid with a crease) and 八重 (double-flowered). Idiom: 紙一重 (razor-thin, by a hair's breadth).

en.meaning: one breath; breather, short break; in one go; just a little more
examples[].german: Since the work had reached a stopping point, I had a coffee and took a breather.
It's just a little further to the finish line. Hang in there!
en.notes: 一息つく (to take a breather, to pause briefly), 一息に飲む (to drink in one go), あと一息 / もう一息 (just a little more, almost there).

examples[].german: The criminal took a bank clerk hostage and barricaded himself in.
Three days later, all the hostages were released unharmed.
en.notes: 人質に取る (to take hostage), 人質を解放する (to release hostages). Figuratively: 〜を人質に取る (to use something as a bargaining chip).

en.meaning: figure of a person; silhouette of a person
examples[].german: There wasn't a single soul in the park at night.
I saw a suspicious figure outside the window.
en.notes: Mostly in statements about presence: 人影がない (deserted), 人影もまばら (hardly anyone in sight).

examples[].german: The park at night had no one around, and it was a little scary.
She walked home alone along a deserted road.
On the station platform early in the morning, there were hardly any people yet.
en.notes: Means "sign of human presence" and is almost always used in the negative: 人気がない / 人気のない場所 "deserted". Written exactly like 人気（にんき）"popularity", so the context decides: 人気のない店 can mean "unpopular shop" (にんき) or "deserted shop" (ひとけ). To avoid misunderstandings, it is often written 人け or ひと気.

en.meaning: for a while (in the past), at one time
examples[].german: That singer isn't as popular as she once was.
For a while I used to go out drinking almost every night, but now I hardly go at all.
en.notes: Usually in kana. Refers to a past phase: ひところほどの人気はない (not as popular as at one time). Similar: 一時 (いちじ).
