examples[].german: I recognized him at a single glance.
Many people gathered to catch a glimpse of the famous painter's picture.
en.notes: A brief look: 一目で分かる (to understand at a glance), 一目見たい (to want to take a look), 一目惚れ (love at first sight).

examples[].german: He sang loudly at the station, paying no attention to the people around him.
I left through the back door so as not to be seen.
en.notes: 人目を気にする (to worry about what people think), 人目につく (to attract attention), 人目を避ける (to avoid being seen). Same sound: 一目 (a glance).

examples[].german: She was raised with great care as the only child of an elderly couple.
God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.
en.notes: A literary or biblical word for a single child, for example in novels or in the Bible translation (ひとり子 "the only begotten Son"). In everyday speech 一人っ子 (separate card) is used, which is much more common and neutral. Note: 一人子 can also appear as an irregular spelling of ひとりっこ.

en.meaning: sheep (8th sign of the Chinese zodiac); (formerly) hour of the Sheep (1-3 p.m.), south-southwest
examples[].german: I was born in the year of the Sheep.
The eighth sign of the twelve zodiac signs is the Sheep.
In the past, the time around two in the afternoon was called the hour of the Sheep.
en.notes: The eighth of the twelve zodiac signs (十二支), mainly in 未年 (ひつじどし) "year of the Sheep"; on New Year's cards 未 often stands instead of 羊. In the old system of timekeeping it is also the hour of the Sheep (about 1-3 p.m.) and the direction south-southwest. The animal itself is written 羊 (separate card); 未〜/み as a prefix means "not yet" (separate card).

en.meaning: to tease, make fun of; to browse (in a shop) without buying
examples[].german: My friends teased me when they saw me walking with my girlfriend.
I had no intention of buying and just browsed around the shops.
en.notes: 冷やかされる = to be teased, e.g. about a romantic relationship. 冷やかし = someone who only browses; also a mocking remark. Not to be confused with 冷やす (to cool).

examples[].german: In autumn, the rice ears in the paddies ripen to a golden color.
The plumes of Chinese silver grass swaying in the wind are beautiful.
en.notes: 稲の穂 (ear of rice), 穂が出る (ears form). Tip of a brush or spear: 穂先.

en.meaning: nursery teacher; kindergarten teacher (dated; today 保育士)
examples[].german: In her youth, my mother worked as a nursery teacher at a daycare center.
The children gathered around the teacher and sang songs.
Today, rather than 保母, the term 保育士 is the common designation.
en.notes: 保母 is the older term for a female childcare worker in a nursery or kindergarten; since 1999 the state-certified profession has had the gender-neutral name 保育士, which should be used today. 保母 is still found in older texts, memoirs and in the form of address 保母さん. Not to be confused with the common adverb ほぼ "almost, nearly" (own card), which sounds the same.

examples[].german: The old school building was reinforced in preparation for earthquakes.
The team strengthened its defense by bringing in new players.
en.notes: As the verb 補強する: to make something sturdier: 壁を補強する (to reinforce a wall); also figuratively: チームを補強する (to strengthen a team).

examples[].german: On hot days, please replenish your fluids frequently.
The plane refueled at an airport along the way.
en.notes: As the verb 補給する: to make up for what has been used: 水分を補給する (to take in fluids), 燃料の補給 (refueling).

en.meaning: home (of a product or culture); birthplace; authentic place
examples[].german: I went to Paris to eat authentic French cuisine.
He went to Italy to learn cooking at the source.
en.notes: The place where something comes from or is done best: 本場のイタリア料理 (authentic Italian cuisine), 本場の英語 (authentic English).

examples[].german: The ambassador contacted the government of his home country.
The company withdrew from Japan, and the employees returned to their home country.
en.notes: One's own country, mainly from the viewpoint of diplomats, companies or people abroad: 本国の政府 (the government of one's home country), 本国に戻る (to return home). Cf. 母国 (homeland, more personal).

en.meaning: genuine, true-to-form manner; authentic, orthodox (e.g. 本格派, 本格化, 本格ミステリー)
examples[].german: The rainy season has ended, and summer has begun in earnest.
An authentic Indian restaurant has opened in front of the station.
He is known as a detective-story writer of the orthodox school.
en.notes: Base word of 本格的 (separate card); rare on its own, but productive in compounds: 本格化 "to get going in earnest", 本格派 "representative of the classical style". It also stands directly before nouns in the sense of "genuine, authentic": 本格カレー, 本格ミステリー "classic puzzle mystery". For adjectival use, 本格的な is usually taken.

examples[].german: At this restaurant you can eat authentic Italian cuisine.
The rainy season is said to begin in earnest next week.
en.notes: な-adjective. 本格的な (genuine, authentic: 本格的な料理) and adverbial 本格的に (in earnest, fully: 本格的に始まる). Derived from 本格 (the proper, genuine way).

en.meaning: main unit; the device itself (without accessories)
examples[].german: The box contained only the unit itself and the manual.
The camera body is light, but the lens is quite heavy.
en.notes: The device itself as opposed to accessories or packaging: パソコン本体 (the computer unit). 本体価格 = price excluding tax. Further meanings: "true form, real nature" (本体を現す, to reveal one's true form) and the main object of worship enshrined in a shrine or temple.

examples[].german: Please keep the rice warm in the rice cooker.
This cup has excellent heat retention, so coffee doesn't cool down easily.
en.notes: As the verb 保温する: to keep something warm. Common with appliances: 炊飯器の保温 (keep-warm function of a rice cooker), 保温性 (heat retention).

en.meaning: hall; auditorium; dining floor (in a restaurant)
examples[].german: The graduation ceremony was held in the city hall.
In my part-time job at the restaurant, I work on the floor rather than in the kitchen.
en.notes: A large hall for events: コンサートホール. In the restaurant business, the dining room; someone who waits tables works in the ホール (as opposed to the kitchen). Homophone: ホール (a hole in golf).

examples[].german: I watered the flowers in the garden with a hose.
The washing machine hose came off, and the floor was flooded.
en.notes: Water or garden hose: ホースで水をまく (to water with a hose). A different word that sounds the same: ホース (English "horse").

examples[].german: Babies' cheeks are very soft.
This cake is so delicious it melts in your mouth!
en.notes: Colloquial for 頬【ほお】, mostly in kana; in child language also ほっぺ. ほっぺたが落ちる = so delicious that your cheeks fall off.

examples[].german: This fish isn't dried enough; let's leave it in the sun a bit longer.
Drying nori requires plenty of sunshine.
Please store the dried persimmons in a cool place.
In the mountains, I ate jerky little by little to keep up my strength.
en.notes: 干し（ほし）as a noun denotes drying or the degree of drying, for example in 干しが足りない "not dried enough". Before another noun, it forms words for dried products, such as 干し柿（ほしがき）"dried persimmons" or 干し肉（ほしにく）"dried meat". Here "dried" is a prefix meaning, not an adjective used independently. 乾し is also attested; 干 and 乾 without し are irregular writing variants for exactly this reading and meaning. Other readings of 乾 are not derived from this. The accent of the nominal entry is not carried over unchecked to the prefix and its compounds.

examples[].german: It looks like rain, so please bring in the laundry.
A lot of laundry is hanging in a row on the balcony.
en.notes: Things dried in the sun, mainly laundry: 干し物を取り込む (to bring in the laundry). Today 洗濯物 is usually said. Not to be confused with 干物【ひもの】 (dried fish); the spelling 乾物 is usually read かんぶつ (dried foods).

examples[].german: My grandfather had a heart attack in the middle of the night and was hospitalized.
I always carry medicine in case I have an asthma attack.
en.notes: A sudden onset of illness: 発作が起きる (an attack occurs), 心臓発作 (heart attack), 喘息の発作 (asthma attack). Note the reading: ほっさ, not はっさ.

examples[].german: A new committee is scheduled to be set up next month.
This year marks fifty years since this organization was founded.
en.notes: As the verb 発足する: an organization, body or government starts its work: 新政権が発足した (a new government was inaugurated). Also read はっそく.

examples[].german: There is a small inn on the shore of the lake.
The traveler sat down at the roadside and spread out his map.
en.notes: ほとり often denotes the shore of a lake or river, but also the edge or immediate vicinity of a place. 湖のほとり is "on the shore of the lake"; 道のほとり sounds rather literary and means the wayside. The word is usually written in hiragana. The writing 辺り is unusual for this reading; as あたり it usually denotes a whole surrounding area.

en.meaning: relieved (to breathe a sigh of relief)
examples[].german: I felt relieved when I heard that I had passed the exam.
When the child came home safely, the mother breathed a sigh of relief.
en.notes: Usually ほっとする: to feel relieved, to breathe easy. ほっと一息つく = to take a short breather. Not to be confused with ホット (hot).

examples[].german: "Would you like your coffee hot or iced?" "Hot, please."
On cold days, I feel like drinking hot milk tea.
en.notes: Mainly for warm drinks: ホットコーヒー; in a cafe, simply ホット (hot coffee) as opposed to アイス. Not to be confused with ほっと (relieved).

examples[].german: He studied law at university and became a lawyer.
Knowledge of law is also useful in business.
en.notes: 法学部 (faculty of law), 法学を学ぶ (to study law). Similar sound: 方角 (direction), 邦楽 (Japanese music).

examples[].german: Japan in the Edo period was a feudal society.
In class, we learned about the European feudal system.
My father's way of thinking is still feudalistic.
en.notes: Occurs almost only in compounds: 封建制度 "feudal system", 封建時代 "feudal era", 封建社会 "feudal society" and 封建的 "feudalistic", figuratively also "backward, authoritarian" (封建的な考え方). A technical word from history and social criticism. For Japan, 封建時代 usually means the era of samurai rule until the Meiji Restoration.

examples[].german: This temple preserves an old mirror regarded as a national treasure.
The royal family's treasures were put on special display at the museum.
He is a talent you could call a treasure of our company.
en.notes: 宝器 is a rare, elevated written word for a precious object, often a ritual or ceremonial vessel, and figuratively for an exceptionally capable person. In everyday speech 宝物 or 宝 is used more. The reading ほうき is shared by several cards - 放棄 "abandonment", 箒 "broom" and 法規 "laws and regulations" - so 宝器 can practically only be recognized by its written form.

en.meaning: to throw out; to fling out; to drop (a job)
examples[].german: Because of the sudden braking, cargo was flung from the truck bed onto the road.
He dropped his work halfway and went off on a trip.
en.notes: Transitive: to throw or fling something out; figuratively to give up a task halfway: 仕事を途中で放り出す.

en.meaning: to throw in; to stuff in
examples[].german: He threw the clothes he had taken off into the washing machine.
I was in a hurry, so I stuffed the documents into my bag and left the house.
en.notes: Transitive: to toss something into something carelessly or with a swing: かばんに放り込む. Counterpart: 放り出す (to throw out).

examples[].german: This year, with favorable weather, there was a bumper rice harvest.
The villagers prayed for a good harvest at the shrine.
en.notes: Opposite: 凶作 / 不作 (crop failure). 豊作を祈る (to pray for a good harvest).

examples[].german: From next year, the company will calculate salaries using a new system.
This exam will be conducted in mark-sheet format.
en.notes: A fixed way of carrying something out, often for technical or organizational systems: 支払い方式 (payment method), 選挙方式 (electoral system). For an individual approach, 方法 is more usual.

examples[].german: Harmful gases were being emitted from the factory.
The government released its stockpiled rice onto the market.
en.notes: As the verb 放出する: to give off energy, gas or heat (熱を放出する), or to release stockpiles or let players go (在庫を放出する).

en.meaning: to report, to inform; to repay (written form of 報じる)
examples[].german: The local newspaper ran an article that reported the incident in detail.
The prime minister's resignation was reported prominently in all the papers.
I intend to repay the kindness I received without fail.
en.notes: Written-language ずる variant of 報じる (separate card) with the same meaning: "to report, to announce" (新聞が事件を報ずる) and, elevated, "to repay, to return" (恩に報ずる). Typical of newspaper language and older literature; in modern usage 報じる is more common. The forms follow partly 報じる (報じた, 報じない), partly the classical pattern (報ぜず, 報ぜられる).

examples[].german: Every year my grandmother spends about a week recuperating at a hot spring resort.
Looking at the beautiful garden was a treat for the eyes.
en.notes: Rest for body and mind: 温泉で保養する (to recuperate at a hot spring), 保養地 (health resort). Idiom: 目の保養 (a feast for the eyes).

examples[].german: Perhaps he has already gone home.
Might you be Mr. Tanaka's younger sister?
en.notes: Almost only in fixed combinations: ひょっとしたら / ひょっとすると / ひょっとして (perhaps, possibly). Expresses a rather unexpected possibility.

examples[].german: I voted for the young candidate.
The difference between the two candidates was only ten votes.
en.notes: Also as a counter: 一票, 百票. 票を入れる (to cast one's vote), 票を集める (to collect votes). Election, voting: 投票.

examples[].german: The school invited slogans for eliminating bullying.
A slogan reading "Please don't rush onto the train" is posted at the station.
en.notes: A short guiding phrase for campaigns, e.g. 交通安全の標語. From English: スローガン.

en.meaning: difference, dissenting opinion (異を唱える); strange
examples[].german: No one in the meeting objected to his opinion.
They say fate works in strange ways, and the two met on a trip.
Encountering a foreign culture while studying abroad is an important experience.
en.notes: As an independent word, 異 lives almost only in set phrases: 異を唱える "to object, to raise objections" and in the proverb 縁は異なもの "fate is strange" (異な = "strange"). As a prefix it means "different, foreign" (異文化, 異国). For "to be different", one uses 違う or 異なる in everyday life (own cards); 胃 "stomach" is only a homophone.

examples[].german: I sincerely express my gratitude for everyone's cooperation.
She made up her mind and told the president the truth.
He paid no attention at all to the opposition around him.
en.notes: As an independent word it is written-language and appears almost only in set phrases: 感謝の意を表す "to express thanks", 意を決する "to make up one's mind", 意に介さない "to pay no heed", 意のままに "as one pleases". Otherwise the character appears in everyday life in compounds like 意味, 意見, 注意. Do not confuse it with the homophones 胃 "stomach" and 〜位 "rank".

examples[].german: Three years have flown by since we last saw each other.
At their first reunion since parting, the two instinctively took each other's hands.
"I have not been in touch for a long time since we last met," he began the letter.
en.notes: Elevated word for the separation since the last meeting, used almost only in letters and greetings: ご一別以来 "since we last saw each other" is a fixed opening formula, often followed by ご無沙汰しております. As a suru verb (一別する) it is rare. Do not confuse it with the homophone 一瞥 "a quick glance".

examples[].german: This is only a small part of the problem.
Only one part of the wall has a different color.
en.notes: A part of a whole, slightly more emphatic than 一部: ほんの一部分にすぎない.

examples[].german: All of the staff sincerely thank you.
Everyone listened quietly to the teacher's talk.
en.notes: Formal, often in greetings: 社員一同 (all the employees), 家族一同 (the whole family).

en.meaning: first-time visit (without introduction); new unknown customer
examples[].german: This place does not accept first-time customers without an introduction.
In Kyoto, there are still teahouses that don't let in unknown first-time customers.
I'm looking for a bar that even a first-time customer can easily walk into.
en.notes: 一見/いちげん denotes the first visit to an inn or establishment without an introduction by a regular customer, and also such an unknown guest. It is best known from 一見さんお断り "no customers without an introduction", typical of traditional teahouses and restaurants in Kyoto. The card 一見/いっけん with the same writing, by contrast, means "at first glance" and is much more common; いちげん is used almost only in connection with guests and establishments.

en.meaning: a (single) word (elevated; mainly in 一言居士)
examples[].german: The department head is the sort of person who has to put in his two cents at every meeting.
My proposal was rejected out of hand with a single word.
Every word and deed of a leader has a great influence on young people.
en.notes: Elevated Sino-Japanese reading of 一言 alongside the everyday 一言/ひとこと (separate card). いちげん survives almost only in fixed expressions: 一言居士 "someone who has to put in his two cents on everything", 一言のもとに "with a single word, out of hand" and 一言一行 "every word and deed". If you simply want to "say a word", you always say ひとこと; do not confuse it with the homophone 一見/いちげん "first-time visitor without an introduction".

en.meaning: one day (elevated; mainly in 一日の長, 一日千秋)
examples[].german: When it comes to cooking, my older sister has a slight edge in experience.
The mother is waiting with great longing for her son, who is studying abroad, to come home.
en.notes: Elevated reading of 一日 alongside 一日/いちにち "one day, all day" and 一日/ついたち "the first of the month" (both separate cards). いちじつ appears almost only in fixed phrases: 一日の長 "a slight edge in experience" and 一日千秋 "to wait longingly (one day feels like a thousand autumns)". In normal talk about days and dates, it is never read いちじつ.

en.meaning: one side; the whole surface; front page
examples[].german: When I woke up in the morning, it was all snow outside.
I saw an unexpected side of him.
en.notes: Several meanings: whole surface (一面の雪 = everything covered in snow), an aspect (意外な一面 = an unexpected side) and the front page of a newspaper.

en.meaning: a glance; a stone (Go) - mainly in 一目置く, 一目瞭然
examples[].german: Shown as a graph, the change in sales is clear at a glance.
Even veteran players hold his ability in respect.
Barked at by a dog, the children ran away as fast as they could.
en.notes: A separate word alongside 一目/ひとめ (separate card): いちもく also means "a glance", but occurs almost only in fixed expressions: 一目瞭然 "clear at a glance", 一目散に "headlong (run away)" and 一目置く "to respect someone, to acknowledge as superior". The last comes from Go, where 一目 means "one stone": the weaker player places a stone in advance. A simple short glance (一目で分かる) is read ひとめ.

en.meaning: one person (elevated; mainly in 一人前, 一人称)
examples[].german: My son has finally become a full-fledged carpenter, too.
This novel is told in the first person from the protagonist's viewpoint.
I ordered just one serving of sushi for delivery.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 一人 alongside the everyday 一人/ひとり (separate card). On its own, いちにん is hardly heard anymore; the reading is, however, found in important compounds such as 一人前 "full-fledged, adult; one portion" and 一人称 "first person (grammar)" (separate card). For counting people and for "alone", ひとり is always used.

examples[].german: Hearing the question, the students all tilted their heads in the same way.
The sky was covered with a uniformly gray layer of clouds.
The circumstances are not the same everywhere, depending on the region.
en.notes: na-adjective (also with の) for "the same everywhere, uniform": 一様な色, 一様に広がる. Very common adverbially as 一様に "all in the same way", e.g. 参加者は一様に驚いた. In the negative (一様ではない) it means "not uniform, varying from case to case". More written-language than 同じ; related to 一律 "across the board, without exception" (separate card), which is used more for rules and amounts.

examples[].german: My son ran away from home and hasn't come back for three days.
I ran away from home once, when I was in junior high school.
en.notes: Secretly leaving one's parents' home; as a verb 家出する.

en.meaning: landlord/landlady; house owner, head of the household
examples[].german: The owner of the vacant house cannot be found, and the city is at a loss how to respond.
While the owner of the house was away, a neighbor took care of the garden.
In old tales, there are often scenes where a traveler asks the master of the house for a night's lodging.
en.notes: A rarer reading of 家主 alongside 家主/やぬし (separate card), with the same meaning. In a rental context (家主に家賃を払う), やぬし is usual; いえぬし sounds more like "owner or master of the house" and appears in narratives, older texts and reports about residential houses. Colloquially, 大家さん is mostly said for the landlord, and 貸主 in contracts.

en.meaning: yes (agreement, e.g. イエスかノーか, イエスマン)
examples[].german: Please answer yes or no.
It is not good to say yes to everything your boss says.
Behind his back, he is said to be the president's yes-man.
en.notes: Loanword "yes", which does not serve as an ordinary answer (for that, はい/ええ), but stands in fixed patterns: イエスかノーか "yes or no", イエスと言う "to agree" or イエスマン "yes-man". The spelling イェス is a rarer variant. The identically written イエス "Jesus" is a proper name and is not learned here.

examples[].german: I had my cold looked at by the clinic in my neighborhood.
This clinic is closed on Saturday afternoons.
en.notes: A small practice run by an independent doctor, often part of the name: 田中医院. Large hospitals are called 病院. Homophone: 委員.

examples[].german: Don't be so stubborn; why don't you just apologize honestly?
Out of sheer stubbornness, he kept running to the end.
en.notes: Obstinate will or defiance: 意地を張る (to stay stubborn), 意地でも (out of sheer stubbornness). Cf. 意地悪 (mean).

en.meaning: to be angry; to be indignant
examples[].german: The voices of people angry at the unfair treatment echoed across the square.
He was angry, but he did not say any words blaming the other person.
en.notes: いかる expresses anger or indignation and often sounds more literary than おこる. The cause can be marked with に, as in 不公平な扱いに怒る. Here it is an intransitive verb of emotion: "to scold someone" is not simply expressed with a direct object marked by を. It is a Godan verb: いかって, いかった and いからない.

examples[].german: Only he voiced a dissenting opinion at the meeting.
Anyone with an objection to that proposal, please raise your hand.
en.notes: An opposing opinion: 異見を述べる. Homophone and more common: 意見 (opinion in general). Synonym: 異論.

examples[].german: Mother arranged seasonal flowers in the entrance hall.
The flowers I arranged withered in three days.
en.notes: Transitive Ichidan verb: to arrange flowers artistically: 花を生ける. Hence 生け花 (ikebana). Also written 活ける.

examples[].german: If your payment crossed with this email, please excuse us.
A small misunderstanding made the relationship between the two worse.
en.notes: Passing each other by (letters, people) and the misunderstanding that results. Fixed formula in business letters and payment reminders: 本状と行き違いの際はご容赦ください (If this letter has crossed with your payment or reply, please excuse us). Also read ゆきちがい.

examples[].german: Tariffs are charged on imports from outside the EU.
This insurance cannot be used for accidents outside the area.
We need to cooperate with countries outside the region as well.
en.notes: 域外 is a formal word from politics, economics and news and means "outside a (economic) area": EU域外 "outside the EU", 域外からの輸入 "imports from outside". As an attribute, it takes の (域外の国). The opposite is 域内 "inside the area". Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding 生き甲斐/いきがい "purpose in life" (own card).

en.meaning: to be fired up; to be keen
examples[].german: He is determined to pass this year for sure.
I started out full of enthusiasm, but got bored after three days.
en.notes: Intransitive Godan verb: to approach something with great eagerness: 今年こそ優勝すると意気込む. Noun: 意気込み.

en.meaning: one breath, in one go; "Bottoms up!" (drinking cheer)
examples[].german: At the party, the senior colleagues clapped and shouted "Bottoms up! Bottoms up!"
Chugging a drink is dangerous for the body, so by all means don't do it.
The night before the deadline, he wrote the paper in one go.
en.notes: 一気 is the base word behind the adverb 一気に "in one go, all at once" (separate card). On its own it is today mainly a colloquial drinking cheer "Bottoms up!" (often doubled: 一気！一気！) and appears in compounds such as 一気飲み "chugging" or 一気呵成 "in one go". Pressuring someone to chug is now regarded as harassment; in a normal sentence, 一気に is used for "all at once".

en.meaning: at a stroke; all at once
examples[].german: The new medicine improved the symptoms all at once.
I cleared the backlog of work in one go.
en.notes: Literary: everything at once: 問題を一挙に解決する. Synonym: 一気に.

examples[].german: Let's confirm the person's wishes before deciding.
The company president indicated his intention to retire next year.
en.notes: Formal: the will or intention of a person or organization: 本人の意向を尊重する. Homophones: 移行, 以降.

examples[].german: We plan to switch over to the new system next month.
The old method can also be used during the transition period.
en.notes: Transition to a new state or system; as a verb 移行する: 新しいシステムに移行する.

examples[].german: She confessed to her partner that she had faked an orgasm.
He told his partner, "I haven't climaxed yet."
en.notes: Colloquial verb for "to have an orgasm", often written in katakana as イク. It is an expression for intimate conversations between adults; in neutral language オルガスムに達する is clearer. Only いく is read here. The form ゆく does not belong to this meaning. This intransitive godan verb forms the te-form いって and the past tense いった; the negative is いかない. The motion meaning "to go" is covered on its own card.

examples[].german: An army marches on its stomach. (proverb; lit. "you can't fight on an empty stomach")
The young samurai went into battle for the first time.
Even though they knew it was a losing battle, they kept defending the castle.
en.notes: Old Japanese word for "war, battle", today mainly in historical contexts (samurai era), literature and proverbs: 戦に出る, 負け戦, 腹が減っては戦ができぬ. Less often written 軍. For modern wars 戦争 is used, for fights in general 戦い (both separate cards); the reading せん occurs only as a suffix (〜戦, separate card, e.g. 決勝戦).

examples[].german: He succeeded after overcoming countless difficulties.
This town has gone through many wars.
en.notes: Literary, mostly before nouns: 幾多の困難 (countless difficulties). In everyday speech たくさんの.

en.meaning: seal, stamp; stamp impression; mudra (hand gesture)
examples[].german: Please stamp your seal here on the document.
This seal is different from the one registered with the bank.
The Buddha statue forms a mudra with both hands in front of its chest.
en.notes: 印/いん is the (name) seal or its impression, especially in formal phrases such as 印を押す "to stamp" and in compounds such as 実印 or 認め印. In everyday speech, はんこ or 印鑑 (separate cards) is said instead. Written the same but read differently is 印/しるし "sign, mark"; 印を結ぶ refers to the Buddhist hand gesture (mudra) or ninja finger signs.

examples[].german: A flash of lightning ran across the night sky.
A while after the lightning was visible, thunder rumbled.
en.notes: The flash of lightning itself; thunder is 雷 or 雷鳴. Synonym: 稲妻.

examples[].german: If you don't know the way, please ask at the information desk.
Information about the event is on the website.
en.notes: Often the information counter in stations or department stores: インフォメーションで聞く. In general, people prefer 情報.

examples[].german: Let's get off the expressway at the next interchange.
There is a large warehouse near the interchange.
en.notes: The on- and off-ramp of an expressway, often shortened to IC: 次のインターチェンジで降りる.

examples[].german: The intercom rang, so I went to the door.
I spoke with the delivery person over the intercom.
en.notes: Intercom system at the front door or in a building; also written インターホン.

examples[].german: We send our child to an international school.
The event had a very international atmosphere.
en.notes: な-adjective: インターナショナルな雰囲気. Often in names: インターナショナルスクール (international school). In everyday speech 国際的 is more common.

examples[].german: He is an intellectual, but doesn't act arrogant at all.
The magazine is said to be aimed at intellectuals.
en.notes: An educated person, a brainy type; often slightly mocking. Short form of インテリゲンチャ.

examples[].german: The basketball team got through the qualifying round with three wins and one loss.
We lost the first match, but there is still hope for the title.
The champion suffered a crushing defeat against an unknown newcomer.
en.notes: 一敗 "one defeat" appears mainly in sports records (三勝一敗, 一勝一敗) and can be used as a verb with する (一敗する). Not to be confused with the similar-sounding いっぱい "full, a lot" (own card); in writing, the kanji 敗 "to lose" makes it clear. Elevated is the phrase 一敗地にまみれる "to suffer a crushing defeat"; the general "victory or defeat" is 勝敗.

examples[].german: His life changed completely after the accident.
With the new store manager, the atmosphere of the shop changed completely.
en.notes: A sudden, complete transformation; as a verb 一変する: 状況が一変した. Homophone: 一遍 (once).

examples[].german: The entrance is on a back street, so it is hard for first-time visitors to find.
Following the staff's guidance, the line that had formed at the entrance slowly began to move.
en.notes: 入口 can be read いりくち as well as いりぐち. In this reading the く stays voiceless; both writings 入口 and 入り口 are possible. It means the place where one goes in; 出口 is the exit. In 入口にできた列, に marks the place where the line formed.

en.meaning: to enter, to go in; to set (sun, moon)
examples[].german: The traveler entered the castle gate at dusk.
By the time the sun set behind the mountains, the village had grown quiet.
en.notes: This reading of 入る is found mainly in set phrases and literary texts. For ordinary entering, one now usually says はいる. In 日が入る, いる can denote sunset. In 門に入る, に marks the area entered. Despite the ending いる, this is a Godan verb: いります, いって, いった. The identically sounding 居る "to be present" is conjugated differently: います, いて.

examples[].german: Before moving, I packed my clothes into cardboard boxes.
This detergent can also be used on delicate clothing.
en.notes: Collective term for garments, e.g. on washing labels or when moving: 冬物の衣類 (winter clothing).

examples[].german: The power of the typhoon was terrifying.
The new vacuum cleaner fully demonstrated its power.
en.notes: Great effective force: 台風の威力 (the might of the typhoon), 威力を発揮する (to show one's strength).

examples[].german: This supermarket sells clothing on the second floor.
We sent the donated clothing to the disaster area.
en.notes: Clothing as a product category, often in compounds: 衣料品 (clothing items), 衣料品店 (clothing store). Homophone: 医療 (medical care).

examples[].german: An old monument stands quietly by the roadside on the pass.
The characters carved on the stone have been worn away by wind and rain and are almost unreadable.
The villagers carved the lesson of the tsunami into a monument and left it for posterity.
en.notes: Native Japanese reading of 碑 with the same meaning as 碑/ひ (separate card): a stone with an inscription carved into it, meant to commemorate an event or a person. いしぶみ sounds literary and archaic and appears in poems, song lyrics and titles; also written 石文. In compounds such as 記念碑 or 慰霊碑 it is always read ひ.

examples[].german: At the board meeting three days ago, this matter was formally approved.
According to the police, the man has been missing since the evening three days ago.
en.notes: Formal Sino-Japanese reading of 一昨昨日, typical of news, minutes and official speeches; it can also be used adverbially without a particle. In everyday speech さきおととい (separate card) is said, and even when written 一昨昨日 is usually read that way. Similarly, 一昨日 "the day before yesterday" has the formal reading いっさくじつ alongside おととい.

examples[].german: Just wanting to see my mother, I drove through the night.
Solely wanting to pass, I kept studying every day.
en.notes: Mostly in 〜たい一心で (driven solely by the wish to ...): 会いたい一心で. Also in 一心不乱 (utterly absorbed).

examples[].german: If I am this torn, shouldn't I just give it up?
Since the repair costs a lot, I decided to just buy a new one.
en.notes: Introduces a more drastic step: いっそ辞めてしまおうか (Shouldn't I just quit?). Emphasized: いっそのこと.

en.meaning: to grow into it; to become second nature
examples[].german: She has by now grown fully into her role as a teacher.
The new employees don't yet look quite natural in suits.
en.notes: From the theater: an actor "fits the boards" (板 = stage). Today: a role, job or clothing looks natural and self-evident. Also written 板に付く.

examples[].german: There is still snow on the mountain peak.
The morning sun lit up the top of the tower.
en.notes: Elevated word for the highest point: 山の頂 (mountain peak). More everyday: 頂上, てっぺん.

examples[].german: My grandfather is ninety, but he is in perfect health.
The exam result was completely average.
en.notes: Slightly formal adverb: 至って元気だ (in perfect health), 至って普通 (perfectly ordinary).

en.meaning: to care for; to go easy on
examples[].german: I want to value the feeling of caring for the elderly.
If you are tired, you should go easy on your body a little.
en.notes: Transitive Godan verb: to treat someone considerately (お年寄りを労る) or to take care of one's own body (体を労る). Usually written in kana.

en.meaning: farewell (taking leave); free time, leisure; leave, dismissal
examples[].german: It's getting late, so I'll be taking my leave soon.
There is no end of troubles of this kind.
The samurai asked his lord for leave and returned to his hometown.
en.notes: いとま is a word in its own right, more elevated than 暇/ひま "free time" (separate card), and is mostly written in kana. It is alive mainly in おいとまする "to politely take one's leave" and in 枚挙にいとまがない "to be countless"; 暇を乞う "to ask for leave/dismissal" sounds historical. For everyday free time one says ひま, never いとま.

examples[].german: Heavy rain flooded this whole area.
Redevelopment is under way throughout the area around the station.
en.notes: The whole surroundings of a place: この辺り一帯, 関東一帯. Homophone: 一体 (what on earth; one body).

examples[].german: The child reluctantly started his homework.
He attended the meeting reluctantly.
en.notes: To do something only unwillingly: いやいや手伝う. Also written 嫌々. Not to be confused with the interjection いやいや (no, no!).

en.meaning: no, no!; oh no, not at all (interjection)
examples[].german: "Thank you so much." "Oh no, I didn't do anything special."
No, no, you are mistaken there.
en.notes: A doubled "no" used to wave something off or to modestly decline (e.g. in response to praise or thanks). The spelling 否々 is rare and literary; in everyday life it is almost always written いやいや or, more politely, いえいえ (JMdict lists both readings). Do not confuse it with いやいや/嫌々 ("reluctantly, unwillingly"), which has its own card.

examples[].german: It's strangely quiet today. Did something happen?
He was oddly kind, which was a bit creepy.
en.notes: Stresses that something is unusually intense, often with slight unease: いやに静かだ (suspiciously quiet). Also written 嫌に.

examples[].german: Laughing at other people's failures; what a nasty person.
I wish you would stop that unpleasant way of talking.
en.notes: い-adjective: unpleasant, mean (いやらしい言い方) and also suggestive, lecherous. Also written 嫌らしい.

en.meaning: now; when it comes to it
examples[].german: Let's have water ready for an emergency.
But when I actually tried to speak, the words wouldn't come.
en.notes: Introduces the decisive moment: いざとなると (when push comes to shove), いざという時 (in an emergency), いざ始めると (once we actually started).

en.meaning: a little less than, just under (after quantities, e.g. 3時間弱); weakness, the weak; weak setting; lower level (earthquake intensity, e.g. 震度5弱)
examples[].german: It takes just under twenty minutes on foot from the station to my house.
Last night, an earthquake of intensity 5-lower occurred in this area.
When I sleep, I set the air conditioner to low.
en.notes: Mainly a suffix after quantities, meaning "a little less than, just under": 1時間弱 "just under an hour", 100人弱. The counterpart is 強/きょう "a little more than" (card). In the Japanese earthquake scale, 弱 denotes the lower level (震度5弱, 6弱), and on devices the weak setting (弱・中・強). In this usage it is always read じゃく, not よわ-.

examples[].german: This shop's jumbo parfait is too much even for three people.
In the old days, people used to fly abroad on a jumbo jet.
en.notes: Mostly used as a prefix: ジャンボサイズ (jumbo size), ジャンボ宝くじ (jumbo lottery); also short for the Boeing 747 (ジャンボジェット).

examples[].german: It was cold, so I put on a jacket and went out.
Work jackets are issued by the company.
en.notes: In Japanese, a short jacket, not the British "jumper" (pullover). In sports also "ski jumper".

examples[].german: The cat jumped up to a high place.
He won the jumping competition.
en.notes: A jump; as a verb ジャンプする. In sports also the discipline of ski jumping (スキージャンプ).

examples[].german: What genre of music do you often listen to?
This bookstore arranges its books by genre.
en.notes: A category of music, literature or film: 好きなジャンル (favorite genre), ジャンルを問わず (regardless of genre).

examples[].german: On the weekend I'm going to a live jazz show.
My father has liked jazz since his youth.
en.notes: A genre of music; ジャズ喫茶 are cafes in Japan where jazz records are played.

examples[].german: This library holds storytelling sessions for young children.
The nurse measured the newborn's weight.
en.notes: In compounds, 児 means a child, for example 幼児（ようじ）, small child, and 新生児（しんせいじ）, newborn. You will meet it especially in texts about education, childcare and medicine. Such terms fix the context or age; they are not always interchangeable. In ordinary conversation, 子供 is the general word for a child. Learn each word with its whole reading, because 児 is not read じ in all compounds.

examples[].german: Let's decide the detailed schedule at the next meeting.
The budget for the next fiscal year includes equipment repair costs.
en.notes: 次（じ）stands before a noun and denotes the next in a sequence, for example 次回（じかい）, next time, or 次年度（じねんど）, next business, school or fiscal year. In 次回の会議, the compound noun is specified further with の. The independent word 次（つぎ）, by contrast, is connected directly with の, for example in 次の会議. The reading depends on the whole form.

examples[].german: My hay fever is bad, so I went to the ENT doctor.
If your ear hurts, you should have it looked at by an ENT doctor.
en.notes: Short for 耳鼻咽喉科. Responsible for ears, nose and throat, e.g. for hay fever.

examples[].german: Around age two, a child's sense of self begins to emerge.
He has a strong ego and does not listen to other people's opinions.
en.notes: Psychological term for self-awareness: 自我が芽生える (the sense of self awakens, e.g. in toddlers).

examples[].german: On days off I usually wear jeans.
I bought these jeans ten years ago.
en.notes: Japanese short form of "jeans pants"; today ジーンズ or デニム are also common.

examples[].german: This plate is Arita ware porcelain.
Porcelain is thinner and harder than earthenware.
en.notes: Hard-fired white ceramic; the umbrella term for pottery and porcelain: 陶磁器. Similar sound: 時期, 磁気.

examples[].german: I'm going back to my parents' home for New Year.
A package of vegetables came from my parents' home.
en.notes: The house of one's parents, where one grew up: 実家に帰る (to go home to one's parents). For married people, also the home they lived in before marriage.

examples[].german: The Earth rotates around its axis.
He is the central player of the team.
en.notes: A technical axis (車軸, axle) and an axis in mathematics (Ｘ軸); figuratively the core: チームの軸になる選手.

en.meaning: battle formation; camp, position; group, team (suffix, e.g. 報道陣)
examples[].german: The Takeda army set up camp on the far side of the river.
Numerous reporters were crowded in front of the press conference hall.
This year's team is said to have a weak pitching staff.
en.notes: 陣 originally means a battle formation or a field camp, as in 陣を張る ("to pitch camp, to take up position") or 背水の陣 ("with one's back to the wall"). Today it is mainly productive as a suffix for a group or team: 報道陣 ("press corps"), 首脳陣 ("leadership"), 投手陣 ("pitching staff"). Compounds such as 陣営 ("camp, faction") have their own cards.

examples[].german: "Government of the people, by the people, for the people" is a famous saying of Lincoln's.
The revolution succeeded through the power of the people.
en.notes: The people of a state, often with a political tone: 中華人民共和国 (People's Republic of China). More neutral: 国民, 市民.

examples[].german: That eccentric building astonished the public.
A major incident occurred that shook the public.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese, written-language reading of 人目; in everyday speech and in fixed phrases such as 人目を引く or 人目を気にする, it is almost always read ひとめ (separate card). じんもく appears mainly in elevated phrases such as 人目を驚かす "to cause a stir" or 人目を聳動する "to shake the public". Without a reading aid, ひとめ is the standard reading.

examples[].german: At this level of radiation, there is no effect on the human body.
About 60 percent of the human body is made of water.
en.notes: Technical/formal: 人体への影響 (effects on humans), 人体実験 (human experimentation). In everyday speech: 体.

examples[].german: A single landowner owns the land around here.
I rented a field with the landowner's permission.
en.notes: The owner of a plot of land, which he often leases out. The landlord of an apartment is called 大家.

examples[].german: He keeps practicing on his own even after class.
This school values the independence of its students.
en.notes: Often in compounds: 自主的 (voluntary), 自主練習 (self-directed practice), 自主規制 (voluntary restraint). Similar sound: 自首.

en.meaning: turning oneself in; surrender (to the police)
examples[].german: The culprit turned himself in to the police the next day.
Persuaded by his family, he decided to turn himself in.
en.notes: A perpetrator surrenders to the police before being identified: 警察に自首する. Similar sound: 自主.

examples[].german: The kanji on this stone monument are written in the old character forms.
This typeface is easy to read on a screen.
en.notes: The form of a written character (新字体 vs. 旧字体, e.g. 国 and 國) and the typeface of a text. Similar sound: 事態, 辞退.

examples[].german: The Earth rotates once a day.
Day and night occur because of the Earth's rotation.
en.notes: The turning of a celestial body around its own axis; its movement around the sun is called 公転. Not to be confused with 自転車.

examples[].german: He is an entrepreneur who succeeded at a young age.
My grandfather was a well-known businessman in town.
en.notes: Someone who runs or has founded a company. 実業 refers to commerce and industry as opposed to science or politics.

examples[].german: She met her birth mother for the first time in twenty years.
To tell the truth, I don't really understand either.
en.notes: Prenominal word (連体詞): 実の親 (biological parents), 実の兄弟 (blood siblings). Also "truly": 実のところ (in truth).

en.meaning: assistant, auxiliary, supporting (prefix, e.g. 助監督, 助教, 助演)
examples[].german: My older brother works on a film set as an assistant director.
She won the best supporting actress award for this film.
After graduate school, he became an assistant professor at a regional university.
en.notes: Prefix before job and role designations that marks a helping, subordinate position: 助監督 "assistant director", 助演 "supporting role", 助教 "assistant professor". To be distinguished from 副〜 "vice-, deputy" (副社長), which implies authority to act as a substitute. 助 does not occur as an independent word; cf. also 助手 "assistant" (card).

examples[].german: The protagonist of the story is depicted as an imposing, dignified man.
The poet praised him as a hero because he did not fear danger in order to save the villagers.
en.notes: 丈夫（じょうふ）in elevated or older language denotes a man portrayed as brave and imposing. It is a noun: 堂々たる丈夫 describes a man of impressive bearing. In present-day conversation the term sounds unusual. The reading じょうぶ, by contrast, mostly means "healthy, sturdy" or "durable" and belongs to a different use of the same kanji.

en.meaning: Ms.; Madam (respectful title for distinguished women)
examples[].german: At the lecture, Ms. Suzuki spoke about environmental issues.
Ms. Brown served as chair of the meeting.
en.notes: Placed after the name of a distinguished woman (scholar, artist, politician): 山田女史. Rather old-fashioned and literary today. Not to be confused with 女子 (girl, women's), which is read the same.

en.meaning: article, section, clause (e.g. 第九条); counter for strips and lines (counter)
examples[].german: We discussed Article 9 of the Constitution in class.
Article 5 of the contract states the conditions for cancellation.
A single ray of light shone in between the clouds.
en.notes: Mainly in references to laws and contracts: 第〇条 ("Article ..."), e.g. 憲法第9条 ("Article 9 of the Constitution"); the subdivision below it is called 項. As a literary counter for strips and lines (一条の光 "a ray of light"). It appears in 条件, 条約, 条例 and 信条.

examples[].german: If you keep an animal for a long time, you grow attached to it, whatever it is.
He is warm-hearted and cannot leave people in trouble alone.
en.notes: Warm feelings and sympathy: 情が深い (warm-hearted), 情が移る (to grow attached), 情に流される (to be swayed by emotion).

en.meaning: old man (Noh role/mask); white ash of charcoal; hist. third official rank (判官) in the guard offices of the ritsuryo system
examples[].german: In the Noh play "Takasago", the old man and the old woman appear as spirits of the pines.
The charcoal in the brazier was completely covered with white ash.
In the guard offices of the ritsuryo system, the jo was the third of the four official ranks.
en.notes: As an independent word, it appears today only in technical contexts: in Noh, 尉 denotes the role or mask of the old man (counterpart 姥 "old woman"), and also the white ash on glowing charcoal. The officer ranks 大尉, 中尉, 少尉 and the collective term 尉官 contain the same kanji, but are read with い and are not this word. Do not confuse it with the identically sounding cards 上, 状, 畳 and 情.

en.meaning: jō (old unit of length, ten shaku, approx. 3.03 m); length; honorific suffix for actors' names
examples[].german: In the old units of measurement, one jō is ten shaku, about three meters.
In an old temple in Nara, a Buddha statue one jō and six shaku tall is enshrined.
In theater reviews, 丈 is attached after the names of kabuki actors to show respect.
en.notes: Traditional unit of length: 一丈 = 十尺 (approx. 3.03 m), usually with a numeral such as 一丈, 三丈; familiar from 丈六 "Buddha statue of 1 jō 6 shaku". As a suffix after the names of kabuki actors, 丈 expresses respect. Do not confuse it with the kanji in the reading たけ ("height, length", e.g. 身の丈) or with 丈夫 (じょうぶ "sturdy"). Obsolete in everyday use; today mostly in historical and literary texts.

en.meaning: unmarried young woman; Miss (suffix after names); -girl, -lady (suffix for occupations, e.g. 受付嬢)
examples[].german: I asked the receptionist where the meeting room was.
The engagement of Miss Yamada was announced in the newspaper.
The little girl next door turns five this year.
en.notes: Rare on its own; mostly a suffix: after names (山田嬢 "Miss Yamada", formal and old-fashioned) or in job titles such as 受付嬢 "receptionist", 案内嬢 "hostess", which are often regarded as old-fashioned today (more neutral: 受付係). The polite form of address for someone else's daughter or a young lady is お嬢さん (separate card), and familiarly also 嬢ちゃん. Do not confuse it with the homophones 上, 状, 畳, 情.

examples[].german: He placed high in the marathon.
This product is near the top of the popularity ranking.
en.notes: A higher place in a ranking: 上位に入る (to place among the top). Opposite: 下位.

en.meaning: area around a castle; castle town
examples[].german: Old samurai residences remain in the castle town.
In the Edo period, many merchants lived around the castle.
en.notes: The area below and around a castle; mostly in 城下町 (castle town). Homophone: 浄化.

examples[].german: An airplane flew low over the town.
Cold air has moved in high up, so it is more likely to snow.
en.notes: The sky above a place: 東京の上空 (the sky over Tokyo), 上空の寒気 (cold air aloft).

en.meaning: landing; going ashore; landfall (of a typhoon)
examples[].german: Typhoon No. 10 is expected to make landfall in Kyushu tonight.
The ship reached the harbor and the passengers went ashore on the island.
en.notes: 〜する: to go ashore from a ship (passengers, troops). Also of a typhoon hitting land: 台風が上陸する.

examples[].german: All kinds of trees are planted in the park.
Many trees were knocked down by the typhoon.
en.notes: Neutral term for trees in general, e.g. in science or urban planning: 樹木を植える (to plant trees).

en.meaning: to correspond to; to follow; to be treated as equal to
examples[].german: Detailed procedures are carried out in accordance with these rules.
Part-time employees also receive allowances equivalent to those of regular employees.
en.notes: Literary Ichidan verb, mostly 〜に準じる/〜に準じて (in accordance with, according to): 規則に準じて処理する (to handle according to the rules). Also 準ずる.

examples[].german: The semi-express arrives earlier than the local train.
The semi-express does not stop at this station.
en.notes: Short for 準急行: stops more often than an 急行 but less often than a 各駅停車. Train types differ by railway company.

en.meaning: to correspond to; to follow; to be treated as equal to
examples[].german: A prize will be given to the winner or to those with results equivalent to that.
This qualification is treated as equivalent to a university degree.
en.notes: Literary; same meaning as 準じる, but conjugated like a ずる verb. Common in regulations: これに準ずる (equivalent to this).

examples[].german: She set a new Japanese record in the 100 meters.
After the war, a new government was established.
en.notes: To create something lasting: 政権を樹立する (to establish a government), 新記録を樹立する (to set a new record).

examples[].german: Of clothing, food and housing, the cost of housing is the largest.
This organization works to support housing for the elderly.
A safe living environment is indispensable for raising children.
en.notes: Rarely appears alone; as an independent noun mostly in enumerations such as 食と住 or in reference to 衣食住 "clothing, food, shelter" (card). More often it is part of words such as 住環境 "living environment", 住宅 or 住居. For a concrete dwelling, 住まい or 家 is said in everyday speech.

examples[].german: This factory has five hundred employees.
Please enter through the staff-only entrance.
en.notes: All the people who work at a business: 従業員数 (number of employees). More general than 社員.

examples[].german: This sword has been handed down through the generations as a family treasure.
Treasures preserved at the temple were shown to the general public for the first time.
This is a famous painting that could be called a national treasure.
en.notes: In the meaning "precious treasure, valuable heirloom", 重宝 is read じゅうほう; in the far more common meaning "handy, useful; to use gladly", on the other hand, ちょうほう (card 重宝/ちょうほう, e.g. 重宝する). じゅうほう is written-language and occurs mainly with family heirlooms, temple treasures and works of art. Close in meaning are 宝物 and 家宝.

examples[].german: Turn right at the next intersection.
I am now at a crossroads in my life.
en.notes: A cross-shaped road intersection; figuratively a turning point: 人生の十字路 (a crossroads in life).

en.meaning: going off duty; end of guard duty
examples[].german: As the time for going off duty approached, the next guard came to the gate.
After going off duty, the soldiers rested in their quarters.
en.notes: 下番（かばん）denotes the end of an assigned duty, especially in the military. As a noun it appears, for example, in 下番の時刻 "time of going off duty" or 下番後 "after duty". 下番する is also possible. The opposite 上番（じょうばん）denotes the start of duty. The similar-sounding かばん "bag" is a different word.

en.meaning: to get a rash; to be overly influenced
examples[].german: The new cosmetics gave me a skin rash.
Since studying abroad, he has become completely smitten with everything foreign.
en.notes: Skin reaction: 漆にかぶれる (to get a rash from lacquer). Figuratively, mostly derogatory: 西洋かぶれ (overly Westernized). Noun: かぶれ (N4).

en.meaning: gate; entrance to a house (reading かど)
examples[].german: My grandfather was waiting for me outside the gate.
Since there was no answer, I knocked on the gate once more.
en.notes: In this entry 門 is read かど and means the gate or entrance of a house. 門の外 names the area outside the gate; 門をたたく means to knock on the gate. The same writing can also be read もん. The reading かど also appears in 門口（かどぐち）. 角（かど）meaning corner is a different word.

examples[].german: When hydrogen and oxygen combine, water is formed.
In this experiment, we observe the combination of two substances.
en.notes: As a verb 化合する; the result is called 化合物 (N2) (compound).

examples[].german: In biological classification, the kingdom is a rank above the phylum.
The teacher asked whether these two organisms belong to the same kingdom.
en.notes: 界 here is the biological "kingdom", a level in the classification of living things. It lies above 門 and below the superordinate domain. Words such as 動物界 and 植物界 name individual kingdoms; as a noun, 界 can also denote the rank itself or one of these kingdoms. The classification and the number of kingdoms depend on the system used. The meaning "world or social sphere" in 政界 is a different use.

examples[].german: That team has been languishing near the bottom all season.
In the sales ranking, this product was near the bottom.
en.notes: Opposite: 上位. 下位に落ちる (to drop down the ranking), 下位チーム (a bottom-ranked team).

examples[].german: The new rule was criticized as a change for the worse rather than an improvement.
The app update made it harder to use, and it felt like a downgrade.
en.notes: Opposite: 改善／改良. Often critical of changes to rules or laws: それは改悪だ (that makes things worse).

examples[].german: The prime ministers of the two countries held talks for two hours.
The content of the talks was not made public.
en.notes: Mostly between politicians or heads of companies: 首脳会談 (summit meeting). Homophones: 階段 (stairs), 怪談 (ghost story).

examples[].german: The children picked up seashells on the beach.
I received a necklace made of shells.
en.notes: The shellfish as an animal or food is called 貝.

en.meaning: nursing; looking after (a sick or drunk person)
examples[].german: I looked after my dead-drunk colleague until morning.
A nearby shop clerk was tending to the person who had collapsed on the street.
en.notes: Short-term care: 酔った友達を介抱する (to look after a drunk friend). Long-term care is called 介護 or 看病. Homophone: 解放 (liberation).

examples[].german: In the past, the class one was born into determined one's occupation.
He held a high rank in the military.
en.notes: 社会階級 (social class), 軍の階級 (military rank); in sports also a weight class.

examples[].german: The meeting materials were circulated within the department.
Please pass this document on to the next person after reading it.
en.notes: A document is passed on from person to person in turn: 回覧する. Neighborhood notices go around via the 回覧板 (N4).

examples[].german: We will collect the questionnaire forms tomorrow.
After a defect was found, the manufacturer recalled the product.
en.notes: As a verb 回収する: ゴミの回収 (garbage collection), 製品の回収 (product recall), 資金を回収する (to recover funds).

examples[].german: This bus is out of service, so you can't board.
I had my mail forwarded to my new address.
en.notes: On trains and buses, the sign 回送 means no passengers are carried. To forward mail: 回送する.

examples[].german: Japan's trade depends heavily on sea transport.
Sea transport takes longer than air freight, but it is cheaper.
en.notes: Freight transport by sea; the industry is called 海運業.

examples[].german: In the past, you could buy things on credit at neighborhood shops.
At the end of the month, you pay the bills for credit purchases all at once.
en.notes: 掛けで買う (to buy on credit), 掛けで売る (to sell on credit). Today mainly in business dealings; colloquially also ツケ.

examples[].german: I was about to be late, so I ran to the station.
There is little time, so I will explain it quickly.
en.notes: 駆け足で (at a run, in haste): 駆け足で説明する (to explain something in a rush).

en.meaning: to stir; to rummage through; to stir up (confusion)
examples[].german: I slowly stirred the soup in the pot.
A remark by the newcomer threw the meeting into disarray.
en.notes: Literally: スープをかき回す (to stir soup). Figuratively: 会議をかき回す (to stir up a meeting). Kanji 掻き回す.

en.meaning: to write down; to take down
examples[].german: I hurriedly jotted down the phone number on a memo.
I wrote down every word the teacher said.
en.notes: To write down what is spoken: 先生の話を書き取る. Noun: 書き取り (dictation).

en.meaning: epoch-making turning point; start of a new era
examples[].german: This discovery marked a major turning point in the history of research.
The end of the war became a turning point dividing this country's history.
en.notes: 画期（かっき）is a noun for a break that separates a past era from a new one. It is used in factual or historical language, for example in 画期をなす "to form an epochal turning point". The na-adjective "groundbreaking, epoch-making" is 画期的（かっきてき）; the bare 画期 is not used as an adjective here. The rarer writing 劃期 is also attested. 活気（かっき）"liveliness" means something different.

examples[].german: Please measure the angle formed by these two straight lines.
The bishop in shogi is a piece that moves diagonally.
en.notes: 角 is read かく here and means a geometric angle. In the Japanese chess variant shogi, 角 is the short form of 角行（かくぎょう）, a piece that moves diagonally. With 角を測る you measure an angle; in the game, the meaning is clear from the context of the pieces. 角 read かど means corner, and read つの it means horn or antler.

examples[].german: While reading the poetry collection, I underlined lines that stayed in my mind.
At the haiku gathering, the teacher presented the participants' fine haiku.
en.notes: 佳句（かく）denotes an especially beautiful or successful phrasing in a poem; an outstanding haiku can also be called that. The word belongs to literary criticism and sounds elevated. It does not denote arbitrary everyday sentences. In conversations about poetry, the context is usually needed. 書く "to write", 画 "stroke" and 核 "core" are different words despite the same reading.

examples[].german: This stroke is too long; please make it a little shorter.
The teacher marked the last stroke with a red pen.
en.notes: 画（かく）here denotes a stroke or dot made in one continuous motion of writing that helps build up a kanji. In writing, one speaks, for example, of the last 画 of a character. It is an independent noun; the identically written counter after a number is treated separately. The reading が for a picture and the verb 書く（かく）are different words.

examples[].german: Our store accepts various credit cards.
This factory makes various kinds of parts.
en.notes: Formal, often on signs and in advertisements. More everyday: いろいろな.

examples[].german: In the old days, water was stored in a jar in the kitchen.
My grandmother pickles umeboshi in a clay pot.
This brewery ages shochu in large clay jars.
en.notes: 甕 is a large, bulging vessel made of clay for storing water, sake, miso or pickles: 水がめ "water jar", 甕に漬ける "to pickle in a clay pot". It is also written 瓶, but 瓶 is usually read びん "bottle" (own card); the context decides. The similar-sounding 亀/かめ "turtle" is an entirely different word. Because the kanji 甕 is difficult, かめ is often seen in kana.

examples[].german: Grades are given by taking attendance into account along with exam scores.
Modern ideas were added to the traditional dish.
en.notes: Mostly figurative: 〜を加味する (to factor in ...): 経験を加味して評価する (to evaluate with experience taken into account).

en.meaning: to bite through; to bite off
examples[].german: This meat is so tough that I can't bite through it.
The dog bit through the rope and ran away.
en.notes: Also written かみ切る.

examples[].german: The renovated station looks like a different building from before.
The mountains lit by the setting sun presented the sight of a magnificent painting.
en.notes: As an independent noun, 観（かん）denotes the outward appearance or the impression something gives. ～の観がある means roughly "looks like ..."; ～の観を呈する describes an appearance in elevated language. A personal worldview, by contrast, is expressed by compounds such as 人生観.

en.meaning: ceremonial headwear; crown; historical coming-of-age ceremony
examples[].german: In this picture, the emperor is wearing a ceremonial headdress.
Red jewels were set in the gold crown.
In ancient China, the coming-of-age ceremony was called "kan".
en.notes: The independent reading 冠（かん）appears in scholarly or historical texts for a ceremonial headdress or crown. More everyday is かんむり. In descriptions of ancient Chinese customs, 冠 can also denote the ceremony in which a young man first receives the headwear of an adult; this is not a general meaning "to name".

examples[].german: In this project, the public and private sectors are cooperating.
The report clarified the role of the government in disaster preparedness.
en.notes: 官 means the state or public administration and, in formal texts, is often contrasted with 民, the private sector. 官と民 names both sides, 官の役割 speaks of the task of the governmental side. The word is not a personal form of address for an individual official. For the government, 政府 is used, and for a specific agency 官庁 is often more accurate; here the public side as a whole is meant.

examples[].german: This region continues to preserve its textile technique, outstanding in the world.
At that time, the university had research facilities unsurpassed in the country.
en.notes: 冠（かん）appears in elevated language, especially in the pattern ～に冠たる: "outstanding among/in ...". たる connects the word to the following noun, as in 世界に冠たる技術. Here it is not an ordinary な-adjective and refers neither to headwear nor to the number of titles won.

examples[].german: My experience of studying abroad changed my outlook on life.
To work together, it is important to understand each other's values.
en.notes: The ending 観（かん）forms words for a particular way of seeing: 人生観 is an outlook on life, 価値観 are values. The compound denotes the perspective on a topic, not simply its visible surface. With が or を, the whole compound noun is worked into the sentence.

en.meaning: iron rod, crowbar; iron club (鬼に金棒)
examples[].german: If he, with all his experience, joins the team, it will be like giving an ogre an iron club.
In the Setsubun picture book, a red oni holding an iron club is drawn.
In the past, night watchmen walked through the town striking an iron rod on the ground.
en.notes: 金棒 "iron rod, iron club" is known mainly as the weapon of the oni and from the saying 鬼に金棒 "like an oni with an iron club", i.e. "even stronger, practically unbeatable". The rare spelling 鉄棒 is listed here as an alias; read normally, however, 鉄棒/てつぼう means "horizontal bar" (separate card). For an ordinary crowbar, バール is more commonly said today.

en.meaning: to be no match for; to be unbearable
examples[].german: When it comes to cooking, I'm no match for my mother.
If it's this hot every day, I can't stand it.
en.notes: 〜にはかなわない (cannot compete with ...); この暑さにはかなわない (this heat is unbearable).

examples[].german: I drove a nail in with a hammer.
To tell the truth, I'm a non-swimmer and can't swim at all.
en.notes: A tool for nailing. Jokingly also for someone who can't swim: 私は金槌です (I sink like a hammer).

examples[].german: The company's executives gathered and discussed the future direction.
He became a party executive at a young age.
en.notes: The leadership of an organization (company, party, police): 会社の幹部 (company executive), 幹部候補 (management candidate).

examples[].german: This microphone is very sensitive and picks up even quiet voices.
In the mountains, radio reception gets poor.
en.notes: How sensitively a device, film or sensor responds; for radio and mobile phones also the reception quality: 感度がいい／悪い (good / poor reception).

en.meaning: treasury, money storehouse; financial backer, patron
examples[].german: The large merchant houses of the past had splendid money storehouses.
Thieves broke into the lord's treasury.
He has supported this theater troupe as its financial backer for many years.
en.notes: Historical word for the fireproof storehouse (蔵) in which lords and merchants kept their money; familiar from samurai dramas, for example 金蔵破り "breaking into the treasury". Figuratively also "financial backer, patron". Today's safe is called 金庫 (vocab-n3:2721); the reading きんぞう is obsolete.

examples[].german: I was finally able to go to the shop I had wanted to visit for a long time.
I would like to report on the matter you requested earlier.
en.notes: Elevated, mostly かねてから／かねてより (for some time now). The kanji 予て is rare.

examples[].german: She works in nursing at a hospital.
After the accident, my mother devotedly nursed my father.
en.notes: Care of the sick; as a verb 看護する. Nurse: 看護師. Home care of relatives is often called 看病.

en.meaning: concise; succinct; brief and to the point
examples[].german: Please explain the main points concisely.
His emails are always concise and easy to understand.
The report should be summarized concisely on one page.
en.notes: A na-adjective for brief, clear presentation, mostly adverbial as 簡潔に (簡潔に説明する, 簡潔にまとめる). Unlike 簡単 "simple, easy", 簡潔 describes only style and expression, not difficulty. Do not confuse it with the homophone 完結 "conclusion, completion".

examples[].german: Strong cold air is flowing in from the north.
Because of the cold air, it will probably snow tomorrow.
en.notes: Mainly in weather reports: 寒気が流れ込む (cold air flows in). Read さむけ, the same word means "chills, shivering".

examples[].german: Japanese business practices can be hard for foreign companies to understand.
In accordance with a long-standing custom, the president gives a speech at the first meeting of the new year.
The government decided to review old practices.
en.notes: 慣行 is a formal word for an established practice in business, administration or society: 商慣行 "trade custom", 慣行に従う "to follow the usual practice", 慣行を改める. Attributively it takes の (慣行の手続き); it is not used as a する-verb. For personal habits, one says 習慣; 慣例 is a close synonym. Do not confuse it with the homophones 観光 "tourism" and 刊行 "publication".

examples[].german: Publication of this magazine will begin next month.
The university's publications are lined up in the library.
Publication of the complete works was delayed by a year from the plan.
en.notes: A written-language noun for publishing books, magazines or series: 刊行物 "publication", 定期刊行物 "periodical", 刊行が始まる. The verb form is on the card 刊行する; in everyday speech, one rather says 出版 or 発行. Do not confuse it with the homophones 観光 "tourism" and 慣行 "custom".

examples[].german: My long-held dream has come true, and I am deeply moved.
Seeing her son at the graduation ceremony, the mother seemed overwhelmed with emotion.
en.notes: A feeling that cannot be put into words, mostly on achievements or farewells: 感無量です (I am deeply moved).

examples[].german: He cheated during the exam and was caught by the teacher.
A paper on which cheating occurred gets zero points.
en.notes: From English "cunning"; in Japanese it means only "copying on an exam". As a verb カンニングする.

examples[].german: The department head has an air of authority.
The victorious yokozuna showed a commanding bout.
en.notes: An impressive, dignified presence, often from experience or position: 貫禄がある, 貫禄十分.

examples[].german: How much is this price converted into euros?
One hour converted into minutes is sixty minutes.
en.notes: Converting into another unit or currency: 円に換算する, ドル換算で (in dollar terms). As a verb 換算する.

examples[].german: When the fireworks went up, a loud cheer rose.
The children ran to the sea, shouting with joy.
en.notes: Loud shouts of joy from a crowd: 歓声が上がる, 歓声を上げる. Homophone: 完成 (completion).

examples[].german: An accident stopped the main line, and many people were affected.
A major arterial road runs through the center of the town.
en.notes: The main line of a transport or utility network: 幹線道路 (arterial road). 新幹線 literally means "new trunk line".

examples[].german: Fifty thousand spectators watched the match.
When the winning goal was scored, the whole crowd jumped to their feet.
en.notes: The crowd of spectators at an event, especially in sports. For concerts and lectures 聴衆 is more usual, in general 観客.

examples[].german: This reading is originally incorrect, but it is accepted as established usage.
The dictionary also lists meanings that come from common usage.
en.notes: What has become generally accepted through habit, especially in language use: 慣用的な表現, 慣用読み. Idiom: 慣用句.

examples[].german: He has the physique of an athlete.
Even brothers can have quite different builds.
en.notes: Appearance of the body: がっしりした体つき (a sturdy build). Also written 体付き.

en.meaning: to dry up; to run dry
examples[].german: The drought continued and the well ran dry.
I have cried so much that my tears have run dry.
en.notes: Of springs and wells, or figuratively of strength and tears: 井戸が涸れる, 涙が涸れる. Often also written 枯れる, which actually means "to wither".

examples[].german: I owe him one for helping me.
I will definitely repay you for the other day.
en.notes: 借りがある (to owe someone, also a favor), 借りを返す (to pay back a favor). Opposite: 貸し.

en.meaning: to become hazy; to blur (vision); to be overshadowed
examples[].german: The mountains in the distance look hazy.
I was tired and my eyes began to blur.
en.notes: 目が霞む (one's eyes blur). Figuratively: 彼の活躍で他の選手が霞んだ (next to his performance, the other players were overshadowed).

examples[].german: The earthquake turned the town into ruins in an instant.
With a single failure, all his efforts came to nothing.
en.notes: Literary, mostly 〜と化する／〜と化す: 町は廃墟と化した. As a suffix 〜化 (-ization): 自動化 (automation).

en.meaning: to graze, to brush against; to skim off (a share)
examples[].german: The bullet only grazed his arm, so there was no serious injury.
The shot grazed the goalpost and went wide.
It turned out that the middleman had been skimming off part of the sales.
en.notes: Godan verb, almost always written in kana: 弾が腕をかする "the bullet grazes the arm"; in the negative often かすりもしない "not even come close". Do not confuse it with 擦る/する "to rub" (vocab-n2:2006), which has the same kanji, nor with 化する/かする "to turn into" (a different word, a suru verb). The meaning "to skim off, to pocket a share" is colloquial and derogatory.

examples[].german: Because of information overload, I can't find the article I need.
Oversupply continued in the market, and prices fell.
en.notes: 過多 denotes too large an amount, mostly in factual or technical language. It often follows a noun, for example 情報過多 "information overload" or 供給過多 "oversupply". Unlike 多い, it explicitly means "too much". As a na-adjective, 過多な is also possible; it is not an i-adjective. The identically read words 肩 and 型 have other meanings.

en.meaning: temperament, typical mentality (often as a suffix, e.g. 職人気質, 昔気質)
examples[].german: My grandfather was a carpenter of the old school and hated sloppy work above all.
With his craftsman's temperament, he remakes things as many times as it takes until he is satisfied.
The shop owner has the typical Edo temperament: generous, but sharp-tongued.
en.notes: The reading かたぎ appears almost only as a suffix after a noun and refers to the typical mentality of a group or an era: 職人気質, 昔気質, 江戸っ子気質. The card 気質/きしつ is the neutral word, also used in psychology, for the temperament of an individual (気質が穏やか); 職人気質 is sometimes also read with きしつ. Do not confuse it with 堅気 "respectable, solid (not in the underworld)", which is also read かたぎ.

en.meaning: rival, archenemy (someone you have a score to settle with); revenge
examples[].german: For some reason the department head has it in for me.
To avenge his father, he continued his sword training.
We have been business rivals with the shop next door for years.
en.notes: Native Japanese reading of 敵 for a personal enemy or rival, mainly in fixed phrases: 目の敵にする "to have it in for someone", 敵を討つ "to take revenge", 商売敵 "business rival", 恋敵 "love rival" (in compounds voiced: がたき). For revenge, 仇 is often written (仇討ち). The general enemy in war or opponent in sports is 敵/てき (vocab-n2:116).

en.meaning: and at the same time; moreover
examples[].german: This work needs to be done quickly and accurately.
He is excellent and, moreover, a good person.
en.notes: Literary conjunction between two qualities or actions: 迅速かつ正確に (quickly and accurately). Usually written in hiragana かつ.

en.meaning: side; case of a watch (reading かわ)
examples[].german: Please open the box from this side.
The case of this watch is made of silver.
en.notes: 側 is read かわ here. It means a side and can also mean the case of a watch. With ～の側 you specify which side or which case is meant. The other common reading of the same word for side is がわ; this card specifically practices かわ. The reading そば, by contrast, means the immediate vicinity. 川（かわ）means river and belongs to a different word. The examples use 側 as a noun; the pronunciation of compound direction words is learned as a whole word each time.

examples[].german: It was a long trip, so the three of us took turns driving.
The children took turns holding the puppy.
en.notes: Several people do the same thing one after another: 代わる代わる運転する (to take turns driving).

examples[].german: In the morning I exchanged greetings with the neighbors.
The two formally signed a contract.
en.notes: あいさつを交わす (to exchange greetings), 契約を交わす (to conclude a contract). After a ます-stem: 〜交わす (... one another): 酌み交わす (to pour drinks for each other).

examples[].german: In China, many people eat rice porridge for breakfast.
When your stomach is upset, soft rice porridge is good.
en.notes: In daily life usually called politely お粥; a typical food when ill. On January 7th, 七草がゆ (seven-herb rice porridge) is traditionally eaten.

examples[].german: In old tales, a terrible beast living in the mountains attacks the village.
To hurt people and feel nothing, he is nothing but a beast.
en.notes: Wild animal; today mainly pejorative for a cruel person: あいつはけだものだ. Neutral word for animals: 獣（けもの）.

examples[].german: I can't accept such filthy money.
Even listening to him is disgusting.
en.notes: Morally repulsive or impure, mostly as a strong expression of disgust: 汚らわしいお金.

en.meaning: to be defiled; to be desecrated; to become (morally or ritually) impure
examples[].german: I feel that if I keep lying, my heart will become impure.
People in the past believed that contact with death made one ritually impure.
The sacred land was desecrated by the war.
en.notes: けがれる means becoming morally or ritually impure, for example through lies, crimes, or, according to traditional belief, contact with death; the related noun is 汚れ/穢れ（けがれ）. For physical soiling (服が汚れる), the reading is よごれる (own card). The word is elevated and written-language and is often written 穢れる to make the reading unambiguous. The transitive counterpart is 汚す（けがす）.

en.meaning: to dishonor; to defile; to desecrate
examples[].german: I don't want to do anything that would dishonor my father's name.
He tarnished the school's honor by cheating.
You must not desecrate a sacred place.
en.notes: The reading けがす means moral or ritual defilement: 名を汚す "to dishonor the name", 家名を汚す, 神聖な場所を汚す. For physical soiling (服を汚す), the reading is よごす (own card). Since both readings are written the same, the context decides; けがす is elevated and written-language and is also written 穢す.

examples[].german: The defendant was sentenced to five years of imprisonment.
He finished serving his sentence and returned to society.
en.notes: Court-imposed punishment: 刑が確定する (the sentence becomes final), 刑に服する (to serve a sentence), 懲役三年の刑.

examples[].german: Inspector Tanaka is in charge of the investigation.
He was promoted to inspector at a young age.
en.notes: A rank in the Japanese police, roughly "inspector"; familiar from crime dramas.

examples[].german: A letter begins with "Haikei" and ends with "Keigu".
At the end I wrote Keigu and added the date and my name.
en.notes: Formal closing phrase of a letter, matching the salutation 拝啓 at the beginning.

examples[].german: We moved our bodies to lively music.
Since he started taking the medicine, the symptoms have been improving.
en.notes: な-adjective: light-footed and spirited (軽快な足取り, 軽快な音楽); in medicine: symptoms subside (症状が軽快する). Homophone: 警戒.

examples[].german: The pilot checked the instruments before takeoff.
The indoor humidity is measured with this instrument.
en.notes: An instrument for measuring, e.g. in a cockpit: 計器を確認する. Homophone: 景気 (economic conditions).

examples[].german: Childhood experiences influence the formation of personality.
The flow of the river formed this valley.
en.notes: The coming into being or taking shape of a form: 人格形成 (personality formation), 形成する. Homophone: 形勢.

en.meaning: situation; state of affairs; balance of power
examples[].german: In the second half, the situation was reversed.
The state of the election is still unclear.
en.notes: How a contest currently stands: 形勢が不利になる (the situation turns unfavorable), 形勢を逆転する (to turn the tables). Homophone: 形成.

examples[].german: This road is steep, so it's hard on a bicycle.
We gave the roof a slight slope so that the rain runs off.
en.notes: Degree of inclination: 急な傾斜 (steep slope), 傾斜地 (sloping ground). As a verb: 傾斜する.

examples[].german: The forms of working have become more diverse.
Insects change their form greatly as they grow.
en.notes: The outer form or organizational form: 雇用形態 (form of employment), 生活形態 (lifestyle). Homophone: 携帯.

examples[].german: The sports day will be held even if it rains.
The execution of the plan was postponed to next month.
en.notes: To carry something out resolutely, often despite adverse conditions: 雨天決行 (held rain or shine). As a verb 決行する. Homophone: 結構.

examples[].german: I heard the cry of a beast deep in the forest.
Animal footprints were left in the snow.
en.notes: A furry, four-legged animal: 獣道 (animal trail). As a derogatory term for a cruel person, 獣（けだもの）is more usual.

en.meaning: to smoke; to smolder; to be hazy (from rain, fog)
examples[].german: The damp firewood hardly burns and just smolders.
Kyoto, veiled in rain, was very beautiful.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: to give off smoke or to appear as if wrapped in haze: 雨に煙る町 (a town veiled in rain).

en.meaning: smoky; uncomfortable (of a person one feels awkward around)
examples[].german: The room is smoky from cigarettes.
The strict department head is somewhat of an intimidating presence for young employees.
en.notes: い-adjective: full of smoke that stings the eyes; figuratively a person whose presence one finds uncomfortable (煙たい上司).

examples[].german: I'd like to talk to you briefly about that matter.
