We decided to leave that matter to the department head.
en.notes: The matter under discussion, especially in business: その件については後で連絡します (I will contact you about that matter later). As a counter, 〜件 for cases and inquiries.

examples[].german: Having power can sometimes change a person.
Newspapers have the role of keeping watch over those in power.
en.notes: Political or social power over others: 権力を握る (to seize power), 権力者 (a person in power).

examples[].german: I entered a magazine sweepstakes and won a trip.
A reward was offered for information leading to the arrest of the criminal.
en.notes: A contest or campaign where one can win a prize (懸賞に応募する, to enter a sweepstakes), also a reward: 懸賞金 (reward money).

examples[].german: My grandfather is still going strong at ninety.
He is a retired player, but his popularity is still alive.
en.notes: Someone is in good health or something still works as before: 両親とも健在です (both my parents are well). Also for things: 昔の人気は健在だ (his old popularity is intact).

examples[].german: A sound mind lives in a sound body.
This company is soundly managed.
en.notes: な-adjective: physically and mentally healthy, but also "sound" regarding finances or society: 健全な経営 (sound management), 健全な精神 (a healthy mind).

examples[].german: Momotaro made the dog, the monkey and the pheasant his retainers.
The lord left the castle with his retainers.
en.notes: Historically: followers of a lord or samurai; today jocular for someone who serves another. Known from the fairy tale 桃太郎 (the dog, monkey and pheasant become his 家来).

examples[].german: I formed a band with friends from high school.
The formation of a new political party was announced.
en.notes: Founding of a party, band, union or club: バンドを結成する (to form a band). For companies 設立 is more usual.

examples[].german: We were able to win because the team was so tightly united.
The residents united and opposed the construction of the factory.
en.notes: Close cohesion of a group: チームの結束が固い (the team is tightly knit). As a verb 結束する (to unite).

en.meaning: to kick away; to flatly reject
examples[].german: The child is playing by kicking an empty can away.
He flatly rejected the company's proposal.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to kick something away with the foot; figuratively also to flatly reject an offer.

en.meaning: decision, vote (esp. 決を採る = to put to a vote)
examples[].german: The chairman put the bill to a vote.
Since all opinions have been voiced, let's take a vote soon.
When a vote was taken at the class meeting, fifteen were in favor.
en.notes: As a word in its own right it appears almost only in the meeting formula 決を採る (also 決を取る) "to bring to a vote, to have a vote taken". Equivalent in meaning, but more common, is 採決する (vocab-n3:1785 採決); otherwise 決 lives on in compounds such as 多数決, 可決, 否決. Formal, typical of parliament, clubs and conferences.

en.meaning: the best, top (counter suffix, e.g. 十傑 = the top ten, 三傑 = the great three)
examples[].german: He made it into this season's top ten batters.
The "Three Great Men of the Restoration" refers to Saigo Takamori, Okubo Toshimichi and Kido Takayoshi.
en.notes: Counting suffix that, after a number, denotes the best or most outstanding members of a group: 三傑 "the three greats", 十傑 (じっけつ) "the top ten". It occurs almost only in fixed combinations and in rankings from sports and history; in everyday speech ベストテン or トップテン is more usual. The same character is in 傑作 "masterpiece" and 豪傑 "hero".

examples[].german: A new rule was adopted at the general meeting.
The UN adopted a resolution calling for a ceasefire.
en.notes: A formal decision of an assembly or parliament; as a verb 決議する. Cf. 決定 (decision in general).

examples[].german: Water is formed by hydrogen and oxygen bonding together.
A new product was born from combining the technologies of the two companies.
en.notes: The joining of two or more things, especially in chemistry and technology: 水素と酸素の結合 (the bonding of hydrogen and oxygen). As a verb 結合する.

examples[].german: My father drinks this whisky neat.
With this liquor, you can appreciate the aroma well when it is left undiluted.
en.notes: For drinks, 生（き）means "neat, without dilution". 生で飲む says how one drinks the beverage; 生のまま describes the unchanged state. The reading なま is used in other contexts, for example for raw food or draft beer, and is not the reading learned here.

examples[].german: Raw silk before degumming is used for this fabric.
At this shop, they make the sauce by adding sugar to pure soy sauce.
en.notes: As a prefix, 生（き）describes something unadulterated or not yet further processed. 生糸（きいと）is raw silk before further treatment; 生醤油（きじょうゆ）here means pure soy sauce not mixed with other ingredients. The reading belongs to each whole word and is to be distinguished from なま in other compounds.

examples[].german: Please put the tools you used back in their place neatly.
He is always neatly dressed.
en.notes: Colloquial variant of きちんと: carefully, fitting exactly: きちっと片付ける.

examples[].german: The neighbors' daughter is a good-natured girl.
She is less a beauty than a person with a gentle disposition.
en.notes: A person's nature, mostly positive: 気立てがいい／優しい (good-hearted).

examples[].german: This school has a free-spirited ethos.
The unpretentious character typical of an artisans' town has been preserved.
en.notes: The characteristic nature of a group, region, or era: 自由な気風, 下町の気風.

examples[].german: The culprit said he had no intention of harming the hostages.
This insect does no harm to people.
en.notes: Harm to life and limb inflicted on another person: 危害を加える (to harm someone). Formal, often used in news and warnings.

en.meaning: reserve; hesitation out of consideration for others
examples[].german: Don't hold back; please feel free to use it.
Out of consideration for my in-laws, I can hardly say what I really think.
en.notes: Inhibition out of consideration for others: 〜に気兼ねする, 気兼ねなく (without feeling constrained).

examples[].german: The old lady had an air of elegance.
This tea bowl has a refinement within its simplicity.
en.notes: A fine, dignified aura of a person or work of art: 気品がある, 気品にあふれる.

examples[].german: The heart is an important organ that pumps blood.
The leaves of plants are organs of photosynthesis.
en.notes: Bodily organ in the biological sense: 消化器官, 呼吸器官. An individual internal organ is often called 臓器 in everyday speech.

examples[].german: This magazine is a quarterly, published four times a year.
The university research group publishes a quarterly bulletin.
en.notes: Publication four times a year: 季刊誌 (quarterly journal). Compare 月刊 (monthly), 週刊 (weekly).

en.meaning: to dress up; to get dolled up
examples[].german: People dressed up for the occasion had gathered at the party.
My daughter has been dressing up since morning for her Coming of Age ceremony.
en.notes: To dress especially nicely, for example for celebrations: 着飾った人々. Godan verb.

examples[].german: More and more young people are abstaining from voting.
He withdrew from the final because of an injury.
en.notes: To give up a right, especially to not vote, or to withdraw from a competition. Homophone: 危険 (danger).

examples[].german: This medicine works quickly.
No matter how often I warned him, it had no effect on him.
en.notes: The effect of a remedy or measure: 効き目がある／ない, 効き目が現れる. Also written 利き目.

examples[].german: A fund was established to support the disaster area.
A scholarship fund was created through donations from graduates.
en.notes: Money set aside for a specific purpose, or the foundation that manages it: 奨学基金, 国際通貨基金 (IMF). Homophone: 飢饉 (famine).

examples[].german: The meeting started at nine o'clock sharp.
The change was exactly 500 yen.
en.notes: Exactly at a number or time: 九時きっかり, きっかり千円.

examples[].german: The mechanism of a watch is very complicated.
The government plans to reform the administrative structure.
en.notes: The structure and functioning of a machine or organization; also in names of organizations (〜機構).

examples[].german: The company president is scheduled to return to Tokyo tomorrow evening.
The Obon holidays are over, and the expressways are crowded with cars heading back to Tokyo.
en.notes: Returning to Tokyo, formal and literary: 帰京する. Homophone: 桔梗 (balloon flower).

examples[].german: Mountain weather is fickle.
On a mere whim, I took a different route home.
en.notes: Noun and な-adjective: a sudden notion or changeable nature: 気まぐれな天気, ほんの気まぐれで.

examples[].german: I got the name wrong and felt embarrassed.
He scratched his head sheepishly.
en.notes: The feeling of being ashamed or embarrassed: 決まり悪そうに笑う. Often also きまりが悪い.

en.meaning: end of a period (term, fiscal year)
examples[].german: Final exams start next week.
At the end of the period, the company gets busy preparing its closing of accounts.
en.notes: End of a school term or accounting period: 期末試験 (final exams), 期末決算.

examples[].german: Please write your name on the application form and hand it in at the reception.
You may fill out the survey with or without your name.
en.notes: Writing one's own name on a form or object: 記名する, 記名投票. Opposite: 無記名 (anonymous).

examples[].german: Let's wash our hands well to get rid of germs.
These germs multiply easily in damp places.
en.notes: Microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi: 菌が繁殖する, 大腸菌. Colloquially also ばい菌 (germs).

examples[].german: I'm nearsighted, so I can't see the blackboard without glasses.
My nearsightedness got worse from too much smartphone use.
en.notes: Colloquial for 近視 (nearsightedness). Opposite: 遠視 (farsightedness).

examples[].german: We plan to open a new branch soon.
The repair estimate is said to arrive shortly.
en.notes: きんきん announces an event in the near future without fixing an exact day. It stands as an adverb before the planned or expected action. The writings 近々 and 近近 are attested; 近々 is the form shown here. The word is also read ちかぢか. The spatial meaning "very close" belongs to the reading ちかぢか; this card practices the temporal きんきん.

en.meaning: something to be strictly avoided; taboo
examples[].german: Even if we are winning, complacency is taboo.
When you have a cold, overexertion is out of the question.
en.notes: What is harmful in a situation and should be avoided: 油断は禁物 (complacency is out of place).

en.meaning: first of the ten celestial stems (yang wood, Chinese calendar)
examples[].german: Kinoe is the first of the ten stems and means "elder brother of wood".
Koshien Stadium was named after the fact that the year it was completed was a Kinoe-Ne year.
The sexagenary-cycle year 2024 was Kinoe-Tatsu (Wood Dragon).
en.notes: Calendar term: the first of the ten celestial stems (十干), derived from 木の兄 "elder brother of wood". It appears mainly together with the twelve earthly branches as the name of a year in the sixty-year cycle, e.g. 甲子 (きのえね) or 甲辰 (きのえたつ). The same character is read こう when it means "first rank, party A (in a contract)" or "shell, carapace" (甲乙, 甲羅); the reading きのえ is purely calendrical.

examples[].german: November 23 is Labor Thanksgiving Day, a national holiday.
Under the Japanese Constitution, work is both a right and a duty of the citizens.
en.notes: Formal term for diligent, paid work: 勤労意欲, 勤労者. The holiday on November 23: 勤労感謝の日.

en.meaning: to prohibit; to forbid; to suppress
examples[].german: Smoking is prohibited in this building.
An order prohibiting going out at night was issued in that country.
en.notes: Literary ずる-variant of 禁じる (N4): 法律で禁ずる. Phrase: 〜を禁じ得ない (cannot help feeling ...).

examples[].german: She flatly turned down his invitation.
My father quit smoking for good last year.
en.notes: Clearly and without hesitation: きっぱり断る (to refuse flatly), きっぱりやめる (to quit for good).

examples[].german: Actors in gorgeous costumes danced on the stage.
The night town was bathed in dazzling lights.
en.notes: な-adjective: shiny and magnificent: きらびやかな衣装. The kanji 煌びやか is rare.

examples[].german: Living alone is nice and carefree.
Don't be so nervous; just take it easy.
en.notes: な-adjective: without pressure or worries: 気楽に考える, お気楽 (happy-go-lucky, often ironic).

examples[].german: The sun was visible through a gap in the clouds.
Please score the meat before grilling it.
en.notes: A place where something is interrupted or cut: 雲の切れ目, 切れ目を入れる (to make a cut).

examples[].german: Let's take a break at a good stopping point.
Once you start complaining, there is no end to it.
en.notes: A suitable point to stop: 切りのいいところで (at a good stopping point), 切りがない (to be endless). Often in kana: きり.

examples[].german: My grandmother keeps her kimonos in a paulownia chest.
When May comes, the paulownia flowers bloom purple.
Expensive tea bowls are sold in paulownia-wood boxes.
en.notes: 桐 is the paulownia (empress tree), a fast-growing tree with large leaves and violet flowers. Its light, moisture-resistant wood is used for 桐のたんす "clothing chest of paulownia wood", 桐の箱 and the instrument koto; the paulownia crest is the emblem of the Japanese government. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding 霧 "fog". In biology, it is written キリ.

examples[].german: The switchover to the new system will take place next month.
Even after a failure, he is someone who shifts his mindset quickly.
en.notes: Noun of 切り替える: switching, changing over: 気持ちの切り替え (changing one's mindset, putting something behind one), システムの切り替え.

examples[].german: The airplane hit turbulence and shook violently.
A warm air current rises along the mountain.
en.notes: Movement of air in the atmosphere: 乱気流 (turbulence), 上昇気流 (updraft).

examples[].german: The custom of drinking tea came to Japan from China.
This museum also has a cafe area.
en.notes: Drinking tea or coffee, also a short form for a cafe: 喫茶コーナー, 喫茶室. The cafe itself is usually called 喫茶店.

en.meaning: coming; upcoming; to come, to arrive
examples[].german: We will hold a commemorative ceremony on the coming May 10.
The long winter ended, and spring finally came.
en.notes: 来る／来たる with the reading きたる sounds elevated in announcements and solemn statements. Before a date, 来たる means "coming": 来たる五月. As a verb it denotes arrival, for example 時が来たる "the time comes". This reading follows Godan conjugation: きたります, きたった. It does not belong to the irregular conjugation of 来る／くる with きます and きた.

examples[].german: I paid back the borrowed money to the last yen.
Please close the lid of the bottle tightly.
en.notes: Exactly and without deviation: きっちり払う, 時間きっちりに. Also "snug, tight": ふたをきっちり閉める.

examples[].german: Nihonbashi was the starting point of the Tokaido.
This incident became the starting point of the reform.
en.notes: The starting point of a route or development: 東海道の起点. Opposite: 終点. Homophone: 機転 (quick wit).

en.meaning: to be completely baffled; to feel bewitched
examples[].german: The wallet suddenly turned up again - I feel bewitched.
Even after the explanation, everyone still looked completely baffled.
en.notes: In folk belief, the fox bewitches people. It describes confusion about something inexplicable, usually as 狐につままれたような顔／気分.

en.meaning: edge, brink, outermost point; moment (just before ...)
examples[].german: Standing at the edge of the cliff, my legs froze.
I sat in a seat by the window and looked outside.
As she was leaving, she said "thank you" in a small voice.
en.notes: Native reading of 際: "edge, outermost limit" (崖の際 "edge of a cliff") or "the moment immediately before or at something". As a suffix it becomes voiced ぎわ: 窓際 "by the window", 瀬戸際 "at the critical juncture", 帰り際 "as one is leaving"; likewise in 際どい "risky, close" and 際立つ "to stand out". The card 際/さい "occasion; on the occasion of" is a different word and stands after clauses (その際, 出発の際); きわ, by contrast, denotes a spatial or temporal boundary and is rather rare on its own.

examples[].german: He says corny lines without batting an eye.
You'd better drop that pretentious getup.
en.notes: な-adjective: showy and artificial in manner or speech: きざなせりふ. Usually written in kana; kanji 気障.

examples[].german: We donated my grandfather's book collection to the city library.
This painting was donated by a local painter.
en.notes: To give an item (books, artworks, equipment) to an institution: 寄贈する. JMdict also lists the older reading きそう; today きぞう is the usual one. Money is usually donated with 寄付.

en.meaning: counter for houses and dwelling units
examples[].german: There are five hundred dwelling units in this district.
In the new apartment building, ten units will be put on sale next month.
en.notes: 戸（こ）follows a number and counts houses, households or individual dwelling units. For an apartment building with several flats, it therefore often counts the flats. Examples are 五百戸（ごひゃっこ）"five hundred units" and 十戸（じゅっこ）"ten units". The number can change the pronunciation: here こ becomes a doubled k. This card deals with the counter, not an independent word for a door; a door is called 戸（と）. The accents of complete number combinations are determined separately.

en.meaning: the late, deceased (prefix before names, e.g. 故田中氏)
examples[].german: The funeral of the late Mr. Tanaka will be held next week.
A song by the late John Lennon was playing in the venue.
I dedicate this book to my late mentor.
en.notes: Formal prefix before the name or title of a deceased person, "the late": 故田中氏, 故山田一郎先生. Typical of obituaries, news, dedications and funeral speeches; in conversation 亡くなった田中さん is more usual. Related are 故人 "the deceased" (separate card) and 故郷 "hometown", where 故 means "old, former".

examples[].german: I bought a dark brown coat.
These shoes are not black but dark brown.
en.notes: A dark, almost black brown (literally "scorched brown"); also 焦げ茶色.

en.meaning: to congeal, to solidify, to set (gel); to freeze
examples[].german: When I put it in the refrigerator, the sauce of the simmered fish set into jelly.
The pond water began to freeze over from the cold.
Nikogori is a dish made by cooling and setting fish simmering liquid.
en.notes: Intransitive verb "to congeal, to gel, to solidify", especially of liquids such as broth, fat or blood that become solid when cooled. Mostly written in kana; known from 煮凝り (にこごり) "aspic of fish or meat stock". Despite the same spelling, it is a different verb from 凝る/こる "to be stiff; to be absorbed in something" (肩が凝る). In everyday speech 固まる is mostly said instead of こごる.

en.meaning: to row; to pedal (a bicycle); to swing
examples[].german: I rowed a boat on the lake.
Pedaling a bicycle up a slope is hard work.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb, often written in kana: ボートを漕ぐ (to row a boat), 自転車を漕ぐ (to pedal a bicycle), ブランコを漕ぐ (to swing on a swing). Idiom: 舟を漕ぐ (to nod off while sitting).

en.meaning: to fall in love; to love (romantically)
examples[].german: For the first time, she knew what it is like to fall in love with someone.
To someone in love, every day seems enjoyable.
en.notes: Suru verb: to love romantically, to be in love: 恋する乙女 (a girl in love). Somewhat more literary than 好きになる.

examples[].german: Many of the deceased's friends gathered at the funeral.
The family quietly shared their memories of the deceased.
en.notes: Polite term for a dead person, especially at funerals: 故人をしのぶ (to remember the deceased). Homophone: 個人 (individual).

examples[].german: I want to value each individual opinion.
There are so many problems that it is hard to deal with each one individually.
en.notes: Each one separately: 個々の問題 (individual problems), 個々に対応する (to deal with each individually). The spelling 箇箇 is rare.

examples[].german: During the earthquake I felt as if my life was in danger.
When I heard I had passed, it felt like a dream.
en.notes: A feeling or mood: 生きた心地がしない (to be scared to death), 夢を見ているような心地 (a dreamlike feeling). As a suffix 〜心地（ごこち）: 住み心地 (comfort of living), 着心地 (comfort of wearing).

examples[].german: The attitude of studying a little every day is important.
You brought an umbrella; that is thoughtful of you.
en.notes: The inner attitude with which one approaches something: 心掛けがいい (to be thoughtful, to have a good attitude). From the verb 心掛ける (to make an effort, to keep in mind).

examples[].german: This is the first attempt of its kind in Japan.
Unfortunately, the new attempt ended in failure.
en.notes: An attempt or new approach; from the verb 試みる. Common: 新しい試み (a new attempt), 初めての試み (a first attempt).

en.meaning: to aspire to; to set one's sights on
examples[].german: He aspired to become a doctor from childhood.
Aiming to become a painter, I studied abroad in Paris.
en.notes: Godan verb: to set a life goal, mostly with を or に: 医者を志す (to aspire to be a doctor), 音楽の道を志す (to set out on a path in music).

examples[].german: The government increased the defense budget.
The public is divided on national defense.
en.notes: Defense of the country against external attack: 国防費 (defense spending), 国防政策 (defense policy).

examples[].german: Most of Japan's land area is mountainous.
In countries with little land, land prices tend to be high.
en.notes: The territory of a country: 国土が狭い (the national territory is small), 国土交通省 (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport).

examples[].german: The headquarters of the United Nations is in New York.
She says she wants to work at the United Nations in the future.
en.notes: Short form of 国際連合 (United Nations): 国連本部, 国連事務総長 (UN Secretary-General).

examples[].german: This supermarket only sells domestically grown vegetables.
Domestic beef is more expensive than imported beef.
en.notes: Produced in one's own country (usually Japan): 国産の牛肉 (domestic beef), 国産車 (domestic car). Opposites: 外国産 (foreign-made), 輸入品 (imported goods).

examples[].german: The area around this lake is designated a quasi-national park.
State-prescribed textbooks were used in prewar schools.
en.notes: Determined or designated by the state: 国定公園 (quasi-national park), 国定教科書 (state-prescribed textbook).

examples[].german: The forests around here are all state-owned.
It became an issue that state-owned land was sold cheaply.
en.notes: Owned by the state: 国有地 (state land), 国有林 (state forest), 国有化 (nationalization). Opposites: 民有, 私有.

examples[].german: This song became famous through a TV commercial.
There are too many commercials in the middle of the movie.
en.notes: An advertisement on television or radio; short form CM（シーエム）.

examples[].german: I was moved by the ryokan's attentive service.
My mother raised us with tender affection.
en.notes: な-adjective: warm and attentive (細やかな愛情 tender affection, 細やかな気配り thoughtful consideration). Not to be confused with 細やか（ささやか, modest）.

en.meaning: to shut oneself in; to be filled with; to be stuffy
examples[].german: He shut himself in his room all weekend.
I was happy to receive a heartfelt letter.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: to withdraw (部屋にこもる), to be filled with feeling (心のこもった, heartfelt), or smoke or smell builds up (煙がこもる, smoke gets trapped).

examples[].german: The glass I dropped shattered into pieces.
The window glass was shattered to bits by the earthquake.
en.notes: な-adjective: completely broken or crushed, mostly 粉々になる / 粉々に割れる (to shatter).

examples[].german: I drew a circle with a compass.
In the mountains I walk with a compass and a map.
en.notes: A drawing instrument for circles (a pair of compasses) and a magnetic compass. Colloquially also leg length: コンパスが長い (long-legged).

examples[].german: When I wake up in the morning, the first thing I do is put in my contact lenses.
My job is to get in touch with business partners.
en.notes: To make contact (コンタクトを取る) and short for コンタクトレンズ (contact lens).

examples[].german: I decided to enter a Japanese speech contest.
I won first place in the photo contest.
en.notes: A competition judged by a jury: 写真コンテスト, スピーチコンテスト.

examples[].german: The contrast between the blue sky and white snow is beautiful.
The screen was hard to read, so I increased the contrast.
en.notes: Opposition of colors, brightness or characteristics: 色のコントラスト (color contrast), 画面のコントラストを上げる (to raise the screen contrast).

examples[].german: It is hard to control one's anger.
That pitcher has good control.
en.notes: To steer or have something under control; as a verb コントロールする: 感情をコントロールする (to control one's emotions). In baseball: pitching accuracy.

examples[].german: I looked for a dictionary in the foreign-language section of the bookstore.
On the last bend, the runner overtook one competitor.
en.notes: Bend (race track), area in a store (食品コーナー) or segment of a broadcast.

examples[].german: When I strained my eyes in the darkness, I could make out a figure.
The restaurant attracts customers with an ingeniously devised menu.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb, fixed in set phrases: 目を凝らす (to look closely), 工夫を凝らす (to put ingenuity into something), 息を凝らす (to hold one's breath).

examples[].german: I strained the soup through a cloth to make it smooth.
You filter the coffee through a paper filter.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to pass a liquid through a sieve or cloth; also written 漉す. Homophones: 越す, 超す.

examples[].german: I cannot possibly bear the heat in a room without windows.
I can endure one night, but being unable to sleep for several days is hard.
en.notes: 堪える／こたえる here means enduring a burden. The reading is especially common in 堪えられない "unbearable" and in compound verbs such as 持ちこたえる; this card shows the independent verb. The burden can be marked with に. It is an Ichidan verb: こたえます, こたえて. Do not confuse it with: 応える／こたえる in 暑さが身に応える describes the effect of the heat on the body. The readings こらえる and たえる also have their own uses.

en.meaning: retreat; backward movement; setback; backspace key
examples[].german: I think canceling the plan is a major setback.
Please do not stand behind the car while it is reversing.
I deleted the last character I had typed with the backspace key.
en.notes: 後退 is a noun for a retreat, a movement backward, or a setback. 前進 is the opposite direction. With する it forms the intransitive verb 後退する. In computer terminology, 後退 can also mean the backspace key; 後退キー makes this connection clear. The identically read 交代 means change or switching. The pitch accent of this card applies to 後退 alone, not to 後退する or 後退キー.

examples[].german: When water is cooled, it becomes solid ice.
Matter has three states: solid, liquid and gas.
en.notes: The solid state of matter; alongside 液体 (liquid) and 気体 (gas). Homophone: 個体 (individual).

examples[].german: In winter I like eating mandarin oranges at the kotatsu.
I fell asleep under the kotatsu.
en.notes: A low table with a heater underneath and a quilt over it; typical for Japanese winters. Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: I will let you know by email what was decided at the meeting.
I cannot answer questions about personal matters.
en.notes: A matter or point under discussion; somewhat more formal than こと.

en.meaning: depending on the circumstances (esp. ことによっては = possibly); to be due to
examples[].german: Depending on the circumstances, we may have to rethink the plan from scratch.
Perhaps I can take next week off.
The cause of the accident was that the driver had dozed off.
en.notes: Usually written in kana and used mainly in the forms ことによっては ("depending on the circumstances, if necessary") and ことによったら ("possibly"). After a verb, 〜ことによる means "is due to the fact that ..." (原因は…ことによる). Related to the fixed expression ことによると ("possibly, perhaps"), which has its own card.

en.meaning: possibly; perhaps; it may be that
examples[].german: It may snow tomorrow.
Maybe he already knows, doesn't he?
en.notes: Expresses a cautious conjecture; often with かもしれない: ことによると雨になるかもしれない (it might rain).

examples[].german: I have a message from my mother for the teacher.
The department head was out, so I asked the secretary to pass on a message.
en.notes: A message that one has conveyed through a third person: 言付けを頼む (to ask someone to pass on a message). From the verb 言付ける.

examples[].german: I asked a friend to pass on a message and went home first.
I heard through the grapevine that he got married.
en.notes: A message passed on orally or something known by hearsay: 言伝に聞く (to hear secondhand). Somewhat more old-fashioned than 伝言.

examples[].german: My grandfather's hobby is collecting antiques.
This plate seems to be an antique from the Edo period.
en.notes: Old, valuable objects for collecting: 骨董品店 (antique shop). Jokingly also for very old appliances.

examples[].german: In Buddhism, kalpa is a word for an immeasurably long time.
When a ko arises in Go, the opponent cannot immediately recapture the stone.
en.notes: 劫 in Buddhism is an unimaginably long span of time, a "world age". In the game of Go, it denotes the ko position, in which stones could be captured back and forth again and again; there it is usually written コウ. In compounds it is read ごう (永劫 "eternity", 未来永劫 "for all eternity"), and 億劫 おっくう "troublesome" is a word of its own.

en.meaning: shell, carapace (e.g. 亀の甲); first, top (rank A); back of the hand/instep; Party A (in contracts)
examples[].german: In the contract, the seller is designated Party A and the buyer Party B.
I fell and scraped the back of my hand.
As the saying goes, "Age beats a turtle's shell": experience is important.
en.notes: Has several separate meanings: the hard shell of turtles and crabs (亀の甲), the back of the hand or instep (手の甲, 足の甲), and the first rank in the series 甲・乙・丙. In contracts, 甲 and 乙 stand for the first and second contracting party. Cf. 甲乙 ("difference in rank, A and B"), e.g. 甲乙つけがたい.

examples[].german: Sales of the new product are strong.
The team has been in good form since the start of the season.
en.notes: な-adjective: business, sales or athletes are doing well: 売れ行きが好調だ (sales are good), 好調な滑り出し (a good start). Opposite: 不調.

examples[].german: My grandparents lived for a long time in a public housing complex.
That road was built by a public corporation.
en.notes: A body established by the state for public tasks; colloquially also short for its rental housing (公団住宅).

examples[].german: In the past, this port flourished through trade with foreign countries.
The Silk Road was a trade route between East and West.
en.notes: Trade between countries or peoples, often historical: 東西交易 (East-West trade), 交易品 (trade goods). Today 貿易 is more usual. Homophone: 公益 (public interest).

examples[].german: I spent the summer vacation on a cool highland.
In the morning, the air on the plateau is clear.
en.notes: High-lying, flat land, popular in Japan as a summer retreat: 高原の避暑地 (a highland summer resort).

en.meaning: promotion of industry; founding of new industries
examples[].german: The Meiji government put effort into promoting industry.
In the Meiji period, the government encouraged the founding of new industries throughout the country and built state-run factories.
en.notes: The founding and promotion of new industries, especially in 殖産興業 (the Meiji-era industrial promotion policy). Homophones: 工業 (industry), 鉱業 (mining), 興行 (performance, show).

examples[].german: The new menu is popular with customers.
Due to popular demand, the exhibition was extended by a week.
en.notes: When something is well received: 好評を得る (to be well received), 好評につき (due to popular demand). Opposite: 不評. Homophone: 公表 (public announcement).

examples[].german: I have feelings for him.
I took my senior colleague up on his kind offer and let him drive me.
en.notes: A friendly disposition or affection: 好意を持つ (to like someone), 好意に甘える (to accept a kind offer). Homophone: 行為 (act).

examples[].german: The bank clerk at the counter explained it to me politely.
About a thousand employees work at this bank.
en.notes: Employee of a bank (銀行員). 行 here stands for 銀行.

examples[].german: By practicing every day, my skills improved.
The company is working on improving the quality of its service.
en.notes: Getting better in ability, quality or standard of living; as a verb 向上する: 技術が向上する (skills improve), 向上心 (drive to improve). Homophone: 工場.

examples[].german: The writer completed the novel by dictation.
The witness's oral statement was recorded.
en.notes: To state something orally or to dictate: 口述試験 (oral exam), 口述筆記 (dictation).

examples[].german: The ship returned to port after a month-long voyage.
In the old days, sea voyages relied on the stars.
en.notes: A trip across the sea; as a verb 航海する. Homophones: 公開, 後悔.

examples[].german: Even though it is the middle of the night, the lights of the building are shining brightly.
The moon lit up the night road brightly.
en.notes: Describes bright, shining light, mostly as 煌々と: 明かりが煌々とついている (the lights are blazing). Literary.

examples[].german: Many people run around the Imperial Palace.
The public New Year greeting is held at the Imperial Palace.
en.notes: The residence of the Japanese Emperor in Tokyo, on the grounds of the former Edo Castle.

examples[].german: This record received official recognition from the organizers.
Even the parents now officially accept the two's relationship.
en.notes: Officially recognized or approved: 公認会計士 (certified public accountant), 公認記録 (official record), 党の公認候補 (party-endorsed candidate). As a verb 公認する.

examples[].german: My child goes to the public elementary school nearby.
Anyone can use public libraries for free.
en.notes: Run by a prefecture or municipality: 公立学校 (public school), 公立病院 (public hospital). Opposite: 私立 (private). Homophone: 効率 (efficiency).

examples[].german: The athletes marched in for the opening procession.
The children marched in time to the music.
en.notes: To march or move in rows: 入場行進 (entrance march), デモ行進 (protest march). As a verb 行進する. Homophone: 更新.

examples[].german: I attended a course when renewing my driver's license.
During summer vacation I attended a course at a cram school.
en.notes: A short course to acquire certain knowledge: 夏期講習 (summer course), 救命講習 (life-saving course), 講習を受ける (to attend a course). Homophone: 公衆.

examples[].german: Factional struggles within the party are intensifying.
Many people were caught up in the conflict between the two organizations.
en.notes: A prolonged fight between groups: 派閥抗争 (factional struggle), 暴力団の抗争 (gang war). As a verb 抗争する.

examples[].german: The probability of precipitation tomorrow is 70 percent.
There was less precipitation this year than usual.
en.notes: Meteorological term for rain and snow: 降水確率 (probability of precipitation), 降水量 (amount of precipitation). Homophone: 香水.

examples[].german: This silk cloth has a beautiful luster.
I printed the photos on glossy paper.
en.notes: Shiny surface of fabric, paper, metal or lacquer: 光沢のある布 (glossy cloth), 光沢紙 (glossy paper).

examples[].german: The result was communicated orally.
A verbal promise alone makes me uneasy, so please put it in writing.
en.notes: Mostly as 口頭で (orally) or 口頭の: 口頭試問 (oral examination), 口頭で伝える (to tell verbally). Opposite: 書面 (in writing).

examples[].german: The relationship between the two was an open secret.
He openly criticized the company president at the meeting.
en.notes: What is open and generally known, often as 公然と or 公然の秘密 (open secret).

examples[].german: A little bird is singing in the treetop.
The wind swayed the treetops.
en.notes: The outermost tips of the branches or the top of a tree; rather literary.

en.meaning: suffering, pain; trouble, worry (e.g. 苦にする, 苦もなく, 苦あれば楽あり)
examples[].german: He doesn't mind getting up early in the morning.
She lifted the heavy luggage without any effort.
They say that after pain comes pleasure, so let's keep at it now.
en.notes: As an independent noun it is elevated and appears almost only in fixed phrases: 苦にする ("to take to heart, to feel as a burden"), 苦もなく ("effortlessly"), 苦あれば楽あり ("after pain comes pleasure"). For everyday trouble, 苦労 (vocab-n3:269) or 苦しみ is said. Not to be confused with the identically sounding cards 九, 区 and 句.

examples[].german: I received a pearl necklace from my grandmother.
The museum displays necklaces from ancient times.
en.notes: Jewelry worn around the neck; today often ネックレス.

examples[].german: I put a new collar on the dog.
The collar has a name and phone number written on it.
en.notes: The collar for dogs or cats: 犬に首輪をつける.

examples[].german: That bird catches fish with its long beak.
Someone uninvolved butted in from the side.
en.notes: A bird's beak. Idiom: くちばしを挟む／入れる (to butt in uninvited). Kanji 嘴.

en.meaning: to hum; to sing softly to oneself
examples[].german: My mother was humming an old song while cooking.
I found myself humming my favorite song.
en.notes: To sing or recite a song or poem quietly to oneself. Godan verb.

examples[].german: The aforementioned man was standing in front of the shop again.
I have already handed the documents in question to the president.
en.notes: Literary and elevated for something already mentioned, used almost only as 件の + noun: 件の男 (the man in question). With the reading けん, 件 means "matter".

examples[].german: When I reach a stopping point in my work, I plan to take time off.
Please read paying attention to the breaks between sentences.
en.notes: A point at which something is divided or brought to a close: 区切りをつける (to draw a line, to wrap up), 一区切り.

examples[].german: I have been on a TV quiz show before.
We had fun quizzing the children.
en.notes: A riddle or knowledge question: クイズを出す (to pose a quiz), クイズ番組 (quiz show).

examples[].german: Let's decide the order by drawing lots.
I won a travel voucher in the shopping street's lottery.
en.notes: A lot for drawing, or a lottery: くじを引く, くじに当たる. Usually in kana; the kanji 籤 is rare. State lottery: 宝くじ.

examples[].german: The "Sendai Kuji Hongi" is a historical work said to have been compiled in the early Heian period.
My grandfather talked nostalgically about the old events of the village.
en.notes: A written-language word, rare today, for "past happenings, old stories". The reading くじ is the older one and is known mainly from the title of the historical work 先代旧事本紀 (せんだいくじほんぎ); in modern texts 旧事 is mostly read きゅうじ. Do not confuse it with くじ "lot, lottery" (籤); in everyday speech 昔のこと or 過去の出来事 is said instead.

examples[].german: The seats were decided by drawing lots.
I won first prize in the lottery draw at the festival.
en.notes: Drawing lots to decide something or to distribute prizes: くじ引きで決める.

examples[].german: Because of an accident, service on this section is suspended.
In an ekiden, each runner runs one section.
en.notes: A partial stretch between two points: 運休区間 (suspended section), 区間快速 (section rapid service).

examples[].german: This sunflower has a very thick stem.
When arranging flowers, it is good to cut the stems at an angle.
en.notes: The stem of a plant between root and leaves.

examples[].german: On clear days Mt. Fuji can be seen distinctly.
Animal footprints remained clearly visible in the snow.
en.notes: Clearly outlined and easy to see: くっきり見える, くっきりした輪郭.

en.meaning: border (between provinces or countries); national border
examples[].german: When the train came out of the long tunnel at the border, there lay the snow country.
In the past, this pass was the border between Shinano and Echigo.
The samurai fled over the border mountains to the neighboring domain.
en.notes: Native Japanese reading of 国境, in which 国 usually means the old province: the border between 信濃 and 越後 or between two feudal domains. It sounds literary and historical; famous is the opening of 雪国 "国境の長いトンネルを抜けると…", which is traditionally read this way. For modern national borders, 国境/こっきょう (vocab-n2:25) is always used, e.g. 国境を越える "to cross the national border".

examples[].german: In that country the monarch held great power.
Quite a few countries still have a monarchy today.
en.notes: A hereditary ruler such as a king or emperor: 君主制 (monarchy).

examples[].german: For an appetizer, I ordered one crab cake.
The cook steamed a stone crab and cracked open its shell.
en.notes: A noun derived from English "crab", for a crab or its meat. In Japanese it appears especially as part of food or species names, such as クラブケーキ "crab cake" and ストーンクラブ "stone crab". The ordinary Japanese word for the animal is かに（蟹）. In such compound names, クラブ designates the animal or its meat. The identically written word derived from "club", for an association, nightclub or golf club, belongs to the other card. Its accent information does not automatically apply to the crab sense.

examples[].german: Steel beams are being lifted with a large crane.
Several cranes stand in a row at the port.
en.notes: Lifting crane at construction sites and ports. The bird crane is called 鶴.

examples[].german: It tickles when someone touches the soles of my feet.
Being praised by everyone makes me feel somehow embarrassed.
en.notes: Ticklish; figuratively also the embarrassed feeling of being praised: 褒められてくすぐったい. Usually in kana.

examples[].german: Exercising on an empty stomach can make you feel unwell.
Please do not take this medicine on an empty stomach.
en.notes: Literary for "hungry": 空腹を感じる, 空腹時 (on an empty stomach). In everyday speech: おなかがすいた.

examples[].german: That novel was adapted for film.
I think his story is a bit embellished.
en.notes: To adapt a novel or an event for stage, film, or television; figuratively: to embellish facts.

examples[].german: She is an interpreter with ten years of experience.
I'd like to build a career abroad.
en.notes: Professional career and accumulated experience: キャリアを積む. In the civil service, also the career track of those who passed the top national exam. Homophone: キャリア (carrier, mobile network operator).

examples[].german: She has a slender build.
This chair is so fragile that I'm a little afraid to sit on it.
en.notes: な-adjective: slimly built and delicate (華奢な体) or looking fragile (華奢な椅子).

examples[].german: The outfielder caught the ball securely.
The reporter picked up the information first.
en.notes: As the verb キャッチする: to catch a ball, but also to pick up information or signals: 情報をキャッチする.

en.meaning: a little over; just over (after quantities)
examples[].german: The repair cost a little over three thousand yen.
Slightly more than ninety percent of the participants agreed with the plan.
en.notes: After a quantity, 強 means that the actual amount is slightly above it: 三千円強 is a little more than three thousand yen. The figure is approximate; it does not state the exact extra amount. The counterpart 弱（じゃく）means a little less than. This usage goes after the whole quantity and has a different function from 強い（つよい）, strong.

examples[].german: The number of foreigners living in this area is increasing.
Please write your current place of residence on the application form.
en.notes: Official term for "to live, to reside": 居住する, 居住者, 居住地.

examples[].german: Whenever I hear this song, I remember my school days.
He writes his own songs and sings them.
en.notes: A piece of music: 好きな曲, 曲を作る (to compose). The counter is also 曲: 三曲.

examples[].german: The damage was confined to a few areas.
Let's limit the discussion to this issue.
en.notes: To confine to a narrow scope: 〜に局限する. More formal than 限定する.

examples[].german: Local dishes were served at the festival.
I want to pass on the history of our hometown to the children.
en.notes: The area one comes from, or a region with its own culture: 郷土料理 (regional cuisine), 郷土史.

examples[].german: The high school I attended was coed.
That girls' school will become coed from next year.
en.notes: Boys and girls being taught together: 男女共学. Opposite: 男子校／女子校.

examples[].german: Labor and management are continuing to negotiate over wage increases.
We will decide the details after consulting the people concerned.
en.notes: Formal deliberation among several parties: 協議する, 協議会, 協議離婚. Homophone: 競技 (competition).

examples[].german: He set an astonishing record.
The vastness of the universe is truly a wonder.
en.notes: Something astonishing: 驚異的な (astonishing), 自然の驚異. Homophone: 脅威 (threat).

examples[].german: She worked as an elementary school teacher for twenty years.
This university is short of teaching staff.
en.notes: Official term for teaching staff at schools and universities: 教員免許, 教員採用試験. In everyday speech one says 先生.

examples[].german: My favorite subject is mathematics.
A new subject will be added from next year.
en.notes: A subject in the school curriculum: 得意な教科, 教科書 (textbook). Homophone: 強化 (strengthening).

examples[].german: The other country did not soften its hardline stance.
The president firmly opposed the price increase.
en.notes: な-adjective: an uncompromising attitude: 強硬な態度, 強硬派 (hardliners). Do not confuse with 強行 (to push through).

en.meaning: forcing through; carrying out despite obstacles
examples[].german: The game was held despite the rain.
Overriding the opposition, they pushed the plan through.
en.notes: To push something through despite resistance or bad conditions: 強行する, 強行採決 (forcing a vote). Do not confuse with 強硬.

examples[].german: A cool summer led to a poor rice harvest.
Crop failures continued, and life in the village became hard.
en.notes: A very bad harvest: 冷夏で米が凶作になる. Opposite: 豊作.

examples[].german: I take driving lessons three times a week.
There was training on how to use the new machine.
en.notes: Practical training, especially at a driving school: 教習所 (driving school), 教習車.

examples[].german: The two countries concluded a new trade agreement.
An agreement was reached between the company and the union.
en.notes: A formal accord between states or organizations: 協定を結ぶ, 貿易協定.

en.meaning: republicanism, republican form of government; cooperation
examples[].german: Japan is a monarchy, but France has a republican system.
The two major parties in the United States are the Democratic Party and the Republican Party.
Different peoples worked together in harmony and built a new nation.
en.notes: Rarely used on its own; mainly the basic component of 共和国 "republic", 共和制 "republican form of government" and 共和党 "Republican Party". The second meaning "to work together in harmony" (共和する) is written-language and appears mainly in historical slogans such as 五族共和. The opposite of 共和制 is 君主制 "monarchy".

examples[].german: His offer was flatly rejected.
Children sometimes refuse new foods outright.
en.notes: Firm refusal: 拒絶する, 拒絶反応 (rejection reaction). Stronger than 断る.

examples[].german: The president and I have known each other since our student days.
I ran into an old friend at the station by chance.
en.notes: Someone one has known for a long time: 旧知の仲 (old friends). Homophone: 窮地 (predicament).

examples[].german: In Vienna I toured an old palace.
The king lived in a splendid palace.
en.notes: A ruler's palace: ベルサイユ宮殿. The Japanese Imperial Palace is called 皇居.

examples[].german: At the ryokan, the maid served us our meal.
In the past, my grandfather worked as a waiter at a hotel.
en.notes: Serving at table, or the person who serves; somewhat old-fashioned. As a verb: 給仕する.

examples[].german: The two countries agreed to a three-day truce.
Even the brothers' quarrel ended in a truce with a word from their mother.
en.notes: Temporary cessation of fighting: 休戦協定. The final end of a war is called 終戦.

examples[].german: Today's school lunch was curry.
This factory provides a midday meal.
en.notes: A meal provided by a school or company, especially the lunch at Japanese schools: 給食当番 (lunch duty).

examples[].german: I marked the important parts in red.
This shop's logo is a blue bird.
en.notes: As a noun a sign or logo (星のマーク); as the verb マークする: to mark or underline something. In sports also "to mark an opponent".

en.meaning: meeting up; arranged meeting (at an agreed place)
examples[].german: I'm meeting a friend in front of the station.
I was five minutes late for the meeting time.
en.notes: An arranged meeting at a place: 待ち合わせ場所 (meeting place), 駅で待ち合わせをする (to meet at the station). Verb: 待ち合わせる.

examples[].german: The children can hardly wait for Christmas.
I can't wait for the day I see my grandchildren who live far away.
en.notes: い-adjective: one can hardly wait for something: 夏休みが待ち遠しい (I can't wait for summer vacation). The subject is the thing awaited, not the person waiting.

en.meaning: to be mistaken; to be wrong; to make a mistake
examples[].german: There is a mistake somewhere in this calculation.
Let's be careful not to post wrong information online.
en.notes: Mostly intransitive: 答えが間違っている (the answer is wrong). Common in 間違った (wrong) and 間違っても〜ない (never, under no circumstances). For "to make a mistake, to mix up", 間違える is more common.

examples[].german: Even experts' opinions differ on this issue.
The participants' ages varied, from teens to seventies.
en.notes: な-adjective, mostly in kana (rarely 区々): opinions, figures or traits differ: 意見がまちまちだ (opinions are divided).

en.meaning: to long for; to eagerly await
examples[].german: The villagers were longing for rain to fall.
The long-awaited new game was finally released.
en.notes: Transitive, literary: to wait long and eagerly for something: 平和を待ち望む (to long for peace). Often 待ち望んでいた (long-awaited).

examples[].german: Enough of the preamble, let's get down to the main topic.
The principal's talk had such a long introduction that everyone was bored.
en.notes: Introductory words before the actual topic: 前置きが長い (to have a long-winded introduction). As a verb: 前置きする.

examples[].german: Concert tickets are 500 yen cheaper if bought in advance.
The movie is popular, so advance tickets had already sold out.
en.notes: Sale of tickets before the day of the event: 前売り券 (advance ticket), 前売りで買う (to buy in advance). Often cheaper than tickets on the day (当日券).

examples[].german: My mother wrote the letter with all her heart.
Thanks to her loving, devoted care, my father got well again.
en.notes: Honest, wholehearted sentiment: 真心を込めて (with all one's heart). Reading まごころ; the reading まこころ is obsolete.

en.meaning: to be confused; to be flustered
examples[].german: The first time I went to Tokyo Station, I was confused by the many exits.
The clerk was flustered when suddenly asked a question in English.
en.notes: Intransitive, colloquial: to become unsure and not know what to do, for example in unfamiliar surroundings: 初めての駅でまごつく (to be at a loss at an unfamiliar station). Synonym: 戸惑う.

examples[].german: As an aftereffect of the accident, my right hand is slightly paralyzed.
Heavy snow brought traffic in Tokyo to a standstill.
en.notes: As the verb 麻痺する. Medical: 手足が麻痺する (arms and legs are paralyzed); figuratively: 大雪で交通が麻痺した (traffic came to a standstill). Often also in kana まひ.

en.meaning: my own, personal (prefix, e.g. マイカー, マイホーム, マイバッグ)
examples[].german: My father commutes to work every day in his own car.
Since plastic bags started costing money, I carry my own bag with me.
My dream is to build a home of my own someday.
en.notes: Loan prefix from English "my" that expresses personal ownership in Japanese coinages: マイカー ("one's own car"), マイホーム ("one's own home"), マイバッグ ("one's own shopping bag"), マイペース ("one's own pace"). It is used only before loanwords and is not used as an independent word. Do not confuse it with 毎〜/まい ("every"), マイク or マイナス.

examples[].german: A microphone is installed in the ceiling of the conference room.
This laptop has a built-in microphone.
High-performance microphones are used in recording studios.
en.notes: Full form of マイク (vocab-n3:3350); in everyday life, at karaoke or on stage people almost always say マイク. マイクロフォン, or the older technical spelling マイクロホン, appears mainly in technical texts, product specifications and standards. There is no difference in meaning.

examples[].german: Large amounts of natural gas lie buried beneath this region.
There is a legend that a lord of old buried gold coins in this castle.
en.notes: As the verb 埋蔵する, mostly in the passive: 石油が埋蔵されている (there are oil deposits). 埋蔵量 = reserves, 埋蔵金 = buried treasure.

en.meaning: to include; to mix in; to exchange (words)
examples[].german: The teacher explained it clearly, mixing in jokes.
In the meeting, we discussed the matter with outside experts included.
en.notes: Transitive, rather formal: 冗談を交えて話す (to talk with jokes mixed in), 専門家を交えて議論する (to discuss with experts taking part), 言葉を交える (to exchange a few words).

examples[].german: My little brother beat our father at shogi and was overjoyed.
This year we soundly beat the opponent we had lost to last year.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 負ける: to defeat someone: 相手を負かす. Not to be confused with 任す (to entrust).

en.meaning: roll, winding (e.g. cloth, head of cabbage); winding up (clock); volume, part (of a work, e.g. 若紫の巻); to speed things up (jargon: 巻きで)
examples[].german: In class, we read the "Wakamurasaki" chapter of The Tale of Genji.
This cabbage is tightly wrapped and heavy.
The shoot is running behind, so please pick up the pace a bit.
en.notes: 巻（まき） is the native Japanese reading of 巻 and refers to what is wound or to winding; as an independent noun it is mostly written 巻き (巻きがしっかりしている), in titles on the other hand 〜の巻. Numbered volumes are called 第一巻 with the reading かん (separate card 巻/かん); 〜の巻 names rather chapters of classical works or, humorously, an "episode". The word is very often found in compounds such as 巻き寿司, 春巻き or ねじ巻き; in television and stage jargon, 巻きで means "to speed up".

en.meaning: last stage; final period; terminal stage
examples[].german: In the final years of the Edo period, many foreign ships began to come to Japan.
I'm truly glad the illness was found before it reached the terminal stage.
en.notes: The last phase of an era or development: 江戸時代の末期 (the last years of the Edo period); for illnesses 末期がん (terminal cancer). The reading まつご, on the other hand, means "the hour of death".

examples[].german: He apologized to the victims with all sincerity.
I meant it as a joke, but it came true - a lie turned into truth.
The single character "sincerity" was dyed onto the Shinsengumi banner.
en.notes: Elevated noun for "sincerity" and "truth", typical in fixed phrases such as 誠を尽くす "to make a sincere effort" or the proverb 嘘から出た誠 "a joke turns into earnest". The adverb 誠に "truly, sincerely" (separate card) is a separate word and much more common in polite formulas such as 誠に申し訳ございません. For the meaning "truth", the spellings 真 and 実 are also seen; as the ideal of the Shinsengumi and as a given name, 誠 is culturally present.

examples[].german: A thin skin formed on the surface of the heated milk.
Cells are surrounded by a thin membrane.
en.notes: A thin layer or skin: 細胞膜 (cell membrane); a 膜 forms on warm milk. Homophones: 幕 (curtain), 巻く (to wind).

en.meaning: to roll up; (after a verb stem) to do like crazy, to do endlessly
examples[].german: He rolled up his sleeves and began washing the dishes.
During the trip, I ate delicious food non-stop every day.
en.notes: Mostly in kana: 袖をまくる (to roll up one's sleeves). After the masu-stem, colloquial for doing something excessively: 食べまくる (to eat non-stop), 買いまくる (to buy like crazy). The kanji spelling 捲る is also read めくる (to turn over).

examples[].german: When you're in a hurry, mistakes like this happen from time to time.
The weather forecast also occasionally turns out wrong.
en.notes: Literary, mostly in ままある (happens occasionally), often also in kana. Not to be confused with まま (as is) and ママ (mama).

examples[].german: The children were playing, covered all over in mud.
Working at a construction site in summer, I was drenched in sweat all day.
en.notes: Suffix on nouns: 汗まみれ (drenched in sweat), 泥まみれ (covered in mud), 借金まみれ (deep in debt). Mostly negative; the kanji spelling 塗れ is rare. Verb: 塗れる【まみれる】.

examples[].german: Thank you very much for inviting me today.
At the invitation of the university, he gave a lecture in Japan.
en.notes: Formal noun of 招く: お招きいただき、ありがとうございます (thank you for the invitation). Cf. 招待 (invitation to an event).

en.meaning: the whole hall; the entire audience
examples[].german: When his speech ended, the whole hall broke into applause.
The entire audience watched the athlete's final jump.
en.notes: Everyone present in a hall: 満場の拍手 (applause of the whole hall). Well known from 満場一致 (unanimous).

en.meaning: right in front of; directly opposite
examples[].german: My house is right in front of the station.
At the concert, I got a seat right in front of the stage.
en.notes: A colloquial intensified 前: 駅の真ん前 (right in front of the station).

examples[].german: A perfectly round moon is out tonight.
The startled child looked at me with eyes wide open.
en.notes: An い-adjective, an intensified 丸い: 真ん丸い月 (the perfectly round full moon). Also 真ん丸 (noun).

en.meaning: right in two; exactly in half
examples[].german: The plate fell on the floor and broke exactly in two.
On that issue, the class was split right down the middle.
en.notes: Mostly 真っ二つに: 真っ二つに割れる/切る (to break/cut exactly in two). Figuratively: 意見が真っ二つに分かれる (opinions are split into two camps).

examples[].german: The girls are playing in the garden, bouncing a ball.
The ball my grandmother made was wrapped in colorful threads.
en.notes: A traditional ball, often wrapped in colorful threads, which children used to play with (手まり). Rather literary today; for sports balls, ボール is used.

examples[].german: I don't understand French at all.
It was a completely different room from the one I saw in the photo.
en.notes: Colloquial, mostly with a negative: まるっきりわからない (not to understand at all). Similar to まるで and 全然.

examples[].german: It took a full week to prepare the materials.
A round, fat cat is sleeping on the veranda.
en.notes: As an adverb: completely, a full ...: 丸々一日 (a whole day). With と/とした: plump, chubby (丸々とした赤ちゃん, a chubby baby). Also in kana まるまる.

en.meaning: to make round; to crumple; to shave (one's head)
examples[].german: He crumpled the misspelled sheet of paper and threw it in the trash.
Because it's cold, the cat is sleeping curled up.
en.notes: Transitive: 紙を丸める (to crumple paper), 背中を丸める (to hunch one's back). 頭を丸める = to shave one's head, traditionally as a sign of repentance.

examples[].german: This is undoubtedly the wallet I lost.
I think what he says is exactly right.
en.notes: Emphatic affirmation, similar to まさに: まさしくその通り (exactly so). Mostly in kana; the kanji spelling 正しく is otherwise read ただしく.

en.meaning: better (than something else); the lesser evil
examples[].german: Doing even a little is better than doing nothing.
It's better than yesterday, but my head still hurts.
en.notes: な-adjective, mostly in kana: AよりBの方がましだ (B is still better than A). Expresses that something is not good, but less bad. As the suffix 〜増し also "increase, surcharge": 二割増し (20% more).

examples[].german: Right below my apartment there is a convenience store.
I took shelter from the rain right under the bridge.
en.notes: Exactly vertically below something: 橋の真下 (right under the bridge). Opposite: 真上.

en.meaning: let alone; still more; all the more
examples[].german: It's a kanji that is difficult even for Japanese people, so foreigners surely can't read it.
It's crowded even on weekdays, so it must be packed on the weekend.
en.notes: Intensifies a comparison: if A is already (not) so, then B all the more (not): 大人でも難しいのに、まして子どもには無理だ (it's hard even for adults, let alone children). Mostly in kana.

examples[].german: I was exhausted, so I went to get a massage.
I massaged my mother's shoulders for her.
en.notes: Also as a verb マッサージする: 肩をマッサージする. To get a massage: マッサージを受ける.

examples[].german: After the incident, many reporters gathered in front of the house.
The actor's marriage was widely covered in the media.
en.notes: Short for マスコミュニケーション; in everyday speech the media as a whole, often with a critical undertone: マスコミに騒がれる (to be hounded by the media). More neutral: メディア, 報道機関.

examples[].german: He straddled his bicycle and rode down the slope.
This national park extends across three prefectures.
en.notes: Intransitive, mostly in kana. With に: 馬にまたがる (to mount a horse), 自転車にまたがる (to straddle a bicycle). Figuratively: to extend over several areas: 三県にまたがる山 (a mountain spanning three prefectures).

examples[].german: The twinkling of the stars in the night sky looked beautiful.
The flickering of the lights of a distant town can faintly be seen beyond the fog.
She gazed intently at the flickering of the candle flame.
en.notes: 瞬き with the reading またたき refers mainly to the twinkling of stars and the flickering of light (星の瞬き, 灯の瞬き); it is the literary noun of the verb 瞬く/またたく (separate card), which is also in またたく間に "in an instant". The same spelling with the reading まばたき (separate card) is the usual word for blinking of the eyes. Rule of thumb: eyes → まばたき, stars and light → またたき.

examples[].german: The arrow hit the very center of the target.
The new smartphone became the center of attention in the class.
en.notes: Literally the target (的に当たる, 的を外す); figuratively: 注目の的 (center of attention), 的を射た意見 (a pertinent remark). The suffix 〜的 (e.g. 経済的) is read てき.

examples[].german: This team is cohesive and very strong.
What he says is so disjointed that I can't tell what he wants to say.
en.notes: Mostly in kana: チームのまとまり (team spirit), まとまりのない文章 (an incoherent text). Verb: まとまる.

examples[].german: Finally, we will wrap up today's lesson.
I put the contents of the meeting into a brief summary and sent it by email.
en.notes: Mostly in kana: 授業のまとめ (summary of the lesson). Verb: まとめる. Also in まとめ買い (bulk buying).

examples[].german: The construction is scheduled to finish at the end of March.
At the end of November, you can see snow on the mountaintop.
en.notes: The reading まつ can serve as a noun for the end of a period. The dictionary attests 三月の末: the end of March. Here の links a period with its end; a following に names the time of an action. In present-day general usage, an independent 末 is often read すえ, and 三月末（さんがつまつ）is a common compound form. This entry specifically practices the attested noun reading まつ.

examples[].german: Please submit the application form by the end of March.
At the end of the year, more people return to their parents' home.
en.notes: 末 is attached to a time expression and denotes its end, for example 三月末（さんがつまつ）, end of March, or 年末（ねんまつ）, year-end. With まで you set a deadline, with に you name the time of an event. The ending follows the preceding part of the word directly. An expression like 三月末 means the last part of the month and need not refer to a single fixed day.

examples[].german: A clock hangs directly above the shelf.
A plane flew right over our house.
en.notes: Exactly vertically above something: 頭の真上 (directly above one's head). Opposite: 真下.

examples[].german: The other passengers frowned at the young people talking loudly on the train.
The teacher frowned at his rude words.
en.notes: To knit one's eyebrows - an expression of displeasure or concern about other people's behavior. Also written 眉を顰める.

examples[].german: Which manufacturer is this computer from?
My older brother works for a major car manufacturer.
en.notes: A manufacturing company, especially larger firms: 自動車メーカー (car manufacturer), 大手メーカー.

examples[].german: Grateful for the bounty of the sea, the fishermen hold a festival.
The rain after the long drought was truly a blessing.
en.notes: Gifts of nature or divine grace: 自然の恵み, 恵みの雨 (longed-for rain after dryness). Verb: 恵む.

examples[].german: The ball he threw hit the target perfectly.
The missile did not hit its target.
en.notes: As a verb 命中する: to hit the target: 的に命中する. 命中率 = hit rate.

examples[].german: The company will change its name starting next year.
Do you know the official name of this festival?
en.notes: The official name of a thing, organization or product: 正式名称 (official designation). For people, one says 名前 or 氏名. Homophone: 名勝 (scenic spot).

examples[].german: The fishmonger weighed the fish and set the price.
These sweets are sold by weight.
en.notes: A somewhat old-fashioned word for 重さ, especially when weighing goods: 目方を量る, 目方で売る (to sell by weight).

examples[].german: I read the scale on the thermometer and recorded it in my notebook.
I poured 200 milliliters of water, matching the markings on the measuring cup.
en.notes: The divisions on measuring instruments: 定規の目盛り, 温度計の目盛りを読む.

examples[].german: I went to visit my grandmother in the hospital.
I asked for a meeting with the company president, but was refused.
en.notes: A meeting in person, especially a visit to patients, prisoners, or a high-ranking person: 面会時間 (visiting hours), 面会を申し込む (to request a meeting). Also usable as a する-verb: 面会する.

en.meaning: to face, overlook (a street, the sea, etc.)
examples[].german: All the rooms in this hotel face the sea.
The shop faces the main street in front of the station and gets a lot of foot traffic.
en.notes: With に: 海に面した部屋 (a room facing the sea), 大通りに面する (to face a main street). Mostly in the forms 〜に面した / 〜に面している. A written-style する-verb.

examples[].german: A melody I had heard somewhere before started playing.
I like this song's melody more than its lyrics.
en.notes: The tune of a song: 懐かしいメロディー. Also written メロディ.

examples[].german: Our cat is a female, and her name is Momo.
Female rhinoceros beetles have no horn.
en.notes: A female animal (also plant): 雌の猫. Opposite: 雄【おす】. Often written in kana めす or メス.

en.meaning: look in one's eyes; expression of the eyes
examples[].german: That man has a nasty look in his eyes, but he is actually a kind person.
The cat was staring at the bird with a sharp gaze.
en.notes: The way someone looks, often negative: 目つきが悪い (to have a nasty look), 鋭い目つき. Also written 目付き.

examples[].german: In the Buddhist classification of the six objects of perception, the object grasped by the tongue is called taste.
When I explained smell and taste as the same thing in Buddhism class, the teacher cautioned me to distinguish them.
en.notes: み here is an independent technical term in Buddhist descriptions of perception. It denotes taste as the object that the tongue perceives. In the classification into six objects of perception, 味 stands beside 香 こう, the object of smell. What is meant is the perceived taste, not the sense organ or the ability to taste. For the ordinary taste of a dish, one says あじ. The suffix in 甘み and the counter for kinds of food or medicine have other uses.

en.meaning: arranged meeting (with a view to marriage)
examples[].german: My parents met through an arranged meeting and got married.
At my aunt's suggestion, I am going to have an arranged meeting next week.
en.notes: Usually お見合い: a meeting between prospective spouses arranged by family or matchmakers. 見合い結婚 = a marriage that comes about through such a meeting (as opposed to 恋愛結婚).

en.meaning: to look at each other; to postpone, to suspend for the time being
examples[].german: At the sudden news, the two of them exchanged glances.
Because of the heavy rain, train service is temporarily suspended.
en.notes: Transitive. 1. 顔を見合わせる: to look at each other (in surprise). 2. Formal: to suspend for the time being, often in announcements: 運転を見合わせる (to temporarily suspend train service).

examples[].german: There are still many unknown things in the universe.
Studying abroad was like jumping into an unknown world.
en.notes: Literary, mostly 未知の + noun: 未知の世界 (an unknown world), 未知数 (an unknown, an uncertain quantity). Opposite: 既知. Homophone: 道.

en.meaning: to pick the right moment; to choose at one's own discretion
examples[].german: I waited for a moment when my boss was in a good mood and asked for time off.
Please choose the bouquet at your discretion, within the budget.
en.notes: Transitive. Mostly タイミングを見計らう / 頃合いを見計らう: to wait for the right moment. Also: to choose by one's own judgment.

examples[].german: The hotel at the top of the mountain has a wonderful view.
Since a tall building went up in front of the window, the view has gotten worse.
en.notes: A wide view over a landscape: 見晴らしがいい (to have a nice view). Verb: 見晴らす.

en.meaning: speck, tiny bit; (with negative) not in the least
examples[].german: He didn't have the slightest sense of remorse.
I minced the onion finely and mixed it with the ground meat.
en.notes: Mostly 微塵も〜ない: not the slightest bit (反省の色は微塵もない). In cooking: みじん切り (finely chopped).

examples[].german: At that time, this region was still undeveloped land.
This field has few researchers and still has many unexplored areas.
en.notes: Not yet developed or explored: 未開の地 (undeveloped land), 未開の分野 (uncharted territory in research). The older meaning "uncivilized" is now considered derogatory.

examples[].german: I caught a cold and my sense of taste is off.
A cook must have a keen sense of taste.
en.notes: One of the five senses (五感): 味覚が鋭い (to have a fine palate). 秋の味覚 = the culinary delights of autumn.

examples[].german: The source of this river is in those mountains.
My family's smiles are the source of my energy.
en.notes: Literally the source of a river (川の源), mostly figurative: 力の源 (source of strength), 情報の源.

en.meaning: to follow the example of; to learn by watching
examples[].german: Take a little example from your older brother.
When I was new, I learned the work by watching my senior colleagues.
en.notes: Transitive: to take someone as a role model: 先輩を見習う. The noun 見習い = apprentice, trainee.

examples[].german: Before the interview, I straightened my appearance in the mirror.
A well-dressed gentleman came into the shop.
en.notes: How someone is dressed and groomed: 身なりを整える (to tidy oneself up), 身なりのいい紳士.

examples[].german: The snow-capped peaks shone in the morning sun.
Above the clouds, I could see the peaks of distant mountains.
en.notes: The summit or ridge of a mountain, rather literary. In everyday speech one says 山頂 or 頂上.

en.meaning: personal belongings; one's immediate surroundings, daily life
examples[].german: I packed the personal items I need for the hospital stay into a bag.
My mother mainly takes care of my grandmother's daily needs.
en.notes: 身の回りの物 (personal belongings), 身の回りの世話 (help with daily care, e.g. for elderly people).

examples[].german: For the first time, she began to talk about her own life.
Everyone sympathized with his situation, having lost his parents early.
en.notes: A person's personal situation and past: 身の上話 (life story), 身の上相談 (personal advice column, e.g. in newspapers).

examples[].german: He is showing off his new watch to everyone.
Stop showing off your brand-new smartphone.
en.notes: Transitive, derogatory: to deliberately show something in order to be admired or envied: 新しい時計を見せびらかす.

examples[].german: The scene of the accident turned into a spectacle, and many people were taking photos.
Some people say it is cruel to put animals on display.
en.notes: Formerly fairground performances (見世物小屋 = sideshow booth). Today mostly derogatory: 見世物になる/にする (to become a spectacle, to put on display). Also written 見せ物.

examples[].german: This brand has a lot of clothing aimed at married women in their thirties.
The readers of this magazine are said to be mainly married women.
en.notes: From the English "Mrs.": used mainly in advertising and fashion for married women (ミセス向けの服). Rare as a form of address in Japanese.

examples[].german: Old houses are densely packed in this area.
Beware of pickpockets in places where people are crowded together.
en.notes: As a verb 密集する: to stand close together or crowd: 住宅が密集している (densely built-up). Known from 三密 (密閉・密集・密接) during the COVID pandemic.

examples[].german: He was wearing shabby clothes, but was actually extremely rich.
The shabby hut in front of the station has been reborn as a fine cafe.
en.notes: An い-adjective, usually written in kana: みすぼらしい服 (shabby clothes), みすぼらしい家.

examples[].german: A misprint was found in the textbook.
The date on the invitation was misprinted and was off by one day.
en.notes: An error in printed text. Synonym, more literary: 誤植.

examples[].german: A butterfly is sucking nectar from a flower.
Bees store the nectar they have collected in their hive.
en.notes: A sweet liquid: 花の蜜 (flower nectar); honey is usually 蜂蜜. 黒蜜 = dark sugar syrup.

examples[].german: The bicycle tire got stuck in the gutter at the side of the road.
Since that fight, a deep rift has formed between the two.
en.notes: Literally a ditch or drainage channel (溝に落ちる); figuratively an estrangement: 二人の間に溝ができる. Other reading: こう (in technical terms such as 海溝, ocean trench).

examples[].german: Please drain the washed vegetables well.
This pear is juicy and sweet.
en.notes: Water contained in something: 水気を切る (to drain), 水気の多い果物 (juicy fruit). Other reading: すいき.

examples[].german: The Go game ended in a draw, and the two laughed as they cleared the board.
In the poetry contest, no better entry could be determined, and that round was ruled a draw.
en.notes: 持ち（もち）here denotes a draw: in a contest, no winner can be determined. The reading is attested especially in older texts about 歌合わせ "poetry contests" or board games. Today 引き分け is usually more common. 持ちとなる and 持ちとされる mean in this context "to end in a draw" and "to be ruled a draw" respectively. The reading じ of 持 as well as "possession" and "durability" are not equated on this card.

en.meaning: the talk of the town, the only topic
examples[].german: The whole school is talking about nothing but the new teacher.
The town was buzzing with talk about the Olympics.
en.notes: Almost always in 〜の話で持ち切りだ (everyone is talking only about ...). Also written 持ちきり.

examples[].german: By the time I noticed, it was already too late.
Such old-fashioned ways of thinking no longer work.
en.notes: Written style; stresses that a state has already come about and cannot be reversed: もはや手遅れだ (it is already too late). With negation: もはや〜ない (no longer).

examples[].german: The cause of the accident is currently under investigation.
For the time being, there is no new information.
He is currently writing a new novel.
en.notes: 目下 read もっか is a formal word for "currently", typical of news and business language: 目下調査中, 目下のところ "for the time being". In conversation, one says 今 or 現在. The same kanji read めした mean "junior, subordinate" (own card); as a time expression before a statement it is もっか, as a person めした.

examples[].german: I checked the library catalog to find where the book is.
You can get the exhibition's list of works free at the reception desk.
en.notes: A list of items or works: 図書目録 (book catalog), 財産目録 (inventory of assets), 作品目録 (list of works).

examples[].german: The president's plan to double sales fell through.
He must have some scheme in mind.
en.notes: Often with a slightly negative tone (ulterior motive) or for failed plans: 目論見が外れる (the plan falls through). Verb: 目論む (to plan, to scheme).

en.meaning: to quarrel, get into a dispute
examples[].german: The siblings are quarreling over the inheritance.
The meeting got into a dispute over the allocation of the budget.
en.notes: Intransitive; the subject is the people quarreling or the matter itself: 会議が揉める (the meeting gets contentious), 遺産で揉める (to quarrel over an inheritance). Often in kana: もめる. Noun: 揉め事 (dispute, trouble).

examples[].german: I ran too much and my thigh muscles hurt.
The ball hit my thigh and left a bruise.
en.notes: 腿 means "thigh"; it is often written もも or 太もも. 股 can also be read もも in this sense. The other reading また of 股 refers to a different part of the body. 鶏もも肉 is chicken thigh meat; 桃 "peach" is a different word with the same sound.

examples[].german: I bought a large monitor for work.
We are looking for testers for new cosmetics.
en.notes: Screen (パソコンのモニター) or monitoring (モニターする). Also a person who tests and evaluates products or programs: 商品モニター.

en.meaning: curiosity about the unusual, eccentric taste; eccentric
examples[].german: Swimming in the sea on such a cold day - there are some odd people out there.
Eccentrically, he collects nothing but old typewriters.
en.notes: Slightly mocking, for unusual preferences: 物好きな人 (a person with odd tastes), 物好きにも … (out of sheer fancy, of all things ...). Used as a na-adjective and as a noun.

examples[].german: The bicycle crashed head-on into a utility pole.
Hit squarely by the weak yen, prices of imported goods rose.
en.notes: Colloquial: something hits directly and unchecked: もろに影響を受ける (to be hit full force), もろにぶつかる (to collide head-on). Usually in kana.

examples[].german: The house is old, so rain leaks through the ceiling on days of heavy rain.
This bucket has a crack in the bottom and leaks water.
en.notes: Intransitive, mainly for roofs and containers: 雨が漏る (rain leaks in), 屋根が漏る. Noun: 雨漏り. More general is 漏れる (to leak out, seep through). Same sound: 盛る (to heap up, to serve).

en.meaning: could it be that; perhaps, possibly
examples[].german: Aren't you Mr. Tanaka, by any chance?
You look pale - might you have a fever?
en.notes: Spoken language, often in questions when one has a guess: もしかして田中さんですか (Are you Mr. Tanaka, by any chance?). Similar: もしかしたら, もしかすると. Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: Please apply by phone or e-mail.
Only people aged 20 or over, or with the consent of a guardian, may participate.
en.notes: Formal conjunction in writing, forms, and announcements: 電話もしくはメールで (by phone or e-mail). In everyday speech, または or か is more common.

en.meaning: to dawdle; to be stuck; to falter
examples[].german: At the register I fumbled with the payment and kept the people behind me waiting.
The introduction of the new system is not making progress.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: one does not get ahead because of clumsiness or delay (準備にもたつく). Related to the onomatopoeic もたもた.

en.meaning: to be popular (especially with the opposite sex)
examples[].german: He's funny, so he's very popular with the girls in his class.
My father is said to have been very popular when he was young.
en.notes: Colloquially usually written モテる: 女性にモテる (to be popular with women). Not to be confused with 持てる as the potential form of 持つ (to be able to carry / hold).

examples[].german: Education is precisely the foundation of a nation.
My grandfather laid the foundation of this company within a single generation.
en.notes: Elevated, literary reading of 基 for "basis, foundation", mostly in phrases such as 〜の基を築く "to lay the foundation of ..." or 〜の基となる. In normal usage, もと (card 元/もと, which lists 基 as a spelling) or 基礎 or 土台 is said. Do not confuse it with the interjection もとい "uh, I mean", with which one corrects oneself.

en.meaning: with, by means of; because of, due to; as of (point in time, e.g. 本日をもって); intensifier (まったくもって); moreover, therefore
examples[].german: Our store will close as of today.
We will notify you of the result in writing at a later date.
Even with his ability, winning was difficult.
en.notes: Formal function word, almost always in kana and mostly as 〜をもって: "by means of" (書面をもって), "with/as of" for a cutoff date (本日をもって閉店) or "even with" in 〜をもってしても. Typical of announcements, business letters and speeches; in everyday speech で is used instead. Do not confuse it with 持って, the te-form of 持つ "to hold, to carry"; the spelling 以て is rare today. As an intensifier it appears in まったくもって "really, absolutely".

en.meaning: fault, objection (mostly: 申し分ない = perfect)
examples[].german: There is nothing to find fault with in his work.
Close to the station and spacious - this room is perfect.
en.notes: Almost only in the negative: 申し分ない / 申し分のない (flawless, impeccable, nothing to complain about). More polite: 申し分ありません.

en.meaning: offer, proposal, report (made on one's own initiative)
examples[].german: A friend offered to help, which was a great relief.
Thank you for the kind offer, but I will decline this time.
en.notes: Noun of 申し出る: something one offers, applies for, or reports on one's own initiative. 申し出を受ける / 断る (to accept / decline an offer). The spelling 申出 without okurigana is common in official documents.
