en.meaning: (formal) to put forward, formally request or propose
examples[].german: The labor union formally requested a wage increase from the company.
We intend to formally lodge a protest with the other company.
en.notes: To formally address a request, proposal, or protest to an organization: 抗議を申し入れる (to lodge a protest), 交渉を申し入れる (to propose negotiations). Noun: 申し入れ.

examples[].german: It is pointless to continue such a discussion.
I want to reduce pointless meetings and have more time for work.
en.notes: な-adjective: 無意味な争い (a pointless quarrel). More colloquial: 意味がない.

examples[].german: After I changed the orientation of the desk, the room started to look bigger.
This job is suited to people who like detailed work.
en.notes: Direction: 風の向き, 向きを変える. As a suffix 〜向き: suited to (子ども向き, 初心者向き) or facing toward (南向きの部屋). Cf. 〜向け (intended for ...).

examples[].german: My father is taciturn, but a very kind person.
He goes quiet when he is nervous.
en.notes: な-adjective: 無口な人 (a taciturn person). Opposite: おしゃべり.

examples[].german: The players who lost in the final shed tears of regret.
When I think of my father's bitterness at dying without fulfilling his dream, my heart aches.
en.notes: Deep disappointment or resentment over a failure: 無念の涙 (tears of regret), 無念を晴らす (to wipe out the disgrace). Stronger and more formal than 残念.

examples[].german: The paint on the wall is applied unevenly.
His grades fluctuate and are not stable.
She is moody, so she is hard to get along with.
en.notes: Mostly written in kana (むら/ムラ), typically with がある/のない: 色むら "color patches", 成績にむらがある "uneven performance", 気分にむらがある "to be moody". The spelling 斑 with the reading まだら (vocab-n1:3050) is a different word and means "spotted, mottled"; 村/むら "village" is merely a homophone.

examples[].german: I contacted the port by radio from the ship.
This room connects to the internet wirelessly.
en.notes: Radio communication (無線で連絡する) and, in general, "wireless": 無線LAN (Wi-Fi). Opposite: 有線.

examples[].german: On Sunday, I pulled up the weeds in the garden.
I picked the flesh off the grilled fish with chopsticks and fed it to the child.
en.notes: Transitive, usually in kana: 草をむしる (to weed), 鶏の羽をむしる (to pluck a chicken). Also: to pick flesh off bones (魚の身をむしる).

en.meaning: conclusion; closing (of a speech, a text)
examples[].german: At the end of my speech, I expressed gratitude to the people who had helped me.
At the end of the letter, I wrote "Take care of yourself."
en.notes: The concluding part: 手紙の結び, 結びの言葉 (closing words). Other meanings: knot (蝶結び = bow) and おむすび (rice ball).

en.meaning: to tie on; to link, to connect
examples[].german: I tied the balloon to the chair so the wind wouldn't blow it away.
The police are linking the two cases.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 結び付く: 木にひもを結び付ける (to tie a string to a tree); figuratively: 二つの事件を結び付ける (to link two cases).

examples[].german: Japan and this country have strong economic ties.
I value my bond with my family.
en.notes: A close relationship between people, countries or things: 地域の結び付き, 経済的な結び付き. Often also written 結びつき.

en.meaning: to be connected; to lead to
examples[].german: Daily practice finally led to victory.
This sweet scent is linked to my childhood memories.
en.notes: Intransitive: AとBが結び付く (A and B are connected); 〜に結び付く = to lead to something: 努力が結果に結び付く. Transitive: 結び付ける.

examples[].german: After winning the match, the mood of the team brightened.
The two were in a good mood, but then the phone rang and ruined it.
en.notes: The mood of a situation or group: いいムード, ムードメーカー (mood maker). Similar: 雰囲気.

examples[].german: I read the contract carefully to avoid unnecessary trouble.
As for me, there is no need to worry.
en.notes: な-adjective, rather formal: 無用な争い (an unnecessary quarrel), 心配ご無用 (no need to worry). On signs, "not allowed": 天地無用 (do not turn upside down).

en.meaning: next, coming (prefix: 明朝, 明年, 明後日); (Buddhism) wisdom (vidya), mantra
examples[].german: A meeting will be held at the head office at nine o'clock tomorrow morning.
The draft budget for the coming fiscal year is scheduled to be announced next month.
The company president will also attend the ceremony the day after tomorrow.
en.notes: 明〜 (みょう) is a formal prefix meaning "next, coming" in time words: 明朝 (みょうちょう), 明年 (みょうねん), 明後日 (みょうごにち), 明日 (みょうにち). These readings belong in announcements, business letters and news; in daily life one says あした, あさって, 来年. In Buddhism, 明 also means "wisdom" (vidya) or a mantra. Not to be confused with 妙 (みょう) "strange".

examples[].german: The dance began at the cue "Music, start!"
I like pop music and listen to it every day.
en.notes: Mainly in compounds, names and commands: ミュージックビデオ, ポップミュージック. The general word is 音楽.

examples[].german: This town is famous for its beautiful rows of cherry trees.
The works of a renowned painter were shown in Japan for the first time.
en.notes: More elevated than 有名な: 〜で名高い (famous for ...).

examples[].german: I planted tomato seedlings in the garden.
In May, rice seedlings are planted in the paddies.
en.notes: 苗を植える (to plant seedlings). In rice farming, the seedlings (稲の苗) are set out in the field in spring (田植え).

examples[].german: All the conference participants wore name tags on their chests.
I put a name tag on my child's umbrella.
en.notes: 名札をつける (to wear or attach a name tag). Also used for name plates on doors or objects.

en.meaning: long; at great length; stretched out
examples[].german: The principal's talk went on and on, and the students were bored.
I'm sorry for staying so long.
en.notes: Mostly 長々と: 長々と話す (to talk at great length), 長々と寝そべる (to lie stretched out). Often slightly critical or apologetic: 長々と失礼しました.

examples[].german: Please leave the used dishes in the sink.
The kitchen sink is clogged and the water won't drain.
en.notes: The kitchen sink (台所の流し); today often called シンク. Derived from 流す (to let flow).

en.meaning: to throw down; to stretch out; to give up; to abandon; to sacrifice (life, fortune)
examples[].german: Even if it is difficult, you must not give up halfway.
He sat on the floor and stretched out his legs to rest.
en.notes: Transitive: 足を投げ出す (to stretch out one's legs), 仕事を途中で投げ出す (to abandon one's work halfway), 命を投げ出す (to sacrifice one's life).

examples[].german: The two of us walked slowly along the shore at dusk.
The children were picking up seashells at the water's edge.
en.notes: Poetic word for the strip of beach where the waves run out; common in songs and names. More everyday: 浜辺 or 海岸.

examples[].german: Civil war continued in that country, and many people fled abroad.
The government sent in the army and put down the rebellion.
en.notes: Collocations: 内乱が起こる (a civil war breaks out), 内乱を鎮める (to put down a rebellion).

examples[].german: Inland towns are hot in summer and cold in winter.
Switzerland is a landlocked country with no coast.
en.notes: Often in compounds: 内陸部 (interior region), 内陸国 (landlocked country), 内陸性気候 (continental climate).

examples[].german: It is expected to take three to five days until completion.
Please have either the person themselves or a family member submit the application.
en.notes: Literary conjunction, nowadays mostly written in kana ないし. Between numbers "from ... to" (三日ないし五日), between nouns "or" (本人ないし家族).

en.meaning: inner thoughts; true feelings; inwardly; secretly
examples[].german: He was smiling, but he seemed to be angry inside.
When I heard I had passed the exam, I was secretly relieved.
en.notes: Often adverbial: 内心ほっとした (I was inwardly relieved). Contrasts with what one shows on the outside.

examples[].german: After work I went with a friend to watch a baseball night game.
Tonight's night game was canceled because of rain.
en.notes: A word coined in Japan (from English night + -er). Mainly in baseball; counterpart: デーゲーム (day game).

examples[].german: This computer has a built-in camera.
The built-in battery cannot be replaced.
en.notes: Mostly with する or attributive: バッテリーを内蔵する (to have a built-in battery), カメラ内蔵のスマートフォン (smartphone with a built-in camera). Not to be confused with 内臓 (internal organs), which is read the same.

en.meaning: to rebuke; to reproach; to take to task
examples[].german: She harshly rebuked her friend who had broken a promise.
Merely reproaching a subordinate for a mistake will not solve the problem.
en.notes: Transitive: 相手の不誠実を詰る (to reproach someone for their insincerity). Mostly written in kana なじる, because the spelling 詰る can also be read つまる.

examples[].german: It is crowded, so please move toward the middle of the car.
Around the middle of the movie, I got a little sleepy.
en.notes: In space or time: 列の中程 (in the middle of the line), 話の中程 (midway through the story). Typical train announcement: 中程までお進みください.

en.meaning: smelling of raw fish or blood; sordid, shady
examples[].german: If you don't wash the cutting board, a fishy smell remains.
Behind the scenes of the election, there is a constant stream of sordid stories about money.
en.notes: Literally: 魚が生臭い (the fish smells strongly). Figuratively, for dealings involving money and power: 生臭い話 (a sordid affair).

examples[].german: Athletes are also human beings of flesh and blood, so they get tired sometimes.
We must not forget that the person on the other side of the screen is also a flesh-and-blood human being.
en.notes: Almost always 生身の人間 (a human being of flesh and blood); it emphasizes vulnerability and humanity.

examples[].german: I forgot to put the beer in the fridge, and now it has gone lukewarm.
Such half-hearted measures won't prevent accidents.
en.notes: Literally, usually unpleasant: 生ぬるいビール (lukewarm beer). Figuratively: 生ぬるい対策 (half-hearted measures), 生ぬるい処分 (a punishment that is too mild). Also written 生温い.

examples[].german: Lead is sometimes used in old water pipes.
I'm so tired that my body feels as heavy as lead.
en.notes: The metal lead (Pb). Figuratively: 鉛のように重い (heavy as lead). Not to be confused with 訛り (dialect coloring, accent), which has the same reading.

en.meaning: to become dull; to get out of practice, to get rusty
examples[].german: I haven't exercised for a while, so I've gotten out of shape.
If you don't play every day, your piano skills get rusty.
en.notes: Intransitive, colloquial and often written in kana: 体がなまる (to get out of shape physically), 腕がなまる (to get out of practice). The same kanji is also read にぶる.

en.meaning: average, ordinary, mediocrity; (as suffix) on a par with
examples[].german: You can't pass this exam with ordinary effort.
His cooking skills are on a par with a professional's.
en.notes: 並みの (ordinary, average): 並みの努力では足りない. As a suffix: プロ並み (professional level), 人並み (like everyone else). For food, 並 denotes the standard grade: in the ranking 並・上・特上 it is the lowest quality, and in 並盛 (as opposed to 大盛) it is the regular portion.

examples[].german: A fire broke out, but the whole family escaped harm.
It's a good hotel, but if I had to find fault, it's a little far from the station.
en.notes: As a free-standing noun mainly in set phrases: 難を逃れる (to escape danger), 難を言えば (if one had to find fault), 難なく (without difficulty). Frequent as a word component: 困難, 就職難.

en.meaning: south-, southern (prefix, e.g. 南米, 南極, 南西)
examples[].german: Next year I plan to travel through South America for a month.
The ice of Antarctica is shrinking year by year.
The typhoon is moving north over the sea to the southwest of Kyushu.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 南 in compounds: 南米 "South America", 南極 "South Pole", 南西 "southwest", 南部 "the south (of an area)", 南下 "to move south". Alone and before Japanese words or katakana, it is read みなみ (separate card): 南口, 南アメリカ. Do not confuse it with the cards 何 (なん) "what" and 難 (なん) "difficulty".

en.meaning: somehow, for some reason, a little
examples[].german: I feel somehow sluggish today.
As moving day approached, I somehow started to feel lonely.
en.notes: Expresses a vague feeling: なんだか寂しい (somehow sad), なんだか変だ (somehow strange). More colloquial than 何となく.

en.meaning: this and that, all sorts of things
examples[].german: With one thing and another, I haven't had a single day off this week.
Whatever one may say, he is a friend you can rely on.
en.notes: Colloquial: なんだかんだで忙しい (busy with one thing and another), なんだかんだ言っても (whatever one may say, in the end). Also written 何だかんだ.

examples[].german: A casual remark can hurt the other person deeply.
Falling ill made me realize the value of ordinary everyday life.
en.notes: Often used adverbially as 何気なく (casually, without intention): 何気なく言った一言. Attributively: 何気ない日常 (the perfectly ordinary everyday life).

examples[].german: If anything is unclear, please ask whatever you like.
If you have any trouble, just tell me, whatever it is.
en.notes: Almost only in the polite phrase 何なりと: 何なりとお申し付けください (please tell me whatever you wish).

examples[].german: Judging ability by age alone is nonsense.
He does nothing but make nonsensical jokes.
en.notes: As a noun or attributively with な: そんな話はナンセンスだ, ナンセンスな質問 (a nonsensical question).

examples[].german: What a beautiful sunset!
What a kind person!
Sorry, what? I couldn't hear well.
en.notes: Exclamatory word before adjectives or nouns: なんてきれいなんだろう "how beautiful!", なんて素敵な人 "what a wonderful person"; the sentence often ends in 〜んだ, 〜んだろう or 〜でしょう. Mostly written in kana. Do not confuse it with the particle なんて "something like" (separate card), which stands after a noun (勉強なんて嫌い). Colloquially also as the question なんて？ "what did you say?".

en.meaning: what, how; what a ...!; surprisingly, believe it or not
examples[].german: What a beautiful view!
That woman is, believe it or not, said to be a hundred years old.
en.notes: Interrogative (なんと言えばいいか = how should I put it), exclamatory (なんと美しい景色だろう), and as a surprised opener (なんと百歳だ = a hundred years old, believe it or not).

examples[].german: Before the meal, I spread the napkin on my lap.
I bought sanitary napkins at the convenience store.
en.notes: At the table: 紙ナプキン (paper napkin), ナプキンを膝に広げる. Hygiene product: 生理用ナプキン (sanitary napkin).

examples[].german: The members' names and addresses are entered in the register.
Honored guests and parents, thank you for attending today.
en.notes: Formal conjunction of written and official language, similar to 及び. Often joins larger units: A及びB、並びにC.

en.meaning: to accustom, to get used to; (animals) to tame, to train
examples[].german: Before the actual event, let's run a little to get my body used to it.
In this region, horses have long been tamed and used for farm work.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 慣れる: 体を寒さに慣らす (to accustom the body to the cold). For animals usually written 馴らす: 馬を馴らす. Not to be confused with 鳴らす (to ring, to sound), which has the same reading.

en.meaning: getting used to something, practice, routine
examples[].german: This job isn't difficult, but it takes practice.
Many accidents are caused by carelessness born of routine.
en.notes: Noun of 慣れる: 慣れが必要だ (practice is needed), 慣れからくる油断 (carelessness resulting from routine). Suffix-like: 場慣れ (ease in a situation from experience).

examples[].german: Even though we were meeting for the first time, he spoke to me in an overly familiar way.
You must not act overly familiar with customers.
en.notes: Pejorative for inappropriately familiar behavior: 初対面なのに馴れ馴れしい. Often also written in kana なれなれしい.

en.meaning: as much as possible, as far as possible
examples[].german: Please reply as soon as possible.
Let's travel with as little luggage as possible.
en.notes: Colloquial variant of なるべく, usually in kana: なるたけ早く (as soon as possible).

examples[].german: My grandmother was a compassionate person who couldn't ignore people in trouble.
The lord was merciful and exempted poor villagers from taxes.
en.notes: From 情け (compassion) + 深い. A slightly elevated description of character: 情け深い人.

en.meaning: seductive, enchanting; tormenting, tricky (hard to decide)
examples[].german: Both proposals have advantages, so it's a tough decision.
On the stage, the dancer struck a seductive pose.
en.notes: Today often used in the sense of "hard to decide": 悩ましい問題 (a thorny issue). Besides that, literary "seductive": 悩ましい姿.

en.meaning: to torment, to plague, to trouble
examples[].german: I've been racking my brains over the new project the whole time.
I am troubled by the noise from the next room every night.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 悩む. Set phrase: 頭を悩ます (to rack one's brains). Passive: 騒音に悩まされる (to suffer from noise).

en.meaning: to name; to give a name to
examples[].german: The parents named their newborn daughter "Hana".
The newly discovered star was named "Yamato" by its discoverer.
en.notes: Transitive, usually 〜を〜と名付ける: 娘を「はな」と名付ける. The noun 名付け親 means the person who gives the name (namer; godparent).

examples[].german: In the garden at dusk, the chirping of insects echoed quietly.
Every time I hear the sound of a distant bell, I remember the mornings in my hometown.
en.notes: 音（ね）is used for the sound of a bell or the chirping of insects, for example: 鐘の音, 虫の音. The reading often appears in vivid descriptions that emphasize the perceived sound. おと is the general reading for noises; ね and おと are therefore not interchangeable in every combination. ね stays short.

en.meaning: to beg, to pester, to coax
examples[].german: The child pestered me to buy a toy.
She coaxed her father into getting her a new smartphone.
en.notes: Transitive: 親におもちゃをねだる. Usually in kana; the spelling 強請る is also read ゆする (to extort).

examples[].german: The negatives of old photos turned up from the closet.
I had new prints made from the negatives.
en.notes: Short for ネガフィルム; counterpart: ポジ (positive, slide).

examples[].german: This violin is characterized by its soft tone.
I could hear the cool sound of a wind chime.
en.notes: The characteristic sound of an instrument or a voice: バイオリンの音色. In technical contexts also read おんしょく.

examples[].german: I tightened the loose screw with a screwdriver.
To assemble the shelf, you need one screwdriver.
en.notes: Today usually called ドライバー; ねじ回し is the Japanese term.

en.meaning: to twist, to be warped; (relationship, mind) to become twisted
examples[].german: Your necktie is twisted.
After repeated misunderstandings, the two people's relationship has become warped.
en.notes: Intransitive counterpart of ねじる (to twist), usually in kana: ネクタイがねじれる. Politics: ねじれ国会 (a parliament whose two houses have different majorities).

en.meaning: to put to bed, to lay down; to let rest or age
examples[].german: After putting the children to bed, I read a book in peace.
Please let the bread dough rest for about an hour.
en.notes: Transitive: 子どもを寝かせる, 瓶を横に寝かせる (to store a bottle lying down), 生地を寝かせる (to let dough rest). Same meaning, slightly more casual: 寝かす.

examples[].german: I stayed up late yesterday, so I'm sleepy all day today.
My little brother was rubbing his sleepy eyes.
en.notes: Same meaning as 眠い, slightly more colloquial: 眠たそうな目 (sleepy eyes).

examples[].german: I am filled with a sense of gratitude toward my former teacher.
I reminded everyone once more not to get the meeting time wrong.
en.notes: Free-standing mainly in set phrases: 感謝の念 (gratitude), 念を押す (to make sure once more, to remind emphatically), 念を入れる (to proceed carefully), 念のため (just to be safe).

examples[].german: She is the oldest in the group.
My daughter will move up to the oldest kindergarten class in April.
en.notes: 年長の (older), 年長者 (older people). In kindergarten, the classes by age are called 年少, 年中 and 年長 (the oldest, usually five- to six-year-olds).

en.meaning: New Year's greeting, New Year's visit
examples[].german: At New Year, we go to relatives' houses to pay New Year visits.
Because we are in mourning, we will refrain from sending New Year's greetings.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds: 年賀状 (New Year's card), 年賀はがき. Free-standing: 年賀に行く (to pay a New Year's visit), 年賀の挨拶 (New Year's greetings).

examples[].german: In 2019, the era name changed from Heisei to Reiwa.
On the form, please write your date of birth using the era name, not the Western calendar.
en.notes: The Japanese system of dating by eras (also 元号): 年号が変わる. Besides the Western year (西暦), the era year is often used in Japan.

examples[].german: At the library, I looked through last year's statistical yearbook.
That company publishes an industry yearbook every year.
en.notes: A reference work published annually: 統計年鑑 (statistical yearbook). Not to be confused with 年間 (annual, per year), which has the same reading.

en.meaning: combustion, burning; (figurative) giving one's all, burning oneself out
examples[].german: Exercise burns the fat in your body.
I gave it everything in the last match, so I have no regrets.
en.notes: 燃焼する (to burn): 脂肪が燃焼する. Figuratively: 完全燃焼 (to give everything, holding nothing back).

en.meaning: to knead; to refine, to work out (plan, text)
examples[].german: Add water to the flour and knead it well.
We discussed it many times as a team and refined the plan.
en.notes: Transitive: 生地を練る (to knead dough), 計画を練る / 作戦を練る (to work out a plan / a strategy). Not to be confused with 寝る (to sleep), which has the same reading.

examples[].german: Moved by his enthusiasm, I decided to cooperate.
In a job interview, it is important to convey enthusiasm for the work.
en.notes: 熱意がある, 熱意を持つ; 熱意が伝わる (the enthusiasm comes across). More formal than やる気.

en.meaning: amount of heat, calorific value (calories); passion, energy
examples[].german: The calorific value of this food is 200 kilocalories per 100 grams.
I felt tremendous energy in the young director's work.
en.notes: In physics, measured in calories or joules: 食品の熱量 (calorific value of a food). Figuratively: 熱量のある演技 (a passionate performance).

examples[].german: Pour boiling water over the instant noodles and wait three minutes.
Please sterilize the baby bottle with boiling water.
en.notes: Boiling hot water, not merely warm (お湯): 熱湯を注ぐ, 熱湯で消毒する.

examples[].german: This old clock is said to be quite valuable.
That movie is worth seeing once.
en.notes: 値打ちがある (to be worth something, to be worthwhile): 一見の値打ちがある (worth a look). More everyday than 価値.

examples[].german: I helped unload the cargo from the truck.
The exam is over, and at last a weight has been lifted from my shoulders.
en.notes: Collocations: 荷を積む / 荷を降ろす (to load / to unload cargo). Figuratively: 荷が重い (too heavy a responsibility), 肩の荷が下りる (a weight is lifted from one's shoulders).

en.meaning: to become dull; to weaken, to decline (instinct, resolve)
examples[].german: The kitchen knife had become dull, so I had it sharpened.
Seeing my family's faces weakened my resolve to study abroad.
en.notes: Intransitive: 切れ味が鈍る (the blade gets dull), 勘が鈍る (one's instinct declines), 決心が鈍る (one's resolve wavers). The same kanji is also read colloquially as なまる.

examples[].german: The researchers are working day and night on developing a new drug.
Firefighters protect the safety of the town day and night.
en.notes: Literary: 日夜努力する (to work ceaselessly), 日夜を問わず (day or night).

en.meaning: to run away, to flee, to escape
examples[].german: The cage door was open, and the lion escaped.
Even if the work is hard, I don't want to run away halfway.
en.notes: Intransitive; the place left takes を or から: 家を逃げ出す (to run away from home). Also figurative: 現実から逃げ出す (to flee from reality).

en.meaning: to closely resemble, to be very similar
examples[].german: The two people's opinions are very similar.
There are many similar products, so I can't decide which to choose.
en.notes: Intransitive, usually as 似通っている or attributively 似通った: 似通った意見 (similar opinions). Somewhat more literary than 似ている.

examples[].german: I often get pimples before exams.
If you squeeze a pimple, a scar may remain.
en.notes: Usually in kana (also ニキビ). にきびができる (to get a pimple), にきびをつぶす (to squeeze a pimple). The kanji spelling 面皰 is rare.

examples[].german: Even if the body declines, I want to stay young at heart.
Work at a construction site is physical labor, so you need stamina.
en.notes: Emphasizes the physical body as opposed to the mind: 肉体と精神, 肉体労働 (physical labor).

examples[].german: This part-time job pays 10,000 yen a day.
On business trips, a daily allowance is paid in addition to travel expenses.
en.notes: Pay or expense rate per day: 日当一万円, 日当が出る. Not to be confused with 日当たり (sunniness; exposure to sunlight).

examples[].german: The event drew a cumulative total of 50,000 visitors over three days.
A cumulative total of 1,000 workers were involved in this construction work.
en.notes: Before numbers and counters: 延べ人数 (total number, in which the same person counts several times if present on several days), 延べ一万人. Not the same as the number of distinct people.

en.meaning: to swallow; to grasp, to take in
examples[].german: I can't swallow large tablets well.
The newcomer quickly grasped the work procedures.
en.notes: Transitive: 薬を飲み込む (to swallow a pill). Figuratively: 事情を飲み込む (to grasp the situation), 言葉を飲み込む (to hold back a remark).

en.meaning: to get on board, to board; to march in, to barge in (resolutely)
examples[].german: As soon as everyone had boarded the bus, it set off.
An angry customer stormed into the president's office.
en.notes: Intransitive with に: 車に乗り込む. Figuratively: 敵地に乗り込む (to advance into enemy territory), 相手の会社に乗り込む (to go to the other party's company to confront them energetically).

en.meaning: to take over, to seize; (aircraft, ship) to hijack
examples[].german: Someone hijacked my social media account.
Terrorists hijacked a passenger plane.
en.notes: Transitive: 会社を乗っ取る (to take over a company), 飛行機を乗っ取る (to hijack an aircraft). Today often: アカウントを乗っ取られる (to have one's account hijacked). Not to be confused with 則る (のっとる, to follow, to conform to).

examples[].german: This area used to be all farmland.
With no one to take over, unused farmland is increasing.
en.notes: 農地を耕す (to cultivate farmland), 農地を宅地に転用する (to convert farmland into building land).

en.meaning: to leave out, to skip; to overtake
examples[].german: In my hurry, I left one name off the list.
Just before the finish line, he overtook two runners.
en.notes: Transitive: 一行抜かす (to skip a line), 朝食を抜かす (to skip breakfast), 前の走者を抜かす (to overtake the runner ahead). Set phrase: 腰を抜かす (to be so frightened that one's legs give way).

en.meaning: to slip away, to get out, to break free
examples[].german: I slipped out of the boring meeting unnoticed.
This country's economy has finally pulled out of the recession.
en.notes: Intransitive with を or から: 会議を抜け出す (to sneak out of a meeting), 不況から抜け出す (to emerge from a recession).

examples[].german: Deep in the forest, there is a small swamp.
My foot got stuck in the swamp and I could hardly pull it out.
en.notes: Standing water, usually shallow and muddy. Recent colloquial usage: 〜の沼にハマる (to become completely hooked on a hobby).

en.meaning: master, head; owner, proprietor; originator (of a rumor); guardian spirit, long-established being (e.g. 沼の主)
examples[].german: They say the master of this pond is a big carp that has lived for a hundred years.
I could not immediately tell whose voice it was on the phone.
Mr. Tanaka has been in this section for thirty years and is practically its fixture.
en.notes: Read independently as ぬし when it means the "master" or "owner" of something: 家の主, 声の主 ("the one the voice belongs to"), うわさの主. Also typical is the old fish or spirit that has always lived in a lake (沼の主), and, figuratively, the old-timer who has been at a company forever. It appears in many compounds such as 持ち主, 飼い主, 株主, 地主. Do not confuse it with 主/しゅ (lord, God; main thing, e.g. 主として).

examples[].german: He was in need and committed theft.
Theft is never excusable.
en.notes: Noun of 盗む. Set phrase: 盗みを働く (to commit theft). As a first element: 盗み聞き (eavesdropping), 盗み見 (a furtive glance).

examples[].german: My urine was tested at the health checkup.
I was told that sugar was found in my urine.
en.notes: Medical term; in everyday speech おしっこ. 尿検査 (urinalysis), 糖尿病 (diabetes).

en.meaning: new, new- (prefix), before loanwords, e.g. ニューモデル, ニューフェース
examples[].german: A new-model smartphone will be released next month.
A newly opened cafe has appeared in front of the station.
This year's TV dramas have many new faces.
en.notes: Loan element from English "new" that stands only before other loanwords: ニューモデル "new model", ニューフェース "new face", ニューオープン "new opening"; also in place names such as ニューヨーク. Alone or before Japanese words, 新しい or the prefix 新 is used. It shares only a similar sound with ニュース "news".

en.meaning: winning a prize, placing among the prize winners
examples[].german: My daughter's painting won a prize at the city contest.
Prize winners are given a certificate and a souvenir.
en.notes: Mostly 入賞する (to win a prize, to place among the prize winners): コンクールで入賞する. It need not be first place (a victory is 優勝).

examples[].german: Please refrain from bathing when you have a fever.
At this inn, you can bathe 24 hours a day.
en.notes: More formal than お風呂に入る: 入浴する, 入浴中 (while bathing), 入浴剤 (bath additive).

examples[].german: A comet streaked across the night sky, trailing a long tail.
That bird has a long, beautiful tail.
en.notes: Literary word for tail (colloquial しっぽ); also the tail of a comet. Idiom: 尾を引く (to linger on).

en.meaning: to wear (sword, decoration); to be entrusted with; to take on (quality, tinge)
examples[].german: Toward evening, the sky took on a reddish tinge.
The plan gradually became more realistic.
en.notes: Mostly figurative: 赤みを帯びる (to take on a red tinge), 現実味を帯びる (to become realistic), 使命を帯びる (to be entrusted with a mission).

examples[].german: I have no recollection of saying such a thing.
This child learns quickly.
en.notes: 覚えがある／ない (to remember / not to remember), 覚えが早い (to learn quickly).

en.meaning: to be depressed; to slump (business); to fall into
examples[].german: After losing the match, he is deeply depressed.
Sales have slumped sharply this year.
en.notes: Most common meaning: to be down in the dumps - 試験に落ちて落ち込んでいる. Also economically: 売り上げが落ち込む.

examples[].german: My little brother is restless and can't sit still.
Although she is young, she has an air of composure.
en.notes: 落ち着きがある (to be composed), 落ち着きがない (to be restless, fidgety). Verb: 落ち着く.

examples[].german: Flattery won't get you anything.
Everyone egged me on, and I ended up taking on the organizing.
en.notes: To praise someone to get them to do something: おだてられて引き受けた (was flattered into accepting). The kanji 煽てる is rare.

en.meaning: timidly, nervously, fearfully (おどおどする)
examples[].german: The child was timid in front of the unfamiliar adults.
He apologized for being late in a nervous manner.
In the interview, don't be timid; answer confidently.
en.notes: おどおど is an onomatopoeic word describing fearful, unsure behavior out of fear or shyness, mostly as おどおどする, おどおどした様子 or おどおどと + verb. The opposite is 堂々と "confidently, with composure". Related are びくびく (flinching out of fear of something specific) and おずおず (approaching hesitantly); it is occasionally also written オドオド.

examples[].german: His victory was a surprise to everyone.
She was so astonished that she couldn't make a sound.
en.notes: Noun of 驚く. 驚きを隠せない (cannot hide one's astonishment).

en.meaning: my mother (familiar, mostly used by men)
examples[].german: My mom's cooking is the best.
I'm planning to go home at New Year's and show my face to my mother.
en.notes: Colloquial, often used by adult men about their own mother. For the father, correspondingly: 親父（おやじ）.

en.meaning: to be arrogant, to be haughty, to boast
examples[].german: Pride goes before a fall (lit. the arrogant Taira do not last long).
You must not get arrogant just because you won once.
Conceited about his talent, he began to neglect his practice.
en.notes: 驕る (also 傲る, often in kana) means "to be arrogant, haughty" and is a different word from the identically sounding 奢る "to treat someone; to live in luxury" (separate card). Typical is 〜に驕る "to be conceited about ..." (才能に驕る, 勝利に驕る) and the proverb 驕る平家は久しからず. The word is written-language and elevated; in everyday speech 威張る or 傲慢だ (separate cards) is said.

en.meaning: to corner; to drive into; to push oneself (in a final push)
examples[].german: The criminal was cornered by the police and had nowhere to run.
In the week before the exam, I really pushed myself to study.
en.notes: Transitive: 牛を柵に追い込む (to drive cattle into a pen), 相手を窮地に追い込む (to corner an opponent). Noun 追い込み (final spurt): 最後の追い込み.

examples[].german: I returned to my parents' home to take care of my aging parents.
Everyone grows old.
en.notes: Literary; in everyday speech 年を取る. Often in the た-form before nouns: 老いた両親. Noun: 老い (N3).

examples[].german: That teacher is scary when he gets angry.
The mountain road at night was dark and scary.
en.notes: Colloquial for 怖い.

examples[].german: It's because of how well you behave day to day that the weather cleared up, isn't it?
His conduct became a model for everyone.
en.notes: Behavior judged in moral terms: 日頃の行い (everyday conduct). Verb: 行う.

en.meaning: to delay; to postpone; to slow down
examples[].german: Because of the rain, we decided to delay our departure by an hour.
This medicine has the effect of slowing the progression of the disease.
en.notes: Transitive; 遅らせる has the same meaning and is more common.

examples[].german: The candy came with a free toy.
Because I bought a lot, the shop clerk gave me a hundred-yen discount.
en.notes: Mostly in hiragana. Also common as the conjunction おまけに (on top of that): 雨が降ってきた。おまけに風も強い (It started to rain. On top of that, the wind is strong).

examples[].german: A summer festival is held at the village shrine.
My grandfather visits the shrine every morning.
en.notes: Familiar word for 神社. A baby's first shrine visit is called お宮参り.

examples[].german: That was just an idea that came to me; I didn't think it through.
That's a good idea. Let's try it right away.
en.notes: Often slightly pejorative: 思いつきで決める (to decide on impulse, without thinking). Verb: 思いつく.

examples[].german: The main purpose of this study is to clarify the current state of the regional economy.
The main cause of the accident was the driver's carelessness.
Leading figures from all walks of life were invited to the ceremony.
en.notes: Formal, written-language attributive form of 主な ("main"): it stands only directly before a noun (主なる目的, 主なる原因) and cannot be used predicatively. In everyday speech and in the news, 主な is almost always used; the adverb is 主に (おもに, separate card). Caution: in 主なる神 ("God the Lord"), 主 is read しゅ, and the rare spelling 重なる has nothing to do with かさなる ("to overlap").

en.meaning: to value highly; to put great weight on
examples[].german: This family has valued etiquette since long ago.
He was a merchant who valued trust above all else.
en.notes: Literary ずる-form of 重んじる (N1), same meaning: 伝統を重んずる (to value tradition).

examples[].german: "Raise your face," the lord commanded his retainer.
The moon was reflected on the surface of the quiet lake.
She lowered her face in embarrassment.
en.notes: An elevated, literary reading of 面 for "face, countenance" (面を上げる "to raise one's gaze", 面を伏せる "to lower one's face"), for a water surface (湖の面) and for the Noh mask. The card 面/めん teaches the usual on-reading ("side, aspect; surface", e.g. この面では); 表/おもて "front side, outside" is a different word. In everyday language one says 顔 for "face".

examples[].german: In the old folktale, a woman of the village showed the traveler the way.
My grandfather used to call a little girl a "small onago", using the regional word.
en.notes: 女子（おなご）denotes a woman or girl in older texts and some regional speech. Today the word can sound rough or condescending; 女性 and 女の子 are usually more suitable as a neutral term. The same kanji are mostly read じょし in present-day standard language. Here, おなご therefore appears in an old tale or as a quoted expression.

en.meaning: same age; person of the same age
examples[].german: We are the same age, so we became friends quickly.
A friend my age got married before me.
en.notes: Colloquial; more formal: 同じ年齢.

examples[].german: If you keep making an effort, results will come naturally.
If you line up the facts, the answer becomes clear by itself.
en.notes: Literary; same meaning as 自ずと.

examples[].german: This region has a mild climate all year round.
He is a gentle person and rarely gets angry.
en.notes: な-adjective: 温和な気候 (a mild climate), 温和な性格 (a gentle personality).

examples[].german: My father is big and also strong.
I bought a dress with a large flower pattern.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun: 大柄な男性 (a big-framed man), 大柄の着物 (a kimono with a large pattern). Opposite: 小柄.

examples[].german: Even though he had only taken a small fall, he made a big show of his pain.
It's not such a big deal.
en.notes: な-adjective: 大げさに言う (to exaggerate). The kanji 大袈裟 is rare. Similar: オーバー (colloquial).

examples[].german: The wound was shallow, and it did not turn into anything serious.
Learning that a company secret had leaked outside, the president said, "This is a serious matter."
en.notes: 大事（おおごと）is a noun for a matter with major consequences. 大事になる means "to become a serious matter"; 大事にならずに済む expresses relief that it ended without serious consequences. With the other reading だいじ, 大事 can mean "important" or "valuable" as a な-adjective. For おおごと, this adjective meaning must not simply be carried over.

en.meaning: hey!; hello! (call to someone far away)
examples[].german: Hey, is that you across the river?
Before the boat pulled away, I shouted from the shore, "Hey, you forgot something!"
en.notes: おおい is a loud call to someone at some distance. It can, for example, get the attention of a friend on the other side of the street or call for a person. The writing おーい is also common. The call is casual; for politely addressing someone nearby, something like すみません is suitable. 多い（おおい）"many" and 覆い（おおい）"cover" are different words.

en.meaning: the greater part; most people; for the most part; probably
examples[].german: Contrary to most people's expectations, that team won the championship.
The work is mostly finished.
en.notes: As a noun "the greater part" (大方の人 = most people), as an adverb "for the most part; probably": 大方そんなことだろう (that's probably what it is).

examples[].german: The department head finally gave his OK.
"Is ten tomorrow all right?" "OK."
en.notes: Also pronounced オッケー and written OK. オーケーを出す／もらう (to give / to get approval).

examples[].german: Heavy rain made the river overflow, and the village was hit by flooding.
After the floodwater receded, cleaning up the house was hard work.
en.notes: A vivid, somewhat older word; in news reports 洪水 or 浸水 is more usual.

examples[].german: The two companies agreed in outline.
I will explain the outline of the plan.
en.notes: 大筋で合意する (to agree in principle). For the plot of a story, あらすじ is more common.

examples[].german: Watch your words in public.
The incident finally became public half a year later.
en.notes: 公の場 (in public), 公にする (to make public), 公になる (to become public).

examples[].german: The lion at the zoo is pacing around in its cage.
The escaped monkey was safely returned to its cage.
en.notes: For animals; figuratively also a prison cell.

examples[].german: When you come to Kyoto, please be sure to contact me.
When the opportunity arises, I'll try talking to the president.
en.notes: Elevated: その折は (on that occasion), 折を見て (when the opportunity arises), 〜の折に (on the occasion of ...).

en.meaning: weaving, weave; woven fabric (e.g. 西陣織)
examples[].german: This obi has a fine weave and is very elegant.
Nishijin-ori is a traditional craft representing Kyoto.
My grandmother made me a bag from hand-woven cloth.
en.notes: 織り is the noun of 織る "to weave" (separate card) and refers to the weave or its quality (織りが細かい) or the woven product. In place-of-origin names of fabrics it usually stands without okurigana and is pronounced -おり: 西陣織, 博多織; likewise in 手織り "hand-woven". 織物 (separate card) is the general word for textiles as a product.

en.meaning: to fold back; to turn back; to double back
examples[].german: I wore the trousers with the hems turned up.
The marathon runners turned back at the ten-kilometer point.
en.notes: The noun 折り返し is very common adverbially in the office: 折り返し電話する／折り返しご連絡します (to call back / get back to you right away). Also a turning point: 折り返し地点.

examples[].german: For many years he was loved by the people as the village head.
No one could go against the word of the head of the clan.
The wolf that leads the pack is running at the front.
en.notes: おさ is the old native Japanese reading of 長 for the head of a community (村の長, 一族の長, 群れの長) and sounds elevated, literary or fairy-tale-like. The card 長/ちょう is the Sino-Japanese reading for leader/boss and the suffix in 社長 or 校長. In modern factual language, 村長 or リーダー is said rather than 村の長.

en.meaning: to subside; to calm down; to be settled
examples[].german: After I took the medicine, my headache subsided.
The uproar would not die down for a long time.
en.notes: Intransitive: 痛みが治まる (the pain subsides), 騒ぎが治まる (the commotion dies down). Transitive: 治める. Homophones: 収まる and 納まる.

examples[].german: My older sister gave birth earlier than planned.
My wife has gone back to her parents' home for the delivery.
en.notes: Everyday word for 出産. お産が軽い／重い (an easy / a difficult birth).

examples[].german: She went to study abroad against her parents' opposition.
The company president pushed the plan through over opposing opinions.
en.notes: Mostly 〜を押し切って (pushing through despite ...): 親の反対を押し切って結婚した (married despite her parents' objections).

en.meaning: to cram in; to push in; to break in
examples[].german: I crammed all my clothes into the suitcase.
I was forced into the packed train.
en.notes: Transitive: 荷物をかばんに押し込む (to stuff luggage into a bag). Less often also "to break in" (押し込み強盗 = home-invasion robbery).

examples[].german: On the first day of the sale, customers flooded into the store.
Big waves came surging onto the shore.
en.notes: Many people or masses of water surge in: 観光客が押し寄せる (tourists flood in), 波が押し寄せる (waves surge in).

examples[].german: Is this puppy a male or a female?
Among peafowl, the male has the more beautiful feathers.
en.notes: Often in katakana オス. Opposite: 雌（めす）. Not used for people.

en.meaning: giving up; at one's wits' end
examples[].german: This problem is too hard, I give up.
The computer suddenly stopped working, and I was at my wits' end.
en.notes: Literally "raising the hands" as a sign of surrender: これはお手上げだ (I give up on this).

examples[].german: On the morning his older brother set off, the younger brother saw him off in front of the gate.
The older sister told her little sister a tale from long ago.
en.notes: A historical noun for a younger brother or younger sister. Today 弟（おとうと）usually denotes the younger brother; the short reading おと appears in older texts. The writing 乙 is also attested for this old word. The examples are narrative contexts with the deliberately historical reading おと. The noun is kept separate here from the old prefix for "younger" and from the name of a kyogen mask.

examples[].german: The feelings of a girl in love are complicated.
She is a Virgo, and her birthday is in September.
Old waka poems often depict a maiden picking flowers.
en.notes: 乙女 "young girl, maiden" sounds poetic or romantically old-fashioned and emphasizes innocence and girlishness; today it appears mainly in 乙女心 "a girl's heart", 乙女座 "Virgo (zodiac sign)" or jokingly in 乙女チック. The spelling 少女 read おとめ is rare (poems, song lyrics); normally 少女 is read しょうじょ (separate card), the neutral word for "girl".

examples[].german: I'll accompany you to the station.
I accompanied the company president on a business trip to Osaka.
en.notes: Humble: お供します (I will accompany you). Jokingly also for side dishes: ご飯のお供 (something to go with rice).

en.meaning: party B (in contracts); second rank; stylish, tasteful
examples[].german: In the contract, the company is party A and the employee is party B.
Drinking a cold beer in winter has its own special charm.
en.notes: In contracts, 甲（こう）and 乙 stand for the two contracting parties. As a な-adjective: 乙な味 (a refined, special taste).

examples[].german: As a child, I often went to buy bread on errands for my mother.
I was asked to run an errand and went to the post office.
en.notes: Especially for children: お使いに行く (to go on an errand, shopping for one's parents). Also written お遣い.

en.meaning: to bear; to take on (responsibility); to suffer (injury); to owe
examples[].german: The company should bear responsibility for the accident.
He injured his leg during the match.
en.notes: Mainly figurative: 責任を負う (to bear responsibility), けがを負う (to suffer an injury), 〜に負うところが大きい (to owe a great deal to ...). Carrying on the back is usually 背負う.

examples[].german: That temple has a golden Buddha statue.
The autumn rice fields shone golden.
en.notes: Elevated word for gold (everyday 金（きん）). Often figurative: 黄金時代 (golden age), 黄金色 (golden color).

en.meaning: emergency, makeshift, temporary measure (e.g. 応急手当, 応急処置)
examples[].german: I gave the injured person first aid until the ambulance arrived.
As an emergency repair, I plugged the hole with duct tape.
After the earthquake, temporary emergency housing was built for the victims.
en.notes: 応急 "emergency, makeshift" refers to a quick, provisional measure until a proper solution is found, and almost always stands before another noun or with の: 応急手当 "first aid", 応急修理, 応急の措置. The fixed combination 応急処置 has its own card. 救急 "emergency rescue", by contrast, stresses the emergency itself, 応急 the interim solution.

examples[].german: Because my fever was high, I asked the doctor to make a house call.
This doctor makes house calls to elderly people twice a week.
en.notes: As a verb 往診する. The doctor comes to the patient's home instead of the patient going to the clinic.

examples[].german: This solution takes on a yellow color when heated.
The machine's yellow warning light was blinking, so I stopped the work.
en.notes: 黄色（おうしょく）is a rather formal term for the color yellow, for example in technical descriptions. As a noun it can take を: 黄色を呈する "to show a yellow coloring". Before another noun, の links the color with the object. In everyday use, the reading きいろ is far more common.

examples[].german: There are several pachinko parlors in front of the station.
As a child, I played by shooting nuts with a slingshot.
en.notes: Pachinko is a vertical ball game on machines in game halls (パチンコ店). Also the children's slingshot.

examples[].german: After getting out of the bath, I changed into my pajamas.
On Sunday, I stayed in my pajamas until noon.
en.notes: パジャマに着替える (to change into pajamas), パジャマのまま (still in one's pajamas).

examples[].german: My bicycle tire got a flat, so I pushed it to the station.
A flood of orders overloaded the server.
en.notes: パンクする = to get a flat tire: タイヤがパンクした. Figuratively: to be overloaded, to break down (電話回線がパンクする). Same sound: パンク (punk music).

examples[].german: In class, we formed pairs and practiced conversation.
We gave a pair of glasses as a wedding gift.
en.notes: ペアを組む (to form a pair), ペアのグラス (a matching pair of glasses). Same sound, rare: ペア (pear).

examples[].german: His position in soccer is goalkeeper.
She holds an important position in the company.
en.notes: From English: position in sports (ポジションを守る, to hold one's position) or in an organization. At work, 地位 or 役職 are often used as well.

examples[].german: Water is drawn from the well with a pump.
I pumped air into the bicycle tire with a pump.
en.notes: A device for moving liquids or air: ポンプで水をくみ上げる (to pump up water).

examples[].german: I'm going to take a photo, so strike a pose.
His showing remorse is nothing but an act.
In a speech, it is effective to pause briefly before saying something important.
en.notes: ポーズ is first of all a body posture, for example for a photo: ポーズを取る or ポーズを決める "to pose". Figuratively it means a feigned attitude, an "act": ただのポーズ, ポーズにすぎない. Written the same but derived from English "pause", ポーズ also means "pause, break" when playing back media (ポーズボタン) or when speaking (ポーズを置く "to pause briefly"). For a break at work or school, on the other hand, 休憩 or 休み is used, not ポーズ.

examples[].german: There is hot water in the pot, so help yourself to tea.
I put tea leaves in the pot and waited three minutes.
en.notes: A teapot or coffee pot (ティーポット), and in Japanese households often the electric hot water dispenser (電気ポット) or thermos flask.

en.meaning: blushing slightly; suddenly (lighting up, appearing); absent-mindedly
examples[].german: When she was praised, she blushed slightly.
A light suddenly came on in the dark room.
I can't afford to lose to a newcomer who has just popped up out of nowhere.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic adverb for something that appears softly and suddenly: redness in the face (顔をぽっと赤らめる), a light coming on, or a person who turns up unexpectedly, hence ぽっと出 "newcomer, upstart". Do not confuse it with ほっと "relieved" (separate card) and the loanword ポット "pot" (separate card).

examples[].german: The place of production is written on the wine label.
It is handy to put labels on moving boxes.
en.notes: A label on bottles, goods or folders: ラベルを貼る (to stick on a label). For the figurative "to label someone", レッテルを貼る is more usual.

en.meaning: attendance (at an event); coming to a venue
examples[].german: Thank you very much for coming today.
As there is no parking, please refrain from coming by car.
en.notes: Formal in announcements: ご来場の皆様 (dear visitors), ご来場ありがとうございます (thank you for coming). 来場者 (visitors).

examples[].german: The hamburger steak comes with rice and soup.
Can I get a large portion of rice?
en.notes: In Western-style restaurants for cooked rice served on a plate: ライスの大盛り (large portion of rice). At home and in Japanese restaurants, ご飯 is used.

examples[].german: Please watch out for falling objects at the construction site.
A strong wind made a sign fall onto the sidewalk.
en.notes: Formal / technical: 落下物 (falling objects), 落下傘 (parachute). As a する-verb: 屋根から落下する (to fall from the roof). In everyday speech: 落ちる. Homophone: 落果 (fallen fruit).

examples[].german: We cannot be optimistic about the economic outlook.
The doctor said that the patient's condition still gives no grounds for optimism.
en.notes: 楽観的 (optimistic), 楽観視する (to view optimistically), 楽観できない / 楽観を許さない (no grounds for optimism). Opposite: 悲観.

examples[].german: At the mountain hut, we ate dinner by lamplight.
A warning light came on in the car, so I went straight to the garage.
en.notes: Mainly oil lamps or indicator lights: 石油ランプ (kerosene lamp), 警告ランプ (warning light). For room lighting, 電気 or ライト is usually used. Homophone: ランプ (highway on-ramp).

examples[].german: Drug abuse seriously harms health.
The mayor is being investigated on suspicion of abuse of authority.
en.notes: 薬物乱用 (drug abuse), 職権乱用 (abuse of authority), 権利の濫用 (abuse of rights). 濫用 is the original spelling and is common in legal texts. As a する-verb: 乱用する.

examples[].german: In an emergency, please pull this lever.
The driver operated a lever and opened the door.
en.notes: Lever on machines or vehicles: レバーを引く (to pull a lever). Homophone: レバー (liver as food, e.g. レバニラ炒め).

examples[].german: My daughter has really become a fine young lady.
He always makes a point of observing ladies first.
en.notes: Polite or humorous: 立派なレディー (a proper young lady), レディーファースト (ladies first). Homophone: レディー (ready, e.g. レディー・ゴー).

examples[].german: He came in third in the marathon race.
On the weekend, we went to watch a yacht race.
en.notes: 自動車レース (car race), レースに出る (to take part in a race). Homophone: レース (lace, as a fabric).

en.meaning: regular; standard; regular player; regular gasoline
examples[].german: My son has finally become a regular on the soccer team.
Fill it up with regular, please.
en.notes: レギュラーになる (to become a regular player), レギュラー番組 (regular program), ガソリンのレギュラー (regular gasoline; contrast: ハイオク).

examples[].german: After opening, please keep refrigerated and eat soon.
This product is delivered refrigerated.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 冷蔵する (to store cold). On packaging: 要冷蔵 (keep refrigerated). 冷蔵庫 (refrigerator); cf. 冷凍 (freezing).

en.meaning: microwave (short for 電子レンジ); range, stove
examples[].german: I heated my lunch box in the microwave.
This container cannot be used in a microwave.
en.notes: Colloquially mostly the short form of 電子レンジ: レンジで温める (to heat in the microwave). Originally also a kitchen range (ガスレンジ).

examples[].german: The nagauta ensemble lined up in a row at the back of the stage.
My grandfather went to a hot spring every year with his old friends.
en.notes: A rare secondary reading of 連中（れんちゅう）"people, guys, gang". In present-day standard language, one almost always says れんちゅう (あの連中); れんじゅう sounds old-fashioned and survives mainly in the traditional stage arts, where 〜連中 denotes the group of musicians and singers of an ensemble (長唄連中, 清元連中). As active vocabulary, れんちゅう is usually enough.

en.meaning: several days off in a row; long weekend
examples[].german: We went to a hot spring with the family over the long weekend.
After the holidays, the trains are very crowded.
en.notes: 三連休 (three days off in a row), 大型連休 (a longer holiday period such as Golden Week), 連休明け (after the days off).

examples[].german: On Okinawa, we rented a car and toured the island.
I filled up the tank before returning the rental car.
en.notes: レンタカーを借りる (to rent a car). Also used for the rental business itself: レンタカー会社, レンタカー屋 (car rental company).

examples[].german: I take piano lessons every Saturday.
An English conversation lesson is 40 minutes each.
en.notes: Mainly for music, sports and languages outside of school: ピアノのレッスン, レッスンを受ける (to take lessons). For lessons at school: 授業.

examples[].german: The Japanese team is leading by two points.
Please keep dogs on a leash in the park.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 試合をリードする (to lead in a game), 会話をリードする (to lead the conversation). 三点のリード (a three-point lead). Also: dog leash (犬のリード).

examples[].german: He was known from early childhood as a bright child.
Making use of his innate cleverness, he made a name for himself at a young age.
The master warned his disciples that the gifted are the ones who easily grow arrogant.
en.notes: 利根 is an archaic literary word for innate cleverness and quickness of understanding; as a な-adjective, 利根な means "clever, bright". In present-day Japanese one says 賢い, 利口 or 聡明 instead. The common 離婚 "divorce" (own card) sounds the same; furthermore, the spelling 利根 is mainly known from the river 利根川, which is however read とね.

en.meaning: counter for flowers and wheels, e.g. 一輪の花, 一輪車
examples[].german: I put just a single rose in the vase.
Two or three plum blossoms in the garden have begun to bloom.
My daughter can now ride a unicycle.
en.notes: Counter for single blossoms (一輪, 二輪, 三輪 - without sound change) and for wheels, especially in vehicle words such as 一輪車 "unicycle" or 二輪車 "two-wheeler". 一輪挿し is a vase for a single flower. The noun 輪（わ） "ring, circle" is a separate card; 車輪 "wheel" shows the same reading りん in a fixed word.

examples[].german: This pool holds about 500 cubic meters of water.
The cube of three is twenty-seven.
en.notes: 立方メートル (cubic meter), 立方体 (cube), 2の立方 (2 cubed). Homophone: 立法 (legislation).

examples[].german: We calculate the volume of solids such as cylinders and spheres.
This picture looks almost three-dimensional.
en.notes: 立体的 (three-dimensional, plastic), 立体駐車場 (multi-story car park), 立体交差 (grade-separated crossing). Opposite: 平面 (plane, flat surface).

examples[].german: I've been so busy lately that I haven't eaten anything decent.
If you keep telling lies, nothing good will come of it.
en.notes: Only with negation: ろくなことがない (nothing good), ろくな物を食べていない (not eating anything decent). Related: ろくに〜ない (hardly, not properly). Mostly written in kana.

examples[].german: We had dinner at a romantic restaurant with a view of the night scenery.
He has a surprisingly romantic side.
en.notes: ロマンチックな雰囲気 (romantic atmosphere). Also written ロマンティック. A romantic person is a ロマンチスト. な-adjective.

examples[].german: The new bill provoked a great debate in the Diet.
The plan was decided without sufficient discussion.
en.notes: Formal, often for public debates: 論議を呼ぶ (to provoke debate), 論議を尽くす (to discuss thoroughly). Similar: 議論.

examples[].german: We tied the boat to the shore with a rope.
Ropes are stretched across off-limits areas.
en.notes: A thick rope: ロープを張る (to stretch a rope), ロープで縛る (to tie with a rope). Thinner: ひも, 縄.

examples[].german: We took the ropeway to the summit.
The ropeway is not running because of strong winds.
en.notes: Aerial cable car in mountains or tourist areas; also written ロープウエー. Similar: ケーブルカー (funicular).

examples[].german: In class, the students recited a poem one by one.
A reading of the novel by an actor was broadcast on the radio.
en.notes: Expressive reading aloud of literature: 詩の朗読 (poem recitation), 朗読会 (reading event). As a する-verb: 朗読する. For plain reading out: 読み上げる.

examples[].german: As the saying goes, "birds of a feather flock together": all his friends love fishing.
This is a large-scale construction project unparalleled even in the world.
en.notes: 他に類のない (unique, without equal), 類を見ない (unprecedented). As a suffix: 哺乳類 (mammals), 書類 (documents). Proverb: 類は友を呼ぶ (birds of a feather flock together).

examples[].german: From the kanji I knew, I inferred the meaning of the unknown word.
It is dangerous to judge only by analogy with past cases.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 〜から類推する (to infer by analogy from ...). In language learning: 知っている漢字から意味を類推する (to infer the meaning from kanji one knows).

examples[].german: He is lax about time and always arrives late to meetings.
You'd better not lend money to people who are careless with money.
en.notes: Mainly sloppy with time, money or promises: 時間にルーズな人 (someone who isn't strict about punctuality). For clothing: loose-fitting, baggy. な-adjective.

examples[].german: During the war, many works of art were plundered.
After the riot, looting occurred one after another in the shopping street.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 町を略奪する (to plunder a town). 略奪者 (plunderer). Also written 掠奪.

examples[].german: This airport is used by tens of thousands of passengers every day.
A large passenger plane landed on the runway.
en.notes: Formal, mainly in transportation: 旅客機 (passenger aircraft), 旅客船 (passenger ship). Also read りょきゃく. In everyday speech: 乗客.

en.meaning: end, conclusion (e.g. at the end of a text); consent (了とする)
examples[].german: Even the long serial ended with the single character "end".
I wrote "end" on the last page of the manuscript.
The department head accepted my explanation.
en.notes: On its own, 了 appears almost only in written texts: as "end" at the close of a manuscript, a novel or a serial, and in the elevated phrase 了とする "to approve, to accept". In normal usage, the character is met mainly in compounds such as 終了 "end, completion" and 了解 "understood" (both own cards). For "end", people say 終わり in everyday life.

examples[].german: Each daimyo ruled over his own domain.
The victorious country gained part of the enemy's territory.
en.notes: Mainly historical: the land of a feudal lord or state. 領地を治める (to rule a territory). For present-day states, 領土 is usually used.

examples[].german: A foreign fishing boat entered Japanese territorial waters.
This law does not apply outside territorial waters.
en.notes: Sea area under state sovereignty (generally up to 12 nautical miles): 領海侵犯 (violation of territorial waters). Cf. 領土 (national territory), 領空 (airspace). Homophone: 了解 (understood).

en.meaning: both extremes; both poles; positive and negative poles
examples[].german: The opinions of the two were polarized at opposite extremes.
At both of the Earth's poles, the ice keeps on melting.
en.notes: 両極端 (two extremes), 両極化 (polarization). Geography: 北極と南極 (North and South Pole); electricity: プラス極とマイナス極 (positive and negative poles).

en.meaning: to skip (class); to slack off; to shirk
examples[].german: Because it was raining, I skipped class and slept at home.
If you slack off on practice, your stamina drops quickly.
en.notes: Colloquial godan verb formed from サボ(タージュ) + る: 授業をサボる (to skip class), 仕事をサボる.

en.meaning: to be decided; to become settled
examples[].german: The company's policy has finally been decided.
My hand is shaking and I cannot aim steadily.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: 方針が定まる, 狙いが定まらない. Transitive: 定める.

en.meaning: to be clear; to be wide awake; to be bright
examples[].german: I drank too much coffee and I'm wide awake and can't sleep.
You look pale today. What's wrong?
en.notes: Ichidan verb: clear and bright (冴えた月, a bright moon), mentally alert (目が冴える = to be unable to fall asleep); negated 冴えない = dull, gloomy.

examples[].german: In the morning, little birds were chirping outside the window.
In the spring forest, the birds chirp happily.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb for birdsong; usually written in kana: 小鳥がさえずる (a little bird chirps).

examples[].german: I exchanged it for a cheaper product and got the difference back.
If you change to a larger room, please pay the difference.
en.notes: The difference between two amounts: 差額を払う, 差額ベッド (surcharge for a better hospital room).

en.meaning: not so much; not particularly (with negative)
examples[].german: The exam this time was not particularly difficult.
It is not very far from the station to the venue.
en.notes: Mostly with a negative: さほど難しくない (not particularly difficult). Somewhat more literary than それほど; usually written in kana.

examples[].german: The police reconstructed the circumstances of the accident.
This restaurant recreates the townscape of the past.
en.notes: To recreate or reenact something faithfully (事故を再現する, to reconstruct an accident; 再現ドラマ, a dramatized reenactment); also the reappearance of something.

examples[].german: I met my high school friends again for the first time in ten years.
The two parted, promising to meet again.
en.notes: Meeting again after a long time; as a verb 再会する. Homophone: 再開 (resumption).

examples[].german: This village is famous for its bamboo craftwork.
Someone seems to have tampered with the documents.
en.notes: Fine craftsmanship (竹細工 bamboo work, ガラス細工 glasswork) and, pejoratively, a trick or manipulation (細工をする, to tamper).

examples[].german: With night shifts continuing, my daily rhythm got disrupted.
This machine operates in a ten-minute cycle.
en.notes: A regularly recurring process: 生活のサイクル (daily rhythm), 景気のサイクル (economic cycle).

examples[].german: Silver was once mined in this mountain.
Extracting oil costs a great deal.
en.notes: To extract mineral resources from the earth: 石炭の採掘 (coal mining), 金を採掘する (to mine gold).

examples[].german: For my summer vacation homework I collected insects.
For research, I collected seashells on the beach.
en.notes: To collect samples or specimens: 昆虫採集 (insect collecting), 植物採集 (plant collecting). Homophone: 最終 (final).

examples[].german: A new proposal was adopted at the meeting.
The committee adopted the draft resolution unanimously.
en.notes: To formally adopt a motion, resolution or textbook: 決議を採択する (to adopt a resolution), 教科書の採択 (textbook adoption).

examples[].german: Do you have this shirt one size larger?
The shoes don't fit, and my feet hurt.
en.notes: Size of clothing, shoes and objects: サイズが合わない, Mサイズ.

examples[].german: You should not fuss over trifles but look at the whole picture.
He meddles even in trivial matters.
en.notes: Literary word for insignificant things: 些事にこだわる. Homophone: さじ (spoon).

examples[].german: We practiced handstands in P.E. class.
Even if I stood on my head, I could never beat that player.
en.notes: Standing on one's hands or head; as a verb 逆立ちする. Idiom: 逆立ちしても (even if one stood on one's head, i.e. impossible).

en.meaning: to gain vigor, to flare up (fire); to flourish (obsolete); to be in heat (animals)
examples[].german: Since the fire was blazing well, I stopped adding firewood.
A firefighter rescued the child from the raging flames.
In spring, cats are in heat and cry at night.
en.notes: さかる is intransitive and describes something gaining strength, above all fire: 火が盛る and especially the compound 燃え盛る "to burn fiercely". The meaning "to thrive, prosper" is obsolete; for animals, さかる means "to be in heat" (often written サカる). Do not confuse it with the transitive 盛る/もる "to serve, to pile up" (own card), as in ご飯を盛る.

examples[].german: My grandfather poured sake into his cup and drank it slowly.
The two exchanged cups and swore brotherhood.
en.notes: A small cup for sake; also the ritual exchange of cups as a sign of a bond (杯を交わす). As a counter, however, 杯 is read はい.

examples[].german: As stated earlier, this plan has problems.
I'm tired, so I'll go to bed first.
en.notes: Earlier in time (先に述べたように = as already mentioned) or first, before others: お先に失礼します.

en.meaning: urgent, immediate, as soon as possible
examples[].german: We apologize for the inconvenience. We will respond immediately.
This accident-prone intersection needs urgent countermeasures.
Your documents were incomplete, so please resubmit them as soon as possible.
en.notes: Na-adjective, mostly adverbial as 早急に "immediately" or attributive in 早急な対策/早急な対応. The traditional reading is さっきゅう; そうきゅう is by now just as widespread and generally accepted - it is the same word. Typical of business language, government offices and news; related are 至急 "urgent, immediate" and 緊急 "emergency, urgent", which stress haste and an emergency respectively.

examples[].german: There is a fence around the pasture.
It is dangerous, so please do not climb over the railing.
en.notes: A barrier made of posts, slats or bars: 柵を作る, 柵を越える.

examples[].german: This painting is said to be a work by Picasso.
The weather was good this year, so the rice harvest is good.
en.notes: A work (ピカソの作 = a work by Picasso); also the crop yield (今年は米の作がいい). As a suffix: 〜作 (最新作, 代表作).

examples[].german: This short story is an early work the author wrote in his twenties.
Critics judged his works harshly.
The atmosphere of an era is reflected in an artist's works.
en.notes: Elevated, written-language word for a literary or artistic "work"; in everyday speech 作品 is said. Same spelling as 作物/さくもつ "crops", but a separate word - which reading is meant follows from the context (literature and art versus agriculture). Typical of literary criticism and older texts, often with a possessor such as 彼の作物.

examples[].german: I've had the chills since morning, and when I took my temperature it was 38 degrees.
Hearing the scary story sent a chill down my spine.
en.notes: 寒気がする = to have the chills, to shiver (often with a fever). With the reading かんき, 寒気 means "cold air" in weather forecasts.

examples[].german: This liquid is a strong acid, so please do not touch it with your hands.
The acid in the stomach breaks down food.
en.notes: In chemistry: acid (opposite: アルカリ). The adjectival form is 酸性 (acidic in the chemical sense); a sour taste is 酸っぱい.

examples[].german: The poet wrote a poem praising the nature of his hometown.
His courageous act was praised by many people.
en.notes: Elevated word for high praise: 自然を賛美する. In church: 賛美歌 (hymn).

examples[].german: Apples are a typical product of this region.
This new medicine is the product of many years of research.
en.notes: Products of a region (土地の産物) and figuratively the result of something: 努力の産物, 時代の産物.

examples[].german: When I found out I was pregnant, I went to see an OB-GYN.
It is hard to get an appointment at this hospital's OB-GYN department.
en.notes: Hospital department or clinic for obstetrics (産科) and gynecology (婦人科).

examples[].german: Please don't overexert yourself for a while after giving birth.
My mother came to help until my health recovered after the birth.
en.notes: The period after childbirth: 産後休暇 (postnatal leave). Opposite: 産前 (before birth). Similar sound: さんご (coral).

examples[].german: I will call on you again tomorrow afternoon.
I have come today regarding your request.
en.notes: Humble word (謙譲語) for one's own visit to a superior: 明日参上いたします. Today formal or jocular.

examples[].german: "You dropped this." "Thank you!"
Thanks for helping. You were a great help.
en.notes: Casual "thank you" from English, only among friends. Polite: ありがとうございます.

examples[].german: A small temple stands on the mountainside.
Heavy rain caused part of the mountainside to collapse.
en.notes: The middle part of a mountain slope, between the foot (麓) and the summit (山頂).

examples[].german: This country produces large quantities of oil.
This region has produced high-quality stone since long ago.
en.notes: Mainly for mineral resources and products of a region: 石油を産出する (to produce oil). As a verb: 産出する.

examples[].german: The children are looking forward to presents from Santa Claus.
My father put on a Santa Claus costume and surprised the children.
en.notes: Often shortened to サンタ（さん）. In Japan, Santa Claus brings children presents on Christmas Eve.

examples[].german: I hung the laundry on the pole.
The rod bent, and a big fish was hooked.
en.notes: A long, thin pole: 釣り竿 (fishing rod), 物干し竿 (laundry pole).

en.meaning: to snatch away; to carry off; (applause, prizes) to take all for oneself
examples[].german: A big wave swept my hat away.
The new singer won the crowd's favor at the venue.
en.notes: Mostly written in kana さらう. To take someone or something away by force (子どもをさらう, 波にさらわれる) and figuratively: 人気をさらう (to steal the spotlight).

en.meaning: to hold out; to hand over; to submit; to send
examples[].german: He held out his hand with a smile.
I handed over my business card at the reception desk.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to stretch out one's hand, to hand over or submit something; 差出人 is the sender.

en.meaning: to approach; to come to (a place or stage)
examples[].german: When the car came to the bridge, it started to rain.
The negotiations have finally reached their final stage.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb with に: to come to a place (橋に差し掛かる) or enter a phase (交渉が山場に差し掛かる).

examples[].german: I take orders from no one.
He does nothing himself and only gives orders to others.
en.notes: Giving instructions, often with the nuance of "bossing people around": 人の指図は受けない. As a verb 指図する.

examples[].german: The mother stroked her crying child's back.
I rubbed my bumped knee with my hand.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to rub gently over something with the hand, usually written in kana: 背中をさする.

examples[].german: After such a long journey, you must be very tired.
Having heard that you passed, your parents must have been very happy.
en.notes: Sympathetic conjecture, usually with だろう or でしょう: さぞ大変だったでしょう. Stronger forms: さぞかし, さぞや.

examples[].german: The air conditioner will be installed next Monday.
It has been decided to install security cameras at the station.
The government announced the establishment of a new committee.
en.notes: The noun for 設置する (own card): the setting up of equipment (エアコンの設置, 設置場所, 設置工事) and the establishment of bodies or offices (委員会の設置). Typical of official, corporate and manual texts; for devices, one colloquially often says 取り付け. Do not confuse it with the homophone 接地 "grounding".

examples[].german: My son will also be a university student from next year.
My son has agreed to take over the shop.
en.notes: A humble, somewhat old-fashioned word for one's own son: うちの倅. Also written 伜, often in kana せがれ. Neutral: 息子.

examples[].german: This restaurant is reservation-only.
This gym is members-only, so you cannot use it unless you are a member.
en.notes: Suffix after nouns: 会員制 (members only), 予約制 (by reservation only), 二交代制 (two-shift system), 六三制 (school system with six years of elementary and three of middle school).

en.meaning: pure and impure; good and evil; unvoiced and voiced sounds
examples[].german: A leader of a large organization needs the generosity to accept both good and bad.
In Japanese kana there is a distinction between unvoiced and voiced sounds.
en.notes: Mainly in 清濁併せのむ (to accept both the good and the bad, to be broad-minded). In linguistics: 清音 and 濁音, e.g. か and が.

examples[].german: This sake is brewed by a traditional method.
The shop owner taught me in detail how miso is made.
en.notes: How something is made: 伝統的な製法, 昔ながらの製法 (traditional method), 製法を守る (to keep to the method).

examples[].german: This year the weather has been favorable and the vegetables are growing well.
This plant grows well even in the shade.
en.notes: 〜する: to grow and thrive, especially of plants: 稲の生育, 生育が悪い (poor growth). For animals 成育 is usually written.

en.meaning: growing up, growth (to maturity; esp. humans and animals)
examples[].german: The fry are growing well in the warm sea.
Sufficient sleep is indispensable for the growth of children.
This zoo keeps records of the pandas' growth.
en.notes: Technical term for growing up to maturity, also as 成育する. Identical in sound with 生育 (vocab-n1:correction:seiiku), which by newspaper and government usage is rather used for plants, while 成育 is preferred for animals and humans. The general everyday word for growth is 成長 (vocab-n2:149).

examples[].german: She is an actress popular for her pure image.
That song sings of the pure feelings of first love.
en.notes: な-adjective, mostly about young women and their image: 清純な少女, 清純派 (actress with an innocent image).

examples[].german: He makes his living by painting.
My mother supported the family's livelihood with a part-time job.
en.notes: 生計を立てる (to earn one's living), 一家の生計を支える (to support the family's livelihood). More formal than 暮らし. Read the same as 整形 (cosmetic surgery, orthopedics).

examples[].german: I obtained the visa through the proper procedures.
He went from being a temp worker to a regular employee.
en.notes: Mostly with の or in compounds: 正規の手続き (proper procedure), 正規雇用 (permanent employment; opposite 非正規), 正規品 (genuine goods).

examples[].german: This watch is exquisitely made, and you can see the craftsman's high skill.
Elaborate counterfeit bills that look just like the real thing were found.
en.notes: な-adjective: 精巧な細工 (fine handiwork), 精巧な機械 (precision machine), 精巧に作られた偽物 (an elaborately made fake).

examples[].german: The government issued a statement about the incident.
The leaders of the two countries signed a joint statement.
en.notes: A public statement: 声明を出す/発表する, 共同声明 (joint statement). Read the same as 生命 (life). Buddhist chanting is also written 声明 but read しょうみょう.

examples[].german: In Japan, you become an adult at 18.
Until you reach adulthood, parental consent is required.
en.notes: Legal: 成年に達する (to reach the age of majority), 未成年 (minor). In Japan the age of majority has been 18 since 2022. Not to be confused with 青年 (young person), which is read the same.

examples[].german: The students lined up on the schoolyard.
The passengers were lined up on the platform waiting for the train.
en.notes: 〜する: to line up neatly (school, sports, platform): 二列に整列する (to line up in two rows).

examples[].german: He is studying the physiology of sleep at university.
During my period, I sometimes get stomach pain.
en.notes: 1. The body's life processes: 生理学 (physiology), 生理的 (physiological). 2. Everyday word for menstruation: 生理痛 (period pain). Read the same as 整理 (sorting out).

en.meaning: life and death; life or death
examples[].german: This is a matter of life and death for the patient.
Three days after the accident, it is still not known whether the passengers are alive or dead.
en.notes: 生死にかかわる (a matter of life and death, life-threatening), 生死不明 (unknown whether dead or alive).

examples[].german: Many guests gathered at the party in formal attire.
On Coming-of-Age Day, my daughter went out dressed up in a furisode.
en.notes: 〜する: to dress especially splendidly (celebration, reception). Read the same as 正装 (prescribed formal dress) and 清掃 (cleaning).

en.meaning: to restrain; to curb; to win; to control
examples[].german: He raised his hand and restrained the noisy students.
After extra time, the home team won the match.
en.notes: Transitive, formal. 騒ぐ人を制する (to quiet noisy people), 試合を制する (to win a match), 市場を制する (to dominate a market). Proverb: 先んずれば人を制す (he who acts first has the upper hand).

examples[].german: This painting has a static composition and gives a calm impression.
Static stretching is best done after exercise.
en.notes: な-adjective, opposite: 動的 (dynamic). Technical and educated usage: 静的な状態 (static state), 静的なストレッチ (static stretching).

examples[].german: The athletic meet was blessed with fine weather.
Fine weather continued, and the fields dried out completely.
en.notes: Formal, e.g. in weather reports: 晴天に恵まれる (to be blessed with fine weather). The expression 青天の霹靂 (a bolt from the blue) is written with 青天.

examples[].german: This town flourished on ironmaking.
A large amount of coal is used in ironmaking.
en.notes: 製鉄所 (ironworks, steel mill), 製鉄業 (iron and steel industry).

en.meaning: flattery, compliment (without the polite prefix; cf. お世辞)
examples[].german: That salesman is good at flattery.
I'm bad at paying compliments I don't mean.
Flattery aside, this dish is really delicious.
en.notes: Base form of お世辞 (separate card), which is almost always used in present-day conversation. Without お, 世辞 appears mainly in written language and fixed phrases: 世辞がうまい "to be good at flattery", 世辞を言う "to pay compliments", 世辞抜きで "flattery aside, honestly". When speaking freely, it is better to say お世辞.

en.meaning: to hurry (someone); to rush; to urge
examples[].german: My mother rushed me, saying to get ready quickly.
I don't mean to rush you, but I'd like a reply this week.
en.notes: Transitive: to urge someone to hurry. Often passive: 急かされる (to be rushed). To hurry oneself is 急ぐ.

examples[].german: The doctor made an incision in the affected area and drained the pus.
My daughter was born by cesarean section.
en.notes: 〜する: to cut open with a scalpel: 切開手術 (incision surgery), 帝王切開 (cesarean section).

examples[].german: My mother worked at frugality for years and prepared the money for her children's school fees.
The mayor reviewed how public funds are used and showed an attitude that values frugality.
en.notes: 節倹 means holding back on spending and living simply. As a noun it appears in phrases such as 節倹に努める "to strive for frugality" or 節倹を重んじる "to value frugality". 節倹する is also recorded. The examples show a personal way of life and the handling of public funds. The identically pronounced 石鹸・せっけん means "soap" and is a different word.

examples[].german: In health class, students learn correct knowledge about sex and contraception.
In medicine, biological sex is called "sex" and social sex "gender" to distinguish them.
en.notes: Loanword for "sexual intercourse", also as the verb セックスする (with a partner marked by と); it is direct, but not vulgar. 性行為 sounds more factual or official, エッチ is a colloquial euphemism. In biology and medicine, セックス also denotes biological sex as opposed to ジェンダー; in everyday speech 性別 is said for this.

examples[].german: He will be transferred to a different section next month.
The report is divided into three sections.
en.notes: A subdivision within a company or organization; also a section of a text.

examples[].german: In the second half, the team switched from defense to attack.
The new president grew the company with an aggressive management style.
