en.notes: Noun form of 攻める; opposite 守り (defense). 攻めに転じる (to go on the offensive), 攻めの姿勢 (offensive stance). Not to be confused with 責め (blame, torment), which is read the same.

en.meaning: attacker; attacking side; method of attack
examples[].german: In the second half the team lacked attacking options and ended up scoreless.
The opponent's defense is solid, and I just can't find a way to attack.
The player who had focused entirely on defense suddenly switched to attack in the closing stages.
en.notes: Noun of 攻める "to attack" (separate card), mainly in sports reports, go/shogi and combat sports. Typical phrases: 攻め手を欠く "to lack means of attack", 攻め手に回る "to go on the offensive"; the opposite is 守り手. Not to be confused with the identically sounding adverb せめて "at least", which is always written in kana.

en.meaning: former, previous, late (e.g. 先の家 = the former house); first move (go/shogi, martial arts)
examples[].german: This is a photo from when we lived in our previous house.
In go, Black is supposed to play first.
In kendo, it is important to take the initiative before your opponent.
en.notes: Read せんの in colloquial speech (先の) for "former, previous" (先の家, 先の社長); in written, formal language 先の is usually read さきの instead. It is also a technical term for the first move or the initiative in go, shogi and kendo (先を取る). The everyday reading さき ("ahead, tip, before") has its own card (先/さき).

examples[].german: In ancient China, there were people who trained in the mountains aiming to become immortals.
Kakinomoto no Hitomaro is counted among the great masters of poetry.
The old man who had left the secular world lived just like a hermit-immortal.
en.notes: Written-language short form of 仙人 (separate card), the usual word for the Taoist mountain hermit. Rare on its own, but common in compounds: 歌仙 "poet saint, master of poetry", 詩仙 "master of Chinese poetry", 仙境 "fairyland". Do not confuse it with the homophones 千, 線, 栓 and 〜戦.

examples[].german: A gift will be given to the first 100 people.
Seats are first come, first served.
en.notes: Mainly in 先着順 (in order of arrival) and 先着〜名 (the first ... people), e.g. for promotions and registrations.

examples[].german: The taste of this shop has not changed since the previous owner's time.
The previous president was a person who valued his employees greatly.
en.notes: The previous owner of a business, title or head of a family: 先代の社長, 先代から続く店 (a shop that has continued from the previous generation). Read the same as the city 仙台.

examples[].german: Thank you for your help the other day.
About the matter we discussed the other day, how are things since then?
en.notes: Formal, especially in polite phrases and letters: 先だってはありがとうございました. Similar: 先日.

examples[].german: Please keep a sufficient distance from the vehicle ahead.
My feelings are running ahead and my body can't keep up.
en.notes: 〜する: to go ahead, to precede in time: 先行する車 (preceding vehicle), 先行研究 (previous research), 先行販売 (advance sale). Read the same as 選考 (selection).

examples[].german: We will notify you of the selection result by email next week.
I passed the document screening and moved on to the interview.
en.notes: 〜する: to examine and select applicants: 書類選考 (screening by documents), 選考委員 (selection committee). Read the same as 先行 (going ahead).

en.meaning: missionary work; propagation of a religion
examples[].german: Xavier carried out Christian missionary work in Japan.
The missionaries traveled around the regions and continued their missionary work.
en.notes: 〜する: to proclaim and spread a religion. 宣教師 (missionary).

examples[].german: The reporter infiltrated the factory as a worker.
A police officer infiltrated the yakuza and gathered information.
en.notes: 〜する: to infiltrate somewhere secretly: 潜入捜査 (undercover investigation), 潜入取材 (undercover reporting).

en.meaning: fighting strength; military strength; valuable asset (to a team)
examples[].german: As a newcomer, he has already become a major asset to the team.
There was a big difference in the military strength of the two armies.
en.notes: Military: armed forces, fighting strength. Figuratively: someone who contributes to the success of a team or company: 即戦力 (someone who can contribute immediately).

examples[].german: After the war, Japan was occupied by the Allied Powers.
My younger brother is occupying the sofa in front of the TV all by himself.
en.notes: 〜する: to occupy militarily (占領軍 occupation forces, 占領下 under occupation). In everyday use: to claim a place for oneself alone: ソファーを占領する.

en.meaning: infinitely varied; to each their own
examples[].german: Tastes are all different.
The same question drew completely different answers.
en.notes: Literally "a thousand differences, ten thousand variations". It stresses the great diversity of opinions, tastes or people; similar to 十人十色.

examples[].german: This temple escaped war damage and remains as it was long ago.
The center of the town was almost entirely burned down in the war.
en.notes: Destruction caused by war: 戦災を受ける (to suffer war damage), 戦災を免れる (to be spared by the war), 戦災孤児 (war orphan). Read the same as 繊細 (delicate, sensitive).

examples[].german: At university I specialized in Japanese history.
He studied cooking at a vocational school.
en.notes: 〜する: to concentrate on one subject. 専修学校 (vocational school). More common for one's major: 専攻. Read the same as 先週 (last week).

examples[].german: She has good taste in clothes.
He has a sense of humor.
en.notes: センスがいい (tasteful, with flair), ユーモアのセンス (sense of humor), ファッションセンス. Not "sense" in the meaning of significance (= 意味). Read the same as 扇子 (folding fan).

examples[].german: His heart disease is congenital.
Is musical talent innate, or can it be acquired through effort?
en.notes: な-adjective; opposite: 後天的 (acquired). 先天的な病気 (congenital disease), 先天的な才能 (innate talent).

examples[].german: This parking lot is for residents only.
He works in a room reserved for his own use.
en.notes: Often as a suffix: 女性専用車両 (women-only car), 歩行者専用 (pedestrians only), 専用の部屋 (a room of one's own).

examples[].german: A ceremony was held to celebrate the completion of the new bridge.
The winning team received the trophy at the award ceremony.
en.notes: A formal celebration, often at public occasions: 開会セレモニー (opening ceremony), 表彰セレモニー (award ceremony). Japanese equivalents: 式, 式典.

examples[].german: The cars touched lightly, but nobody was hurt.
The reporter tried to get in contact with people connected to the incident.
en.notes: 〜する: 接触事故 (accident from a scrape), 接触が悪い (poor contact, loose connection). With people: 〜と接触する (to make contact with).

examples[].german: I blended the two proposals and made a new plan.
This house has a blend of Japanese and Western styles.
en.notes: 〜する: to combine different things and take the best of each: 和洋折衷 (blend of Japanese and Western style), 折衷案 (compromise proposal).

en.meaning: occasion, time (その節は); section, paragraph, stanza; clause (grammar); season; principles, integrity; knot (nautical mile per hour)
examples[].german: Thank you very much for your great help on that occasion.
Please read section 2 of chapter 3 by next week.
No matter what pressure he was under, he did not compromise his principles.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 節, as opposed to ふし (separate card) "knot, joint; melody" as a concrete word. せつ appears in elevated phrases such as その節はお世話になりました "thank you for your help back then", for text sections (第二節 "section 2") and for principles in 節を曲げる "to betray one's principles". Do not confuse it with the homophone 説 "theory".

en.meaning: to be stiff and formal; to be tense
examples[].german: Don't be so stiff in the job interview; speak naturally.
My grandfather greeted everyone in a stiff, formal way and made them laugh.
en.notes: From 鯱 (しゃちほこ), the stiff fish figure on castle roofs: someone behaves in an overly formal way out of nervousness. Often used as しゃちほこばった. The kanji spelling 鯱張る is rare.

examples[].german: He is bad at socializing and rarely goes to parties.
Socializing is also important in business.
en.notes: Dealing with other people in society: 社交的 (sociable), 社交辞令 (polite formality), 社交ダンス (ballroom dancing).

en.meaning: free and easy, carefree, open-hearted, unpretentious
examples[].german: My grandfather was an easygoing person who didn't fuss over things.
His free and easy character attracted many friends.
In his late works, a carefree state of mind can be detected.
en.notes: A rare na-adjective of elevated written language for a character that is free of pettiness and open, e.g. 洒落な人柄. Same spelling as 洒落/しゃれ "pun, joke" (card), but a separate word; without a reading aid, 洒落 is almost always read しゃれ. Close in meaning are 洒脱 "smart, unconstrained" and 磊落 "magnanimous, easygoing".

en.meaning: to be stylish; to dress up; to joke
examples[].german: A stylish cafe has opened in front of the station.
He lightened the mood with a witty remark.
en.notes: Ichidan verb, mostly in the form しゃれた (stylish, tasteful): しゃれた店 (a stylish shop). Less often "to make a pun". Noun: 洒落.

examples[].german: Since my transfer, my family and I have been living in company housing.
Company housing has cheap rent, but many colleagues live in the neighborhood.
en.notes: Housing that a company provides to its employees at a low price.

examples[].german: My grandfather is currently not allowed any visitors.
I politely declined the interview request.
en.notes: Formal refusal, known from 面会謝絶 (no visitors allowed in a hospital).

examples[].german: The king left the castle in a four-horse chariot.
The coachman led the team of four to a stream.
en.notes: A historical noun, found mainly in texts about ancient China, for the four horses of a team or the chariot they pull. The reading is し; on this card, the kana writing し is to be understood exclusively as a phonetic writing of this noun. Today one usually says 四頭立ての馬車 or names the team explicitly. The two examples distinguish riding in the chariot from leading the four horses.

en.meaning: shh!, hush! (for quiet); shoo!, scat! (to drive off animals)
examples[].german: Shh, be quiet! The baby is sleeping.
When we were talking in the library, the teacher warned us with a "shh".
I shooed away the cat that had come into the garden with "shoo, shoo".
en.notes: Interjection said with the index finger in front of the mouth to make someone be quiet; doubled, しっしっ serves to shoo away animals or annoying people. Normally written in kana; the spelling 叱 is ateji and rare. It has nothing to do with 叱る "to scold", even though it is the same kanji.

examples[].german: This shirt has a very careful finish.
The photos will be ready next week.
en.notes: How something turned out in the end: 仕上がりがきれいだ (neatly finished). Verb: 仕上がる (to be finished).

examples[].german: Top it with parsley as a finishing touch, and it is done.
The finishing of the work took three days.
en.notes: The last step of the work: 仕上げにこしょうを振る (to sprinkle pepper at the end). Verb: 仕上げる.

examples[].german: I have to finish the report by the deadline.
The craftsman finished the chair in one day.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb: to bring a piece of work to completion (レポートを仕上げる). Intransitive: 仕上がる.

examples[].german: Mowing the lawn in the garden is my father's job.
The turf at the racecourse is neatly kept.
en.notes: The lawn grass itself; the lawn area is usually called 芝生. 芝を刈る (to mow the lawn).

examples[].german: The opposing team fought tenaciously to the end.
This weed is tenacious and grows back even after I pull it out.
en.notes: い-adjective: someone who does not give up or is hard to beat, sometimes praising, sometimes derogatory (しぶとい相手).

examples[].german: Please do not save personal data on the company computer.
Before I quit, I cleared my personal belongings from my desk.
en.notes: Personal items as opposed to company or school property: 私物を持ち込む (to bring personal items in).

examples[].german: You can see the whole city from the top of the hill.
Many streets in the city were flooded by the typhoon.
en.notes: The built-up streets of a city: 市街戦 (street fighting). Common in 市街地 (urban area).

examples[].german: This zoo keeps pandas.
At the elementary school, the children take care of the rabbits.
en.notes: More technical than 飼う: 動物を飼育する, 飼育係 (animal keeper). For plants one says 栽培.

en.meaning: to stock up; to purchase (goods); to pick up (information)
examples[].german: This restaurant buys fish at the market every morning.
Before the trip, I gathered information about the local area.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb for a shop's purchasing of goods; figuratively also 情報を仕入れる. Noun: 仕入れ.

examples[].german: I moved the car seat back a little.
The seats on this bus are wide and comfortable to sit in.
en.notes: Seat in vehicles and at events: シートベルト (seat belt), チャイルドシート (child seat). Homophone: シート (sheet; tarp; sheet of paper).

examples[].german: This clock has a mechanism where figures come out at noon.
The magician said, "There is no trick or gimmick."
en.notes: A device (からくり) or a trick: 仕掛け時計 (mechanical figure clock), 種も仕掛けもない (no trick at all). Verb: 仕掛ける.

en.meaning: to go damp; to go soft (snacks)
examples[].german: I left the bag open, and the potato chips went soft.
In the rainy season, matches get damp and are hard to light.
en.notes: Godan verb: salty snacks or matches absorb moisture and go soft: せんべいが湿気る.

en.meaning: ceremony hall; venue for a ceremony
examples[].german: We booked the hall a year before the wedding.
Please check in at the entrance of the hall.
en.notes: A venue for weddings or funerals: 結婚式場 (wedding hall), 葬儀式場 (funeral hall).

examples[].german: That athlete was disqualified for a false start.
If you can't keep your promises, you are unfit as a leader.
en.notes: In sports: to be disqualified (反則で失格になる). Also a verdict on someone: 親として失格だ (a failure as a parent).

examples[].german: She always wears chic clothes.
I decorated the room in black and white in a stylish way.
en.notes: な-adjective from French "chic": シックな服 (elegant clothes), often for subdued, stylish colors.

examples[].german: The minister fell from power in a corruption scandal.
Some people were aiming for their rival's downfall.
en.notes: The loss of a position of power, mostly in politics or business: スキャンダルで失脚する.

examples[].german: Health-oriented foods have been selling well lately.
She had long aspired to work overseas.
en.notes: Often as a suffix: 健康志向 (health consciousness), ブランド志向 (brand orientation). Similar sound: 思考 (thinking), 嗜好 (preference).

examples[].german: When I'm tired, my thinking stops.
This class fosters logical thinking.
en.notes: Thinking as a process: 思考力 (thinking ability), プラス思考 (positive thinking).

en.meaning: to botch; to blow it; to fail
examples[].german: I was nervous and blew the interview.
Even if you fail once, you should not give up and just try again.
en.notes: Colloquial godan verb: 試験をしくじる (to botch an exam). More neutral: 失敗する.

examples[].german: A doctor's mission is to save patients' lives.
He works with a strong sense of mission.
en.notes: An important task one must fulfill: 使命を果たす (to fulfill one's mission), 使命感 (sense of mission). Homophones: 氏名, 指名.

examples[].german: All his life he served the king as a faithful servant.
In the Bible, believers call themselves servants of God.
You must not become a slave to money.
en.notes: Literary word for "servant, menial", today almost always written in kana (しもべ); the spelling 僕 is rare and is usually read ぼく "I" (card 僕/ぼく). Typical in Bible translations (神のしもべ), fairy tales and fantasy, and figuratively as in 金のしもべ "slave to money". In modern usage, 召使い or 使用人 correspond to it.

examples[].german: She is gentle but has great inner strength.
Deep in his heart, he wished to continue that work.
en.notes: しん denotes a person's mental attitude or inner nature. The reading sounds more literary, or related to inner firmness, than the everyday こころ. In phrases like 心が強い, mental steadfastness is in the foreground. In the second example, 心から is also read specifically しんから, a literary-sounding phrase for "from the bottom of one's heart". In everyday speech, the reading こころから is common. The material core of an object is usually written 芯. That does not mean that 心 can be replaced by 芯 in every expression.

examples[].german: A new product will be released next month.
Let me introduce the team's new member.
en.notes: Prefix before Sino-Japanese words and loanwords: 新製品 (new product), 新学期 (new school year/semester), 新メンバー. As a free adjective one says 新しい.

examples[].german: The cucumber I forgot to put in the fridge has shriveled up.
Because I didn't water them, the flowers have withered.
en.notes: Ichidan verb, usually written in kana: vegetables or skin lose moisture and become wrinkled (野菜がしなびる).

examples[].german: The screenplay of this film was written by a famous author.
We need to consider the worst-case scenario as well.
en.notes: The script of a film or play, and figuratively a planned course of events: 最悪のシナリオ (worst-case scenario).

examples[].german: Bamboo is flexible and does not break even in strong wind.
I was captivated by the dancer's graceful movements.
en.notes: な-adjective: elastic and not brittle (しなやかな枝) or graceful in movement (しなやかな動き).

examples[].german: The remains of an ancient temple survive on the hill.
A statue of a god was enshrined at the back of the temple.
en.notes: A building in which a deity is worshipped, such as an ancient temple (パルテノン神殿) or a shrine building. Buddhist temples are called 寺.

en.meaning: progress; pace (of a curriculum or plan)
examples[].german: The lessons in this class move at a fast pace.
I adjusted the pace to the students' understanding.
en.notes: How far a planned course, especially a lesson plan, has progressed: 授業の進度, 進度が速い/遅れる (the pace is fast / falls behind). Not to be confused with 震度 (seismic intensity), which is read the same.

en.meaning: rear guard; last in a line; anchor (relay)
examples[].german: During the retreat, a young commander served as the rear guard.
On mountain paths, an experienced guide walks at the rear.
I was entrusted with the anchor leg of the relay and felt the pressure.
en.notes: Originally military: the "rear guard" that covers a retreat (殿を務める "to form the rear guard"). Figuratively it means "the last in a line", or in relays the anchor runner (≈ アンカー). Mostly written in kana, because 殿 would otherwise be read どの (card 〜殿, form of address in letters) or との "lord"; the opposite is 先頭 "the head, the front".

examples[].german: He is a devout Buddhist.
That idol's devoted fans defend her no matter what is said.
en.notes: A follower of a religion: キリスト教の信者. Colloquially also for unconditional fans of a person or brand.

examples[].german: This year's newcomers are all serious.
She won the newcomer award for her debut work.
en.notes: New to a company, team or industry: 新人社員 (new employee), 新人研修 (training for new employees), 新人賞 (newcomer award).

examples[].german: Thinking of the feelings of the victims' families, my heart aches.
Emotionally I want to side with him, but the rules must be followed.
en.notes: Formal: what someone feels inside. 心情を察する (to empathize with someone's feelings), 心情的には (emotionally speaking).

examples[].german: In the Edo period, many plays were written about the double suicide of lovers.
The incident is believed to be a family suicide.
en.notes: 〜する. A joint suicide of two lovers or of an entire family (一家心中). With the reading しんちゅう, however, 心中 means "in one's heart, inner feelings".

examples[].german: The two are still newlyweds, so they seem happy every day.
We went to Hawaii for our honeymoon.
en.notes: With だ/の or before nouns: 新婚夫婦 (newlywed couple), 新婚旅行 (honeymoon), 新婚生活 (newlywed life).

examples[].german: Emerging internet companies are growing rapidly.
Growth is expected to continue in the economies of emerging countries.
en.notes: Mostly before nouns: 新興国 (emerging country), 新興企業 (young company), 新興住宅地 (new housing development). Not to be confused with 振興 (promotion), which is read the same.

examples[].german: The town is putting effort into promoting tourism.
The prefecture announced a plan to promote local industry.
en.notes: 〜する: to publicly promote and revitalize a field: 産業振興, 地域振興, 観光振興. Not to be confused with 新興 (emerging), which is read the same.

en.meaning: confidence; trust (in someone's performance in office)
examples[].german: The president won the shareholders' confidence and it was decided he would stay on.
A cabinet that has lost the people's confidence will not last long.
en.notes: Formal, especially in politics and organizations: 信任を得る (to win confidence), 信任投票 (vote of confidence), 不信任案 (no-confidence motion).

examples[].german: In April the campus is full of new students.
The welcome party for new students was held in the gymnasium.
en.notes: A new student at a school or university (in Japan usually from April). New company employees are called 新入社員.

examples[].german: The typhoon changed its course to the north.
I talked with my teacher about my path after graduation.
en.notes: The direction in which something moves: 台風の進路. At school: 進路を決める (to decide on further study or a career), 進路相談 (academic and career counseling).

examples[].german: This hospital is open for consultations on Saturdays too.
Because of a shortage of doctors, treatment at night is no longer possible.
en.notes: 〜する. 診療時間 (consultation hours), 診療所 (clinic, small medical practice), 休診 (no consultation hours).

en.meaning: advance; expansion (into a market); advancing (to the next round)
examples[].german: The company plans to expand into the Asian market next year.
The Japanese national team advanced to the final.
en.notes: 〜する: to advance into a new area: 海外に進出する (to expand overseas), 政界に進出する (to enter politics); in sports: 決勝に進出する (to advance to the final).

examples[].german: The truth about the incident is still unknown.
The reporter tried to uncover the truth about the accident.
en.notes: What really lies behind an event: 事件の真相, 真相を明らかにする/究明する. More general: 真実 (truth).

examples[].german: The negotiations are progressing little by little.
There was major progress in the investigation.
en.notes: 〜する: a matter moves forward: 交渉が進展する, 捜査に進展がない (no progress in the investigation), 事態の進展 (development of the situation).

en.meaning: human waste, excrement, sewage (feces and urine)
examples[].german: This facility treats the human waste of the region.
In the past, human waste was spread on the fields as fertilizer.
In a disaster, the disposal of human waste at evacuation shelters becomes a serious problem.
en.notes: Technical word from administration and environmental engineering for human excretions, feces and urine together. Since 屎 is not a jōyō kanji, officially it is almost always written し尿, e.g. in し尿処理 "human waste disposal" or し尿処理場. In everyday speech the word is avoided; medically, 便 and 尿 are spoken of separately.

examples[].german: An exchange meeting was held to deepen friendship between the two countries.
A friendly soccer match between Japan and Brazil was played.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds: 国際親善 (international goodwill), 親善試合 (friendly match), 親善大使 (goodwill ambassador).

examples[].german: According to the police investigation, the cause of the fire was a cigarette.
In the quiet night, a beautiful piano melody came drifting in.
en.notes: Noun of 調べる: 警察の調べによると (according to the police investigation), 取り調べ (interrogation). In elevated usage also "melody, sound": ピアノの調べ.

examples[].german: An order to withdraw came from headquarters.
They are acting on instructions from above.
en.notes: Instruction from above (headquarters, authorities, command): 指令を出す/受ける. Not to be confused with 司令 (command, 司令官 = commander), which is read the same.

en.meaning: substitute; material; price, payment; (margin) area (e.g. glue margin)
examples[].german: The culprit demanded a ransom of one hundred million yen.
When cutting the paper, please leave a glue margin at the edge.
In spring, farmers raise rice seedlings in seedbeds.
en.notes: The reading しろ now occurs almost only in set compounds: 身代金 "ransom", 糊代 "glue margin", 苗代 "rice seedbed", 代物 "thing, goods" (often derogatory). On its own, 代 is mostly read だい: the card 〜代 "-cost, -fee" (電気代, 食事代) is a different word. 城 "castle" and 白 "white" sound the same but have nothing to do with it.

examples[].german: The body buried in a damp clay layer had turned into adipocere.
In forensic medicine class, we learned about the conditions under which adipocere forms.
en.notes: Technical term from forensic medicine and archaeology for the waxy substance that forms on corpses in a damp, oxygen-poor environment; also found in crime novels. Often used as 屍蝋化する "to turn into adipocere". The spelling 死蝋 is a rarer variant; the character 蝋 means "wax" as in 蝋燭.

en.meaning: to write down; to record; to describe
examples[].german: Please write your name and address on the form.
This book describes life during the war in detail.
en.notes: Transitive, literary for 書く: to note down or put something in writing. 名前を記す, 日記に記す.

examples[].german: The prime minister inspected the disaster area.
City officials went on an inspection trip to facilities overseas.
en.notes: An official visit to see conditions on the spot: 被災地を視察する. As a verb: 視察する.

examples[].german: I hear the president's son is getting married next month.
Is your son doing well?
en.notes: Formal, mostly as ご子息 about someone else's son. For one's own son one says 息子.

examples[].german: The once-popular boom has completely died down by now.
By night, the forest fire finally subsided.
en.notes: A fire that is weakening, and figuratively anything that is subsiding: ブームが下火になる (the boom fades).

examples[].german: When I bought a new car, I traded in my old one.
This store takes old smartphones as trade-ins.
en.notes: A dealer accepts the old item when you buy a new one and credits its value: 車を下取りに出す.

examples[].german: His kindness seems to have an ulterior motive.
I only helped, with no ulterior motive.
en.notes: Mostly negative: a hidden, self-serving intention, often romantic in nature. 下心がある (to have ulterior motives).

examples[].german: He has a background in Chinese, so he improves quickly.
Before painting, prepare the base of the wall.
en.notes: Preparatory foundation (下地がある = to have a grounding) and, in crafts, the base coat: 化粧の下地 (makeup base).

en.meaning: to become familiar with; to befriend; to enjoy regularly
examples[].german: I have been familiar with music since childhood.
On weekends I go to the mountains and enjoy nature.
en.notes: Godan verb, mostly with に: 自然に親しむ (to enjoy nature), 本に親しむ (to get into books). Common: 親しみやすい (approachable).

examples[].german: Before the trip, I looked into the area around the hotel in advance.
Let me prepare for tomorrow's class.
en.notes: To investigate or prepare something beforehand: 旅行の下調べ, 授業の下調べ. As a verb: 下調べする.

en.meaning: to write (a letter), to put down in writing, to draft (elevated)
examples[].german: My grandfather wrote a letter to his former teacher every year.
I wrote a few lines to express my gratitude.
He recorded his memories of the trip in his diary.
en.notes: したためる is an elevated, written-language verb for "to compose carefully (a letter, a document)": 手紙をしたためる, 一筆したためる "to write a few lines". It is mostly written in kana because the kanji writing 認める is normally read みとめる "to recognize, to admit" (own card). In everyday speech, one simply says 書く; したためる sounds solemn or old-fashioned. The meaning "to take (a meal)" is obsolete.

examples[].german: Due to ongoing stress, I am suffering from autonomic nervous system dysfunction.
An extreme diet leads to malnutrition.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds: 栄養失調 (malnutrition), 自律神経失調症 (autonomic dysfunction).

examples[].german: It is the parents' job to raise children properly.
This dog is well trained.
en.notes: Ichidan verb, mostly written in kana しつける: 子どもをしつける, 犬をしつける. Noun: 躾（しつけ）.

en.meaning: to be accustomed, to do habitually; to baste (sewing); to plant (rice)
examples[].german: Before the final sewing, you baste the sleeve with basting thread.
I'm completely exhausted from work I'm not used to.
In May, the village plants rice seedlings in the paddies.
en.notes: A separate word alongside 躾ける (card: "to train, to teach manners"), which today is mostly written in kana or as 躾ける. 仕付ける carries older meanings: "to be accustomed to something" (almost only negated: 仕付けない仕事 "unaccustomed work"), "to baste with large stitches" in sewing (cf. しつけ糸 "basting thread") and "to plant rice seedlings". The sewing term is the one that is still alive; the rest sounds archaic.

examples[].german: I'm sorry to say it's a personal matter, but I will be taking tomorrow off.
You must not use the company phone for private purposes.
en.notes: In a work context: 私用で休む (to take time off for personal reasons), 私用の電話 (a private call). Homophones: 使用, 仕様.

examples[].german: There were ten servants in that mansion.
He treated his servants as carefully as if they were family.
en.notes: A person employed by someone, especially as household staff. Sounds old-fashioned today; for company employees one says 社員 or 従業員.

examples[].german: Beyond this point is private land, so please do not enter.
Some countries do not recognize private ownership of land.
en.notes: Legal usage: 私有地 (private land), 私有財産 (private property). Opposites: 公有 (public ownership), 国有 (state ownership).

examples[].german: A raindrop fell from the tip of the leaf.
There are drops on the windowpane.
en.notes: A single drop, especially of water: 雨の滴. Also written 雫. The reading てき is used as a counter (一滴).

examples[].german: Those who break the rules will be punished.
Penalties for drunk driving have become stricter.
en.notes: 〜する/〜される: to punish officially. More general: 罰.

examples[].german: You must carry your passport when entering the country.
The man was arrested for carrying a bladed weapon.
en.notes: 〜する: to have something on one's person or to own it; typical of official and legal language. 所持品 (belongings carried), 所持金 (cash one has on hand).

examples[].german: I was greatly shocked by failing the exam.
I hurt my knee from the impact of landing.
en.notes: Emotionally: ショックを受ける (to be shocked), ショックだ (that is a shock). Physically/technically: impact, jolt.

examples[].german: He fulfilled his duties to the end.
Drinking alcohol on duty is prohibited.
en.notes: Formal: the tasks that belong to a post. 職務を果たす (to carry out one's duties), 職務質問 (police questioning on the street).

examples[].german: I saw a dolphin show at the aquarium.
A motor show will be held in Tokyo next month.
en.notes: A performance or trade show: ファッションショー (fashion show), モーターショー (motor show), イルカのショー (dolphin show).

en.meaning: here and there, in various places (elevated)
examples[].german: In the old streetscape, buildings from the Edo period remain here and there.
Errors can be seen here and there in the report.
Snow still remained in places on the mountainside.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese, written-language reading of 所々; in normal usage 所々 is almost always read ところどころ (card 所々/ところどころ). In the reading しょしょ the word is usually written 諸所 or 諸処 and sounds formal or old-fashioned, e.g. in reports and older literature. Usage as with ところどころ: adverbially or with に (所々に).

en.meaning: constantly; all the time; very often
examples[].german: My little brother is constantly losing his keys.
I talk with her on the phone all the time.
en.notes: Colloquial: again and again, incessantly. More formal: 頻繁に or 常に.

examples[].german: The mountains showed a majestic aspect in the light of the setting sun.
This painting conveys the look of the stormy sea well.
en.notes: An elevated or literary noun for the visible appearance, form or state of a thing. Here 象 is read specifically しょう; the everyday reading ぞう means "elephant". For a concrete phenomenon, one now usually says 現象（げんしょう）. The examples use the older independent sense "appearance", for example in a landscape description or when viewing a painting.

en.meaning: to carry on one's back, to take upon oneself (colloquial); しょってる: to be conceited
examples[].german: The children go to school with their school backpacks on their backs.
I climbed the mountain carrying a heavy load on my back.
Calling yourself a genius - you're pretty full of yourself.
en.notes: しょう is a colloquial reading of 背負う (own card 背負う/せおう) and likewise means "to carry on the back" and figuratively "to take something upon oneself". You hear it mainly in the て-form: リュックをしょって. しょってる (from しょっている) also means "to be conceited, to be very sure of oneself"; this meaning exists only with しょう, not with せおう. Since 背負う is normally read せおう, しょう is mostly written in kana.

en.meaning: consumption, exhaustion, wear (original, rare reading of 消耗/しょうもう)
examples[].german: Because of the protracted war, the attrition of troop strength was severe.
Working in the intense heat, I used up a great deal of my stamina.
Machine parts wear out little by little as they are used.
en.notes: The original reading of 消耗, since 耗 actually has the on reading こう; today the customary reading しょうもう (card 消耗/しょうもう) is the generally used one, in news, in everyday speech and in words such as 消耗品. しょうこう appears only in older texts or with deliberately traditional pronunciation. Meaning and usage are identical, as a noun and as a suru verb (体力を消耗する).

examples[].german: I deleted all the old data.
When I don't know, I choose the answer by process of elimination.
en.notes: To delete data or entries: データを消去する; also 消去法 (process of elimination).

examples[].german: The company encourages its employees to commute by bicycle.
The government is providing subsidies to promote energy saving.
en.notes: 〜する: to (officially) promote something and urge people to do it, especially authorities, companies, schools. 奨励金 = incentive payment, grant.

examples[].german: He went off on a mountain climb and has not been heard from since.
I have heard nothing at all about Tanaka since graduation.
en.notes: Literary: news about how someone is and where they are. 消息を絶つ (to cut off all contact, to go missing), 消息不明 (whereabouts unknown), 消息筋 (well-informed sources).

en.meaning: to call; to name; to claim to be
examples[].german: I got a call from a man claiming to be a police officer.
In this region, this festival is called the "Fire Festival".
en.notes: Literary: 〜と称する (to call oneself ..., to claim to be ...): 警察官と称する男 (a man claiming to be a police officer).

en.meaning: true form; true colors; true identity
examples[].german: The culprit finally revealed his true colors.
The source of the sound heard in the middle of the night turned out to be the neighbors' cat.
en.notes: What lies behind a mask or appearance: 正体を現す (to show one's true colors), 正体不明 (of unknown identity/origin). Not to be confused with 招待 (invitation), which is read the same.

examples[].german: He owns land in Tokyo.
Many people in Tokyo do not own a car.
en.notes: 〜する: to own, especially in the legal sense. 所有者 (owner), 所有権 (right of ownership).

examples[].german: This sect spread during the Kamakura period.
This cemetery can be used regardless of sect.
en.notes: 宗 means a religious school or the community of its followers, especially in connection with Buddhist schools. この宗は refers to a school already mentioned. 宗を問わず means regardless of religious affiliation. The word is rather technical or written; 宗派（しゅうは）is a clearer general term. The translation "sect" need not carry a derogatory tone here.

en.meaning: lord, master; head (of a household); the Lord (God); main thing (e.g. 主として)
examples[].german: This insurance is aimed mainly at elderly people.
At the Sunday service, everyone recites the Lord's Prayer together.
Our company's main business is food import.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 主; as a free word it is rare and elevated: in Christianity "the Lord" (主イエス, 主の祈り "the Lord's Prayer"), as well as in 主として "mainly", 主たる "main, principal" and 主と従 "principal and subordinate". In everyday speech 主に (おもに, separate card) is said. しゅ is very common in compounds such as 主人, 主婦, 主要; do not confuse it with the homophone 種/しゅ "species".

examples[].german: This team has strong defense.
He is poor at batting but good in the field.
en.notes: Defense in sports or the military: 守備を固める (to strengthen the defense); in baseball, fielding (守備位置 = fielding position).

examples[].german: This plan is being carried out under the government's leadership.
It was the opposing team that took the initiative in the match.
en.notes: The leading role in an undertaking: 主導権を握る (to seize the initiative), 政府主導の計画 (a government-led plan).

examples[].german: At night a guard patrols the building.
When entering the building, please tell the guard your name.
en.notes: Security staff at the entrance of companies, schools or government offices: 守衛室 (guard room).

examples[].german: She played the lead in a film for the first time.
The lead role in this work was played by a newcomer actor.
en.notes: To play the lead in a film or play: 主演する, 主演女優 (leading actress).

examples[].german: My mother's hobby is handicrafts, and she often makes bags.
I bought yarn and needles at the craft shop.
en.notes: Handicrafts such as knitting, sewing or embroidery: 手芸店 (craft shop).

examples[].german: The protagonist of this novel is a sixteen-year-old girl.
Let's try reading while putting ourselves in the protagonist's shoes.
en.notes: The main person of a story; figuratively: 自分の人生の主人公 (the master of one's own life).

examples[].german: Various problems were discussed at the meeting.
This shop handles all kinds of stationery.
en.notes: Literary for いろいろ: 種々の問題 (various problems), 種々雑多 (all sorts of).

examples[].german: A celebration was held in honor of the victory.
A commemorative ceremony was held to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the founding.
en.notes: Formal: 祝賀会 (celebration party), 祝賀パレード (victory parade).

examples[].german: The two are called fated rivals.
That was the destiny given to him.
en.notes: An unchangeable, predetermined fate; stronger than 運命: 宿命のライバル (arch-rival).

en.meaning: person in charge; chief; supervisor (lowest management level)
examples[].german: If you have any problems, please consult the supervisor.
She has been the grade-level head since this year.
en.notes: The person responsible for an area: 学年主任 (grade-level head), 現場主任 (site supervisor). In companies often one rank below 係長.

en.meaning: exhibiting; entering (a work); putting up for sale
examples[].german: His painting was entered in the exhibition.
I listed clothes I no longer wear on a flea market app.
en.notes: To submit a work to an exhibition or to offer goods for sale, e.g. on an auction site.

examples[].german: The staple food of the Japanese is rice.
In the morning I have bread as my staple.
en.notes: The main food of a meal or culture, traditionally rice in Japan; side dishes are called おかず.

examples[].german: My older sister gave birth to a girl last month.
The due date is in March next year.
en.notes: To give birth to a child: 出産する, 出産予定日 (due date). Congratulations: ご出産おめでとうございます.

en.meaning: success in life; getting ahead; promotion
examples[].german: He was promoted the fastest among his peers.
I value time with my family more than career advancement.
en.notes: To rise in society or in a company: 出世する, 出世が早い (to rise quickly). 出世払い = to pay back once one has made it.

examples[].german: Japan's birth rate is falling year by year.
Little is known about his origins.
en.notes: Official, factual: 出生率 (birth rate), 出生届 (birth registration). Also read しゅっせい.

examples[].german: This question was also on last year's exam.
I checked with the teacher what the exam covers.
en.notes: To set exam questions: 試験に出題される (to appear on the exam), 出題範囲 (exam coverage).

examples[].german: Following the fire report, the fire engine was dispatched.
Rescue teams have been dispatched to the disaster site.
en.notes: Fire fighters, police or the military go out on a mission: 消防車が出動する (the fire engine turns out).

en.meaning: appearance (in a film, on TV); performance
examples[].german: He appeared on yesterday's TV program.
All the performers in the production greeted the audience.
en.notes: To appear in film, television or on stage: テレビに出演する (to appear on TV), 出演者 (performers).

examples[].german: The advent of the internet greatly changed life.
A bear has appeared on the mountain trail, so please be careful.
en.notes: The (sudden) appearance of something new: スマホの出現で生活が変わった (life changed with the emergence of smartphones).

en.meaning: many people, the crowd; numerical superiority
examples[].german: She proposed a new method ahead of everyone else.
It is cowardly to rely on one's superior numbers to intimidate the other side.
en.notes: 衆（しゅう）here is an independent noun for a large number of people or the numerical superiority of a group. It sounds elevated and appears in phrases such as 衆に先んじる "to be ahead of others" or 衆を頼む "to rely on superior numbers". The attached ～衆 in 旦那衆 or 若い衆 has a different grammatical function. The reading しゅ and historical court offices are not practiced on this card. 週 "week" is a different word.

en.meaning: circumference of a figure; counter for laps
examples[].german: The perimeter of this triangle is twelve centimeters.
The athletes ran three laps around the stadium track.
The spacecraft orbited the Earth twice.
en.notes: As a mathematical noun, 周（しゅう）denotes the boundary or perimeter of a closed figure. As a counter, it counts complete laps or revolutions: 一周（いっしゅう）is one lap, 三周（さんしゅう）is three laps. When counting, the number comes directly before. The accent information applies to the single word stem; number and counter together form their own word whose accent can differ. The Zhou dynasty 周 and the rare noun for surroundings have their own cards; 週 means "week".

examples[].german: The soldiers made camp in the area around the castle.
A dense forest spread around the temple.
en.notes: An elevated or older independent noun for the area around a place. Here 周 is read しゅう; the everyday words for "surroundings" are 周囲（しゅうい）or まわり. In a deliberately elevated description, 城の周 can, for example, denote the surroundings of a castle. This spatial sense means neither the mathematically measured perimeter nor a counted lap, nor the Zhou dynasty. The examples reproduce the older nominal usage in a historical narrative and a landscape description.

examples[].german: The course length at this school is two years.
Certificates were given to the students who had completed their course.
en.notes: Learning knowledge or skills, formal: 修業年限 (course length), 修業証書 (completion certificate). In the sense of a craft apprenticeship it is usually read しゅぎょう (料理の修業). Not to be confused with 修行（しゅぎょう）: religious austerities or martial arts training.

examples[].german: Smoking is prohibited all day at this station.
Because of heavy snow, trains were suspended all day.
en.notes: Formal for 一日中, typical on signs: 終日禁煙 (no smoking all day), 終日運休 (service suspended all day).

examples[].german: In this sentence, the adjective modifies the noun.
Let's avoid excessive embellishment and write concisely.
en.notes: Grammatically, one word qualifies another (形容詞が名詞を修飾する); 修飾語 = modifier. Homophone: 就職.

examples[].german: This hall can hold a thousand people.
The injured were taken to a nearby hospital.
en.notes: To take in people or things: 五万人収容のスタジアム (a stadium holding 50,000 people); also placement in camps or hospitals.

examples[].german: Her speech is polite, and you can sense her good upbringing.
It has rained little this year, so the vegetables are growing poorly.
en.notes: Noun of 育つ. 育ちがいい (of good upbringing); after place names "raised in": 東京育ち.

examples[].german: After the war, my grandfather endured a life of plain clothes and meager food to support his family.
Dressed in plain clothing, he continued his ascetic training at a mountain temple.
en.notes: 粗衣 (そい) is a written-language word for "plain, simple clothing" and appears almost only in the four-character phrase 粗衣粗食 "plain clothes and meager food", which describes a modest, frugal life. In everyday speech, 質素な服 or 粗末な服 is said instead.

examples[].german: His replies are always curt.
I regret having been so cold.
en.notes: Without friendliness or warmth (reply, attitude); also unadorned (素っ気ない部屋). Often in kana: そっけない.

examples[].german: I bought three pairs of white socks.
The rule is to wear navy blue socks with the school uniform.
en.notes: Mostly short socks; 靴下 is more common in general. Knee-high socks are called ハイソックス.

en.meaning: around there, somewhere thereabouts; about that much
examples[].german: The key should be somewhere around there.
The repair will be done in an hour or so.
en.notes: Colloquial: そこら(へん) "somewhere around there"; after quantities "or so": 千円かそこら. Similar: そこいら.

en.meaning: to conform to, to be based on, to be adapted to (〜に即して)
examples[].german: We should make a plan that is grounded in reality.
We will handle this matter appropriately in accordance with the law.
Many voices say that school rules that no longer suit the times should be reviewed.
en.notes: Formal, written-language verb, used almost only as 〜に即して "in accordance with, in line with" or 〜に即した + noun: 現実に即した計画 "a plan grounded in reality", 実情に即して. Close in meaning are 〜に沿って and 〜に基づいて; 則する is preferred when it is about rules and laws. Do not confuse it with 即/そく "immediately" (vocab-n2:1848).

examples[].german: A fire extinguisher is installed in each room.
The hotel rooms are equipped with a refrigerator.
en.notes: To provide devices or furniture fixed in a place; often resultative: 備え付けてある. Noun: 備え付け (備え付けの家具 built-in furniture).

en.meaning: to be provided, to be equipped; (quality) to possess
examples[].german: This room is equipped with an air conditioner.
He has the makings of a leader by nature.
en.notes: Intransitive counterpart of 備える: equipment is present, or someone possesses a quality or talent (才能が備わる).

en.meaning: the other way (そっぽを向く: to look away)
examples[].german: I spoke to my little brother, but he just looked away.
Because of the price increase, customers have turned their backs on us.
en.notes: Almost only in そっぽを向く: to turn away; figuratively "to give the cold shoulder, to want nothing to do with" (客にそっぽを向かれる).

examples[].german: He is a sincere person. For that reason, he is trusted by many people.
Resources are limited. Therefore, we must use them carefully.
en.notes: Written-language conjunction; in conversation, だから or そのため are more usual. Cf. 故に.

examples[].german: The children slid down the snowy slope on a sled.
Santa Claus comes riding in a reindeer sleigh.
en.notes: Usually written in kana; kanji 橇. Dog sled: 犬ぞり (with rendaku).

en.meaning: warp, curvature; curve (of a sword blade)
examples[].german: The board warped from the humidity.
Japanese swords have a beautifully curved blade.
en.notes: Noun of 反る. Idiom: 反りが合わない (not to get along with each other; literally, the blade does not fit the scabbard).

examples[].german: She left the band and is now active as a solo artist.
At the concert, the guitar solo got the crowd most excited.
en.notes: A musical solo or a performance as a solo artist: ソロで活動する. Also generally "alone": ソロキャンプ (solo camping).

examples[].german: The cheering squad wore matching uniforms.
I bought a sweater that matches my older sister's.
en.notes: 揃いの〜: matching, uniform; usually with お: お揃い (the same items, matching outfits). After nouns with rendaku, 〜揃い (ぞろい) "all ...": 傑作揃い (けっさくぞろい, nothing but masterpieces).

en.meaning: to warp, to curve; to bend backward
examples[].german: Exposed to the sun, the book cover has warped.
Startled, my body arched backward involuntarily.
en.notes: Intransitive: wood or paper warps, the body bends backward. Transitive: 反らす. Homophone: 剃る (to shave).

en.meaning: appearance, look; physiognomy (fortune-telling, cf. 人相, 手相); phase (physics)
examples[].german: The fortune-teller looked at my face and said, "You have unusual features."
Water changes into three phases, solid, liquid and gas, depending on temperature.
When I had my palm read at the festival, I was told that I had the signs of a long life.
en.notes: As an independent noun it is rare: in fortune-telling "signs in the face or hand" (良い相をしている, 死相), in physics "phase" (固相, 液相). It is more familiar in compounds such as 人相, 手相, 様相. The card 相〜/あい is the prefix in 相手, 相変わらず; in 首相 it is read しょう.

examples[].german: Three small fishing boats were moored in the harbor.
A boat is floating in the middle of the lake.
Several rubber boats were launched for the rescue.
en.notes: Counter for small boats such as rowboats, fishing boats or rubber boats: 一艘 (いっそう), 二艘, 三艘, 数艘. For large ships 隻/せき is preferred (タンカー三隻), and in casual speech simply 〜つ or 台 is also used. The kanji is rare; the expression appears mainly in narratives, news and phrases such as 二艘の舟に乗る.

en.meaning: to meet (wishes, expectations); to accompany; to stay by (someone)
examples[].german: We will do our utmost to meet your expectations.
Unfortunately, we cannot comply with your request.
en.notes: Intransitive, formal; mainly 期待に添う (to meet expectations), 希望に添う (to comply with a wish); 沿う is also written for this. "To accompany" appears in 付き添う and 寄り添う. Do not confuse the potential 添える (to be able to meet) with the verb 添える (to attach).

examples[].german: The monks at the temple have been chanting sutras since early morning.
He renounced the world in his youth and became a monk.
en.notes: Formal; in everyday speech お坊さん. 僧侶 (monk, priest), 高僧 (high-ranking monk).

examples[].german: To climb a mountain in winter, you need solid equipment.
This car is equipped with the latest safety systems.
en.notes: Equipment for mountaineering, the military or vehicles; as a verb 装備する (to equip, to be equipped with).

examples[].german: Due to the rise in rice prices, riots broke out in various places.
That remark caused a huge uproar.
en.notes: Ranging from riots and uprisings to a media frenzy or a quarrel (お家騒動 a family feud). Cf. 騒ぎ (noise, commotion, more general).

en.meaning: launch of a publication; first issue
examples[].german: This magazine was launched fifty years ago.
The first issue contains a novel by a famous writer.
en.notes: 〜する: to publish a newspaper or magazine for the first time. 創刊号 (first issue); opposite: 廃刊 (discontinuation).

examples[].german: If you make an effort, you should get results to match.
He has a composure appropriate to his age.
en.notes: Mostly after nouns or with の: 年齢相応 (appropriate to one's age), 身分相応 (suited to one's station), それ相応の (corresponding, due). Opposite: 不相応. Same kanji, different reading: 相応しい (ふさわしい).

en.meaning: utterly, completely (intensifying prefix, e.g. 素っ裸, 素っ頓狂)
examples[].german: The children were playing in the river stark naked.
When my name was suddenly called, I let out an utterly shrill voice.
When my mother heard the news, she dashed off to the hospital.
en.notes: A colloquial intensifying prefix that doubles the following consonant; only in a few set words such as 素っ裸 "stark naked", 素っ頓狂 "shrill, utterly crazy" and 素っ飛ぶ "to fly off, to dash off". Not productive. 素っ気ない, by contrast, is read そっけない, and 素 (す) in 素足 or 素顔 means "bare, uncovered".

examples[].german: Mice are nimble and hard to catch.
That player is small but very agile.
en.notes: い-adjective for quick, skillful movements (animals, children, athletes). Colloquially also すばしっこい.

examples[].german: I smoothed the wrinkles out of the shirt with steam.
This machine cleans floors with high-temperature steam.
en.notes: Water vapor, especially in technical and household terms: スチームアイロン (steam iron), スチームオーブン (steam oven). In general: 蒸気, 湯気.

examples[].german: From the train window I could see paddy fields stretching endlessly.
In this region, the area of rice paddies is shrinking year by year.
en.notes: Formal and technical word for 田んぼ.

examples[].german: White vapor was rising from the lake surface in the early morning.
In Kampo medicine, swelling of the body is called "suiki" (edema).
en.notes: Elevated or technical reading of 水気; in everyday speech (vegetables, laundry, cooking), みずけ (separate card) is said, e.g. 水気を切る "to drain". すいき is used rather in written language for "water vapor, mist" and in traditional (Kampo) medicine for "edema, dropsy". When in doubt, みずけ is the usual reading.

examples[].german: Dirty parts are rinsed with water and then dried.
This village has finally gotten flush toilets too.
en.notes: 〜する: to rinse with water. Mostly in 水洗トイレ (flush toilet). Read the same as 推薦 (recommendation) and 水仙 (narcissus).

examples[].german: The national anthem was played by wind instruments at the start of the ceremony.
In high school I played trumpet in the wind band.
en.notes: 〜する: to play a wind instrument, formal. Common in 吹奏楽 (wind music) and 吹奏楽部 (school wind band club).

examples[].german: The people in distress in the mountains cried out for help.
The fact that nobody was hurt is at least a saving grace.
en.notes: Noun form of 救う: 救いを求める (to ask for help). Often: 〜のが（せめてもの）救いだ (... is at least a consolation).

examples[].german: I was worried, but the proposal passed smoothly.
She has slender long legs.
en.notes: Mostly "without difficulty": すんなり決まる, すんなり受け入れる. Of body shapes: slender, supple (すんなりした脚).

examples[].german: The room is small and there is no space to put a desk.
Please put a space between words.
en.notes: Free room: 駐車スペース (parking space), スペースを空ける (to leave space). In writing and typing: a blank, spacing. For outer space one usually says 宇宙.

examples[].german: Please slow down before the curve.
He works at a fast pace.
en.notes: スピードを出す (to drive fast), スピードを落とす (to slow down), スピード違反 (speeding violation). Also figurative: 仕事のスピード.

examples[].german: My older brother drives a red sports car.
Someday I want to drive along a coastal road in a sports car.
en.notes: A fast, sporty car; from English "sports car".

examples[].german: The springs of the old sofa have broken.
The mattress springs have weakened and my lower back hurts.
en.notes: A metal spring in mattresses, sofas, machines; synonymous with ばね.

examples[].german: I wore navy slacks to the interview.
These slacks can be washed at home.
en.notes: Long dress trousers for office or suits, for men and women. In general: ズボン, パンツ.

en.meaning: passing each other; missing each other; growing apart
examples[].german: The road is narrow, so it is hard for cars to pass each other.
The husband and wife keep missing each other because work is busy.
en.notes: Noun form of すれ違う. Literally: passing one another (cars, pedestrians). Figuratively: constantly missing each other or drifting apart emotionally: 気持ちのすれ違い. Also written 擦れ違い.

examples[].german: The printing of this book is beautiful, and the photos are vivid too.
With old woodblock prints, the way the colors come out differs from impression to impression.
en.notes: Noun form of 刷る: 刷りがきれい/悪い (cleanly/poorly printed). In compounds read ずり: 色刷り (color printing), 試し刷り (proof print). Not to be confused with すり (pickpocket).

examples[].german: In the old novel, there is a scene in which a man shaves his beard every morning.
After shaving his head, he checked the back in the mirror too.
en.notes: する is an attested variant of 剃る／そる that also occurs in literary texts. It means cutting off hair with a blade, for example 髭をする "to shave the beard". The hair removed takes を. It is a Godan verb in る: すります, すらない, すって, すった. The identically sounding irregular する "to do", by contrast, has the forms します and した.

en.meaning: hem (of clothing); cuff; foot (of a mountain)
examples[].german: The trouser hems were too long, so I had them shortened a little.
I walked in the rain, so the hem of my skirt got wet.
en.notes: The lower edge of clothing: ズボンの裾 (trouser leg end), 裾上げ (hemming trousers). Figuratively: 山の裾 (foot of a mountain).

examples[].german: Please rinse well so that no detergent remains.
I rinsed the washed shirt in water and then hung it up to dry.
en.notes: Transitive: to rinse with clean water (laundry, dishes). The kanji 濯ぐ is rare; ゆすぐ means the same.

examples[].german: The construction is progressing more slowly than I expected.
How is the work coming along?
en.notes: Noun form of 進む: 進みが早い/遅い (progresses quickly/slowly).

examples[].german: The singer is recording a new song in the studio.
The program is being broadcast live from the studio.
en.notes: A recording, TV or photo studio; also a dance or yoga studio. 録音スタジオ, 写真スタジオ.

examples[].german: The railway company's labor union goes on strike from tomorrow.
Because of the strike, almost no trains ran in the morning.
Demanding a wage increase, the employees carried out a 24-hour strike.
en.notes: スト is the common short form of ストライキ ("strike", separate card) and appears mainly in news and headlines. Typical combinations are ストに入る ("to go on strike"), ストを行う, ストを打つ and スト決行; in compounds such as 時限スト ("time-limited strike") or ゼネスト ("general strike") the short form is almost always used. The full ストライキ sounds more explanatory, スト terser and more journalistic.

examples[].german: The drivers went on strike demanding a pay raise.
Because of the strike, trains are stopped on all lines.
en.notes: A work stoppage; often shortened to スト. ストライキを行う, ストライキに入る (to go on strike).

examples[].german: The use of flash is prohibited inside the building.
It was a dark room, so I used the flash to take the photo.
en.notes: In everyday use mainly the camera flash (also フラッシュ): ストロボをたく (to fire the flash). Technically also a stroboscope lamp.

examples[].german: The child drank juice through a straw.
Recently, more shops have been using paper straws.
en.notes: A tube for drinking. Straw as a material is called 麦わら.

en.meaning: dancer (in Japanese dance, Noh, Kabuki; as opposed to the musicians 地方); way of standing
examples[].german: At the banquet, the dancer danced gracefully while the musician played the shamisen.
She stood on stage as a dancer for the first time at the age of fifteen.
If you acquire the correct way of standing, the strain on your lower back is reduced.
en.notes: Technical word of the traditional stage arts: in geisha and Kabuki dance, the 立方 dance while the 地方 (じかた) sing and play the shamisen. In the meaning "way of standing, posture" 立ち方 is usually written. Do not confuse it with 立方 (りっぽう) "cube, third power" (separate card), which appears in mathematics and in units such as 立方メートル.

en.meaning: to stop by, to drop in on the way
examples[].german: On the way home, I stopped by the bookstore.
When you are in the neighborhood, please do stop by.
en.notes: To make a short stop somewhere along the way; politely お立ち寄りください (please stop by). Colloquial: 寄る.

examples[].german: I lost my way, but finally reached the inn late at night.
After a long discussion, we finally reached a conclusion.
en.notes: To arrive finally after effort or a long journey, also figuratively (結論にたどり着く). Cf. たどる (to follow a path).

examples[].german: The child wrote me a letter in clumsy handwriting.
He explained it with great effort in halting Japanese.
en.notes: い-adjective for halting speech, reading or writing and unsteady steps, for example of children or learners: たどたどしい日本語.

examples[].german: I don't believe in ghosts and the like.
She is the possessor of a rare talent.
en.notes: Literary: 〜の類い "... and the like"; 類いまれな "unparalleled, extraordinary". The spelling 類 is usually read るい.

examples[].german: The trains are crowded at this time of day, so I leave a little earlier.
Even within the temperate zone, the amount of rain differs greatly by region.
en.notes: 帯／たい is a word component here, placed after a noun. It denotes a delimited area, often band-shaped in extent: 時間帯 "time slot, time window", 温帯 "temperate climate zone". The meaning is clear from the whole word; in this use たい does not stand alone as a sentence predicate. The belt of a kimono is called 帯／おび. For compound words, you must also learn the pronunciation of the whole word.

examples[].german: I have no ulterior motive. I just stated the facts.
I know there is no hidden meaning in his words.
en.notes: Almost only in the negative: 他意はない (no ulterior motive, no ill intent).

examples[].german: One of the squad members left the squad and went missing.
The party advanced along the mountain path in formation.
en.notes: An organized group or military unit; usually as a suffix: 救助隊 (rescue team), 探検隊 (expedition), 自衛隊 (Self-Defense Forces).

examples[].german: The long-awaited new work has finally been released.
The people are longing for the arrival of peace.
en.notes: Mostly attributive 待望の〜 (long-awaited): 待望の新作, 待望の初優勝. As a verb 待望する (to long for).

en.meaning: voluminous, bulky (book); the greater part, the bulk
examples[].german: I read through the voluminous dictionary over three years.
A thick report was distributed before the meeting.
The bulk of the damage was concentrated in the coastal areas.
en.notes: Mainly with の before nouns: 大部の書物 "a voluminous work", 大部の報告書 "a thick report". In the sense of "the greater part" it is written-language; in everyday speech 大部分 "most part" (separate card) is said. Do not confuse it with 大分 (だいぶ) "considerably, quite a lot", which is a different word.

examples[].german: In this triangle, please point to the side opposite the red angle.
The opposite sides of a rectangle are equal in length.
en.notes: 対辺 is a geometric technical term. In a triangle, the 対辺 lies opposite a particular interior angle; in a quadrilateral, two sides facing each other can be called that. The reference point must be clear from the problem or the drawing. The identically read 大変 means, among other things, "difficult" and does not belong to this card.

examples[].german: Momotarou headed to Demon Island to defeat the oni.
I exterminated the cockroach in the kitchen.
en.notes: Getting rid of something harmful: pests, or monsters in fairy tales (鬼退治). As a verb 退治する.

examples[].german: Fish living in caves have degenerated eyes.
If you rely too much on convenient tools, your ability to think deteriorates.
en.notes: Biologically, the regression of organs; figuratively, the atrophy of abilities. Opposite: 進化 (evolution).

examples[].german: That teacher is known as a great authority on Japanese painting.
In his youth, he became an apprentice to a great master chef.
en.notes: The same writing as 大家 (おおや) "landlord", which is far more common in everyday life; たいか denotes a recognized master of his field, mostly in the pattern X の大家 (書道の大家, 経済学の大家). Which reading is meant becomes clear from the context: apartment and rent → おおや, art and science → たいか. The homophones 耐火 "fireproof" and 退化 "degeneration" are different words.

examples[].german: My older brother has a good build and is suited to rugby.
Children's physiques have become larger compared with the past.
en.notes: Overall build (height, weight, strength): 体格がいい (well built). Cf. 体型 (figure).

en.meaning: large sum of money, a lot of money
examples[].german: He won the lottery and came into a large sum of money.
It is dangerous to carry around so much money.
en.notes: A large sum of money: 大金を払う, 大金をつぎ込む. Not to be confused with 代金 (だいきん, price paid).

examples[].german: I set the timer on the rice cooker so the rice would be ready in time for breakfast.
We took a group photo using the camera's timer.
en.notes: A timer on appliances (タイマーをセットする) or the camera's self-timer (セルフタイマー).

examples[].german: I met my brother, from whom I had been separated, for the first time in twenty years.
I would like to take classes in person rather than online.
en.notes: A personal encounter; today often as the opposite of online: 対面授業 (in-person class). As a verb 対面する.

examples[].german: He ran his personal best time in the 100 meters.
The coach called a time-out and gave the players instructions.
en.notes: In sports, the measured time (タイムを計る) or a time-out (タイムを取る). Homophone: タイム (thyme).

examples[].german: Programs that take up topical issues are popular.
His advice was truly timely.
en.notes: At the right time, topical: タイムリーな話題. In baseball also タイムリーヒット (a hit that drives in a run).

examples[].german: One tile in the bathroom is cracked.
I put white tiles on the kitchen wall.
en.notes: Tile; タイル張り (tiled).

examples[].german: Preparations for rescue operations are being made in case of an earthquake.
As soon as everything is ready for admission, we will move the patient.
en.notes: Organized readiness for a task: 態勢を整える, 受け入れ態勢. Homophones: 体制 (system), 大勢 (general situation), 体勢 (body posture).

en.meaning: toward; regarding; per (e.g. 一人に対して); in contrast (それに対して)
examples[].german: You must not say rude things to customers.
In this class, there is one teacher for every three students.
The older brother is tall. The younger one, by contrast, is small.
en.notes: The te-form of 対する as a fixed phrase, almost always after に: 先生に対して "toward the teacher", 学生三人に対して "per three students", それに対して "in contrast to that". Before nouns, に対する or に対しての is used instead (客に対する態度). Not to be confused with the identically read adverb 大して "not particularly", which is used with negation.

examples[].german: I don't remember this book's title.
He won the world title in boxing.
en.notes: Title of a work (book, film, song) or a championship title in sports: タイトルを防衛する (to defend the title).

en.meaning: to rise, to increase, to grow stronger
examples[].german: As the match drew closer, the tension rose.
Interest in environmental issues is growing.
en.notes: Intransitive: feelings, interest, tension or reputation increase. Transitive: 高める.

en.meaning: height, stature; length (of clothing); the whole (of what one has)
examples[].german: This skirt is a little short in length.
I wrote all my feelings in a letter.
en.notes: Today mainly the length of clothing (スカート丈, 着丈) and in 思いの丈 (all one's feelings). Not to be confused with だけ (only).

examples[].german: On the camping night, we all sat around the bonfire.
We gathered fallen leaves and made a bonfire.
en.notes: A fire of wood or leaves outdoors; 焚き火をする (to make a bonfire). From the verb 焚く (to burn, to light a fire).

en.meaning: callus, corn (ペンだこ; 耳にたこができる: to have heard something too often)
examples[].german: Because I played guitar every day, I got calluses on my fingertips.
I've heard that story so many times that I'm sick of it.
My shoes didn't fit, and I got a callus on the sole of my foot.
en.notes: A hardened patch of skin caused by constant friction, almost always written in kana (たこ or タコ); the kanji 胼胝 are very rare. Typical: 指にたこができる, ペンだこ "writing callus". The idiom 耳にたこができる means "to have heard something to the point of boredom". Same sound, but different words: 蛸/たこ "octopus" and 凧/たこ "kite".

en.meaning: accumulation, heap, puddle; gathering place, hangout; tamari (thick soy sauce)
examples[].german: After the heavy rain, a pool of rainwater formed in a dip in the road.
This park has become a hangout for the young people of the neighborhood.
You eat sashimi with tamari soy sauce.
en.notes: Noun of the verb 溜まる (たまる, "to accumulate"): it refers to what has accumulated, or the place where something or someone gathers. On its own it is rather rare; mostly it is in compounds such as 水溜まり "puddle" or 溜まり場 "gathering place, regular haunt". As soy sauce it is almost always written in kana: たまり醤油. The spelling 溜り without the まり okurigana is obsolete.

en.meaning: to give, to grant, to bestow (honorific, literary); as an auxiliary after a verb stem: to deign to ...
examples[].german: God gives us our daily bread.
Lord, protect us.
Cherish the life that God has given you.
en.notes: Archaizing honorific verb, today almost only in prayers, Bible and song lyrics, or deliberately old-fashioned style. More common as an auxiliary after the verb stem: 守り給え "protect (us)", 与え給うた "graciously gave", where 給うた is pronounced たもうた. The more modern verb, still in use, is 賜る (たまわる, separate card) "to receive; to be granted".

examples[].german: Thank you for giving us your valuable opinions today.
We ask that you continue to favor us with your guidance in the future.
en.notes: Humble word for もらう, typical in speeches and business letters: ご指導を賜る. Less often also "to bestow" (by a superior).

en.meaning: precedent; example (〜したためしがない: it has never happened that ...)
examples[].german: He has never once come at the appointed time.
I have never won anything in a lottery.
en.notes: Almost only in the phrase verb in the past form + ためしがない "it has never happened that ...", usually slightly reproachful and almost always written in kana. The reading れい (例, "example") is the normal word for examples (例えば, 例を挙げる). 試し "attempt, trial" (試しに, お試し) is a separate word with the same pronunciation.

en.meaning: tan: cloth measure for one kimono (approx. 10 m); land area of 300 tsubo (approx. 991.7 m²) (counter)
examples[].german: To tailor one kimono, you need one bolt of cloth (one tan).
My grandfather owns three tan of rice fields.
Thanks to the new variety, the rice yield per tan has increased.
en.notes: Traditional unit of measure that follows numbers: 一反 (いったん), 二反, 三反 (さんたん). For cloth, one 反 is the bolt for one kimono, hence 反物 "kimono fabric"; as a unit of area it lives on in agriculture (一反あたりの収量). Do not confuse it with the prefix 反〜 (はん) "anti-" or the identically sounding adverb 一旦 "for the time being, once".

examples[].german: A single currency is used in the eurozone.
This product is made of a single material, so it is easy to recycle.
en.notes: Single, not composite: 単一の〜, 単一通貨 (single currency). For batteries: 単一 = size D, 単三 = AA.

examples[].german: Months and days passed with no chance for him to act, and he was lamenting his enforced idleness.
The scope of the research is so vast that one cannot help sighing in despair.
en.notes: Written-language noun that today appears almost only in fixed phrases of the form "〜の嘆": 髀肉の嘆をかこつ "to lament enforced idleness", 望洋の嘆 "a sigh at one's own inadequacy", 亡羊の嘆. In everyday speech the verb 嘆く (なげく) or the noun 嘆き is used instead; in compounds it is found in 感嘆 "admiration" and 悲嘆 "grief". The variant 歎 is an older spelling.

examples[].german: Who the culprit was was as plain as the palm of one's hand.
When he lost the game, he changed his attitude as quickly as turning over his hand.
The old monk placed a small Buddha statue on his palm and showed it to me.
en.notes: Literary reading of 掌; the normal word is 手のひら (てのひら, separate card), which can also be written 掌. たなごころ lives on mainly in idioms: 掌を指す "to be perfectly clear" (like pointing at one's palm) and 掌を返す "in the blink of an eye; to suddenly change one's attitude". In novels and poems 掌 often stands for てのひら, so context helps with the reading.

examples[].german: My older sister graduated from junior college and became a nursery teacher.
At junior college I studied nutrition for two years.
en.notes: Short for 短期大学: a two- to three-year college with a practical focus.

examples[].german: As a child, I loved exploring the woods in my neighborhood.
Thorough preparation is essential for an Antarctic expedition.
en.notes: Exploring unknown territory; as a verb 探検する. 探検家 (explorer), 探検隊 (expedition party). Also written 探険.

examples[].german: I listened to overseas broadcasts on a shortwave radio.
Shortwave was used to communicate with ships.
en.notes: A radio frequency band; cf. 中波 (medium wave), 長波 (long wave).

examples[].german: With age, I've become more concerned about the sagging of my face.
Please pull the rope tight so that there is no slack.
en.notes: Noun of 弛む: 顔のたるみ (slack skin); figuratively laxity (気のたるみ). Often in kana; the kanji 弛み can also be read ゆるみ.

en.meaning: to sag, to slacken; to become lax
examples[].german: The power line is sagging and getting closer to the ground.
Lately your attitude has been slack during practice!
en.notes: Ropes, skin or discipline become slack: 気持ちがたるむ. Often in kana; the kanji 弛む can also be read ゆるむ.

examples[].german: Even at her age, my grandmother is still hale and hearty.
She is proficient in English.
en.notes: Healthy and vigorous (お達者で! "Take care of yourself!" when parting) or skilled: 口が達者 (eloquent; also: all talk).

examples[].german: A person drowning in the river was calling for help.
Without my friends' help, I wouldn't have finished this job.
en.notes: Noun of 助ける: 助けを求める (to ask for help), 助けになる (to be helpful). Cry for help: 助けて!

examples[].german: The class was divided in opinion, so we decided by majority vote.
A majority decision is not necessarily right.
en.notes: A decision by majority of votes: 多数決で決める, 多数決を取る.

examples[].german: The soldiers blocked the arrows with their shields.
He used the law as a pretext to refuse payment.
en.notes: A protective shield; figuratively 〜を盾に(取る) (to take cover behind something, to use as a pretext). Cf. 矛盾 (literally "spear and shield": contradiction).

en.meaning: to pay on someone's behalf, to advance (money)
examples[].german: I had forgotten my wallet, so a friend paid for my lunch.
Please pay the transportation costs yourself first, and claim them from the company later.
en.notes: To pay temporarily for someone else, expecting repayment. Homophone: 建て替える (to rebuild).

en.meaning: to offer, to dedicate; (nominally) to install in a high position
examples[].german: Offerings were presented before the altar of the gods.
He has been installed as chairman in name only.
en.notes: Very reverent, today mainly religious or archaic. Figuratively: to put someone in a high position in name only.

en.meaning: to value highly; to revere, to respect
examples[].german: Politeness has been prized in this country since long ago.
We should respect the wisdom of our predecessors.
en.notes: Literary; also read とうとぶ and also written 貴ぶ.

examples[].german: A tall tower was built in front of the station.
We could see Mt. Fuji from the observation deck of Tokyo Tower.
en.notes: A tower as a modern structure (東京タワー); also a high-rise: タワーマンション (tower apartment building). Traditional towers: 塔.

examples[].german: For him, solving this problem is easy.
It is easy to say, but difficult to carry out.
en.notes: Literary for 簡単 or 易しい; often also in kana たやすい. 容易 (ようい), by contrast, is a na-adjective: 容易な.

examples[].german: For detailed instructions, please read this guide.
The culprit apparently got into the building with the help of an insider.
en.notes: Guiding or leading someone, also in crimes: 内部の者の手引き (help from an insider). As a publication: guide, handbook (利用の手引き).

en.meaning: to handle personally; to work on; to be in charge of
examples[].german: This building was designed by a famous architect.
She has composed the music for many films so far.
en.notes: To take on a job personally or be significantly involved in it: 彼が手掛けた作品 (a work he created). Also written 手がける.

examples[].german: It's arranged that a car will meet us at the airport.
I have made all the arrangements for the meeting.
en.notes: Arrangements made in advance for how something will proceed: 手筈を整える (to make all preparations), 〜する手筈になっている (it is arranged that ...). Often written 手はず.

examples[].german: He answered the question as if he knew nothing.
The party, soaked by the rain, was a pitiful sight.
en.notes: 体（てい）here denotes the outwardly recognizable form or state of a person or thing, sometimes also a deliberately created appearance. It sounds literary and often follows の or a descriptive form, as in 何も知らない体 "as if one knew nothing". 態 is also attested for this reading. 体（からだ）"body" and 体（たい）in other technical or counter uses are separate readings. The ending ～体 as a disparaging designation is not practiced here.

en.meaning: set meal; fixed menu (main dish with sides)
examples[].german: For lunch I had a grilled fish set meal at the eatery in front of the station.
At this restaurant, refills of rice are free with the set meal.
en.notes: A fixed meal with rice, miso soup and side dishes, typical of cafeterias and simple restaurants: 焼き魚定食, 日替わり定食 (set meal of the day).

en.meaning: close at hand; handy; familiar, everyday
examples[].german: I always keep my dictionary within reach.
Let me explain with a familiar example.
en.notes: Within easy reach: 手近な所に置く, 手近にある物. Figuratively: familiar, everyday (手近な例). Cf. 身近 (close, familiar).

en.meaning: number of moves (shogi, Go), number of blows (boxing); trouble, effort
examples[].german: This shogi mating problem takes so many moves that it is hard to solve.
The challenger landed more blows and won by decision.
In a capturing race, the side with more moves wins.
en.notes: The reading てかず is preferred when counted moves or blows are meant: 手数が多い/少ない, 手数で勝る; in Go also the liberties of a stone in a capturing race (攻め合い). For "trouble, effort", on the other hand, てすう is usual, especially in the polite formula お手数 (おてすう, separate card) and in 手数料 "fee".

examples[].german: The entrance exam includes an aptitude test in addition to the written exam.
I think he has an aptitude for teaching.
en.notes: Natural fitness for a task or occupation: 適性検査 (aptitude test), 適性がある. Not to be confused with 適正 (appropriate), which is pronounced the same.

examples[].german: The export volume of iron and steel decreased from the previous year.
This town has prospered on the steel industry since long ago.
en.notes: Umbrella term for iron and steel products, mainly in economic texts: 鉄鋼業 (steel industry), 鉄鋼メーカー (steelmaker). Homophone: 鉄鉱 (iron ore).

examples[].german: I bought a radio that can be charged by hand crank in case of disasters.
You've even made the reservation already? You're well prepared.
en.notes: 1) Turned by hand: 手回しのオルゴール (hand-cranked music box). 2) Preparations in advance: 手回しがいい (to be well prepared).

examples[].german: All we can do is leave it to fate and wait for the result.
A tall tower rises toward the sky.
en.notes: Heaven as the counterpart of earth (天と地) and as a higher power: 天の恵み (heaven's blessing), 運を天に任せる (to leave it to fate). For the visible sky in daily life, usually 空.

en.meaning: heaven and earth; the world; one's own sphere
examples[].german: It was a huge incident that turned the world upside down.
He went abroad in search of a new world.
en.notes: Elevated: the universe (天地創造 = the Creation) or the world in which one lives and works: 新天地 (new world, fresh start). On parcels: 天地無用 (this side up, do not turn over).

examples[].german: He isn't listening to me at all.
I'm hopeless at math.
en.notes: Colloquial, mostly with negation or a negative expression: てんで話にならない (completely out of the question), てんでだめ. More formal: 全然, まったく.

examples[].german: Dinosaur fossils are on display at the museum.
Please do not touch the exhibits.
en.notes: Displaying objects: 展示品 (exhibit), 展示会 (exhibition, trade show). As a verb 展示する. Homophone: 点字 (braille).

en.meaning: to turn; to shift; to change (something) to
examples[].german: In the afternoon, stock prices turned upward.
He steered the conversation to work.
en.notes: Literary; intransitive (株価が上昇に転じる = stock prices turn upward) and transitive (話題を転じる = to change the subject). Proverb: 災い転じて福となす (to turn misfortune into good fortune). Same meaning: 転ずる.

examples[].german: The Olympic flame was lit at the opening ceremony.
The rocket's engines were ignited and the launch began.
en.notes: To light a fire or ignite an engine: 聖火の点火 (lighting of the Olympic flame), エンジンに点火する. As a verb 点火する.

en.meaning: the whole world; the whole country; rule over the country; the public (e.g. 天下を取る, 天下一)
examples[].german: Toyotomi Hideyoshi finally took control of the whole country.
