The ramen at this shop is without equal.
When I get home, my wife rules the roost.
en.notes: Classic in 天下を取る ("to win rule over the country") and 天下一品 ("matchless, the best in the land"). Figuratively, 〜の天下 means "where ... has the say", e.g. かかあ天下 ("the wife wears the pants"). Do not confuse it with 天下り (あまくだり, vocab-n3:1777, officials moving into private business) and the identically sounding 点火 "ignition".

examples[].german: U-turns are prohibited at this intersection.
The ship slowly turned around and began heading back to port.
en.notes: Turning or changing direction, especially of vehicles: 転回禁止 (no U-turn; the official term for Uターン禁止). For a change of course in politics etc., usually 転換. Homophone: 展開 (development).

examples[].german: Because of my father's job, I changed schools three times.
I hear a transfer student is joining our class next month.
en.notes: To change schools, e.g. after a move; 転校生 = a new classmate transferred from another school. As a verb 転校する. Homophone: 天候 (weather).

examples[].german: After moving, you must file a notification within two weeks.
I informed the post office of my new address.
en.notes: Formal and official word for 引っ越し: 転居届 (change-of-address notification), 転居先 (new address). As a verb 転居する.

examples[].german: Our homeroom teacher was transferred to another school in spring.
I visited the principal's office to give my farewell greeting on my transfer.
en.notes: A move to a different post, especially for teachers and civil servants. Cf. 転勤 (transfer to another location, mainly in companies).

examples[].german: A barrier was installed to prevent falls from the platform.
After a string of defeats, the team dropped to last place.
en.notes: Falling down (ホームから転落する) or, figuratively, a drop in rank or circumstances: 最下位に転落する (to fall to last place). As a verb 転落する.

examples[].german: You never know when natural disasters like earthquakes or typhoons will strike.
This damage is not a natural disaster but a man-made one.
en.notes: A calamity caused by nature (earthquake, typhoon, flood); antonym 人災 (man-made disaster). Homophone: 天才 (genius).

examples[].german: Please cut along the dotted line with scissors.
The dotted line on the map shows the prefectural border.
en.notes: A line made of dots or short dashes: 点線に沿って切る (to cut along the dotted line). Cf. 実線 (solid line).

examples[].german: Countless celestial bodies shine in the night sky.
My son was moved when he saw Saturn through the telescope.
en.notes: Stars, planets, moons, etc.: 天体観測 (astronomical observation), 天体望遠鏡 (astronomical telescope).

en.meaning: to turn; to shift; to change (something) to
examples[].german: The economy is expected to turn toward recovery next year.
You need to judge the right moment to switch from offense to defense.
en.notes: The literary ずる-form of 転じる with the same meaning; conjugated like other ずる verbs (passive 転ぜられる, also 転じられる).

en.meaning: too late (to act or to save)
examples[].german: By the time he was taken to the hospital, it was already too late.
It's never too late to start studying.
en.notes: The time when one could still have acted has passed: もう手遅れだ; 今からでも手遅れではない (it's not too late even now). Often about illness.

en.meaning: top; summit; crown of the head
examples[].german: We finally reached the top of the mountain.
He was soaked from head to toe.
en.notes: The highest point: 山のてっぺん, 頭のてっぺんから足の先まで (from head to toe). More colloquial than 頂上. Usually in kana.

en.meaning: to reflect (light, heat); to radiate back
examples[].german: The snow reflects the sunlight and it is dazzling.
In summer the asphalt radiates heat back, so you sweat just from walking.
en.notes: Sunlight or heat is thrown back from a surface: 雪が日光を照り返す. Noun: 照り返し (reflected glare).

en.meaning: trouble, bother, effort; number of moves (Go/shogi)
examples[].german: The procedure for these documents takes surprisingly much effort.
I don't like causing other people trouble.
He checkmated the opponent's king with few moves.
en.notes: Neutral base word of お手数 (vocab-n3:1432), which is used toward others as the polite formula お手数をおかけします; 手数 itself appears in 手数がかかる "to be troublesome" and 手数をかける "to cause trouble". In board games it denotes the number of moves. There is also the reading てかず; the derivative 手数料 "fee" is well known too.

examples[].german: Children are playing on the horizontal bar in the schoolyard.
After practicing, I can finally do a backward swing-up on the horizontal bar.
en.notes: In school, the horizontal bar: 鉄棒で逆上がりをする (to do a backward swing-up on the bar). Literal meaning: iron bar.

en.meaning: division of labor; splitting up the work
examples[].german: Everyone split up and searched for the lost key.
Let's decide how to divide up the work before we begin.
en.notes: Mostly 手分けして〜する (to split up and do ...): 手分けして探す.

examples[].german: I put a box of tissues on the table.
During hay fever season, tissues run out quickly.
en.notes: In daily life usually shortened to ティッシュ: ティッシュを一枚ください. The spelling ティシュペーパー is a rarer variant.

en.meaning: promoted pawn in shogi (short form of と金)
examples[].german: I captured the opponent's promoted pawn and stopped the attack.
I advanced a pawn, promoted it, and pressed in on the king.
en.notes: と is, in shogi, the short form of と金（ときん）, the promoted pawn. The piece arises from a 歩（ふ）through promotion and then moves like a 金（きん）. The short form appears mainly in commentary, notation and talk about a game. The expression is an independent noun, not a conditional particle.

examples[].german: The veil of night fell, and the town grew quiet.
The room was divided in two by a thick curtain.
en.notes: Literary: 夜の帳が下りる (night falls). Otherwise the character is usually read ちょう (手帳, 帳面).

examples[].german: I slowly opened the heavy door.
Studying abroad opened a door to a new world for me.
en.notes: More elevated than ドア and often figurative: 未来への扉 (door to the future), 心の扉を開く (to open one's heart).

en.meaning: to cease; to be cut off
examples[].german: After graduation, contact with him broke off.
At night, this street has no more foot traffic.
en.notes: Something ongoing stops: 連絡が途絶える (contact is lost), 人通りが途絶える (no one passes by anymore). Cf. 途切れる (to break off briefly, to falter).

en.meaning: to stop; to hold back; to limit; to record
examples[].german: We were able to keep the damage to a minimum.
The lessons from the accident need to be put on record.
The police officer sensed danger and stopped the passengers from departing.
en.notes: 留める／止める read as とどめる is transitive: you hold someone or something back, limit a process, or record a fact. The person or thing affected takes を. 出発をとどめる means "to prevent the departure", 被害を最小限にとどめる "to keep the damage small", and 記録にとどめる "to put on record". For the sense of recording, 留める is used in particular. The reading とどめる is an ichidan verb with とどめます and とどめて; とめる is a separate reading with other common expressions.

en.meaning: to blame; to reproach; to prick (one's conscience)
examples[].german: No one blamed him for his failure.
Because I lied, my conscience has been bothering me the whole time.
en.notes: To hold someone's mistake against them: 失敗を咎める. Intransitive in 気が咎める (to have a guilty conscience). Often in kana: とがめる.

examples[].german: A rose thorn pricked my finger.
There was a sting in her words.
en.notes: A plant's thorn (バラのとげ), a splinter lodged in the skin (指にとげが刺さる), or figuratively a hurtful edge: とげのある言い方 (a barbed remark). Usually in kana.

en.meaning: to break off; to be interrupted; to falter
examples[].german: The voice on the phone keeps cutting out, and I can hardly hear it.
The conversation stalled, and an awkward silence fell.
en.notes: Something continuous breaks off (temporarily): 話が途切れる (the conversation lulls), 電波が途切れる (the signal drops), 人通りが途切れる (foot traffic stops for a while). Cf. 途絶える (to cease entirely).

examples[].german: The hotel is a five-minute walk from the station.
There are no buses, so the only way is to go on foot.
en.notes: Formal for 歩いて: 駅から徒歩五分 (five minutes' walk from the station), typical in apartment and hotel listings.

examples[].german: Before going out, I checked that everything was locked.
There have been many burglaries lately, so please be careful to lock up.
en.notes: Securing everything before leaving or going to bed: 戸締まりをする, 戸締まりに気をつける.

examples[].german: I put the meeting materials together and bound them.
The receipts are filed in a binder by month.
en.notes: To staple sheets together or bind them into a booklet: ファイルに綴じる (to file). Homophone: 閉じる (to close).

en.meaning: en route; in the process; in progress
examples[].german: He was in an accident on his way to work.
This technology is still at the research stage.
en.notes: Elevated: 帰宅の途上 (on the way home), 発展途上国 (developing country), 〜の途上にある (to be in the midst of ...).

examples[].german: Now and then you can hear birdsong from outside the window.
She occasionally shows a lonely expression.
en.notes: More elevated than 時々: 時折雨が降る. Also written 時おり.

examples[].german: Since I have to get up early tomorrow morning, I'm going to bed at nine tonight.
I read a letter from the family to my mother, who lay ill in bed.
en.notes: 床／とこ means the bed or bedding, especially in phrases like 床に就く "to go to bed". In illness it can mean the sickbed: 病の床に伏す means to lie ill in bed. The person concerned takes は or が. For the floor, use the other reading ゆか. Also 床の間／とこのま "decorative alcove" is a fixed word combination of its own.

en.meaning: to explain; to expound; to preach; to persuade
examples[].german: The doctor impressed upon the patient the importance of exercise.
Buddha preached the Buddhist teachings to the people.
en.notes: To explain a teaching or necessity earnestly: 必要性を説く, 教えを説く; also to try to persuade someone (説き伏せる = to talk someone round). Homophone: 解く (to solve).

examples[].german: The newspaper sent a reporter to the scene.
He worked as a correspondent in London for three years.
en.notes: Mostly in 特派員 (foreign correspondent, special reporter); verb 特派する (to dispatch specially).

examples[].german: Apples are a specialty of Aomori Prefecture.
At my travel destination I bought local specialties.
en.notes: A product typical of a region: 特産品 (regional specialty), 〜の特産 (a specialty of ...).

examples[].german: This month's magazine has a feature on Kyoto.
I watched a special program about earthquakes on TV.
en.notes: A featured topic in a magazine, newspaper, or program: 特集記事 (feature article), 特集番組 (special program). As a verb 特集する or 特集を組む.

examples[].german: He built up an enormous fortune within a single generation.
The wealth gap has become a social problem.
en.notes: Formal: 富を築く (to build a fortune), 富の格差 (wealth gap). More everyday: 財産, お金.

en.meaning: attendant, retinue, companion (e.g. 供をする)
examples[].german: The lord set out for Edo with a large retinue.
A young samurai was to accompany the princess.
As his master's attendant, he went to the castle every day.
en.notes: 供 (とも) refers to someone who accompanies a person of higher rank, or the whole retinue; typical are 供をする ("to accompany"), 供を連れる and 供の者 ("attendants"). The plain 供 sounds historical or literary today; in everyday speech the polite form お供 (おとも, separate card) is used, e.g. お供します. Not to be confused with 友 (とも, "friend", separate card).

examples[].german: We both work, so we share the housework.
The number of dual-income households is rising year by year.
en.notes: Both spouses work: 共稼ぎの夫婦. Today 共働き is more common.

examples[].german: I saw the lights of a village in the distance and felt relieved.
That activity became a light of hope for the people affected by the disaster.
Business results worsened, and the company is now hanging by a thread.
en.notes: Elevated word for a (small) light in the darkness, often figurative: 希望の灯火 "light of hope", 風前の灯火 "a light in the wind" (= on the verge of ruin). Mostly written 灯火; the same spelling is read とうか in technical words (灯火管制). The reading ひ (separate card, 灯を消す) and 明かり (あかり) are the plain everyday words for light.

examples[].german: My wallet was stolen on the trip, and I had a terrible time.
To say that I'm the culprit is a complete misunderstanding.
en.notes: Prenominal word, used only before nouns: とんだ災難 (a terrible misfortune), とんだ目に遭う (to have a bad experience), とんだ誤解 (a huge misunderstanding).

examples[].german: The road was crowded, so I took a detour home.
Even if it looks like a detour, learning from the basics is best.
en.notes: To take a longer route (遠回りする); figuratively also a roundabout approach. Proverb: 急がば回れ (more haste, less speed).

examples[].german: Please lower the tone of your voice in the library.
I repainted the walls of the room in a calm tone of color.
en.notes: 声のトーン (tone of voice), トーンを落とす (to speak more quietly; also: to tone down). Also for colors: 落ち着いたトーン (a calm tone).

en.meaning: to move away; to become distant; to drift away from
examples[].german: The ship slowly moved away from the harbor.
Since I started working, I have drifted completely away from sports.
en.notes: To move farther away in space (足音が遠ざかる) or, figuratively, to lose contact with something: 政治から遠ざかる. Transitive: 遠ざける.

examples[].german: Three transistors are used in this circuit.
My grandfather treasures his old transistor radio.
en.notes: Electronic component for amplifying and switching; also written トランジスター. トランジスタラジオ = transistor radio.

examples[].german: The air conditioner's filter needs to be replaced regularly.
If the size doesn't fit, we will gladly exchange it.
en.notes: Noun of 取り替える: 部品の取り替え. Also written 取り換え.

examples[].german: At the airport, a crowd of fans surrounded the actor.
The environment surrounding children has changed greatly over the past twenty years.
en.notes: Transitive: ファンが歌手を取り巻く (fans crowd around a singer). Common in 〜を取り巻く環境 / 〜を取り巻く状況 (the environment, the situation surrounding ...). The noun 取り巻き refers derogatorily to an entourage.

examples[].german: The box contains twenty apples, large and small mixed.
We served the guests an assortment of Japanese and Western sweets.
en.notes: Transitive, mostly in the て-form: 大小取り混ぜて (large and small mixed), 新旧取り混ぜて (old and new mixed).

examples[].german: Crackdowns on drunk driving get stricter at the end of the year.
The police stepped up enforcement against illegal parking.
en.notes: Official enforcement against violations: スピード違反の取り締まり (speed enforcement), 取り締まりを強化する. Verb: 取り締まる.

en.meaning: to supervise, control; to crack down on
examples[].german: The police are strictly cracking down on speeding.
A law was enacted to crack down on the sale of counterfeits.
en.notes: Mainly: to punish and stop violations (違法行為を取り締まる). Originally the general sense "to supervise, manage"; hence 取締役 (board member).

examples[].german: The police questioned the suspect for three hours.
My luggage was thoroughly inspected at customs.
en.notes: Mostly in police contexts: to question suspects (容疑者を取り調べる); noun: 取り調べ (interrogation). For checking in general: 調べる.

en.meaning: to collect (debts); to promote; to single out
examples[].german: The loan shark came to collect the debt.
There is no problem worth mentioning.
en.notes: 1) To demand money: 借金を取り立てる. 2) To promote or favor someone: 部長に取り立てる. 3) To mention specially, usually in the negative: 取り立てて言うほどのことではない (not worth mentioning).

en.meaning: to pass on; to announce (visitor, call); to mediate
examples[].german: Calls to the president are to be put through by the secretary.
When a customer arrives, please announce them to me right away.
en.notes: Transitive: 電話を取り次ぐ (to put a call through), 伝言を取り次ぐ (to pass on a message). The noun 取り次ぎ means relaying or mediation; in the book trade also wholesale distribution.

en.meaning: to install; to attach; to obtain (consent, promise)
examples[].german: A contractor came and installed a new air conditioner.
The department head finally obtained the president's consent.
en.notes: Transitive. Concretely: エアコンを取り付ける (to install an air conditioner). Figuratively: 同意を取り付ける (to obtain consent), 約束を取り付ける (to secure a promise).

en.meaning: to order in; to have sent; to send for
examples[].german: That book is out of stock, so we will have to order it in.
I ordered fresh crab from Hokkaido.
en.notes: Transitive: 本を取り寄せる (to order a book that is not in stock). The noun 取り寄せ (お取り寄せ) is already in the vocabulary.

en.meaning: instant; on the spur of the moment; reflexive
examples[].german: On a split-second decision, I hit the brakes.
When asked my name, I lied on the spur of the moment.
en.notes: Mostly as 咄嗟の (spontaneous, on the spot: 咄嗟の判断) or 咄嗟に (instinctively, instantly). Often in kana: とっさ.

examples[].german: The drawer handle came off.
It's hot, so please hold the pot by its handle.
en.notes: A handle on a door, drawer, cup, or pot: ドアの取っ手, カップの取っ手. Similar: 持ち手.

examples[].german: Three new apartment buildings went up in front of the station.
My friend lives in the next building of the same housing complex.
en.notes: Mainly a counter for buildings: マンション三棟 (three apartment buildings). As a noun, e.g. 隣の棟 (the next building) or A棟 (Building A); in compounds: 病棟 (hospital ward), 研究棟 (research building). The reading むね means ridge of a roof.

examples[].german: The committee deliberated on the draft budget.
After a long deliberation, a conclusion was finally reached.
en.notes: A formal discussion aimed at reaching a result: 討議を重ねる. Cf. 議論 (discussion in general), 討論 (debate with pro and con).

examples[].german: The children go to school at eight every morning.
Because of the heavy snow, it was decided that we don't have to go to school today.
en.notes: To go to school as a pupil: 登校時間 (time to go to school), 集団登校 (walking to school in a group), 不登校 (school refusal). Opposite: 下校 (leaving school). Homophone: 投稿 (post, submission).

examples[].german: Fruit is divided into grades according to size and color.
This beef was given the highest grade.
en.notes: Classification by quality or rank: 等級をつける (to grade). In astronomy, also the magnitude of a star.

en.meaning: the person concerned; the person in question
examples[].german: It's not good to badmouth someone behind their back.
Even though everyone around is worried, the person himself looks unconcerned.
en.notes: The person under discussion: 当人の気持ち (the feelings of the person concerned). Same meaning and more common: 本人.

examples[].german: During the war, prices were controlled by the state.
This team is well organized.
en.notes: State or organizational control: 言論統制 (restriction of free speech), 統制が取れている (to be well organized, disciplined). As a verb 統制する.

en.meaning: winning an election; winning a prize draw
examples[].german: He was finally elected on his third attempt.
I won a sweepstakes and got a travel voucher.
en.notes: To be elected (選挙で当選する) or drawn in a lottery (宝くじに当選する). Opposite: 落選.

examples[].german: The captain leads the team well.
He has the ability to lead a large number of subordinates.
en.notes: Leading and holding a group together: 統率力 (leadership ability). As a verb 統率する.

examples[].german: The culprit fled by car.
The police are tracking the whereabouts of the man on the run.
en.notes: Escape, especially of criminals: 逃走中の犯人 (fugitive), 逃走経路 (escape route). As a verb 逃走する; more everyday: 逃げる.

en.meaning: with a chopping sound (axe felling wood), with a dull thudding (taru-adjective, written language)
examples[].german: The sound of an axe echoes from deep in the mountains.
A woodcutter was chopping down a big tree with thudding blows.
The thud of driving in stakes broke the morning stillness.
en.notes: Literary onomatopoeia for the rhythmic chopping of an axe or the driving in of a stake, mostly as 丁々と or attributively 丁々たる. Do not confuse it with the identically sounding cards とうとう "at last", 等々 "etc." and 蕩蕩 "vast, boundless". The same spelling is read ちょうちょう for clashing swords, e.g. in 丁々発止 "a heated exchange of blows".

examples[].german: Below us, a broad, mighty river flowed leisurely.
Under the gentle sunlight, the wide, calm spring sea stretches out.
en.notes: Literary taru-adjective, mostly 蕩々たる before a noun or 蕩々と adverbially, especially for wide, calm stretches of water. Do not confuse it with the identically sounding cards とうとう "at last" and 〜等々 "and so on", or with 滔々 "flowing torrentially; eloquent" (滔々と語る), which is more common in everyday use. Usually written with 々.

en.meaning: pot; jar; vase; target, aim; crux; pressure point
examples[].german: An old vase is displayed on the shelf.
If you get angry now, you'll be playing right into their hands.
en.notes: A bulging vessel of clay or porcelain. In figurative senses usually written ツボ: 話のツボ (crux of a story), 肩のツボを押す (to press a pressure point on the shoulder). 思う壺 = exactly as the other person wanted.

examples[].german: The puppy is looking at us with big round eyes.
The baby's round, bright eyes made everyone smile.
en.notes: Used almost only in つぶらな瞳 / つぶらな目 (big, round, adorable eyes), mostly of children and animals. Usually in kana.

examples[].german: Please close your eyes and take a slow, deep breath.
I was scared of the injection and shut my eyes without thinking.
en.notes: Only with 目: 目をつぶる (to close one's eyes), figuratively "to turn a blind eye" (see the idiom 目をつぶる). Same meaning as 目を閉じる, but somewhat more colloquial.

examples[].german: My grandfather goes for walks with a cane.
When the wizard waved his staff, flowers bloomed.
en.notes: A walking stick (杖をつく: to walk with a cane), also a magic wand. Proverb: 転ばぬ先の杖 (better safe than sorry).

examples[].german: Water is leaking from the joint of the pipe.
Every time the train passes over a rail joint, it goes clunk.
en.notes: A place where two parts are joined: in pipes, boards, rails, or fabric. Cf. 縫い目 (seam in sewing).

en.meaning: to join; to set (a bone); to graft
examples[].german: The doctor set the broken bone and fixed it with a cast.
You graft an apple branch onto another tree and grow it.
en.notes: To join parts into a whole: 骨を接ぐ (to set a bone), 木を接ぐ (to graft a tree). Homophone: 継ぐ (to succeed, to continue).

examples[].german: First the company president gave a greeting, and next the guests of honor offered congratulatory remarks.
Tokyo has the largest population, followed by Yokohama.
en.notes: Literary; from the verb 次ぐ. Not to be confused with ついで (序で, opportunity: ついでに).

examples[].german: He was expelled from the country.
Let's drive violence out of our town.
en.notes: Expulsion or banishment of people (国外追放) and the eradication of evils (暴力追放). As a verb 追放する.

en.meaning: to pursue (guilt, responsibility); to hold accountable
examples[].german: The opposition sharply pressed the minister on his responsibility.
He could not escape the police investigation.
en.notes: Persistently pursuing guilt or responsibility: 責任を追及する. Homophones: 追求 (pursuit of happiness, profit) and 追究 (investigating the truth).

examples[].german: A patrol car pursued the fleeing vehicle.
You can track the delivery status of a package online.
en.notes: Pursuit (of culprits, animals) and tracking (of shipments, studies): 追跡調査 (follow-up study). As a verb 追跡する.

examples[].german: His story doesn't add up.
The culprit desperately tried to make his lies consistent.
en.notes: Used almost only in set phrases: 辻褄が合う (to be coherent), 辻褄が合わない (not to add up), 辻褄を合わせる (to smooth over contradictions). Often in kana: つじつま.

examples[].german: I haven't yet decided what to spend my bonus on.
This old box has various uses.
en.notes: What money or things are used for: 使い道がない (useless). Also written 使いみち.

examples[].german: I enjoyed a brief rest.
My joy was short-lived, as another problem came up.
en.notes: A fleeting moment: 束の間の幸せ; 〜のも束の間 (... but only briefly).

examples[].german: It may sound trite, but health is what matters most.
His speech was banal and left no impression.
en.notes: Lacking originality: 月並みな表現 (cliche), 月並みな感想. The original meaning "every month" is now rare.

examples[].german: This bag is solidly made and will last a long time.
Architects gathered to see the construction of the old temple.
en.notes: The way something is made or built: 丈夫な作り (sturdy construction). For buildings often written 造り: 石造りの家. Also appearance (若作り = made up to look young) and physique (体の作り). As a second element often voiced: 手作り (てづくり).

en.meaning: to mend, to patch; to tidy up; to keep up (appearances)
examples[].german: My grandmother carefully mended my torn shirt for me.
He smoothed over the situation with a laugh, but he was inwardly flustered.
en.notes: To repair something damaged (靴下を繕う), to tidy one's appearance (身なりを繕う), or figuratively 体裁を繕う (to keep up appearances), その場を繕う (to smooth over the situation). Cf. 取り繕う.

examples[].german: Since I started living alone, I have keenly felt how grateful I am to my parents.
I gazed intently at my face reflected in the mirror.
en.notes: Describes a deep feeling, often gained from experience: つくづく思う / 感じる. Also "to look intently": つくづく眺める. Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: Wondering if I was dreaming, I pinched my cheek.
My little brother pinched my little sister's arm and made her cry.
en.notes: To squeeze skin between the fingers: 頬をつねる. 夢じゃないかと頬をつねる = to pinch oneself to check whether one is dreaming. Usually in kana.

en.meaning: to become stiff, to tighten; to stand firm; to put on a tough act
examples[].german: I suddenly started running, and my calf cramped up and hurts.
He refused to admit his mistake and held out to the end.
en.notes: Basic meaning: to become stiff or taut (足が突っ張る, 肌が突っ張る). Figuratively: to stick to one's position or to act defiant and tough.

en.meaning: to extend in a line; to stretch; to be connected with
examples[].german: Snow-capped mountains stretch away in the distance.
He is a person who belongs to an old samurai family line.
en.notes: Many things standing in a row: 山々が連なる (a mountain range stretches), 車が連なる. Figuratively: to be connected with something (〜に連なる). Transitive: 連ねる.

en.meaning: to line up; to list (names); to string together
examples[].german: Restaurants stand side by side in front of the station.
Famous scholars are among the authors of the book.
en.notes: To arrange things in a row: 軒を連ねる (to stand eave to eave), 名を連ねる (to be on a list, to take part), 言葉を連ねる (to string words together). Intransitive: 連なる.

examples[].german: The temple bell rang at six in the evening.
This temple bell is said to have been made three hundred years ago.
en.notes: The large hanging bronze bell of a Buddhist temple, struck with a wooden beam; on New Year's Eve it is rung 108 times (除夜の鐘).

en.meaning: strap; hanging handle (on trains and buses)
examples[].german: The ride may be bumpy, so please hold on to the straps.
I'm short and can't reach the strap.
en.notes: The hanging strap in trains and buses: つり革につかまる (to hold on to the strap).

en.meaning: authoritative word (from a person in power)
examples[].german: The meeting dragged on, but the boss's word settled the matter.
At a word from grandfather, Kyoto became the travel destination.
en.notes: Literally "a cry of the crane": a single word from a powerful person ends a long discussion. Typical in companies and families.

en.meaning: to be up to the job; to be able to fill a post
examples[].german: I wonder whether someone as frail as he is can handle a job with lots of night shifts.
Since I'm bad with mornings, I can't handle this job.
en.notes: Intransitive counterpart of 勤める: to be able to fill a position. Mostly used negatively or in questions (勤まるだろうか), often as modesty about oneself.

examples[].german: Please write your address and place of work on the form.
My father's workplace is near the station.
en.notes: The company or agency where one is employed; on forms often next to 住所. More formal: 勤務先.

en.meaning: as far as possible; with effort; deliberately
examples[].german: She made an effort to act cheerful.
In meetings I try to speak as calmly as possible.
en.notes: Literary: consciously and as best one can: 努めて冷静に振る舞う (to make an effort to stay calm). From 努める (to strive).

examples[].german: I rolled up the graduation certificate and put it in the tube.
I filled a bamboo tube with water and arranged flowers in it.
en.notes: A hollow, cylindrical object: 竹の筒 (bamboo tube), 卒業証書の筒 (tube for a diploma). Cf. 管 (pipe, conduit).

en.meaning: to poke; to pick at; to nitpick
examples[].german: The person next to me poked me with an elbow, and I woke up.
My boss keeps nitpicking at the small mistakes in my reports.
en.notes: Colloquial intensified form of つつく: to poke lightly several times (肩を突っつく), to pick at food, or figuratively to pick on someone (欠点を突っつく). Often in kana.

examples[].german: Failing the exam made me keenly aware that I hadn't studied enough.
The disaster made me acutely aware of the importance of preparation.
en.notes: To experience something (usually unpleasant) firsthand and understand it deeply; as a verb 痛感する.

examples[].german: I felt deeply how precious peace is.
The poignant appeals of the disaster victims struck a chord.
en.notes: Deeply and painfully felt: 痛切に感じる. Similar: 痛感する.

examples[].german: As night fell, the wind grew even stronger.
Criticism of the government is growing day by day.
en.notes: Intransitive; transitive counterpart: 強める. Typical with wind, rain, trends, and criticism: 風が強まる, 批判が強まる.

en.meaning: to strengthen; to intensify; to emphasize
examples[].german: The police have stepped up vigilance around the station.
At the end, turn up the heat and let the liquid evaporate.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 強まる: 警戒を強める (to heighten vigilance), 語気を強める (to speak emphatically), 火を強める (to turn up the heat).

examples[].german: Let's arrange the order of the presentations before the meeting.
I coordinated the trip schedule with the guide.
en.notes: Transitive Ichidan verb: to discuss details in advance: 日程を打ち合わせる. The noun 打ち合わせ (meeting) is more common.

examples[].german: "Nai" is a word that expresses negation.
The company was busy denying the rumors.
en.notes: Negation (grammar: 打ち消しの形 = negative form) and the denial of a rumor. Verb: 打ち消す.

en.meaning: to drive in; to enter; to devote oneself
examples[].german: He is devoted to his research and hardly takes any time off.
I entered the data from the name list into the computer.
en.notes: Transitive Godan verb with several meanings: 釘を打ち込む (to drive in a nail), データを打ち込む (to enter data), 仕事に打ち込む (to throw oneself into work).

en.meaning: top and bottom, upper and lower side; upside down (上下逆さま)
examples[].german: Please check which side is up and which is down before opening the box.
This photo is pasted in upside down.
This picture looks like a face whether you view it from the top or from the bottom.
en.notes: うえした is the native Japanese reading of 上下 and refers concretely to the top and bottom of an object, or to "upside down" (上下が逆). The card 上下/じょうげ is the more general Sino-Japanese reading: movement up and down (上下する), hierarchy (上下関係), two-volume works (上下巻). With 上下逆さま both readings are common; うえした sounds more everyday.

examples[].german: As the saying goes, upbringing counts for more than birth: character is determined more by environment than by family background.
Every autumn, the festival of the local tutelary deity is held in the village.
In ancient Japan, each clan had a fixed role at the imperial court.
en.notes: うじ is the old native Japanese reading of 氏 for lineage, family name and the clan of early times (e.g. in the 氏姓制度). Today it appears mainly in the proverb 氏より育ち "upbringing counts more than birth" and in 氏神 "tutelary deity of a place or clan". To be distinguished are the cards 〜氏/し (polite name suffix "Mr./Ms.") and 氏/し "clan"; names like 藤原氏 are today mostly read with し.

examples[].german: This town is proactive in accepting refugees.
The hospital began taking in the injured.
en.notes: Noun of 受け入れる: 留学生の受け入れ (accepting exchange students), 受け入れ先 (receiving party).

examples[].german: Ms. Yamada is in charge of this class.
That isn't my responsibility, so I'll call the person in charge.
en.notes: What one is in charge of, especially a teacher's class: 受け持ちのクラス (the class one is in charge of), 受け持ちの先生 (the teacher in charge).

examples[].german: Lights are set into the ceiling.
I embedded a video in my blog.
en.notes: Transitive Godan verb: to insert or bury something into something else: 壁に照明を埋め込む; also digitally: 動画をページに埋め込む.

examples[].german: He keeps making excuses like "I have no time" and so on.
It is too early to talk about success or failure before the results are out.
en.notes: Replaces the rest of a quotation ("... and so on") or, as the verb 云々する, means "to comment on something". Literary.

examples[].german: I asked a shipping company to handle my moving boxes.
Fuel costs rose, so transport costs increased.
en.notes: Conveyance of goods: 運送会社 (shipping company), 運送料 (freight charges).

examples[].german: It is conceit to think you're a genius after just a little praise.
Everyone is fed up with his conceit.
en.notes: Exaggerated self-confidence: 自惚れが強い (very conceited). Verb: 自惚れる. Often in kana: うぬぼれ.

examples[].german: I didn't notice I was wearing my shirt inside out.
His strong words may be the flip side of his anxiety.
en.notes: Turned the wrong way round (シャツが裏返し) and, figuratively, the flip side: 不安の裏返し (a manifestation of hidden anxiety). Verb: 裏返す.

examples[].german: This store has a sale on the first of every month.
I bought clothes cheaply at the year-end sale.
en.notes: A sales promotion with special prices: 大売り出し (big sale). Also the launch of a new product.

en.meaning: to put on the market; to put on sale
examples[].german: The company will put a new smartphone on the market next month.
The limited items go on sale from 10 a.m. tomorrow.
en.notes: Transitive Godan verb: to launch a product or offer it for sale: 新商品を売り出す. Noun: 売り出し (sale); 売り出し中 also means "up-and-coming" (売り出し中の歌手).

examples[].german: I dozed off while watching TV.
If you doze off at the kotatsu, you'll catch a cold.
en.notes: A short nod-off, usually unplanned and without going to bed: ソファでうたた寝する. The kanji 転寝 is rare.

examples[].german: He was looking out the window with vacant eyes.
The trunk of the old tree was hollow inside.
en.notes: な-adjective: hollow inside or, more often, expressionless and absent-minded: 虚ろな目 (vacant eyes). Also written 空ろ.

examples[].german: You need a copy of your residence certificate for the application.
Could I have one copy of the contract?
en.notes: A copy of a document, often at government offices: 住民票の写し (copy of the residence certificate). More everyday: コピー.

examples[].german: Following the residents' complaints, the city started an investigation.
He filed a lawsuit against the company.
en.notes: Noun of 訴える: a legal lawsuit (訴えを起こす) and, more generally, a complaint: 住民の訴え.

examples[].german: A big cherry tree is planted in the garden.
Flowers are planted on both sides of the road, and it's very pretty.
en.notes: Intransitive Godan verb, counterpart of 植える: mostly 植わっている (... is planted there).

examples[].german: An old shrine can be seen at the upper part of the slope.
In the negotiations, she, with her experience, had the upper hand by one notch.
en.notes: うわて denotes an upper area or superiority in comparison. The spatial use sounds rather elevated in descriptions. In 一枚上手 "one notch superior", no sheets are being counted: the phrase compares skill or ability. The general "good at something", by contrast, is 上手／じょうず. For the stage side, 上手 is read かみて.

en.meaning: to be buried; to be covered over; to be filled to capacity
examples[].german: The car was buried in snow and couldn't move.
Many houses were buried under rubble by the earthquake.
The square was filled with festival spectators.
en.notes: うずまる is a secondary reading of 埋まる (own card 埋まる/うまる) with the same meanings: "to be buried, covered over, completely covered" and "to be packed". It sounds somewhat more literary and is used especially for sinking into or being embedded in something: 雪にうずまる, がれきにうずまる. In everyday speech, one mostly says うまる (席がうまる); because 埋まる is read that way, うずまる is often written in kana. The transitive counterpart is うずめる "to bury, to fill".

examples[].german: I apologized to my boss for being late.
We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience caused.
en.notes: Formal, mostly with お: お詫び申し上げます (we offer our sincere apologies), お詫びの品 (a gift as an apology), 詫びを入れる (to apologize). Verb: 詫びる. Homophone: 侘び (rustic simplicity).

examples[].german: Translate the following Japanese text into English.
The contract is prepared in two versions, English and Japanese.
en.notes: Text in the Japanese language, especially as opposed to a foreign language: 和文英訳 (translation from Japanese into English). Counterparts: 欧文, 英文.

examples[].german: Please write your answer inside the box.
We are careful not to exceed the budget limit.
en.notes: 窓の枠 (window frame), 枠内 / 枠外 (inside / outside the frame), 予算の枠 (budget limit), 枠にとらわれない (unconventional). Homophones: 沸く, 湧く.

examples[].german: Please serve the rice into the rice bowls.
This bowl is Arita ware and is made very thin.
In the tea room, I was served a bowl of matcha.
en.notes: 碗 is a bowl made of ceramic or porcelain, whereas 椀 (own card) refers to a wooden or lacquer bowl, typically for soup; in everyday writing one often simply writes お椀 or お碗. On its own 碗 is rare; one meets it mainly in 茶碗 "rice bowl, tea bowl"; in the tea ceremony it also counts bowls (一碗のお茶). Not to be confused with the homophone 湾 "bay".

examples[].german: In the old days, farmers thatched their roofs with straw.
Clutching at straws, he consulted a fortune-teller.
en.notes: Often written in kana: わら. 藁葺き屋根 (thatched roof). Proverb: 溺れる者は藁をもつかむ (a drowning man will clutch at a straw).

examples[].german: In folk tales, the villain is defeated in the end.
Even though I hadn't done anything wrong, only I was made out to be the bad guy.
en.notes: The bad guy in stories: 悪者を退治する (to defeat the villain). Figurative: 悪者にされる (to be made the scapegoat).

examples[].german: In autumn, migratory birds fly south.
Many migratory birds come to this lake in winter.
en.notes: Birds such as swallows (ツバメ) or wild geese (ガン) that move on with the seasons.

examples[].german: This microwave can put out up to 1000 watts.
I changed the light bulb in the room from 60 watts to 40 watts.
en.notes: Unit of electrical power (symbol W): 百ワットの電球 (a 100-watt light bulb). Homophone: わっと (suddenly and loudly, e.g. わっと泣き出す).

en.meaning: suddenly and loudly (e.g. わっと泣き出す: to burst into tears)
examples[].german: The moment she lost the game, she burst into tears.
At the teacher's joke, the whole classroom burst out laughing.
When the sale began, customers rushed all at once to the sales floor.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic adverb for something that bursts out suddenly and loudly: わっと泣き出す ("to burst into tears"), わっと笑う ("to burst into loud laughter"), わっと歓声が上がる. It also describes many people suddenly rushing somewhere (客がわっと押し寄せる). Often written in katakana ワッと; not to be confused with the loanword ワット ("watt", separate card).

examples[].german: The archer hit the exact center of the target with his arrow.
The days and months passed like an arrow.
en.notes: Arrow for a bow (弓): 矢を射る (to shoot an arrow). Idioms: 矢のように (like an arrow, swiftly), 矢の催促 (relentless pressing). Same sound: 〜屋 (shop).

en.meaning: question particle for questions and rhetorical questions (older language)
examples[].german: Could this news be true?
How could one break that promise?
en.notes: An older or deliberately elevated sentence-final question particle marking a question or rhetorical question. The rare writing 哉 is read や here; the usual writing is the kana や. In present-day everyday speech, one would mostly use か or a corresponding question form. 哉 here denotes a spoken word marking a question, not a punctuation mark like "?". The examples deliberately use an elevated question tone. The reading かな for an exclamation and the enumerating particle や are other uses.

en.meaning: at night; during the night (written language)
examples[].german: In the desert it is hot during the day, but at night it gets cold enough to fall below freezing.
The police called on residents to refrain from going out at night.
en.notes: やちゅう is a rare, written-language reading of 夜中 and means "during the night" in general, often in contrast to 日中 "during the day". The usual reading is よなか "the middle of the night" (separate card), and without a reading aid the kanji is almost always read that way. In formal style, 夜間 (separate card) is usually used instead of やちゅう.

examples[].german: During summer vacation, the children went camping outdoors.
The open-air concert was canceled because of the rain.
en.notes: Mainly as a modifier: 野外コンサート (open-air concert), 野外活動 (outdoor activities). Similar: 屋外 (outside, outside of buildings).

examples[].german: The inn staff laid out the bedding in our room.
In preparation for winter, I took the thick bedding out of the closet.
en.notes: A somewhat old-fashioned word for futon and blankets; in everyday speech 布団 or 寝具 is used.

examples[].german: An old mansion stands deep in the forest.
The lord of this region used to live in that residence.
On a summer night, we went down the Sumida River on a covered pleasure boat.
en.notes: やかた is the native, elevated reading of 館 and refers to a manor, a noble residence or a small castle; it is typical of novels, fairy tales and titles (〜の館, 幽霊の館). The Sino-Japanese reading かん (separate cards), by contrast, means a public building or hall and appears almost only in compounds such as 図書館 or 美術館. The spelling 屋形 appears today mainly in 屋形船 ("covered pleasure boat").

examples[].german: You're strikingly quiet today. Did something happen?
There are an unusual number of mosquitoes this summer.
en.notes: Colloquial, when something is conspicuously and unexpectedly strong: 今日はやけに暑い (it's unusually hot today). Not to be confused with やけになる (to become reckless out of despair).

en.meaning: servant, retainer (of a samurai, Edo period); cube of tofu (short for 冷奴)
examples[].german: At the head of the daimyo procession, the retainers walked brandishing their spears.
On hot days, I eat chilled tofu topped with ginger and scallions.
I cut the tofu into cubes and put it in the miso soup.
en.notes: Historical word for the servants and spear-bearers of the samurai in the Edo period. Today it appears almost only in compounds: 冷奴（ひややっこ） "chilled tofu", 奴に切る "to cut tofu into cubes" (after the crest pattern on the servants' clothing) or 奴凧 "kite in the form of a servant". The reading やつ (separate card 奴/やつ) is a completely different, colloquial word for "guy, fellow".

examples[].german: In the novel, the man told his younger brother, "Stay away from drugs."
The reporter wrote an article about the arrest of a man who had been selling drugs.
en.notes: やく here is a colloquial word for narcotics; it is often written ヤク. It sounds much more slangy than 麻薬 and can appear in crime stories or in quoted speech. For ordinary medicine, one says くすり. The reading やく in compounds for medicines therefore does not automatically mean the narcotics meant here.

en.meaning: to be useful, serve a purpose
examples[].german: This book was very helpful for studying Japanese.
We have compiled information that is useful in disasters.
en.notes: A shorter, somewhat more written form of 役に立つ: 仕事に役立つ資格 (a qualification useful for work). Transitive: 役立てる (to put to use).

examples[].german: At forty, she took the position of department manager.
The business card shows name and title.
en.notes: A position in a company or agency, especially a management position: 役職に就く (to take up a post), 役職名 (title such as 部長 or 課長).

examples[].german: My grandfather died after a long illness.
They say "illness begins in the mind", so don't worry too much.
en.notes: More formal than 病気: 不治の病 (incurable disease), 病に倒れる (to fall seriously ill). Proverb: 病は気から (illness begins in the mind). Figuratively also a bad habit or weakness.

en.meaning: darkness; the hidden; black market, illegal channels
examples[].german: The power outage plunged the room into darkness.
The truth about the incident was buried in darkness.
en.notes: 暗闇 (pitch darkness). Figurative: 闇に葬る (to cover up), 闇市 (black market), 闇取引 (illegal dealing).

en.meaning: young; young people, youth (e.g. ヤング向け)
examples[].german: This magazine is made for young people.
My father still thinks of himself as young.
This shop is always bustling with young customers.
en.notes: A somewhat old-fashioned-sounding loanword from English that stands mainly attributively: ヤング向け ("for young people"), ヤングの客. It sounds like the advertising and media language of the 70s and 80s and is often used jokingly today. In normal usage 若者 (わかもの, separate card) or 若い is said.

en.meaning: to accomplish; to carry through successfully
examples[].german: It took three years, but we finally accomplished the project.
It is impossible to accomplish this work alone.
en.notes: To bring a difficult task to a successful conclusion: 仕事をやり遂げる. Puts more emphasis than やり通す on the result achieved.

en.meaning: to see through; to persevere to the end
examples[].german: I intend to see through to the end whatever I have once started.
Even though people around him objected, he stuck to his own way of doing things.
en.notes: To carry something out to the end despite difficulties: 最後までやり通す. Similar: やり遂げる (to complete successfully).

examples[].german: You can see wild monkeys on this island.
You shouldn't just eat mushrooms that grow wild in the mountains.
en.notes: 野生の動物 (wild animals), 野生のキノコ (wild-growing mushrooms). As a する-verb: 野生する (to grow wild). Related: 野生化 (becoming feral).

examples[].german: He has the ambition to become a politician.
The young president burned with the ambition to make the company number one in the world.
en.notes: 野心的 (ambitious), 野心家 (ambitious person). Often with a slightly negative tone: 野心を抱く (to harbor ambitious plans).

examples[].german: There is a small shrine deep in the forest.
The villagers hold a festival every year in front of the shrine in the forest.
en.notes: Literary reading of 社 for a Shinto shrine, especially a small one; in everyday speech usually 神社. Not to be confused with 社【しゃ】 (company, e.g. 我が社).

en.meaning: to let rest; to pause (an activity)
examples[].german: I want to do nothing this weekend and just rest my body.
She kept on working silently without pausing her hands.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 休む: 体を休める (to rest), 手を休める (to take a break), 目を休める (to rest one's eyes). Not to be confused with 休める as the potential form of 休む (to be able to take time off).

examples[].german: This bag was expensive, but it looks cheap.
I don't need your cheap sympathy.
en.notes: Pejorative: looks cheap or inferior, regardless of the price: 安っぽい服. Also used for feelings and statements: 安っぽい同情 (cheap sympathy).

examples[].german: This form is so complicated to fill in that I hardly understand it.
If you butt in, the matter will only get more complicated.
en.notes: Colloquial: ややこしい話 (a tricky matter), 話をややこしくする (to complicate matters). More neutral: 複雑な.

examples[].german: His works only became known to the world after his death.
There is no perfect person in this world.
en.notes: この世 (this world), あの世 (the afterlife), 世に出る (to become known, to come out into the public), 世の中 (the world, society). As an era: 江戸の世 (the Edo period).

en.meaning: to call out to and stop; to hail
examples[].german: Just as I left the station, a stranger stopped me.
When I was about to go home, the department head called me back.
en.notes: To make someone stop by calling out: 警官に呼び止められる (to be stopped by a police officer). Also: タクシーを呼び止める (to hail a taxi).

examples[].german: The fortune-teller's prophecy came true perfectly.
He had predicted the current recession ten years ago.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 未来を予言する (to predict the future). 予言者 (prophet). For sober forecasts, 予測 or 予想 are more usual.

examples[].german: This detergent removes grease stains well.
Stains are conspicuous on a white shirt.
en.notes: Noun of 汚れる: 汚れを落とす (to remove dirt), 汚れが目立つ (stains stand out). Read as けがれ, 汚れ (also 穢れ) means religious impurity.

examples[].german: To get that angry, something very unpleasant must have happened to him.
Unless something extraordinary happens, the meeting will be held as planned.
en.notes: The neutral standard form; よっぽど is the colloquially intensified variant. Typical: よほど〜のだろう (must be very ...), 〜よりよほど (far more ... than), よほどのこと (something extraordinary). Usually in kana (余程).

examples[].german: I've had a bad feeling since the morning.
My bad premonition came true: the trains had stopped.
en.notes: 嫌な予感がする (to have a bad premonition), 予感が当たる (a hunch turns out right). As a する-verb: 予感する.

examples[].german: He has no ambition and doesn't seem interested in getting ahead.
If I may ask for a bit more, I'd have liked a somewhat larger room.
en.notes: 欲がない (modest, unambitious), 欲が出る (to want more, to become greedy), 欲を言えば (if I may ask for more). As a suffix: 食欲 (appetite), 物欲 (materialistic desire). Homophone: よく (often, well).

examples[].german: Human desires know no limits.
I couldn't suppress the desire to eat something sweet.
en.notes: Stronger and often more negative than 欲: 欲望を抑える (to restrain one's desires), 欲望に負ける (to give in to one's desires).

examples[].german: The greedy merchant took money even from poor people.
People often say that humans are greedy creatures.
en.notes: Pejorative for people who always want more: 欲深い人. Also read よくぶかい. Similar: 貪欲 (voracious).

examples[].german: The bathroom in this apartment is spacious.
The bathroom ventilation fan broke and mold has grown.
en.notes: A room for bathing (with a tub or shower); more formal than お風呂 or 風呂場. In Japan the toilet is usually separate.

examples[].german: At the wedding reception, friends sang a song as entertainment.
At the year-end party, the new employees performed magic tricks as entertainment.
en.notes: A small performance at festivities, weddings or company parties (song, skit, magic trick): 余興を披露する (to perform an act of entertainment).

en.meaning: to read aloud; to read out
examples[].german: The teacher read out the names of those who passed, one by one.
The master of ceremonies read out the program of the ceremony.
en.notes: To read aloud loudly and clearly, often in front of an audience: 名前を読み上げる (to call out names), 原稿を読み上げる (to read out a manuscript).

examples[].german: To fall asleep without saying a word, you must have been really tired.
Cooking at home is much cheaper than eating out.
en.notes: Colloquial, emphatic form of よほど (余程): よっぽど疲れていたんだね (you must have been very tired). With comparison: 〜よりよっぽどいい (much better than ...). Mostly written in kana.

en.meaning: close to, leaning toward (suffix, e.g. 駅寄り, 左寄り); (sumo) forward push in a belt grip
examples[].german: I'd prefer a seat nearer the window.
Tomorrow, a strong wind from the north is expected.
That newspaper is criticized for having many pro-government articles.
en.notes: As a suffix, 〜寄り denotes a position close to something or a leaning in one direction: 駅寄り ("closer to the station"), 北寄りの風 ("wind from a northerly direction"), 保守寄り or 左寄り ("conservative / left-leaning"). It comes from the verb 寄る ("to approach", separate card); it has nothing to do with the comparative particle より ("than"). In sumo, 寄り denotes the forward pushing against the opponent in a belt grip (cf. 寄り切り).

en.meaning: twist, twisting (of threads); cf. よりを戻す (to get back together)
examples[].german: The two who had broken up have apparently gotten back together recently.
My mother pulled out all the stops and made a birthday feast.
This thread is loosely twisted, so it breaks as soon as you pull on it.
en.notes: The noun of 縒る "to twist, to spin"; on its own mainly in crafts and textile terminology (縒りが甘い "loosely twisted"). It is well known from the phrases よりを戻す "to get back together (with an ex)" and 腕によりをかける "to put all one's skill into it", which are mostly written in kana. Not to be confused with the comparison particle より "than".

en.meaning: good, right (classical form of 良い; e.g. 良しとする = to approve, それも良し = that is fine too)
examples[].german: All's well that ends well.
You can go alone or with friends; either is fine.
His boss did not approve of his arbitrary behavior.
en.notes: Classical adjective (ku-inflection, attributive 良き), the predecessor of 良い/よい (vocab-n5:71). Today it survives in set phrases: 良しとする "to approve, to be satisfied with", 〜も良し "... is fine too", and the proverb 終わり良ければすべて良し. Do not confuse it with the interjection よし! "good, let's go!", which is written in kana.

en.meaning: reason, means; (I hear) that ... (e.g. 知る由もない: no way of knowing)
examples[].german: There is no way to know now what he was thinking at the time.
I hear that your whole family is well as well, which is the best news.
I hear that you will be coming here next month, and I am looking forward to it.
en.notes: Elevated noun with two main uses: "means, possibility" in the fixed phrase 知る由もない ("to have no way of knowing"), and "I hear that ..." in letters: 〜の由, お元気の由 ("I hear that you are well"). Outside these patterns it is hardly used; in everyday speech 方法 or 〜そうだ is said. The Sino-Japanese reading is in 理由 and 自由.

examples[].german: Dense reeds grow along the riverbank.
In summer, people lean up reed screens to block the sunlight.
Many wild birds gather in the reed beds of Lake Biwa.
en.notes: The same plant as あし (also written 葦): because あし recalls 悪し "bad", よし "good" prevailed as a euphemistic reading. In botany and nature conservation, ヨシ in katakana is the standard name, and よし is in words such as 葦簀（よしず） "reed screen". Literary phrases like 考える葦 (Pascal), on the other hand, are read あし; the word has nothing to do with 足/脚 "leg".

en.meaning: good and bad; quality; pros and cons
examples[].german: Small children cannot yet tell right from wrong.
Too much convenience has its good and bad sides.
en.notes: 物事の善し悪し (what is good and what is bad), 善し悪しを判断する (to judge the quality). As a verdict: それも善し悪しだ (that has its pros and cons). Also written 良し悪し.

examples[].german: I looked away during class and was warned by the teacher.
Looking away while driving is a cause of accidents.
en.notes: As a する-verb: よそ見する (to look elsewhere, to not pay attention). よそ見運転 (inattentive driving). Also written 余所見.

examples[].german: You achieved outstanding results in this tournament. Therefore, this prize is awarded to you.
The plaintiff's claims have no basis. Therefore, the suit in this case is dismissed.
en.notes: Formal conjunction at the start of a sentence, typical in certificates, court rulings and proofs: よって、〜とする (therefore it is held that ...). On certificates: よってこれを賞します (hereby this prize is awarded). Not to be confused with 〜によって (by, depending on).

examples[].german: You dissolve sugar in water to make a solution.
Please do not pour the solution used in the experiment down the sink.
en.notes: Chemistry: 食塩の溶液 (salt solution), 水溶液 (aqueous solution). Verb: 溶かす (to dissolve).

examples[].german: My mother takes care of elderly people at a nursing home.
I felt unwell, so I consulted the school nurse in the infirmary.
en.notes: Mainly in fixed expressions: 児童養護施設 (children's home), 養護教諭 (teacher in charge of the school infirmary, 保健室の先生). Homophones: 擁護 (defense, advocacy), 用語 (technical term).

examples[].german: All the equipment needed for camping can be rented on site.
I bought running shoes at the sporting goods store in front of the station.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds: 事務用品 (office supplies), スポーツ用品 (sporting goods), 日用品 (daily necessities).

examples[].german: Please take the medicine according to the directions and dosage.
This word has two usages.
en.notes: 用法・用量を守る (to follow the directions and dosage, for medicine), 言葉の用法 (the usage of a word).

examples[].german: Excuse me, but what is it regarding?
I'm busy, so please just tell me what you want, briefly.
en.notes: The reason why one calls or visits someone: ご用件は何でしょうか (What can I do for you?), 用件を伝える (to state one's business). Polite with ご.

examples[].german: This university has long put effort into teacher training.
The company has started a training program to train young engineers.
en.notes: Systematic training of skilled workers: 教員養成 (teacher training), 人材を養成する (to train personnel), 養成所 (training institute). Homophones: 要請 (request), 妖精 (fairy).

en.meaning: form; blank sheet; paper (for writing or printing)
examples[].german: Please write your name and address on this form.
The printer is out of paper.
en.notes: 申込用紙 (application form), 解答用紙 (answer sheet), 原稿用紙 (manuscript paper with squares), A4の用紙 (A4 paper). Homophones: 養子 (adopted child), 要旨 (gist).

examples[].german: After the earthquake, the look of the town changed completely.
The election is turning into a fierce contest.
en.notes: Written language, mostly for situations: 〜の様相を呈する (to take on the appearance of ..., to develop into ...), 様相が一変する (the situation changes completely).

en.meaning: false advertising; all show and no substance
examples[].german: This advertisement was criticized as false advertising.
The course had a grand name, but the content was all show and no substance.
en.notes: Literally "a sheep's head (displayed), dog meat (sold)": the exterior promises more than the content delivers - for example in advertising or products. Written language.

examples[].german: In the evening, the rain eased off a little.
With age, muscle strength weakens.
en.notes: Intransitive: 風が弱まる (the wind dies down), 影響力が弱まる (influence wanes). Transitive: 弱める.

en.meaning: to weaken; to turn down; to reduce
examples[].german: Once it boils, turn down the heat and simmer thoroughly.
You take the medicine after meals to reduce its side effects.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 弱まる: 火を弱める (to turn down the heat), 力を弱める (to weaken the force). Opposite: 強める.

en.meaning: to weaken; to be at a loss
examples[].german: My grandmother's legs have become quite weak since she was hospitalized.
I forgot my wallet. What am I going to do?
en.notes: Physical: 体が弱る (to be weakened). Colloquially also: 弱ったなあ (What am I going to do?), 〜には弱る (... is a problem for one).

en.meaning: reason, cause; because of (e.g. 〜が故に, 若さゆえの過ち)
examples[].german: Mistakes born of youth are something everyone makes.
Precisely because he is honest, he often loses out.
For certain reasons, I cannot tell you the details.
en.notes: Written-language noun for "reason, cause", mostly written in kana. It follows nouns with の or verb and adjective forms: 若さゆえの過ち ("a mistake born of youthful rashness"), 〜がゆえに ("precisely because"), 故あって ("for certain reasons"). The sentence-opening conjunction 故に (ゆえに, "therefore, consequently") has its own card; in everyday speech ため or から is usually said instead of 故.

en.meaning: connection, relationship (to a place or person) (e.g. ゆかりの地, 縁もゆかりもない)
examples[].german: There are many places in Kyoto connected with The Tale of Genji.
I moved for work to a town with which I have no connection whatsoever.
Items associated with the writer are on display in the memorial hall.
en.notes: ゆかり refers to a historical or personal connection to a place or person, typical in 〜ゆかりの地 ("place associated with ...") and in the phrase 縁もゆかりもない ("to have no connection at all"), in which 縁 is read えん. The word is mostly written in kana; the spelling 縁 is otherwise read えん ("bond of fate, relationship") or ふち ("edge"), both with their own cards.

examples[].german: The players took the field in their new uniforms.
In this shop, the staff uniform changes every year.
en.notes: Mainly sports and work clothing: チームのユニフォーム (team kit). Also written ユニホーム. School or police uniforms are usually called 制服.

examples[].german: She always comes up with original ideas.
That shop is famous for its uniquely shaped building.
en.notes: In Japanese usually positive, in the sense of "original, witty, offbeat": ユニークな発想 (an original idea). Not "one of a kind" in the strict sense. な-adjective.

examples[].german: I left home with time to spare.
I'm so busy that I have no peace of mind.
en.notes: 時間にゆとりがある (to have plenty of time), 心のゆとり (inner calm), 生活のゆとり (financial leeway).

en.meaning: excellent (grade, 優・良・可); superiority; gentle, graceful (優な)
examples[].german: It is quite difficult to get an A in this class.
At this university, grades are rated on four levels: excellent, good, pass, fail.
To keep the scholarship, you need an A in more than half of your subjects.
en.notes: Mainly the top grade in the 優・良・可・不可 rating system used at universities and on older report cards: 優を取る/もらう ("to get an A"). The meaning "gentle, graceful" (優な) is literary. Do not confuse it with the adverb 優に ("easily, at least") or with 優しい (やさしい) and 優れる (すぐれる).

en.meaning: being, existence; possession (opposite of 無, e.g. 無から有を生む)
examples[].german: He is a genius who creates something out of nothing.
In philosophy, the relation between being and nothingness has been debated since ancient times.
en.notes: 有 (ゆう) is an abstract, written-language noun for "being, existence" and almost always stands in contrast to 無 (む, separate card): 無から有を生む ("to create something from nothing"). As a prefix it means "with, equipped with" (有資格者 "qualified person"), and (有) is the abbreviation for 有限会社 ("limited company"). In everyday speech existence is expressed with ある; 有 alone appears mainly in philosophy and fixed phrases.

examples[].german: In Mongolia there are still people who continue to live as nomads.
Nomads move with their livestock according to the seasons.
en.notes: 遊牧民 (nomads), 遊牧生活 (nomadic life). As a する-verb: 遊牧する (to wander as nomads).

examples[].german: He is a promising young player with a bright future.
Solar power generation is considered a promising field.
en.notes: 将来有望な (with a promising future), 有望な新人 (promising newcomer), 有望株 (rising star). な-adjective.

en.meaning: guidance; direction; leading (of people or vehicles)
examples[].german: The staff guided the spectators to the emergency exits.
At the scene of the accident, a police officer is directing the cars.
en.notes: As a する-verb: 客を出口へ誘導する (to guide guests to the exit). 誘導尋問 (leading question); in physics also induction.

examples[].german: In terms of performance, this product is superior to those of other companies.
He is always basking in a sense of superiority.
en.notes: Mainly in 優越感 (feeling of superiority; opposite: 劣等感). As a する-verb: 〜に優越する (to be superior to ...).

examples[].german: The two of us took a walk along the seashore at dusk.
In autumn, dusk comes earlier.
en.notes: More poetic than 夕方: 夕暮れ時 (at twilight). Similar: 日暮れ, 黄昏 (たそがれ).

examples[].german: In negotiations, it is important to gain the upper hand over the other side.
The home team was dominant throughout the first half.
en.notes: 優位に立つ (to gain the upper hand), 優位を保つ (to keep the lead). Homophone: 有意 (significant).

en.meaning: predominance; superiority; to have the advantage
examples[].german: In the opinion polls, the opposition is ahead.
The opposing team had the upper hand in the first half, but we turned the game around in the second.
en.notes: 優勢な (dominant), 優勢になる / 優勢に立つ (to gain the upper hand). Opposite: 劣勢 (inferiority).

en.meaning: to have; to possess; to be endowed with
examples[].german: All citizens equally have the right to receive an education.
This company has five factories in Japan.
en.notes: Very formal (laws, contracts, news): 権利を有する (to have a right), 資格を有する者 (persons with the relevant qualification). In everyday speech: 持つ, ある.

examples[].german: Three writers took part in the magazine's round-table discussion.
We invited international students and held a round-table discussion.
en.notes: An informal discussion among several people on a topic, often for magazines or events.

examples[].german: He made his fortune in trade.
My grandfather built a fortune in a single generation.
en.notes: Wealth, especially in 財を成す / 財を築く (to make a fortune). In compounds also "goods": 文化財 (cultural property).

examples[].german: A cute general goods shop has opened in front of the station.
This store sells everything from food to sundries.
en.notes: Various everyday items; 雑貨屋 are nowadays often shops for decor and design goods.

examples[].german: I checked my account balance in the bank's app.
The card balance was insufficient, and I couldn't get through the ticket gate.
en.notes: The remaining amount in an account or on a card: 口座の残高, 残高不足 (insufficient balance).

examples[].german: I've paid the deposit, so I'll pay the remaining balance next month.
When I counted my leftover money at the end of the trip, there was only 3,000 yen.
en.notes: Money left over or still to be paid: 残金を払う (to pay the balance). An account balance is more often called 残高.

examples[].german: His work is fast, but sloppy.
The handwriting is so sloppy that I cannot read what it says.
en.notes: な-adjective: done without care: 仕事が雑だ, 雑な字. As a prefix 雑〜 it means "miscellaneous, various" (雑貨, 雑談).

examples[].german: Brushwood was growing thick on the vacant lot.
During the winter, we cut the trees on the hill behind the house and made firewood from them.
Assorted other trees are growing mixed in with the cedar plantation.
en.notes: A rarer alternative reading of 雑木 with the same meaning as the card 雑木/ぞうき: mixed small trees and bushes of little economic value. ぞうき is usual, especially in fixed combinations such as 雑木林/ぞうきばやし; ざつぼく is heard only occasionally. When in doubt, use ぞうき, but be able to recognize ざつぼく when you hear it.

examples[].german: We chatted a little before the meeting.
Please stop chatting during class.
en.notes: A casual conversation without a set topic; as a verb 雑談する.

examples[].german: I submitted my tax return documents to the tax office.
I got a call from the tax office and felt a little nervous.
en.notes: The local tax authority; this is where one files, for example, the tax return (確定申告).

examples[].german: Two months after the surgery, my father recovered completely.
It looks like it will still take time until full recovery.
en.notes: 〜する: to become fully healthy again. Read the same as 前回 (last time) and 全開 (fully open, full throttle).

examples[].german: The heavy rain wiped out all the vegetables in the field.
Every company I applied to rejected me; I couldn't get a job offer from anywhere.
en.notes: 〜する: to be completely wiped out (troops, crops). Colloquially also: everything fails (試験は全滅だった, "I failed every exam").

examples[].german: Fraud targeting honest citizens is increasing.
He is a decent person who would never deceive anyone.
en.notes: な-adjective, formal: 善良な市民 (law-abiding citizens), 善良な人 (a decent person).

examples[].german: In the Edo period, this port town reached the height of its prosperity through trade.
In his heyday he was the best player in the world.
en.notes: The time of greatest success: 全盛期 (heyday), 全盛を極める (to be at the peak).

examples[].german: I look forward to the achievements of the young people who have a future ahead of them.
Many difficulties await this plan in the future.
en.notes: Formal: 前途有望 (promising), 前途多難 (many difficulties ahead), 前途ある若者 (young people with a future).

examples[].german: I made orange jelly for dessert.
Even when I have no appetite because of a cold, jelly is easy to eat.
en.notes: A sweet dish made from gelatin or agar (フルーツゼリー); also gel-like substances (ゼリー状).

examples[].german: I took a walk along the riverside road.
Small shops are lined up along the railway tracks.
en.notes: Suffix after nouns for rivers, roads, coasts etc.; read ぞい: 川沿い (along the river), 線路沿い (along the railway line), 海沿い (along the coast). Verb: 沿う (to run along).

examples[].german: The lion is an animal of the genus Panthera in the cat family.
In classification, below the family comes the genus, and below the genus the species.
en.notes: Technical term of biological classification for the genus, which stands between 科 "family" and 種 "species"; usually a suffix after the genus name (ヒョウ属, バラ属). The verb 属する "to belong to" uses the same kanji and is often used together with it (ヒョウ属に属する). Rare outside biology and technical texts.

examples[].german: You must not talk to customers so roughly.
Please don't handle borrowed books carelessly.
en.notes: な-adjective: ぞんざいな言葉遣い; adverbially ぞんざいに扱う "to treat carelessly". It criticizes a lack of care or respect; not an onomatopoeic word.

examples[].german: A famous statue of a dog stands in front of the station.
A statue of the person who founded the town has been erected in the park.
en.notes: Sculpture: 銅像 (bronze statue), 仏像 (Buddha statue). Also a mental image as a suffix: 理想像 (ideal image), 人物像 (portrait of a person). Read the same as 象 (elephant).

en.meaning: assorted small trees, brushwood; trees used for timber and firewood
examples[].german: Dense brushwood of mixed trees grows thick behind the house.
In autumn, the mixed trees on the mountain turn red and yellow.
In the past, people cut the trees around here and made firewood from them.
en.notes: Collective term for a motley mix of trees of little economic value that used to serve as firewood; rarely also read ざつぼく. Far more common is the compound 雑木林/ぞうきばやし "mixed woodland, coppice". Do not confuse it with the homophone 臓器 "organ".

examples[].german: The government decided to strengthen its defense forces.
The factory expanded its production facilities.
en.notes: Strengthening or expanding forces, personnel or capacity: 戦力の増強, 人員を増強する. As a verb 増強する.

examples[].german: Moderate exercise stimulates the appetite.
The city is putting great effort into promoting its citizens' health.
en.notes: Increase of health, appetite or capability: 食欲増進, 健康の増進. As a verb 増進する.

examples[].german: The finance minister announced the draft budget for the coming fiscal year.
My grandfather remembers well the names of the postwar finance ministers.
en.notes: Short for 大蔵大臣, the finance minister before the ministry reform of 2001; today the post is called 財務大臣 (short: 財務相).

en.meaning: bluntly; straight to the point; exactly
examples[].german: He pointed out the problem bluntly.
She guessed my age exactly.
en.notes: To say something without mincing words or to hit the mark exactly: ずばり言う, ずばり当てる. Often with と: ずばりと指摘する.

examples[].german: I got soaked in a sudden rain.
A drenched dog was sitting at the entrance.
en.notes: Mostly ずぶ濡れになる (to get soaked) or ずぶ濡れの + noun. Similar: びしょ濡れ.

en.meaning: in a long row; lined up
examples[].german: Customers are lined up in a long row in front of the shop.
Old dictionaries were lined up in a row on the bookshelf.
en.notes: Colloquial variant of ずらりと: many things or people side by side, mostly with 並ぶ.

examples[].german: The earthquake caused a gap between the wall and the pillar.
There is a big gap between their ways of thinking.
en.notes: Noun form of ずれる: 時間のずれ (time lag), 意見のずれ (difference of opinion), 認識のずれ (difference in perception).

en.meaning: dragging, trailing; sliding gradually; dragging on endlessly without a decision; slurping; limp, indecisive
examples[].german: I walked to the station dragging the heavy suitcase behind me.
I kept putting off my reply.
My father slurped his soba noodles.
en.notes: Onomatopoeic adverb, mostly with と or directly before the verb: ずるずる引きずる "to drag along", ずるずる滑り落ちる "to slide down slowly", ずるずる延びる "to drag on endlessly". Figuratively it describes a state that drags on without a clear decision (ずるずるとした関係), and also the slurping of noodles. In manga and advertising often in katakana ズルズル.

examples[].german: A new government has taken office.
As a result of the election, there was a change of government for the first time in ten years.
That party held power for a long time.
en.notes: 政権 is governmental power or the sitting government as a political entity, often named after the head of government: 〇〇政権 ("the 〇〇 administration"). Typical collocations: 政権を握る ("to come to power"), 政権交代 ("change of government"), 長期政権, 新政権が発足する. 政府, by contrast, refers to the government as a state institution; people say 政府の発表, but 政権が倒れる. Typical news vocabulary.

examples[].german: He formed a new political party.
Which political party do you support?
She doesn't belong to any political party.
en.notes: 政党 is the general term for a political party. Specific party names usually end in 党 (自民党, 共産党), and in the news often just 党 is said. Typical: 政党を結成する ("to found"), 政党に所属する ("to belong to"), 支持する政党 ("the party one supports"), 政党政治. Do not confuse it with 正当 ("justified") or 正統, which sound the same.

examples[].german: The two got engaged last month.
I received an engagement ring from him on my birthday.
After talking it over, the two decided to break off their engagement.
en.notes: 婚約 is "engagement"; as an intransitive する-verb, 〜と婚約する means "to get engaged to someone". Common compounds: 婚約者 ("fiance(e)"), 婚約指輪 ("engagement ring"), 婚約発表. Breaking off an engagement is 婚約を解消する (by mutual agreement) or 婚約を破棄する (unilaterally). Neutral to slightly formal.

examples[].german: I noticed the mistake and corrected it right away.
After getting off the train, I realized I had forgotten my umbrella.
I got a haircut, but he didn't notice at all.
en.notes: 気付く (nowadays mostly written 気づく) means "to notice, become aware, realize" and is intransitive: what is noticed takes に - ミスに気づく, 彼の変化に気づく; a whole clause is attached with 〜ことに or 〜と. Unlike 分かる, 気づく stresses the moment when something strikes you; the literary 認識する means a conscious, factual grasp. Equivalent and very common is 気がつく, which can also mean "to come to."

en.meaning: to like; to take a liking to
examples[].german: I like my new apartment very much.
I like both the color and the design of this bag, so I'll buy it.
I hope you'll like your birthday present.
en.notes: 気に入る means "to please, to find pleasing." The thing liked takes が (この店が気に入った) or, equally common, を (この店を気に入った). For a lasting state, use 気に入っている: "to be fond of something." In contrast to 好き, it stresses that something appeals to you when you get to know or try it. Derived from it are お気に入り ("favorite") and 気に入らない ("not to suit, to displease"), also toward people: あの人の態度が気に入らない.

en.meaning: to recognize; to be aware of
examples[].german: It is necessary to recognize the seriousness of the problem.
I plugged the USB stick into the computer, but it was not recognized.
As for that matter, I understand it the same way.
en.notes: 認識する means "to recognize, be aware of, grasp" and is a rather literary, factual word: 問題の重要性を認識する, 〜と認識している ("to understand it as, to assume"). In companies and news you often hear 認識が甘い ("to underestimate something") or 認識の違い ("difference in understanding"). In technology it means "to recognize" in the sense of recognition: 顔認識, 音声認識, USBが認識されない. For everyday "to notice", one rather says 気づく.

en.meaning: to be aware of; to realize
examples[].german: You must be aware of your responsibility.
I didn't feel tired myself, but the doctor told me to rest.
Since he realized he is the team leader, his behavior has changed.
en.notes: 自覚する means to "be aware of" or "become aware of" one's own situation, role, weakness or responsibility: 責任を自覚する, 自分の弱点を自覚している. The object almost always concerns oneself, which distinguishes it from 認識する, which also grasps external facts. In medicine, 自覚症状 stands for "subjectively felt symptoms": 自覚症状がない. The counterpart 無自覚 means "without noticing it oneself, unconscious".

en.meaning: to be conscious of; to be aware of
examples[].german: I try to eat in a way that is mindful of my health.
When the person I like sits next to me, I can't help being self-conscious and can't talk.
When you give your presentation, please be conscious of speaking slowly.
en.notes: 意識する means "to be aware of something, to pay conscious attention to something" and also "to keep thinking about someone." With を: 健康を意識する, 周りの目を意識する ("to worry about what others think"). Very common is 〜を意識した ("geared toward ..."): 若者を意識した商品. Regarding people, it often hints at rivalry or romantic interest: 彼のことを意識してしまう. The noun 意識 also means "consciousness" (意識を失う "to lose consciousness").

en.meaning: to be prepared (for the worst); to resign oneself
examples[].german: I decided to take on the challenge, prepared for the difficulties.
Prepared to be scolded, I told the department head the truth.
You should be prepared for a lot of overtime in this job.
en.notes: 覚悟する means to brace oneself inwardly for something unpleasant or to knowingly accept it: 失敗を覚悟する, 反対されるのは覚悟の上だ ("I had expected that"). Also typical is 〜を覚悟で ("at the risk of ..."). Unlike 決心する and 決意する ("to resolve"), it is less about the decision itself than about the readiness to bear the consequences. As a threat or in jest: 覚悟しろ! ("Prepare yourself!").

en.meaning: to resolve; to make up one's mind
examples[].german: I resolved to study abroad.
The player decided to retire because of his injury.
For the new year, I resolved to keep a diary every day.
en.notes: 決意する means to "make a firm decision", often one that has matured over time: 〜ことを決意する, 〜と決意する. It sounds more serious and solemn than 決心する and likes to appear in speeches, news and narratives, e.g. 引退を決意する ("to decide to retire"). The noun occurs in phrases such as 固い決意 ("firm resolve") and 決意を新たにする ("to renew one's resolve"). For small everyday decisions, one simply says 決める.

en.meaning: to make up one's mind; to resolve
examples[].german: I've made up my mind to change jobs.
I decided to quit smoking for my health.
I want to propose to her, but I just can't make up my mind.
en.notes: 決心する means "to resolve, make a decision," mostly after some hesitation: 〜ことを決心する, 〜と決心する. Very typical is 決心がつく ("to finally come to a decision") and 決心がつかない ("cannot bring oneself to decide"). Compared with 決意する, it is somewhat more everyday and stresses the inner decision process; 決める is the neutral base word for "to decide, set."

examples[].german: It is difficult to memorize a large amount of information accurately.
I remember that day clearly.
This app remembers the address you entered last time.
en.notes: 記憶する means "to commit to memory, retain in memory" and sounds more factual than 覚える. As a verb it often appears in sober or technical contexts (データを記憶する "to store data"); in everyday speech the noun is more common: 記憶がある/ない ("to remember / have no memory of"), 記憶に残る ("to stay in memory"), 記憶力 ("memory"). For deliberate rote learning, people more often say 暗記する, and for "to recall," 思い出す.

en.meaning: to memorize; to learn by heart
examples[].german: I'm bad at memorizing historical dates.
I memorized the whole script of my speech, so I could talk without looking at the paper.
The day before the exam, I memorized a hundred words.
en.notes: 暗記する means "to learn by heart," i.e. to commit something to memory word for word: 単語を暗記する, 公式を暗記する. It is a typical school and exam word; 丸暗記 means "to memorize mechanically without understanding." Unlike 覚える ("to remember, learn"), 暗記 stresses literal memorizing, and compared with 記憶する the learning process is in the foreground. A common aid is the 暗記カード ("flashcard").

examples[].german: Rain is forecast for tomorrow.
The test was harder than expected.
Let's all guess which team will win.
en.notes: 予想する means "to predict, to expect, to guess"; you estimate how something will turn out: 試合の結果を予想する, 〜と予想される. Very common are 予想通り ("as expected"), 予想外 ("unexpected") and 予想以上に ("more than expected").
