en.notes: 反射する means "to reflect, throw back" and is used mainly for light, sound and heat. Transitive: 鏡が光を反射する; intransitive: 光が水面に反射する "the light is reflected on the water surface". In biology 反射 is a "reflex"; 反射的に means "reflexively, involuntarily". For the mirror image itself, one says 映る/映す, not 反射する.

en.meaning: to play (an instrument); to make (music) sound
examples[].german: She played a beautiful piece on the piano.
In the forest, the birds were making beautiful harmonies.
The audience listened intently to the tone of the old violin.
en.notes: 奏でる is an elevated, literary verb for "to play an instrument, to let music sound"; the piece takes を, the instrument takes で (ギターで曲を奏でる). In daily life one simply says 弾く (piano, guitar), 吹く (flute) or 演奏する. 奏でる stresses the beautiful sound and is often used figuratively, e.g. when birds or the wind "play" melodies.

examples[].german: I smelled the flowers.
The dog is sniffing at the ground.
I smelled the milk to check whether it had gone bad.
en.notes: 嗅ぐ is transitive: actively "to smell, to sniff at something", mostly with 匂い/におい as object: 匂いを嗅ぐ. This differs from におう (匂う/臭う), where the thing itself "smells, is fragrant or stinks" (このシャツはにおう). Figuratively 嗅ぎつける means "to get wind of something". Since the kanji is rare, the verb is often written in kana as かぐ.

en.meaning: to carry on one's back; to shoulder (a burden)
examples[].german: I climbed the mountain carrying a heavy rucksack on my back.
My father failed in his business and took on a large debt.
He entered the match carrying the hopes of all Japan.
en.notes: 背負う is transitive: to carry something or someone on the back with を (リュックを背負う, 子供を背負う); colloquially there is also the reading しょう (しょって). Figuratively it means "to take a burden or responsibility upon oneself": 借金を背負う, 責任を背負う, 期待を背負う. Carrying on the shoulder, by contrast, is 担ぐ; giving a child a piggyback ride is also おんぶする.

examples[].german: I carried the portable shrine at the festival.
He carried a heavy bag of rice on his shoulder.
The day before the entrance exam, I ate katsudon for good luck.
en.notes: 担ぐ is transitive: to carry something on the shoulder with を (荷物を肩に担ぐ, 神輿を担ぐ). There are also fixed figurative meanings: 縁起を担ぐ "to be superstitious, to pay attention to good omens", 人を担ぐ "to pull someone's leg" and "to put someone up as a candidate". Unlike 背負う (on the back), with 担ぐ the load rests on the shoulder. The kanji 担 is also known from 担当.

examples[].german: The suspect was formally indicted.
The man was indicted on a charge of fraud.
Due to insufficient evidence, he was not prosecuted.
en.notes: 起訴 is the bringing of charges by the public prosecutor's office (検察) before a criminal court. It usually appears in the passive: 〜の罪で起訴される "to be indicted for ..."; the opposite is 不起訴 "no indictment, dropping of the case". Do not confuse it with 告訴 (complaint by the victim) and the general 訴える "to sue". A word of news and judicial language.

en.meaning: to lean against; to depend on
examples[].german: I was tired and leaned against the wall.
Please do not lean against the train doors.
Stop leaning on your parents forever and work for yourself.
en.notes: 寄りかかる is intransitive: what one leans on takes に (壁に寄りかかる, ドアに寄りかかる); also written 寄り掛かる. Figuratively it means "to rely on someone, depend on someone", often critically: 親に寄りかかって生活する. Similar is もたれる, which also means "to lean against" but in addition "to sit heavily on the stomach" (胃がもたれる).

examples[].german: He knelt before her and proposed.
The woman knelt in the church and prayed quietly.
The knight knelt before the king.
en.notes: 跪く means "to kneel down", mostly as a sign of reverence, submission, or when proposing marriage. It is intransitive; the person before whom one kneels takes の前で or の前に. The kanji is rare, so it is mostly written in kana as ひざまずく. For mere kneeling in daily life (e.g. while cleaning), ひざをつく is more usual; formal sitting on the knees is 正座する.

examples[].german: We harvest rice in autumn.
On the weekend, the family harvested the tomatoes in the field.
I was able to learn a lot at this seminar, so it was a great gain.
en.notes: 収穫する means "to harvest" (米を収穫する, 野菜を収穫する); in everyday speech, for fruit and vegetables people also say 採る, for rice 刈り取る. The noun 収穫 also denotes the harvest itself (今年の収穫, 収穫量). Very common is the figurative use "yield, gain" from an experience: 今回の旅行は大きな収穫があった. In this sense 収穫 is mostly used as a noun with がある.

en.meaning: to tailor; to make up; to turn into
examples[].german: The tailor made a suit.
My mother had a kimono made for me for my Coming-of-Age ceremony.
The incident was later made into a movie.
en.notes: 仕立てる is transitive and means above all "to tailor, make (clothing)": スーツを仕立てる; when having it made, one says 仕立ててもらう. The noun 仕立て is found in 仕立て屋 "tailor's shop". Figuratively it means "to turn into something" (小説をドラマに仕立てる) or, pejoratively, "to cast someone as something" (犯人に仕立てる, strengthened as 仕立て上げる). Simple sewing is 縫う.

examples[].german: As soon as I got home, I changed into my loungewear.
I had sweated, so I changed my shirt.
The players are changing into their uniforms in the locker room.
en.notes: 着替える means "to change clothes"; the new clothing takes に (パジャマに着替える), and the garment being changed can take を (シャツを着替える). Besides きがえる, the reading きかえる is also common. The noun 着替え means "changing clothes" and also "a change of clothes" (着替えを持っていく). Not to be confused with 着る "to put on" and 脱ぐ "to take off".

en.meaning: to wear; to be clad in
examples[].german: She was wearing a beautiful dress.
That actor has a somewhat lonely air about him.
The mountain donned white snow and changed into its winter appearance.
en.notes: 纏う is an elevated, rather literary verb for "to wear, to wrap oneself in": ドレスを纏う, 鎧を纏う; it is mostly written in kana as まとう. The figurative use for an aura or mood is common: 不思議な雰囲気をまとう. For clothing in daily life one simply says 着る; 纏う sounds poetic and is found in novels or advertising copy. Related is まとわりつく "to cling to someone, to stick to".

examples[].german: I decorated the Christmas tree.
I have family photos displayed in my room.
He is unpretentious and quickly becomes friends with anyone.
en.notes: 飾る means "to decorate, to adorn" (ツリーを飾る, 部屋を花で飾る) and likewise "to put up or hang as decoration": 写真を飾る, 絵を壁に飾る, 玄関に花を飾る. Merely putting something somewhere without a decorative purpose is 置く. The noun 飾り is "decoration", and 飾らない人 figuratively describes a natural, unpretentious person.

examples[].german: I carved a beautiful pattern into the wood.
I had both our names engraved on the inside of our wedding rings.
This Buddhist statue is said to have been carved from a single piece of wood.
en.notes: 彫る is transitive: "to carve, to engrave, to chisel" in wood, stone or metal. The material takes に (木に模様を彫る), the result takes を (仏像を彫る, 名前を彫る). Colloquially, getting a tattoo is also 彫る (タトゥーを彫る). Do not confuse it with the identically read 掘る "to dig" (穴を掘る). Related nouns are 彫刻 "sculpture" and 木彫り "wood carving".

en.meaning: to shave; to sharpen; to cut back; to delete
examples[].german: I sharpened the pencil with a knife.
Because of the recession, the company slashed its advertising budget.
Before the exam, I cut into my sleeping time to study.
en.notes: 削る is transitive: to remove material in thin layers - "to plane, to scrape, to sharpen": 鉛筆を削る, 木を削る, かつお節を削る. The figurative meaning "to cut back, to economize" is very common: 予算を削る, 人件費を削る, 睡眠時間を削る. It also means "to strike out, to remove" in texts: 不要な部分を削る. The related 削除する "to delete" is more formal and is used above all for data and text.

en.meaning: to sharpen; to whet; to wash (rice)
examples[].german: I sharpened the kitchen knife on a whetstone.
Please wash the rice about three times before cooking it.
The cat is sharpening its claws on a pillar.
en.notes: 研ぐ is transitive: to "grind, sharpen" blades on a whetstone (包丁を研ぐ, 刀を研ぐ). In the kitchen, 米を研ぐ means "to wash rice" by rubbing it in water - a very common use. Figuratively it appears in 爪を研ぐ "to sharpen one's claws", i.e. to lie in wait for a chance. For polishing surfaces or brushing teeth, one says 磨く, not 研ぐ.

examples[].german: The witness's testimony became the key to the trial.
The eyewitness testified that the culprit was a tall man.
We are preserving the testimonies of people who experienced the war.
en.notes: 証言 is a witness statement, i.e. what someone attests about something experienced or seen firsthand - in court (法廷で証言する) or in a wider sense, such as accounts of eyewitnesses to history (被爆者の証言). As a する-verb: 〜と証言する "to testify that ...". The person testifying is the 証人. Statements by suspects during interrogation, on the other hand, are called 供述.

en.meaning: to train; to strengthen; to forge
examples[].german: I work out my body at the gym every day.
When I was a newcomer, I was trained hard by a strict senior.
The craftsman forges a sword by hammering heated iron.
en.notes: 鍛える is transitive: originally "to forge, harden" metal (刀を鍛える), today mostly "to train, toughen": 体を鍛える, 筋肉を鍛える, 精神を鍛える. People can also be 鍛える - "to train hard, drill": 新人を鍛える, passive 厳しく鍛えられる. Unlike 練習する or トレーニングする, 鍛える stresses becoming stronger in the long term through effort.

examples[].german: The craftsman cast metal and made a Buddhist statue.
The bell of this temple was cast here in town during the Edo period.
People in ancient times poured molten copper into molds and cast coins.
en.notes: 鋳る is transitive and means "to cast (metal)", i.e. to pour molten metal into a mold: 鐘を鋳る, 貨幣を鋳る. The verb is rare today and sounds archaic; modern speech uses 鋳造する or paraphrases with 型に流し込む. Compounds are more common, such as 鋳型 "casting mold" and 鋳物 "cast goods". Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding いる "to be/to need" or 射る "to shoot (an arrow)".

examples[].german: Steel plates were welded together.
My older brother works in a factory welding car parts.
When welding, be sure to wear protective goggles.
en.notes: 溶接する means "to weld", i.e. to join metal parts by heat; the workpiece takes を, the counterpart takes に or と (パイプを板に溶接する). The noun 溶接 appears in 溶接工 "welder" and 溶接機 "welding machine". To be distinguished are はんだ付け "soldering" and 接着する "to glue". It is a technical term from industry and trades and rather rare in daily life.

en.meaning: to fix; to fasten; to immobilize
examples[].german: I fixed the shelf to the wall with screws.
When shooting night views, it is better to fix the camera on a tripod.
My broken arm was immobilized with a cast.
en.notes: 固定する is transitive: to "fasten, fix" something with を at a place; the place takes に, the means takes で (棚をネジで壁に固定する). The resulting state is expressed with 〜が固定されている. Figuratively 固定 means "fixed, unchanging": 固定給 "fixed salary", 固定電話 "landline phone", 固定観念 "preconceived notion". In everyday speech, for simple fastening, 留める is also used.

examples[].german: I measured the temperature of the room.
It seemed like I had a fever, so I took my temperature.
I timed the 100-meter dash with a stopwatch.
en.notes: はかる "to measure" has different kanji depending on what is measured: 測る for length, height, depth, temperature or blood pressure (身長を測る, 体温を測る), 計る for time and countable things (時間を計る, タイムを計る), 量る for weight and volume (体重を量る). In everyday writing 測る and 計る are often mixed up; when in doubt, write はかる in kana. The verb is transitive with を and has no intransitive counterpart. Not to be confused with 図る "to aim at, plan."

examples[].german: I measured out the sugar for cooking.
I had my package weighed at the post office.
Please measure 200 milliliters of water with the measuring cup.
en.notes: 量る is transitive: weight or quantity "to weigh, measure out" (砂糖を量る, 体重を量る). The identically read はかる verbs divide up like this: 量る for weight and volume, 測る for length, height, depth and temperature, 計る for time and numbers, 図る for "to plan, aim at." For body weight, both 量る and 測る are common. In the sense of "to estimate, gauge," the compound 推し量る is usually used.

examples[].german: I calculated the total amount with a calculator.
I left home early, factoring in the time for traffic jams.
Her tears were all a calculated act.
en.notes: 計算する is transitive: to "calculate, work out" something with を (合計を計算する, 費用を計算する). Set phrases are 計算に入れる "to factor in, take into account" and 計算が合う "the numbers add up." Said of people, 計算された and 計算高い mean "calculating, scheming" (negative). In math class, 計算 is calculating in general, e.g. 計算問題; mental arithmetic is 暗算.

examples[].german: The annual sales were calculated.
I roughly worked out how much the move would cost.
By what method was this figure calculated?
en.notes: 算出する means "to calculate, to work out", i.e. to determine a value or amount by calculation; transitive with を: 費用を算出する, 平均値を算出する. It sounds factual and formal (reports, statistics, business); in daily life 計算する is enough. 計算 stresses the process of calculating, 算出 the result worked out. Note: the identically read 産出 "production, output" (of raw materials) is a different word.

examples[].german: I had the repair costs estimated.
Even at a conservative estimate, it will take at least three months to finish.
Before the move, I asked three companies for quotes.
en.notes: 見積もる is transitive: to "estimate, to assess" costs, time or quantities with を (費用を見積もる). Common is the noun 見積もり (also 見積り) "cost estimate": 見積もりを取る, 見積書. The phrase 少なく見積もっても means "at a conservative estimate, at least". Unlike 推測する (to guess), it concerns concrete figures; 評価する means "to evaluate".

examples[].german: I inferred the cause from the situation.
I could tell the exam result from his expression.
Please don't speak based on mere guesses.
en.notes: 推測する is transitive: to "guess, infer" something from available clues; the basis takes から (表情から気持ちを推測する). Often with a quotation: 〜と推測する, in a factual-formal style 〜と推測される. 推測で物を言う means "to talk off the cuff". Similar are 推定する (more technical, e.g. 推定年齢), 予想する (about the future) and 想像する (free imagination).

examples[].german: There was a contradiction in the suspect's statement.
The suspect is stating that he "was in financial trouble."
He changed his statement partway through the interrogation.
en.notes: 供述 is the statement that a suspect, defendant or also a witness gives on record to the police, public prosecutor or court. Typical in the news: 容疑者は「…」と供述している, 供述を変える, 供述調書 "interrogation record". A confession in the narrower sense is 自白 - a 供述 can also be a denial. 証言, by contrast, is a witness's statement about what was observed.

examples[].german: I calculate by assuming certain conditions.
Let's suppose we won a hundred million yen in the lottery.
I can't answer hypothetical questions.
en.notes: 仮定する means "to assume, to presuppose" in the sense of a hypothetical assumption, typically with a quotation: 〜と仮定する "assuming that ...". The noun 仮定 means "assumption, hypothesis": 仮定の話 "a purely hypothetical question". In school grammar, 仮定形 is the conditional form (〜ば). To be distinguished are 想定する "to anticipate, to assume a scenario" and 推測する "to guess".

examples[].german: We will verify the results of the experiment.
Experts are examining the cause of the accident in detail.
On the program, we tested whether that rumor is true.
en.notes: 検証する is transitive: to systematically "verify, to check" a claim, result or cause with を (仮説を検証する, データを検証する). It sounds factual and formal and is typical of science, media and government offices; 現場検証 is a police "examination of the scene". For simple checks in daily life one rather says 確認する or チェックする; 点検する refers to technical inspections.

examples[].german: We verify a person's identity by checking against the database.
The accounting clerk cross-checked the receipts against the books.
The police compared the fingerprints left at the scene with the suspect's.
en.notes: 照合する is transitive: to compare two things in order to establish a match; the object of comparison takes と (領収書と帳簿を照合する, データベースと照合する). Typical for administration, the police and bookkeeping: 指紋を照合する, 本人照合. In everyday speech people rather say 確かめる or 比べる; 照合 sounds official and technical.

examples[].german: The car is inspected regularly.
Before the mountain climb, I checked my equipment once more.
The elevator is currently under inspection and cannot be used.
en.notes: 点検する is transitive: to "check, inspect" equipment, vehicles or facilities with を point by point (車を点検する, ガス設備を点検する). Common are 定期点検 "regular inspection" and 点検中 "out of service for maintenance". Unlike 検査 (examination, test, also medical) and 確認 (checking in general), 点検 is about function and safety.

examples[].german: I corrected the errors in the report.
Let's revise the plan a little to fit the change in the situation.
The app's bug is scheduled to be fixed in the next update.
en.notes: 修正する is transitive: to "correct, improve, adjust" errors or defects with を (誤りを修正する, 計画を修正する). Unlike 訂正する (correcting false statements), 修正 also covers adjustments and revisions without an actual error, such as 予算を修正する or photo editing (写真を修正する). In everyday speech people often simply say 直す.

examples[].german: I corrected the mistakes in the article.
There was an error in my previous statement, so I would like to correct it.
I wrote a wrong number in the document, so I crossed it out with a double line and corrected it.
en.notes: 訂正する is transitive: to "correct, set right" wrong statements in speech or writing (誤りを訂正する, 発言を訂正する). Typical for newspapers (訂正記事), forms (訂正印 "correction stamp") and public statements. Unlike 修正する, it is always about something wrong being replaced with the right thing. Politely one says: 訂正させていただきます.

examples[].german: The teacher corrected the student's composition.
I had a senior student go over and improve my job-hunting entry sheet.
I write a diary in Japanese and have it corrected online.
en.notes: 添削する means to "correct, improve" other people's texts by adding (添) and deleting (削), typically done by teachers: 作文を添削する, 履歴書を添削してもらう. Unlike 校正 (proofreading for typos and sentence errors), it concerns content, expression and style, often with comments. Well known is 通信添削 "correspondence course with corrections sent back". One corrects one's own mistakes rather with 直す or 修正する.

examples[].german: The manuscript is proofread before printing.
I have a part-time job at a publisher proofreading magazine articles.
To measure accurately, the machine must be calibrated regularly.
en.notes: 校正する means "to proofread": to compare printer's proofs with the manuscript and correct typos or sentence errors (原稿を校正する, ゲラを校正する). It belongs to publishing and printing; a proofreader is a 校正者. In technology 校正 also means "to calibrate" (計器を校正する). Unlike 添削, it is not about style or content but about formal errors.

examples[].german: I edited the video before publishing it.
She edits a women's magazine.
This file is read-only, so it can't be edited.
en.notes: 編集する is transitive: to "edit, to revise, to compile" texts, books, films or data with を (雑誌を編集する, 動画を編集する). Job titles are 編集者 "editor", 編集長 "editor-in-chief" and 編集部 "editorial department". On a computer, 編集 appears as the menu item "Edit". Unlike 修正 (fixing errors), it is about shaping and putting together content.

examples[].german: I deleted the unnecessary files.
I removed the names of members who had left from the roster.
Inappropriate comments were deleted by the administrator.
en.notes: 削除する is transitive: to "delete, to strike out" data, passages of text or names with を (ファイルを削除する, 名簿から名前を削除する). It is more formal than 消す and typical of computers, contracts and legal texts. Related is 削る, which besides "to plane" also means "to cut back, to strike out". The opposite is 追加する "to add".

examples[].german: A not-guilty verdict was handed down to the defendant.
Twenty years later, new evidence proved his innocence.
Having been found not guilty at trial, she finally returned to her family.
en.notes: 無罪 is the opposite of 有罪: "not guilty" or "acquittal". Typical phrases: 無罪を主張する "to plead not guilty, to assert one's innocence", 無罪判決 "acquittal", 無罪になる "to be acquitted", 無罪が証明される. For innocence in a general, moral sense, people more often say 潔白 or 罪のない (罪のない人々 "innocent people").

examples[].german: I inserted an image into the document.
Please insert your card into the ATM and enter your PIN.
The insert song of this movie became very popular.
en.notes: 挿入する is transitive: to "insert, to put in" something with を into something else (に) (文書に画像を挿入する, カードを挿入する). It sounds formal to technical and appears with machines, software or medical instruments. In daily life one mostly says 入れる or 差し込む. A well-known derived word is 挿入歌 "a song used within a film or series".

examples[].german: Necessary information is extracted from the data.
This machine slowly extracts coffee from the beans.
We conducted a survey of a thousand people randomly selected from across the country.
en.notes: 抽出する is transitive: to "draw out, to extract" something from a set with を; the source takes から (データから情報を抽出する). In chemistry and cooking it refers to extracting substances (コーヒーを抽出する). In statistics, 無作為に抽出する means "to select at random" (sampling). It is a formal technical word; in daily life one rather says 取り出す or 選ぶ.

examples[].german: Items of good quality are selected.
The harvested mandarins are sorted by size and packed in boxes.
In the factory, a machine automatically sorts out defective products.
en.notes: 選別する is transitive: to "sort, to screen" a set according to certain criteria (大きさで選別する, 不良品を選別する). It is about classifying by quality, size or suitability - both picking out the good pieces and sorting out the bad ones. Garbage, by contrast, is separated with 分別する (ぶんべつ). 選ぶ is the general "to choose"; 選別 sounds factual and, applied to people, slightly derogatory (応募者を選別する "to weed out applicants").

examples[].german: Important documents are kept in the safe.
Lost items are kept at the station office for a week.
Please store this medicine in a cool place away from direct sunlight.
en.notes: 保管する is transitive: to keep objects (を) safely; the place takes に or で (金庫に保管する, 涼しい場所で保管する). It stresses care and responsibility, e.g. for lost property, documents or other people's belongings. Unlike 保存する (to preserve, conserve, save), it is about safe custody in one place; in everyday speech people often say しまう or 取っておく.

en.meaning: to save; to preserve; to store
examples[].german: I saved the file on my computer.
If you freeze curry, you can keep it for about a month.
In this town, the old townscape of the Edo period is carefully preserved.
en.notes: 保存する is transitive: to "preserve, conserve" something with を in good condition over a long time - food (冷凍して保存する), buildings and cultural assets (町並みを保存する). On the computer it means "to save" (ファイルを保存する, 上書き保存 "overwrite and save"). Related are 保存食 "preserved food" and 保存料 "preservative." 保管する, by contrast, stresses safe keeping in one place.

examples[].german: I recorded the contents of the meeting.
For my summer vacation homework, I recorded the weather and temperature every day.
Tokyo recorded 38 degrees today, the hottest of the year.
en.notes: 記録する is transitive: to "record, document, log" events or data with を in writing or by technical means (会議の内容を記録する, 毎日の気温を記録する). In sports and news it means "to reach, register a value": 過去最高を記録する. The noun 記録 also means "record": 記録を破る, 記録を更新する. For sound and video recordings, people more often say 録音する and 録画する respectively.

examples[].german: I registered as a member on the website.
I saved my new friend's phone number in my smartphone.
After moving, you have to register your residence at city hall within two weeks.
en.notes: 登録する is transitive: to officially "sign up, register, enter" oneself or something; the list or place takes に (サイトに登録する, スマホに番号を登録する). Compounds such as 会員登録, ユーザー登録, 住民登録 and チャンネル登録 ("to subscribe" on video platforms) are very common. Unlike 申し込む ("to apply, to sign up"), 登録 emphasizes the permanent entry in a registry.

en.meaning: to publish; to carry (in a publication)
examples[].german: An advertisement was placed in the newspaper.
His paper was published in a well-known science journal.
The latest information is posted on our homepage.
en.notes: 掲載する is transitive: to "print, publish, run" articles, advertisements or photos with を in a medium (に): 新聞に広告を掲載する, サイトに情報を掲載する. Very common in the passive: 論文が雑誌に掲載される. Unlike 発表する (to announce) and 公開する (to make publicly accessible), 掲載 always refers to appearing in a newspaper, magazine or on a website. A common notice: 無断掲載禁止 "reproduction without permission prohibited".

examples[].german: The research results were made public.
This movie will be released nationwide next month.
The castle garden, normally off limits, will be open to the public only this weekend.
en.notes: 公開する means "to make accessible to the public": data, information, research results or a website are 公開される. For films, 公開 means the theatrical release (映画が公開される), for buildings or gardens the opening to visitors (一般公開). The opposite is 非公開 "not open to the public". 発表する, by contrast, stresses announcing or presenting, 公表する the official announcement of facts. Note: 後悔する "to regret" sounds the same.

examples[].german: I reported the progress to my boss.
We will report the results of the survey at next week's meeting.
I reported to my parents that I had passed.
en.notes: 報告する means "to report on results or the state of a matter," typically to superiors, an organization or people who should know: 上司に進捗を報告する, 結果について報告する. In everyday work it belongs to the mnemonic 報連相 (報告・連絡・相談). 連絡する is merely contacting someone or passing on information, and 知らせる is more everyday. You can also 報告する personal news in a formal-happy way, e.g. an exam result or a marriage to one's parents. The written document is 報告書.

examples[].german: The jury returned a guilty verdict.
The former president's conviction was finalized.
If he is found guilty, he will lose his medical license.
en.notes: 有罪 means "guilty" in the legal sense, or the court's finding of guilt. Typical: 有罪判決 "guilty verdict, conviction", 有罪になる "to be convicted", 有罪が確定する "to be convicted with final effect". The opposite is 無罪. For guilt in an everyday or moral sense ("That's my fault"), you do not use 有罪 but 責任 or 〜のせい.

examples[].german: We notified the successful candidates by e-mail.
When the password is changed, the user is notified.
The company notified the employees of the closure of the factory.
en.notes: 通知する means "to notify officially", mostly in writing or electronically: 人に結果を通知する. It sounds factual and official; 連絡する is more general and personal, 知らせる is colloquial. As a noun it often appears: 合格通知 "notice of acceptance", 通知表 "school report card", スマホの通知 "push notification". The counterpart from the recipient's side is 通知を受ける.

examples[].german: The materials for the meeting were distributed to the participants.
Samples of a new product are being handed out free of charge in front of the station.
Masks are handed out at the reception, one per person.
en.notes: 配布する is the formal word for "to distribute, hand out (to many people)": documents, flyers, samples or relief supplies are 配布される. Pattern: X を人に配布する. In everyday speech people mostly just say 配る; 配布 sounds organizational or official. Typical are 配布資料 "handout" and 無料配布 "free distribution". Do not confuse it with 配達 "to deliver".

examples[].german: We collected data through a questionnaire.
My father's hobby is collecting old stamps.
In this district, burnable garbage is collected on Mondays and Thursdays.
en.notes: 収集する means "to collect systematically": data or information (情報を収集する), collectibles such as stamps or art, and in everyday life garbage collection (ごみの収集, 収集日). It is more formal than 集める, which fits any kind of collecting. 採集 is used for collecting insects or plants in nature. Often in the passive: ごみが収集される.

examples[].german: For details, please refer to the manual.
This report was prepared with reference to government statistics.
I read the old letter while consulting a dictionary.
en.notes: 参照する means "to consult (a source), look up, refer to": マニュアルを参照する, データを参照して作る. In texts, the noun alone often serves as a cross-reference: 10ページ参照 "see page 10". 参考にする, by contrast, means "to take guidance from, use as a hint", and 調べる is the general "to look up, research". 参照 is factual and typical of technical texts, instructions and computing.

examples[].german: I cited previous research in my paper.
The president quoted the words of a famous writer in his speech.
When you quote other people's writing, be sure to give the source.
en.notes: 引用する means "to quote verbatim, to cite as evidence": 論文を引用する, 作家の言葉を引用する, 〜から引用する. The quotation itself is 引用文, the source 引用元. In contrast to 参照する (consulting a source), with 引用 you take over the wording. Typical of academic texts, speeches and articles.

examples[].german: I summarized the long report on one page.
Summarize the content of this article in 200 characters or less.
To sum up what he said, he is against the plan.
en.notes: 要約する means "to summarize the core of a text or speech concisely": 記事を要約する, 〜字以内に要約する. The fixed phrase 要約すると introduces a conclusion ("in short"). まとめる is the everyday, broader word, which also means "to put in order, to bundle". Note the homophone: the adverb ようやく "finally" is written differently and has nothing to do with it.

examples[].german: The cause of the accident is being investigated.
The city surveyed the living conditions of elderly people.
We regularly test the water quality of this river.
en.notes: 調査する denotes a systematic, often official investigation or survey: 原因を調査する, 住民の意識を調査する; as a noun 調査を行う, 世論調査 "opinion poll". 調べる is the everyday "to look up, to examine", 検査 the inspection of bodies or devices, 捜査 the police investigation. 調査 sounds like government, academia or business.

examples[].german: I am studying environmental problems at university.
My grandfather has researched old Japanese architecture for many years.
I watched videos of the opposing team's games and studied their tactics carefully.
en.notes: 研究する means "to research, to investigate scientifically": 環境問題を研究する or 〜について研究する. In a broader sense also "to study something thoroughly", such as an opponent's tactics or a cooking recipe. 勉強する, by contrast, is "to study" (students, exams), 調査する a concrete investigation. Related: 研究者 "researcher", 研究室 "lab, chair".

en.meaning: to tell; to talk about; to narrate
examples[].german: My grandmother told me about her memories of the past.
Old photographs tell the history of this town.
At the press conference, the president spoke about future plans.
en.notes: 語る means "to tell at length, recount" and stresses the content: experiences, memories, plans or feelings (思い出を語る, 夢を語る, 〜について語る). It sounds more elevated and narrative than 話す, which also fits any conversation or chat. Figuratively, things can "speak" too: 写真が歴史を語る, 数字が語る. Related are 物語 "tale, story" and 語り合う "to talk with each other."

examples[].german: The doctor told the patient the results of the examination.
The flowers in the garden announce the arrival of spring.
He left the house without telling anyone where he was going.
en.notes: 告げる means "to tell, announce (something important)": 人に結果を告げる, 名前を告げる, 行き先を告げずに. Figuratively "to herald, signal": 春の訪れを告げる, 時計が正午を告げる. A set phrase is 別れを告げる "to say goodbye". It sounds more literary and weighty than 言う or 伝える; in everyday speech one rather says 言う or 知らせる.

examples[].german: That dynasty flourished for several hundred years.
The dynasty fell due to a rebellion.
The Tale of Genji is a representative work of court literature.
en.notes: 王朝 is a dynasty, i.e. a ruling family and the period of its rule: 清王朝, ブルボン王朝, 王朝が滅びる "a dynasty perishes", 王朝を開く "to found a dynasty". In Japan, 王朝 also stands for the court culture of the Heian period, e.g. 王朝文学 "court literature". The ruling family itself, without reference to an era, is 王家 or 王室. In sports, 〜王朝 is used figuratively for a long era of victories by a team.

en.meaning: to contact; to get in touch
examples[].german: I will contact you later, so please wait a moment.
Let me know when you get to the station.
I suddenly ran a fever, so I called the company to say I would be absent.
en.notes: 連絡する means "to get in touch, to let someone know, to make contact" - by phone, message or e-mail: 人に連絡する, 人と連絡を取る. Important expressions: 連絡がつく/つかない "to be able/unable to reach someone", 連絡先 "contact information". 報告する, by contrast, is a report on results, 通知する a formal notification. With 〜と連絡する you give the content: 休むと連絡する.

examples[].german: I asked my teacher for advice about my future path.
I discussed the moving costs with my family.
en.notes: 相談する means to ask someone for advice or to discuss something together. The person from whom one wants advice often takes に: 先生に相談する. と emphasizes the conversation partner in a joint discussion: 家族と相談する. The topic can be named with について. In the first example, 進路 means the further educational or career path. The forms are, for example, 相談します, 相談した and 相談して; 相談 alone is the noun.

examples[].german: We discussed environmental problems.
Without rushing to a conclusion, we discussed the strengths and weaknesses of the method.
That issue has been debated in the Diet for a long time as well.
en.notes: 議論する means "to discuss something objectively, exchange arguments": 問題について議論する or 問題を議論する. Phrases: 議論を交わす, 議論になる "to end up in a discussion," 議論の余地がない "beyond dispute." An 議論 need not be a quarrel; a heated verbal argument is 口論. 討論 is a formal debate with opposing positions, and 話し合う is talking something over together with the aim of reaching an agreement.

examples[].german: The students debated about politics.
Before the election, the candidates debated on television.
In class, we split into groups and debated whether school uniforms are necessary.
en.notes: 討論する means "to debate": several people represent different positions and exchange arguments, often in a fixed setting such as a 討論会, a テレビ討論 or in class. Pattern: 〜について討論する. 議論する is broader and can also be an informal discussion; ディベート refers to the strictly regulated competitive form. 討論 sounds formal.

en.meaning: to argue; to give a speech; to plead
examples[].german: She won the speech contest.
At the trial, the plaintiff's side argued first.
In its closing argument, the defense claimed that the defendant was innocent.
en.notes: 弁論 refers to presenting arguments in public, for example as a speech or in court. It appears most often as a noun: 弁論大会 "speech contest", 最終弁論 "closing argument", 口頭弁論 "oral proceedings". The verb 弁論する is rare and mainly legal: a party presents its arguments in a trial. In everyday speech one says 主張する "to assert, advocate" or スピーチをする.

examples[].german: He spent the whole night trying to win her over.
I talked the company president into providing the budget for the new project.
I was uncomfortable when an unknown man hit on me in a bar.
en.notes: 口説く has two meanings: "to work on someone persistently, to talk someone round" (社長を口説いて予算を出してもらう) and "to hit on, to woo" (女性を口説く). The second is the more common today and sounds colloquial. Often in the passive: 口説かれる "to be hit on". 説得する is the neutral, factual word for persuading; a pickup line is 口説き文句.

en.meaning: to recommend; to advise; to offer
examples[].german: I recommended this book to a friend.
My doctor advised me to exercise more.
I offered my seat to an elderly person on the train.
en.notes: 勧める has three uses: to recommend something (本を友人に勧める), to advise someone to do something (〜するように勧める) and to offer something (席を勧める, お茶を勧める). The noun おすすめ "recommendation" comes from it. Not to be confused with the identically sounding 進める "to move forward"; 薦める is often written when recommending a person for a post.

examples[].german: I advised my friend to stop wasting money.
My senior colleague urged me to read the contract carefully.
Ignoring the doctor's advice, he started drinking again.
en.notes: 忠告する means "to advise earnestly, warn in admonition", usually so that someone refrains from something or is careful: 人に〜ように忠告する. As a noun: 忠告を聞く/無視する. It usually comes from more experienced people; toward superiors it seems presumptuous. アドバイス or 助言 are neutral "advice", 注意する is everyday admonishing, 警告 an explicit warning of danger.

examples[].german: He warned the residents that a typhoon was approaching.
The doctor warned that it would be dangerous if I kept smoking like this.
A warning appeared on the computer screen saying that a virus had been found.
en.notes: 警告する means "to expressly warn of a danger": 人に〜と警告する, 〜ないよう警告する. As a noun: 警告を受ける/無視する, 警告音, and on screens 警告 "warning"; in sports also the yellow card. 注意する is milder, and 忠告する is personal advice. Official severe-weather warnings, on the other hand, are 警報 (大雨警報).

examples[].german: The Roman Empire ruled vast territories.
After World War I, many empires collapsed.
He built a huge IT empire in a single generation.
en.notes: 帝国 is an empire, i.e. a large state ruled by an emperor (皇帝) or dominating many peoples: ローマ帝国, 大英帝国, 帝国が崩壊する "an empire falls apart". Historically it also stands for the Japanese empire before 1945 (大日本帝国); derived from it is 帝国主義 "imperialism". Figuratively it denotes a powerful corporate empire: IT帝国.

examples[].german: The criminal threatened the clerk with a knife.
I was threatened: "If you don't hand over the money, I'll spill your secret."
It is not good to make children obey by threatening them.
en.notes: 脅す means "to threaten, intimidate": 人をナイフで脅す, 〜と言って脅す, 脅して〜させる "to force someone to do something through threats". Often in the passive: 脅される. The formal, legal word is 脅迫する. Be careful with 脅かす: read おどかす it means "to scare", read おびやかす "to endanger" (平和を脅かす).

examples[].german: I was cheated out of my money by a fraudster.
I fell for the claim that "you'll definitely make a profit" and lost a lot of money.
I keep using my old computer somehow, nursing it along.
en.notes: 騙す means "to deceive, to trick, to cheat": 人を騙す, especially common in the passive 騙される "to fall for it" (〜に騙される). 騙し取る means "to swindle out of". It is often written in kana: だます. Unlike 嘘をつく "to lie", 騙す aims at deceiving as a whole. 騙し騙し使う means "to keep using (something old) somehow".

examples[].german: I misunderstood his remark.
I mistook the short reply for a sign that he was angry.
It's better to avoid ways of speaking that are easily misunderstood.
en.notes: 誤解する means "to understand wrongly," mostly words, intentions or people: 発言を誤解する, AをBだと誤解する "to mistake A for B." Important phrases: 誤解を招く "to cause misunderstandings," 誤解を解く "to clear up a misunderstanding," 誤解しないでください. 勘違いする is one's own mistake out of carelessness (mixing up a date or place), while 誤解 concerns more the interpretation of something said.

examples[].german: Everyone agreed to his proposal.
After agreeing to the terms of use, I completed the registration.
I cannot agree with that opinion.
en.notes: 同意する means "to agree, consent" and takes に: 意見に同意する, 規約に同意する - not 意見を同意する. As a noun: 同意を得る/求める, 同意書 "consent form". 賛成する is "to be in favor" (of proposals, votes), 合意 a mutual agreement between parties, 承認 an official approval.

examples[].german: The draft budget was approved by the committee.
My vacation request was approved, so I bought a ticket.
When you approve a friend request, the other person can see your page.
en.notes: 承認する means "to officially approve, sanction": 申請・計画・予算を承認する; very common in the passive (承認される) and in 上司の承認が必要 "approval by the supervisor is required." Also "to recognize" in the political sense (国家を承認する) and "to confirm" digitally (友達申請を承認する). 許可する permits an action, 確認する only means to check or confirm, and 同意する to agree personally.

examples[].german: The principal approved the field trip.
Photography is not permitted inside this building.
The company allowed employees to work from home.
en.notes: 許可する means "to allow, to approve" (officially): X を許可する, 〜ことを許可する. As a noun it is very common: 許可を得る/もらう/取る, 許可なく "without permission", 許可証 "permit". It sounds official or institutional; in private settings one more often says 許す or いいと言う. 承認する refers to plans and applications, 許可 to a concrete action.

examples[].german: He refused the interview.
The device rejected the connection with the old password.
She refused to undergo the examination.
en.notes: 拒否する means "to refuse firmly, reject": 要求・取材・接続を拒否する, 〜ことを拒否する "to refuse to do something". It is more explicit and formal than 断る, which can also be a polite decline. Related: 拒否権 "right of veto", 登校拒否 "school refusal". Devices and systems can also 拒否する (アクセス拒否).

examples[].german: I argued against his opinion.
She rebutted him by showing documents, saying that the figures were out of date.
Even when the teacher admonished him, he did not say a word in rebuttal.
en.notes: 反論する means "to contradict with counterarguments": 意見に反論する, 〜に対して反論する. Fixed expressions: 反論の余地がない "irrefutable", 反論を述べる "to state a rebuttal". 反対する can be mere rejection without reasons, whereas 反論 brings arguments. The colloquial "to talk back" is 言い返す.

en.meaning: to condemn; to censure; to blame
examples[].german: The international community condemned the act.
He harshly condemned the friend who had broken his promise.
The politician's remarks were criticized by many people.
en.notes: 非難する means "to criticize sharply, to condemn, to denounce", usually misconduct: 行為を非難する, 人を〜だと非難する; in the passive 非難される, and the fixed 非難を浴びる "to be subjected to fierce criticism". 批判する is more objective and can also be constructive, 責める is a personal reproach. Note the homophone: 避難する means "to get to safety, to evacuate".

en.meaning: to defend; to stand up for
examples[].german: The lawyer defended the defendant.
Everyone blamed him, but only I stood up for him.
Instead of only defending yourself, you should apologize first.
en.notes: 弁護する means "to defend", mainly in a legal sense: 弁護士が被告人を弁護する. In everyday life also "to stand up for someone" when others criticize them; colloquially one often says かばう for this. 自己弁護 is justifying oneself. 擁護する defends rather rights, principles or positions, and 守る is the general "to protect".

examples[].german: The budget proposal was passed in the Diet.
On a social studies field trip, we went to see the National Diet Building.
The prime minister answered the opposition's questions in the Diet.
en.notes: 国会 is above all the name of the Japanese parliament with the chambers 衆議院 and 参議院. Typical: 国会で審議する, 国会を召集する, 国会議員, 国会議事堂. For the parliaments of other countries one usually says 議会, though 国会 is also possible. The component 国 makes clear that it is the national level, in contrast to 市議会 or 県議会.

examples[].german: Many castles were built in medieval Europe.
Medieval streetscapes remain in this town.
I study medieval Japanese history at university.
en.notes: 中世 is the Middle Ages: roughly the 5th to 15th century for Europe, and for Japan mainly the Kamakura and Muromachi periods. As an attribute it takes の or stands directly before the noun: 中世の城, 中世ヨーロッパ, 中世史. The usual periodization is 古代 - 中世 - 近世 - 近代 - 現代. "Medieval" in the derogatory sense ("backward") is expressed rather by 時代遅れ.

examples[].german: He is involved in activities to protect human rights.
As criticism mounted, the manager defended his players.
That newspaper takes the position of defending freedom of speech.
en.notes: 擁護する means "to stand up for (publicly), to defend": 人権・憲法・言論の自由を擁護する, also to take a person or their position under protection against criticism. It is literary and typical of politics and media. 弁護する is above all the legal defense of a person, 保護する is the protection of the weak, animals or nature.

examples[].german: Her courageous action was praised.
The judges praised his performance highly.
Her efforts deserve praise.
en.notes: 称賛する means "to praise, to extol (publicly)" and is literary; it is common in the passive (称賛される) and in expressions such as 称賛を浴びる "to receive great praise", 称賛に値する "to be praiseworthy". The spelling 賞賛 also occurs. In daily life one says 褒める, which often points from top to bottom (parents praise children). 称賛 expresses admiring recognition.

examples[].german: It is not good to run down other people's work.
He always criticizes my cooking, so I lose the desire to make it.
The movie was panned by critics but was popular with audiences.
en.notes: けなす means "to put down, disparage", i.e. to speak disparagingly of someone or their work: 作品をけなす, 人をけなす. It is almost always written in kana. The opposite is ほめる. 批判する is objective criticism, 悪口を言う is rather bad-mouthing behind someone's back, ばかにする is making fun of someone. In the passive: 批評家にけなされる "to be panned by critics".

examples[].german: Insulting him in public is not acceptable.
Saying something like that is the same as insulting my family.
Even when a customer insulted him, the clerk responded calmly.
en.notes: 侮辱する means "to insult, hold in contempt" and is a strong, rather formal word: 人を侮辱する, 侮辱を受ける; in law there is 侮辱罪 "insult" as a criminal offense. ばかにする is the everyday "to make fun of, look down on", けなす a disparaging running down, 悪口 bad-mouthing. 侮辱 violates the dignity or honor of a person or group.

examples[].german: She forgave his mistake.
If time permits, I'd like to stop by the art museum on the way home.
My father wouldn't allow me to live on my own.
en.notes: 許す has two main meanings: "to forgive" (人の過ちを許す, 絶対に許せない "unforgivable") and "to allow, permit" (〜ことを許す, 時間が許せば "if time permits"). Formally you ask for forgiveness with お許しください. 許可する is official permission, 許す is more personal. Other phrases: 気を許す "to trust someone," 点を許す "to concede a point" in sports.

examples[].german: If you fear failure, you can't start anything.
Many residents evacuated, fearing that the river would overflow.
He feared his boss and could not tell the truth.
en.notes: 恐れる means "to fear, be afraid of" and takes を: 失敗を恐れる, 〜ことを恐れる. It sounds somewhat more elevated than 怖がる, which describes visible fearful behavior and is often used for other people; in everyday speech people usually say 〜が怖い. Very important is the noun in 〜恐れがある "there is a risk that." For reverence it is also written 畏れる.

en.meaning: to be deeply moved; to be thrilled
examples[].german: I was deeply moved by the teacher's warm words.
I got to meet my favorite singer and cried from sheer emotion.
When I saw my own book on display in a bookstore for the first time, I was overwhelmed.
en.notes: 感激する means "to be deeply moved, overwhelmed", usually out of joy or gratitude about something personal: 〜に感激する, 感激のあまり泣く. 感動する is rather used for being moved by art, nature or stories; 感激 is more emotional and immediate, e.g. when meeting someone or experiencing kindness. 興奮する is mere excitement.

en.meaning: to get excited; to be agitated
examples[].german: I got excited watching the soccer match.
The children were so looking forward to tomorrow's outing that they were too excited to fall asleep for a long time.
Please don't get worked up; speak calmly.
en.notes: 興奮する means "to be excited, aroused" - from joy, tension or also anger: 試合に興奮する, 興奮して眠れない, 興奮しないで "don't get worked up". As a noun: 興奮を抑える, 興奮状態. わくわくする is joyful anticipation, 感激する is being touched. Caution: depending on context, 興奮 can also mean sexual arousal.

examples[].german: When the earthquake struck, I ran outside in a panic.
I overslept and rushed out of the house so hurriedly that I forgot my wallet.
Even if you are asked a question suddenly, just answer calmly.
en.notes: 慌てる means "to get into a rush or panic, to act headlessly". The て-form is very common as an adverb: 慌てて家を出る "rush out of the house"; 慌てずに / 慌てないで "without panicking". 焦る is inner impatience under time pressure, 急ぐ is the neutral "to hurry". A scatterbrain is called 慌て者. Intransitive, with no object.

en.meaning: to be bewildered; to be at a loss
examples[].german: I was bewildered by the sudden question.
When I had just come to Japan, I was bewildered by how detailed the garbage sorting was.
Many employees are bewildered by the new system.
en.notes: 戸惑う means "to be unsure, at a loss" because something is unexpected or unfamiliar: 突然の質問に戸惑う, 新しい環境に戸惑う. The noun appears in 戸惑いを感じる / 戸惑いを隠せない. 迷う is indecision between options, 困る is generally "to be in trouble", 慌てる is hectic panic. Intransitive; the trigger takes に.

examples[].german: Modernization progressed rapidly.
In the Meiji period, Japan began to walk the path toward a modern state.
In modern literature class, we read a novel by Natsume Soseki.
en.notes: 近代 denotes the modern era as a period; in Japan usually the time from the Meiji Restoration to 1945, for Europe roughly since industrialization. Common in compounds: 近代化 "modernization", 近代的 "modern", 近代文学, 近代国家. Unlike 現代 (the present, "today"), 近代 is a historical period; before it comes 近世 (in Japan the Edo period).

en.meaning: to worry; to agonize; to be troubled
examples[].german: I'm worried about the future.
I'm still agonizing over which university to go to.
Many farmers are troubled by a labor shortage.
en.notes: 悩む means "to struggle with something, suffer from something, go back and forth": 将来のことで悩む, 人間関係に悩む, どちらにするか悩む. It is an inner, lasting struggle with a problem. 心配する, by contrast, is worry about someone or something ("to be concerned about"), and 迷う is indecision between options. The noun 悩み means "worry, trouble."

examples[].german: He suffered from illness for a long time.
In that country, many people are suffering from food shortages.
I have trouble understanding his attitude.
en.notes: 苦しむ means "to suffer, be in agony," physically or mentally: 病気・痛み・借金・貧困に苦しむ. The set phrase 理解に苦しむ means "to be unable to make sense of something." The adjective is 苦しい, the transitive counterpart 苦しめる "to torment." 悩む is more inner brooding over a problem, while 苦しむ stresses the suffering itself.

examples[].german: I endured the strict training.
This building is designed to withstand even large earthquakes.
She endured the pain and kept running to the end.
en.notes: 耐える means "to endure, put up with" and takes に: 痛み・寒さ・厳しい訓練に耐える, 〜に耐えられない. For things it means "to withstand": 地震に耐える建物. 我慢する is more everyday and stresses holding oneself back or going without; 耐える sounds more serious and suggests longer strain. For emotional matters, 堪える is sometimes written as well.

examples[].german: I still regret the decision I made back then.
I regret not having studied more.
It's better to do something and regret it than to regret not having done it.
en.notes: 後悔する means "to regret," referring to one's own past action: 決断を後悔する, 〜たことを後悔する, 〜ばよかったと後悔する. Well known is the proverb 後悔先に立たず "regret always comes too late." 反省する, by contrast, means to recognize one's mistake and want to improve. Note: 公開する "to make public" sounds the same.

examples[].german: I was ashamed of my ignorance.
I want to play in a way that does justice to the name of the champion team.
Being poor is nothing to be ashamed of.
en.notes: 恥じる means "to be ashamed (of)" and is literary: 自分の無知を恥じる, 恥じることではない "nothing to be ashamed of". The negative 〜に恥じない "worthy of something" (名に恥じない) is common. In everyday speech one says 恥ずかしい or 恥ずかしく思う; 恥をかく means "to be embarrassed, lose face". The object of shame takes を.

en.meaning: to bear a grudge against; to resent
examples[].german: Resenting him won't change anything.
She long held a grudge against the lover who had abandoned her.
Rain on the very day of the match - it makes you want to curse the weather.
en.notes: 恨む means "to bear a grudge against someone, to resent something" because of a wrong suffered: 人を恨む, 〜を恨んでいる. As a noun: 恨みを持つ, 恨みを買う "to make enemies", 逆恨み "unjustified resentment". One can also 恨む fate or the weather, i.e. "rail against" it. 憎む is stronger and means "to hate".

en.meaning: to long for; to look up to
examples[].german: I have admired pilots since I was a child.
Having grown up in the countryside, she had always longed for city life.
The senior student in the club was an object of admiration for everyone.
en.notes: 憧れる means "to long for, to be crazy about, to admire as a role model" and always takes に: パイロットに憧れる, 都会の生活に憧れる. The noun is very common: 憧れの人 "great role model, idol", 憧れの職業 "dream job". 尊敬する means, more soberly, "to respect, to look up to", and うらやましい is "to be envious". Intransitive, so not with を.

en.meaning: to look back fondly; to reminisce
examples[].german: I look back fondly on my student days.
My grandfather reminisced about his youth while looking through an old album.
My older sister, who lives abroad, longs for Japanese home cooking.
en.notes: 懐かしむ means "to look back on something with nostalgia, to miss something" and takes を: 学生時代を懐かしむ, 故郷を懐かしむ. It is rather literary; in conversation the adjective 懐かしい is used much more often ("Oh, how nice, this brings back memories!"). Mostly in the forms 懐かしんでいる or 懐かしみながら. 恋しい more strongly stresses missing people or places.

examples[].german: He lamented the unfairness of the world.
I deeply grieved the sudden death of my friend.
Many people lament that young people these days don't read books.
en.notes: 嘆く means "to lament, mourn" and expresses deep grief or serious regret: 死を嘆く, 現状を嘆く, or with a quotation: 〜と嘆く. It is more elevated and serious than everyday complaining, for which one says 愚痴をこぼす or 文句を言う. The adjective 嘆かわしい means "deplorable"; 嘆き悲しむ intensifies the sorrow.

examples[].german: We must not forget the horrors of war.
My grandfather experienced the war as a child.
I hope the war ends soon and peace comes.
en.notes: 戦争 is "war" between states; typical are 戦争が始まる/終わる/起こる and 戦争をする. In Japan, 戦前 and 戦後 without further qualification refer to the Second World War. Figuratively it means fierce competition: 受験戦争 "exam war", 価格戦争 "price war". A single fight or battle, on the other hand, is 戦い; the opposite concept is 平和.

examples[].german: There are many voices worrying about the country's future.
Young people concerned about environmental destruction were collecting signatures in front of the station.
He was worried about his friend's health and urged him several times to go to the hospital.
en.notes: 憂う is a literary, elevated verb for deep concern about something serious or large-scale, often society or the future; the object takes を: 国の将来を憂う, 世を憂う. It is a more recent variant of the ichidan verb 憂える (憂えて, 憂えない), which is traditionally considered more correct; of 憂う, mainly the dictionary form and 憂い before a comma are common. In daily life one says 心配する. Related are the noun 憂い "worry, sorrow" and 憂鬱 "melancholy".

examples[].german: I'm starting a new job next month.
Well then, let's start the meeting.
It started to rain, so I hurried home.
en.notes: 始める is transitive: you start something (仕事を始める, 会議を始めましょう); its intransitive partner 始まる says that something begins by itself (授業が始まる). After the verb stem, 〜始める means "begin to ...": 降り始める, 読み始める. Also "to open a business": 店を始める. Do not confuse it with 初めて "for the first time", which is written with the kanji 初.

examples[].german: I finished all the work without incident.
When you finish reading this book, I'll lend it to you.
He finished university and got a job at a local company.
en.notes: 終える is transitive: 仕事を終える "to finish the work"; the intransitive counterpart is 終わる (仕事が終わる). It sounds somewhat more formal than 終わらせる and is often used in reports and news. After the verb stem it forms compounds such as 読み終える or 食べ終える "to finish reading/eating." 学校を終える can also mean "to complete school."

en.meaning: to miss hearing; to fail to catch
examples[].german: I missed an important announcement.
I can't let that remark pass.
I set the radio timer so as not to miss my favorite program.
en.notes: 聞き逃す means failing to catch something because one was inattentive or not there: アナウンスを聞き逃す. To be distinguished is 聞き取れない, where one is listening but acoustically cannot understand. In the negative potential form 聞き逃せない it means "I can't just let that pass". Parallel to it is 見逃す "to overlook, to miss".

en.meaning: to catch (by ear); to make out
examples[].german: I couldn't catch his dialect.
The phone was so quiet that I couldn't make out the address.
The police took down from the eyewitness what the scene had been like at the time.
en.notes: 聞き取る means to acoustically grasp and understand what is spoken; very common in the potential form 聞き取れる/聞き取れない. The simple 聞く is broader ("to hear, to listen, to ask"). 聞き取り is also the name of the listening comprehension part of exams. In official and business language, 聞き取る also means "to question, to have something explained" (聞き取り調査 "interview survey").

en.meaning: to read (from); to interpret; to scan
examples[].german: I read his feelings from the other person's expression.
When you scan the code with the camera, a map is displayed.
Please explain what can be read from this graph.
en.notes: 読み取る means to read information or intent out of something visible: 表情から気持ちを読み取る, グラフから傾向を読み取る. The typical frame is 〜から〜を読み取る, often in the potential form 読み取れる. Technically it means "to scan, to read in" (コードを読み取る, 読み取り機 "reader"). For simply reading a text one says 読む; 察する is sensing without visible clues.

examples[].german: The teacher told me to, so I rewrote the report.
My handwriting was messy, so I rewrote the address.
I don't like the ending, so I'm rewriting the last chapter of the novel.
en.notes: 書き直す means "to write once more (better)": レポートを書き直す, 宛名を書き直す. The suffix 〜直す generally means "to redo, to correct", cf. やり直す, 言い直す. 書き換える, by contrast, stresses changing or replacing content (data, laws), whereas 書き直す rather means a new, improved version.

en.meaning: to write down; to jot down
examples[].german: I wrote the important things down in a memo.
I wrote down in a notebook the old tales I heard from my grandmother.
I'll give you the number; could you please write it down?
en.notes: 書き留める means to put something in writing so that it is not forgotten: メモに書き留める, ノートに書き留める. The place takes に, the thing noted takes を. In daily life one often just says メモする; 書き留める sounds a little more careful and can also mean recording stories. 書き込む, by contrast, means "to write into something" (a form, a forum).

en.meaning: to rephrase; to put another way
examples[].german: I rephrased the difficult expression in simple words.
In other words, he is afraid of failure.
So that the same word wouldn't repeat, I replaced "taisetsu" with "juyo".
en.notes: 言い換える means to say the same thing in other words: AをBに言い換える. The meaning stays the same, only the expression changes; 言い直す, by contrast, rather means correcting oneself or saying it once more. Very common is the conditional form 言い換えれば "in other words" at the start of a sentence, equivalent to つまり. The noun 言い換え means "paraphrase".

examples[].german: I added a word to the explanation.
One more thing to add at the end: tomorrow's meeting starts at ten.
I added a list of references to the report.
en.notes: 付け加える means to add something more to what already exists, especially words or explanations: 一言付け加える, 説明を付け加える. The target takes に. In speeches, 付け加えますと or 付け加えると introduces an addition. 加える is more general (also ingredients, pressure), and 付け足す is more colloquial and stresses attaching something afterwards.

examples[].german: Fierce fighting continued.
A ceasefire was reached between the two countries and the fighting ended.
The combat scenes in this game are incredibly intense.
en.notes: 戦闘 refers to a concrete military engagement or combat between armed units: 戦闘が始まる／続く, 戦闘に参加する, 戦闘機 "fighter aircraft". 戦争, by contrast, is war as a whole, and 戦い generally "fight" (also in sports or figuratively). In video games, 戦闘 is the usual term for fights (戦闘シーン). As a する-verb it is intransitive, but is rarely used that way.

examples[].german: The amount after deducting taxes is the take-home pay.
The value of my points was deducted from the hotel price.
You should take his stories with a grain of salt.
en.notes: 差し引く means "to deduct", especially of sums of money: 給料から税金を差し引く, often in the passive 〜から差し引かれる. The noun 差し引き means "balance, net result". Figuratively, 差し引いて聞く/考える means to view something with some discount. In school arithmetic one simply says 引く; 控除する is the technical tax term.

examples[].german: I removed the weeds in the garden.
I removed the fish bones before letting my child eat it.
Relieving patients' anxiety is also an important part of a doctor's job.
en.notes: 取り除く means "to remove, eliminate" - something disturbing or unwanted is taken out: ゴミ・雑草・原因・不安を取り除く. Transitive with を; the place of origin takes から: スープから脂を取り除く. 除く alone rather means "to exclude, except" (日曜日を除く "except Sundays"), and 取り外す means "to detach" (parts that can be reattached). Very often also abstract, with feelings and problems.

examples[].german: I repainted the walls of the house white.
She broke the world record.
This new product rewrote the common sense of the industry.
en.notes: 塗り替える first means "to repaint", often in a different color: 壁を白く塗り替える. Figuratively it means "to redo completely": 記録を塗り替える "to break a record", 地図を塗り替える "to change the balance of power". 塗り直す, by contrast, only means touching up or repainting, usually in the same color.

examples[].german: I rearranged the members of the team.
The classes will be reshuffled in the new school term.
A sudden business trip came up, so I rearranged my plans for next week.
en.notes: 組み替える means to rearrange the composition of something: クラスを組み替える "to reassign classes", 予定を組み替える "to rearrange a plan", 予算を組み替える. In biology it is mostly written 組み換える (遺伝子組み換え "genetic engineering"). 入れ替える stresses exchanging individual parts, 並べ替える only the order.

examples[].german: I replaced the old batteries with new ones.
Let's open the window and air out the room.
I turned over a new leaf and decided to work seriously.
en.notes: 入れ替える means "to exchange, to swap": AをBに入れ替える "to replace A with B"; the intransitive counterpart is 入れ替わる. Fixed expressions are 空気を入れ替える "to air out" and 心を入れ替える "to reform, to become a new person". 取り替える is used more for replacing a broken part or exchanging with someone; 交換する is more neutral and formal.

examples[].german: I switched gears and focused on the next match.
Please switch the display to Japanese.
I plan to switch my electricity contract to another company from next month.
en.notes: 切り替える means to switch from one state or system to another: AをBに切り替える; intransitive 切り替わる. Typical are 気持ちを切り替える "to switch mental gears, move on", 画面/モードを切り替える and changing over contracts or systems. 変える is the general "to change"; 切り替える stresses a clear switch between two options. The noun 切り替え means "switchover".

examples[].german: I took on the difficult job.
My neighbor took care of the cat while I was traveling.
I was asked to give a speech at a wedding and gladly accepted.
en.notes: 引き受ける means to take on a task, role or responsibility, usually at the request of others: 仕事を引き受ける, 世話を引き受ける. Typical are 快く引き受ける "to gladly take on" and 引き受けてくれる. 受け取る, by contrast, only means to receive an object, and 受け入れる to accept a proposal or people. 担当する rather describes a fixed responsibility.

examples[].german: The weather got bad, so I turned back.
I noticed I had forgotten something and went back home from the station.
The plan has advanced to the point of no return.
en.notes: 引き返す is intransitive and means "to turn back halfway": 途中で引き返す, 駅から家に引き返す; with を the path taken back is expressed (来た道を引き返す). 戻る is the general "to return", whereas 引き返す stresses turning around before reaching the destination. Figuratively, もう引き返せない means "there is no turning back".

en.meaning: to push ahead; to charge forward
examples[].german: I pressed on without giving in to difficulties.
Once I've decided, I just push forward on the path I believe in.
The athletes pushed through the rain toward the finish line.
en.notes: 突き進む is intransitive and means to advance energetically without hesitation, literally and figuratively: 夢に向かって突き進む, 信じる道を突き進む. Depending on context it sounds determined and positive or reckless and blind. It is stronger than 進む; colloquially similar is 突っ走る.

en.meaning: to cut in; to interrupt; to fall below
examples[].german: It is rude to cut in line.
Please don't interrupt other people when they are talking.
This month's sales fell well below the target.
en.notes: 割り込む means to push one's way into something: 列に割り込む "to cut in line", 話に割り込む "to interrupt someone", in traffic 車線に割り込む "to cut into a lane". With を, with numbers it means "to fall below a mark": 目標を割り込む. The noun 割り込み means "cutting in"; colloquially one also says 横入りする.

examples[].german: Invading other countries is prohibited under international law.
That country has a history of being invaded by a neighboring country.
In the movie, aliens come to invade Earth.
en.notes: 侵略 is a military invasion or aggression in which a state attacks and appropriates foreign territory: 他国を侵略する, 侵略戦争 "war of aggression", 侵略者. The word is strongly judgmental; more neutral is 侵攻, which only describes the military advance. In biology there is the technical term 侵略的外来種 "invasive alien species".

en.meaning: to jump over; to leap across
examples[].german: I jumped over the fence and into the garden.
Birds fly across the sea to the southern countries.
He was promoted to department head, skipping over his seniors.
en.notes: 飛び越える means "to jump over something": 塀を飛び越える; the obstacle takes を. For jumping with the legs, the spelling 跳び越える is also seen. Figuratively it means to skip over borders or sequences: 国境を飛び越える, 先輩を飛び越えて昇進する. 越える alone only means "to cross, to exceed".

examples[].german: I looked up at the night sky and gazed at the stars.
I got a stiff neck from looking up at the tall building.
Picking up trash every morning - what admirable dedication.
en.notes: 見上げる means "to look up at something": 空を見上げる, ビルを見上げる; the opposite is 見下ろす. Figuratively it means "to look up to someone, to admire"; today mainly in the fixed form 見上げた "admirable" (見上げた心がけ, 見上げた根性). For "to revere" in daily life one rather says 尊敬する.

en.meaning: to look down on; to overlook
examples[].german: I looked down at the town from the observation deck.
From the hotel on the hill, you can look down on the sea.
The tall man always talks as if he were looking down on people.
en.notes: 見下ろす means "to look down on something from above": 展望台から町を見下ろす; the opposite is 見上げる. With the potential form one describes views: 海が見下ろせる部屋. The meaning "to look down on someone, to despise" is possible but is mostly expressed with 見下す (みくだす).

en.meaning: to stand up; to rise; to boot up
examples[].german: I stood up from my chair and gave a greeting.
The computer won't start up for a long time.
After the earthquake, the people of the town joined forces and got back on their feet.
en.notes: 立ち上がる is intransitive: to get up from sitting or lying (椅子から立ち上がる), as opposed to 起きる "to wake up, get out of bed." Figuratively it means "to pick oneself up again" or "to take action" (困難から立ち上がる). For computers it means "to boot up." The transitive counterpart 立ち上げる means "to start, found" (パソコン/会社を立ち上げる).

examples[].german: I stopped when I saw the beautiful scenery.
When someone called my name, I stopped involuntarily.
Even in busy daily life, I want to pause once in a while and think about life.
en.notes: 立ち止まる is intransitive and is used for people (and animals) who stop while walking: 足を止めて立ち止まる, 思わず立ち止まる. For vehicles and machines one says 止まる. Figuratively, 立ち止まって考える means "to stop and think".

en.meaning: to sit down (and stay); to hold a sit-in
examples[].german: I was so tired that I sat down at the roadside.
When she heard the news, she sank to the ground on the spot.
Residents held a sit-in at the site in protest against the construction.
en.notes: 座り込む is intransitive and means to sit down and stay sitting, often from exhaustion or shock: 道端に座り込む, その場に座り込む. The place takes に. It can also mean "to stage a sit-in"; the noun 座り込み means "sit-in blockade". The neutral 座る only describes sitting down.

examples[].german: I lay on the lawn and looked at the sky.
I was lying on the sofa watching TV when my mother scolded me.
On hot days, lying on the floor feels nice, with the coolness on your back.
en.notes: 寝転ぶ is intransitive and means to lie down loosely and comfortably, without intending to sleep: 芝生に寝転ぶ, ソファで寝転ぶ. The place takes に (destination) or で (place of the action). Synonymous and somewhat more colloquial is 寝転がる; neutral and polite is 横になる. 寝る, by contrast, mostly means "to sleep, to go to bed".

en.meaning: to slide into; to just make it
examples[].german: I just made it right at the deadline.
The runner slid into second base.
As the departure bell rang, I slipped onto the train.
en.notes: 滑り込む is intransitive and literally means "to slide in": 二塁に滑り込む in baseball, 布団に滑り込む. Very common is the figurative meaning "to just make it": 締め切りに滑り込む, 発車間際の電車に滑り込む. The expression 滑り込みセーフ "just in time" belongs here. The destination takes に.

en.meaning: to fly off; to take off
examples[].german: The bird flew off from the tree branch.
The plane took off from Narita as scheduled.
The graduates have flown off into society.
en.notes: 飛び立つ is intransitive and describes birds and aircraft taking off: 〜から飛び立つ, 空へ飛び立つ. 離陸する is the technical term for aircraft, 飛ぶ is simply "to fly". Figuratively it means setting out into life or the world: 社会へ飛び立つ, 世界へ飛び立つ.

examples[].german: It is important to nurture children's talents.
The two of them have nurtured their friendship over a long time.
The rich forest nurtures many living things.
en.notes: 育む is an elevated, rather literary verb for "to nurture, to foster, to let flourish": 才能を育む, 友情/愛を育む, 自然が命を育む. For the concrete raising of children, animals or plants, daily speech uses 育てる. 育む stresses the careful, long-term growing of something valuable, often abstract.

examples[].german: Alexander the Great conquered a vast region.
Everest was first conquered in 1953.
Anime villains are often aiming to conquer the world.
en.notes: 征服 is the conquest and subjugation of a country or people: 〜を征服する, 世界征服 "world domination" (often jokingly for anime villains). Figuratively it also means "to conquer, master": 山を征服する, 病気を征服する. Unlike 侵略 (judgmental: aggression, invasion), 征服 emphasizes the successful subjugation. Do not confuse it with the homophone 制服 "uniform".

examples[].german: The teacher guided the students onto the right path.
His strong performance led the team to victory.
It is not easy to draw a conclusion from data.
en.notes: 導く means to lead someone to a goal or result: AをBに導く, e.g. チームを勝利に導く, 成功に導く. 案内する, by contrast, is the concrete leading and showing of a way, 率いる the leading of a group. In logic and mathematics, 導く (or 導き出す) means "to derive, deduce": 結論を導く. The noun 導き means "guidance".

examples[].german: He led the team to the championship.
The company president heads three thousand employees.
Led by their teacher, the students toured the museum.
en.notes: 率いる means to lead a group as its leader: チーム/軍/会社を率いる. In the passive, 〜に率いられて describes who is leading a group. It stresses the position at the head of a group; 導く, by contrast, stresses guiding toward a goal, and colloquially one says 引っ張る. Note: it is an ichidan verb (率いて, 率いない).

en.meaning: to be accompanied by; to have in tow
examples[].german: He attended the meeting accompanied by his subordinates.
The singer appeared on stage with her band behind her.
The king subdued the surrounding countries one after another.
en.notes: 従える is the transitive counterpart of 従う "to follow, to obey" and means "to have someone in one's retinue, to lead along": 部下を従えて, バンドを従えて. It is mostly used in the て-form before a verb of movement or action. In historical texts it also means "to subjugate" (国々を従える). It sounds elevated to literary.

examples[].german: He served the king for many years.
As someone who serves God, I want to live honestly.
She is a veteran secretary who has served three company presidents.
en.notes: 仕える is intransitive and means "to serve (someone)", with に: 王に仕える, 神に仕える. It sounds old-fashioned or solemn and occurs mainly in historical or religious contexts; for ordinary employment one says 勤める or 働く. Do not confuse it with 使える "to be usable" and つかえる "to get stuck", which are read the same.

examples[].german: We hired three new part-timers.
I hired a lawyer to prepare for the trial.
I'm currently working for a small company.
en.notes: 雇う means "to employ, hire": アルバイトを雇う, 弁護士を雇う. In the passive, 〜に雇われる means "to be employed by someone"; 雇い主 is the employer. 採用する is more formal and stresses the decision in the application process. With vehicles, 雇う also means "to charter, rent" (船を雇う).

examples[].german: I'll leave this job to you.
I've done all the preparation, so all I can do is leave the result to luck.
I'll leave it to your imagination what happened after that.
en.notes: 任せる means to leave a task or decision to someone: 〜に〜を任せる; 任せて！ "Leave it to me!" It can also mean leaving something to chance or its own course: 運に任せる, ご想像にお任せします. 頼む is merely asking, 委ねる the more formal variant. 力に任せて means "by brute force."

examples[].german: The final decision was left to the committee chairman.
I gave myself over to the sound of the waves and rested slowly.
The education of children should not be left to schools alone.
en.notes: 委ねる is the formal, literary equivalent of 任せる: 〜に判断を委ねる "to leave the decision to someone". It often appears in news, administration and law (判断を委ねる, 権限を委ねる). The expression 身を委ねる means "to give oneself up, to let oneself drift" (流れに身を委ねる).

examples[].german: To entrust the future to the young.
I entrusted a letter to a friend so that she would deliver it to her.
He put his feelings into this song.
en.notes: 託す means to entrust something important to someone: 〜に〜を託す, such as 未来/夢/希望を託す. One can also have a message or object conveyed through someone (伝言を託す). Figuratively it means to express feelings in something: 思いを歌に託す. 任せる is more everyday and refers to tasks, 預ける to having things kept.

en.meaning: to rob; to take away; to deprive
examples[].german: A robber snatched the woman's bag.
That accident took many lives.
My eyes were captivated by the beautiful scenery.
en.notes: 奪う means to take something from someone by force or against their will: 〜から〜を奪う, バッグを奪う. Unlike 盗む "to steal secretly," 奪う stresses violent snatching. Abstract objects are common: 命を奪う, 時間を奪う, 自由を奪う. In the passive, 目/心を奪われる means "to be captivated, enraptured."

examples[].german: Those who violate the law are punished.
Just punishing children harshly won't solve the problem.
As if to punish himself, he worked late every night.
en.notes: 罰する is a formal verb for "to punish," often in a legal context and frequently in the passive 罰せられる. It belongs to the special する class: 罰して, 罰しない, passive 罰せられる. In everyday speech people more often say 罰を与える; 叱る only means "to scold," and 処罰する is more official.

examples[].german: The slave system was abolished in the nineteenth century.
Lincoln is known for emancipating the slaves.
I do nothing but overtime every day - I feel like a slave to the company.
en.notes: 奴隷 denotes a slave or slavery as an institution, often in compounds such as 奴隷制度 "slavery", 奴隷制, 奴隷解放 "emancipation of slaves". Figuratively it describes someone completely dominated by something: 会社の奴隷, お金の奴隷, 〜の奴隷になる. The word is strong and negative; for servants or attendants people say 召使い.

examples[].german: He loudly abused the other person.
Let's stop abusing strangers online.
The fans violently abused the manager of the losing team.
en.notes: 罵る means to abuse someone fiercely and loudly: 〜を罵る, often with 大声で or 口汚く. It is a strong, rather literary word. 悪口を言う means rather "to speak ill of someone", often behind their back; 怒鳴る is "to yell at" without necessarily using insulting words. The noun 罵り means "abuse, insult".

examples[].german: She cursed her fate.
There is a rumor that this house is cursed.
I ran to the station cursing myself for oversleeping.
en.notes: 呪う means "to curse, to put a curse on someone": 〜を呪う. Literally it appears in ghost and horror stories (呪われた家, 呪い "curse"). Figuratively it expresses fierce resentment against one's own fate or oneself: 運命を呪う, 自分の不注意を呪う. Do not confuse it with 罵る, loudly insulting someone.

examples[].german: I celebrated my friend's wedding.
The family celebrated my grandmother's eightieth birthday.
We all made a toast to celebrate passing the exam.
en.notes: 祝う means to celebrate a joyful occasion or to congratulate on it: 誕生日を祝う, 合格を祝う. The object is the occasion, not the person; "to congratulate someone" is 〜におめでとうと言う. The noun お祝い means "celebration, congratulations, gift." For a party without a special occasion, people more often say パーティーをする; 祝福する is more solemn.

examples[].german: I swore never to lie again.
The two of them vowed eternal love before God.
I resolved in my heart to win at the next tournament without fail.
en.notes: 誓う means "to swear, to vow solemnly": 〜と誓う, 愛を誓う, 神に誓う. The one sworn to takes に, and the content is expressed with と or を; 心に誓う means "to firmly resolve". 約束する is the everyday "to promise"; 誓う is much more solemn and binding. The noun 誓い means "oath, vow".

en.meaning: to promise; to make an appointment
examples[].german: We promised to meet again tomorrow.
I promised my mother I would come home early, so I can't go out drinking today.
I have arranged to meet a friend at the station at three o'clock.
en.notes: 約束する means "to promise" and "to arrange to meet": 〜と約束する (content), 〜に約束する (person), 友達と会う約束をする. The noun 約束 appears in set phrases such as 約束を守る "to keep a promise" and 約束を破る "to break"; 約束がある means "to have plans". 誓う is more solemn, whereas 予約する means "to reserve".

examples[].german: Anyone who commits a serious crime will be severely punished.
I want to make sure never to make the same mistake twice.
Sometimes one breaks a law without knowing it.
en.notes: 犯す means "to commit" for crimes and mistakes (罪/過ち/ミスを犯す) and "to violate, break" (法を犯す). Read the same are 侵す "to violate, invade" (領土/権利を侵す) and 冒す "to risk, to afflict" (危険を冒す, 病に冒される); the choice of kanji matters. With a person as the object, 犯す means "to rape", so be careful with its use.

examples[].german: A reporter exposed the politician's corruption.
The detective finally uncovered the culprit's true identity.
I don't want to do anything like exposing other people's secrets.
en.notes: 暴く means to bring something hidden, usually wrongdoing, to light: 不正/秘密/正体を暴く. It has an exposing, often accusatory undertone. More neutral is 明らかにする; colloquial is ばらす "to blab". Literally it can also mean "to open a grave" (墓を暴く).

examples[].german: He tried to hide the truth.
I hid the birthday present under the bed.
She covered her face with her hands, looking embarrassed.
en.notes: 隠す is transitive: to hide or conceal something (〜を〜に隠す); the intransitive counterpart is 隠れる "to hide oneself." It applies to objects (プレゼントを隠す) as well as abstract things (真実/気持ちを隠す). The noun 隠し事 means "secret," 隠さずに "openly, without holding anything back."

en.meaning: to suppress; to hold back; to keep down
examples[].german: I suppressed my anger and spoke calmly.
This month I have to keep my spending down.
I brought the fever down with medicine.
en.notes: 抑える means to keep something within limits or hold it back: 怒り/感情を抑える, 費用/出費を抑える, 熱/痛みを抑える. Do not confuse it with the identically read 押さえる "to hold down, to press, to secure" (傷口を押さえる, 席を押さえる). Rule of thumb: 抑える for limiting and suppressing, 押さえる for physically holding down.

examples[].german: I finally accomplished my long-held goal.
