en.notes: 人口密度 is population density, composed of 人口 "population" and 密度 "density". One says 人口密度が高い / 低い (not 多い / 少ない). It is usually given as the number of inhabitants per square kilometer (1平方キロメートルあたり). Related terms: 過密 "overcrowding" and 過疎 "depopulation of rural areas".

examples[].german: Apartments in the city center have high rents.
I live thirty minutes by train from the city center.
Last night, even central Tokyo got five centimeters of snow.
en.notes: 都心 is the city center, primarily the center of Tokyo; in weather reports, 都心 usually means central Tokyo. It can, however, also be used for other big cities. Typical: 都心に通う, 都心まで〇分, 都心部. 副都心 are the sub-centers such as Shinjuku or Ikebukuro. More general is 中心部, and for entertainment districts 繁華街.

en.meaning: busy shopping and entertainment district; downtown
examples[].german: The entertainment district glitters with neon at night.
As soon as you leave the east exit of the station, the busy downtown area spreads out.
Walking alone through the entertainment district late at night is a little scary.
en.notes: 繁華街 is a lively district with many shops, restaurants and bars, where many people are out and about (繁華 "bustle", 街 "street, district"). Typical: 駅前の繁華街, 夜の繁華街. 商店街 is instead a smaller, local shopping street, and 歓楽街 stresses nightlife and entertainment establishments more strongly.

examples[].german: I built a house in a quiet residential area.
In residential areas, please do not make loud noises late at night.
This area used to be fields, but now it is a residential district.
en.notes: 住宅地 is a residential area, that is, an area made up mainly of dwellings. Typical: 静かな住宅地, 高級住宅地 "upscale residential district", 新興住宅地 "newly developed housing area". 住宅街 is almost synonymous but sounds more everyday and stresses the streets; the opposites are 商業地 and 工業地帯.

examples[].german: The area in front of the station is developing as a commercial district.
This year, land prices in commercial areas rose sharply.
Since this land is zoned commercial, more people build shops than homes.
en.notes: 商業地 is an area used for trade and business, a rather technical term from urban planning and real estate, for example in land price reports (商業地の地価). The opposites are 住宅地 and 工業地. In everyday speech people more often say 繁華街, 商店街 or ビジネス街.

examples[].german: This region is one of Japan's leading industrial zones.
In social studies class, we learned about Japan's main industrial zones.
Boat tours to see the industrial zone's night view are popular.
en.notes: 工業地帯 is a large industrial area with many factories (地帯 "zone, belt"). In Japanese geography class, you learn the major 工業地帯 such as 京浜工業地帯, 中京工業地帯 and 阪神工業地帯. Smaller areas are often called 工業地域 or 工業団地 "industrial park". Opposites: 住宅地, 商業地, 農業地帯.

examples[].german: Yokohama is famous as a port town with a long history.
At the market in the port town, you can buy fresh fish cheaply.
He was born and raised in a small port town in Hokkaido.
en.notes: 港町 is a port town, read with the native Japanese reading みなとまち. The word often has a nostalgic or romantic ring (sailors, fish markets, old warehouses) and is popular in songs and travel guides. Formed similarly are 城下町 "castle town" and 門前町 "temple town". In a factual, official register one says 港湾都市.

examples[].german: The groom gave a speech.
And now, the bride and groom enter.
I am a friend of the groom from his university days.
en.notes: 新郎 is the "bridegroom" in the context of the wedding celebration, very often in the pair 新郎新婦 ("bride and groom"). It is heard mainly in wedding announcements and speeches: 新郎側の親族, 新郎の友人. Outside a wedding one simply says 夫 or 彼. The more everyday, somewhat more poetic word is 花婿.

examples[].german: It is fun to stroll through the hot spring town in a yukata.
In the hot spring town, inns and souvenir shops line up in a row.
During winter vacation, my family went to the Kusatsu hot spring town.
en.notes: 温泉街 is the district of a town around the hot springs, with ryokan, bathhouses and souvenir shops. Here 街 is read がい, as in 商店街 or 繁華街. 温泉地, by contrast, generally refers to a spa resort with hot springs. Typical is strolling through the 温泉街 in a yukata, often with 温泉まんじゅう.

examples[].german: Redevelopment of the urban area is progressing.
In built-up areas, please slow down when driving.
Heavy rain made the river overflow, and part of the urban area was flooded.
en.notes: 市街地 is the built-up urban area, as opposed to 郊外 "suburbs" or 山間部 "mountain areas". Common in news, urban planning and traffic law: 市街地の再開発, 市街地を走る, 中心市街地 "city center". In everyday speech people mostly say 町中 or 街中. 市街 alone appears in compounds such as 旧市街 and 市街戦.

examples[].german: There are many historic buildings in the old town.
The old town has such narrow streets that cars can't enter.
On trips to Europe, my greatest pleasure is walking through the old towns.
en.notes: 旧市街 is the "old town", the historic core of a city. It is used mainly for European and foreign cities, for example in travel guides. For Japanese cities one rather speaks of 古い町並み, 城下町 or 旧市街地; 下町 is something else, namely the traditional district of ordinary people. The counterpart is 新市街.

examples[].german: Modern buildings line the new town.
The hotel is in the new town, so it's about ten minutes by bus to the old town.
There is a large shopping mall in front of the station in the new town.
en.notes: 新市街 is the "new town", the later-built, modern part of a city, usually as the counterpart to 旧市街. The word appears mainly in travel guides about European or Middle Eastern cities. For Japanese planned towns on the city outskirts, one rather says ニュータウン or 新興住宅地.

examples[].german: There is a large park in the center of the city.
There is a lot of traffic in the center of town, so I get around by bicycle.
The interior of the Earth is thought to be extremely hot.
en.notes: 中心部 is the central area of something, usually a city (市の中心部, 町の中心部), but also of a body or object (地球の中心部). While 中心 refers more to the center point, 部 stresses the whole area. For the center of Tokyo specifically, one says 都心; the opposite is 周辺部 or 郊外.

examples[].german: Farmland stretches across the outskirts.
On the outskirts of the city, new houses are being built one after another.
The edges of the photo came out a little dark.
en.notes: 周辺部 is the outer area or periphery of a region, formed from 周辺 "surroundings" and 部 "part"; the opposite is 中心部. It sounds factual and appears in urban planning, statistics or technology (for example, the edges of a photo). In everyday speech people usually say 周辺, 周り, or for cities 郊外 "suburbs".

examples[].german: The boundary line between the two countries follows the river.
The boundary with the neighboring house was unclear, so I asked for a survey.
It was a movie in which the boundary between dream and reality becomes blurred.
en.notes: 境界 is a "boundary" between two areas: plots of land, regions, but also abstractly (夢と現実の境界). It sounds factual to formal; the boundary line is called 境界線. In everyday speech people often say 境 (さかい) or 境目. For national borders, 国境 (こっきょう) is usual, and for prefectural borders 県境.

examples[].german: This mountain is located on the border of two prefectures.
When we came out of the long tunnel at the prefectural border, a snowy landscape spread out before us.
During the holidays, people were urged to refrain from traveling across prefectural borders.
en.notes: 県境 is the border between two prefectures and is usually read けんざかい; in official and news language one also hears けんきょう. Note: 境 is read さかい here, but きょう in 国境 (こっきょう). Typical: 県境を越える, 県境のトンネル; during the Corona period, 県境をまたぐ移動 "travel across prefectural borders" became a catchphrase.

examples[].german: Beyond the city limits, a pastoral landscape spreads out.
This river forms the boundary between the two cities.
We live right near the city limits, so the station in the neighboring city is closer.
en.notes: 市境 is the boundary between two cities or municipalities with city status, formed in analogy to 県境 and usually read しざかい. The word is relatively rare and appears mainly in news, on maps or in administrative matters; in conversation people often simply say 市の境. Correspondingly there are 町境 and 区境.

examples[].german: Smoking is prohibited on school grounds.
This university's grounds are so large that you need a bicycle to get around.
Before building the house, I measured the size of the lot accurately.
en.notes: 敷地 is the plot of land on which a building stands or which belongs to an institution, such as a school, company or temple. Very common is 敷地内 "on the premises" (敷地内禁煙, 敷地内立入禁止). Also typical: 敷地が広い, 敷地面積. 土地 is more general, "land, ground", and 用地 is land earmarked for a specific purpose.

examples[].german: The bride wore a beautiful dress.
The bride's father cried throughout the ceremony.
I was asked to give a speech on behalf of the bride's friends.
en.notes: 新婦 is the "bride" during the wedding celebration, usually in the pair 新郎新婦. Typical in announcements and speeches: 新婦の父, 新婦側の席, 新婦の友人代表. The more everyday word is 花嫁 (also 花嫁衣装). Beware of the homophone: 神父 (しんぷ) is a Catholic "priest".

en.meaning: land; plot of land; soil; locality
examples[].german: Land near the station is expensive.
When traveling, I look forward to eating the local specialties.
The soil around here is poor and not suited to growing rice.
en.notes: 土地 has two main meanings: "plot of land, land" as property or ground (土地を買う, 土地の値段, 土地がやせている) and "area, place" (その土地の料理, 土地の人 "locals"). Also typical is 土地勘 "familiarity with an area". For soil as earth one rather says 土, for the surface of the ground 地面.

en.meaning: land for a specific purpose; site
examples[].german: We are looking for a construction site for the new hospital.
Securing land to expand the airport is not easy.
The city bought up that land as a site for road construction.
en.notes: 用地 is land earmarked for a specific purpose and appears almost always in compounds: 建設用地 "construction site", 道路用地, 工場用地, 住宅用地. Typical in official and business language: 用地を確保する, 用地買収 "land acquisition". Unlike 敷地, the land is usually not yet built on.

examples[].german: A park was built on the site of the old factory.
How to use the former Olympic venue sites has become an issue.
An apartment building was built on the site of the closed elementary school.
en.notes: 跡地 is land on which something used to stand, such as a factory, school or station, that has since been demolished or abandoned (跡 "trace, remains"). Typical: 工場跡地, 〜の跡地に…が建つ, 跡地利用 "reuse of the site". For historical remains such as castles, 城跡 (しろあと) is more usual; archaeological sites are called 遺跡.

examples[].german: The children were playing soccer in a vacant lot.
It seems a new house will be built on the vacant lot next door.
Please do not dump garbage in the vacant lot.
en.notes: 空き地 is an undeveloped, vacant plot of land, especially in residential areas, the classic playground of children (known from "Doraemon"). Formed like 空き家 "vacant house" or 空き部屋. The spelling 空地 also occurs. A cleared plot ready for building is called 更地; fallow agricultural land is 休耕地 or 荒れ地.

examples[].german: Japan has a complex topography with many mountains.
Because of the terrain, this region gets a lot of snow in winter.
Before the mountain climb, I checked the terrain on a map.
en.notes: 地形 refers to the shape of the earth's surface in an area: mountains, valleys, plains, coastlines. Typical are 複雑な地形, 険しい地形, 山がちな地形 and the phrase 〜な地形をしている. Unlike 地質 ("composition of rock and soil"), 地形 is only about the visible surface form; 地理 is more generally the "geography" of an area. In technical language it appears in 地形図 ("topographic map").

examples[].german: A geological survey was carried out before construction.
The geology of this mountain is complex, and many unusual stones are found there.
I majored in geology at university and am researching volcanoes.
en.notes: 地質 refers to the makeup of the ground: rock types, soil layers and how they formed. Common in compounds: 地質調査 ("geological survey"), 地質学 ("geology" as a science), 地質図 ("geological map"). It is mostly found in technical or news language, for example regarding construction, earthquakes or volcanoes. It differs from 地形 ("landform") in that it concerns the material beneath the surface, not the outer shape; the soil in a garden is simply 土.

en.meaning: to think of; to come up with
examples[].german: I thought of a good method.
I can't think of at all what to buy as a present.
While taking a shower, I came up with an idea for a new project.
en.notes: 思い付く (usually written 思いつく) describes the moment when an idea or solution suddenly occurs to you: いい案を思いつく, 名前が思いつかない. The object can take を or, especially in the negative, が. Unlike 考え付く, 思いつく stresses the spontaneous, almost accidental; 思い出す, by contrast, means "to remember something forgotten". The noun 思いつき means "spontaneous idea", often disparagingly: 思いつきで決める ("to decide on a whim").

examples[].german: Nobody came up with such a solution.
I tried every method I could think of, but nothing worked.
Children play in ways that adults would never think of.
en.notes: 考え付く (also 考えつく) means "to think up, to hit upon something", as the result of one's own thinking: 方法を考えつく, 誰も考えつかなかったアイデア. Compared with 思いつく ("to occur to one suddenly"), it sounds more like deliberate mental effort. Very common are the negative 考えつかない and the phrase 考えつく限り ("everything one can possibly think of").

en.meaning: to reconsider; to think over again
examples[].german: Please think it over once more.
When I said I would quit the company, my boss told me to reconsider.
Because the budget was insufficient, I reconsidered my travel plans.
en.notes: 考え直す means to "think over again" a decision or opinion already made, often with the result of changing it. Typical are 計画を考え直す, もう一度考え直す and the request 考え直してください, with which one tries to talk someone out of a decision. The suffix 〜直す generally expresses "to do anew, to do again (properly)", as in 書き直す or やり直す. Plain 考える is only "to think", and 見直す is more "to review, to reassess".

examples[].german: I could sense her anxiety.
The moment I entered the room, I sensed an atmosphere as if something had happened.
The author's deep sorrow can be sensed from this poem.
en.notes: 感じ取る means to "pick up on, sense" something unspoken or subtle: 相手の気持ちを感じ取る, 雰囲気を感じ取る, 季節の変化を感じ取る. Compared with plain 感じる ("to feel"), 〜取る stresses actively grasping and understanding what one perceives. Often in the potential form: 感じ取れる, 感じ取ることができる. The tone is neutral to slightly literary.

examples[].german: This meat is very fatty and a bit heavy.
I wiped the fat left in the frying pan with paper.
en.notes: Solid (mostly animal) fat, e.g. in meat: 脂の多い肉. Liquid oil is written 油. Skin oil: 脂.

en.meaning: to roast (over a fire); to grill; to warm
examples[].german: Roasting nori over a flame improves its aroma.
On the cold night, I warmed my hands at the bonfire.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to hold something briefly over a flame to roast or warm it: 海苔をあぶる, 手をあぶる. Often written in kana.

examples[].german: Cherry trees are blooming here and there in the park.
Looking for the key, I searched all around the house.
en.notes: A somewhat more formal form of あちこち: in various places. The kanji 彼方此方 is rare.

examples[].german: If a good idea comes to you, please write it down right away.
A new product was born from his idea.
en.notes: An idea or inspiration; also written アイディア. "To have an idea": アイデアが浮かぶ／アイデアを出す.

examples[].german: He made a displeased face, making no attempt to hide it.
Nobody will believe such a blatant lie.
When the clerk realized I wasn't going to buy anything, her attitude changed blatantly.
en.notes: A na-adjective for something shown openly and without disguise, often with a negative flavor: あからさまな嘘 "a barefaced lie", あからさまに嫌な顔をする, あからさまな差別. It is almost always written in kana; the spelling 明白 is ateji and is normally read めいはく (card 明白 "obvious, clear", factual and neutral). あからさま, by contrast, usually describes behavior that someone does not conceal.

examples[].german: The fisherman cast his net into the sea.
I grilled fish on a grill.
en.notes: A net for catching or grilling: 魚を網でとる, 網で焼く. Figuratively also a network (in compounds: 通信網).

examples[].german: My grandmother knits when winter comes.
I made a scarf while looking at a knitting book.
en.notes: Knitting or crocheting as an activity and the finished piece: 編み物をする (to knit). Verb: 編む.

examples[].german: There is a big antenna on the roof.
She always keeps her antennae out for new trends.
en.notes: Also figurative: アンテナを張る (to keep one's antennae out, to stay up to date).

examples[].german: Before watching the movie, I read the synopsis.
Please write a summary of this novel in three lines.
en.notes: A short summary of the plot of a book, film or plan. Kanji: 粗筋.

examples[].german: That scholar has written many books.
He wrote down his travel experiences in a book.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb, literary: to write and bring out a work. Homophones: 表す (to express), 現す (to show).

en.meaning: this and that; all sorts of things
examples[].german: On my days off I tidy up this and that around the house.
I agonized over it this way and that, but in the end I decided to go.
en.notes: Also used adverbially: あれこれ考える (to think it over from every angle). The kanji 彼此 is rare.

en.meaning: to wash one's hands of; to quit (a shady life)
examples[].german: He has broken with his bad friends and is now working honestly.
I have already quit gambling for good.
en.notes: Literally "to wash one's feet". Figuratively: to stop a bad or shady activity (crime, gambling), and today also generally "to hang up one's boots" from a job.

en.meaning: (at one's) feet; the ground underfoot; one's step
examples[].german: It's dark underfoot, so please be careful.
The cat is sleeping at my feet.
en.notes: The area right at one's feet: 足元に気をつけてください (watch your step). Also written 足下. Idiom: 足元を見る (to take advantage of someone's predicament).

examples[].german: Warm spring sunlight is streaming in through the window.
I sincerely thank you all for your warm support.
This winter was warmer than usual.
en.notes: 暖か (あたたか) is the na-adjective form alongside the i-adjectives 暖かい (vocab-n5:75) and 温かい (vocab-n2:719); it sounds somewhat more elevated and often stands attributively as 暖かな: 暖かな日差し, 温かな心. The spelling 暖か is used for weather and room temperature, 温か for food, objects and warmth of heart. Colloquially also あったか.

examples[].german: The child waved and said "bye-bye".
Well then, see you tomorrow. Bye-bye.
en.notes: Casual farewell among friends and to children; often with a wave. Not used toward superiors.

examples[].german: More and more people are buying and selling used goods on the internet.
A contract is needed for buying and selling land.
en.notes: Formal word for commercial transactions: 土地の売買 (land sale), 売買契約 (sales contract). As a verb 売買する.

examples[].german: I bought a newspaper at the station kiosk.
The shop in the hospital is open until 8 p.m.
en.notes: A small store in stations, hospitals or schools: 駅の売店, 病院の売店.

examples[].german: I drew water into a bucket and watered the flowers.
Because the roof was leaking, I put a bucket on the floor.
en.notes: Bucket for water or cleaning: バケツに水をくむ. The spelling 馬穴 is an old ateji.

examples[].german: We took a photo with Mt. Fuji in the background.
In the parking lot, I slowly backed the car up.
en.notes: Versatile loanword: 山をバックに写真を撮る (to take a photo with a mountain as backdrop), 車をバックさせる (to reverse a car), 大企業がバックについている (to have a big company's backing). Not to be confused with バッグ (bag).

examples[].german: I got the house number wrong in the address, and the letter came back.
The lot numbers in this area are hard to figure out.
en.notes: Part of a Japanese address (〜丁目〜番地). Japanese addresses refer to blocks rather than streets.

examples[].german: This toy jumps by the force of a spring.
Basketball players have strong spring in their legs.
en.notes: A mechanical spring (ばねが伸びる); figuratively the spring of the legs (足のばね). The kanji 発条 is rare.

examples[].german: The wrong answers were marked with a cross.
He crossed his arms to make an X and said "no".
en.notes: The mark ×, which means "wrong/no" in Japan; opposite: 丸（まる, ○） = correct. Also shown with the arms: 腕でバツを作る.

examples[].german: When you're in trouble, it's good to consult an experienced senior colleague.
She is a veteran with thirty years in this field.
en.notes: Someone with long experience in a field: ベテランの先生, ベテラン社員. Not used in the sense of "war veteran" (退役軍人).

examples[].german: On rainy days, I use a plastic umbrella.
I put the wet clothes in a plastic bag.
en.notes: In everyday use for soft plastic: ビニール袋 (plastic bag), ビニール傘 (clear plastic umbrella).

examples[].german: I wrote a letter to a friend on cute letter paper.
I bought letter paper and envelopes at a stationery store.
en.notes: Paper for letters; the envelope is called 封筒. Also in kana: びんせん.

examples[].german: A twenty-story building was built in front of the station.
The old building is to be demolished.
en.notes: Full form of ビル; today almost only in names and written language. In everyday speech ビル is used.

examples[].german: Fruit contains a lot of vitamins.
In winter, I try to take more vitamin C.
en.notes: ビタミンC, ビタミン剤 (vitamin tablet), ビタミン不足 (vitamin deficiency).

examples[].german: Getting plenty of sleep is also good for your looks.
My older sister attends a vocational school for beauty care.
en.notes: Care of one's appearance: 美容にいい (good for the skin/beauty), 美容院 (hair salon), 美容師 (hairdresser).

examples[].german: Livestock farming has long been thriving in this region.
In lands with little rain, livestock farming suits better than agriculture.
en.notes: Keeping and breeding livestock such as cattle or sheep. Related: 牧場 (pasture, ranch), 畜産 (animal husbandry as an industry).

en.meaning: tray; Bon festival (festival of the dead, short for お盆)
examples[].german: At Obon and New Year, the whole family gathers at my parents' home.
At the summer festival, I wore a yukata and danced the Bon dance.
The staff member brought the teacups on a tray.
en.notes: 盆 has two meanings: "tray" and the summer festival of the dead. Used alone for the latter, one usually says the polite お盆 (separate card); the bare 盆 appears mainly in compounds such as 盆踊り "Bon dance", 盆休み "Bon holidays" and 盆栽 "bonsai" as well as in phrases such as 盆と正月 "Bon and New Year" or 覆水盆に返らず "what is done cannot be undone".

examples[].german: I bought a new computer with my winter bonus.
The company did badly this year, and no bonus was paid.
en.notes: In Japan usually paid twice a year (summer and winter) in addition to the monthly salary; formally 賞与.

examples[].german: I wiped the dirt off the bicycle with a rag that was in the storeroom.
He pretended to know everything, but his ignorance soon showed.
en.notes: Old, torn cloth or clothing; figuratively, a flaw one wants to hide: ぼろが出る (to give oneself away). Adjective: ぼろい (shabby). The kanji 襤褸 is very rare.

en.meaning: son (of another family, polite); spoiled rich boy
examples[].german: Is your son already in elementary school?
He is said to be a spoiled boy who has never known hardship.
en.notes: Polite term for someone else's son: お宅の坊ちゃん. Also pejorative for a naive young man from a wealthy home. Also written 坊っちゃん; known from Natsume Soseki's novel 『坊っちゃん』.

examples[].german: Hey, little boy, where is your mother?
That little boy is said to be only three years old.
en.notes: A friendly form of address or term for a little boy: 坊や、いくつ？ Said of a young man it can also be condescending ("greenhorn").

examples[].german: I got my stationery ready before the new school term.
Japanese stationery is popular with foreigners too.
en.notes: Pens, notebooks, erasers, etc.: 文房具屋 (stationery shop).

examples[].german: When I followed the amounts in the recipe exactly, it turned out well.
Please take the medicine in exactly the prescribed dose.
en.notes: The amount of ingredients or work: 砂糖の分量, 仕事の分量. Similar: 量.

examples[].german: I learned how to calculate with fractions in elementary school.
Please convert the fraction into a decimal.
en.notes: A fractional number such as ½ (二分の一 = "one half"; in Japanese the denominator comes first). Decimal: 小数.

en.meaning: to hang (something); to dangle; to carry in one's hand
examples[].german: My father came home carrying a shopping bag.
I hung a wind chime in the window.
en.notes: To carry something dangling or to hang it up: 袋をぶら下げて歩く, 風鈴をぶら下げる. Intransitive: ぶら下がる.

examples[].german: I brushed my hair before going out.
I brushed the mud off my shoes.
en.notes: A brush for hair, clothes or shoes: ヘアブラシ, 歯ブラシ (toothbrush). ブラシをかける = to brush.

examples[].german: I paired a white blouse with a navy skirt.
This blouse doesn't need ironing.
en.notes: A woman's top; ワイシャツ is the men's dress shirt.

examples[].german: I pinned the brooch I got from my grandmother to my chest.
Flower-shaped brooches are lined up in the shop.
en.notes: A decorative pin for clothing: ブローチをつける.

en.meaning: long silence, not keeping in touch (no letters, calls, visits)
examples[].german: Caught up in being busy, I have completely neglected to keep in touch with my parents' home.
I apologize for my long silence.
Until the person I was meeting arrived, I looked at my phone with nothing to do.
en.notes: 無沙汰 denotes a long absence of letters, calls or visits. In everyday speech it appears almost always politely as ご無沙汰 (separate card), e.g. ご無沙汰しています "I haven't been in touch for a long time"; the bare 無沙汰 is found more in letters and written language (無沙汰を詫びる). Also very common is 手持ち無沙汰 "having nothing to do, standing around idly".

en.meaning: to bump; to hit against; to vent (feelings)
examples[].german: I bumped my head on the corner of the shelf.
It is not good to take out your frustration with work on your family.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of ぶつかる: 頭をぶつける (to bump one's head), 車をぶつける; figurative 怒りをぶつける (to vent one's anger). The kanji 打付ける is rare.

examples[].german: A brown dog is running through the park.
With autumn, the leaves have turned brown.
en.notes: い-adjective from 茶色 (brown): 茶色い靴. Before nouns also 茶色の.

en.meaning: arriving at ... (suffix, e.g. 東京着); counter for clothes, suits; n-th place (e.g. 一着) (counter)
examples[].german: This Shinkansen arrives at Tokyo at twelve o'clock.
I bought a suit for the interview.
He came in first in the marathon.
en.notes: After a place or time, 〜着 means "arrival" and appears on timetables as the counterpart of 〜発: 12時東京着. As a counter it counts suits and garments (スーツ一着, 二着) as well as placings in a race (一着 "first place"); note いっちゃく for 一着. Do not confuse it with the verb 着る (きる) or with 到着, which denotes arrival as a process.

examples[].german: This aircraft will shortly begin its landing approach.
Because of an engine failure, we were forced to make an emergency landing.
In 1969, the first human moon landing succeeded.
en.notes: A noun for the landing of an aircraft or spacecraft, the opposite of 離陸 "takeoff". Typical in compounds such as 着陸態勢, 緊急着陸, 月面着陸 and in onboard announcements. The verb "to land" (〜に着陸する) is taught by the card 着陸する.

en.meaning: to shorten; to reduce; to shrink
examples[].german: Through practice, I cut five seconds off my time.
It was so cold that I instinctively pulled my head into my shoulders.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 縮む (to shrink): 時間を縮める, 差を縮める (to narrow the gap), 首を縮める (to pull in one's head).

en.meaning: to become curly; to be wavy
examples[].german: On rainy days my hair gets frizzy.
These ramen are made with wavy noodles.
en.notes: Of hair or cloth: to become curly. Adjectival use: 縮れた髪 (curly hair), 縮れ麺 (wavy noodles).

examples[].german: She sang in a powerful voice.
Since my senior colleague is coming along, I feel very reassured.
en.notes: Full of strength (力強い声) or encouraging (君がいると力強い = I feel safe with you around).

examples[].german: It's dangerous, so please do not go near the machine.
When someone came near, the cat ran away.
en.notes: Intransitive: to go close to a person or thing, often negated as a warning: 近寄らないでください.

en.meaning: to bring closer; to move near
examples[].german: I brought my face close to the screen and read the small print.
New technology has brought the dream closer to reality.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 近づく (to approach): to bring something closer, or to bring something nearer to a goal.

examples[].german: This place name is hard to read.
The history of a place lives on in its place name.
en.notes: The name of a place. Many Japanese place names have unusual kanji readings.

examples[].german: You don't need to pay a tip at restaurants in Japan.
In American restaurants, it is normal to pay a tip.
en.notes: A tip; in Japan it is uncommon and is often even refused. Homophone: チップ (computer chip, gambling chip); potato chips are called ポテトチップス.

en.meaning: to be messy; to be scattered about
examples[].german: It's a bit messy, but please come in.
Documents are scattered on the desk.
en.notes: Intransitive: 部屋が散らかっている (the room is messy). Transitive: 散らかす (to make a mess).

examples[].german: The wind scattered the cherry blossom petals.
Please sprinkle green onions on top to finish.
en.notes: Transitive: to scatter something (花びらを散らす) or to disperse (気を散らす = to get distracted).

examples[].german: I blew my nose with a tissue.
In the old days, plain paper was kept in the toilet.
en.notes: Plain paper for blowing one's nose or as toilet paper; today usually ティッシュ.

examples[].german: The accident happened at this spot.
I reached the turnaround point of the marathon.
en.notes: A specific point on the terrain or on a map: 出発地点 (starting point), 折り返し地点 (turnaround point).

examples[].german: All the corners of a square are right angles.
The road turns at a right angle there.
en.notes: An angle of 90 degrees; in everyday use also "to turn at a right angle": 直角に曲がる.

en.meaning: immediately after, right after; right behind
examples[].german: Right after the earthquake, it was hard to get phone calls through.
It started raining right after I left the house.
Doing intense exercise right after a meal is not good for the body.
en.notes: 直後 means "immediately after" and connects with の to a noun (地震の直後) or to a verb in the た-form (家を出た直後に). It is the counterpart of 直前 "shortly before" (separate card) and sounds more factual than すぐ後. More rarely it means "directly behind" in the spatial sense.

examples[].german: Batteries supply direct current.
This device can be used with either direct or alternating current.
en.notes: Electrical direct current (DC); alternating current is 交流.

examples[].german: This train goes directly to the airport.
Please give me the manager's direct number.
en.notes: Without transfer or switchboard: 直通電車 (through train), 直通電話 (direct line).

examples[].german: The teacher wrote on the blackboard with chalk.
The children are drawing pictures on the road with chalk.
en.notes: Writing chalk for the blackboard (黒板).

en.meaning: head, chief, leader (一家の長); -head (suffix, e.g. 社長, 校長); strength, advantage
examples[].german: My father has supported the family as its head.
On Monday morning, the heads of every department gathered for a meeting.
In terms of experience, he has a slight edge.
en.notes: As a standalone noun it is elevated and rather literary: 一家の長, 各部署の長; in everyday life it appears almost only in compounds such as 社長, 部長, 校長, 課長. The meaning "advantage, strength" lives on in 長所 and the phrase 一日の長（いちじつのちょう）"a small lead in experience". Do not confuse with the homophones 蝶 "butterfly", 兆 "trillion", 腸 "intestine" or the prefix 超〜.

en.meaning: -book, -notebook, register (suffix, e.g. 手帳, 電話帳, 通帳)
examples[].german: I wrote next week's schedule in my planner.
I had my passbook updated at the bank ATM.
I collect new words in a vocabulary notebook.
en.notes: A suffix for books and notebooks for entering things: 手帳 "notebook, planner", 電話帳 "phone book", 通帳 "bankbook", メモ帳 "notepad", 単語帳 "vocabulary notebook", 日記帳 "diary". Related is 帳簿 "account book". 帳 hardly stands alone; the card 帳/とばり "curtain" is a different, literary word with the same spelling.

examples[].german: I am gradually gathering furnishings that suit my new home.
The exhibition room displays furnishings that were used in houses long ago.
en.notes: 調度 denotes household goods, everyday utensils and smaller pieces of furniture or furnishings. The word sounds elevated or literary and also appears in 調度品. It refers to objects, not to the act of furnishing. 丁度／ちょうど "exactly, just" is a different word. The historical meaning "bow and arrows" is not learned here.

examples[].german: Calculate the area of the rectangle.
The room is a long, narrow rectangle.
en.notes: A geometric shape; square: 正方形.

examples[].german: Mr. Tanaka's eldest daughter is said to be getting married next year.
I am the eldest of three sisters.
en.notes: The firstborn daughter; eldest son: 長男, second daughter: 次女.

examples[].german: My luggage was over the weight limit, so I paid an extra fee.
The meeting ran thirty minutes over the scheduled time.
en.notes: Exceeding a limit: 時間超過, 重量超過 (excess weight of luggage); as a verb 超過する.

examples[].german: Every method has its pros and cons.
In Japanese, the length of a sound changes the meaning.
en.notes: Literally "long and short": length (音の長短) or strengths and weaknesses (それぞれに長短がある).

examples[].german: He reached the peak of his popularity in his twenties.
A triangle has three vertices.
en.notes: The highest point: 人気の頂点 (peak of popularity); in geometry, the corner of a triangle.

examples[].german: We store vegetables in preparation for winter.
This warehouse stores rice at low temperatures.
en.notes: Keeping supplies in storage: 食料を貯蔵する, 貯蔵庫 (storeroom).

examples[].german: There is a convenience store halfway between the station and the school.
We decided to take a middle ground between the two opinions.
en.notes: The middle between two points or times: 中間テスト (midterm exam), 中間地点.

examples[].german: He dropped out of university partway through.
You must not abandon a job halfway.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds: 中途半端 (half-hearted, unfinished), 中途採用 (hiring of experienced workers outside the new-graduate recruitment cycle), 中途で (halfway).

examples[].german: I booked a double room at the hotel.
Today is a day when points are doubled.
en.notes: Double...: ダブルベッド, ダブルの部屋 (double room with one bed). The verb ダブる ("to overlap") is a separate word.

examples[].german: The meeting and my dentist appointment ended up overlapping.
I accidentally bought two copies of the same book, so I have a duplicate.
en.notes: A colloquial godan verb from ダブル: appointments overlap (予定がダブる), something exists twice; also "to repeat a school year".

examples[].german: The table is oval-shaped.
The Earth orbits the Sun in an elliptical path.
en.notes: A geometric shape; "oval" as a property: 楕円形.

examples[].german: After taking the medicine, my fever went down quite a bit.
This area, too, has changed quite a lot compared with the past, hasn't it?
My grandfather still says, "It's gotten quite cold, hasn't it."
en.notes: A secondary reading of 大分 with the same meaning as だいぶ (separate card): "quite, considerably", mostly with changes (だいぶん良くなった, だいぶん寒くなった). Today だいぶ is the standard reading; だいぶん sounds older and more leisurely and survives mainly in western Japan and among older speakers. Both are mostly written in kana, also because 大分 as a place name is read おおいた.

examples[].german: I can't remember the title of this book.
Please give your essays a title.
en.notes: Title of a book, film or song. Similar: タイトル; also shortened to 題.

examples[].german: "He" and "this" are pronouns.
The name of this town has now become synonymous with hot springs.
en.notes: Grammatical term: words like 私, 彼, これ. Figuratively also "synonym, byword": 富士山は日本の代名詞だ.

examples[].german: Stones of all sizes are lined up in the garden.
Regardless of the size of the company, the rules are the same.
en.notes: Large and small things together, or size itself: 大小の箱 (boxes of every size), 大小を問わず (regardless of size).

examples[].german: The railway company decides the intervals between trains by looking at the schedule diagram.
This book contains a diagram showing the work process.
en.notes: In general a diagram, in railways the train schedule diagram; in everyday speech usually shortened to ダイヤ ("timetable": ダイヤが乱れる).

examples[].german: Diamond is the hardest stone.
My mother treasures her diamond ring.
en.notes: The gemstone; often shortened to ダイヤ (ダイヤの指輪). However, ダイヤ also means "timetable".

examples[].german: I turned the knob to raise the volume.
My grandfather's house has a rotary-dial telephone.
en.notes: A rotating knob on devices (ダイヤルを回す) and the dial of old telephones; as a verb ダイヤルする "to dial a number".

examples[].german: This dam supplies water to the town.
Because there has been little rain, the water in the dam is decreasing.
en.notes: A wall built to store water or generate electricity. The reservoir is called ダム湖.

en.meaning: group, troupe, body; -group, -corps (suffix, e.g. 応援団, 劇団)
examples[].german: A group of tourists got off the bus.
My older brother was in the cheering squad in high school.
An investigation team was sent to the site to look into the cause of the accident.
en.notes: An organized group of people; mostly as a suffix in compounds: 応援団 "cheering squad", 劇団 "theater troupe", 調査団 "investigation team", 選手団 "team, delegation", 暴力団 "yakuza gang". With numbers: 一団 "a band, a group". More general are 集団 "group, mass" and 団体 "group, association". Do not confuse with 段/だん "step, rank" and 壇/だん "platform".

examples[].german: I lived in a housing complex when I was a child.
This housing complex has a park and a small supermarket.
en.notes: A large residential area with uniform apartment blocks, often publicly built.

en.meaning: water outage; suspension of water supply
examples[].german: Because of construction work, the water will be off tomorrow morning.
After the earthquake, the town had no water for a week.
en.notes: When no tap water flows, for example during construction work or after an earthquake; as a verb 断水する.

en.meaning: conclusion, firm decision, definite assertion; (grammar) affirmation
examples[].german: At this point, we cannot say anything definite about the cause of the accident.
He avoided making a definite statement and only said, "It's possible."
The Japanese "da" is called an assertive auxiliary verb.
en.notes: 断定 is a firm, unambiguous statement or conclusion; typical are 断定を避ける "to avoid committing oneself", 断定はできない "cannot be said with certainty" and the adjective 断定的な "categorical". The verb 断定する "to state with certainty" has its own card. In grammar, だ/である is called 断定の助動詞 "auxiliary verb of assertion".

en.meaning: full of ...; covered in ... (negative) (suffix, e.g. 間違いだらけ, 泥だらけ)
examples[].german: The children came home covered in mud.
This report is full of mistakes and can't possibly be submitted.
The room is full of trash, with nowhere to step.
en.notes: Attached directly to a noun, it means "full of ..., covered all over with ...", almost always with a negative undertone: 間違いだらけ, 泥だらけ, 傷だらけ, 借金だらけ. The result behaves like a noun or na-adjective (〜だらけだ, 〜だらけの, 〜だらけになる). A neutral "full of" would be 〜でいっぱい; 〜まみれ, by contrast, emphasizes something sticking to the surface (汗まみれ). Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: In an emergency, please use this exit.
After the accident, the escape of all passengers was confirmed.
On the weekend, I went to an escape room with friends.
en.notes: A noun for getting out of an enclosed place or danger, often in compounds: 脱出口 "emergency exit", 国外脱出 "fleeing the country", 脱出ゲーム "escape room". As a verb ("to escape", 〜から脱出する) there is the separate card 脱出する. Unlike the everyday 逃げる, 脱出 emphasizes getting out of a predicament and sounds factual to journalistic.

en.meaning: coming out; outflow; origin, descent; (suffix) graduate of
examples[].german: The water comes out weakly from this faucet.
He is an engineer and a graduate of the University of Tokyo.
My grandmother comes from a farming family and cooks very well.
en.notes: 出 (で) is the noun of the verb 出る: "coming out, outflow" (水の出が悪い "the water doesn't come out well"), the rising of the sun and moon (日の出, own card) and "origin" (農家の出 "from a farming family"). After school or place names it serves as a suffix meaning "graduate of, coming from" (東大出); more neutral are 出身 and 卒業. Not to be confused with the particle で.

examples[].german: Many people come and go in this shop all day.
Because of construction work, entry is prohibited for anyone other than authorized personnel.
en.notes: The coming and going of people or things: 人の出入りが多い; 出入り禁止 (no entry).

examples[].german: Please do not place things in front of the entrance/exit.
This building has only one entrance and exit.
en.notes: A door or opening for going in and out; on signs often written 出入口.

examples[].german: Put the green onions on top at the end, and it's done.
The photos will be ready next week.
en.notes: Being finished or the finished result: 出来上がりが楽しみ; in recipes "done!" (これで出来上がり).

examples[].german: I'll go to the airport to meet you.
My friend met me at the station.
en.notes: To pick up or greet someone on arrival: 空港まで出迎えに行く. Verb: 出迎える.

examples[].german: It is dangerous if the current is too strong.
Current is flowing through this wire.
en.notes: In physics: the flowing current (amperage in アンペア); voltage is 電圧.

examples[].german: You shouldn't believe such nonsense.
His explanation was incoherent, and I could hardly understand it.
en.notes: Noun and な-adjective: made-up talk (でたらめを言う) or haphazard (でたらめな計画). The kanji 出鱈目 are ateji.

en.meaning: to move aside, to clear away, to shift
examples[].german: I moved the books off the desk and put down the plates.
Excuse me, could you move the bicycle parked here?
When I moved the big stone, there were many small insects underneath.
en.notes: The transitive counterpart of どく: to move something or someone out of the way, e.g. 荷物をどける, 車をどける. Almost always written in kana and rather colloquial; politely, for example, どけていただけますか. The same spelling 退ける read しりぞける (separate card) is literary and means "to repel, to reject" (敵を退ける, 要求を退ける).

en.meaning: far from ...; on the contrary; let alone; not to mention
examples[].german: I'm so busy that I can't take time off even on weekends, let alone travel.
Far from being praised, I was scolded severely by the teacher.
Far from stopping, the rain has gotten even heavier.
en.notes: Placed after a noun or the plain form of a verb/adjective: AどころかB means either "instead of A, even the opposite B" (褒められるどころか叱られた) or "not even B, let alone A" (旅行どころか休みも取れない). Almost always written in kana. At the beginning of a sentence, the conjunction それどころか ("on the contrary") is used instead, which has its own card.

en.meaning: to move out of the way, to step aside, to make room
examples[].german: Excuse me, could you please move aside for a moment?
You're in the way, could you move away from there?
The cat just won't get off the chair.
en.notes: A colloquial intransitive verb "to get out of the way", almost always written in kana, especially as the command どいて！ "Make room!" (more politely: どいていただけますか). The place takes を or から: そこをどいて, いすからどく. The same spelling 退く read しりぞく (separate card) is literary and means "to withdraw, to step down". The transitive counterpart is どける; do not confuse with 毒 (どく) "poison".

en.meaning: all at once; in a rush
examples[].german: After the exam was over, the fatigue hit me all at once.
On the first day of the sale, customers poured in.
en.notes: Suddenly and in large numbers: 人がどっと押し寄せる, どっと笑う, 疲れがどっと出る. Not to be confused with ドット (dot).

examples[].german: I bought a white dress with red polka dots.
When reading out an address, "." is pronounced "dot".
Old video games were made of coarsely pixelated pictures.
en.notes: ドット is a loanword from English "dot": the dot in internet addresses (ドットコム), the polka-dot pattern (ドット柄, synonymous with 水玉模様) and the pixel (ドット絵 "pixel art"). Not to be confused with the adverb どっと "all at once, in crowds" (separate card), which is written in hiragana. For the period at the end of a sentence, one says 点 or 句点 instead.

examples[].german: The article introduces a new high school and also includes remarks by that school's principal.
The record says: "Entered in Reiwa 5, graduated in the same era's year 7."
en.notes: 同／どう refers to something mentioned earlier in factual texts. Before a noun it can mean "the same" or "the aforementioned", for example 同校 "the said school". In lists or records, 同 also replaces a repeated entry, similar to "ditto": 令和五年入学、同七年卒業. You need the preceding context to understand the reference. The question word どう "how" has a different meaning. The pronunciation of longer words such as 同校 is learned as a whole.

en.meaning: agreement; consent; same opinion; same meaning
examples[].german: Before the surgery, please sign this consent form.
In the case of minors, parental consent is required.
"美しい" and "きれい" are nearly synonymous words.
en.notes: A noun for (often formal) agreement or consent: 同意を得る, 同意を求める, 同意書, 保護者の同意. Also "same meaning" as in 同意語 "synonym". 賛成 expresses support for a proposal, while 同意 is consent, which may also be legally required. The verb 〜に同意する has its own card.

examples[].german: Many old copper coins turned up from my grandfather's drawer.
Copper coins from the Roman era are on display in the museum.
They say that in the old days you could buy bread with one copper coin.
en.notes: A coin made of copper or a copper alloy, often in a historical or numismatic context (古い銅貨, ローマ時代の銅貨). The general term "coin" is 硬貨/こうか; formed in the same way are 金貨 "gold coin" and 銀貨 "silver coin". Do not confuse with the homophones どうか "please; somehow" and 同化 "assimilation".

examples[].german: The two are treated as equals in the company.
The "の" in this sentence expresses apposition.
en.notes: Of equal rank (同格に扱う) and, in grammar, apposition.

examples[].german: My grandfather has become slow in his movements.
This computer runs slowly.
en.notes: Bodily movement (ゆっくりした動作) and the operation of devices (パソコンの動作が遅い).

examples[].german: Talking loudly on the phone is a breach of etiquette.
When coughing, it is good manners to cover your mouth.
en.notes: Manners and consideration for others: 電車の中のエチケット. Similar: マナー.

examples[].german: Um, where was the station again?
"What's the date today?" "Let me think... it's the 15th."
en.notes: A filler word used while thinking; also written えーと. Similar: あのう (when addressing someone).

examples[].german: My father's hobby is gardening.
I bought tomato seedlings at a garden center.
en.notes: Growing flowers, vegetables and fruit, also as a hobby: 園芸店 (garden center). Homophone: 演芸 (variety entertainment).

examples[].german: I painted the sky blue with paint.
For my daughter's birthday I bought a set of 24 colors of paint.
en.notes: Paint as a painting material (watercolors, oil paints), not color as a property, for which 色 is used. One says 絵の具で描く／塗る.

examples[].german: Find the length of the circumference.
The circumference of the Earth is about 40,000 kilometers.
en.notes: Mathematics: 円周率 (the number pi). Homophone: 演習 (exercise, practice).

examples[].german: I put on an apron when I cook.
All the shop assistants wear green aprons.
en.notes: An apron for cooking or working: エプロンをする／つける.

examples[].german: The zipper on the bag is broken and won't close.
I zipped my jacket up to my neck.
en.notes: Zipper; colloquially also チャック. ファスナーを閉める／開ける (to zip up/open).

examples[].german: How can I explain it so that even children understand?
That kind of way of thinking was fresh to me.
en.notes: 風（ふう）denotes a kind or manner. こんな風に means "in this way"; どんな風に asks how something is done. With に it describes the manner of an action, and with な a corresponding description can stand before a noun. In these phrases the hiragana spelling ふう is also common. The reading かぜ for "wind" and the suffix in フランス風 are other usages.

examples[].german: A parents' meeting was held at school.
Please write your parents' names on the application form.
en.notes: Formal word for parents, e.g. in schools: 父母会 (parents' meeting). Everyday words: 両親, 親.

en.meaning: sign; tag; label; playing card; talisman, amulet (お札)
examples[].german: A "In use" sign is hanging on the meeting room door.
Please take a numbered ticket at reception and wait your turn.
At the New Year shrine visit, I received an amulet from the shrine.
en.notes: A small sign or card for marking: 札を掛ける, 札を下げる; in compounds the reading stays ふだ: 名札, 値札, 荷札, 番号札. お札 is ambiguous: おふだ "talisman from a shrine" vs. おさつ "banknote" (card 札/さつ); the context decides.

examples[].german: Morse code represents letters with signs made of dots and dashes.
When you get a calculation result, check the sign carefully.
en.notes: An agreed-upon sign (モールス符号) or a mathematical sign (プラスの符号).

examples[].german: The discussion deepened our mutual understanding.
Autumn has deepened, and the mountains have begun to turn red.
en.notes: Intransitive: 理解が深まる, 秋が深まる (autumn progresses). Transitive: 深める.

examples[].german: The vice president of the company attended the meeting.
This medicine has almost no side effects.
en.notes: Prefix for deputies and secondary things: 副社長 (company vice president), 副作用 (side effect), 副業 (side job).

en.meaning: to inflate; to blow up; to swell
examples[].german: The children are blowing up balloons.
The new students are full of expectations.
en.notes: To fill something with air: 風船を膨らます; figurative 期待に胸を膨らます (to be full of expectations). Intransitive: 膨らむ.

examples[].german: There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.
It took us three hours from the foot to the summit.
en.notes: The lower part of a mountain: 山の麓の村. Opposite: 頂上 (summit). Often written in kana.

examples[].german: The books were heavy, so I sent them by sea mail.
By sea mail, it takes about a month to arrive.
en.notes: Shipping by boat, cheaper but slower than 航空便 (airmail).

en.meaning: free; unattached; free of charge; freelance
examples[].german: My brother quit his company and became a freelance designer.
Free Wi-Fi is available at this cafe.
en.notes: Unattached (フリーのカメラマン = freelance photographer), free of charge (フリーの Wi-Fi) or as the suffix "-free" (バリアフリー).

en.meaning: to turn around; to look back
examples[].german: When I turned around after hearing my name called, an old friend was there.
She left without looking back even once.
en.notes: To turn one's head or body backward: 名前を呼ばれて振り向く.

examples[].german: This coat is a hand-me-down from my father, but it is still perfectly wearable.
I tied up the old newspapers and left them in the entrance hall until collection day.
en.notes: ふる denotes a used item, usually with お: 父のお古 is something that previously belonged to the father. As a word element, 古 before a noun can mean "old" or "used", for example 古新聞 "old newspapers". Not every word with 古 is read this way; learn new compounds as a whole. The ordinary adjective "old" is 古い／ふるい. For a used item, お古 is used in everyday speech rather than a standalone ふる.

en.meaning: to be blocked; to be occupied
examples[].german: The road is blocked by an accident, and the cars cannot move forward.
My hands are full right now, so could you open the door?
en.notes: Intransitive: 道が塞がる (blocked), 穴が塞がる (to close up), 手が塞がっている (to have one's hands full). Transitive: 塞ぐ.

examples[].german: Put a lid on the pot and simmer for about ten minutes.
The lid of the jar is tight and won't open.
en.notes: Lid of a pot or container: 蓋をする (to put a lid on), 蓋を開ける. Often written in kana: ふた.

examples[].german: Because of the typhoon, train service is suspended.
After the earthquake, the phone lines were down for a while.
en.notes: Traffic or communication is interrupted: 大雪で電車が不通になる. Homophone: 普通 (normal).

examples[].german: Unfortunately, I came down with a fever on the day of departure.
He didn't let the misfortune of his injury beat him and kept training.
en.notes: Opposite of 幸運: 不運な事故, 不運にも (unfortunately).

en.meaning: to fool around; to joke; to make fun of
examples[].german: I messed around during class and was warned by the teacher.
The children are fooling around with each other and laughing.
en.notes: To be silly (授業中にふざける) or to make fun of someone; as an angry exclamation: ふざけるな！ (Stop the nonsense!). The kanji 巫山戯る are ateji.

examples[].german: This camera comes with a charger.
She works at the university hospital.
en.notes: Belonging to something: 付属品 (accessory), 大学付属の病院 (university hospital), 付属高校 (high school affiliated with a university). Also written 附属.

en.meaning: picture, painting (mostly in compounds, e.g. 日本画, 洋画, 漫画)
examples[].german: My grandfather has kept painting in the Japanese style since his youth.
At the museum I took my time appreciating Impressionist landscape paintings.
The cover of the picture book says "Story: Hanako Yamada, Illustrations: Ichiro Sato".
en.notes: The Sino-Japanese reading of 画 for pictures and paintings, almost always as a compound element: 日本画, 風景画, 漫画, 画家. On its own, 画 appears mainly in book and manga credits for the illustrator (作・…　画・…). The everyday word for "picture" is 絵 (え); the reading かく (separate card), on the other hand, means "stroke" as in 画数 or 計画.

examples[].german: This entrance cannot be used outside business hours.
That question is outside the scope of today's lesson.
en.notes: 外（がい）follows a noun and expresses that something lies outside its limits or does not belong to it. 営業時間外 denotes the time outside business hours; 範囲外 means outside a certain range. It also covers abstract limits such as the scope of a topic. The free word for "outside" is read 外（そと）. The suffix is attached directly.

en.meaning: -street; -district (suffix, e.g. 商店街, 住宅街, 中華街)
examples[].german: The shopping street in front of the station is always bustling with people.
This area is a quiet residential district.
I ate a meat bun in Yokohama's Chinatown.
en.notes: A suffix attached to nouns, denoting streets or districts with a particular character: 商店街 "shopping street", 住宅街 "residential area", 中華街 "Chinatown", 繁華街 "entertainment district". Standing alone, 街 is read まち (card 町/まち, where it appears as a spelling variant); the reading がい occurs only in such compounds. Do not confuse it with 〜外/がい "outside of" and 害/がい "harm".

examples[].german: The class was shut down because of influenza.
There are thirty students in one class.
en.notes: Official word for a school class: 学級委員 (class representative), 学級閉鎖 (closing of a class due to illness). In everyday speech: クラス.

examples[].german: I'm chewing gum so that I don't get sleepy.
Please don't throw chewing gum on the street.
en.notes: Short for チューインガム: ガムをかむ (to chew gum).

examples[].german: On New Year's Day we go to the first shrine visit of the year as a family.
This shop is closed only on New Year's Day.
en.notes: January 1; 元旦 strictly means the morning of New Year's Day.

examples[].german: She has worked in show business for twenty years.
Old folk performing arts still survive in this village.
en.notes: Film, television, music and traditional stage arts: 伝統芸能 (traditional arts such as Kabuki and Noh). 芸能人 = celebrities from the entertainment industry.

examples[].german: Over the past ten years, the number of foreign tourists has risen sharply.
In response to the sharp increase in accidents, the city began taking countermeasures.
en.notes: Written style, often in the news; as a verb 激増する. Opposite: 激減 (sharp decrease).

examples[].german: The new company pays a good monthly salary.
I spend half of my monthly salary on rent.
en.notes: The salary paid every month; compare 時給 (hourly wage), 年収 (annual income).

en.meaning: current, present, incumbent (prefix, e.g. 現政権, 現会長, 現住所)
examples[].german: The current administration has submitted its budget proposal for the next fiscal year to the Diet.
Please enter your current address and phone number on the application form.
The term of the current chairman runs until March next year.
en.notes: A frequent prefix in news, business texts and forms that denotes the present office or current state: 現首相, 現政権, 現住所. Counterparts are 元〜 (もと, "former": 元会長) and 前〜 (ぜん, "previous, immediately before": 前会長). As a separate word for "now", 現在 (separate card) is used instead.

examples[].german: The tomato is a vegetable native to South America.
This flower is said to be native to Africa.
en.notes: Original region of origin of plants, animals and products: 南米原産, 原産地 (place of origin), 原産国 (country of origin).

examples[].german: On the island, forest remains just as it was in primeval times.
Humans have used fire since primeval times.
en.notes: The earliest, untouched beginnings: 原始時代 (primeval age), 原始的 (primitive), 原始の森 (primeval forest). Homophone: 原子 (atom).

examples[].german: For the museum, get off at East Station and walk five minutes.
This ticket becomes invalid if you get off at a station along the way.
en.notes: Formal, typical in announcements and directions: 〇〇駅下車 (get off at 〇〇 Station), 途中下車 (breaking one's journey). Everyday word: 降りる.

examples[].german: The sewers overflowed because of the heavy rain.
Please do not pour oil into the drain.
en.notes: Wastewater and the pipes for it: 下水道 (sewer system). Opposite: 上水 (clean water supply).

examples[].german: It was my first time wearing a kimono, so my way of walking was awkward.
After the quarrel, the conversation between the two was a bit stiff.
en.notes: I-adjective for stiff, unpracticed movements or a tense, unnatural atmosphere（ぎこちない会話）. It is not an onomatopoeic word, even though it sounds like one.

examples[].german: I have a bit of a cold, so I'll go to bed early today.
Work has been busy lately, so I'm a little tired.
The train is running a bit late, and I'm worried whether I'll make it to the meeting.
en.notes: 〜気味 (ぎみ) is attached to nouns or the verb stem and means "slightly, somewhat, with a tendency to": 風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 太り気味, 遅れ気味. Mostly for undesirable states; it combines like a na-adjective (気味だ, 気味の, 気味で). As an independent word, 気味 is read きみ (vocab-n3:3303), for example in 気味が悪い "creepy"; ぎみ is the voiced form in the suffix.

examples[].german: The box was packed full of apples.
My schedule is jam-packed this week; I have no time to rest.
en.notes: Something is so full that no room remains: 予定がぎっしり (a full schedule), 本がぎっしり詰まった棚.

examples[].german: My grandfather plays Go with his friends every evening.
The rules of Go are simple, but it is hard to get good at it.
en.notes: Strategy game with black and white stones, also called 囲碁; "to play Go" is 碁を打つ. Homophone: 五 (five).

examples[].german: Please refrain from taking photographs inside the building.
Please refrain from making inquiries by telephone.
en.notes: Polite prohibition formula on signs and in announcements: 〜はご遠慮ください. Friendlier than 〜禁止 or 〜しないでください.

examples[].german: People learning Japanese first memorize the gojūon.
The names are arranged in gojūon order.
en.notes: The arrangement of kana in five columns and about ten rows (五十音図); dictionaries are sorted in 五十音順 (gojūon order).

examples[].german: The cooking teacher explained that the five traditional flavors include spiciness.
For this menu, I chose the ingredients with a balance of the five traditional flavors in mind.
en.notes: 五味 denotes, in the traditional classification, sweet, sour, pungent, bitter and salty. This card teaches that older culinary classification. It differs from the five basic tastes of modern taste physiology, which contain umami instead of pungency. The Buddhist classification of dairy products and the family name 五味 are not practiced here. ゴミ "garbage" is a different word.

examples[].german: The soles of these shoes are made of rubber.
I tied my hair back with a rubber band.
en.notes: From Dutch "gom": ゴムの木 (rubber tree), 輪ゴム (rubber band), ゴム手袋 (rubber gloves). An eraser is 消しゴム.

en.meaning: every; each; per (suffix, e.g. 一時間ごと, 日ごとに)
examples[].german: Don't forget the periodic inspection every three months.
It's getting colder day by day.
It gets warmer with each rainfall.
en.notes: A suffix after nouns or verbs, usually written in kana: 三か月ごとの点検 "inspection every three months", 日ごと "day by day", 会うごとに "every time we meet". The adverbial form with に has its own card (〜毎に/ごとに, vocab-n3:2554); this card covers the bare 〜ごと, especially 〜ごとの + noun. Before a noun, by contrast, 毎 is read まい (毎日, 毎週); do not confuse it with 〜ごと "together with" (皮ごと "with the skin").

examples[].german: The next issue of this magazine will go on sale next month.
That article appeared in last month's issue.
en.notes: Issue of a magazine (次の号, 最新号), serial number (三号室, 台風十号) and name suffix for ships or trains (のぞみ号).

examples[].german: This year three towns are holding the festival jointly.
The merger of the two clubs has been decided.
en.notes: Several groups do something together: 合同練習 (joint practice), 二つの学校が合同で運動会を開く (two schools hold a joint sports day). In geometry also "congruent".

examples[].german: Two, four and six are even numbers.
Garbage can be put out only on even-numbered days.
en.notes: Opposite: 奇数（きすう） (odd number).

examples[].german: In the movie, gangsters robbed a bank.
The town became dangerous because of gang fights.
en.notes: An armed criminal gang, especially in films about America. The Japanese mafia is called 暴力団 or ヤクザ.

en.meaning: trade, industry, business; studies (often as a suffix, e.g. 製造業, 農業)
examples[].german: My older brother works for a manufacturing company.
In this town, tourism is the most important industry.
After graduating from university, he took over his father's family business.
en.notes: Rare on its own, mostly as an industry suffix: 製造業 "manufacturing", 観光業 "tourism industry", 不動産業, サービス業. In the sense of "studies, coursework" it is found in 授業 and 卒業. Written the same but a different word is 業/ごう "karma" (separate card, Buddhist); for concrete work one says 仕事.

examples[].german: Please write your name on the first line.
The sentence is long, so I split it into two lines.
en.notes: A line of text: 三行目 (the third line), 一行あける (to leave one line blank). Also the rows of the kana table: あ行, か行.

en.meaning: to be no match for; to be unable to make a dent in
examples[].german: This math problem is too hard; I can't make any headway at all.
Against the champion, I was no match.
en.notes: Literally "the teeth do not stand" - also literal with hard food. Figuratively: to be no match for an opponent or a task.

examples[].german: I served the salad in a large bowl.
I repotted the flower into a new pot.
en.notes: Deep bowl (料理を鉢に盛る) and flowerpot (植木鉢). Homophones: 八, 蜂.

examples[].german: Cotton is good for baby underwear.
Because it is cold, I am wearing thick underwear.
en.notes: Clothing worn directly on the skin (undershirt, etc.). Similar: 下着.

examples[].german: The handouts will be collected after the meeting.
They were giving out free tissues in front of the station.
Questionnaire forms are distributed at reception.
en.notes: The noun for distributing to many people, factual and official: 配布資料 "handout", 無料配布 "free distribution", チラシの配布. In everyday speech one rather uses the verb 配る; 配達, by contrast, means delivery to an address. The verb 〜を配布する has its own card.

examples[].german: The match will be live-streamed on the internet.
Once you register, news is delivered to you every week.
en.notes: As a verb with する: 動画を配信する (to stream), ニュースを配信する (to distribute). Livestream: ライブ配信.

examples[].german: I weighed out 200 grams of flour on the scale.
I checked the weight of the package on the scale at the post office.
en.notes: Device for weighing: 秤で量る. A bathroom scale is usually called 体重計.

en.meaning: clearly and distinctly, briskly, lively (speaking, answering)
examples[].german: In the interview, let's answer the questions clearly and crisply.
That child is always so lively and bright, it's a pleasure.
You're speaking too quietly, please speak more clearly and distinctly.
en.notes: はきはき describes clear, brisk and confident speaking or demeanor, mostly with 答える, 話す or しゃべる, with or without と. As はきはきする it characterizes a bright, decisive person (はきはきした子). The opposite is, for example, ぐずぐず "hesitant" or もごもご "mumbling indistinctly"; it is also often seen in katakana ハキハキ.

examples[].german: I'm traveling to Kyoto for three days and two nights.
Since my plans changed, I extended my hotel stay by one night.
en.notes: 泊 counts the nights of a stay, while 日 counts the days. 二泊三日 means two nights and three days. With 泊まる you describe the stay; 一泊延ばす means to extend it by one night. Learn the number together with the counter: 二泊 is にはく, and 一泊 becomes いっぱく. The basic reading はく alone does not reveal this sound change.

examples[].german: Many people took part in the anti-war demonstration.
Such antisocial behavior cannot be tolerated.
en.notes: Prefix meaning "against, anti-": 反社会的 (antisocial), 反戦 (anti-war), 反比例 (inversely proportional).

en.meaning: to get on one's nerves; to become grating
examples[].german: His boasting has gradually started to get on my nerves.
This perfume is too strong and a bit overpowering.
en.notes: Literally "to stick to the nose": a behavior, way of speaking or smell becomes irritating over time. Typical: 自慢話が鼻につく (the boasting is annoying).

examples[].german: Let's solve the problem by talking it over.
After a long discussion, the plan was canceled.
en.notes: A conversation to reach an agreement: 話し合いで決める (to decide through discussion), 話し合いがつく (to reach an agreement). Verb: 話し合う.

examples[].german: No matter how many times I called, the line was busy.
Sorry to interrupt your conversation, but a visitor has arrived.
en.notes: The line is busy: 電話が話し中だ; also "currently talking": お話し中すみません.

en.meaning: to speak to; to address someone
examples[].german: A foreigner spoke to me in English at the station.
I mustered up my courage and spoke to the person in the next seat.
en.notes: To approach someone (often a stranger): 知らない人に話しかけられた. Often written in kana: 話しかける.

examples[].german: The bride was wearing a white dress.
The bride's father gave a speech.
en.notes: The woman on her wedding day; groom: 花婿（はなむこ）. 花嫁姿 = the bride in her wedding attire.

examples[].german: On snowy roads, please steer slowly.
The bicycle handlebar has gotten bent.
en.notes: Steering wheel of a car (ハンドルを切る = to turn the wheel), handlebar of a bicycle, door handle. A handle in the sense of a grip on a bag or pot is rather 取っ手.

examples[].german: Please pay the tuition at the bank by the end of the month.
I paid the electricity bill at a convenience store.
en.notes: To pay money into an account or to an office: 授業料を払い込む. Noun: 払い込み（払込）.

en.meaning: to be full of energy; to be raring to go
examples[].german: My younger brother is raring to go for tomorrow's match.
My mother was full of energy and has been cooking a feast since morning.
en.notes: To be motivated and full of energy: 新しい仕事に張り切っている. Often in te-form: 張り切って準備する.

examples[].german: I climbed onto the roof using a ladder.
I leaned the ladder against the wall and wiped the window.
en.notes: Ladder: 梯子を上る／かける. Colloquially also "to go from one bar to another" (はしご酒). Often in hiragana.

en.meaning: departing from ... (suffix, e.g. 東京発, 8時発); counter for shots, blows (e.g. 一発) (counter)
examples[].german: I missed the express that departs at eight o'clock.
The Shinkansen from Hakata to Tokyo is delayed.
I heard two gunshots in the middle of the night.
en.notes: After a place or time, 〜発 means "departing, leaving from": 8時発の電車, 博多発東京行き; the counterpart is 〜着. In news, ロンドン発 means "reported from London". As a counter it counts shots and blows, with sound changes: 一発 (いっぱつ), 二発 (にはつ), 三発 (さんぱつ). Do not confuse it with 初 (はつ, "first-") or 出発, which denotes departure as a process.

examples[].german: The explanation at the reception desk was spoken so fast that I couldn't catch the room number.
You get your point across better by explaining things clearly one at a time than by talking fast.
en.notes: 早口 has the reading はやぐち in addition to はやくち. Both denote fast talking. 早口で explains the manner of speaking, as in 早口で話す. The word says something about speed, not about whether the person is articulate or speaks many foreign languages. In the first situation the speed prevents understanding; the second recommends a clearer explanation. The identically read place name 早口 belongs to a different usage.

en.meaning: to be in fashion; to spread (illness); to thrive
examples[].german: This song is popular among young people right now.
The flu is going around at school.
en.notes: To be popular (若者に流行っている), to be rampant (風邪が流行っている) or to flourish (店が流行る). Noun: 流行（りゅうこう）.

examples[].german: I watched the closing ceremony of the Olympics on TV.
The tournament was closed with a speech by the chairperson.
en.notes: Official end of an event: 閉会式 (closing ceremony), 閉会の挨拶. Opposite: 開会.

en.meaning: edited by; editorship; part, volume, chapter (of a work) (suffix)
examples[].german: This dictionary was edited by Yamada Taro and published in 1990.
The first part of the movie was interesting, but the second part was a bit long.
This report summarizes the survey results in Part Two.
en.notes: 〜編 is attached to names and means "edited by" (山田編, 編集部編), or it denotes or counts parts and volumes of a work (前編・後編, 第一編, 全五編). The related verb is 編集する "to edit, compile"; 長編 "long work" is a fixed compound. Do not confuse it with 辺/へん "vicinity" and 変/へん "strange" (separate cards).

en.meaning: times (counter for repetitions, e.g. 何遍も, 一遍)
examples[].german: How many times do I have to tell you before you understand?
I have already reread this novel three times.
Even if it's just once, I'd like to climb Mt. Fuji.
en.notes: 〜遍 (へん) counts how often something happens and corresponds to 〜回 or 〜度; it sounds somewhat more colloquial and is especially common in the Kansai area. Note the sound changes: 一遍 (いっぺん), 三遍 (さんべん), 何遍 (なんべん). Typical are 何遍も "over and over" and 一遍に "all at once". Not to be confused with 辺 (へん) "area" and 変 (へん) "strange".

examples[].german: I gently wiped the baby's navel clean.
In Japan, children are told, "If thunder rumbles, your belly button will be taken."
en.notes: Navel; idiom: へそを曲げる (to get in a huff). The kanji 臍 is rare.

examples[].german: The lights of the town came into view in the distance.
When night fell, lights came on in the windows of the houses.
The lights of the ships sway in the harbor at night.
en.notes: 灯 (ひ) is a rather literary word for artificial light, the light of a lamp: 町の灯, 灯がともる "a light comes on", 灯を消す. It is common in songs and literature; in everyday life one usually says 明かり/灯り (あかり, own cards) or 電気. 火 "fire" is read the same, but 灯 always means shining light.

examples[].german: Calling in the middle of the night is thoughtless.
The prime ministers of the two countries met informally.
He immediately admitted his own fault and apologized.
en.notes: 非 is mainly a negating prefix before Sino-Japanese nouns: 非常識 "lacking common sense, inconsiderate", 非公式 "unofficial", 非喫煙者 "non-smoker". Unlike 不 or 無, which prefix fits depends on the individual word (不可能, 無責任, 非常識), so it has to be learned along with the word. As a standalone noun, 非 means "fault, wrong" and appears in fixed expressions such as 自分の非を認める "to admit one's own fault" or 非の打ち所がない "flawless, impeccable".

examples[].german: The sound of the temple bell could be heard far away.
"Sakura" is a nice-sounding name.
en.notes: Reverberation (鐘の響き) and the sound effect of a word or voice: 美しい響きの名前.

en.meaning: usually; normally; in everyday life; for a long time
examples[].german: I make a point of exercising regularly.
I passed thanks to my daily effort.
I sent a thank-you gift to the people who have helped me.
en.notes: Denotes the habitual everyday as opposed to special occasions: 日頃から "already in daily life, always", 日頃の努力 "daily effort". A fixed formula in business letters: 日頃のご愛顧に感謝申し上げます. Somewhat more literary than 普段 (separate card), which is more usual in conversation; 日ごろ is a common mixed spelling.

examples[].german: It's hot, so let's rest in the shade for a bit.
This flower grows well even in the shade.
en.notes: A place without direct sunlight: 日陰で休む. The shadow of a figure is called 影（かげ）.

examples[].german: I tried to quit the company, but my boss talked me out of it.
Sorry for keeping you so long.
en.notes: To stop someone from leaving or resigning: 帰ろうとする客を引き止める. Also written 引き留める.

en.meaning: to get caught (on); to be taken in (by); to nag at one's mind
examples[].german: The balloon got caught on a tree branch.
My grandmother almost fell for a telephone scam.
en.notes: Literally to get caught on something (枝に引っかかる); figuratively to fall for a trick (詐欺に引っかかる) or to leave an odd impression (その言葉が引っかかる).

examples[].german: Please do not forget to bring writing materials to the exam.
I passed the written exam; the interview is next.
en.notes: Writing down: 筆記用具 (writing materials), 筆記試験 (written exam) as opposed to 面接 (interview).

en.meaning: to withdraw; to be set back; to cave in
examples[].german: After the meal, my father immediately withdrew to his room.
The shop is located a little set back from the main street.
en.notes: To withdraw (部屋に引っ込む), to be set back (道から引っ込んだ家) or to stay out of it: 引っ込んでろ！(Stay out of it!). Transitive: 引っ込める.

en.meaning: to be overturned; to flip over; to fall down
examples[].german: The tent was blown over by the strong wind.
I slipped on the ice and fell over.
en.notes: Intransitive counterpart of ひっくり返す: 車がひっくり返る (a car flips over), 滑ってひっくり返る (to slip and fall on one's back).

en.meaning: to turn over; to knock over; to overturn (a decision)
examples[].german: I flipped the pancake in the frying pan.
The cat knocked over the glass and the water spilled.
en.notes: Transitive: to turn something over (ホットケーキをひっくり返す), to knock over (コップをひっくり返す) or to completely reverse a situation (試合をひっくり返す). Intransitive: ひっくり返る.

en.meaning: date; day (of an appointment); number of days
examples[].german: The date of the trip hasn't been decided yet.
There aren't many days left until the exam.
en.notes: The day of a planned event (日にちを決める) or the number of days remaining (日にちがない).

examples[].german: In winter, the sun sets early.
We watched the sunset at the beach.
en.notes: The time when the sun goes down; opposite: 日の出 (sunrise). Similar: 日没.

examples[].german: A festival was held in the square in front of the station.
The children are playing ball in the open space.
en.notes: A public square in a city (駅前広場) or an open area for playing.

examples[].german: The living room in the new house is spacious.
A vast sea stretched out before us.
en.notes: Mostly 広々とした: 広々とした部屋 (spacious room), 広々とした海 (vast sea).

examples[].german: I want to spread Japanese culture around the world.
Traveling is a good opportunity to broaden one's horizons.
en.notes: To make something known (うわさを広める) or to expand (知識を広める). Intransitive: 広まる.

en.meaning: for now; for the time being
examples[].german: The operation was a success, and I am relieved for now.
Let's end today's meeting here for now.
en.notes: Provisionally, before going further: ひとまず安心した (relieved for now). Similar: とりあえず.

examples[].german: In the dark, the pupils get larger.
The child gazed at me with big eyes.
en.notes: The pupil of the eye, poetically also the eyes: 澄んだ瞳 (clear eyes). In everyday speech 目 is used more often.

examples[].german: Although there was no wind, the door closed by itself.
This wound will probably heal by itself.
en.notes: Without outside action: ドアがひとりでに開いた. Similar: 自然に, 勝手に.

examples[].german: I'm tired, so let's take a short break here.
After a short breather, I started working again.
en.notes: To rest briefly: ここで一休みしよう. As a verb 一休みする.

en.meaning: step, pace; counter for steps (e.g. 一歩, 二歩)
examples[].german: He stepped back two paces and bowed deeply.
The hotel is only a few steps from the station.
The two countries took steps toward peace.
en.notes: 歩 (ほ) means "step" and serves mainly as a counter for steps, with sound changes: 一歩 (いっぽ, vocab-n5:1032), 二歩 (にほ), 三歩 (さんぽ), 六歩 (ろっぽ), 何歩 (なんぽ). As a standalone noun it is elevated, as in 歩を進める "to advance" or 歩を緩める "to slow one's pace". Not to be confused with 穂 (ほ) "ear of grain" and the 将棋 piece 歩 (ふ).

examples[].german: Please take great care in safeguarding your valuables.
This medicine must be stored in a cool, dark place.
The retention period for documents is set at five years.
en.notes: 保管 is the noun "storage, safekeeping"; as a verb it becomes 保管する (separate card) with を: 書類を保管する. Typical combinations are 保管場所, 保管期間, 冷蔵保管 and 保管料. Unlike 保存 "preservation, saving (data, food)", 保管 emphasizes keeping important or others' belongings safely in one's custody.

examples[].german: The city is putting effort into the health of its residents.
In next week's health class we will learn about sleep.
en.notes: Maintaining health: 保健所 (public health center), 保健室 (school infirmary), also the school subject health education. Homophone: 保険 (insurance).

examples[].german: For details, please contact the head office.
The tournament headquarters is at the entrance of the gymnasium.
en.notes: The headquarters of an organization: 本部に連絡する. Opposite: 支部 (branch). For events also 対策本部 (task force, crisis headquarters).

examples[].german: The station is only five minutes from here.
This is just a small token, but please accept it.
en.notes: A prenominal word (連体詞) that stands directly before a noun and emphasizes a small amount: ほんの少し, ほんの気持ちです (just a small token - when handing over a gift).

en.meaning: to throw; to toss; to leave alone, to neglect
examples[].german: He tossed his bag onto the bed.
He leaves his homework untouched and only plays games.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb, more colloquial than 投げる: ボールを放る. Also "to stop caring": 仕事を放っておく (to leave work lying).

examples[].german: The cover picture of this book is beautiful.
That actor appeared on the cover of a magazine.
en.notes: Cover of a book or magazine: 雑誌の表紙を飾る (to appear on a magazine cover). Homophone: 拍子 (rhythm).

examples[].german: This morning it got noticeably colder still.
Thanks to practice, his playing has become noticeably better.
en.notes: Stresses a marked increase compared with before: 一段と寒くなった (it has become noticeably colder still). More literary than もっと.

en.meaning: each and every time, one by one; over every little thing
examples[].german: You don't need to explain every little thing, I understand.
He complains about everything I do.
en.notes: Often slightly annoyed: いちいち文句を言う (to nitpick about everything). The kanji 一々 is rare.

examples[].german: This research has great significance.
We discussed the significance of volunteer work.
en.notes: Meaning in the sense of value or purpose: 意義がある (to be meaningful), 歴史的意義. Homophone: 異議 (objection).

en.meaning: to order, to instruct; to tattle (on someone)
examples[].german: My mother told me to go shopping.
If you're mean, I'll tell the teacher!
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb: 1. to assign someone a task (用事を言いつける); 2. in children's speech, to rat on someone (先生に言いつける).

examples[].german: The children are playing with great energy.
Since starting his new job, he has been full of life.
