en.notes: Also 生き生きとした／生き生きしている: full of life. Also written in kana as いきいき.

en.meaning: circumstances; background; how it came about
examples[].german: I heard how the two of them came to marry.
How did you come to join this company?
I explained the whole background to the department head.
en.notes: いきさつ is a special reading of 経緯 and refers to the circumstances of how something came about: 事件のいきさつ, いきさつを説明する, どういういきさつで "how did it come about that ...". The card 経緯/けいい has the same spelling and meaning but sounds factual and formal (reports, news); いきさつ is more everyday and often emphasizes personal background. Because 経緯 is usually read けいい, いきさつ is almost always written in kana.

examples[].german: Two plus three equals five.
Being rich does not necessarily equal being happy.
en.notes: Mathematical "equals" (二たす三イコール五) and figurative: A イコール B (A is equivalent to B).

examples[].german: Several guests were waiting at the entrance.
After repeating the same mistake a few times, I finally noticed the cause.
I wonder how many participants gathered at the venue?
en.notes: 幾（いく）is a prefix before quantity words and counters. With か it can denote an indefinite number: 幾人か "several people". In a question it can mean "how many"; in conversation 何人 for "how many people" is usually more common than 幾人. 幾度か means "a few times". 幾 is not used here on its own as an independent numeral. The words 行く and 幾つ remain separate cards.

examples[].german: What kind of image did you have of Tokyo before coming to Japan?
The incident damaged the company's image.
en.notes: A mental picture or impression of something: イメージが湧く (an image comes to mind), 会社のイメージ. As a verb イメージする (to imagine).

examples[].german: In autumn, many rice grasshoppers are jumping around in the rice fields.
In Nagano there is a custom of eating inago simmered in soy sauce.
As a child, I often played catching grasshoppers with my friends.
en.notes: Name of a grasshopper species that lives in rice fields (hence 稲子, literally "rice child"). In everyday use almost always in kana, in factual texts often in katakana イナゴ; the kanji 稲子 or 蝗 are rare. In general バッタ is used for locusts and grasshoppers; いなご is the smaller species typical of rice fields, which in some regions is eaten as いなごの佃煮.

en.meaning: ink, printing ink (older form of インク)
examples[].german: This factory makes printing ink for newspapers.
Characters written with oil-based ink do not disappear even if they get wet.
The ink in the stamp pad is getting faint.
en.notes: An older form of インク "ink", derived from Dutch. In everyday speech インク is mostly used today (separate card); インキ survives mainly in the printing industry (印刷インキ, 油性インキ) and on product labels of stamp pads or markers. Same meaning as インク, only older or technical; do not confuse with 陰気 "gloomy".

examples[].german: Do you have a container for these cookies?
Please wash empty containers and return them.
en.notes: General word for anything in which something is kept: tin, box, case. More formal: 容器.

en.meaning: relocation, move (of a location); transfer (of rights)
examples[].german: With the relocation of the office, the phone number will change.
Notice of store relocation: from next month we will be open in a new building in front of the station.
Registration is required for the transfer of ownership of land.
en.notes: Noun for the verb 移転する (separate card): the relocation of a company headquarters, store or office, typical in notices such as 移転のお知らせ, in 本社移転 or 移転先 "new address". For a private move of residence, 引っ越し is more usual. In legal use 移転 also means "transfer" of property or rights (所有権の移転).

examples[].german: My cousin is two years older than me.
When I got lost during a trip, I called my cousin and she helped me.
en.notes: In this spelling, 従姉妹 denotes a female cousin. The reading いとこ is often written in kana; the gender then follows from context. 従兄弟 is the corresponding male spelling. In 年上です one describes an age difference, while in 従姉妹に電話する the に names the cousin who is called.

examples[].german: The general adopted the strategy of resting and awaiting the exhausted enemy.
The old man enjoyed his leisure in a quiet mountain village.
en.notes: A rare, literary noun for comfortable rest or a life of leisure. The reading is いつ; the identically sounding question word いつ "when" is a different word. The phrase 佚を以て労を待つ is well known: one rests and awaits the enemy who is already tired. In everyday speech one says 休息 or のんびりする instead. This card covers the standalone sense of rest; other meanings of the character 佚, such as "to be lost", do not belong to this word usage.

en.meaning: before one knows it, without noticing
examples[].german: While I was reading, it had turned to night before I knew it.
Before I knew it, my daughter had become taller than me.
en.notes: Something happened without one noticing: いつの間にか寝ていた (I had fallen asleep before I knew it). Can also be written entirely in kana.

examples[].german: She is a journalist who reports from war zones.
I want to become a journalist in the future.
en.notes: Often used for freelance or well-known journalists; a newspaper reporter is also called 記者.

examples[].german: Let's decide who goes by rock-paper-scissors.
I lost at rock-paper-scissors and ended up having to clean.
en.notes: A hand game with グー (rock), チョキ (scissors) and パー (paper); you call out じゃんけんぽん. Rarely also written じゃん拳.

examples[].german: Ten old temples still remain in this town.
The head temple sent a notice to a hundred temples in various regions.
en.notes: 寺 is used after a number with the reading じ to count temples. This form is found especially in descriptions of temple precincts, pilgrimage routes or historical holdings. A temple as a standalone word is てら. The mere occurrence of 寺 in a temple name is not yet counting: for the counter, a number must precede it.

examples[].german: There are many old temples in Kyoto.
During my trip I visited a famous mosque.
en.notes: Formal word for temple (in everyday speech お寺); also used for places of worship of other religions: イスラム寺院 (mosque).

examples[].german: First period is math.
The third period class was canceled.
en.notes: Suffix after a number for the class period in a school timetable: 一時間目 (first period), 三時間目. The question word is 何時間目.

examples[].german: The timetable for the new term was announced.
I looked at the timetable and packed tomorrow's textbooks in my bag.
en.notes: Weekly schedule of lessons; also the time schedule of an event. Train timetables, by contrast, are called 時刻表.

en.meaning: -ish, to seem like, to look like ... (suffix, e.g. 子供じみた, 年寄りじみる); to be stained/soaked with (汗じみる)
examples[].german: I'm fed up with his childish excuses.
Please stop this theatrical behavior.
I put the sweat-stained shirt in the washing machine.
en.notes: Attached to nouns and almost always written in kana; mostly attributive as 〜じみた or 〜じみている: 子供じみた, 芝居じみた, 年寄りじみた. Sounds disparaging ("childish, theatrical"), unlike the neutral 〜らしい or 〜っぽい. Second meaning "stained with": 汗じみたシャツ. Do not confuse with the verb 染みる/しみる "to soak in, to sting".

examples[].german: The humanities include literature and history.
She is a researcher in the humanities.
en.notes: Sciences of human beings and their culture, such as literature, history and philosophy. Compare 社会科学 and 自然科学.

examples[].german: Human life must be given priority above everything else.
Many lives were lost in this accident.
en.notes: Formal, often in news: 人命救助 (lifesaving), 人命にかかわる (life-threatening). Homophone: 人名 (personal name).

examples[].german: After school, I study by myself in the library.
The teacher was absent, so third period became self-study.
en.notes: Studying alone; at school also a period without a teacher (今日は自習だ). 自習室 = study room.

examples[].german: The Shinkansen runs at 300 kilometers per hour.
On this road, please drive at no more than 40 km/h.
en.notes: Speed per hour: 時速六十キロ (60 km/h). Compare 秒速 (per second), 分速 (per minute).

examples[].german: She is not my blood sister but my sister-in-law.
To tell the truth, I haven't finished my homework yet.
It's a reform in name only, with no substance behind it.
en.notes: The Sino-Japanese reading of 実 as an independent noun, mainly in fixed expressions: 実の親 "biological parents", 実を言うと "to be honest", 実がない "lacking substance", 名より実を取る "to prefer substance over appearance". The adverb 実は "actually, frankly" has its own card (vocab-n3:3281). 実/み (vocab-n3:correction:mi-fruit), by contrast, is "fruit" and is read in expressions such as 実を結ぶ.

en.meaning: the real thing; the actual object (as opposed to a picture)
examples[].german: In person, it is much bigger than in the photo.
At the museum I saw real dinosaur bones.
en.notes: The real object as opposed to a photo, model or copy: 実物大 (life-size).

examples[].german: This bag emphasizes practicality over design.
The new technology has entered the stage of practical use.
en.notes: Often in 実用的 (practical, functional) and 実用化 (putting into practical use).

examples[].german: Because the advance preparation was thorough, the meeting went smoothly.
Advance registration is required to take part in this event.
As a result of the preliminary survey, the plan was partly changed.
en.notes: A noun used mainly attributively with の or in compounds: 事前の準備 "preparation in advance", 事前登録 "advance registration", 事前調査 "preliminary survey". The adverbial form 事前に "in advance" has its own card (vocab-n2:1323). The opposite is 事後 "after the fact" (事後報告); do not confuse it with the homophone 慈善 "charity" (vocab-n2:37).

en.meaning: woman; girl; daughter (literary or in compounds)
examples[].german: The woman made her living selling flowers.
The couple has a son and a daughter.
en.notes: 女（じょ）denotes a woman, a girl or a daughter. As a standalone noun this reading sounds elevated or historical; in everyday speech 女（おんな）is usually used for "woman". In compounds じょ is usual, for example 一男一女（いちなんいちじょ）for one son and one daughter. The examples show the older standalone use and the "daughter" meaning in a number compound. The name suffix on women's names and the identically written constellation belong to other usages.

examples[].german: My father used to be an associate professor at a university.
The protagonist of that novel is a young associate professor.
en.notes: Former job title at Japanese universities; since 2007 this position has officially been called 准教授（じゅんきょうじゅ）. Still common in older texts.

examples[].german: An invitation to my friend's wedding arrived.
This medicine is in powder form, so please take it with water.
en.notes: A suffix with two meanings: form or state (液状 = liquid, 粉状 = powdery) and written document (招待状 = invitation, 年賀状 = New Year's card).

en.meaning: counter for tatami mats; tatami floor-area unit
examples[].german: I put a desk and a futon in the six-mat room.
I ordered eight tatami mats from the tatami shop.
en.notes: 畳（じょう）follows a number and counts tatami mats; such figures are also used to describe the size of a room. 六畳（ろくじょう）means roughly "six tatami in size". The area of one mat varies by region, so 畳 is not a square-meter figure that is the same everywhere. The single mat is 畳（たたみ）. The accent of complete number compounds is not derived from the isolated dictionary entry.

en.meaning: top and bottom; up and down
examples[].german: Please don't turn this box upside down.
The elevator is moving up and down.
en.notes: Top and bottom (上下を逆にする), up-and-down movement (上下に動く) and difference in rank (上下関係 = hierarchy). The reading うえした refers more concretely to "above and below".

examples[].german: When boarding, please watch your step.
Please refrain from rushing to board at the last moment, as it is dangerous.
en.notes: Railway and official language: 乗車券 (ticket), ご乗車ください. Opposite: 下車 (getting off). In everyday speech: 乗る.

en.meaning: emotion; feelings; atmosphere, mood (alternative reading of じょうちょ)
examples[].german: Music has a good influence on the emotional development of children.
Recently she has been emotionally unstable and bursts into tears easily.
This town still retains the atmosphere of an old port town.
en.notes: じょうしょ is the original reading of 情緒; today じょうちょ (separate card) is clearly more common in everyday use. Both are correct and mean the same. じょうしょ is heard mainly in technical language such as psychology and education (情緒障害, 情緒の発達) and in formal speech. Typical combinations are 情緒が不安定だ "emotionally unstable" and 〜の情緒が残る "the atmosphere of ... remains".

examples[].german: He is so innocent that he blushes right away.
I saw a film depicting the love of an innocent girl.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun: 純情な青年 (an innocent young man). Describes a pure, inexperienced nature, especially in love.

examples[].german: Please enter the room one by one, starting with the person whose name is called.
The teacher read the students' compositions one after another.
en.notes: Mostly 順々に: one after the other. Similar: 順番に; 次々に stresses a rapid succession.

en.meaning: heavy-, serious- (prefix, e.g. 重工業, 重症); -fold, -layer (suffix, e.g. 二重, 三重)
examples[].german: My father works for a heavy industry company.
The driver was seriously injured in the accident.
This window is triple-glazed, so you can hardly hear any noise from outside.
en.notes: As a prefix, 重 stands for something heavy or serious: 重工業 "heavy industry", 重傷 "serious injury", 重症 "serious illness". As a suffix after Sino-Japanese numbers it means "-fold": 二重 "double" (separate card), 三重 "triple". Not to be confused with 重/え (separate card), which counts layers with native Japanese number forms (一重, 八重); the adjective "heavy" is 重い.

examples[].german: Many people lost their homes in the disaster.
In this building, the first floor is a shop and the second floor is a residence.
en.notes: Formal word for a dwelling or place of residence, e.g. in forms and official language; in everyday speech 家 or 住まい.

examples[].german: The baggage may weigh up to twenty kilograms.
Heavy trucks cannot cross this bridge.
en.notes: Objective word for weight, e.g. for luggage and goods: 重量オーバー (overweight). In everyday speech: 重さ.

examples[].german: The driver was critically injured in the accident.
The patient was in critical condition for a while, but is recovering now.
en.notes: Mainly in accident reports: 意識不明の重体 (unconscious and in critical condition). Also written 重態. Homophone: 渋滞 (traffic jam).

examples[].german: My father is an executive at a bank.
All the company's senior executives attended the meeting.
en.notes: Member of a company's management: 重役会議 (board meeting). Today often 役員.

examples[].german: The phone rang, so I picked up the receiver.
After finishing the conversation, I quietly put down the receiver.
en.notes: The handset of a telephone: 受話器を取る (pick up), 受話器を置く (hang up).

en.meaning: department; faculty (suffix, e.g. 内科, 英文科); course of study; family (biology, e.g. ネコ科)
examples[].german: My fever wouldn't go down, so I saw an internal medicine doctor.
My older sister studies literature in the English department at university.
Lions and tigers are both members of the cat family.
en.notes: 〜科 is a productive suffix for specialist departments: in hospitals (内科 "internal medicine", 外科 "surgery", 小児科 "pediatrics"), at schools and universities for courses of study (英文科, 普通科), and in biology for families (ネコ科, バラ科). Do not confuse it with 課 (separate card), which denotes lessons and sections in companies and government offices; hospitals and universities have 科. Related is 学科 "department".

examples[].german: I was bitten by mosquitoes at night and couldn't sleep well.
In summer, mosquitoes come in when you open the window.
en.notes: A one-syllable noun; context distinguishes it from the question particle か. "To be bitten by a mosquito" is 蚊に刺される.

examples[].german: That region was under the influence of its neighboring country for a long time.
The workers continued the repairs under adverse conditions.
en.notes: 下 follows a noun that names a condition, an influence or a control. 影響下 means "under the influence", 悪条件下 "under adverse conditions". The whole word can state the circumstances of an action with で. This か attaches to the preceding word; it does not replace a standalone した as a spatial "under". The form is common especially in reports and factual texts.

examples[].german: Please be careful, there is a sharp curve ahead.
The pitcher struck him out with a curveball.
en.notes: A curve in the road (急なカーブ) and, in baseball, a pitch that curves.

en.meaning: cover; to cover for, make up for
examples[].german: Could you put a cover on this book for me?
A senior colleague covered for my mistake.
en.notes: Protective cover (本のカバー, スマホカバー); as a verb カバーする: to make up for a shortcoming (ミスをカバーする). Also a cover version of a song.

examples[].german: I put a hat on the child and went outside.
I covered the food with plastic wrap and put it in the refrigerator.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb related to かぶる: to place something over something (鍋にふたをかぶせる) or to put something on someone (子どもに帽子をかぶせる). Often in kana.

en.meaning: limit, bounds; as long as, as far as (〜限り); only (今日限り)
examples[].german: We will contact you as soon as possible.
As far as I know, he is still single.
This sale price is valid today only.
en.notes: 限り is the noun of 限る (vocab-n3:2501) and means "limit"; but it mostly follows verbs or nouns: できる限り "as much as possible", 私の知る限り "as far as I know", 〜ない限り "unless", 今日限り "today only". Fixed phrases are 限りない "boundless" and 限りある資源 "limited resources". As a grammar pattern it is often also written in kana (かぎり).

examples[].german: The meeting will open at ten in the morning.
The mayor gave the opening address.
en.notes: The start of an assembly: 開会式 (opening ceremony), 開会の挨拶. Opposite: 閉会.

examples[].german: A concert will be held at the city public hall.
The main hall of the building seats five hundred people.
en.notes: A building for meetings and events: 市民会館, 学生会館. Homophone: 快感 (pleasant sensation).

examples[].german: This rice was created through many years of cultivar improvement.
We plan to make further improvements to the product and release it next year.
The new model has better fuel economy thanks to engine improvements.
en.notes: 改良 refers to the improvement of products, processes or varieties, typical in 品種改良 "(selective) breeding", 改良を加える "to improve" and 改良の余地がある "to have room for improvement". The verb 改良する has its own card. Compared with 改善 "improvement (of conditions, procedures)", 改良 emphasizes the technical further development of a concrete object; 改革, by contrast, is the fundamental reform of a system.

examples[].german: The day of the sports festival was perfectly clear.
Tomorrow it will be clear across the country.
en.notes: Technically: a sky almost without clouds. Stronger than 晴れ. Homophone: 改正 (revision).

en.meaning: sea bathing; swimming in the sea
examples[].german: During the summer vacation, we went swimming in the sea as a family.
This beach opens in July.
en.notes: Swimming and bathing at the beach: 海水浴に行く, 海水浴場 (swimming beach).

examples[].german: The electricity rates will be revised next month.
An explanatory meeting for employees was held about the revision of the work regulations.
The railway company announced a fare revision.
en.notes: 改定 is the renewed setting of rules, prices, rates or laws, typical in 料金改定, 運賃改定, 価格改定 and 〜の改定を行う; 料金改定 is often a euphemism for a price increase. The verb 改定する has its own card. The identically read 改訂 (separate card), by contrast, means the revision of a text or book (改訂版 "revised edition"); 海底 "seabed" is merely a homophone.

en.meaning: opening (of a route); start of service
examples[].german: A new tunnel will open next month.
The road that had been closed by snow has finally reopened.
en.notes: When a road, railway line or line of communication goes into service: 新しい道路が開通する; also the reopening after a closure.

examples[].german: Tomorrow there is a kanji writing test.
We practiced with sentences the teacher read aloud, writing them down.
en.notes: Writing down what is heard or read; at school especially kanji writing (漢字の書き取り). Verb: 書き取る.

en.meaning: to scratch; to break out (a sweat); to shovel
examples[].german: I scratched the spot where a mosquito had bitten me.
Since the morning I have been shoveling the snow in front of the house.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 頭をかく (scratch one's head), 汗をかく (sweat), 雪をかく (shovel snow). Usually written in kana.

examples[].german: The taste of rice balls eaten on a mountaintop is exceptional.
This winter the cold is particularly severe.
en.notes: な-adjective and adverb: 格別な味, 格別おいしい. With negation: 格別～ない (not particularly).

examples[].german: I'm convinced that he is the culprit.
By continuing to practice, I came to feel sure I could pass.
Seeing that photo deepened my conviction.
en.notes: 確信 is the firm conviction that something is certainly so: 確信がある "to be sure", 確信を持つ "to be convinced", 確信が深まる "the conviction grows firmer". The content usually precedes with という (成功するという確信). The verb 確信する "to be firmly convinced" has its own card. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding 核心 "core (of a matter)" and 革新 "innovation".

examples[].german: May I open the window?
"Sorry for being late." "No, it's no problem."
en.notes: Polite form of 構わない (from 構う): 〜ても構いません = it's all right if .... Example: ここに座っても構いませんか.

examples[].german: I picked up the scraps of paper that had fallen on the floor and threw them in the trash can.
The company went bankrupt, and its shares became worthless.
en.notes: Discarded paper; often written 紙くず. Figurative: 紙くず同然 (worthless as scrap paper, e.g. shares).

examples[].german: I shaved my beard with a razor.
I cut my finger on the razor blade.
en.notes: Razor blade or razor; often in kana かみそり. Electric shaver: 電気かみそり／シェーバー.

examples[].german: One year after his injury, he made a splendid comeback.
The band's comeback after ten years became a topic of conversation.
en.notes: As a verb: カムバックする (to make a comeback).

en.meaning: the distance; the far side; beyond
examples[].german: The ship disappeared into the distance over the sea.
The sun set beyond the mountains.
en.notes: Literary: far away, on the other side: 山の彼方, 空の彼方. Often written in kana.

examples[].german: Old books are written in historical kana orthography.
The teacher corrected the kana orthography in my composition.
en.notes: The rules for how words are written in kana: 現代仮名遣い (present-day rules), 歴史的仮名遣い (older orthography, e.g. けふ for きょう).

examples[].german: I looked after the feverish child all night.
Thanks to my family's care, I recovered quickly.
en.notes: To nurse a sick person at home: 母を看病する. Professional nursing: 看護, elder care: 介護.

examples[].german: The batteries in the remote control have run out.
Go buy four AA batteries.
en.notes: Ordinary disposable battery: 単三乾電池 (AA battery). Rechargeable: 充電池.

examples[].german: Please heat it in the microwave for two minutes.
Please heat this meat thoroughly before eating.
en.notes: As a verb 加熱する: 電子レンジで加熱する. On packaging: 加熱してお召し上がりください (heat before eating).

examples[].german: Meeting my favorite player, I was moved to tears.
I still can't forget the emotion when my own book was first displayed in a bookstore.
I am filled with deep gratitude for everyone's warm support.
en.notes: Noun for the verb 感激する (separate card): a strong, joyful emotion, often triggered by kindness or a special experience. Fixed phrases are 感激のあまり "out of sheer emotion" and 感激の涙. In contrast to 感動 "being moved by art or achievement", 感激 emphasizes the personal, emotional surge.

examples[].german: Snow is expected in the Kanto region tomorrow.
Kanto and Kansai differ in seasoning.
en.notes: The region with Tokyo and the surrounding prefectures. Its counterpart in the west: 関西 (Kansai).

examples[].german: I looked up a kanji I couldn't read in a kanji dictionary.
In a kanji dictionary, you can look things up by radical.
en.notes: Mostly in 漢和辞典: a dictionary that explains kanji and kanji words in Japanese. Homophone: 緩和 (easing, relaxation).

examples[].german: I bought canned food in preparation for disasters.
Just before the deadline, the author is shut away in a hotel to write.
en.notes: Food in a can: ツナの缶詰. Figuratively: 缶詰になる (to be stuck somewhere, e.g. shut in to work).

en.meaning: to feel, to sense; to be moved (literary form of 感じる)
examples[].german: I sense deep sincerity in his words.
If he feels responsible, he should resign of his own accord.
I increasingly feel the changes of the times firsthand.
en.notes: The literary ずる-form of 感じる (separate card, N4) with the same meaning: to feel or perceive something or be moved by it (〜を感ずる, 〜に感ずる). It is found in essays, speeches and older literature; in conversation 感じる is used. Some forms coincide (感じて, 感じた); typical for writing are 感ずる, 感ずれば and 感ぜず.

en.meaning: to be mortified with shame; to turn bright red
examples[].german: I fell over in front of everyone and was so embarrassed I wanted to sink through the floor.
I called someone by the wrong name and was mortified.
en.notes: Literally "fire comes out of the face": extreme embarrassment, mostly as 顔から火が出るほど恥ずかしい. Mostly about one's own embarrassing moments.

examples[].german: Many houses collapsed in the earthquake.
An old Japanese-style house was renovated into a cafe.
en.notes: Written-language word, e.g. in news and official language: 家屋の被害, 日本家屋 (traditional Japanese house).

examples[].german: My younger sister is lively and loves playing outside.
A lively exchange of opinions took place at the meeting.
en.notes: な-adjective: 活発な子ども, 活発な議論 (lively discussion), 活発に活動する.

examples[].german: Please print these materials in color.
This school has a free-spirited character.
en.notes: Color (カラー印刷 = color printing) and the character of a group (チームカラー, 学校のカラー). Homophone: カラー (collar).

examples[].german: At New Year we played karuta as a family.
I took part in a Hyakunin Isshu karuta tournament.
en.notes: A traditional card game, especially at New Year: 百人一首のかるた. The word comes from Portuguese (carta).

examples[].german: I underlined the important parts.
Translate the underlined part into Japanese.
en.notes: A line under text: 下線を引く (to underline); in exams often 下線部 (the underlined part).

examples[].german: I used to listen to music on cassette.
As a child, I traded game cartridges with friends.
en.notes: Audio or video cassette; also a game cartridge for consoles (ゲームのカセット). In compounds also a cartridge: カセットコンロ (portable gas stove with a cartridge).

examples[].german: A sign reading "Room for rent" was posted in front of the house.
As a student I lived in a rented room in my landlord's house.
en.notes: A single room for rent; a rather old-fashioned word (today 貸し部屋 or an apartment). Sign: 貸間あり.

examples[].german: I'm looking for a house to rent near the station.
This rental house has a big garden, and the rent is cheap.
en.notes: An entire house for rent. Opposite in housing: 持ち家 (owned home).

examples[].german: I bought a whole chunk of meat at the supermarket and cut it myself.
He is a child who is brimming with curiosity.
en.notes: A solidly clumped mass: 肉の塊, 氷の塊. Figurative: 努力の塊 (the embodiment of diligence). Also written 固まり.

examples[].german: Products are displayed divided by category.
This movie doesn't fit into any category.
en.notes: Also written カテゴリ. 〜のカテゴリーに入る (to belong to the category of ...).

examples[].german: My older brother is in a doctoral program at graduate school.
At this school you complete the entire curriculum in three years.
en.notes: A fixed course of study or training: 博士課程 (doctoral program). Homophones: 過程 (process), 家庭 (family; household).

examples[].german: The old print shop still has metal type.
He gets restless if he isn't reading something in print.
en.notes: Originally printing type, now mainly printed text: 活字離れ (turning away from reading), 活字中毒 (bookworm; addicted to print).

en.meaning: on one's own; without permission; by itself
examples[].german: Please don't use other people's computers without asking.
The door shut by itself because of the wind.
en.notes: Without permission or without anyone doing anything: 勝手に使わないで (Don't just use it!); ドアが勝手に開いた (The door opened by itself). Noun: 勝手.

en.meaning: hot-tempered, quick to anger (カッとなる: to flare up in anger); suddenly glaring, scorching hot; (eyes, mouth) wide open
examples[].german: He is the type who flies off the handle easily.
The midsummer sun is blazing down fiercely.
Startled by the sound, he opened his eyes wide.
en.notes: An onomatopoeic adverb for something that flares up suddenly. Most common in カッとなる "to flare up in anger, to lose one's temper" (カッとなって言い過ぎた); also for glaring heat (太陽がカッと照りつける) and wide-open eyes (目をカッと見開く). Mostly written in katakana. Do not confuse with the loanword カット "cut"; similar but milder is むっとする "to be annoyed".

en.meaning: to love; to treat affectionately; to dote on
examples[].german: My grandmother dotes on her grandchildren.
The department head looks after the newcomers and often takes them out for meals.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 孫をかわいがる (spoil one's grandchildren), 部下をかわいがる (nurture subordinates). Kanji: 可愛がる.

en.meaning: family; house (suffix after a family name)
examples[].german: Tonight I am being treated to dinner at the Sato family's.
I am researching the history of the Tokugawa house.
en.notes: 家（け）is attached after a family name and denotes the family or house as a kinship group. 佐藤家 therefore means the Sato family, not just any house. With a historical family such as 徳川家, "house" can also mean a dynasty. The reading いえ for the building and the suffix か in 作家 are other usages.

examples[].german: I went to watch the horse races with my father at the weekend.
He lost a lot of money on horse racing.
en.notes: Horse racing with betting; the racecourse is called 競馬場. Other officially sanctioned racing bets: 競輪 (bicycle racing), 競艇 (boat racing).

examples[].german: The fluorescent light in the kitchen has burned out.
I replaced the fluorescent light with an LED.
en.notes: The classic ceiling light in Japanese offices and homes, now often replaced by LEDs. Colloquially also used for someone slow to react.

examples[].german: So many bus routes leave from the station square that it is hard to tell which bus to take.
I chose curtains in the same color family as the walls.
en.notes: A connected whole: バスの系統 (bus route), 電気系統 (electrical system), 同じ系統の色 (colors of the same group). Also means line of descent.

examples[].german: In Japan, you have the right to vote from age eighteen.
The copyright of this photograph belongs to the photographer.
At the meeting, the young employees took the initiative.
en.notes: 〜権 forms words for a right or authority: 選挙権 "right to vote", 著作権 "copyright", 所有権 "ownership right", 人権 "human rights". In the meaning "power, authority" it appears in 政権 "governing power" or 主導権 "initiative, leadership". The general word for "right" is 権利 (separate card); 権 itself appears almost only as a word component. Do not confuse it with the identically pronounced 〜県 and 〜圏.

examples[].german: Trains in the Tokyo metropolitan area are very crowded in the morning.
I want to study abroad in an English-speaking country.
In the Arctic region in summer, there are days when the sun doesn't set.
en.notes: 〜圏 forms words for a space or area defined by something: 英語圏 "English-speaking world", 首都圏 "Greater Tokyo area", 北極圏 "Arctic, Arctic Circle", 大気圏 "atmosphere". On a mobile phone, 圏外 means "no signal", 圏内 "within coverage". 圏 is hardly used alone; do not confuse it with the identically pronounced 〜県 "prefecture" and 〜権 "right".

examples[].german: I applied for a passport at the prefectural government office.
The prefectural office is about a ten-minute walk from the station.
en.notes: Administrative seat of a prefecture; the city where it is located is called 県庁所在地 (prefectural capital). In Tokyo, the equivalent is 都庁.

en.meaning: like cats and dogs; bitter enemies
examples[].german: Those two are bitter enemies; as soon as they meet, they start fighting.
Two companies that had long been enemies are going to cooperate this time.
en.notes: Literally "relationship of dog and monkey": in Japanese, dog and monkey are the proverbial enemies, not dog and cat. 犬猿 is read with the on-readings: けんえん.

examples[].german: The time is not yet ripe to announce the plan.
He waited for the right moment and made a new proposal to the president.
en.notes: On its own mainly in set phrases: 機が熟す (the time is ripe), 機を逃す (to miss the opportunity), 機を見る (to wait for the right moment). As a suffix also "machine" (洗濯機) and "aircraft" (旅客機).

examples[].german: A faint voice could be heard from the old telephone receiver.
In the experiment, the water was heated with an electric heater.
en.notes: 器（き）is here a nominal word-forming element at the end of names of devices, such as 受話器（じゅわき）for a telephone receiver or 電熱器（でんねつき）for an electric heater. In these compounds it is pronounced together with the preceding part. This card covers the device meaning; the standalone 器（うつわ）for a vessel and the elevated meaning "talent" are separate usages. The spellings 器 and 機 cannot be freely interchanged for devices.

examples[].german: Sales in this period increased compared with the previous period.
The construction work will be carried out in two phases.
en.notes: 期 here denotes a delimited period or phase. In business, この期 can refer to the accounting period under consideration; in a project, several phases are distinguished. The word also appears as a suffix, but the emphasis of this card is on the complete standalone word き. The fixed expression この期に及んで uses the other reading ご and does not belong to this reading.

examples[].german: There is a large military base on the island.
As a child, I built a secret hideout in the forest.
en.notes: Military base (米軍基地) or base of operations, e.g. 南極の観測基地 (research station in Antarctica), 秘密基地 (children's secret hideout).

examples[].german: This experiment requires a special apparatus.
Before the operation, the doctor checked the instruments one by one.
en.notes: Mostly smaller devices and instruments without their own power, for example in medicine, laboratories or sports (器械体操 = apparatus gymnastics). Large, powered machines are called 機械（きかい）.

examples[].german: An old locomotive is on display at the station.
The locomotive runs along pulling a long freight train.
en.notes: The engine that pulls cars: 蒸気機関車 (steam locomotive, SL for short), 電気機関車 (electric locomotive).

examples[].german: Long ago, great famines occurred many times in this region.
It did not rain, so there was an acute water shortage in summer.
en.notes: Famine after crop failures. Also figuratively a severe shortage: 水飢饉 (water shortage).

examples[].german: The mother dressed the baby in warm clothes.
He put the blame for his mistake on a subordinate.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb corresponding to 着る: 子どもに服を着せる (to dress a child). Figuratively: 罪を着せる (to pin a crime on someone).

examples[].german: Water turns into gas when heated.
This gas has neither color nor smell.
en.notes: A state of matter alongside 固体 (solid) and 液体 (liquid). Homophone: 期待 (expectation).

en.meaning: to be numb with cold; to freeze
examples[].german: While I waited outside, my hands went numb with cold.
On the freezing night, I was grateful for the warm soup.
en.notes: Intransitive ichidan verb for people and body parts that become stiff from the cold: 手が凍える. Water that freezes, by contrast, is 凍る.

examples[].german: My older brother works as a cook in a hotel restaurant.
The cook is wearing a white hat.
en.notes: A cook in Western-style restaurants (from Dutch "kok"); today often シェフ or 料理人. Homophone: コック (tap, valve).

examples[].german: My older brother attends a national university.
This art museum is state-run, so the admission fee is cheap.
en.notes: Founded and operated by the state: 国立大学, 国立公園, 国立博物館. Compare 県立 (prefectural), 市立 (municipal), 私立 (private).

examples[].german: This semester I am taking two Japanese classes.
Tonight I will cook dinner at home.
en.notes: 今（こん）stands here at the beginning of a time expression: 今学期 means this semester and 今晩 tonight. The meaning depends on the following element; with a longer span of time it refers to the current period, with a day expression to today. The independent 今（いま）meaning "now" has a different reading.

examples[].german: I wore a navy blue suit to the interview.
The school uniform is navy blue with a white stripe on the chest.
en.notes: A dark blue, typical for school uniforms and suits: 紺のスーツ. Also 紺色.

examples[].german: I ran into my teacher at the station the other day.
Thanks for the other day. I had a lot of fun.
en.notes: Colloquial form of この間（このあいだ）; very common in conversation. The kanji 此間 is obsolete.

examples[].german: When the two liquids are mixed, the color changes.
In this tournament, mixed teams of men and women compete.
en.notes: As a verb 混合する; attributively: 男女混合 (mixed, men and women), 混合物 (mixture).

examples[].german: My daughter won first place in a piano competition.
I practice every day for next month's competition.
en.notes: From French "concours"; mainly artistic competitions: ピアノコンクール, 作文コンクール.

examples[].german: My older sister is in a choir club at university.
Three people sang backing vocals behind the singer.
en.notes: Choir and part singing: コーラス部 (school choir club). Synonym, rather formal: 合唱.

examples[].german: This hiking trail is easy even for beginners.
For our anniversary, I reserved a set menu at a restaurant.
en.notes: A route (マラソンのコース), a course of study (初級コース) or a menu with several courses (フルコース). A lane in a swimming pool is also called コース.

examples[].german: My father's hobby is collecting old cameras.
The spring collection was unveiled in Paris.
en.notes: Collected items (切手のコレクション) and, in fashion, a season's new collection (春のコレクション).

examples[].german: I sat down on a bench in the park and rested.
I meant this job to be temporary, but it has already been ten years.
en.notes: A simple seat without a backrest, or a bench. Figuratively: a job one takes only temporarily (腰掛けの仕事).

examples[].german: Because I was tired, I sat down on a bench.
He sat down on the edge of the bed and began to talk.
en.notes: Ichidan verb: to sit on a chair or ledge (ベンチに腰掛ける). To sit on the floor is 座る.

en.meaning: to rub, to scrub, to scour
examples[].german: The child came up rubbing his sleepy eyes.
The burnt-on residue in the pot didn't come off even when I scrubbed hard with the sponge.
I scrubbed the dirt off the floor vigorously with a brush.
en.notes: An everyday verb for rubbing and scrubbing with pressure or a back-and-forth motion (目を擦る, 汚れを擦って落とす). It shares its kanji with 擦る/する (separate card), which stands mainly for "to strike a match" and "to gamble away money"; because of the double reading, こする is usually written in kana. Colloquially also "to rehash a joke or topic over and over" (ネタを擦る).

en.meaning: fixing; fastening; fixed (e.g. 固定給, 固定電話)
examples[].german: Recently, the number of households without a landline is increasing.
If you review fixed costs such as rent, you can reduce your monthly expenses.
A broken leg needs to be immobilized in a cast.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 固定する "to fasten" (vocab-n2:543), very common in compounds: 固定電話 "landline telephone", 固定費 "fixed costs", 固定給 "fixed salary", 固定観念 "fixed idea, stereotype". As a noun it takes の or が: ギプスでの固定, 固定が甘い "not properly fastened". The opposite is 変動 "fluctuation" (固定費 vs. 変動費).

examples[].german: The Tale of Genji is famous as a classic of Japanese literature.
In high school, classical Japanese was my worst subject.
en.notes: Old, authoritative works: 古典文学, 古典音楽 (classical music = クラシック). At school, 古典 is the subject "classical Japanese".

en.meaning: to leave a message (or item) with someone to pass on
examples[].german: I gave the letter to my mother and had her hand it to the teacher.
Since nobody was home, I left the package with the neighbor.
en.notes: Ichidan verb: to give someone a message or item to pass on to a third person. Noun: 言付け (message).

en.meaning: port, harbor (suffix in port names, e.g. 横浜港)
examples[].german: The ship arrives at Yokohama Port at eight o'clock in the morning.
Kobe Port has prospered on foreign trade since long ago.
Because of the typhoon, all ships leaving Hakata Port were canceled.
en.notes: The Sino-Japanese reading of 港 as a suffix after place names: 横浜港, 神戸港, 博多港. Used on its own, "harbor" is always 港（みなと）; こう appears only in compounds such as 空港 "airport", 漁港 "fishing port" or 入港 "entering port", while 港町 is read みなとまち. 島（とう）in island names works similarly.

en.meaning: high-, Hoch- (prefix, e.g. 高収入, 高価格); high school (suffix after school names, e.g. 〇〇高)
examples[].german: My father has high blood pressure, so he cuts back on salt.
A high-paying job isn't necessarily fun.
At Koshien, the local Kita High School advanced to the final.
en.notes: As a prefix, 高 means "high-": 高血圧 "high blood pressure", 高収入 "high income", 高性能 "high-performance". After a school name it is the short form of 高校 (separate card): 北高 "North High School", 〇〇高の生徒. To be distinguished from 高/たか "amount, sum" (売上高, separate card) and from the adjective 高い.

examples[].german: He bowed deeply and begged for forgiveness.
He came from far away to ask a famous teacher for instruction.
en.notes: Formal godan verb like 問う (te-form 請うて): 許しを請う (to beg forgiveness), 教えを請う (to ask for instruction). Also written 乞う.

en.meaning: school (suffix, e.g. 進学校, 母校); schools (counter, e.g. 全国200校); proof (初校, 再校)
examples[].german: My older brother attends a college-prep school that is well known even within the prefecture.
Forty-eight schools from across the country took part in this year's tournament.
Please check the first proofs by next week.
en.notes: A suffix for schools in words such as 母校 "alma mater", 出身校 "school one comes from", 進学校 "college-preparatory school", and a counter for schools (3校, 48校 with the sound change はっこう). In publishing it denotes the proofreading stage: 初校 "first proof", 再校 "second proof", cf. 校正 "proofreading". On its own, the word for "school" is 学校; do not confuse it with the identically pronounced suffix 〜港 "harbor".

examples[].german: Five hundred workers are employed at this factory.
When he was young, my father was a worker at a car factory.
en.notes: A worker in a factory; today often replaced by the more neutral 作業員 or 従業員.

examples[].german: The mayor is away on an overseas business trip on official duty.
I gave priority to my official duties and changed my personal plans.
en.notes: Duties in government or public offices: 公務員 (public servant), 公務で出張する (to travel on official business).

examples[].german: There is a legend that the stork brings babies.
In Toyooka city, efforts are being made to return storks to the wild.
A stork landed in the rice field.
en.notes: The rare kanji 鸛 is hardly used; こうのとり is usual, or as the animal name コウノトリ in katakana. As in Europe, the stork is regarded as the bringer of babies. Do not confuse with the crane 鶴 (つる), which symbolizes good fortune and long life in Japan.

examples[].german: Two roads cross here.
There is a railroad crossing where the tracks and the road intersect.
en.notes: Lines or paths cross: 交差する, 交差点 (intersection). Homophone: 考査 (examination).

examples[].german: Strong light is bad for the eyes.
The morning light is streaming in through the window.
en.notes: Rays of light, also in physics: 太陽光線 (sunbeams), レーザー光線 (laser beam).

examples[].german: The old school building will be demolished next year.
The new school building has an elevator.
en.notes: The building of a school; 新校舎 (new building), 旧校舎 (old school building). The school grounds are called 校庭 or キャンパス.

en.meaning: so; in this way; and so
examples[].german: And so the two of them ended up getting married.
If you practice a little every day like this, you will surely get better.
en.notes: Introduces the result in a narrative ("And so ...") or means "in this way". The kanji 斯うして is obsolete. Compare そうして, ああして.

examples[].german: Stop shouting in front of everyone.
The facility is open to the public free of charge.
en.notes: Mostly in compounds and set expressions: 公衆電話 (public telephone), 公衆トイレ (public toilet), 公衆の面前で (in full view of the public).

examples[].german: High-rise buildings are being built one after another in front of the station.
When high-altitude clouds spread, the weather often turns bad.
en.notes: Mostly attributive: 高層ビル (high-rise building), 高層マンション (high-rise apartment building), 高層の建物. In meteorology also "upper layers of the atmosphere" (高層の雲).

examples[].german: Children are playing in the schoolyard during break.
The schoolyard can't be used because of rain, so PE is held in the gym.
en.notes: The area in front of the school building for breaks, sports and ceremonies. Homophones: 肯定 (affirmation), 工程 (work process).

en.meaning: to poke one's nose into; to meddle
examples[].german: You'd better not poke your nose into other people's problems.
He wants to get involved in everything.
en.notes: Literally "to stick one's neck in". Mostly critical: to meddle in things that are none of one's business; less often neutral "to get deeply involved in something".

examples[].german: It was cold and my lips turned purple.
In winter, lips dry out easily.
en.notes: Upper lip: 上唇, lower lip: 下唇. Lipstick is called 口紅.

examples[].german: His explanation was so long-winded that I got sleepy halfway through.
This sauce is too sweet and a little heavy.
en.notes: I-adjective: someone repeats the same thing annoyingly often (説明がくどい) or a taste is too strong and heavy (くどい味). Kanji 諄い is rare.

examples[].german: I hammered a nail into the wall and hung a picture.
I pulled rusty nails out of the old board.
en.notes: Nails are driven in: 釘を打つ. Idiom: 釘を刺す (to warn someone firmly). Often also in kana くぎ.

en.meaning: to divide, to partition; to punctuate (sentences)
examples[].german: I divided the large room into two with a curtain.
Long sentences are easier to understand if you read them broken up by units of meaning.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 部屋を区切る (to partition a room), 文を区切って読む (to read a sentence in segments). Noun: 区切り (break, section).

en.meaning: to draw (water); to take into account (feelings)
examples[].german: In the past, we drew water from the well every morning.
Out of consideration for her feelings, I didn't ask anything.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 井戸の水を汲む (to draw water from a well). Figuratively: 気持ちを汲む (to sympathize with and take someone's feelings into account). Homophone: 組む (to put together).

en.meaning: by all means; without fail (in requests and greetings)
examples[].german: Please take good care of yourself.
Make sure you do not let these documents out of the building.
en.notes: Strengthens polite requests and greetings: くれぐれもお体に気をつけてください (please take good care of yourself), くれぐれもよろしくお伝えください.

examples[].german: I took my suit to the dry cleaner's.
After I had the coat cleaned, it looked like new.
en.notes: Usually professional cleaning: クリーニングに出す (to take to the cleaner's); the shop is called クリーニング屋.

examples[].german: I wrapped the baby in a warm blanket.
So that it wouldn't break, I wrapped the glass in newspaper.
en.notes: くるむ means "to wrap up, to swaddle". The object being wrapped takes を, the material takes で: 赤ちゃんを毛布でくるむ. This godan verb forms くるんで and くるんだ. 包む is also read くるむ here; the same kanji read つつむ can be a more general verb meaning "to wrap".

examples[].german: Before going out, I combed my hair.
My grandmother treasures an old wooden comb.
en.notes: "To comb one's hair": 髪を櫛でとかす. Often written in kana as くし; a brush is called ブラシ.

examples[].german: My grandmother came up with this dish through much painstaking effort.
After ten years of effort, the author completed the novel.
en.notes: Much effort and ingenuity put into something: 苦心の作 (a painstakingly produced work), 苦心して完成させる.

examples[].german: She wears a ring on the ring finger of her left hand.
I caught my ring finger in the door and hurt it.
en.notes: The fourth finger, on which the wedding ring is usually worn in Japan. The fingers: 親指, 人差し指, 中指, 薬指, 小指.

en.meaning: to get tired, to be worn out; to be worn (out)
examples[].german: I walked all day and am completely exhausted.
My father still uses his worn-out bag.
en.notes: Ichidan verb, more colloquial than 疲れる. Also for things worn out by long use: くたびれた靴. Kanji 草臥れる is rare.

en.meaning: to stick on, to attach; to put together (closely)
examples[].german: I glued the broken plate back together with adhesive.
For the group activity, we pushed four desks together.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb corresponding to くっつく (to stick): のりで紙をくっつける, 机をくっつける (to push desks together). More colloquial than 付ける.

examples[].german: A balloon is floating in the air.
The athlete did one rotation in the air and landed.
en.notes: The space above the ground: 空中に浮かぶ (to float in the air), 空中ブランコ (circus trapeze).

examples[].german: Because it was hot, I turned on the air conditioner in the room.
The air conditioner was set too cold, and I got chilled.
en.notes: In everyday use, an air conditioner for cooling (today usually called エアコン) and a cooler for drinks (クーラーボックス).

en.meaning: to hold in the mouth (or between the teeth)
examples[].german: The dog brought the newspaper in its mouth.
My father was talking with a cigarette in his mouth.
en.notes: Ichidan verb: 犬がボールを咥える (the dog carries the ball in its mouth), たばこを咥える. Also written 銜える. Homophone: 加える (to add).

examples[].german: Bread crumbs are lying on the table.
The factory also reuses metal scraps.
en.notes: Small leftovers and waste: 紙くず (scraps of paper), パンくず (bread crumbs). Often in kana くず. As an insult (人間のくず) it is very offensive.

examples[].german: I showed the guest into the reception room.
My grandfather's house has a large guest room.
en.notes: A room in a house where guests are received; in traditional houses often a tatami room (和室).

examples[].german: The seats filled up before the concert started.
When the singer waved, loud applause broke out from the audience.
en.notes: The seats for guests in a theater, stadium or restaurant, and figuratively the audience itself: 客席から拍手が起こった.

examples[].german: This campus has three libraries.
In spring, the campus becomes lively with new students.
en.notes: The grounds of a university. Many universities have several キャンパス in different parts of the city.

examples[].german: During the Cold War, that country belonged to the communist bloc.
The newspaper ran the headline "Communists double their seats".
After the war, that country rapidly became communist.
en.notes: Rarely stands alone, but mostly as a word element: 共産主義 "communism" (vocab-n2:21), 共産党 "Communist Party" (vocab-n3:3013), 共産圏 "Eastern bloc, communist bloc", 共産化 "communization". In newspaper headlines and election reports, 共産 stands alone as a short form for the Communist Party. The opposing concept is 資本主義 "capitalism".

examples[].german: Second period today is canceled.
The teacher was sick, so the class was canceled.
en.notes: A class is canceled; as a verb 休講する / 休講になる. Notices about it are posted on the 掲示板 (bulletin board) or sent via app.

examples[].german: The doctor told me to get plenty of rest.
After long work, you need rest.
en.notes: More formal than 休み or 休憩: sufficient rest, e.g. 十分な休息をとる.

examples[].german: The test result was so-so.
Now, now, don't get so angry.
en.notes: "Not good, not bad": 味はまあまあだ. As a soothing exclamation: まあまあ、落ち着いて (now, now, calm down).

examples[].german: The summer sunlight is dazzling.
When I opened the curtains, the morning sun was dazzling.
en.notes: I-adjective for glaring light, also figuratively radiantly beautiful: まぶしい笑顔. Kanji 眩しい.

en.meaning: to arrange to meet (at a place); to meet up
examples[].german: Let's meet at the ticket gate of the station at six.
I arranged to meet a friend, but he took a long time to come.
en.notes: To meet at a place at an agreed time: 駅で友達と待ち合わせる. Noun: 待ち合わせ (appointment to meet, meeting place).

examples[].german: There is a small flower shop on the street corner.
A TV station was asking people on the street for their opinions.
en.notes: The corner of a street, also generally "on the street": 街角インタビュー (street survey). Also written 町角.

en.meaning: flustered; at a loss (to stand around)
examples[].german: At a station I was visiting for the first time, I couldn't find the exit and wandered around confused.
If you dawdle like that, you'll miss the train.
en.notes: Not knowing what to do and hesitating awkwardly: 駅でまごまごする. Similar: おろおろ (anxiously), もたもた (dawdling).

en.meaning: every, each (prefix, e.g. 毎週末, 毎日曜, 毎朝)
examples[].german: Every weekend, our family goes to the nearby park.
Take one tablet of this medicine after every meal.
He scores a goal in practically every match.
en.notes: 毎〜 (まい) is a productive prefix "every, each" for regularly recurring times and events: 毎週末, 毎日曜, 毎試合, 毎食後. Frequent compounds such as 毎日 (vocab-n5:199), 毎朝 and 毎週 are learned as separate words. Not to be confused with the counter 枚 (まい) for flat objects.

examples[].german: This morning the temperature was minus three degrees.
Being late counts against you in an interview.
en.notes: The minus sign and sub-zero temperatures (マイナス五度), also figuratively a disadvantage: マイナスになる (to be detrimental). Opposite: プラス.

examples[].german: The house went pitch dark because of the power outage.
When I failed the exam, everything went black.
en.notes: Na-adjective: 真っ暗な部屋. Figuratively: 目の前が真っ暗になる (to see everything black, to despair).

examples[].german: When spring comes, let's sow seeds in the field.
I sowed flower seeds in the garden.
en.notes: To put seeds in the soil: 種を蒔く. Often written in kana as まく. Homophones: 撒く (to scatter, to sprinkle), 巻く (to wind).

examples[].german: Next month I will run a marathon for the first time.
I watched the broadcast of a marathon on TV.
en.notes: A long-distance run of 42.195 km, also long-distance running in general: マラソン大会 (marathon race, school run).

en.meaning: first of all; the very first
examples[].german: I told my mother the news of passing first of all.
In an earthquake, put out the fire first.
en.notes: Mostly as 真っ先に (first of all): 家に帰ると、真っ先に手を洗う.

examples[].german: Today the sky is deep blue without a single cloud.
When he heard about the accident, he turned deathly pale.
en.notes: Vivid blue (真っ青な空), but also pale in the face from fright: 顔が真っ青になる. Special reading まっさお.

examples[].german: When I got up in the morning, the garden was pure white with snow.
I was so nervous that my mind went blank.
en.notes: Na-adjective: 真っ白な雪. Figuratively: 頭が真っ白になる (to have a blackout). Also 真っ白い as an i-adjective.

en.meaning: to be settled, to come together; to be gathered; to be well organized
examples[].german: After a long discussion, opinions finally came together.
This class is well united.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: 話がまとまる (an agreement is reached), 考えがまとまる (one's thoughts get organized). Transitive: まとめる. The kanji 纏まる is rare.

examples[].german: There was construction, so I took a detour home.
I took a detour, but I'm glad I found my current job.
en.notes: A longer way than necessary: 回り道をする. Also figuratively a detour in life. Similar: 遠回り.

examples[].german: My brother's marriage has been decided; it is truly a happy occasion.
She happily passed the entrance exam of her first-choice university.
en.notes: For happy occasions (めでたい日, めでたく合格する). Polite: おめでたい. Ironically also "naive, gullible": おめでたい人.

examples[].german: The taxi meter keeps going up.
A staff member came to check the gas meter.
en.notes: A meter such as 電気のメーター or a taximeter (タクシーのメーター). As a unit of length, メートル is more usual.

examples[].german: I would like to make a reservation for two. Do you have seats?
Ten people took part in the information session.
en.notes: 名（めい）counts people in polite or formal statements, for example for a reservation or the number of participants. 二名です means "there are two of us"; with 十名 you state ten participants. In ordinary conversation 人（にん）is more common. Only the counter is practiced here, not 名 for a given name or the prefix in 名探偵.

en.meaning: to order; to command; to appoint
examples[].german: The company president issued a notice ordering all employees to reduce overtime.
He was appointed manager of the Osaka branch from April.
en.notes: Literary; same meaning as 命じる (N3), but conjugated on the ずる pattern (命ぜられる). Also "to appoint": 課長に命ずる.

examples[].german: With November, it has become noticeably colder.
My grandfather has aged markedly lately.
en.notes: For a clearly perceptible change, mostly with seasons or age: めっきり寒くなった.

en.meaning: measuring device; meter (usually メーター)
examples[].german: An old article says that a meter inspector examined the devices in each household.
An old manual says to check the gas meter every month.
en.notes: Besides the unit of length, メートル has an attested meaning as a measuring device or meter. For such devices メーター is usually used today, e.g. ガスメーター. The term メートル検査員 means someone who inspects measuring devices; here it contains no indication of a length. According to the dictionary, the rare spelling 米 can also carry this meaning. First practice the katakana form and pay attention to the context in older or technical texts.

en.meaning: -ness (nominalizing suffix on adjectives, e.g. 甘み, 痛み, 楽しみ)
examples[].german: These tomatoes are sweet and delicious.
After I took the medicine, my headache went away a little.
The president's words carry weight.
en.notes: Attaches to the stem of i-adjectives and forms nouns for a perceptible, felt quality: 甘み "sweetness", 痛み "pain", 重み "weight, significance", 深み "depth". In contrast to 〜さ, which names a measurable degree (甘さ, 重さ), 〜み emphasizes the impression; not every adjective forms a 〜み form. Mostly in kana; the spelling 甘味 is not to be confused with 味/み "taste" (separate card).

en.meaning: not yet, un- (prefix, e.g. 未成年, 未完成, 未解決)
examples[].german: Drinking alcohol by minors is prohibited by law.
The case is still unsolved.
The date of the next meeting has not yet been decided.
en.notes: A negating prefix before Sino-Japanese nouns for something that has not yet happened or been achieved: 未成年 "minor (underage)", 未完成 "unfinished", 未解決 "unsolved", 未定 "not yet decided". In contrast to 不〜 (不可能, impossible in principle) and 無〜 (無料, without something), 未〜 carries the nuance "but perhaps later". Typical of forms, signs and news.

examples[].german: I checked the route from the station to the venue on the map.
Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the post office?
en.notes: The sequence of roads to a destination: 道順を教える (to give directions).

examples[].german: This restaurant looks old, but the food is very good.
Despite his looks, he is strong.
en.notes: How something or someone looks from the outside: 見かけによらず (contrary to appearances). Proverb: 人は見かけによらない (appearances are deceiving).

en.meaning: to visit (the sick); to be hit by
examples[].german: I visited my grandfather, who is in the hospital.
The region was hit by heavy snow.
en.notes: To visit and comfort someone in the hospital: 入院中の友人を見舞う. Also "to be struck by something": 台風に見舞われる. Noun: お見舞い.

en.meaning: to be used to the sight; to be familiar
examples[].german: Even a familiar town looks different at night.
A person I had never seen was standing in front of the house.
en.notes: Often attributive: 見慣れた景色 (familiar scenery), 見慣れない人 (an unfamiliar face).

en.meaning: democracy, popular sovereignty; democratic (in compounds: 民主的, 民主化, 民主党)
examples[].german: Representatives should be chosen by democratic means.
In that country the military regime fell and democratization advanced.
In a democratic state, the people choose the government through elections.
en.notes: 民主 rarely stands alone; mostly it forms compounds such as 民主的 "democratic", 民主化 "democratization", 民主国家 "democratic state" and 民主主義 "democracy" (separate card). For the form of government itself, ordinary text uses 民主主義, not just 民主. It is also common in party names such as 自由民主党 or 立憲民主党.

examples[].german: Fifty millimeters of rain fell in one hour.
This screw has a diameter of three millimeters.
en.notes: Prefix meaning "one thousandth" (ミリグラム, ミリリットル) and short form of ミリメートル (mm).

examples[].german: Long ago, many shops lined this street.
I bought stamps at a nearby shop.
en.notes: A somewhat old-fashioned word for a small shop; today usually 店 or お店. Well known: 店屋物 (food delivered from a restaurant).

examples[].german: My mother made children's clothes with the sewing machine.
It has been a while since I used the sewing machine.
en.notes: Shortened from the English "(sewing) machine". ミシンをかける = to sew with the machine.

examples[].german: This battery lasts a long time, so it's good for traveling.
That fabric didn't last well and soon wore out.
en.notes: 持ち（もち）here, as an independent noun, refers to how long quality, function or effect is retained. 持ちがいい means "lasts long", 持ちが悪い "doesn't last long". The word is used for batteries, clothing or foods, for example. It does not denote an owner and is not an attached ending here. 保ち is an occasional spelling for this meaning. In context, it must be clear which property is being retained.

en.meaning: holding; possession; at one's expense (nominal ending)
examples[].german: This camera is heavy, so it isn't stable when held with one hand.
I carry two mobile phones, one for work and one for private use.
Today's lunch is on me.
en.notes: 持ち（もち）here refers to holding, using or owning, and to taking on a task or expense. After a noun it forms nominal compounds: 片手持ち "holding with one hand", 二台持ち "owning two devices" and 私持ち "at my expense". The particle follows the whole expression. 費用は私持ちだ names the person who pays. This card covers such nominal compounds, not the verb form 持ち from 持つ. The independent meanings "durability" and "tie (draw)" have separate cards.

examples[].german: A modern hotel has been built in front of the station.
We remodeled the tatami room to have a modern atmosphere.
en.notes: Na-adjective, often for style and design: モダンな建物. In everyday speech 現代的 is also common.

examples[].german: She works as a magazine model.
The new model of this car will be released next month.
en.notes: Several meanings: fashion model, model of a product (新しいモデル) and a model for a character (小説のモデル).

en.meaning: to massage, to knead; to rub
examples[].german: I massaged my tired mother's shoulders.
I rubbed the paper in my hands to soften it.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 肩を揉む (to massage the shoulders). Idiom: 気を揉む (to worry).

examples[].german: Please write the answer to question 1 on the blackboard.
The test has 50 questions in total, with a time limit of 60 minutes.
It was difficult, and I could only solve three out of ten questions.
en.notes: 〜問 counts questions and exam problems: 一問, 二問, 三問, 十問 etc.; also 第1問 "question 1", 全20問 "20 questions in total" and the phrase 一問一答 "question and answer". 問 hardly stands alone; the noun for question is 問い (separate card) or 問題. Do not confuse it with 門/もん "gate" (separate card).

en.meaning: to tell; to testify to, to show
examples[].german: My grandmother quietly told of her experiences during the war.
These old tools tell of the lives of people in the past.
en.notes: Often figurative: things "tell" something, i.e. they bear witness to it: この写真が当時の生活を物語っている.

examples[].german: I measured the length of the paper with a ruler.
You should not judge people only by your own yardstick.
en.notes: A ruler for measuring, figuratively a standard for judgments: 自分の物差しで人を判断する.

examples[].german: There was a tremendous noise outside.
The station was full of people, an incredible number.
en.notes: Intensified form of すごい: ものすごい音, ものすごく速い. Kanji 物凄い.

examples[].german: On Sunday I took a mock exam for the university entrance exam.
The result of the mock exam was good, which reassured me a little.
en.notes: Short for 模擬試験, e.g. before entrance exams: 模試を受ける. Homophone: もし (if).

examples[].german: Maybe he has already gone home.
This plan may possibly fail.
en.notes: Expresses a weak supposition, often with かもしれない: もしかすると雨になるかもしれない. Same meaning: もしかしたら.

examples[].german: This weekend there are various events in the park.
Many families gathered for the city event.
en.notes: A public event or celebration: 夏の催し, 催し物. Verb: 催す (to hold an event).

examples[].german: I'm looking for a plain white shirt.
Plain items are easier to match than patterned ones.
en.notes: Fabric or paper without a pattern: 無地のシャツ. Opposite: 柄物 (patterned).

examples[].german: Purple flowers are blooming beautifully.
If you mix red and blue, you get purple.
en.notes: A color word used as a noun: 紫の花, 紫色. Traditionally a noble color in Japan. A mixed color of red and blue.

examples[].german: Countless stars were shining in the night sky.
There are countless answers to this question.
en.notes: Mostly as 無数の + noun or 無数に: 無数の星 (countless stars).

examples[].german: From the station to my house, a gentle slope continues.
The graph is rising gradually.
en.notes: な-adjective: gently inclined (なだらかな坂, なだらかな丘) or running without breaks (なだらかな曲線). Mostly in hiragana.

examples[].german: Please speak quietly inside the building.
I got the necessary furniture within the budget.
en.notes: 内（ない）is attached directly to a noun and denotes its interior or limits. 館内 means inside a building; 予算内 means within the budget. The context may be spatial or concern a fixed limit. After the compound comes the appropriate particle, such as 館内では or 予算内で. The reading うち and ない meaning "not existing" are separate words.

examples[].german: This bag is made of nylon and is light.
Nylon rope is strong and hard to break.
en.notes: Synthetic fiber, e.g. for bags, stockings and ropes: ナイロンのバッグ.

examples[].german: You can reach the accounting department at extension 120.
Could you call the section chief on the internal line?
en.notes: Internal telephone line in companies and offices: 内線番号 (extension number), 内線で呼ぶ. Opposite: 外線 (outside line).

examples[].german: He lost his mother last year.
A woman who had lost her husband in an accident spoke about her experience.
en.notes: To lose a person through death: 父を亡くす. Losing objects is written 無くす.

examples[].german: A row of trees continues along the street in front of the station.
In autumn, the trees lining the street turn yellow.
en.notes: Trees along a road: 桜並木 (row of cherry trees), 並木道 (tree-lined avenue).

examples[].german: Do you remember the license plate of the car that caused the accident?
At the venue, each participant was assigned a number.
en.notes: Number in general (ナンバーを振る = to number) and short for ナンバープレート (car license plate): 車のナンバー.

examples[].german: Japan is a country that is long from north to south.
This road runs north-south through the town.
en.notes: The north-south axis: 南北に長い国 (a country with great north-south extent). In Japanese the order is "south-north". Compare 東西 (east and west).

examples[].german: On the application form, please write something like "graduated from so-and-so University".
What, an interesting story? Tell me too.
en.notes: Placeholder for unspecified things (何々という店 = a shop called so-and-so) and an eager question: なになに？(What? Tell me!).

en.meaning: really, extremely; (with negation) not at all
examples[].german: No matter what that person says to me, it doesn't bother me at all.
This scenery is truly beautiful.
en.notes: With a negative, "not at all": なんとも思わない (to not care); without a negative, "really, extremely": なんとも美しい. Set phrase: なんとも言えない (indescribable; hard to say).

examples[].german: I rang the doorbell, but nobody came out.
The car behind us honked its horn.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 鳴る: ベルを鳴らす (to ring the bell), クラクションを鳴らす (to honk the horn). Figuratively: 警鐘を鳴らす (to sound a warning).

examples[].german: We decided to follow our seniors' way of doing things.
A new system was created following the example of other countries.
en.notes: To follow a model: 前例に倣う (to follow a precedent), 右に倣え (right dress!). Not to be confused with 習う (to learn).

examples[].german: The tree in the garden bore lots of persimmons.
These tomatoes bear fruit in summer.
en.notes: Fruit growing on a plant: 実が生る, 柿が生る. Mostly written in hiragana; not to be confused with なる (to become).

examples[].german: Think about what you ought to do.
Faced with the torrential rain, people were helpless.
en.notes: Elevated word for "to do": 為すべきこと (what must be done), 為す術がない (to be unable to do anything). In everyday speech する is used.

examples[].german: Even though we had just met, I was asked about my family in great detail.
The reporter asked question after question about the incident.
en.notes: Literally "digging up roots, digging up leaves". Almost always with 聞く／尋ねる and slightly reproachful: to question someone nosily.

examples[].german: I tightened the screw with a screwdriver.
I wound up the old clock.
en.notes: Screw: ねじを締める (to tighten), ねじを緩める (to loosen); also the spring of a clock mechanism (ねじを巻く = to wind up). Often also written ネジ.

examples[].german: I received a necklace from my mother for my birthday.
Today I am wearing a white necklace.
en.notes: Neck jewelry; ネックレスをする／つける (to wear, to put on).

examples[].german: I grow vegetables in a garden the size of a cat's forehead.
In Tokyo, even a tiny plot of land is expensive.
en.notes: Literally "cat's forehead": a very small area, said especially modestly about one's own garden or plot of land.

en.meaning: to put on an act; to act innocent; to play the innocent
examples[].german: In front of the teacher, she acts all well-behaved.
At first he put on an act, but gradually his true nature showed.
en.notes: Literally "to put a cat over oneself": to hide one's true nature behind a well-behaved, gentle facade. Often said of someone who behaves quite differently in front of strangers or superiors than usual. Noun: 猫かぶり.

examples[].german: I changed into my nightclothes and got into the futon.
At the ryokan, a yukata is provided as nightwear.
en.notes: Clothing for sleeping; also written 寝巻き. Western-style pajamas are usually called パジャマ.

examples[].german: Work is very busy at the end of the fiscal year.
In Japanese schools, the new school year begins in April.
en.notes: In Japan, the fiscal and school year usually runs from April 1 to March 31: 今年度 (this fiscal year), 来年度 (next fiscal year), 年度末 (end of the fiscal year).

examples[].german: Heat the frying pan well before adding the oil.
He is quick to get enthusiastic and quick to lose interest.
en.notes: Written-style word for "to heat": フライパンを熱する, 熱した油. Figuratively: 熱しやすく冷めやすい (quick to get enthusiastic, quick to cool off).

examples[].german: The rooms in this inn are Japanese-style; you sleep on tatami.
Even overseas, there are companies that adopt Japanese-style management.
en.notes: 式 = way, style: 日本式のトイレ (Japanese-style squat toilet), 日本式の経営. Similar: 和式.

examples[].german: Please refrain from alcohol during pregnancy.
My older sister is now five months pregnant.
I'm worried about when to tell my workplace about the pregnancy.
en.notes: The noun for pregnancy or conception, factual and medical: 妊娠中, 妊娠三か月, 妊娠検査. Related are 妊婦 (にんぷ, "pregnant woman") and 出産 ("childbirth"). The verb "to become pregnant" (妊娠する) is taught by the card 妊娠する.

examples[].german: I can't readily believe that story.
Suddenly the sky grew dark.
en.notes: な-adjective: にわか雨 (sudden rain shower), にわかには信じられない (hard to believe right away). Also "newcomer who only briefly joins in" (にわかファン).

en.meaning: ascent; up direction (toward Tokyo or the line's starting point)
examples[].german: Up trains toward Tokyo come every ten minutes.
From here on, there is a steep climb.
en.notes: Opposite of 下り: 上り坂 (uphill slope), 上りの電車 (train toward Tokyo or the line's starting station), 上り線 (up line).

examples[].german: I want that guitar desperately.
Every company is desperate to get experienced personnel.
en.notes: Literally "a hand comes out of the throat": such great desire that one wants to reach out for it. Mostly used as 喉から手が出るほど欲しい.

en.meaning: to move aside, to remove, to exclude; (...てのける) to pull off something boldly/in spite of difficulties
examples[].german: I cleared the things off the desk and spread out the map.
He pulled off that difficult job all by himself.
Please set aside the damaged goods.
en.notes: Transitive verb: to clear something out of the way or to set aside (荷物を退ける, 不良品を除けておく). As an auxiliary verb after the て-form, then mostly in kana, it expresses that one boldly accomplishes something difficult (やってのける, 言ってのける). The identically written but different word is 退ける/しりぞける "to repel, to reject"; in everyday speech どける is more usual for "to clear away", and 除ける/よける means "to dodge".

examples[].german: I cut the board in half with a saw.
Be careful of your hands when using a saw.
en.notes: A tool for sawing; Japanese saws cut on the pull stroke. The kanji 鋸 is rare.

en.meaning: without leaving any; without exception; all
examples[].german: The children ate up all of the food.
Every single member of the class took part.
en.notes: Nothing is left over: 一人残らず (every single person), 残らず食べる (to eat everything).

examples[].german: I glued the photo into my notebook.
I had my shirt starched at the dry cleaner's.
en.notes: Adhesive for paper: 糊で貼る (to glue on); also starch for laundry (シャツに糊をつける). Homophone: 海苔 (seaweed).

examples[].german: I fell asleep and rode past my stop.
If you rode past your stop, please pay the fare at the fare adjustment machine.
en.notes: If you travel farther than your ticket covers, you pay the difference at the 精算機 (fare adjustment machine): 乗り越し料金.

examples[].german: He works so slowly that he is always doing overtime.
This computer is old and slow to respond.
The tortoise walks slowly, but it did not rest until the end.
en.notes: A colloquial i-adjective for "slow, sluggish", mostly in kana: 仕事がのろい, 足がのろい, 動きがのろい; sounds more disparaging than 遅い. Also "slow-witted" (頭の回転がのろい). The same spelling 鈍い read にぶい (separate card) rather means "dull, insensitive" (鈍い痛み, 勘が鈍い). Do not confuse with the homophone 呪い "curse"; the adverb のろのろ is related.

examples[].german: When you are tired, your work efficiency drops.
The new machine has increased work efficiency.
en.notes: How much work gets done in a given time: 能率が上がる／下がる (efficiency rises/falls), 能率的 (efficient). Similar: 効率.

examples[].german: Agricultural production is thriving in this region.
At the roadside station you can buy local farm products.
en.notes: Products of farming (rice, vegetables, fruit). Compare 水産物 (marine products).

examples[].german: The number of young people in farming villages is decreasing.
My grandparents live in a small farming village.
en.notes: A community shaped by agriculture: 農村地帯 (rural area). Counterpart: 都市 (city).

examples[].german: These vegetables were grown without pesticides.
Using too many pesticides is bad for the environment.
en.notes: Chemical agents in agriculture: 農薬を使う (to use pesticides), 無農薬の野菜 (pesticide-free vegetables).

examples[].german: My wife is good at cooking.
If I come home late, my wife gets angry with me.
en.notes: A casual, somewhat old-fashioned word a man uses for his own wife: うちの女房. More neutral: 妻; for someone else's wife: 奥さん.

examples[].german: Oh, are you going out now?
I'm looking for a place that's perfect for a weekend outing.
en.notes: Polite noun from 出かける: お出かけですか (Are you going out?). Also an outing: 週末のお出かけ.

examples[].german: My little brother scared me from behind.
Don't scare me like that, I thought my heart would stop.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to scare someone (後ろからおどかす) or to threaten. The kanji 脅かす is also read おびやかす (to endanger).

en.meaning: oil (motor oil, cooking oil, care oil)
examples[].german: I changed the oil in my car.
I poured olive oil over the salad.
en.notes: Often for motor or cosmetic oil: エンジンオイル, オリーブオイル. General word: 油.

examples[].german: Would you like another helping of rice?
It was delicious, so I had a second helping of soup.
en.notes: Another portion of the same food or drink: ご飯のお代わり. As a verb お代わりする. Often written in kana.

examples[].german: "I hurt my foot and can't go on the trip." "I'm sorry to hear that."
Poor thing, he came down with a fever on the day of the exam.
en.notes: Sympathy for another person's misfortune: それはお気の毒に. Not for one's own mistakes (for that, すみません). From the noun 気の毒 (pitiable).

en.meaning: Thank you for waiting; here you are (after a wait)
examples[].german: Here you go, thanks for waiting. Two ramen.
Thanks for waiting. Now, let's go.
en.notes: A friendly, casual apology for keeping someone waiting, e.g. when serving in a restaurant. More formal: お待たせしました.

en.meaning: visit (to a shrine, temple or grave)
examples[].german: At New Year we went to the shrine as a family to pray.
At Obon we visit my grandfather's grave.
en.notes: Praying at a shrine, temple or grave: お墓参り (grave visit), 神社にお参りする.

examples[].german: Today is a happy day: my sister's wedding.
Believing a story like that, you really are naive.
en.notes: An occasion for congratulations: おめでたい日 (a joyous day); おめでた = pregnancy/birth. Ironic: gullible (おめでたい人).

examples[].german: On my trip I ran into someone unexpected.
My mother was delighted with the unexpected present.
en.notes: い-adjective: 思いがけない出会い (an unexpected encounter). Adverb: 思いがけなく.

en.meaning: to one's heart's content; with all one's strength; resolve
examples[].german: When the exams are over, I want to play to my heart's content.
I kicked the ball as hard as I could.
en.notes: Adverb meaning "as much as one can": 思い切り泣く, 思い切り遊ぶ; colloquially 思いっきり. As a noun: resolve (思い切りがいい).

examples[].german: This box is so heavy that I can't carry it alone.
A heavy atmosphere hung over the meeting room.
en.notes: Spoken variant of 重い, stressing the felt weight; also for mood: 重たい空気.

en.meaning: honorific prefix in formal words (prefix, e.g. 御社, 御中, 御礼)
examples[].german: I would like to hear more details about your company's new service.
On an envelope addressed to a company, one writes "Attn: Personnel Department".
We sincerely thank you for your continued patronage.
en.notes: 御 with the reading おん is a particularly formal honorific prefix that today occurs almost only in fixed words of business and letter language: 御社 "your company" (spoken), 御中 as an address suffix for companies or departments, 御礼 (おんれい) in 御礼申し上げます. Otherwise 御 is read お (vocab-n5:correction:o-honorific-prefix, before native Japanese words) or ご (vocab-n5:correction:go-honorific-prefix, before Sino-Japanese words); おん is not productive. In writing, 貴社 is usually used for "your company".

en.meaning: Messrs.; Dear Sirs (addressee suffix for a company or department)
examples[].german: I wrote "Sales Department" on the envelope.
When addressing a letter to a company, you add 「御中」.
en.notes: Placed after the name of a company or department on letters: 〇〇株式会社 御中. For individuals, use 様 instead. Do not combine the two.

examples[].german: I'm growing tomatoes in a greenhouse.
Tropical flowers were blooming in the greenhouse of the botanical garden.
en.notes: A heated house for plants. Figurative: 温室育ち (raised in a sheltered, pampered way). Greenhouse effect: 温室効果.

examples[].german: Trains stopped because of yesterday's heavy rain.
At the end of the year, the whole family did a big cleaning.
