The main street in front of the station was overflowing with shoppers.
en.notes: 大〜 with the Japanese reading おお means "big, strong, main" and stands mainly before native Japanese words (大雨, 大雪, 大通り, 大喜び), but also in fixed words such as 大掃除 and 大勢. Before Sino-Japanese words 大/だい (separate card) is usual, e.g. 大問題, 大成功; some words have たい (大会, 大切). There is no firm rule, so it is best to learn the reading with each word.

examples[].german: It was bitterly cold this morning, so I went out wearing a thick overcoat.
I inherited this overcoat from my grandfather.
en.notes: オーバーコート is a loanword from English "overcoat" and denotes a long, warm winter coat worn over a suit or other clothing. Today one usually simply says コート. The short form オーバー (vocab-n3:correction:oobaa) is a separate card and mostly means "excessive"; the spelling オーバコート is rare.

examples[].german: If you go out to the main street, you can find a taxi right away.
A new shop has opened across the main street.
en.notes: A large, wide street in a city. Opposite: 路地 (alley).

examples[].german: This factory runs almost entirely on automation.
As automation advanced, jobs for people decreased.
en.notes: Automated production: 工場のオートメーション化. Today also often 自動化.

examples[].german: There was an organ in the elementary school classroom.
I listened to a pipe organ performance at the church.
en.notes: Also the harmonium (足踏みオルガン) common in Japanese schools. Large church organ: パイプオルガン.

en.meaning: before you; ahead of you; (I'm leaving) ahead of you
examples[].german: Please, go in first.
Well then, I'll start eating before you.
en.notes: Polite: お先にどうぞ (After you, please). When leaving work: お先に失礼します (I'll be heading out now).

examples[].german: A stylish cafe has opened in front of the station.
I dressed up a little for the party.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun: おしゃれな服 (stylish clothes), おしゃれをする (to dress up). The kanji お洒落 is rare.

examples[].german: There are two housekeepers in that house.
The housekeeper cleans for us every day.
en.notes: Polite term for a hired housekeeper. Today often 家事代行 (housework service).

examples[].german: Please show the guest to the reception room.
I was so busy receiving visitors that my work didn't progress.
en.notes: Receiving visitors, mostly in compounds: 応接室 (reception room), 応接間.

examples[].german: The staff at that shop treat customers very well.
The new employees are practicing answering the phone.
en.notes: How one deals with customers, callers or visitors: 電話の応対, 客に応対する.

en.meaning: to respond to, to answer, to comply with (literary form of 応じる)
examples[].german: Our company is prepared to meet our customers' requests.
The culprit did not respond to negotiations with the police and remained barricaded.
The company president stated that he has no intention of responding to press interviews.
en.notes: The literary ずる-form of 応じる (separate card, N3) with the same meaning: to respond to a request, demand or invitation (〜に応ずる). Typical in official, corporate and news language, e.g. 要求に応ずる or 取材に応ずる; the written negative is 応ぜず. In conversation 応じる is almost always used.

examples[].german: This shop is closed every Monday.
Well then, good night. See you tomorrow.
en.notes: Polite noun for 休み (明日はお休みです = Tomorrow is a day off) and the short good-night greeting おやすみ (more polite: おやすみなさい).

examples[].german: For the trip I packed three pairs of underpants and three pairs of socks.
White pants have been in fashion lately.
en.notes: Traditionally underpants; in fashion also (women's) trousers (ワイドパンツ). Trousers in general are otherwise called ズボン.

en.meaning: suddenly, in a flash; striking, brilliant (ぱっとしない: unremarkable, mediocre)
examples[].german: When his name was called, he stood up at once.
When I turned on the light, the room suddenly brightened.
The weather hasn't been great lately, has it?
en.notes: An onomatopoeic adverb for something that happens or spreads suddenly: ぱっと立ち上がる "to jump up", ぱっと明るくなる "to suddenly brighten", ぱっと見 "at first glance". With する it means "to be striking, splendid", almost only negated as ぱっとしない "unremarkable, lackluster, mediocre". Often also written in katakana パッと. The rare ばっと feels more violent; さっと emphasizes the quick, smooth movement.

examples[].german: I cut the wire with pliers.
Can you get me the pliers from the toolbox?
en.notes: A tool for gripping and cutting wire; a loanword from the English "pinchers".

examples[].german: Stars are twinkling in the night sky.
The new shoes are so shiny that it feels a waste to wear them.
I did a big cleaning and made the kitchen sparkling clean.
en.notes: ぴかぴか (also ピカピカ) describes repeated sparkling or shining (ぴかぴか光る) and something polished spotless or brand-new (ぴかぴかの車, ピカピカにする). As an adjective it takes の, だ or で; ぴかぴかの一年生 is a "brand-new first-grader". ぴかっと, by contrast, denotes a single flash, きらきら rather a gentle glitter.

examples[].german: When spring comes, pink cherry blossoms bloom.
My older sister is wearing a pink sweater.
en.notes: A color word used as a noun: ピンクのシャツ, ピンク色. Traditional equivalent: 桃色（ももいろ）. In some compounds ピンク also hints at the erotic.

examples[].german: The starting pistol went off.
In Japan, owning a pistol is in principle prohibited.
en.notes: Handgun; in sports also the starting pistol (スタートのピストル). General term for firearms: 銃.

examples[].german: The weather forecast was exactly right.
The child's crying stopped abruptly.
en.notes: Something fits exactly (予想がぴたりと当たる), sits snugly or stops abruptly (雨がぴたりとやむ). Mostly with と; similar to ぴったり.

examples[].german: There was a concert poster at the station.
I put a poster of my favorite movie on the wall of my room.
en.notes: A placard for advertising or information, also a poster as wall decoration: ポスターを貼る (to put up).

examples[].german: Many people are waiting for the train on the platform.
Please do not walk along the edge of the platform, as it is dangerous.
en.notes: Full form; in everyday speech usually shortened to ホーム. Track number: 〜番線.

examples[].german: The teacher handed out the homework worksheets.
I printed the photos at a convenience store.
en.notes: In schools, a handed-out worksheet (プリントを配る); also printing and a printout (写真をプリントする).

en.meaning: visit to Japan; arrival in Japan
examples[].german: A famous singer will come to Japan next month.
It has been three years since I came to Japan, but I'm still bad at keigo.
en.notes: As a verb, 来日する - for foreigners coming to Japan: 大統領が来日する. Opposite: 離日.

examples[].german: I had lunch at a restaurant near the office.
The lunch at this restaurant is 1,000 yen and comes with coffee.
en.notes: Lunch, especially at a restaurant: ランチメニュー, 日替わりランチ (daily lunch special). Neutral: 昼ご飯.

examples[].german: I go running in the park every morning.
Because it was hot, I slept in just a tank top.
en.notes: Running as a sport: 毎朝ランニングをする. Also short for a sleeveless undershirt (ランニングシャツ).

examples[].german: Trains during rush hour are very crowded.
To avoid the rush hour, I left home early.
en.notes: The time of heaviest commuter traffic; often shortened to ラッシュ: 朝のラッシュ.

examples[].german: On rainy days, I wear a raincoat when riding my bicycle.
I bought a yellow raincoat for my child.
en.notes: A coat against rain; also 雨がっぱ (rain cape) or, for short, カッパ.

examples[].german: During summer vacation, we enjoyed leisure activities as a family.
There are many leisure facilities in this area.
en.notes: Leisure time and outings: レジャー施設 (leisure facility), 夏のレジャー.

examples[].german: On the company trip, there was a recreation period in the evening.
This park is ideal for recreation.
en.notes: Group games and activities for relaxation, for example at companies or schools: レクリエーションの時間. Also written レクリェーション.

examples[].german: Tokyo Station is built of brick.
I lined up bricks in the garden and made a flower bed.
en.notes: Fired clay block for building: れんが造りの建物. Kanji 煉瓦, often also written レンガ.

examples[].german: Several small political parties formed an alliance.
Neighboring towns joined together and held a festival.
en.notes: Union of states or groups: 国際連合 (United Nations), 欧州連合 (EU). Verb: 連合する.

examples[].german: I wiped the camera lens with a cloth.
The lens of my glasses got scratched.
en.notes: Glass lens in cameras or glasses; コンタクトレンズ (contact lens).

examples[].german: I tied a red ribbon around the present.
My daughter is wearing a ribbon in her hair.
en.notes: A ribbon for gifts or hair: プレゼントにリボンをかける.

examples[].german: In science class we observed plants.
My younger brother is good at science.
en.notes: School subject covering physics, chemistry, biology and earth science (地学). The science track in high school and university is called 理系 (opposite: 文系).

examples[].german: A reporter is reporting live from the scene.
Please submit the lab report by next week.
en.notes: Alternative spelling of レポート; especially common for TV reportage (現地からのリポート).

examples[].german: This plastic bottle holds two liters.
How many liters of hot water does the bathtub hold?
en.notes: Unit of measurement for liquids (L). For how to count, see the counter リットル.

en.meaning: argument, discussion; theory, doctrine; treatise (also suffix: 進化論, 文化論)
examples[].german: Proof is better than argument. Let me show you by actually doing it.
Darwin's theory of evolution had a great influence on biology.
There are various views on that problem.
en.notes: As a noun, 論 means "argument, view, thesis" (様々な論がある, 論を立てる) and belongs more to written and technical language; well known is the proverb 論より証拠 "proof counts more than words". More often it is a suffix for theories and treatises: 進化論, 文化論, 日本人論. For debate or dispute use 議論 or 論争, for the conclusion 結論, and for theory in general 理論.

examples[].german: This book discusses Japan's educational problems.
The merits and demerits of that proposal need no discussion.
en.notes: Literary; same meaning as 論じる (N3), but conjugated on the ずる pattern. Idiom: 論ずるまでもない (goes without saying, needs no discussion).

examples[].german: Please write your name in the Latin alphabet.
On a computer, you type Japanese in romaji.
en.notes: Japanese in Latin letters, e.g. for names or computer input (ローマ字入力).

en.meaning: -power, -ability, -strength (suffix, e.g. 経済力, 想像力, 能力)
examples[].german: In economic power, this country is among the world's leading.
Children's imagination truly amazes me.
I'm tired and can't keep my concentration up.
en.notes: 〜力 (りょく) is the Sino-Japanese suffix reading of 力 and forms words for abilities and strength: 経済力, 想像力, 集中力, 説得力, 影響力. As an independent word, 力 is read ちから (vocab-n4:1398). In some words the suffix is りき, e.g. 馬力, 自力, 他力.

en.meaning: both (prefix, e.g. 両手, 両親); car (counter, e.g. 十両編成)
examples[].german: It's heavy, so please hold it with both hands.
Cherry trees line both sides of the road.
This train has ten cars.
en.notes: 両〜 stands before pairs and means "both": 両手 "both hands", 両親 "parents", 両側 "both sides", 両国 "both countries". After a number, 〜両 counts railway cars (十両編成 "a train of ten cars"). The standalone noun for "both" is 両方; 量 "quantity" and 寮 "dormitory" are differently written words with the same reading.

examples[].german: I live in a university dormitory.
This company has a dormitory for single employees.
en.notes: A dormitory for students or employees: 学生寮, 社員寮. Similar sounding: 量, 両.

en.meaning: fee; charge (suffix, e.g. 入場料); material (suffix, e.g. 材料)
examples[].german: The admission fee for this art museum is 1,000 yen.
Shipping is free if you buy 3,000 yen or more.
University tuition goes up every year.
en.notes: 〜料 forms words for fees: 入場料 "admission", 授業料 "tuition", 送料 "shipping costs", 手数料 "handling fee"; also 無料 "free of charge" and 有料 "paid". In 材料 and 調味料 it means "stuff, material". Similar suffixes are 〜代 (電気代), 〜費 (交通費) and 〜賃 (家賃); 料 hardly stands alone.

en.meaning: territory, domain (suffix, e.g. アメリカ領)
examples[].german: Guam is an island that belongs to the USA.
Hong Kong was British territory until 1997.
You must not enter another country's airspace without permission.
en.notes: 〜領 after a country name denotes a territory belonging to that state: アメリカ領, イギリス領, also abbreviated 英領 or 仏領. The same meaning is found in 領土 "national territory", 領海 "territorial waters" and 領空 "airspace". It is common mainly in news, history and geography.

examples[].german: We acknowledge receipt of the payment.
I forgot to get the receipt stamp.
en.notes: Formal, mainly in 領収書 (receipt) and as 領収する (to receive payment). On receipts: 上記正に領収いたしました.

examples[].german: He has never learned to cook; it's all self-taught.
More and more overseas hotels are adopting Japanese-style hospitality.
My grandmother has been practicing Ohara-school flower arranging for forty years.
en.notes: 〜流 is attached to countries, persons or names and means "-style, in the manner of" (日本流, アメリカ流, 自己流, 我流), or it denotes a school in traditional arts such as ikebana, tea ceremony or martial arts (小原流). As an independent noun, 流 hardly occurs; in compounds such as 一流 "first-class", 交流 "exchange" or 電流 "electric current" it has other meanings. A similar, somewhat softer suffix for "style, manner" is 〜風.

examples[].german: At university I joined a photography club.
I play soccer every week in a company club.
en.notes: Voluntary interest group, especially at universities (テニスサークル). Official school clubs are rather called 部 or 部活.

examples[].german: The old bicycle has rust on it.
I removed the rust and then painted it.
en.notes: Verb: 錆びる (to rust); 錆止め (rust protection). Often also written in kana as さび.

en.meaning: to grope for; to probe, to explore
examples[].german: In the dark, I fumbled in my pocket and took out the key.
Experts are trying to find out the cause of the accident.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to feel around in a pocket for something (ポケットを探る) or to carefully find something out (原因を探る, 相手の気持ちを探る).

examples[].german: Since I failed, I will take the retest.
The rerun of this program is next week.
en.notes: 再（さい）stands before another word and expresses that something happens once more: 再試験 is a retest, 再放送 a rebroadcast. The prefix stands directly before the following element. It is not a free adverb like もう一度. In 再来週, however, 再 is read さ; that other reading does not belong to this card. No separate accent is attested for the bound prefix.

examples[].german: If it does not work, please try restarting once.
After the update, the smartphone restarted automatically.
en.notes: 再 (again) + 起動 (starting up). As a verb with する: パソコンを再起動する.

examples[].german: In the middle of the night I heard an ambulance siren.
The siren signaling the start of the match sounded.
en.notes: Warning sound of a fire engine, ambulance or factory: サイレンが鳴る.

examples[].german: Although I warned him repeatedly, he was late again.
The company finally responded to the repeated requests.
en.notes: Formal, usually with a slight tone of reproach: 再三注意したのに (although I warned him repeatedly). Stronger: 再三再四.

examples[].german: I scooped up the medicine with a spoon and gave it to him.
I fed the baby weaning food with a small spoon.
en.notes: Often written in kana as さじ; especially in recipes: 大さじ (tablespoon), 小さじ (teaspoon). Idiom: 匙を投げる (to give up). In everyday speech, スプーン is usually used.

examples[].german: Old taverns line the back of the station.
After work, I stopped by a small bar with my colleagues.
en.notes: Somewhat old-fashioned word for places that serve alcohol; today mostly 居酒屋 or バー.

examples[].german: I was holding the map upside down, so I got lost.
A ketchup container is easier to use if you store it upside down.
The picture on the wall was hanging upside down, but nobody noticed.
en.notes: Short form of 逆さま (separate card) with the same meaning. Mostly adverbial in 逆さにする "to turn upside down", 逆さになる or 逆さに持つ, attributive with の (逆さの文字) and in compounds such as 逆さ吊り or 逆さ富士 (the reflection of Mt. Fuji in a lake). 逆さま sounds more complete, 逆さ is more concise and usual in compounds.

examples[].german: My fever hasn't gone down since three days ago.
That package arrived three days ago.
en.notes: The day before the day before yesterday (おととい). Kanji: 一昨昨日, usually written in kana. Future counterpart: しあさって.

examples[].german: The moment I entered the room, I sensed a menacing atmosphere.
The culprit's eyes were full of murderous intent.
en.notes: A palpably hostile, dangerous atmosphere: 殺気を感じる, 殺気立つ (to become tense and aggressive). Homophone: さっき (a while ago).

examples[].german: This workshop makes furniture.
The exhibition model was made over three months.
en.notes: Making objects (模型の作製). For documents and plans, 作成（さくせい）is usually written.

examples[].german: I let the hot tea cool a little before drinking it.
The bad news dampened everyone's excitement.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb related to 冷める (to get cold): スープを冷ます. Not to be confused with 覚ます (to wake up).

en.meaning: birth; origin; product of, from ... (suffix, e.g. 日本産, 北海道産)
examples[].german: This wine is from France and is a little expensive.
At the supermarket, domestic and foreign beef are sold side by side.
My grandfather was a businessman who amassed a huge fortune in a single generation.
en.notes: Most often as an origin suffix on labels: 北海道産, フランス産, 外国産; 国産 is a separate word (separate card). 〜産 applies mainly to agricultural and natural products, 〜製 to manufactured goods (日本製の時計). On its own, 産 means "fortune" in written language (産を成す) or "birth"; in everyday speech the polite お産 (separate card) is used for the latter.

examples[].german: I want to climb Mt. Fuji someday.
I borrowed a photo book about Mt. Aso from the library.
en.notes: 山（さん）appears in names of mountains, such as 富士山（ふじさん）or 阿蘇山（あそさん）. This reading is part of the full name. Other mountain names use やま or ざん, so you cannot automatically put さん on every name. The free noun 山（やま）and the title さん are separate entries.

examples[].german: My grandfather owns a large piece of mountain forest.
Part of the mountain forest collapsed because of the heavy rain.
en.notes: Forested mountain land, also as property: 山林を所有する (to own mountain forest). About two thirds of Japan is forested.

examples[].german: Lemon juice is acidic.
This soil is strongly acidic, so vegetables do not grow well.
en.notes: Opposite: アルカリ性 (alkaline), in between 中性 (neutral). 酸性雨 = acid rain. Homophone: 賛成 (agreement).

examples[].german: For details, see the next page.
Following the dictionary's cross-references, you can find related words.
You can choose the destination folder with the "Browse" button.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 参照する "to look up, refer to" (vocab-n2:573), typical of written language and instructions: 〜を参照のこと "see ...", 相互参照 "cross-reference", 参照ボタン "Browse button" on a computer. Unlike 参考 "a guide, reference for orientation", 参照 means looking something up at a specific place.

examples[].german: My father is an ordinary office worker.
The morning trains are full of office workers.
en.notes: A word coined in Japan (from salary + man) for employees with a fixed salary, especially in company offices. More neutral: 会社員.

examples[].german: After subtracting expenses from income, ten thousand yen was left.
Gains and losses cancel out; on balance it is zero.
en.notes: The result after subtracting: 差し引きゼロ (net zero). Verb: 差し引く (to deduct).

en.meaning: to insert; to put (flowers) in a vase
examples[].german: I put one rose in the vase.
Please plug the plug into the outlet.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to stick something into an opening, especially flowers (花瓶に花を挿す) or a plug. Many meanings of the same verb are also written 差す.

en.meaning: to pour in, to add a liquid
examples[].german: Since there was little hot water left, I poured water into the kettle.
Please put a little oil on the squeaky hinge.
en.notes: 注す／さす here means adding a liquid. The thing poured takes を, the container or treated object takes に: やかんに水をさす, 機械に油をさす. The verb is often written in kana; 注す emphasizes the pouring. It is transitive and conjugated as a godan verb: さします, さして. Light shining in is described with the other verb 差す／射す.

examples[].german: In today's class we thought about life and death.
She was born in Tokyo in 1990.
My grandfather quietly ended his ninety years of life.
en.notes: An elevated, literary word for "life" in the philosophical sense, especially in the contrast 生と死 "life and death" and in the phrase この世に生を受ける "to be born". In everyday speech one says 命 "life (that one can lose)" or 人生 "life course, life". The same character read なま (vocab-n3:3325) means "raw, fresh, live", read き (N1 cards) "pure, undiluted"; as the suffix せい it is known from 一年生 "first-year student".

en.meaning: right, true (logic); positive (mathematics); regular, main (opposite of 副)
examples[].german: Numbers greater than zero are called positive numbers.
Please submit the application form in two copies, original and duplicate.
He will start working as a regular employee next month.
en.notes: A formal, rather technical noun: in mathematics 正の数 "positive number" (opposite 負の数), in logic "true", in administrative language 正副 "original and copy" or "principal and deputy". In everyday life it appears mainly in compounds such as 正社員 "regular employee" or 正解 "correct answer". Not to be confused with the homophones 背 "height (of a person)", 姓 "family name" and 〜製 "made in".

examples[].german: My surname changed after I got married.
Please write your surname and given name separately here.
en.notes: Formal word for surname, e.g. in forms (姓・名). In everyday speech: 名字（みょうじ）.

examples[].german: If there isn't enough sunlight, plants grow more slowly.
I observed the growth of the rice plants every day.
en.notes: Used mainly for plants; growth of people and animals and economic growth are written 成長.

examples[].german: I cut the paper to make a square.
Find the area of a square with sides of five centimeters.
en.notes: Four equal sides and right angles. Rectangle: 長方形.

examples[].german: The test results showed that my blood pressure was normal.
The system is currently operating normally.
Relations between the two countries have finally returned to normal.
en.notes: A na-adjective and noun, the opposite of 異常 "abnormal": 正常に動く "to function normally", 正常な値 "normal value", 正常に戻る "to return to normal". Typical of technology, medicine and news; for people or things in everyday speech, one rather says 普通. 通常, by contrast, means "usual, regular (in procedure)", e.g. 通常営業 "regular operation".

examples[].german: We agreed to meet in front of the school's main gate.
The main gate closes at night, so please use the back gate.
en.notes: The main entrance of a school, company or temple. Back gate: 裏門.

examples[].german: This film took three years to make.
She is currently creating a new work.
en.notes: Creating artistic or media works: 映画を制作する, 番組制作. For industrial manufacturing, 製作 or 製造 is usually written.

examples[].german: I reviewed the draft and then made a fair copy.
For New Year's cards, I try writing in pencil before making the fair copy.
en.notes: The clean final version after the draft (下書き); as a verb 清書する.

examples[].german: The city built a sports facility for young people.
There is concern about the influence of the internet on young people.
en.notes: Formal, e.g. in official and news language: 青少年の健全な育成 (healthy development of youth).

examples[].german: The restroom is currently being cleaned.
The residents gathered and cleaned the river.
en.notes: Formal word for cleaning, especially of facilities and public places: 清掃中 (under cleaning), 清掃員 (cleaner). In everyday speech: 掃除.

examples[].german: Let's add up all the integers from one to ten.
3.5 is not an integer.
en.notes: Mathematics: 正の整数 (positive integer). Compare 小数 (decimal), 分数 (fraction).

en.meaning: counter for ships; one half of a pair
examples[].german: Two ships are anchored in the harbor.
Of the pair of folding screens, only one is on display.
en.notes: 隻 counts ships. You also encounter it with folding screens: a pair of matching 屏風 is called 一双（いっそう）, and a single screen from it 一隻（いっせき）. So the same unit can denote a number of ships in the harbor and one half of a pair of screens in a museum. Note the small っ in 一隻; two ships is 二隻（にせき）.

en.meaning: approach, drawing near; closeness (in age, ability); closer relations
examples[].german: With the approach of the typhoon, there are disruptions to transportation.
An alarm sounded warning of the approach of a large ship.
In view of the rapid rapprochement between the two countries, neighboring states are becoming more vigilant.
en.notes: Noun for the verb 接近する (separate card): spatial approach, especially of storms, vehicles or celestial bodies (台風の接近), but also political or personal rapprochement (両国の接近). Very common in news and warnings, often with 〜に伴い or 〜に注意. In everyday speech 近づく is more usual for "to come closer".

examples[].german: Mixing cement with sand and water makes mortar.
The hole in the road was filled with cement.
en.notes: A binder for construction; with sand and water it becomes mortar (モルタル), and with gravel added, concrete (コンクリート).

en.meaning: war, battle; match, contest (suffix, e.g. 決勝戦, 選挙戦)
examples[].german: The soccer final will be held this coming Sunday.
With the official announcement, the election campaign has begun in earnest.
After extra time, the home team scored a dramatic victory.
en.notes: A productive suffix for wars, battles and contests: 決勝戦 "final", 延長戦 "extra time", 選挙戦 "election campaign", 情報戦 "information war". The standalone word for "war" is 戦争 (separate card), for "battle" 戦い (たたかい). Not to be confused with the identically sounding cards 千, 線 and 栓.

examples[].german: I pulled the cork out of the wine.
Please put in the plug first, and then run the hot water in the bath.
en.notes: Seal of a bottle or tub: 栓を抜く (uncork, pull the plug); also ガスの元栓 (main gas valve) and 耳栓 (earplugs).

examples[].german: This box is thirty centimeters high.
Please cut about five centimeters off my hair.
en.notes: Short for センチメートル (cm); for counting see also the counter センチ. Formerly also short for "sentimental".

en.meaning: face washing, washing up (of face and hands)
examples[].german: The washroom is at the end of the corridor over there.
After getting up and washing my face, I had breakfast.
I packed the toiletries for the trip into my bag.
en.notes: 洗面 is the Sino-Japanese word for "washing one's face" and appears mainly in compounds: 洗面所 "washroom", 洗面台 (vocab-n5:790) "washbasin", 洗面器 "washbowl", 洗面用具 "toiletries". On its own it sounds written (洗面を済ませる); in everyday speech one says 顔を洗う. 洗面する exists but is rare.

examples[].german: The king continued despotic rule for a long time.
The people rose up against despotism.
en.notes: Rule by one person or group without checks: 専制政治, 専制君主. Homophone: 先生.

examples[].german: I moved on Saturday the week before last.
I've had that book on loan since the week before last.
en.notes: The week before last week. Likewise: 先々月 (the month before last).

examples[].german: The person at the front of the line has been waiting since five in the morning.
In the marathon, a Japanese runner is in the lead.
en.notes: The foremost position in a line or group: 先頭に立つ (to be at the head, to lead). Homophones: 銭湯 (public bath), 戦闘 (combat).

examples[].german: My mother has been busily tending the garden since morning.
He is diligently saving money for studying abroad.
The ants are industriously carrying food to their nest.
en.notes: せっせと describes, onomatopoeically, that someone works tirelessly and busily at something, often at small, repeated tasks: せっせと働く, せっせと貯金する, せっせと運ぶ. It sounds appreciative or affectionate and is also readily used for animals such as アリ. It stands directly before the verb without a particle; synonyms are 一生懸命 and こつこつ "steadily, step by step".

examples[].german: I'll go back to the office once and then go to the client's.
This matter doesn't fit the company's policy.
en.notes: Short for one's own company or a company just mentioned, mainly in business language: 社の方針 (company policy), 社に戻る. As a suffix: 出版社 (publisher), 新聞社. Counter for companies: 三社.

examples[].german: The baby is sucking on its finger.
A child is walking along sucking on a candy.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 飴をしゃぶる (suck on a candy), 指をしゃぶる (suck one's finger).

examples[].german: I crouched down to the child's eye level and talked to him.
I crouched down on the spot to get a good look at the flower.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: その場にしゃがむ. For "to sit down" in general: 座る.

examples[].german: I'm majoring in social sciences at university.
Economics is one of the social sciences.
en.notes: Sciences of society such as economics, sociology and political science. Alongside: 自然科学 (natural sciences), 人文科学 (humanities).

examples[].german: My dad often makes lame puns.
Nobody got the joke, and the room went quiet.
en.notes: A pun on similar-sounding words; usually in kana しゃれ. だじゃれ = a corny pun. Not to be confused with お洒落（おしゃれ, stylish).

examples[].german: I sketched trees and flowers in the park.
During art class we went out to sketch.
en.notes: Painting or drawing what is in front of you; as a verb 写生する. 写生大会 = outdoor drawing contest.

examples[].german: Excuse me, could you press the shutter for us?
When night fell, the shop pulled down its shutter.
en.notes: Camera shutter: シャッターを切る／押す (to release the shutter). Also the roll-down shutter or rolling door in front of shops: シャッターを下ろす.

examples[].german: If you delve into history, you can understand how this town came into being.
To compile a history of this era, you need to examine many records.
en.notes: As a noun, 史（し）can mean history or its written account. Used as a standalone word it sounds literary; 史をひもとく means to delve into historical records, and 史を編む to compile a history or chronicle. In everyday language 歴史 is more common. The bound suffix in 日本史 is practiced on a separate card.

examples[].german: At university I am majoring in Japanese history.
To put together the company's hundred-year history, I collected old photos.
en.notes: 史（し）is used as a suffix after the field whose history is meant. 日本史 is the history of Japan; 会社の百年史 describes the hundred-year history of a company. The suffix attaches directly to the preceding word and is not an honorific title like 氏（し）.

en.meaning: to be finished; to be completed
examples[].german: The suit I ordered is scheduled to be ready next week.
The report is finally finished.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb related to 仕上げる (to finish): 作品が仕上がる. Noun: 仕上がり (result, finish).

en.meaning: in three days (two days after tomorrow)
examples[].german: The exam is in three days, on Monday.
Please reply within three days.
en.notes: The day after the day after tomorrow (あさって). Kanji 明明後日, usually in kana. In some regions しあさって refers to a different day; if in doubt, give the date.

en.meaning: dead silent, utterly quiet (しいんとする: to fall completely silent)
examples[].german: When the principal began to speak, the gymnasium fell dead silent.
The hospital corridor in the middle of the night was silent, and it was a little scary.
I meant it as a joke, but the meeting room fell awkwardly silent.
en.notes: An onomatopoeic adverb for complete, often tense or awkward silence: しいんとする or しいんとなる "to fall dead silent", often together with 静まり返る. In manga and novels mostly written しーんと or シーン; the shorter form しんと sounds calmer and more literary. Not to be confused with 信徒/しんと "believer".

examples[].german: When the ski season comes, the hotels are fully booked.
The professional baseball season has started.
en.notes: The peak time for something: 野球のシーズン, スキーシーズン, 受験シーズン; オフシーズン (off season).

en.meaning: constantly; all the time; from beginning to end
examples[].german: My younger brother plays nothing but video games all the time.
She was smiling throughout the meeting.
en.notes: Constantly, over and over: 始終文句を言う. As a noun in 一部始終 (the whole story).

examples[].german: Ms. Tanaka is chairing today's meeting.
I am going to be the emcee at a friend's wedding.
en.notes: Chairing a meeting or event: 会議の司会をする; the person is called 司会者. Homophone: 視界 (field of vision).

examples[].german: Humidity easily builds up in rooms during the rainy season.
In this region it is humid and muggy in summer.
Please store the books away from moisture.
en.notes: しっき is a rarer secondary reading of 湿気 with the same meaning "humidity". In everyday speech one almost always says しっけ (separate card), for example 湿気が多い or 湿気を取る; しっき is heard more in formal or older texts and lectures. When speaking, choose しっけ. Do not confuse with the homophone 漆器 "lacquerware".

examples[].german: Please call the office immediately.
This is an urgent matter.
en.notes: Formal, typical in business messages: 至急ご連絡ください (please contact us immediately), 大至急 (extremely urgent).

examples[].german: I bought a blue and white striped shirt.
Zebras have black stripes on their bodies.
en.notes: Stripes on fabric or fur: 縞模様 (striped pattern), 縞のシャツ. Often also written in kana しま.

en.meaning: to shut tightly; to close off (applications, entries)
examples[].german: Because it was cold, I shut all the windows in the room tight.
We will close applications tomorrow at five o'clock.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to close off acceptance or applications (受付を締め切る) and to shut doors and windows completely (in that sense usually written 閉め切る: 窓を閉め切る). Noun: 締め切り (deadline).

examples[].german: Great, the bus hasn't come yet.
When I saw that my opponent had taken the wrong road, I thought, "Got him."
en.notes: Exclamation used when something turns out unexpectedly well; usually in kana, rarely written 占めた. Colloquial, often said to oneself.

en.meaning: deeply, from the heart, earnestly; quietly, reflectively
examples[].german: Only after becoming a parent did I deeply feel how grateful I should be to my parents.
I talked quietly about old times with a friend I hadn't seen in a long time.
My grandmother was gazing wistfully at the old photographs.
en.notes: Describes a feeling that "soaks in" deeply: to feel something deeply or to think about something quietly and reflectively (しみじみと感じる, しみじみ思う, しみじみ語り合う). Often with と, attributively as しみじみした気持ち. Almost always written in kana; the kanji 沁み沁み are rare. Related to the verb 染みる "to soak in, to permeate".

examples[].german: The pencil lead broke.
She looks gentle, but she has a strong core.
en.notes: The innermost part: 鉛筆の芯 (pencil lead), りんごの芯 (apple core), ろうそくの芯 (candle wick). Figurative: 芯が強い (strong inside).

examples[].german: I spent a night in a berth on an overnight train.
I lay down on the bed at the hospital and had an examination.
en.notes: Formal or technical word for bed: 寝台車 (sleeping car), 寝台列車 (night train with sleeping cars). In everyday speech: ベッド.

examples[].german: The ship changed its course to the south.
The typhoon changed its course to the east.
en.notes: Strictly the compass heading of a ship or aircraft: 針路を変える. For one's own future (studies, career) one writes 進路.

en.meaning: to believe, to trust (literary form of 信じる)
examples[].german: I believe in his innocence.
There is a saying: "Those who believe will be saved."
Dear graduates, go forth on the path you believe in.
en.notes: The literary ずる-form of 信じる (separate card, N4) with the same meaning: to believe in something, to trust someone (〜を信ずる). Today mainly in fixed phrases such as 信ずる者は救われる, in speeches, legal texts and older literature; in everyday speech 信じる is used. Typical written forms are 信ずれば and 信ぜず.

examples[].german: This soup is a little salty.
Eating too many salty things is bad for your health.
en.notes: い-adjective, synonymous with しょっぱい (more colloquial). The noun 塩辛 refers to salted seafood.

examples[].german: I've read all the books in this series.
The latest film in the series has been released.
en.notes: A series of related books, films or products: 人気シリーズ, シリーズ第二弾 (second installment).

examples[].german: I eat it with a little lemon juice squeezed over it.
The broth for this soup is made from kombu.
en.notes: Liquid from fruit or food (レモンの汁) and Japanese soup: 味噌汁, 豚汁. Politely also お汁（おしる）.

en.meaning: rounding off (to the nearest whole number)
examples[].german: Please round off everything after the decimal point.
If you round 3.6, you get 4.
en.notes: Literally "discard four, take in five": up to 4 is rounded down, from 5 up is rounded up. 小数点以下を四捨五入する.

examples[].german: My grandmother's face has gentle wrinkles.
I smoothed out the wrinkles in the shirt with an iron.
en.notes: Wrinkles in skin (目じりのしわ) and creases in fabric or paper: しわになる (to get wrinkled), しわを伸ばす (to smooth out). Kanji: 皺 (rare).

examples[].german: I am majoring in natural sciences at university.
The development of natural science has changed our lives.
en.notes: Physics, chemistry, biology, etc.; compare 社会科学 (social sciences) and 人文科学 (humanities).

en.meaning: to become quiet; to calm down, to subside
examples[].german: When the teacher came in, the classroom fell silent.
In the evening, the wind finally died down.
en.notes: Intransitive godan verb: 会場が静まる (the hall falls silent), 風が静まる (the wind dies down). Transitive: 静める. For pain or unrest, 鎮まる is also used.

en.meaning: calligraphy, writing; handwriting; book, document; letter (elevated)
examples[].german: My grandmother started learning calligraphy at seventy.
An exhibition of calligraphy by a famous master is being held at the art museum.
Please enter your name and address on the application form.
en.notes: On its own, 書 stands above all for calligraphy as an art work: 書を習う, 書の展覧会; 書道 is the discipline. As a suffix it forms documents: 教科書, 証明書, 申込書, 報告書. For "book", 本 is used in everyday speech; 書 in this sense is elevated. Do not confuse with the verb 書く or the prefix 諸〜.

en.meaning: -office, -place, -institute (suffix, e.g. 事務所, 研究所/じょ); counter for places
examples[].german: My father works in an office in front of the station.
Evacuation shelters were set up at three places in the city.
I went to the city office to get a copy of my residence certificate.
en.notes: A very productive suffix for facilities and offices: 事務所, 役所, 紹介所; after some words it is voiced as じょ: 研究所, 避難所, 発電所. As a counter for places usually written 〜か所: 三か所, 何か所. The card 所/ところ is the standalone noun "place, spot"; しょ/じょ occurs only in bound form.

en.meaning: first ten days (of a month); beginning
examples[].german: I plan to move at the beginning of next month.
The cherry blossoms were in full bloom in early April.
en.notes: A month is divided into three parts: 初旬／上旬 (1st-10th), 中旬 (11th-20th), 下旬 (21st to the end of the month).

examples[].german: This printer uses ink in four colors.
It is difficult to paint a picture using only one color.
en.notes: 色（しょく）follows a number when counting colors. 四色 is read よんしょく and means four colors; 一色 is read いっしょく. The compound counts the different colors, not the number of objects. The free word for "color" is read 色（いろ）. Only the counter is practiced here.

examples[].german: Please add a little salt to the soup.
This food contains a lot of salt.
en.notes: More technical and used on packaging; in everyday speech simply 塩. 食塩水 = salt solution.

examples[].german: A craftsman makes each of these desks by hand.
After ten years of training, he became a full-fledged craftsman.
en.notes: Someone who has mastered a trade: 寿司職人, 家具職人. 職人気質 = a craftsman's work ethic.

examples[].german: A new shop has opened in the station.
This shop sells cute miscellaneous goods.
en.notes: Mostly for modern shops or in compounds: コーヒーショップ, ネットショップ. In general: 店.

examples[].german: I bought a new dictionary at the bookstore in front of the station.
This book is on sale at bookstores nationwide.
en.notes: Somewhat more formal than 本屋. Online bookstore: オンライン書店.

examples[].german: Ten divided by two gives a quotient of five.
Find the quotient and remainder of the division.
en.notes: Mathematical term. The results of the basic operations are called 和 (sum), 差 (difference), 積 (product) and 商 (quotient).

examples[].german: The child went to pee before going to sleep.
On the park wall was written, "Do not urinate here."
en.notes: Rather vulgar; politely one says お手洗いに行く, medically 尿（にょう）. 立ち小便 = urinating outdoors.

en.meaning: it can't be helped; there's no use
examples[].german: It can't be helped that it was canceled due to rain.
There's no use regretting what's already over.
en.notes: Colloquial short form of しようがない, same meaning as 仕方がない: one has to accept it. With 〜ても: "there's no use" (悔やんでもしょうがない). After the て-form also "terribly, unbearably": 眠くてしょうがない (I'm terribly sleepy).

examples[].german: We are hurrying to match the fingerprints left at the scene.
Matching deposits against invoices is an important part of accounting work.
Password verification failed.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 照合する "to check against" (vocab-n2:552): something is checked against a template, e.g. 指紋の照合 "fingerprint matching", データ照合, 本人照合 "identity verification". The verb is used with 〜と照合する; in colloquial speech 照らし合わせる corresponds to it. 比較, by contrast, is general comparing without the intention of checking.

examples[].german: I answered the quiz correctly and received a prize.
The first prize was a travel voucher.
en.notes: An item won in a contest; a cash prize is called 賞金. Homophone: 商品 (goods).

examples[].german: The net weight without the box is five kilograms.
Excluding breaks, I actually worked two hours.
en.notes: After deducting packaging or breaks: 正味の重さ (net weight), 正味三時間 (three hours net).

examples[].german: Please write the answer as a decimal.
There was a problem about converting fractions into decimals.
en.notes: A number with digits after the decimal point; the decimal point is called 小数点. Homophone: 少数 (small number, minority).

examples[].german: Old shops line this street.
My grandfather ran a small shop in town.
en.notes: Rather a small retail shop: 商店街 (shopping street). In everyday speech: 店.

en.meaning: to arise, to occur; to cause, to produce (literary form of 生じる)
examples[].german: Due to the change in plans, additional costs may arise.
A big conflict can also arise from a small misunderstanding.
Any and all disputes arising in connection with this contract shall be settled at the Tokyo District Court.
en.notes: The literary ずる-form of 生じる (separate card, N3): something arises or occurs (問題が生ずる), more rarely transitive "to produce, to cause" (損害を生ずる). Very common in contracts, laws and news, e.g. 〜から生ずる損害; in conversation 生じる or 起こる is used. The written negative is 生ぜず.

examples[].german: He took part in the Olympics.
Because of the injury, playing in the next match is difficult.
en.notes: Taking part in a competition, tournament or broadcast: 大会に出場する. Opposite: 欠場 (non-participation).

examples[].german: I bought a photo book by my favorite photographer.
Before the exam, I finished a whole workbook of practice problems.
en.notes: Suffix for collections and compilations: 写真集 (photo book), 作品集 (collection of works), 問題集 (problem collection), 詩集 (poetry collection).

examples[].german: Please assemble in front of the station at eight o'clock tomorrow morning.
We set off only after waiting for everyone to gather.
en.notes: As a verb 集合する: to gather. 集合時間 (meeting time), 集合場所 (meeting place). In mathematics: set.

examples[].german: When I was in elementary school, I took penmanship lessons.
In penmanship class I wrote the character "spring".
en.notes: Practicing characters with a brush or pen; part of the curriculum in elementary schools. The art form itself is rather called 書道.

examples[].german: A rally on environmental issues was held in front of the station.
I attended the meeting of the apartment building's residents.
en.notes: A gathering of many people for some purpose, also political: 集会を開く. The fundamental right is called 集会の自由 (freedom of assembly).

examples[].german: The new company president took office in April.
Right after taking office, the mayor announced a new plan.
en.notes: Taking up an office or post: 社長に就任する. Opposite: 辞任 (resignation), 退任 (leaving office).

examples[].german: My grandfather's hobby is collecting old stamps.
Garbage collection in this district is on Tuesdays and Fridays.
Gathering information about the incident is taking time.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 収集する "to collect" (vocab-n2:572), often with の or in compounds: 切手の収集 "stamp collecting", 情報収集 "information gathering", ごみ収集 "garbage collection", 収集家 "collector". The spelling 蒐集 emphasizes collecting works of art or collectibles and is rare. In everyday speech, for simple gathering one rather says 集める.

examples[].german: I repaired the roof of the old house.
I had the torn clothes mended.
en.notes: Repairing buildings, furniture or clothing; as a verb 修繕する. For devices usually 修理; in everyday speech also 直す.

examples[].german: The ship picked up speed and left the harbor.
The train slowed down and entered the station.
en.notes: More for vehicles and in the phrase 全速力で (at full speed). In general: 速度, スピード.

examples[].german: The land was surveyed before building the house.
It is difficult to measure a mountain's height accurately.
en.notes: Surveying land or buildings; as a verb 測量する. 測量士 = land surveyor.

en.meaning: at that time; in those days
examples[].german: At that time, I still lived in Osaka.
Please come on the tenth of next month. By then, preparations will be done.
en.notes: Refers to a time mentioned earlier, in the past or the future.

en.meaning: because of that; for that reason
examples[].german: There was heavy snow. Because of that, the trains stopped.
This shop is particular about its ingredients. For that reason, the prices are a little high.
en.notes: Connects cause and effect, rather written style: 大雪が降った。そのため、電車が止まった. As そのために also "for that purpose". Kanji: その為.

examples[].german: This restaurant is cheap. On top of that, it's very tasty.
We got lost, and on top of that it even started to rain.
en.notes: Adds something, often as an escalation: 安い。その上、おいしい. Similar: さらに, しかも. Also written in kana そのうえ.

en.meaning: and yet; in spite of that
examples[].german: I studied as hard as I could. And yet, I failed the exam.
He promised. And yet, he came late again.
en.notes: Introduces a sentence that contradicts what was expected, often with disappointment or reproach: "And yet...!" More neutral: それでも.

examples[].german: "It looks like rain." "In that case, let's take an umbrella."
You don't have time? Then let's do it another time.
en.notes: Draws a conclusion from what the other person has just said. In casual speech also じゃあ or それじゃ.

examples[].german: Two coffees, please. And also a piece of cake.
We meet at eight tomorrow. Also, don't forget your lunch box.
en.notes: A colloquial conjunction at the beginning of a sentence used to add something: "and one more thing". Not to be confused with それとも ("or" in questions).

examples[].german: At Obon, we welcome the spirits of our ancestors.
Birds are thought to have descended from dinosaurs.
en.notes: Ancestors of a family or forebears of a species: 人類の祖先. Similar: 先祖 (more family ancestors).

examples[].german: My scatterbrained little brother often forgets his umbrella.
I was so careless that I got on the wrong train.
en.notes: い-adjective for people who often make mistakes or forget things out of haste.

examples[].german: The total cost of the trip was about 100,000 yen.
A general election will be held next month.
en.notes: A prefix before nouns in the sense of "total, all": 総人口 (total population), 総選挙 (general election), 総額 (total amount).

examples[].german: We held a farewell party for our senior colleague who is being transferred.
We offered words of farewell to the graduates.
en.notes: Mostly in 送別会 (farewell party) or 送別の言葉 (words of farewell).

en.meaning: come to think of it; by the way
examples[].german: By the way, how is Mr. Tanaka doing?
Come to think of it, tomorrow is my mother's birthday.
en.notes: Introduces a topic one has just remembered; also written そう言えば, colloquially そういや.

en.meaning: and then; and so; in that way
examples[].german: He practiced every day. And so, in the end, he won.
You mix the ingredients and bake the dough made that way.
en.notes: そうして connects a sequence in the sense of "and so, and then". It can also refer to the manner just described: そうしてできた生地 is the dough made in that way. 然うして is a rare dictionary spelling; the usual form is the kana spelling そうして.

examples[].german: The next room is so noisy that I can't sleep.
Lately the world has been rather turbulent in many ways.
en.notes: い-adjective, stronger than うるさい: 騒々しい音. Also for restless times: 世の中が騒々しい.

examples[].german: When I was a child, my dream was to become a stewardess.
The stewardess is handing out drinks.
en.notes: An outdated term; today people prefer 客室乗務員 or CA (キャビンアテンダント), which also include men.

examples[].german: Cedar trees line the mountain slope.
When spring comes, cedar pollen flies.
en.notes: Japan's most common timber tree; its pollen (杉花粉) is a main cause of hay fever in spring.

examples[].german: On hot days, please drink fluids frequently.
This watermelon is juicy and sweet.
en.notes: Water content or fluid intake: 水分をとる (take in fluids), 水分が多い (juicy, watery).

examples[].german: I checked whether the shelf was level.
Please raise your arms horizontally.
en.notes: Noun and な-adjective: 水平に置く (place horizontally). Opposite: 垂直 (vertical).

examples[].german: The evening sun is sinking on the horizon.
I could see one ship near the horizon.
en.notes: The line where sea and sky meet; over land one speaks of 地平線.

examples[].german: When water is heated, it turns into water vapor.
Water vapor in the air cools and forms clouds.
en.notes: Water in gaseous form; the visible steam above hot water is called 湯気（ゆげ）in everyday speech.

examples[].german: The moon is reflected on the surface of the pond.
A fish leaped from the surface of the water.
en.notes: Surface of water: 水面に映る (be reflected on the water). Poetically also read みなも.

examples[].german: This town has prospered on fisheries since long ago.
My older brother is studying fisheries science at university.
en.notes: Catching fish and seafood: 水産業 (fishing industry), 水産物 (marine products).

examples[].german: Let's bring a water bottle on the field trip.
I filled my water bottle with tea and went out.
en.notes: A reusable bottle for drinks on the go; a disposable plastic bottle is called ペットボトル.

examples[].german: I gave my mother a scarf for her birthday.
Since the wind was strong, I tied a scarf around my head.
en.notes: A light cloth for the neck or head; a thick winter scarf is called マフラー.

examples[].german: I took advantage of my opponent's opening and scored a goal.
She is always neat and proper, and shows no weak spot.
en.notes: A gap in space or time and a moment of inattention: 隙を見て (seizing a good moment), 隙がない (to show no weakness). Narrow gap: 隙間. Homophone: 好き.

examples[].german: Our child is very picky about food.
This is no time to be picky about work.
en.notes: Often about food: 好き嫌いが多い (to be very picky), 好き嫌いしないで食べなさい.

examples[].german: Which color is better is a matter of taste.
Whether one likes spicy food is a matter of personal taste.
en.notes: Mostly 好き好きだ or 人の好き好き: that is a matter of taste. Compare 十人十色.

examples[].german: I'm learning dance at a school in front of the station.
This school also has classes for children.
en.notes: Mostly for private schools and courses: 英会話スクール, 料理スクール. A regular school is called 学校.

examples[].german: He is tall and slim.
I was impressed by the shop assistant's smooth handling.
en.notes: な-adjective. Unlike English "smart" (clever), it usually means "slim" (スマートな体) or "stylish, smooth" (スマートな対応); "intelligent" only in compounds such as スマートフォン.

examples[].german: Where do you live?
I'm looking for a place to live close to the station.
en.notes: Somewhat more refined than 家: お住まいはどちらですか (Where do you live?). 一人住まい = living alone.

examples[].german: Sorry, I'll be a little late.
I feel I did him wrong.
en.notes: Casual apology, especially used by men or older people: すまない、遅れた. Polite: すみません. Also "to have wronged someone": 彼にすまないことをした.

examples[].german: Music is coming from the speaker.
The speaker is too loud.
en.notes: Loudspeaker, e.g. ワイヤレススピーカー (wireless speaker). Rarely also "speaker (a person giving a talk)".

examples[].german: I made the slides to use in the presentation.
Please look at the next slide.
en.notes: A slide of a presentation or a photographic slide. As a verb スライドする: to slide, to shift.

examples[].german: The new drama series starts next week.
At the start signal, the athletes all began running at once.
en.notes: As a verb スタートする (to start, to begin). スタートライン = starting line.

examples[].german: When the singer appeared on stage, the hall came alive.
In this game, it is hard to get to the next stage.
en.notes: Stage and performance (ステージに立つ), also a phase or game level (次のステージ).

examples[].german: My stockings got a run.
I put on black stockings and went out.
en.notes: Thin nylon stockings or pantyhose; thick tights are called タイツ, socks 靴下.

examples[].german: The trains stopped because of the snow.
Stop for a moment! Don't go any further.
en.notes: As a verb ストップする (to stop, halt); also as an exclamation: ストップ！

examples[].german: The bonus was only a pittance.
Bank interest is a pittance.
en.notes: Literally "sparrow's tears": a ridiculously small amount, usually of money (wages, bonus, interest). Slightly complaining or ironic.

examples[].german: A huge tree stands on the shrine grounds.
A large tree fell down in the typhoon.
en.notes: A large, old tree. Colloquially also 大きな木.

examples[].german: The two have a strong sense of rivalry toward each other.
Next week there is an inter-class relay tournament.
In the next election, a young legislator is seen as the incumbent's rival candidate.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 対抗する "to compete with, match" (vocab-n2:474), frequent in compounds: 対抗意識 "competitive spirit", 対抗馬 "rival candidate", クラス対抗 "competition between classes", 対抗策 "countermeasure". 対立 emphasizes the opposition, 対抗 the measuring oneself against an opponent. Do not confuse it with the homophone 対向 "oncoming" (対向する, vocab-n2:1437; 対向車).

examples[].german: This movie wasn't particularly interesting.
It's not particularly cold today, so I don't need a coat.
en.notes: Almost always with a negative: 大して難しくない ("not particularly difficult"). Similar: それほど, あまり.

examples[].german: Grandmother was very pleased with her grandchild's letter.
It's not such a big deal.
en.notes: As an adverb, formal "very" (大層喜ぶ); as a な-adjective "exaggerated, pompous" (大層なことを言う).

examples[].german: I changed the tires before winter came.
Please put air in the bicycle tire.
en.notes: Tire of a car or bicycle. The spelling タイア is rare. Flat tire: パンク.

en.meaning: amount; sum; volume; as a suffix 〜だか (売上高, 生産高)
examples[].german: This year's sales rose by ten percent compared with last year.
Before shopping, I checked my account balance.
What one person can do alone is limited.
en.notes: As a suffix, 高 is usually read だか and denotes a quantity or sum: 売上高 "sales", 生産高 "production volume", 残高 "balance" (separate card). Standing alone, たか appears mainly in the phrase 高が知れている "is limited, not worth mentioning", from which also comes the adverb たかが "merely". Do not confuse it with the adjective 高い "high, expensive" or the homophone 鷹 "hawk".

examples[].german: This basket is made of bamboo.
Bamboo can sometimes grow more than a meter a day.
en.notes: The plant and the material: 竹林 (bamboo grove), 竹の子 (bamboo shoots). In the 松・竹・梅 ranking, the middle grade.

en.meaning: to burn; to light (a fire); to heat
examples[].german: At the campsite we made a fire and everyone warmed up.
In the old days, bath water was heated by burning firewood.
en.notes: Transitive: 火を焚く (to make a fire), 落ち葉を焚く. Homophone: 炊く (to cook rice).

en.meaning: rare; occasional (with の or な)
examples[].german: On my rare days off, I read quietly at home.
It is rare for him to stay silent in a meeting.
en.notes: たま describes something that happens only rarely. Before a noun it often takes の, as in たまの休み "a rare day off"; たまなこと "something rare" is also possible. The spelling 偶 is uncommon; it is usually written in hiragana. The longer たまに means "occasionally" as an adverb; "even number", by contrast, is 偶数（ぐうすう）.

examples[].german: He heaved a big sigh.
The exam was over, and I let out a sigh of relief.
en.notes: "To sigh": ため息をつく. A sigh of relief is ほっとため息をつく.

examples[].german: Every day is the same task repeated, so the work is monotonous.
Listening to a monotonous rhythm makes me sleepy.
This novel's plot is monotonous, and I got bored partway through.
en.notes: A na-adjective for something without variety: 単調な仕事 "monotonous work", 単調な生活, 単調なリズム; as a noun 単調さ. It describes the thing itself, whereas 退屈 (たいくつ) emphasizes the feeling of boredom. Do not confuse it with the homophone 短調 "minor key"; in mathematics, 単調増加 means "monotonically increasing".

examples[].german: Working hours are being shortened thanks to work-style reform.
Because of the typhoon, classes were shortened today.
I registered my mother's number on the phone's speed dial.
en.notes: The noun for the verb 短縮する "to shorten" (vocab-n2:451), mainly for time and duration: 時間短縮 "time reduction", 短縮授業 "shortened classes", 短縮営業 "shortened business hours", 短縮ダイヤル "speed dial". The opposite is 延長 "extension". For omitting parts of a text, one rather says 省略.

examples[].german: English distinguishes between singular and plural.
This noun is used in the singular form.
en.notes: Grammatical term. Opposite: 複数 (plural). Japanese nouns usually do not distinguish singular and plural.

en.meaning: to suffice; to be worthy of
examples[].german: He is a person worthy of trust.
That is a trivial problem.
en.notes: Literary; mostly 〜に足る ("worthy, worth": 信頼に足る人) or in the negative 取るに足らない ("insignificant"). In everyday speech, 足りる is used.

en.meaning: to compare (to); to liken; to express figuratively
examples[].german: Life is often compared to a journey.
I don't know what to compare this feeling to.
en.notes: To describe something with an image: AをBに例える (to compare A to B). Noun: 例え (comparison, parable).

examples[].german: I will leave Tokyo tomorrow morning.
He left Japan to study abroad.
en.notes: To leave a place in order to travel: 成田を発つ. Homophones: 立つ (to stand), 建つ (to be built).

examples[].german: When May comes, rice planting begins in the village.
The children tried rice planting for themselves.
en.notes: Transplanting rice seedlings into the flooded field, usually in May or June.

en.meaning: to have one's hands full (with); to be unable to cope with
examples[].german: I have my hands full with my son's selfishness.
I had a lot of trouble setting up this old computer.
en.notes: Literally "to burn one's hand". Mostly used with に: 子どもに手を焼く. Similar: 手に負えない (unmanageable).

examples[].german: Physical strength declines with age.
Please be careful of the drop in temperature.
en.notes: A fall in values or quality: 気温の低下, 体力の低下; as a verb 低下する.

examples[].german: My father tends the garden every weekend.
If you take good care of these shoes, you can use them for a long time.
en.notes: To tend and keep in good condition: 庭の手入れ, 肌の手入れ; as a verb 手入れする.

examples[].german: This train will stop at the next station.
The train is temporarily stopped because of an accident.
en.notes: A vehicle stops briefly: 各駅停車 (local train), 停車中 (stopped). Parking is 駐車.

examples[].german: The train is crossing the iron bridge over the river.
This iron bridge was built a hundred years ago.
en.notes: A bridge made of iron or steel, especially for trains.

en.meaning: this side; just before; in front
examples[].german: The post office is just before the station.
Please tidy up in order, starting with the shelf nearest to you.
en.notes: The side closer to the speaker: 駅の手前 (just before the station). For the grammar pattern 〜手前 ("since one has ..."), see the grammar section.

examples[].german: I have reserved a tennis court for the weekend.
There are two tennis courts behind the school.
en.notes: A court for playing tennis; to reserve one is コートを予約する.

examples[].german: This piece has a fast tempo.
This movie has good pacing.
en.notes: Speed in music, and figuratively in conversation or a story: 話のテンポ.

en.meaning: from place to place; back and forth
examples[].german: Because of my father's work, I moved around from place to place in childhood.
In his youth he drifted from job to job.
en.notes: Mostly as 転々とする: 職を転々とする (to change jobs frequently), 各地を転々とする.

examples[].german: Houses can be seen scattered in the mountains.
Drops of blood were scattered on the floor.
en.notes: Scattered in several places: 家が点々とある. Also "in drops".

examples[].german: Firearms were introduced to Japan in the sixteenth century.
The samurai of old used not only swords but also firearms.
en.notes: An older word for firearms, especially historical matchlock guns; today usually 銃.

examples[].german: The sun has been shining since morning, and it's hot.
After the rain, the sun began to shine again.
en.notes: Intransitive, especially of the sun and moon: 日が照る. Transitive: 照らす (to illuminate).

en.meaning: to remain; to stay; to be limited to
examples[].german: He stayed in the town even after the disaster.
The damage was limited to some areas.
en.notes: 留まる／止まる read とどまる means to stay in one place or to remain limited to an area. Both uses are intransitive: 町にとどまる, 一部にとどまる. とどまる is often written in kana. 止まる／とまる is a different reading, for example for a vehicle that stops. とどまる follows the godan conjugation: とどまります, とどまって. With にとどまらない one says that something goes beyond the stated range.

en.meaning: to be pointed; to be sharp; to be on edge
examples[].german: This pencil is well sharpened.
He is tired and on edge.
en.notes: Mostly as 尖った: 尖った鉛筆 (sharp pencil), 神経が尖る (to be on edge).

en.meaning: to melt into; to blend in
examples[].german: She quickly blended in with the class.
The sugar has dissolved in the tea.
en.notes: To dissolve into something or to fit into a group: 新しい環境に溶け込む.

examples[].german: I finished my homework long ago.
The train left long ago.
en.notes: Emphasizes that something happened a long time ago: とっくに終わった. The kanji 疾っくに are rare.

examples[].german: There are puddles here and there on the road.
I didn't understand his story in places.
en.notes: In some places: 所々に雪が残っている. Also written in kana ところどころ.

en.meaning: to dissolve; to beat; to mix in liquid
examples[].german: I beat the eggs and put them into the frying pan.
You dilute the paint with water before using it.
en.notes: To dissolve something in liquid or to whisk: 卵を溶く, 絵の具を水で溶く. Intransitive: 溶ける.

examples[].german: The strong point of this car is its fuel efficiency.
I emphasized my strengths in the interview.
en.notes: An especially positive feature. Homophone: 特徴 (feature, neutral).

examples[].german: This school is distinctive for its international education.
The dishes make use of the characteristics of each region.
en.notes: A distinctive quality: 地域の特色, 特色のある学校.

en.meaning: tock; tap (a light knock, a light setting down)
examples[].german: Someone tapped me lightly on the shoulder from behind.
She set the glass down on the table with a soft clack.
He tapped the papers briefly on the desk to line them up.
en.notes: とん is onomatopoeic for a short, light knock or setting down, and usually takes と: 肩をとんとたたく "to tap lightly on the shoulder", とんと置く. Doubled (とんとん) it describes repeated knocking; the duller, heavier sound is どん. Not to be confused with the katakana card トン "ton" and the adverb とんと "not at all".

examples[].german: When I happened to pass in front of the shop, I met a friend.
A passerby called an ambulance.
en.notes: To pass a place by chance: 店の前を通りかかる.

examples[].german: We can't find a breakthrough in the negotiations.
It was announced that exhibition attendance had topped one million.
The team practices every day aiming to get through the qualifying round.
en.notes: A noun for breaking through a barrier, overcoming a hurdle and surpassing a mark. Very frequent in 突破口 "starting point for a breakthrough", 予選突破 and in headlines such as 〜万人突破. The verb (〜を突破する) is taught by the card 突破する.

examples[].german: When I was a child, I often caught fish in the river.
The outfielder caught the high fly ball.
en.notes: A spelling of とる used specifically for catching animals, fish or insects (魚を捕る) and in baseball (ボールを捕る). The general "to take" is written 取る.

examples[].german: There are three elephants at the zoo.
The person in charge brought two horses.
en.notes: 頭（とう）follows a number when counting large animals such as cattle, horses or elephants. 象が三頭いる states the number of animals present; 馬を二頭連れてくる describes animals that someone brings along. For many smaller animals 匹（ひき）is used. The standalone word for "head" is 頭（あたま）; the same kanji has a different reading and function here.

en.meaning: etc.; and so on (written-language suffix); class, rank (e.g. 一等) (counter)
examples[].german: I won first prize in the drawing.
Rents are high in big cities such as Tokyo and Osaka.
Old trains had first-class and second-class cars.
en.notes: As a suffix meaning "etc.", 等 appears in news, forms and legal texts and is read とう there (東京、大阪等); in everyday language one says など (separate card), written in kana, instead. As a counter, 〜等 denotes classes and ranks: 一等 "first prize, first class", 二等, 三等賞. Do not confuse it with 〜等々 "and so on" or with 等 as the plural suffix ら (彼等).

examples[].german: I checked the location of Iwo Jima on the map.
Researchers are studying the volcanic activity of Iwo Jima.
en.notes: In some island names, the final 島 is read とう. One attested example is 硫黄島（いおうとう）. This reading belongs to the full place name; other names may contain しま or じま. The general word for an island is 島（しま）. So with a new island name always learn the whole reading instead of inserting とう everywhere.

en.meaning: this; our; the ... in question (prefix, e.g. 当店, 当社)
examples[].german: You can use credit cards at our store.
Breakfast at our hotel starts at seven o'clock.
All of our company's products are made in Japan.
en.notes: A formal prefix with which a store or organization refers to itself: 当店 "our store", 当社 "our company", 当ホテル. It often appears on signs, in announcements and on websites. More humble than 当社 is 弊社 "our (humble) company"; in the sense of "in question, said", 当 is also found in 当日 "the day in question" and 当時 "at that time".

examples[].german: It's my turn to clean this week.
We take turns taking out the trash.
en.notes: A task taken on in turns: 掃除当番, 給食当番 (school lunch duty).

examples[].german: I cut the cake into six equal pieces.
Let's split the profit equally among the three of us.
en.notes: To divide into equal parts: ケーキを四等分する. Homophone: 当分 (for the time being).

examples[].german: The protagonist appears in the second half of the story.
A new smartphone has appeared on the market.
en.notes: Appearing on stage or in a story (登場人物 = characters) and the appearance of new products.

en.meaning: letter to the editor; reader's letter; submission
examples[].german: My grandfather often writes letters to the newspaper.
The road was repaired because of a letter from a citizen.
en.notes: An opinion sent to a newspaper or an authority: 新聞に投書する.

examples[].german: Reaching the summit takes about six hours.
I confirmed this term's attainment goals with my teacher.
This agreement cannot be called the final point reached in the negotiations.
en.notes: A noun for reaching a goal, point or level, also abstractly; rather literary. Typical in 到達点, 到達目標, 山頂への到達. Unlike 到着 (arrival of people or vehicles at a place), 到達 emphasizes that a goal is reached after a path or effort. The verb 〜に到達する has its own card.

examples[].german: Bread, drinks, sweets and so on are sold at the venue.
Cleaning, laundry, cooking and so on - there is plenty of housework every day.
Please prepare documents such as the application form, a photo, ID, etc.
en.notes: 等々 closes a list and stresses that there is more (パン、飲み物等々); it sounds written and somewhat more emphatic than 〜等. In speech one usually says など or the doubled などなど, which can also be written 等々. Do not confuse it with the identically sounding adverb とうとう "finally, at last" (its own card), which is never written 等々.

examples[].german: Eastern and Western ways of thinking sometimes differ.
I am studying East Asian history at university.
en.notes: Asia, especially East Asia, as a cultural sphere; opposite: 西洋 (the West).

examples[].german: I often buy kerosene in winter.
The heater has run out of kerosene.
en.notes: Fuel for kerosene heaters (石油ストーブ), which are common in Japan in winter.

examples[].german: This road runs east to west through the town.
I am studying the differences between Eastern and Western culture.
en.notes: Direction (東西に走る道) and, figuratively, East and West as cultural spheres: 東西の文化.

examples[].german: I ate the rice without leaving a single grain.
Big raindrops are hitting the window.
en.notes: A small round particle: 米の粒, 雨の粒. As a counter for grains: 一粒.

en.meaning: to rank next to; to come second to
examples[].german: The Osaka area is the largest metropolitan area after Tokyo.
After Britain, France also enacted the same law.
en.notes: Rank or order: 東京に次ぐ大都市圏 (the largest metropolitan area after Tokyo). Homophones: 継ぐ (to inherit, to continue), 注ぐ (to pour).

en.meaning: pair, set (of things that belong together); counterpart (対になる); counter for pairs (一対)
examples[].german: A pair of guardian lions stands at the entrance of the shrine.
These two vases form a pair.
I received a matching pair of teacups as a wedding present.
en.notes: Denotes two things that belong together as a pair or set: 対になる "to form a pair", 対の茶碗; as a counter 一対 (いっつい) "one pair". The reading たい (see the cards 対/たい), in contrast, stands for "versus, to" (3対1, 日本対ブラジル) and "opposite, counterpart" in abstract or literary use. For concrete, identically shaped pairs such as vases, figures or tableware, it is read つい; for shoes or socks one rather uses 足 or ペア.

en.meaning: convenience; opportunity (to do something along the way)
examples[].german: Please return this book when you get the chance.
If you're going to the station, I'll come along, since it's on my way anyway.
en.notes: The opportunity to take care of something while doing something else: ついでの時に (when it happens to be convenient). For the grammar pattern 〜ついでに, see the grammar section.

examples[].german: I've come on the department head's errand to deliver some documents.
A messenger came from the company.
en.notes: An assignment to fetch or deliver something, and the person who carries it out. Polite/childish: お使い (errand).

examples[].german: I left the dirty shirt soaking in water for a while.
It feels good to soak tired feet in hot water.
en.notes: Transitive: to put something in liquid (水に浸ける). Read the same as 漬ける (to pickle, to marinate), which is mainly used for pickled food. Intransitive counterpart: 浸かる (to be immersed).

examples[].german: The restroom is at the end of the corridor.
Please turn left at the end of this road.
en.notes: The place where a road or corridor ends, typical in directions: 突き当たりを右に.

en.meaning: to run into; to come to the end
examples[].german: If you go straight, you will come to a big street.
The research has run into a major problem.
en.notes: To go to the end of a road (道に突き当たる) or to hit an obstacle (問題に突き当たる).

examples[].german: Time really flies.
A long time has passed since then.
en.notes: The time that has passed, often with feeling: 月日が経つのは早い (time passes quickly). The reading がっぴ means "date".

en.meaning: to thrust in; to plunge into; to press (on a point)
examples[].german: He was walking with his hands stuffed in his pockets.
There was an accident in which a car crashed into a shop.
en.notes: To stuff something in (ポケットに手を突っ込む), to crash into (車が店に突っ込む) or to question critically. In comedy, the partner's retort (ツッコミ).

en.meaning: to exhale; to sigh; to tell a lie
examples[].german: Hearing the result, she breathed a sigh of relief.
You must not tell lies about the reason you couldn't keep your promise.
en.notes: The reading つく is used, among others, in 息をつく "to catch one's breath, breathe out", ため息をつく "to sigh" and 嘘をつく "to lie". The verb is often written in kana in these expressions. The exhaled breath or the lie takes を. The godan forms are つきます, ついて, ついた. For "to vomit", the other reading はく is the usual choice; this card practices the expressions with breath and lies.

examples[].german: At the sports day tug-of-war, we all pulled on the thick rope.
We tied the boat to the shore with a rope.
en.notes: A thick rope: 綱引き (tug-of-war), 命綱 (lifeline).

examples[].german: I value my ties with the people in the community.
There seems to be a connection between these two incidents.
en.notes: Usually written in kana つながり: 人とのつながり (relationships with people), 話のつながり (coherence of a story).

examples[].german: I connected my computer to the TV and watched a movie.
I want to turn this failure into the next success.
en.notes: Transitive: to connect two things (ケーブルを繋げる), also figuratively: 経験を次に繋げる. Often written in kana つなげる.

en.meaning: to balance; to match; to be in proportion
examples[].german: The two sides of the scale balanced.
This hat goes well with the clothes.
en.notes: To keep balance (重さが釣り合う) or to suit each other (二人は釣り合っている).

examples[].german: I hung a lamp from the ceiling.
I broke my arm and am carrying it in a sling.
en.notes: To let something hang down from above: 棚を吊る. 吊るす is more common. Homophone: 釣る (to fish).

examples[].german: I hung a wind chime in the window.
I hang the laundry inside the room to dry.
en.notes: Transitive: to hang something so that it dangles: 洗濯物を吊るす, 風鈴を吊るす.

en.meaning: connoisseur, expert; counter for letters and documents (e.g. 一通)
examples[].german: They say that connoisseurs eat tempura with salt.
This morning three emails arrived from the business partner.
He is a sake connoisseur and can guess the brand just by drinking it.
en.notes: As a noun or na-adjective "connoisseur, specialist": 彼はワインの通だ, 通の食べ方; as a suffix in 日本通, 事情通, 食通. Also a counter for letters, emails and documents: 一通 (いっつう), 二通, 三通. Not to be confused with 通り (とおり, "street; as ...") and the verb 通る, which use the same kanji with a different reading.

examples[].german: A notice of acceptance arrived from the university.
I turned off the app notifications.
en.notes: Noun for 通知する (to notify, already N2). An official notice (合格通知), but also the push notification on a phone (スマホの通知).

examples[].german: English is not widely understood in this country.
That kind of excuse won't work.
en.notes: To be generally accepted or to work: 英語が通用する (English is understood), 世界で通用する (to hold up worldwide).

en.meaning: to lead to, to be connected; to be understood; to be well versed in (literary)
examples[].german: This narrow road used to be a highway leading to the castle town.
The ways of thinking of the two writers have something in common.
Even if the languages differ, feelings do get through.
en.notes: 通ずる is the literary zuru-form of 通じる (separate card) and has the same meanings: "to lead to" (駅に通ずる道), "to be understood" and "to be well versed in". It is found in texts, speeches and fixed phrases such as 相通ずる "to have something in common" or the proverb すべての道はローマに通ず. In conversation 通じる is almost always used; the て-form is 通じて for both, with 通ずれば and 通ぜず also literary.

examples[].german: This furniture is old, but it still has a shine.
Her hair is glossy and beautiful.
en.notes: Shimmering gloss of a surface: 髪の艶, 艶のある声. Often written in kana つや.

examples[].german: He always makes assertive statements.
Let's go in confident before the match.
en.notes: Confident and determined, sometimes overconfident. Opposite: 弱気 (timid).

en.meaning: to deny, to refute; to cancel out, to drown out (a sound)
examples[].german: The company president denied the rumor of bankruptcy.
These headphones cancel out the surrounding noise.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to negate or reject something (うわさを打ち消す); also to mask a sound or a feeling.

examples[].german: I practiced every day, and my cooking skills improved.
Your tennis has improved a lot this past year.
en.notes: 腕 stands for skill: 腕が上がる = one's abilities improve (料理の腕が上がった). Related: 腕がいい (to be skilled), 腕を磨く (to hone one's skills).

examples[].german: The waitress brought us water.
When I was a student, I worked as a waitress in a coffee shop.
en.notes: Also written ウエートレス. Today the gender-neutral 店員 or ホールスタッフ is often used.

examples[].german: I water the plants every morning.
I put a small potted plant on the balcony.
en.notes: A tree or shrub planted in a garden, and a potted plant: 植木に水をやる. Gardener: 植木屋.

en.meaning: to float (something); to show (a smile, tears); to imagine
examples[].german: The children floated paper boats on the river and played.
With tears in her eyes, she said thank you.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 浮かぶ（to float, to come to mind）. Common: 笑みを浮かべる "to smile", 涙を浮かべる "to have tears in one's eyes", 思い浮かべる "to imagine".

examples[].german: A signature is required to receive the package.
We have confirmed receipt of the payment.
en.notes: The act of receiving (荷物の受け取り) and the acknowledgment of receipt. On forms often written 受取. Verb: 受け取る.

en.meaning: presence or absence; yes or no
examples[].german: Please write on the application form whether you have any allergies.
Without allowing any objection, he put me in the car.
en.notes: Literary, often used on forms: 経験の有無 (experience: yes/no). Idiom: 有無を言わせず (without allowing any objection).

examples[].german: Let's eat a lot today and get our energy back.
This shop here is much cheaper.
en.notes: Colloquial for "very much": うんと食べる, うんと安い. In writing, 大いに or ずっと are more usual.

en.meaning: to turn over, to turn inside out
examples[].german: Before washing it, I turned the shirt inside out.
I turned the card over and checked the number.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: to turn something to the other side (シャツを裏返す, カードを裏返す). Intransitive: 裏返る.

examples[].german: I had my fortune for this year told at the shrine.
This game is an important match that foretells the outcome of the tournament.
en.notes: Transitive: 運勢を占う "to read one's fortune". Also used figuratively for forecasts: 今後を占う. The related noun is 占い（うらない）"fortune-telling, horoscope".

examples[].german: Reading in a dim room tires your eyes.
After five o'clock it was already getting dim outside.
en.notes: I-adjective from 薄（light, faint）and 暗い（dark）: not completely dark but faintly lit, used for rooms, paths or twilight.

en.meaning: to attack, to strike down; to avenge
examples[].german: The samurai avenged his father by killing the enemy.
The imperial court sent a large army to put down the rebels.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb, mostly historical or literary: to strike down an enemy, 敵を討つ (to take revenge). Homophones: 打つ (to hit), 撃つ (to shoot).

examples[].german: My older sister is a driven career woman.
I read a special feature on working women in a magazine.
en.notes: Almost only in compounds: キャリアウーマン (career woman), ビジネスウーマン. On its own one says 女性.

examples[].german: This sweater is one hundred percent wool.
Please do not wash woollen clothes in the washing machine.
en.notes: Sheep's wool as a material: ウールのセーター. The Japanese word is also 羊毛（ようもう）.
