Rather literary and formal (chapters, meetings, wars, articles of law); in daily life people often use the suffixed 〜番目 or 〜回目 instead. The card 第一 (だいいち) teaches the independent word "first of all, above all"; 台, 代, 題 and 大 are homophones, but different words.

examples[].german: The title of the essay is "My Dream".
If you were to give this photo a title, what would be good?
en.notes: Title or subject: 作文の題 (essay topic), 題をつける (to give a title). Compounds: 問題, 話題, 宿題, 題名.

examples[].german: I attended the meeting in place of the department head.
If you cannot come yourself, a representative is also fine.
en.notes: Someone who acts in place of another: 部長の代理 (deputy for the department head), 代理で出席する. Agency: 代理店.

en.meaning: train schedule; diamond (short for ダイヤモンド)
examples[].german: Train schedules are disrupted because of heavy snow.
A new timetable takes effect next month.
She showed me the diamond on her engagement ring.
en.notes: ダイヤ is short for ダイヤグラム and refers to the operating schedule of a train or bus, i.e. when which train runs - not the printed booklet, which is called 時刻表. Typical are ダイヤが乱れる "train service is disrupted" and ダイヤ改正 "timetable revision". The same sound ダイヤ is also short for ダイヤモンド "diamond" (ダイヤの指輪); the playing-card suit "diamonds" is also called ダイヤ. Which word is meant depends on the context.

examples[].german: I wanted to go. But I had work.
It's expensive, isn't it? But it's really delicious.
en.notes: Casual sentence-initial conjunction, meaning the same as でも; often shortened to けど. More polite: ですが, けれども.

examples[].german: This class has fifteen boys and fifteen girls.
The men's 100 meters final has begun.
en.notes: Mainly in school and sports: 男子生徒, 男子トイレ, 男子サッカー. Counterpart: 女子.

examples[].german: My younger sister takes dance lessons every week.
At the party I danced with everyone.
en.notes: Mostly Western or modern dance; as a verb, ダンスする. Traditional Japanese dance is more often called 踊り（おどり）.

examples[].german: "Why are you late?" "Well, because the train stopped."
Even a child understands something like that.
en.notes: Colloquial, at the start of a sentence as a justification ("but ... because ..."): だって、知らなかったんだもん. After a noun "also, even": 子どもだって分かる.

examples[].german: I have a date with my girlfriend on Sunday.
On our first date we went to see a movie.
en.notes: A romantic meeting between two people; as a verb デートする. A calendar date is 日付, not デート.

examples[].german: Tomorrow is a holiday. Therefore, the shop is closed.
The roads are crowded. So let's leave early.
en.notes: Polite form of だから at the beginning of a sentence. It can sound impatient when you are repeating something: ですから、先ほど申し上げたように….

examples[].german: I want to go out somewhere on the weekend.
His smile looked somehow sad.
en.notes: Indefinite place: どこかへ行きたい. Adverbially also "somehow, in a certain way": どこか寂しそうだ. The kanji 何処か is rare.

examples[].german: This mushroom is poisonous, so you must not eat it.
Staying up late is bad for your health.
en.notes: Poisonous substance (毒キノコ, 毒蛇) and, figuratively, something harmful: 体に毒だ (bad for the body), 目の毒 (a tempting sight one shouldn't indulge in).

examples[].german: No matter how hard I tried, I couldn't beat him.
How happy I was when I passed!
en.notes: A question or exclamation (どんなにうれしかったか = how happy I was) and, with ても, "no matter how much": どんなに頑張っても.

examples[].german: On Sunday we drove to the sea.
Let's go for a drive to see the autumn leaves.
en.notes: An outing by car: ドライブに行く／ドライブする. It does not mean "driving a car" in general (that is 運転する).

examples[].german: Every Wednesday I watch my favorite drama.
The way the two met was just like a drama.
en.notes: Mostly a television series（テレビドラマ）. Figuratively also a dramatic event: ドラマのような話.

examples[].german: I bought a new dress for the wedding.
The bride's white dress was very beautiful.
en.notes: Usually an elegant dress (ウエディングドレス = wedding dress). An everyday dress is more often ワンピース.

examples[].german: I played soccer in the rain and my clothes got covered in mud.
The car's tires are stuck in the mud and won't move.
en.notes: Wet earth: 泥だらけ (covered in mud), 泥んこ. Idiom: 顔に泥を塗る (to bring shame on someone). 泥棒 = thief.

examples[].german: I watch videos on my smartphone before going to bed.
I filmed my child's birthday on video.
en.notes: Literally "moving picture"; the usual word for online videos (動画を見る／撮る). ビデオ sounds more like a recording or a cassette.

en.meaning: please (polite, earnest); somehow; whether (〜かどうか); strange (どうかしている)
examples[].german: I sincerely ask for your kind cooperation.
I don't know whether it will be sunny tomorrow.
Something is wrong with him today.
en.notes: どうか is almost always written in kana. At the start of a sentence it strengthens a request: どうかお願いします "please, I beg you" - more earnest and formal than どうぞ, which rather offers something. It also forms 〜かどうか "whether (or not)" and どうかしている "to not be quite oneself, to be strange".

en.meaning: by all means, at any cost; (with negative) just can't
examples[].german: I really want to see this movie.
I just can't remember his name.
en.notes: With a wish: "by all means" (どうしても行きたい). With a negative: "try as I might, can't" (どうしても思い出せない). Kanji 如何しても are rare.

examples[].german: As in last year, the festival will be held this year too.
There was a similar accident before.
en.notes: な-adjective: 同様の問題 (a similar problem), 同様に (likewise). More formal than 同じ. Homophones: 動揺 (agitation), 童謡 (children's song).

examples[].german: The handle of my umbrella broke.
I cut the broom handle shorter.
en.notes: The handle of a tool or device: 傘の柄, ほうきの柄, 包丁の柄. The same kanji read がら means "pattern".

examples[].german: Someday I want to see the pyramids in Egypt.
It doesn't rain much in Egypt.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. Pyramids: ピラミッド.

examples[].german: I always take a reusable bag when I go shopping.
This eco bag folds up small and is handy.
en.notes: Very common since plastic bags became chargeable in Japan (2020). Counterpart: レジ袋.

examples[].german: I found out how my friends are doing through social media.
It's better not to post personal information on social media.
en.notes: Written in Latin letters (SNS, also full-width ＳＮＳ) and read エスエヌエス. In Japanese, the usual word for "social media" (ソーシャルメディア is less common).

examples[].german: The Philippines has many islands.
I took English classes in the Philippines.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. No plural: フィリピン stands for the whole island nation.

examples[].german: I follow my favorite singer on social media.
A senior colleague covered for the newcomer's mistake.
en.notes: As a verb with する. On social media: アカウントをフォローする. At work it also means "to support someone, to cover for a mistake" (部下をフォローする).

examples[].german: I put the photos in a new folder.
Which folder is that file in?
en.notes: Also written フォルダー. A paper folder is more often called ファイル.

en.meaning: un-, non- (prefix, e.g. 不便, 不安, 不可能)
examples[].german: This town is far from the station and inconvenient.
I was so anxious about the exam results that I couldn't sleep.
Finishing this job in one day is impossible.
en.notes: The negating prefix 不 "un-, non-" in its standard reading ふ: 不便 "inconvenient", 不安 "anxiety, worry", 不足 "shortage", 不可能 "impossible", 不正確 "inaccurate". It combines mainly with Sino-Japanese words and usually forms nouns or na-adjectives. The reading ぶ (its own card 不〜/ぶ) applies only in a few fixed words such as 不器用 or 不気味; when in doubt, ふ is right. Close in meaning is 無〜, which rather expresses the absence of something ("without, -less").

examples[].german: The rim of the cup is chipped.
A man wearing glasses with black frames came.
en.notes: The rim or edge of an object: コップの縁 (rim of a glass), 眼鏡の縁 (rim of glasses). In the reading えん, 縁 means "fate, bond, relationship" (ご縁).

examples[].german: He is always complaining about his work.
Discontent is spreading among the employees.
en.notes: Dissatisfaction that one voices: 不平を言う (to complain). Often as a pair: 不平不満.

examples[].german: The president's wife visited the school.
The company president's wife also attended the party.
en.notes: Respectful term for the wife of a (usually well-known) person: 首相夫人 (the prime minister's wife), 田中夫人. Not to be confused with 婦人 (woman in general, 婦人服).

examples[].german: Eating and drinking are not allowed in this hall.
My exam grade was "fail".
en.notes: Written form for "not allowed, not possible": 持ち込み不可 (no outside items), 使用不可. As a university grade, "fail" (scale 優・良・可・不可).

en.meaning: pretending, appearance (〜ふりをする: to pretend to); behavior; swing, swinging
examples[].german: When Mother came, my little brother pretended to be asleep.
She is pretending not to know anything.
That batter has a sharp swing of the bat.
en.notes: Mostly in kana, especially in 〜ふりをする "to pretend to" after a verb form or noun + の: 寝たふり, 知らないふり, 学生のふり; also 見て見ぬふり "to deliberately look away". In kanji, 振り also stands for "swing, swinging" (バットの振り) and dance movements. Do not confuse with the suffix 〜ぶり "manner; after a long time" and with 不利/ふり "disadvantageous" (their own cards).

examples[].german: Bamboo has many nodes.
I have heard the melody of this song somewhere before.
en.notes: Several meanings: a knot in wood or bamboo, a joint (指の節), the melody of a song, and "point, spot" (思い当たる節がある = something comes to mind). The reading せつ means section or season (季節).

examples[].german: I suddenly remembered the old days.
When I happened to look up at the sky, there was a rainbow.
en.notes: Something happens without intention or cause: ふと思い出す (to suddenly remember), ふと見ると (when one happens to look). The kanji 不図 is very rare.

en.meaning: tends to; prone to; often (usually negative) (suffix)
examples[].german: In winter I tend to catch colds.
When busy, you tend to get too little exercise.
My grandmother is often ill and can't go out much.
en.notes: A suffix for a (usually undesirable) tendency: attached to a verb stem (忘れがち, 遅れがち, なりがち) or to a noun (病気がち, 曇りがち). It behaves like a na-adjective: 忘れがちだ, 忘れがちな人. 〜やすい expresses more the easy possibility, 〜ぎみ a slight touch of something. Mostly written in kana; 勝ち/かち "victory" is a different word with its own card.

examples[].german: Smoking is harmful to the body.
This insect does no harm to people.
en.notes: "To cause harm": 害を与える; "harmful": 害がある. In compounds: 被害, 公害, 害虫.

examples[].german: I went around the temples of Kyoto with a guidebook in hand.
I looked for shops that are not in the guidebook.
en.notes: The guidebook as a book; the person who guides is called ガイド.

examples[].german: My grandfather had no education, but he was a very wise man.
I am studying psychology at university.
en.notes: On its own, somewhat literary: 学がある (to be educated). As a suffix meaning "-ology, -science": 経済学, 心理学, 言語学.

en.meaning: picture frame, framed picture; amount, sum (also suffix, e.g. 金額, 総額)
examples[].german: I framed my graduation certificate and hung it in my room.
The repair cost turned out to be a considerably larger sum than I expected.
The amount of the donation differs from person to person.
en.notes: With the reading がく, 額 means on the one hand "picture frame, framed picture" (額に入れる "to frame", 額縁), and on the other "amount, sum" (かなりの額, 多額, 金額, 総額). The same kanji read ひたい means "forehead" (its own card); the context shows which reading is meant.

examples[].german: He looks rough, but he is kind at heart.
The pattern of this shirt is too loud.
en.notes: Pattern on fabric (花柄 = floral pattern, 柄のシャツ); also nature or physique: 柄が悪い (rough, uncouth), 大柄 (large-framed). The same kanji read え means "handle".

examples[].german: I put the car in the garage.
I cleaned out the garage to make space for the bicycles.
en.notes: At or in a house; a parking lot is 駐車場.

en.meaning: lower grade, poor quality; last volume
examples[].german: The quality of the goods was rated on three levels: high, medium and low.
The first and middle volumes were at the library, but the last one was on loan.
en.notes: As a noun, げ refers to the lower level of a classification, e.g. 下 in 上・中・下. It can therefore sound derogatory when ranking people or performances. For a two- or three-volume work, 下 stands for the last volume. The reading した, by contrast, is used in ordinary spatial expressions such as "under the table"; for a stretch of a river, しも is found.

examples[].german: On Monday mornings, the trains are always crowded.
It's a holiday, so there's no class this Monday.
Please put out burnable trash on Mondays and Thursdays.
en.notes: 月曜 is the short form of 月曜日 "Monday" (its own card). It is common in spoken language as well as in timetables, garbage collection calendars and schedules, e.g. 月曜の朝 or 月曜と木曜. In formal texts and announcements the full form 月曜日 is preferred; calendars often show just 月.

examples[].german: She won a silver medal at the Olympics.
My mother treasures her silver ring.
en.notes: Silver as a metal and a color: 銀のスプーン, 銀色. Silver medal: 銀メダル; gold: 金（きん）.

en.meaning: after, later (suffix, e.g. 三日後 = three days later; その後 = after that)
examples[].german: I was able to leave the hospital a week after the surgery.
Please take this medicine after meals.
I met him at university, but I haven't contacted him once since then.
en.notes: 〜後 (ご) is the Sino-Japanese reading of 後 and stands directly after time spans and events: 三日後 "three days later", 卒業後 "after graduation", 食後 "after a meal"; その後 means "after that, since then". The independent noun 後 (あと, its own card), by contrast, is connected with の or the past form (食事の後で, 食べた後で) and sounds more everyday. 〜後 is more concise and rather literary; see also 以後 "from now on" (its own card).

examples[].german: A cockroach appeared in the kitchen and caused a big commotion.
There are more cockroaches in summer, so I take the trash out right away.
en.notes: Usually written in katakana; often referred to euphemistically as G（ジー）. A common nuisance in the Japanese summer.

examples[].german: This is quite ordinary home cooking.
Only a very small number of people opposed it.
en.notes: Intensifier before adjectives and nouns: ごく普通 (quite ordinary), ごく一部 (only a very small part), ごくわずか. Usually in kana; kanji 極く／極. Not to be confused with すごく.

examples[].german: He scored a goal at the end of the match.
I crossed the finish line of the marathon after five hours.
en.notes: A goal in soccer (ゴールを決める = to score a goal), the finish line in running, and figuratively a goal in life or a project. As a verb ゴールする (to reach the finish line).

examples[].german: Gorillas are very strong.
The gorilla at the zoo was staring straight at us.
en.notes: A zoo animal, written in katakana.

examples[].german: My grandfather was in the military when he was young.
The armies of both countries are gathering at the border.
en.notes: Military, army: 陸軍 (army), 海軍 (navy), 空軍 (air force). Japan's armed forces are officially called 自衛隊 (Self-Defense Forces). Similar sounding: 郡 (district).

examples[].german: After school, we practiced soccer on the field.
The field is muddy from the rain, so the game is canceled.
At the morning assembly, all the students gathered on the field.
en.notes: グランド is a common spelling of グラウンド "sports field, playing field"; both are the same word, and グラウンド is regarded as a more accurate rendering of English "ground". One trains or plays グランドで; a school's sports field is typical. 校庭 (its own card) is the more general "schoolyard". Do not confuse with グランド "grand" as in グランドピアノ.

examples[].german: I poured wine into the glass.
I dropped a glass and it broke.
en.notes: A drinking glass, especially for wine and beverages (ワイングラス); a water glass is often コップ. In compounds also eyeglasses: サングラス (sunglasses). Homophone: グラス (grass).

examples[].german: "We have overtime again tomorrow." "Oh, I see..."
Haa, I was tired again today.
en.notes: Hesitant agreement (はあ、そうですか); with rising intonation a disbelieving "Huh?"; and as a sigh. With superiors, はあ? can come across as impolite.

examples[].german: Please don't drop cigarette ash on the floor.
Volcanic ash fell on the town.
en.notes: Residue left after burning: たばこの灰, 火山灰 (volcanic ash). Ash gray: 灰色.

examples[].german: On the weekend I went hiking in the mountains with friends.
Autumn is just the right season for hiking.
en.notes: An easy walk in nature, usually as a day trip; strenuous mountain climbing is called 登山. As a verb: ハイキングする.

examples[].german: Spring is the beginning of a new life.
The origin of this festival is said to date back to the Edo period.
en.notes: Noun form of 始まる (to begin). Common: 新しい生活の始まり, 事件の始まり. Opposite: 終わり.

examples[].german: My daughter really wants to keep a hamster.
At night the hamster becomes lively and runs around.
en.notes: A popular pet (ペット), written in katakana.

examples[].german: This novel is said to be a reflection of the society of its time.
It may take a few minutes for the settings change to take effect.
The citizens' opinions were properly reflected in the new plan.
en.notes: Noun for the verb card 反映する: "reflection" (社会の反映, 世論の反映) and, in IT and office life, "incorporation, taking effect of changes" (変更の反映, 設定の反映). Common in patterns like 〜の反映だ "is a mirror image of ..." or 〜に反映される "is taken into account in ...". Not to be confused with the homophone 繁栄 "prosperity, flourishing".

examples[].german: My son is in a defiant phase right now and won't talk to me.
The teacher is struggling with his rebellious attitude.
Rebelling against one's parents is part of growing up.
en.notes: 反抗 is the noun "resistance, defiance", especially against parents, teachers or superiors: 親への反抗, 反抗期 "rebellious phase, adolescence", 反抗的な態度 "defiant attitude". The verb form 反抗する (with に) has its own card. 抵抗 is the more neutral "resistance" (also in physics); the homophone 反攻 means "counterattack".

examples[].german: Her older brother is very handsome.
A handsome actor plays the lead role.
en.notes: な-adjective, used almost only for men: ハンサムな人. For women, きれい or 美人 is more usual.

examples[].german: The children are playing in the wide field.
Long ago, this area was all open field.
en.notes: A wide, undeveloped area, mostly in compounds: 野原 (meadow), 草原, 焼け野原. Also a common family name. Homophone: 腹 (belly).

examples[].german: The button had come off, so I sewed it on with a needle and thread.
The clock hands point to twelve.
en.notes: Sewing needle (針と糸), hand of a clock (時計の針) and sting. Sounding the same: 梁 (roof beam).

examples[].german: These scissors cut well.
Please cut the paper in half with scissors.
en.notes: Usually written in hiragana; kanji 鋏. To cut with scissors: はさみで切る.

examples[].german: Please walk along the edge of the road.
I cleaned the room from one end to the other.
en.notes: The outer end or edge: 道の端 (edge of the road), 端から端まで (from one end to the other). Similar sounding: 橋 (bridge) and 箸 (chopsticks). Colloquially also 端っこ.

examples[].german: The rocket launch is scheduled for six o'clock tomorrow morning.
Everyone became anxious when they heard the news of the missile launch.
The children went to see the rocket standing on the launch pad.
en.notes: Noun for the verb card 発射する: the firing or launch of rockets, projectiles and the like. Typical: ミサイル発射, ロケットの発射, 発射台 "launch pad", 発射ボタン. For the launch of a spacecraft, 打ち上げ is also common; 発射 stresses the firing itself and belongs more to news and technical language.

examples[].german: The train will depart shortly.
There are five more minutes until the bus departs.
Rushing to board just before departure is dangerous.
en.notes: 発車 denotes the departure of a vehicle (train, bus, car) and is used as a verb with する: 電車が発車する. Typical at a station are 発車時刻 "departure time" and the 発車ベル "departure bell". 出発 (its own card) is more general and also applies to people; the homophone 発射 means "to fire" (rocket, shot).

examples[].german: Thanks to his work, we finished early.
This medicine improves stomach function.
en.notes: Work performed (いい働きをする) and the function of something: 心臓の働き (heart function), 薬の働き (effect of a medicine).

examples[].german: Please don't feed bread to the pigeons in the park.
The dove is a symbol of peace.
en.notes: Common in parks and at temples; a symbol of peace (平和の象徴). Often in kana (ハト).

examples[].german: With advances in technology, life has become more convenient.
The typhoon is moving north while intensifying.
Sleep is important for the mental and physical development of children.
en.notes: 発達 is development as growth from within: physical and mental (子どもの発達, 筋肉が発達する), technical (交通の発達) and in weather (台風が発達する "to intensify"). As a verb with する it is intransitive. 発展 (its own card), by contrast, stresses expansion and upswing, e.g. of cities and the economy (経済の発展).

examples[].german: I hear this year's trendy color is green.
The popular cafe in front of the station always has a line.
Even if I buy trendy clothes, I soon stop wearing them.
en.notes: A colloquial noun from the verb 流行る (はやる) "to be in fashion"; typically attributive with の: 流行りの服, 流行りの店, 今の流行り. In meaning it corresponds to 流行 (りゅうこう), which is more formal and literary (流行語, インフルエンザの流行). The spelling 流行 without り can also be read はやり, but is ambiguous; therefore people mostly write 流行り or はやり.

examples[].german: I was startled to see a big snake on a mountain path.
I just can't stand snakes.
en.notes: Often written in kana (へび／ヘビ). Zodiac sign: 巳年（みどし）.

examples[].german: The flight time from Tokyo to Osaka is about one hour.
There are places where a permit is required to fly a drone.
en.notes: Flying (formal): 飛行時間 (flight time), 夜間飛行 (night flight). As a verb 飛行する. Airplane: 飛行機.

en.meaning: to hit; to run over (with a vehicle)
examples[].german: A car ran over a person who was crossing the road.
I heard that dog was run over by a car.
en.notes: 轢く means to hit or run over someone or something with a vehicle. The affected living being comes before を; in a passive sentence, 車に names the vehicle responsible. The godan verb becomes 轢きます, 轢いて and 轢かれる. It is also written ひく in hiragana; the identically pronounced word 引く means "to pull" depending on context and is a different entry.

examples[].german: Your shoelace is untied.
I tied up the old newspapers with a string and put them out.
en.notes: String, cord, shoelace (靴の紐). Colloquially also a derogatory term for a man who lives off his partner.

examples[].german: There is a refinement in the way she speaks.
Stop using such vulgar language.
en.notes: A refined manner or good taste: 品がある (to be elegant), 品のない言葉 (vulgar words). Adjectives: 上品 (refined), 下品 (vulgar).

examples[].german: When I can't sleep, I count sheep.
I fed the sheep at a ranch in Hokkaido.
en.notes: Also a zodiac sign (未年). Wool is 羊毛（ようもう）; lamb meat is ラム, mutton マトン.

en.meaning: match; rivalry; being comparable (mostly as 〜に匹敵する)
examples[].german: His cooking skills rival those of professionals.
Tokyo's population is comparable to that of a small country.
No student in this class can match her in math.
en.notes: 匹敵 is practically only used with する: 〜に匹敵する "to be equal to, to rival"; the thing compared takes に; there is a separate verb card 匹敵する. Typical are 〜に匹敵するほど "to such a degree that it equals ..." and, negated, 〜に匹敵するものはない "nothing equals ...". The expression is rather literary; in conversation people often say 〜と同じくらい or 〜に負けない.

en.meaning: to come undone; to loosen (a knot, shoelace); to relax
examples[].german: Oh, your shoelace is untied.
The ribbon on the present came undone right away.
Seeing the teacher's smile, my nervousness melted away.
en.notes: The intransitive counterpart of ほどく "to untie" (separate card): 靴ひもがほどける "the shoelace comes undone", but 靴ひもをほどく "to undo the shoelace". Figuratively tension also loosens: 緊張がほどける. Mostly written in kana, because 解ける would otherwise be read とける "to be solved" (separate card).

examples[].german: Dust has collected on the bookshelf.
I opened the window and dusted the room.
en.notes: Usually written in kana (ほこり). "To dust": ほこりを払う／拭く. Similar sound: 誇り (pride).

en.meaning: to be hard work; to take a lot of effort
examples[].german: Cooking for a hundred people is hard work.
Translating all of these materials is laborious work.
en.notes: Literally "bones break", but it means great effort (骨が折れる仕事 = laborious work). Related: 骨を折る (to make an effort, to go out of one's way for someone).

examples[].german: The candle flame is flickering in the wind.
The house was engulfed in flames in an instant.
en.notes: The visible flame of a fire; also figurative for strong emotions: 怒りの炎, 情熱の炎. Fire in general is 火.

examples[].german: Really? Are you coming here tomorrow?
Actually, I haven't told anyone yet.
en.notes: ほんと is the shortened reading of ほんとう. In conversation, 本当？ alone can ask whether something is really true. 本当は introduces the actual state of affairs, often in contrast to a supposition or what has been said so far. The final う of ほんとう is dropped here; the form is therefore shorter.

examples[].german: There is a deep moat around the castle.
In spring, cherry trees bloom around the moat.
en.notes: A water-filled moat around a castle (お堀) or an artificial canal. Common in place names and surnames (堀川, 堀田).

examples[].german: Obeying the law is a citizen's duty.
This book introduces effective study methods.
en.notes: Law in general: 法を守る (to obey the law), 法に触れる (to violate the law). As a suffix also "method": 学習法, 方法.

examples[].german: I searched everywhere for my lost wallet but could not find it.
He travels all over Japan for work.
en.notes: In many places: 方々探す (to search everywhere), 方々に知り合いがいる. Often written in kana too (ほうぼう). The same spelling read かたがた means "ladies and gentlemen".

examples[].german: I summarized the survey results in a table.
At the station, I checked the train timetable.
For the detailed figures, please see Table 2.
en.notes: 表 in the reading ひょう means "table, list, chart" and very often stands at the end of compounds such as 時刻表 "timetable", 一覧表 "overview list" or 成績表 "report card". Typical are 表にする／表にまとめる "to put in tabular form" and 表1 "Table 1" in texts. Do not confuse with the same spelling 表/おもて "front side, outside" (表に出る) and the homophone 雹/ひょう "hail".

examples[].german: On Sunday mornings, a market is held at the harbor.
I bought fresh fish at the morning market at my travel destination.
I found an old camera at the flea market in the park.
en.notes: 市 in the reading いち means "market, fair", a place where goods are sold regularly. On its own it appears mainly in 市が立つ "a market is held"; it is more often found in words such as 朝市 "morning market", 蚤の市 "flea market" and 市場/いちば "market (hall)". The reading し (its own card 市/し), by contrast, means "city" as an administrative unit (横浜市). Do not confuse with 位置/いち "position".

en.meaning: market, marketplace (concrete place, e.g. fish market)
examples[].german: Every morning, fresh fish is laid out at the fish market near the harbor.
On weekends I buy vegetables and fruit at the market.
When traveling, I like to walk around the local markets.
en.notes: いちば is the concrete market with stalls where goods are sold: 魚市場 (うおいちば) "fish market", 青果市場 "fruit and vegetable market". The identically written 市場/しじょう (its own card), by contrast, refers to the abstract economic market: 株式市場, 市場経済, 市場調査. Rule of thumb: if you can go there and shop, いちば is usually meant.

en.meaning: one o'clock; once, for a time; temporary
examples[].german: The meeting starts at one o'clock in the afternoon.
As the rain got heavier, the game was temporarily suspended.
en.notes: Three meanings: one o'clock (午後一時), once or for a while (一時は人気があった) and temporary (一時停止, 一時的).

en.meaning: to harbor (hope, doubt, grudge); to hold in one's arms, to embrace (formal)
examples[].german: Since childhood I had harbored the dream of becoming a pilot.
Many citizens harbor doubts about this plan.
The mother held the newborn to her chest.
en.notes: Same spelling as 抱く/だく "to embrace" (its own card), but いだく is formal and is used mainly for feelings and thoughts: 夢を抱く "to harbor a dream", 疑問を抱く "to harbor doubts", 不安を抱く "to feel anxious". Physically embracing a person is だく in everyday speech; いだく sounds literary in this sense. Since the kanji form can have both readings, the collocation decides.

examples[].german: No, I booked for tomorrow.
No, thank you. I don't need a taxi.
en.notes: いえ is a short form of いいえ. With this reply you contradict or correct an assumption; an explanation can follow. いえ、結構です politely declines an offer. Pronounce two morae, い・え; いいえ is longer. The identically read 家 means "house" and is a different word. This card practices the negative reply, not older exclamations of surprise or forms of address.

examples[].german: I went by train on the way there and by bus on the way back.
I bought a souvenir at a shop I stopped by on the way there.
en.notes: 行き（いき）is the outbound trip or the way there. 行き and 帰り（かえり）are often contrasted: one means of transport out, another back. 行きに means "on the way there". The card covers the noun; the identically written form in destination expressions and the reading ゆき must be distinguished according to their respective usage.

examples[].german: What kind of creatures live in this pond?
If you keep a living creature, take responsibility for it to the end.
en.notes: General term for everything alive, especially animals and insects. More everyday than 生物（せいぶつ）, which is used more in science and school.

examples[].german: Just you wait. I will definitely win.
If you eat that much, you'll upset your stomach before long.
en.notes: Announces something that will soon happen, often as a warning: 今に分かる (you'll see soon enough). Not to be confused with 今にも (any moment now).

examples[].german: Bali is in Indonesia.
I work with a colleague from Indonesia.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. Do not confuse it with インド (India).

examples[].german: In autumn, the rice plants in the paddies turn yellow.
The farmers are harvesting the rice.
en.notes: The plant in the field; harvested, hulled rice is called 米, cooked rice ご飯. Rice harvest: 稲刈り（いねかり）.

examples[].german: The printer is out of ink.
This pen uses blue ink.
en.notes: Ink for fountain pens and printers (プリンターのインク). Also written インキ.

examples[].german: I installed new software.
Please do not turn off the power until the installation is finished.
en.notes: As a verb with する. Opposite: アンインストール. For apps, people often simply say ダウンロード.

examples[].german: Welcome! Please come in.
Come visit us again anytime.
en.notes: Casual greeting for guests (at home, in a small shop); in stores the formal form is いらっしゃいませ. Also a polite request: こっちへいらっしゃい (come here).

examples[].german: It is important to state your intentions clearly.
The person himself does not seem to intend to quit.
en.notes: What one wants to do or communicate: 意思を伝える, 本人の意思. 意志 is written more for strong will and willpower (意志が強い).

examples[].german: If you're in trouble, contact me anytime.
This convenience store is always open.
en.notes: "Whenever": いつでも来てください. "Never" is not expressed with いつでも or いつも, but with 一度も～ない or 決して～ない. The kanji 何時でも is rare.

examples[].german: Please stay healthy forever.
Don't sleep forever, get up already.
en.notes: "For all eternity" (いつまでも元気で) or, reproachfully, "for ages" (いつまでも寝ている). Kanji 何時までも is rare.

examples[].german: I received a wristwatch from my grandfather as a gift for starting school.
To celebrate the victory, the team went out for yakiniku together.
At the celebration, I gave the toast.
en.notes: The plain form of お祝い (its own card), which is more polite and more common in conversation. Without お, 祝い appears mainly in compounds such as 誕生祝い, 入学祝い, 結婚祝い "gift for ..." and in fixed expressions such as 祝いの席 "celebration, festive occasion". Related verb: 祝う "to celebrate, to congratulate".

examples[].german: "Are you tired?" "No, I'm still fine."
I think there were a hundred people in the hall, no, two hundred.
No, I don't think that's right.
en.notes: A casual "no" in conversation; the more polite form is いいえ (its own card). In the middle of a sentence, いや corrects one's own statement: 百人、いや二百人 "a hundred, no, rather two hundred". Almost always written in kana; 否 is a rare spelling. A word that sounds the same but is a different word is 嫌/いや "unpleasant, to dislike".

examples[].german: A big jet is flying across the sky.
The company president apparently owns a private jet.
en.notes: ジェット (jet) + 機 (machine, aircraft). Today people usually just say 飛行機.

examples[].german: I always wear jeans on weekends.
The jeans at this store are durable and cheap.
en.notes: Pants made of denim; also ジーパン. Pants are put on with はく: ジーンズをはく.

examples[].german: It is better to ask the person concerned directly about important matters.
Please do not apply this medicine directly to the skin.
en.notes: Without a detour or intermediate layer: 床に直に座る, 本人に直に聞く. Often in kana じかに. Not to be confused with じきに (soon), which can also be written 直に.

examples[].german: It will soon be spring, won't it?
He will come soon, so let's wait a little.
en.notes: Colloquial for すぐ／まもなく, usually in kana: もうじき (very soon), じきに分かる (will be clear soon). Kanji 直.

examples[].german: Please check the departure time of the train.
He did not come even at the agreed time.
en.notes: A specific point in time, especially for timetables and appointments: 出発時刻, 時刻表 (timetable). 時間, by contrast, often means a length of time.

examples[].german: I do clerical work at a bank.
The administrative procedures took a long time.
en.notes: Desk and administrative work: 事務の仕事, 事務員 (office worker), 事務所 (office).

examples[].german: He decided that himself.
They say that the teacher himself was also bad at studying when he was young.
en.notes: Emphasizes a noun or pronoun: 彼自身 (he himself), 自分自身 (oneself). Similar sounding: 地震 (earthquake), 自信 (self-confidence).

en.meaning: superior grade, upper level; first volume
examples[].german: My grades were in the upper middle.
This novel is split into three volumes. I bought the first one first.
en.notes: As a noun, じょう refers to a higher quality grade or to the first volume of a two- or three-volume edition. In a ranking it often appears together with 中 and 下, e.g. 中の上 "upper middle". On menus, 上 can mark a better version. When reading a book series, 上 is the counterpart of 下, or of 中 and 下. The identically written suffix in 安全上 "for safety reasons" has its own use.

examples[].german: For safety reasons, this door cannot be opened.
Even if there is no legal problem, you should explain it to the neighbors.
en.notes: Here 上 is attached to a noun and names the viewpoint or area to which a statement relates. 安全上の理由 are reasons concerning safety; 法律上 means "legally speaking". Often の and another noun follow, or は as a topic particle. Unlike うえ "above", this じょう is firmly attached to the preceding word. It does not rate quality and does not denote a book volume.

en.meaning: to go up to Tokyo; to move to Tokyo
examples[].german: At eighteen, I moved to Tokyo to enter university.
My mother is coming to Tokyo next week, so I plan to show her around.
en.notes: Formerly "to go to the capital", today almost always "to go or move to Tokyo", especially from the provinces. As a verb 上京する. Homophone: 状況 (situation).

examples[].german: Today I bought good meat.
This coat is old, but the fabric is first-rate.
en.notes: Of good quality: 上等な肉, 上等な服. Sounds a little old-fashioned; today 高級 is often used.

en.meaning: order, sequence (also suffix: 番号順 = in numerical order)
examples[].german: Please enter the room in the order your names are called.
The children lined up in order of height.
The words in this dictionary are arranged in gojuon order.
en.notes: 順 means "order, sequence" and appears mainly in fixed patterns: 順に "in order", 〜の順に "in the order of ..." and as a suffix as in 五十音順 "in gojuon (kana) order" or 背の順 "in order of height". On its own, e.g. for "to be one's turn", one usually says 順番 (its own card): 順番が来る.

examples[].german: In Japan, owning a gun is strictly restricted.
The police officer aimed his gun.
en.notes: Firearm in general; handgun: 拳銃. In Japan, private gun ownership is strictly restricted. Similar sounding: 十.

examples[].german: I left my charger at home.
Excuse me, could I borrow a charger?
en.notes: 充電 (charging) + 器 (device). Portable battery pack: モバイルバッテリー.

examples[].german: This company values character more than experience.
We continue to make products with an emphasis on quality.
en.notes: To regard something as important, as a verb 重視する: 経験を重視する (to value experience). As a suffix: 品質重視 (quality first). Opposite: 軽視 (to belittle).

examples[].german: Pets are allowed in this apartment, so I can keep a dog.
The job ad said "inexperienced applicants welcome".
In math, I only got a "pass" in the first semester.
en.notes: Means "allowed, permissible" and appears mainly in brief form on signs, in ads and on forms: ペット可, 喫煙可, 未経験者可. The opposite is 不可 "not allowed"; 可もなく不可もなく means "neither good nor bad, mediocre". In university grades, 可 is the lowest passing level (優・良・可). Do not confuse with the question particle か.

en.meaning: day (counter and day of the month, e.g. 二日, 三日, 十日, 二十日)
examples[].german: I'll contact you again in three days regarding the details.
May 5 is Children's Day, and schools are closed.
This work should be finished in ten days.
en.notes: Native Japanese reading of 日 in dates and day counts with native numerals: ふつか, みっか, よっか up to とおか as well as じゅうよっか, はつか (20) and にじゅうよっか. All other numbers take 〜日/にち (its own card), e.g. じゅういちにち; the first is ついたち, "one day" is いちにち. The same form denotes the day of the month and the duration in days.

examples[].german: Today we will study Lesson 5.
A senior colleague from my section taught me the work.
en.notes: A lesson in a textbook (第三課 = Lesson 3) and a section in a company or government office (課長 = section chief). Similar sounding: 蚊 (mosquito).

examples[].german: I rented a car at the airport and drove all the way around Hokkaido.
In big cities, many people don't own a car.
A police car with its siren on drove past.
en.notes: Rare on its own; mainly a component of loanwords and compounds: レンタカー "rental car", マイカー "one's own car", パトカー "patrol car", カーナビ "car navigation", カーシェア "car sharing". The normal everyday word for "car" is 車 (くるま), more formally 自動車.

examples[].german: I laid a new carpet in the living room.
I spilled coffee on the carpet.
en.notes: Also じゅうたん. カーペットを敷く (to lay a carpet).

examples[].german: It's hot, so let's rest in the shade of the tree.
Stop badmouthing people behind their backs.
en.notes: A place without direct light (木の陰 = in the shade of a tree) or something hidden: 陰で (behind someone's back). The silhouette of a person or thing is more often 影.

examples[].german: Toward evening the shadows grow long.
The mountain is reflected in the lake.
en.notes: The outline that a body casts (人の影), or a reflection (水に映る影). In contrast, a shady place is 陰（かげ）.

examples[].german: It is difficult to judge how much force to use.
How are you feeling?
en.notes: The right degree: 火加減 (heat level), 塩加減 (amount of salt), 手加減 (going easy). Also one's condition: お加減はいかがですか (How are you feeling?). Verb: 加減する (to adjust, to regulate).

examples[].german: I picked a whole basket full of mandarin oranges.
I let the bird out of the cage.
en.notes: Basket (買い物かご = shopping basket) or cage (鳥かご). Usually written in hiragana かご.

examples[].german: Next week there is a welcome party for the new students.
I joined a society that researches the town's history.
en.notes: Meeting, gathering, party (歓迎会 = welcome party, 飲み会 = drinking party) and society, club (会に入る). Very productive as a suffix.

examples[].german: If you have questions, please ask the person in charge.
In class, I became the one in charge of watering the flowers.
en.notes: Person or office responsible for something: 係の人, 受付係 (reception). In school classes, tasks are assigned as 係 (掃除係).

en.meaning: to catch (an illness); to fall ill with
examples[].german: Last year I caught the flu and stayed away from school for a week.
Before the trip, I looked up illnesses that are easy to catch locally.
en.notes: 病気にかかる means to fall ill with a disease. The illness takes に, the affected person takes が or は. The spelling 罹る marks this illness sense; in everyday writing, kana かかる is usual. As an intransitive godan verb it forms かかります, かかって, かかった. The identically read uses of 掛かる for time spent or hanging belong to a different card.

examples[].german: Children are racing each other in the park.
I came in first in the footrace at the sports day.
en.notes: A children's word; at the school sports day: 運動会の駆けっこ.

en.meaning: to draw; to paint; to sketch (reading かく)
examples[].german: My younger sister drew a picture of a cat on paper.
Please draw a simple map here.
en.notes: 描く is read かく here and denotes drawing, painting or sketching. The picture or depicted thing comes before を; the surface can be marked with に. The て-form is 描いて（かいて）. The same kanji also has the reading えがく; for "to describe" or "to depict", えがく is normally used. This entry practices concrete drawing with かく.

en.meaning: establishment; consolidation; setting up (of a system)
examples[].german: Establishing a new treatment takes time.
The government is aiming to establish a safe system.
This brand took ten years to establish its position.
en.notes: 確立 is the noun for "to firmly establish something": a system, method or position is set up permanently. Typical are 制度の確立 "establishment of a system", 地位の確立 "consolidation of one's position" and 確立を目指す. The verb 確立する "to establish, settle" has its own card. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding 確率 "probability".

examples[].german: I ordered a cocktail at the bar.
She can't hold her liquor, so she had just one sweet cocktail.
en.notes: A mixed alcoholic drink: カクテルを作る (to mix a cocktail).

examples[].german: We called a professional photographer to the wedding.
A cameraman from the TV station was filming the scene of the accident.
en.notes: Occupation: photographer (press, weddings) or cameraman in film and television.

en.meaning: upper or first part; upstream; the authorities; superior quality (older)
examples[].german: The boat slowly moved upstream along the river.
Please read this story in order, starting with the first volume.
The merchant in this story calls fine-quality bolts of cloth "top grade".
The villagers obeyed the notice handed down from the authorities.
en.notes: かみ refers to the beginning or upper side of a connected whole: for a river, the direction toward the source; for a text, the front part. Its counterpart is しも. 上の巻 can be read かみのまき in older texts; for the first volume, じょう is usual today. Rating something as especially good quality also belongs to older uses. In historical narratives, 上 can refer to the authorities or their offices; with お this meaning appears in お上. The reading うえ is used for ordinary location expressions such as "on the table".

examples[].german: Staff of the library discussed the operation of the facility.
This facility prohibits photography in its exhibition rooms.
en.notes: 館 can refer independently to an institution already mentioned, such as a library or a museum. 館の運営 means the operation of this house; この館では introduces a statement about its rules. This usage is more common in reports and descriptions. The identically written word 館 (やかた) for a stately residence has a different reading. The ending in building names is practiced separately.

en.meaning: building; hall; house (suffix in building names)
examples[].german: Cooking classes are held at the community center every week.
I could see the river from my room at the ryokan.
en.notes: The suffix 館 belongs to names of larger buildings and institutions: 公民館 (こうみんかん) is a community center, 旅館 (りょかん) a Japanese inn. The whole expression determines the kind of house. In older descriptions 館 can also denote a lodging or a large house; it does not follow that every apartment or hotel is simply called 館 today. For an ordinary hotel, ホテル is usual.

examples[].german: Hearing his explanation, I got the impression that the preparations were not sufficient.
When I first saw that building, I was struck by a sense of strangeness.
en.notes: 感 is a rather literary noun for a feeling or an impression. 感を抱く means to gain an impression or harbor a feeling; 奇異の感に打たれる describes feeling something strange. The content can be explained by a statement with という. In everyday conversation, 感じ is often more common. Here you practice 感 as a noun in its own right; compound feeling words such as 安心感 are further expressions.

examples[].german: We send water into another container through a thin pipe.
Because the old pipe developed a crack, it had to be replaced.
en.notes: In technical descriptions, 管（かん） refers to a hollow pipe or tube. 管を通して水を送る describes a conduit; 管に亀裂が入る describes damage to the component. The other reading くだ can also refer to a tube; かん is found especially in technical descriptions and compounds.

examples[].german: This volume depicts the protagonist's childhood.
The last reel of the old film was found in a warehouse.
en.notes: 巻 (かん) denotes a volume of a multivolume book or a reel of a film. この巻 means the volume currently being looked at; 映画の最後の巻 the last film reel. After numbers, 巻 can also be used to count these units, but this card practices the noun without a preceding number. The reading まき and the verb 巻く (まく) are thereby not practiced.

examples[].german: I have no money this month, so I'll skip eating out.
They say time is money, so let's not waste time.
He isn't working for the money.
en.notes: Means the same as お金 (its own card), but sounds more direct without お: rather casual or rough in conversation (金がない "to have no money"), matter-of-fact in writing. Common in compounds and sayings such as 金持ち "rich person" and 時は金なり "time is money". The same kanji read きん means "gold"; 鐘/かね "bell" is a different word.

examples[].german: Kangaroos raise their young in the pouch on their belly.
A kangaroo jumped out onto the road.
en.notes: Zoo animal in katakana; the pouch is called 袋（ふくろ）.

examples[].german: When I opened the box that had arrived, it was empty inside.
My wallet is empty, so I'll walk home today.
en.notes: 空／から refers to a state without contents. As a noun it can take の: 空の箱 "an empty box"; at the end of a sentence it is 箱は空だ. For a wallet, 空 means there is no money in it. Other uses as part of a word are learned with the respective compound. 空／そら means "sky" and is a different reading.

en.meaning: loan; debt owed to one, favor owed
examples[].german: He owes me ten thousand yen.
I helped you, so now you owe me one.
en.notes: What has been lent, or what someone owes you: 〜に貸しがある = someone owes me something (also a favor). Opposite: 借り. As a prefix in 貸し切り, 貸し出し.

examples[].german: I thank all the people who cooperated with us.
Many local people gathered at the venue.
en.notes: Respectful plural of 方（かた）: 関係者の方々 (all those involved), ご来場の方々. The same spelling read ほうぼう means "everywhere".

examples[].german: At the end of the year I'm busy tidying my room.
Everyone helped with the cleanup after the party.
en.notes: Noun of 片付ける; 後片付け (tidying up afterward, e.g. after a meal).

examples[].german: I had my hair cut at the hair salon.
That scene was cut because of the budget.
en.notes: As the verb カットする: 髪をカットする, 予算をカットする (to cut back), シーンをカットする (to cut out).

examples[].german: I got a leather wallet for my birthday.
This leather bag gets better the more you use it.
en.notes: Tanned animal hide: 革の靴, 革製品. Raw hide is 皮. The reading かく appears in 革命 (revolution). Similar sounding: 川 (river).

examples[].german: Please peel the apple.
I got sunburned and the skin on my back peeled.
en.notes: The outer covering of living things and fruit: りんごの皮をむく (to peel an apple), 木の皮. Tanned leather is written 革.

examples[].german: Lovely flowers are blooming in the garden.
The child sang in a sweet voice.
en.notes: い-adjective, somewhat more refined than かわいい; emphasizes an endearing impression. Kanji 可愛らしい.

examples[].german: I have a meeting on Tuesday afternoon.
Burnable trash is collected every Tuesday and Friday.
Next week I'll be away on a business trip from Tuesday to Thursday.
en.notes: Short form of 火曜日 "Tuesday", very common in timetables, schedules, opening hours and casual conversation (火曜の午後, 毎週火曜). Meaning and use are the same, just without 日; in tables it is often shortened further to 火. Do not confuse with the homophones 通う "to go regularly" and 歌謡 "song".

examples[].german: He is so stingy that he won't even treat you to a cup of coffee.
Don't be so petty.
en.notes: Noun and な-adjective: けちな人 (a stingy person), けちをつける (to find fault). Often in katakana, ケチ.

examples[].german: At New Year, I discussed this year's plan with my family.
The policy of protecting the forest was decided as the town's hundred-year plan.
en.notes: Here 計 means a plan or scheme and appears especially in literary compounds such as 一年の計. In ordinary conversation, 計画 is the usual, more explicit word. の links the plan with its time frame or its owner. In other compounds the same character also has meanings such as measuring instrument or total; this reading means the scheme.

examples[].german: I pay my respects to the athletes' efforts.
You should speak to older people with respect.
en.notes: Formal: 敬意を表す／払う (to express one's respect). Similar sound: 経緯 (course of events).

examples[].german: Please show your ticket at the entrance.
In this shop, you buy a ticket first and then order.
en.notes: Often in compounds: 乗車券 (train ticket), 入場券 (admission ticket), 食券 (meal ticket), 割引券 (discount coupon).

examples[].german: I have no idea who the culprit is.
I walked on the assumption that the station was roughly around here.
en.notes: A rough estimate: 見当がつく (to be able to guess), 見当もつかない (to have no idea), 見当違い (misjudgment). Similar sounding: 検討 (examination, consideration).

en.meaning: to be satisfied; to feel better (once something is done)
examples[].german: You may cry until you feel better.
I can't rest until I have checked everything myself.
en.notes: The inner need is satisfied. Common: 気が済むまで ("until one is satisfied") and, reproachfully, 何度謝れば気が済むの？

examples[].german: My message shows as read, but I haven't gotten a reply.
When someone leaves my message on read, I feel a little lonely.
en.notes: Indicator in messenger apps such as LINE. 既読スルー／既読無視: to read a message but not reply. Opposite: 未読（みどく）.

en.meaning: gold; gold color; gold medal, first place; (abbr.) Friday
examples[].german: That athlete won a gold medal at the Olympics.
This ring is made of real gold.
Do you know the proverb "Silence is golden"?
en.notes: 金 with the reading きん means the metal "gold", the color (金色) and first place (金メダル); on calendars it is also an abbreviation for 金曜日 "Friday". The same kanji with the reading かね means "money" and in everyday use is almost always used politely as お金 (its own card). In sayings, 金 stands for something very valuable, such as 沈黙は金.

examples[].german: After the entrance ceremony, we took a commemorative photo in front of the school gate.
To mark our tenth wedding anniversary, we went on a family trip.
I bought this little doll as a souvenir of the trip.
en.notes: 記念 means "commemoration, remembrance of an event" and is found in many compounds such as 記念写真 "commemorative photo"; 記念日 and 記念品 have their own cards. Typical patterns are 〜の記念に "in memory of ..." and 〜を記念して "on the occasion of, in honor of ...". Do not confuse with the homophone 祈念 "prayer" (its own card).

examples[].german: It is better not to lend or borrow money with friends.
He has a sound sense of money.
en.notes: Formal word for money: 金銭トラブル (money trouble), 金銭感覚 (sense of money). In everyday speech, お金 is used.

examples[].german: On Friday nights, I usually go out for drinks with friends.
The deadline for the report is next Friday.
This shop is open from Monday to Friday.
en.notes: 金曜 is the short form of 金曜日 "Friday" (its own card). It is common in spoken language as well as in timetables, schedules and calendars, e.g. 金曜の夜 or 月曜から金曜まで. In formal texts and announcements the full form 金曜日 is preferred; calendars often show just 金.

en.meaning: to dislike; to hate; to avoid
examples[].german: Cats are said to dislike water.
If you say things like that, everyone will dislike you.
en.notes: Transitive verb: 〜を嫌う. In everyday speech, the な-adjective 嫌い（〜が嫌いだ）is much more common; 嫌う sounds more written and often describes a general aversion. The passive 嫌われる means "to be disliked".

en.meaning: piece, slice; scrap of cloth; sharpness
examples[].german: May I have a piece of cake?
This kitchen knife cuts very well.
en.notes: A cut-off piece (パン一切れ = a slice of bread; also a counter), a piece of cloth (布切れ) and the sharpness of a blade (切れがいい).

examples[].german: I tied the boat to the shore.
I swam across to the opposite bank of the river.
en.notes: The edge of a body of water: 川岸 (riverbank), 向こう岸 (the opposite shore), 海岸 (seashore).

examples[].german: The kitchen in the new apartment is spacious.
My mother is cooking in the kitchen.
en.notes: Modern kitchen (in apartment listings: 1LDK = one room plus living, dining and kitchen area). Traditional word: 台所.

examples[].german: I stayed near Lake Biwa and walked along the lakeshore in the morning.
I'm looking for old photos of Lake Suwa in the library.
en.notes: 湖（こ）stands at the end of lake names. 琵琶湖 is read びわこ, 諏訪湖 すわこ. The suffix marks the lake as part of the name; the free word for lake is 湖（みずうみ）. Not every name has to be read by the same pattern, so one learns the full place name.

en.meaning: small- (prefix, e.g. 小鳥, 小雨); somewhat, a little (小一時間); petty (小役人)
examples[].german: A light rain has kept falling since morning.
Please speak in a low voice in the library.
I was made to wait nearly an hour at the station.
en.notes: A native Japanese prefix before nouns: "small" (小鳥 "little bird", 小雨 "drizzle", 小声 "low voice"), "just under, about" before quantities (小一時間 "nearly an hour") and derogatory "insignificant, petty" (小役人 "petty official"). Before adjectives it intensifies slightly (小ぎれい "neat and pretty"). The on reading しょう is used in Sino-Japanese words such as 小学校; the independent adjective is 小さい.

examples[].german: Koalas spend almost the whole day sleeping.
I held a koala in Australia.
en.notes: A zoo animal, written in katakana; lives in Australia (オーストラリア).

examples[].german: I fell in love for the first time in high school.
This film is a story of the painful love between two people.
en.notes: Romantic, yearning love: 恋をする (to fall in love), 初恋 (first love). 愛 is broader and deeper (including parental love and love of one's neighbor). Similar sound: 鯉 (carp).

examples[].german: On rainy days I dry my clothes at the laundromat.
There is a laundromat near the apartment.
en.notes: Coin-operated laundry; many have large dryers (乾燥機) suitable for futons.

examples[].german: My grandfather returned to his hometown for the first time in sixty years.
I left my hometown for work and came to Tokyo.
Japan is my second home.
en.notes: こきょう is the Sino-Japanese reading of 故郷 and sounds more matter-of-fact than ふるさと (its own card), which sounds emotional and poetic. Typical are 故郷に帰る "to return to one's hometown", 故郷を離れる "to leave one's hometown" and 第二の故郷 "second home". In songs and poems, 故郷 is usually read ふるさと; in reports, news and forms, rather こきょう.

examples[].german: Bread and udon are made from wheat.
This product contains wheat.
en.notes: The plant or grain; flour is called 小麦粉. Allergy notice on packaging: 小麦を含む (contains wheat).

examples[].german: I never thought it would be this cold.
I can't eat this much.
en.notes: Refers to something close to the speaker or in the current situation: こんなに寒いとは思わなかった. Series こんなに・そんなに・あんなに・どんなに.

en.meaning: these days; today (reading こんにち)
examples[].german: These days it is easy to contact people overseas.
As of today, we are changing the location of the reception.
en.notes: こんにち can mean "these days" or, in a formal text, "today". 今日では contrasts the present time with earlier conditions; 今日より can mean "from today" in a notice. For the single day of today, きょう is also used. Do not confuse the word with the greeting こんにちは: its final part is pronounced wa.

examples[].german: I take lessons from a tennis coach.
The training schedule was changed on the coach's instructions.
en.notes: The coach of a team; as a verb コーチする (to coach, to instruct). The head coach is often called 監督.

en.meaning: code (identifier, program code); code of rules
examples[].german: If you enter this code, shipping is free.
My older brother writes code on his computer every day.
en.notes: Code in the sense of an identifier or symbol (QRコード, バーコード), program code, and rules (ドレスコード). Homophones: コード (cord) and コード (chord).

examples[].german: Please read these materials by tomorrow.
All of these are handmade.
en.notes: Plural of これ, mainly in texts and presentations. In conversation, mostly これ or こういうもの. Also written これ等.

examples[].german: My mother taught me the trick to cooking delicious rice.
I finally got the knack of riding a bicycle.
There is a little knack to Japanese pronunciation.
en.notes: コツ is the practical knack that makes something easier to accomplish: 料理のコツ, 〜するコツ. Typical is コツをつかむ "to get the hang of it". In this meaning it is almost always written in katakana; the kanji 骨 is normally read ほね "bone" (separate card).

examples[].german: My father works in a small workshop in town.
This small neighborhood factory makes aircraft parts.
There is an old workshop behind the house, and I hear the machines every day.
en.notes: Same spelling as 工場（こうじょう） "factory", but with the mixed reading こうば (Sino-Japanese こう + native ば). こうば sounds more colloquial and refers more to a small workshop or craft business, especially in 町工場（まちこうば） "small family-run factory". For large, modern industrial plants (自動車工場) one says こうじょう; in written text without context, こうじょう is usually meant.

examples[].german: I dropped an expensive watch.
This painting is extremely valuable.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun, more formal than 高い: 高価な宝石. Similar sounding: 効果 (effect), 硬貨 (coin).

examples[].german: Cultural exchange is actively carried out between the two countries.
At the weekend, I took part in a social event with international students.
Alternating current flows through household outlets.
en.notes: Noun for the verb card 交流する: 文化交流 "cultural exchange", 国際交流 "international exchange", 交流会 "get-together", 〜との交流 "exchange with ...". Typical are 交流が盛んだ and 交流を深める. In electrical engineering, 交流 means "alternating current" (opposite 直流 "direct current"). Not to be confused with the homophones 拘留/勾留 "detention".

examples[].german: The two have been together for three years.
He has a wide circle of acquaintances and knows many people.
en.notes: Formal term for social contact (交際が広い = to have many connections) and for a romantic relationship: 交際している (to be going out).

examples[].german: Between tea and coffee, I like the latter.
Of the two proposals, the latter was chosen at the meeting.
en.notes: Refers to the second of two things mentioned; counterpart: 前者（ぜんしゃ, the former). Typical in comparisons and written texts.

examples[].german: The expressway was crowded on the weekend.
This train runs at high speed.
en.notes: High speed (高速で走る, 高速インターネット) and, in conversation, short for 高速道路 (expressway): 高速に乗る. Similar sounding: 拘束 (restraint).

examples[].german: We spent a night in a hut at the top of the mountain.
An old bicycle is stored in the shed in the garden.
en.notes: A small, simple building: 山小屋 (mountain hut), 物置小屋 (tool shed), 犬小屋 (doghouse).

examples[].german: Explain the meaning of the following phrase.
My grandfather composes a haiku every morning.
en.notes: A linguistic segment (語句 = words and phrases), a verse of five or seven morae, and especially a haiku (句を詠む). Homophones: 九, 区.

examples[].german: The outbound train is five minutes late.
From here on, a long downhill road continues.
en.notes: Direction away from Tokyo or from the starting point of a line: 下りの電車. Opposite: 上り（のぼり）. Also a downward slope: 下り坂.

en.meaning: to pass through; to go under something
examples[].german: I passed through the shrine's torii gate and went inside.
This road goes under the railway tracks and comes out on the opposite side of the station.
The culprit slipped past the police and escaped.
en.notes: くぐる means "to pass under something" or "to go through an opening"; what is passed through takes を (門をくぐる, 鳥居をくぐる). Figuratively it means "to get around, slip through" (法の網をくぐる, 警察の目をくぐる). It is almost always written in kana, because 潜る is normally read もぐる "to dive, go underground" (separate card).

examples[].german: I could see a whale from the boat.
A whale is not a fish but a mammal.
en.notes: Often written in kana (くじら／クジラ). Despite the 魚 radical, it is a mammal. Whale watching: ホエールウォッチング.

examples[].german: I am in class 3-2.
We divided the class into four groups and played a game.
en.notes: School class (三年二組 = class 2 of the 3rd year), group or team, and a set of things that belong together. As a counter for pairs and groups: 一組.

examples[].german: My father belongs to his company's union.
The farmers got together and formed a cooperative.
en.notes: A union of people with shared interests: 労働組合 (labor union), 協同組合 (cooperative).

en.meaning: to put together; to fold (arms, legs); to team up
examples[].german: He was thinking with his arms crossed.
I formed a team with friends and entered the tournament.
en.notes: Godan verb, mostly transitive: 腕を組む (to fold one's arms), 足を組む (to cross one's legs), チームを組む (to form a team), 予定を組む (to draw up a plan); intransitive 〜と組む (to team up with someone). Related: 取り組む (to tackle, to work on something).

en.meaning: kun reading (Japanese reading of a kanji)
examples[].german: Please memorize the kun and on readings of this kanji.
In this dictionary, the kun readings are written in hiragana.
en.notes: The Japanese reading of a kanji, e.g. 山 = やま; counterpart: 音 (Sino-Japanese reading, 山 = さん). Mostly as 訓読み. Similar sounding: 〜君.

examples[].german: In the past, only people of high rank could enter.
Give the digit in the hundreds place.
en.notes: Rank in a hierarchy or level of quality (位が高い) and a digit position (十の位 = tens place). The homophone くらい "about" is a particle and is usually written in hiragana.

examples[].german: Listening to classical music before bed calms me down.
This restaurant has a classic atmosphere.
en.notes: On its own it usually means "classical music" (クラシックを聴く); also "classic, timeless" (クラシックなデザイン).

examples[].german: The end of the year is so busy that I can't rest properly.
In autumn, dusk comes early.
en.notes: Especially 年の暮れ／暮れ (year-end, also the お歳暮 season) and 日の暮れ (nightfall). Verb: 暮れる.

examples[].german: I put plenty of cream on the cake.
My hands get dry in winter, so I apply cream.
en.notes: Cream for cakes (生クリーム = whipped cream) and skin cream (ハンドクリーム). Ice cream: アイスクリーム.

examples[].german: I ate cake with my family at Christmas.
When December comes, the town is full of Christmas decorations.
en.notes: Not a public holiday in Japan. Christmas Eve (クリスマスイブ) is seen more as an evening for couples; many people eat chicken and クリスマスケーキ.

examples[].german: The dog is tied up with a chain.
I chained the bicycle to a post.
en.notes: A chain made of metal links: 犬を鎖でつなぐ. Compound: 連鎖 (chain reaction, linkage).

examples[].german: He is the captain of the soccer team.
The captain encouraged everyone on the team.
en.notes: Mainly a team captain in sports; in a school club also 部長. A ship's captain is usually 船長.

examples[].german: A new bureau in charge of tourism was set up at city hall.
The program was cancelled due to the station's policy.
en.notes: An administrative department (〜局 in ministries) and short for a broadcasting station or post office: テレビ局 (TV station), 郵便局. In conversation, 局 alone means "the station".

en.meaning: coexistence; living together (alternate reading of きょうぞん)
examples[].german: Coexistence between humans and wild animals is not easy.
We aim for the mutual prosperity of local shops and the large supermarket.
In this town, various cultures coexist.
en.notes: 共存 "coexistence, peaceful living side by side" has two readings: きょうそん is the original, traditional one, and きょうぞん (separate card) is more common today in daily life and the media. Both are considered correct and mean the same; in the set phrase 共存共栄 "to exist and prosper together" one often hears きょうそん. Typical combinations are 自然と共存する and 共存を図る.

en.meaning: former, old, previous (prefix, e.g. 旧姓, 旧市街); old lunar calendar
examples[].german: I hear this old school building will be demolished next year.
Even after getting married, I use my maiden name at work.
I have traveled through the countries of the former Soviet Union.
en.notes: 旧〜 is a Sino-Japanese prefix for "former, old, previous" and stands directly before nouns: 旧校舎 "old school building", 旧ソ連 "former Soviet Union". Common compounds such as 旧姓, 旧暦 and 旧市街 have their own cards. The counterpart is 新〜 "new" (新校舎); 古い, by contrast, is the general adjective "old" and not a prefix.

examples[].german: I passed level 3 of the Kanji Test.
He is in a different class from me, so we won't meet in the competition.
en.notes: Rank or level, e.g. in exams (漢字検定3級) or weight classes in sports. Compounds: 高級 (high-class), 上級 (advanced), 同級生 (classmate). Similar sounding: 九.

examples[].german: A problem asking to find the volume of a sphere came up.
The pitcher put all his strength into the last pitch.
en.notes: Geometric sphere (球の体積); in compounds e.g. 野球 (baseball), 地球 (the Earth), 電球 (light bulb). In baseball also a counter for pitches: 一球.

examples[].german: After a brief pause, I answered the question.
Please arrange the chairs with gaps between them.
en.notes: 間 is read ま here and denotes an interval in time, a pause or a gap. 間を置く means to pause or leave an interval. 間がある describes free space between things. The reading あいだ of the same kanji belongs to a different usage and is not replaced by this entry.

examples[].german: Come on, don't be so angry.
Oh, what beautiful flowers!
en.notes: A versatile filler word: soothing (まあ、落ち着いて), qualifying "fairly, so-so" (まあまあ), hedging "well" and as an exclamation of surprise (まあ、きれい！).

examples[].german: I bought vegetables at the market in front of the station.
This product is popular in the Asian market.
en.notes: Market as a place (フリーマーケット = flea market) and as a sales market (海外マーケット). A traditional market is also called 市場（いちば）.

examples[].german: Today's game was a 3-1 loss for us.
It is also important to admit defeat honestly.
en.notes: Noun from 負ける: 勝ち負け (victory and defeat), 負けを認める (to admit defeat). Opposite: 勝ち.

examples[].german: I was so embarrassed that my face turned bright red.
That is a downright lie.
en.notes: な-adjective: 真っ赤なりんご, 顔が真っ赤になる (from shame or anger). Also 真っ赤なうそ (outright lie). Similarly formed: 真っ白, 真っ青.

examples[].german: Mom, I'm hungry.
I went to lunch with the other mothers I'm friends with.
en.notes: Child language for "mama"; also the proprietress of a bar (ママさん). Formal: 母; term of address: お母さん.

examples[].german: I have insurance just in case.
If by any chance you are late, please call.
en.notes: For very unlikely, usually undesirable cases: 万一の場合 (in an emergency), 万一遅れたら (if I should be late).

examples[].german: I go to work on a packed train every morning.
On a packed train, let's hold our bags in front of us.
en.notes: 満員 (full to capacity) + 電車. Typical of the rush hour (ラッシュアワー) in Tokyo.

en.meaning: circle; whole, full (e.g. 丸一日); suffix for ship names
examples[].german: Please circle the correct answer.
Yesterday I spent a whole day cleaning my room.
A large ship called "Nippon Maru" is moored in the harbor.
en.notes: 丸 まる is the "circle" and, in everyday Japanese, also the mark for "correct, yes" (丸をつける, opposite バツ). As a prefix it means "whole, full": 丸一日 "a whole day", 丸ごと "as a whole", 丸三年 "three full years". As a suffix it appears in ship names (〜丸). The adjective 丸い "round" is its own card; the spelling 円 for まる is rare and not to be confused with 円/えん "yen".

examples[].german: I caught a cold, so I'm wearing a mask.
I can't do without a mask during pollen season.
en.notes: Mostly the face mask that people in Japan wear for colds or hay fever: マスクをする／つける. Also a theatrical or facial mask.

examples[].german: The owner of the coffee shop made me a coffee.
I mastered driving in one year.
en.notes: The owner of a small cafe or bar, also as a form of address: マスター. As a verb マスターする = to master a skill.

examples[].german: Pine trees line the coast.
I asked a gardener to take care of the pine in the garden.
en.notes: An evergreen tree and a symbol of good luck (long life); 門松 are set up at New Year. In the 松竹梅 ranking, 松 is the highest. Similar sound: 待つ.

en.meaning: to be crazy about; to have a weakness for
examples[].german: I can't resist chocolate.
He has no eye for people, so he often gets fooled.
en.notes: Used with に: 甘いものに目がない ("to be crazy about sweets"). Less often also "to have no eye for something": 人を見る目がない (to be a poor judge of character).

en.meaning: to order, to command; to appoint
examples[].german: The president ordered his subordinates to conduct an investigation.
He was appointed manager of the Osaka branch.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb, formal; the person takes に: 部下に調査を命じる. Passive: 〜を命じられる (to be appointed to something). Written variant: 命ずる.

examples[].german: Mexican cuisine has many spicy dishes.
Mexico is south of the United States.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. Mexican food: メキシコ料理.

examples[].german: Please make a note of the important things.
There was a note lying on the desk.
en.notes: A short note; as a verb メモする (to jot down), colloquially メモる. Notepad: メモ帳.

examples[].german: This plan has a problem in terms of cost.
At the festival I wore a demon mask.
en.notes: Side or aspect (費用の面で = in terms of cost), mask (能の面) and surface (水面). The face itself is 顔.

examples[].german: This shirt is 100% cotton, so it is gentle on the skin.
In summer, cotton T-shirts are the coolest.
Before washing, please check whether it is cotton or polyester.
en.notes: 綿 めん is the Sino-Japanese reading for "cotton" as a material, as used on labels and when buying clothes: 綿100%, 綿のシャツ, 綿製品. The card 綿/わた, by contrast, means the cotton plant or "cotton wool, stuffing" (布団の綿, 綿あめ). Rule of thumb: fabric and clothing → めん, fluffy filling → わた; for cotton cloth, 木綿 (もめん) is also said in daily life.

examples[].german: The team has eleven members in all.
Let me introduce a new member.
en.notes: A member of a group, team or band. For registered members of a club, 会員 is also used.

en.meaning: food, meal; cooked rice (colloquial, rather male speech)
examples[].german: I'm hungry. Let's go get something to eat.
I was so busy that I didn't even have time for lunch.
A problem like this is a piece of cake.
en.notes: 飯 めし is the colloquial, rather masculine and rough word for "food, meal" and "cooked rice"; typical is 飯を食う instead of the polite ご飯を食べる (its own card ご飯). It is very common in compounds: 昼飯 "lunch", 朝飯 "breakfast", 晩飯 "dinner" and the idiom 朝飯前 "a piece of cake". With superiors or in polite speech, the standalone 飯 is avoided.

examples[].german: Learning a foreign language takes time.
You have to protect yourself.
en.notes: The body and one's own person, especially in set phrases: 身につける (to acquire; to wear), 身を守る (to protect oneself), 相手の身になる (to put oneself in someone's shoes).

examples[].german: In autumn, this tree bears red fruit.
The children gathered nuts in the forest.
It was a long meeting, but hardly anything substantial came of it.
en.notes: 実 み is the native word for "fruit, nut, berry" on plants: 実がなる "to bear fruit", 木の実 "nuts, tree fruit". Figuratively it stands for "substance, content" (実のある話) and in 実を結ぶ "to bear fruit, to lead to success". Edible fruit in a shop is called 果物; do not confuse with the homophones 身/み "body" and 味/み.

en.meaning: to be full, filled; to rise (tide)
examples[].german: Her voice was full of confidence.
When the tide comes in, this road is submerged in the sea.
en.notes: Intransitive ichidan verb, rather literary: 自信に満ちる (to be full of confidence), 喜びに満ちた顔. For tides: 潮が満ちる (the tide comes in). Transitive: 満たす.

en.meaning: visit to a sick person, visit of sympathy; get-well letter, gift (esp. in compounds like 暑中見舞い, 見舞い金)
examples[].german: The hospital lobby was bustling with visitors coming to see patients.
In summer, I send midsummer greeting cards to friends.
The company sent sympathy money to employees affected by the disaster.
en.notes: 見舞い みまい is a visit or greeting to someone who is ill or has suffered a misfortune, also the accompanying gift or letter. On its own, in conversation the polite form お見舞い (its own card, お見舞いに行く) is almost always used; the bare form appears mainly in compounds such as 見舞い客 "visitor to a patient", 見舞い金 "sympathy money" and 暑中見舞い "midsummer greeting". The related verb is 見舞う "to visit; to strike (of misfortune)".

examples[].german: I went to the airport to see a friend off.
The plan was put off for lack of budget.
en.notes: Accompanying someone to say goodbye (空港まで見送りに行く); figuratively also shelving a plan (計画は見送りになった). Verb: 見送る.

examples[].german: Would you like milk in your coffee?
It's time to give the baby his milk.
en.notes: Cow's milk for drinking is usually called 牛乳 in daily life; ミルク is used especially for milk in coffee or tea and for infant formula.

examples[].german: There was a mistake in the calculation.
I'll be careful not to make the same mistake twice.
en.notes: Mistake, blunder; as a verb ミスする, colloquially ミスる. Homophone: ミス "Miss" (ミス日本).

en.meaning: dense, close; close (relationship), intimate; precise, careful; secret
examples[].german: At work, it is important to keep in close contact with your boss.
The two companies have a close relationship.
In urban areas the population is dense and there is little vacant land.
en.notes: 密 みつ is a na-adjective or noun for "dense, close", both spatially (人口が密だ) and for relationships and contact (密な関係, 連絡を密にする "to stay in close contact"). Since the coronavirus period it has been widely known through 密を避ける and 三密 "the three Cs (closed spaces, crowded places, close contact)". In compounds it is more common than on its own: 密接, 秘密, 密度. Do not confuse with the homophone 蜜/みつ "honey, nectar".

examples[].german: Kyoto was the capital of Japan for a long time.
Paris is called the "city of flowers".
en.notes: Capital, imperial residence (literary, often historical: Kyoto was the 都 for over 1000 years). Also "city as a center": 花の都パリ.

examples[].german: This box is so heavy that I can't lift it by myself.
Flattered by everyone, he got completely carried away.
en.notes: Transitive ichidan verb: to raise something (荷物を持ち上げる). Figuratively: to praise someone excessively to put them in a good mood.

examples[].german: Please put out burnable garbage on Mondays and Thursdays.
Paper scraps go into the burnable garbage.
en.notes: Garbage category; also written 燃えるゴミ, officially 可燃ごみ. Opposite: 燃えないごみ. The collection days are in the municipality's garbage calendar.

examples[].german: I have a meeting on Thursday afternoon.
This shop's regular closing day is every Thursday.
Please submit the report by next Thursday.
en.notes: 木曜 もくよう is the short form of 木曜日 "Thursday" and is often used in conversation, in schedules and on signs (木曜の夜, 毎週木曜). Meaning and use correspond to 木曜日 (its own card); the full form sounds a little more careful, the short form more casual and terse. Parallel to it is 火曜 "Tuesday"; in calendars it is often just (木).

examples[].german: In autumn, the maple in the garden turns bright red.
On the weekend we went to Kyoto with the family to see the autumn leaves.
The baby has tiny hands like maple leaves.
en.notes: Same spelling as 紅葉 (こうよう): こうよう is the Sino-Japanese word for the changing of leaf color as a natural event (紅葉が見頃 "the autumn leaves are at their best", in news and weather reports), while もみじ is the native word for the maple and its red leaves. The reading もみじ is fixed in 紅葉狩り "trip to see the autumn leaves" and もみじのような手 "tiny child's hands"; the word is often written in kana to avoid confusion.

examples[].german: The characters on the old stone monument had become illegible because of the rain.
I could feel my grandfather's feelings from the handwriting in the letter.
en.notes: もんじ and もじ can both mean "written character". The reading もんじ keeps the ん between も and じ; monji therefore has three morae. This reading also occurs in older literary texts. The examples focus on the visible writing of an inscription and a letter; "letter" as a whole message is 手紙.

examples[].german: The person in charge will come shortly, so please wait a moment.
The young people of this town have all moved to the city.
en.notes: Person, almost always with a modifier before it: 若い者 (young people), 担当の者 (the person in charge). Humble, about one's own side: 係の者が参ります. As a suffix, read しゃ in 医者 or 学者. Sounding the same: 物 (thing).

examples[].german: He is a person who looks at things positively.
Everything has its order, so don't rush.
en.notes: Things of life in general: 物事をよく考える, 物事には順序がある (everything has its order). Somewhat more abstract than こと.

examples[].german: In the middle of the night, I heard a strange noise in the kitchen.
There was not a single sound in the house.
en.notes: A sound whose source one cannot see: 変な物音がする, 物音一つしない (not a sound can be heard).

examples[].german: If it rains, the game is canceled.
Let's buy water just in case.
en.notes: Emphatic もし, stressing that something is unlikely. もしものとき／もしもの場合 = in an emergency. The kanji 若しも is rare.

en.meaning: origin, cause; basis; former, ex- (元社長); original, former (元の場所)
examples[].german: A cold is said to be the source of all illnesses.
This drama is based on a true story.
Please put used items back in their original place.
en.notes: もと means "origin, cause" (事故の元, 風邪は万病の元) and "basis"; in the meaning "basis" it is usually written 基: 〜を基にする "to be based on something". For base materials and ingredients, 素 is used: スープの素 "soup base". As a prefix, 元 means "former, ex-" (元社長, 元彼), and 元の〜 or 元に戻る means "original, former" or "to return to the original state" (元の場所に戻す).

en.meaning: apology, excuse, justification (esp. in 申し訳ありません, 申し訳が立たない)
examples[].german: I am sorry to have kept you waiting.
After making such a mistake, I can't face the team.
The dish had a token amount of vegetables on the side.
en.notes: 申し訳 もうしわけ is the noun "apology, excuse" and appears almost only in fixed expressions: 申し訳ありません／申し訳ございません "I am very sorry" (much more polite than すみません), 申し訳が立たない "to be unable to justify oneself" and 申し訳程度 "just for show, a token amount". The adjective 申し訳ない "sorry, inexcusable" has its own card.

en.meaning: nothing, zero; un-, -less (prefix, e.g. 無料, 無意味, 無責任)
examples[].german: If I fail, all my efforts so far will come to nothing.
He built the company from nothing.
Such an irresponsible remark is unacceptable.
en.notes: As a noun, 無 む means "nothing, zero" (無になる "to come to nothing", 無から "from nothing") and is above all the main reading of the prefix "without, -less, un-": 無料 "free of charge", 無理 "impossible", 無意味 "meaningless", 無責任 "irresponsible".
