The reading ぶ (its own card 無〜/ぶ) applies only in a few words such as 無事 or 無難. Unlike 不〜 "non-", 無〜 stresses the absence of something.

en.meaning: opposite, across from; the opposite side
examples[].german: The post office is across from the station.
A new family has moved into the house across the street.
en.notes: The opposite side: 駅の向かい (across from the station), 向かいの家. Verb: 向かう.

examples[].german: Disregard of the rules is not permitted.
Being ignored by him made me sad.
en.notes: 無視 is a noun for deliberately ignoring or disregarding. 規則の無視 names the disregard of rules as a matter being discussed. With する it forms the transitive verb 無視する; 無視される is its passive form. The one who ignores stands before に in the passive. The similar-sounding 虫, by contrast, means "insect".

en.meaning: the day after tomorrow (formal reading みょうごにち)
examples[].german: I will send you the materials by the day after tomorrow.
The day after tomorrow, our counter will be closed for training.
en.notes: みょうごにち denotes the day after tomorrow just like あさって, but sounds more formal and suits e.g. a business notice. 明後日までに sets a deadline: by the day after tomorrow at the latest. 明後日は makes the day the topic of an announcement. The ょ forms a unit with み; う then lengthens the o sound.

examples[].german: In the middle of the night, I heard a strange noise from the kitchen.
The classroom is oddly quiet today, isn't it?
His way of speaking had a peculiar persuasiveness.
en.notes: 妙 みょう is a na-adjective meaning "strange, odd": 妙な音 "a strange noise", 妙な話 "an odd story"; adverbially, 妙に means "remarkably, somehow" (妙に静かだ). It sounds a bit more elevated than 変 (変な音) and stresses that one cannot quite explain the strangeness. The older meaning "excellent, exquisite" lives on in 絶妙 "exquisite" and 巧妙 "clever".

examples[].german: Do you know the name of that flower?
His name is known all over the world.
en.notes: Elevated for 名前: 名を名乗る (to give one's name), 名もない (nameless). Also reputation, fame: 名が知られる (to be well known). In compounds usually めい (有名).

examples[].german: I'm moving in the middle of May.
He said it half in jest, half seriously.
en.notes: The middle of a period (四月の半ば = mid-April), the half and, adverbially, "half, partly" (半ばあきらめている = I have half given up).

examples[].german: Why didn't you come yesterday?
Why would you say such a thing?
en.notes: Colloquial for どうして／なぜ, often with a reproachful tone. The same spelling can also be read なにで "with what" (何で行きますか).

examples[].german: I haven't eaten anything since this morning.
There's no need to get so angry about it.
en.notes: With a negative, "nothing" (なにも食べていない). Also "there's no need to (go so far as to)": なにも泣くことはない (There's no need to cry). Often also written 何も.

examples[].german: How about some sweets as a souvenir?
Someone like me is still far from good.
en.notes: Colloquial, after nouns: gives an example (お茶なんかどう？) or plays something down (私なんか…). Cf. the grammar entry ～なんて／～なんか. Identical in sound: なんか = 何か (somehow, something).

examples[].german: I never want to study math again.
I never imagined I'd run into you in a place like this.
There's no one called Tanaka in our department.
en.notes: A colloquial particle that singles something out while disparaging or downplaying it (勉強なんて嫌い), expresses surprise or indignation after sentences (…なんて信じられない) and can mean "someone named" (田中なんて人). Compared with なんか (separate card), なんて is a bit more emphatic and also follows whole sentences. Do not confuse it with the exclamation 何て "how ...!" (なんてきれいなんだ).

examples[].german: I tied the luggage up firmly with a rope.
I lowered a rope into the old well and measured its depth.
en.notes: Rope made of straw or hemp. Jump rope: 縄跳び（なわとび）. Related: 縄張り (territory, turf).

examples[].german: Vegetable prices are rising because of the unseasonable weather.
That old painting fetched a higher price than expected.
This watch is a bit pricey, but you can use it for a lifetime.
en.notes: 値 (ね) is the price as a market quantity and is found in 値段 (its own card), 値上げ "price increase" and 値下げ "price reduction". On its own it appears mainly in fixed expressions: 値が上がる/下がる, 値がつく "to fetch a price", 値が張る "to be expensive". For the price of a specific item one usually says 値段; the reading あたい means "value", also in the mathematical sense.

examples[].german: My son is totally into soccer.
I was so absorbed in my book that I forgot to get off the train.
en.notes: As a verb 熱中する: to immerse oneself in something (ゲームに熱中する). Not to be confused with 熱中症 (heatstroke).

en.meaning: years and months, a long time
examples[].german: This bridge was completed after many years of work.
After ten years, the two met again.
The research took an enormous amount of time and money.
en.notes: 年月 has two readings with the same meaning "years and months, a long time". ねんげつ is the Sino-Japanese, more matter-of-fact reading and is more common in news and factual texts (長い年月をかけて, 十年の年月); としつき (its own card) sounds softer and more literary, often emotional. In writing, the reading cannot be told; 年月日 "date", by contrast, is read ねんがっぴ.

examples[].german: There seems to be a mouse in the ceiling of the old house.
The cat is chasing a mouse.
en.notes: Usually written in kana (ねずみ／ネズミ); in everyday Japanese there is no distinction between mouse and rat. Zodiac sign: 子年（ねどし）. Also the color 鼠色 (mouse gray).

en.meaning: during the day, in the daytime
examples[].german: It is hot during the day, but cool at night.
I can't answer the phone during the day because of work.
en.notes: The daylight hours: 日中は暑い. In the meaning "Japan-China" (日中関係) it is also read にっちゅう.

examples[].german: I'm going to Tokyo on the 21st.
The trip lasts ten days.
en.notes: 日 after a number stands for a calendar day or a number of days. The basic reading にち appears e.g. in 二十一日（にじゅういちにち）. Many low numbers form special forms: 三日（みっか）, 十日（とおか）. For a duration, 間 can follow: 十日間, for ten days. 日曜日, by contrast, denotes a day of the week.

examples[].german: The baby looked at me and smiled.
The shop assistant smiled and said, "Thank you very much."
en.notes: A brief, warm smile: にっこり笑う／にっこりする. A lasting smile: にこにこ.

examples[].german: Japan is a country with many islands.
I support the athletes from Japan.
en.notes: にっぽん and にほん are two readings of the country name 日本. In にっぽん, the small っ creates a brief closure before p; romanization therefore has pp. 日本の links the country name with e.g. 選手, "athletes from Japan". Both readings denote the same country; にっぽん is not a different territory.

examples[].german: My grandmother keeps chickens at her house.
I woke up early in the morning to the crowing of a rooster.
en.notes: The living animal; the meat is called 鶏肉（とりにく）or simply とり. Zodiac sign: 酉年.

examples[].german: I picked wildflowers and arranged them in a vase.
The children played, running around the fields and mountains.
en.notes: Open land, meadow (rather literary): 野の花 (wildflowers); in everyday speech 野原 is used. Common in names (上野, 野村).

examples[].german: Tomorrow will be sunny, later cloudy.
I will contact you later with the details.
He later became a famous painter.
en.notes: 後 in the reading のち means "later, afterward" and is more formal than あと (its own card); it is often written in kana. Typical are 後に "later (on)", 後ほど "later" (polite) and the weather report: 晴れ後曇り "sunny, later cloudy". In everyday speech one says あとで rather; 後ろ (うしろ), by contrast, means "behind" in a spatial sense.

examples[].german: Since it started to rain, I took shelter from the rain under the eaves.
Icicles are hanging from the eaves.
en.notes: The part of the roof that projects beyond the wall of the house: 軒下 (under the eaves). The reading けん is the counter for houses (一軒).

examples[].german: When you don't want something, you should say no clearly.
Wednesday is a no-overtime day.
en.notes: A clear "no" (ノーと言う) and, as a prefix, "without": ノーメイク, ノー残業デー (no-overtime day).

examples[].german: Let's have lunch soon.
Let's meet at the station around noon.
en.notes: Polite, very common form of 昼: お昼にしよう (Let's have lunch). Lunch is also お昼ご飯.

examples[].german: Lately I feel my body aging.
Old age comes to everyone.
en.notes: Noun from 老いる (to grow old): aging and its effects. Rather literary; in conversation one says 年を取る. Similar sounding: 甥 (nephew).

examples[].german: The fishing boats went out to sea early in the morning.
There was an earthquake off the coast of Chiba Prefecture.
en.notes: The sea some distance from the shore: 沖に出る (to head out to the open sea), 東京湾沖 (off Tokyo Bay). Also in earthquake reports: 〜沖で地震.

examples[].german: The key I had been looking for was at the back of the drawer.
His words remain deep in my heart.
en.notes: The back or inner part of a room or place: 引き出しの奥, 店の奥. Also figurative: 心の奥 (deep in the heart). Related: 奥さん (someone else's wife).

en.meaning: waiting (polite), wait; cf. お待ちください
examples[].german: The person in charge will come shortly, so please wait a moment.
While you wait, please take a look at this brochure.
We sincerely look forward to your visit.
en.notes: Polite form of the verbal noun 待ち from 待つ. Most often in fixed patterns: お待ちください (request), お待ちしております (humble), お待ちになる (honorific), plus お待ちの間 "while you wait". To be distinguished from the thank-you formula お待ちどおさま (its own card). Almost always written in kana with お; 御待ち is rare.

examples[].german: I changed the baby's diaper.
I bought extra diapers for the trip.
en.notes: Mostly written in hiragana (the kanji 襁褓 is very rare). Disposable diaper: 紙おむつ. おむつを替える (to change a diaper).

examples[].german: I will never forget my teacher's kindness as long as I live.
Someday I want to repay my parents for all they have done.
en.notes: A kindness received that one feels obliged to repay - central to Japanese thinking: 恩を返す (to repay a favor), 恩を忘れる (to be ungrateful), 恩人 (benefactor).

examples[].german: I played the same note on the piano over and over.
It is difficult to tell these two sounds apart.
The on reading of this character is "san", the kun reading is "yama".
en.notes: 音（おん）denotes here a musical tone, a speech sound, or the reading of a kanji borrowed from Chinese. In the last sense, 音 contrasts with 訓（くん）, the Japanese reading. For an everyday noise, 音（おと）is the usual reading; おん is especially useful in explanations about music and language.

en.meaning: to carry piggyback; to depend on others
examples[].german: My father carried his tired daughter piggyback and walked home.
I can't keep depending on my parents forever.
en.notes: As a verb おんぶする (to carry a child on one's back). Figuratively: 親におんぶする (to live off one's parents). To carry in one's arms is だっこ.

en.meaning: exaggerated; excess, over the limit; overcoat
examples[].german: He always exaggerates when he tells a story.
This month I went over budget.
en.notes: Several meanings: exaggerated (オーバーな話), excess (予算オーバー = over budget) and overcoat (short for オーバーコート).

examples[].german: A new cafe opened in front of the station.
She has an open personality and can talk to anyone.
en.notes: As a verb オープンする (to open): 新しい店がオープンした. As a な-adjective "open, open-minded": オープンな性格.

examples[].german: Vienna is the capital of Austria.
I often mix up Austria and Australia.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. Easily confused with オーストラリア (Australia); Japanese people joke about this themselves.

examples[].german: My license is limited to automatic cars.
This camera focuses automatically.
en.notes: Short form: オートマ (automatic transmission). Opposite: マニュアル.

examples[].german: The Netherlands is famous for flowers and windmills.
In the Edo period, Japan traded with the Netherlands.
en.notes: Country name (from Portuguese "Holanda"). Historically important: in the Edo period, the Dutch (on Dejima in Nagasaki) were the only Europeans allowed to trade with Japan; hence 蘭学（らんがく）"Dutch learning" for Western sciences.

examples[].german: There will be an orientation after the entrance ceremony.
At the orientation, I was taught how to choose classes.
en.notes: E.g. for new students or employees: 新入生オリエンテーション.

en.meaning: help, care, looking after (polite; e.g. お世話になります)
examples[].german: Could you take care of the cat while I'm traveling?
Thank you all very much for your help.
"Why don't you get married soon?" "Mind your own business."
en.notes: Polite form of 世話 "care, looking after" (its own card), friendlier in tone and typical when it comes to children, animals or guests: 猫のお世話をする. It is the core of fixed expressions such as お世話になります / お世話になりました (its own card お世話になる) and 余計なお世話 or 大きなお世話 "mind your own business" (its own card). The usual spelling is お世話; 御世話 is rare.

examples[].german: I chatted with friends at a cafe for a full two hours.
He is a chatterbox, so you'd better not tell him secrets.
en.notes: Noun (楽しいおしゃべり), verb おしゃべりする, and な-adjective for people who talk a lot or too much: おしゃべりな人. Kanji お喋り.

examples[].german: When you cross at the crosswalk, check carefully left and right.
He attempted to cross the Pacific in a sailing yacht.
Crossing this road is prohibited, so please use the pedestrian bridge.
en.notes: Noun for 横断する "to cross" (its own card). Very common in fixed compounds: 横断歩道 "crosswalk", 横断禁止 "no crossing", 大陸横断 "crossing of a continent". The counterpart is 縦断 "traversing lengthwise" (日本列島を縦断する).

examples[].german: All items in this store are 20 percent off.
Eighty percent of the students in the class passed the exam.
en.notes: Comes after the number: 50パーセント; often written with %. "... percent off" is …パーセント引き.

examples[].german: Water is leaking from the pipe in the kitchen.
He has strong connections in the political world.
en.notes: Pipe or conduit (水道のパイプ), tobacco pipe, and figuratively a connection between people or organizations (政界とのパイプ).

examples[].german: When I was a child, I wanted to become a pilot.
The pilot made an announcement on board.
en.notes: Airplane pilot; more formal: 操縦士. As a prefix also "pilot": パイロット版 (pilot version).

en.meaning: pass (an exam); pass, ticket; pass (sports); to pass, skip
examples[].german: I passed the difficult exam on the first try.
I'll skip the drinking party this time.
en.notes: Many meanings: 試験にパスする (to pass an exam), a travel or free pass, a pass in ball sports (パスを出す) and "to pass, to decline" (今回はパスします). The file path on a computer is a different word with the same spelling.

examples[].german: I painted the wall.
I accidentally sat on a bench with a "Wet Paint" sign.
en.notes: Loanword from Dutch (pek). "Wet paint" sign: ペンキ塗りたて. Paints for pictures are called 絵の具.

examples[].german: We had a picnic in the park.
On Sunday we plan to go on an outing with the family.
en.notes: An outing with food outdoors: ピクニックに行く, ピクニックをする.

en.meaning: pin (straight pin, hairpin, safety pin); bowling pin
examples[].german: I pinned the map to the wall.
She keeps her bangs pinned with a hairpin.
en.notes: A pin for fastening: 安全ピン (safety pin), ヘアピン (hairpin); a thumbtack, on the other hand, is called 画びょう. Also the pin in bowling.

examples[].german: Do you have a points card?
My wallet is full of points cards.
en.notes: At the cash register you are almost always asked ポイントカードはお持ちですか (Do you have a points card?). If you don't, answer: 持っていません／大丈夫です.

examples[].german: Three plus four is seven.
The experience of studying abroad was also an asset for my work.
en.notes: The arithmetic sign "plus" (三プラス四), but also "advantage": プラスになる (to be of benefit). Opposite: マイナス.

examples[].german: He is a professional photographer.
Typical pro: fast and clean work.
en.notes: Short for プロフェッショナル; opposite: アマ(チュア). Often a prefix: プロ野球 (professional baseball), プロ選手.

en.meaning: plural suffix, and others (suffix, mostly in kana: 彼ら, 僕ら, 子供ら)
examples[].german: They walk to the station together every morning.
When we were kids, there was no such thing as smartphones.
In the park, the neighborhood children were playing energetically.
en.notes: A plural suffix for people, almost always written in kana (彼ら, 僕ら, 子供ら); 等 as a kanji looks old-fashioned. Compared with 〜たち, 〜ら sounds more familiar and can seem condescending toward others (お前ら), or modest for one's own group (私ら). Do not confuse with the same spelling 〜等 in the reading とう "etc.; rank" (its own card).

en.meaning: next, coming (prefix, e.g. 来学期, 来年度); since (suffix, e.g. 先月来, 十年来)
examples[].german: I hear tuition fees will rise from next semester.
The budget for the next fiscal year has not been decided yet.
I've known him for ten years.
en.notes: 来 らい is a time affix. As a prefix it means "next, coming" and combines with time periods: 来学期, 来年度, 来シーズン (compare the fixed words 来年, 来月, 来週). As a suffix after time expressions it means "since, for ... now": 十年来の友人, 昨年来の問題. Do not confuse with the verb 来る (くる) with the same kanji; on its own, 来 is never used as らい.

examples[].german: Could you lend me your lighter?
I lit the candle with the lighter's flame.
en.notes: Lighter. Homophone: ライター "writer" (フリーライター).

examples[].german: I bought a new tennis racket.
I forgot my table tennis racket.
en.notes: A racket with strings or a rubber surface. A golf club is called クラブ, a baseball bat バット.

examples[].german: After I took the medicine, I felt much better.
This job looks easy but is actually hard.
en.notes: な-adjective and noun: 楽な仕事 (an easy job), 楽になる (to feel relieved), 気が楽だ. The same kanji is in 楽しい (たのしい, "enjoyable, fun").

examples[].german: I thanked the teacher and then left the classroom.
At the start of class, everyone bows to the teacher.
He really has no manners, does he?
en.notes: 礼 without お appears mainly in fixed expressions: 礼を言う "to thank", 礼をする "to bow" and the school command 起立、礼！. For "thanks" in everyday speech one usually says the polite お礼 (its own card, おれい). Related are 礼儀 "courtesy, manners" and 失礼 "rude; excuse me". Do not confuse with the similar-sounding 例 "example".

examples[].german: Would you like a bag?
Since bags started costing money, fewer people use them.
en.notes: レジ (cash register) + 袋. At the register: レジ袋はご利用ですか (Do you need a bag?). Costs extra since 2020.

examples[].german: Many people think of Japan when they hear Mt. Fuji.
This song reminds me of the sea in summer.
en.notes: Something evokes another image; as a verb: AからBを連想する (to think of B from A), Bを連想させる (to remind one of B).

examples[].german: A long line had formed in front of the popular ramen shop.
Please line up in order and wait.
At the cinema, I sat in the third row from the front.
en.notes: Basic word for a row or waiting line: 列に並ぶ "to line up", 列を作る "to form a line", 列に割り込む "to cut in line". As a counter it counts rows (一列, 三列目); in tables it denotes the column (行 = row). The compound 行列 (its own card) stresses more a long waiting line or a procession; 列 is the neutral basic word.

examples[].german: This dog is very smart and seems to understand words.
If you are good, I'll buy you ice cream later.
en.notes: な-adjective: clever (利口な犬) and, of children, "well-behaved", often as お利口さん. Slightly more colloquial than 賢い.

examples[].german: After the long voyage, land finally came into view.
Frogs can live both in the water and on land.
en.notes: Land as opposed to the sea: 陸に上がる (to go ashore). Compounds: 大陸 (continent), 着陸 (landing), 陸上 (track and field).

examples[].german: The pass rate for this exam is very low.
The younger the people, the lower the voting rate.
en.notes: On its own somewhat technical (率が高い); mostly as a suffix: 合格率 (pass rate), 失業率, 確率. Note: in 引率 (to lead a group), the same kanji is read そつ.

examples[].german: On a shared computer, be sure to log out.
If you don't do anything for a while, you will be logged out automatically.
en.notes: As a verb with する. On computers that aren't yours: 使ったあとは必ずログアウトする.

examples[].german: The rocket was launched into space.
The children made rockets out of plastic bottles.
en.notes: Rocket; launch: ロケットを打ち上げる. Homophone: ロケット "locket" (a pendant that opens).

examples[].german: This book discusses Japan's education problems.
At the meeting we discussed the advantages and disadvantages of the two proposals.
en.notes: Literary ichidan verb: to discuss a topic systematically (問題を論じる). Also 論ずる. In conversation, 話し合う or 議論する is more usual.

en.meaning: occasion; when, at the time of
examples[].german: When getting off, please be careful not to leave anything behind.
I want to say it clearly on this occasion.
en.notes: Formal "when, on the occasion of": 〜の際(に), 〜する際. この際 = on this occasion. Common in announcements and written documents.

en.meaning: in the middle of, right in the midst of (〜の最中に)
examples[].german: The phone rang in the middle of the meal.
I'm in the middle of a meeting right now, so I'll call back later.
It started raining in the middle of the game.
en.notes: 最中 (さいちゅう) means "in the middle of, right while" and follows 〜の or 〜ている: 食事の最中に, 話している最中に. It stresses that something happens exactly during an activity, usually as an interruption; 途中 (its own card) means more "on the way, not yet finished". With the same spelling, もなか denotes a wafer confection with bean paste (its own card); the reading さなか is formal.

examples[].german: Please sign at the bottom of the document.
I got an autograph from my favorite player.
en.notes: A signature on documents (ここにサインしてください), a star's autograph, and a sign or signal (OKのサイン). In Japan, a seal (印鑑) is often used instead of a signature.

examples[].german: The cherry blossoms are at their peak right now.
It would be a waste to spend one's youthful prime only studying.
en.notes: The peak of a season or condition: 夏の盛り, 桜が盛りだ, 働き盛り (prime working age). The reading もり means "portion".

examples[].german: My father drinks a little alcohol with dinner every evening.
I can't hold my alcohol, so my face turns red after a single beer.
If you've been drinking, you must never drive a car.
en.notes: 酒 (さけ) generally means "alcohol, alcoholic drink" and specifically "sake"; in polite everyday speech one usually says お酒 (its own card). The plain form is used in matter-of-fact speech, rules and expressions such as 酒に強い/弱い "to have a high/low tolerance". In compounds the reading changes: 日本酒 (しゅ), 酒屋 (さか). Do not confuse with the homophone 鮭 "salmon".

examples[].german: Last year I worked in this town.
The ground in the garden is wet from last night's rain.
en.notes: 昨 is a time prefix. It stands before a time expression, e.g. 昨年（さくねん）for last year and 昨夜（さくや）for last night. It is read as part of a compound and is not a standalone word for yesterday. 昨日 has the formal reading さくじつ and the everyday reading きのう; the reading of the whole word must therefore be learned too.

examples[].german: This year there was little rain, and the crops did not grow well.
This region mainly produces crops such as rice.
en.notes: Cultivated plants such as rice, grain or vegetables: 作物を育てる. The reading さくぶつ, on the other hand, means "(artistic) work".

en.meaning: to wake up (someone); to dispel (sleep, intoxication)
examples[].german: I woke up to a loud noise.
I washed my face with cold water to chase away my sleepiness.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: 目を覚ます (to wake up), 眠気を覚ます (to dispel sleepiness), 酔いを覚ます (to sober up). Intransitive: 覚める. Similar sounding: 冷ます (to let cool).

examples[].german: Sharks sometimes show up on this coast.
I saw a big shark at the aquarium.
en.notes: Usually written in katakana; kanji: 鮫. Shark fin soup: ふかひれスープ.

en.meaning: to wake up; to sober up
examples[].german: I woke up at five this morning.
In the fresh air outside, I sobered up.
en.notes: Intransitive ichidan verb: 目が覚める (to wake up), 酔いが覚める (to sober up). Transitive: 覚ます. Similar sounding: 冷める (to cool down).

examples[].german: I saw monkeys in the mountains of Nikko.
A monkey snatched a tourist's food.
en.notes: Mostly the Japanese macaque (ニホンザル). Proverb: 猿も木から落ちる (Even monkeys fall from trees). Sounding the same: 去る (to leave).

examples[].german: Well then, let's move on to the next agenda item.
Well, shall we get going soon?
en.notes: Introduces a new topic or the next step, typical in speeches and letters: さて、次の話題です. Kanji 扠／偖 are rare.

examples[].german: There seems to be some kind of commotion in front of the station.
That photo caused a big uproar online.
en.notes: Noise, unrest or a big stir: 大騒ぎ, 騒ぎになる (to cause a stir). Verb: 騒ぐ.

en.meaning: fault, cause (〜のせいで = because of, due to, with a negative result)
examples[].german: Because of the rain, the game was canceled.
It's my fault that it failed.
Maybe because I didn't sleep enough, I have a headache today.
en.notes: Almost always written in kana; the kanji form 所為 is rare. It follows nouns with の or follows a clause: 〜のせいで "because of", 〜のせいだ "is to blame", 〜せいか "maybe because". In contrast to 〜のおかげで "thanks to", せい denotes a cause with a negative result and often shifts the blame. Homophones: 背 "height", 姓 "family name".

en.meaning: sex, gender; nature, character; -ness, -ity (suffix, e.g. 可能性)
examples[].german: In this survey, there were hardly any differences by gender.
It is important to teach sex education properly at school.
There is a high probability of rain tomorrow.
en.notes: On its own, 性 means mainly "sex, gender" (性の違い, 性別) and "sexuality" (性教育), more rarely "nature, character of a person". Very common is the suffix -性, which forms qualities like English "-ity/-ness": 可能性 "possibility", 安全性 "safety", 重要性 "importance". On forms, 性別 is usually used instead of 性. Homophones: 背 "height", 姓 "family name".

examples[].german: In the group photo, the company president stood in the center.
For details, please inquire at the center's counter.
en.notes: A facility (ショッピングセンター, 保健センター) or a central position (center stage; in baseball, center field).

examples[].german: There are several theories about why the dinosaurs went extinct.
Hardly anyone believes that theory today.
en.notes: A theory or opinion, often alongside others: いろいろな説がある (there are various theories). Compounds: 学説, 仮説, 小説.

examples[].german: Establishing a company requires many documents.
This volunteer organization has existed for only three years since its founding.
The establishment of a new research institute was announced today.
en.notes: 設立 is the founding of an organization such as a company, association, foundation or school: 会社の設立, 設立者 "founder", 設立記念日. The verb form "to found" has its own card, 設立する. 創立 emphasizes more the historical founding event (創立百周年), whereas 建設 is the construction of a building, not the founding of an institution.

examples[].german: I ordered a set of a hamburger and fries.
I set the alarm clock for six o'clock.
en.notes: A set of things that belong together (食器のセット), a menu combination (ランチセット), a set in tennis/volleyball, and as the verb セットする (to set, to prepare: 目覚ましをセットする).

en.meaning: person, -er (suffix, e.g. 研究者, 参加者, 医者)
examples[].german: There are twenty participants in the meeting in total.
Please let me speak with the person in charge.
My older sister works as a researcher at a university.
en.notes: A very productive suffix attached to Sino-Japanese words to denote persons: 研究者 "researcher", 参加者 "participant", 責任者 "person in charge"; it is also found in basic words such as 医者 and 学者. Read on its own, 者 is もの (its own card 者/もの, e.g. 田中という者です). For nationality or occupation, 〜人 or 〜家 (日本人, 作家) is often used instead of 〜者.

examples[].german: 氏 refers to a family group with common descent.
In history class, I learned how such clans came to be.
en.notes: As an independent noun, 氏（し） refers to a family group with common descent. This card practices the meaning in a historical context. The name suffix 〜氏 has a different function. For a present-day surname one usually uses 姓 or 名字; in other contexts 氏 is also read うじ.

examples[].german: I went to see a play with friends on the weekend.
When I was a child, I acted in a play at the school festival.
en.notes: A play or performance: 芝居を見る (to go to the theater), 芝居に出る (to act in a play). Colloquially also "act, show" in the sense of pretense. 紙芝居 is paper theater.

examples[].german: In this region it often snows in winter.
He often arrives late to meetings.
en.notes: More literary than よく or たびたび. Kanji 屡々 are rare.

en.meaning: course of events; depending on; as soon as
examples[].german: I checked the program of the ceremony before entering the venue.
I explained how things had come about even to people who did not know the circumstances.
Whether I take part depends on tomorrow's weather.
We will set off as soon as preparations are ready.
en.notes: 次第 can denote, as a noun, the course or sequence of events of something, e.g. 式の次第 or 事の次第. After a noun it also expresses dependence: 天気次第 means depending on the weather. After the stem of the ます-form it means "as soon as", as in でき次第. This attachment form distinguishes the temporal use from the dependence use.

examples[].german: The country was under foreign rule for a long time.
The king's rule extended to every corner of the country.
This market is controlled by just three companies.
en.notes: 支配 is the noun "rule, control"; the verb is 支配する "to rule" (its own card). Typical combinations are 〜の支配を受ける "to be under someone's rule", 〜の支配下にある "to be under the control of ..." and 支配者 "ruler". The word is rather literary and is used for states and markets, and figuratively for emotions.

examples[].german: The fee can be paid by card.
The company pays its employees a salary every month.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb; more formal than 払う, typical for bills, fees and wages. Noun: 支払い.

examples[].german: The two plan to hold their wedding next spring.
Write the equation for solving this problem.
en.notes: Ceremony, celebration (式を挙げる = to hold a wedding; 卒業式, 入学式), mathematical formula (式を立てる) and style (日本式 = in the Japanese way).

examples[].german: In this company, transportation costs are fully reimbursed.
New employees are issued a uniform.
en.notes: Official, businesslike: money, goods or equipment is handed out - 交通費を支給する (to reimburse travel expenses), 制服が支給される. As a verb 支給する.

examples[].german: Oops! I left my umbrella on the train.
Damn, it's already this late.
en.notes: Exclamation when one notices a mistake (literally the past tense of しまう). Very common in everyday life, usually said to oneself.

examples[].german: After the rain, the water in the lower reaches of the river was muddy.
The surplus water from the upper rice field was channeled to the lower rice field.
en.notes: しも names the lower or final part of a connected whole. For a river, 下 is closer to the mouth; its counterpart is 上 かみ. In older or technical descriptions it can also refer to a lower-lying section. For everyday location expressions, した is usually used. The division into book volumes or quality grades is usually read げ.

examples[].german: This shop stocks good merchandise.
I sent a congratulatory gift.
en.notes: Goods in a shop, or an item: 品物, 品数 (range of goods), 品切れ (sold out), お祝いの品 (congratulatory gift). Read ひん, 品 means "elegance, refinement".

examples[].german: I am 170 centimeters tall.
Height and weight were measured at the health checkup.
en.notes: A person's height: 身長が高い／低い, 身長を測る. Similar sounding: 慎重 (cautious).

examples[].german: I had a treatment in which the nerve of my tooth was removed.
It is delicate work, so it takes a lot of concentration.
en.notes: Anatomically the nerve; figuratively the nerves or attention: 神経を使う (to have to concentrate hard), 神経質 (nervous, overly sensitive), 無神経 (insensitive, tactless).

examples[].german: The progress of science and technology is very fast.
Great progress can be seen in his Japanese.
Thanks to progress in medicine, many diseases have become curable.
en.notes: Noun for 進歩する (vocab-n3:27), mostly with の before it: 技術の進歩 "technological progress", 医学の進歩 "progress in medicine". Typical combinations are 進歩が速い "to advance quickly" and 進歩が見られる "progress can be seen". Unlike 発展 "development, growth", 進歩 stresses improvement toward a higher level.

en.meaning: buttocks, bottom; rear end, tail end
examples[].german: I sat for so long that my bottom started to hurt.
He is under his wife's thumb.
My little brother is lazy and just won't start his homework.
en.notes: 尻 is the plain word for "buttocks, bottom"; in everyday speech and with children, the more polite お尻 (its own card) is usually used. The bare form sounds a bit coarse and appears mainly in idioms: 尻に敷く "to have under one's thumb", 尻が重い "to be slow to act". Figuratively it also means "end, last place"; 尻尾 (しっぽ, its own card), by contrast, is an animal's "tail".

examples[].german: I burned my tongue on the hot soup.
The child stuck out his tongue and laughed.
en.notes: Tongue: 舌を出す (to stick out one's tongue), 舌をかむ (to bite one's tongue). Similar sounding: 下 (below).

examples[].german: Quality is more important than quantity.
The service at this shop is of high quality.
en.notes: Quality, often in contrast to 量 (quantity): 量より質 (quality over quantity). Compounds: 品質, 性質, 体質. The reading しち means "pawn" (質屋).

examples[].german: He lost his job last year.
I want to learn a trade.
en.notes: Occupation or place of work: 職を探す (to look for work), 職を失う (to lose one's job). Idiom: 手に職をつける (to learn a trade). Compounds: 職業, 職場, 就職.

examples[].german: I have a food allergy, so I can't eat eggs.
Animals migrate in search of food.
en.notes: Formal word for food, especially in science and health: 食物アレルギー, 食物繊維 (dietary fiber). In everyday speech: 食べ物.

examples[].german: In preparation for the typhoon, I bought water and food.
I'm taking three days' worth of food on the camping trip.
en.notes: Food in general: 食料品 (groceries in a store). For staple foods such as grain, e.g. in politics, 食糧 is often written.

examples[].german: This book is divided into ten chapters in all.
The next chapter explains the history of Japan.
en.notes: A chapter of a book or text: 第一章 (Chapter 1). Also a counter for chapters. Related: 文章 (text, writing).

en.meaning: small, small size; small- (prefix, e.g. 小規模)
examples[].german: You can choose the coffee size from large, medium or small.
This company is small-scale, but its technical ability is high.
Saying "large can serve as small", my mother bought a big pot.
en.notes: 小 (しょう) denotes the small size in the series 大・中・小 and is the counterpart of 中 (ちゅう) "medium size" (its own card) and 大 (だい). As a prefix it means "small-", e.g. 小規模 "small scale" or 小学校 (its own card). On its own it appears almost only in size indications and in sayings such as 大は小を兼ねる; the normal adjective "small" is 小さい, and in native words 小 is read こ (小鳥).

en.meaning: land formed by sediment, or an island (older dictionary meaning)
examples[].german: When I looked up "州" in the dictionary, I also found the meaning of land formed by accumulated earth and sand.
The teacher explained that this meaning of "州" is different from the "state" of the American states.
en.notes: This card covers a geographical meaning of 州 read しゅう, which the 精選版日本国語大辞典 records with an old attestation. Classifying it as older dictionary usage is an editorial judgment. For present-day geographical descriptions you will more often encounter 州・す, 中州・なかす or 砂州・さす. The examples show looking up and explaining this meaning. The common meaning "state, province" belongs to the other card 州・しゅう.

examples[].german: In history class, I learned about the political system of the Zhou.
Bronzeware made in the Zhou period is on display at the museum.
en.notes: 周 (しゅう) is here the name of the ancient Chinese Zhou dynasty. It appears in history texts and in the terms 西周 "Western Zhou" and 東周 "Eastern Zhou". "Zhou" and the older romanization "Chou" render the Chinese name; when reading a Japanese text, the reading is しゅう. The identically written word for laps or the circumference of a figure has a different meaning. 週 "week" and the family name 周 are likewise not studied here.

examples[].german: Every week my father reads a weekly magazine on the train.
This manga is serialized in a weekly magazine.
That newspaper is a weekly and comes out every Friday.
en.notes: Refers to publications that come out once a week; mostly in compounds or attributively with の: 週刊誌 "weekly magazine", 週刊の新聞. Formed in parallel are 日刊（にっかん） "published daily" and 月刊（げっかん） "published monthly". Do not confuse with the homophones 週間 "week (as a period of time)" and 習慣 "habit" - the kanji 刊 means "to publish".

examples[].german: At the teacher's suggestion, I made a few revisions to my composition.
This plan still needs revision.
A revised budget proposal was discussed in the Diet.
en.notes: 修正 is the noun "correction, revision"; the verb 修正する has its own card. Common are 修正を加える "to make changes", 修正が必要だ and 修正案 "amendment proposal"; for photos, 修正 also means "retouching". 訂正 (its own card) corrects a clear mistake, whereas 修正 adjusts or improves something even if it was not wrong.

examples[].german: I traveled to the major cities of Japan.
The main theme of the conference was environmental issues.
en.notes: な-adjective, mostly before nouns: 主要な都市 (the major cities), 主要国. Homophone: 腫瘍 (tumor).

examples[].german: Because it was hot, I rolled up my shirt sleeves.
The sleeves of this sweater are a little long.
en.notes: Sleeve: 半袖 (short-sleeved), 長袖 (long-sleeved), 袖をまくる (to roll up one's sleeves).

examples[].german: I sat on the sofa and watched TV.
We carried the new sofa into the room.
en.notes: Also written ソファ.

examples[].german: The roads were crowded. So I decided to go by train.
The budget is insufficient. So we decided to look for sponsors.
en.notes: Conjunction: introduces what one does in response to the situation (そこで、私は…). Not to be confused with そこで = "there" (そこ + で).

examples[].german: Next week there is a physical fitness test at school.
The measurement showed that the tap water is safe.
This measuring instrument displays temperature and humidity at the same time.
en.notes: A neutral, factual noun for "measurement", the basis of the verb card 測定する. Common in compounds: 体力測定 "fitness test", 測定器 "measuring device", 測定結果 "measurement result", 測定値 "measured value". In everyday life one measures with the verb 測る (はかる); 測定 sounds more technical and is used in school, reports and science.

examples[].german: You must not waste food.
He lived alone in a shabby hut.
en.notes: な-adjective: simple, of low quality (粗末な食事). Important: 〜を粗末にする = to treat something carelessly, to waste (食べ物を粗末にする). Modest phrase when giving a gift: 粗末なものですが.

examples[].german: I bought it thinking it was cheap, and ended up losing out instead.
If you're always holding back, you lose out.
My older brother took a loss of one million yen on stocks.
en.notes: The opposite of 得 "gain, advantage"; typical are 損をする "to lose money, to get the short end of the stick" and 損得 "gain and loss". As a na-adjective it means "disadvantageous": 損な役 "the thankless role"; 〜と損だ means "it would be a disadvantage if ...". For large losses in business texts, 損失 or 損害 are more usual.

examples[].german: The constitution stipulates respect for fundamental human rights.
This school places great importance on respect for each student's individuality.
Without respect for the other person's opinion, a discussion won't make progress.
en.notes: Noun for 尊重する (vocab-n3:18): 人権の尊重 "respect for human rights", 個性の尊重 "respect for individuality". It sounds formal and often appears in legal, school and newspaper language. Unlike 尊敬 "admiration (of a person)", 尊重 refers to opinions, rights and decisions that one takes seriously.

examples[].german: In spring, white flowers bloom in the plum garden.
The traveler rested quietly in the shade of the trees in the garden.
en.notes: 園 (その) refers to a delimited, cultivated piece of land with flowers, fruit trees or other plants. The reading often sounds literary and appears in, for example, 梅の園 "plum garden". For a public park, 公園 is more common in daily life. The attested spellings 苑 and the rarer 薗 apply here to the same reading and meaning. The identically read その "that" is a demonstrative word. The reading えん, as in 公園, belongs to other word forms.

en.meaning: as it is, unchanged; straight away
examples[].german: You can keep your shoes on.
I was tired, so I fell asleep as soon as I got home.
en.notes: Without changing anything (そのままでいい) or without interruption (そのまま寝てしまった). Kanji 其の儘 are very rare.

examples[].german: Let's go for a drink together sometime soon.
Ten people applied, and three of them passed.
en.notes: "Sometime soon" (そのうち会おう). With numbers also "of those": 十人来て、そのうち三人は学生だった. Kanji その内.

examples[].german: It was raining. Even so, the game went on.
No matter how many times he failed, he still did not give up.
en.notes: Conjunction: what follows holds even though the preceding statement argues against it. The kanji spelling 其れでも is rare.

examples[].german: I shave every morning.
When summer comes, many people also shave their leg hair.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb: ひげを剃る (to shave one's beard), 頭を剃る (to shave one's head bald).

examples[].german: What happens to the result when you add a negative number to a positive number?
Before multiplying two numbers, please check the sign of each.
en.notes: 数（すう） denotes in mathematical texts a number as a concept or arithmetic value. 正の数 are positive numbers; 二つの数を掛ける means to multiply two numbers. In general everyday use, the independent word 数 is often read かず. This entry specifically practices the technical noun reading すう. The identically read prefix before quantities, e.g. 数人, means "several" and is practiced separately.

examples[].german: Several students helped me tidy up.
The repair is said to take a few days.
en.notes: 数 stands before a quantity and leaves the exact number open: 数人（すうにん） are several people, 数日（すうじつ） several days. It can also stand before larger units, e.g. 数百, several hundred. The meaning depends on the following unit; 数 alone gives no fixed numerical value. This prefix use is to be distinguished from 数（すう） as a mathematical noun and 数（かず） as a count.

examples[].german: Please submit the report by the end of this month.
After careful consideration, I decided to quit the company.
en.notes: The end of a period: 今月の末 (the end of this month). After a verb in the た-form: 考えた末に (after long deliberation). Also 末っ子 (youngest child).

examples[].german: Swiss watches are expensive but durable.
Four languages are spoken in Switzerland.
en.notes: Country name in katakana. Known for watches (スイスの時計) and the Alps (アルプス).

examples[].german: In winter we skate on the lake.
It's my first time skating, so I can't glide well yet.
en.notes: Mainly ice skating (スケートをする); skating rink: スケートリンク. Skateboard is スケボー.

examples[].german: During winter vacation I'm going skiing in Nagano.
How much does it cost to rent skis?
en.notes: Refers to the sport and to the skis themselves. "To go skiing": スキーに行く; "to ski": スキーをする.

examples[].german: She became a star overnight.
I mark important emails with a star.
en.notes: A famous person (映画スター) and the star symbol. A star in the sky is 星.

en.meaning: stand; grandstand; floor lamp; gas station
examples[].german: The stands were full of fans.
I turned on the desk lamp and read a book.
en.notes: Several meanings: spectator stand in a stadium, vending stand, desk or floor lamp (電気スタンド), and short for gas station (ガソリンスタンド).

examples[].german: Instead of a reply, I sent a cute sticker.
I collected stamps at the stations.
en.notes: Two meanings: a stamp (e.g. スタンプラリー at train stations, a stamp card) and the large stickers in messenger apps such as LINE.

en.meaning: other, another, the rest (e.g. その他, 他の人)
examples[].german: Please write your name, address and other information here.
As for fruit, there are apples, mandarins and many other kinds.
Let's think again whether there isn't another method.
en.notes: Sino-Japanese reading of 他, fixed mainly in その他 "others, and other things" and 自他 "oneself and others". With 他の "other", both readings are possible: in conversation the native reading ほか (vocab-n5:1433) predominates, while the reading た sounds more literary and matter-of-fact. ほかに "besides", on the other hand, is never read た.

examples[].german: In spring, the paddies are flooded with water.
Rice is growing lush and green in the paddy.
en.notes: Rare on its own, mostly in 田んぼ (rice field), 田植え (rice planting) and in many names (田中, 山田). Dry field: 畑.

examples[].german: I bundled up the old newspapers and put them out.
A bundle of old letters turned up in the drawer.
en.notes: Things tied together: 花束（はなたば, bouquet), 札束 (wad of banknotes). Also a counter: ほうれん草一束.

examples[].german: Next month I am going on a trip to Hokkaido by myself.
I wrote my travel memories in my diary.
en.notes: A little more evocative than 旅行: 一人旅 (solo trip), 旅に出る (to set out on a journey). Proverb: かわいい子には旅をさせよ.

examples[].german: Thank you for your help on this occasion.
Every time I hear this song, I remember the old days.
en.notes: Mostly as この度 (this time, formal) or 〜たびに (every time): 会うたびに. Often written in kana; 度 is otherwise also read ど (degree, time).

examples[].german: Sorry to contact you again and again.
Accidents happen frequently on this road.
en.notes: Something happens repeatedly (often slightly annoying): たびたびすみません (sorry for the repeated disturbance). Kanji 度々.

en.meaning: only, just; free of charge; ordinary; however
examples[].german: Admission to this event is free.
It's just an ordinary cold, so don't worry.
en.notes: Several uses: "only" (ただ見ているだけ), "free" (ただで = free of charge), "ordinary" (ただの風邪) and, at the start of a sentence, "however". The kanji 只／唯 are rare.

examples[].german: These two phrases form a matching pair in terms of meaning.
The poet thought of a fitting counterpart to the first line.
en.notes: In older or literary language, the reading たい can refer to a matching pair or its fitting counterpart, e.g. two verses that relate to each other. This rare meaning is explicitly attested as a noun. In today's everyday language, 対 for an ordinary pair is usually read つい; 一対 is also read いっつい. The examples deliberately use the literary sense with the reading たい.

examples[].german: The counterpart of 「動」 is 「静」.
This painting depicts light and darkness as opposites.
en.notes: As an independent noun, 対（たい）here means a counterpart or an opposite, especially in a conceptual contrast. The word sounds objective or formal. Its use between sports teams or numbers belongs to other meanings; an ordinary pair of objects is usually called 対（つい）.

examples[].german: My grandfather lived through the Second World War.
This building burned down once during the war.
After the war, the town was gradually rebuilt.
en.notes: Refers to a large, usually worldwide war and appears almost always in 第一次世界大戦 / 第二次世界大戦 "First/Second World War", or in short as 大戦中 "during the war" and 大戦後 "after the war". The general word for war is 戦争. Do not confuse with the homophone 対戦 "match, competition" (vocab-n2:400).

examples[].german: This photo is my greatest treasure.
The children played a treasure-hunting game on the island.
en.notes: A valuable possession, also figuratively: 子どもは国の宝 (children are the treasure of the nation). Related: 宝物（たからもの）, 宝くじ (lottery).

examples[].german: Vegetables arrived from my parents' home by parcel delivery.
I would like to send this package by parcel delivery.
en.notes: Parcel delivery to the front door, for example by Yamato (宅急便 is their brand name). If nobody is home: 不在票 in the mailbox.

examples[].german: The soldier was hit by a bullet and injured.
There are no more bullets in this gun.
en.notes: A bullet from a firearm; same reading as 玉 (ball, sphere), but written 弾 when ammunition is meant. Also 弾丸（だんがん）.

examples[].german: Today is unbearably hot.
I miss my family terribly.
en.notes: A very strong feeling: unbearable (暑くてたまらない), irresistibly good (この味がたまらない) or "wanting badly" (会いたくてたまらない). Kanji 堪らない.

en.meaning: to accumulate, to pile up, to bottle up (e.g. stress, water); to let (bills) build up
examples[].german: To avoid bottling up stress, I exercise on weekends.
Could you run some water into the bath for me?
I let three months of rent pile up and got scolded by my landlord.
en.notes: Transitive counterpart of 溜まる: one lets something accumulate, e.g. ストレスを溜める, 風呂にお湯を溜める, 目に涙を溜める. Also used for things left undone: 仕事を溜める, 家賃を溜める "to fall behind on the rent". For money or points that one saves deliberately, 貯める (its own card) is written; in kana, ためる, both are very common.

examples[].german: I tried out a new restaurant just to see.
He has never once kept a promise.
en.notes: Mostly in 試しに (as a trial): 試しに使ってみる. 〜た試しがない = it has never happened that ... Verb: 試す.

examples[].german: The teacher explained it using an easy-to-understand analogy.
His talks contain many analogies and are very entertaining.
That's not a true story, just a parable.
en.notes: 例え is a figurative comparison or an illustrative example; it belongs to the verb 例える "to compare", typical are 例え話 "parable" and 例えを使う. 例 れい, by contrast, is a concrete example, and 例えば means "for example". Do not confuse with the adverb たとえ "even if" (たとえ〜ても), which is usually written in kana and has its own card.

examples[].german: A letter arrived from my mother back home.
I haven't heard from my friend studying abroad for a while.
en.notes: News from someone, especially a letter: 便りがない (to not hear from someone). Proverb: 便りのないのは良い便り (No news is good news).

examples[].german: I'll get off at the next stop.
I waited twenty minutes for the bus at the stop.
en.notes: A bus or tram stop; in everyday speech usually shortened to バス停. Train stations are called 駅.

examples[].german: I performed magic tricks at the party and amazed everyone.
I just can't figure out how this trick works.
en.notes: A sleight-of-hand trick for entertainment; "to perform a trick": 手品をする. Magician: 手品師 or マジシャン.

examples[].german: This land is suitable for growing rice.
It is hard to find a job that suits you.
en.notes: Mostly 〜に適する (to be suitable for something), often attributive: 子どもに適した本. The negative is usually 適さない. More formal than 向いている.

examples[].german: We pitched the tent near the river.
The rain soaked even the inside of the tent.
en.notes: To pitch a tent: テントを張る. Very common when camping (キャンプ).

examples[].german: I telework two days a week.
Teleworking has eliminated my commuting time.
en.notes: Working from home or on the go; similar: リモートワーク, 在宅勤務 (N3).

en.meaning: when; as soon as (conditional and temporal particle)
examples[].german: When you press this button, the door opens.
When I came out of the station, a friend was waving.
en.notes: Here と follows the plain form of a verb or i-adjective and links a condition or event to a following result. It is especially suited to regular or automatic results, e.g. ボタンを押すと "when you press the button". It can also introduce the event that immediately follows in a narrative. Requests and freely chosen intentions as the result usually fit たら or なら better. The functions "and", "with" and quoting have their own uses; the identically read shogi piece is a noun.

en.meaning: seventh in the iroha order; the note G (Japanese note name)
examples[].german: In the application form, please answer the seven items from イ to ト.
The column ト of the table lists the seventh candidate.
The teacher played the note G on the piano for us to hear.
This piece is written in G major.
en.notes: In the iroha order イ・ロ・ハ・ニ・ホ・ヘ・ト, ト comes seventh and can thus mark the seventh position of an ordered list. As a Japanese note name, ト denotes the note G, e.g. in ト長調 "G major". These are different systems of reference: counting from ハ（C）, G is the fifth note; "seventh iroha position" does not mean "seventh degree of the C major scale". The particle と and the shogi piece と have other functions. Katakana is usually used for the note name.

examples[].german: I thought it would be sunny. But suddenly it started to rain.
I had heard it was an easy exam. But I couldn't do any of it.
en.notes: Introduces an unexpected result: one expected something, but it turned out differently. Kanji 所が are rare.

examples[].german: Only certain employees can enter this room.
People with an allergy to specific foods, please let us know in advance.
The security camera footage led to the identification of the culprit.
en.notes: Used mainly attributively with の: 特定の人 "specific people", 特定の目的 "a specific purpose", 不特定多数 "an unspecified large number". As a noun it means "identification, determination" (犯人の特定, 原因の特定); the verb form is the card 特定する. Unlike 特別 "special, extraordinary", 特定 only says that something particular has been selected, not that it stands out.

examples[].german: He is my lifelong friend.
When traveling alone, I always have a book as my companion.
en.notes: More elevated, often more poetic than 友達: 生涯の友 (friend for life). Also "constant companion": 本を友とする.

examples[].german: This truck can carry ten tons of cargo.
Every year, millions of tons of food are thrown away.
en.notes: A unit of weight, usually the metric ton. The kanji 屯 is a rare ateji spelling. Homophone: とん (sound of a knock).

examples[].german: An unbelievable accident happened in front of the station.
"Thank you very much." "Not at all, don't mention it."
en.notes: い-adjective: outrageous, preposterous (とんでもない値段). As a modest reply to thanks or praise, "Not at all, don't mention it": とんでもないです.

en.meaning: to pass by; to go past
examples[].german: I was so absorbed in the conversation that I rode past my station.
The typhoon passed and the sky became bright.
en.notes: Ichidan verb from 通る and 過ぎる; the place takes を: 駅を通り過ぎる (to go past a station without getting off).

examples[].german: She got the top score on the exam.
The company's top management apologized at a press conference.
en.notes: First place (クラスでトップ), the head of an organization (会社のトップ), and the upper side. Also the home page of a website (トップページ).

examples[].german: Turkey lies between Europe and Asia.
Turkish ice cream is very stretchy.
en.notes: Country name in katakana (since 2022 also officially テュルキエ, but in daily life mostly トルコ).

examples[].german: This bridge was completed over many years.
Thirty years have passed since then.
en.notes: Evocative word for a long span of time that has passed: 長い年月がたつ. Also read ねんげつ (more literary). Not to be confused with 年月日 (date).

examples[].german: On the train, let us offer our seats to elderly people.
Only old people are left in this village.
en.notes: Colloquial; usually the polite form お年寄り. Rude as a direct form of address; neutral: 高齢者. In sumo, also an elder of the association.

examples[].german: Please return these books by next week.
The city is expanding its collection of children's books.
en.notes: Written-language collective term for books, mainly in compounds: 図書館 (library), 図書室 (school library), 図書券 (book voucher). In everyday speech, individual books are called 本.

examples[].german: The moment I left the house, it started to rain.
The moment he saw my face, he burst out laughing.
en.notes: Mostly as ～た途端(に): immediately after something happened, often surprisingly. Practiced in grammar as ～たとたん; often also written in hiragana.

examples[].german: He founded a new party.
I haven't decided yet which party to vote for.
en.notes: Political party, often as a suffix: 自民党, 野党 (opposition), 与党 (ruling party). Homophone: 問う (to ask).

examples[].german: The five-story pagoda of the temple was built 700 years ago.
A white tower stands on the hill and is clearly visible even from afar.
en.notes: A tall, slender structure: 東京タワー is called タワー, but a temple's pagoda is a 塔 (五重塔 = five-story pagoda). Similar sound: 問う.

examples[].german: Back then there were no mobile phones yet.
At the time of the accident, I was abroad.
en.notes: Noun/adverb for a point in the past: 当時の日本 (Japan at that time), 大学生の当時. Not used for the present.

examples[].german: The bird spread its large wings and flew away.
Snow is piled on the wings of the airplane.
en.notes: Wings of birds and airplanes; poetically also a symbol of freedom and dreams.

en.meaning: to pour (into a cup/glass); to serve (food)
examples[].german: Please pour tea for the guest.
Shall I serve you a bit more rice?
At the drinking party, I poured beer into the department head's glass.
en.notes: 注ぐ in the reading つぐ means "to pour into a vessel" and is mostly written in kana: お茶をつぐ, ご飯をつぐ "to fill a bowl with rice". The reading そそぐ (its own card) is more general and more formal; rivers also flow into the sea, or one "pours" energy into something (力を注ぐ). For eating and drinking in daily life one says つぐ; do not confuse with 継ぐ "to inherit" and 次ぐ "to follow".

examples[].german: After ten years, my dream finally came true.
I waited, but he never showed up in the end.
en.notes: After a long time or many steps: 遂に完成した. Usually written in hiragana ついに. With a negative: not until the very end (遂に来なかった). Similar: とうとう, やっと.

examples[].german: I have known him for over ten years.
I attended the drinking party out of social obligation.
en.notes: Dealings with others: 付き合いが長い (to have known each other for a long time), 近所付き合い (relations with neighbors); also obligatory events such as drinking parties with colleagues (付き合いで飲む).

examples[].german: That deer has long antlers.
Please don't go near this cow so you don't get hurt by its horns.
en.notes: 角 is read つの here and refers to a horn or an antler. In 鹿の角, の names the animal the antler belongs to. 角で describes that a horn can cause, for example, an injury. This card is about the body part; the readings かど for corner and かく for angle belong to other entries.

en.meaning: painful; emotionally hard; hard to bear
examples[].german: It is painful to part from my family.
It was hard doing all the work alone, so I had a colleague help me.
en.notes: 辛い is read つらい here and describes emotional pain or a situation that is hard to bear. It is often written in hiragana as つらい. The reading からい of the same kanji denotes a spicy taste and belongs to a different word. As an i-adjective, つらい becomes つらかった in the past and つらくて before て.

examples[].german: Has your companion arrived yet?
My companion is running late, so I will wait a little longer.
en.notes: A person one is traveling or going out with: お連れ様 (your companion, polite), 子ども連れ (with a child). Verb: 連れる.

en.meaning: to poke; to tap; to peck (at food); to nitpick (at mistakes); to egg on
examples[].german: When my shoulder was tapped and I turned around, a friend was standing there.
Pigeons are pecking at breadcrumbs in the park.
Stop picking at other people's small mistakes.
en.notes: つつく is almost always written in kana; without context, the kanji 突く is usually read つく (separate card "to thrust, stab"). つつく means a light, repeated tapping: 肩をつつく "to tap on the shoulder", a bird つつく "pecks". Figuratively, 人のミスをつつく means "to nitpick at mistakes" and 箸でご飯をつつく "to poke listlessly at one's food". Colloquial intensified form: 突っつく.

examples[].german: This train passes through the next station without stopping.
I passed the first round of the exam without any problem.
en.notes: Passing through without stopping (この電車は次の駅を通過します) and, figuratively, passing an exam or a bill (法案が通過する). As a verb 通過する. Similar sounding: 通貨 (currency).

examples[].german: I want to see the next part of this drama soon.
Let's continue the conversation tomorrow.
en.notes: Continuation of a story, series or activity: 話の続き. As a suffix, "continuous": 雨続き. Not to be confused with 手続き (procedures, formalities).

examples[].german: When you get home, wash your hands and gargle.
My throat hurt, so I gargled with salt water.
en.notes: As a verb うがいする. In Japan, 手洗い・うがい (hand washing and gargling) after coming home is considered a basic rule against colds. Kanji 嗽／含嗽 are rare.

examples[].german: My father drinks a little whisky before bed.
Japanese whisky is popular overseas too.
en.notes: Also written ウィスキー. Japanese whisky is internationally known; mixed with soda it is called ハイボール.

examples[].german: I got my wallet back because I was lucky.
I had bad luck today: the bus I was about to take broke down.
en.notes: 運 is a noun for luck, fate or the role of chance. 運がいい describes good luck, 運が悪い accordingly bad luck. The word should be distinguished from the identically sounding casual reply うん. 運 itself is not inflected; in 運が悪く, the following i-adjective 悪い takes its connective form.

examples[].german: I could see the shadows of fish swimming along the river bottom.
When the net was pulled in, a silver fish leapt.
en.notes: 魚 is read うお on this card; the reading さかな has the same meaning. Pronounce u and o one after the other: うお has two morae and does not become a long vowel. In 魚河岸（うおがし, fish market district）this reading is preserved. The examples describe fish as animals, not a prepared fish dish.

en.meaning: to obtain (formal); to be able to, to be possible (after a verb stem)
examples[].german: Obtaining the residents' approval is a condition for moving the plan forward.
Even a small mistake can lead to a big accident.
en.notes: In formal language, 得る／うる can mean "to obtain", e.g. 承認をうる. After the stem before ます it expresses possibility: 起こりうる "can happen", 予想しうる "can be foreseen". These forms say nothing about whether something actually happens. The reading うる is used mainly at the end of a sentence or before a noun; in today's negative and past, えない and えた are used, not うない or うた. The ordinary reading える is learned separately. The accent shown here applies to 得る／うる on its own; compound words have their own accents.

examples[].german: There is a small injury on the upper lip.
The wind is cold, so I'll put on one more jacket.
en.notes: うわ stands as a word component before another word: 上唇（うわくちびる）is the upper lip, 上着（うわぎ）a garment for the upper body or the outer layer of clothing. In 上着, き becomes ぎ. For the independent location word "above/on", 上（うえ）is normally used; うわ cannot simply be substituted there.

en.meaning: counter for birds and rabbits (counter; 一羽, 三羽/さんば)
examples[].german: Two sparrows have come to the garden.
We keep one rabbit at our house.
Six ducks were swimming in the pond.
en.notes: The standard counter for birds, traditionally also for rabbits: 一羽（いちわ）, 二羽（にわ）, but 三羽（さんば）, 六羽（ろっぱ）, 十羽（じゅっぱ） with sound changes. Do not confuse with the card 羽/はね "feather, wing" - same spelling, different reading and meaning. For other animals one uses 〜匹 or 〜頭.

examples[].german: Everyone held hands and formed a circle.
Since I started university, my circle of friends has grown.
en.notes: Ring or circle: 輪になる (to form a circle), 輪ゴム (rubber band). Figuratively: 友達の輪 (circle of friends). The reading りん is a counter for flowers (一輪).

examples[].german: I had a glass of red wine with dinner.
This wine was imported from France.
en.notes: Grape wine; rice wine is called 日本酒. Red wine is 赤ワイン, white wine 白ワイン.

examples[].german: At the station, I was reluctant to say goodbye to my friend.
Having gone through a painful breakup, she became stronger.
en.notes: Parting (別れのあいさつ) and the breakup of a couple (別れ話). Verb: 別れる.

en.meaning: technique; art; skill; (martial arts) hold, throw
examples[].german: In the judo match, he executed a beautiful technique.
The craftsman has polished his skill over decades.
This skater showed off one difficult trick after another.
en.notes: A native Japanese word for a technique or craftsmanship acquired through practice, especially in martial arts (柔道の技 "judo technique", 技をかける "to apply a technique") and crafts (職人の技). Set phrase: 技を磨く "to hone one's skill". Unlike 技術/ぎじゅつ ("technique, technology", more factual-technical), 技 emphasizes personal ability; 特技 is one's own special skill.

examples[].german: The city's website has information on how to dispose of garbage.
I work on building new websites.
en.notes: Full form; in conversation usually shortened to サイト or (increasingly outdated) ホームページ.

examples[].german: I found a cheap place to stay near the station.
Since it is a long holiday weekend, you should book lodging early.
en.notes: Lodging when traveling, especially traditional inns; "to book lodging": 宿を取る. More formal: 宿泊, 旅館, ホテル.

examples[].german: I fed the goats at the ranch.
Goats are said to eat paper - is that true?
en.notes: Often written in kana (やぎ／ヤギ); 山羊 is a jukujikun spelling: the kanji ("mountain sheep") convey the meaning, not the reading. Goat's milk: ヤギのミルク.

examples[].german: I took on the role of moderating the meeting.
In this film, he plays the role of a father.
en.notes: 役 denotes an assigned duty or function and also the role of a character in theater or film. 役を引き受ける means to take on the duty; 父親の役 names a father figure that is played. The exact function is clear from the context. This noun is read やく and should be distinguished from similar-sounding words such as 焼く or 約.

examples[].german: We left the harbor before dawn.
While we were talking, it had become deep night.
en.notes: よ means "night" just like よる. This shorter reading appears e.g. in 夜が明ける, "day breaks", and 夜が更ける, "the night wears on". Here が marks the night as the subject. In 夜が明ける前に, the action takes place before dawn. Pronounce よ short; it is neither よう nor や.

examples[].german: Just in case, I brought extra paper.
I try not to buy unnecessary things.
en.notes: More than needed: 余分なお金 (surplus money), 余分に買う (to buy extra).

examples[].german: An unexpected problem occurred.
The result was as expected.
en.notes: Mostly negated: 予期しない出来事 (an unexpected event), in writing 予期せぬ. As a verb 予期する.

examples[].german: A child suddenly crossed the road, so I stopped the car.
A black cat ran across in front of me.
en.notes: Transitive godan verb (not ichidan despite the る ending): 道を横切る, 目の前を猫が横切った. Similar: 渡る (to cross over).

examples[].german: Please tell me the reading of this kanji.
The coach's judgment was right, and we won the game.
en.notes: The reading of a kanji (音読み, 訓読み), reading itself, and the assessment of a situation (読みが当たる = to predict correctly). Verb: 読む.

en.meaning: good!, all right!, let's go! (exclamation of determination or approval)
examples[].german: Good, that's everything prepared.
"I'm done!" "Good, well done."
All right, today I'm finally going to run ten kilometers!
en.notes: An exclamation with which one spurs oneself or others on ("let's go!"), ticks something off as done, or gives someone approval ("good!"). Stretched as よーし or ようし it sounds more determined. Casual; not really used toward superiors. Unlike さあ, which urges others to begin, よし mainly expresses one's own resolve. Do not confuse with the classical adjective 良し (良しとする "to approve").

examples[].german: That's dangerous, so stop that!
It's raining harder, so let's not go out after all.
en.notes: Colloquial for やめる; usually in kana: よしなさい (Stop that!), 行くのはよそう (Let's not go after all). Kanji 止す.

examples[].german: In summer I go sailing on the sea.
Many sailboats are lined up in the harbor.
en.notes: In Japanese, usually a sailboat, not a motorized luxury yacht.

en.meaning: caution, care; precaution (用心する: to be careful)
examples[].german: The air is dry in winter, so let's be careful with fire.
Please be careful when walking alone on a night road.
As a precaution, I put two locks on the front door.
en.notes: 用心 ようじん "caution, precaution" is used as a noun and as a suru-verb: 用心する "to be on guard", 用心のため "as a precaution", 火の用心 "beware of fire" (the classic call of the night watch). Compared with 注意 "attention, warning", 用心 stresses preventive vigilance against danger, thieves or fire. Derivatives: 用心深い "cautious", 不用心 (ぶようじん) "careless, insecure".

examples[].german: I put the leftover curry in a container and froze it.
This container cannot be used in a microwave.
en.notes: A neutral word for containers of all kinds (plastic, glass), often seen on packaging and in waste-disposal notices: プラスチック容器. Similar sound: 陽気 (cheerful).

en.meaning: to require; to need; to take (time, effort)
examples[].german: This task requires advanced skills.
It takes about twenty minutes on foot from the station to the venue.
This is a matter requiring urgent attention, so please respond right away.
en.notes: 要する is a literary verb: what is needed takes を (時間を要する, 注意を要する), the purpose often takes に (この作業には〜を要する). In daily life people say 必要とする, いる or, for time and money, かかる instead. The adverb 要するに "in short" (separate card) derives from it; 擁する "to possess, comprise" sounds the same but is a different word.

en.meaning: to say; to call, to be named (pronounced ゆう)
examples[].german: My mother says, "You don't need to hurry."
There was a phone call from a person called Tanaka.
en.notes: At the end of a sentence and before a noun, 言う is often pronounced like ゆう. In ordinary kana spelling, however, it is still written いう. ～と言う reports what someone says; ～という人 names a person with a particular name. This pronunciation belongs to the same verb as 言う（いう）. In the polite form the stem stays いい: 言います is iimasu. The usual forms 言わない（いわない）and 言った（いった）remain the standard for learning; no polite form ゆいます is formed from ゆう.

examples[].german: My father has a sense of humor.
His speech was full of humor.
en.notes: To have a sense of humor: ユーモアがある, ユーモアのセンス. A single joke is more often 冗談 or ジョーク.

examples[].german: Being able to speak English is an advantage in finding a job.
The team playing at home has the advantage.
en.notes: な-adjective: 有利な条件 (favorable conditions), 就職に有利だ. Opposite: 不利.

examples[].german: Many of this app's users are young people.
Please enter your username and password.
en.notes: A user of a product or service. Username: ユーザー名. Also written ユーザ.

examples[].german: My grandfather donated all of his assets.
This experience has become a treasure to me.
en.notes: Assets and property (money, land); figuratively also a valuable asset: 友達は一生の財産だ.

examples[].german: Roughly five hundred people gathered at the venue.
Before the meeting, I skimmed through the materials.
en.notes: An approximate amount (ざっと百人 = about a hundred people) or a quick skim (ざっと目を通す).

examples[].german: A ten percent tax is added to the price of goods.
The state collects taxes from its citizens.
en.notes: Tax in general, often as a suffix: 消費税 (consumption tax), 所得税 (income tax). In everyday speech usually 税金. Price indications: 税込み (tax included), 税抜き (tax excluded).

en.meaning: whole, entire, all- (prefix, e.g. 全世界, 全社員); total (before numbers, e.g. 全10巻)
examples[].german: The news was reported to the whole world.
At nine in the morning, all employees gathered in the meeting room.
This manga is complete in 20 volumes in total.
en.notes: A productive Sino-Japanese prefix before nouns: 全世界 "the whole world", 全社員 "all employees", 全国民 "the whole nation". Before numbers with a counter it means "in total": 全10巻 "ten volumes in total". Fixed words such as 全部, 全国, 全員 are learned as vocabulary of their own; similar is 総〜, which stresses "total, general" (総人口). Homophones: 前 "former", 善 "good", 禅 "Zen".

examples[].german: Small children cannot yet tell good from evil.
Don't put off a good deed. I'll call right now.
Some people think that human nature is good.
en.notes: An abstract, rather literary word for the morally good, usually in contrast to 悪 "evil": 善と悪, 善悪 "good and evil". The proverb 善は急げ "don't put off a good deed" is well known. For everyday "good" one says 良い/いい; 善 on its own is used only in the ethical sense. Do not confuse with the homophones 禅 "Zen", 膳 "tray" and 前 "former".

examples[].german: Reaching agreement in the discussion is a big step forward.
The car could not move forward and went back.
en.notes: 前進 is a noun for forward movement and for progress on a task. 大きな前進です evaluates a result as great progress. With する it becomes the intransitive verb "to move forward" or "to make progress"; 前進できる expresses that this is possible. The identically read 全身 means "the whole body".

examples[].german: Society is changing.
Let's talk about social problems.
en.notes: 社会 here means society or community. 社会が変わる describes social change; 社会の問題 names problems within society. With の, the noun can specify another term more closely. The abbreviated name for the school subject 社会科 is a different dictionary meaning and is not taught here.

examples[].german: I'm interested in politics.
Let's stop talking about politics.
en.notes: 政治 denotes politics or the exercise of government. 政治に興味がある means to be interested in politics; 政治の話 is a conversation about politics. The noun takes に as the object of interest and の before 話. This card deals with the field itself, not a personal name written the same way.

examples[].german: Unfortunately, I can't go.
It was a disappointing result.
en.notes: 残念 is a na-adjective meaning regrettable or disappointing. 残念ですが introduces a refusal with "unfortunately"; 残念な結果 describes a disappointing result. Before a noun it takes な, and at the end of a sentence です. The word expresses an evaluation from the speaker's point of view.

examples[].german: Please prepare the tools.
Where are the cleaning supplies?
en.notes: 道具 is a general word for tools, devices, and utensils needed for an activity. The activity often precedes it with の: 掃除の道具, "cleaning supplies". Here it refers to concrete aids. The long first syllable どう is rendered with ō in dōgu.

examples[].german: During spring break, we're planning to go to Japan with the family.
I'm traveling during spring break.
When spring break is over, the new school year begins.
en.notes: 春休み is the spring vacation; in Japan it falls between two school years (roughly the end of March to the beginning of April), and at universities it lasts from February to March. One says 春休みに～する or 春休み中. Parallel to it there are 夏休み and 冬休み; time off from work, by contrast, is 休暇 or 休み.

examples[].german: These days, more and more people are addicted to social media.
The economic situation these days is tough.
In these times when everything is expensive, more and more people make their own bento.
en.notes: 昨今 is a formal, literary word for "nowadays, recently"; it is used as a noun (昨今の経済状況, 昨今は) and often in news, speeches and letters, with a critical undertone about current trends. In conversation, people say 最近, この頃 or 近頃.

examples[].german: Good evening. What are you doing in a place like this?
Good evening, how are you?
When I meet neighbors in the evening, I greet them with "Good evening".
en.notes: 今晩は is the greeting in the evening, once it is dark; it is mostly written in hiragana こんばんは, and the は is pronounced "wa" (the spelling こんばんわ is considered wrong). It is used to greet acquaintances, neighbors or guests, but not one's own family. When parting in the evening, one does not say 今晩は but お休みなさい or 失礼します.

examples[].german: He ended up being hospitalized for food poisoning.
Please be careful about food poisoning.
My younger brother is addicted to video games and plays them all day.
en.notes: 中毒 is first of all poisoning: 食中毒 "food poisoning", 一酸化炭素中毒 "carbon monoxide poisoning"; you say 中毒になる or 中毒を起こす, 中毒する is rare. As a suffix it colloquially means "-addiction": ゲーム中毒, スマホ中毒, アルコール中毒. In formal medical texts, addiction is more often 依存症 (アルコール依存症).

examples[].german: Are rattlesnakes poisonous?
This mushroom is poisonous.
Smoke from fires contains toxic gases.
en.notes: 有毒 is a formal, technical な-adjective or noun for "poisonous, toxic": 有毒な植物, 有毒ガス, 有毒物質; the opposite is 無毒 "non-toxic". In daily life people mostly say 毒がある (このきのこには毒がある). It appears mainly in warnings, news and nonfiction texts.

examples[].german: His farts always stink like poison gas.
Poison gas is extremely dangerous.
Poison gas has been used in wars.
en.notes: 毒ガス is "poison gas", above all as a chemical weapon (毒ガス兵器) or in historical and news contexts. For toxic gases from accidents, fires or volcanoes, 有毒ガス is more common; but foul smells are also jokingly compared to 毒ガス. ガス (from Dutch) is written in katakana.

examples[].german: Anyone who stays in Japan after their visa has expired is in the country illegally.
Illegal parking is subject to a fine.
It is annoying that some people dump their trash illegally in the park.
en.notes: 不法 means "unlawful, illegal" and mostly appears as the first element of compounds: 不法駐車 "illegal parking", 不法滞在 "illegal stay", 不法投棄 "illegal dumping of waste", 不法入国; adverbial 不法に. The closely related 違法 is more common in media and technology: 違法コピー, 違法ダウンロード. Both are rather formal; in colloquial speech people say 法律違反 or だめ.

examples[].german: This kitten is still drinking its mother's milk.
I found a cute kitten.
Our cat had four kittens.
en.notes: 子猫 is a kitten, i.e. a young cat; also written 仔猫 or こねこ. The prefix 子 forms many words for young animals: 子犬, 子馬, 子牛. It is counted with 匹 (子猫が三匹). Affectionately one says 子猫ちゃん; a cat giving birth to kittens: 子猫を産む.

examples[].german: Do you know that a great fire broke out in Rome in AD 64?
In the calendar, 紀元前 and 紀元後 are distinguished (BC and AD).
en.notes: 紀元後 refers to the period after the start of a calendar era. In the Christian calendar, 紀元後64年 corresponds to the year AD 64. Year numbers with 西暦 are more common. The examples show a historical year date and the distinction between 紀元前 and 紀元後; they do not claim a precisely known birth year of Jesus.

examples[].german: I'm studying English.
This letter is written in English.
en.notes: 英語 is the noun for the English language. 英語を勉強する names it as what is being studied; 英語で names it as the language of a statement or text. 英語の本 is a book in English. The reading is えいご; ei stays ei in romanization: eigo.

examples[].german: This is a good opportunity.
I'd be happy if there is a chance to meet again.
en.notes: 機会 means "opportunity / chance" and is read きかい. The possible action can precede the noun as a verb: お会いする機会, "an opportunity to meet". A favorable opportunity is いい機会. 機械, "machine", sounds the same but is a different word.

examples[].german: My older brother is good at English conversation, but bad at math.
I attend an English conversation class.
I use it for work, so I started learning English conversation.
en.notes: 英会話 is English conversation as a skill and a subject of study: 英会話を習う, 英会話が得意. 英会話教室 and 英会話スクール are very common; in short, 英会話 can also mean the language school itself (英会話に通う). 英語 is the language in general, while 英会話 emphasizes speaking as opposed to reading and grammar.

examples[].german: Her English writing is easy to understand and easy to read.
I translated the English text into Japanese.
My older sister majors in English literature at university.
en.notes: 英文 is an English text or sentence in written form: 英文を読む, 英文を書く, 英文を訳す; 英文法 is English grammar. At universities, 英文 is short for 英文学（科）"English literature (department)". The counterpart is 和文 "Japanese text"; the language itself is 英語.

examples[].german: He is from Britain.
I once studied in Britain.
In the news, people often say "Eikoku" rather than "Igirisu".
en.notes: 英国 is the formal, written-language term for the United Kingdom or Great Britain, not just England. It appears in news, official documents and company names; in conversation people almost always say イギリス. The abbreviation 英 appears in 英語, 日英 "Japanese-British" and 英首相 "British prime minister".

examples[].german: Is this the English-Japanese one?
I looked it up using an English-Japanese dictionary.
I have both a Japanese-English and an English-Japanese dictionary.
en.notes: 英和 means "English-Japanese" and almost always refers to dictionaries: an 英和辞典 (or simply 英和) looks up English words and explains them in Japanese. The opposite direction is 和英 "Japanese-English" (和英辞典). 和 stands for Japan here, as in 和食 or 和室.
